column2: 猎人们说他们感到 \x02\x03恶灵的存在/不知从何处刮起一阵冷风/附近潜伏着邪恶之物\x02 ，于是仓促撤退。消息令人悲伤，但并不意外。

column1: The party we sent to explore the \x01@O found an odd rock crystal which is warm to the touch. This is a tear shed by Chalana Arroy’s son, Arroin. It has great healing powers.
column2: 我们派去探索 \x01@O 的队伍发现了一块奇异的岩晶，摸上去温热。这是查拉娜·阿罗伊之子阿罗因落下的一滴泪水，拥有强大的治愈之力。

column1: our tula
column2: 我们的领地

column1: to the \x01@O
column2: 前往 \x01@O

column1: While we were exploring \x01@\x1A, we found a set of old bagpipes. At first we thought they were broken and worthless. But then one of us remembered a story about the Bagpipes of Ronskei, whose music routed the trolls during the Battle of Swen’s Ford. The last we knew they had been stolen from the \x02\x02Rastoskuli/Three Winds\x02 clan in the Holy Country, but now we’ve found them!
column2: 在我们探索 \x01@\x1A时，发现了一套旧风笛。起初我们以为它已破损无用。但有人记起了朗斯凯之风笛的传说——它的乐声曾在斯温福德之战中击退巨魔。我们最后得知它被圣国的拉斯托斯库利/三风 \x02\x02\x02 氏族偷走，但如今我们找到了它！

column1: \x01@O of here
column2: \x01@O 此处

column1: While exploring \x01@\x1A, we found a bull-roarer, similar to the ones used in Orlanth’s ceremonies. Of course, someone had to twirl it a few times. When he did, our horses ran away. We never did find one of them. But we brought back the bull-roarer, since it’s a magical treasure.
column2: 在探索 \x01@\x1A时，我们发现了一个牛吼器，类似于奥兰斯仪式中使用的那种。当然，有人忍不住转了几圈。结果我们的马都跑了，至今也没找回其中一匹。但我们带回了牛吼器，因为它是一件魔法宝物。

column1: The exploration party we sent to the \x01@O found a piece of amber that glows at night. This is a drop of Elmal’s blood, and we can use it on a raid to shoot fire-arrows.
column2: 我们派往 \x01@O 的探索队发现了一块在夜间发光的琥珀。这是埃尔马尔的一滴血，我们可以在突袭中用其射出火箭。

column1: While we were exploring \x01@\x1A, we found an odd gem. I noticed that if you looked into it, you could see faces. It turns out they’re trapped spirits of fear. We could loose them at our foes in battle.
column2: 在我们探索 \x01@\x1A时，发现了一颗奇特的宝石。我注意到，如果你凝视其中，能看到面孔。原来那是被困住的恐惧之灵。我们可以在战斗中释放它们对付敌人。

column1: While we were exploring \x01@\x1A, we stumbled onto an old grave. Everything had crumbled away, except for the head, which spoke to us, saying his name was Markanth Margrainsson.
column2: 在我们探索 \x01@\x1A时，偶然发现了一座古墓。一切都已腐朽殆尽，只剩一颗头颅。它对我们开口说话，自称马尔坎斯·马格赖恩松。

column1: He said he was pleased to see his distant descendants, and said he could help us confound our foes in battle if we carried him in the charge. So we brought the skull back.
column2: 他说很高兴见到远方的后裔，并说如果在冲锋时带上他，他能帮我们在战斗中迷惑敌人。于是我们带回了这颗头骨。

column1: The exploration party we sent to the \x01@O found a dingy grey net. They noticed it was magical, and brought it back.
column2: 我们派往 \x01@O 的探索队发现了一张灰暗的灰网。他们察觉到它具有魔法，便带了回来。

column1: It will be useful when we want to capture prisoners in battle.
column2: 若我们想在战斗中俘虏敌人，它会很有用。

column1: It will be useful if we want to capture prisoners in battle. It might be a good idea to trade it away, since our ancestors never kept thralls.
column2: 若我们想在战斗中俘虏敌人，它会很有用。或许最好把它交易掉，因为我们的祖先从不蓄奴。

column1: the \x01@O

The party we sent to \x01@\x1A found an old, partly charred battle standard. They brought it back because they thought it was magical. They were right. I’ve learned the standard’s secrets: if we ignite the standard at the start of a battle it will help us maneuver our troops. It might burn up during the fight, but it will be powerful magic while it lasts.
column2: 我们派往 \x01@\x1A 的队伍发现了一面老旧、部分烧焦的战旗。他们觉得它有魔法，便带了回来。他们是对的。我已掌握了战旗的秘密：如果在战斗开始时点燃它，它将帮助我们机动部队。它可能在战斗中烧尽，但在持续期间能释放强大的魔法。

column1: The party we sent to \x01@\x1A found an unusual piece of quartz. It seemed to spark easily, so they brought it back. It wasn’t too hard to learn its secret, because our clan magic increased as soon as we received it. It’s a Seventh Wind Crystal. If we ever lose it, we’ll lose that magic.
column2: 我们派往 \x01@\x1A 的队伍发现了一块不寻常的石英。它似乎很容易迸出火花，于是他们带了回来。它的秘密不难参透，因为我们一收到它，氏族魔法就增强了。这是第七风水晶。一旦失去它，我们也会失去那魔法。

column1: The party we sent to \x01@\x1A found an unusual piece of flint. They thought it might be special, so they brought it back. They were right, as I’ve recently learned that it’s a Splinter Rock. We can use it at the start of a battle to improve the effectiveness of our combat magic.
column2: 我们派往 \x01@\x1A 的队伍发现了一块不寻常的燧石。他们认为它可能特别，于是带了回来。他们是对的——我最近得知这是一块裂石。我们可以在战斗开始时用它来提升战斗魔法的效果。

column1: Chaotic place known as Snakepipe Hollow
column2: 被称为蛇管谷的混沌之地

column1: Our expedition to the \x01@\x17 is a great success. \x01@\x05 found and eradicated several nests of Chaos creatures, recovering not only valuable \x02\x04metals/relics of ancient times/fabric/spices\x02, but also a fabulous treasure.
column2: 我们前往 \x01@\x17 的远征大获成功。 \x01@\x05 发现并消灭了好几处混沌生物的巢穴，不仅回收了珍贵的 \x02\x04金属/古代遗物/布料/香料\x02，还找到了一件绝妙的宝物。

column1: An expedition to the \x01@\x17 recovered valuable goods, and a fabulous treasure.
column2: 前往 \x01@\x17 的远征回收了贵重货物和一件绝妙的宝物。

column1: The treasure is called Uralda’s Milk-Pot, and it will make us wiser when our knowledge of animals is tested.
column2: 那宝物名为乌拉尔达的奶壶，当我们的动物知识受到考验时，它将使我们更为睿智。

column1: The treasure is a jewelled half-mask called the Beard of Lhankor Mhy; it will aid our lawspeakers in interpreting legal precedents.
column2: 那宝物是一件镶宝石的半面具，名为兰科尔·米的胡须；它将帮助我们的法律宣讲者诠释法律先例。

column1: It is one of the legendary rings made from the crown of King Vingkot Orlanthsson. It will make our clan leaders wiser and more persuasive.
column2: 它是用文戈特·奥兰斯森王的王冠制成的传奇指环之一。它将使我们氏族的首领更加睿智，更具说服力。

column1: Our expedition to the \x01@\x17 is a success. \x01@\x05 found and eradicated several nests of Chaos creatures, recovering valuable \x02\x04metals/relics of ancient times/fabric/spices\x02.
column2: 我们对 \x01@\x17 的远征取得了成功。 \x01@\x05 发现并清除了数个混沌生物的巢穴，回收了珍贵的 \x02\x04金属/远古遗物/布料/香料\x02。

column1: An expedition to the \x01@\x17 recovered valuable goods.
column2: 对 \x01@\x17 的远征回收了有价值的货物。

column1: Members of our expedition to the \x01@\x17 have all returned safely to us. \x01@\x05 found several nests of Chaos creatures, and did ferocious battle with them. They were not all slain, but our explorers still managed to recover a few items of value.
column2: 我们对 \x01@\x17 的远征成员均已安全返回。 \x01@\x05 发现了数个混沌生物的巢穴，并与它们展开了激烈的战斗。它们并未被全部杀死，但我们的探险者仍设法回收了一些有价值之物。

column1: An expedition to the \x01@\x17 recovered some goods of value.
column2: 对 \x01@\x17 的远征回收了一些有价值的货物。

column1: Members of our expedition to the \x01@\x17 have all returned safely to us, although some of them were wounded. They say that the place is crawling with Chaos creatures, and that they were lucky to escape with their lives, and a little bit of loot they found \x02\x05under a rock/hidden in a log/among a pile of corpses/baiting a trap for them/scattered in a cavern\x02.
column2: 我们对 \x01@\x17 的远征成员均已安全返回，尽管其中有人受伤。他们说那地方到处是混沌生物，他们能带着找到的一点战利品 \x02\x05在岩石下/藏在圆木中/在一堆尸体间/作为引诱它们的陷阱/散落在洞穴中\x02而保住性命，已是幸运。

column1: An expedition to the \x01@\x17 found a little bit of loot, and survived pitched battle with its many creatures of Chaos.
column2: 对 \x01@\x17 的远征找到了一点战利品，并在与众多混沌生物的激烈战斗中幸存。

column1: Survivors of our expedition to the \x01@\x17 have returned to our tula. Some of them are wounded. \x01@\x0B explorers are dead. They say that the place is crawling with Chaos creatures, and that it is surprising that any of them survived their excursion into this place of dread.
column2: 我们对 \x01@\x17 的远征幸存者已返回我们的领地。其中有人受伤。 \x01@\x0B 名探险者阵亡。他们说那地方到处是混沌生物，他们中竟有人能在这次恐怖的旅程中幸存，实属意外。

column1: An expedition to the \x01@\x17 found itself in pitched battle with its many creatures of Chaos; some were killed, and others wounded.
column2: 对 \x01@\x17 的远征与众多混沌生物展开了激烈战斗；有人被杀，有人受伤。

column1: Survivors of our expedition to the \x01@\x17 have returned to our tula. Almost all of them are wounded. \x01@\x0B explorers are dead. They say that the place is crawling with Chaos creatures, and that it is surprising that any of them survived their excursion into this place of dread.
column2: 我们对 \x01@\x17 的远征幸存者已返回我们的领地。几乎所有人都有伤。 \x01@\x0B 名探险者阵亡。他们说那地方到处是混沌生物，他们中竟有人能在这次恐怖的旅程中幸存，实属意外。

column1: An expedition to the \x01@\x17 found itself in pitched battle with its many creatures of Chaos; many were killed, and most others wounded.
column2: 对 \x01@\x17 的远征与众多混沌生物展开了激烈战斗；多人被杀，其余大多受伤。

column1: \x01@\x05 returns from our expedition to the \x01@\x17 as its sole survivor. \x05 reports that the land seethes with Chaos creatures, and that it is a miracle that \x06 survives to tell the tale.
column2: \x01@\x05  \x01@\x17 返回，是我们远征的唯一幸存者。 \x05 报告说那片土地充斥着混沌生物， \x06 能活下来讲述这个故事，简直是个奇迹。

column1: An expedition to the \x01@\x17 ended in disaster; all but the expedition leader were slain by creatures of Chaos.
column2: 对 \x01@\x17 的远征以灾难告终；除远征队长外，所有人均被混沌生物杀害。

column1: No one has returned from our expedition to the \x01@\x17. Sadly, we can now assume that all of them are dead. The remaining warriors are openly criticizing us for sending explorers to such a dangerous place.
column2: 我们对 \x01@\x17的远征无人返回。悲哀的是，现在我们只能认为他们全都死了。幸存的战士们公开批评我们，指责我们将探险者派往如此危险的地方。

column1: An expedition was sent to the \x01@\x17, but no one returned. The warriors openly criticized the ring for sending explorers to such a dangerous place.
column2: 曾派遣一支远征队前往 \x01@\x17，但无人返回。战士们公开批评长老会将探险者派往如此危险的地方。

column1: Our expedition to the lands of the Horse-Spawn has returned in triumph. Our explorers found a small encampment of the cruel horse nomads, and an opportunity for plunder too tempting to resist. We swept down upon them before they could react in kind.
column2: 我们对马裔之地的远征凯旋。我们的探险者发现了一处残忍马背游牧者的小型营地，以及一个难以抗拒的劫掠机会。我们趁他们还没来得及做出反应，便席卷而下。

column1: Our explorers triumphed in the lands of the Horse-Spawn.
column2: 我们的探险者扬威于马裔之地。

column1: They rescued our enslaved clan-mates.
column2: 他们救回了我们被奴役的族人。

column1: They rescued our enslaved clan-mates. The people rejoiced.
column2: 他们救回了我们被奴役的族人。人民欢欣鼓舞。

column1: They took a dozen fine horses, kitted out in jeweled leathers, from the nomads.
column2: 他们从游牧者那里缴获了十二匹好马，配着珠宝镶嵌的皮革马具。

column1: They also took a great treasure from the Horse-Spawn thanes.
column2: 他们还从马裔贵族那里夺取了一件巨大的宝物。

column1: The treasure is a golden bowl. Our god-talkers say that it is meant to collect sacrificial blood, and that we could use it in our own rituals, to increase their power.
column2: 宝物是一只金碗。我们的神言者说，它是用来收集祭血的法器，我们可以在自己的仪式中使用它，以增强仪式的力量。

column1: The treasure is a set of golden horseshoes. Our god-talkers say that these will help us when we enter the realm of the gods.
column2: 宝物是一套金马蹄铁。我们的神言者说，当我们进入神域时，它们将帮助我们。

column1: The treasure is a wheat sheaf made from gold; it will increase our wisdom when our knowledge of planting is tested.
column2: 宝物是一只金制的麦穗；当我们的种植知识受到考验时，它将增强我们的智慧。

column1: They rescued some of our enslaved clan-mates, although others remained behind.
column2: 他们救回了一些被奴役的族人，但仍有其他人留在了那里。

column1: They rescued some of our enslaved clan-mates. The people were pleased.
column2: 他们救回了一些被奴役的族人。人们感到欣慰。

column1: They took half a dozen fine horses, kitted out in jeweled leathers, from the nomads.
column2: 他们从游牧者那里缴获了六匹好马，配着珠宝镶嵌的皮革马具。

column1: Our expedition to the lands of the Horse-Spawn was a success. \x01@\x05 found a small encampment of the cruel horse nomads, and an opportunity for plunder too tempting to resist. We swept down upon them. They fought back fiercely, with their fiery magic and leaping horses, but none of our explorers was seriously hurt.
column2: 我们对马裔之地的远征获得了成功。 \x01@\x05 发现了一处残忍马背游牧者的小型营地，以及一个难以抗拒的劫掠机会。我们席卷而下。他们用炽热的魔法和跳跃的战马激烈反击，但我们的探险者中无人受重伤。

column1: Our explorers were valiant in the lands of the Horse-Spawn.
column2: 我们的探险者在马裔之地英勇奋战。

column1: They rescued a few of our enslaved clan-mates, but others remained behind.
column2: 他们救回了几名被奴役的族人，但仍有其他人留在了那里。

column1: They rescued a few of our enslaved clan-mates.
column2: 他们解救了我们几名被奴役的族人。

column1: They took three fine horses, kitted out in jeweled leathers, from the nomads.
column2: 他们从游牧者那里夺走了三匹好马，配着镶宝皮革鞍辔。

column1: The members of our expedition to the lands of the hated Horse-Spawn have returned. They tell of a daring adventure, in which they swept down on an encampment of the horse nomads and survived the onslaught of their fiery magics and leaping horses. Only a few were wounded, and several ornamental weapons were seized as loot.
column2: 前往可憎马裔之地的远征成员已经返回。他们讲述了一次大胆的冒险，他们突袭了一座马背游牧者的营地，并经受住了他们烈火魔法与腾跃战马的猛攻。仅有少数人受伤，并缴获了几件装饰武器作为战利品。

column1: Our explorers engaged in a daring raid while in the territory of the hated Horse-Spawn, and very few of them were wounded.
column2: 我们的探索者在可憎马裔的领地上发动了一次大胆的突袭，受伤者寥寥无几。

column1: They were unable to rescue our enslaved clan-mates, however.
column2: 然而，他们未能解救我们被奴役的族人。

column1: Survivors of our expedition to the territory of the hated Horse-Spawn have returned to our tula. Some of them are wounded. \x01@\x0B explorers were captured by the nomads and enslaved. \x01@\x05 says that their fiery magics and leaping horses were terrifying to behold, and that it is surprising that any of them escaped the clutches of the cruel horse folk.
column2: 前往可憎马裔领地的远征幸存者已回到我们的领地。其中一些人受了伤。 \x01@\x0B 探索者被游牧者俘虏并成了奴隶。 \x01@\x05 说目睹他们烈火魔法与腾跃战马实在可怖，任何人能从残暴马族手中逃脱都令人惊讶。

column1: Survivors of an unfortunate expedition to the territory of the hated Horse-Spawn returned to our tula. Some of them were wounded. \x01@\x0B explorers had been captured by the nomads and enslaved.
column2: 一次不幸远征可憎马裔领地的幸存者回到了我们的领地。其中一些人受了伤。 \x01@\x0B 探索者已被游牧者俘虏并成了奴隶。

column1: \x01@\x05 has returned from our expedition to the lands of the hated Horse-Spawn, alone. \x05 reports that the party engaged a weak-seeming group of the horse nomads, but were overwhelmed by their fiery magics and leaping horses. The others are now captives of the Horse-Spawn, and will be enslaved.
column2: \x01@\x05 已从前往可憎马裔之地的远征中独自返回。 \x05 报告说队伍遭遇了一群看似弱小的马背游牧者，却被他们的烈火魔法和腾跃战马所压制。其他成员现已成为马裔的俘虏，将被奴役。

column1: \x01@\x05 returned from our expedition to the lands of the hated Horse-Spawn, alone. \x03 companions had been taken as thralls by the Horse-Spawn.
column2: \x01@\x05 从前往可憎马裔之地的远征中返回，孤身一人。 \x03 同伴已被马裔掳为奴隶。

column1: No one has returned from our expedition to the lands of the hated Horse-Spawn. Sadly, we can now assume that all of them are dead. The remaining warriors are openly criticizing us for sending explorers to such a dangerous place.
column2: 前往可憎马裔之地的远征无人生还。悲痛的是，我们现在可以推定他们全部阵亡。余下的武士公开批评我们派遣探索者前往如此危险之地。

column1: An expedition was sent to the territory of the Horse-Spawn, but no one returned. The warriors openly criticized the ring for sending explorers to such a dangerous place.
column2: 一支远征队被派往马裔领地，但无人生还。武士们公开批评长老会将探索者派往如此危险之地。

column1: Our expedition to the harsh plains of Prax has returned in triumph. Our explorers found an opportunity for plunder too ripe to resist: a vulnerable-seeming encampment of strange nomads who rode upon \x02\x05small, striped horses/big lizards/huge, humped cattle/furry, long-necked beasts/sleek deer-like beasts with knife-like horns\x02. Our people swept down upon them, driving them like sheep before a clever alynx. The nomads did not have much loot, but what loot they had, our explorers took.
column2: 前往严酷的普拉克斯平原的远征凯旋而归。我们的探索者发现了一个无法抗拒的劫掠良机：一座看似脆弱的陌生游牧者营地，他们骑着 \x02\x05小型条纹马/大蜥蜴/巨大的驼峰牛/毛茸茸的长颈兽/有着刀锋般尖角的灵巧鹿状野兽\x02。我们的人向他们猛扑过去，如同机灵的艾林克斯驱赶羊群一般驱赶他们。游牧者并没有多少战利品，但凡是他们有的，我们的探索者都拿走了。

column1: Our explorers triumphed in the harsh plains of Prax.
column2: 我们的探索者在严酷的普拉克斯平原取得了胜利。

column1: They also took a magical treasure from the primitive plainsmen.
column2: 他们还从原始平原民那里夺取了一件魔法宝物。

column1: The treasure is a pair of strange, hairy shells. Our god-talkers said that these were holy to Uralda, who the plainsmen worship under the false name of Eiritha. They said that this treasure would help us to soothe the affronted.

column1: After defeating a fearsome nomad army from the far northern land of Pent, their old king, Varstapoor, has ascended to the immortal guardianship of the Great Earthshaker Temple in Wintertop. His son, Ovartien Twinson, has been chosen to succeed him. Ovartien is popular among his people; he mounts frequent raids against the part of the Lunar Empire called Sylila, thus enriching his thanes. He has allied with our hated foes, the Horse-Spawn, who they call Grazers. The Horse-Spawn help them on their raids against the Lunars.

Some of the people blame Ovartien for not reining in his steed-mad son, but others support the hot-blooded young man. I say it is good that our Horse-Spawn enemies are drawn to fight someone else for a change.

column1: Our explorers heard that Yarandros, son of Ovartien Twinson, was the new king of Tarsh. After Yarandros had provoked war with Ovartien’s Horse-Spawn allies, Ovartien abdicated his throne in protest. Yarandros’ ascent to the throne had been controversial, for his supporters said that both his qualifications and his bloodline ought to make him king. The notion of a hereditary dynasty was offensive to many freedom-loving Orlanthi, as well it should be. On the other hand, it could not be said that any foe of the Horse-Spawn was altogether bad.
column2: 我们的探子听闻，奥瓦蒂恩·特温森之子亚兰卓斯，成了塔什的新国王。亚兰卓斯主动挑起了与奥瓦蒂恩的马裔盟友的战争，奥瓦蒂恩为此退位抗议。亚兰卓斯登位一事争议颇大，因其支持者声称：论资历、论血脉，他都理应成为国王。世袭王朝的观念触怒了许多热爱自由的奥兰斯人，这本就该如此。不过话说回来，任何与马裔为敌的人，倒也不能说全无可取之处。

column2: \x05 和其他人正在探索奥尔兰斯之母的雪域时，他们发现自己被卷入了一场古老的战斗，与洛卡玛亚顿的军队作战，这位背叛者祭司试图掩盖奥尔兰斯的光芒。

column1: \x01@\x05 and the others fought against \x02\x05armored foes who fought in tight formation/lancers who fought from horseback/fighters with fiery spears, whose magic pinned them to the ground/dragonewts riding monstrous lizards/berserkers who opened doorways to the underworld with every blow they struck\x02. column2: \x01@\x05 和其他人对抗 \x02\x05结成紧密阵型作战的装甲敌人/骑在马上的枪骑兵/手持火焰长矛的战士，他们的魔法将他们钉在地上/骑在巨型蜥蜴上的龙人/每击出一击就打开冥界大门的狂战士\x02。尽管情况混乱、胜负难料，我们的探险者战斗得很出色。

column1: Another great gust blew them back to Kero Fin, where wind spirits rewarded us.

column1: They pledged to come to our aid and fight on our behalf against any other clan of Dragon Pass. They would fight one battle only, but would come whenever we called.
column2: 他们承诺来援助我们，代表我们对抗龙隘的任何其他氏族。他们只打一仗，但会随叫随到。

column1: For a moment, they let us see the world from the top of Mount Kero Fin; they said we should look for a place we wanted to explore. They said that this view would give us a great advantage the next time we went wandering.
column2: 那一刻，他们让我们从凯罗芬山巅眺望世界；他们说要寻找一个我们想要探索的地方。他们说这视野会在我们下次游荡时给我们巨大优势。

column1: We gained a shrine to Kero Fin, mother of Orlanth. The spirits said that she would shelter us during winter and could protect our children if we sacrificed to her.
column2: 我们获得了一座献给凯罗芬的神龛，她是奥尔兰斯之母。神灵们说她在冬天会庇护我们，如果我们向她献祭，她还能保护我们的孩子。

column1: Our expedition to Mount Kero Fin has not returned. That great mountain, the mother goddess who gave birth to Orlanth, encompasses many mysteries. Some say that time progresses there as it does in the realm of the gods, which is to say that anything might have happened to them. Sadly, we must mourn them and assume that they are dead.

Our fellow Orlanthi call them the Horse-Spawn, for they are clearly not entirely human, if you know what I mean.
column2: 我听说 \x02\x02西方/龙之山峰西方\x02 爬满了邪恶的外来者，他们是游牧的骑手，崇拜恶皇帝耶尔姆——也就是奥兰斯被迫杀死又复活的神明。我们的同胞奥兰斯人称他们为“马裔”，因为他们显然不完全是人类，如果你明白我的意思的话。

column1: I am also told that they take prisoners as slaves, which of course they cruelly mistreat. So it may be that those who were taken are not dead or sacrificed to the Bad Emperor, but are prisoners in one of their roving camps.
column2: 我还听说他们将俘虏当作奴隶，当然会残酷虐待。所以那些被掳走的人可能并未死去或被献祭给恶皇帝，而是囚禁在某个游荡营地中。

column1: We also learned that they preferred to enslave their prisoners, which meant that our lost people might still live in bondage to these crazy and dangerous foreigners.
column2: 我们还得知他们更喜欢奴役俘虏，这意味着我们失踪的同胞可能仍在这些疯狂危险的外来者奴役下活着。

column1: A prophecy, first whispered by the gentlest wind spirits, then sung by the small pools of water which collect after an evening rain, and passing to the lips of children in the form of a nonsense rhyme, has now reached the understanding of adult men and women. It says: “Many years ago, the dragon’s firstborn son was sent to the protection of the Island of Hills. But the chieftains of that land were capricious and cruel, or maybe just crazy, and proved a greater threat to the safety of the dragon’s son than anyone else. Long has he been in bondage, but now from the ashes of the dragon a great carriage arises, a carriage designed by Goldentongue. Those who help build it will be rewarded by the freedom of the dragon’s son, and a glorious new day will begin.”
column2: 一则预言，最初由最轻柔的风之精魂低语，后经夜雨后汇集的小水池吟唱，又以无意义的童谣形式传到孩童唇边，如今已传入成年的男女耳中。预言道：“多年前，龙之长子被送往山丘岛庇护。但那片土地上的酋长们反复无常、残忍暴虐，又或许是疯狂，竟成了龙子安全的最大威胁。他长久受缚，如今从龙之灰烬中升起一辆伟大的车驾，一辆由金舌者设计的车驾。助其建成者，将因龙子的自由而受赏，一个光辉的新纪元即将开启。”

column1: listening to the story in the Sacred Way.

column1: listening to the poetry of a bleating calf.

column1: severing more ties than the Death Maker asks.

column2: 猎捕龙人。

column1: fasting.

column1: seeking allies, then letting trolls find and fight them.

column2: 在普拉克西亚部落之间调停和平。

column1: sitting in a briar patch and challenging seven spirits to six contests.
column2: 坐在荆棘丛中，向七个灵魂挑战六场竞赛。

column1: healing their enemies.
column2: 治愈他们的敌人。

column1: The \x01@! people have a lot more cows now.
column2: \x01@! 人现在拥有更多的牛只了。

column1: Several new herds appeared in the night, because Uralda has smiled upon them.
column2: 夜间出现了几群新的畜群，因为乌拉尔达向他们微笑了。

column1: Their trickster won several herds in a bet with elders of the \x01@a clan.
column2: 他们的恶作剧者与 \x01@a 部落的长老打赌赢了几群畜群。

column1: They raided them from a troll caravan. Goodness knows where the trolls got them.
column2: 他们从一支巨魔商队那里抢来了它们。天知道巨魔从哪儿弄来的。

column1: The cows were brought from the Holy Country. Maybe the Pharaoh is trying to curry the favor of \x01@! elders.
column2: 这些牛是从圣国带来的。也许法老在试图讨好 \x01@! 长老们。

column1: They say it has something to do with the secret of Kaluga, but I don’t know what this means.
column2: 他们说这与卡卢加的秘密有关，但我不明白这意味着什么。

column1: The Uroxi brought the cattle, to compensate them for broo-infected cattle they once had to kill. The \x01@! leaders must be persuasive; I never heard of Storm Bull men caring about the property they destroy.
column2: 乌洛希带来了这些牛，作为对他们曾经不得不杀死的感染布罗病的牛的补偿。 \x01@! 领袖们一定很有说服力；我从未听说过风暴公牛的信徒会关心他们毁坏的财产。

column1: Their trickster set himself up behind a drum, and drummed for fourteen days and nights without stopping for more than an hour of sleep each night. On the fifteenth day, the cows came wandering into their tula. But the trickster says he meant to attract \x01@\x1A porcupines instead, and is beside himself with rage!
column2: 他们的恶作剧者在一面鼓后面坐定，连续敲了十四天十四夜，每晚只睡了不超过一小时。第十五天，那些牛自己游荡进了他们的图拉领地。但恶作剧者说他本来是想吸引 \x01@\x1A 豪猪，结果气得发狂！

column1: The \x01@! people have lost a bunch of cows.
column2: \x01@! 人丢失了一大群牛。

column1: They died of \x02\x05sudden chill winds/hoof-and-mouth disease/red burstings disease/the quivering disease/white tongue\x02.

column1: They died of fright, when ghosts came to the \x01@! tula.
column2: 当鬼魂来到 \x01@! 图拉领地时，它们吓死了。

column1: They died from jealousy when a Spirit Man told them how sleek and fat the cows of the \x01@a clan were.
column2: 当一个灵人告诉它们 \x01@a 部落的牛有多油光水滑、多肥壮时，它们因嫉妒而死。

column1: A \x02\x06bell-jingling/pouch-wearing/pole-toting/one-eyed/motley-wearing/mummer-masked\x02 trickster of the \x01@a clan won them in a bet.
column2: \x01@a 部落的一个 \x02\x06摇铃铛的/挂袋子的/扛杆子的/独眼的/穿杂色衣的/戴哑剧面具的\x02 恶作剧者在打赌中赢了它们。

column1: They were stolen by a massed force of \x02\x05outlaws and dragonewts/trolls and troll-men/ducks and centaurs/Tusk Riders and Tarshites/Horse-Spawn and Wasp Riders\x02.
column2: 它们被一支由 \x02\x05歹徒与龙人/巨魔与巨魔仆从/鸭人与半人马/獠牙骑手与塔什人/马裔与黄蜂骑士\x02组成的大军偷走了。

column1: Rumor has it that the \x01@! clan is now considerably richer, having gained goods worth \x01@\x19 cows.
column2: 有传言说 \x01@! 部落现在富了很多，获得了价值 \x01@\x19 头牛的货物。

column1: They found \x02\x04old relics/jewelry/gem stones/ingots of silver\x02 while exploring \x02\x07Horse-Spawn territory/the Stinking Forest/the arid plains of Prax/up Tarsh way/a Chaos place/Beast Valley/where the dragonewts live\x02.
column2: 他们在探索 \x02\x07马裔领地/恶臭森林/普拉克的干旱平原/塔什之路/混沌之地/野兽谷/龙人居住地\x02时发现了 \x02\x04古老遗物/珠宝/宝石/银锭\x02 。

column1: They outfoxed the \x02\x04Tarshites/Heortlanders/Pharaoh’s men/Red Empire People\x02 in a trade deal.
column2: 他们在一笔交易中智胜了 \x02\x04塔什人/赫奥特兰人/法老的人/红色帝国的人\x02 。

column1: \x02\x04Tarshites/Heortlanders/Men of the Pharaoh/Red Empire People\x02 paid this much for cloth woven by their women. They wonder why the cloth was so valuable, and wonder if they shouldn’t have asked for more.
column2: \x02\x04\x02 塔什人/赫奥特兰人/法老的人/红色帝国的人为他们女人织的布支付了这么多。他们奇怪为什么布这么值钱，也想知道自己是不是不该要价更高。

column1: They learned a secret story called \x02\x06Eurmal Steals The Wheat/Orlanth Gifts His War-Thanes/Dancing With the Dark Tribe/Issaries and the Third Bean/Ernalda Watches Young Orlanth Bathing/The Seduction of the Fire Tribe Women\x02, and soon knew how to find wealth in places where no one else would look.
column2: 他们学会了一个秘密故事，名为 \x02\x06尤尔马尔偷麦/奥兰斯赠予战斗领主/与暗部族共舞/伊沙里斯与第三豆/埃纳尔达偷看年轻奥兰斯洗澡/诱惑火焰部落女子\x02，很快就知道如何在别人不会寻找的地方找到财富。

column1: They went to Tarsh, and caused great troubles there, and had to pay this amount in compensation to the earth-shaking thanes of that distant land.
column2: 他们去了塔什，在那里惹了大麻烦，不得不向那片遥远土地上地动山摇的领主们支付这个数额的补偿金。

column1: They gave this in gifts to the \x02\x08elves/dwarfs/trolls/dragonewts/beast men/Tusk Riders/holy warriors of Urox/holy warriors of Humakt\x02, who they had offended. They feared that their tula would otherwise be torn apart.
column2: 他们把这些作为礼物送给了 \x02\x08精灵/矮人/巨魔/龙人/兽人/獠牙骑手/乌洛克斯的圣战士/胡玛克特的圣战士\x02，他们曾冒犯了这些种族。他们担心否则自己的图拉领地会被撕碎。

column1: Their clan trader dreamt of betting with Asrelia, and in the dream lost every bet. When he awoke, every bauble and gewgaw was missing from his stead, and from the steads of the chief and war leader, too.
column2: 他们的部落商人梦见与阿斯雷利亚打赌，在梦中输掉了每一局。当他醒来时，他的农庄里以及酋长和战争领袖的农庄里所有的小玩意儿和小饰品都不见了。

column1: One of their steads burned down, with many valuable tapestries, silks, and fine woods within it. They should have been more careful.
column2: 他们的一座农庄被烧毁了，里面有许多珍贵的挂毯、丝绸和上等木材。他们本该更小心些。

column1: They let a woman who wasn’t right in the head do their cooking for them, and she wasted several barrels of valuable spices, due to be traded to the \x01@a clan for a herd of fine horses.
column2: 他们让一个脑子不太灵光的女人做饭，她浪费了好几桶贵重香料，那些香料本是要和 \x01@a 族交易，换一群好马的。

column1: They gave gifts to discontented weaponthanes, who left anyway.
column2: 他们给心怀不满的武器领主送上礼物，那些人终究还是走了。

column1: Their trickster demanded gifts of fine weapons and three big carts, or else he would continue to dress as a woman and bring embarrassment to the clan. Then he turned around and burnt these things as sacrifices to the Betraying God.
column2: 他们的戏弄者索要精美武器和三辆大车作为礼物，否则将继续男扮女装，令氏族蒙羞。然后他转身就把这些东西烧了，当作献给背叛之神的祭品。

column1: new weaponthanes.
column2: 新的武器领主。

column2: 他们从赫奥特兰赶来——更多坚毅的奥兰斯人，对篡位法老的暴行义愤填膺。

column2: 马裔。

column1: minotaurs, centaurs and ducks.

column2: 特尔莫里狼人。

column2: 土匪。

column2: 震颤之灵。

column1: They were all brothers and sisters. The eldest, \x01@\x0B, fell in love with a beautiful maiden from far away, who would not leave her homeland for him. So he and his siblings have gone there to live, ignoring the protests and pleas of their former clan-mates.
column2: 他们都是兄弟姐妹。最年长的 \x01@\x0B爱上了一位远方的美丽少女，但少女不肯为他离开故土。于是他和他的兄弟姐妹们便去了那里生活，不顾昔日族人的抗议和恳求。

column1: A walktapus strangled one of them, \x01@\x0B by name, and the others so mourned him that they could not bear to look upon his old stead or kinfolk.
column2: 一只行触手怪勒死了他们中的一位，名叫 \x01@\x0B ，其余人哀悼至深，不忍再看他的旧宅和亲人。

column1: They were too virtuous to live in this world, so the chariot of Mastakos the Moving God came for them and took them away to the Higher World.
column2: 他们美德过盛，不存于世，因此移动之神马斯塔科斯的战车降临，将他们带往上界。

column1: They heard a prophecy about a great king, and went off to make it come true.
column2: 他们聆听了一位伟大君王的预言，便动身去实现它。

column1: No one knows why they went away, but they left a large oak box behind, painted red and black. They left instructions that no one was to open it until the young boy \x01@\x0B was old enough to be married. Some say that the departed weaponthanes will die if the box is opened before then.
column2: 无人知晓他们为何离去，只留下一个红黑漆面的大橡木箱。他们留下指令：在男孩 \x01@\x0B 长大成婚之前，谁也不许打开它。有人说，若在此之前打开箱子，离去的武器领主们便会死去。

column1: composing a poem which mocked them.
column2: 编了一首嘲笑他们的诗。

column1: scolding them for their lack of pride in fine clothes.
column2: 责骂他们对华服缺乏自豪感。

column1: refusing them the right to build a shrine to their chosen war god.
column2: 拒绝他们为他们所选的战争之神建造神龛的权利。

column1: trading away the \x02\x06Glowing Bowl/Crimson Rod/Carmanian Flute/Arrival Boots/Blood Count’s Mane/Heler Pole\x02, a treasure they had fought hard to wrest from the \x02\x07dragonewts/elves/trolls/Tusk Riders/Beastfolk/ducks/Telmori\x02.
column2: 交易掉了 \x02\x06发光碗/深红杖/卡马尼亚笛/抵达之靴/血伯爵之鬃/赫勒杆\x02，那是他们浴血奋战从 \x02\x07龙人/精灵/巨魔/獠牙骑手/兽人/鸭人/特尔莫里\x02手中夺来的珍宝。

column1: giving hospitality to agents of the hated Pharaoh, who had slain their kin.
column2: 款待了可恨的法老（他杀害了他们的亲人）的使者。

column1: arguing that a blue tunic was in fact black.
column2: 争论一件蓝色外衣其实是黑色。

column1: saying that it would be good to build a town, and encourage craftsmen to populate it.
column2: 说建一座城镇、鼓励工匠定居会很好。

column1: looking the wrong way at the war leader’s lover.

column2: 连续十四天十四夜拒绝下床。

column2: 和他们一起战吼，尽管 \x04 嗓音并不适合，他们反复请求 \x08 克制。

column1: The people take heart from good news.
column2: 人们从好消息中振作起来。

column2: 在我们的领地上发现了一面古代战旗，我们的神言者说这是好兆头。

column1: Our hunters found a pile of silver rings while stalking a deer.
column2: 我们的猎人在追踪一头鹿时发现了一堆银环。

column2: \x01@! 袭击者。

column2: \x01@r 族中一个更加高明的骗子。

column2: 坏消息。人们忧心忡忡。

column2: 我们派了一些年轻自由民去 \x01@! 族学习他们的种植秘诀，但他们归来时并不比离开时更明智。

column1: feast
column2: 盛宴

column1: at the \x01@! tula.
column2: 在 \x01@! 领地。

column1: Some of the young people are disheartened by the difficulty of life here. They hear about how easy things were back in Heortland, and wish their elders had never left that place. They do not remember the terrors of the Pharaoh’s rule, and make the older people sad with their thoughtless complaints.
column2: 一些年轻人因这里生活的艰难而沮丧。他们听说赫奥特兰的日子曾多么安逸，便希望长辈从未离开过那里。他们不记得法老统治的恐怖，轻率的抱怨令长辈伤心。

column1: They have heard a prophecy which says that a catastrophe of \x02\x04darkness/fire/water/earth\x02 will be visited upon our land this year, and await its fulfillment with dread anticipation.
column2: 他们听闻一则预言，说 \x02\x04黑暗/火焰/洪水/大地\x02 的灾难将于今年降临我们的土地，便心怀恐惧地等待着它的应验。

column1: One of the children drowned in the creek this morning.
column2: 今天早上，一个孩子淹死在小溪里。

column1: The weaponthanes are in good spirits.
column2: 武器领主们心情不错。

column1: \x01@a clan.
\x01@! clan.
\x02\x07trolls/beastfolk/dragonewts/Praxian raiders/elves/undead/forces of Chaos\x02.
column2: \x02\x07巨魔/兽人/龙人/普拉克斯袭击者/精灵/亡灵/混沌势力\x02。

column1: The young warrior Kallyr is showing great promise, they say.
column2: 年轻战士卡莉尔展现出卓越的潜力，他们说道。

column1: They went to the \x01@! marketplace and saw how much disrespect the carls of that clan show for their weaponthanes. By contrast, they say, our carls treat them with proper deference.
column2: 他们去了 \x01@! 集市，看到那个氏族的自由民对他们的武器领主多么不敬。相比之下，他们说，我们的自由民对他们表现出恰当的尊重。

column1: Some of their horses were sick, but now they are well.
column2: 他们的一些马匹曾经生病，但现在已痊愈。

column1: They are pleased by the fervor with which \x01@\x10 told the story of \x02\x06Humakt the Cleanser/How Elmal Lit the Way/Urox Fights On/Elmal Finds the Horses/Orlanth Makes the Corpse-Road/Vinga the Subtracter\x02 in the clan hall last night.

column1: They think that the food being prepared for them is much-improved of late.
column2: 他们认为最近为他们准备的食物大有改善。

column1: They heard a rumor that our rivals among the clans are all so afraid of us that they are going to become peace clans, and beg us not to hurt them.
column2: 他们听到一个流言，说我们氏族间的对手全都如此惧怕我们，以至于他们打算变成和平氏族，并恳求我们不要伤害他们。

column1: \x01@\x17 found two new allied spirits to help \x08 fight, a
column2: \x01@\x17 找到了两个新的结盟精魂来帮助 \x08 战斗，一只

column2: 小龙虾放在 \x04 肩膀上，一条蛇系在 \x04 腰带上。

column1: \x02\x04storm hawk and a sharp-clawed alynx/horse that can cast spells, and a powerful wind/rat to bite our foes, and a bat to vex them/sharp-eyed owl and a quick-witted fox\x02.
column2: \x02\x04风暴鹰和一只利爪山猫/会施法的马，以及一股强劲的风/老鼠来咬我们的敌人，还有一只蝙蝠去骚扰他们/尖眼猫头鹰和一只机敏的狐狸\x02。

column1: They heard that they’re known as the \x02\x06Ghost-Frightening/Falcon-Fast/Year-Honed/Trap-Sharp/Victory-Wreathed/Dry-Browed\x02 Fighters.
column2: 他们听说他们被称为 \x02\x06惊鬼/猎隼之速/年磨砺/陷阱锐利/胜冠/干眉\x02 战士。

column1: Their war leader, \x01@\x17, composed a poem on honor and bravery which is now recited throughout Dragon Pass.
column2: 他们的战争领袖 \x01@\x17创作了一首关于荣誉与勇气的诗歌，如今在龙之隘口广为传诵。

column1: The bachelors among them went among the young women of the \x01@! clan during the recent market there, and were much-admired for their technique and stamina.
column2: 他们中的单身汉们在最近的那个集市上去了 \x01@! 氏族的年轻女子中间，并因其技巧与耐力而备受赞赏。

column1: The morale of the weaponthanes has suffered a blow.
column2: 武器领主们的士气遭受了打击。

column1: Rude Uroxi warriors called some of them “Dog-Keepers” when they went to the \x01@! market, and they were in no position to retaliate for this slight against their honor.
column2: 粗鲁的尤洛克斯追随者战士们在他们去 \x01@! 集市时称其中一些人为“养狗人”，而他们无法对此侮辱他们荣誉的轻蔑进行报复。

column1: Fanatical Humakti warriors told them they were not doing enough to fight the undead, questioning their bravery and honor.
column2: 狂热的胡马克特追随者战士们告诉他们，他们对亡灵作战不够努力，质疑他们的勇气和荣誉。

column1: They heard a prophecy which said that they would taste no true victory for the next six years.
column2: 他们听到一个预言，说他们在接下来的六年里尝不到真正的胜利。

column1: Their favorite alynx, \x02\x06Fly-Catcher/Seven Leaps/Red Tip/Hound Hurter/South Watcher/Whisperless\x02, died this morning.
column2: 他们最喜爱的山猫 \x02\x06捕蝇者/七跃/红尖/伤犬者/南方守望者/无低语\x02今早死了。

column1: The bachelors among them, after spending time with the young women of the \x01@! clan, learned that they had been nicknamed \x02\x06The Small Tree Warriors/The Speed Demons/The Bad Breath Men/The Snore-Too-Soons/The False Promisers/The Speckled Ones\x02.
column2: 他们中的单身汉们与 \x01@! 氏族的年轻女子共度时光后，得知他们被起了绰号 \x02\x06小树勇士/速度恶魔/口臭男/打鼾太早者/虚假承诺者/斑点一族\x02。

column1: Their ancestor spirits were heard to murmur that the sun might stop in the sky again, just like it did in a terrible disaster that happened a thousand years ago.
column2: 有人听到他们的祖先精魂喃喃低语，说太阳可能再次停在天空中，就像一千年前发生的那场可怕灾难一样。

column1: They say that the carls are taking advantage of privileges which should be granted only to weaponthanes.
column2: 他们说自由民正在利用本应只授予武器领主的特权。

column1: They say that their women are purposely over-salting the food, to prod them into taking vengeance against the \x01@! clan. They also say that the \x01@! clan have not truly offended us, and that it would be dishonorable to attack them.
column2: 他们说他们的女人故意在食物中放太多盐，以刺激他们对 \x01@! 氏族复仇。他们还表示 \x01@! 氏族并未真正冒犯我们，攻击他们是不光彩的。

column1: They say that they feel the hot breath of angry spirits on their necks whenever they mount their horses.
column2: 他们说每当他们上马时，就感到愤怒精魂的热气喷在脖子上。

column1: The carls are in a good mood of late.
column2: 最近自由民们心情不错。

column1: They have been experimenting with the recipe for making ale. I don’t know if they are happy because they’ve succeeded in finding a good new recipe, or if they’re just enjoying the testing.
column2: 他们一直在试验酿造麦芽酒的配方。我不知道他们是因成功找到好的新配方而高兴，还是仅仅享受试验过程。

column1: The ancestral spirits say that we will get the good kind of rain next year.
column2: 祖先精魂说明年我们会迎来丰沛的雨水。

column1: Our grain stores were being robbed by mice and the spirits of mice, but they tricked them, so that they have now been eaten by alynxes and the spirits of alynxes.
column2: 我们的粮仓一直被老鼠和鼠精偷窃，但他们设下圈套，如今那些老鼠已被山猫和山猫精吃掉。

column1: The soil, which has been unyielding of late, is once more giving up its bounty to Barntar’s plow.
column2: 最近一直贫瘠的土地，如今再次向巴恩塔的犁头奉献丰收。

column1: They have found better ways of doing their work, and now have more time to rest and enjoy the fruits of their labors.
column2: 他们找到了更好的工作方法，如今有更多时间休息和享受劳动成果。

column1: They are pleased with recent decisions of the clan ring, which they believe is now treating them with the proper respect.
column2: 他们对氏族议会近期的决定感到满意，他们认为议会现在给予他们应有的尊重。

column1: A golden bird was found dead on the ground, and this is a good omen. It means that \x02\x07raiders who try to steal our cattle will fail/clan leaders will make decisions which will favor the carls/the sun will not scorch the moisture from the land/our magic will grow stronger/the snakes that eat rodents will eat many of them, fearing no predators from above/the earth will draw energy towards it, and send that energy into the grain, and into the grass that the cows and sheep eat/we will all be free from the depredations of tyrants and false kings\x02.
column2: 地上发现一只金鸟死尸，这是个好兆头。它意味着 \x02\x07试图偷窃我们牛群的劫掠者必将失败/氏族领袖的决策将惠及自由民/太阳不会烤干大地的水分/我们的魔法将变得更强大/捕食啮齿类的蛇将无所畏惧地吃掉许多老鼠/大地将汲取能量，将那股能量注入谷物，注入牛群和羊群啃食的青草/我们所有人都将从暴君与伪王的劫掠中获得自由\x02。

column1: The carls of the \x01@a clan have agreed to trade \x02\x08cattle/sheep/grain/ale/pottery/crafting/hog/cooking\x02 secrets with us.
column2: \x01@a 氏族的自由民已同意与我们交易 \x02\x08牛/羊/谷物/麦酒/陶器/手工/猪/烹饪\x02 的秘密。

column1: They hear that there are good trading opportunities up in Tarsh, and think that we will send an expedition there.
column2: 他们听说塔什那边有很好的贸易机会，认为我们会派一支远征队去那里。

column1: They hear that there are good trading opportunities to the northwest, and think that we will send an expedition there.
column2: 他们听说西北方有很好的贸易机会，认为我们会派一支远征队去那里。

column1: The carls are in a bad mood these days.
column2: 这些日子自由民们心情不好。

column1: They entered into a log-sawing competition with the carls of the \x01@! clan, and lost.
column2: 他们与 \x01@! 氏族的自由民进行了一场锯木比赛，结果输了。

column1: They are unhappy with recent decisions of the clan ring, and say that we favor the warriors over them. They say it is as if the ring is made up of seven tricksters.
column2: 他们对氏族议会最近的决策不满，说我们偏袒战士胜过他们。他们说这议会简直是由七个骗子组成的。

column1: Their tools and implements are going astray without good cause, and are never found once lost.
column2: 他们的工具和器具无缘无故地丢失，一旦遗失就再也找不到。

column1: There is no one cause for their sense of resentment. They are irked by many small and insignificant things, which together are like a volcano readying itself for an explosion.
column2: 他们的怨恨并非源于单一原因。众多琐碎小事令他们恼火，这些事累积起来就像一座即将爆发的火山。

column1: They have found small, white eggs in the soil, and fear an infestation of insects when we next plant.
column2: 他们在土壤里发现了白色小卵，担心下次播种时会爆发虫灾。

column1: They dream about the kinfolk they left behind when we left Heortland, and fear that they are starving and bereft of good cows.
column2: 他们梦见当年我们离开赫奥特兰时留下的亲族，担心他们正在挨饿，失去了好牛。

column1: They are convinced that the kinfolk they left behind when we left Heortland have grown unfairly prosperous by accepting the misbegotten rule of the Pharaoh.
column2: 他们深信当年我们离开赫奥特兰时留下的亲族，因接受了法老那不合法的统治，竟不义地富裕起来了。

column1: The weaponthanes roister long into the night, preventing them from sleeping. Unlike the shiftless warriors, they must rise early in the morning.
column2: 武器领主们狂欢至深夜，使他们无法入睡。与那些游手好闲的战士不同，他们必须在清晨早起。

column1: The stead we just built is already \x02\x06sinking into the ground/leaking water/infested with red-pocked spiders/groaning at night like a ghost/full of useless junk put there by the warriors/shedding its paint like a cat shaking off rain droplets\x02.
column2: 我们刚建好的农庄已经开始 \x02\x06陷入地下/漏水/爬满红斑蜘蛛/夜晚像鬼魂般呻吟/被战士们塞满了无用垃圾/像猫甩掉雨滴般脱落油漆\x02。

column1: They found a plant of good omen, but the weaponthanes ground it up and drank it in their wine, to give them good luck in battle.
column2: 他们发现了一株吉兆的植物，但武器领主们却将它磨碎，混入酒中喝下，以求战斗好运。

column1: News comes from our former clan-mates in our old homeland, Heortland.
column2: 消息来自我们故土赫奥特兰的昔日氏族同胞。

column1: \x01@p, who is now chieftain of our old clan, says that the Pharaoh is not all that bad. He did not \x02\x07forbid all Orlanthi worship/tax all their grain away/order them to stop eating meat/devour babies/make them into slaves/turn out to be a Chaos worshipper/dishonor their ancestors\x02 as we had thought he would.
column2: \x01@p，如今是我们旧日氏族的酋长，他说法老并没有那么坏。他并没有像我们预想的那样 \x02\x07禁止所有奥兰斯崇拜/征走他们全部谷物/命令他们停止吃肉/吞噬婴儿/将他们变为奴隶/原来是个混沌信徒/侮辱他们的祖先\x02 。

column1: They are ravaged by disease, and are too sick to pray.
column2: 他们遭受疾病蹂躏，病重得无法祈祷。

column1: They have \x02\x02stolen/learned\x02 magics from the Pharaoh, and now get sick a lot less often.
column2: 他们 \x02\x02偷学/习得\x02 了法老的魔法，现在生病的次数大大减少。

column1: They have been encouraged by the Pharaoh to make an alliance with trolls, who are not so bad, once you get to know them, when they are not hungry.
column2: 法老鼓励他们与巨魔结盟——巨魔其实没那么坏，只要你了解它们，而且它们不饿的时候。

column1: They have taken to raiding the trolls, even though the Pharaoh forbids it.
column2: 他们开始劫掠巨魔，尽管法老禁止这样做。

column1: They have gone to the Grandmother Lands, where Orlanth’s role as chief god and sole husband of Ernalda is denied, and have won many converts to the proper forms of worship.
column2: 他们前往祖母之地——那里否认奥兰斯是主神及厄娜尔达唯一丈夫的地位——并赢得了许多皈依者，使其接受正确的崇拜形式。

column1: They are sorely pressed by missionaries from the Grandmother Lands, who say that Orlanth is just one of Ernalda’s consorts, that women should have the power and men should shut up.
column2: 他们被来自祖母之地的传教士逼得喘不过气来，那些传教士说奥兰斯只是厄娜尔达的配偶之一，女人应当掌权，男人应当闭嘴。

column1: They are so enraptured by the cruel Pharaoh that they have taken to calling the land of Kathaela the Holy Country, in his honor!
column2: 他们被残暴的法老迷得神魂颠倒，竟开始尊称卡萨拉之地为“圣国”，以他之名！

column1: They say that is now safe to heroquest there, even though it was too dangerous before the Pharaoh came.
column2: 他们说如今在那里进行英雄探索是安全的，尽管在法老到来之前那里太过危险。

column1: They say that their neighbors believe that it is now safe to heroquest there, even though it was too dangerous before the Pharaoh came. But they do not believe what their foolish neighbors say.
column2: 他们说他们的邻居相信如今在那里进行英雄探索是安全的，尽管在法老到来之前那里太过危险。但他们并不信那些愚蠢邻居的话。

column1: \x01@p, who is now chieftain of our old clan, says that the Pharaoh is even worse than we had predicted, and that others may soon follow us to Dragon Pass. The Pharaoh \x02\x08taxes them unfairly/places fools in position of authority/openly consorts with trolls/blatantly favors the grandmothers of Esrolia, who deny Orlanth’s place at Ernalda’s table/sends his people to cheat them in games of chance/practices foul magic/devours babies/has turned out to be a Chaos worshipper\x02.
column2: \x01@p他现在是我们旧氏族的酋长，说法老甚至比我们预料的还要糟糕，而且其他人可能很快就会跟随我们来到龙隘。法老 \x02\x08不公平地征税/让蠢人掌权/公然与巨魔勾结/公然偏袒埃斯罗利亚的祖母们，她们否认奥兰斯在厄娜尔达餐桌旁的位置/派他的人去赌博欺骗他们/施展邪恶魔法/吞噬婴儿/结果变成了混沌信徒\x02。

column1: One of our weaponthanes has died, in unusual circumstances.
column2: 我们的一位武器领主死了，情况异常。

column1: One of our carls has died, in unusual circumstances.
column2: 我们的一位自由民死了，情况异常。

column1: was struck dead by the rays of the sun.
column2: 被阳光击死。

column1: fell into a sinkhole and fractured \x01@\x12 skull.
column2: 掉进天坑，摔裂了 \x01@\x12 颅骨。

column1: bolted up in \x01@\x12 sleep, shouting the name of an ancient hero, and then died of apoplexy.
column2: \x01@\x12 睡梦中猛然坐起，喊出一位古代英雄的名字，然后中风而死。

column1: was staring up into the clear blue sky when a rock fell from it and crushed \x01@\x12 head.
column2: 正仰望清澈的蓝天，一块石头从天上掉下来砸碎了 \x01@\x12 的头。

column1: was killed by a stray arrow fired by the young men practicing their archery skills.
column2: 被练习箭术的年轻人射出的一支流矢杀死。

column1: saw a sight in the mist that frightened \x01@\x13 to death.
column2: 在雾中看到了一个景象，把 \x01@\x13 吓死了。

column1: died of embarrassment when \x01@\x12 daughter behaved shamelessly in the temple.
column2: 当 \x01@\x12 的女儿在神庙中行为无耻时，羞愤而死。

column1: was killed when an improperly stacked pile of logs rolled onto \x01@\x13.
column2: 一堆没堆好的圆木滚到 \x01@\x13身上，被砸死了。

column1: was torn apart by holy spirits of reprisal when \x01@\x10 offended the gods.
column2: 当 \x01@\x10 冒犯了神灵时，被神圣的复仇之灵撕碎。

column1: had \x01@\x12 spirit shorn away by the ghost of \x01@\x12 twin, who died in childbirth.
column2: \x01@\x12 的灵魂被 \x01@\x12 的双胞胎（死于分娩）的鬼魂割裂。

column1: was trampled by a bull who had always been docile before.
column2: 被一头以前一直温顺的公牛踩死。

column1: died of sadness because \x01@\x12 lover in the \x01@! clan chose to marry someone else.
column2: 因悲伤而死，因为 \x01@\x12 的爱人在 \x01@! 氏族选择了嫁给别人。

column1: lit \x01@\x12 own funeral pyre, although \x01@\x10 seemed perfectly healthy. When the flames reached their greatest height, all life left \x01@\x13, and \x01@\x0B’s kinfolk gently lifted \x01@\x12 body onto them.
column2: 点燃了 \x01@\x12 自己的火葬柴堆，尽管 \x01@\x10 看起来非常健康。当火焰达到最高时，生命离开了 \x01@\x13， \x01@\x0B的亲属轻轻地将 \x01@\x12 的遗体抬到火上。

column1: died of forgetfulness.
column2: 因健忘而死。

column1: died from music that was too sad.
column2: 因音乐过于悲伤而死。

column1: died of exhaustion while running from \x02\x04troll/elfin/dragonewt/undead\x02 pursuers.
column2: 因逃跑而力竭而死，身后是 \x02\x04巨魔/精灵/龙人/亡灵\x02 追兵。

column1: They are getting spiders from all of their trading partners, to make powerful poisons.
column2: 他们从所有贸易伙伴那里获取蜘蛛，用来制作强力毒药。

column1: They have been preparing for many weeks, making their war leader into a great Humakti hero of the past, who will come and slice us with his awful, moaning sword.
column2: 他们已经准备了数周，将他们的战争领袖变成过去的一位伟大的胡玛克提英雄，他会带着他那可怕的、呻吟的剑来砍杀我们。

column1: They have been sacrificing to the gods and telling their ancestors to petition Orlanth himself that we might be struck down for our so-called impiety.
column2: 他们一直在向众神献祭，并告诉他们的祖先去恳求奥兰斯本人，让我们因所谓的不敬而被打倒。

column1: They have been scouring Dragon Pass for lost spirits who might be willing to vex us with their unfamiliar magics.
column2: 他们一直在龙隘搜寻迷失的魂魄，这些魂魄可能愿意用它们不熟悉的魔法来骚扰我们。

column1: They are remaking their initiation rite, so that all of the boys must promise to fight to destroy us before they may become men.
column2: 他们正在重新制定他们的成年礼，所有男孩在成为男人之前必须承诺战斗以毁灭我们。

column1: They said to their allies that they had found a secret in the myths of Orlanth, one which would seal our fate.
column2: 他们对盟友说，他们在奥兰斯的神话中发现了一个秘密，一个将决定我们命运的秘密。

column1: They have learned new magic from emissaries of the Evil Red Empire, and will use it against us.
column2: 他们从邪恶红色帝国的使者那里学到了新的魔法，并将用它来对付我们。

column1: \x01@\x08, one of the clan’s finest hunters, met a \x02\x08living rainbow/talking bear/ten-foot salmon/forgotten earth spirit/wind spirit from Orlanth’s court/holy wind/Godplane army/hero-form of an ancient god\x02 that taught \x08
column2: \x01@\x08氏族最优秀的猎人之一，遇到了一个 \x02\x08活的彩虹/会说话的熊/十英尺长的鲑鱼/被遗忘的地灵/来自奥兰斯宫廷的风灵/圣风/神界军队/古代神灵的英雄形态\x02 ，它教会了 \x08

column1: \x02\x07secrets of the chase/hidden paths in the mountains/secret ways through the Godplane/forgotten names of the first animals/stories that are so powerful and funny that animals gather to hear them/secrets our ancestors had forgotten in the Darkness/how to move as quietly and quickly as the breeze\x02.
column2: \x02\x07捕猎的秘密/山中隐藏的小径/穿越神界的秘密通道/最初动物的遗忘之名/强大又有趣到动物们会聚集来听的故事/我们的祖先在黑暗时代遗忘的秘密/如何像微风一样安静而快速地移动\x02。

column1: God Time secrets \x06 is not allowed to share with the rest of us.
column2: 神代秘密 \x06 不允许与其他人分享。

column1: \x01@\x08 seems to have gained a great deal of power.
column2: \x01@\x08 似乎获得了巨大的力量。

column1: We don’t have trading relations with any other clans. This makes our market the sorriest in all Dragon Pass. I strongly suggest we send me and other traders to create as many trading routes as we can.
column2: 我们与其他氏族没有贸易关系。这使得我们的市场成为整个龙隘最糟糕的。我强烈建议我们派我和其他商人尽可能多地开辟贸易路线。

column1: During the past year, several of the visitors I’ve hosted made note of how well our clan ring has been handling things.
column2: 在过去的一年里，我接待的几位访客都注意到我们的氏族议会处理事务有多好。

column1: They said the grumbling of the people would pass.
column2: 他们说人们的抱怨会过去。

column1: We should think about forming a tribe soon — the other clans would be willing to listen to us.
column2: 我们应该考虑尽快组建一个部落——其他氏族会愿意倾听我们的意见。

column1: I heard a really funny story from a Trickster of the \x01@! clan. It was about how \x01@\x03 was reciting \x04 lineage all the way back to Bad King Urgrain, and… Why are all of you looking at me like that?
column2: 我从 \x01@! 氏族的一位诡术师那里听到一个非常有趣的故事。是关于 \x01@\x03 如何背诵 \x04 世系一直追溯到恶王乌格兰，然后……你们为什么都那样看着我？

column1: As I’ve been visiting other clans to trade this past year, I’ve frequently been asked for advice on various matters. And so have the guards I’ve taken.
column2: 过去一年里我走访其他氏族做买卖，经常被问及各种事务的建议。我带去的护卫也是如此。

column1: Not every clan likes us, but they all show us great respect.
column2: 并非所有氏族都喜欢我们，但他们全都对我们敬重有加。

column1: During my trading visits to other clans this past year, I’ve noticed a change in the way they treat us. Even among our friends, our goods are picked after those from other clans.
column2: 过去一年我在走访其他氏族做买卖时，注意到了他们对待我们方式的变化。即便是我们的朋友，也优先挑选其他氏族的货物，然后才轮到我们的。

column1: And no one will talk to us outside the market.
column2: 而在市场之外，没人愿意跟我们交谈。

column1: I’ve been asking around, talking to \x02\x02warriors and traders/weaponthanes and explorers\x02 from other clans, trying to figure out who those horse-riding people are. The ones with the \x02\x03fiery lances/flaming arrows/weird fire magic\x02 who attacked us recently.
column2: 我四处打听，跟其他氏族的 \x02\x02武士和商人/武器领主和探险者\x02 交谈，想搞清楚那些骑马的人是谁。就是那些用 \x02\x03火焰长矛/燃烧箭矢/怪异火魔法\x02 最近袭击我们的家伙。

column1: I’m told that the lands to the west are full of these evil foreigners. They never get off their horses, so the other clans call them the “Horse-Spawn.” They worship Orlanth’s enemy, Yelm the Bad Emperor, so I know we haven’t seen the last of them.
column2: 我听说西边的土地上到处都是这些邪恶的外邦人。他们从不从马背上下来，所以其他氏族称他们为“马裔”。他们崇拜奥兰斯的敌人、恶皇帝耶尔姆，所以我知道我们还没见到他们全部。

column1: A delegation from the \x01@! clan visited the tula, bringing a minimal amount of gifts. Their clan was among the first to migrate to Dragon Pass. Their leader, \x01@\x08 said that they like to see if new clans would make it or not before extending the hand of friendship. “Why waste good gifts on incompetent newcomers?” he shrugged. They ate and drank as often as they could, and asked a lot of questions. Before they left, \x01@\x08 said that he would be surprised if we lasted another few years. “But, cheer up!” he said, “You might get lucky!”
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的使团访问了图拉，带来的礼物少得可怜。他们的氏族是首批迁入龙隘的氏族之一。首领 \x01@\x08 说，他们总要先看看新氏族是否能撑下去，再伸出友谊之手。“何必把好礼物浪费在无能的新来者身上？”他耸耸肩说道。他们尽可能多地吃喝，问了很多问题。离开前， \x01@\x08 说，要是我们还能再撑几年，他会感到惊讶。“不过，打起精神！”他说，“你们或许会走运！”

column1: A delegation from the \x01@! clan visited us. Their clan was among the first to migrate to Dragon Pass. They said that they would be surprised if we lasted another few years.
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的使团访问了我们。他们的氏族是首批迁入龙隘的氏族之一。他们说，要是我们还能再撑几年，他们会感到惊讶。

column1: A delegation from the \x01@! clan visited the tula, bringing a small amount of gifts. Their clan was among the first to migrate to Dragon Pass. Their leader, \x01@\x08 said that they always waited to see if new clans would make it or not before extending the hand of friendship.“Why waste good gifts on incompetent newcomers?” he shrugged. They ate and drank as often as they could, asked a lot of questions, and then left. We weren’t entirely sure what to make of their visit.
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的使团访问了图拉，带来了少量礼物。他们的氏族是首批迁入龙隘的氏族之一。首领 \x01@\x08 说，他们总要先看看新氏族是否能撑下去，再伸出友谊之手。“何必把好礼物浪费在无能的新来者身上？”他耸耸肩说道。他们尽可能多地吃喝，问了很多问题，然后离开了。我们并不完全确定该如何看待这次访问。

column1: A delegation from the \x01@! clan visited us. Their clan was among the first to migrate to Dragon Pass. We weren’t entirely sure what to make of their visit.
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的使团访问了我们。他们的氏族是首批迁入龙隘的氏族之一。我们并不完全确定该如何看待这次访问。

column1: A delegation from the \x01@! clan arrived at our tula with much fanfare, bringing gifts. Their leader, \x01@\x08, said that he was happy to see that we were still here. “We were among the first to settle these lands, and lived by ourselves for long time before other clans showed up. Then they often moved away, or starved, or got eaten.”
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的使团大张旗鼓地抵达我们的图拉，带来了礼物。首领 \x01@\x08说，他很高兴看到我们还在。“我们是首批定居这片土地的人，在其他氏族出现之前独自生活了很长时间。然后他们常常迁走、饿死，或者被吃掉。”

column1: He congratulated us for having lasted this long. Some of the carls reminded him of the previous emissary’s dour prediction that we would not last.
column2: 他祝贺我们坚持了这么久。一些自由民提醒他，先前那位使节曾阴沉地预言我们撑不下去。

column1: A delegation from the \x01@! clan arrived to congratulate us for having lasted this long. They told us tales of their early days, when they were alone in the valley, and brought us gifts.
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的使团抵达，祝贺我们坚持了这么久。他们给我们讲述了早年的故事，那时他们独自在山谷中生活，并带来了礼物。

column1: \x01@\x08 just smiled and stated that there was still plenty of time for our clan to disintegrate. “We never know when the gods will bless us,” he said, “though it looks like you could use a few blessings soon.” We thanked them rather stiffly, fed them what hospitality required, and were relieved to see them go.
column2: \x01@\x08 只是笑了笑，说我们氏族还有很多时间来瓦解。“我们永远不知道众神何时会赐福，”他说，“不过看样子你们很快就能得到一些赐福了。”我们颇为生硬地道谢，按好客之仪招待了他们，看到他们离开才松了口气。

column1: \x01@\x08 just smiled and stated that they were always glad to be wrong when it meant good things for Orlanthi. They ate much meat, drank much beer, and told tall tales from their early days in Dragon Pass. We were sad when they finally had to go.
column2: \x01@\x08 只是笑了笑，说他们总是乐于自己猜错，只要这对奥兰斯人来说是好事。他们吃了很多肉，喝了很多啤酒，还讲述了他们在龙隘早年经历的夸张故事。当他们最终不得不离开时，我们都感到伤心。

column1: Our traders report that the \x01@! clan was irate when they heard we had destroyed that big skull we found. It seems that they value any item of antiquity, and are accusing us of being too stupid to know a treasure when we find one.
column2: 我们的商人报告说， \x01@! 氏族听说我们破坏了找到的那颗大颅骨后非常愤怒。看来他们珍视任何古物，并指责我们蠢到发现珍宝也不认识。

column1: Our traders report that the \x01@! clan thinks better of us now, since we are displaying that big skull we found. It seems that they value any item of antiquity, and were pleased to see that we would value such things, too.
column2: 我们的商人报告说， \x01@! 氏族现在对我们的看法有所改观，因为我们展示了那颗找到的大颅骨。看来他们珍视任何古物，很高兴看到我们也会珍视这样的东西。

column1: Our traders reported that the \x01@! clan approved of our reburying that big skull we found. It seems that they value any item of antiquity.
column2: 我们的商人报告说， \x01@! 氏族赞同我们重新埋掉了那颗找到的大颅骨。看来他们珍视任何古物。

column1: Though they might have liked to trade for it, they were glad that we left it in peace.
column2: 虽然他们或许本想要用它做交易，但他们很高兴我们让它安息了。

column1: They said that when we were reduced to stickpickers, they would come and find it, claiming it for their own.
column2: 他们说，等我们沦落成拾柴人时，他们就会来找它，据为己有。

column1: Our traders reported that the \x01@! clan was sorry to hear that we had traded away that big skull we found. It seems that they value any item of antiquity. They said that if we found anything else like that, they would like the first chance to trade for it.
column2: 我们的商人报告说， \x01@! 氏族很遗憾听到我们把找到的那个大颅骨卖掉了。看来他们珍视任何古董。他们说如果我们再找到类似的东西，他们希望有优先交易权。

column1: Our traders reported that the \x01@! clan hooted when they heard we traded away that big skull we found. It seems that they value any item of antiquity, and our failure to keep the skull confirmed their bad opinion of us.
column2: 我们的商人报告说， \x01@! 氏族听到我们把找到的那个大颅骨卖掉时发出了嘘声。看来他们珍视任何古董，而我们没能保留颅骨更印证了他们对我们的坏印象。

column2: 一位商人来自

column2: 我们的盟友， \x01@! 氏族，

is here with \x01@\x03 horses for sale.

column1: A trader from the \x01@! clan is here with \x01@\x03 horses for sale. They want us to pay \x01@\x16 cows or the same in goods for each animal. I did a close inspection and know that the beasts are not from the best \x01@! herds. They have admitted as such, and agreed to let them go for the price of \x01@\x17. Theses horses will suffice until we can obtain better steeds.
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的一位商人带着 \x01@\x03 匹马来出售。他们想要每匹马付 \x01@\x16 头牛或等值货物。我仔细检查过，知道这些牲口并非来自最好的 \x01@! 马群。他们承认了这一点，并同意以 \x01@\x17的价格出手。在弄到更好的战马之前，这些马匹足以应付。

column1: Traders from the \x01@! clan are here with \x01@\x03 horses for sale. They want \x01@\x16 cows worth of goods each. Even though they are taking slight advantage of us, I say we should agree to the price and get these fine steeds.
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的商人们带着 \x01@\x03 匹马来出售。他们每匹要价价值 \x01@\x16 头牛的货物。虽然他们占了些便宜，但我说我们应该同意这个价格，买下这些好马。

column1: A trader from the \x01@! clan offered us \x01@\x03 horses in trade for \x01@\x16 worth of cows.
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的一位商人提出用 \x01@\x03 匹马交换价值 \x01@\x16 头牛的货物。

column1: Send the traders on their way.
column2: 让这些商人上路吧。

column1: They left, surprised and pleased that we knew a thing or two about horses.
column2: 他们走了，惊讶并高兴地发现我们懂一点马。

column1: They left, surprised that we knew a thing or two about pricing horses.
column2: 他们走了，惊讶地发现我们懂一点马匹定价。

column1: They left, shaking their heads over our obstinate refusal to buy their “perfectly fine” horses.
column2: 他们走了，对我们顽固拒绝购买他们“完美无瑕”的马匹直摇头。

column1: They shrugged and left. “Your loss!” they said. \x01@\x15 sighed and shook his head once they were out of sight. \x05 refused to speak about our horse problem for several days.
column2: 他们耸耸肩走了。“你们的损失！”他们说。 \x01@\x15 叹了口气，在他们消失后摇了摇头。 \x05 好几天拒绝谈论我们的马匹问题。

column1: They shook their heads and smirked as they left. \x01@\x15 turned pink, and refused to speak about our horse problem for several days.
column2: 他们摇头傻笑着走了。 \x01@\x15 脸红了，好几天拒绝谈论我们的马匹问题。

column1: We refused their offer.
column2: 我们拒绝了他们的提议。

column1: Buy as many of the horses as you can afford, paying goods only.
column2: 能买多少马就买多少，只付货物。

column1: Buy all of the horses offered with goods first, then cattle.
column2: 先拿货物买下所有提供的马，再用牛买。

column1: They gladly took the payment and left the horses. One of our cottars thought he heard the \x01@! traders laughing as they left the tula.
column2: 他们高兴地收下货款，留下马匹。我们的一名佃农似乎听到 \x01@! 商人们离开图拉时在笑。

column1: They took the payment and we took the horses. \x01@\x15 glared when anyone mentioned the deal, but most of the clan appreciated the addition to the herds.
column2: 他们收了货款，我们得了马匹。每当有人提起这笔交易， \x01@\x15 就怒目而视，但氏族里大多数人还是高兴牲口增加了。

column1: They took the payment and we took the horses. The traders said that we would appreciate their fine steeds, no matter the price. \x01@\x15 beamed and led the animals away, cooing softly to them.
column2: 他们收了货款，我们得了马匹。商人们说无论什么价格，我们都会欣赏他们的好马。 \x01@\x15 眉开眼笑，领着牲口走了，轻声对它们咕哝着。

column1: We bought \x01@\x03 of them.
column2: 我们买了 \x01@\x03 匹。

column1: A party from
column2: 一队人马来自

column1: Under their honeyed words and well-timed phrases, \x01@\x15 hears a fanatical desire to own the great horse we captured from the Horse-Spawn. They are offering outrageous sums of wealth and swear eternal friendship if we will part with the magical steed.
column2: 在他们甜言蜜语和恰到好处的措辞之下， \x01@\x15 听出了一种狂热想要得到我们从马裔那里捕获的那匹神骏。他们出价高得离谱，并发誓如果肯割爱那匹神驹，将与我们永结友好。

column1: Traders from the \x01@! offered outrageous sums of wealth and swore eternal friendship with us if we would sell the magical steed we captured from the Horse-Spawn.
column2: 来自 \x01@! 的商人们出价高得离谱，并发誓如果我们肯卖掉从马裔那里捕获的神驹，就与我们永结友好。

column1: Refuse them.
column2: 拒绝他们。

column1: They frothed and spluttered, and one of them had to be restrained from attacking us there and then. “Such a magnificent beast belongs with those who know how to care for it!” their leader barked. “You will waste, utterly waste, this wonderful horse!” And they left.
column2: 他们口吐白沫、语无伦次，其中一人差点当场要攻击我们。“如此神骏属于懂得照料它的人！”他们的首领咆哮道。“你们会浪费、彻底浪费这匹好马！”然后他们走了。

column1: We refused them, in spite of their anger at us for doing so.
column2: 我们拒绝他们，尽管他们因此对我们很愤怒。

column1: Ask for \x01@\x17 cattle, and \x01@\x19 goods.
column2: 索要 \x01@\x17 头牛和 \x01@\x19 货物。

column1: They wailed and protested, but \x01@\x15 reminded them of their promises upon first seeing the horse, and they finally agreed.
column2: 他们哭嚎抗议，但 \x01@\x15 提醒他们初见那匹马时许下的承诺，他们最终同意了。

column1: After some dickering, we sold them the great steed for a handsome amount.
column2: 一番讨价还价后，我们把那匹骏马卖了个好价钱。

column1: Ask for \x01@\x17 cattle, \x01@\x19 goods, and an end to the feud.
column2: 索要 \x01@\x17 头牛、 \x01@\x19 货物，并了结世仇。

column1: After some dickering, we sold them the great steed for a handsome amount and an end to the feud between our clans.
column2: 一番讨价还价后，我们把那匹骏马卖了个好价钱，并了结了我们两族之间的世仇。

column1: Sad news. One of the carls found our wonderful, magical horse lying on its side, dead, under a great oak tree. We shall sing melancholy songs and remember how this glorious steed pranced into battle, aiding us to vanquish our enemies.
column2: 悲伤的消息。一名自由民发现我们那匹神奇骏马侧卧在一棵大橡树下，已经死了。我们将会唱起哀歌，铭记这匹荣光战马如何驰骋沙场，助我们克敌制胜。

column1: We heard from traders that the great horse we stole from the Horse-Spawn but no longer own is dead. Perhaps it would have lived longer under our care, but who can tell?
column2: 我们从商人那里听说，我们从马裔那里偷来但如今已不拥有的那匹骏马死了。或许在我们的照料下它能活得更久，但谁知道呢？

column1: One of our
column2: 我们的一名

column1: the \x01@! clan, has a trade proposal for us. They want to trade game for goods, since they know our forest is small. “We would much rather spend our time in the woods than toil to make things, even things we need.”
column2: \x01@! 氏族向我们提出了一个贸易提议。他们想用猎物换取货物，因为他们知道我们的森林很小。“我们宁愿把时间花在树林里，也不愿辛苦地制造东西，哪怕是我们需要的东西。”

column1: There is plentiful game all over Dragon Pass, so we are safe in receiving food from \x01@\x18 hunters in exchange for \x01@\x19 goods each year.
column2: 龙之隘口各处猎物都很丰富，所以我们每年从 \x01@\x18 猎人那里换取 \x01@\x19 货物来获得食物是安全的。

column1: A fair offer would be \x01@\x18 hunters’ worth of game for \x01@\x19 goods each year.
column2: 一个公平的提议是每年用相当于 \x01@\x18 猎人产出的猎物换取 \x01@\x19 货物。

column1: Envoys of the \x01@\x1E clan proposed a deal where they would give us food from hunting on our land, in exchange for worked goods.
column2: \x01@\x1E 氏族的使者提出了一项交易：他们用在我们领地上狩猎得来的食物，换取我们加工的货物。

column1: Thank them for their interest, but decline the offer.
column2: 感谢他们的兴趣，但婉拒了这个提议。

column1: They took our refusal in good spirits. “We’ll be back another time, when your mouth hungers for fine venison!” they said.
column2: 他们愉快地接受了我们的拒绝。“等你们馋美味的鹿肉时，我们会再来的。”他们说。

column1: Offer \x01@\x19 goods each year in exchange for \x01@\x18 hunters’ worth of game.
column2: 每年提供 \x01@\x19 货物，换取相当于 \x01@\x18 猎人产出的猎物。

column1: They said it sounded like a good deal. “You will savor the good venison and roasted duck when you tire of grain and beef. And we will have freedom from craft work, freedom for hunting which we dearly love.”
column2: 他们觉得听起来不错。“等你们吃腻了谷物和牛肉，会品尝到美味的鹿肉和烤鸭。而我们则能摆脱手工活，重获我们深爱的狩猎自由。”

column1: We accepted.
column2: 我们接受了。

column1: We agreed to swap goods for extra game from the \x01@\x1E each year.
column2: 我们同意每年用货物换取 \x01@\x1E 氏族多余的猎物。

column1: High-ranking members from our allies, the \x01@! clan, approach our tula. “We hear that you have a store of ivory. Those old teeth and horns are of some interest to us, and we want to trade for them,” explains their leader, \x01@\x0B.
column2: 来自我们盟友 \x01@! 氏族的地位尊贵的成员来到了我们的领地。“我们听说你们有象牙存货。那些老牙和角对我们有些用处，我们想交易它们。”他们的领袖 \x01@\x0B解释道。

column1: High-ranking members from the nearby \x01@! clan approach our tula. “We hear that you have a store of ivory. Those old teeth and horns are of some interest to us, and we want to trade for them,” explains their leader, \x01@\x0B.
column2: 来自附近 \x01@! 氏族的地位尊贵的成员来到了我们的领地。“我们听说你们有象牙存货。那些老牙和角对我们有些用处，我们想交易它们。”他们的领袖 \x01@\x0B解释道。

column1: High-ranking members from the \x01@! clan came to us to trade for our ivory.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的地位尊贵的成员来与我们交易象牙。

column1: Refuse them politely, but firmly.
column2: 礼貌但坚定地拒绝他们。

column1: \x01@\x0B started by naming a piddling amount, then increased the offer to a substantial sum. But we wanted to carve and trade the ivory ourselves, and would not change our minds. Finally, \x01@\x0B and her group went home.
column2: \x01@\x0B 起初报了一个微不足道的数目，然后逐步加价到一个可观的数额。但我们想自己雕琢并交易象牙，不会改变主意。最后， \x01@\x0B 和她的随从们回家了。

column1: They were unhappy when we refused them.
column2: 当我们拒绝他们时，他们很不高兴。

column1: Let them fill three wagonloads with ivory, in exchange for \x01A\x0F cattle.
column2: 让他们装满三车象牙，换取 \x01A\x0F 头牛。

column1: We offered them three wagonloads in exchange for \x01A\x0F cattle.
column2: 我们提出用三车象牙换取 \x01A\x0F 头牛。

column1: They weren’t completely pleased with this proposal, but they agreed to it. They promised to send the wagons and the cattle in a few weeks.
column2: 他们对这个提议并不完全满意，但还是同意了。他们承诺几周后送牛车来。

column1: They weren’t completely pleased with this proposal, but they agreed to it.
column2: 他们对这个提议并不完全满意，但还是同意了。

column1: They didn’t like this proposal at all, but we would not bend. \x01@\x0B finally sighed and shook her head, and they left.
column2: 他们完全不满意这个提议，但我们不愿让步。 \x01@\x0B 终于叹了口气，摇了摇头，然后离开了。

column1: They didn’t like this proposal at all, but neither side would bend, and they finally went home.
column2: 他们完全不满意这个提议，但双方都不肯让步，最终他们回家了。

column1: Offer to set up a trade agreement, instead, whereby they get first pick of the year’s ivory gathering.
column2: 提议改为建立贸易协议：他们可以优先挑选当年收集的象牙。

column1: The little foxes met bigger foxes and that was the end of the little foxes.

column1: Tell them we are not hiring warriors right now.

column1: They looked around the clan hall and sneered, “By the crowds of weaponthanes in this hall, I can see why you would not want to hire us. Why, we’d certainly all just trip over each others’ swords.” Their reply confirmed that we had made the right decision.
column2: 他们在部族大厅里环顾四周，冷笑道：“看这大厅里武器领主的人山人海，我明白为什么你们不想雇佣我们了。哎呀，我们肯定都会互相绊到彼此的剑。”他们的回答证实我们做了正确的决定。

column1: They said that we could not blame them for asking, and headed off to try their luck with other clan.
column2: 他们说我们不能怪他们开口问，然后前往其他氏族碰运气。

column1: Question them closely before agreeing to hire them.
column2: 在同意雇佣他们之前仔细盘问他们。

column1: they declared that we were the best clan they’d ever known. They sang poems praising our warm hearth and thanking Humakt for a place where people knew how to treat a fighter. Then they slept for two days. But they quickly shaped up into good enough weaponthanes.
column2: 他们宣称我们是有史以来最棒的氏族。他们吟唱诗歌赞美我们温暖的火炉，感谢胡玛克特让人们知道如何对待战士。然后他们睡了两天。但他们很快就成长为足够优秀的武器领主。

column1: After questioning them closely, we hired them.
column2: 仔细盘问之后，我们雇佣了他们。

column1: After questioning them closely, we found out that they were meant to spy on us.
column2: 仔细盘问之后，我们发现他们被派来监视我们。

column1: Kill them.
column2: 杀了他们。

column1: Send them away.
column2: 把他们赶走。

column1: We marched them to edge of our tula and booted them off our land. They must have been sober enough to find their way back, for we haven’t heard about them since.
column2: 我们把他们押到图拉边缘，踢出了我们的土地。他们大概清醒得足够找到回去的路，因为此后我们再没听说他们的消息。

column1: We sent them away.
column2: 我们把他们赶走了。

column1: Hire them.
column2: 雇佣他们。

column1: We took advantage of their offer to strengthen our own thin defenses.
column2: 我们利用他们的提议来加强自己薄弱的防御。

column1: We hired them.
column2: 我们雇佣了他们。

column1: and the others died from foolhardy actions during raids.
column2: 其余的人则因在突袭中鲁莽行事而丧命。

column1: and the others drank too much beer, fell off their horses, sickened and died.
column2: 其余的人啤酒喝得太多，从马上摔下来，染病而死。

column1: He said they sent him to tell us, since it was supposed to be our vision, not theirs. Then he left.
column2: 他说他们派他来告诉我们，因为那本该是我们的幻象，不是他们的。然后他就离开了。

column1: He said they interpreted it to mean that we would prove unreliable, and that the alliance between our clans was over. Then he left.
column2: 他说他们解读为我们将不可靠，我们氏族之间的联盟就此结束。然后他就离开了。

column1: The \x01@  chieftain, \x01@\x0B, stomps onto the tula, shouting and waving \x04 spear. When \x06 and \x04 escort reach the clan hall, \x06 tells us that \x06 is sick and tired of hearing us laughing at \x04 clan. When we ask where \x06 heard this, \x06 bellows “I can hear your mocking tones in the wind as it blows through the aspens, in the stream as it rills over the rocks! It’s clear! Clear to me!”
column2: \x01@  首领 \x01@\x0B跺着脚冲进图拉，挥舞着 \x04 长矛大喊大叫。当 \x06 和 \x04 护卫到达部族大厅时， \x06 告诉我们， \x06 已经听腻了我们嘲笑 \x04 氏族。当我们问 \x06 从哪听说的， \x06 吼道：“我能从吹过白杨的风中、从淌过岩石的溪流中听到你们的嘲弄声！清清楚楚！对我而言清清楚楚！”

column1: \x05 continues, “I am so tired of it that I say if you give us a token peace offering, we will forget what we were feuding over!”
column2: \x05继续说道：“我对此厌倦至极，所以我说，如果你们给我们象征性的和平祭品，我们就忘记我们在为什么而世仇！”

column1: \x01@\x0B, mad chief of the \x01@! clan, came to our tula and told us that a token offering would end the feud between our two clans.
column2: \x01@\x0B \x01@! 氏族的疯首领来到我们的图拉，告诉我们一份象征性的祭品就能结束两族之间的世仇。

column2: 给他们5头牛，并宣布世仇结束。

column1: They turned and left, as a sudden summer squall blows over your field then moves on. For weeks afterwards, the children stomped around the tula, swinging sticks and shouting nonsense.
column2: 他们转身离开，就像一场突如其来的夏日暴风雨掠过你的田地然后远去。在接下来的几周里，孩子们在图拉四周跺脚走来走去，挥舞着棍棒，大喊大叫着胡言乱语。

column1: We declined this strange offer.
column2: 我们婉拒了这个奇怪的提议。

column1: Escort them off your lands.
column2: 护送他们离开你们的土地。

column1: We told them that if they wanted to end the feud, they could pay reparations to us. We said we would not slay them this afternoon, but this evening we might change our minds. They left quickly. The children stomped around the tula, swinging sticks and shouting nonsense, for weeks afterwards.
column2: 我们告诉他们，如果他们要结束世仇，可以向我们支付赔偿。我们说今天下午不会杀死他们，但今晚我们可能会改变主意。他们迅速离开了。在接下来的几周里，孩子们在图拉四周跺脚走来走去，挥舞着棍棒，大喊大叫着胡言乱语。

column1: We escorted them off the tula.

column1: No one thought to tell \x08 that as far as we knew, we were already feuding with the \x01@! clan.

column1: “If their war tactics are as well-coordinated as their chief, we shall squash them when they creep out of their tula to make war on us.”
column2: “如果他们的战争策略像他们的首领一样协调一致，那么当他们爬出图拉向我们开战时，我们就会把他们碾碎。”

column1: “We can hope that their weaponthanes swing their swords as poorly as \x01@\x0B. But I will take care not to underestimate their threat.”
column2: “我们可以希望他们的武器领主挥剑像 \x01@\x0B一样糟糕。但我会小心，不低估他们的威胁。”

column1: The \x01@! clan’s leading weaponthane, \x01@\x0B, comes bearing gifts and a message from his chieftain. “You think we are mad. But we know you think this, and you know that we know that you think this, unlike other people who pretend to us that they think we are normal even though it is obvious that they think we are mad.”
column2: \x01@! 氏族的首席武器领主 \x01@\x0B带着礼物和他族长的口信到来。“你们认为我们疯了。但我们知道你们这么想，你们也知道我们知道你们这么想，不像其他人，他们向我们假装认为我们正常，尽管很明显他们认为我们疯了。”

column1: \x01@\x0B pauses for breath. “Therefore, we can trust you.” He proposes an alliance between our clans. “At least,” \x01@\x0B said, “that was the chief’s wish when I left the tula.” We told him we would think about it.

column1: Decline politely, give reciprocal gifts.

column1: The \x01@! clan is known for electing mad leaders.
column2: \x01@! 氏族以选举疯狂领袖而闻名。

column1: The \x01@! clan sent their leading weaponthane, \x01@\x0B, bearing a strange blue cheese as a gift from his clan.
column2: \x01@! 氏族派出了他们的首席武器领主 \x01@\x0B，带着一块奇怪的蓝色奶酪作为他氏族的礼物。

column1: Decline the cheese politely.
column2: 礼貌地拒绝奶酪。

column1: The aroma from \x01@\x0B’s wagons did not bode well for this gift. He said that we did not know the value of what we were refusing, turned his wagons around, and left. Later that season, hunters followed a horrific stench and found the cheese dumped in a ravine near the edge of our land.
column2: 从 \x01@\x0B的马车上散发出的气味对这份礼物来说并非好兆头。他说我们不知道自己所拒绝之物的价值，然后掉转马车离开了。那季晚些时候，猎人们循着可怕的恶臭，发现奶酪被倾倒在我们土地边缘附近的一条峡谷里。

column1: We refused the smelly gift, but politely.
column2: 我们拒绝了这份难闻的礼物，但很礼貌。

column1: Thank him for the cheese, give a reciprocal gift.
column2: 感谢他的奶酪，给予回礼。

column1: We told him to express our gratitude to his clan and his chief. After he left, the carls gathered around the wagons wondering what to do with this cheese, which smelled bad and good at the same time.
column2: 我们让他向他的氏族和族长表达我们的感激之情。他离开后，自由民们聚集在马车周围，不知道如何处理这块闻起来又臭又香的奶酪。

column1: We thanked him, and gave a reciprocal gift.
column2: 我们感谢了他，并给了回礼。

column1: Try a piece.
column2: 尝一块。

column1: \x01@\r eventually nibbled at a piece off a cheese wheel. Her brows lifted, her eyes watered, and her face puckered up. Then she smacked her lips and proclaimed this a wonderful food.
column2: \x01@\r 终于从一块乳酪轮上啃下了一小块。她扬起眉毛，泪水盈眶，脸皱成一团。然后她咂了咂嘴，宣称这是美味佳肴。

column1: \x01@\r eventually nibbled at a piece off a cheese wheel. She spat it out as fast as she could, coughing and retching. We wound up feeding it all to the pigs.
column2: \x01@\r 终于从一块乳酪轮上啃下了一小块。她以最快的速度吐了出来，咳嗽干呕。我们最后把它全喂了猪。

column1: Feed it to the pigs.
column2: 喂猪吧。

column1: The swine waded right into the cheese, giving happy little grunts as they swallowed it down. Then they all took a long nap, now and then letting loose harmonious belches.
column2: 猪崽们直接冲进乳酪里，欢快地哼哼着吞下去。然后它们全都睡了长长一觉，时不时发出和谐的饱嗝声。

column1: Tell him that you consider the offer as good as the deed, and tell him to keep his cheese.
column2: 告诉他，你把这份心意当作已经实践了的礼数，让他留着乳酪。

column1: “Either you accept a gift or you don’t!” he snarled, turning his wagons around and storming off the tula.
column2: “要么你接受礼物，要么就不接受！”他咆哮着，掉转他的货车车队，气冲冲地离开了图拉。

column1: Later that season, carls followed a terrible stink and found the cheese dumped in a ditch near our fields.
column2: 那季晚些时候，自由民循着一股恶臭，发现乳酪被扔在我们田地附近的一条沟渠里。

column1: We told him that the offer was as good as the deed, and he could keep the cheese.
column2: 我们告诉他，心意已领，礼物可留。
