column2: 昨天牧人们发现那头被称为黑尾之子的公牛死了。它繁育了许多优良的牲畜，但没有一只能比得上它或黑尾。

column1: Our Garland of Reeds, symbolizing friendship with the elves has rotted away. We must tend our relations with the elves very carefully from here on in.
column2: 象征与精灵友谊的芦苇花环已经腐烂。从今往后我们必须极其小心地维护与精灵的关系。

column1: Our god-talkers say that
column2: 我们的神言者说

column1: one of our Spirit Fetches
column2: 我们的一个精魂护符

column1: our Spirit Fetch
column2: 我们的精魂护符

column1: caught some of the magic we lost recently. \x02\x03We have some of our luck back, though it cost us the treasure./The Fetch returned our magic and then its spirit left./As we expected, the Spirit Fetch disintegrated afterwards.\x02
column2: 捕获了我们最近失去的一些魔力。 \x02\x03我们找回了一些运气，虽牺牲了宝物。/护符归还了魔力，然后它的精魂离开了。/正如我们所料，精魂护符随后分解了。\x02

column1: The earthshakers we rode into battle on have become old and slow. They are no longer reliable mounts, and we must put them out to pasture — or whatever you do with an old earthshaker. The warriors promise to keep tending them in their old age.
column2: 我们曾骑乘作战的地动者已经年老迟缓。它们不再是可靠的坐骑，我们必须让它们退役放牧——或者按老地动者的处置来办。武士们承诺在它们晚年继续照料。

column1: All the carls are \x02\x02overjoyed by/ecstatic over\x02 the Earthshaker Plow Team. Not only did they produce long, straight furrows with a minimum of effort, but they have \x02\x02added to/enhanced\x02 our clan magic.
column2: 所有自由民都 \x02\x02因撼地犁队而欣喜若狂/兴奋不已\x02 。它们不仅毫不费力地犁出又长又直的沟，还 \x02\x02增加/增强\x02 了我们的氏族魔法。

column1: The Earthshaker Plow team not only proved their worth at plowing our fields, but they increased our clan magic by a prodigious amount.
column2: 撼地犁队不仅在犁田时证明了它们的价值，还极大地增强了我们的氏族魔法。

column1: Unfortunately, they worked so hard this year that they burst their hearts and died.
column2: 不幸的是，它们今年过于辛劳，心脏爆裂而死。

column1: The earthshakers which effortlessly pulled our plows for so long have become old and slow. We must put them out to pasture — or whatever you do with an old earthshaker. The carls promise to keep tending them in their old age, and will make sure they don’t stray into the crops.
column2: 这些长久以来毫不费力拉犁的地动者已经年老迟缓。我们必须让它们退役放牧——或者按老地动者的处置来办。自由民们承诺在它们晚年继续照料，并确保它们不会误入庄稼地。

column1: The undead are gaining a foothold in the area around our tula. Our treasure, Humakt’s Warning Rune, has changed color.
column2: 亡灵正在我们领地周围的区域站稳脚跟。我们的宝物“胡马克特警告符文”已经变色。

column1: Ignore the warning for now.
column2: 暂时忽略警告。

column1: Sacrifice 5 cows to Humakt.
column2: 向胡马克特献祭5头牛。

column1: Sacrifice goods worth 5 cows to Humakt.
column2: 向胡马克特献祭价值5头牛的货物。

column1: Sacrifice 10 cows to Humakt.
column2: 向胡马克特献祭10头牛。

column1: Sacrifice goods worth 10 cows to Humakt.
column2: 向胡马克特献祭价值10头牛的货物。

column1: Our god-talkers said that Humakt would \x02\x02grant his protection/keep the undead at bay\x02.
column2: 我们的神言者说胡马克特会 \x02\x02赐予保护/抵挡亡灵\x02。

column1: Our god-talkers \x02\x02said that Humakt had not received our sacrifice/were unsure of Humakt’s protection\x02.
column2: 我们的神言者 \x02\x02说胡马克特没有接受我们的献祭/不确定胡马克特的保护\x02。

column1: The weaponthanes
column2: 武器领主们

column1: The warriors
column2: 武士们

column1: are \x02\x03displeased/disgruntled/grumbling\x02 because we didn’t even bother listening to the gods last year, when they said we’d have luck with our cattle raids.
column2: \x02\x03不满/不快/抱怨\x02 ，因为去年神说我们牲畜突袭会有好运，我们却连听都不听。

column1: We never did \x02\x02go cattle raiding/make a cattle raid\x02.
column2: 我们从未 \x02\x02进行牲畜突袭/发动过一次牲畜突袭\x02。

column1: All the god-talkers agree: Chalana Arroy was pleased that we didn’t \x02\x02launch any raids/send our warriors raiding\x02 this last year. We should have little problem with disease for a few years.
column2: 所有神言者一致认为：查拉娜·阿洛伊很高兴我们去年没有 \x02\x02发动任何突袭/派武士去袭击\x02 。未来几年我们应很少受疾病困扰。

column1: Chalana Arroy spoke to me in a vision. She was \x02\x02unhappy/saddened\x02 that we didn’t \x02\x02listen to her when she asked us/heed her advice\x02 not to raid. She is too merciful to curse us, but she will not be giving us her special blessing, either.
column2: 查拉娜·阿洛伊在异象中对我说话。她对我们没有 \x02\x02在她请求时听从她/听从她的劝告\x02 不要突袭感到 \x02\x02不悦/悲伤\x02 。她太过仁慈不会诅咒我们，但也不会赐予我们特别的祝福。

column1: Orlanth and Issaries \x02\x02judged us as they had promised, and found us worthy because/were pleased that\x02 we have more cows than we did a year ago.
column2: 奥兰斯和伊萨里斯 \x02\x02如约审判了我们，因我们比一年前拥有更多牛而认为我们值得/感到满意\x02 。

column1: The god-talkers of those two deities \x02\x02are now closer to their gods/were granted magical strength\x02.
column2: 这两位神祇的神言者 \x02\x02现在更接近他们的神/获得了魔法力量\x02。

column1: Orlanth and Issaries \x02\x02judged us as they had promised, and found us lacking because/were displeased that\x02 we have no more cows than we did a year ago.
column2: 奥兰斯与伊萨里斯 \x02\x02如约审判了我们，并发现我们有所欠缺/因我们与一年前相比并未拥有更多牛只而不悦\x02 。

column1: The god-talkers of those two deities \x02\x02are now in less favor with their gods/feel weaker and less able to work magic\x02.
column2: 那两位神祇的神言者 \x02\x02如今在神明面前恩宠减少/感到力量削弱，施展魔法能力下降\x02。

column1: The year began on a bad note: Maran Gor shook one of the hills and
column2: 这一年开局不利：马兰·戈尔摇晃了一座山丘，并且

column1: sent a river of earth down onto a carl’s stead. The entire family smothered in the dirt, and their livestock are missing.
column2: 将一股土流倾泻到一位自由民的农庄上。全家人都被泥土掩埋窒息而死，他们的牲畜也失踪了。

column1: flattened part of the forest. Several hunters are missing. A large pit appeared in a nearby pasture at the same time, and swallowed a small herd of our cattle.
column2: 压平了部分森林。几名猎人失踪。同时，附近的牧场出现了一个大坑，吞没了我们的一小群牛。

column1: The next time the god-talkers warn of Ernalda’s sister’s wrath, we should pay attention.
column2: 下次神言者警告厄纳尔达姐妹的怒火时，我们应该留意。

column1: Once again, the god-talkers heard Ernalda crying beneath the earth. We were not able to devote magic to crops, because we did not learn one of her blessings last year.
column2: 神言者再次听到厄纳尔达在地下哭泣。我们无法将魔法用于庄稼，因为去年我们没学会她的一个赐福。

column1: \x02\x06found a magic sword while exploring the northwest/befriended a huge wind spirit in the mountains near Prax/met a foreign magician who promised their warriors prowess in battle in exchange for a new song/explored the lands to the northeast and found a dragon who promised them ancient secrets of battle/explored the lands to the southwest and found a magic battle standard/explored far into the west and found shamans willing to give them battle spirits\x02.
column2: \x02\x06在西北探索时发现了一把魔法剑/在普拉克斯附近的山中结交了一位巨大的风灵/遇见了一位外国法师，他承诺用新歌换取他们战士的战斗勇猛/探索了东北方的土地，发现了一条龙，它承诺传授古老的战斗秘密/探索了西南方的土地，发现了一面魔法战旗/远赴西方，找到了愿意赐予他们战斗之灵的萨满\x02。

column1: They say they mean to use their new power against our clan. We should have heeded Lhankor Mhy’s warning last year.
column2: 他们说打算用新获得的力量来对付我们氏族。我们去年本该听从兰科尔·米的警告。

column1: Orlanth is displeased that we did not succeed at making a pilgrimage to Kero Fin last year, and has withheld some of his favor from us.
column2: 奥兰斯对我们去年未能成功前往凯罗芬朝圣感到不悦，因此扣留了他的一部分恩惠。

column1: Orlanth has not forgotten that he asked us to make a pilgrimage to \x02\x03Mount Kero Fin/his mountain mother/his birthplace\x02, and has \x02\x02endowed us with extra luck/given us his favor\x02.
column2: 奥兰斯并未忘记他曾要求我们前往 \x02\x03凯罗芬山/他的山岳母亲/他的诞生地\x02朝圣，并 \x02\x02赐予我们额外的运气/给予我们他的恩惠\x02。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors are \x02\x03sad/puzzled/angry\x02 that we did not sacrifice to them last year. They say they do not make such requests \x02\x02often/lightly\x02, and that our clan magic will be \x02\x02harmed/reduced\x02 for a while because we did not help them.
column2: 我们祖先之灵 \x02\x03因我们去年未向他们献祭而感到悲伤/困惑/愤怒\x02 。他们说他们并不 \x02\x02经常/轻易\x02提出这样的要求，并且我们的氏族魔法将会 \x02\x02受损/减弱\x02 一段时间，因为我们没有帮助他们。

column1: We didn’t learn any blessings of Odayla last year. I think this is why there is now no game to be found in our forests and wild lands.
column2: 去年我们没有学会奥达伊拉的任何赐福。我想这就是为什么现在我们的森林和野地中找不到猎物。

column1: The good news is that the gods are not angry we failed to heroquest last year. The bad news is that the gods themselves needed our help. Because we failed to dare the god-plane, Chaos and all our other worst enemies have been strengthened.
column2: 好消息是，神明并未因我们去年未能进行英雄任务而发怒。坏消息是，神明本身需要我们的帮助。因为我们未能勇闯神域，混沌和我们所有其他最凶恶的敌人都得到了增强。

column1: Humakt is not only the god of war, but also of oaths and promises. And we didn’t keep our promise to him, to raid before we were raided. Our war magic will suffer for years to come as a consequence.
column2: 胡马克特不仅是战争之神，也是誓约与承诺之神。而我们没有遵守对他的承诺——在被劫掠之前先发制人。因此，我们的战争魔法将在未来数年受影响。

column1: It is too bad that we were unable to explore the northwest, as the omens indicated. I feel we lost \x02\x02an amazing chance/a fabulous opportunity\x02 of some sort or another.
column2: 很遗憾我们没能像征兆所指示的那样探索西北。我觉得我们失去了 \x02\x02某个绝佳的机遇/某个极好的机会\x02 。

column1: Everyone, in neighboring clans as well as our own folk, everyone is talking about the land of Tarsh, which we recently explored. They are pleased to have learned that the dragons didn’t eat everybody in the lands to the north. They would be glad to learn more.
column2: 所有人——邻族和我们自己人——都在谈论我们最近探索过的塔什之地。他们很高兴得知巨龙并没有吃掉北方土地上的所有人。他们乐意了解更多。

column1: People are still talking about our trip back to Tarsh. They were very interested in the news we brought back, and would no doubt be pleased if we took another trip.
column2: 人们仍在谈论我们返回塔什的旅行。他们对我们带回的消息非常感兴趣，如果我们再次出行，无疑会很高兴。

column1: We have gained treasures over the past two years. We have pleased Issaries, so our market will be more profitable for \x02\x02a number of/several\x02 years.
column2: 过去两年我们获得了财宝。我们取悦了伊萨里斯，因此我们的市场将在 \x02\x02多年/数年\x02 内利润更高。

column1: We were unable to increase our store of treasures over the last two years, as Issaries had hoped. For several years, he will be withholding his favor from our market. We should have done more exploring and trading.
column2: 正如伊萨里斯所期望的，我们过去两年未能增加财宝储备。他将数年不向我们的市场赐予恩惠。我们本该进行更多探索和贸易。

column1: The god-talkers heard the sad, distant lowing of Uralda’s herd. We were not able to devote magic to our own herds, because we did not learn one of Uralda’s blessings last year.
column2: 神言者听到了尤拉尔达牛群悲伤遥远的哞叫声。我们无法将魔法用于自己的畜群，因为去年我们没有学会尤拉尔达的一个赐福。

column1: The Storm Bull is furious with us. We can expect wild gales and punishing storms as evidence of his wrath. Worse, our war magic will suffer for years to come.
column2: 风暴公牛对我们极为愤怒。我们将遭遇狂风和惩戒性的风暴，以证明他的愤怒。更糟的是，我们的战争魔法将在未来数年受损。

column1: Brandgor, a thane of the \x01@! clan, sweeps into your hall, four grim warriors at his side. Last season, his nephew, Hend Aslandarsson, was killed by Orlmar Half-Foot, a member of your clan. Brandgor demands 30 cows as compensation for his kinsman’s death.
column2: 布兰德戈尔， \x01@! 氏族的一个乡绅，带着四名面色严峻的战士大步走进你的大厅。上季，他的侄子亨德·阿斯兰达松被你氏族成员奥尔玛·半足所杀。布兰德戈尔要求赔偿30头牛作为他亲属的死亡补偿。

column1: Brandgor of the \x01@! clan lodged a legal claim against us, demanding many cows as compensation for the death of his nephew, who was slain by Orlmar Half-foot.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的布兰德戈尔向我们提起了一项法律诉讼，要求我们为他的侄子——被奥尔玛·半足所杀——支付大量牛只作为补偿。

column1: “Nobody from the \x01@" clan killed Hend!”
column2: “ \x01@" 氏族没有人杀了亨德！”

column1: Offer to stop the feud.
column2: 提议中止世仇。

column1: Pay 10 cows.
column2: 支付10头牛。

column1: We paid him a third of what he asked.
column2: 我们支付了他所要的三分之一。

column1: Brandgor left with our wealth, but didn’t seem pleased.
column2: 布兰德戈尔带着我们的财富离开，但似乎并不满意。

column1: Pay 20 cows.
column2: 支付20头牛。

column1: We paid him a just wergild, though less than he had asked.
column2: 我们支付了一笔公正的血偿金，虽然少于他的要求。

column1: Brandgor left with our wealth.
column2: 布兰德戈尔带着我们的财富离开。

column1: Pay 30 cows.
column2: 支付30头牛。

column1: We honored his request.
column2: 我们满足了他的要求。

column1: Brandgor left with our wealth, in a much better mood than he arrived.
column2: 布兰德戈尔带着我们的财富离开，心情比来时好得多。

column1: Refuse to pay.
column2: 拒绝支付。

column1: We rejected his claim.
column2: 我们驳回了他的诉讼请求。

column1: Brandgor departed, his warriors muttering vague threats.
column2: 布兰德戈尔离开了，他的战士们嘟囔着含糊的威胁。

column1: Take the matter up at the next tribal moot.
column2: 在下一次部落大会上提出此事。

column1: We told him to take up the issue at the next tribal moot.
column2: 我们告诉他，在下一次部落大会上提出这个问题。

column1: Brandgor left. He didn’t seem surprised.
column2: 布兰德戈尔离开了。他似乎并不惊讶。

column1: 30 cows would feed 4 families.
column2: 30头牛能养活4个家庭。

column1: They would probably settle for less.
column2: 他们可能会接受更少的赔偿。

column1: We can withstand their raids.
column2: 我们可以抵御他们的袭击。

column1: They have more warriors than we do, and we would have difficulty if they raided.
column2: 他们的战士比我们多，如果他们来袭击，我们会很困难。

column1: They already hate us, and will raid us if they can.
column2: 他们早已恨我们，只要有机会就会来袭击。

column1: No wergild is due because Hend provoked Orlmar.
column2: 不应支付血偿金，因为亨德挑衅了奥尔玛。

column1: A young warrior of his rank is due a wergild of 20 cows.
column2: 像他这样级别的年轻战士应得20头牛的血偿金。

column1: A young warrior of his rank is due a wergild of 20 cows. However, Orlmar and his brother suffered compensating injuries in the incident, worth about 10 cows.
column2: 像他这样级别的年轻战士应得20头牛的血偿金。不过，奥尔玛和他的兄弟在此次事件中也受了相应的伤，价值约10头牛。

column1: We are already feuding with them. Still, if we pay some compensation, we can keep matters from getting worse.
column2: 我们已经与他们有世仇。不过，如果我们支付一些补偿，可以防止事态恶化。

column1: Ending the feud would be a bold move.
column2: 结束世仇将是一个大胆的举动。

column1: They are our allies. We should pay their claim.
column2: 他们是我们的盟友。我们应该满足他们的索赔要求。

column1: Regardless of the justness of their claim, we risk offending them if we don’t pay some compensation.
column2: 无论他们的索赔要求是否正当，如果不支付一些补偿，我们就有冒犯他们的风险。

column1: I always knew that Orlmar Half-foot would cause trouble!
column2: 我早就知道奥尔玛·半足会惹麻烦！

column1: Hend and Orlmar never got along. I think it was something about a woman. Nobody was very surprised when they came to blows.
column2: 亨德和奥尔玛从来就合不来。我想是为了一个女人。他们动手打架时，没人感到意外。

column1: This is why we joined a tribe — to resolve disputes like this.
column2: 这正是我们加入部落的原因——解决这样的争端。

column1: We don’t need more killing.
column2: 我们不需要更多的杀戮。

column1: We can stop this from getting worse.
column2: 我们可以阻止事态恶化。

column1: If more of you read the ancient sagas, you wouldn’t have to ask me what to do in situations like this.
column2: 如果你们多读读古代传说，就不必问我在这种情况下该怎么做了。

column1: Orlmar got the wrong man. He should have started with Brandgor.
column2: 奥尔玛找错了人。他应该先去找布兰德戈尔。

column1: Either way, tell him the truth.
column2: 无论怎样，告诉他真相。

column1: Brandgor snorts indignantly. “Many of you witnessed Orlmar’s attack. You can stand here and baldly deny that it happened, yet still call yourselves honorable Orlanthi? Your villainy defies belief.”
column2: 布兰德戈尔愤愤不平地哼了一声。“你们很多人目睹了奥尔玛的攻击。你们可以站在这里公然否认这件事，却还自称可敬的奥兰提人？你们的邪恶行径令人难以置信。”

column1: Apologize and give him 30 cows.
column2: 道歉并给他30头牛。

column1: We humbled ourselves and acceded to his demands.
column2: 我们低声下气，同意了他的要求。

column1: Apologize and offer 40 cows.
column2: 道歉并提供40头牛。

column1: We humbled ourselves and gave him more cows than he asked for.
column2: 我们低声下气，给了他比他所要更多的牛。

column1: Offer 20 cows, without admitting fault.
column2: 提供20头牛，但不承认过错。

column1: Without admitting fault, we gave him fewer cows than he had asked for.
column2: 我们没有承认过错，给他的牛少于他所要的。

column1: Show him the door.
column2: 把他赶出去。

column1: We told him to go, and speak no more to us of his demands.
column2: 我们让他离开，别再跟我们提他的要求。

column1: Threaten him with warfare if he does not apologize.
column2: 如果他不道歉，就以战争威胁他。

column1: We’ve angered Brandgor! Now we have him where we want him!
column2: 我们激怒了布兰德戈尔！现在他落入了我们的掌控！

column1: Lying about an obvious fact may not have been the best way to win him over.
column2: 对明显的事实撒谎，可能不是赢得他支持的最佳方式。

column1: The only way to mollify him now is to offer him more than he asked.
column2: 现在安抚他的唯一办法，就是给他比他所要更多的东西。

column2: 告诉他们，他们可以自由寻找任何愿意帮助他们的人。

column1: Our council told them that, while justice is a matter for the clan, vengeance is a matter for the individual. \x01B3 and the others were made free to pursue vengeance, as individuals.
column2: 我们的议会告诉他们，虽然公正是氏族的事，复仇是个人的事。 \x01B3 和其他人作为个人被允许自由寻求复仇。

column1: \x01B3 said that she would have no trouble finding warriors with more sense of honor than the clan ring.
column2: \x01B3 说她不费吹灰之力就能找到比氏族议会更有荣誉感的战士。

column1: Try to convince them to let go of hatred and live for their children.
column2: 试着说服他们放下仇恨，为了孩子而活。

column1: Eloquent words were spoken, and \x01B3 proclaimed that mercy had beaten hatred.
column2: 雄辩之词被说出， \x01B3 宣告仁慈战胜了仇恨。

column1: Members of the council urged \x01B3 to find forgiveness within herself. Alas, she seemed little moved by these words.
column2: 议会成员敦促 \x01B3 在自己内心找到宽恕。唉，她似乎对这些话无动于衷。

column1: Blood for blood, that’s the most basic law.
column2: 血债血偿，这是最基本的法则。

column1: Although the widows have a right to seek vengeance, the clan is not obligated to support their quest.
column2: 虽然寡妇有权寻求复仇，但氏族没有义务支持她们的诉求。

column1: If we do not act against the killers, our people will wonder why they work so hard to support warriors and buy horses.
column2: 如果我们不对凶手采取行动，我们的人民会质疑为何他们如此努力供养战士、购买马匹。

column1: The most vocal of our people cry for blood, but most are secretly afraid of sustaining further losses.
column2: 我们氏族中最大声疾呼者要求流血，但大多数人在心底害怕遭受更多损失。

column1: Vengeance will have to wait until after planting is done.
column2: 复仇必须等到播种完成之后。

column1: If we raid during the planting season, our crops will suffer. But \x01B3 knows this.
column2: 如果我们在播种季节劫掠，我们的庄稼会受损。但 \x01B3 知道这一点。

column1: Vengeance will have to wait until after the harvest.
column2: 复仇必须等到收获之后。

column1: If we raid during the harvest, we will leave grain in the fields. But \x01B3 knows this.
column2: 如果我们在收获时劫掠，谷物会留在田里。但 \x01B3 知道这一点。

column1: Do we care no more for the deaths of our proud men than if a cow or horse dies? Strike swift, and strike sure!
column2: 难道我们对我们骄傲战士的死亡，还不如对一头牛或马的死更在意？迅速出击，确保命中！

column1: There are men in the \x01@! clan in need of killing. It is our duty to bring them the gift of Death.
column2: \x01@! 氏族里有些人必须被杀死。我们的职责是给他们带去死亡之礼。

column1: Blood never healed a wound. Only time can cure their sorrow.
column2: 鲜血从未治愈过伤口。唯有时间能抚平他们的悲伤。

column1: Vengeance is important. But don’t forget, there is always another way.
column2: 复仇很重要。但别忘了，总有另一条路。

column1: Surely we can talk to them, and effect a conciliation.
column2: 我们当然可以与他们交谈，达成和解。

column1: Do not disregard their words because they are women! \x01B3’s influence is strong.
column2: 不要因为她们是女人就无视她们的话！ \x01B3的影响力很强。

column1: scene006
column2: scene006

column1: Mordrim the Stout, a prosperous farmer from the \x01@! clan, has come to offer to trade for Blacktail, the best bull in your herds. He is accompanied by his two adult sons Korlmar and Harnkorl. He makes no secret of his determination to get that bull, offering \x01@\r cows worth of trade goods for it.
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的富裕农夫壮汉莫德里姆前来提出交易，想换取你们牛群中最好的公牛黑尾。他的两个成年儿子科尔玛和哈恩科尔陪同。他毫不掩饰要得到那头公牛的决心，出价 \x01@\r头牛的等值货物。

column1: Mordrim the Stout of the \x01@! clan wanted to buy our treasured bull, Blacktail.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的壮汉莫德里姆想购买我们珍爱的公牛黑尾。

column1: Accept his offer.
column2: 接受他的出价。

column1: We sold it to him for \x01@\r cows.
column2: 我们以 \x01@\r头牛的价格卖给了他。

column1: Mordrim and his sons left with Blacktail, looking mightily pleased with themselves.
column2: 莫德里姆和他的儿子们带着黑尾离开了，看上去得意洋洋。

column1: Gift him with the bull.
column2: 把公牛赠予他。

column1: In a great show of generosity, we gave the bull to Mordrim, who seemed to want it very much.
column2: 出于极大的慷慨，我们把公牛送给了莫德里姆，他似乎非常想要它。

column1: Refuse to sell, but offer stud service.
column2: 拒绝出售，但提供配种服务。

column1: Although we could not part with the fertile bull, we did offer Mordrim’s clan Blacktail’s stud service.
column2: 尽管我们无法割舍这头健壮的公牛，但我们确实向莫德里姆的氏族提供了黑尾的配种服务。

column1: Although he wasn’t completely happy, Mordrim accepted our offer, and gave us a small gift.
column2: 虽然不太高兴，莫德里姆还是接受了我们的提议，并送了我们一份小礼物。

column1: Refuse to sell the bull.
column2: 拒绝出售公牛。

column1: Whatever Mordrim’s offer, we could not bear to part with the fecund Blacktail, who has strengthened our herds for so long.
column2: 无论莫德里姆出什么价，我们都不忍心舍弃多产的黑尾，它长久以来一直壮大我们的牛群。

column1: Mordrim and his sons left, looking very displeased.
column2: 莫德里姆和他的儿子们离开了，看上去很不高兴。

column1: Sell him Blacktail for \x01@\x08 cows worth of goods.
column2: 以 \x01@\x08 头牛等值的货物将黑尾卖给他。

column1: We sold it to him, but exacted a heavy price.
column2: 我们卖给了他，但要了高价。

column1: Mordrim grumbled, but in the end paid our price.
column2: 莫德里姆抱怨了几句，但最终还是按我们的价格付了账。

column1: Blacktail is extremely fertile, but sure to give out sooner or later. Best to get rid of him while he’s still valuable.
column2: 黑尾极其多产，但迟早会不行。趁它还有价值，最好处理掉。

column1: Blacktail is extremely fertile. We might have fewer strong calves without him.
column2: 黑尾极其多产。没有它，我们强壮的小牛可能会减少。

column1: Blacktail is extremely fertile. We’d have fewer strong calves without him.
column2: 黑尾极其多产。没有它，我们强壮的小牛会减少。

column1: Refuse his offer outright. He’ll be back later, offering twice as much.
column2: 直接拒绝他的出价。他以后会回来，出双倍的价钱。

column1: Look at the gleam in his eyes. He’ll pay more than \x01@\r, if need be.
column2: 看他眼里的光芒。如有必要，他会支付超过 \x01@\r的价格。

column1: He doesn’t just want Blacktail. He needs Blacktail. He could do something bad if we refuse him.
column2: 他不只是想要黑尾。他需要黑尾。如果我们拒绝，他可能会做出坏事。

column1: I’ve heard that the \x01@! clan does terrible things to their cows — but don’t let him know we’ve heard those stories.
column2: 我听说 \x01@! 氏族对他们的牛做可怕的事情——但别让他知道我们听过那些传言。

column1: Whatever happens, we haven’t seen the last of Mordrim. I can feel it in my bones.
column2: 无论发生什么，我们还没见识到莫德里姆的底牌。我骨子里能感觉到。

column1: The seed is nothing without good earth.
column2: 没有好土壤，种子什么也不是。

column1: Even \x01@\x08 cows isn’t really enough. But if you feel we must, then it’s close.
column2: 即使 \x01@\x08 头牛也不太够。但如果你觉得必须如此，那也差不多了。

column1: The cows are nothing without good seed.
column2: 没有好种子，牛什么也不是。

column1: This is our chance to make our clan’s name shine throughout Dragon Pass!
column2: 这是让我们氏族名震龙隘的机会！

column1: Mordrim must think we’re simple, to sell a clan treasure for mere silver.
column2: 莫德里姆一定以为我们傻，才会为了区区银币卖掉氏族珍宝。

column1: There is no shame in keeping something good.
column2: 保留好东西并不丢人。

column1: scene007
column2: scene007

column1: One of your carls saw them do it, without mistake: Korlmar and Harnkorl, sons of Mordrim the Stout, stole away your treasured and fertile bull, Blacktail! Your refusal to sell the animal clearly did nothing to quench Mordrim’s desire to own it.
column2: 你的一个自由民亲眼看到他们干的，千真万确：壮汉莫德里姆的儿子科尔玛和哈恩科尔偷走了你珍爱且多产的公牛黑尾！你拒绝出售显然丝毫未能熄灭莫德里姆占有它的欲望。

column1: A grave offense was committed against us by members of the \x01@! clan. Korlmar and Harnkorl, sons of Mordrim the Stout, stole our treasured bull, Blacktail.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的成员对我们犯下了严重罪行。壮汉莫德里姆的儿子科尔玛和哈恩科尔偷走了我们珍爱的公牛黑尾。

column1: Ignore the incident for now.
column2: 暂时忽略这件事。

column1: The people were happy that we retaliated against the \x01@! clan, and even happier that Blacktail was back in his own pasture.
column2: 人民对我们报复 \x01@! 氏族感到高兴，而黑尾回到自己的牧场更让他们欢欣。

column1: The people knew that we had to try to punish the \x01@! clan, but sad that the raiders did not bring Blacktail back to his own pasture.
column2: 人们知道我们必须设法惩罚 \x01@! 氏族，但悲哀的是袭击者没有把黑尾带回他自己的牧场。

column1: Send warriors to kill Mordrim or his sons.
column2: 派遣战士去杀死莫德里姆或他的儿子们。

column1: Harnkorl Mordrimsson paid for his vile thievery with his life.
column2: 哈恩科尔·莫德里姆森以性命偿还了他那卑劣的盗窃行为。

column1: The Mordrimssons were not brought to justice.
column2: 莫德里姆森家族没有被绳之以法。

column1: Try to steal back the bull.
column2: 试着把牛偷回来。

column1: We met robbery with robbery, and sent a few fleet-footed warriors who reclaimed Blacktail in the dead of night.
column2: 我们以劫还劫，派出几个脚快的战士，在深夜夺回了黑尾。

column1: We sent fleet-footed warriors to reclaim Blacktail in the dead of night. Alas, they broke into the wrong corral, and we lost one of our men in the ensuing brawl.
column2: 我们派出脚快的战士在深夜夺回黑尾。唉，他们闯错了畜栏，在随后发生的斗殴中我们损失了一个人。

column1: Seeking to meet robbery with robbery, we sent men to steal Blacktail back. But our knack for thievery was found wanting, and we failed to recover the blessed beast.
column2: 试图以劫还劫，我们派人去把黑尾偷回来。但我们的偷窃本事捉襟见肘，未能找回这头被祝福的牲口。

column1: It is possible that this theft will adversely affect the strength of our herd.
column2: 这次盗窃有可能对我们畜群的强壮造成不利影响。

column1: Blacktail is as essential to the strength of our herd as ever. We must get him back!
column2: 黑尾对我们畜群的力量依然至关重要。我们必须把他弄回来！

column1: The theft of cattle is a grave offense.
column2: 偷牛是严重的罪行。

column1: The theft of cattle is a grave offense. We must appeal to Orlanth’s justice.
column2: 偷牛是严重的罪行。我们必须诉诸奥兰斯的正义。

column1: We can’t go raiding during planting season!
column2: 我们不能在播种季节发动袭击！

column1: If we raid during the planting season, our crops will suffer.
column2: 如果在播种季节袭击，我们的庄稼会遭殃。

column1: We can’t go raiding during the harvest!
column2: 我们不能在收获季节发动袭击！

column1: If we raid during the harvest, we will leave grain in the fields.
column2: 如果在收获季节袭击，我们会把谷物留在田里。

column1: Mordrim needs to be taught a lesson, one that can only be taught by pounding hooves and slashing swords.
column2: 莫德里姆需要被教训一顿，而那种教训只能用铁蹄和利剑来传授。

column1: It was after the minions of Emperor Yelm stole cattle from Orlanth that Orlanth first attended the Emperor’s Court and protested Yelm’s misrule.
column2: 正是在皇帝耶尔姆的爪牙偷了奥兰斯的牛之后，奥兰斯才首次前往皇帝的宫廷，抗议耶尔姆的暴政。

column1: Inaction is sometimes the strongest action of all.
column2: 不作为有时是最强有力的作为。

column1: Mordrim, who bought the bull Blacktail, returned to seek the return of his goods, because the bull had died.
column2: 买下黑尾公牛的莫德里姆回来要求归还他的货物，因为那头公牛死了。

column1: Offer another bull.
column2: 提供另一头公牛。

column1: We offered him another bull in exchange for Blacktail.
column2: 我们给了他另一头公牛来交换黑尾。

column1: After lengthy discussions, Mordrim finally acquiesced and took the bull home with him.
column2: 经过漫长的讨论，莫德里姆终于默许了，牵着那头牛回了家。

column1: After lengthy bargaining, Mordrim convinced us to give him \x01@\x0E bulls as compensation.
column2: 经过漫长的议价，莫德里姆说服我们给他 \x01@\x0E 头公牛作为补偿。

column1: Refuse this claim.
column2: 拒绝这个要求。

column1: We refused his claim, and he left bitterly protesting our “unholy disregard for justice.”
column2: 我们拒绝了他的要求，他愤然离去，指责我们“不敬神明地藐视正义”。

column1: He left bitterly protesting our “unholy disregard for justice.”
column2: 他愤然离去，指责我们“不敬神明地藐视正义”。

column1: Return all his goods.
column2: 归还他所有的货物。

column1: We did as he asked.
column2: 我们照他说的做了。

column1: Mordrim claims he will speak widely of your justice.
column2: 莫德里姆声称他会四处宣扬你的公正。

column1: Return half his goods.
column2: 归还他一半的货物。

column1: We suggested that both clans should share the burden of Blacktail’s death evenly.
column2: 我们提议两个氏族应共同分担黑尾之死的损失。

column1: After lengthy discussions, Mordrim conceded the merit of this proposal.
column2: 经过漫长的讨论，莫德里姆承认了这项提议的合理性。

column1: Mordrim left with half of what he had paid, though he made it clear he was unsatisfied with the arrangement.
column2: 莫德里姆带着他支付的一半货物离开了，尽管他明确表示对这个安排并不满意。

column1: It’s difficult to say whether or not Blacktail was healthy when we sold him.
column2: 很难说我们卖掉黑尾时他是否健康。

column1: Two seasons is a long time for a disease to appear. I think Mordrim let Blacktail get sick.
column2: 两个季节才出现疾病，时间太长了。我认为是莫德里姆让黑尾生病的。

column1: Blacktail was definitely healthy when he left our care.
column2: 黑尾离开我们照料时绝对健康。

column1: Mordrim is a difficult man. It will be hard to convince him that he deserves less than he asks.
column2: 莫德里姆是个难缠的人。很难说服他接受比他要求的更少的东西。

column1: If Blacktail was healthy when he left our possession, Mordrim has no case against us.
column2: 如果黑尾离开我们时是健康的，莫德里姆就无权向我们索赔。

column1: Mordrim is pursuing his claim with such vigor because he thinks we overcharged in the first place.
column2: 莫德里姆如此卖力地追索他的要求，是因为他一开始就觉得我们收费太高了。

column1: I knew we were making a mistake in selling Blacktail.
column2: 我早知道卖掉黑尾是个错误。

column1: By Uralda’s soothing teats! Surely we are not going to reward this prattling bucket of fat for killing our prize bull!
column2: 凭乌拉尔达那安抚人心的乳头！我们肯定不该奖励这头喋喋不休的肥猪，就因为他杀了我们的宝贝公牛！

column1: This is a petty matter. The crimson stench of Chaos pollutes our land.
column2: 这是件小事。混沌那猩红的恶臭正在玷污我们的土地。

column1: scene009
column2: scene009

column1: or a bull calf sired by Blacktail?
column2: 还是一头黑尾所生的公牛犊？

column1: a bull calf sired by Blacktail, or a shrine to Uralda built at his expense?
column2: 一头黑尾所生的公牛犊，还是由他出资建造一座乌拉尔达的神坛？

column1: Mordrim the Stout returned and offered us our choice of gifts. He considered himself indebted to us, because we gave him Blacktail the bull.
column2: 壮汉莫德里姆回来了，让我们选择礼物。他认为自己亏欠我们，因为我们给了他黑尾公牛。

column1: Accept his offer to build a shrine to Uralda.
column2: 接受他建造乌拉尔达神坛的提议。

column1: Devoutly, Mordrim offered to buy us a shrine to Uralda, and we accepted.
column2: 虔诚地，莫德里姆主动提出给我们建造一座乌拉尔达的神坛，我们接受了。

column1: Mordrim’s thanks helped us please the Cow Mother, and what pleases the Cow Mother pleases the herders.
column2: 莫德里姆的感谢帮助我们取悦了母牛女神，而取悦母牛女神也就取悦了牧人们。

column1: Accept the bull calf.
column2: 接受那头公牛犊。

column1: We accepted a bull calf sired by Blacktail, and hope that one day he will prove Blacktail’s equal.
column2: 我们接受了一头黑尾所生的公牛犊，希望有一天他能证明自己与黑尾不相上下。

column1: The son’s tail was already as black as his father’s.
column2: 这头儿子的尾巴已经黑得像它父亲一样了。

column1: Accept the selection of goods.
column2: 接受那批货物。

column1: We took the assortment of goods.
column2: 我们收下了那批杂货。

column1: The carls and cottars thanked the ring for making such a generous friend.
column2: 自由民和佃农感谢长老会结交了如此慷慨的朋友。

column1: Accept the sword.
column2: 接受那把剑。

column1: We accepted the legendary sword, Thanestriker.
column2: 我们接受了那把传奇之剑——领主杀手。

column1: Our warriors said that wielding Thanestriker was like fighting with an extra sword, and an invisible shield, and the strength of a bull.
column2: 我们的战士说，挥舞领主杀手就像是多了一把剑、一面看不见的盾牌，还有一头公牛的力量。

column1: Ask for Blacktail back instead.
column2: 改为要回黑尾。

column1: We instead asked him to give Blacktail back.
column2: 我们反而要求他把黑尾还回来。

column1: Mordrim’s ebullience turned to displeasure, and he left us soon afterwards.
column2: 莫德里姆的兴奋转为不悦，随后便离开了我们。

column1: Decline his offers; ask instead for a feast for your two clans.
column2: 拒绝他的提议；改为要求为你们两个氏族举办一场宴会。

column1: We instead asked for a great feast which both of our clans could share.
column2: 我们反而提出要举办一场盛大的宴会，让我们的两个氏族共同分享。

column1: Mordrim agreed, and at the feast, many songs were sung, and many flagons drained.
column2: 莫德里姆同意了，宴会上歌声不断，酒盏不绝。

column1: One thing led to another, and before the feast was over, we had concluded an alliance with the \x01@! clan.
column2: 事情一环扣一环，宴会还没结束，我们就与 \x01@! 氏族缔结了联盟。

column1: Our herd has suffered in Blacktail’s absence. It would be good to gain Blacktail’s scion, better to regain Blacktail.
column2: 黑尾不在，我们的畜群遭了殃。能得到黑尾的后代固然好，但能重新迎回黑尾就更好了。

column1: We have prospered, and so has Mordrim. We must show our gratitude to Uralda, the Cow Mother.
column2: 我们兴旺了，莫德里姆也是如此。我们必须向母牛女神乌拉尔达表达感激。

column1: He is impertinent not to offer us Blacktail back, with the luck our bull has given him.
column2: 他竟不把黑尾归还给我们，这是无礼——我们的公牛给他带来了好运。

column1: It would be shockingly improper to ask for the return of Blacktail, no matter how much we may regret our display of generosity.
column2: 开口索回黑尾将是极为失礼的，无论我们多么后悔当初展示慷慨。

column1: Let us propose a great feast to unite our clans, who have been at odds for far too long.
column2: 让我们提议举办一场盛大的宴会，联合我们这两个长久不和的氏族。

column1: The sword! The sword! Take the sword!
column2: 剑！剑！拿剑！

column1: Mordrim is generous. Too generous.
column2: 莫德里姆很慷慨。过于慷慨了。

column1: I know our warriors would be grateful if we chose the sword, but I believe his other offers are also good.
column2: 我知道如果我们选剑，我们的勇士会感激，但我认为他的其他提议也不错。

column1: He doesn’t have a sword called Chaos Striker, does he?
column2: 他没有一把叫“混沌打击者”的剑，对吧？

column1: This reminds me of the story called “Uralda and the Carl Who Gained by Giving Away.”
column2: 这让我想起一个故事，叫《乌拉尔达与因施予而获益的自由民》。

column1: Why are we even taking time discussing this? I already know exactly where that shrine can sit.
column2: 我们为什么还要花时间讨论这个？我早就知道那座神龛该安在哪儿了。

column1: Feast? Did someone say feast?
column2: 宴会？谁提到宴会了？

column1: If we take the selection of goods, we can share them among the people.
column2: 如果我们接受那批货物，就可以在族人中分享。

column1: Thanestriker is a marvelous treasure! He is most generous.
column2: 领主杀手是一件奇妙的宝物！他真是慷慨至极。

column1: Blacktail has bred true, we must take this calf into our herds!
column2: 黑尾的后代很纯正，我们必须把这头小牛纳入我们的畜群！

column1: Generosity is the way of kings.
column2: 慷慨是王者之道。

column1: We must not turn his generous offer into just another excuse for war.
column2: 我们不能把他的慷慨提议变成另一个开战的借口。

column1: The gods have rewarded our generosity.
column2: 众神回报了我们的慷慨。

column1: I confess I’m surprised. I never thought he would acknowledge our generosity so graciously.
column2: 我承认我很惊讶。我从没想过他会如此优雅地认可我们的慷慨。

column1: Why is he forcing us to choose? What a miser!
column2: 他凭什么逼我们选择？真是吝啬鬼！

column1: scene010
column2: scene010

column1: A big, bristly boar is wreaking havoc among your pigs, chasing the sows. If it mates with them, complain the carls, the offspring are wild, and the sows become skittish. The pig-tenders want you to do something about the boar problem.
column2: 一头又大又鬃毛粗硬的野猪正在你的猪群里肆虐，追逐着母猪。自由民们抱怨说，如果这野猪与母猪交配，生下的崽子会变野，母猪也会变得神经质。养猪人希望你解决野猪的问题。

column1: A large wild boar disturbed the pig-tenders, whose sows were sorely troubled by them.
column2: 一头大野猪搅得养猪人不得安宁，他们的母猪深受其扰。

column1: Assign some men to guard the pigs for the season.
column2: 指派一些人在这整个季节里看守猪群。

column1: Our stout warriors guarded the herd, and saved us from loss.
column2: 我们雄壮的勇士们守卫了畜群，使我们免遭损失。

column1: Compensate the farmers for their loss.
column2: 赔偿农夫们的损失。

column1: The pig-tenders were compensated by the clan ring.
column2: 氏族议会赔偿了养猪人。

column1: The pig-tenders were pleased, and praised our generosity.
column2: 养猪人很高兴，称赞了我们的慷慨。

column1: Hunt down the boar.
column2: 猎杀那头野猪。

column1: A great hunt for the boar was declared. A worthy opponent, it gored two of our men before it found a place of honor in our larder.
column2: 宣布对野猪进行一场大型狩猎。它是个值得一战的对手，在光荣地成为我们储藏室里的猎物之前，它捅伤了我们两个人。

column1: Our hunters tracked the boar for two days, but it seemed to realize it was being stalked, and would not allow them to close, even when they worked Odayla’s magics.
column2: 我们的猎人追踪了野猪两天，但它似乎意识到被跟踪了，即使猎人施展奥达伊拉的魔法，也不让他们靠近。

column1: Ignore the incident.
column2: 忽略此事。

column1: The carls complained that the ring was not concerned with their problems. The boar was spotted a few more times, but then didn’t return.
column2: 自由民们抱怨长老会不关心他们的问题。那头野猪又被目击了几次，但之后就再没出现过。

column1: If we didn’t let our pigs forage in the forest, they would never fatten.
column2: 如果我们不让猪在森林里觅食，它们永远长不肥。

column1: The farmers are discontented already. We must show them that their problems are our problems.
column2: 农夫们已经很不满了。我们必须让他们知道，他们的问题就是我们的问题。

column1: The carls haven’t been complaining too much lately. They can live with a few skittish sows.
column2: 自由民最近抱怨得不算太多。几只神经质的母猪他们还能忍受。

column1: Our warriors would surely relish the chance to guard pigs and chat with the carls.
column2: 我们的勇士们肯定很乐意有机会去守猪，和自由民们聊聊天。

column1: If we send our warriors to guard a herd of stinking pigs, they’ll mutiny. And I can’t say I’d blame them.
column2: 如果我们派勇士去守一群臭烘烘的猪，他们会哗变的。而且说句公道话，我也不怪他们。

column1: The boar is a fearsome beast; to hunt it would be sport, indeed!
column2: 野猪是可怕的猛兽；猎杀它，确实是一项运动！

column1: This is a matter of no importance. The rancid breath of Chaos rolls like fog across our land.
column2: 此事无关紧要。混沌的腐臭气息像雾一样翻滚在我们的土地上。

column1: When Orlanth was a babe, he wrestled twin boars sent by giants to vex him.
column2: 奥兰斯还小的时候，就摔跤过巨人派来折磨他的双生野猪。

column1: We can’t afford to compensate every carl who suffers a minor loss. Without a strong central treasury, we are without authority.
column2: 我们赔不起每一个遭受微小损失的农夫。没有强大的中央金库，我们就毫无权威。

column1: Some of us don’t care about the sows, do we? But if it was the warrior’s stallions being violated, we’d see a much different attitude.
column2: 我们中有些人根本不在乎那些母猪，是吧？但如果是勇士们的种马被糟蹋了，那态度可就大不一样了。

column1: Didn’t I warn you all that this would happen?
column2: 我不是警告过你们这会出事吗？

column1: I wonder if this could be the famous Blue Boar of legend…
column2: 我在想，这会不会是传说中的著名蓝野猪……

column1: scene011
column2: scene011

column1: A family of travelers petitions you, seeking membership in your clan. The father, \x01B5, speaks on behalf of the others. His family made the dangerous trek from Esrolia, in search of freedom and prosperity. So far, they have found only misery. \x01B5 promises hard work and loyalty in return for your generosity.
column2: 一家旅行者前来请求，寻求加入我们氏族。父亲 \x01B5代表其他人发言。他的家人从遥远的埃斯罗利亚一路艰难跋涉，寻求自由与繁荣。但迄今为止，他们只找到了苦难。 \x01B5 承诺以辛勤工作和忠诚回报你的慷慨。

column1: \x01B5 and his family came from distant Esrolia, to ask for membership in our clan.
column2: \x01B5 和他的家人从遥远的埃斯罗利亚来，请求加入我们氏族。

column1: MightBeSad
column2: MightBeSad

column1: Accept them as cottars.
column2: 接纳他们为佃农。

column1: We adopted them as tenders of sheep.
column2: 我们收养了他们作为牧羊人。

column1: Although \x01B5 looks disappointed, he thanks you politely for adopting his family.
column2: 尽管 \x01B5 面露失望，但他仍礼貌地感谢您接纳了他的家族。

column1: Assign them fine land and a starter herd.
column2: 赐予他们良田与起始畜群。

column1: We accepted them, and on that day they became \x01@".
column2: 我们接纳了他们，从那天起，他们便成了 \x01@"。

column1: “Thank you! We will speak forever of your generosity. I only hope we can live up to the high standards of our new clan.”
column2: “感谢您！我们将永远传颂您的慷慨。我只希望我们能不负新氏族的高标准。”

column1: Assign them some land.
column2: 分给他们一些土地。

column1: Force them to be thralls.
column2: 强迫他们为奴。

column1: We took them as thralls.
column2: 我们将他们收为奴隶。

column1: \x01B5 says nothing, but gives the members of the ring a look of resigned despair.
column2: \x01B5 一言不发，只是向长老会成员投去一个认命绝望的眼神。

column1: Shocked by the ring’s decision to turn the petitioners into thralls, \x01@\x0F resigns from the council in protest. Many rank-and-file carls and warriors speak out to support \x04 stand.
column2: 震惊于长老会将请愿者贬为奴隶的决定， \x01@\x0F 愤而辞去议会职务以示抗议。许多普通自由民与武士公开声援 \x04 的立场。

column1: Shocked by the ring’s decision, \x01@\x0F resigned from the council in protest. Many rank-and-file carls and warriors spoke out to support \x04 stand.
column2: 震惊于长老会的决定， \x01@\x0F 辞去议会职务以示抗议。许多普通自由民与武士曾公开声援 \x04 的立场。

column1: Shocked by the ring’s decision to turn the petitioners into thralls, \x01@\x03 resigns from the council in protest. Many rank-and-file carls and warriors speak out to support \x04 stand.
column2: 震惊于长老会将请愿者贬为奴隶的决定， \x01@\x03 愤而辞去议会职务以示抗议。许多普通自由民与武士公开声援 \x04 的立场。

column1: Shocked by the ring’s decision, \x01@\x03 resigned from the council in protest. Many rank-and-file carls and warriors spoke out to support \x04 stand.
column2: 震惊于长老会的决定， \x01@\x03 辞去议会职务以示抗议。许多普通自由民与武士曾公开声援 \x04 的立场。

column1: \x01B5 says nothing, but gives the members of the ring a look which is hard to meet.
column2: \x01B5 一言不发，只是向长老会成员投去一个令人难以直视的眼神。

column1: \x01B5 looks disappointed, but thanks you for the introduction.
column2: \x01B5 面露失望，但感谢您的引见。

column1: After careful deliberation, we regretfully turned down their petition.
column2: 经过慎重商议，我们遗憾地拒绝了他们的请求。

column1: The people wondered why we didn’t just take them as thralls.
column2: 人们疑惑我们为何不干脆将他们收为奴隶。

column1: The people wondered why we didn’t just adopt them as cottars.
column2: 人们疑惑我们为何不干脆将他们收为佃农。

column1: Although it would be virtuous to help them, we don’t have enough cows to support the clan as it is.
column2: 尽管帮助他们本是善举，但我们现有的牛只已不足以供养整个氏族。

column1: Our herds prosper; we can afford to give them a starter herd, should we wish to welcome \x01B5’s family.
column2: 我们的畜群兴旺；若我们愿意接纳 \x01B5的家族，完全可以赐予他们一份起始畜群。

column1: They are at our mercy. Take them as thralls, and force them to serve us.
column2: 他们任我们处置。收为奴隶，迫其效命于我们。

column1: We are not obligated to accept them, but we must treat them with justice while they are here.
column2: 我们没有义务接纳他们，但他们在此期间，我们必须予以公正对待。

column1: If we wish to help them without offending our long-suffering carls, we can make them cottars.
column2: 若我们想帮助他们又不触怒长期受苦的自由民，可以将他们收为佃农。

column1: Hard work? Loyalty? Good! We need more thralls!
column2: 勤劳？忠诚？好！我们需要更多奴隶！

column1: Our ancestors would have taken them as thralls.
column2: 我们的祖先定会将其收为奴隶。

column1: We have lost many children; our future is imperiled. Our clan needs new blood.
column2: 我们失去了众多子嗣；前途危在旦夕。氏族需要新鲜血脉。

column1: We have no special need to add to our clan.
column2: 我们没有特别的必要扩充氏族。

column1: The carls feel slighted already. If we give too much to these newcomers, they will protest.
column2: 自由民已感被怠慢。若我们给这些新来者太多，他们会抗议。

column1: They made it all the way from Esrolia alone? I don’t trust their story.
column2: 他们孤身从埃斯洛里亚一路走来？我不信他们的说辞。

column1: Look at how desperate they are. We will not sleep at night if we turn them away.
column2: 看看他们何等绝望。若将其拒之门外，我们将夜不能寐。

column1: Our temples need more worshippers; let them in.
column2: 我们的神殿需要更多信众；让他们进来。

column1: Good things come to those who are merciful.
column2: 仁慈之人终得善报。

column1: We don’t need more mouths to feed. We need more fists, to smite our enemies.
column2: 我们不需要更多张嘴吃饭。我们需要更多拳头来痛击敌人。

column1: Back in the Darkness, the ragged remnants of the Nalda Bin came to our ancestors, who adopted them into the clan.
column2: 在黑暗时代，纳尔达·宾的褴褛遗民来到先祖面前，先祖将他们收归氏族。

column1: Back in the Darkness, the ragged remnants of the Nalda Bin came to our ancestors, who took them as thralls.
column2: 在黑暗时代，纳尔达·宾的褴褛遗民来到先祖面前，先祖将他们收为奴隶。

column1: scene012
column2: scene012

column1: \x01B6, a young, energetic farmer, on the road to prosperity, asks the clan council for help. He claims that his stead is haunted. Objects move about. Wailing noises come from nowhere. \x01B6’s wife and child have even seen an apparition.
column2: \x01B6一位朝气蓬勃的年轻农夫，正走在致富之路上，向氏族议会求助。他声称自己的农庄闹鬼。物件自行移动。莫名传来哭嚎声。 \x01B6的妻子与孩子甚至见到了鬼影。

column1: The young farmer \x01B6 reported that his stead was haunted.
column2: 年轻农夫 \x01B6 报告说他的农庄闹鬼。

column1: Conduct a lawsuit against the ghost.
column2: 对幽灵提起诉讼。

column1: We filed suit against the ghost.
column2: 我们对幽灵提起了诉讼。

column1: Our lawspeaker charged it with unlawful trespass, and a juror ruled against the ghost, who was forced to depart.
column2: 我们的律法师以非法侵入罪指控它，一位陪审员裁定幽灵败诉，被迫离开。

column1: Our lawspeaker lost the case, and the stead was ceded to the ghost. \x01B6 was forced to move.
column2: 我们的律法师输了官司，农庄被判归幽灵所有。 \x01B6 被迫迁走。

column1: Launch a thorough investigation into the haunting.
column2: 对闹鬼事件展开彻底调查。

column1: Our priests and wise people went to the stead, spending many nights investigating the nature of the haunting.
column2: 我们的祭司与智者前往农庄，花费多个夜晚调查闹鬼的本质。

column1: Our priests and wise people went to the stead and began investigating the haunting. They said it could take a while to determine the nature of the spirit.
column2: 我们的祭司与智者前往农庄，开始调查闹鬼事件。他们称需要一些时间才能确定那灵体的本质。

column1: Order \x01B6 to move; burn down his stead.
column2: 命令 \x01B6 迁走；烧毁他的农庄。

column1: The ring ordered \x01B6 to move, and burned down the haunted stead.
column2: 长老会命令 \x01B6 迁走，并烧毁了闹鬼的农庄。

column1: \x01B6 agreed that this was a wise decision.
column2: \x01B6 同意这是明智的决定。

column1: \x01B6 complied, but didn’t seem pleased with this drastic measure.
column2: \x01B6 遵从了，但似乎对这种激烈措施并不满意。

column1: Recommend that \x01B6 move.
column2: 建议 \x01B6 迁走。

column1: The ring recommended that \x01B6 move to a new stead.
column2: 长老会建议 \x01B6 搬到新农庄。

column1: Not wishing to deal further with ghosts, he did so.
column2: 不愿再与幽灵纠缠，他照做了。

column1: \x01B6 did so, though he and others said they feared more trouble from the ghost.
column2: \x01B6 照做了，尽管他和其他人表示担心幽灵会带来更多麻烦。

column1: Send a devotee of Ernalda to bless \x01B6’s house.
column2: 派遣一位厄娜尔达的信徒去祝福 \x01B6的房屋。

column1: We sent \x01@\x05 to bless \x01B6’s stead.
column2: 我们派出 \x01@\x05 为 \x01B6的农庄祈福。

column1: The blessing of Ernalda, Queen of the Earth Goddesses, ended the hauntings.
column2: 大地女神女王厄娜尔达的祝福终结了萦绕的鬼祟。

column1: \x01@\x05 was seized by the ghost, and afterwards forgot some things she had previously known.
column2: \x01@\x05 被那幽灵攫住，之后忘掉了一些曾经知晓的事物。

column1: Send a devotee of Humakt to threaten the ghost.
column2: 派一位胡马克特的信徒去威胁那幽灵。

column1: We sent \x01@\x08 to scare the ghost away.
column2: 我们派出 \x01@\x08 去吓跑那幽灵。

column1: Afraid of Humakt’s wrath, the ghost ceased its hauntings.
column2: 因畏惧胡马克特的怒火，那幽灵停止了作祟。

column1: The ghost struck \x01@\x08 with a case of the shudders, which thereafter weakened \x04 grip when \x06 reached for \x04 sword.
column2: 幽灵降下一阵战栗击中 \x01@\x08 ，自此后 \x04 握剑伸手时 \x06 力道便弱了几分 \x04 。

column1: Send a devotee of Issaries to persuade the ghost to leave.
column2: 派一位伊萨里斯的信徒去说服那幽灵离开。

column1: We sent \x01@\t to bargain with the ghost.
column2: 我们派出 \x01@\t去与那幽灵议价。

column1: \x01@\t used silvered words to convince the ghost to leave.
column2: \x01@\t用甜言蜜语说服了那幽灵离开。

column1: \x01@\t was terribly shaken by the encounter, and was not the same for a long time afterwards.
column2: \x01@\t被这次遭遇狠狠动摇，此后很长一段时间都不复从前。

column1: Bargaining with a ghost is unusual, but I don’t see why it would be any more difficult than bargaining with the living.
column2: 与幽灵议价虽不寻常，但我不见得多难，比之与活人讨价还价。

column1: I don’t know what a ghost would want from us; how can I then bargain with one?
column2: 我不知那幽灵想要些什么；那我又如何与它议价？

column1: None of Heort’s Laws obligate us to aid the victim of a haunting.
column2: 赫尔特法令并无哪条要求我们援助被鬼祟所害之人。

column1: Horvator Farsee once conducted a case against a spirit, so there may be precedents for outlawing the ghost.
column2: 远视者霍瓦托曾办理过一起针对灵体的案讼，因此可能有剥夺幽灵法权的先例。

column1: Exorcism is not a specialty of the gods we worship. We must improvise a solution.
column2: 驱魔并非我们所信奉神祇的专长。我们必须临机应变，想个办法。

column1: My mistress, Ernalda, is leader of the female gods. Perhaps, through her, we could seek the aid of Ty Kora Tek, Goddess of the Dead.
column2: 我的女主人厄娜尔达是众女神之首。或许，通过她，我们能求得死亡女神泰·科拉·特克的协助。

column1: My lord Humakt despises ghosts, who flout the line between life and death. Let me banish this revenant.
column2: 我的主人胡马克特憎恶那些模糊生死界限的幽灵。让我来驱逐这亡者吧。

column1: \x01B6 must have forgotten the name of one of his ancestors. Let us make sport of his foolishness.
column2: \x01B6 一定是忘记了某位祖先的名讳。我们且拿他的愚行取笑一番吧。

column1: Most of our gods were dead, but brought back to life by Orlanth and the Lightbringers.
column2: 我们的大多数神明都已死去，但被奥兰斯和光明使者们带回了生命。

column1: We cannot risk contact with ghosts. Burn down the stead!
column2: 我们不能冒险触碰幽灵。烧掉那农庄！

column1: By Elmal’s fiery beard, we cannot let a mere will-o-the-wisp mock us in our very homes!
column2: 以埃尔玛尔炽燃的胡须起誓，我们岂能让区区一团鬼火就在自己家里嘲弄我们！

column1: \x01B6 reports that your attempt to exorcise the ghost is a failure. Now what do you do?
column2: \x01B6 报告称你试图驱魔之举已经失败。你现在作何打算？

column1: \x01B6 reported that the ghost was still haunting his stead.
column2: \x01B6 报告称那幽灵仍在它的农庄里作祟。

column1: Launch an investigation into the haunting.
column2: 对此次鬼祟事件发起调查。

column1: The ghost struck \x01@\x08 with a case of the shudders, which thereafter weakened his grip when he reached for his sword.
column2: 幽灵降下一阵战栗击中 \x01@\x08 ，自此后他握剑伸手时力道便弱了几分。

column1: This ghost is clearly malign. We have no hope of reconciling with it.
column2: 这幽灵分明恶毒。我们与它和解无望。

column1: It is dangerous, but I think I can talk the ghost into leaving.
column2: 虽有凶险，但我认为自己能说动那幽灵离开。

column1: This ghost is very powerful; it could do more harm to us if we continue to disturb it.
column2: 这幽灵极为强大；我们若继续搅扰它，恐会招致更甚的祸害。

column1: Who said the ghost was just an unhappy ancestor spirit? I didn’t say that.
column2: 谁说过那幽灵只是个不快的先祖灵魂？我可没这么说。

column1: The carls all fear that their steads are the next to be haunted.
column2: 自由民们都惶恐自家农庄会是下一个闹鬼之地。

column1: Ghosts are more than an ordinary problem. The carls will understand our failure.
column2: 幽灵之事非同寻常麻烦。自由民们会理解我们的失败的。

column1: This ghost is powerful. It has obviously been summoned up by a Chaos cultist, and threatens us all.
column2: 这幽灵力量强大。它显然是某个混沌信徒召唤而来的，正威胁着我们所有人。

column1: Surely, if our devotion to the gods is strong enough, they will send us the strength to banish the ghost.
column2: 诚然，若我们对神祇的虔诚足够坚定，他们自会赐予我们驱逐这幽灵的力量。

column1: When the Great Darkness came, all seemed lost. But Orlanth fought on.
column2: 当大黑暗降临时，一切似乎都无可挽回。但奥兰斯奋战不息。

column1: I knew the ghost would harm us if we tried to banish it.
column2: 我早知我们若试图驱逐，那幽灵定会加害于我们。

column1: Through trial and error, the wise people teach the ghost to communicate by knocking and rapping. It claims to be a spirit who served the Empire of Wyrm’s Friends. There are many such loose spirits trapped on this plane, it taps.
column2: 通过反复试错，智者教会那幽灵用敲击叩响来沟通。它自称曾效力于龙之友帝国的一位灵体。它叩击示意，像这样困于此界漂泊无依的灵体还有许多。

column1: We learned to speak to the ghost. It told us it had once served the dragons.
column2: 我们学会了与那幽灵交谈。它告诉我们它曾侍奉过龙族。

column1: Ask the spirit to leave; offer it two sheep.
column2: 请求那灵体离开；献上两只羊。

column1: We offered to sacrifice two sheep to the spirit if it would leave us alone.
column2: 我们提出若那灵体肯离开，便献祭两只羊给它。

column1: It agreed to our offer.
column2: 它同意了我们的提议。

column1: Instead, it slew one of our horses, and galloped away on our charger’s spirit.
column2: 它却转而杀死我们一匹马，然后骑乘着我们战马的精魂疾驰而去。

column1: Ask the spirit to leave; offer it magical power.
column2: 请求那灵体离开；献上魔法力量。

column1: We offered it some of our magic as a parting gift. We conducted a ritual of exchange.
column2: 我们拿出一部分魔法作为临别赠礼献给那灵体。我们举行了一场交换仪式。

column1: It accepted our offer, and the hauntings ceased.
column2: 它接受了我们的献礼，鬼祟随之停止。

column1: During the ritual, it took more from us than we had offered. The hauntings stopped, however.
column2: 仪式期间，它从我们这里取走的比我们献上的更多。然而，鬼祟确实停了。

column1: Ask the spirit to stay on and serve the clan.
column2: 请求那灵体留下，为氏族效力。

column1: We asked the spirit to serve us, as once it had served the dragon empire.
column2: 我们请求那灵体效力于我们，如同它曾效力于龙之帝国一般。

column1: The spirit took offense at our offer, and left our tula rather than help us in any fashion.
column2: 那灵体被我们的请求触怒，就此离开我们的领地，未以任何方式帮助我们。

column1: How many sheep do you offer to sacrifice to it each year?
column2: 你每年愿献祭多少只羊给它？

column1: It agreed, and bad magic became good magic.
column2: 它同意了，于是恶咒变成了吉兆。

column1: The spirit was offended by our offer.
column2: 那灵体被我们的献礼所触怒。

column1: It slew one of our horses, and galloped away on our charger’s spirit.
column2: 它杀死我们一匹马，然后骑乘着我们战马的精魂疾驰而去。

column1: It announced that it was unwilling to remain in a tula such as ours, and departed.
column2: 它宣称不愿留在此类领地中，便离去了。

column1: Banish it in the name of Ernalda.
column2: 以厄娜尔达之名将其驱逐。

column1: We attempted to banish the ghost in the name of Ernalda.
column2: 我们试图以厄娜尔达之名驱逐幽灵。

column1: Banish it in the name of Humakt.
column2: 以呼玛克特之名驱逐它。

column1: We attempted to banish the ghost in the name of Humakt.
column2: 我们曾试图以呼玛克特之名驱逐那鬼魂。

column1: Everyone knows that spirits are afraid of sheep.
column2: 谁都知道精魂怕羊。

column1: We could afford to sacrifice a sheep or two to it, if need be.
column2: 如有必要，我们还能献祭一两头羊给它。

column1: We don’t have enough sheep to waste one bribing a spirit. Our animals are too valuable to squander this way.
column2: 我们没有足够的羊可以浪费一头去贿赂精魂。我们的牲口太宝贵，不能这么挥霍。

column1: There’s no point having spent all this time in communication if we’re just going to try to banish it.
column2: 既然到头来还是要驱逐它，那花这么多时间沟通就毫无意义。

column1: It wants a home, and respect. If given these, it will ask but a token price.
column2: 它想要一个家，还有敬奉。只要给它这些，它只会要一个象征性的报酬。

column1: It wants a home, and respect. If given these, it will ask but a token price — two sheep a year, I think.
column2: 它想要一个家，还有敬奉。只要给它这些，它只会要一个象征性的报酬——每年两头羊，我想。

column1: We cannot trust this spirit. It served the dragon empire, and doubtless intends us harm.
column2: 我们不能信任这精魂。它曾效忠于龙之帝国，无疑是想加害我们。

column1: If this spirit was bound by the dragon friends, it must be powerful. We should ally with it.
column2: 如果这精魂曾被龙之友束缚过，它必然强大。我们应该与其结盟。

column1: What point is there in allying with a ghost? It can’t feed a cow, or plow a field.
column2: 与一个鬼魂结盟有什么用？它既不能喂牛，也不能耕田。

column1: The spirit can provide us with additional magic.
column2: 这精魂能为我们提供额外的魔法。

column1: The spirit can teach us magic, and may be helpful if we run into dragonewts.
column2: 这精魂能教我们魔法，如果我们碰到龙人，它或许能派上用场。

column1: Are we insane, tapping and rapping with a ghost? Any moment now, it will drag us off to the Underworld!
column2: 我们疯了吗，跟一个鬼魂敲敲打打交流？它随时会把我们拖入冥界！

column1: I told you we could learn much by investigating the ghost.
column2: 我告诉过你们，调查这鬼魂能学到很多东西。

column1: On the anniversary of its promise, the spirit in \x01B6’s stead gave us a gift of magic. It was pleased to receive the sheep we sacrificed to it, and promised to gift us each year as long as we remembered it.
column2: 在承诺周年之际， \x01B6农庄里的精魂赠予了我们一份魔法礼物。它乐于收下我们献祭给它的羊，并许诺只要我们记得它，每年都会赐予我们礼物。

column1: The spirit which had once haunted a stead didn’t answer when the god-talkers sacrificed its annual sheep. It looks like it won’t be sharing its luck with us again.
column2: 那个曾出没于农庄的精魂，在神言者献上年度羊祭时没有回应。看来它不会再与我们分享它的好运了。

column2: 我们使用强硬措辞，鼓励 \x01A` 停止对 \x01B=的不当骚扰。

column1: Both \x01B= and \x01A` are certain that they are right.

column1: Violence is always an option.

column1: Our men might be willing to fight against tough odds, but not for the sake of a few misplaced boundary stones.
column2: 我们的人或许愿意在艰难困境中战斗，但不会为了几块放错位置的界石而战。

column1: \x01B= is clearly in the wrong here.
column2: \x01B= 在此事中显然有错。

column1: \x01B= is clearly in the right here.
column2: \x01B= 在此事中显然有理。

column1: When the boundaries are not honored, it is hard to say who is in the right.

column1: It is difficult to say for certain, but something tells me that \x01B=’s claim is just.

column1: Boundaries, boundaries, it’s all the men argue about. All belongs to the Earth Mother.

column1: A plague of snakes came upon us, upsetting the cattle and frightening the children.

column1: Sacrifice a cow to Ernalda.

column1: The snakes went away.

column1: Sacrifice a cow to Eurmal.

column1: \x01@\x14 claimed all the credit, and everyone had to admit that \x06 did seem more confident afterwards.
column2: \x01@\x14 宣称揽下所有功劳，所有人都不得不承认 \x06 事后确实显得更加自信。

column1: Sacrifice a cow to Orlanth.
column2: 向奥兰瑟献祭一头牛。

column1: We sacrificed to Orlanth.
column2: 我们向奥兰瑟献祭。

column1: Snakes are dragon-kin, but what I Saw was much worse than this. My vision has failed.
column2: 蛇是龙裔，但我所见到的远比这更糟。我的视野已失效。

column1: Surely Eurmal can remove these pests.
column2: 尤尔马尔肯定能移除这些害虫。

column1: I don’t like having to heal snake bites. The most poisonous bites can’t be healed at all.
column2: 我不喜欢治疗蛇咬伤。最毒的咬伤根本无法治愈。

column1: Ernalda maintains dominion over snakes and other creatures that crawl upon the earth. We must petition her for relief from this plague.
column2: 厄尔纳尔达统治着蛇和其他在地上爬行的生物。我们必须向她祈求，以摆脱这场瘟疫。

column1: Orlanth is famed for slaying dragons. Snakes are like dragons. Honor Orlanth, and he will slay these snakes.
column2: 奥兰瑟以屠龙闻名。蛇就像龙。尊崇奥兰瑟，他会杀死这些蛇。

column1: The snake is a tricky creature, for you can’t tell its head from its tail. To beat a trickster, you must find a bigger trickster. Sacrifice a cow to Eurmal.
column2: 蛇是一种狡猾的生物，因为你分不清它的头和尾。要打败恶作剧者，你必须找一个更大的恶作剧者。向尤尔马尔献祭一头牛。

column1: Whatever you do, don’t listen to the trickster. The stories say that Ernalda protects us from snakes.
column2: 无论你做什么，都别听恶作剧者的。传说厄尔纳尔达保护我们免受蛇害。

column1: Don’t bother the gods. We can solve this problem by killing these pests ourselves.
column2: 别去打扰众神。我们可以自己杀死这些害虫来解决这个问题。

column1: These loathsome creatures have the wiggle of Chaos about them.
column2: 这些可憎的生物身上带有混沌的扭动。

column1: Elmal guarded Orlanth’s hearth when Orlanth slew dragons. Sacrifice to Orlanth.
column2: 埃尔玛在奥兰瑟屠龙时守护了奥兰瑟的炉灶。向奥兰瑟献祭。

column1: This will not be a good hunt.
column2: 这次狩猎不会顺利。

column1: Make them go away before they hurt the herds.
column2: 在它们伤害畜群之前让它们离开。

column1: These snakes may be just the beginning.
column2: 这些蛇可能只是个开始。

column1: If we caught and skinned these snakes, we could fashion their skins into decorative items, which we could trade for other useful items.
column2: 如果我们捕捉并剥下这些蛇的皮，我们可以将蛇皮制成装饰品，用以交换其他有用的物品。

column1: Orlanth once slew a snake which seemed to threaten Ernalda. She was vexed, for the serpent was a gift from her sisters.
column2: 奥兰瑟曾杀死一条似乎威胁到厄尔纳尔达的蛇。她很气恼，因为那条蛇是她姐妹的礼物。

column1: Agghh! I hate snakes!

column1: We shouldn’t squander cows on such a minor threat.
column2: 我们不应该在这种小威胁上浪费牛只。

column1: Whatever we do, we shouldn’t harm these kin of the dragons.
column2: 无论我们做什么，都不应该伤害这些龙之亲族。

column1: If we the had the Charm of the Seven Flowers, these snakes would be as tame and helpful as alynxes.
column2: 如果我们拥有七花护符，这些蛇就会像艾林克斯猫一样温顺有用。

column1: Trust the gods.
column2: 信任众神。

column1: Children will be killed if we don’t act quickly.

column1: A milk-white calf was born into Orendal’s herd.
column2: 一头乳白色牛犊诞生于奥伦达尔的牛群中。

column1: Let Orendal tend to the calf.

column2: 奥伦达尔留下了牛犊，我们的牛群增多了。自由民对长老会的决定感到满意。

column1: We sacrificed it to Orlanth, and gained his good fortune.
column2: 我们把它献祭给奥兰瑟，获得了他的好运。

column1: The priests said that Orlanth was well-pleased by our gift, and would gift us with good fortune in the weeks to come.
column2: 祭司们说奥兰瑟对我们的礼物非常满意，并将在未来几周赐予我们好运。

column1: Sacrifice the calf to Uralda, the Cow Mother.
column2: 向母牛女神乌拉尔达献祭这头牛犊。

column1: We sacrificed it to Uralda, and gained her blessing.
column2: 我们把它献祭给乌拉尔达，获得了她的祝福。

column1: The Uralda women said that the signs were very good, and that the Cow Mother had blessed our wisdom.
column2: 乌拉尔达的女人们说征兆非常好，母牛女神保佑了我们的智慧。

column1: Take the calf into the chief’s herds.
column2: 将牛犊纳入酋长的牛群。

column1: \x01@\x10 took the blessed beast into \x04 herds, gaining prestige. Our neighbors soon spoke of \x01@\x10 as the White Cow Chief.
column2: \x01@\x10 他将这头受祝福的牲畜纳入 \x04 牛群，赢得了声望。我们的邻居很快就称 \x01@\x10 为白牛酋长。

column1: Trade the calf to another clan.
column2: 将牛犊交易给另一个氏族。

column1: We traded the calf for \x01@\x0E cows.
column2: 我们用牛犊换取了 \x01@\x0E 头牛。

column1: White calves are sickly, and soon die.
column2: 白色牛犊体弱多病，很快就会死去。

column1: This is no ordinary calf. Whoever owns it gains great good fortune.
column2: 这可不是普通的牛犊。谁拥有它，谁就能获得巨大的好运。

column1: Orendal will understand if we take the calf from him.
column2: 如果我们从他那里拿走牛犊，奥伦达尔会理解的。

column1: Orendal wishes to seem generous, but does not want to give up the calf.
column2: 奥伦达尔希望显得慷慨，但并不想放弃牛犊。

column1: We can argue that it is Orendal’s duty to give up the calf, provided that the whole clan would benefit.
column2: 我们可以辩称，若整个氏族都能受益，奥伦达尔便有义务交出那头牛犊。

column1: The carls will dislike it if we confiscate Orendal’s calf.
column2: 若我们没收奥伦达尔的牛犊，自由民会心生不满。

column1: We could gain great magical benefits by sacrificing the cow.
column2: 献祭那头牛能为我们带来巨大的魔法收益。

column1: If we sacrifice the calf to Uralda, our herds will benefit. If we sacrifice it to Orlanth, our wisdom will be fortified.
column2: 若将牛犊献祭给乌拉尔达，我们的畜群将受益；若献祭给奥兰斯，我们的智慧将得以增强。

column1: When Uralda’s favorite calf wandered into the land of the dead, it turned white. When Ty Kora Tek returned it, Orlanth’s tribe rejoiced.
column2: 当乌拉尔达最珍爱的牛犊误入死者之地时，它变成了白色。泰·科拉·特克将它归还后，奥兰斯一族欢欣鼓舞。

column1: The calf is a gift from the gods. The gods will reward us if we repay their generosity by sacrificing it to them.
column2: 这头牛犊是众神的馈赠。若我们将其献祭以回报他们的慷慨，众神定会赐福于我们。

column1: The gods are mighty, and we are hungry. If we decide to keep the calf, they will not begrudge us.
column2: 众神威能无边，而我们却饥肠辘辘。若我们决定留下牛犊，他们不会责怪我们。

column1: Nobody told me that white calves were special. I could probably make one any time.
column2: 没人告诉过我白牛犊有什么特别。我大概随时都能弄出一头来。

column2: scene016

column1: Another season has passed without rain. Your once-green pastures are still brown.
column2: 又一个季节过去，依然无雨。你曾经翠绿的牧场依旧枯黄。

column1: Many weeks have passed without rain. Your once-green pastures are now brown.
column2: 许多星期过去，滴雨未下。你曾经翠绿的牧场现已枯黄。

column1: Your crops are dying. Starvation looms if the drought doesn’t end soon.
column2: 你的庄稼正在枯萎。若干旱不早日结束，饥荒就将逼近。

column1: Drought struck our lands. The spectre of starvation hovered over us.
column2: 干旱降临我们的土地。饥荒的幽灵在我们头顶盘旋。

column1: WoeAlasAlack
column2: WoeAlasAlack

column1: The ducks, whose wetlands suffered less from the drought, were induced to increase their tribute.
column2: 鸭人的湿地受干旱影响较轻，我们说服他们增加了贡品。

column1: Go raiding for extra food.
column2: 外出劫掠以获取额外食物。

column1: Who do you wish to raid?
column2: 你想劫掠谁？

column1: Make sacrifices to Heler.
column2: 向海勒尔献祭。

column1: How many cows do you want to sacrifice?
column2: 你打算献祭多少头牛？

column1: We sacrificed to Heler, but our pleas for help went unanswered.
column2: 我们向海勒尔献祭，但求助的恳求无人回应。

column1: Perform the Orlanth and Aroka ritual.
column2: 举行奥兰斯与阿罗卡仪式。

column1: We went with Orlanth to help him free Heler from the dragon’s maw.
column2: 我们随奥兰斯一同前往，助他将海勒尔从龙口解救出来。

column1: Enemies aided Daga and Aroka, and Heler remained imprisoned. Rain did not come.
column2: 敌人相助达加与阿罗卡，海勒尔仍被囚禁。雨水并未降临。

column1: Petition other clans for food aid.
column2: 向其他氏族请求粮食援助。

column1: We sought the help of others, but they said they too were afraid of the drought.
column2: 我们向他人求助，但他们说他们也畏惧干旱。

column1: They said they too were afraid of the drought.
column2: 他们说他们也畏惧干旱。

column1: Propitiate Daga, enemy god of Drought and Famine.
column2: 安抚达加——干旱与饥荒之神，我们的敌人。

column1: We sacrificed to Daga, the enemy god of Drought and Famine, hoping that he would show us mercy.
column2: 我们向达加献祭，这位干旱与饥荒的敌对之神，希望他能施以怜悯。

column1: Our priests had no experience dealing with Daga, and could not interpret the omens. We could only hope that he would show us mercy.
column2: 我们的祭司从未接触过达加，无法解读征兆。我们只能祈求他的怜悯。

column1: Wait out the drought.
column2: 耐心等待干旱过去。

column1: We were lucky, and the drought ended after one season.
column2: 我们运气不错，干旱仅持续一季便结束了。

column1: We tried to wait out the drought, but its patience exceeded ours. Suffering abounded.
column2: 我们试图熬过干旱，但它的耐心远胜于我们。苦难四起。

column1: We will lose one in ten of our cows if this drought doesn’t let up.
column2: 若干旱再不缓解，我们将失去十分之一的牛只。

column1: If the drought lasts \x02\x03too long/several seasons/more than a season\x02, we could lose \x02\x03a lot/a substantial part/half\x02 of our herd.
column2: 若干旱持续 \x02\x03太久/数个季节/超过一季\x02，我们可能失去 \x02\x03大量/相当一部分/半数\x02 的畜群。

column1: Better to sacrifice cows and end the drought, then to lose them slowly and watch them die pathetically.
column2: 与其眼睁睁看着牛只慢慢死去，不如献祭它们以终结干旱。

column1: The longer this continues, the fewer cattle we have available for sacrifice.
column2: 这种情况持续越久，我们能用于献祭的牛就越少。

column1: We have \x02\x03fewer and fewer/pitifully few/a sadly small amount\x02 of cattle to sacrifice. And those that are left are \x02\x04scrawny/dispirited/dull-eyed/sallow-skinned\x02 and hardly fit to go to the gods.
column2: 可供献祭的牛已 \x02\x03越来越少/少得可怜/数量可悲地少\x02 。而残存下来的那些也 \x02\x04瘦骨嶙峋/了无生气/目光呆滞/肤色蜡黄\x02 ，几乎不配献给众神。

column1: There is no law against raiding other clans when times are dire.
column2: 时局艰难时，劫掠其他氏族并不违法。

column1: There is no law against raiding other clans when times are dire, but we’ll \x02\x03also collect the permanent resentment/also bring home the long-lasting curses/earn the undying hatred\x02 of our victims if we do.
column2: 时局艰难时，劫掠其他氏族并不违法，但若我们这样做， \x02\x03也将招致永久的怨恨/也会带回长久的诅咒/会赢得受害者不死的仇恨\x02 。

column1: The drought will have the bellies of the \x01@! weaponthanes grumbling. If we strike before our own men are weakened, we will triumph.
column2: 干旱会让 \x01@! 武器领主的肚子咕咕叫。若我们在自己的战士衰弱之前出击，定能取胜。

column1: If you try to steal food from a starving enemy, you can expect a desperate struggle. My men know that, and fear it.
column2: 若想从饥饿的敌人那里偷取食物，就要做好拼死一战的准备。我的部下明白这点，并为此感到畏惧。

column1: Petitioning our allies solves the immediate food problem, but it does not end the drought.
column2: 向盟友求援能解决眼下的食物问题，但无法终结干旱。

column1: Our magic is strong. We should try sending a devotee of Orlanth on the heroquest of Orlanth Dragonslayer. That is the best way to stop this drought.
column2: 我们的魔法强大。应当派遣一位奥兰斯的信徒去完成奥兰斯屠龙者的英雄探索。这是终止干旱的最佳途径。

column1: Times are desperate. We must risk sending a devotee of Orlanth on the heroquest of Orlanth Dragonslayer, who freed the Rain God from Aroka’s belly.
column2: 时势危急。我们必须冒险派遣一位奥兰斯的信徒去完成奥兰斯屠龙者的英雄探索——正是他当年将雨神从阿罗卡腹中解救出来。

column1: Our magic is weak. If only we could risk performing the heroquest of Orlanth Dragonslayer! But, alas, failure would only add to our woes.
column2: 我们的魔法薄弱。若能冒险进行奥兰斯屠龙者的英雄探索该多好！但唉，失败只会雪上加霜。

column1: Once we \x02\x03end/solve/resolve\x02 this crisis, we should sacrifice to Orlanth to learn the secrets of his quest against Aroka.
column2: 一旦我们 \x02\x03终结/解决/化解\x02 这场危机，就应向奥兰斯献祭，以探知他对抗阿罗卡探索之旅的秘密。

column1: Droughts end by themselves. There is nothing we can do.
column2: 干旱自会结束。我们无能为力。

column1: We must petition Heler, God of Rain, to end our misery.
column2: 我们必须祈求雨神海勒尔终结我们的苦难。

column1: The carls want us to keep trying to end this drought — for there is no future for them if we fail.
column2: 自由民希望我们继续努力终结这场干旱——因为我们若失败，他们便没有未来。

column1: Though they \x02\x03are loathe to admit it/hate to bring it up/unhappy at the idea\x02, the carls wonder if these \x02\x03desperate/terrible/hard\x02 times don’t call for an \x02\x03risky/dangerous/unconventional\x02 solution.
column2: 尽管他们 \x02\x03不愿承认/讨厌提起/对此感到不悦\x02，自由民仍在思忖，这些 \x02\x03绝望/可怕/艰难\x02 的时代是否正需要一种 \x02\x03冒险/危险/非传统\x02 的解决之道。

column1: This is a time for our neighbors to show that they are generous, and thereby gain the blessings of Issaries.
column2: 此刻该让我们的邻人展现慷慨，从而赢得伊萨里斯的祝福。

column1: Heroquests are always the best solution in desperate times.
column2: 英雄任务向来是绝境中的最佳出路。

column1: Heroquests are the best way — how I wish we had enough magic to risk one.
column2: 英雄任务是最好的办法——我多希望我们有足够的魔法去冒险一试。

column1: It’s a shame we don’t know the secrets of the “Orlanth and Aroka” myth well enough to reenact it as a heroquest.
column2: 可惜我们对“奥兰斯与阿罗卡”神话的秘密了解不够，无法将其重演为英雄任务。

column1: We must have offended some god. Daga? Heler? Orlanth? Maybe even all three!
column2: 我们一定是触怒了某位神明。达加？赫勒？奥兰斯？甚至三者全得罪了！

column1: A large sacrifice to Heler is the only way — we should fear further drought, not losing cows to sacrifices.
column2: 向赫勒献上大祭是唯一出路——我们该恐惧的是持续干旱，而非献祭损失牛只。

column1: I will go \x02\x03into a cave/climb the highest tree/sit in the desert\x02 myself, and \x02\x03humble/mortify/abase\x02 myself before the gods to \x02\x03repent/apologize/atone\x02 for whatever sins brought this on the clan.
column2: 我将亲自 \x02\x03进入洞穴/爬上最高的树/坐在沙漠中\x02 ，在诸神面前 \x02\x03谦卑/苦修/贬抑\x02 己身，以 \x02\x03忏悔/道歉/赎罪\x02 那些给氏族招致此祸的罪愆。

column1: Surely this drought is caused by the cruel hand of slain Ragnaglar.
column2: 这场旱灾定是被杀死的拉格纳格拉那残忍的手所致。

column1: I would gladly risk performing the heroquest myself, if only to have something solid to fight.
column2: 我甘愿冒险亲自进行英雄任务，只为能有个实实在在的东西与之战斗。

column1: Give me \x02\x03a foe/an enemy/an adversary\x02 with substance to \x02\x03defeat/slash at/get my hands on\x02!
column2: 给我 \x02\x03一个切实的仇敌/敌人/对手\x02 ，让我 \x02\x03击败/砍杀/抓住\x02！

column1: Daga can send the dry wind to bury the land in dust, entombing everything in his path.
column2: 达加能遣来干风，将大地掩埋于尘土，葬送其路径上的一切。

column1: The cruelest thing is to see the cloud-wisps to the west, but none overhead.
column2: 最残酷之事莫过于西边可见云絮，头顶却一丝也无。

column1: I hate to suggest this, but perhaps we should sacrifice to the dread god Daga.
column2: 我厌恶提出此议，但或许我们应向可怖之神达加献祭。

column1: I guess \x02\x03we won’t laugh about this/we’ll have a cursing contest/the gods will laugh at us\x02 \x02\x03in the downpours of/when we get flooded/when everything is damp and soggy\x02 next Storm season.
column2: 我猜 \x02\x03我们不会为此发笑/我们将有一场咒骂比赛/诸神会嘲笑我们\x02 \x02\x03在下一个风暴季的倾盆大雨中/当我们被洪水淹没时/当一切潮湿泥泞时\x02 。

column1: We sacrificed to Heler, who broke the clouds and showered our lands with blessed rain.
column2: 我们向赫勒献祭，他驱散云层，将赐福之雨倾洒在我们的土地上。

column1: Orlanth triumphed. Freed, Heler broke the clouds and showered our lands with blessed rain.
column2: 奥兰斯获胜了。被释放的赫勒驱散云层，将赐福之雨倾洒在我们的土地上。

column1: We sought the help of other clans, and it was granted.
column2: 我们寻求了其他氏族的帮助，并且得到了应允。

column1: They granted our request.
column2: 他们应允了我们的请求。

column2: scene017

column1: The carls, represented by \x01BI the Restive, are unhappy. “The clan is trying to support too many weaponthanes, priests, and other folk who eat the food we produce but don’t produce any themselves. They’re parasites, I tell you, parasites!”
column2: 由 \x01BI 不安者代表，自由民表示不满。“氏族试图供养太多武器领主、祭司以及其他只吃我们产出的粮食、自己却不生产任何东西的人。他们是寄生虫，我跟你说，寄生虫！”

column1: A representative of the carls protested to the clan ring, stating that they were tired of supporting a great number of priests and weaponthanes.
column2: 一位自由民代表向氏族议会抗议，称他们厌倦了供养大量祭司和武器领主。

column1: Dismiss \x01@\x06 weaponthanes.
column2: 遣散 \x01@\x06 武器领主。

column1: We agreed that we had too many weaponthanes, and released some from our service.
column2: 我们同意武器领主过多，便解除了其中一些人的职务。

column1: Do you wish to give each dismissed warrior a cow worth of goods as compensation?
column2: 你是否愿意给每位被遣散的战士价值一头牛的财物作为补偿？

column1: Dismiss \x01@\r weaponthanes.
column2: 遣散 \x01@\r武器领主。

column1: We agreed that we had far too many weaponthanes, and severely pruned the ranks.
column2: 我们同意武器领主实在太多了，于是大幅削减了编制。

column1: Give the chief complainers a cow apiece.
column2: 给主要抱怨者每人一头牛。

column1: The petitioners were compensated for their grievances.
column2: 请愿者获得了怨情补偿。

column1: They ceased their grumbling.
column2: 他们停止了抱怨。

column1: Persuade \x01BI that he’s mistaken.
column2: 说服 \x01BI 他错了。

column1: Our chieftain spoke eloquently, and \x01BI left the hall.
column2: 我们的酋长口若悬河，然后 \x01BI 离开了大厅。

column1: Take the matter under advisement, then forget about it.
column2: 将此事纳入考虑，然后置之不理。

column1: The ring promised to consider their complaints.
column2: 长老会承诺会考虑他们的投诉。

column1: It’s true that we could use a few more hands in the fields, but \x01BI is really concerned with a long list of minor slights.
column2: 不错，田里的确需要多几双手，但 \x01BI 真正在意的是长长一串微不足道的冒犯。

column1: \x01BI is right. The weaponthanes are in danger of eating us into oblivion.
column2: \x01BI 说得对。武器领主有把我们吃光抹净的危险。

column1: We can afford to buy off these complainers.
column2: 我们有钱收买这些抱怨者。

column1: If we dismiss weaponthanes, we should at least give them parting gifts, and we can’t afford that right now.
column2: 如果我们遣散武器领主，至少该给他们离别赠礼，而我们现在负担不起。

column1: We brought the weaponthanes into the clan. We can’t summarily dismiss them because we overestimated our need for them.
column2: 我们曾把武器领主带进氏族。不能因为我们高估了对他们的需求就草率遣散他们。

column1: If we do dismiss any weaponthanes, we will have to compensate them.
column2: 如果我们真的遣散任何武器领主，就必须补偿他们。

column1: It is always difficult to balance the needs of the carls and those of the warriors.
column2: 平衡自由民与战士的需求向来艰难。

column1: I believe I can talk some sense into \x01BI, and get him to calm himself.
column2: 我相信我能说服 \x01BI明白事理，让他冷静下来。

column1: The warriors will be more than annoyed if they’re dismissed due to the bleatings of a few discontented dirt-diggers.
column2: 若因几个不满的挖土工的牢骚就被遣散，战士们会极其恼火。

column1: King Heort said, “When the carls and weaponthanes stop quarrelling, that is when you will know that the golden Storm Age has returned.”
column2: 赫奥特王曾说：“当自由民与武器领主停止争吵之时，你便知道黄金风暴时代回归了。”

column1: Carl or weaponthane, he has no right to complain! Let him go stuff a squash!
column2: 自由民也好，武器领主也罢，他无权抱怨！让他去塞满一个南瓜吧！
