column2: scene018

column1: \x01BJ, a man who moves with the confidence of an experienced warrior, applies for refuge in your clan. He is a proud warrior, and doesn’t like being reduced to begging for help, but he has little wish to be a bandit in the hills.
column2: \x01BJ一个步履间透露出久经沙场战士般自信的男人，向我们的氏族寻求庇护。他是个骄傲的战士，不愿沦落到乞求帮助，但也不愿成为山里的强盗。

column1: The warrior \x01BJ, outlawed from his clan, came to us for refuge.
column2: 这名战士 \x01BJ被他的氏族驱逐，前来投靠我们。

column1: IsItAdventure
column2: IsItAdventure

column1: Give him a place in the chief’s hall.
column2: 给他一个在酋长大厅中的席位。

column1: We gave him an honored place in the chief’s hall.
column2: 我们给了他一个酋长大厅中的尊贵席位。

column1: \x01BJ didn’t get along well with the other weaponthanes, but proved to be an able warrior.
column2: \x01BJ 与其他武器领主相处不睦，但证明了自己是一名能干的战士。

column1: Give him hospitality for the night, but send him on his way.
column2: 招待他过夜，但次日送他上路。

column1: We gave him hospitality, then sent him on his way
column2: 我们招待了他，然后送他上路。

column1: \x01BJ gave gruff thanks for your hospitality, but did not speak with anyone or acknowledge questions before he left.
column2: \x01BJ 粗声感谢了我们的招待，但在离开前没有与任何人交谈，也没有回应任何问话。

column1: Offer him quarters in the fort.
column2: 提供他在堡垒中的住处。

column1: We made him one of our weaponthanes.
column2: 我们让他成为我们的武器领主之一。

column1: \x01BJ proved to be an able warrior.
column2: \x01BJ 证明了自己是一名能干的战士。

column1: Recommend his services to an allied clan.
column2: 向一个盟族推荐他的服务。

column1: He stayed with them briefly, then drifted away to parts unknown.
column2: 他在那里短暂停留，然后飘然离去，去向不明。

column1: Send him packing.
column2: 赶他走。

column1: We denied his request.
column2: 我们拒绝了他的请求。

column1: \x01BJ wheeled and left with a curse.
column2: \x01BJ 转身离开，并咒骂着。

column1: The carls will worry that he’ll kill one of them, or seduce someone’s wife.
column2: 自由民们会担心他会杀死他们中的某个人，或者勾引某个人的妻子。

column1: It’s all well and good to prevent him from turning bandit, but we’re feeding enough warriors as it is.
column2: 防止他沦为强盗固然是好事，但我们已经有足够的战士要养活。

column1: We could use another reliable sword at the fort.
column2: 我们在堡垒里能用上另一把可靠的剑。

column1: I admit that we have enough weaponthanes, but this \x01BJ’s martial abilities are renowned.
column2: 我承认我们有足够的武器领主，但这位 \x01BJ的武艺声名远扬。

column1: We sorely need more fighters, and I have heard of this \x01BJ. We would be lucky to snare him.
column2: 我们急需更多的战士，而我听说过这位 \x01BJ。能网罗到他算是我们走运。

column1: We are neither obligated to help him, nor prohibited from doing so.
column2: 我们既没有义务帮助他，也不被禁止这么做。

column1: He was outlawed either for a killing, which may have been justified or not, or an act of adultery.
column2: 他被驱逐，或是因杀人（此事或许情有可原，抑或不然），或是因通奸。

column1: This is an opportunity to display our generosity.
column2: 这是彰显我们慷慨的机会。

column1: He’ll slit our throats in the night!
column2: 他会在夜里割断我们的喉咙！

column1: Everyone deserves a second chance.
column2: 每个人都值得第二次机会。

column1: If we do accept him, we must not treat him as a favorite, lest we offend those with a long record of loyalty to us.
column2: 如果我们接受他，绝不能厚待他，以免得罪那些长期忠于我们的人。

column1: Gordangar, who slew many of our ancient enemies during King Heort’s travails, was outlawed not once, but twice.
column2: 高登加尔在赫尔特王受难期间斩杀了众多我们的宿敌，但他被驱逐不是一次，而是两次。

column1: scene019
column2: scene019

column1: We found \x01@! hunters poaching deep within our territory.
column2: 我们发现 \x01@! 猎人在我们领土深处偷猎。

column1: Drive them off.
column2: 驱赶他们。

column1: We drove them off, warning them never to trespass again.
column2: 我们驱赶了他们，警告他们不得再越界。

column1: They fled, promising never to trespass again.
column2: 他们逃走了，承诺永不再犯。

column1: Initiate legal action.
column2: 提起法律诉讼。

column1: We launched a legal claim against them.
column2: 我们向他们提起了法律诉讼。

column1: Their chief ruled in our favor, and they were fined for their poaching.
column2: 他们的酋长做出了对我们有利的裁决，他们因偷猎被罚款。

column1: Their chief was deaf to the righteousness of our claim.
column2: 他们的酋长对我们诉讼的正当性充耳不闻。

column1: Their chief was deaf to our claim.
column2: 他们的酋长对我们的诉讼充耳不闻。

column1: They mocked us and pelted our emissary with dead mice. “Our feud is not ended, and yet you come squalling to us over a minor matter like this? Be glad we do not kill you today just for annoying us!”
column2: 他们嘲笑我们，并用死老鼠投掷我们的使者。“我们的世仇尚未了结，你们竟敢为这点小事跑来哭诉？庆幸我们今天没有因为你惹恼我们而杀了你！”

column1: They paid for their effrontery with their lives.
column2: 他们为自己的无礼付出了生命的代价。

column1: Offer to sell them hunting rights on your land.
column2: 提出向他们出售我们土地上的狩猎权。

column1: We offered their clan the chance to buy hunting rights on our land.
column2: 我们向他们的氏族提供了购买我们土地上狩猎权的机会。

column1: How many hunters from their clan do you allow on your tula?
column2: 你允许他们氏族有多少猎人进入你的图拉领地？

column1: How many cows per year do you ask in return?
column2: 你每年要求多少头牛作为回报？

column1: They agreed to our terms.
column2: 他们同意了我们的条件。

column1: They agreed to our terms, and promised to send the cows every Earth season.
column2: 他们同意了我们的条件，并承诺每个地季都送来牛只。

column1: “What!” they cried, “trade \x01@\x03 of our fine cattle for a few specimens of your mangy game?”
column2: “什么！”他们喊道，“拿我们 \x01@\x03 上好的牛只换你们几只癞皮猎物？”

column1: And so we could not reach a deal.
column2: 于是我们未能达成协议。

column1: They bargained skillfully, and we reached a deal. Some of the hunters grumbled that we’d lessened the clan reputation by accepting only \x01BM cows in exchange for letting \x01@\x18 \x01@! hunters “tramp on our land and scare off our game.”
column2: 他们巧妙议价，我们达成了协议。一些猎人抱怨说，我们只接受了 \x01BM 头牛，就允许 \x01@\x18 \x01@! 个猎人“在我们的土地上乱踩，吓跑我们的猎物”，这降低了氏族声誉。

column1: Their trader was surprisingly skillful. We reached a deal but some of the hunters grumbled that we’d gotten the short end of the stick. “\x01BM cows? When we will have to put up with the \x01@! folk tramping in our forest!” they complained.
column2: 他们的商人出奇地精明。我们达成了协议，但一些猎人抱怨我们吃了亏。“\x01BM 头牛？就为了忍受那 \x01@! 人在我们的森林里乱踩！”他们抱怨道。

column1: Treat them as guests.
column2: 以宾客之礼相待。

column1: To demonstrate our generosity, we provided them with food, drink, and song.
column2: 为彰显我们的慷慨，我们提供了食物、饮品和歌舞。

column1: At first they were despondent, thinking we would kill them since our clans were feuding. After we gave them food and drink, though, they cheered up enough to toast our hospitality.
column2: 起初他们垂头丧气，以为我们会杀了他们，因为我们的氏族之间有世仇。但给了他们食物和饮品后，他们高兴起来，足以举杯祝颂我们的好客。

column1: Some of the clan grumbled at feeding the enemy, but others praised our mercy and generosity.
column2: 氏族中有些人抱怨给敌人吃喝，但其他人赞扬了我们的仁慈与慷慨。

column1: They toasted our hospitality long into the night.
column2: 他们一整夜都在为我们的好客祝酒。

column1: The small game they have taken is no great loss to us.
column2: 他们猎取的小猎物对我们来说不是什么大损失。

column1: Game is scarce now. Every rabbit and pheasant is precious.
column2: 现在猎物稀少。每一只兔子和野鸡都很珍贵。

column1: The knocking knees of these hunters announces the poverty of their bargaining position.
column2: 这些猎人打颤的膝盖暴露了他们议价地位的贫弱。

column1: Is justice so important that we must injure ourselves by ignoring an opportunity to profit?
column2: 难道公义如此重要，以至于我们必须忽视获利机会而伤害自己吗？

column1: Alas, we have already sold hunting rights.
column2: 唉，我们已经卖掉了狩猎权。

column1: They are clearly in the wrong.
column2: 他们显然理亏。

column1: They are in the wrong, but their offense is not serious. We must not be too harsh.
column2: 他们理亏，但过错并不严重。我们不可过于严厉。

column1: Our relations with their clan are good.
column2: 我们与他们的氏族关系良好。

column1: Our relations with their clan could be better.
column2: 我们与他们的氏族关系不算太好。

column1: Their clan is less than friendly towards us.
column2: 他们的氏族对我们谈不上友好。

column1: Mercy is the food of the soul.
column2: 怜悯是灵魂的食粮。

column1: Forgiveness is overrated.
column2: 宽恕被高估了。

column1: They were careless of the boundary of our lands, but sometimes the hunt is too great a lure.
column2: 他们疏忽了我们领地的边界，但有时猎物诱惑太大。

column1: Let’s consider this a license to hunt on their lands whenever we feel like it.
column2: 就当作是我们随时可以进入他们领地狩猎的许可吧。

column1: This incident is good justification for a raid against their clan.
column2: 这起事件是我们对他们氏族发动突袭的绝好理由。

column1: The Bad Emperor was unjust to Orlanth when Orlanth took a few small birds from his garden. Orlanth was thus compelled to slay him.
column2: 恶皇帝对奥兰斯不公，只因奥兰斯从他园中取了几只小鸟。奥兰斯只得将其诛杀。

column1: scene020
column2: scene020

column1: The herds of another carl, \x01@\x15, are infested with evil, Chaotic broos. Everyone knows that the cattle must be destroyed before they give birth to more broos. What other measures do you take?
column2: 另一位卡尔的畜群 \x01@\x15被邪恶的混沌布鲁斯侵染。人人都知道必须在牛群生出更多布鲁斯之前将其销毁。你还采取其他什么措施？

column1: A herd of cattle was again infested by broos, and had to be destroyed.
column2: 一群牛再次被布鲁斯侵染，不得不销毁。

column1: The herds of the carl \x01@\x15 have been infested by the evil, Chaotic beings called broos. Everyone knows that the cattle must be destroyed before they give birth to more broos. What other measures do you take?
column2: 卡尔 \x01@\x15 的畜群被名为布鲁斯的邪恶混沌生物侵染。人人都知道必须在牛群生出更多布鲁斯之前将其销毁。你还采取其他什么措施？

column1: A herd of cattle was infested by broos, and had to be destroyed.
column2: 一群牛被布鲁斯侵染，不得不销毁。

column1: “It is sufficient to destroy the herd.”
column2: “销毁畜群就足够了。”

column1: Recruit weaponthanes from outside the clan; step up patrols.
column2: 从氏族外招募武器领主；加强巡逻。

column1: We sought more warriors, to protect us from the broo menace.
column2: 我们寻求更多战士，以保护我们免受布鲁斯威胁。

column1: How many warriors do you seek?
column2: 你寻求多少战士？

column1: Warriors we found.
column2: 我们找到了战士。

column1: We were able to recruit the warriors we sought.
column2: 我们成功招募到了所需的战士。

column1: Unfortunately, other clans had heard of the broo threat, and we found only a single available fighter.
column2: 不幸的是，其他氏族也听说了布鲁斯的威胁，我们只找到一名可用的战士。

column1: Seek help of nearby clans in fighting the broos.
column2: 向附近氏族寻求帮助，共同对抗布鲁斯。

column1: We sought to unite the clans to fight the broos.
column2: 我们试图联合各氏族对抗布鲁斯。

column1: We spread the risk among many, and the glory of victory as well.
column2: 我们将风险分摊给众人，胜利的荣耀也一同分享。

column1: The other clans agreed to share the risk, and the glory of victory as well.
column2: 其他氏族同意分担风险，也分享胜利的荣耀。

column1: We talked much, but accomplished little.
column2: 我们谈了很多，但收效甚微。

column1: Send a small party of warriors to search for broos.
column2: 派遣一小队战士搜索布鲁斯。

column1: How many weaponthanes do you send?
column2: 你派出多少武器领主？

column1: Who do you send to lead the party?
column2: 你派谁带领小队？

column1: We sent a small force to hunt for broos.
column2: 我们派出了一支小部队猎杀布鲁斯。

column1: We found the broos, and a terrible fight ensued. We lost several doughty weaponthanes, but the broos were exterminated.
column2: 我们找到了布鲁斯，一场恶战随之而来。我们损失了几名勇猛的武器领主，但布鲁斯被消灭了。

column1: The broos ambushed our war party, inflicting heavy losses before we were able to beat a safe retreat.
column2: 布鲁斯伏击了我们的战团，在我们安全撤退前造成了重大损失。

column1: Wage a concerted campaign against the broos.
column2: 发动一场联合行动对付布鲁斯。

column1: Our warriors set out to eradicate the broos.
column2: 我们的战士出发去消灭布鲁斯。

column1: We waited anxiously for their return.
column2: 我们焦急地等待他们归来。

column1: This is every herd owner’s worst fear. Everyone imagines himself in \x01@\x15’s position.
column2: 这是每个畜群主最害怕的事。每个人都设想自己处于 \x01@\x15的处境。

column1: Chaos is always a frightening foe, but our men know they must fight it.
column2: 混沌总是可怕的敌人，但我们的人知道必须与之战斗。

column1: We don’t have enough men to both defend our lands and send out a major expeditionary force.
column2: 我们没有足够的人手既保卫领地又派出大规模远征部队。

column1: I’ve been building our forces in preparation for a situation like this. Whatever you need, my men shall do.
column2: 我一直在扩充军力以备此类情况。无论你需要什么，我的人都会照办。

column1: We need more skilled fighters before we set out to kill broos. A small party may just get slaughtered.
column2: 我们需要更多熟练的战士才能出发去杀布鲁斯。一小队人可能只会被屠杀。

column1: We must wipe out these fiends, and rid our lands of them.
column2: 我们必须消灭这些恶魔，将我们的领地清除干净。

column1: More fighters won’t hurt in the campaign against the broos, but we can do it ourselves if we must.
column2: 在对抗布鲁斯的战役中，更多的战士不会有坏处，但必要时我们可以自己来。

column1: If we hire warriors and increase patrols we can kill the broos as they seek out our animals.
column2: 如果我们雇佣战士并加强巡逻，就能在布鲁斯寻找我们的牲畜时杀掉它们。

column1: Every chieftain has a stake in the fight against Chaos.
column2: 每位酋长在对抗混沌的战斗中都有利害关系。

column1: If we approach our neighbors, we can combine our efforts against the broos.
column2: 如果我们联络邻居，就能联手对抗布鲁斯。

column1: Although there is no worthier fight than the fight against Chaos, our neighbors hate us too much for an alliance to work.
column2: 尽管没有比对抗混沌更高尚的战斗，但我们的邻居对我们仇视太深，联盟难以奏效。

column1: Of course we have to destroy the herd. But we will lose more cattle to these monstrosities if we don’t strike them hard, and strike them soon.
column2: 我们当然必须销毁畜群。但如果不狠狠地、尽快地打击这些怪物，我们会失去更多牛只。

column1: It is not enough to destroy the infested cows — not enough by half! We must set out to eradicate all the broos in the area, or watch our herds become infested over and over.
column2: 仅仅销毁被感染的牛是不够的——远远不够！我们必须出发消灭这片区域所有布鲁斯，否则只能眼睁睁看着畜群一次次被侵染。

column1: We must keep trying to attract weaponthanes so that our patrols are thick and no broo dare penetrate our tula.
column2: 我们必须继续努力吸引武器领主，使我们的巡逻队密集，让任何布鲁斯都不敢侵入我们的领地。

column1: Our neighbors are in as much danger as we are. We must try again to convince them to join us and end this menace.
column2: 我们的邻居和我们处于同样危险之中。我们必须再次尝试说服他们加入我们，终结这一威胁。

column1: We must send a large party of fighters against the deadly broos this time.
column2: 这次我们必须派出一大群战士对抗致命的布鲁斯。

column1: We must keep trying and fighting until all the broos around here are gone.
column2: 我们必须不断尝试和战斗，直到这里的布鲁斯全部消失。

column1: Broos are dangerous opponents. If we engage them, we can expect some of our warriors to die hideous deaths.
column2: 布鲁斯是危险的对手。如果我们与其交战，可以预料一些战士会惨死。

column1: There is no conciliation with Chaos.
column2: 混沌绝无和解可言。

column1: If we fight the broos, they’ll send even more broos, and they’ll destroy us all.
column2: 如果我们与布鲁斯作战，他们会派来更多布鲁斯，然后把我们全部毁灭。

column1: I hope the other clans won’t blame us for the broos if we ask them for help.
column2: 我希望其他氏族不会因为我们有布鲁斯而责怪我们，如果我们向他们求助的话。

column1: Don’t send too many fighters away — they might get infested themselves. Then how would we fight the broos?
column2: 别派太多战士出去——他们自己可能被感染。到时我们怎么对抗布鲁斯？

column1: \x02\x03Kill the broos! Kill the broos!/Slay the broos and their Chaos minions!/Find broos! Slaughter broos!\x02
column2: \x02\x03杀光布鲁斯！杀光布鲁斯！/屠尽布鲁斯及其混沌爪牙！/找到布鲁斯！宰掉布鲁斯！\x02

column1: If we sacrificed more to the gods, the broos would strike elsewhere.
column2: 如果我们多向众神献祭，布鲁斯就会去别处作乱。

column1: Usually Chaos is caused by kinstrife, but sometimes it arrives on its own.
column2: 混沌通常源于族内纷争，但有时也会自行到来。

column1: Broos are cunning, but they have only one mission in their nasty lives — to make more broos.
column2: 布鲁斯很狡猾，但它们肮脏一生中只有一个使命——制造更多布鲁斯。

column1: Bad King Urgrain sold a herd of cattle to an ally, a herd he suspected was infested with broos. Then this ally attacked Bad King Urgrain’s tula, slaughtering many cattle, and was an ally no more.
column2: 恶王乌格兰卖了一群牛给一位盟友，他怀疑那群牛已被布鲁斯 infestation。随后这位盟友袭击了恶王乌格兰的图拉领地，屠杀了许多牛只，盟友也不再是盟友。

column1: For two seasons our warriors scoured the countryside, slaying broos wherever they found them.
column2: 整整两个季节，我们的武士扫荡乡野，所到之处布鲁斯尽数斩杀。

column1: Some of us lost our lives. All broos lost their lives.
column2: 我们有些人失去了性命。所有布鲁斯都失去了性命。

column1: We found that our lands were seething with these Chaos creatures. Many warriors were cruelly slain.
column2: 我们发现自己的土地上到处涌动着这些混沌生物。许多武士惨遭屠戮。

column1: scene021
column2: scene021

column1: A young shepherd reports another theft of several sheep by ragged-looking men. They are surely the outlaws who stole from us before.
column2: 一个年轻牧人报告说，几个衣衫褴褛的人又偷了几只羊。他们肯定就是之前偷过我们东西的流寇。

column1: Outlaws stole sheep from us again.
column2: 流寇又偷了我们的羊。

column1: A young shepherd reports the theft of several sheep. From his description of the ragged-looking men, they are surely outlaws, men stripped of the protection of their clans.
column2: 一个年轻牧人报告羊只被偷。从他描述的衣衫褴褛者的模样来看，他们肯定是流寇——被剥夺了氏族保护的人。

column1: Outlaws stole sheep from us.
column2: 流寇偷了我们的羊。

column1: Do nothing
column2: 按兵不动

column1: The shepherds reported that maybe the outlaws had gone away.
column2: 牧人们报告说，流寇也许已经离开了。

column1: Drive off the outlaws
column2: 驱逐流寇

column1: We gave chase, and drove them off.
column2: 我们追了上去，把他们赶走了。

column1: We chased them, but they were either long gone, or were better at hiding than we were at searching.
column2: 我们追过他们，但他们要么早已远遁，要么比我们更善于躲藏。

column1: Hunt down and kill the outlaws
column2: 追剿流寇

column1: Without pause, we pursued the criminals. Without mercy, we slew them.
column2: 我们毫不犹豫地追捕罪犯。毫不留情地将其斩杀。

column1: Pardon the outlaws, recruiting them as weaponthanes.
column2: 赦免流寇，招募他们为武器领主。

column1: Although the people did not strain themselves to run and welcome our new clan members, neither did they reject them.
column2: 尽管百姓并不热情奔放地迎接我们的新族人，但也没有排斥他们。

column1: The people tried to conceal their misgivings about our new clan members, but fell short of the mark.
column2: 百姓试图掩饰对新族人的疑虑，却没能完全藏住。

column1: Recompense the farmers
column2: 赔偿农夫

column1: The ring compensated the owners of the sheep.
column2: 长老会赔偿了羊的主人。

column1: The owners of the sheep thought this was only just.
column2: 羊的主人认为这很公正。

column1: The people are \x02\x04mistrustful/downcast/unhappy/dispirited\x02. Harsh punishment of \x02\x03the crime they most hate/these miscreants/for this loathsome crime\x02 might renew their confidence in us.
column2: 百姓感到 \x02\x04疑惧/沮丧/不快/消沉\x02。严惩 \x02\x03他们最憎恶的罪行/这些恶徒/这桩可憎的罪行\x02 或许能重拾他们对我们的信心。

column1: Better to steal sheep than cows or pigs.
column2: 偷羊总比偷牛或猪强。

column1: Even sheep losses get \x02\x03annoying/irritating/upsetting\x02 if they go on long enough.
column2: 即便是羊只损失，如果持续太久，也会变得 \x02\x03烦人/恼人/惹人心烦\x02 。

column1: I like wool as much as the next person, but sheep aren’t valuable enough to kill for.
column2: 我跟别人一样喜欢羊毛，但羊还不够珍贵到值得为此杀人。

column1: Bandits plague our trade routes. Let’s make an example of these ruffians.
column2: 匪徒祸害我们的商路。拿这些恶棍杀一儆百吧。

column1: Thieves start with something small, like sheep. Then they move on to larger targets.
column2: 小偷小摸从羊开始，然后就会盯上更大的目标。

column1: These ruffians might have asked for hospitality and offered their services. But they didn’t — they rustled our sheep instead.
column2: 这些恶棍原本可以请求款待并献上效力。但他们没有——他们偷了我们的羊。

column1: It’s harder than it sounds to catch a couple of outlaws in this terrain.
column2: 在这片地形上抓到几个流寇比听起来要难。

column1: I could bring these men to heel aided only by a child and armed only with a piece of straw.
column2: 我只需一个孩子和一根稻草就能让这些人服服帖帖。

column1: Since they’re outlaws, we could do anything we wanted with these men, stolen sheep or no stolen sheep.
column2: 既然他们是流寇，不管有没有偷羊，我们都可以对他们为所欲为。

column1: We could use a couple more men who know how to hold a weapon…
column2: 我们正需要几个懂得握武器的人……

column1: You have to be quite the miscreant to get outlawed from some of the rough clans of this frontier.
column2: 能在这边疆一些凶悍氏族中被逐出为流寇，想必是十足的恶徒。

column1: We warned them once. Now we will do what we must.
column2: 我们警告过他们一次。现在该做我们必须做的事了。

column1: We might stop this better with honey than with arms. We could always use a few more fighters.
column2: 用蜜糖而不是刀剑或许更能阻止此事。我们总是能多招几个战士。

column1: If we had the horses, we could hire them as weaponthanes, which we can always use a few more of.
column2: 如果我们有马，就能雇他们做武器领主——这种人我们总是用得上的。

column1: They’re not sprouting Chaos features, so who cares? Outlaws will be outlaws.
column2: 他们又没有长出混沌特征，谁在乎呢？流寇终归是流寇。

column1: I told you we needed to \x02\x03guard the sheep better/step up our patrols/keep our eye open\x02.
column2: 我告诉过你，我们得 \x02\x03把羊看紧些/加强巡逻/睁大眼睛\x02。

column1: I admire their \x02\x03nerve/spunk/pluck\x02!
column2: 我佩服他们的 \x02\x03胆量/勇气/血性\x02！

column1: scene022
column2: scene022

column1: A terrible storm from the far north descends on your land. The cattle are frost-bitten. This is no ordinary storm, but an assault by the forces of cold and darkness. Some of the carls think they saw ice demons hiding in the driving snow.
column2: 一场来自遥远北方的可怕风暴降临你的土地。牛只被冻伤。这不是普通的风暴，而是寒冷与黑暗势力的袭击。有些自由民认为他们看到了冰魔藏在飘扬的雪中。

column1: Since it is Fire season, this
column2: 由于现在是火之季，这

column1: Since it is Earth season, this
column2: 由于现在是地季，这

column1: This
column2: 这

column1: must be the result of your Summons of Evil ritual not long ago.
column2: 必定是不久前你举行召唤邪恶仪式的结果。

column1: The forces of cold and darkness attacked our land with snow and wind. Our herds were threatened.
column2: 寒冷与黑暗的势力以风雪侵袭了我们的土地。我们的牧群受到威胁。

column1: Gather Wind Lords from many clans to fight the ice demons
column2: 召集各氏族的风领主来对抗冰魔

column1: We sought the help of Orlanthi Wind Lords from many clans.
column2: 我们寻求了许多氏族的奥兰斯风领主帮助。

column1: The Wind Lords were driven back, and the demons left only when they wanted to. Our herds suffered serious losses.
column2: 风领主被击退，恶魔只在它们想离开时才离开。我们的牧群遭受了严重损失。

column1: Squabbling between the clans gave the ice demons time to do their worst. Our herds suffered terrible losses.
column2: 氏族之间的争吵给了冰魔时间造成最大破坏。我们的牧群遭受了可怕损失。

column1: Propitiate Valind, enemy god of Cold
column2: 向瓦林德——寒冷之敌神——献祭求恕

column1: We propitiated Valind, god of Cold.
column2: 我们向寒冷之神瓦林德献祭求恕。

column1: How many cows do you sacrifice to Valind?
column2: 你向瓦林德献祭多少头牛？

column1: The storm continued for a while, and Valind’s winds claimed more cows than we had offered him.
column2: 暴风雨持续了一段时间，瓦林德的风夺走的牛比我们献给他的还要多。

column1: Sacrifice to Orlanth
column2: 向奥兰斯献祭

column1: We called on Orlanth to help us against his ancient enemies.
column2: 我们呼唤奥兰斯帮助我们对抗他的宿敌。

column1: How many cows do you sacrifice to Orlanth?
column2: 你向奥兰斯献祭多少头牛？

column1: Some time after the sacrifices were made, the enemy storm lifted.
column2: 献祭过后不久，敌方的暴风雨散去了。

column1: Send a war party out to fight the ice demons
column2: 派出一支战团去对抗冰魔

column1: We assembled a party of warriors to fight the ice demons.
column2: 我们召集了一支勇士队伍去与冰魔作战。

column1: Desperately we fought them. We took terrible losses. The ice demons did not leave for a long time.
column2: 我们拼命与他们战斗。我们损失惨重。冰魔很久才离去。

column1: Wait out the storm
column2: 等待暴风雨结束

column1: We suffered greatly.
column2: 我们遭受了巨大的苦难。

column1: Ernalda warned us about this, and we have prepared.
column2: 厄娜尔达就此警告过我们，我们也做好了准备。

column1: Cattle are big and strong. They can take a little cold.
column2: 牛又大又壮。它们能忍受一点寒冷。

column1: If it is too cold for men, it is too cold for cows.
column2: 如果对人来说太冷，那对牛来说也太冷。

column1: We could lose a large number of cows if we do nothing.
column2: 如果我们不采取行动，可能会损失大量牛只。

column1: We should make a deal with who or whatever is causing this.
column2: 我们应该与造成这一切的人或物做交易。

column1: Although it may be tempting to deal with enemy gods, the people always suffer for it in the end.
column2: 尽管与敌对神祇做交易可能很诱人，但人民最终总会因此受苦。

column1: Demons can be slain, just like men. Give me a small force, and I will prove it to you.
column2: 恶魔是可以被杀死的，就像人一样。给我一支小部队，我会向你证明。

column1: I know how to fight men. I do not know how to fight demons.
column2: 我知道如何与人战斗。但不知道如何与恶魔战斗。

column1: We can win, but not alone. We need an elite force of Wind Lords, the best and holiest warriors of Orlanth.
column2: 我们能赢，但不能独自取胜。我们需要一支由风领主组成的精锐部队——奥兰斯最优秀、最圣洁的战士。

column1: The ice demons serve an enemy god. They do not recognize our laws.
column2: 冰魔侍奉一位敌对神祇。他们不承认我们的律法。

column1: Our ancient enemies, the servants of Valind, have returned to vex us. If we defeat them, we will be renewed in the magical ways of our clan.
column2: 我们古老的宿敌，瓦林德的仆从，又回来骚扰我们了。如果我们击败他们，我们氏族将在魔法之道上重获新生。

column1: This storm affects all of our neighbors, too. We should band together, for the common good.
column2: 这场暴风雨也影响了我们所有邻邦。为了共同的利益，我们应该团结起来。

column1: Our Summons of Evil ritual has brought them here so we can defeat them.
column2: 我们的“召唤邪恶”仪式将他们引到这里，这样我们就能击败他们。

column1: Orlanth fought the ice demons. We must sacrifice to him.
column2: 奥兰斯曾与冰魔战斗。我们必须向他献祭。

column1: Although the snows are bad now, they will later melt and provide water for our crops.
column2: 虽然现在雪灾严重，但日后冰雪融化会为我们的庄稼提供水源。

column1: Our clan has always fought against Valind and his ice demons, the hollri. We must beat them again.
column2: 我们氏族一直与瓦林德及其冰魔——霍利里——作战。我们必须再次击败他们。

column1: The ice demons are called hollri. They are very powerful servants of Valind, a glacial enemy god defeated by Orlanth in ancient times.
column2: 冰魔被称为霍利里。他们是瓦林德非常强大的仆从，瓦林德是一位冰川敌对神祇，远古时期被奥兰斯击败。

column1: “Ice melts, but water freezes.”
column2: “冰会融化，但水会冻结。”

column1: We cannot hope to defeat them alone.
column2: 我们不能指望独自击败他们。

column1: The solution where we stay the warmest is to ask Valind to call off his ice demons.
column2: 让我们保持最温暖的解决办法是请求瓦林德召回他的冰魔。

column1: Hollri in Sea season? Who would have thought?
column2: 海之季的霍利里？谁能想到？

column1: The ice demons were driven off before serious harm was done to the herd. Together the clans feasted to the defeat of Valind.
column2: 在牛群遭受严重伤害之前，冰魔被赶走了。各氏族共同欢宴，庆贺击败了瓦林德。

column1: The storm lifted, and the ice demons went away.
column2: 暴风雨散去了，冰魔也离开了。

column1: Soon after the sacrifices were made, the enemy storm lifted.
column2: 献祭过后不久，敌方的暴风雨散去了。

column1: Desperately we fought them. Ultimately we prevailed.
column2: 我们拼命与他们战斗。最终我们获胜了。

column1: scene023
column2: scene023

column1: The famed poet Ordangmar of clan \x01@! is your honored guest at a great feast. As he recites, most are enraptured by his satirical verse. But \x01BX, one of your thanes, looks angry. Perhaps he thinks that the “dung-daubed nobleman” of Ordangmar’s poem is meant to be him.
column2: 氏族 \x01@! 的著名诗人奥当马尔是您盛大宴会上的尊贵客人。当他吟诵时，大多数人都被他的讽刺诗句迷住了。但您的领主之一 \x01BX面露怒色。也许他认为奥当马尔诗中那个“粪污涂抹的贵族”指的是他。

column1: The famed poet Ordangmar was our honored guest at a great feast. All were enraptured by his poesy, except for \x01BX, who thought the poet defamed his honor.
column2: 著名诗人奥当马尔曾是我们盛大宴会上的尊贵客人。大家都被他的诗歌迷住了，除了 \x01BX，他认为诗人玷污了他的荣誉。

column1: Allow a duel between \x01BX and Ordangmar.
column2: 允许 \x01BX 与奥当马尔之间进行决斗。

column1: In a fair duel, Ordangmar struck a lucky blow against \x01BX, who was slain.
column2: 在一场公平的决斗中，奥当马尔对 \x01BX 幸运一击，后者被杀死。

column1: In a fair duel, \x01BX slew the great poet Ordangmar. Ordangmar was mourned throughout Heortling Dragon Pass.
column2: 在一场公平的决斗中， \x01BX 杀死了伟大的诗人奥当马尔。奥当马尔在整个赫奥特林龙隘地区被哀悼。

column1: Ask Ordangmar to apologize.
column2: 要求奥当马尔道歉。

column1: Ordangmar made it plain that he meant no offense to \x01BX. \x01BX toasted him many times, and paid him the compliment of learning one of his epics.
column2: 奥当马尔明确表示他无意冒犯 \x01BX。 \x01BX 多次向他祝酒，并学习了他的一首史诗以示敬意。

column1: Ordangmar said: “The verse didn’t pertain to \x01BX, but if a man smells dung about himself, he is surely right.”
column2: 奥当马尔说：“诗句并非针对 \x01BX，但如果一个人闻到自己身上有粪味，那他肯定是对的。”

column1: Convince \x01BX he isn’t the character in the poem.
column2: 说服 \x01BX 他不是诗中的角色。

column1: \x01BX refused to pardon what he saw as a certain affront.
column2: \x01BX 拒绝原谅他所认为的某次冒犯。

column1: Mind your own business.
column2: 别多管闲事。

column1: \x01BX proclaimed that he had been offended, and demanded satisfaction from the poet.
column2: \x01BX 宣称他受到了冒犯，并要求诗人满足（决斗）。

column1: \x01BX did not force the issue, so the feast was not marred.
column2: \x01BX 没有强行争论，因此宴会没有受损。

column1: Propose an arm-wrestling match between the two.
column2: 建议两人进行掰手腕比赛。

column1: We proposed that the two resolve their differences with an arm-wrestling match.
column2: 我们提议两人通过掰手腕比赛解决分歧。

column1: Ordangmar surprised all and sundry by defeating \x01BX in an arm-wrestling match. \x01BX toasted him many times, and paid him the compliment of learning one of his epics.
column2: 奥当马尔在掰手腕比赛中击败 \x01BX ，令所有人惊讶。 \x01BX 多次向他祝酒，并学习了他的一首史诗以示敬意。

column1: As expected, \x01BX easily bested Ordangmar. The poet disappointed many by leaving immediately, and vowing never to return.
column2: 不出所料， \x01BX 轻易战胜了奥当马尔。诗人立即离开并发誓永不回来，令许多人失望。

column1: Ordangmar would not deign to participate. He disappointed many by leaving immediately, vowing never to return.
column2: 奥当马尔不屑于参加。他立即离开，并发誓永不回来，令许多人失望。

column1: Ordangmar is tougher than he looks; he could kill \x01BX.
column2: 奥当马尔比他看上去更强悍；他能杀掉 \x01BX。

column1: \x01BX is a fierce and determined battler, especially in a one-on-one fight.
column2: \x01BX 是一位凶悍果决的斗士，尤其擅长单打独斗。

column1: From his verses of battle, you can tell Ordangmar has never been in a real fight.
column2: 从他那些战斗诗句可以看出，奥当马尔从未经历过真正的战斗。

column1: What are we worried about? It’s only a poem.
column2: 我们在担心什么？不过是一首诗罢了。

column1: If the poem is truly about \x01BX, and he does nothing to challenge Ordangmar, his honor will be forever stained.
column2: 如果这首诗确实是在讲 \x01BX，而他毫无挑战奥当马尔之举，那他的荣誉将永远蒙上污点。

column1: Unless \x01BX identifies himself as the “dung-daubed thane,” or Ordangmar makes his insult explicit, no dishonor is incurred.
column2: 除非 \x01BX 自认是“涂粪领主”，或者奥当马尔将侮辱明确点明，否则不算失誉。

column1: If Ordangmar is hurt while under our hospitality, our reputation with the other clans will suffer.
column2: 如果奥当马尔在我们好客庇护之下受伤，我们在其他氏族中的声誉会受损。

column1: It is easiest to make peace before the war has begun.
column2: 在战争开始前讲和是最容易的。

column1: The poem is carefully worded so that one who seeks offense will find it.
column2: 这首诗措辞精心，有意寻衅之人自会找到由头。

column1: The poem mocks not only \x01BX, but all brave warriors. Punish him.
column2: 这首诗不仅嘲弄了 \x01BX，还嘲弄了所有勇敢的武士。惩罚他。

column1: Poets drink deeply of Orlanth’s gift.
column2: 诗人畅饮奥兰斯的恩赐。

column1: The thanes are loyal to us. Let us not be disloyal to them.
column2: 武器领主们对我们忠诚。我们也不应对他们不忠。

column1: Tame this potential fight, as Ernalda tamed battle-eager Orlanth.
column2: 平息这场潜在的争斗，就像埃娜尔达平息了好战的奥兰斯一样。

column1: \x01BX is a stubborn man. He will not let go of this offense easily.
column2: \x01BX 是个固执的人。他不会轻易放过这次侮辱。

column1: Pah! The men are always ready to die for honor, and the women forever forced to weep for them.
column2: 呸！男人们总是随时准备为荣誉赴死，而女人们却永远被迫为他们流泪。

column1: Words bear power like the wind carries birds aloft.
column2: 言辞有力量，如同风托起飞鸟。

column1: One never knows when someone will take a poem’s meaning the wrong way.
column2: 谁也不知道什么时候会有人曲解一首诗的含义。

column1: Ordangmar and \x01BX have exchanged words that can’t be erased. Unless \x01BX fights Ordangmar, his honor will be tainted. But if the great poet Ordangmar is harmed while under your hospitality, the other clans will despise you.
column2: 奥当马尔和 \x01BX 已交换了无法抹去的言辞。除非 \x01BX 与奥当马尔决斗，否则他的荣誉将受玷污。但如果伟大的诗人奥当马尔在您的庇护下受伤，其他氏族会鄙视您。

column1: Allow a duel between them.
column2: 允许他们两人决斗。

column1: \x01@\x03 stepped in as the poet’s champion, and cut \x01BX on the arm. Thus all could see that Orlanth favored Ordangmar.
column2: \x01@\x03 作为诗人的捍卫者介入，在 \x01BX 手臂上划了一刀。于是所有人都看到奥兰斯眷顾奥当马尔。

column1: \x01@\x03 stepped in as the poet’s champion, and was cut in the leg. Thus all could see that Ordangmar’s words were not true of \x01BX.
column2: \x01@\x03 作为诗人的捍卫者介入，腿部被划了一刀。于是所有人都看到奥当马尔的话并非 \x01BX的真实写照。

column1: Unfortunately, \x01@\x03’s wound was more serious than it looked at first, and \x06 was lame for some time.
column2: 不幸的是， \x01@\x03的伤比最初看起来更严重， \x06 跛了好一阵子。

column1: Force them to settle their dispute by arm-wrestling.
column2: 强迫他们以掰手腕解决争端。

column1: We ordered that the two resolve their differences with an arm-wrestling match.
column2: 我们下令让两人以掰手腕比赛化解分歧。

column1: Ordangmar surprised all and sundry by defeating \x01BX in an arm-wrestling match. He then stalked from the hall, promising to compose a poem about the rudeness of clan \x01@".
column2: 奥当马尔在掰手腕比赛中击败了 \x01BX ，让所有人惊讶不已。然后他大步走出了厅堂，承诺要写一首诗讽刺 \x01@"氏族的无礼。

column1: As expected, \x01BX easily bested Ordangmar. Ordangmar was quiet for the rest of the feast, and quietly slunk from the hall. Later, we heard that he had composed a satirical ode against us.
column2: 果不其然， \x01BX 轻松战胜了奥当马尔。奥当马尔在宴席余下的时间里沉默不语，悄悄溜出了厅堂。后来我们听说他写了一首讽刺诗针对我们。

column1: Order \x01BX to drop his claim.
column2: 命令 \x01BX 放弃他的要求。

column1: The clan ordered \x01BX to drop his claim.
column2: 氏族命令 \x01BX 放弃他的要求。

column1: \x01BX obeyed, but the weaponthanes protested, and said that our clan leaders had acted dishonorably in making this demand of him.
column2: \x01BX 服从了，但武器领主们提出抗议，说我们的氏族首领向他提出这一要求是行事不光彩。

column1: Order Ordangmar to leave.
column2: 命令奥当马尔离开。

column1: We demanded that the troublesome poet leave us. Ordangmar slunk quietly from the hall. Later, we heard that he had composed a satirical ode against us.
column2: 我们要求那位麻烦的诗人离开我们。奥当马尔悄悄溜出了厅堂。后来我们听说他写了一首讽刺诗针对我们。

column1: Ordangmar slunk quietly from the hall. Later, we heard that he had composed a satirical ode against us.
column2: 奥当马尔悄悄溜出了厅堂。后来我们听说他写了一首讽刺诗针对我们。

column1: A poet as good as Ordangmar can compose a satire which will cause the udders of our cows to dry.
column2: 像奥当马尔这样出色的诗人能写出让母牛乳房干瘪的讽刺诗。

column1: The mood has soured. We should have prevented this.
column2: 气氛变得糟糕了。我们本该阻止这一切的。

column1: The warriors will be angry if we prevent \x01BX from restoring his honor.
column2: 如果我们阻止 \x01BX 恢复荣誉，武士们会愤怒。

column1: Only a contest for Orlanth’s favor will show who is right.
column2: 只有一场争夺奥兰斯恩宠的比试才能证明谁是对的。

column1: Ordangmar is entitled to have a champion in his duel.
column2: 奥当马尔有权在决斗中指定一名护卫者。

column1: We will suffer politically if Ordangmar composes a satire against us.
column2: 如果奥当马尔写一首讽刺诗针对我们，我们将在政治上受害。

column1: A fight between Ordangmar and \x01BX will end in death.
column2: 奥当马尔和 \x01BX 之间的打斗将以死亡收场。

column1: \x01BX is humorless. Do not reward him for it.
column2: \x01BX 缺乏幽默感。不要为此奖励他。

column1: We will be shamed if we expel Ordangmar from our hall.
column2: 如果我们把奥当马尔逐出厅堂，我们将蒙受耻辱。

column1: No matter what his reputation, Ordangmar is a fool if he insults one of our thanes. Let him take his lumps.
column2: 不管他名声多大，奥当马尔侮辱我们的一位武器领主就是蠢货。让他尝尝苦头吧。

column1: Actually, I think Ordangmar meant that I smelled of dung.
column2: 其实，我觉得奥当马尔指的是我身上有粪臭。

column1: The Battle of Extinguish Field began with bad poetry and ill-chosen words.
column2: 熄灭原之战始于拙劣的诗和不当的言辞。

column1: Ordangmar, the famous poet of the \x01@! clan,
column2: 奥当马尔， \x01@! 氏族著名的诗人，

column1: is dead. He
column2: 死了。他

column1: \x02\x03died when he mis-spoke a satire/was killed by a jealous husband/passed away in his sleep\x02.
column2: \x02\x03因念错讽刺诗而死/被一个嫉妒的丈夫杀死/在睡梦中去世\x02。

column1: I will miss his verses, though I confess I’m glad we will no longer be the target of his satires.
column2: 我会怀念他的诗句，不过我承认，很高兴我们不再是他的讽刺目标了。

column1: I for one will miss his clever verses.

column1: Strange and primitive
column2: 古怪而原始

column1: Strange and primitive warriors in wolf skins
column2: 身披狼皮的古怪而原始的武士

column1: warriors get past your patrols to take two cows from you. The wolfskin-clad raiders are so bold that they butcher the cows on the spot, rather than driving them away. The carls are sure that this will happen again.
column2: 勇士们突破了你们的巡逻队，抢走了两头牛。这些披着狼皮的袭击者如此胆大妄为，竟当场宰杀牛只，而不是把它们赶走。自由民们确信这种事还会发生。

column1: took two cows in a bold raid.
column2: 在一次大胆的袭击中抢走了两头牛。

column1: Find their camp and talk peace with them.
column2: 找到他们的营地，与他们和平谈判。

column1: We sought out the primitives for talk of peace.
column2: 我们找到那些原始人，寻求和平谈判。

column1: We sought in vain.
column2: 我们徒劳搜寻。

column1: We found their encampment.
column2: 我们找到了他们的营地。

column1: They refused to speak with us.
column2: 他们拒绝与我们交谈。

column1: Their leaders were reluctant at first, but before long we were teaching them great poems, and they were teaching us how to howl.
column2: 他们的首领起初不情愿，但没过多久，我们就教他们伟大的诗歌，而他们也教我们如何嚎叫。

column1: Find their camp and launch a punitive strike against them.
column2: 找到他们的营地，对他们发起惩罚性打击。

column1: We fell among their camp, slaying at will. They fled in all directions, yelping.
column2: 我们冲入他们的营地，随意屠戮。他们四散奔逃，哀嚎不止。

column1: We attacked them in their camp.
column2: 我们在他们的营地里进攻了他们。

column1: Their numbers overwhelmed us, and we lost many good men.
column2: 他们人数众多，压倒了我们，我们损失了许多好战士。

column1: Have hunters hunt and trap wolves.
column2: 派遣猎人去猎捕和设陷阱捕捉狼。

column1: We trapped wolves whenever possible. Whether we caught wolf-men or ordinary animals, none could say.
column2: 我们尽可能设陷阱捕狼。至于抓到的究竟是狼人还是普通野兽，无人能说清。

column1: Tell other clans that you want many wolf skins.
column2: 告诉其他氏族，你们想要大量狼皮。

column1: Our traders spread the word to other clans. We offered good prices for the skins of wolves.
column2: 我们的商人将消息传给其他氏族。我们为狼皮出价不菲。

column1: The other clans seemed receptive to the good prices we offered.
column2: 其他氏族似乎对我们提供的好价码很感兴趣。

column1: Track down and kill these particular raiders.
column2: 追踪并杀死这些特定的袭击者。

column1: It was hard to find them, but when we did, we made them rue the day they stole from us.
column2: 找到他们很困难，但一旦找到，我们就让他们后悔曾抢夺我们。

column1: We tracked them for days, finding nothing but the distant, barking laughter of the wolf men.
column2: 我们追踪了他们好多天，除了一阵阵远处传来的狼人的吠笑，什么也没找到。

column1: If they turn into wolves, they can be hunted like wolves.
column2: 如果他们变成狼，就可以像猎狼一样猎杀他们。

column1: Like wolves, the Telmori can prove difficult to find and talk to.
column2: 像狼一样，泰尔莫里人也可能很难找到并与之交谈。

column1: Wolves are crafty to begin with. Wolves that have been hunted grow craftier still.
column2: 狼天生狡猾。被猎捕过的狼只会变得更加狡猾。

column1: The lambs and calves appreciate our wolf-hunting efforts, but whether this discourages the Telmori is hard to say.
column2: 羊羔和牛犊感激我们猎狼的努力，但这是否能让泰尔莫里人却步，却很难说。

column1: These savages will tear our men to bits.
column2: 这些野蛮人会把我们的人撕成碎片。

column1: These primitives are no match for us in a fight
column2: 这些原始人在战斗中最不是我们的对手。

column1: We can make these primitives howl, if we can find them, that is.
column2: 我们能让这些原始人哀嚎——只要我们能找到他们的话。

column1: These wolf-men are harder to fight than they first appear.
column2: 这些狼人比他们最初看起来更难对付。

column1: These wolf-folk are easy for us to best. However, they’re difficult to bring to a fight.
column2: 我们很容易胜过这些狼人，但很难让他们投入战斗。

column1: These primitives are no match for us in a fight. However, they’re very difficult to draw into battle.
column2: 这些原始人在战斗中最不是我们的对手，但很难把他们引到战场上。

column1: These primitive folk might need some of our civilized goods.
column2: 这些原始人或许需要一些我们的文明商品。

column1: We’ve tried unfriendly solutions before. Why not try conquering these folk through trade?
column2: 我们之前试过不那么友好的办法。为什么不尝试通过贸易征服这些家伙呢？

column1: I have heard rumors of these people, the Telmori. By day they are human, by night they are wolves.
column2: 我听说过关于这些人——泰尔莫里人的传闻。白天他们是人，晚上他们是狼。

column1: We have enough strange enemies right now.
column2: 我们眼下已经有够多奇怪的敌人了。

column1: We don’t need any more strange enemies. Let’s keep trying for a peaceful solution.
column2: 我们不需要更多奇怪的敌人了。继续寻求和平解决办法吧。

column1: We might as well try to talk to them, instead of courting their hatred.
column2: 也许我们该试着跟他们谈谈，而不是招致他们的仇恨。

column1: These Telmori are a stain upon our fine land. Our ancestors would approve if we could wipe them out.
column2: 这些泰尔莫里人是我们美好土地上的污点。如果我们能消灭他们，祖先也会赞许。

column1: Whatever we do, let’s not waste more time than our lost cows are worth.
column2: 无论我们做什么，可别在这上面浪费比我们丢失的牛还值钱的时间。

column1: When our clan was young, we fought the beastmen called the Basmoli. By fighting these beastmen, we will gain ritual power.
column2: 当我们氏族还年轻时，我们曾与被称为巴莫利人的兽人作战。与这些兽人作战，我们将获得仪式力量。

column1: Ever notice how none of these \x02\x03wolf-men/enemies/raiders\x02 ever try to \x02\x03run off with our wheat sacks/steal our barley/harvest our grain\x02?
column2: 有没有注意到这些 \x02\x03狼人/敌人/袭击者\x02 从来没想过去 \x02\x03偷走我们的麦袋/偷走我们的大麦/收割我们的谷物\x02？

column1: When Orlanthi last lived in Dragon Pass, they met these beastmen. They are called Telmori, and they turn into wolves once a week.
column2: 当奥兰提人最后一次住在龙隘时，他们遇到过这些兽人。他们被称为泰尔莫里人，每周会变成一次狼。

column1: When these beastmen, the Telmori, turn into wolves, then they must act as wolves do.
column2: 当这些兽人——泰尔莫里人变成狼时，他们就必须像狼一样行事。

column1: These creatures are the Telmori. They turn into wolves once a week. It’s impossible to tell a true wolf from a Telmori when they are out howling under the moon.
column2: 这些生物就是泰尔莫里人。他们每周会变成一次狼。当他们在月下嚎叫时，根本无法区分真狼和泰尔莫里人。

column1: The only way to deal with \x02\x03hostile neighbors/half-humans/strange people\x02 is to \x02\x03beat them thoroughly/make them hurt when they hurt us/make them fear us\x02.
column2: 对付 \x02\x03敌对的邻居/半人类/奇怪的家伙\x02 的唯一办法就是 \x02\x03把他们彻底打败/让他们在伤害我们时感到痛苦/让他们怕我们\x02。

column1: They are strange, but they are not Chaos.
column2: 他们很奇怪，但并非混沌。

column1: If they steal a little from us now, they will steal a lot from us later.
column2: 如果他们现在偷我们一点点，以后就会偷很多。

column1: If talking peace keeps our cattle safe, by all means try it. Just don’t bring them a lot of gifts.
column2: 如果和平谈判能保住我们的牲畜，那尽管去试。只是别送给他们很多礼物。

column1: If we can get other clans to suppress the Telmori for us, so much the better for us.
column2: 如果我们能让其他氏族替我们压制泰尔莫里人，那就再好不过了。

column1: We are spending too much on wolf skins. We should just exterminate them.
column2: 我们在狼皮上花的钱太多了。应该直接消灭他们。

column1: We must be careful not to spend more effort catching them we did in raising the two cows they’ve taken.
column2: 我们必须小心，别在抓他们上花的心思比养他们抢走的那两头牛还要多。

column1: \x01B], of the \x01@! clan, has returned, demanding their annual tribute of 40 cattle and 80 sheep.
column2: \x01B]来自 \x01@! 氏族的，回来了，要求他们每年进贡的40头牛和80只羊。

column1: “You are still weak,” \x01B] says, “and you will serve us, or be smashed.”
column2: “你们依然孱弱，” \x01B] 说道，“你们必须侍奉我们，否则将被碾碎。”

column1: \x01B] of the \x01@! clan again demanded heavy tribute, lest they attack us again.
column2: \x01B] 来自 \x01@! 氏族的再次要求沉重的进贡，以免他们再次攻击我们。

column1: two recent raids.
column2: 两次最近的袭击。

column1: three recent raids.
column2: 三次最近的袭击。

column1: “You are weak,” \x01B] says, “and you will serve us, or be smashed.”
column2: “你太弱了，” \x01B] 说，“你要么为我们效劳，要么被粉碎。”

column1: \x01B] of the \x01@! clan, who had bested us in several raids, demanded heavy tribute, lest they attack us again.
column2: \x01B]  \x01@! 氏族的家伙，曾在几次突袭中击败我们，要求我们缴纳重贡，否则就再次攻打我们。

column1: “We never pay tribute!”
column2: “我们从不进贡！”

column1: We refused to pay. They attacked us.
column2: 我们拒绝进贡。他们就攻打我们。

column1: Furiously we defended, and they came to regret their attack.
column2: 我们奋力防守，他们开始后悔发起进攻。

column1: Everyone wondered if we’d seen the last of the \x01@! demands.
column2: 每个人都想知道我们是否已摆脱 \x01@! 的索求。

column1: “We will do as you ask.”
column2: “我们会照你说的做。”

column1: We acceded to their demands.
column2: 我们答应了他们的要求。

column1: “We will pay this year only.”
column2: “我们只付今年。”

column1: We agreed to pay once only.
column2: 我们同意只付一次。

column1: Agree to pay, but try to bargain the tribute down.
column2: 同意进贡，但试图讨价还价降低贡品。

column1: We negotiated a less onerous tribute.
column2: 我们谈成了一项较轻的贡品。

column1: We tried to bargain them down, but were assessed a penalty for so trying.
column2: 我们试图压价，却因这种尝试被罚了款。

column1: We attacked them, and they soon forgot their demands for tribute.
column2: 我们攻打他们，他们很快就忘了索贡的事。

column1: Our victory ensured that we would not have to listen to their hollow threats.
column2: 我们的胜利确保我们不必再听他们空洞的威胁。

column1: We attacked them, yet were repulsed.
column2: 我们攻打他们，却被击退。

column1: After they repulsed our raid, they returned with their demands for tribute.
column2: 他们击退我们的突袭后，又回来索要贡品。

column1: Offer a treasure instead of tribute.
column2: 用宝物代替贡品进献。

column1: What do we want to give them?
column2: 我们想给他们什么？

column1: We offered them\x01@\x01\x01@\x14 instead of tribute.
column2: 我们给他们进献了\x01@\x01\x01@\x14 代替贡品。

column1: They accepted our offer.
column2: 他们接受了我们的进献。

column1: They would not consider this.
column2: 他们不予考虑。

column1: They ask much of us, but we can pay it.
column2: 他们索求甚多，但我们付得起。

column1: We’ll starve to death if they take that much from us.
column2: 他们若夺走那么多，我们会饿死的。

column1: \x01B] has outfought us, but I can outthink him. Let me whittle down his demands.
column2: \x01B] 他在武力上胜过了我们，但我可以在智谋上胜他。让我去削减他的要求。

column1: We can try haggling him down, but if we fail, he’ll assess us a penalty for trying.
column2: 我们可以试着跟他讨价还价，但如果失败，他会因我们的尝试而罚款。

column1: We can try paying once, but he will be back again regardless of what we say.
column2: 我们可以试着付一次，但不管我们怎么说，他还会再来的。

column1: We might lose less in battle than with the continual tribute.
column2: 我们打仗的损失可能比持续进贡还少。

column1: They’ve just been lucky so far. Let’s attack them, and hit them with the full fury of Orlanth.
column2: 他们迄今只是运气好。让我们攻打他们，用奥兰斯全部的怒火击垮他们。

column1: I wish I could say the odds are with us if we fight. They aren’t.
column2: 我多希望我能说，如果我们战斗，胜算在我们这边。但并非如此。

column1: There are legal precedents in our favor. Unfortunately, their power rests not in the law, but in the sword.
column2: 有法律先例对我们有利。不幸的是，他们的力量不在法律，而在剑。

column1: They outnumber us, but if we could hurt them they might drop this idea of tribute.
column2: 他们人数多于我们，但如果我们能重创他们，他们或许会放弃进贡的念头。

column1: We must strengthen our forces and make it painful for them to collect their loot.
column2: 我们必须加强兵力，让他们为抢夺战利品付出惨痛代价。

column1: If we hired more weaponthanes and made our forces bigger, they might not come back again.
column2: 如果我们雇佣更多武器领主，壮大军队，他们或许就不会再来了。

column1: We let ourselves become weak. We have no good options.
column2: 我们让自己变得软弱。我们没有好的选择。

column1: We have allowed ourselves to become weak. Let us pay now, but build our forces and alliances for next year.
column2: 我们让自己变得软弱。现在我们先支付，但要为来年积蓄力量、缔结联盟。

column1: We are still too weak to \x02\x03fight/best/challenge\x02 them. Pay again, but we must arm ourselves and train hard for next year.
column2: 我们仍太弱，无法 \x02\x03与之一战/击败/挑战\x02 他们。再付一次吧，但我们必须武装起来，为明年苦练。

column1: A raid in planting season means our crops will suffer. Tribute means we will suffer, too.
column2: 播种季节遭到突袭意味着我们的庄稼会受损。进贡也意味着我们要受苦。

column1: A raid at harvest time means our storehouses will suffer. Tribute means we will suffer, too.
column2: 收获时节遭到突袭意味着我们的粮仓会受损。进贡也意味着我们要受苦。

column1: When things got darkest for the world, when Wakboth ran rampant, the Lightbringers began their quest.
column2: 当世间最黑暗之时，当沃克伯斯肆虐之时，光明使者们开始了他们的探寻。

column1: Bad King Urgrain demanded tribute from his neighbors, until his weaponthanes deserted him for other reasons. Then, his neighbors banded together and smashed him.
column2: 恶王乌格兰向邻国索要贡品，直到他的武器领主因其他原因离弃他。随后，他的邻国联合起来将他击溃。

column1: I knew we shouldn’t have stinted on the fortifications.
column2: 我就知道我们不该在防御工事上吝啬。

column1: I knew we shouldn’t have agreed to give them even one sick lamb.
column2: 我就知道我们不该答应给他们哪怕一只病羊。

column1: Don’t be too forlorn. The peaceful clan always wins in the end.
column2: 别太沮丧。和平的氏族终会获胜。

column1: He reminds you of the obligations you owe to the \x01à, and tells you that the storehouses of the \x01á are like a tantalizing fruit, ripe for the picking.
column2: 他提醒你对 \x01à, 欠下的义务，并告诉你， \x01á 的粮仓就像诱人的果实，已熟透待摘。

column1: Offer sacrifices to a war god of \x01B_’s choice.

column2: 我们没有派出战士，而是向 \x01B_的战争之神献祭。

column1: How much do you offer to sacrifice?

column1: We offered sacrifices to \x01B_’s war god, but he refused them and asked again for warriors.
column2: 我们向 \x01B_的战争之神献祭，但他拒绝了，再次索要战士。

column1: “We already made our sacrifices. We need warriors,” said \x01B_.
column2: “我们已经献祭过了。我们需要战士，” \x01B_说。

column1: “Our war magic is strong. We need brave warriors, not more sacrifices,” said \x01B_.
column2: “我们的战争魔法很强。我们需要勇敢的战士，而不是更多献祭，” \x01B_说。

column1: “I have come for warriors, not for god-talkers. Let us fight together against the \x01á.”
column2: “我来是为了战士，不是为了神言者。让我们并肩作战，对抗 \x01á.”

column1: “I’m asking for your battle-cries, not the chanting of your priests.”
column2: “我要的是你们的战吼，不是你们祭司的诵经。”

column1: Politely decline his request.
column2: 礼貌地拒绝他的请求。

column1: We declined to take part in his raid.
column2: 我们拒绝参与他的突袭。

column1: \x01@\x0E-\x01B_ said that the \x01à would no longer consider us as their allies. He said that the god Humakt would punish us for being oath-breakers.
column2: \x01@\x0E-\x01B_ 说， \x01à 将不再视我们为盟友。他说，胡马克特神会惩罚我们这些背誓者。

column1: \x01@\x0E-\x01B_ said that the edge of a sword not used grows dull, and that he would look for friends elsewhere.
column2: \x01@\x0E-\x01B_ 说，不用的剑会变钝，他要去别处寻找朋友。

column1: \x01@\x0E-\x01B_ grimaced and said that he would look for friends elsewhere.
column2: \x01@\x0E-\x01B_ 皱了皱眉，说要去别处找朋友。

column1: Send a full war party.
column2: 派遣一支完整的战团。

column1: We sent a full complement of warriors to aid them.
column2: 我们派出了满编的战士去支援他们。

column1: Thanks to our aid, the \x01à drove the \x01á from the field.
column2: 多亏我们的援助， \x01à 将 \x01á 逐出了战场。

column1: We were pleased with the loot we gained.
column2: 我们对自己获得的战利品感到满意。

column1: Send only a token force.
column2: 只派一支象征性的部队。

column1: To show our esteem for the \x01à, we sent a few warriors on the raid.
column2: 为向 \x01à, 表示敬意，我们派了几名战士参与袭击。

column1: Our men took part in a glorious fight.
column2: 我们的人参加了一场光荣的战斗。

column1: \x01@\x0E-\x01B_’s forces were routed. During the retreat, he cursed us for not helping him more.
column2: \x01@\x0E-\x01B_的军队被击溃。撤退时，他诅咒我们未提供更多帮助。

column1: Together, we drove the \x01á from the field.
column2: 我们一起将 \x01á 逐出了战场。

column1: Your warriors make up two thirds of the raiding force. What percentage of the spoils do you take?
column2: 你的战士占袭击部队的三分之二。你拿走战利品的多少比例？

column1: We took our fair share of the spoils.
column2: 我们拿了自己应得的那份战利品。

column1: Although we had shouldered most of the risk, we generously gave to the \x01à, because it was they who first saw the opportunity.
column2: 尽管我们承担了大部分风险，但仍慷慨地分给了 \x01à, ，因为是他们最先发现了机会。

column1: The \x01á fought ferociously, and both we and the \x01à suffered losses.
column2: \x01á 战斗凶猛，我们和 \x01à 都遭受了损失。

column1: \x01@\x0E-\x01B_ does us the favor of attacking our enemies.
column2: \x01@\x0E-\x01B_ 赏脸攻击了我们的敌人。

column1: The more warriors we send, the more loot we can grab.
column2: 我们派的战士越多，能抢到的战利品就越多。

column1: Even if we send more warriors than the \x01à, \x01B_ will have cause to be offended if we try to take most of the loot.
column2: 即使我们派出比 \x01à, \x01B_ 更多的战士，也会因为我们试图拿走大部分战利品而感到被冒犯。

column1: We have enough warriors to defend our lands and equip a war party.
column2: 我们有足够的战士来守卫土地并组建一支战团。

column1: We don’t have warriors to spare.
column2: 我们没有多余的战士可派。

column1: The \x01á are unpredictable. Sometimes they fight poorly; sometimes, ferociously.
column2: \x01á 难以预测。有时他们作战不力；有时則凶猛异常。

column1: Clans that answer such requests are respected, and follow Orlanth’s way.
column2: 回应这种请求的氏族会赢得尊重，并遵循奥兰斯的道路。

column1: Alliances can’t be taken for granted; they must be tended.
column2: 联盟不能视为理所当然；必须加以维系。

column1: We cannot be so eager that we threaten to steal the \x01à’s thunder.
column2: 我们不能过于急切，以免抢了 \x01à’的风头。

column1: An appeal to the gods might be just as useful as the provision of soldiers.
column2: 向诸神祈祷或许和提供士兵一样有用。

column1: If we decide on sacrifice, the war gods will expect no less than three and no more than six cows.
column2: 如果我们决定献祭，战争之神会要求至少三头，至多六头牛。

column1: The \x01à may be willing to raid in Sea season, but we should tend to our fields instead.
column2: \x01à 或许愿意在海季发动袭击，但我们应当照料田地。

column1: The \x01à may be willing to raid in Earth season, but we should tend to the harvest.
column2: \x01à 或许愿意在地季发动袭击，但我们应当忙收割。

column1: The \x01à always act as if they really like us, but I’m not sure they really do.
column2: \x01à 总是表现得好像真的很喜欢我们，但我不确定他们是否真心。

column1: “When you open a door, look to see if there’s a broo behind it.”
column2: “当你开门时，先看看门后有没有一个布噜。”

column1: If we sacrifice to the gods, we honor both the \x01à and ourselves.
column2: 如果我们向诸神献祭，既荣耀了 \x01à ，也荣耀了我们自己。

column1: Let us show the \x01à what we are made of. Sacrifice twelve cows. Or send as many weaponthanes as we can muster.
column2: 让我们向 \x01à 展示我们的本事。献祭十二头牛。或者派出我们能召集的所有武器领主。

column1: If he’s so big, why doesn’t he do it himself?
column2: 他既然这么厉害，为什么不自己去做？

column1: This is a trap set up by the \x01á. Don’t fall for it.
column2: 这是 \x01á. 设下的陷阱。别上当。

column1: Speaking of ripe fruit, have any of you seen \x01@\x0E-\x01B_’s daughter? Yum.
column2: 说到成熟的果实，你们谁见过 \x01@\x0E-\x01B_的女儿？啧啧。

column1: Listen to the chief. The chief is always right, yup yup yup.
column2: 听酋长的。酋长总是对的，嗯嗯嗯。

column1: The \x01á are going to be sorry they chose to feud with us.
column2: \x01á 会后悔选择与我们结仇。

column1: I would like to refuse him, but then the \x01à might raid us instead.
column2: 我想拒绝他，但那样的话 \x01à 可能会转而袭击我们。

column1: How can we be proper Orlanthi if we refuse him?
column2: 如果我们拒绝他，还怎么配做真正的奥兰斯人？

column1: You decide.
column2: 你来决定。

column1: C
column2: C

column1: scene028
column2: scene028

column1: He has also come with an offer to end the feud between our clans, if we will agree to the marriage.
column2: 他还带来了一个提议：如果我们同意联姻，就结束两族之间的世仇。

column1: He offered to end the feud between our clans if we agreed to the marriage.
column2: 他提出如果我们同意联姻，就结束两族之间的世仇。

column1: Approve the marriage.
column2: 同意联姻。

column1: We agreed to the match.
column2: 我们同意了这桩婚事。

column1: How many cows do you slaughter for the wedding feast?
column2: 你们为了婚宴宰杀多少头牛？

column1: The marriage ended the hostilities between our two clans. Both sides’ best poets toasted the other’s clan at the wedding feast.
column2: 这场联姻结束了两族之间的敌对。双方最优秀的诗人在婚宴上为对方氏族祝酒。

column1: No blows were exchanged, but the feud continued.
column2: 没有发生冲突，但世仇仍在继续。

column1: “He must first prove himself worthy.”
column2: “他必须先证明自己配得上。”

column1: We required him to prove his worthiness.
column2: 我们要求他证明自己的价值。

column1: \x01@\x0C asks you to name a test for \x01B`:
column2: \x01@\x0C 请你为 \x01B`指定一项考验：

column1: Skill at arms
column2: 武艺

column1: Poetry
column2: 诗歌

column1: Pig calling
column2: 唤猪

column1: Plowing
column2: 耕田

column1: \x01B` wins the contest.
column2: \x01B` 赢得了比赛。

column1: The marriage ended the hostilities between our two clans. The best poets on both sides toasted the other’s clan at the wedding feast.
column2: 这场联姻结束了两族之间的敌对。双方最优秀的诗人在婚宴上为对方氏族祝酒。

column1: He failed to prove himself.
column2: 他未能证明自己。

column1: Let \x01Ba decide.
column2: 让 \x01Ba 决定。

column1: \x01B` wins her heart.
column2: \x01B` 赢得了她的心。

column1: The marriage ended the feud between our two clans. Each clan’s best poets toasted \x01Ba’s wisdom and beauty.
column2: 这场联姻结束了两族之间的世仇。每个氏族最优秀的诗人都为 \x01Ba的智慧与美貌祝酒。

column1: We left the matter to \x01Ba, and the eternal attraction between man and woman took its course.
column2: 我们把事情交给 \x01Ba，而男女之间永恒的吸引力自会发挥作用。

column1: She declined to take his extended hand.
column2: 她拒绝了他伸出的手。

column1: Refuse the marriage.
column2: 拒绝联姻。

column1: We refused the marriage.
column2: 我们拒绝了联姻。

column1: Although \x01B` left us courteously, everyone could tell he was greatly displeased.
column2: 尽管 \x01B` 礼貌地离开了我们，但每个人都能看出他非常不悦。

column1: “\x01Ba’s rank requires an additional marriage-gift of 20 cows.”
column2: “\x01Ba的身份要求额外二十头牛的聘礼。”

column1: We honored \x01Ba by insisting on a high bride-gift.
column2: 我们坚持高额的聘礼，以此向 \x01Ba 表示敬意。

column1: \x01@\x0C agreed, and we exchanged a generous dowry for a generous bride-gift.
column2: \x01@\x0C 我们同意了，然后用丰厚的嫁妆换取了丰厚的聘礼。

column1: \x01@\x0C was offended on \x01B`’s behalf. He thought that we doubted \x01B`’s wealth and status, and withdrew the offer of marriage.
column2: \x01@\x0C 为 \x01B`感到受辱。他认为我们怀疑 \x01B`的财富和地位，于是撤回了婚事提议。

column1: It is a bad time for a marriage. We can afford but a meager dowry.
column2: 现在不是结婚的好时机。我们只能拿出微薄的嫁妆。

column1: We can afford to send \x01Ba into wedded life with a generous dowry.
column2: 我们可以为 \x01Ba 置办丰厚的嫁妆，送她进入婚姻生活。

column1: Although it is irregular, I can convince the bearded wordsmith to cough up additional bride gifts for a girl so fair as \x01Ba.
column2: 虽然这不合常规，但我能说服那位大胡子言官为 \x01Ba这样美丽的姑娘再添些聘礼。

column1: I can’t feel good about giving them \x01Ba — who knows how long a peace could last?
column2: 把 \x01Ba 给他们，我心里不踏实——谁知道和平能持续多久？

column1: This marriage could bring us closer together despite our feud. I have to approve.
column2: 这场婚姻能让我们放下世仇，更加亲近。我必须赞同。

column1: His clan and ours are forbidden to intermarry.
column2: 他的氏族和我们的氏族禁止通婚。

column1: It is customary to give a generous dowry when marrying off a girl of high rank.
column2: 按习俗，高等级的女儿出嫁应给丰厚嫁妆。

column1: The marriage of a chieftain’s daughter has great political consequences.
column2: 酋长女儿的婚姻有重大的政治影响。

column1: The marriage of a chieftain’s daughter has great political consequences. We’ll be seen as eccentric if we let her decide.
column2: 酋长女儿的婚姻有重大的政治影响。如果让她自己做主，我们会被视为怪人。

column1: It’s \x01Ba who’ll have to spend her life with this callow fop. Let her decide.
column2: 是 \x01Ba 要跟这个浅薄的花花公子过一辈子。让她自己做主。

column1: I think a pig calling contest is called for here, no doubt he’ll win!
column2: 我想这里应该来一场唤猪比赛，他肯定能赢！

column1: I became a Humakti precisely to avoid, ah, matters of… this nature.
column2: 我成为胡马特信徒，就是为了避免，呃，这种……事。

column1: Let him prove himself with sword and spear.
column2: 让他用剑与矛来证明自己。

column1: If their offer is to believed, he must first prove himself with sword and spear.
column2: 如果他们的提议可信，他必须先以剑与矛证明自己。

column1: Marry her off, and send a small herd after her. All the tulas in the area must know of our greatness.
column2: 把她嫁出去，再陪送一小群牲畜。要让附近所有图拉都知道我们的伟大。

column1: Look at the poor lad! How nervous he is!
column2: 看看那个可怜的小伙子！他多紧张啊！

column1: How do we know this isn’t some kind of trick?
column2: 我们怎么知道这不是某种诡计？

column1: This marriage will inaugurate an era of peace and prosperity for both clans.
column2: 这场婚姻将开启两个氏族和平与繁荣的时代。

column1: We might be able to forge an alliance. I would be proud to have my daughter’s marriage provide the spark.
column2: 我们也许能缔结盟约。我女儿的婚姻能点燃这个火花，我会以此为荣。

column1: scene029
column2: scene029

column1: There is a great rock in the back pastures of your tula. Randan Korlmarson was walking by it one day when it spoke to him. It claims to be named Tarard Riel, and to be the guardian spirit of the local hills.
column2: 在你的领地后方的牧场里有一块巨石。有一天兰丹·科尔马森路过时，它对他说话了。它自称名叫塔拉德·里尔，是当地山丘的守护灵。

column1: Randan Korlmarson walked past a great rock in the back pastures of our tula. One day it spoke to him. It claimed to be named Tarard Riel, and to be the guardian spirit of the local hills.
column2: 兰丹·科尔马森路过我们领地后方牧场的一块巨石。有一天它对他说话了。它自称名叫塔拉德·里尔，是当地山丘的守护灵。

column1: Commit to sacrifice annually to the spirit, to worship it.
column2: 承诺每年向该灵献祭，供奉它。

column1: We began to sacrifice to the spirit of the hills.
column2: 我们开始向山丘之灵献祭。

column1: Who leads the rituals?
column2: 谁主持仪式？

column1: How many cows do you sacrifice to the spirit this year?
column2: 今年你们向灵献祭多少头牛？

column1: Tarard Riel said we were under its protection, but it expected further sacrifices in the future.
column2: 塔拉德·里尔说我们受其庇护，但它期望将来有更多献祭。

column1: The spirit told us it would go back to napping, pronouncing itself sorely disappointed in our era’s standards of worship.
column2: 灵告诉我们它将回去打盹，宣称对我们这个时代的供奉标准深感失望。

column1: Ignore this, it’s not that important.
column2: 别管这个，没那么重要。

column1: So far as we could tell, Tarard Riel ignored us as well.
column2: 就我们所知，塔拉德·里尔也对我们置之不理。

column1: Make a one-time sacrifice to the rock, to befriend it.
column2: 向巨石献祭一次，以示友好。

column1: We made offerings to show our friendship to the spirit.
column2: 我们献上供品以示对灵的友善。

column1: Tarard Riel became our friend. It said it would entertain sacrifices in the future.
column2: 塔拉德·里尔成了我们的朋友。它说将来会接纳献祭。

column1: The spirit told us it would go back to napping, pronouncing itself sorely disappointed in the quality of folk in our era.
column2: 灵告诉我们它将回去打盹，宣称对我们这个时代的人品深感失望。

column1: Test the spirit to see if you can trust it.
column2: 考验灵，看是否可信。

column1: We asked the spirit to prove itself.
column2: 我们要求灵证明自己。

column1: Who performs the interrogation?
column2: 谁来进行盘问？

column1: We decided that it spoke true, and would be able to protect us.
column2: 我们断定它所言为真，并能保护我们。

column1: Horrified, we learned that it spoke false — it was not the protective spirit it claimed to be.
column2: 我们惊恐地发现它说了谎——它并非自称的保护灵。

column1: Try to put the spirit back to sleep.
column2: 试着让灵重新入睡。

column1: We decided that it would be best if the spirit were returned to its ancient slumber.
column2: 我们决定最好让灵回归它古老的沉睡。

column1: Who performs the rituals?
column2: 谁主持仪式？

column1: \x01@\x03 performed a ritual, and no one heard the rock speak again.
column2: \x01@\x03 举行了一场仪式后，再也没有人听到巨石说话。

column1: No one heard the rock speak again.
column2: 再也没有人听到巨石说话。

column1: The rock spirit lashed back at \x01@\x03, scratching deep into \x04 soul.
column2: 岩石之灵回击了 \x01@\x03，在 \x04 的灵魂深处划下伤痕。

column1: Propitiation of spirits is like a trade deal. Let me see what the spirit will give us if we worship it.
column2: 安抚灵就像做交易。让我看看如果我们供奉它，灵会给我们什么。

column1: Perhaps a hill spirit would watch over us, causing marauders to lose their way.
column2: 也许山丘之灵会看顾我们，让掠袭者迷失方向。

column1: These spirits are almost always malign.
column2: 这些灵几乎总是恶意的。

column1: Spirits can be good or bad. If it is good, it can offer us much.
column2: 灵有善有恶。如果是善灵，它就能给我们很多。

column1: If we befriend it, it will do us some good. If we are willing to worship it, it will help us year in and year out.
column2: 如果我们与之交好，它会给我们带来好处。如果我们愿意供奉它，它会年复一年地帮助我们。

column1: Just like men, spirits can lie. I can determine the truth of its words.
column2: 就像人一样，灵也会说谎。我能判断它话中的真假。

column1: My mistress Ernalda is mother of the earth. I am best qualified to deal with hill spirits.
column2: 我的女主人厄纳尔达是大地之母。我最适合处理山丘之灵的事务。

column1: This is an Earth matter. Let the Ernalda priestess handle it.
column2: 这是大地的事务。让厄纳尔达女祭司来处理。

column1: Spirits are known to be peevish. We’ll annoy it to no end if we quiz it as if it were a common vagabond.
column2: 众所周知灵脾气暴躁。如果我们像盘问普通流浪汉一样盘问它，会把它惹毛的。

column1: Whatever you do, don’t offend it!
column2: 无论你做什么，都别冒犯它！

column1: “When a guest arrives, he needs hot food, cold drink, and dry clothes.”
column2: “客人到来时，他需要热食、冷饮和干衣服。”

column1: Our luck with rock spirits has been good in the past.
column2: 我们过去对岩石之灵的运气一直不错。

column1: “When Harmast was fifteen, the shadow spoke to him.”
column2: “哈玛斯特十五岁时，阴影对他说话。”

column1: Not all local spirits are evil.
column2: 并非所有本地之灵都是邪恶的。

column1: Temples and shrines don’t have to be buildings. No reason we can’t treat this rock like one.
column2: 神殿和神龛不一定是建筑物。我们没有理由不能把这块岩石当作一座。

column1: Won’t Orlanth and Ernalda be offended if we treat a mere rock-sprite with the respect we owe to them?
column2: 若我们用只应献给奥兰斯和厄尔纳达的敬意来对待一个普通的岩石精灵，他们不会动怒吗？

column1: I slept on the hillside near this spirit, and had good dreams.
column2: 我在靠近这个精灵的山坡上睡觉，做了好梦。

column1: I slept on the hillside near this spirit, and had good dreams. This won’t be like that other time.
column2: 我在靠近这个精灵的山坡上睡觉，做了好梦。这次不会像上次那样了。

column2: scene030

column1: Arglain, a stranger from afar, needs help with a bold plan. He proposes to perform the Salmon Rite, and bring that fish back to your waterways. In order to perform the rite, he will have to swim from the ocean and leap the falls. To succeed, he requires the ritual backing of an entire clan.
column2: 阿尔格莱恩，一位远方的陌生人，需要一个大胆计划的帮助。他提议举行鲑鱼仪式，将那种鱼带回你们的水道。为了举行仪式，他必须从海洋游过来并跃过瀑布。要成功，他需要一个整个氏族的仪式支持。

column1: Arglain, a stranger, came to us and said he could perform the Salmon Rite. He asked for our ritual backing in this feat of legendary difficulty.
column2: 阿尔格莱恩，一个陌生人，来到我们面前说他能举行鲑鱼仪式。他请求我们在这个传说级难度的壮举中给予仪式支持。

column1: Do as Arglain asks.
column2: 按阿尔格莱恩要求的做。

column1: We agreed to provide it.
column2: 我们同意提供支持。

column1: To everyone’s amazement, Arglain’s ritual succeeded.
column2: 令所有人惊叹的是，阿尔格莱恩的仪式成功了。

column1: He returned to us after befriending the river goddess at the source of our river.
column2: 他在我们河流的源头与河神交上朋友后回到了我们身边。

column1: We adopted him into our clan, and together we waited to see if the salmon would return to Dragon Pass.
column2: 我们将他收纳入氏族，一同等待看鲑鱼是否返回龙之隘口。

column1: Other clans respected us as powerful magicians.
column2: 其他氏族尊敬我们为强大的法师。

column1: Arglain made it halfway up the falls, but then faltered. His body was broken on the rocks below. We buried him by our creekbed.
column2: 阿尔格莱恩爬到了瀑布的一半，但随后失足。他的身体在下面的岩石上摔碎。我们把他葬在了河床边。

column1: Offer to recruit other clans to share the magical burden of support.
column2: 提议招募其他氏族分担支持的魔法负担。

column1: We proposed to spread the magical risk among many clans.
column2: 我们提议将魔法风险分散给许多氏族。

column1: Arglain was doubtful of the efficacy of this plan.
column2: 阿尔格莱恩对此计划的有效性表示怀疑。

column1: We never found out who was right, because the other clans refused us. Dejected, Arglain departed.
column2: 我们从未知道谁是对的，因为其他氏族拒绝了我们的请求。沮丧之下，阿尔格莱恩离开了。

column1: Other clans agreed to help.
column2: 其他氏族同意帮助。

column1: To everyone’s amazement, Arglain succeeded.
column2: 令所有人惊叹的是，阿尔格莱恩成功了。

column1: We waited to see if the salmon runs would return to Dragon Pass. Arglain joined our clan. Poems were composed to celebrate his deed, and our clan was named in them.
column2: 我们等待看鲑鱼洄游是否返回龙之隘口。阿尔格莱恩加入了我们的氏族。人们创作诗歌歌颂他的功绩，我们的氏族在诗中被提及。

column1: Arglain made it halfway up the falls, but then faltered. His body was broken on the rocks below. We buried his ashes by our creekbed.
column2: 阿尔格莱恩爬到了瀑布的一半，但随后失足。他的身体在下面的岩石上摔碎。我们把他葬在了河床边。

column1: Refuse Arglain. It’s a silly idea.
column2: 拒绝阿尔格莱恩。这是个愚蠢的主意。

column1: We thought his proposal ridiculous, and told him so. He sought the aid of the \x01@! clan.
column2: 我们认为他的提议可笑，并如实告诉他。他转而寻求了 \x01@! 氏族的帮助。

column1: Arglain made it halfway up the falls, but then faltered. His body was broken on the rocks below. We were proven right.
column2: 阿尔格莱恩爬到了瀑布的一半，但随后失足。他的身体在下面的岩石上摔碎。我们的判断被证明是正确的。

column1: Refuse Arglain. It’s too risky.
column2: 拒绝阿尔格莱恩。这太冒险了。

column1: We thought his proposal too risky, and told him so. He sought the aid of the \x01@! clan.
column2: 我们认为他的提议太冒险，并如实告诉他。他转而寻求了 \x01@! 氏族的帮助。

column1: What we feared came to pass. Arglain made it halfway up the falls, but then faltered. His body was broken on the rocks below.
column2: 我们所担心的发生了。阿尔格莱恩爬到了瀑布的一半，但随后失足。他的身体在下面的岩石上摔碎。

column1: Try to perform the rite without Arglain.
column2: 尝试在没有阿尔格莱恩的情况下举行仪式。

column1: Who performs the ritual?
column2: 谁来举行仪式？

column1: We decided to have \x01@\x12 perform the salmon rite instead.
column2: 我们决定改为由 \x01@\x12 举行鲑鱼仪式。

column1: To everyone’s amazement, \x01@\x12’s ritual succeeded. We waited to see if the salmon runs would return to Dragon Pass.
column2: 令所有人惊叹的是， \x01@\x12的仪式成功了。我们等待看鲑鱼洄游是否返回龙之隘口。

column1: \x01@\x12 made it halfway up the falls, but then faltered. \x03 body was broken on the rocks below. We buried \x08 by our creekbed.
column2: \x01@\x12 爬到了瀑布的一半，但随后失足。 \x03 的身体在下面的岩石上摔碎。我们把 \x08 葬在了河床边。

column1: No mere ritual can bring the salmon back to Dragon Pass.
column2: 单靠仪式不可能把鲑鱼带回龙之隘口。

column1: Salmon is very good food. If our streams were stocked with them, we’d need fewer cows.
column2: 鲑鱼是非常好的食物。如果我们的溪流中有大量鲑鱼，我们就不需要那么多牛了。

column1: If we had an uncommon item like salmon to trade, we would prosper.
column2: 如果我们有像鲑鱼这样稀有的物品用于交易，我们就会繁荣。

column1: Anyone completing this quest will need not just powerful magic, but great physical strength.
column2: 任何完成此任务的人不仅需要强大的魔法，还需要强大的体能。

column1: Anyone completing this quest will need not just powerful magic, but great physical strength. Arglain clearly possesses the latter.
column2: 任何完成此任务的人不仅需要强大的魔法，还需要强大的体能。阿尔格莱恩显然具备后者。

column1: If we ridicule Arglain, and he turns out to be right, then we’ll be the ridiculous ones.
column2: 如果我们嘲弄阿尔格莱恩，而他若是对的，那么我们就成了可笑的人。

column1: If we spread out the risk, we may gain less magically, but more politically.
column2: 如果我们分散风险，魔法上可能获益较少，但政治上获益更多。

column1: The carls are dubious, with good reason. We take great risks if we shoulder the magical burden alone.
column2: 自由民们心存疑虑，这很有道理。如果我们独自承担魔法负担，就要冒很大风险。

column1: If we devote our fertility magic to his quest, our harvest could very well fail.
column2: 如果我们把丰收魔法投入到他的任务中，我们的收成就很可能会失败。

column1: After the Dragonkill War, the dragons were still hungry. So they ate the fishes, whose spirits had offended them.
column2: 屠龙战争之后，龙仍然饥饿。于是它们吃掉了鱼，而鱼的灵魂冒犯了它们。

column1: Don’t leave a job to others when you can do it just as well yourself.
column2: 当你自己能做得一样好时，不要把工作留给别人。

column1: Arglain knows the ritual well, and we don’t. He might or might not succeed, but we’re likely to fail without him.
column2: 阿尔格莱恩对仪式很了解，而我们不了解。他可能成功也可能失败，但没有他我们很可能会失败。

column1: “A man must be reticent, proper, and bold.”
column2: “一个男人必须寡言、得体且勇敢。”

column1: Refuse him if we must, but let’s not be rude to him.
column2: 如果必须拒绝他，但不要对他无礼。

column1: Our magic is a resource more precious than sheep, cows and grain put together. We can’t afford the risk!
column2: 我们的魔法是一种比羊、牛和谷物加起来还要珍贵的资源。我们承担不起这个风险！

column1: The salmon ritual worked! We caught enough fish to feed \x01Bf people this year, and can expect the same teeming salmon runs as long as we keep up the rites.
column2: 鲑鱼仪式奏效了！我们今年捕获的鱼足够养活 \x01Bf 人，只要保持祭祀，就能期待同样丰盛的鲑鱼洄游。

column1: And other clans are trading for salmon as well.
column2: 其他部族也在交易鲑鱼。

column1: The carls, represented by \x01BI, are up in arms. “The clan is always at war. This incessant raiding and counter-raiding is playing hell with the crops.”
column2: 以 \x01BI为代表的自由民群情激愤。“部族总是在打仗。这无休止的突袭和反突袭把庄稼搞得一团糟。”

column1: \x01BI led a delegation of carls to complain that we were too war-like, and that the crops were suffering as a result.
column2: \x01BI 带领一队自由民前来抱怨我们太好战，导致庄稼受损。

column1: To end the dispute, we compensated the aggrieved parties.
column2: 为了解决争端，我们补偿了受损方。

column1: This seemed to satisfy them.
column2: 这似乎让他们满意了。

column1: The carls proved difficult to mollify.
column2: 事实证明自由民很难安抚。

column1: Promise to curtail raids.
column2: 承诺减少突袭。

column1: We promised to reduce the number of raids.
column2: 我们承诺减少突袭次数。

column1: The farmers thanked us for hearing their complaints.
column2: 农夫们感谢我们听取了他们的抱怨。

column1: We arranged for a parley next season.
column2: 我们安排了下一个季节的和谈。

column1: Upbraid \x01BI for his foolishness.
column2: 斥责 \x01BI 的愚蠢。

column1: Firmly did we upbraid the foolish carl.
column2: 我们狠狠地斥责了那个愚蠢的自由民。

column1: \x01BI left, but didn’t seem convinced.
column2: \x01BI 离开了，但似乎并未信服。

column1: We can’t give out cows every time someone comes to complain. That rewards frivolous petitions.
column2: 我们不能每次有人来抱怨就给出牛只。那会助长轻率的请愿。

column1: The weaponthanes will be greatly offended if you give credence to these mewling complaints.
column2: 如果你听信这些哀怨的抱怨，武器领主们会非常恼怒。

column1: You could compensate them directly. They’ll look churlish if they press the point.
column2: 你可以直接补偿他们。如果他们继续纠缠，反而显得无礼。

column1: Have I mentioned lately how hard it is to keep both carls and weaponthanes happy?
column2: 我最近有没有提过同时让自由民和武器领主都满意有多难？

column1: I’m feeling eloquent today. I’ll have \x01BI singing drinking songs with the warriors by the seventeenth hour.
column2: 我今天心情口若悬河。我会让 \x01BI 在第十七小时前和战士们一起唱饮酒歌。

column1: \x01BI is mistaken when he says that our crops are suffering.
column2: \x01BI 错误地声称我们的庄稼正在受损。

column1: \x01BI is right; we’re losing more than we’re gaining with these constant raids.
column2: \x01BI 说得对；这些不断的突袭让我们得不偿失。

column1: Harmast Barefoot once said, “Swill to the carl is mead to the weaponthane.”
column2: 哈马斯特·赤足曾说过：“对自由民是泔水，对武器领主就是蜂蜜酒。”

column1: Don’t swear an oath when a mere promise will suffice.
column2: 如果只需承诺就能解决问题，就别立誓言。

column1: \x01BI’s grating voice makes me want to trample a field of barley myself.
column2: \x01BI那刺耳的声音让我想亲自去踩踏一片大麦田。

column1: I hate it when the carls are upset at us. Carls are the backbone of our clan.
column2: 我讨厌自由民对我们不满。自由民是我们部族的脊梁。

column1: We have certainly fought many battles in the last couple years.
column2: 我们过去两年的确打了不少仗。

column1: So what if we have had to fight a couple times in the last few years? \x01BI has no business complaining.
column2: 那又怎样，过去几年我们不过打了几次仗？ \x01BI 没理由抱怨。

column1: In the days of the Empire of the Wyrm’s Friends, we wouldn’t have had to fight so frequently.
column2: 在亚龙之友帝国时代，我们本不必如此频繁地战斗。
