column1: A strange group of travellers has arrived in your tula, riding old-fashioned chariots. Their speech is unintelligible, but they gave the Orlanthi greeting. By using the Trader’s Talk used by Issaries priests, they manage to convey that they are travellers from distant Ralios. As near as you can make out, they’re on a quest to Orlanth’s “starting point.”
column2: 一群奇怪的旅人乘坐老式战车抵达了你的领地。他们言语不通，但行了奥兰斯教徒的问候礼。通过伊萨里斯祭司使用的商人语，他们勉强传达出自己是来自遥远拉利奥斯的旅人。据你判断，他们正在寻找奥兰斯的“起点”。

column1: We were visited by strange chariot-riders, who said they were from distant Ralios.
column2: 我们被一群奇怪的战车骑手拜访，他们说来自遥远的拉利奥斯。

column1: Ask them for new myths.
column2: 向他们询问新的神话。

column1: The travellers spend several days relating the myths of their land, where Ernalda is not Orlanth’s wife, Issaries is not a trader, and Humakt is Orlanth’s loyal brother. Your priests are at first confused, then engage in lengthy arguments, and finally refuse to talk with them. They’re especially vexed at being unable to prove the Ralian myths as false.
column2: 旅人们花了几天时间讲述他们土地的神话：在那里厄纳尔达不是奥兰斯的妻子，伊萨里斯不是商人，胡马克特是奥兰斯的忠诚兄弟。你的祭司起初困惑，继而陷入冗长的争论，最后拒绝与他们交谈。他们尤其恼火于无法证明拉利奥斯神话是假的。

column1: Our priests grew confused by their myths, which were twisted versions of our own.
column2: 我们的祭司被他们的神话弄糊涂了，那些神话是我们神话的扭曲版本。

column1: As they dashed off in their chariots, their tallest warrior turned and hurled a slingstone. It hit Verlain between the eyes with a crash of thunder, killing him instantly. Later, one of the carls complained that six of his cattle were missing.
column2: 当他们驾着战车疾驰而去时，其中最高大的战士转身投出一颗投石，伴随着雷鸣击中维尔兰的眉心，瞬间杀死他。后来，一个自由民抱怨说他的六头牛不见了。

column1: We drove them off, but they killed a weaponthane and stole some cattle.
column2: 我们赶走了他们，但他们杀了一名武器领主，还偷了一些牛。

column1: Give gifts to visiting heroes.
column2: 向来访的英雄赠送礼物。

column1: We gave them gifts.
column2: 我们赠送了礼物。

column1: Before they left, they gave us silver torcs and gold arm bands of surpassing quality.
column2: 在他们离开前，他们赠给我们品质超凡的银环项链和金臂环。

column1: The jewelry became one of the clan’s treasures.
column2: 这些首饰成了部族的宝物之一。

column1: Give them hospitality.
column2: 款待他们。

column1: We gave them hospitality.
column2: 我们款待了他们。

column1: After they left, one of the carls complained that three of his cattle were missing.
column2: 他们离开后，一个自由民抱怨说他的三头牛不见了。

column1: “The Lightbringers Quest began at the Hill of Orlanth Victorious, but we don’t know where it is.”
column2: “光明使者任务始于奥兰斯胜利之丘，但我们不知道它在哪。”

column1: Send warriors and interpreters to aid them on their quest.
column2: 派遣战士和翻译去协助他们的任务。

column1: How many warriors?
column2: 派多少战士？

column1: Do you send anyone else with them?
column2: 你派其他人随行吗？

column1: Who accompanies them?
column2: 谁陪同他们？

column1: \x01@\x10 accompanied them on their quest, along with \x01Bi warriors and interpreters.
column2: \x01@\x10 陪同他们踏上任务之路，连同 \x01Bi 名战士和翻译。

column1: We sent \x01Bi warriors and interpreters with them, to aid them on their quest.
column2: 我们派遣了 \x01Bi 名战士和翻译随行，协助他们的任务。

column1: Several of our people went with them as they continued their quest.
column2: 我们有好几个人随他们一起继续任务。

column1: Tell them about Kero Fin, Orlanth’s birthplace.
column2: 告诉他们凯罗·芬，奥兰斯的诞生地。

column1: “Yes, we have been to Orlanth’s mother’s hall. Here is part of its roof.” They handed us a piece of bluish ice, which never melted.
column2: “是的，我们到过奥兰斯母亲的大厅。这是她屋顶的一部分。”他们递给我们一块永不融化的淡蓝色冰块。

column1: When we mentioned Kero Fin, they gave us ice from the mountain.
column2: 当我们提到凯罗·芬时，他们给了我们山上的冰块。

column1: Their horses look too small to carry them.
column2: 他们的马看起来太小，驮不动他们。

column1: It’s impossible and unwise to treat with strangers.
column2: 与陌生人打交道既不可能也不明智。

column1: Trading with strangers can be difficult, but surely they will exchange gifts.
column2: 与陌生人交易可能困难重重，但他们定会交换礼物。

column1: Orlanthi fought from chariots back in the Storm Age.
column2: 风暴时代，奥兰斯信徒曾乘战车作战。

column1: Orlanthi fought from chariots back in the Storm Age. I’m not sure how to best defend against chariot warriors.
column2: 风暴时代，奥兰斯信徒曾乘战车作战。我不确定如何最好地防御战车战士。

column1: Anyone who looks like that can’t be an Orlanthi.
column2: 长成那样的人不可能是奥兰斯信徒。

column1: Anyone who gives the Greeting is a proper Orlanthi.
column2: 行问候礼的人才是真正的奥兰斯信徒。

column1: Although they follow some Orlanthi customs, clearly they have also learned some foreign customs. We could inadvertently offend them.
column2: 尽管他们遵行某些奥兰斯习俗，但显然也学会了一些异域风俗。我们可能会无意中触怒他们。

column1: Our clan will gain prestige if we deal with them wisely.
column2: 若我们明智应对，氏族将赢得声望。

column1: They must know many long-lost legends.
column2: 他们必定知晓许多久已失传的传说。

column1: Coming from a foreign land, they will know many different legends. Some of them may be useful only in Ralios.
column2: 来自异国，他们当会知晓许多不同的传说。其中一些可能仅在拉利奥斯有用。

column1: How do they get their hair to look like that?
column2: 他们是怎么把头发弄成那样的？

column1: We should exchange stories of Orlanth.
column2: 我们应该交换关于奥兰斯的故事。

column1: They’ve come all the way from Ralios — what a great quest!
column2: 他们一路从拉利奥斯赶来——多么了不起的追寻！

column1: Weren’t there stories of great raids from Ralios in the Second Age? I don’t trust them.
column2: 第二纪元不是流传着来自拉利奥斯的伟大突袭故事吗？我不信任他们。

column1: Alakoring Dragonbreaker came from Ralios to fight the Empire of Wyrms Friends.
column2: 屠龙者阿拉科林从拉利奥斯前来与龙之友帝国作战。

column1: We’re doomed to be flooded by another flood of warriors from Ralios, just like in the sagas.
column2: 我们注定要再度被来自拉利奥斯的战士洪流淹没，就像传说中那样。

column1: I wonder if they know how to write?
column2: 不知他们是否会写字？

column1: I don’t see why we should share anything with these Ralians — we’ll never be repaid once they go home.
column2: 我看不出为何要与这些拉利奥斯人分享任何东西——他们一回家就再也不会回报我们。

column1: “The Hill of Orlanth Victorious? At least you know its name! Surely it is somewhere in these hills. Perform a divination for us, and we will speak ever of your generosity.”
column2: “奥兰斯胜利之丘？至少你们知道它的名字！它肯定就在这些山丘中的某处。为我们进行一次占卜，我们将永颂你们的慷慨。”

column1: They asked us to perform a divination about the Hill of Orlanth Victorious.
column2: 他们请求我们为奥兰斯胜利之丘进行占卜。

column1: Decline politely
column2: 礼貌婉拒

column1: They must have misunderstood our words — one started putting a stone into a sling before the others hustled him outside. They vaulted into their chariots and stormed off. Two days later, a carl reported a dozen cows missing.
column2: 他们一定是误解了我们的话——其中一人开始把石头放进投石索，其他人才把他推搡出去。他们跃上战车，疾驰而去。两天后，一名自由民报告说少了十二头牛。

column1: We declined, and they stormed off, stealing some cattle on their way.
column2: 我们拒绝了，他们便愤然离去，路上偷了一些牛。

column1: Perform a divination ritual to Lhankor Mhy
column2: 向兰科·米举行占卜仪式

column1: \x01@\x03 put a leather sheet over his head and sat alone until \x06 remembered ancient stories which put the Hill of Orlanth Victorious northeast of the Quivin Mountains. Thanking us profusely, the Ralians set out immediately.
column2: \x01@\x03 将一张皮革盖在头上，独自静坐，直到 \x06 记起古老的故事，将奥兰斯胜利之丘定位在奎文山脉东北。拉利奥斯人千恩万谢，即刻出发。

column1: The Knowing God revealed the location, and the Ralians headed there.
column2: 全知之神揭示了地点，拉利奥斯人便向那里进发。

column1: \x01@\x03 put a leather sheet over \x04 head and sat alone all night, but no inspiration came. Disappointed, the Ralians departed the next day.
column2: \x01@\x03 将一张皮革盖在 \x04 头上，独自静坐整夜，但毫无灵感。失望之余，拉利奥斯人次日便离开了。

column1: The Knowing God did not answer our question.
column2: 全知之神没有回答我们的问题。

column1: Perform a divination ritual to Lhankor Mhy, but ask for a gift first
column2: 向兰科·米举行占卜仪式，但先索要一份礼物

column1: They gave us silver torcs and gold arm bands of surpassing quality.
column2: 他们给了我们品质超群的银环项链和金臂环。

column1: Perform a divination ritual to Orlanth
column2: 向奥兰斯举行占卜仪式

column1: \x01@\x0F’s spirit flew with Orlanth’s hosts to a hill northeast of the Quivin Mountains, where they triumphed over rebellious giants. Thanking us profusely, the Ralians set out immediately.
column2: \x01@\x0F的灵魂与奥兰斯的众军一同飞向奎文山脉东北的一座山丘，在那里他们战胜了反叛的巨人。拉利奥斯人千恩万谢，即刻出发。

column1: \x01@\x0F saw a vision of the hill, and the Ralians headed there.
column2: \x01@\x0F 看到了山丘的幻象，拉利奥斯人便向那里进发。

column1: \x01@\x0F saw visions of Orlanth winning battles on dozens of hills, but none stood out.
column2: \x01@\x0F 看到奥兰斯在多座山丘上赢得战斗的幻象，但没有一座特别突出。

column1: Disappointed, the Ralians departed the next day.
column2: 失望之余，拉利奥斯人次日便离开了。

column1: Perform a divination ritual to Orlanth, but ask for a gift first
column2: 向奥兰斯举行占卜仪式，但先索要一份礼物

column1: We’re not obliged to give away our magic.
column2: 我们没有义务赠予我们的魔法。

column1: Our reserves of magic are sufficient that a divination should work.
column2: 我们的魔法储备充足，占卜应当成功。

column1: We have exhausted our magic; a divination would likely fail.
column2: 我们的魔法已经耗尽；占卜很可能会失败。

column1: Lhankor Mhy is the Knowing God, source of all information. But knowledge freely given is worthless.
column2: 兰科·米是全知之神，一切信息之源。但免费给予的知识毫无价值。

column1: Who better than Orlanth?
column2: 还有谁比奥兰斯更合适？

column1: If we learn where the Hill is, we can undertake the complete Lightbringers Quest ourselves!
column2: 如果我们得知山丘的位置，我们自己就能完成完整的寻光者追寻之旅！

column1: What will they do if our divination fails?
column2: 如果我们的占卜失败，他们会怎么做？

column1: Our spendthrift ways will be the talk of Ralios.
column2: 我们的挥霍无度将成为拉利奥斯人的谈资。

column1: The mead of poetry is the Thunderer’s brew.
column2: 诗歌的蜜酒是雷鸣者酿造的。

column1: Having spoken of the Hill, we can hardly refuse them now.
column2: 既然提到了山丘，我们现在很难拒绝他们。

column1: Orlanth would never charge strangers merely to answer a question.
column2: 奥兰斯绝不会仅仅为了回答问题而向陌生人收费。

column1: Lhankor Mhy.
column2: 兰科·米。

column1: The old stories don’t say where the Hill of Orlanth Victorious was, but that was before we left Dragon Pass. It may well be around here somewhere.
column2: 古老的故事没有说奥兰斯胜利之丘在哪里，但那是在我们离开龙隘之前。它很可能就在这附近某处。

column1: The heroes who went with the chariot riders now reside in the Halls of the Dead, though I don’t think they arrived there by the normal route. Their sacrifice has strengthened our clan magic.
column2: 那些与战车骑手同行的英雄如今居于死者之厅，尽管我认为他们并非通过寻常路径抵达那里。他们的牺牲增强了我们的氏族魔法。

column1: Mordrim the Stout, a prosperous farmer from the \x01@! clan, and his sons Korlmar and Harnkorl, arrive at your tula. “I understand you have\x01@\x10\x01@\x14,” he says. “I am prepared to offer \x01A\x0F cows worth of goods for it.”
column2: 壮汉莫德里姆，一位来自 \x01@! 氏族的富裕农民，与他的儿子科尔马尔和哈恩科尔来到你的领地。“我听说你们有\x01@\x10\x01@\x14，”他说，“我准备为此提供价值 \x01A\x0F 头牛的货物。”

column1: Mordrim the Stout came to trade for\x01@\x10\x01@\x14.
column2: 壮汉莫德里姆前来交易以换取\x01@\x10\x01@\x14。

column1: “Thank you. I’m sure this will be a profitable trade for both of us.”
column2: “谢谢你。我相信这对我们双方都是有利可图的交易。”

column1: We accepted his offer.
column2: 我们接受了他的提议。

column1: We accepted, but demanded a favor in the future.
column2: 我们接受了，但要求未来欠我们一个人情。

column1: Dicker with him.
column2: 与他讨价还价。

column1: We bargained for a better price.
column2: 我们讨价还价争取更好的价格。

column1: Mordrim was unwilling to pay much more.
column2: 莫德里姆不愿再多付了。

column1: Give him\x01@\x10\x01@\x14.
Mordrim and his sons praised our generosity.
column2: 莫德里姆和他的儿子们称赞我们的慷慨。

column1: We gave it to him.
column2: 我们把它给了他。

column1: Offer another treasure.
column2: 提供另一件宝物。

column1: Which one?
column2: 哪一件？

column1: Mordrim was only too happy to purchase the treasure he’d come for.
column2: 莫德里姆非常乐意购买他专程来寻的这件宝物。

column1: “I’m afraid that’s of no use to me now. Perhaps we can deal another time.”
column2: “恐怕那现在对我没用。也许我们下次再做交易。”

column1: We offered another treasure instead, but Mordrim wasn’t interested.
column2: 我们转而提供了另一件宝物，但莫德里姆不感兴趣。

column1: Mordrim accepted our counter-offer.
column2: 莫德里姆接受了我们的还价。

column1: Refuse to sell.
column2: 拒绝出售。

column1: Mordrim tried to argue, but we stood firm in our refusal.
column2: 莫德里姆试图争辩，但我们坚持拒绝。

column1: We refused to sell it.
column2: 我们拒绝出售它。

column1: I don’t think this is a good idea.
column2: 我认为这不是个好主意。

column1: We’re robbing him!
column2: 我们这是在抢劫他！

column1: It’s difficult to put a value on a unique treasure.
column2: 为一件独一无二的宝物估价很困难。

column1: It’s difficult to put a value on a unique treasure. However, \x01A\x0F is not enough.
column2: 为一件独一无二的宝物估价很困难。然而， \x01A\x0F 还不够。

column1: We should keep it until we need to use it in battle.
column2: 我们应该留着它，直到战斗时需要用它。

column1: The carls would rather keep the treasure.
column2: 自由民们更愿意保留这件宝物。

column1: Couldn’t he ask for something else?
column2: 他就不能要点别的吗？

column1: We can never part with something of Humakt’s!
column2: 我们绝不能舍弃与休马克特有关的东西！

column1: I’m not sure we can trust this fellow. He didn’t become “The Stout” by ending up with the short end of his deals.
column2: 我不确定我们能信任这个家伙。他可不是靠交易吃亏才得到“壮汉”这个名号的。

column1: Begone with the stinking thing!
column2: 把这臭东西拿走！

column1: What does he take us for, fools?
column2: 他把我们当什么了，傻瓜吗？

column1: We don’t know what he’ll do if we refuse his offer.
column2: 我们不知道如果拒绝他的提议，他会做什么。

column1: There’s something about this… perhaps we should… that is, if we…
column2: 这事有点蹊跷……也许我们应该……就是说，如果我们……

column1: I think we’d better keep the banner.
column2: 我觉得我们最好留着这面旗帜。

column1: We can’t give up a book!
column2: 我们不能放弃一本书！

column1: I wonder if those boys are married, or if they’d be interested in meeting some of our unmarried girls?
column2: 我在想那些小伙子是否已婚，或者他们是否愿意见见我们的一些未婚姑娘？

column1: No!
column2: 不！

column1: We can assure Mordrim’s friendship by making him a gift.
column2: 我们可以通过赠礼来确保莫德里姆的友谊。

column1: He’ll pay more.
column2: 他会付更多的。

column1: We need all our treasures for use as tribal regalia.
column2: 我们所有的宝物都需要留作部落的礼器。

column1: If I were him, I’d just steal it.
column2: 如果我是他，我就直接偷走了。

column1: Sora Goodseller, a trader-priestess of the talking god, Issaries, returns to trade.
column2: 索拉·好商，交流之神伊萨里斯的商人女祭司，回来进行交易。

column1: Sora Goodseller, a trader-priestess of the talking god, Issaries, comes to trade.
column2: 索拉·好商，交流之神伊萨里斯的商人女祭司，前来进行交易。

column1: In addition to the usual exchange of goods, she asks if we have any white horses.
column2: 除了常规的货物交换，她还问我们是否有白马。

column1: The Issaries priestess Sora Goodseller came to our clan and asked if we had any white horses to trade.
column2: 伊萨里斯女祭司索拉·好商来到我们氏族，问我们是否有白马可供交易。

column1: “Poor Snowflower was killed while we were escaping from \x02\x03a giant/some trolls/Chaos monsters\x02.”
column2: “可怜的雪花在我们逃离 \x02\x03一个巨人/一些巨魔/混沌怪物\x02时被杀死了。”

column1: The one we’d sold her before had been killed.
column2: 我们之前卖给她的那匹被杀死了。

column1: \x02\x02mare/stallion\x02
column2: \x02\x02母马/公马\x02

column1: We do have a single white \x01@\x08 in our herd. Sora made an opening offer of 3 cows worth of goods.
column2: 我们的马群中确实有一匹白色的 \x01@\x08 。索拉开价价值3头牛的货物。

column1: Although we have some light grey horses, none can truly be called white.
column2: 虽然我们有一些浅灰色的马，但没有一匹能真正称为白色。

column1: We had no white horses.
column2: 我们没有白马。

column1: Apologize for not having one.
column2: 因为没有而道歉。

column1: Sora said that the lack of a white horse reflected poorly on neither our generosity nor our hospitality.
column2: 索拉说缺少白马既无损于我们的慷慨，也无损于我们的好客。

column1: Apologize for not having one, and throw her a feast.
column2: 因为没有而道歉，并为她举办一场宴会。

column1: Sora said that the lack of a white horse reflected poorly on neither our generosity nor our hospitality, and the feast was proof of both.
column2: 索拉说缺少白马既无损于我们的慷慨，也无损于我们的好客，而这场宴会正是这两者的证明。

column1: Embarrassed that we had no white horse, we gave her a feast instead.
column2: 因没有白马而尴尬，我们便以一场宴会代替。

column1: Give her the white horse.
column2: 把白马给她。

column1: Sora inspected the horse closely, then insisted on paying for it. She seemed very pleased with the \x01@\x08, which she named Snowflower. After taking it for a ride, she told us about her visit to the \x01@! clan, which had spoken ill of us. However, we realized it was due to a misunderstanding, and she agreed to let them know of this.
column2: 索拉仔细检查了这匹马，然后坚持要付钱。她似乎对这匹 \x01@\x08非常满意，给它取名为雪花。骑了一圈后，她告诉我们她去过 \x01@! 氏族，那个氏族曾说过我们的坏话。不过，我们意识到那是个误会，她同意让他们知道这一点。

column1: Offer to save the next white horse for her.
column2: 提议为她保留下一匹白马。

column1: “That’s a kind offer, but I’m sure I’ll be able to find one on my travels.”
column2: “好意心领，但我相信在旅途中我能找到一匹。”

column1: Sell her another horse.
column2: 卖给她另一匹马。

column1: Sora turned down our offer, then packed up her mules and left, before everyone had finished trading with her.
column2: 索拉拒绝了我们的提议，然后收拾好她的骡子离开了，还没等大家都和她交易完。

column1: We offered a different horse, which seemed to offend her.
column2: 我们提供了一匹不同的马，这似乎冒犯了她。

column1: “You have some fine horses, but I’m looking for a white one.”
column2: “你们有些好马，但我在找一匹白马。”

column1: We offered a different horse, but she only wanted a white.
column2: 我们提供了一匹不同的马，但她只想要白马。

column1: Sell the white horse for 4 cows worth of goods.
column2: 以价值4头牛的货物出售白马。

column1: Sora inspected the horse closely, then agreed to our price. She seemed very pleased with the \x01@\x08, which she named Snowflower. After taking it for a ride, she told us about her visit to the \x01@! clan, which had spoken ill of us. However, we realized it was due to a misunderstanding, and she agreed to let them know of this.
column2: 索拉仔细检查了这匹马，然后同意了我们的价格。她似乎对这匹 \x01@\x08非常满意，给它取名为雪花。骑了一圈后，她告诉我们她去过 \x01@! 氏族，那个氏族曾说过我们的坏话。不过，我们意识到那是个误会，她同意让他们知道这一点。

column1: Sell the white horse for 10 cows.
column2: 以10头牛的价格出售白马。

column1: Sora inspected the horse closely, then agreed to our price. She seemed very pleased with the \x01@\x08, which she named Snowflower.
column2: 索拉仔细查看了那匹马，然后同意了我们的价格。她对 \x01@\x08非常满意，给它取名为“雪花”。

column1: We got a good price for it.
column2: 我们卖了个好价钱。

column1: Sell the white horse for 20 cows.
column2: 以20头牛的价格卖掉白马。

column1: Sora inspected the \x01@\x08 closely, then sadly turned down the deal. She returned to gaze at the white \x01@\x08 several more times before she finally left.
column2: 索拉仔细查看了 \x01@\x08 ，然后遗憾地拒绝了交易。她离开前又回头看了那匹 \x01@\x08 好几次。

column1: She was unwilling to pay our price.
column2: 她不愿支付我们的要价。

column1: Sell the white horse for a treasure.
column2: 用白马换一件宝物。

column1: “I have no magical treasures I can offer, I’m afraid.”
column2: “恐怕我没有什么魔法宝物可以给你。”

column1: Trade the White Calf instead.
column2: 改用白牛犊交易。

column1: “I’ve heard of your famous White Calf. Uralda has indeed blessed your herds. But I don’t deal in cattle, I’m afraid.”
column2: “我听说过你们那著名的白牛犊。乌拉尔达确实保佑了你们的畜群。但恐怕我不做牛的生意。”

column1: We offered her the White Calf, but she wasn’t interested.
column2: 我们向她提出用白牛犊交易，但她不感兴趣。

column1: White horses are sickly. We’d be looked down on by the other clans for selling one.
column2: 白马体弱多病。卖掉一匹会让我们被其他氏族看不起。

column1: A horse is usually worth four cows.
column2: 一匹马通常价值四头牛。

column1: A horse is usually worth four cows, but white horses are fairly rare.
column2: 一匹马通常价值四头牛，但白马相当稀有。

column1: Since she wants a particular item, we can easily command five times the normal price.
column2: 既然她想要特定的东西，我们很容易就能要到正常价格的五倍。

column1: We can undoubtedly get more than the standard price.
column2: 我们无疑能卖到比标准价格更高的价钱。

column1: I bargained with Sora several years ago, at the great market. She had a fine white horse back then, and she’s probably trying to replace it.
column2: 几年前我在大集市上与索拉讨价还价过。那时她有一匹好白马，现在她大概是想要一匹替代的。

column1: We have failed in our obligation to a guest.
column2: 我们未能尽到对宾客的义务。

column1: Although we can’t fulfill our guest’s request, nothing says we have to honor unreasonable requests.
column2: 虽然我们无法满足宾客的要求，但也没有规定我们必须答应不合理的要求。

column1: We might be able to fetch a high price, but if we show generosity, she will be obligated to us.
column2: 我们或许能卖高价，但如果我们展现慷慨，她就会对我们负有情义。

column1: We should at least show generosity, so she will spread our good name among the other clans.
column2: 我们至少应该表现得慷慨，这样她就会在其他氏族中传扬我们的好名声。

column1: White horses are sacred to Elmal and to his wife Redalda, the horse goddess.
column2: 白马对埃尔玛和他的妻子——马女神雷达尔达——是神圣的。

column1: She’s probably looking for some item of prophecy. We shouldn’t trade a white horse even if we had one.
column2: 她大概是在找某种预言之物。就算我们有白马也不该交易。

column1: She’s probably looking for some item of prophecy. We shouldn’t trade it.
column2: 她大概是在找某种预言之物。我们不该交易它。

column1: You can’t get cheese or cream from a horse.
column2: 你没办法从马身上得到奶酪或奶油。

column1: We could paint a horse white, I’ve done it before.
column2: 我们可以把一匹马涂成白色，我以前干过。

column1: Let’s paint our white horse black so she doesn’t know we have it.
column2: 咱们把白马涂黑，这样她就不知道我们有白马了。

column1: Let’s go steal her a white horse!
column2: 咱们去给她偷一匹白马吧！

column1: She’ll never find a white horse, they’re just too rare.
column2: 她永远找不到白马，它们太稀少了。

column1: She really wants to own a white horse.
column2: 她真的很想拥有一匹白马。

column1: The poor dear has come all this way for nothing. The least we can do is give her a good meal.
column2: 可怜的人大老远跑来一无所获。我们至少可以给她一顿好饭。

column1: Path-follower seeks Redalda’s winter-born offspring with lures of silver.
column2: 寻路者以银锭为诱饵，寻找雷达尔达的冬季所生的后代。

column1: We mustn’t offend her by asking too much.
column2: 我们绝不能要价太高得罪她。

column1: Warriors from the \x01@! clan have snuck onto your tula and killed one of our carls, \x01Bl. They identified themselves as \x01@\x18 and \x01@\x19, and let \x01Bl’s son go so that we would know they did this to avenge their \x01@\x12 \x01Bm, who had been killed during a raid by \x01Bl’s \x01@\x13, \x01Bn.
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的战士潜入了你们的领地，杀死了我们的一个自由民 \x01Bl。他们表明自己是 \x01@\x18 和 \x01@\x19，放走了 \x01Bl 的儿子，让我们知道他们这样做是为了替自己的 \x01@\x12 \x01Bm 报仇，他是在 \x01Bl 的 \x01@\x13 \x01Bn 发起的袭击中被杀的。

column1: One of our carls, \x01Bl, was killed by the \x01@! warriors \x01@\x18 and \x01@\x19, who said they were avenging kinfolk.
column2: 我们的一个自由民 \x01Bl被 \x01@! 氏族的战士 \x01@\x18 和 \x01@\x19杀害，他们说自己是在为亲属报仇。

column1: Bide your time.
column2: 等待时机。

column1: Demand wergild for \x01Bl.
column2: 要求为 \x01Bl支付血偿金。

column1: Who leads the delegation?
column2: 谁率领使团？

column1: How much do you ask for?
column2: 你们要求多少？

column1: half the usual amount
column2: 通常数量的一半

column1: the usual amount, \x01A  cows in silver
column2: 通常数量， \x01A  头牛的银价

column1: twice the usual amount
column2: 通常数量的两倍

column1: The \x01@! chief agreed that \x01@\x18, \x01@\x19, and their kin should pay compensation for the death of \x01Bl.
column2: \x01@! 酋长同意 \x01@\x18、 \x01@\x19及其亲属应为 \x01Bl之死支付赔偿。

column1: We collected wergild for his death.
column2: 我们为其死亡收取了血偿金。

column1: In order to placate us, the \x01@! chief outlawed \x01@\x18 and \x01@\x19. Their kinsmen glowered darkly at our delegation.
column2: 为了安抚我们， \x01@! 酋长将 \x01@\x18 和 \x01@\x19放逐。他们的亲属阴沉地怒视我们的使团。

column1: The \x01@! lawspeaker argued convincingly that this was not a secret murder, since \x01@\x18 and \x01@\x19 had announced the killing. Therefore, a sentence of outlawry was inappropriate.
column2: \x01@! 律法师令人信服地辩称这不是秘密谋杀，因为 \x01@\x18 和 \x01@\x19 已宣布了此次杀人。因此，放逐的判决是不恰当的。

column1: Send weaponthanes to kill \x01@\x18 and \x01@\x19.
column2: 派遣武器领主去杀死 \x01@\x18 和 \x01@\x19。

column1: This is not just a challenge against me, it’s a challenge to the entire ring.

column1: Somehow, I don’t think \x01Bq is behind this.
column2: 不知怎的，我不认为 \x01Bq 是幕后主使。

column1: \x01Bq is acting on behalf of someone.
column2: \x01Bq 是在替某人行事。

column1: Unfortunately, \x01Bp does have more of a knack for leadership than does \x01@\x03.
column2: 不幸的是， \x01Bp 确实比 \x01@\x03更有领导才能。

column1: Someone has assembled a powerful bloc; \x01Bq is only the spokesman.
column2: 有人已经组建了一个强大的集团； \x01Bq 只是发言人。

column1: Unfortunately, \x01Bp does have more of a knack for leadership than does \x01@\x03, and will be able to maintain a strong anti-\x01@\x03 faction if we don’t ask \x01@\x03 to resign.

column1: The carls are certainly not very happy these days.
column2: 这些日子自由民们当然不太高兴。

column1: The carls have no particular complaints about \x01@\x03.
column2: 自由民们对 \x01@\x03没有特别的抱怨。

column1: Our ancestral spirits never answer me, and I talk to them all the time.
column2: 我们的先祖之灵从不回应我，而我总是跟他们说话。

column1: We could hold a belching contest, and the winner gets to be chief.
column2: 我们可以举办一场打嗝比赛，胜者当酋长。

column1: I don’t see why I can’t just thump anyone who complains about the chief.
column2: 我不明白为什么我不能直接揍那些抱怨酋长的人。

column1: We could all die, or worse, with \x01@\x03 as chief!
column2: 让 \x01@\x03 当酋长，我们可能会全死掉，或者更糟！

column2: 我们的法律保护人民免受反复无常的酋长之害。

column1: I think \x01Bp has formed a powerful base of support, but is too cunning to confront the ring directly.
column2: 我认为 \x01Bp 已经形成了一个强大的支持基础，但过于狡猾，不会直接对抗长老会。

column1: Are we going to listen to a pack of whining men? We picked our chief, and she’s one of the best this clan has ever had.

column2: 我们要听这群哭哭啼啼的女人说话吗？我们选出了酋长，就这样。

column1: He certainly seems sincere. We should consider his complaint.
column2: 他看起来确实很真诚。我们应该考虑他的抱怨。

column1: She certainly seems sincere. We should consider her complaint.
column2: 她看起来确实很真诚。我们应该考虑她的抱怨。

column1: Get rid of the trickster.
column2: 除掉那个恶作者。

column1: Factions…
column2: 派系……

column1: It’s true that \x01@\x03 has not always made the best decisions.
column2: 确实， \x01@\x03 并不总是做出最佳决策。

column2: 如果我们真的要选一个新酋长，我们应该同时选择成为一个战争氏族。

column2: 我告诉过你，当 \x06 没有被选为酋长时， \x01Bp 并不高兴。

column2: 我早就告诉过你，让一个恶作剧者当酋长不是个好主意。

column2: 酋长是选举产生的，长老会或民众的意愿可以将其罢免。

column1: When the will of the people repeats its demand for a new chief, the wise ring listens.
column2: 当民众的意愿一再要求选举新酋长时，明智的长老会就会倾听。

column1: When Bad King Urgrain was just a clan chief, he refused to step down, in spite of many heated demands that he do so. Then he woke up one morning and found that the entire clan had packed up and left.
column2: 恶王乌格兰还只是个氏族酋长时，尽管多次激烈要求他下台，他仍拒绝退位。然后有一天早上他醒来，发现整个氏族都收拾东西搬走了。

column1: \x01@\x14, a wandering trickster, turns up in the tula with two bodyguards. As they approach the ring, \x01@\x14 starts to giggle and belches loudly.

column1: “What is this before my eyes? Only the funniest clan ring in Dragon Pass!” he says.
column2: “我眼前这是啥？龙之谷最搞笑的氏族议会！”他说道。

column1: A raggedy-looking man came to the tula to jeer and mock the clan ring.
column2: 一个衣衫褴褛的人来到图拉领地，嘲笑和讥讽氏族议会。

column1: “Why, I hear that you have not completed even one teeny little heroquest. Surely your magic is not so low as all that, is it?” he jeered.
column2: “哎呀，我听说你们连一个丁点大的英雄任务都没完成过。你们的魔法总不至于这么差劲吧，对吧？”他嘲笑道。

column1: He scoffed at us for not completing heroquests, among other things.
column2: 他嘲笑我们没有完成英雄任务，还有其他事情。

column1: “Your farmers are grumpy.
column2: “你们的农夫脾气暴躁。

column1: Your weaponthanes are mutinous.
column2: 你们的武器领主心怀叛意。

column1: What kind of glorious leadership produces that, ha?” He paused to scratch himself.
column2: 什么样的光辉领导力能搞成这样，哈？”他停下来挠了挠自个儿。

column1: “Your fighting is like dainty ladies, dancing!” he said.
column2: “你们的战斗就像娇弱的淑女在跳舞！”他说道。

column1: “You must be so extremely powerful that you don’t need trade routes to survive. Or extremely stupid to think so!” he chortled.

column2: “还有你们的邻居都说，这片地方臭味来自……来自……就是这儿！”

column1: And he collapsed, laughing, on the floor while letting pass odoriferous gas that caused all in the hall to step back a few paces.
column2: 然后他笑倒在地板上，同时放出臭气熏天的屁，致使大厅里所有人都后退了几步。

column1: Attack him.
column2: 攻击他。

column1: The bodyguards were much stronger than they appeared. They picked up one of our fighters and swung him by his heels to clear an arc around them.
column2: 那两个保镖比看起来强壮得多。他们抓起我们一名战士，拎着他的脚后跟抡起来，以此在周围清出空地。

column1: In the confusion, the trickster escaped. His guards followed shortly after, but not before we got a few good blows on them. The heel-swung weaponthane was wounded when they let go and he landed in the rafters.
column2: 混乱中，恶作剧者逃走了。他的保镖紧随其后离开，不过我们也在他们身上砸了好几记好拳。那个被抡脚后跟的武器领主被放开后摔在椽子上，受了伤。

column2: 那两个保镖比看起来强壮得多，强得多。他们扔火把、扔椅子，制造混乱，让恶作剧者逃走了。

column2: 不知怎的，他们还杀了一名武器领主，打伤了其他人，并重伤了一名长老会成员。我们庆幸他们很快跟着恶作剧者离开了。

column2: “滚开！你们又可笑又无礼！”

column1: We demanded they leave the tula.
column2: 我们要求他们离开图拉领地。

column2: 恶作剧者站起身，叹了口气，哼着一首关于兔子的奇怪小调离开了。

column1: Show him hospitality.

column1: The clan was dismayed to think that our allies held such a low opinion of us.

column1: Ask his advice.

column1: “We do not like what you say, but we acknowledge it, and will feed you before you go.”

column1: We thanked him and showed him good Orlanthi hospitality.
column2: 我们向他道谢，并以优秀的奥兰斯好客之道款待他。

column1: \x01@\x14 said that it was a rare thing for people to listen when he spoke. He said that he wouldn’t even make the joke about people who listen to tricksters, since we also fed them.
column2: \x01@\x14 他说，人们能在听他讲话时认真倾听，实属罕见。他还说，他甚至不会拿那些听信恶作剧者的人开玩笑，因为我们也给了他们吃的。

column1: “There may be some merit in this clan yet, if you do not dawdle. But hurry!” The people were happy that we showed them hospitality, but even happier when they left.

column1: Get him out of here. The sheep are nervous.

column1: He’s right about our trade situation.
column2: 他对我们的贸易状况说得对。

column1: We should be sending emissaries and gaining the goodwill of our neighbors.
column2: 我们应该派遣使者，赢得邻邦的善意。

column1: It’s not like he’s offering us anything, other than this bizarre message.
column2: 他又没给我们提供什么，除了这个古怪的消息。

column1: Maybe he thinks his \x02\x03so-called wisdom is/tales are/words are\x02 worth a \x02\x03dish of stew/tankard of ale/free meal\x02, but I say, get more information before we feed him. If we feed him, that is.

column1: I can get rid of this \x02\x03noxious insect/ugly toad/chattering little rat\x02, if you like.

column1: If we had healthy weaponthanes, we could kill this rogue, or escort him off the tula.
column2: 如果我们有健康的武器领主，就能杀掉这个恶棍，或者把他押送下图拉领地。

column1: Get rid of this obnoxious oaf!
column2: 赶走这个可恶的蠢货！

column1: We may not like what he says, but we should show good Orlanthi manners anyway.
column2: 我们可能不喜欢他说的话，但无论如何应该展现出优秀的奥兰斯礼节。

column1: We may \x02\x03hate the message and hate the messenger/despise the way he comes to mock us/loathe the very sight of him\x02, but we should \x02\x03show a teeny bit of/grant him just a little/give him a small mite\x02 of Orlanthi hospitality anyway.
column2: 我们可能 \x02\x03憎恨这讯息也憎恨这信使/蔑视他前来嘲笑我们的方式/厌恶看到他那副嘴脸\x02，但无论如何我们应当 \x02\x03展示出一丁点/赐予他一点点/给他一小撮\x02 奥兰斯的好客之道。

column1: Let them tell us more.
column2: 让他们多说一些。

column1: Truth is often difficult to swallow. At least it is only a trickster giving us this message.
column2: 真相往往难以接受。至少，递来这消息的只是个恶作剧者。

column1: Truth comes in odd packages. We should be grateful it is merely a trickster giving us advice.
column2: 真相常以怪异的方式呈现。我们应该庆幸这只是个恶作剧者在给出建议。

column1: Truth comes in all sizes. We should be glad this is a small thing and fairly painless.
column2: 真相有大有小。我们应该高兴这只是件小事，而且相当无痛。

column1: We cannot choose the way and shape that Truth comes to us. We can choose if we listen or not.
column2: 我们不能选择真相以何种方式和形态来到我们面前。我们可以选择是否倾听。

column1: Nasty trickster! We don’t need another one! Send them away!
column2: 讨厌的恶作剧者！我们不需要再来了！赶他们走！

column1: Even tricksters are right now and then. The trick is know which utterance is the true one.
column2: 就连恶作剧者也有对的时候。诀窍在于知道哪句话是真的。

column1: King Heort gave audience to all manners of creatures in his search for wisdom and truth.
column2: 赫欧特王在追寻智慧与真理时，接见了各种各样的生物。

column1: Bad King Ugrain requested an audience with a trickster, then tried to kill him when the trickster spoke the truth. But he escaped, and stole Bad King Urgrain’s best horse.
column2: 坏王乌格瑞恩请求接见一个恶作剧者，当那个恶作剧者说出真相时，他试图杀死他。但他逃脱了，并偷走了恶王乌格兰最好的马。

column1: The sun reaches its highest point once a day. A trickster is right, at least once in a day.

column1: Asking \x01@\r for an apology would not be out of place.
column2: 要求 \x01@\r道歉并不过分。

column1: Neither \x01@\r nor \x01@\x13 have behaved well.
column2: \x01@\r 和 \x01@\x13 的表现都不好。

column1: Why is anyone even thinking about a duel? This was a peaceful delegation.
column2: 为什么有人会想到决斗？这是一次和平的使团访问。

column1: If both parties agree, a duel would not violate hospitality. I think that \x01@\r and \x01@\x13 are pretty evenly matched.
column2: 如果双方都同意，决斗并不违反好客之道。我认为 \x01@\r 和 \x01@\x13 势均力敌。

column1: Fighting won’t settle anything.
column2: 打架解决不了任何问题。

column1: \x01@\x13 was right to stand up for the rights of our women, but wrong to forget about the laws of hospitality.
column2: \x01@\x13 为维护我们氏族女性的权利挺身而出是对的，但忘记了待客之道是错的。

column1: \x01@\x13 should never have endangered the clan by nearly breaking the sacred laws of hospitality, no matter how badly \x01@\r provoked her.
column2: \x01@\x13 绝不应该因险些破坏神圣的好客之道而危及氏族，无论 \x01@\r 多么严重地激怒了她。

column1: Let it blow over.
column2: 任其过去吧。

column1: Give them enough parting gifts, and they will remember our generosity instead of this unfortunate incident.

column1: \x01@\x06 is clearly too good for \x01@\r. And while it would be fun to see \x01@\x13 defeat him, it would not be a fair fight.

column2: 在灌木丛中寻找浆果时，氏族的妇女们遇到了一只说话的狐狸。

column2: 狐狸说我们很快会注意到好运降临。然后它把牛群赶进了森林。

column1: People saw no change in luck, and began to say we had given away cows for nothing.
column2: 人们没有看到运气有任何改变，开始说我们白白送出了牛。

column2: 抓住狐狸，把它卖给另一个氏族。

column2: 你把它卖给哪个氏族？

column2: 他们为这宝物开出的最高价是 \x01@\x18。你接受他们的出价吗？

column2: 显然，没人觉得会说话的狐狸有什么价值。我们放了它，它一边消失在树林里一边朝我们咆哮着诅咒。

column1: This is not the same fox that talked to us before.
column2: 这不是之前跟我们说话的那只狐狸。

column2: 会说话的动物是强大的灵友。它很可能能赐福我们。

column2: 虽然罕见，但每种动物都有特别聪明的个体能说话，甚至能施放法术。

column1: The fox is one of Eurmal’s favorite animals. He would be honored by the sacrifice of a talking one.
column2: 狐狸是欧尔兰最喜欢的动物之一。献祭一只会说话的狐狸会让他感到荣耀。

column1: Its pelt would make a fine cloak decoration.
column2: 它的皮能做成一件上好的斗篷装饰。

column2: 这个魔法征兆是诸神的赐礼。我们必须通过献祭回赠这份礼物。

column1: In Oskul’s Saga, the trade of a talking fox leads to six generations of peace.
column2: 在奥斯库尔的传说中，交易一只会说话的狐狸带来了六代和平。

column1: I think it’s lying.
column2: 我觉得它在撒谎。

column1: If we treat it well, maybe it will spy on the elves for us.

column1: What could a talking fox do for us?
column2: 一只会说话的狐狸能为我们做什么？

column1: Red-coat seeks Uralda’s daughters, but its offer is like a visit to Casino Town.
column2: 红毛皮在寻找乌拉尔达的女儿们，但它的出价就像去赌场镇走一趟。

column1: Few people have the chance to talk to a fox! When it comes back, we should invite it to our clan hall for a feast.

column1: “It is not only the fox, even the snail arrives at its destination.”

column1: Unlike dragons, foxes can’t be trusted.
column2: 跟龙不一样，狐狸不可信。

column1: It certainly did not happen overnight, but we have seen a string of good luck lately. Our clan magic is much stronger now, and I can only credit the talking fox we traded with.
column2: 这当然不是一夜间发生的，但我们近来确实走了一连串好运。我们的氏族魔法现在强大多了，我只能把这归功于我们交易来的那只会说话的狐狸。

column1: The god-talkers said that the talking fox had kept its promise, and given us good luck and strong clan magic.
column2: 神言者们说，那只会说话的狐狸兑现了承诺，赐予我们好运和强大的氏族魔法。

column1: I’ve been waiting and watching for some sign, but it’s pretty clear that our clan magic is not much stronger, and our luck has not changed for the better. We were tricked by that talking fox.
column2: 我一直在等待和观察征兆，但现在很明显，我们的氏族魔法并没有强大多少，运气也没有好转。我们被那只会说话的狐狸骗了。

column2: 人们抱怨议会听了但什么都没做。

column2: 虽然所有人都享受了宴会，但几个家庭之间的小争执反而突出了最初的观点：氏族很快就会变得过于庞大。

column1: Throw a feast for those with no relative on the ring.
column2: 为那些在议会中没有亲属的人举办一场宴会。

column1: We held a feast for those with no relative on the ring.
column2: 我们为那些在议会中没有亲属的人举办了一场宴会。

column2: \x01@N 明确表示这场宴会是为了倾听每个血统长老的意见，而议会成员的家庭并不介意被排除在外。

column1: Feast.

column2: 请求食物。

No more jokes. I challenge your finest warrior to a duel to the death. Let’s see if you’ll be laughing then. And don’t bother sending out your hairy-faces and healer-women to try and talk me out of this. I’m not in the mood.”
column2: “我听够了你们的战士嘲笑我们。我一生都在杀亡灵，好让你们这些无知的泥腿子农夫能睡个安稳觉，而不会从六尺沼泽水下醒来。别再开玩笑了。我向你们最优秀的战士发出死斗挑战。到时候看你们还笑不笑得出来。别费心派你们的毛脸汉子和女医者来劝我。我没心情。”

column1: A duck claiming to be a Humakti Deathlord stalked into the tula, challenging our finest warrior to a duel.
column2: 一个自称胡马克特死亡领主的鸭人潜入图拉领地，向我们最优秀的战士发起决斗挑战。

column1: \x02\x04the sword that walked with a waddle/the duck who beat up a stickpicker by turning itself into a zombie/Orlanth and the three eggs/Ernalda’s duck soup\x02
column2: \x02\x04蹒跚行走的剑/把自己变成僵尸殴打拾柴人的鸭子/奥兰斯与三颗蛋/埃尔纳尔达的鸭汤\x02

column1: \x01B~ repeated, “I challenge your finest warrior to a duel to the death.”
column2: \x01B~ 重复道：“我向你们最优秀的战士发出死斗挑战。”

column1: Accept the challenge, but only to first blood.
column2: 接受挑战，但仅限见血为止。

column1: We accepted the challenge, but only to first blood.
column2: 我们接受了挑战，但仅限见血为止。

column1: “Very well,” said \x01B~, “only to first blood.”
column2: “很好，” \x01B~说道，“仅限见血为止。”

column1: Who do you choose as your champion?
column2: 你选择谁作为你的冠军？

column1: For a moment no one moved. Then \x01@\x05 and \x01B~ cut at each other as if they had agreed to swing at the same moment. \x01B~ fell to the ground bleeding from a deep cut and \x01@\x05’s head fell off. They both died.
column2: 一时无人动弹。随后 \x01@\x05 与 \x01B~ 同时挥砍，仿佛事先约定。 \x01B~ 因一道深伤流血倒地，而 \x01@\x05的头颅滚落。两人都死了。

column1: \x01B~’s companions took his body away. After they were gone, our Humakti said that \x01B~ must have had a holy gift to kill the next person who challenged him to a duel to first blood.
column2: \x01B~他的同伴带走了他的尸体。待他们离开后，我们的胡马克特信徒说， \x01B~ 必定拥有神圣天赋，能杀死下一个向他发起见血决斗的人。

column1: To our shock, \x01B~ and \x01@\x05 killed each other with their first blows. Our Humakti said \x01B~ bore a gift from Humakt.
column2: 令我们震惊的是， \x01B~ 与 \x01@\x05 第一击便互杀致死。我们的胡马克特信徒说 \x01B~ 身负胡马克特所赐的天赋。

column1: \x01@\x05 stepped forward to give battle, but \x01B~ remained motionless without even drawing his sword. Just as we thought \x01@\x05 would smash the little duck in the bill, \x01B~’s largest sword whistled out of its scabbard and cut \x01@\x05 in two pieces. \x01B~ had the courtesy not to swagger as he left. After the ducks were gone, our Humakti said that \x01B~ must have had a holy gift to kill the next person who challenged him to a duel to first blood.
column2: \x01@\x05 迈步上前迎战，但 \x01B~ 纹丝不动，甚至没有拔剑。就在我们以为 \x01@\x05 会一拳打烂那小鸭人的鸭嘴时， \x01B~的最大号剑呼啸出鞘，将 \x01@\x05 斩为两段。 \x01B~ 离去时很有礼数，没有趾高气扬。待鸭人们离开后，我们的胡马克特信徒说， \x01B~ 必定拥有神圣天赋，能杀死下一个向他发起见血决斗的人。

column1: To our shock, \x01B~ killed \x01@\x05 with his first blow. Our Humakti said \x01B~ bore a gift from Humakt.
column2: 令我们震惊的是， \x01B~ 一击便杀死了 \x01@\x05 。我们胡马克提信徒称 \x01B~ 携带胡马科特赐予的礼物。

column1: Accept the challenge.
column2: 接受挑战。

column1: A weaponthane.
column2: 一位武器领主。

column1: \x01@\x08, one of our weaponthanes, accepted \x01B~’s challenge.
column2: \x01@\x08我们的一位武器领主接受了 \x01B~的挑战。

column1: \x01@\x08 accepted the duck’s challenge. We realized it wasn’t going to be an easy duel when \x01B~ made no effort to strike for the first minute of the duel, instead simply dodging, parrying, and drawing and sheathing his different swords. When \x01@\x08 paused to catch his breath, \x01B~ lunged forward to strike him, but \x01@\x08 had just been faking, and survived the Humakti’s fierce cut long enough to spit the duck on his sword. They both died. The people said we should have known better than to send a weaponthane against a Deathlord, even if the Deathlord was a duck.
column2: \x01@\x08 接受了鸭子的挑战。我们意识到这场决斗不会轻松，因为在决斗的第一分钟里， \x01B~ 根本没有出招的意图，只是一味闪避、格挡，并不断拔出和插回不同的剑。当 \x01@\x08 停下来喘口气时， \x01B~ 向前猛冲想击中他，但 \x01@\x08 刚刚只是在佯攻，而且扛住了胡马克提信徒的猛烈斩击，活下来将鸭子刺穿在自己的剑上。两人都死了。人们说我们早该知道不该派武器领主去对付死亡领主，就算那死亡领主是只鸭子。

column1: \x01@\x08 killed \x01B~, but was probably lucky to do so, and took a lethal blow himself. The people were not happy we sent a weaponthane to do a champion’s work.
column2: \x01@\x08 杀死了 \x01B~，但八成是运气好，自己也挨了致命一击。人们很不高兴我们派武器领主去干冠军该干的活。

column1: \x01@\x08 accepted the duck’s challenge. We realized it wasn’t going to be an easy duel when \x01B~ made no effort to strike for an entire minute, instead simply dodging, parrying, and testing his different swords with his thumb. When \x01@\x08 paused to catch his breath, \x01B~ strolled towards him, then killed him before anyone realized he was going to strike.
column2: \x01@\x08 接受了鸭子的挑战。我们意识到这场决斗不会轻松，因为在整整一分钟里 \x01B~ 没有作出任何攻击动作，只是一味闪避、格挡，并用拇指测试不同的剑锋。当 \x01@\x08 停下来喘口气时， \x01B~ 缓步走向他，然后在他尚未意识到即将遭到攻击时就杀死了他。

column1: “Thank you for the pleasure of killing one of your weaponthanes. But surely you have true champions. Or is this the best you can do?”
column2: “感谢您让我愉快地杀死了您的一位武器领主。不过您肯定还有真正的冠军吧。还是说你们就这点本事？”

column1: \x01B~ killed \x01@\x08 with ease, then challenged us again, this time to fight one of our true champions.
column2: \x01B~ 轻松杀死了 \x01@\x08 ，然后再次向我们挑战，这次要和我们的一位真正冠军交手。

column1: Accept \x01B~’s challenge.
column2: 接受 \x01B~的挑战。

column1: Tell \x01B~ that he has defeated our best warrior. Let him walk away victorious.
column2: 告诉 \x01B~ 他已经打败了我们最优秀的战士。让他带着胜利离开。

column1: We told \x01B~ that he had defeated our best warrior, even though that wasn’t true. We were greatly shamed by this action, but no more of our warriors perished that day.
column2: 我们告诉 \x01B~ 他已经打败了我们最优秀的战士，尽管事实并非如此。我们为此深感耻辱，但那天再没有战士阵亡。

column1: One of the more promising carls.
column2: 一位颇有前途的自由民。

column1: \x01@\x08, one of our carls who wished to become a weaponthane, stepped forward to fight the duck. After we agreed upon the dueling space, \x01@\x08 leapt forward to finish the smaller warrior with a quick blow to the neck. \x01B~ dodged to the side, posed and took several moments to select a small sword from the blades hung around his body. \x01@\x08 died on the next pass without even seeing \x01B~’s strike. “I will be happy to kill as many of these lambs as you wish to send me, but if that was one of your clan champions, you’re in more trouble than I thought.” said \x01B~.
column2: \x01@\x08我们的一位自由民，希望成为武器侍卫，迈步上前与那只鸭子战斗。在我们商定好决斗场地后， \x01@\x08 纵身跃前，一记快击命中脖颈，干脆利落地了结那个较小的战士。 \x01B~ 侧身闪避，摆好架势，花了几息功夫从腰间悬挂的利刃中挑出一把短剑。 \x01@\x08 在下一回合中当场毙命，甚至没看清 \x01B~的突袭。“只要你愿意派遣，我很乐意杀死尽可能多的这些羔羊——但如果那是你们氏族的冠军武士，那你遇到的麻烦可比我想象的严重得多。” \x01B~说道。

column1: We made a mistake by sending one of our carls to fight against the Humakti. \x01@\x08 died for our mistake, and the duck insulted us.
column2: 我们犯了一个错误，派了一名自由民去对抗胡马克特人。 \x01@\x08 因我们的错误而死，而那个鸭人侮辱了我们。

column1: One of your leaders.
column2: 你的一位首领。

column1: We agreed to the challenge.
column2: 我们接受了挑战。

column1: \x01@\x05 defeated \x01B~, though not without a hard fight, and the other ducks took \x01B~’s body away with them, back to the marsh.
column2: \x01@\x05 击败了 \x01B~，虽然历经苦战，其他鸭人将 \x01B~的尸体带走，回到了沼泽。

column1: \x01B~ fought with two swords at once, aiming to catch \x01@\x05 by surprise. \x01@\x05 was hit once but did not fall for the two swords trick, killing the Humakti with a blow to the head. Everyone agreed that it had been an impressive fight, and we allowed \x01B~’s companions to take his body away with honor
column2: \x01B~ 同时挥舞双剑，试图出其不意攻击 \x01@\x05 。 \x01@\x05 中了一击，但没有中双剑的诡计，一击击中头部杀死了胡马克特人。所有人都承认这是一场令人印象深刻的战斗，我们允许 \x01B~的同伴们将他的尸体体面地带走。

column1: \x01B~ proved to be a true Deathlord of Humakt. He killed \x01@\x05 in a fair fight, and then left without boasting or swaggering.
column2: \x01B~ 证明了自己是胡马克特真正的死亡领主。他在一场公平的战斗中杀死了 \x01@\x05 ，然后没有夸耀或趾高气扬地离开了。

column1: \x01B~ fought with two swords at once. \x01@\x05 kept parrying the first sword, but the smaller blade cut \x08 many times before \x01B~ stopped playing with \x08 and cut \x01@\x05 down. Several warriors wanted to rush the ducks right then but everyone else agreed that it had been a fair fight. \x01B~ was a true Deathlord of Humakt, and left our tula without boasting or swaggering. We were left to mourn \x01@\x05.
column2: \x01B~ 同时用双剑战斗。 \x01@\x05 不断格挡第一把剑，但较小的刀刃在 \x01B~ 停止玩弄 \x08 并砍倒 \x01@\x05 之前，就已多次击中 \x08 。有几个勇士想要立即冲向鸭人，但其他人都同意这是一场公平的战斗。 \x01B~ 是胡马克特一位真正的死亡领主，没有夸耀或趾高气扬地离开了我们的领地。我们只能哀悼 \x01@\x05。

column1: Refuse the challenge; ask if he’s heard the one about \x01@\n.
column2: 拒绝挑战，问他是否听过那个关于\x01@\n的笑话。

column1: We asked the duck if he’d heard the one about \x01@\n, but he just repeated his challenge.
column2: 我们问那只鸭子是否听说过关于\x01@\n的笑话，但他只是重复了他的挑战。

column1: \x01B~’s companions squawked enough to wake the pigs, but \x01B~ merely smiled to show teeth filed to points. Then he repeated his challenge.
column2: \x01B~他的同伴吵得足以吵醒猪，但 \x01B~ 只是笑了笑，露出锉成尖的牙齿。接着他重复了自己的挑战。

column1: Refuse the challenge; escort \x01B~ off the tula.
column2: 拒绝挑战；护送 \x01B~ 离开图拉领地。

column1: “You are not a proper Orlanthi warrior and have no right to challenge us to a duel.”
column2: “你不是一个正统的奥兰西战士，没有权利向我们挑战决斗。”

column1: We told the duck that he was not a proper Orlanthi warrior and had no right to challenge us to a duel. He laughed at us and insulted us.
column2: 我们告诉那只鸭人，他并不算个正宗的奥兰斯战士，没资格向我们发起决斗。他嘲笑并侮辱了我们。

column1: \x01B~ laughed at us. “No fur, no feathers, no brains. Maybe you should be asking your Humakti whether I’m a fit champion, they may be the only people in this whole diseased nest with any honor.”
column2: \x01B~ 嘲笑我们。“没毛没羽没脑子。也许你们该去问问你们的胡马克特，看我算不算个称职的冠军——这整个败坏巢穴里，可能就他们还剩下点荣誉。”

column1: How can we make this fair? Fight left-handed? With our legs tied together?
column2: 我们怎么才能让这公平点？用左手打？把腿绑起来？

column1: Well, he’s carrying enough swords to be a real Humakti.
column2: 嗯，他带的剑足够多，倒像个真正的胡马克特。

column1: \x01B~ is a warrior, and a Humakti. He should not be taken lightly.
column2: \x01B~ 是个战士，也是个胡马克特。不可小觑。

column1: He has no right to challenge us in this fashion. Get him out of here before I laugh again and hurt myself.
column2: 他没资格以这种方式挑战我们。把他赶出去，免得我又笑岔了气。

column1: He has every right to challenge us. We have every right to accept the challenge as we see fit.
column2: 他完全有资格挑战我们。我们也完全有权按自己意愿接受挑战。

column1: This duck has a strange look in his eyes. He’s not going to turn away without a fight.
column2: 这只鸭人眼神古怪。他不会不打就走的。

column1: He’s a Humakti Deathlord on a heroquest. This is going to end in death.
column2: 他是一位踏上英雄追寻的胡马克特死亡领主。此事终将招致死亡。

column1: It’s not like the ducks have ever helped us against the elves.
column2: 鸭人可从来没帮我们对付过精灵。

column1: Is there no way to make peace with this great foe of the undead?
column2: 难道就没有办法与这位亡灵的大敌和解吗？

column1: What do you call a duck hero? A suicide that tastes good in sauce!
column2: 管一个鸭人英雄叫什么？蘸酱味道不错的自杀者！

column1: Look at all those swords! Something bad will come of this.
column2: 看看那些刀剑！准没好事。

column1: His challenge requires a fight to the death. I will be honored to accept.
column2: 他的挑战要求拼死一战。我很荣幸接受。

column1: He deserves respect. But there is no need for anyone to die.
column2: 他值得尊敬，但没必要让任何人死。

column1: Clearly the ducks have some great warriors.
column2: 显然鸭人中有一些了不起的战士。

column1: The ducks of the Upland Marsh are great zombie fighters. Any Deathlord of Humakt is even better.
column2: 高地沼泽的鸭人是优秀的僵尸斗士，而胡马克特的任何一位死亡领主则更胜一筹。

column1: I told you the Ducks were getting too feisty for their own good.
column2: 我早说过那些鸭人越来越不安分，这对他们自己没好处。

column1: Oh please, let me entertain this visiting dignitary, oh please, oh please…
column2: 噢求你了，让我来招待这位来访的大人物吧，噢求你了，噢求你了……

column1: Aaaaaarh! Let me at him!
column2: 啊啊啊啊啊！让我去会会他！

column1: After we kill this pipsqueak, I think it’s time to raid the ducks.
column2: 干掉这个小不点之后，我觉得该去抢掠鸭人了。

column1: Arrange suitable marriages with surviving bachelors.
column2: 安排幸存的单身汉结下合适的婚姻。

column1: The clan ring arranged marriages between widows and the clan’s surviving bachelors.
column2: 氏族议会为寡妇和氏族幸存的单身汉安排了婚姻。

column1: Sadly, several of the new marriages, were not quite suitable, and it was difficult to say whether they would last long enough to matter.
column2: 可悲的是，有几桩新婚姻并不太合适，很难说它们能否长久到产生影响。

column1: The ring attempted to arrange suitable marriages with the clan’s surviving bachelors.
column2: 长老会试图与氏族幸存的单身汉安排合适的婚姻。

column1: “There are not enough men to provide half of us with husbands, much less husbands of substance \x02\x03whose looks wouldn’t curdle milk/who aren’t bitter old wretches/who know the difference between a plow and a drinking horn\x02.”
column2: “没有足够的男人给我们一半人提供丈夫，更别说那些 \x02\x03长相不至于让牛奶变酸的/不是苦涩的老家伙/分得清犁和饮酒角的\x02有分量的丈夫了。”

column1: Ask the women to be patient.
column2: 让女人们耐心等待。

column1: Authorize women to temporarily form joint households.
column2: 授权女人们临时组成联合家庭。

column1: Although it was unorthodox, the women agreed that the best way to hold their families together within the clan was to form joint households until the clan could attract more men.
column2: 尽管不合常规，女人们还是同意，在氏族能吸引更多男人之前，维系家族团结的最好方式就是组成联合家庭。

column1: The ring suggested that the women form joint households until the clan could attract more men.
column2: 长老会建议女人们组成联合家庭，直到氏族能吸引更多男人。

column1: The women said they wanted men, not to live with other women.
column2: 女人们说她们要的是男人，不是和其他女人住在一起。

column1: “Just be thankful that we’ve kept you and your children safe.”
column2: “知足吧，我们保住了你和孩子们的安全。”

column1: The ring told the women to be thankful for what they had.
column2: 长老会告诉女人们要对自己拥有的心怀感激。

column1: Send \x01@\x1A to the Holy Country seeking former kinsmen.
column2: 派遣 \x01@\x1A 前往圣国寻找昔日的族人。

column1: It was agreed that \x01@\x1A would travel to the clan’s old home and inquire whether any bachelors from our old clan wished to join
column2: 大家同意 \x01@\x1A 将前往氏族旧居，询问我们旧氏族是否有单身汉愿意加入

column1: us.
column2: 我们。

column1: us in the north with a gift of land and a starter herd.
column2: 我们在北方，带着土地和起始畜群的礼物。

column1: “We will only bring back brave young men, men who were too young to leave the first time and will relish the chance for freedom now.”
column2: “我们只会带回勇敢的年轻人，那些第一次离开时太年轻、如今渴望自由机会的人。”

column1: The women were mollified. It was agreed that \x01@\x1A would travel to the clan’s old home and inquire whether bachelors from our old clan wished to join us in the north with a gift of land and a starter herd.
column2: 女人们被安抚了。大家同意 \x01@\x1A 将前往氏族旧居，询问我们旧氏族是否有单身汉愿意带着土地和起始畜群的礼物加入我们在北方的队伍。

column1: The women were shamed by the ring’s response, and agreed that sending to the Holy Land might be a good way of attracting new clansmen.
column2: 女人们因长老会的回应感到羞愧，并同意派往圣地可能是吸引新氏族成员的好办法。

column1: The ring determined to send to the Holy Country to find former clansmen willing to come north. The women complained and said they did not wish to marry cowards, but the ring shamed them for their harshness and sent \x01@\x1A to the south.
column2: 长老会决定派人前往圣国寻找愿意北上的旧族人。女人们抱怨说她们不想嫁给懦夫，但长老会以她们的刻薄为耻，并派遣 \x01@\x1A 南下。

column1: The ring determined to send to the Holy Country to find former clansmen willing to come north. The women complained and said they did not wish to marry cowards, and had no shame when the ring chastised them for their harshness.
column2: 长老会决定派人前往圣国寻找愿意北上的旧族人。女人们抱怨说她们不想嫁给懦夫，并且当长老会指责她们刻薄时毫无悔意。

column1: Sponsor a Marriage Contest to draw men from other clans.
column2: 举办一场婚姻竞赛，以吸引其他氏族的男人。

column1: The ring suggested a Marriage Contest.
column2: 长老会提议举办婚姻竞赛。

column1: The women agreed, and we held a merry contest for bachelors from all over Dragon Pass.
column2: 女人们同意了，我们为龙之隘口各地的单身汉举办了一场欢乐的竞赛。

column1: The widows agreed.
column2: 寡妇们同意了。

column1: “Games are all very well, but we wish to marry men, not boys who play games.”

column1: If we don’t warn them away, these dwarfs will keep coming back.
column2: 如果我们不警告他们离开，这些矮人会不断回来。

column1: The leader cleared his throat four times and stuttered something we could not understand. He cocked his head sideways. The dwarfs spun around and marched outside the hall. Then the leader fired his crossbow at a child and we had to attack them.
column2: 首领清了四次嗓子，结巴着说了些我们听不懂的话。他歪了歪头。矮人们转身，列队走出大厅。然后首领用弩射向一个孩子，我们只得攻击他们。

column1: We told the dwarfs to leave. They marched outside the hall and attacked our children, so we had to attack them.
column2: 我们叫矮人离开。他们走出大厅，攻击了我们的孩子，所以我们不得不攻击他们。

column1: No one is happy with the new chief, \x01@\x0B. The god-talkers complain that \x06 interferes with rituals, the nobles are not amused by \x04 constant mocking, and the feasting often degenerates into a food fight at \x01@\x0B’s instigation.
column2: 没有人对新酋长 \x01@\x0B满意。神言者抱怨 \x06 干扰仪式，贵族们对 \x04 的持续嘲弄感到不悦，宴饮也常在 \x01@\x0B的煽动下沦为食物大战。

column1: Everyone agrees that we are in danger of being the laughingstock of this new land.
column2: 大家都同意，我们有成为这片新土地笑柄的危险。

column1: For once the carls and the weaponthanes agree: they all despise what the chief, \x01@\x0B, has been up to. The carls complain that \x06 scares the cattle, and are tired of finding \x01@\x0B in a drunken stupor in the grain bins. The warriors are fed up with \x04 making fun of them during training. Worse, \x06 wants them to line up for battle by height. They wonder when we will have a chief who acts like a chief.
column2: 这一次自由民和武器领主意见一致：他们都鄙视族长， \x01@\x0B，的所作所为。自由民抱怨 \x06 吓到了牛群，而且受够了在粮仓里发现烂醉如泥的 \x01@\x0B 。战士们受够了 \x04 在训练时取笑他们。更糟的是， \x06 想让他们按身高排队作战。他们想知道我们什么时候才能有一个像样子的族长。

column1: A group of carls comes to the ring to protest the chief, with warriors and others crowding behind them. “We cannot serve such a worthless and capricious chief,” their leader says. “\x01@\x0B is courting feuds on all sides with \x04 behavior. Belching at god-talkers from other clans! Fondling visiting nobles! Feeding good beer to the pigs in the clan hall! We speak for the entire clan today, to show you that even the lowliest and slowest to anger are incensed.
column2: 一群自由民来到长老会抗议族长，战士和其他人簇拥在他们身后。“我们无法侍奉这样一个毫无价值且反复无常的族长，”他们的首领说道。“\x01@\x0B 正用 \x04 的行为四处树敌。对着其他氏族的神言者打嗝！抚摸来访的贵族！把好啤酒喂给部族大厅里的猪！今天我们代表整个氏族发言，向你们表明，即使是最卑微、最不易动怒的人也怒火中烧。

column1: Remove \x01@\x0B as chief!”
column2: 罢免 \x01@\x0B 的族长之位！”

column1: Carls complained that the chief’s actions were hurting the clan and the clan’s reputation. They demanded that we ask \x01@\x0B to step down.
column2: 自由民抱怨族长的行为损害了氏族及其声誉。他们要求我们请求 \x01@\x0B 下台。

column1: Try to mollify them with words and livestock.
column2: 尝试用言语和牲畜安抚他们。

column1: The ring spoke about how strange times call for strange leaders, and offered to give some of \x01@\x0B’s cattle to the carls.
column2: 长老会说道非常时期需要非常领袖，并提出将 \x01@\x0B的一些牛只送给自由民。

column1: The carls refused the cows, and the rest of the clan backed them up. Everyone left the hall, leaving \x01@\x0B and the ring alone.
column2: 自由民拒绝了牛只，氏族其他人也支持他们。所有人都离开了大厅，只留下 \x01@\x0B 和长老会。

column1: The ring tried to distract them with soft words and cows, but the carls were not swayed. The entire clan supported them.
column2: 长老会试图用温和的话语和牛只转移他们的注意力，但自由民不为所动。整个氏族都支持他们。

column1: Demand that they honor the ring and the chief.
column2: 要求他们尊重长老会和族长。

column1: The ring insisted that they had the right of tradition and that \x01@\x0B’s actions were acceptable, if odd or inconvenient, because \x06 was chief.
column2: 长老会坚持他们拥有传统的权利，并且 \x01@\x0B的行为是可以接受的，尽管奇怪或不方便，因为 \x06 是族长。

column1: The carls snorted, the warriors hooted, and they and the rest of the clan left the hall.
column2: 自由民嗤之以鼻，战士起哄，他们和氏族其他人离开了大厅。

column1: The ring demanded honor and respect from the clan, as their customary due. No one believed their arguments.
column2: 长老会要求氏族给予荣誉和尊重，这是他们习俗应得的。没有人相信他们的论点。

column1: Ask for \x01@\x0B’s resignation.
column2: 要求 \x01@\x0B的辞职。

column1: The ring grudgingly agreed that perhaps they made a mistake when they agreed to serve with \x01@\x0B as chief. They woke \x08 from \x04 beery nap, and told \x08 it was time to resign.
column2: 长老会勉强同意，或许他们当初同意与 \x01@\x0B 共同担任酋长是个错误。他们把 \x08 从 \x04 的啤酒酣睡中叫醒，告诉 \x08 该辞职了。

column1: \x01@\x0B burped loudly, swore, then gave a great cackle and bowed. \x05 did not seem too surprised or upset by the ring’s decision.
column2: \x01@\x0B 大声打了个嗝，咒骂着，然后发出一声大笑并鞠了一躬。 \x05 对长老会的决定似乎并不太惊讶或沮丧。

column1: The ring asked \x01@\x0B to step down as chief, and \x06 did so.
column2: 长老会要求 \x01@\x0B 辞去酋长职务， \x06 照做了。

column1: Outlaw \x01@\x0B.
column2: 放逐 \x01@\x0B。

column1: The ring members woke \x01@\x0B from \x04 beery nap, and told \x08 that as of that moment, \x06 was outlawed from the clan.
column2: 长老会成员把 \x01@\x0B 从 \x04 的啤酒酣睡中叫醒，告诉 \x08 从那一刻起， \x06 被氏族放逐了。

column1: \x01@\x0B tried to argue that, as chief, \x06 could extend protection to \x08self. \x05 kept up \x04 argument while the weaponthanes escorted \x08 to the edge of the tula.
column2: \x01@\x0B 试图争辩说，作为酋长， \x06 可以为 \x08自己提供保护。 \x05 一直进行着 \x04 争辩，同时武器领主们护送 \x08 到图拉领地边缘。

column1: Now that \x01@\x0B is outlawed, do you kill \x08?
column2: 既然 \x01@\x0B 已被放逐，你要杀死 \x08吗？

column1: Who kills \x01@\x0B?
column2: 谁来杀死 \x01@\x0B？

column1: The clan wondered if \x01@\x0B would go to some other clan and cause us grief from there.
column2: 氏族怀疑 \x01@\x0B 是否会投靠其他氏族，给我们带来麻烦。

column1: Everyone was glad to see \x08 gone, but said it would be better if we’d killed \x08.
column2: 大家都乐见 \x08 离去，但表示如果我们当初杀死了 \x08会更好。

column1: Apologize for poor leadership, offer to replace the entire ring.
column2: 为糟糕的领导道歉，提议更换整个长老会。

column1: The ring members woke \x01@\x0B from \x04 beery nap and told \x08 that \x06 and the entire ring were resigning.
column2: 长老会成员把 \x01@\x0B 从 \x04 的啤酒酣睡中叫醒，告诉 \x08  \x06 和整个长老会都将辞职。

column1: The entire ring, including \x01@\x0B, resigned.
column2: 整个长老会，包括 \x01@\x0B，都辞职了。

column1: \x01@\x0B belched loudly, then declared that \x06 and the ring could now have a “really fine drinking spree.” The former ring members carried \x01@\x0B out of the hall and dumped \x08 in a ditch.
column2: \x01@\x0B 大声打了个嗝，然后宣布 \x06 和长老会现在可以“好好畅饮一番”。前任长老会成员把 \x01@\x0B 抬出大厅，扔进了 \x08 沟里。

column1: They are upset, but are they so upset that kind words and cattle will not turn their hearts?
column2: 他们很难过，但难道难过到好言相劝和牛群也无法挽回他们的心吗？

column1: If we are ever to regain the respect of other clans, we must outlaw \x01@\x0B.
column2: 如果我们想要重获其他氏族的尊重，就必须放逐 \x01@\x0B。

column1: We must remove \x01@\x0B from the ring, if not outlaw \x08 completely.
column2: 我们必须将 \x01@\x0B 从长老会中移除，如果不完全放逐 \x08 的话。

column1: The people should remember their obligation to respect their leaders, even when the leaders are difficult.
column2: 人民应铭记尊重领袖的义务，即使领袖难以相处。

column1: Their concerns are not unjustified. Replacing the chief could restore their respect for us.
column2: 他们的担忧并非没有道理。更换酋长或许能恢复他们对我们的尊重。

column1: Their concerns are justified. We should be ashamed that we let matters decline to this point.
column2: 他们的担忧是有道理的。我们应该为自己让事情恶化到这种地步而感到羞愧。

column1: Their claims are justified. We have failed in our obligations to the clan, and should make way for leaders that the clan can trust.
column2: 他们的主张是正当的。我们对氏族未尽义务，应为氏族可信赖的首领让路。

column1: Shaming them is risky, but it might work.
column2: 羞辱他们风险很大，但也许能奏效。

column1: An apology will help, but getting rid of \x01@\x0B will do the most good.
column2: 道歉会有帮助，但除掉 \x01@\x0B 是最有益的。

column1: If we really want the respect of the clan, we must step down and let new people lead the way.
column2: 若我们真想赢得氏族的尊重，就必须退位，让新人引领前路。

column1: It is true that the livestock are easily spooked these days.
column2: 牲畜如今确实容易受惊。

column1: When the warriors and the carls unite against the ring, how can we argue?
column2: 当武士与自由民联合对抗长老会，我们如何争辩？

column1: The weaponthanes want to fight for someone they can respect.
column2: 武器领主希望为他们敬重的人而战。

column1: A grave error needs a grave solution.
column2: 严重的错误需要严厉的解决办法。

column1: Snort! Wha-a - snore.
column2: 哼！呼啊——呼噜。

column1: You could have made me chief, you know.
column2: 你本可以让我做酋长的，你知道的。

column1: I knew that this \x01@\x0B would bring us nothing but trouble.
column2: 我早知这 \x01@\x0B 只会给我们带来麻烦。

column1: All must resign.
column2: 所有人都必须辞职。

column1: Yes, we must remove \x01@\x0B as chief, but gently.
column2: 是的，我们必须罢免 \x01@\x0B 的酋长之位，但要温和。

column1: Carl agrees with weaponthane? Noble unites with priest? Strange bedfellows in strange times!
column2: 自由民赞同武器领主？贵族与祭司结盟？乱世出奇侣！

column1: How embarrassing. We must all resign.
column2: 真难堪。我们都得辞职。

column1: No one in the clan will speak to the ring about any matter whatsoever. After our failure to remove the chief, they have given up on the clan ring. Our kinsmen avert their eyes when they pass us, and pretend not to hear us when we call to them. The soldiers direct themselves, as do our crafts people and farmers. Though \x01@\x0B seems unaffected by this turn of events, I find it hard to lead a clan that acts as if I am a ghost!
column2: 氏族中无人愿与长老会谈论任何事务。我们未能罢免酋长后，他们已对氏族议会死心。族人路过我们时移开目光，我们呼唤他们时装作听不见。士兵自行指挥，工匠与农夫亦是如此。虽然 \x01@\x0B 似乎不受此事影响，但我很难领导一个视我如鬼魂的氏族！

column1: sceneR032
column2: sceneR032

column1: The renowned prophet, Einarth Milk-Eyes, wanders onto the tula and into the clan hall.
column2: 著名先知艾纳斯·奶眼，漫游至图拉领地，步入部族大厅。

column1: “I see before me a tribe, a tribe with a journey to make. The path will be cleared by homage to
column2: “我眼前是一个部落，一个要踏上旅程的部落。道路将因向……致敬而畅通

column1: Einarth Milk-Eyes came to us with a prophecy that seemed to mean we must reenact our main deity’s heroquest, and six others.
column2: 艾纳斯·奶眼带来一个预言，意为我们必须重演主神的英雄探索，以及其他六位神祇的。

column1: “I see before me a clan, a clan that will take its tribe on a journey. First, this clan must become the head of the tribe. Then the path will be cleared by homage to
column2: “我眼前是一个氏族，一个将带领其部落踏上旅程的氏族。首先，这个氏族必须成为部落之首。然后道路将因向……致敬而畅通

column1: Einarth Milk-Eyes came to us with a prophecy that seemed to mean we must become king of the tribe, and reenact our main deity’s heroquest, and six others.
column2: 艾纳斯·奶眼带来一个预言，意为我们必须成为部落之王，重演主神的英雄探索，以及其他六位神祇的。

column1: Elmal, treading the steps he has taken before.
column2: 埃尔马尔，踏上他以前走过的步伐。

column1: Ernalda, treading the steps she has taken before.
column2: 埃尔纳尔达，踏上她以前走过的步伐。

column1: Orlanth, treading the steps he has taken before.
column2: 奥兰斯，踏上他以前走过的步伐。

column1: The tribe will travel not alone, but in the company of six other gods. Before the path reaches its end, the wayfarers must visit the god-plane for each of the deities that go with them.
column2: 部落不会独行，而是有六位其他神祇相伴。在道路抵达终点前，旅者必须去往随行每位神祇的神域拜访。

column1: I cannot make out what is at the destination, but it is something new.
column2: 我看不清目的地的景象，但那将是崭新之物。

column1: Ah, I see glory, if these clan halls contain sufficient resolve and courage.”
column2: 啊，我看见了荣耀——只要这些部族大厅拥有足够的决心与勇气。”

column1: ReallyReallyGood
column2: ReallyReallyGood

column1: Honor Einarth with gifts.
column2: 以礼物尊崇艾纳斯。

column1: We were pleased to honor Einarth with gifts.
column2: 我们很高兴以礼物尊崇了艾纳斯。

column1: How much do you give him?
column2: 你给他多少？

column1: Einarth said that our generosity was a first step on our new path, and gave us his blessing before wandering off again.
column2: 艾纳斯说我们的慷慨是新道路上的第一步，并在再次云游之前赐予我们祝福。

column1: Throw a feast to celebrate.
column2: 举办宴会庆祝。

column1: He toasted our generosity, and said that this confirmed the prophecy. Our people made merry, and toasted Einarth and the clan ring.
column2: 他为我们的慷慨祝酒，并说这证实了预言。我们的人民尽情欢乐，向艾纳斯和氏族议会祝酒。

column1: Thank Einarth for bringing us his prophecy.
column2: 感谢艾纳斯为我们带来他的预言。

column1: We thanked him for giving us his vision. The people were displeased that we did nothing special to honor him.
column2: 我们感谢他赐予我们他的异象。人民对我们未做特别之事尊崇他感到不满。

column1: Embark on the “Elmal Guards the Stead” heroquest right away.
column2: 立即启程进行“埃尔马尔守护农庄”英雄探索。

column1: The people were elated that we gained Elmal’s blessing so quickly.
column2: 人民因我们如此迅速获得埃尔马尔的祝福而兴高采烈。

column1: The people said that this meant we were dazzled by the prophet’s vision, and must strengthen our magic and our reputation before rushing into action again.
column2: 人民说这表明我们被先知的异象冲昏了头脑，必须在再次仓促行动前加强我们的魔法与声望。

column1: Embark on the “Ernalda Feeds the Tribe” heroquest right away.
column2: 立即启程进行“埃尔纳尔达喂养部落”英雄探索。

column1: The people were elated that we gained Ernalda’s blessing so quickly.
column2: 人民因我们如此迅速获得埃尔纳尔达的祝福而兴高采烈。

column1: Embark on the “Orlanth and Aroka” heroquest right away.
column2: 立即启程进行“奥兰斯与阿罗卡”英雄探索。

column1: The people were elated that we gained Orlanth’s blessing so quickly.
column2: 人民因我们如此迅速获得奥兰斯的祝福而兴高采烈。

column1: Ask him for more details of his vision.
column2: 向他询问更多关于他异象的细节。

column1: When we questioned him further, he just smiled and hummed a strange tune.
column2: 我们进一步追问时，他只是微笑，哼着一首奇异的曲调。

column1: Einarth has Seen what can be. It’s up to us to make it so. We must be sure not to disappoint him.
column2: 艾纳斯已预见可能之事。能否实现取决于我们。我们必须确保不让他失望。

column1: We don’t have enough cows to throw a big feast.
column2: 我们没有足够的牛只来举办盛大宴会。

column1: We can spare a few cattle to celebrate this wonderful news.
column2: 我们能匀出几头牲畜来庆祝这个好消息。

column1: We should honor Einarth for making this journey to us.
column2: 我们应当尊崇艾纳斯，因为他长途跋涉来到我们这里。

column1: Gifts are the right way to repay Einarth.
column2: 礼物是回报艾纳斯的正确方式。

column1: We should rejoice at this glad news, for it means we have a glorious future.
column2: 我们应当为这喜讯欢呼，因为它意味着我们有光辉的未来。

column1: Resolve we have; courage we have, Humakt’s blessing would be best.
column2: 我们有决心；我们有勇气，胡马克特的祝福将是最好的。

column1: Of course the first the heroquest we attempt must be Ernalda’s.
column2: 当然，我们尝试的第一个英雄探索必须是埃尔纳尔达的。

column1: We must be sure to honor Ernalda as one of the six deities we choose.
column2: 我们必须确保尊崇埃尔纳尔达为我们选择的六位神祇之一。

column1: The sooner we obtain Elmal’s blessing, the better chance we have of fulfilling this vision.
column2: 我们越早获得埃尔马尔的祝福，实现这个异象的机会就越大。

column1: We cannot leave Elmal behind on this fateful journey. We must include him in our heroquests.
column2: 我们不能在这场命运之旅中把埃尔玛抛在身后。我们必须将他纳入我们的英雄任务。

column1: Orlanth would want us to start with his favor, the sooner the better.
column2: 奥兰斯会希望我们从他的恩惠开始，越快越好。

column1: With a prophecy like this, we cannot afford not to honor Orlanth alongside our main deity.
column2: 面对这样的预言，我们绝不能不在敬奉主神的同时也尊崇奥兰斯。

column1: We must prepare to walk in Humakt’s footsteps.
column2: 我们必须准备踏上休玛克特的足迹。

column1: Why does everyone listen to this white-eyed old beggar, and never listen to me?
column2: 为什么人人都听这个白眼老乞丐的话，却从不听我的？

column1: Thank him, and let him wander on his way.
column2: 感谢他，然后让他继续游历。

column1: From this I see more temples in our future!
column2: 由此我预见我们未来会有更多神庙！

column1: If we heroquest now, the prophecy will come to us sooner. His arrival proves we are ready!
column2: 如果我们现在进行英雄任务，预言就会更快应验。他的到来证明我们已经准备好了！

column1: I told you we were a special clan, and a special tribe, and that Einarth would be back.
column2: 我告诉过你们，我们是一个特殊的氏族，一个特殊的部落，而且艾纳斯会回来的。

column1: This fraud duped us into forming a tribe the last time he was here. Let’s find out what hidden pitfalls lie on this path of his before we walk it.
column2: 上次他来的时候，这个骗子骗我们组成了部落。在走上他的道路之前，我们先弄清楚这条路上藏着什么陷阱。

column1: We really ought to wait before heroquesting, it’s just so risky!
column2: 我们在进行英雄任务前真的该等一等，这实在太冒险了！

column1: We should find out more about these quests — will our male deities be best to honor first?
column2: 我们应该进一步了解这些任务——是否最好先尊崇我们的男性神祇？

column1: We should find out more about these quests — will our goddesses be best to honor first?
column2: 我们应该进一步了解这些任务——是否最好先尊崇我们的女神？

column1: That poor old man has travelled far again for us. We must do something for him.
column2: 那位可怜的老人又为我们远道而来。我们必须为他做点什么。

column1: We must be generous, and maintain our kingship.

column2: 他们免费向我们提供这符咒。当被问及原因时，较年轻的萨满说：“我大半生以来一直听闻谣言，说你们的部落注定要成就伟大。也许这符咒能帮助你们加快脚步，以便活出你们的命运。”

column2: 我们收到了流浪灵语者提供的魔法符咒，作为催促我们响应艾纳斯·奶眼预言的手段。

column2: 灵语者们出现并责备我们尚未实现艾纳斯·奶眼的预言。

column2: 年长的灵语者说：“你们将来会看到远比这更扰人的事物，而你们自己才会感到怪异！”

column2: 人们对我们赶走他们感到愤怒，更因他们话语的真实而愈加愤怒。

column1: “What do you mean by this?”
column2: “你这是什么意思？”

column2: 他耸耸肩咕哝道：“你们甚至连王都还不是。但谁知道呢？也许你们终究不是预言之中的部落。”

column2: 我们接受了符咒并回赠了实物礼物。

column2: 年长的灵语者跳了一支舞，往手掌里吐了口唾沫，然后看着太阳。他说：“倾听符咒。好好听！”

column1: The people were not sure what to make of this, but hoped that the ring would at least listen to the shaman, if not the charm.
column2: 人们不确定该如何理解这件事，但希望长老会至少能听萨满的话，即便不听符咒的。

column1: “Sell us your potion.”
column2: “把你们的药水卖给我们。”

column1: We asked them to sell us the potion.
column2: 我们请他们把药水卖给我们。

column2: 年长的灵语者转了一圈，舔湿手指举到空中。他说：“那要花掉你们价值 \x01@\x19 头牛的银子。”

column1: They gave the potion to the clan ring, who drank it down. Then the spirit-talkers packed up and left. Some of the ring felt a bit queasy for a few hours, but no one became ill.
column2: 他们把药水交给氏族议会，后者喝了下去。然后灵语者们收拾东西离开了。议会中有几个人有几个小时感到有点恶心，但没有人因此生病。

column1: The people watched and whispered, expecting to hear some kind of announcement soon.
column2: 人们看着并低声议论，期待很快听到某种宣告。

column1: We changed our minds when we learned how high their price was.

column1: The people were a little disappointed that they did not get to see the clan ring transformed by the potion.
column2: 人们有点失望，因为他们没看到氏族议会因药水而发生变化。

column1: We had to change our minds when we learned how high their price was.
column2: 当得知他们的要价有多高时，我们不得不改变主意。

column1: “We will seek our destiny in our way, at our own pace.”
column2: “我们将以自己的方式、自己的步调寻求命运。”

column1: We told them that we would find our destiny in our own way, at our own pace.
column2: 我们告诉他们，我们会以自己的方式、自己的步调找到命运。

column1: Some of the people were cheered that the ring wasn’t goaded by the shaman’s chiding, but the rest muttered that our way seemed to be through brambles, and our pace was that of a snail.
column2: 得知长老会并未被萨满的训斥所激怒，有些人松了口气，但剩下的人却抱怨说我们的前路似乎荆棘丛生，步伐也如蜗牛般缓慢。

column1: Many in the clan wondered if the leaders knew the path, and said that we were moving too slowly to grasp the ring of fate.
column2: 氏族中许多人怀疑首领们是否认得路径，并说我们行动太慢，抓不住命运之环。

column1: “We do not need your spirit-talker gossip, but we shall feed you anyway, as befits Orlanthi generosity.”
column2: “我们不需要你们的灵语者闲话，但无论如何我们会招待你们吃喝，如同奥兰斯人的慷慨之道。”

column1: We chided them in return, but gave them hospitality before they left.
column2: 我们反过来斥责了他们，但在他们离开前仍然提供了款待。

column2: 灵语者们吃得足够三人份，但继续说着阴阳怪气的话，直到他们离去。人们很高兴看到他们离开。

column1: We did not listen to their comments, but gave them hospitality.
column2: 我们没有理会他们的话，但还是给了他们款待。

column1: The old one ate as much as the younger, who ate enough for three. They thanked us for our generosity.
column2: 那位年长者吃得和年轻人一样多，而年轻人则吃了三人份。他们感谢了我们的慷慨。

column1: “Thank you, we need no magic items, but will bear what you say in our hearts, and feed you before you go.”
column2: “多谢，我们不需要魔法物品，但会将你们的话语铭记在心，并在你们离开前招待你们吃喝。”

column1: We promised to consider what they said and gave them hospitality before they left.

column1: The spirit-talkers ate enough for three. They thanked us for our generosity.

column1: We could afford to buy the potion. Or we could just heed their warning.

column2: 我们付不起钱向他们买那瓶药剂。而且我们也没办法知道它是否有效。

column1: Something for free? Tempting, but will we get what we pay for?
column2: 白送的东西？很诱人，但我们能得到物有所值的东西吗？

column1: They are not like us, yet not unlike us.
column2: 他们与我们不同，却又并非全然不同。

column2: 他们又来嘲笑我们的习惯了？把他们打发走！

column1: The heart-heard hard-truth shakes the stead-beams.
column2: 那发自肺腑的严酷真相，撼动了厅堂的梁柱。

column1: I could’ve told you we were lax and lazy in pursuing our glory. But I was napping in the pigsty.

column1: Yes! They see our problem clearly. We must act quickly or destiny will pass over us like a summer cloud!

column2: 我跟你们说过，我们应该更常进行英雄任务。

column2: 我跟你们说过，我们本应努力成为王。

column1: We will do what we want, when we want, without prompting from raggedy spirit-men.
column2: 我们想做什么就做什么，想什么时候做就什么时候做，用不着那些衣衫褴褛的灵人来指手画脚。

column1: They are laughing at us! Does this mean we’ve failed in some way?
column2: 他们在嘲笑我们！这是否意味着我们在某方面做错了？

column2: 这些可怜人一路赶来，就只是为了警告我们。我们必须善待他们。

column1: What are we waiting for?
column2: 我们还在等什么？

column2: 按习俗，他们欠我们的人情价值二十头牛。

column2: 如果我们慷慨，将来更容易和他们讨价还价。

column1: If we give him more than he asks, we will maintain our reputation for generosity, which will help us lead the tribe.

column1: We must show by example how a tribe supports its members.

column1: \x01@\x03 is very pious, the gods smile upon \x08 every day.
column2: \x01@\x03 非常虔诚，诸神每天都对 \x08 微笑。

column1: \x01@\x03 is said to have a set of scales next to \x04 high seat, so that \x06 can weigh out gifts.
column2: \x01@\x03 据说在 \x04 高座旁放有一副天平，以便 \x06 可以称量礼物。

column1: \x01@\x03 is as generous as any other chief.
column2: \x01@\x03 和任何其他首领一样慷慨。

column1: Just tell him what we think of him, as if we were speaking about \x01@\x03.
column2: 直接告诉他我们对他怎么想，就好像我们在谈论 \x01@\x03一样。

column1: Just tell him any old thing. I’ll roll the dice to determine our answer.
column2: 随便告诉他点什么。我会掷骰子来决定我们的回答。

column1: Don’t tell him anything about \x01@\x03 — give him information about another chief instead.
column2: 不要告诉他任何关于 \x01@\x03 的事——而是给他另一位酋长的情报。

column1: If we \x02\x03are wrong/give misleading information/say the wrong thing\x02, we’ll be in trouble.
column2: 如果我们 \x02\x03犯错/提供误导信息/说错话\x02，我们就会遇到麻烦。

column1: Our information about \x01@\x03 might be \x02\x03out of date/influenced by our enemies/wrong\x02.
column2: 我们关于 \x01@\x03 的情报可能 \x02\x03过时/受到敌人影响/有误\x02。

column1: Does \x01@\x01 think we are as \x02\x04insidious/gossipy/back-biting/mealy-mouthed\x02 as he is?
column2: \x01@\x01 是否认为我们和他一样 \x02\x04阴险/爱说闲话/背后中伤/花言巧语\x02 ？

column1: Not asking for cows? Not asking for food, or goods? What a \x02\x03wonderful way/great chance/perfect means\x02 to gather a favor for nothing!
column2: 不是要牛？不是要食物或货物？多么 \x02\x03好办法/好机会/绝佳手段\x02 来轻松获得一份恩惠！

column1: The best gift of all is… well, a gift.
column2: 所有礼物中最棒的……嗯，就是礼物本身。
