column2: sceneR454

column1: He reminds you that as tribe-mates, clans can share their knowledge and each become stronger.
column2: 他提醒你，作为同族，氏族之间可以分享知识，让彼此都变得更强大。

column1: Just make up the details.
column2: 把细节编出来就行。

column1: Instead of telling him the truth, we invented new details.
column2: 我们没有告诉他真相，而是编造了新的细节。

column1: We didn’t know the details, so we just made them up.
column2: 我们不知道那些细节，所以就编了一套。

column1: He thanked us and departed.
column2: 他道谢后便离开了。

column1: They shuddered at the loss of our good name, should this story get known by the rest of the tribe.
column2: 他们担心，若是这个故事被氏族其他人知晓，我们会名誉扫地。

column1: Offer him details of another story instead.
column2: 把另一个故事的细节告诉他吧。

column1: We offered him the details of another story instead.
column2: 我们便把另一个故事的细节告诉了他。

column1: Tell him what he wants to know.
column2: 告诉他他想知道的事。

column1: We told him what he wanted to know.
column2: 我们告诉了他他想知道的事。

column1: “We don’t know these details.”
column2: “我们不知道这些细节。”

column1: We told him we did not have the knowledge he sought.
column2: 我们告诉他，我们没有他想要的知识。

column1: He said he was sorry to have bothered us, and left. The people laughed and made sport of him after his departure, for of course we did know the secrets he wanted.
column2: 他说抱歉打扰了我们，然后离开了。他走后，人们嘲笑戏弄他，因为我们当然知道他想要的秘密。

column1: He accused us of lying and departed in anger, saying that all of Dragon Pass would know that membership in our tribe counted for naught.
column2: 他指责我们撒谎，愤怒地离开了，说整个龙口之地都会知道加入我们氏族毫无价值。

column1: He said he was sorry to have bothered us, and left. The people were sad that he made a journey for nought, for we did not know the secrets he wanted.
column2: 他说抱歉打扰了我们，然后离开了。人们为他白跑一趟感到难过，因为我们不知道他想要的秘密。

column1: “We know, but we’re not going to tell you.”
column2: “我们知道，但我们不会告诉你。”

column1: We said to him, “We know, but we’re not going to tell you.”
column2: 我们对他说：“我们知道，但我们不会告诉你。”

column1: He turned purple and departed in anger, saying that all of Dragon Pass would know that membership in our tribe counted for nothing.
column2: 他脸色发紫，愤怒地离开了，说整个龙口之地都会知道加入我们氏族毫无价值。

column1: Better to tell them stories than to have to give them cows.
column2: 与其给他们牛，不如给他们讲故事。

column1: It costs us nothing to tell a sacred secret.
column2: 讲述一个神圣的秘密对我们来说毫无代价。

column1: Too bad this is not a story we know, or we could profit for nothing.
column2: 可惜这不是我们知道的故事，否则我们就能不劳而获。

column1: Secrets will help them prosper on the god-plane, and they may bring back powerful weapons. Make sure they stay our friends, in or out of the tribe.
column2: 秘密会帮助他们在神域繁荣，他们可能带回强大的武器。确保他们一直是我们的朋友，无论是否在氏族内。

column1: Secrets will help them prosper on the god-plane, and they may bring back powerful weapons. They do not like us, and could use these weapons against us.
column2: 秘密会帮助他们在神域繁荣，他们可能带回强大的武器。他们不喜欢我们，可能会用这些武器对付我们。

column1: We can ask them for a similar favor in the future.
column2: 我们日后可以请求他们给予类似的恩惠。

column1: We need not grant them exactly the favor they request.
column2: 我们不必完全答应他们所请求的恩惠。

column1: This is a good opportunity to improve support from one of the least loyal clans.
column2: 这是提升一个最不忠诚的氏族支持的好机会。

column1: I don’t think the gods will appreciate lies told about them, even harmless little fibs.
column2: 我不认为众神会喜欢关于他们的谎言，即便是无害的小谎。

column1: If we tell lies about the gods, our clan magic will suffer. We don’t have to share our knowledge, though.
column2: 如果我们编造关于众神的谎言，我们的氏族魔法就会受损。不过，我们不必分享我们的知识。

column1: We don’t know the secrets of that myth, but if we tell lies about the gods, our clan magic will suffer.
column2: 我们不知道那个神话的秘密，但如果我们编造关于众神的谎言，我们的氏族魔法就会受损。

column1: The more favors they owe us, the more generous we appear to be.
column2: 他们欠我们的恩惠越多，我们显得越慷慨。

column1: The more favors they owe us, the more they may support us the next time we need a new king.
column2: 他们欠我们的恩惠越多，下次我们选新王时，他们就越可能支持我们。

column1: If we \x02\x03must deny him/say no to him/do refuse him\x02, we should at least \x02\x02do so honestly/be forthright about it\x02.
column2: 如果我们 \x02\x03必须拒绝他/对他说不/必须拒绝他\x02，我们至少应该 \x02\x02诚实以对/坦率相告\x02。

column1: Secret stories of the gods bring power to those who know them.
column2: 众神的秘事能给知晓者带来力量。

column1: When Bad King Urgrain was denied the secrets of a myth, he tried to beat it out of the thane who denied him. Then Bad King Urgrain forgot what little he knew about that myth to begin with.
column2: 当恶王乌格兰被拒绝得知一个神话的秘密时，他试图从拒绝他的领主口中逼问出来。然后，恶王乌格兰连自己原本所知的那一点点也忘记了。

column1: The secrets of myths are powerful tools, whether they are in the right hands or not.
column2: 神话的秘密是强有力的工具，无论落入谁的手中。

column1: Let me tell the secret — I can bamboozle them with made-up detail so they never know the difference.
column2: 让我来说出秘密——我可以用编造的细节糊弄他们，让他们永远看不出破绽。

column1: Let me tell them my “Eurmal Takes A Bath” secrets!
column2: 让我告诉他们我“尤尔马尔洗澡”的秘密！

column1: First, tell them that they must paint their faces green and recite gibberish before we can let them in on the secret. Then, when they do this, refuse them.
column2: 首先，告诉他们必须把脸涂绿并胡言乱语，我们才能让他们知道秘密。然后，等他们照做后，拒绝他们。

column1: They are telling their tale of woe to any other clan in the tribe who will listen.
column2: 他们正对着部落里任何愿意听的氏族诉说着他们的悲惨遭遇。

column1: \x01@\x01, a thane of the \x01@! clan, asks you for a gift of luck and divine favor on behalf of his people.
column2: \x01@\x01 \x01@! 氏族的一位领主，代表他的人民向你请求一份好运与神圣恩惠的赠礼。

column1: Give him nothing.
column2: 什么也不给他。

column1: We refused his request.
column2: 我们拒绝了他的请求。

column1: \x01@\x01 spat. “What use is a tribe? I will make sure that everyone knows how stingy you are.”
column2: \x01@\x01 吐了一口唾沫。“一个部落有什么用？我一定要让所有人都知道你们有多吝啬。”

column1: Give less than the customary amount.
column2: 给予少于惯例的数量。

column1: We gave less than the customary amount.
column2: 我们给予了少于惯例的数量。

column1: \x01@\x01 was displeased, but did not say anything.
column2: \x01@\x01 很不悦，但什么也没说。

column1: \x01@\x01 grumbled a bit, but did not stop the ritual.
column2: \x01@\x01 嘟囔了几句，但没有中止仪式。

column1: Give more than the customary amount.
column2: 给予多于惯例的数量。

column1: We gave more than the customary amount.
column2: 我们给予了多于惯例的数量。

column1: Give the customary amount.
column2: 给予惯例的数量。

column1: We gave the customary amount.
column2: 我们给予了惯例的数量。

column1: \x01@\x01 said it was good that we honored tribal relations.
column2: \x01@\x01 说我们维护部落关系是好事。

column1: Offer him gifts instead.
column2: 改为赠予他礼物。

column1: We offered him gifts instead.
column2: 我们改为赠予他礼物。

column1: \x01@\x01 was surprised that we lacked magic,
column2: \x01@\x01 对我们没有魔法感到惊讶，

column1: “I would prefer a gift of magic,” \x01@\x01 said.
column2: “我宁愿要一份魔法的赠礼，” \x01@\x01 说道。

column1: \x01@\x01 would have preferred a gift of magic,
column2: \x01@\x01 本来更愿意要一份魔法的赠礼，

column1: “But I suppose that I could find shamans, trade these gifts to them, and receive spiritual power in return. Or I could use these gifts to trade with some other clan for magic, though either is a round-about way of getting the magic we need.”
column2: “但我想我能找到萨满，把这些礼物和他们交易，从而换取灵力。或者我可以用这些礼物与另一个氏族交换魔法，尽管这两种做法都是得到我们所需魔法的迂回方式。”

column1: but he was willing to accept our gifts and owe us a favor for them.
column2: 但他愿意接受我们的礼物，并为此欠我们一个人情。

column1: “Our clan magic is weak right now.”
column2: “我们氏族的魔法现在很弱。”

column1: We replied, “Our clan magic is weak right now.”
column2: 我们回答：“我们氏族的魔法现在很弱。”

column1: \x01@\x01 had some god-talkers with him, and they confirmed what we said.
column2: \x01@\x01 他身边带着几位神言者，他们证实了我们的话。

column1: He said that he was sorry to trouble us, and would ask this favor of some other clan.
column2: 他说他很抱歉打扰我们，会去向其他氏族请求这个恩惠。

column1: \x01@\x01 had some god-talkers with him, and they did not believe us.
column2: \x01@\x01 他身边带着几位神言者，他们不相信我们的话。

column1: \x01@\x01 accused us of lying, and said, “I promise that the whole tribe will know what cheats you are!”
column2: \x01@\x01 指责我们撒谎，并说：“我保证整个部落都会知道你们是什么骗子！”

column1: Our herds are large. We could offer them cows instead of magic.
column2: 我们的牧群规模很大。我们可以向他们提供牛只代替魔法。

column1: We can better afford to give them trade goods.
column2: 我们更有能力给他们贸易货物。

column1: If we are generous, they will spread our good name throughout the tribe and it will be easier to bargain with everyone in it.
column2: 如果我们慷慨，他们就会在部落中传扬我们的好名声，这样和部落里的每个人讨价还价都会更容易。

column1: We will help them, and they will help us.
column2: 我们将帮助他们，他们也会帮助我们。

column1: When they owe us a favor we will be able to call on them when our magic is low.
column2: 当他们欠我们人情时，我们魔法不足时就能请求他们相助。

column1: We don’t necessarily have to give them exactly what they want, exactly when they want it.
column2: 我们不一定非得在他们想要的时间，给他们想要的精确东西。

column1: Luck and divine favor are not to be lightly given away.
column2: 好运与神圣恩惠不可轻易赠予。

column1: Our clan magic is unusually strong; we can afford to be generous.
column2: 我们氏族的魔法异常强大；我们可以慷慨解囊。

column1: Our clan magic is strong; we can afford to help them.
column2: 我们氏族的魔法强大；我们帮得起他们。

column1: Our clan magic is not so strong; we can’t afford to give them the customary amount.
column2: 我们氏族的魔法没有那么强大；我们无力给予他们惯例的数量。

column1: Our clan magic is already weak; we can’t afford to help them at all.
column2: 我们氏族的魔法已经衰弱；我们根本无力帮助他们。

column1: Our clan magic is strong; we can afford to help them. If we say otherwise, they will know it.
column2: 我们氏族的魔法强大；我们帮得起他们。如果我们反过来说，他们会识破。

column1: Our clan magic is unusually strong; we can afford to be generous. If we say otherwise, they will know it.
column2: 我们氏族的魔法异常强大；我们可以慷慨解囊。如果我们反过来说，他们会识破。

column1: Bad King Urgrain rarely granted favors. And when he did, he asked for payment five time over the original amount, enforced by his weaponthanes.
column2: 恶王乌格兰很少赐予恩惠。即便赐予，他也会要求五倍于原数的回报，并由他的武器领主们强制执行。

column1: When Bad King Urgrain granted favors, he asked for repayment at sword and spear tip.
column2: 恶王乌格兰赐予恩惠时，要求以剑尖和矛尖来偿还。

column1: Bad King Urgrain rarely granted favors. And when he asked for one, he found every gate barred and every sword drawn against him.
column2: 恶王乌格兰很少赐予恩惠。当他向别人请求恩惠时，他发现每扇门都紧闭，每把剑都指向他。

column1: Orlanth granted Biskala the Bee the favor of nesting in his garden. Then Orlanth could give Ernalda sweet fresh honey when he courted her.
column2: 奥兰斯赐予蜜蜂比斯卡拉在他的花园里筑巢的恩惠。于是奥兰斯在向埃尔纳尔达求爱时，就能献上甜美新鲜的蜂蜜。

column1: Ernalda let Mograin the Mouse nest in her shoe one night. And when she found Orlanth cruelly bound in Skipeta’s snares, it was Mograin who chewed through the ropes and set Orlanth free.
column2: 埃尔纳尔达让老鼠莫格兰在她的鞋子里寄宿了一夜。当她发现奥兰斯被斯克佩塔的陷阱残忍地捆绑时，正是莫格兰咬断了绳子，放走了奥兰斯。

column1: Chalana Arroy healed the angry Wasp Queen when her nest fell, and healed all her children. To this day, wasps will not bother a healer.
column2: 查拉娜·阿罗伊在愤怒的黄蜂女王的巢穴坠落后治好了她，并治愈了她所有的孩子。至今，黄蜂不会骚扰治疗者。

column1: Help them; \x02\x02maybe/perhaps\x02 they need the magic \x02\x04for healing their children/for curing their cottars/to perform beneficial rites/to perform rituals of healing\x02.
column2: 帮助他们； \x02\x02也许/可能\x02 他们需要魔法 \x02\x04来治疗他们的孩子/来治愈他们的佃农/来施行有益的仪式/来执行治疗仪式\x02。

column1: I finally figured out \x02\x03what I wanted to say last time, about that other thing/that — that — wait, let me start again/that thing, you know, that I — meant\x02.
column2: 我终于想明白了 \x02\x03我上次想说什么，关于那另一件事/那——那——等等，让我重新开始/那件事，你知道的，就是我——的意思\x02。

column1: \x02\x03Trading favors builds/The exchange of favors fosters/Mutual favors help ensure\x02 peace, and peace is a \x02\x03boon/benefit/blessing\x02 to both parties.
column2: \x02\x03交易恩惠建立/交换恩惠促进/互相恩惠有助于确保\x02 和平，而和平是 \x02\x03福祉/益处/赐福\x02 对双方而言。

column1: We must \x02\x03outshine/surpass/outdo\x02 them in generosity.
column2: 我们必须 \x02\x03超越/胜过/压倒\x02 他们，在慷慨大度上。

column1: sceneR327
column2: sceneR327

column1: Spirits of our most noble ancestors appear in the clan hall, accompanied by ancestral spirits from other clans within our tribe.
column2: 我们最尊贵祖先的灵来到了部族大厅，同行的还有我们部落内其他氏族的祖先之灵。

column1: “You may not realize it, but you are poised to do great honor to this clan and the clans of this tribe. We sense a difference in the air, a change in the way the grasses wave, new omens in the gathering clouds.”
column2: “你们或许尚未察觉，但你们已准备好为这个氏族以及部落中的众氏族赢得莫大荣耀。我们感受到空气中有一丝不同，青草摇曳的方式有了变化，聚拢的云层中也出现了新的征兆。”

column1: They say that we must remember that not all who look like animals are beastfolk.
column2: 他们说，我们必须记住，并非所有外形像兽的都是兽人。

column1: They say that we must remember that not all enemies are forever.
column2: 他们说，我们必须记住，并非所有敌人都是永久的。

column1: “Don’t be afraid of new things. If you succeed in fulfilling your destiny, you will bring renown upon us all. We offer you a blessing to aid you on this path.”
column2: “不要害怕新事物。若你能成功履行你的命运，你将为我们全体带来声名。我们赐你一道祝福，助你走上这条路。”

column1: The spirits of our ancestors appeared and offered us a blessing to help us fulfill our destiny.
column2: 我们祖先的灵显现，赐予我们一道祝福，帮助我们实现命运。

column1: Ask for a blessing on our cattle.
column2: 为我们的牛群祈求祝福。

column1: We asked them for a blessing on our cattle.
column2: 我们为他们为我们的牛群祈求祝福。

column1: “We are pleased to grant it to you,” they said. The room filled with sparkling light and the far-off lowing of cows. The next day, our herders joyfully brought in a herd of cows that appeared on our tula. They had no markings of any other clan, and we added them to our herds.
column2: “我们很乐意赐予你们，”他们说道。房间里充满了闪烁的光芒和远处传来的牛哞声。第二天，我们的牧人欢天喜地地带回一群出现在我们图拉领地上的牛。它们没有任何其他氏族的印记，我们便将它们加入了我们的畜群。

column1: Ask for a blessing on our trade goods.
column2: 为我们的贸易货物祈求祝福。

column1: “Grant us trade goods,” we said.
column2: “赐予我们贸易货物，”我们说道。

column1: “Goods you shall have,” said our ancestors, who then vanished with a crackling sound. When our traders went to check on our supplies, they were elated to see the storehouses bursting with new goods.
column2: “你们会得到货物的，”我们的祖先说道，随后伴随着一声噼啪声消失了。当我们的商人去查看物资时，他们欣喜地看到仓库里堆满了新货物。

column1: Ask for magical blessings.
column2: 祈求魔法祝福。

column1: We asked them for magic.
column2: 我们向他们祈求魔法。

column1: “We are glad to grant you magic,” they said, and faded from view. Our god-talkers reported that our altars fairly glowed with the additional magic.
column2: “我们很高兴赐予你们魔法，”他们说道，然后渐渐隐去。我们神言者报告说，我们的祭坛因这股额外魔法而熠熠生辉。

column1: Thank them and let them decide which blessing they will grace us with.
column2: 感谢他们，并让他们决定将赐予我们何种祝福。

column1: “How will you ever achieve renown if you cannot make a simple decision, where all the choices lie in your favor?” they grumbled.
column2: “如果连这么简单的决定都做不出——所有选择都对你们有利——你们又怎能获得声名？”他们抱怨道。

column1: “And why did we bother to try to bless you when you are so stingy? Still, having ventured this far from Orlanth’s Hall to try and do you good, we will give you some little blessing.”
column2: “而且，既然你们如此吝啬，我们又何必费心从奥兰斯厅远道而来试图祝福你们？不过，既然已经走到这一步，我们还是会给你们一点小小祝福。”

column1: “Still, your generosity and respect towards us gives us some small hope of your success. Take our blessing, and make good with it.”
column2: “不过，你们的慷慨和尊敬让我们对你们的成功还有一丝希望。接受我们的祝福，好好利用它。”

column1: The spirits vanished.
column2: 灵消失了。

column1: The next day, our herders reported finding \x01@\x18 cattle in a glen, cattle without any clan markings on them. We added them to our herds.
column2: 第二天，我们的牧人报告说在一个小山谷里发现了 \x01@\x18 牛，这些牛没有任何氏族印记。我们将它们加入了畜群。

column1: The god-talkers said they felt our magical power grow.
column2: 神言者们说他们感觉到我们的魔法力量在增长。

column1: The next day, our traders found \x01@\x18 cows worth of goods added to the wealth already in our storehouses.
column2: 第二天，我们的商人发现价值 \x01@\x18 牛的货物增加了我们仓库中已有的财富。

column1: Whatever this destiny they are speaking of is, more cows could not possibly hurt us in achieving it.
column2: 无论他们所说的这个命运是什么，更多的牛绝不会妨碍我们实现它。

column1: We have healthy, ample herds, though more cows never hurt a tribe.
column2: 我们拥有健康充足的畜群，不过更多牛对部落总没坏处。

column1: Additional goods will do our tribe good.
column2: 额外的货物将有益于我们的部落。

column1: We can afford to thank them with a sacrifice, if we want to.
column2: 如果我们愿意，我们可以用一次献祭来感谢他们。

column1: Why are they not offering a blessing on weaponthanes? Of course, magic would help us in battle, too.
column2: 他们为什么不为武器领主赐福？当然，魔法在战斗中也对我们有帮助。

column1: It is good to have wise leaders.
column2: 拥有明智的领导者是好事。

column1: A destiny will only shine as brightly as the person it is attached to.
column2: 命运的光彩，取决于它所依附的那个人。

column1: Our clan magic is weak; we must ask them to strengthen it.
column2: 我们的氏族魔法薄弱；我们必须请求他们加强它。

column1: Our clan magic is strong; we should ask for something else.
column2: 我们的氏族魔法强大；我们应该请求别的东西。

column1: If they wanted to choose the blessing, they would not have asked us.
column2: 如果他们想选择祝福，就不会问我们了。

column1: It is never easy to do new things. If I am to lead our tribe to greatness, I could use more wisdom.
column2: 做新事情从来都不容易。如果我要带领我们部落走向伟大，我需要更多的智慧。

column1: Does this destiny include ale? Or feasting? Or dancing?
column2: 这个命运包括麦酒吗？或者宴饮？或者舞蹈？

column1: We will tell of this visit for many generations to come.
column2: 我们将在未来许多代人中讲述这次来访。

column1: I told you our ancestors were watching us.
column2: 我告诉过你我们的祖先在注视着们。

column1: Powerful magic, for battle!
column2: 强大的魔法，用于战斗！

column1: Oh please, wisdom, wisdom, wisdom — for our illustrious king. He will need it.
column2: 哦拜托，智慧，智慧，智慧——给我们杰出的国王。他会需要的。

column1: The queen is wise enough, ask for a practical blessing.
column2: 王后已经足够睿智，请求一个实用的祝福吧。

column1: The king is wise enough, ask for a practical blessing.
column2: 国王已经足够睿智，请求一个实用的祝福吧。

column1: Oh please, wisdom, wisdom, wisdom — for our illustrious queen. She will need it.
column2: 哦拜托，智慧，智慧，智慧——给我们杰出的王后。她会需要的。

column1: Not sp — sp — again! Now … wha — wha —
column2: 别又——又结巴了！现在……什——什——

column1: Destiny implies battle, which implies wounds. Ask for healing magic.
column2: 命运意味着战斗，战斗意味着创伤。请求治愈魔法。

column1: Cattle are the greatness of the clan and the tribe.
column2: 牛群是氏族和部落的伟大所在。

column1: They will be annoyed if we do not choose a blessing.
column2: 如果我们不选择祝福，他们会不高兴的。

column1: Magic will bless every other thing in our lives.
column2: 魔法将祝福我们生活中的一切其他事物。

column1: Ask for magic, to fight Chaos that threatens us.
column2: 请求魔法，以对抗威胁我们的混沌。

column1: Ask for magic, to protect us against the unliving.
column2: 请求魔法，以保护我们免受不死者侵害。

column1: Ask for a practical blessing.
column2: 请求一个实用的祝福。

column1: Maybe the spirits would decide for us.
column2: 或许灵会替我们决定。

column1: Trust in the gods.
column2: 信任神明。

column1: “A child asks mama and papa, a grown up decides for herself.”
column2: “小孩才会问爸爸妈，成年人自己决定。”

column1: A good sacrifice will cheer up our forebears.
column2: 一个好的祭品会让我们的先祖高兴起来。

column1: Cows or goods — ask for things we can count.
column2: 牛或货物——请求我们能数得清的东西。

column1: sceneR457
column2: sceneR457

column1: \x01@\x0E bears gifts for you. “Our clan recently emigrated to Dragon Pass. We cannot remain tribeless if we want to survive. The clans in your tribe are doing well.
column2: \x01@\x0E 为你们带来礼物。“我们的氏族最近迁居到龙隘。要想活下去，就不能没有部落。你们部落里的氏族都过得不错。

column1: \x01@\x0E bears gifts for you. “Our clan has admired your tribe for some time, since we see that your clans are doing well.
column2: \x01@\x0E 为你们带来礼物。“我们的氏族仰慕你们的部落已久，因为我们看到你们的氏族都兴旺发达。

column1: “For our part, we will bring the tribe our renowned skills in crafts, good traders to make your storehouses groan, and farming skills to fatten tribal herds and fields.”
column2: “至于我们，我们将带给氏族我们著名的工艺技能、让你们的仓库满溢的优秀商人，以及让氏族畜群和土地丰饶的农耕技能。”

column1: “For our part, we bring more than a normal share of weaponthanes to defend the tribe. And our fighters are well-known for their fierceness in battle.”
column2: “至于我们，我们带来的武器领主数量远超普通份额，以保卫氏族。我们的战士以战场上的凶猛而闻名。”

column1: “For our part, we bring special knowledge that no other clan has, which can aid the tribe in war or trade.”
column2: “就我们而言，我们带来了其他氏族没有的特殊知识，能在战争或贸易中帮助部落。”

column1: “For our part, we have fine weaponthanes, marriageable young men and women, and will be proud to call ourselves members of your tribe.”
column2: “就我们而言，我们拥有优秀的武器领主、适婚的年轻男女，并且将自豪地称自己为你部落的成员。”

column1: Decline their request.
column2: 拒绝他们的请求。

column1: We declined their request.
column2: 我们拒绝了他们的请求。

column1: They left, unhappy at being denied a chance to join the tribe. They said they hoped we would one day see the merits of their case.
column2: 他们离开了，因被拒绝加入部落而不快。他们说希望我们有一天能看到他们请求的价值。

column1: “It is traditional to offer a treasure to a possible sponsor.”
column2: “向可能的担保人献上宝物是传统习俗。”

column1: We told them: “It is traditional to also offer a treasure to a possible sponsor.”
column2: 我们告诉他们：“向可能的担保人献上宝物同样也是传统习俗。”

column1: Though they hemmed and hawed, they finally agreed to give us a treasure. We gained\x01@\x01\x01@\n from them.
column2: 尽管他们犹豫不决，但最终还是同意给我们一件宝藏。我们从他们那里获得了\x01@\x01\x01@\n。

column1: They said they had offered us enough already.
column2: 他们说他们已经给够我们了。

column1: “While gifts are part of Orlanthi generosity, extortion or bribery are not the Orlanthi way.”
column2: “虽然赠礼是奥兰提慷慨的一部分，但勒索或贿赂并非奥兰提之道。”

column1: Require them to give 5 cows per year to each clan in the tribe.
column2: 要求他们每年向部族中每个氏族进贡5头牛。

column1: We asked them to agree to give 5 cows per year to each clan in the tribe, since they were not in a position to influence the initial tribal agreements.
column2: 我们要求他们同意每年向部族中每个氏族进贡5头牛，因为他们无权影响最初的部族协定。

column1: They agreed to this condition without any argument.
column2: 他们毫无异议地接受了这一条件。

column1: They did not like this requirement at all.
column2: 他们完全不接受这个要求。

column1: Though we explained that most clans of the tribe both received from and gave to other clans in the tribe as part of our tribal founding agreements, they felt that we were trying to take advantage of them.
column2: 尽管我们解释过，作为部族建立协定的一部分，部族中大多数氏族既从其他氏族收取也向其他氏族给予，他们仍然觉得我们是在占他们便宜。

column1: They withdrew their request and departed.
column2: 他们撤回请求，随后离开了。

column1: Require them to give magical support to the tribal ceremonies every year.
column2: 要求他们每年为部族仪式提供魔法支持。

column1: We asked them to agree to give magical support to the tribal ceremonies every year, since they were not in a position to influence the initial tribal agreements.
column2: 我们要求他们同意每年为部落仪式提供魔法支持，因为他们无法影响最初的部族协定。

column1: Offer to speak for them at the moot.
column2: 提议在议会上为他们发言。

column1: We offered to speak for them at the moot.
column2: 我们提议在议会上为他们发言。

column1: They balked at the size of the gifts we suggested, and withdrew their request. “You don’t wish to sponsor us,” they scoffed. “You merely wish to swindle us!”
column2: 他们对我们建议的礼物数量犹豫不决，并撤回了请求。“你们不想赞助我们，”他们嘲笑道，“你们只是想欺骗我们！”

column1: Who presents the petition to the tribal moot?
column2: 谁向部落大会呈递请愿？

column1: Your chieftain.
column2: 你的酋长。

column1: Your best poet.
column2: 你最杰出的诗人。

column1: Your best farmer.
column2: 你最杰出的农夫。

column1: Your lawgiver.
column2: 你的立法者。

column1: Your war leader.
column2: 你的战争领袖。

column1: Your trickster.
column2: 你的诡计大师。

column1: The \x01@! leaders thanked us for making an honest effort on their behalf.
column2: \x01@! 首领们感谢我们为他们做出了真诚的努力。

column1: This clan has fat herds and will bring new animal lore to our tribe. Sponsor them, and ask them to share their good fortune with us.
column2: 这个氏族拥有肥壮的畜群，将为我们的部落带来新的动物知识。赞助他们，并要求他们与我们分享好运。

column1: It would be unseemly to ask for more from them at a time like this.
column2: 在这样的时刻向他们索取更多是不合时宜的。

column1: We won’t get many chances to enter agreements with this rich and valuable clan. Agree to sponsor them.
column2: 我们不会有很多机会与这个富裕而有价值的氏族达成协议。同意赞助他们。

column1: Fighters are useful, but make sure we ask for something in return if we are to argue for them at the moot.
column2: 战士很有用，但如果我们打算在议会上为他们辩护，就必须确保我们要求回报。

column1: Just be sure that the reputation they bring is the reputation we want.
column2: 只需确保他们带来的声望是我们想要的。

column1: They must be willing to contribute something to the whole tribe, not just to our clan.
column2: 他们必须愿意为整个部落做出贡献，而不仅仅是我们氏族。

column1: This clan has traders who could bargain a web from a spider. By all means, accept their offer.
column2: 这个氏族有能从蜘蛛手里讨来蛛网的商人。务必接受他们的提议。

column1: This clan would bring fat storehouses of goods to the tribe.
column2: 这个氏族将为部落带来装满物资的仓库。

column1: A chance to add more fighters is good. A chance to add excellent fighters like these is excellent.
column2: 增加更多战士的机会是好的。增加像这样卓越战士的机会则是卓越的。

column1: Of course we could use more fighters in the tribe.
column2: 我们当然可以在部落中多些战士。

column1: Their weaponthanes are neither especially good, nor especially clumsy.
column2: 他们的武器领主既不是特别出色，也不是特别笨拙。

column1: Don’t agree to sponsor them on account of their weaponthanes, who are not especially talented.
column2: 不要因为他们的武器领主而同意赞助他们，因为他们并不特别有才能。

column1: If they give us a treasure, we are legally bound to speak for them at the moot.
column2: 如果他们给我们一件宝物，我们在法律上就有义务在议会上为他们发言。

column1: Are we so blinded by greed that we cannot see that this clan is friends with our most ancient enemies, the trolls?
column2: 我们是否被贪婪蒙蔽了双眼，竟看不出这个氏族是我们最古老的宿敌——巨魔的朋友？

column1: They know many ways to brew beer, and are friends with the trolls. Ask them in, and ask them for something in return.
column2: 他们懂得多种酿造啤酒的方法，并且是巨魔的朋友。邀请他们加入，并向他们索要回报。

column1: We offer them safety and our tribe’s reputation. We can ask them to give something in return.
column2: 我们向他们提供安全和部落的声望。我们可以要求他们给予回报。

column1: We are well-respected. The others will give a fair hearing to a petition on behalf of the \x01@! clan, if we choose to make it.
column2: 我们备受尊敬。如果我们选择提出，其他人会公平地听取代表 \x01@! 氏族的请愿。

column1: We are not well-respected. If we petition on behalf of the \x01@! clan, we may not get very far.
column2: 我们并不太受尊敬。如果我们代表 \x01@! 氏族提出请求，可能不会有多大进展。

column1: With our allies by our side, we will be stronger than ever.
column2: 有了盟友在我们身边，我们将比以往更强大。

column1: Our magic is weak. Asking them to contribute to the tribal ceremonies would lighten our magical share of the rites.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱。请他们为部落仪式贡献一份力，就能减轻我们在仪式中的魔法份额。

column1: Our magic is strong, but additional support for tribal rites will always be welcome.
column2: 我们的魔法强大，但部落仪式若能获得更多支持总是好的。

column1: Of course! Our allies belong in the tribe.
column2: 当然！我们的盟友本就该属于部落。

column1: They are truly famed for their large harvests and plant-knowledge. Agree to let them join, and ask them to share.
column2: 他们以丰收和植物知识闻名。同意他们加入，并请他们分享知识。

column1: More farmers and herders will strengthen the tribe.
column2: 更多的农夫和牧人能壮大部落。

column1: Ooh, these are the makers of the best wine, ever! And I should know!
column2: 哦，这些人酿过最好的酒！我可清楚得很！

column1: \x02\x04The more the merrier!/Oh boy! More people to annoy!/Why don’t they have acrobats, and jesters? Then they might be of some use./I’ll bet they’ve never heard my jokes…\x02
column2: \x02\x04越多越热闹！/哎呀！更多人来烦人了！/他们怎么不带杂耍和小丑来？那样还有点用。/我打赌他们从没听过我的笑话……\x02

column1: We could always use more people with horse-wisdom, but ask them to contribute in other ways so no loyal clans feel slighted.
column2: 我们总能用上更多懂马的人，但让他们以其他方式贡献，以免让忠诚的氏族感到被冷落。

column1: Do they know healing magics?
column2: 他们懂治疗魔法吗？

column1: Our tribal ceremonies will grow stronger with this clan in the tribe.
column2: 这个氏族加入后，我们的部落仪式会更强大。

column1: More cows are a fine thing.
column2: 更多牛只是好事。

column1: Why not add a clan with known martial prowess to our tribe? But ask them for something, to keep their heads from getting too big.
column2: 为什么不将一支以武力闻名的氏族纳入部落？但得向他们要点东西，免得他们太自大。

column1: This clan is known for silvery tongues and wily trading way. Better they should trade for and with us than against us.
column2: 这个氏族以巧舌如簧和狡猾贸易闻名。与其让他们与我们为敌，不如让他们为我们贸易。

column1: They have much to teach about hunting.
column2: 他们在狩猎方面有许多可教之处。

column1: Is this a question? We should be giving gifts to these famed Chaos-fighters and humbly beseeching them, not the other way around!
column2: 这还用问？我们应该向这些著名的混沌战士献上礼物，谦卑地恳求他们，而不是反过来！

column1: But what do they know about fighting Chaos?
column2: 但他们懂什么对抗混沌？

column1: They have much to teach about tracking and exploring.
column2: 他们在追踪和探索方面有许多可教之处。

column1: More Vingan warriors will bring honor to our tribe, and pride to our daughters.
column2: 更多温干战士会给我们的部落带来荣耀，也让我们的女儿们骄傲。

column1: How can you even think of talking to these elf-lovers? We should attack them instead!
column2: 你怎么能想着跟这些精灵爱好者谈话？我们该攻打他们才对！

column1: They should count themselves lucky that we even listen to their proposal. They had better admire our tribe, if they want in it.
column2: 他们该庆幸我们肯听他们的提议。若想加入，最好先敬仰我们的部落。

column1: Let us ask for a treasure, so whichever way the moot decides we come out ahead.
column2: 我们索要一件珍宝吧，这样无论议会如何裁决，我们都能获利。

column1: They are making a big mistake. We should talk them out of joining our tribe, or any other.
column2: 他们犯了大错。我们得说服他们别加入我们部落，也别加入别的部落。

column1: How sad that this clan of fiercely independent Orlanthi comes begging to belong to our tribe. Refuse them, they will be grateful to us for it some day.
column2: 真可悲，这个极度独立的奥兰斯氏族竟来乞求加入我们的部落。拒绝他们，总有一天他们会感激我们。

column1: They are known for their scroll collection — scrolls containing much wisdom, I’m sure — of course must sponsor them.
column2: 他们以收藏卷轴闻名——里面肯定藏着许多智慧——当然必须资助他们。

column1: They do not field famous weaponthanes, They are just more people for us to protect.
column2: 他们麾下没有著名的武器领主，只是更多需要我们保护的人。

column1: They fled Heortland because they could not get along with the Pharaoh. Our people will be unhappy if we don’t support them.
column2: 他们逃离赫尔特兰是因为与法老不合。若不支持他们，我们的人会不高兴。

column1: A thane from the \x01@! clan offered to recount “Ruthakran and His Chicken Bride.”
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的一位领主自告奋勇要讲述“鲁萨克兰和他的鸡新娘”。

column1: Politely insist that he recite another tale, as we fear for the chicken.
column2: 礼貌地坚持让他讲另一个故事，因为我们担心那只鸡。

column1: We asked for another story, but he didn’t know any.
column2: 我们要求换一个故事，但他一个都不会。

column1: Clap and encourage his antics.
column2: 鼓掌并鼓励他的表演。

column1: It turned out to be a splendid rendition.
column2: 结果演绎得精彩绝伦。

column1: \x01@\x10 gave us a splendid rendition of “Ruthakran and His Chicken Bride,” including the best imitation of a squealing hog we’d ever heard.
column2: \x01@\x10 为我们精彩演绎了“鲁萨克兰和他的鸡新娘”，包括我们听过最逼真的母猪尖叫声。

column1: Sadly, \x01@\x10 could not do the tale justice.
column2: 遗憾的是， \x01@\x10 未能讲好这个故事。

column1: \x01@\x10 tried, but he forgot the part where the mouse got tipsy, and his pig noises sounded more like a sickly calf. Shamefaced, he left the hall.
column2: \x01@\x10 尝试了，但他忘了老鼠微醺的部分，他的猪叫声听起来更像病弱的小牛。羞愧之下，他离开了大厅。

column1: Take offense at his offer, boo and hiss.
column2: 对他的提议感到愤怒，发出嘘声和嘶声。

column1: \x01@\x10 turned beet red, then ghastly pale, then rushed out of the hall, calling curses upon us.
column2: \x01@\x10 脸变得通红，继而惨白，然后冲出了大厅，对我们咒骂不止。

column1: Do we trust him not to hurt the chicken?
column2: 我们相信他不会伤害那只鸡吗？

column1: I’ve always liked this one, especially the part about selling bacon to the pig.
column2: 我一直喜欢这个故事，尤其是把培根卖给猪的那段。

column1: I forget parts of it, and could hear it again. Or not.
column2: 我忘了部分内容，可以再听一遍。或者不听。

column1: Oh, like we haven’t heard that one before.
column2: 哦，好像我们没听过似的。

column1: It’s an old story, but sometimes other clans will have new versions.
column2: 这是个老故事，但有时其他氏族会有新版本。

column1: This is kind of an odd choice for a representative of the \x01@! clan to be telling.
column2: 对于 \x01@! 氏族的代表来说，选这个故事有点奇怪。

column1: I can’t remember the whole thing.
column2: 我记不全整个故事。

column1: We all could use a good laugh.
column2: 我们都需要好好笑一场。

column1: This is an insult — surely we deserve a better tale!
column2: 这是侮辱——我们当然值得听更好的故事！

column1: It’s shameful how the chicken is never asked if she agrees with the wedding.
column2: 真可耻，从来没问过那只鸡是否同意这门婚事。

column1: It’s not the best of stories, nor the worst. I could hear it again.
column2: 这个故事不是最好，也不是最差。我可以再听一遍。

column1: Should the children hear this story?
column2: 孩子们该听这个故事吗？

column1: Ooh, this is one of my favorites!
column2: 哦，这是我最喜欢的故事之一！

column1: This is a great one!
column2: 这个很棒！

column1: It’s a difficult story to tell and most do not attempt it.
column2: 这个故事很难讲，大多数人不轻易尝试。

column1: It would be rude to refuse a guest.
column2: 拒绝客人是无礼的。

column1: Not the… we shouldn’t have to, that is, the chicken. Or the pig.
column2: 不是那个……我们没必要，我是说，那只鸡。或者那只猪。

column1: This will be a great test of how good a storyteller \x01@\x10 is. It’s a tricky tale to tell well. Of course, if you don’t want his version, I can give it a go.
column2: 这将是对 \x01@\x10 讲故事能力的一大考验。要讲好这个故事可不容易。当然，如果你不想听他讲的，我可以试试。

column1: returned and asked to rejoin the clan.
column2: 回来请求重新加入氏族。

column1: returns in poverty with his family to ask forgiveness and a chance to rejoin the clan. The term of his exile has long since passed. \x01@\x03 questioned him closely,
column2: 带着家人穷困潦倒地回来，请求宽恕并重新加入氏族。他的流放期限早已过去。 \x01@\x03 仔细询问了他，

column1: Take him and his family in as thralls for a year and a day, to prove themselves.
column2: 收留他和他的家人为奴隶一年零一天，让他们证明自己。

column1: We took him and his family in as thralls.
column2: 我们收留了他和他的家人为奴隶。

column1: Although our ancestors disapproved of us having any thralls, they seemed somewhat understanding of the circumstances.
column2: 尽管我们的祖先不赞成我们拥有任何奴隶，但他们似乎对这种情况多少有些理解。

column1: Let him rejoin the clan, give him land to start anew.
column2: 让他重新加入氏族，给他土地重新开始。

column1: We took him and his family back.
column2: 我们把他和他的家人接了回来。

column1: But \x01@\x13 said that \x04 goddess was pleased with our mercy.
column2: 但 \x01@\x13 说 \x04 女神对我们的仁慈感到满意。

column1: Send them on their way with some provisions.
column2: 送他们上路，并给一些供给。

column1: We sent him and his family on their way with some provisions.
column2: 我们送他和他家人上路，并给了他们一些供给。

column1: \x01@\x13 said that \x04 goddess was pleased with our mercy.
column2: \x01@\x13 说 \x04 女神对我们的仁慈感到满意。

column1: We heard later that the family \x02\x03had ended up back in Heortland/was attacked and massacred by bandits/was last seen wandering towards unexplored areas and no one has seen them since\x02.
column2: 我们后来听说那家人 \x02\x03最终回到了海尔特兰/遭到土匪袭击并惨遭杀害/最后被人看到朝未探索地区游荡，之后便无人再见到他们\x02。

column1: Send them on their way.
column2: 送他们上路。

column1: We sent him and his family on their way.
column2: 我们送他和他家人上路。

column1: This could reopen old wounds.
column2: 这可能会重新揭开旧伤疤。

column1: I remember him. Once a thief, always a thief.
column2: 我记得他。一次做贼，永远是贼。

column1: Exile doesn’t have to be permanent.
column2: 流放不一定是永久的。

column1: Theft is a very serious offense. Very.
column2: 偷窃是非常严重的罪行。非常严重。

column1: At least he did not engage in banditry against us while he was in exile.
column2: 至少他在流放期间没有对我们实施抢劫。

column1: Oh, him. Make him show us he can be trusted again.
column2: 哦，他。让他向我们证明他再次值得信任。

column1: People do return from exile, but something about this bothers me.
column2: 确实有人从流放中归来，但这事让我有些不安。

column1: Why is he not with his wife’s clan? This is suspicious.
column2: 他为什么不在他妻子的氏族里？这很可疑。

column1: No matter what we do, the situation does not justify taking thralls.
column2: 无论我们怎么做，这种情况都不足以证明收奴隶是正当的。

column1: Making him a thrall would let us test him and please our ancestors.
column2: 让他当奴隶可以考验他，也能取悦我们的祖先。

column1: We don’t need more mouths right now.
column2: 我们现在不需要更多吃饭的嘴。

column1: We could use more hands.
column2: 我们可以多几双干活的手。

column1: His family are not to blame for what he did before he married.
column2: 他的家人不该为他婚前做的事负责。

column1: He has suffered, and his family is suffering, too. Welcome him!
column2: 他已经受了苦，他的家人也在受苦。欢迎他吧！

column1: I suppose he’s learned his lesson.
column2: 我想他已经吸取了教训。

column1: Does he know the tale of “Ruthakran and His Chicken Bride?”
column2: 他知道“鲁萨克兰和他的鸡新娘”这个故事吗？

column1: If he were going to steal from us, he could have simply resorted to banditry.
column2: 如果他要偷我们的东西，他大可以干脆当土匪去。

column1: If we don’t let them return, at least give them some food.
column2: 如果我们不让他们回来，至少给他们一些食物。

column1: Send him away with ample food and goods and he will say good things about our clan!
column2: 送他走时给他充足的食物和物资，他就会说我们氏族的好话！

column1: Did his clan exile him? Did he marry a thief, are they raising little thieves?
column2: 他的氏族流放了他吗？他娶了一个窃贼，他们正在养育小窃贼吗？

column1: We owe them nothing.
column2: 我们不欠他们任何东西。

column1: We owe him another chance.
column2: 我们欠他一次机会。

column1: We can do better than Bad King Urgrain!
column2: 我们可以做得比恶王乌格兰更好！

column1: Bad King Urgrain exiled Biturian the Leaper for a year and a day. Then Biturian returned and attacked Bad King Urgrain. I’m not sure if that exactly relates to this situation, though.
column2: 恶王乌格兰将跳跃者比图里安流放了一年零一天。然后比图里安回来攻击恶王乌格兰。不过我不确定这和当前情况是否完全相关。

column1: \x01@\x10, an aspiring poet from the \x01@! clan, jumped at the chance to entertain us during a visit. But his tale is approaching the length of an epic battle. A long, dull, dreary epic battle.
column2: \x01@\x10一位来自 \x01@! 氏族的、有抱负的诗人，在访问期间抓住机会为我们助兴。但他的故事长度快赶上一场史诗般的战斗了。一场漫长、乏味、沉闷的史诗战斗。

column1: An aspiring poet from the \x01@! clan, \x01@\x10, would not stop telling a long, boring poem.
column2: 一位来自 \x01@! 氏族的有抱负的诗人 \x01@\x10，不停地讲述着一首长而无聊的诗。

column1: Wait patiently for him to finish.
column2: 耐心等他结束。

column1: \x01@\x10 droned on until everyone fell asleep. By morning he was gone.
column2: \x01@\x10 他喋喋不休直到所有人都睡着了。到了早晨他离开了。

column1: Later, we heard that the \x01@! clan were laughing at us for listening to the awful \x01@\x10.
column2: 后来，我们听说 \x01@! 氏族在嘲笑我们听那糟糕的 \x01@\x10。

column1: Rouse the sleepy audience to cheer him until he bows and ends the poem.
column2: 叫醒困倦的观众为他欢呼，直到他鞠躬结束诗篇。

column1: \x01@N roused the sleepy audience to cheer him as if the poem were done, and he mercifully stopped.
column2: \x01@N 叫醒困倦的观众为他欢呼，仿佛诗已结束，他仁慈地停下了。

column1: \x01@\x10 blinked, smiled, and sat down to drink some mead.
column2: \x01@\x10 眨了眨眼，笑了笑，坐下喝了点蜂蜜酒。

column1: \x01@N roused the sleepy audience to cheer him as if the poem were done, but it only encouraged him to start a new epic.
column2: \x01@N 叫醒困倦的观众为他欢呼，仿佛诗已结束，但这反而鼓励他开始一部新的史诗。

column1: Encouraged by our applause, \x01@\x10 launched into another \x02\x03poem/epic/saga\x02. If anything, it was even less inspiring than the first.
column2: 受到我们掌声的鼓励， \x01@\x10 开始了又一首 \x02\x03诗歌/史诗/传说\x02。要说的话，它比第一首更不鼓舞人心。

column1: Stand abruptly and thank him profusely, outshouting his protests until he sits down.
column2: 突然站起来，连连感谢他，大声盖过他的抗议直到他坐下。

column1: \x01@N abruptly thanked him until he stopped.
column2: \x01@N 突然感谢他，直到他停下。

column1: \x01@\x10 finally sat down and accepted a tall flagon of drink.
column2: \x01@\x10 终于坐下，接过一大壶酒。

column1: \x01@N tried to thank him, but \x01@\x10 took offense at the interruption.
column2: \x01@N 试图感谢他，但 \x01@\x10 因被打断而恼怒。

column1: \x01@\x10 went pale, then red, then stormed out of the hall. Fortunately, only a few were awake to hear his parting curses.
column2: \x01@\x10 脸色先变白，再变红，然后冲出大厅。幸好只有少数人醒着听到他的临别诅咒。

column1: Arrange for the children to pelt him with table scraps
column2: 安排孩子们用剩饭扔他。

column1: The children threw bones, rinds, and crusts at \x01@\x10 till he fled the hall.
column2: 孩子们向 \x01@\x10 扔骨头、果皮和面包皮，直到他逃离大厅。

column1: The children threw bones, rinds, and crusts at \x01@\x10, but he finished anyway.
column2: 孩子们朝 \x01@\x10扔骨头、果皮和面包皮，但他还是讲完了。

column1: Undaunted, \x01@\x10 finished the tale. He did speak quite quickly towards the end, though.
column2: \x01@\x10 毫不气馁地讲完了故事。不过快到结尾时他确实说得相当快。

column1: Why is he reciting this drivel here? Why isn’t he boring his own clan?
column2: 他为什么在这里背诵这些废话？为什么不去烦他自己的氏族？

column1: I’ve talked to \x01@! traders. Even they think \x01@\x10 is a bore.
column2: 我跟 \x01@! 的商人谈过。连他们都觉得 \x01@\x10 很无聊。

column1: I’m surprised I haven’t heard about \x01@\x10 from \x01@! traders. Usually they’ll give a warning.
column2: 我很惊讶没有从 \x01@! 商人那里听说过 \x01@\x10 。通常他们会发出警告。

column1: Bad King Urgrain was known to kill and roast bad poets.
column2: 恶王乌格兰以杀死并烤食蹩脚诗人而闻名。

column1: He only wants to be noticed. Give him some applause and he will shut up.
column2: 他只是想引人注目。给他一些掌声，他就会闭嘴。

column1: Well, that didn’t go as I expected.
column2: 嗯，这没有如我所愿。

column1: Challenge him to tell a tongue twisting tale and call on Orlanth to twist his tongue.
column2: 挑战他讲一个绕口令般的故事，并祈求奥兰斯缠住他的舌头。

column1: Maybe a diversion will get him to stop.
column2: 也许转移注意力能让他停下来。

column1: Our warriors are fond of good poetry. That probably explains why most of them are asleep.
column2: 我们的战士喜欢好诗。这大概能解释为什么他们大多数都睡着了。

column1: Encourage him to keep going, surely he will drop by morning.
column2: 鼓励他继续下去，到早上他肯定会倒下。

column1: Why are we listening? Why do we not take action against this outpouring of words?
column2: 我们为什么在听？为什么不对这滔滔不绝的言语采取行动？

column1: This is odious.
column2: 这令人作呕。

column1: This is an affront to Orlanth and Issaries, gods of eloquence and poets.
column2: 这是对奥兰斯和伊萨里斯——口才与诗歌之神——的侮辱。

column1: This guy should become a healer, he could put me to sleep without needing a spell.
column2: 这家伙应该去做治疗师，他不用法术就能让我睡着。

column1: I should go check on the patrols.
column2: 我应该去检查巡逻队。

column1: Word-butcher makes me ill.
column2: 文字屠夫让我恶心。

column1: Let Eninta’s blessings slay the word-butcher.
column2: 愿恩因塔的祝福诛杀这文字屠夫。

column1: Just be glad he’s not trying to recite “Ruthakran and His Chicken Bride!”
column2: 庆幸吧，他至少没在背诵《鲁萨克兰和他的鸡新娘》！

column1: Not again! Can he not take a hint?
column2: 又来？他就不能领会一下暗示吗？

column1: The women were distraught because \x01@\x13 babies in a row were stillborn or died soon after birth.
column2: 妇女们心烦意乱，因为连续 \x01@\x13 个婴儿要么死产，要么出生后不久就夭折了。

column1: Angry women confront the clan ring, the death rune smeared in ash on their foreheads. \x01@\x13 infants in a row were stillborn or died soon after birth. They demand the ring do something to stop this and ease their hearts’ sorrow.
column2: 愤怒的妇女们与氏族议会对峙，额头上用灰烬涂抹着死亡符文。连续 \x01@\x13 个婴儿死产或出生后不久就夭折了。她们要求议会做些什么来阻止这一切，抚慰她们心头的悲伤。

column1: “The gods are mysterious, what they take on one hand they give on another.”
column2: “神祇是神秘的，他们一手拿走，另一手赐予。”

column1: We told them it was fate.
column2: 我们告诉她们这是命运。

column1: The women did not want to listen at first, but eventually seemed to accept this hard wisdom.
column2: 妇女们起初不愿听，但最终似乎接受了这严酷的智慧。

column1: Sacrifice to Chalana Arroy.
column2: 向查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to the healing goddess.
column2: 我们向治愈女神献祭了。

column1: What do you offer to Chalana Arroy?
column2: 你向查拉娜·阿罗伊献上什么？

column1: The sacrifice succeeded, and the signs looked excellent for future fertility.
column2: 献祭成功了，预示未来丰饶的征兆极佳。

column1: Indeed, a healthy baby was born soon afterwards.
column2: 果然，不久后一个健康的婴儿诞生了。

column1: The omens looked bleak, and Chalana Arroy withheld her blessings.
column2: 预兆黯淡，查拉娜·阿罗伊收回了她的祝福。

column1: Perform a divination.
column2: 进行占卜。

column1: We performed a divination.
column2: 我们进行了占卜。

column1: It turned out that we had inadvertently disturbed an ancient burial mound while clearing a field.
column2: 结果发现我们在清理田地时无意中惊扰了一座古墓冢。

column1: We restored the damage, and ended the curse.
column2: 我们修复了损坏，终结了诅咒。

column1: Although we weren’t able to learn who the hero was, the god-talkers conducted a ritual, and the farmers replanted the mound with sod. A healthy baby was born soon afterwards, and the whole clan rejoiced.
column2: 虽然我们无法得知那位英雄是谁，但神言者举行了仪式，农夫们用草皮重新覆盖了墓冢。不久后一个健康的婴儿诞生，整个氏族欢庆不已。

column1: The signs did not indicate magic, nor enemies, nor any clear message.
column2: 征兆没有显示魔法，也没有敌人，也没有任何明确的信息。

column1: Some of the clan were ready to raid right away.
column2: 部分族人已准备好立刻发动突袭。

column1: Many of the clan worried aloud at going against our clan traditions as a Peace Clan.
column2: 许多族人公开担忧违背我们作为和平氏族的传统。

column1: Some of the clan were ready to strike at their enemies right away.
column2: 部分族人已准备好立刻打击敌人。

column1: Some of the clan grumbled at the chance of starting another feud.
column2: 部分族人抱怨又开始另一场世仇的机会。

column1: Aaaaah no!
column2: 啊啊啊不！

column1: Some years many calves die, some years they all live. It is the way of things.
column2: 有些年份许多牛犊死去，有些年份全部存活。世事如此。

column1: This is sad, but it is how things are.
column2: 这很悲伤，但世事就是这样。

column1: Sometimes the crops are poor, sometimes they flourish.
column2: 有时收成不好，有时丰收。

column1: This is heartbreaking, and hard to know if this is a spirit matter or a run of bad luck.
column2: 这令人心碎，很难知道这是灵体作祟还是厄运连连。

column1: They should be glad they did not die in childbirth.
column2: 她们应该庆幸自己没有死于分娩。

column1: A divination would ease the mothers’ grief.
column2: 一次占卜可以缓解母亲们的悲痛。

column1: A proper ceremony might stop this sorrow.
column2: 一场恰当的仪式或许能止住这场悲伤。

column1: It must be bad magic from the \x01@! clan, we should kill them!
column2: 一定是 \x01@! 氏族的恶毒巫术，我们应该杀了他们！

column1: If this continues, we won’t have a clan!
column2: 如果继续这样，我们的氏族就要完了！

column1: Find out who is behind this and raid them!
column2: 找出幕后黑手，突袭他们！

column1: If someone is sending a curse, we can find out.
column2: 如果有人施放诅咒，我们能查出来。

column1: It would be powerful magic if another clan were causing this.
column2: 如果是另一个氏族在搞鬼，那必定是强大的魔法。

column1: This is not a matter for the clan ring.
column2: 这不是氏族议会该管的事。

column1: Bad King Urgrain forgot to honor the gods, and all the infants fell sickly and died.
column2: 恶王乌格兰忘记敬奉神祇，于是所有新生儿都病弱而死。

column1: We can soothe their troubled breasts with the promise of blood.
column2: 我们可以用鲜血的承诺抚慰他们不安的心胸。

column1: The poor babies! I could cry like a man.
column2: 可怜的宝宝们！我简直要像个男人一样哭了。

column1: It’s more important to ease their sorrow than try to find a reason.
column2: 缓解他们的悲伤比试图寻找原因更重要。

column1: The women are very, very \x02\x02distressed/distraught\x02.
column2: 妇女们非常、非常 \x02\x02苦恼/心烦意乱\x02。

column1: sceneR336
column2: sceneR336

column1: A group of ragged, ill-favored travelers asked for hospitality.
column2: 一群衣衫褴褛、面目可憎的旅人请求款待。

column1: A group of ragged travelers ask for your hospitality. Their leader says that they are wanderers and worship Issaries, god of the road. Though they appear repulsive, they promise news of other clans in exchange.
column2: 一群衣衫褴褛的旅人请求你们的款待。他们的首领说他们是流浪者，信奉道路之神伊萨里斯。尽管他们外表令人反感，但他们承诺用其他氏族的消息作为交换。

column1: Attack them.
column2: 攻击他们。

column1: They fled as soon as we tried to attack.
column2: 我们刚试图攻击，他们就逃跑了。

column1: They were wary and fled at the first flash of bronze. Who knew anyone could run so quickly? They melted into the forest like fog.
column2: 他们十分警惕，一见青铜闪光就逃走了。谁知道有人能跑得这么快？他们像雾一样消失在森林中。

column1: Grant them hospitality.
column2: 给予他们款待。

column1: They ate. They drank. They ate and drank some more. Their news was stale, their gossip rancid. We were happy to see them go.
column2: 他们吃了。他们喝了。他们又吃又喝。他们的消息陈旧，流言腐朽。我们很高兴看到他们离开。

column1: Tell them to ask another clan instead.
column2: 让他们去问别的氏族。

column1: They seemed disappointed, but set off in that direction.
column2: 他们似乎很失望，但还是朝那个方向出发了。

column2: 他们奇异的法术成功了， \x01@\x06 把她的花环从岩石上拿了下来。

column1: After a day and a night the girl seemed to wake as from a bad dream. When she saw the garlands on the rock, she laughed and removed them.
column2: 一天一夜之后，女孩仿佛从噩梦中醒来。她看到岩石上的花环，笑着把它们摘了下来。

column1: After a day and a night of their ceremonies, the spirit-talkers seemed troubled. They said her spirit barred the way to healing. The girl refused to speak and started spending more time with the rock.
column2: 经过一天一夜的仪式，灵语者们显得很困扰。他们说她的灵魂阻碍了治疗之路。女孩拒绝说话，并开始花更多时间待在那块岩石旁。

column1: Spirit-talkers offered to heal her, but we decided not to pay them.
column2: 灵语者提出治疗她，但我们决定不付给他们报酬。

column1: Sacrifice to Chalana Arroy to heal \x01@\x06’s confusion.
column2: 向查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭，以治愈 \x01@\x06的迷乱。

column1: We sacrificed to Chalana Arroy, who restored \x01@\x06.
column2: 我们向查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭，她修复了 \x01@\x06。

column1: Chalana Arroy blessed the girl, who seemed to wake as from a bad dream. When she saw the garlands on the rock, she laughed and removed them.
column2: 查拉娜·阿罗伊赐福了那个女孩，她仿佛从噩梦中醒来。看到岩石上的花环，她笑着把它们摘了下来。

column1: We sacrificed to Chalana Arroy, but she did not answer.
column2: 我们向查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭，但她没有回应。

column1: After a time, \x01@\x06 said no more of talking rocks.
column2: 过了一段时间， \x01@\x06 不再提会说话的岩石了。

column1: \x01@\x06 began spending all her time at the rock.
column2: \x01@\x06 开始把所有时间都花在岩石上。

column1: We woke one morning to find a scrap of cloth, a splash of blood and a lock of hair.
column2: 一天早晨我们醒来，发现了一块碎布、一滩血迹和一缕头发。

column1: Strange though she was, the clan will mourn her.
column2: 尽管她行为怪异，氏族仍会悼念她。

column1: We heard that \x01@\x06 was learning much from the spirit-talkers.
column2: 我们听说 \x01@\x06 从灵语者那里学到了很多。

column1: We heard that \x01@\x06 had failed her initiation as a spirit-talker.
column2: 我们听说 \x01@\x06 未能通过灵语者的启蒙仪式。

column1: What might be mad might also be blessed.
column2: 疯狂之物亦可能蒙受恩赐。

column1: If she wants to make offerings, the known gods would appreciate it.
column2: 如果她想献祭，众所皆知的神明会很感激。

column1: Sometimes the spirits speak in strange ways.
column2: 有时灵魂会以奇怪的方式说话。

column1: Does this risk offending our clan’s deities?
column2: 这样做会有冒犯我们氏族神祇的风险吗？

column1: Why worship a rock when we need to strengthen our known gods?
column2: 在我们需要加强已知神祇力量的时候，为什么要崇拜一块岩石？

column1: Tell her stop this foolishness. She can bring her baskets to Ernalda.
column2: 告诉她停止这种蠢行。她可以把篮子带到埃尔纳尔妲那里去。

column1: Her mother is clearly worried. See if we can heal the girl.
column2: 她母亲显然很担心。看看我们能否治愈这个女孩。

column1: \x01@\x06’s mother knows more than she tells, ask further about her daughter.
column2: \x01@\x06的母亲知道的比她说的多，再多问问她女儿的情况。

column1: Chalana Arroy may not be able to help, but there’s little harm in asking.
column2: 查拉娜·阿罗伊可能帮不上忙，但问问也无妨。

column1: The mother is in the best position to tell us more about the girl.
column2: 母亲最了解这个女孩的情况。

column1: When in doubt, consult the gods.
column2: 有疑问时，请教神明。

column1: If this is a spirit matter, the spirits can tell us what we need to know.
column2: 如果这是灵魂的事情，灵魂能告诉我们所需知道的一切。

column1: She is clearly ill, ask Chalana Arroy to mend her.
column2: 她显然是病了，请查拉娜·阿罗伊治好她。

column1: A sacrifice to Chalana Arroy is called for.
column2: 应该向查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭。

column1: Shamans converse with the spirit realm too. Maybe they could train her in their ways.
column2: 萨满也与灵魂领域交流。也许他们能以他们的方式训练她。

column1: Rocks may contain spirits. Butter churns do not.
column2: 岩石中可能寄居着灵魂。搅乳桶可不会。

column1: Send for shamans to see if she has a gift.
column2: 派人去请萨满看看她是否有天赋。

column1: It would seem she is not blessed with a gift after all.
column2: 看来她终究没有蒙受天赋的恩赐。

column1: I say split the rock open — see what is inside!
column2: 我主张把岩石劈开——看看里面是什么！

column1: I still say split the rock open — see what is inside!
column2: 我仍然主张把岩石劈开——看看里面是什么！

column1: Why are we wasting our time with a family problem?
column2: 为什么我们要浪费时间在一个家庭问题上？

column1: There may be no helping her, but at least we should try.
column2: 也许无法帮助她，但至少我们应该尝试。

column1: We shouldn’t let her continue.
column2: 我们不该让她继续下去。

column1: I told you she was cursed.
column2: 我告诉过你她被诅咒了。

column1: We should follow her example and make this rock into a shrine!
column2: 我们应该以她为榜样，把这块岩石建成一个神龛！

column1: The family and neighbors of a quarrelsome couple brought them before the ring.
column2: 一对争吵不休的夫妇的家人和邻居把他们带到了长老会面前。

column1: The couple seemed chagrined to be brought to the clan hall.
column2: 这对夫妇被带到部族大厅，显得很窘迫。

column1: Ignore this, it is not a matter for the ring.
column2: 忽略此事，这不属于长老会该管的事。

column1: The people muttered that the ring did not care if their sleep was interrupted and their dinners spoiled by the couple’s fighting.
column2: 人们在私下议论，说长老会不关心他们的睡眠是否被打断、晚饭是否被这对夫妇的争吵给毁了。

column1: Clan members thought the ring should have gotten involved.
column2: 氏族成员认为长老会本应介入。

column1: The people were glad that the ring did not interfere in a domestic matter.
column2: 百姓们很高兴长老会没有干涉家庭事务。

column1: The clan ring listened but did not get involved.
column2: 氏族议会听取了情况，但没有介入。

column1: Shame them.
column2: 羞辱他们。

column1: The couple were brought before the clan to listen to \x01@\x10’s recitation of “The Badger and the Snake,” a tale that ridiculed pointless sparring and ends in disaster for all the animals in the forest.
column2: 这对夫妇被带到氏族面前，听取 \x01@\x10朗诵《獾与蛇》——一个嘲笑无谓争斗、最终导致森林中所有动物都遭灾的故事。

column1: \x01@\x10 acted out the poem and \x04 antics made the clan wipe their eyes from mirth, while pointing and hooting at the unhappy pair.
column2: \x01@\x10 把这首诗表演了出来， \x04 的滑稽动作让氏族成员笑得擦眼泪，同时对着那对不快活的人指指点点、大声起哄。

column1: The couple were quiet as mice for a long time after.
column2: 那对夫妇此后有很长一段时间安静得像老鼠一样。

column1: The couple rolled their eyes and smirked as \x01@\x10 stumbled on a few tricky lines.
column2: 这对夫妇翻了个白眼，咧嘴一笑，当 \x01@\x10 在一些棘手的台词上绊倒时。

column1: They outshouted \x08 by reciting a rude stanza about a meddling mole sticking his nose in places it didn’t belong.
column2: 他们通过背诵一段关于多管闲事的鼹鼠把手伸到不该伸的地方去的粗鲁诗句，盖过了 \x08 的声音。

column1: Fine them.
column2: 罚他们。

column1: The ring stripped them of their herds, reducing them to cottars.
column2: 长老会剥夺了他们的牲畜，把他们降为佃农。

column1: The carls complained that the ring had interfered in a domestic matter. The weaponthanes were pleased that we had punished the carls.
column2: 自由民抱怨长老会干预了家庭事务。武器领主们对我们惩罚了自由民感到满意。

column1: Threaten them with outlawry.
column2: 以放逐威胁他们。

column1: We threatened to outlaw them.
column2: 我们威胁要放逐他们。

column1: The couple seemed subdued, and wisely decided to part ways soon after.
column2: 这对夫妇似乎被压制了，并明智地决定不久后分道扬镳。

column1: They returned to their stead, subdued.
column2: 他们回到自己的宅地，垂头丧气。

column1: The tension from this couple is affecting the cattle!
column2: 这对夫妇的紧张情绪正在影响牛群！

column1: Give them a reason to end their bickering.
column2: 给他们一个结束争吵的理由。

column1: When the warriors get out of hand, they lose gold and silver.
column2: 当战士们失控时，他们会损失金银。

column1: When family matters become this bad, the ring is right to respond.
column2: 当家庭事务恶化到这种地步时，长老会有权回应。

column1: When family matters become this bad, the ring is right to respond. But family matters never justify outlawry.
column2: 当家庭事务恶化到这种地步时，长老会有权回应。但家庭事务绝不能成为放逐的理由。

column1: This matter should have been settled without the ring, but now we must make a decision or appear weak.
column2: 这件事本应不经过长老会就解决，但现在我们必须做出决定，否则就会显得软弱。

column1: We need a solution that will satisfy the carls, without insulting them.
column2: 我们需要一个既能满足自由民又不侮辱他们的解决方案。

column1: Orlanth and Ernalda formed the Marriage Ring, and every marriage ceremony since echoes that.
column2: 奥兰斯与厄娜尔达结成了婚姻之环，此后的每一场婚礼都效仿这一仪式。

column1: Orlanth and Ernalda formed the Marriage Ring, and every marriage ceremony since echoes that. Their fighting is unseemly, but should not affect the clan’s magic.
column2: 奥兰斯与厄娜尔达结成了婚姻之环，此后的每一场婚礼都效仿这一仪式。他们的争斗不合时宜，但不应该影响氏族的魔法。

column1: What about the crops? We need every farmer in the clan.
column2: 庄稼怎么办？我们需要氏族里的每一个农夫。

column1: The crops will grow better and the work will be smoother without their constant fighting.
column2: 没有他们不断的争吵，庄稼会长得更好，劳作也会更顺利。

column1: Bad King Urgrain threw food at his wife. And his next wife, and the next…
column2: 恶王乌格兰朝他的妻子扔食物。然后是下一任妻子，再下一任……

column1: I shall sleep with them both, and then they will truly know the meaning of a bad spouse!
column2: 我要和他们两个都睡觉，这样他们才能真正体会糟糕配偶的滋味！

column1: Why are the farmers bothering us with this picayune matter?
column2: 为什么农夫们要用这件微不足道的小事来烦我们？

column1: They are bound to fight as long as they are married.
column2: 只要他们结了婚，就注定会吵架。

column1: How is this a decision for the Ring? Cannot the farmers handle their own?
column2: 这怎么是长老会该做的决定？农夫们不能自行处理吗？

column1: Some marriages bloom and fruit, other rot and smell.
column2: 有些婚姻开花结果，另一些则腐烂发臭。

column1: This constant sparring must cease.
column2: 这种无休止的斗嘴必须停止。

column1: Make them pay.
column2: 让他们付出代价。

column1: I said that this marriage was doomed when it hailed on their wedding day.
column2: 我说过这场婚姻注定失败，因为婚礼那天下了冰雹。

column1: Whether shaming works is up to them, but it is probably what the clan expects.
column2: 羞辱是否奏效取决于他们，但这大概是氏族所期望的。

column1: The farmers are unhappy that the couple could not settle their differences, and unhappy at the banishment.
column2: 农夫们对这对夫妇未能解决分歧感到不满，也对流放感到不满。

column1: The farmers are not as unhappy as the ring feared, for they are sleeping soundly at night and do not have to listen the couple’s constant screaming.
column2: 农夫们并没有像长老会担心的那样不满，因为他们晚上能睡个好觉，不用听那对夫妇的持续尖叫。

column1: Cultists of Uralda, mother of cows, visit to complain that we have neglected the proper worship of Uralda, and her grace will fall from the clan if we fail to honor her properly.
column2: 母牛之神尤拉尔达的信徒来访，抱怨我们忽视了正确崇拜尤拉尔达，如果我们不恰当地尊崇她，她的恩宠将离开氏族。

column1: “At the least, she should have a proper shrine.”
column2: “至少，她应该有一座合适的神龛。”

column1: Uralda cultists complained that we were neglecting the Cow Mother’s worship.
column2: 尤拉尔达的信徒抱怨我们忽视了母牛女神的崇拜。

column1: Thank them for their advice and see them on their way.
column2: 感谢他们的建议，然后送他们上路。

column1: We thanked them but took no action.
column2: 我们感谢了他们，但没有采取行动。

column1: The leader shook her head silently, and one of the younger god-talkers mooed rudely.
column2: 首领默不作声地摇了摇头，一位年轻的神言者粗鲁地哞了一声。

column1: The farmers worried that we were not gracious enough, and that our good fortune with the herds was in danger.
column2: 农夫们担心我们不够仁慈，我们畜群的运势将面临危险。

column1: The farmers were angry that we had not been more gracious to the cultists. They said that our poor hospitality would reflect badly on our already thin herds.
column2: 农夫们对我们没有对信徒更仁慈感到愤怒。他们说我们糟糕的好客会对本已稀疏的畜群产生不良影响。

column1: Thank them and promise to honor Uralda properly in the future.
column2: 感谢他们，并承诺将来会恰当地尊崇尤拉尔达。

column1: We promised to honor Uralda properly in the future.
column2: 我们承诺将来会恰当地尊崇尤拉尔达。

column1: The leader said, “Don’t promise me, promise your own herds.”
column2: 首领说：“别向我承诺，向你们自己的畜群承诺。”

column1: The people thought that we could always use magic to improve our herds, but glad that we did not hurry in response.
column2: 人们认为我们总可以用魔法来改善畜群，但对没有仓促回应感到高兴。

column1: The farmers said that they would expect action on this advice sooner, not later, so our sparse herds could be more bountiful.
column2: 农夫们说他们期望对这个建议尽早行动，而非拖延，这样我们稀疏的畜群才能变得更加丰饶。

column1: Ask them how we can honor her more properly.
column2: 询问他们我们如何才能更恰当地尊崇她。

column1: The leader closed her eyes for long minutes, then said that
column2: 首领闭上眼睛好几分钟，然后说

column1: we still did not know the secrets of the myth “Uralda’s Blessing,” and
column2: 我们仍然不知道神话“尤拉尔达的赐福”的秘密，而且

column1: we must be more generous in our sacrifices.
column2: 我们的献祭必须更加慷慨。

column1: the cattle would weep until we built a shrine to Uralda.
column2: 牛群会哭泣，直到我们为尤拉尔达建造一座神龛。

column1: And that the goddess should be represented on the clan ring.
column2: 而且女神应该在氏族议会上有代表。

column1: Ask them conduct a special ceremony to Uralda and throw a feast in their honor.
column2: 请他们为尤拉尔达举行一场特殊仪式，并为他们举办一场宴会。

column1: We asked them to conduct a ceremony, and held a joyful feast in their honor.
column2: 我们请他们举行仪式，并为他们举办了一场欢乐的宴会。

column1: The feast was joyful, and the people looked forward to fattening our already stout herds.
column2: 宴会充满欢乐，人们期待着我们已经健壮的畜群更加肥壮。

column1: The feast was joyful, and the people looked forward to fattening our thin herds.
column2: 宴会充满欢乐，人们期待着让我们稀疏的畜群增肥。

column1: We asked them to conduct a ceremony, but the omens were unclear.
column2: 我们请他们举行仪式，但征兆不明。

column1: The omens were unclear.
column2: 征兆不明。

column1: The feast was subdued, and the farmers worried that we would see our bountiful herds begin to shrink.
column2: 宴会气氛压抑，农夫们担心我们会看到丰饶的畜群开始缩减。

column1: The feast was somber, as the farmers worried that our herds would grow sparser. Even the cultists were subdued.
column2: 宴会阴沉，因为农夫们担心我们的畜群会变得更稀疏。连信徒们也都默然不语。

column1: We must do anything we can to increase our herds.
column2: 我们必须尽一切努力增加我们的畜群。

column1: We always want more cows, but we do not have to rush into any decision.
column2: 我们总是想要更多的牛，但不必急于做出任何决定。

column1: We need more cows, many more and soon.
column2: 我们需要更多牛，很多很多，而且要快。

column1: If we treat them with respect, they can help us to increase our herds.
column2: 若我们敬重它们，它们能助我们壮大畜群。

column1: What clan are they from? Are they true or here to disturb us?
column2: 他们来自哪个氏族？是真心的，还是来搅扰我们的？

column1: Without cattle, we are poor, and without wealth our weaponthanes have no pride.
column2: 没有牛，我们就穷；没有财富，我们的武器领主就没了骄傲。

column1: We do not have listen to every band of cultists that comes through our tula.
column2: 我们不必听信每个路过我们领地的邪教徒帮派。

column1: Wandering groups of worshippers can offer good advice. Or appear to.
column2: 游荡的崇拜者团体能给出好建议——或者貌似如此。

column1: Wandering groups of worshippers can offer advice and assistance if treated with respect.
column2: 游荡的崇拜者团体若被敬重，也能提供建议和帮助。

column1: Uralda sent these cultists to bring us her message. We could ask them for clarity.
column2: 乌拉尔达派这些教徒来传达她的消息。我们可以向他们问个明白。

column1: Uralda sent these cultists to bring us her message. We could ask for their help and must honor them properly.
column2: 乌拉尔达派这些教徒来传达她的消息。我们可以请求他们的帮助，并必须恰当礼待他们。

column1: Our temple to Uralda should be good enough.
column2: 我们献给乌拉尔达的神殿应该已经够好了。

column1: Let’s build a shrine to Uralda right away.
column2: 咱们马上给乌拉尔达建一座神龛。

column1: We have a temple, let us find out more.
column2: 我们有神殿了，再多了解些吧。

column1: Is there anything else they think we should do after building a shrine?
column2: 建完神龛之后，他们还觉得我们该做什么别的事吗？

column1: Question them and find out the proper path.
column2: 盘问他们，找出正途。

column1: More cows means happier farmers, happier farmers means better crops.
column2: 更多牛意味着更快乐的农夫，更快乐的农夫意味着更好的收成。

column1: Maybe they are really bringing a message from Urox, the bull!
column2: 也许他们真的带来了公牛乌洛克斯的口信！

column1: Do we need others to tell us how to worship properly?
column2: 难道还需要别人来教我们如何正确敬拜吗？

column1: Herds will increase. Or not.
column2: 畜群会增长——或者不会。

column1: If we don’t do what they say, we could lose our herds.
column2: 假如我们不照他们说的做，可能会失去我们的畜群。

column1: Um…sacrifice…cow…listen?
column2: 呃……献祭……牛……听？

column1: They’re right, we are terrible worshippers. Just terrible.
column2: 他们说得对，我们是糟糕的崇拜者，简直糟透了。

column1: We should listen to these clever young women.
column2: 我们应该听听这些聪慧的女人的话。

column1: Will their advice cost us cattle?
column2: 他们的建议会花费我们的牛吗？

column1: Increasing our herds by increasing our magic will please Uralda and all the gods.
column2: 通过增强魔法来壮大畜群，会让乌拉尔达与所有神明喜悦。

column1: We should at least listen to them.
column2: 我们至少该听听他们的话。

column1: Happy cows, happy farmers. Happy farmers, happy weaponthanes. Happy weaponthanes, happy clan.
column2: 快乐的牛，快乐的农夫。快乐的农夫，快乐的武器领主。快乐的武器领主，快乐的氏族。

column1: Listen to them.
column2: 听他们的。

column1: Of course we should improve our temples.
column2: 我们当然应该改进我们的神殿。

column1: Of course we should build a shrine to Uralda.
column2: 我们当然应该给乌拉尔达建一座神龛。

column1: I told you that we were neglecting our cow magic.
column2: 我早就说过我们忽略了牛魔法。

column1: Cultists of Uralda, mother of all cows, tell us they are traveling to the \x01@! clan to perform a cow blessing. They ask if we would be willing to sacrifice 5 cows to Uralda at dawn of the same day, to strengthen the magic, and to gain a small share of the blessing.
column2: 乌拉尔达——万牛之母——的教徒告诉我们，他们正要前往 \x01@! 氏族举行一场赐福牛的仪式。他们问我们是否愿意在同一天拂晓献祭5头牛给乌拉尔达，以增强魔法并获得一小份赐福。

column1: Uralda cultists wanted us to sacrifice 5 cows to aid a ceremony at the \x01@! clan.
column2: 乌拉尔达的教徒曾要我们献祭5头牛，以协助在 \x01@! 氏族举行的仪式。

column1: Politely decline their request.
column2: 礼貌地拒绝他们的请求。

column1: The clan was torn – they worried about the cattle but were satisfied that we did not aid our enemies.
column2: 氏族内部意见分裂——他们担忧牛的损失，但对没有帮助我们的敌人感到满意。

column1: The carls were angry that we failed a chance to bring fertility blessings to our herds.
column2: 自由民们很生气，我们错过了为畜群带来丰饶赐福的机会。

column1: The clan was satisfied that we did not aid our enemies.
column2: 氏族对没有帮助我们的敌人感到满意。

column1: The clan grumbled our ample herds might dwindle if we offended the cow mother.
column2: 氏族抱怨说，如果冒犯了母牛女神，我们本很充足的畜群可能会减少。

column1: The farmers are disgruntled to hear this but the weaponthanes look forward to raiding their soon-to-be fat herds.
column2: 农夫们听到这话很不满，但武器领主却盼着去劫掠他们那即将养肥的畜群。

column1: The farmers are unhappy to hear this, when our own herds are still thin and we could have shared in those blessings.
column2: 农夫们听到这话很不高兴——我们自己的畜群还很单薄，本可以分享那些赐福的。

column1: The farmers are disgruntled to hear this, when we too could have shared in those blessings.
column2: 农夫们听到这话很不满——我们本也可以分享那些赐福的。

column1: Agree to the sacrifice.
column2: 同意献祭。

column1: We agreed.
column2: 我们同意了。

column1: The clan hoped this would ease tensions between the two clans, and bring needed fertility blessings to our herds.
column2: 氏族希望这能缓解两个氏族之间的紧张关系，并为我们的畜群带来所需的丰饶赐福。

column1: The clan hoped this would ease tensions between the two clans, and bring blessings to our herds.
column2: 氏族希望这能缓解两个氏族之间的紧张关系，并为我们的畜群带来赐福。

column1: The Uralda cultists conducted their ritual. The ceremony
column2: 乌拉尔达的教徒举行了仪式。仪式

column1: Our ritual succeeded, too.
column2: 我们的献祭也成功了。

column1: Our sacrifice also succeeded and the farmers look forward to fatter herds. A weaponthane commented that raiding might have been a faster way to get more cows.
column2: 我们的献祭也成功了，农夫们盼望着更肥壮的畜群。一位武器领主评论道，劫掠或许能更快地得到更多牛。

column1: Our sacrifice also succeeded and the clan looks forward to increased fertility in our herds.
column2: 我们的献祭也成功了，氏族盼望着我们畜群丰饶增长。

column1: Our ceremonies did not go well, either.
column2: 我们的仪式也不顺利。

column1: The farmers are upset and worried about the already poor herds.
column2: 农夫们既沮丧又担忧已经贫弱的畜群。

column1: The farmers are sad but relieved that we have ample herds right now.
column2: 农夫们虽难过，但庆幸我们眼下畜群还算充足。

column1: How much do you give?
column2: 你愿意出多少？

column1: We sent gifts hoping that the ceremony would ease tensions between the two clans, and bring needed fertility blessings to our herds.
column2: 我们送去礼物，希望仪式能缓解两个氏族间的紧张关系，并为我们的畜群带来所需的丰饶赐福。

column1: We hoped that the fine gifts for the ceremony would ease tensions between our two clans, and bring blessings to our herds.
column2: 我们希望为仪式准备的厚礼能缓解我们两个氏族间的紧张关系，并为畜群带来赐福。

column1: The Uralda cultists held their ritual. The ceremony
column2: 乌拉尔达的教徒举行了他们的仪式。仪式

column1: The farmers are sad that we will not enjoy the blessing, and hope the \x01@! clan does not blame us. The weaponthanes are grumpy that there won’t be bigger herds to raid.
column2: 农夫们很伤心我们无法享受赐福，并希望 \x01@! 氏族不会责怪我们。武器领主们因为没有更大的畜群可劫掠而恼怒。

column1: Why won’t they give us a cow blessing?
column2: 他们为什么不给我们一场牛赐福？

column1: We don’t need to do this, but it never hurts to have more cattle.
column2: 我们不必做这事，但更多牛总没坏处。

column1: It is worth ending feuds to gain cattle.
column2: 为了得到牛，结束世仇是值得的。

column1: We could definitely stand to improve our herds, and this ritual should pay for itself in a few years.
column2: 我们绝对可以改善畜群，这场仪式过几年就能收回成本。

column1: If we agree to sacrifice, we don’t have to part with goods.
column2: 如果我们同意献祭，就不必拿出货物。

column1: Gifts sweeten all relations.
column2: 礼物能缓和一切关系。

column1: Wait until their herds are fat, then raid them.
column2: 等他们的畜群养肥了，再去劫掠。

column1: Better to raid than help those scoundrels.
column2: 劫掠比帮助那些恶棍好。

column1: We have no obligation to help another clan.
column2: 我们没有义务帮助另一个氏族。

column1: Why not keep good relations with our neighbors?
column2: 为何不与我们的邻居保持良好关系？

column1: We should welcome this offer as a way to honor the gods, and do much good for ourselves and others.
column2: 我们应该欢迎这个提议，以此敬奉神明，也为我们自己和他人带来福祉。

column1: We can do this, but our herds are healthy and fertile already.
column2: 我们可以这么做，但我们的畜群已经健壮多产了。

column1: Our herds are poor, we must sacrifice.
column2: 我们的畜群贫弱，我们必须献祭。

column1: This is an honor, and we can contribute.
column2: 这是一份荣耀，我们能够贡献。

column1: Our herds are poor, and this is an honorable way to seek Uralda’s blessings.
column2: 我们的畜群贫弱，而这是寻求尤拉尔达赐福的荣耀之道。

column1: Capture the cultists and make them do their ceremony for us!
column2: 抓住那些异教徒，让他们为我们举行仪式！

column1: Sharing in their ceremony is an honor, and will bless our herds with very little effort on our part.
column2: 参与他们的仪式是一份荣耀，几乎不费我们什么力气就能赐福畜群。

column1: Must we be entreated by every wandering band of cultists?
column2: 难道我们非得被每一群游荡的异教徒恳求不可？

column1: If our herds get fat, then others will raid us!
column2: 如果我们的畜群肥壮起来，别人就会来袭击我们！

column1: Sometimes Uralda ceremonies draw lots of biting things. Could they come here?
column2: 有时尤拉尔达仪式会引来许多噬咬之物。它们会到这儿来吗？

column1: These women know cows, and Uralda.
column2: 这些女人懂牛，也懂尤拉尔达。

column1: I suppose they want us to spend our hard-won wealth.
column2: 我想她们是想让我们花掉辛苦得来的财富。

column1: This is a chance to properly worship Uralda.
column2: 这是恰当地敬拜尤拉尔达的机会。

column1: When two can make three cows, the swords should be sheathed.
column2: 当两头能变三头牛时，就该收起刀剑。

column1: Share.
column2: 分享。

column1: If we had a shrine to Uralda, they would be conducting the ceremony here.
column2: 如果我们有一座尤拉尔达的神龛，她们就会在这里举行仪式了。

column1: This is a good first step towards ending the feud. We will need allies to build a tribe.
column2: 这是结束世仇的良好第一步。我们需要盟友来建立一个部落。

column1: \x01@\r, a Lhankor Mhy god-talker from the \x01@! clan,
column2: \x01@\r，来自 \x01@! 氏族的兰科·姆希神谕者，

column1: told us there was a secret buried in one of our fields.
column2: 告诉我们有一件秘密埋在我们的一块田里。

column1: comes to visit for a while. He spends hours huddled with \x01@\x13, and walks erratically over our clan lands. As he leaves, he tells us that he suspects we have a secret. “I read the scrolls and performed divinations. If you dig in the field between the three immovable rocks, you will find it.” Then he is gone.
column2: 来访小住。他与 \x01@\x13长时间密谈，并在我们氏族领地中漫无目的地走动。临走时，他告诉我们他怀疑我们有个秘密。“我读了卷轴，进行了占卜。如果你们在三块不可移动的岩石之间的田里挖掘，就会找到它。”然后他离开了。

column1: Ignore his advice.
column2: 忽略他的建议。

column1: \x01@\x13 said that \x01@\r meant well, but was not as versed in lore and wisdom as he thought he was.
column2: \x01@\x13 说 \x01@\r本意是好的，但他对学识和智慧的掌握并不如他自己以为的那样深。

column1: The carls were satisfied with the decision to not disturb the field.
column2: 自由民对不扰动田地的决定感到满意。

column1: \x01@\x13 was upset that the ring would turn down a chance for potential blessings. He even went out and tried digging in the field himself, but nothing came of it.
column2: \x01@\x13 对长老会放弃潜在赐福的机会感到沮丧。他甚至亲自去田里挖掘，但一无所获。

column1: The farmers were annoyed that \x01@\x13 had disturbed the field.
column2: 农夫们对 \x01@\x13 扰动了田地感到恼火。

column1: Dig in the field.
column2: 在田里挖掘。

column1: After much digging, we found a Bowl of Plenty.
column2: 经过大量挖掘，我们找到了一个丰饶之碗。

column1: We found the spot, and dug and dug. And dug some more. Just as we were turning to fill in the gigantic hole, a cottar named \x01@\x01 cried out that he found a small, dull, crooked metal bowl. \x01@\x13 said this was one of a very few ancient Bowls of Plenty, and that it would keep us from starving. We took it home, polished it up, and added it to our store of treasures.
column2: 我们找到了那个地点，挖了又挖，又挖了很久。就在我们准备填上那个巨洞时，一个名叫 \x01@\x01 的佃农喊道他找到了一个又小又暗又歪的金属碗。 \x01@\x13 说这是为数不多的古老丰饶之碗之一，能让我们免于饥饿。我们把它带回家，擦亮，并收入我们的宝库。

column1: We dug for quite a while, but found nothing.
column2: 我们挖了很久，但什么也没找到。

column1: We found the spot, and dug and dug. And dug some more. And found nothing but rocks and worms.
column2: 我们找到了那个地点，挖了又挖，又挖了很久。除了石头和虫子，什么也没找到。

column1: \x01@\x13 was troubled that the divinations were not fulfilled.
column2: \x01@\x13 因占卜未能应验而感到困扰。

column1: The farmers were annoyed that we disturbed the field.
column2: 农夫们对我们扰动了田地感到恼火。

column1: Perform our own divination on this matter.
column2: 就此事进行我们自己的占卜。

column1: The divination revealed that we should follow \x01@\r’s advice.
column2: 占卜显示我们应该遵循 \x01@\r的建议。

column1: The divination gave us confusing signs and left us no wiser than we were before.
column2: 占卜给出了令人困惑的征兆，让我们并不比之前更有见识。

column1: \x01@\r and I go way back. If he says it’s worth digging, he is sincere.
column2: \x01@\r和我交情很深。如果他说值得挖掘，他是真诚的。

column1: Let’s hope that it is something that will improve our herds.
column2: 希望那是能改善我们畜群的东西。

column1: Whatever it is, if it helps the clan it can help our herds.
column2: 不管是什么，只要能帮助氏族，就能帮助我们的畜群。

column1: Maybe it’s gold we could trade!
column2: 也许是我们可以交易的金子！

column1: If it’s valuable, we might want to keep it.
column2: 如果它很值钱，我们或许想留着它。

column1: There is no precedent for helping others find what belongs to them, even if they don’t know it.
column2: 没有先例去帮助他人找到属于他们的东西，即使他们自己并不知道。

column1: Let’s look, but not spend too much effort on this.
column2: 我们去看看，但不要在这上面花费太多精力。

column1: Whatever “it” is, it is probably worth the effort we make finding it.
column2: 无论“它”是什么，都值得我们花力气去找。

column1: We just planted that field, and the seedlings will be disturbed!
column2: 我们刚种下那块田，秧苗会被扰乱的！

column1: The crops are growing, do we want to disturb them?
column2: 庄稼正在生长，我们想打扰它们吗？

column1: Can we wait until after harvest?
column2: 我们能等到收获之后吗？

column1: We can afford to disturb a small part of the field if there is a boon to be had.
column2: 如果有好处可得，我们可以承受扰动一小块田地。

column1: If the hole is small enough, we can replant whatever is uprooted.
column2: 如果洞足够小，我们可以重新种下被拔起的作物。

column1: It’s time to harvest anyway, let’s find what \x01@\r is talking about.
column2: 反正也是收获的时候了，我们去看看 \x01@\r说的是什么。

column1: Is this the \x01@! clan’s way of making us look foolish, digging holes for nothing?
column2: 这是 \x01@! 氏族让我们显得愚蠢的方式吗，白挖坑？

column1: I’ll get my spade now, let’s go!
column2: 我现在就去拿铲子，我们走！

column1: “It” will likely be some small boulder of no account.
column2: “它”很可能是什么无关紧要的小圆石。

column1: What if we unearth an ancient curse?
column2: 如果我们挖出一个远古诅咒怎么办？

column1: I feel that \x01@\r is generous and wise, and sending us to something good.
column2: 我觉得 \x01@\r慷慨而明智，是在指引我们得到好的东西。

column1: Ancient writings tell of magic items gone missing, but not forgot.
column2: 古代文字记载了一些失踪但未被遗忘的魔法物品。

column1: It is only right to ask our gods for clarity.
column2: 向我们的神明寻求明晰是理所当然的。

column1: A divination could tell us if \x01@\r is reading the signs correctly, as his magic is not part of our clan’s.
column2: 一场占卜可以告诉我们 \x01@\r是否正确解读了征兆，因为他的魔法不属于我们氏族的体系。

column1: Perhaps this is something to strengthen the women’s magic.
column2: 也许这能增强女性魔法。

column1: I hope “it” is something that will make us richer.
column2: 我希望“那个东西”能让我们更富有。

column1: I hope that whatever happens, we stay calm.
column2: 无论发生什么，我希望我们都保持冷静。

column1: The gods may be smiling on us.
column2: 众神或许正对我们微笑。

column1: Dig.
column2: 挖。

column1: Between the three immovable stones? Oh, that’s not very much land at all! Why, we’ll find whatever “it” is – and I think “it” will some very great boon to the clan — we will find it very quickly if we dig with haste. Let’s go now!
column2: 在那三块无法移动的石头之间？哦，那根本就没多少地！哎呀，不管“那个东西”是什么——我觉得它会是氏族的一份厚礼——如果我们赶紧挖，很快就能找到。咱们现在就去！

column1: I hope it is something that we can use for building temples.
column2: 我希望它是能用来修建神庙的东西。

column1: Didn’t I say that \x01@\r was going to do us a great favor?
column2: 我不是说过 \x01@\r 会帮我们一个大忙吗？

column1: A store of treasures will help us form a tribe.
column2: 一批宝藏能帮助我们组建部落。

column1: Maybe it contains Humakti wisdom so that we can win more in battle!
column2: 也许它蕴含着胡马特智慧，这样我们就能在战斗中赢得更多！

column1: \x01@\x17 \x02\x03Left-Foot/Windblown/Chaser\x02

column1: feeding dragonewt eftlings on the sly.
column2: 偷偷喂养龙蜥幼崽。

column1: in league with the spiders that live in their hair.
column2: 与寄居在他们头发里的蜘蛛勾结。

column1: aligned with the rabbits and learning hopping magic.
column2: 与兔子结盟，学习跳跃魔法。

column1: are secretly plotting to burn down the forests.
column2: 正在秘密策划烧毁森林。

column1: tried to hold him prisoner, but he poisoned their mead and escaped.
column2: 曾试图囚禁他，但他毒害了他们的蜂蜜酒并逃脱了。

column1: have taken to worshipping squirrels.
column2: 开始崇拜松鼠。

column1: He then warns us that we \x02\x03must find badgers and wear them on our heads/should kill all our chickens/not let moonlight touch our children\x02 or we, too, shall be cursed.
column2: 然后他警告我们，我们 \x02\x03必须找到獾并把它们戴在头上/应该杀光我们所有的鸡/不要让月光触及我们的孩子\x02 ，否则我们也会被诅咒。

column1: A lone wanderer arrived, full of crazy tales.
column2: 一位孤独的流浪者到来了，满口古怪传说。

column1: Question him further.
column2: 继续质问他。

column1: Perform a ceremony to drive out his bad spirits.
column2: 举行仪式驱除他的邪恶灵体。

column1: We sacrificed to Chalana Arroy to drive out the bad spirits,
column2: 我们向查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭，以驱除邪恶灵体，

column1: As we sacrificed to Chalana Arroy, he fell, and lay in a fever for three days and three nights.
column2: 就在我们向查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭时，他倒下了，高烧昏睡了三天三夜。

column1: and succeeded. He returned home, lucid.
column2: 并且成功了。他回到家中，神志清醒。

column1: When he came to, he was clear eyed and said he had awoken from a bad dream. He thanked us, and promised to spread good words about us
column2: 他醒来时目光清澈，说自己从一个噩梦中醒来。他感谢了我们，并承诺会传扬我们的美名，

column1: as he headed back to his clan.
column2: 然后动身返回他的氏族。

column1: on his trip back to the \x01@! clan.
column2: 在他返回 \x01@! 氏族的路上。

column1: We gave him food, and sent him on his way with our blessing.
column2: 我们给了他食物，带着祝福送他上路。

column1: but they killed him.
column2: 但他们杀了他。

column1: He did not waken once, and on the fourth morning he lay still. We burned his body just outside clan lands, and his bad spirits dissolved and were dispersed to the four winds with his ashes.
column2: 他一次也没有醒来，第四天早晨他躺在那里一动不动。我们在氏族领地外焚烧了他的尸体，他的邪恶灵体随着骨灰消散，被散入四方之风。

column1: Escort him off our lands, so his foul spirits do not affect us.
column2: 把他护送离开我们的土地，以免他的邪恶灵体影响我们。

column1: Fearing his foul spirits, we sent him on his way.
column2: 由于惧怕他的邪恶灵体，我们打发他上路了。

column1: We provided him with food, and escorted him past the bounds of our lands, setting him on a path that could take him to any of several other clans. We were relieved that his bad spirits did not linger with us.
column2: 我们给了他食物，护送他越过我们的领地边界，为他指明一条可以前往其他几个氏族的路。他的邪恶灵体没有留在我们这里，我们松了口气。

column1: Let him stay with us, assign a few cottars to look after him.
column2: 让他留下来，派几个佃农照顾他。

column1: We took him in, under the care of some cottars.
column2: 我们收留了他，交给一些佃农照料。

column1: The cottars grumbled that they already had enough to do, but took reasonably good care of him. At least he did not starve.
column2: 佃农们抱怨说他们自己已经够忙了，但还是把他照顾得相当不错。至少他没有饿死。

column1: These spirits afflict humans, not cattle.
column2: 这些灵体折磨的是人，不是牲畜。

column1: Does he have anything to offer us besides his delusionary prattle?
column2: 除了那些胡言乱语，他还能给我们什么？

column1: He does not look like a fighter, nor very healthy.
column2: 他看起来不像战士，身体也不怎么健康。

column1: We have been hospitable, but have no further obligation to him.
column2: 我们一直以礼相待，但对他再没有其他义务了。

column1: Spirits like these are hard to remedy, even for the merciful Chalana Arroy.

column1: I want to learn hopping magic!

column2: 他说话像个捣蛋鬼，但我感觉他身上没有尤尔玛尔的灵体。

column2: 我们为什么要在这个没有氏族的流浪者身上浪费时间？

column2: 我们应该试着治好他。

column2: 他完了。

column2: 一个献祭——或者拖——不是松鼠，呃，幼龙，嗯，离开。对，就是这样。

column1: Handled properly, he might be a help after all.

column1: He certainly is not any kind of marriage partner for anyone.

column2: 我们已经给了这个寄生虫上好的食物和麦酒，趁他还没花掉我们更多，送他走吧。

column1: A man must have land and a home to be a proper man.
column2: 一个男人必须有土地和家园才算真正的男子汉。

column1: The gods will smile on us if we are generous and help him.
column2: 如果我们慷慨相助，众神会眷顾我们的。

column2: 给他安排一份家业，让他加入氏族。

column1: Good-bye.

column1: Oh! What if we could heal him? And adopt him? Then we would have extra hands! Wouldn’t that be great!
column2: 哦！要是我们能治好他，再收养他呢？那样我们就能多几双人手！岂不美哉！

column1: Haven’t I always said we should not let every wandering so and so into the hall?
column2: 我不是一直说吗，不该让随便哪个流浪汉都进厅堂来。

column2: 若我们收留他，其他部落会称赞我们的慷慨，还是嘲笑我们的愚蠢？

column1: sad to find him dead in one of the fields the next day.

column2: 我们焚烧了他的尸体，他的恶灵也随之消散，随骨灰散入四方之风。
