column2: 说来遗憾，自由民是对的。我们的牛远远不够自称一个氏族。

column1: All my warnings are of no consequence now.
column2: 我所有的警告如今都无济于事了。

column1: When the people are of one mind, even if they are wrong, the ring has no choice but to listen.
column2: 当众人齐心，即使他们错了，长老会也别无选择，只能倾听。

column1: Even a heroquest will not save us now.
column2: 即便是英雄远征也救不了我们了。

column1: We need enough riches to support enough weaponthanes to keep a clan safe. And we don’t have that wealth anymore.
column2: 我们需要足够的财富来供养足够的武器领主，才能保氏族安全。而我们已经没有那份财富了。

column1: Ours is not the first clan to fall apart. Alas! We will join the ranks of unsung, unnamed, forgotten peoples.
column2: 我们不是第一个崩解的氏族。唉！我们将加入那些无赞歌、无姓名、被遗忘的族群之列。

column1: I did not listen to earlier warnings. Now I am forced to listen to this.
column2: 我当初没有听从早先的警告。如今我被迫听这些。

column1: We were doomed from the start.
column2: 我们从一开始就注定要灭亡。

column1: It’s the end of all of us — whatever will become of us? Will we all starve or be enthralled?
column2: 我们所有人的末日到了——我们会变成什么样？全饿死，还是沦为奴隶？

column1: It’s just too… too… I just can’t… I could just weep.
column2: 这实在……太……我实在……我只能哭。

column1: Each can go their own way, then. As will I.
column2: 那便各走各路吧。我也一样。

column1: Disband the clan? Of course we must disband the clan. We were fools to think we could continue after this debacle. Why, I’m ready leave, myself, right now.
column2: 解散氏族？我们当然必须解散氏族。我们真是蠢货，竟以为这场惨败之后还能继续下去。哈，我自己都准备现在就走人了。

column1: We failed to lead this clan to glory. We failed even to survive.
column2: 我们未能领导这个氏族走向荣耀，甚至未能幸存下来。

column1: If only we’d built up our scrolls, we might have had knowledge to avoid this disaster.
column2: 要是我们当初积攒了更多的卷轴，或许就能掌握避免这场灾难的知识了。

column1: The eligible young men and women will wed better if they can find a bigger clan to join with.
column2: 那些适婚的年轻男女，如果能找到一个更大的氏族加入，就能嫁娶得更好。

column1: It’s no use blaming the women for this mess. And no real use blaming the men, either…
column2: 把这场烂摊子归咎于女人们毫无用处。归咎于男人们也没什么用……

column1: I’m sorry to say it, but some mistakes cannot be forgiven, and those who make them do not get more chances.
column2: 我很遗憾地说，有些错误不可原谅，犯错的人也不配再有机会。

column1: We wasted our most precious treasure — our honor — and so wasted the rest of our greatness.
column2: 我们浪费了我们最珍贵的财富——我们的荣誉——也因此挥霍了我们其余的伟大。

column1: It’s no use blaming the men for this mess. And no real use blaming the women, either…
column2: 把这场烂摊子归咎于男人们毫无用处。归咎于女人们也没什么用……

column1: Mayhap we were too quick to appease, and too slow to respond to threats with shows of strength.
column2: 或许我们太急于安抚，而在用力量回应威胁时又太慢了。

column1: We don’t have enough farmers to spare for brewing beer, and the crops we will grow will not see us through a harsh winter.
column2: 我们没有足够的农夫可以腾出手来酿造啤酒，而且我们种出的作物也无法让我们熬过严冬。

column1: No skill, nor will, nor blade can keep a herd together when the wolves of want nip its haunches.
column2: 当匮乏的狼群撕咬畜群的后腿时，没有技巧、意志或刀剑能维持畜群不散。

column1: The most skillful potter cannot make dishes without clay.
column2: 最娴熟的陶匠没有黏土也做不出器皿。

column1: I’d say give the carls cattle and win them back, but we have no cattle left to be generous with.
column2: 我本想说要给自由民牲畜把他们争取回来，可我们已经没有剩下的牲畜可以慷慨相赠了。

column1: We’re through.
column2: 我们完了。

column1: We cannot maintain any of our shrines, let alone our temples.
column2: 我们连任何一座神龛都维护不了，更不用说我们的神殿了。

column1: Oh! How I wish I had been wrong when I said we would fall apart!
column2: 哦！我真希望我说过我们会分崩离析的话是错的！

column1: There is an hour for japes, a day for pranks, and a season for foolishness. This sad time is none of those.
column2: 有开玩笑的时辰，有恶作剧的日子，也有犯傻的季节。但这段悲伤的时光不属于其中任何一种。

column1: Perhaps we were too quick to fight, and too slow to find to peaceful ways of settling our differences.
column2: 或许我们太急于开战，而在寻找和平解决分歧的方式上又太慢了。

column2: 后来，商人们讲述了一个残余氏族的故事：他们被慷慨接纳，但其中一人不像其他人那样安顿下来。这个人指责、哀怨、抱怨得如此厉害，很快就被剥夺了公民权。之后她究竟怎样了，无人知晓。

column1: As the last clan members left the tula, one of our more poetic carls gazed back at the empty steads, ruined fortifications, and weed-encroached fields. Before turning away for the last time, he uttered our final words:
column2: 当最后一批氏族成员离开图拉时，我们一位较有诗意的自由民回头望向那些空荡荡的农庄、毁坏的防御工事和杂草丛生的田野。在最后一次转身离去前，他说出了我们最后的遗言：

column1: “We will not be remembered as a great clan. Or even an adequate clan. If the sagas mention us at all, they will recall our terrible mistakes. We acted when we should have listened, failed to act when we should have done great deeds, and made enemies where we should have made friends.
column2: “我们不会被铭记为一个伟大的氏族，甚至不会被铭记为一个合格的氏族。如果传说提到我们，它们只会忆起我们可怕的错误。该倾听时我们却行动，该建功立业时我们却无所作为，该交友时我们却树敌。

column1: Our people are dispersed, our ring disgraced, our tula abandoned. Thus ends our sorry tale, the tale of clan \x01@".”
column2: 我们的人民四散，我们的议会蒙羞，我们的图拉被遗弃。我们悲哀的故事就此终结， \x01@"氏族的故事。”

column1: Our scouts found a strange clan of beast folk who were like ducks.
column2: 我们的斥候发现了一个奇怪的兽人氏族，长得很像鸭人。

column1: Approach the ducks and offer them a peace pact.
column2: 接近那些鸭人，向他们提出和平协议。

column1: With justice and mercy, we offered peace to the duck people, who henceforth gave our clan a place of honor in their songs.
column2: 以正义和仁慈，我们向鸭人提出了和平，从此他们在歌谣中给了我们氏族一席荣耀之地。

column1: The ducks accepted, and gave our clan a place of honor in their songs. They said they would also praise us to their kin in the swamp.
column2: 鸭人接受了，并在他们的歌谣中给了我们氏族一席荣耀之地。他们说还会向沼泽中的亲族赞颂我们。

column1: Our elders were incensed that we would make friendly overtures to our ancient enemies, and warned us that our magic would suffer.
column2: 我们的长老们对于我们向宿敌示好感到愤怒，并警告说我们的魔法会受损。

column1: They feared the anger of our ancestral spirits.
column2: 他们惧怕我们先祖之灵的愤怒。

column1: “Each year, you must give us enough food to feed \x01@\x13 of our people.”
column2: “每年，你们必须供给我们足以养活我们 \x01@\x13 民众的食物。”

column1: Tempering mercy with shrewdness, we exacted payment from the ducks, whose larders were heavy.
column2: 以精明调和仁慈，我们向粮仓充实的鸭人榨取了贡品。

column1: We exacted payment from the ducks, whose larders were heavy. They swore oaths to pay after the harvest.
column2: 我们向粮仓充实的鸭人榨取了贡品。他们立誓在收获后支付。

column1: “Each year, you must give us enough food to feed \x01@\x15 of our people.”
column2: “每年，你们必须供给我们足以养活我们 \x01@\x15 民众的食物。”

column1: Demand that the ducks cede you half their lands.
column2: 要求鸭人割让一半土地给你们。

column1: The treacherous ducks rebuffed our kind offer to share their land, responding with a savage attack.
column2: 背信弃义的鸭人拒绝了我们共享土地的善意提议，并以野蛮攻击回应。

column1: Stoutly we defended; swiftly did the ducks waddle from the battlefield.
column2: 我们顽强防御；鸭人迅速摇摆着逃离战场。

column1: By right of the sword, we gained rich land.
column2: 凭借剑的权利，我们获得了丰饶的土地。

column1: By right of the sword, we took all their land, rather than the half we had asked for.
column2: 凭借剑的权利，我们夺走了他们全部的土地，而非我们原先要求的一半。

column1: Nobody worried much about where the surviving ducks might have fled to.
column2: 没多少人担心幸存的鸭人逃往何处。

column1: We swore grim vengeance against a deceptively puissant foe.
column2: 我们立下冷酷的誓言，要向一个看似弱小实则强大的敌人复仇。

column1: Launch a surprise attack against the puny ducks.
column2: 对孱弱的鸭人发动突袭。

column1: Rudely did the impertinent ducks rebuff our offer to share their land with them. Boldly did we raid them, driving them quacking from their homes.
column2: 无礼的鸭人粗暴拒绝了我们要与他们共享土地的提议。我们勇敢地突袭了他们，将他们嘎嘎叫着赶出家园。

column1: We sought to drive the impertinent ducks off land far more suited to us than to them.
column2: 我们试图将无礼的鸭人赶离那远更适合我们而非他们的土地。

column1: We decided to raid our feathered neighbors.
column2: 我们决定突袭我们那些长羽毛的邻居。

column1: We were shocked to discover that they were determined foes.
column2: 我们震惊地发现他们是意志坚决的敌人。

column1: The ducks were here first. It is as if we are their guests. We may not act against them.
column2: 鸭人先在这里定居。我们仿佛是他们的客人。我们不能对他们采取行动。

column1: The ducks are not of our kind. We owe no obligations to them.
column2: 鸭人并非我族类。我们对他们不欠任何义务。

column1: The ducks appear to practice a corrupted version of Orlanthi ways.
column2: 鸭人似乎奉行一种腐化的奥朗斯之道。

column1: Other clans will despise us if we attack such tiny foes.
column2: 若我们攻击如此弱小的敌人，其他氏族会鄙视我们。

column1: It is not as if we will lose the respect of our allies if we displace these creatures.
column2: 即便我们驱逐这些生物，也不至于失去盟友的尊重。

column1: If we don’t attack them, some other clan will.
column2: 若我们不攻击他们，别的氏族也会动手。

column1: We can easily drive off the weakest of the Beast Folk.
column2: 我们能轻易赶走最弱小的兽人。

column1: They look like easy prey, but we don’t know much about them.
column2: 他们看起来像是容易得手的猎物，但我们对他们所知甚少。

column1: The ducks know their home terrain. Many a brave man has been humiliated because he underestimated a foe.
column2: 鸭人熟悉家园地形。多少勇士因低估敌人而蒙羞。

column1: What great good fortune to find our ancient enemies so close at hand, so easy to smash!
column2: 何等天赐良机，竟在近在咫尺之处发现我们的宿敌，且如此易于击溃！

column1: The ducks are our ancient enemies. We must make them pay until we are strong enough to ruin them.
column2: 鸭人是我们的宿敌。我们必须让他们付出代价，直到我们有足够力量将他们毁灭。

column1: We shouldn’t neglect our own land by raiding during planting time, no matter how tempting this new land seems.
column2: 我们不应在播种时节因突袭而荒废自家土地，无论这片新土地多么诱人。

column1: We shouldn’t neglect our own land by raiding during harvest time, no matter how tempting this new land seems.
column2: 我们不应在收获时节因突袭而荒废自家土地，无论这片新土地多么诱人。

column1: Offer them protection, but ask for nothing in return. They’ll be overwhelmed by our generosity, and feel obliged to out-match it.
column2: 向他们提供保护，但不要任何回报。他们将因我们的慷慨而不知所措，并觉得有义务加倍回报。

column1: The better offer we give them, the more we’ll get in return.
column2: 我们给出的条件越好，得到的回报就越多。

column1: They will fear our strength. Make demands with confidence.
column2: 他们会畏惧我们的力量。自信地提出要求。

column1: Demand tribute, but not so much that they feel resistance is the only option. It is better to gain something for no effort than everything at too high a price.
column2: 要求进贡，但不要多到让他们觉得抵抗是唯一选择。不劳而获总好过付出过高代价换取一切。

column1: Let’s not be too bold. You never know what strange magic members of the Elder Races might wield.
column2: 我们不可过于鲁莽。你永远不知古老种族的成员会施展何种奇异法术。

column1: The beastfolk are the ancient enemies of our clan. The spirits of our forefathers demand that we destroy them.
column2: 兽人是我们氏族的宿敌。先祖之灵要求我们毁灭他们。

column1: They are peaceful farmers. It might be legal to extort from them, or even raid them, but it is not right.
column2: 他们是和平的农夫。向他们勒索甚至突袭或许合法，但并不正当。

column1: Carls and fighters agree on something for once, and we’re thinking of denying them? If we don’t attack the ducks, we’ll be deafened by grumbling.
column2: 自由民和战士们难得意见一致，我们却想拒绝他们？若我们不攻击鸭人，抱怨声将震耳欲聋。

column1: Beastfolk? So close? Our ancestors speak clearly.
column2: 兽人？如此之近？先祖之言清晰昭示。

column1: There is a time for mercy and peace. But the beast people are our ancient enemies.
column2: 仁慈与和平自有其时。但兽人是我们宿敌。

column1: Purefeather, leader of the Ducks, rebuffs your approach. “You featherless are all the same. All is force of arms! We may not be strong, but we are fast, mobile, and tenacious. If you or any other featherless attack us, you will regret it!”
column2: 鸭人之主纯羽拒绝了你们的接近。“你们这些无羽者都一样。武力至上！我们或许不强，但我们迅捷、灵活且坚韧。若你们或其他无羽者攻击我们，你们会后悔的！”

column1: QuiteAnAdventure
column2: QuiteAnAdventure

column1: Withdraw from the duck lands without apologies or threats.
column2: 撤离鸭人的土地，不道歉也不威胁。

column1: Our scouts discovered the strange duck people. We learned much about them, revealing little of our own intentions.
column2: 我们的斥候发现了奇异的鸭人。我们了解了他们许多，却极少暴露自身意图。

column1: We left the ducks wondering what we intended.
column2: 我们让鸭人猜疑我们的意图。

column1: Offer the ducks \x01@\x13 food as a token of your sincere apology.
column2: 向鸭人提供 \x01@\x13 食物作为诚心道歉的象征。

column1: Our generous clan chief parleyed with Purefeather, Lord of the Ducks. With a gift, we bought Purefeather’s favor.
column2: 我们慷慨的氏族酋长与鸭人之主纯羽谈判。我们以一件礼物换取了纯羽的恩惠。

column1: Purefeather seemed pleased with our generous gift.
column2: 纯羽似乎对我们慷慨的礼物感到满意。

column1: Castigate the ducks for their rudeness, short stature, and foul smell. Then return home.
column2: 痛斥鸭人的无礼、矮小身材和恶臭，然后返回家园。

column1: Our chieftain’s wit left Purefeather, cantankerous despot of the ducks, speechless.
column2: 我们酋长的机敏让暴躁的鸭人暴君纯羽哑口无言。

column1: Remind the ducks how strong your clan is. Demand \x01@\x13 food as a token of their sincere apology.
column2: 提醒鸭人你们的氏族何等强大。要求 \x01@\x13 食物作为他们诚心道歉的象征。

column1: We humbled Purefeather, haughty chieftain of the ducks, forcing him to apologize for his ill-chosen words.
column2: 我们羞辱了高傲的鸭人酋长纯羽，迫使他为自己措辞不当而道歉。

column1: Return home, then launch a surprise raid against the ducks.
column2: 返回家园，然后对鸭人发动一次突袭。

column1: We drove them quacking from their homes.
column2: 我们将他们嘎嘎叫着赶出家园。

column1: Shocked to discover that they were determined foes, we watched several of our proudest warriors fall among their slings and daggers.
column2: 震惊地发现他们竟是死敌，我们眼睁睁看着几位最骄傲的勇士倒在了他们的投石索和匕首下。

column1: Give them a token of apology. They will be embarrassed and refuse to accept it, and we will gain their respect.
column2: 送他们一份道歉的礼物。他们会尴尬地拒绝接受，而我们则会赢得他们的尊重。

column1: These ducks seem very angry. We have no chance of unruffling their feathers now.
column2: 这些鸭人看上去怒不可遏。现在想平息他们的怒气已无可能。

column1: This is no time to bargain. We must either withdraw or fight. Which is the better course, I cannot say.
column2: 现在不是讨价还价的时候。我们要么撤退，要么战斗。哪条路更好，我无法断言。

column1: Now that I see them up close, I see that I have underestimated these beastfolk. If we fight them, they will destroy us.
column2: 如今近距离观察，我发现我低估了这些兽人。如果我们与他们交战，他们会摧毁我们。

column1: The ducks may be better at sneaking than we are, but they admit that we are better at fighting. Let us fight them.
column2: 鸭人或许比我们更擅长潜行，但他们承认我们更善于战斗。让我们与他们一战。

column1: The ducks are tougher than they look. We can beat them on a raid, but the survivors could whittle us down through petty harassment.
column2: 鸭人比他们看起来更坚韧。我们能通过突袭击败他们，但幸存者会用零星的骚扰慢慢削弱我们。

column1: We cannot abide this nonsense.
column2: 我们无法容忍这种胡闹。

column1: It’s planting time! Surely any retribution these ducks deserve can wait until the crops are sown.
column2: 现在是播种时节！这些鸭人应得的报复，肯定能等到庄稼种下再说。

column1: It’s harvest time! Surely any retribution these ducks deserve can wait until the crops are in.
column2: 现在是收获时节！这些鸭人应得的报复，肯定能等到庄稼收完再说。

column1: I’d say some groveling is in order here.
column2: 依我看，现在就该卑躬屈膝赔个不是。

column1: Whatever we do, we can’t let ourselves be humiliated by a talking duck.
column2: 无论我们做什么，都不能让自己被一只会说话的鸭子羞辱。

column1: There is nothing to be gained from further antagonizing this quacking buffoon.
column2: 继续激怒这个嘎嘎叫的丑角，毫无益处。

column1: Ducks? We are insulted by ducks? By Orlanth, they must pay!
column2: 鸭子？我们被鸭子羞辱？以奥兰斯之名，他们必须付出代价！

column1: They’re not the same as the beastfolk our ancestors fought. But I still think we should smash them.
column2: 他们与我们祖先战斗过的兽人不同。但我仍然认为我们应该把他们揍扁。

column1: War? Yes.
column2: 战争？是的。

column1: The ducks delivered their annual tribute of food.
column2: 鸭人们送来了他们每年的贡品——食物。

column1: sceneR002
column2: sceneR002

column1: The widow \x01B3, who not long ago swore vengeance against the clan that killed her husband, has taken it. Men loyal to her have captured two prisoners from the \x01@! clan. \x01B3’s allies are exultant, but others are worried.
column2: 那位寡妇 \x01B3，不久前还发誓要向杀死她丈夫的氏族复仇，如今已经动手了。忠于她的人从 \x01@! 氏族俘虏了两名囚犯。 \x01B3的盟友欢欣鼓舞，但其他人忧心忡忡。

column1: Apologize, and free the hostages.
column2: 道歉，并释放人质。

column1: We apologized to the men, and let them go.
column2: 我们向那些人道了歉，并释放了他们。

column1: They demanded compensation for the theft of their freedom.
column2: 他们要求为失去自由而获得补偿。

column1: Do you agree to compensate them?
column2: 你同意补偿他们吗？

column1: They left, muttering darkly of our injustice to them.
column2: 他们走了，阴沉地嘟囔着我们对他们不公。

column1: How much do you give them?
column2: 你给他们多少？

column1: They left, assuring us that they understood the widows’ sorrow.
column2: 他们走了，向我们保证他们理解寡妇的悲伤。

column1: The people were stirred by their leaders’ sense of justice, and supported their decision to free the hostages.
column2: 民众被领袖的正义感所打动，支持他们释放人质的决定。

column1: The carls muttered that the leaders had no respect for their rights of vengeance.
column2: 自由民们抱怨说，领袖们根本不尊重他们复仇的权利。

column1: We extracted a goodly price in return for the hostages’ freedom.
column2: 我们以人质的自由为代价，换取了可观的赎金。

column1: We accepted some cattle in return for the hostages’ freedom.
column2: 我们以人质的自由为代价，接受了一些牛只。

column1: Force the men to join the clan as replacements for the slain.
column2: 强迫这些人加入氏族，作为死者的替代者。

column1: We took them into our clan, as replacements for the slain men.
column2: 我们接纳他们加入氏族，作为死者的替代者。

column1: After a few seasons, even \x01B3 accepted the new carls.
column2: 过了几个季节，就连 \x01B3 也接受了这些新自由民。

column1: Free the hostages without apology.
column2: 释放人质，但不道歉。

column1: Without admitting wrongdoing, we let the captives go.
column2: 我们没有承认过错，释放了俘虏。

column1: They left, muttering darkly of our injustice to them. \x01B3 was unhappy, but her anger soon faded.
column2: 他们走了，阴沉地嘟囔着我们对他们不公。 \x01B3 很不高兴，但她的怒火很快消散了。

column1: Let \x01B3 do what she wants with them.
column2: 让 \x01B3 随心处置他们吧。

column1: After a while, we learned that \x01B3 had tortured and killed her hostages.
column2: 过了一阵子，我们听闻 \x01B3 折磨并杀害了她的人质。

column1: Ritually heal \x01B3’s grief.
column2: 通过仪式治愈 \x01B3的悲伤。

column1: \x01B3 clenched her teeth and said that no magic would cure her fury, for it was not an illness, but a thing that was just and true.
column2: \x01B3 咬紧牙关说，没有魔法能治愈她的狂怒，因为那不是疾病，而是公正而真实之物。

column1: Keep them as thralls.
column2: 把他们留作奴隶。

column1: \x01B3 taunted the new thralls, and assigned them heavy, dirty work, but eventually she treated them no differently than any other thrall.
column2: \x01B3 羞辱了这些新奴隶，派给他们繁重肮脏的活计，但最终她对待他们与其他奴隶别无二致。

column1: They have reason to be slighted, but if I honey up my words they’ll be grateful to trade cows for hostages.
column2: 他们理应感到受辱，但如果我把话说得甜些，他们会感激我们用牛换人质的。

column1: We can perhaps get four or five cows for the hostages.
column2: 我们或许能用这些人质换到四五头牛。

column1: This matter is hardly draped in glory, but if the rest of you think we should fight, we can fight.
column2: 这件事算不上光彩，但如果你们其他人都认为该打，那我们就打。

column1: Don’t let this become another feud.
column2: 别让这事变成另一场世仇。

column1: They’re lucky to be alive.
column2: 他们能活着就算走运了。

column1: Their clan killed a few of our men. They can scarcely whine if we borrow a couple of theirs for a few days.
column2: 他们的氏族杀了我们几个人。我们借他们几个人用几天，他们可没资格抱怨。

column1: If we stretch the precedents, we can justify \x01B3’s actions. But stretch them too far, and they will snap back at us.
column2: 如果我们勉强援引先例，可以为 \x01B3的行为辩护。但若牵强过度，反噬的将是自己。

column1: The damage has been done. We can try to make it better, or just take care of ourselves.
column2: 伤害已经造成。我们可以试着补救，或者只管我们自己。

column1: Before we heal this rift, we must heal the hatred in \x01B3’s heart.
column2: 在弥合这道裂痕之前，我们必须先治愈 \x01B3心中的仇恨。

column1: Ernalda’s daughter, Babeester Gor, gave herself to vengeance. Is \x01B3 prepared for that terrible step?
column2: 埃尔纳尔达之女芭碧斯特·戈尔将自己献给了复仇。 \x01B3 准备好迈出那可怕的一步了吗？

column1: Some stories are meant to end in death. Let \x01B3 finish this.
column2: 有些故事注定以死亡收场。让 \x01B3 了结这一切吧。

column1: They look like they would be able to help in the fields.
column2: 他们看起来能在田里帮忙。

column1: When individuals seek justice, they end up with vengeance. Vengeance always ends in war.
column2: 当个人寻求公正时，最终只会得到复仇。而复仇永远以战争告终。

column1: If they show us disrespect, show them what their blood looks like.
column2: 若他们不敬我们，就让他们见识自己的血是什么样子。

column1: One of the ways our ancestors survived the Darkness was by taking thralls from other clans, to help with hard labor.
column2: 我们祖先度过黑暗时代的方法之一，就是从其他氏族掳来奴隶，帮忙干苦活。

column1: Over time, mercy fought a war for \x01B3’s heart, and drove anger out. She married one of her hostages, and took a bride price with her to his clan.
column2: 随着时间的推移，仁慈为 \x01B3的心打了一场战争，驱散了愤怒。她嫁给了她的一名俘虏，并带着彩礼去了他的氏族。

column1: \x01B3 softened her anger, and eventually married one of her hostages.
column2: \x01B3 缓和了她的愤怒，并最终嫁给了她的一名俘虏。

column1: We lodged a legal claim against Mordrim with his chieftain, \x01@\x08.
column2: 我们向他的酋长 \x01@\x08对莫德里姆提出了法律诉讼。

column1: Keep Blacktail; give us another treasure in exchange.
column2: 留下黑尾；给我们另一件宝物作为交换。

column1: We offered to let him keep Blacktail, if he would give us another treasure in exchange.
column2: 我们提议让他留下黑尾，如果他愿意给我们另一件宝物作为交换。

column1: Instead, he returned Blacktail to us.
column2: 相反，他把黑尾还给了我们。

column1: Which treasure do you want in exchange?
column2: 你想要哪件宝物作为交换？

column1: Thanestriker, a legendary sword?
column2: 领主杀手，一把传奇之剑？

column1: We took the legendary sword, Thanestriker.
column2: 我们拿走了传奇之剑，领主杀手。

column1: The warriors were impressed by the sword.
column2: 武士们对这柄剑印象深刻。

column1: The Glass Coin, a treasure of the far-off mermaids?
column2: 玻璃硬币，遥远美人鱼的宝物？

column1: We took a Glass Coin, minted by the far-off mermaids.
column2: 我们拿走了一枚由遥远美人鱼铸造的玻璃硬币。

column1: The god-talkers were impressed by the coin.
column2: 神言者对这枚硬币印象深刻。

column1: \x01@\x08 refused our claim.
column2: \x01@\x08 拒绝了我们的要求。

column1: Our carls rejoiced when they saw that Blacktail was among the spoils of victory.
column2: 我们的自由民看到黑尾在战利品中时欣喜若狂。

column1: The carls lamented that we had twice failed to regain Blacktail, first with words of law, then with swords.
column2: 自由民哀叹我们两次未能夺回黑尾，先用法律言辞，后用刀剑。

column1: Keep Blacktail; give us cows instead.
column2: 留下黑尾；给我们牛只作为替代。

column1: We offered to let them keep the bull, if they would give us cows.
column2: 我们提议让他们留下公牛，如果他们愿意给我们牛只。

column1: How many cows do you demand?
column2: 你要求多少头牛？

column1: Keep the bull, ally with our clan.
column2: 留下公牛，与我们的氏族结盟。

column1: We offered to let them keep Blacktail, in exchange for an alliance between our clans.
column2: 我们提议让他们留下黑尾，以换取我们氏族之间的联盟。

column1: Return of the bull, nothing more.
column2: 归还公牛，仅此而已。

column1: Return the bull and give us cows as a penalty.
column2: 归还公牛并给我们牛只作为惩罚。

column1: We demanded both the return of Blacktail, and the forfeit of a number of cows.
column2: 我们要求归还黑尾，并罚没一定数量的牛只。

column1: Blacktail is worth \x01@\x17 cows over his lifetime.
column2: 黑尾一生价值 \x01@\x17 头牛。

column1: Blacktail is a very valuable animal.
column2: 黑尾是一头非常珍贵的牲畜。

column1: Blacktail is worth \x01@\x18 cows over his lifetime.
column2: 黑尾一生价值 \x01@\x18 头牛。

column1: Blacktail is worth \x01@\x19 cows over his lifetime.
column2: 黑尾一生价值 \x01@\x19 头牛。

column1: If we ask for the return of the bull and a penalty, the penalty should not exceed ten cows.
column2: 如果我们要求归还公牛并处以惩罚，惩罚不应超过十头牛。

column1: One treasure is worth another.
column2: 一件宝物与另一件等价。

column1: If we ask for the return of the bull and a penalty, the penalty should not exceed three cows.
column2: 如果我们要求归还公牛并处以惩罚，惩罚不应超过三头牛。

column1: I am confident that I have assembled all of the relevant precedents.
column2: 我相信我已经收集了所有相关先例。

column1: \x01@\x08 is known for \x04 toughness.
column2: \x01@\x08 以 \x04 强硬著称。

column1: \x01@\x08 is tough, but just.
column2: \x01@\x08 强硬但公正。

column1: \x01@\x08 is known for \x04 toughness, and \x04 disregard for justice.
column2: \x01@\x08 以 \x04 强硬和 \x04 无视公正著称。

column1: I’m relieved that we can try to get the bull back without raiding, since we need every hand for planting.
column2: 我很欣慰我们可以尝试不通过袭击夺回公牛，因为我们需要所有劳力用于播种。

column1: I’m relieved that we can try to get the bull back without raiding, since we need every hand for the harvest.
column2: 我很欣慰我们可以尝试不通过袭击夺回公牛，因为我们需要所有劳力用于收获。

column1: A treasure confers more than just its concrete benefits. It brings our clan prestige.
column2: 一件宝物的价值远不止其具体好处。它为我们的氏族带来声望。

column1: I’ve heard they have a sword called Chaos Striker! We must ask for that!
column2: 我听说他们有一把叫混沌打击者的剑！我们必须要求那把！

column1: No use posting guards after the bull has been stolen.
column2: 公牛被盗后再派卫兵也没用了。

column1: The theft of Blacktail is the ultimate humiliation. It’s like they stole our … you know…
column2: 黑尾被偷是终极羞辱。就像他们偷走了我们的……你知道的……

column1: \x01@\x08 will doubtless use Blacktail to fund temples that will put ours to shame.
column2: \x01@\x08 无疑会用黑尾资助神庙，让我们的相形见绌。

column1: sceneR004
column2: sceneR004

column1: A barn on the outer perimeter of the tula is burned to the ground. Witnesses report that ducks were seen running from the scene. No doubt they belong to the clan ruled by the duck chieftain, \x01@\x10.
column2: 图拉领地外围的一座谷仓被烧为平地。目击者报告看到鸭人从现场跑出。无疑他们属于鸭人酋长 \x01@\x10统治的氏族。

column1: Cruelly and without provocation, troublesome ducks burnt one of our barns.
column2: 残忍且毫无挑衅地，捣乱的鸭人烧毁了我们的一个谷仓。

column1: Demand compensation from \x01@\x10.
column2: 向 \x01@\x10要求赔偿。

column1: How much food do you demand as compensation?
column2: 你要求多少食物作为赔偿？

column1: With stout determination, we demanded compensation from their chieftain, \x01@\x10.
column2: 怀着坚定的决心，我们向他们的酋长 \x01@\x10要求赔偿。

column1: Shown the justice of our cause, \x01@\x10 had to honor our request.
column2: 见证了我们的正义事业， \x01@\x10 不得不尊重我们的请求。

column1: Cravenly, the duck refused us.
column2: 怯懦地，那鸭人拒绝了我们。

column1: Do you wish to launch a punitive raid against them?
column2: 你是否希望对它们发动惩罚性袭击？

column1: Do you wish to launch a punitive raid against them, even though it’s Sea season?
column2: 即使现在是海季，你是否希望对它们发动惩罚性袭击？

column1: Do you wish to launch a punitive raid against them, even though it’s Earth season?
column2: 即使现在是地季，你是否希望对它们发动惩罚性袭击？

column1: Demand that \x01@\x10 punish the arsonists.
column2: 要求 \x01@\x10 惩罚纵火者。

column1: We demanded that \x01@\x10 punish the arsonists.
column2: 我们要求 \x01@\x10 惩罚纵火者。

column1: He promised to do so, and composed a curious poem, in an ancient style, praising our mercy.
column2: 他答应这样做，并创作了一首古怪的诗，以古老风格赞美我们的仁慈。

column1: While rebuilding the barn, the carls complained loudly about the ring’s inaction.
column2: 重建谷仓时，自由民大声抱怨长老会的不作为。

column1: Increase patrols.
column2: 增加巡逻。

column1: We increased our patrols.
column2: 我们增加了巡逻。

column1: Our weaponthanes kept a wary eye out for ducks, but saw no more.
column2: 我们的武器领主警惕地留意鸭人，但再没看到。

column1: Order \x01@\x10 to deliver the arsonists to you.
column2: 命令 \x01@\x10 将纵火者交给你。

column1: Uncompromisingly, we demanded that \x01@\x10 turn the miscreants over to our justice.
column2: 毫不妥协地，我们要求 \x01@\x10 将歹徒移交给我们审判。

column1: He quacked out many irrelevant precedents, but finally saw the equity of our demand.
column2: 他嘎嘎叫出许多无关先例，但最终看到了我们要求的公正性。

column1: What do you do to the arsonists?
column2: 你如何处置纵火者？

column1: Kill them
column2: 处死他们

column1: We made a fiery example of the ducks. They smelled like chicken.
column2: 我们把这些鸭人烧成了警示。他们闻起来像鸡肉。

column1: Beat them
column2: 痛打他们

column1: In full view of their fellows, we beat them like feather pillows.
column2: 在他们的同伴注视下，我们把它们打得像羽毛枕头一样。

column1: Sternly admonish them.
column2: 严厉训诫他们。

column1: We admonished them sternly, until tears of remorse ran down their beaks.
column2: 我们严厉训诫他们，直到悔恨的泪水顺着他们的喙流下。

column1: Increase the tribute owed by the ducks.
column2: 提高鸭人应缴的贡品。

column1: Sternly, we ordered the ducks to increase their tribute to us.
column2: 我们严厉命令鸭人增加对我们的贡品。

column1: Grudgingly, they agreed to bring half again as much food each year.
column2: 他们不情愿地同意每年多带来一半的食物。

column1: A barn is worth twenty-four Bushels of grain.
column2: 一座谷仓值二十四蒲式耳谷物。

column1: A barn is worth sixteen Bushels of grain.
column2: 一座谷仓值十六蒲式耳谷物。

column1: A barn is worth sixteen Bushels of grain, but their houses are of mud and straw. They will think it is worth less.
column2: 一座谷仓值十六蒲式耳谷物，但他们的房子是泥和稻草造的。他们会认为它更不值钱。

column1: Demand that the offending ducks to be turned over to us. We should then kill them, as an example to others.
column2: 要求将冒犯的鸭人移交给我们。然后我们应当杀死他们，以儆效尤。

column1: I can cite precedents that allow the offending ducks to be turned over to us.
column2: 我可以援引先例，允许将冒犯的鸭人移交给我们。

column1: I can cite precedents that allow the offending ducks to be turned over to us. Once honored, we can afford to show mercy.
column2: 我可以援引先例，允许将冒犯的鸭人移交给我们。一旦获得荣誉，我们可以施以仁慈。

column1: This as an opportunity to increase the tribute they owe us.
column2: 这是一个增加他们欠我们贡品的机会。

column1: Our fields need our attention — a couple of steads are not worth losing our crops over.
column2: 我们的田地需要照料——为几个农庄而毁掉庄稼不值得。

column1: If I were asked to turn over several of my people to another clan’s justice, I would not like it.
column2: 如果要求我把我的几个人交给另一个氏族审判，我不会喜欢。

column1: Let us not forget that the beast folk are our ancient enemies.
column2: 我们不要忘记，兽人是我们的宿敌。

column1: Remember, the ducks are Orlanthi, too. Not as Orlanthi as we are, but still…
column2: 记住，鸭人也是奥兰西人。虽然不像我们那么奥兰西，但仍然……

column1: We’re behind in temple building. Squeeze the ducks till they quack for mercy.
column2: 我们在神庙建造上落后了。压榨鸭人，直到他们嘎嘎求饶。

column1: What’s a little fire between friends? What I mean to say is, \x01@\x10 owes loyalty to his people, just as we do to our own.
column2: 朋友之间一点小火算什么？我要说的是， \x01@\x10 效忠于他的人民，就如同我们效忠于我们的人民一样。

column1: I hope they make trouble. Some of these the ducks may be worthy opponents.
column2: 我希望他们惹麻烦。这些鸭人中有些可能够格当对手。

column1: They burned our barn, and that’s bad. But let’s not stoop to their level.
column2: 他们烧了我们的谷仓，这很糟糕。但我们不要降低到他们的水平。

column1: Red feathers flew over home of Uralda’s children. White feathers must give silver eggs in return.
column2: 红色羽毛飞过乌拉尔达孩子们的家。白色羽毛必须回报银色蛋。

column1: Those ducks never attack when we’re strong…
column2: 那些鸭人从来不在我们强大时攻击……

column1: sceneR005
column2: sceneR005

column1: A wounded warrior stumbles desperately into the clan hall, an arm outstretched in a silent plea for help. From the symbols he wears, you recognize him as a holy warrior of Urox the Storm Bull. He says he was ambushed by Chaos worshippers. After you tend to him, what do you do?
column2: 一名受伤的战士绝望地跌跌撞撞进入部族大厅，一条手臂伸出，无声地恳求帮助。从他佩戴的符号，你认出他是风暴公牛乌洛克斯的神圣战士。他说他被混沌崇拜者伏击了。在你照料他之后，你做什么？

column1: A wounded Uroxi stumbled into our clan hall, claiming to have been ambushed by Chaos worshippers.
column2: 一名受伤的乌洛希跌跌撞撞进入我们的部族大厅，声称被混沌崇拜者伏击了。

column1: Don’t even tend to him; tell him to seek help elsewhere.
column2: 甚至不要照料他；告诉他去别处寻求帮助。

column1: He spit on our ring members and said that their ignorance gave comfort to Chaos.
column2: 他朝我们的圆环成员吐口水，并说他们的无知给了混沌安慰。

column1: How do you respond?
column2: 你如何回应？

column1: Take his abuse.
column2: 忍受他的辱骂。

column1: Silently did we endure the abuse of this rough Chaos fighter.
column2: 我们默默忍受了这个粗暴的混沌战士的辱骂。

column1: Our proud warriors had to listen to his abuse in silence.
column2: 我们骄傲的战士不得不沉默地听他的辱骂。

column1: Scold him for his poor manners.
column2: 责骂他无礼。

column1: We scolded him for his poor manners.
column2: 我们责骂他无礼。

column1: Our warriors smiled to see the rude Uroxi stutter and fume when he was chastised.
column2: 我们的战士看到那个粗鲁的乌洛希在被训斥时结结巴巴、怒气冲冲，都笑了。

column1: Tend to his wounds, and increase patrols.
column2: 照料他的伤口，并增加巡逻。

column1: Once healed, the Storm Bull moved on. He praised our vigilance in the eternal struggle against Chaos.
column2: 一旦痊愈，风暴公牛继续前行。他赞扬我们在对抗混沌的永恒斗争中保持警惕。

column1: Heal him, then lend him warriors to fight against Chaos.
column2: 治愈他，然后借给他战士去对抗混沌。

column1: Once he was healed up and rested, we lent him warriors, so that he could track down the Chaos fiends who had wounded him.
column2: 等他痊愈休息后，我们借给他战士，以便他能追踪伤害他的混沌恶魔。

column1: How many warriors do you loan to him?
column2: 你借给他多少战士？

column1: But he cursed us for not providing a sufficiently large force, and stomped off without showing us what a great warrior he was.
column2: 但他因我们没有提供足够大的队伍而诅咒我们，然后跺着脚走了，没有向我们展示他有多伟大。

column1: We care for the Uroxi until he was well, but when he saw the warriors we assigned to him, he cursed us. “You say you want to fight Chaos. You give me just a few sorry warriors. You are broo-bait!” He left.
column2: 我们照料乌洛希直到他康复，但当他看到我们指派给他的战士时，他诅咒我们：“你说你们想对抗混沌。你们只给了我几个可怜的战士。你们就是布鲁的诱饵！”他走了。

column1: Few were sorry to see him go, but some of the god-talkers said that if we had wanted to fight Chaos, we should have taken the fight seriously.
column2: 看到他走，很少有人感到遗憾，但一些神言者说，如果我们真的想对抗混沌，就应该认真对待这场战斗。

column1: A few weeks later, our
column2: 几周后，我们的

column1: warrior returned. He
column2: 战士回来了。他

column1: warriors returned. They
column2: 战士们回来了。他们

column1: said they had found nothing, and that the Storm Bull had grown bored and wandered off.
column2: 说他们什么都没找到，而且风暴公牛感到无聊就游荡走了。

column1: Some of them
column2: 他们中有些人

column1: doubted that those who wounded him were indeed Chaos worshippers.
column2: 怀疑那些伤害他的人是否真的是混沌崇拜者。

column1: The party found a nest of Chaos cultists not far from our tula. Horrific was the battle.
column2: 队伍在离我们领地不远处发现了一窝混沌邪教徒。战斗十分恐怖。

column1: Great was our victory.
column2: 我们的胜利是伟大的。

column1: Terrible were our losses.
column2: 我们的损失是惨重的。

column1: Some feared that our Chaos enemies would be even bolder now.
column2: 有些人担心我们的混沌敌人现在会更加大胆。

column1: Let him stay as long as he wants.
column2: 让他想待多久就待多久。

column1: He stayed for many weeks, drinking much beer, demonstrating his ability to pass wind on command, frightening the children with tales of his exploits, and pinching the women. Then he departed, pronouncing us his favorite clan in all of Dragon Pass.
column2: 他待了许多周，喝了很多啤酒，展示他按命令放屁的能力，用他的功绩故事吓唬孩子，还掐女人。然后他离开了，宣称我们是整个龙之隘口中他最喜欢的氏族。

column1: See him on his way as soon as he’s well.
column2: 他一好就送他上路。

column1: We tended to him, and escorted him to the boundaries of our tula. He spit on the leader of the escort party and said that our ignorance gave comfort to Chaos.
column2: 我们照料他，并护送他到我们领地的边界。他朝护送队伍的领头吐口水，并说我们的无知给了混沌安慰。

column1: We let him go without yelling back at him. With his bad attitude, he wasn’t going to live long anyway.
column2: 我们没有朝他吼回去就让他走了。以他那恶劣的态度，反正他也活不长。

column1: “Pah! Let’s see what good your manners do when Wakboth visits!” said the Uroxi.
column2: “呸！等瓦克博斯来的时候，看看你们的礼貌有什么用！”乌洛希说道。

column1: Storm Bulls are not exactly lawless. But most of them feel that rules are for other people.
column2: 风暴公牛信徒并非完全无法无天，但他们大多觉得规则是给别人定的。

column1: As King Heort once said, “One needs Storm Bulls. Often, one needs them to be somewhere else.”
column2: 正如赫奥特王曾言：“人需要风暴公牛信徒。但常常，需要他们待在其他地方。”

column1: If we are too rude to him, he will make trouble. If we are too welcoming, his friends will come here, and make trouble.
column2: 如果我们对他太粗鲁，他会惹麻烦；如果我们太热情，他的朋友们就会跑来，惹麻烦。

column1: We have had no kinstrife here, and no signs of Chaos.
column2: 我们这里没有发生过亲族相残，也没有混沌的迹象。

column1: We have seen many ill omens and other signs of Chaos recently.
column2: 最近我们见到了许多凶兆和其他混沌的迹象。

column1: I can’t believe we’re even discussing this. Of course we help him! Anyone who thinks different needs some sense knocked into them.
column2: 我简直不敢相信我们居然在讨论这个。当然要帮他！谁要是觉得不该帮，就该被敲醒脑子。

column1: The Uroxi are mighty in battle, but tend to see Chaos under every leaf.
column2: 乌洛希在战斗中很强大，但他们总爱每片叶子底下都看出混沌来。

column1: He looks like a jolly fellow; I don’t see what you’re all afraid of.
column2: 他看起来是个快活的家伙，我真不懂你们在怕什么。

column1: Storm Bull is brother to Orlanth. He is the bad wind. He is the smiter of Chaos, and the breaker of furniture.
column2: 风暴公牛是奥兰斯的兄弟。他是恶风。他是混沌的惩戒者，也是家具的破坏者。

column1: If we’re nice to him, maybe he’ll build a Storm Bull shrine here.
column2: 如果我们对他好点，也许他会在这里建一座风暴公牛神殿。

column1: The carls might be afraid that he’ll hurt them.
column2: 自由民可能会害怕他会伤害他们。

column1: It is easy to be polite to the well-mannered. The true test is if one can be courteous to the rude.
column2: 对彬彬有礼的人客气很容易。真正的考验是对粗鲁的人能否保持礼貌。

column1: Give him what he wants. We don’t want the Storm Bulls thinking we’re stingy.
column2: 给他想要的。我们可不想让风暴公牛信徒觉得我们吝啬。

column1: I’ve heard that Storm Bulls sometimes give generous rewards to those who help them.
column2: 我听说风暴公牛信徒有时会慷慨地回报帮助过他们的人。

column1: Once this mighty Chaos fighter is back on his feet, we should enlist his aid to scour our tula.
column2: 等这位强大的混沌战士恢复过来，我们应该请他帮忙扫荡我们的领地。

column1: He probably is a strong and virile fellow, but he’s not a good match for any of our daughters.
column2: 他大概是个强壮有活力的家伙，但他配不上我们任何一个女儿。

column1: sceneR006
column2: sceneR006

column1: A trio of Storm Bulls descend on your clan hall. They say they’ve just finished cleaning out a nest of Chaos creatures, and are in the mood to celebrate. “We know that you are good friends to Urox,” they say, as they proceed to get spectacularly drunk — and destructively rowdy.
column2: 三个风暴公牛信徒降临到你们的部族大厅。他们说刚清完一窝混沌生物的巢穴，正想庆祝一番。“我们知道你们是乌洛克斯的好朋友，”他们说着，便开始狂饮——喝得酩酊大醉，闹得破坏一切。

column1: Three Storm Bulls came, got drunk, and wrecked things.
column2: 三个风暴公牛信徒来了，喝醉了，把东西砸了个稀烂。

column1: Ask them to leave.
column2: 叫他们离开。

column1: We asked them to leave.
column2: 我们叫他们离开。

column1: Grumbling, they stumbled out of our clan hall.
column2: 他们咕哝着，跌跌撞撞地走出了我们的部族大厅。

column1: They told us that if they were to leave now, it would give comfort to Chaos.
column2: 他们告诉我们，如果现在离开，就会让混沌得逞。

column1: Demand compensation for the damage they cause.
column2: 要求他们赔偿造成的损失。

column1: “Here, take this worthless bauble we found in the Chaos den,” they said, contemptuously. They tossed us a sparkling green gem.
column2: “喏，这是我们在混沌巢穴里找到的破玩意儿，”他们轻蔑地说，扔给我们一颗闪闪发光的绿色宝石。

column1: “Legal bull is not for the Desert Storm, which cannot be contained by words alone,” belched the Storm Bulls.
column2: “合法的公牛管不了沙漠风暴，言语可约束不住，”风暴公牛信徒打着嗝说。

column1: Tell them that Chaos menaces a nearby clan.
column2: 跟他们说混沌正威胁着附近一个氏族。

column1: Which clan do you name?
column2: 你报哪个氏族的名字？

column1: We told them that broos were to be found in the \x01@\x18 clan’s woods.
column2: 我们告诉他们，在 \x01@\x18 氏族的林子里发现了布鲁斯。

column1: “We know very well there is no Chaos there!” they cried. “How dare you deceive us about a thing so serious as Chaos, trickster?” They broke a few more things, and departed.
column2: “我们很清楚那里根本没有混沌！”他们喊道，“你这个骗子，怎么敢在混沌这么严重的事情上欺骗我们？”他们又砸了几样东西，然后离开了。

column1: They laughed. “If a trickster told us that, we would know it to be a lie. But you are no betrayers, so we know you are mistaken.”
column2: 他们大笑起来。“要是骗子告诉我们这事，我们肯定知道是谎话。但你们不是背信者，所以我们知道你们只是搞错了。”

column1: Tell them to leave.
column2: 叫他们离开。

column1: We told them to leave us alone.
column2: 我们叫他们别来烦我们。

column1: “You going to make us?” they grunted.
column2: “你们要赶我们走？”他们咕哝道。

column1: Do you try to eject them forcibly?
column2: 你要强行驱逐他们吗？

column1: “Yes,” we said, “we are going to make you.”
column2: “是的，”我们说，“我们要赶你们走。”

column1: A brawl ensued, and many fixtures of our clan hall were thereby destroyed.
column2: 一场斗殴随之发生，我们部族大厅里的许多陈设都被毁了。

column1: We bested them. They thanked us for giving them a challenging wrestle, and cheerfully promised to come back soon.
column2: 我们打赢了他们。他们感谢我们给了他们一场有挑战的摔跤较量，兴高采烈地保证很快就会再回来。

column1: Easily the Uroxi bested us, proving themselves to be Storm Khans, powerful holy warriors of their god.
column2: 乌洛希轻松地打败了我们，证明了自己是风暴可汗，是他们神的强大圣战士。

column1: We decided not to turn on our guests.
column2: 我们决定不对客人们动手。

column1: Wait them out; they’ll get bored eventually.
column2: 等着他们闹够；他们迟早会厌烦的。

column1: After seven days and seven nights of \x02\x02raucous/disruptive\x02 and boorish behavior, they pronounced us boring, and moved on in search of another Chaos enemy, or another supply of beer.
column2: 经过七天七夜的 \x02\x02喧闹/扰人\x02 且粗鄙的行为后，他们嫌我们无聊，便继续上路去寻找其他混沌敌人，或者另一批啤酒去了。

column1: What’s the problem? They’re just having a little fun.
column2: 有什么问题？他们只是找点乐子而已。

column1: Wealth means nothing to Uroxi warriors, so we can’t buy them off.
column2: 财富对乌洛希战士毫无意义，所以我们没法收买他们。

column1: Roving bands of Storm Bulls don’t belong to any clan. At least there won’t be any political effects from whatever we do.
column2: 风暴公牛信徒的游荡队伍不属于任何氏族。至少我们做什么都不会有政治影响。

column1: Even while drunk, they are alert warriors ready for action. I’d prefer not to fight them.
column2: 就算喝醉了，他们也是随时待命的警觉战士。我宁愿不和他们打。

column1: I hate to see our clan hall get wrecked like this.
column2: 我真不想看到我们的部族大厅被这样糟蹋。

column1: Their obnoxious behavior conceals their heavy hearts.
column2: 他们惹人厌的行为底下藏着沉重的心事。

column1: The best thing about Storm Bulls is their gullibility. Let me at them.
column2: 风暴公牛信徒最棒的一点就是好骗。让我去应付他们。

column1: Bulls will be bulls.
column2: 公牛终究是公牛。

column1: Get them out of here, before all of our boys want to grow up to be Storm Bulls.
column2: 把他们赶出去，免得我们所有孩子都想长大当风暴公牛信徒。

column1: I can’t believe these scoundrels! They’re so — so — arrogant!
column2: 我真不敢相信这些无赖！他们怎么——怎么——这么傲慢！

column1: I’m sorry, I haven’t been paying attention. I’ve had a bit to drink, myself.
column2: 抱歉，我没注意听。我自己也喝了不少。

column1: They’ll fly into a rage and kill us all!
column2: 他们会暴怒起来，把我们全杀了！

column1: A bad wind blows away the awful odor, but brings its own smell.
column2: 恶风吹走了恶臭，却带来了它自己的气味。

column1: “No one can make you do anything” is our most important law. But even Storm Bulls must be responsible for their actions.
column2: “没人能强迫你做任何事”是我们最重要的律法。但就连风暴公牛也必须为自己的行为负责。

column1: sceneR007
column2: sceneR007

column1: While plowing the fields, the carls find something strange. It’s the enormous skull of some kind of dragon creature.
column2: 自由民在犁地时发现了某种奇怪的东西。那是某类龙类生物的巨型头骨。

column1: While plowing the fields, the carls found something strange. It was the enormous skull of some kind of dragon creature.
column2: 自由民在犁地时发现了某种奇怪的东西。那是某类龙类生物的巨型头骨。

column1: Destroy it.
column2: 毁掉它。

column1: We destroyed it.
column2: 我们毁掉了它。

column1: Our warriors made a game of seeing who could smash the most with one blow. A good game, while it lasted.
column2: 我们的武士们以此为戏，看谁一击能砸碎最多碎片。还算不错的一场游戏，趁它还在的时候。

column1: Display it in a temple or shrine.
column2: 放在神殿或圣所中展示。

column1: We decided to display it in our shrine to Maran Gor.
column2: 我们决定把它放在供奉玛兰·戈尔的圣所中展示。

column1: We decided to display it in our temple to Orlanth.
column2: 我们决定把它放在供奉奥兰斯的圣殿中展示。

column1: Since it came from the earth, we put it in our temple to Ernalda.
column2: 既然它来自大地，我们便把它放在了供奉埃尔纳尔达的圣殿中。

column1: We decided to display it in our temple to Elmal.
column2: 我们决定把它放在供奉埃尔玛的圣殿中展示。

column1: We displayed it in a holy building.
column2: 我们把它展示在一座神圣的建筑里。

column1: Display it in the clan hall.
column2: 放在部族大厅里展示。

column1: We used it to decorate our clan hall.
column2: 我们用它来装饰我们的部族大厅。

column1: Visitors from other clans seemed impressed.
column2: 来自其他氏族的访客似乎印象深刻。

column1: Our dragon-hating ancestors, less so.
column2: 而我们那些憎恨巨龙的祖先，则不那么以为然。

column1: Rebury it.
column2: 重新埋回去。

column1: We put it back where we found it.
column2: 我们把它放回了发现的地方。

column1: The carls shrugged and put the bones back into the ground.
column2: 自由民耸耸肩，把骨头重新埋进了土里。

column1: Trade it away.
column2: 拿去交易。

column1: We traded it away.
column2: 我们把它交易掉了。

column1: It fetched a good price from someone who valued curiosities more than silver.
column2: 从某个视奇物重于银币的人那里卖了个好价钱。

column1: A mere novelty, it was worth little.
column2: 不过是件新奇玩意儿，值不了几个钱。

column1: That’s no dragon skull. That’s the skull of a giant troll, or herd mammal.
column2: 那不是龙的头骨。那是一头巨魔或大哺乳动物的头骨。

column1: It might be worth something as a curiosity.
column2: 作为一件奇物，它或许值点钱。

column1: I can probably get a good price for it.
column2: 我大概能给它卖个好价钱。

column1: Let the warriors help the carls.
column2: 让武士们去帮帮自由民。

column1: Remember that dragons ruled this land. And they could still come back.
column2: 记住，巨龙曾统治这片土地。它们仍可能卷土重来。

column1: It’s an Earthshaker. Kin to the great dragons, but not a dragon itself.
column2: 那是撼地者。与巨龙是近亲，但本身并非巨龙。

column1: It’s probably some sort of dragon thing. Not something our ancestors care about, at any rate.
column2: 大概是某种龙类玩意儿。反正在我们祖先眼里不值一提。

column1: Our clan has never trusted dragon things.
column2: 我们氏族从不信任龙类的东西。

column1: For some reason, this makes me think of Maran Gor, Ernalda’s earth-shaking sister.
column2: 不知为何，这让我想到了玛兰·戈尔，埃尔纳尔达那位撼动大地的姐妹。

column1: Perhaps if we trade it to another clan, it will foster harmony.
column2: 假如我们把它交易给另一个氏族，或许能促进和谐。

column1: This treasure is ours. Ours! We would be mad to get rid of it.
column2: 这件宝物是我们的。我们的！把它丢掉简直是疯了。

column1: Will the dragonewts be offended if we display this skull of their ancestors?
column2: 如果我们展示这些祖先的头骨，龙人会不会感到冒犯？

column1: What harm can a pile of brittle bones do to a clan as mighty as ours?
column2: 一堆脆骨头能对我们这样强大的氏族造成什么伤害？

column1: Dedicate this treasure to the gods.
column2: 把这件宝物献给诸神。

column1: Won’t we seem ridiculous if we proudly display something we don’t understand?
column2: 如果我们骄傲地展示自己都不懂的东西，难道不会显得很可笑吗？

column1: It’s very powerful. Other clans will envy us.
column2: 它力量强大。其他氏族会嫉妒我们的。

column1: What would Eurmal do? I mean, what would Orlanth do?
column2: 尤尔马尔会怎么做？我是说，奥兰斯会怎么做？

column1: I don’t really care. Just get it out of the fields.
column2: 我其实不在乎。把它弄出田地就行。

column1: sceneR008
column2: sceneR008

column1: A creature, the likes of which you have never seen before, hails the guards on your perimeter. He introduces himself as Mathrania the Magnificent, and requests a parley with the clan ring.
column2: 一头你们前所未见的生物，向你们外围的守卫打招呼。它自称伟大的马斯拉尼亚，并请求与氏族议会进行会谈。

column1: A creature we had not seen before came to talk to us. He called himself Mathrania the Magnificent, and requested a parley with the clan ring. He was sort of like a dragon, yet not a dragon.
column2: 一头我们从未见过的生物前来与我们交谈。它自称伟大的马斯拉尼亚，并请求与氏族议会进行会谈。它有点像龙，又不是龙。

column1: Invite him into the clan hall.
column2: 请它进入部族大厅。

column1: We invited him inside the clan hall.
column2: 我们请它进入了部族大厅。

column1: Mathrania politely declined to enter the hall, fearing that he would bump his head, but spoke with us in the market square.
column2: 马斯拉尼亚礼貌地拒绝进入大厅，担心会撞到头，但它在集市广场上与我们交谈。

column1: Invite him onto your lands, but no further.
column2: 请它进入你的领地，但仅止于此。

column1: The ring met with him just inside our boundary stones.
column2: 议会就在我们的边界石内侧与它见面。

column1: Invite him to the market square.
column2: 请它到集市广场。

column1: We invited him to the market square to talk.
column2: 我们请它到集市广场交谈。

column1: “It’s a dragon! Kill it!”
column2: “是龙！杀了它！”

column1: Our clan has never trusted dragons, so we attacked it.
column2: 我们氏族从不信任巨龙，于是我们攻击了它。

column1: After a pitched battle, in which our men were beset by many strange magics, we slew the thing.
column2: 经过一场激战，我们的战士被许多奇异魔法所困，最终我们杀死了那东西。

column1: It killed some of our men with strange magics, and stalked off before we could regroup.
column2: 它用奇异魔法杀死了我们一些人，然后在我们重新集结之前大摇大摆地离开了。

column1: Shoo him away.
column2: 把它赶走。

column1: We told him to leave us alone, and he did so.
column2: 我们叫它离我们远点，它照做了。

column1: The creature left us.
column2: 那生物离开了我们。

column1: Talk to him outside the tula’s boundary.
column2: 在图拉领地的边界外与它谈话。

column1: The ring met with him without allowing him past our boundary stones.
column2: 议会在不让它越过边界石的情况下与它见面。

column1: Those teeth of his show him to be trustworthy. He eats plants, not people.
column2: 它的那些牙齿表明它值得信任。它吃植物，不吃人。

column1: Never slap a hand outstretched to you in friendship.
column2: 永远不要推开向你伸出的友谊之手。

column1: If it does mean us harm, we’re better to keep it outside our fortifications.
column2: 如果它确实想害我们，我们最好把它挡在防御工事之外。

column1: The paraphernalia he carries is clearly that of a magician.
column2: 它携带的器具明显是法师之物。

column1: It looks like a dragon to me. Our clan has never had truck with dragons.
column2: 在我看来它像条龙。我们氏族从不跟龙打交道。

column1: Let’s get him inebriated and see if he spills any dragon secrets.
column2: 我们把它灌醉，看看它会不会泄露什么龙的秘密。

column1: There used to be creatures like this all over the continent, but in most places they are now just memories.
column2: 这种生物曾经遍布整个大陆，但在大多数地方，它们如今只是记忆了。

column1: He looks exhausted. Let’s extend him full hospitality.
column2: 它看起来精疲力竭。让我们尽情款待它。

column1: I knew we’d be up to our necks in dragons if we migrated here.
column2: 我就知道，一迁徙到这里，我们就要被龙淹没了。

column1: “Be a friend to your friend’s friends, and a foe to your foe’s friends.”
column2: “对朋友的朋友友善，对敌人的敌人敌对。”

column1: Let’s lay on a huge feast for him, so he will think us the most generous of all clans.
column2: 为它大摆宴席，这样它就会认为我们是所有氏族中最慷慨的。

column1: “Your people are remembered here. It is said that you believe in six social virtues. Assuming, for the sake of argument, that you had to choose between them, which virtue would you say is the most important?”
column2: “你的人民在这里被铭记。据说你们信奉六种社会美德。假设，为了论证起见，你必须在其中做出选择，你会说哪一种美德最重要？”

column1: Mathrania knew of our customs, and asked us which of the Six Social Virtues was most important.
column2: 马斯拉尼亚知道我们的习俗，并问我们六种社会美德中哪一种最重要。

column1: Decline to answer.
column2: 拒绝回答。

column1: We declined to answer.
column2: 我们拒绝回答。

column1: He gave us an archaic form of the Parting Words, and left.
column2: 他用一种古旧的告别语祝福我们，然后离开了。

column1: “Defense”
column2: “防御”

column1: We told him that defense was the most important virtue.
column2: 我们告诉他防御是最重要的美德。

column1: He thanked us for our answer. He gave us an archaic form of the Parting Words, and left.
column2: 他感谢我们的回答。他用一种古旧的告别语祝福我们，然后离开了。

column1: “Honor.”
column2: “荣誉。”

column1: We told him that honor was the most important virtue.
column2: 我们告诉他荣誉是最重要的美德。

column1: “Hospitality”
column2: “好客”

column1: We told him that hospitality was the most important virtue.
column2: 我们告诉他好客是最重要的美德。

column1: “Justice”
column2: “公正”

column1: We told him that justice was the most important virtue.
column2: 我们告诉他公正是最重要的美德。

column1: “Obedience.”
column2: “服从。”

column1: We told him that obedience was the most important virtue.
column2: 我们告诉他服从是最重要的美德。

column1: “Provision.”
column2: “供给。”

column1: We told him that provision was the most important virtue.
column2: 我们告诉他供给是最重要的美德。

column1: Provision is the most important, for, without food, all other questions are moot.
column2: 供给最重要，因为没有食物，其他所有问题都无从谈起。

column1: Obedience is the most important, for without it, the other virtues cannot be enforced.
column2: 服从最重要，因为没有它，其他美德就无法强制执行。

column1: Defense is the most important, for if enemies slay us, the other virtues cannot be upheld.
column2: 防御最重要，因为如果敌人杀死我们，其他美德就无法维持。

column1: Defense is the most important. If enemies slay us, the other virtues cannot be upheld.
column2: 防御最重要。如果敌人杀死我们，其他美德就无法维持。

column1: Defense is the most important. If enemies kill us, the other virtues are worthless.
column2: 防御最重要。如果敌人杀死我们，其他美德就毫无价值。

column1: Justice is the most important. All of the written authorities say so.
column2: 公正最重要。所有典籍都这么说。

column1: Hospitality is the most important. Without it, King Heort’s Ring would never have enumerated the other virtues.
column2: 好客最重要。没有它，赫奥尔特王的议会就不可能列举出其他美德。

column1: Honor is the most important. It is better to die than to lose it.
column2: 荣誉最重要。宁死也不愿失去它。

column1: Let’s not waste time arguing over what is correct. Let’s figure out what he wants to hear.
column2: 别浪费时间争论什么是对的。我们得弄清楚他想听什么。

column1: We shall not be interrogated on our most precious beliefs by a well-dressed skink!
column2: 我们绝不会被一只衣冠楚楚的蜥蜴盘问我们最珍视的信仰！

column1: If we tell him the wrong thing, he will run through our market smashing things!
column2: 如果我们说错了，他会跑遍市场砸烂一切！

column1: How can we possibly pick one of them as the most important? They’re all equal.
column2: 我们怎么可能从中选一个作为最重要的？它们全都同等重要。

column1: Hospitality is the most important virtue. Without it, no one would be able to travel, and we could entertain no guests.
column2: 好客是最重要的美德。没有它，没人能旅行，我们也无法招待客人。

column1: Our ancestors never invited dragon-like beasts into their marketplace.
column2: 我们的祖先从未邀请过龙类野兽进入他们的市场。

column1: sceneR009
column2: sceneR009

column1: Someone, or something, has evaded your patrols to leave a curious gift on the doorstep of your clan hall. The gift is a basket containing large, and peculiarly shaped, eggs. The children are wonderstruck. Adults wonder whether this omen bodes good or ill.
column2: 有人，或者什么东西，避开了你们的巡逻队，在部族大厅的门阶上留下了一件奇特的礼物。礼物是一个篮子，里面装满了大而形状古怪的蛋。孩子们惊叹不已。大人们则猜测这个预兆是吉是凶。

column1: A clutch of big, funny-shaped eggs was left on our doorstep.
column2: 一窝大而形状古怪的蛋被留在了我们的门阶上。

column1: Care for them until they hatch.
column2: 照料它们直到孵化。

column1: We decided to see what would hatch out of them, if anything.
column2: 我们决定看看它们会孵出什么，如果有的话。

column1: The children were happy, and checked the eggs several times a day.
column2: 孩子们很高兴，每天检查好几次那些蛋。

column1: Cook them and serve to prominent carls.
column2: 煮熟后献给重要的自由民。

column1: We served them as the main dish at a feast honoring our carls.
column2: 我们在宴请自由民的宴会上把它们作为主菜。

column1: The carls said they had a strong taste.
column2: 自由民说它们味道很浓。

column1: Cook them and serve to the clan ring.
column2: 煮熟后献给氏族议会。

column1: Their taste was strong, and they were very filling.
column2: 它们味道浓郁，而且很顶饱。

column1: Cook them and serve to top weaponthanes.
column2: 煮熟后献给最高阶的武器领主。

column1: We served them as the main dish at a feast honoring our weaponthanes.
column2: 我们在宴请武器领主的宴会上把它们作为主菜。

column1: Our leading warriors said they had a strong taste, and were very filling.
column2: 我们的主要武士说它们味道很浓，而且很顶饱。

column1: Trade them away.
column2: 卖掉它们。

column1: We decided to trade them away.
column2: 我们决定把它们卖掉。

column1: The eggs fetched a fair price.
column2: 那些蛋卖了个公道的价钱。

column1: No one wanted them.
column2: 没人想要它们。

column1: We don’t know if these are safe to eat or not.
column2: 我们不知道这些蛋能不能安全食用。

column1: These could be very valuable.
column2: 这些可能非常值钱。

column1: They’re worth something, I imagine, but they’re still only eggs.
column2: 我想它们值点钱，但终究只是蛋而已。

column1: At best, we could get \x01@\x13 cows worth of goods for them.
column2: 最多能换到 \x01@\x13 头牛价值的货物。

column1: The carls could use a gesture of respect about now.
column2: 现在自由民正需要一点尊重的表示。

column1: Our warriors need to know that we are grateful to them.
column2: 我们的武士需要知道我们感激他们。

column1: Whoever left these meant them as a gift. We can do whatever we want with them.
column2: 无论谁留下这些，都是把它们当作礼物。我们可以随意处置。

column1: If we are to understand this omen, we should look for clues as to who left them.
column2: 如果要理解这个预兆，我们应该寻找线索，看看是谁留下的。

column1: See the design on the basket? The same design was on the robe of Mathrania the Magnificent.
column2: 看到篮子上的花纹了吗？伟大的马斯拉尼亚的长袍上也有同样的花纹。

column1: These eggs were left as children for adoption, not omelettes in waiting.
column2: 这些蛋是被留下等待收养的孩子，而不是等着做成的煎蛋卷。

column1: Mmm, I can taste them already.
column2: 嗯，我已经能尝到它们的味道了。

column1: We’re always bribing and compensating others. Let’s reserve this feast for ourselves.
column2: 我们总是在贿赂和补偿别人。这顿盛宴留给我们自己享用吧。

column1: Let’s leave them, and see what hatches out. Maybe we’ll get baby dragons of our very own.
column2: 让它们留着，看看会孵出什么。也许我们会有自己的小龙崽。

column1: It would be rude to eat these ourselves.
column2: 我们自己吃掉它们会很失礼。

column1: sceneR010
column2: sceneR010

column1: The strange eggs hatch, and stranger creatures emerge from them. They are large baby lizard-things, with a ruff of bone around their beaked faces. You can be sure that nothing this odd has ever been born in one of your barns before.
column2: 奇怪的蛋孵化了，更奇怪的生物从中钻出。它们是巨大的幼年蜥蜴状生物，鸟喙般的面孔周围有一圈骨质的皱领。你可以肯定，你的谷仓里从未诞生过如此古怪的东西。

column1: The eggs hatched, and weird little lizards came out.
column2: 蛋孵化了，出来了一些古怪的小蜥蜴。

column1: Kill them immediately.
column2: 立即杀死它们。

column1: We killed them right away.
column2: 我们立刻杀死了它们。

column1: Sacrifice them to Ernalda.
column2: 把它们献祭给厄娜尔达。

column1: We sacrificed them to Ernalda.
column2: 我们把它们献祭给了厄娜尔达。

column1: \x01@\x05 said the omens were favorable, and she was now closer to Ernalda.
column2: \x01@\x05 说征兆是吉利的，她现在更接近厄娜尔达了。

column1: \x01@\x05 said she could not determine whether Ernalda was pleased by the sacrifice.
column2: \x01@\x05 称她无法确定厄尔纳尔达是否满意这次献祭。

column1: Sacrifice them to Orlanth.
column2: 将它们献祭给奥兰斯。

column1: We sacrificed them to Orlanth.
column2: 我们将它们献祭给了奥兰斯。

column1: The storm priests could not agree on the meaning of the omens.
column2: 风暴祭司们无法就预兆的含义达成一致。

column1: Sacrifice them to Uralda.
column2: 将它们献祭给乌拉尔达。

column1: We sacrificed them to Uralda.
column2: 我们将它们献祭给了乌拉尔达。

column1: \x01@\x14 said the omens were favorable, and she was now closer to Uralda.
column2: \x01@\x14 称预兆有利，她现在更接近乌拉尔达了。

column1: \x01@\x14 said she could not determine whether Uralda was pleased by the sacrifice.
column2: \x01@\x14 称她无法确定乌拉尔达是否满意这次献祭。

column1: Try to raise them.
column2: 尝试把它们养大。

column1: We decided to try to raise the creatures, to see what they would become.
column2: 我们决定尝试把这些生物养大，看看它们会变成什么。

column1: The carls were not at all sure how they would turn out, but agreed to raise them and see.
column2: 自由民们完全不确定它们会长成什么样，但同意把它们养大看看。

column1: Try to trade them to another clan.
column2: 尝试把它们交易给另一个氏族。

column1: We traded the creatures to another clan.
column2: 我们将这些生物交易给了另一个氏族。

column1: \x01@N was able to exchange the creatures for some trade goods.
column2: \x01@N 成功用这些生物换到了一些贸易货物。

column1: We tried to trade them away, but in the meantime, they grew very large.
column2: 我们试图把它们交易掉，但在此期间，它们长得非常大。

column1: We don’t know anything about these creatures. Are they good to eat? Do they carry diseases?
column2: 我们对这些生物一无所知。它们能吃吗？它们携带疾病吗？

column1: Look at their teeth. They eat plants, just like cows.
column2: 看看它们的牙齿。它们吃植物，就像牛一样。

column1: Look at their shape. Those bones will grow to carry great amounts of meat.
column2: 看看它们的体型。那些骨骼会长到能承载大量肉。

column1: No sane trader would accept one of these loathsome things.
column2: 没有一个理智的商人会接受这些可憎的东西中的一个。

column1: These creatures are a novelty at the very least. Perhaps they are valuable.
column2: 这些生物起码算个新奇玩意。也许很有价值。

column1: How big do you think these get? How much pasture land will they require?
column2: 你觉得它们能长多大？需要多少牧场？

column1: These things could be connected to the dragons. We’re in trouble.
column2: 这些东西可能和龙有关。我们有麻烦了。

column1: These things could be connected to the dragons.
column2: 这些东西可能和龙有关。

column1: These creatures are called Earthshakers, and are holy to Ernalda’s sister, Maran Gor.
column2: 这种生物被称为地动者，对厄尔纳尔达的姐妹玛兰·戈尔来说是神圣的。

column1: Whatever we do, no good will come of it.
column2: 不管我们怎么做，都不会有好结果。

column1: It will be exciting and wondrous to see what these things become.
column2: 看看这些东西会变成什么，会既激动又奇妙。

column1: It is hard to see how we benefit either way.
column2: 很难看出我们如何能从任何一种方式中获益。

column1: Those things are revolting! What fool suggested we keep the eggs?
column2: 那些东西真恶心！是哪个蠢货建议我们留着那些蛋的？

column1: sceneR011
column2: sceneR011

column1: The carls grow exasperated with the big lizards. They still trample the grain once in a while, and their appetites haven’t gone down one whit. The carls say that we should make up our minds what to do with them, soon.
column2: 自由民们越来越不耐烦这些大蜥蜴。它们仍然时不时踩踏谷物，胃口一点也没减。自由民们说我们该尽快决定怎么处理它们。

column1: The carls demanded that we do something with the big lizards, which were still causing some problems.
column2: 自由民们要求我们对这些仍在制造麻烦的大蜥蜴采取行动。

column1: The strange little lizards have grown up into strange, very big lizards. They’re trampling the grain, eating voraciously, and accidentally stomping the occasional chicken. No one knows what to do with them.
column2: 奇怪的小蜥蜴长成了奇怪的大蜥蜴。它们踩踏谷物，狼吞虎咽，还不小心踩死偶尔出现的鸡。没人知道该拿它们怎么办。

column1: The strange little lizards grew up into strange big lizards. They caused many problems.
column2: 奇怪的小蜥蜴长成了奇怪的大蜥蜴。它们造成了许多麻烦。

column1: Leave them alone.
column2: 别管它们。

column1: We learned how to stay out of their way, and they sort of learned how not to stomp on things, most of the time.
column2: 我们学会了如何避开它们，它们也大致学会了如何不踩坏东西——大多数时候。

column1: Sacrifice them to a god.
column2: 把它们献祭给一位神明。

column1: Which god do you sacrifice them to?
column2: 你打算把它们献祭给哪位神明？

column1: We sacrificed them.
column2: 我们献祭了它们。

column1: The god-talkers said that \x01@\x07 had accepted our sacrifice.
column2: 神言者们说 \x01@\x07 接受了我们的献祭。

column1: Slaughter them for their meat.
column2: 宰了它们吃肉。

column1: They died like cows, but weren’t quite as tasty.
column2: 它们像牛一样死了，但味道没那么好。

column1: Try to train them as battle mounts.
column2: 尝试把它们训练成战骑。

column1: We tried to train them as battle mounts.
column2: 我们尝试把它们训练成战骑。

column1: The beasts seemed to slowly respond to our training.
column2: 这些野兽似乎慢慢对训练有了反应。

column1: The beasts were too wild to be tamed for war.
column2: 这些野兽太野了，无法驯服用于战争。

column1: Try to train them as beasts of burden.
column2: 尝试把它们训练成驮兽。

column1: We tried to train them as beasts of burden.
column2: 我们尝试把它们训练成驮兽。

column1: Our efforts were for naught, they did not remember rewards or blows long enough to learn anything.
column2: 我们的努力白费了，它们记不住奖励或惩罚足够长时间来学会任何东西。

column1: I don’t know whether we can train these things or not.
column2: 我不知道我们是否能训练这些东西。

column1: These creatures aren’t that much dumber than cows. I can train them as beasts of burden, I think.
column2: 这些东西不比牛笨多少。我想我可以把它们训练成驮兽。

column1: These beasts aren’t that much more stupid than sheep. I’d still like to try to train them as beasts of burden.
column2: 这些野兽不比羊笨多少。我还是想试试把它们训练成驮兽。

column1: No point in trying to trade them now, when we don’t quite know what to do with them.
column2: 现在还没完全搞明白怎么处理它们，尝试交易也没意义。

column1: No point in trying to trade them, when we still don’t quite know what to do with them or what good to say about them.
column2: 当我们还不太清楚怎么处理它们或怎么夸它们好时，尝试交易也没意义。

column1: Wouldn’t it be something if we could train them as battle mounts? Imagine the effect on our foes!
column2: 要是能把它们训练成战骑，那该多好？想象一下对我们的敌人产生的效果！

column1: I think I can train them as battle mounts. Imagine the effect on our foes as our Earthshakers thunder into sight!
column2: 我想我能把它们训练成战骑。想象一下当我们的地动者轰然出现在视线中时，对我们的敌人产生的效果！

column1: I still want to try to train them as battle mounts. I want to our enemies’ faces as our Earthshakers thunder into sight!
column2: 我还是想试试把它们训练成战骑。我想看到我们的敌人脸上惊恐的表情，当地动者轰然冲入视野时！

column1: The carls are upset with the havoc the beasts are causing.
column2: 自由民们对这些野兽造成的破坏感到不满。

column1: The carls are upset, but they’ll be patient a little while longer if we can promise an eventual benefit.
column2: 自由民们很不安，但如果我们能承诺最终的好处，他们还能再耐心一小会儿。

column1: The carls are at the end of their patience. We must do something, even the wrong thing.
column2: 自由民们的耐心已经到极限了。我们必须做点什么，哪怕是错事。

column1: If our resident herder won’t mention it, I will; these things are each eating as much as 3 cows. And they haven’t stopped growing!
column2: 如果我们的常驻牧人不提，那就由我来说吧；这些东西每只吃的相当于3头牛。而且它们还没停止生长！

column1: These things are practically inhaling food. Make them earn their keep or get rid of them!
column2: 这些东西简直在吞食食物。让它们自己挣口粮，或者处理掉它们！

column1: I just remembered — these Earthshaker creatures are powerful wards against Chaos. During the Darkness, they helped Maran Gor fight Wakboth the Devil.
column2: 我刚想起来——这些地动者生物是对抗混沌的强大守护者。在黑暗时代，它们帮助玛兰·戈尔对抗恶魔瓦克博斯。

column1: How can you even think of getting rid of the Earthshakers, when they give protection against Chaos? A few smashed steads, and wagonloads of grain, is a small price for this blessing.
column2: 你怎能想着赶走地动者？它们可是能抵御混沌的。砸烂几座农庄、几车谷物，换得这份恩赐，代价算小了。

column1: They’re kin to dragons, I tell you, dragons! And we all know what kind of trouble that means!
column2: 它们跟龙是近亲，我跟你说，龙！我们都知道那意味着什么麻烦！

column1: Don’t forget that there’s probably some kind of dragon connection to all of this.
column2: 别忘了，这一切很可能跟龙脱不了干系。

column1: At least some people in this clan see the trouble these dragon-kin bring us!
column2: 至少族里还有人看得清这些龙裔给我们带来的麻烦！

column1: Whatever we do with them, make sure we don’t do something that would offend the dragonewts.
column2: 无论我们怎么处置它们，务必不要冒犯龙人。

column1: I knew it. We should have killed the things as soon as they popped out of their eggs.
column2: 我就知道。我们该在它们一出壳时就杀掉。

column1: I knew we shouldn’t have let those things run around loose.
column2: 我就知道不该让那些东西到处乱跑。

column1: Big horns, big fun!
column2: 大角，大乐子！

column1: If we eat them, our fertility problems will be solved. Forever.
column2: 吃了它们，我们的丰饶问题就解决了。永远解决。

column1: I’ll have them rolling over and begging for scraps in no time.
column2: 我马上就能让它们打滚讨食。

column1: Earth cows!
column2: 地牛！

column1: The menfolk will try to turn the Earthshakers into weapons, but they belong to Ernalda’s sister, and should be used in planting.
column2: 男人们总想把地动者变成武器，但它们属于厄纳尔达的姐妹，该用来耕作。

column1: To ride one of these powerful beasts — what a thrill that would be!
column2: 骑一头这样强大的巨兽——那该多刺激！

column1: “A visitor must not outstay his welcome.”
column2: “客人不可待到惹人厌烦。”

column1: “Don’t empty your host’s larder when you go to visit.”
column2: “做客时别吃光主人家的储藏室。”

column1: \x02\x03Genevra/Asandra/Chella\x02
column2: \x02\x03吉纳维拉/阿桑德拉/切拉\x02

column1: The big lizards we raised haven’t been seen for the last few days. We were just getting to used to them, too! One of our carls, \x01@\x07, reported that she last saw them slowly walking, single file, in the direction of Kero Fin. The children will miss them, but the carls are relieved that the creatures, along with their enormous appetites, are gone.
column2: 我们养的那些大蜥蜴好几天没见着了。我们才刚刚开始习惯它们呢！我们的一位自由民， \x01@\x07，报告说她最后一次看到它们排成一列，慢慢往凯罗·芬的方向走去。孩子们会想念它们，但自由民们松了口气——那些胃口巨大的家伙终于走了。

column1: sceneR012
column2: sceneR012

column1: A trio of strange beings has eluded your patrols. These lizard-men are probably the dragonewts you’ve heard legends about. For twelve hours they have been enacting a mysterious ritual on your lands.
column2: 三个奇怪生物躲过了你们的巡逻队。这些蜥蜴人很可能就是你们听过的传说里的龙人。它们已在你们的土地上举行了一场神秘仪式，持续了十二个小时。

column1: A trio of dragonewts has eluded your patrols. For twelve hours they have been enacting a mysterious ritual on your lands.
column2: 三个龙人躲过了你们的巡逻队。它们已在你们的土地上举行了一场神秘仪式，持续了十二个小时。

column1: Dragonewts eluded our patrols, and did strange things on our land.
column2: 龙人躲过了我们的巡逻队，在我们的土地上做了怪事。

column1: Clear the area until they leave.
column2: 清空区域，直到它们离开。

column1: We avoided them.
column2: 我们避开了它们。

column1: Conduct a ritual to counter their magic.
column2: 举行一场仪式来对抗它们的魔法。

column1: We conducted a ritual in hopes of defusing whatever dragon magic they were brewing.
column2: 我们举行了一场仪式，希望能化解它们在酝酿的某种龙魔法。

column1: Our god-talkers said that their ritual had thwarted the dragonewts.
column2: 我们的神言者说，他们的仪式挫败了龙人。

column1: Our god-talkers said that their ritual had probably thwarted the dragonewts.
column2: 我们的神言者说，他们的仪式可能挫败了龙人。

column1: Try to communicate with them.
column2: 试着与它们沟通。

column1: We tried to communicate with them.
column2: 我们试着与它们沟通。

column1: The dragonewts glanced at us briefly, then went back to their ritual. Two hours later, they left our lands.
column2: 龙人瞥了我们一眼，然后继续它们的仪式。两小时后，它们离开了我们的土地。

column1: Our warriors attacked them.
column2: 我们的战士攻击了它们。

column1: When struck with our swords, they hissed ferociously. Our stream ran thick with their green blood.
column2: 被我们的剑击中时，它们发出凶猛的嘶嘶声。我们的小溪里流满了它们绿色的血液。

column1: Watch them until they leave.
column2: 监视它们直到离开。

column1: The ritual continued for two hours. Then, as abruptly as they came, they left.
column2: 仪式持续了两小时。然后，它们像来时一样突然离开了。

column1: This is all that I Saw. Or rather, there were seven different things that happened \x02\x02afterwards/next\x02. Which \x02\x02isn’t very useful/is not helpful\x02.
column2: 这就是我所见的一切。或者说，之后还发生了七件不同的事 \x02\x02之后/接下来\x02。这些情况 \x02\x02没什么用/没帮助\x02。

column1: Perhaps we can try to communicate with them.
column2: 也许我们可以试着与它们沟通。

column1: Dragonewts are trouble. Very serious trouble.
column2: 龙人就是麻烦。非常严重的麻烦。

column1: Dragonewts are very strange indeed. No one really understands why they do certain things.
column2: 龙人确实非常古怪。没人真正理解它们为什么做某些事。

column1: What is everyone afraid of? It’s not like they’re broos, for Urox’s sake.
column2: 大家都怕什么？它们又不是布鲁斯，看在尤洛克斯的份上。

column1: Run and hide. We must run and hide. Run. And Hide.
column2: 逃跑躲藏。我们必须逃跑躲藏。逃。和藏。

column1: By Maran Gor’s trembling thighs, there shall be no overgrown salamanders cavorting about beside our creek bed!
column2: 以马兰·戈尔的颤抖大腿起誓，绝不能让那些巨蜥在我们的小溪边嬉闹！

column1: Surely we have offended the gods, to bring such a terrible omen down on our heads.
column2: 我们一定是触怒了神灵，才招来如此可怕的预兆。

column1: Please take me off the ring. I’m not up to dealing with dragonewts.
column2: 请让我退出长老会。我应付不了龙人。

column1: We could bribe them… if we could figure out what a dragonewt wants.
column2: 我们可以贿赂它们……如果我们能搞清楚龙人想要什么的话。

column1: “When in the fields, a man should never move an inch from his weapons.”
column2: “身在田野，男人不可离开武器寸步。”

column1: These aren’t the toughest dragonewts. These are the weakest ones.
column2: 这些不是最厉害的龙人。这些是最弱的。

column1: Hey! They’re stealing our honey!
column2: 嘿！它们在偷我们的蜂蜜！

column1: Music is the universal language. I will go sing to them, and learn why they are here.
column2: 音乐是通用语言。我去给它们唱歌，弄清楚它们为什么在这里。

column1: Crested snakes steal flower’s gold.
column2: 冠蛇偷走花的金子。

column1: Dragon’s little brothers dance foot-wet with striped warriors.
column2: 龙的小兄弟与条纹战士赤脚共舞。

column1: This is like the old stories from the Empire of Wyrm’s Friends!
column2: 这就像龙之友帝国的古老传说！

column1: Let’s see how well they fight.
column2: 试试它们多能打。

column1: I think this is wonderful. Good things are sure to follow.
column2: 我觉得这太棒了。好事一定会接踵而至。

column1: sceneR013
column2: sceneR013

column1: Illator, a noble of Tarsh, comes to visit you. He tells you of his land. Tarsh is a kingdom to the northwest. Its people are Orlanthi who, like you, follow the laws of King Heort. They are from another part of the world, though, and may do things very differently from you. Once Illator has given you his news, he has an offer. Tarsh’s king, Arim, is waging war against the empire to his north, called the Lunar Empire. Illator wants to hire some of your weaponthanes as mercenaries for a several-season military campaign. “There will be much loot,” he says. “Many, many cows, you will gain.”
column2: 塔什贵族伊拉托前来拜访您。他向您讲述了他的土地。塔什是西北方的一个王国。其子民是奥兰提人，与您一样，遵循赫奥特王的律法。不过他们来自世界的另一部分地区，行事方式可能与您大相径庭。伊拉托通报消息后，提出了一个提议。塔什的国王阿里姆正与北方的帝国（称为月之帝国）交战。伊拉托想雇佣您的一些武器领主作为雇佣兵，参加一场为期数季的军事战役。“会有大量战利品，”他说，“你们将获得许许多多的牛只。”

column1: We were approached by Illator, a noble of Tarsh. He sought mercenaries for a northern war.
column2: 塔什贵族伊拉托找上了我们。他为一北方战事招募雇佣兵。

column1: Decline his offer.
column2: 拒绝他的提议。

column1: We declined his offer.
column2: 我们拒绝了他的提议。

column1: Do you…
column2: 你是否…

column1: Simply, but politely, decline?
column2: 简单而礼貌地拒绝？

column1: Send a gift to the Tarshite king?
column2: 向塔什国王送去礼物？

column1: However, we sent a gift to the Tarshite king.
column2: 然而，我们向塔什国王送去了一份礼物。

column1: Ask Illator not to bother you again?
column2: 让伊拉托别再打扰您？

column1: Further, we told Illator never to darken our door again.
column2: 此外，我们告诉伊拉托永远别再上门。

column1: Send a quarter of your weaponthanes.
column2: 派出四分之一的武器领主。

column1: Do you send your war leader \x01@\x17 to lead the weaponthanes?
column2: 你是否派遣你的战争领袖 \x01@\x17 率领这些武器领主？

column1: We sent \x01@\x17 and a quarter of our weaponthanes north to help King Arim.
column2: 我们派遣了 \x01@\x17 以及四分之一的武器领主北上援助阿里姆王。

column1: We sent a quarter of our weaponthanes north to help King Arim.
column2: 我们派遣了四分之一的武器领主北上援助阿里姆王。

column1: Send a token force.
column2: 派遣一支象征性的部队。

column1: We sent \x01@\x17 and a token force north to help King Arim.
column2: 我们派遣了 \x01@\x17 以及一支象征性部队北上援助阿里姆王。

column1: We sent a token force north to help King Arim.
column2: 我们派遣了一支象征性部队北上援助阿里姆王。

column1: Send half of your weaponthanes.
column2: 派出半数的武器领主。

column1: We sent \x01@\x17 and half of our weaponthanes north to help King Arim.
column2: 我们派遣了 \x01@\x17 以及半数的武器领主北上援助阿里姆王。

column1: We sent half of our weaponthanes north to help King Arim.
column2: 我们派遣了半数的武器领主北上援助阿里姆王。

column1: Send three-quarters of your weaponthanes.
column2: 派出四分之三的武器领主。

column1: We sent \x01@\x17 and three-quarters of our weaponthanes north to help King Arim.
column2: 我们派遣了 \x01@\x17 以及四分之三的武器领主北上援助阿里姆王。

column1: We sent three-quarters of our weaponthanes north to help King Arim.
column2: 我们派遣了四分之三的武器领主北上援助阿里姆王。

column1: And how exactly are they going to drive “many, many cows” all the way down from the Lunar Empire?
column2: 那么他们究竟打算如何把“许多许多的牛只”一路从月之帝国赶下来？

column1: The greater the force we send, the greater the loot we will gain.
column2: 我们派出的兵力越强，获得的战利品就越多。

column1: No good outcome is ever guaranteed in war. We must balance the chance for great gain with the great risk of sending many warriors.
column2: 战争中从未有任何好结果是有保障的。我们必须权衡巨大收益的机会与派遣众多勇士的巨大风险。

column1: The greater the force we send, the greater the risk we take.
column2: 我们派出的兵力越强，承担的风险就越大。

column1: We’re too vulnerable to be selling our swords.
column2: 我们太过脆弱，无法出售我们的剑。

column1: His foe is the empire of the same red moon that gave our priests headaches before the Pharaoh came.
column2: 他的敌人正是那个在法老降临前让我们祭司头痛不已的红月帝国。

column1: If their enemy is Chaotic, then we should offer to fight for free!\t\t
column2: 如果他们的敌人是混沌，那我们应该主动提出免费作战！\t\t

column1: We can loyally guard the stead while the other warriors go off to fight.
column2: 当其他战士外出征战时，我们可以忠诚地守卫家园。

column1: “It is good to be wise, but not so wise that you acutely feel the misfortunes of the world.”
column2: “明智固然好，但不要明智到对世间的不幸感受过深。”

column1: This reminds me of, there was a time that, something is making me think, I’m sorry, it’s just on the tip of my tongue…
column2: 这让我想起，曾经有那么一次，有些事让我思索……抱歉，话就在嘴边，可一时想不起来了……

column1: The war will unfold as it is destined to unfold, no matter how many warriors we send.
column2: 战争将按照其注定的方式展开，无论我们派出多少战士。

column1: Finally, a chance to prove ourselves in a genuine war!
column2: 终于，有机会在一场真正的战争中证明我们自己了！

column1: sceneR014
column2: sceneR014

column1: Clearly, your neighbors have discovered that you’ve sent many of your warriors off to war. A team of ducks, taking advantage of your temporary weakness, has stolen cows from your herd over a period of several nights.
column2: 显然，你的邻居们发现你已派出了许多战士出征。一队鸭人利用你暂时的虚弱，连续几个夜晚从你的牛群中偷走了牛只。

column1: When our warriors were serving as mercenaries up north, ducks came and stole from our herds.
column2: 当我们的战士在北方充当雇佣兵时，鸭人前来偷走了我们的牛群。

column1: Demand satisfaction from the duck chieftain.
column2: 向鸭人酋长要求赔偿。

column1: We demanded satisfaction from the duck chieftain.
column2: 我们向鸭人酋长要求了赔偿。

column1: \x01@\x03, the duck chieftain, agreed that we had been wronged. He ordered the thieves to return the stolen cattle, and pay compensation to boot.
column2: \x01@\x03鸭人酋长承认我们遭受了不公。他命令小偷归还偷走的牛只，并额外支付赔偿。

column1: \x01@\x03, the duck chieftain, agreed that we had been wronged, but said that the thieves were outlaws from his clan. Without admitting fault, he gave us a cow as “a token of friendship.”
column2: \x01@\x03鸭人酋长承认我们遭受了不公，但表示那些小偷是他氏族中不受法律保护的人。他在不承认过错的情况下给了我们一头牛作为“友谊的象征”。

column1: \x01@\x03, the duck chieftain, agreed that we had been wronged, but said that the thieves were outlaws from his clan. “We are as anxious to catch them as you,” he said, “but they are like feathers on the wind.”
column2: \x01@\x03鸭人酋长承认我们遭受了不公，但表示那些小偷是他氏族中不受法律保护的人。“我们和你们一样急于抓到他们，”他说，“但他们如风中的羽毛般难以捕捉。”

column1: Free the ducks from their obligation to you if they deal with this.
column2: 如果鸭人处理此事，就免除他们对你的义务。

column1: We approached the duck chieftain, \x01@\x03, and offered to end their tribute to us, if he would reign in the Duck cattle thieves. He agreed, and, to show good faith, compensated our losses.
column2: 我们找到鸭人酋长 \x01@\x03，提出如果他能够管束鸭人偷牛贼，我们就免除他们的进贡。他同意了，并为了表示诚意，补偿了我们的损失。

column1: Persuade the carls that any losses now will be offset by loot from the war.
column2: 说服自由民，现在的任何损失都将由战争中的战利品弥补。

column1: They replied that they’d been blinded by their own loss, and had lost sight of the clan as a whole.
column2: 他们回答说，他们被自己的损失蒙蔽了双眼，忽略了整个氏族的利益。

column1: Promise the carls you’ll raid the ducks when the warriors get back.
column2: 向自由民承诺，等战士们归来后就突袭鸭人。

column1: We promised the carls that we would raid the ducks when the warriors returned.
column2: 我们向自由民承诺，等战士们归来后就突袭鸭人。

column1: They looked forward to joining the raiding party, once the weaponthanes returned from the war in the north.
column2: 他们期盼着加入袭击队伍，只等武器领主们从北方的战争中归来。

column1: Send a war party to frighten the rustlers.
column2: 派一支战团去吓唬那些偷牛贼。

column1: We sent a party to find and frighten the thieves.
column2: 我们派出一支队伍去寻找并吓唬那些窃贼。

column1: The guilty ducks could not be found.
column2: 有罪的鸭人无法找到。

column1: Relentlessly did we track them. Remorselessly did we strike fear into their tiny hearts.
column2: 我们无情地追踪他们。我们毫不留情地将恐惧刺入他们渺小的内心。

column1: Our reservists tracked them relentlessly, but were handed a stinging defeat by the tricky thieves.
column2: 我们的后备军无情地追踪他们，却被狡诈的窃贼狠狠击败。

column1: Send a war party to kill the rustlers.
column2: 派一支战团去杀死那些偷牛贼。

column1: We sent a party to find and slay the thieves.
column2: 我们派出一支队伍去寻找并斩杀那些窃贼。

column1: Relentlessly did we track them. Remorselessly did we strike them down.
column2: 我们无情地追踪他们。我们毫不留情地将他们击倒。

column1: It is never a good time to be robbed, but our herds are large, so things could be worse.
column2: 被抢从来不是好时候，但我们的畜群庞大，所以情况还不算太糟。

column1: We cannot stand for this. Our herds are dwindling, and every loss is a serious one.
column2: 我们绝不能容忍这样的行径。我们的畜群正在减少，每一次损失都极为沉重。

column1: It is no use negotiating with thieves. But the duck chieftain may have something to offer us.
column2: 与窃贼谈判毫无用处。但鸭人酋长或许能为我们提供些什么。

column1: We could gain much if we released the ducks from their tribute obligations.
column2: 如果我们免除鸭人的贡赋义务，或许能收获颇丰。

column1: Many of our best men are away at the war. Our reserves may have trouble even with a few ducks.
column2: 我们许多最优秀的战士都出征在外。即便对手只是一些鸭人，我们的后备军也可能难以应付。

column1: Our best men are away at the war. Our reserves might well get themselves killed, even by ducks.
column2: 我们最优秀的战士都在外征战。我们的后备军很可能会阵亡，哪怕面对的只是鸭人。

column1: The carls are discontented now, but they’ve forgotten how many cows Illator has promised us.
column2: 自由民现在心怀不满，但他们已经忘了伊拉托许诺给我们多少牛只。

column1: It is good to be robbed now and then. It teaches humility.
column2: 偶尔被抢一抢也好，能教人懂得谦卑。

column1: We must strike forcefully against the ducks! We must show that we can protect the hearth while the warriors are off questing.
column2: 我们必须对鸭人发起有力打击！我们必须证明，在勇士们外出追寻使命时，我们能守护家园。

column1: We should remind the duck chieftain just how tasty he would be if boiled with cabbages and onions.
column2: 我们应当提醒鸭人酋长，若把他和卷心菜、洋葱一起炖煮，他会有多美味。

column1: Live by the sword, die by the sword.
column2: 仗剑而生，仗剑而死。

column1: We’ve really made fools of ourselves now. The carls will throw us all off the ring if we don’t please them.
column2: 我们这下可真把自己弄得像个笑话。如果不能让自由民满意，他们就会把我们全部赶出长老会。

column1: I told you that enemies would attack us if we sent too many warriors away.
column2: 我告诉过你们，如果我们派遣太多战士离开，敌人就会来攻击我们。

column1: This is a good chance to show our generosity.
column2: 这是个展现我们慷慨的好机会。

column1: The warriors are back from the campaign against the Lunars. Excitedly, they tell the tale of fighting for clever King Arim, whose magical twin children dropped a range of hills on the enemy. Proudly, they tell of their own valiant exploits in battle, and show off their loot.
column2: 勇士们从对抗月民的战役中归来了。他们兴奋地讲述着为机智的阿里姆王作战的故事，他的双胞胎魔法子嗣将一座山岭砸向敌人。他们自豪地述说着自己在战斗中的英勇事迹，并炫耀着战利品。

column1: The warriors returned from the campaign against the northern empire. There, they saw King Arim’s magical twins drop a range of hills on the Chaotic foe. They gathered goodly loot, and brought it back to us.
column2: 勇士们从对抗北方帝国的战役中归来。在那里，他们目睹阿里姆王的双胞胎魔法子嗣将一座山岭砸向混沌之敌。他们收集了丰厚的战利品，带回来交给我们。

column1: The warriors are back from the campaign against the Lunars. Wearily, they tell how they fought for the clever but capricious King Arim. Dejectedly, they tell of their own terrible fate, cut off by Lunar troops and forced to rout through a wall of sorcerous fire. Arim won the battle, but used our warriors as game pieces.
column2: 勇士们从对抗月民的战役中归来了。他们疲惫地讲述着如何为机智却反复无常的阿里姆王作战。他们沮丧地述说着自己可怕的命运——被月民军队切断退路，被迫穿越一道魔法火墙溃逃。阿里姆赢得了战役，却把我们的人当作棋子使用。

column1: Only some of our warriors returned from the campaign against the northern empire. The clever but capricious King Arim won the battle, but used us as game pieces.
column2: 只有部分勇士从对抗北方帝国的战役中归来。机智却反复无常的阿里姆王赢得了战役，却把我们当作棋子使用。

column1: Give some of the warriors’ loot to the carls.
column2: 将部分勇士的战利品分给自由民。

column1: Because all had sacrificed, all were rewarded with loot from the war.
column2: 因为所有人都做出了牺牲，所以所有人都得到了来自战争的奖赏。

column1: The carls were pleased that their sacrifices had not gone unrewarded, but some of the warriors cast lingering looks at the loot they’d brought back.
column2: 自由民很高兴自己的牺牲没有白费，但有些勇士对自己带回来的战利品恋恋不舍。

column1: Launch a raid against the ducks.
column2: 对鸭人发起一次袭击。

column1: In celebration of our victory, we attacked the ducks.
column2: 为庆祝我们的胜利，我们攻击了鸭人。

column1: Recruit additional warriors.
column2: 招募更多战士。

column1: We thought it a good time to seek permanent reinforcements.
column2: 我们认为现在是寻求永久增援的好时机。

column1: We found warriors eager to join the triumphant warriors of the Battle of Falling Hills.
column2: 我们找到了一些战士，他们渴望加入落丘之战的胜利勇士行列。

column1: Warriors refused to join us, saying that our forces were destroyed in a great victory for the Orlanthi. They said we were unlucky.
column2: 战士们拒绝加入我们，说我们的军队在奥兰提人的一场大胜中被摧毁了。他们说我们运气不好。

column1: Our recruiting efforts failed.
column2: 我们的招募努力失败了。

column1: Reward the warriors with a feast.
column2: 用一场盛宴犒赏勇士们。

column1: With a feast, we celebrated the valor of our warriors.
column2: 通过一场盛宴，我们颂扬了勇士们的英勇。
