column1: Our warriors resigned themselves to the fickleness of luck in war. Our carls shared their burdens, and urged them to find cheer in simple things.
column2: 我们的勇士只能接受战争运气的无常。我们的自由民分担了他们的重担，并劝他们在简单的事物中寻找慰藉。

column1: Our warriors composed great poems celebrating their deeds. Our carls toasted them, and observed that no one would dare steal from us now.
column2: 我们的勇士创作了伟大的诗歌，颂扬他们的功绩。我们的自由民向他们举杯致意，并说现在没人敢来偷我们东西了。

column1: Sacrifice to the war gods.
column2: 向战争之神献祭。

column1: To cleanse ourselves of our bad luck, we sacrificed to Orlanth and other war gods.
column2: 为了洗刷我们的厄运，我们向奥兰斯和其他战争之神献祭。

column1: To show thanks for our good luck, we sacrificed to Orlanth and other war gods.
column2: 为了感谢我们的好运，我们向奥兰斯和其他战争之神献祭。

column1: The priests said the omens were good.
column2: 祭司们说预兆是吉利的。

column1: The priests were troubled; they couldn’t read the omens.
column2: 祭司们感到不安；他们无法解读预兆。

column1: So where are all those cows Illator promised us?
column2: 那么伊拉托许诺给我们的那些牛都在哪里？

column1: War is a cruel mistress; our side won, but our forces lost.
column2: 战争是一位残酷的女主人；我们这边赢了，但我们的军队却损失了。

column1: We should trust more in the abilities of our fighting force.
column2: 我们应当更多地信任战斗部队的能力。

column1: War is a cruel mistress; our side won, but our warriors suffered. We must work to restore their confidence.
column2: 战争是一位残酷的女主人；我们这边赢了，但勇士们遭受了苦难。我们必须努力恢复他们的信心。

column1: Illator may be from a foreign land, but he is still an Orlanthi. I trust his oaths to pay us.
column2: 伊拉托虽来自异乡，但他终究是奥兰提人。我相信他向我们所起的诺言会兑现。

column1: King Arim has accomplished much. Perhaps we in Dragon Pass should have a king, too…
column2: 阿里姆王成就斐然。也许我们在龙隘也该有一位王了……

column1: We owe our luck to the gods. We must repay them.
column2: 我们的运气归功于神明，必须回报他们。

column1: War gods respect the victorious. They are unlikely to smile on us now.
column2: 战争之神眷顾胜利者，眼下他们不大可能对我们微笑。

column1: It would be foolish to send our warriors off so soon, especially since it’s planting time.
column2: 这么快派战士出征是愚蠢的，尤其眼下正是播种时节。

column1: It would be foolish to send our warriors off so soon, especially since it’s harvest time.
column2: 这么快派战士出征是愚蠢的，尤其眼下正是收获时节。

column1: While the warriors have been off fighting, the carls have been accumulating resentments. They deserve our attention.
column2: 战士们在外征战期间，自由民积怨已深，他们值得我们关注。

column1: Shame wears us like a dirty cloak. We must smash someone, anyone, to regain our lost reputation.
column2: 耻辱像一件脏斗篷裹着我们。我们必须揍人——随便谁——以挽回失去的名声。

column1: Now that our warriors know of Tarsh, we should launch our own raid!
column2: 既然我们的战士已经知晓塔什，就该发动我们自己的突袭！

column1: I’m sure we haven’t seen the last of Illator.
column2: 我确信伊拉托的事还没完。

column1: The battlefield is the greatest trickster of all.
column2: 战场是最大的骗徒。

column1: We share the ultimate responsibility for this disaster. We should all resign.
column2: 我们对这场灾难负有最终责任，我们都该引咎辞职。

column1: King Arim’s hallowed victory puts us all to shame.
column2: 阿里姆王那场神圣的胜利让我们无地自容。

column1: For mighty warriors, these fellows are easily thrown into a sulk.
column2: 堂堂猛士，这些家伙却动不动就闹别扭。

column1: We’re in for much strutting and posing in the weeks ahead.
column2: 接下来的几周，我们免不了要看到许多昂首阔步、摆架子的场面。

column1: The course of the battle was preordained. Our role in it was too insignificant to predict one way or the other.
column2: 战局的走向早已注定，我们的角色微不足道，无法预测任何走向。

column1: The beastfolk are our ancient enemies. It’s always a good time to raid the ducks.
column2: 兽人是我们的宿敌。任何时候都是突袭鸭人的好时机。

column1: sceneR016
column2: sceneR016

column1: The Tarshite noble Illator is back, bearing payment for your contribution to the Battle of Falling Hills. Unfortunately, he deceived you! Instead of the cows he promised, he’s brought chest after chest of small silver coins bearing the face of a beardless tyrant.
column2: 塔什贵族伊拉托回来了，带着对你在落丘之战中贡献的酬劳。不幸的是，他欺骗了你！他没有带来承诺的牛只，而是一箱又一箱印着无胡须暴君面孔的小银币。

column1: Many members of the clan look crestfallen; they distinctly remember his promise to give us cows.
column2: 氏族里许多人垂头丧气，他们清楚地记得他承诺过给我们牛。

column1: Illator of Tarsh came to pay us for our warriors’ mercenary services, but tried to get us to take foreign coins instead of the cows he promised.
column2: 塔什人伊拉托前来支付我们战士的雇佣费，却试图用外国钱币代替他承诺的牛。

column1: Grudgingly accept the wealth.
column2: 不情愿地收下这笔财富。

column1: With great reluctance, we took his coins.
column2: 万分勉强地，我们收下了他的钱币。

column1: Nobody wanted to give back the coins, but the people still felt cheated. The warriors would have preferred arm rings or torcs, and the herders had clearly been already counting the promised cows.
column2: 没人想把钱币退回去，但人们仍然觉得被骗了。战士们更想要臂环或项圈，而牧人显然早已数过承诺的牛只。

column1: Hold Illator hostage; have his men get the cows.
column2: 扣押伊拉托为人质，派他手下的人去取牛。

column1: We held Illator hostage, and sent his men to get the cows we were owed.
column2: 我们扣押了伊拉托为人质，并派他的人去取我们应得的牛。

column1: Illator said, “You may be brave in battle, but you are fools in council.” We waited for his king to make good on his promise.
column2: 伊拉托说：“你们或许在战场上勇猛，但议政时都是蠢货。”我们等待他的国王兑现承诺。

column1: Kill Illator and send his head back to King Arim.
column2: 杀掉伊拉托，把首级送回给阿里姆王。

column1: To show King Arim that we were no fools to be swindled, we sent him his thane’s head in a box. To show him proper respect, it was a very pretty box.
column2: 为了向阿里姆王证明我们不是好骗的蠢货，我们把他的领主首级装在盒子里送去了。为了表示适当的敬意，那是个非常漂亮的盒子。

column1: Ask him to instead sacrifice to strengthen your clan magic.
column2: 请他改以献祭来强化我们的氏族魔法。

column1: He sacrificed to the gods on our behalf, and the dispute between us was resolved.
column2: 他代替我们向神明献祭，我们之间的争端就此解决。

column1: Send Illator back to Tarsh to get cows.
column2: 派伊拉托回塔什取牛。

column1: Illator says that this would be very difficult, and he will take no responsibility for cows that die on the long trip down.
column2: 伊拉托说这非常困难，而且他不会对长途运输途中死掉的牛只负责。

column1: Do you still insist on cows?
column2: 你们还坚持要牛吗？

column1: We insisted that Illator bring us cows, as he’d promised. He returned to Tarsh to do so.
column2: 我们坚持要伊拉托按承诺给我们牛。他返回塔什去办这件事。

column1: Illator returned to Tarsh. Someone thought he heard Illator call us fools, but it was hard to be certain, given his accent.
column2: 伊拉托返回了塔什。有人觉得自己听见伊拉托骂我们是蠢货，但鉴于他的口音，很难确定。

column1: Illator was glad we’d decided to be reasonable after all.
column2: 伊拉托很高兴我们最终还是决定讲道理。

column1: Cows. Illator promised us cows. So cows we must get.
column2: 牛。伊拉托答应给我们牛。所以我们必须得到牛。

column1: Only effete, prancing minstrels value these coins.
column2: 只有孱弱、蹦跶的吟游诗人才看重这些钱币。

column1: We could at least melt down the silver from these coins.
column2: 我们至少可以把这些钱币上的银子熔了。

column1: Coins are an odd way to work silver, but they are valuable as trade goods, at least.
column2: 钱币处理银的方式很奇怪，但至少作为贸易货物还是有价值的。

column1: These coins are valuable despite their origin, and they are offering a staggering number of them. Take the coins!
column2: 这些钱币尽管来历可疑，但价值不菲，而且他们给的数量惊人。收下钱币！

column1: A promise is a promise.
column2: 承诺就是承诺。

column1: Normally, we’d be able to request that his clan help us in battle, but Tarsh is too distant to arrange that. But they can supply magic we can use in a fight.
column2: 通常我们可以要求他的氏族在战场上帮我们，但塔什太远，无法安排。不过他们可以提供我们战斗中能用上的魔法。

column1: He’s trying to steal from us, and he’s a foreigner. The law allows us to harshly punish him.
column2: 他想偷我们的东西，而且他是个外人。法律允许我们严惩他。

column1: We are entitled to stick to the strict letter of the agreement.
column2: 我们有权坚持合同的字面条款。

column1: Although the Tarshites are foreigners, they are also Orlanthi. Precedent suggests we give them the benefit of the doubt.
column2: 尽管塔什人是外人，但他们也是奥兰斯人。先例表明我们应该给予他们无罪推定的待遇。

column1: Arim is far away, but he is a great king. He won’t take kindly to our killing Illator or taking him hostage.
column2: 阿里姆虽远，但他是伟大的国王。他不会乐见我们杀死或扣押伊拉托。

column1: Orlanth saw Ernalda prisoner in the Emperor’s palace. He stormed the palace, killing all defenders.
column2: 奥兰斯看见厄拉尔达被囚禁在皇帝的宫殿里。他冲进宫殿，杀光了所有守卫。

column1: Tell Illator that our only use for his precious coins is to stick them on his cold, dead eyes.
column2: 告诉伊拉托，他那宝贵的钱币我们只有一个用处——贴在他冰冷死去的眼睛上。

column1: We have fought beside the Tarshites. Let us now see what it is like to fight against them.
column2: 我们曾与塔什人并肩作战。现在来看看与他们为敌是什么滋味。

column1: They are deceivers. Worse than thieves. Cows they promised, and cows they shall give.
column2: 他们是骗子，比贼还坏。他们承诺了牛，就必须给牛。

column1: Take the coins. As each is worth little, it will not pain us to spend them.
column2: 收下钱币。每枚价值不大，花掉它们时不会心疼。

column1: We may have misunderstood Illator when he made his promise — he certainly doesn’t speak our language well.
column2: 伊拉托做出承诺时，我们可能误解了他——他显然不怎么会说我们的语言。

column1: Honor is one of the most important virtues. We should give Illator the chance to make good on his word.
column2: 荣誉是最重要的美德之一。我们应该给伊拉托一个兑现承诺的机会。

column1: Chiefs are ring-givers, not coin-strewers!
column2: 酋长是赠环者，不是撒钱者！

column1: I hate to bring it up, but Illator did promise us cows. Not small bits of silver.
column2: 我讨厌提起这件事，但伊拉托确实答应过给我们牛，不是小碎银子。

column1: Is this some odd magic, all those heads of a foreign tyrant?
column2: 这是一种奇怪的魔法吗，那些外国暴君的头颅？

column1: sceneR017
column2: sceneR017

column1: Normally, good Orlanthi try to avoid looking at the Chaotic red moon that hangs in the northern sky. But one night your holy people notice that great, black scars have appeared on its surface. This means something of great import, surely.
column2: 通常，虔诚的奥兰西人尽量不去看悬挂在北天中的混沌红月。但有一夜，你们的神圣之人注意到其表面出现了巨大的黑色疤痕。这肯定意味着某种重大事件。

column1: Our holy people saw great scars appear on the surface of the Chaotic red moon.
column2: 我们的神圣之人看到混沌红月表面出现了巨大的疤痕。

column1: Do nothing; the moon is not our concern.
column2: 什么也不做；月亮不关我们的事。

column1: Concerned, we increased our patrols.
column2: 出于担忧，我们增加了巡逻。

column1: The weaponthanes kept one eye on the baleful moon and one eye out for other danger.
column2: 武器领主们一眼盯着不祥之月，另一眼提防其他危险。

column1: Sacrifice to Urox, foe of Chaos.
column2: 向混沌之敌乌洛克斯献祭。

column1: Because the moon is of Chaos, we sacrificed to Urox, foe of Chaos.
column2: 因为月亮属于混沌，我们向混沌之敌乌洛克斯献祭。

column1: Our god-talkers said they heard the bellowing of a bull, and that our lands would be protected against Chaos.
column2: 我们的神言者说他们听到了公牛的吼叫，并说我们的土地将受到保护不受混沌侵害。

column1: The god-talkers could not read the omens.
column2: 神言者无法解读征兆。

column1: Use magical divination to understand what is happening.
column2: 使用魔法占卜来理解正在发生的事情。

column1: \x01@\r conducted a divination ritual to understand what was happening.
column2: \x01@\r 进行了占卜仪式来理解正在发生的事情。

column1: \x01@\r looked at the entrails of a sheep, and saw in them the image of a great and terrible horseman. This horseman had ridden to the moon, where he was destroying the Lunar servants of Chaos.
column2: \x01@\r查看了羊的内脏，在其中看到了一个伟大而可怕的骑手的形象。这个骑手已经骑到月亮上，正在那里摧毁混沌的月民仆从。

column1: \x01@\r looked at the entrails of a sheep, and saw that the Lunars were readying their forces on the moon to launch an assault against the peoples of Dragon Pass.
column2: \x01@\r 查看了羊的内脏，看到月民正在月亮上整备军队，准备向龙之隘口的人民发动攻击。

column1: Warn nearby clans of supernatural menace.
column2: 警告附近氏族超自然的威胁。

column1: We warned our neighbors of the possibility of supernatural trouble. It turned out that they had seen the scars, too, though no one could agree on what they meant.
column2: 我们警告了邻居可能发生超自然的麻烦。结果他们也都看到了疤痕，尽管没人能就它们的含义达成一致。

column1: The scars mean that our cow’s milk is going to dry up.
column2: 疤痕意味着我们母牛的奶要干涸了。

column1: This is frightening, but perhaps it gives us a chance to patch up relations with our neighbors.
column2: 这很可怕，但也许它给了我们一个修复与邻居关系的机会。

column1: This is a bad omen for any raids conducted at night.
column2: 这对任何夜间进行的袭击都是不祥之兆。

column1: This means that our wheat will be afflicted with a poisonous blight.
column2: 这意味着我们的小麦将遭受毒枯萎病。

column1: I hear Urox stomping in the night, asking to be unleashed against the enemy.
column2: 我听到乌洛克斯在夜里跺脚，请求被释放来对抗敌人。

column1: The moon is an invader, its light is not pure.
column2: 月亮是入侵者，它的光不纯净。

column1: Those are wounds.
column2: 那些是伤口。

column1: I can perform a divination ritual to perhaps explain this strange occurrence.
column2: 我可以举行一个占卜仪式，或许能解释这个奇怪的现象。

column1: The wild old world does not always revolve around our clan.
column2: 狂野的旧世界并不总是围绕我们的氏族旋转。

column1: The moon is a thing of Chaos. If it is scarred, that means Chaos has lost a great battle.
column2: 月亮是混沌之物。如果它受伤了，那意味着混沌输掉了一场大战。

column1: What goes up, must come down.
column2: 升得高，摔得重。

column1: Let us sacrifice every cow we can spare to Urox, foe of Chaos.
column2: 让我们把每一头能省下的牛都献给混沌之敌乌洛克斯。

column1: If we continue our sacrifices to Orlanth, perhaps the moon will come down!
column2: 如果我们继续向奥兰斯献祭，也许月亮就会掉下来！

column1: This has nothing to do with us.
column2: 这和我们无关。

column1: Scars on the moon! I never promised you I could help you with scars on the moon when I agreed to join the ring!
column2: 月亮上的疤痕！我同意加入长老会时，从未承诺过能帮你处理月亮上的疤痕！

column1: I don’t think this is bad.
column2: 我不觉得这是坏事。

column1: I feel sick. Don’t the rest of you feel sick, too?
column2: 我感到恶心。你们其他人难道不也感到恶心吗？

column1: The Lunar Empire is being punished for its war-like ways. The scars are an omen of peace.
column2: 月之帝国因其好战方式受到惩罚。疤痕是和平的征兆。

column1: Only the gods can protect us from such a frightening omen.
column2: 只有神明才能保护我们免受如此可怕的预兆。

column1: We should make sure other clans recognize this danger.
column2: 我们应该确保其他氏族认识到这个危险。

column1: The world is connected in strange ways. We need to be careful.
column2: 世界以奇异的方式相连。我们需要小心。

column1: There’s a proverb about the moon that seems appropriate, but I can’t quite remember it.
column2: 有一条关于月亮的谚语似乎很合适，但我不太记得了。

column1: So?
column2: 所以呢？

column1: I knew this was going to be a year for great omens.
column2: 我就知道今年会有重大预兆。

column1: The moon has been attacked. It is a good omen for all attackers. Let’s launch a raid soon.
column2: 月亮遭到了攻击。这对所有攻击者都是好兆头。我们很快发起一次袭击吧。

column1: sceneR018
column2: sceneR018

column1: Foreigners are found in one of the holy sheds where women’s magic is practiced. This is double sacrilege. Not only are these people so strange to you that you don’t even know where they’re from, but there are men among them! No men are ever permitted to step inside one of these sheds. The priestesses must conduct a ritual of purification, but even so, your clan fertility may be seriously disrupted.
column2: 在一间进行女性魔法的神圣棚屋里发现了陌生人。这是双重亵渎。这些人不仅对你们来说如此陌生以至于不知道他们来自哪里，而且其中还有男人！从来不允许任何男人踏入这种棚屋。女祭司必须进行净化仪式，但即便如此，你们氏族的丰饶可能会受到严重干扰。

column1: Strange foreigners were found defiling one of Ernalda’s holy sheds. Our women conducted a ritual of purification.
column2: 发现奇怪的陌生人玷污了厄娜尔达的一间神圣棚屋。我们的女性进行了净化仪式。

column1: We showed mercy and merely drove them off.
column2: 我们展现了怜悯，只是把他们赶走了。

column1: The women were too busy purifying the holy sheds to protest the ring’s decision until the foreigners had fled. Some people still can’t believe we let them live.
column2: 妇女们忙于净化神圣棚屋，直到陌生人们逃走后才有空反对长老会的决定。有些人仍然不敢相信我们让他们活了下来。

column1: Force them into thralldom.
column2: 强迫他们沦为奴隶。

column1: We forced them into thralldom.
column2: 我们强迫他们沦为奴隶。

column1: They begged for better treatment, saying that they were refugees from the Lunar Empire. They said their homeland had been attacked by a barbarian horseman called Sheng Seleris, and that war had torn out the Empire’s heart. They were on the run from an unjust usurper, just as we were when we fled Heortland. We told them they were lucky to be alive.
column2: 他们乞求更好的待遇，说他们是来自月之帝国的难民。他们说自己的家园遭到了一个名叫盛·塞勒里斯的野蛮骑手袭击，战争撕裂了帝国的心脏。他们正在逃离一个不义的篡位者，就像我们逃离希尔特兰时一样。我们告诉他们能活着就算幸运了。

column1: Kill the men; enslave the women.
column2: 杀死男人，奴役女人。

column1: We killed the men and enslaved the women.
column2: 我们杀死了男人，奴役了女人。

column1: They begged for better treatment, saying that they were refugees from the Lunar Empire. They said their homeland had been attacked by a barbarian horseman called Sheng Seleris, and that war had torn out the Empire’s heart. They were on the run from an unjust usurper, just as we were when we fled Heortland. We told them they should be grateful we weren’t killing their women, too.
column2: 他们乞求更好的待遇，声称自己是月之帝国的难民。他们说家园遭到了一名叫做盛·塞勒里斯的蛮族骑手袭击，战争撕裂了帝国的心脏。他们正逃亡躲避一个不公的篡位者，就像我们逃离赫欧特兰时一样。我们告诉他们，他们没有连女人也被我们杀掉就该感恩了。

column1: Of course, we killed the defilers.
column2: 当然，我们杀掉了那些亵渎者。

column1: The people were glad that we’d killed the defilers.
column2: 人们很高兴我们杀掉了亵渎者。

column1: Ask them who they are, then kill them.
column2: 问清他们是谁，然后杀掉他们。

column1: The defilers said they were refugees from the Lunar Empire. They said their homeland had been attacked by a barbarian horseman called Sheng Seleris, and that war had torn out the Empire’s heart. They were on the run from an unjust usurper, just as we were when we fled Heortland. We killed them, of course.
column2: 亵渎者声称自己是月之帝国的难民。他们说家园遭到了一名叫做盛·塞勒里斯的蛮族骑手袭击，战争撕裂了帝国的心脏。他们正逃亡躲避一个不公的篡位者，就像我们逃离赫欧特兰时一样。我们当然杀掉了他们。

column1: Conduct a ritual to ask Ernalda for guidance.
column2: 举行一场仪式，向厄娜尔达祈求指引。

column1: We conducted a ritual to try to divine Ernalda’s desires.
column2: 我们举行了一场仪式，试图占卜厄娜尔达的意愿。

column1: The divination indicated mercy, so we simply drove them off.
column2: 占卜指示应施以仁慈，于是我们只是将他们赶走了。

column1: The divination indicated regret for the inevitable fate of the defilers. With little joy, we slew them.
column2: 占卜指示对亵渎者不可避免的命运表示遗憾。我们毫无喜悦地杀掉了他们。

column1: The sanctity of the women’s shed isn’t that important.
column2: 女圣棚的神圣性没那么重要。

column1: This is a crime so grave that no Orlanthi would even think of committing it.
column2: 这是如此严重的罪行，任何奥兰斯人都不会想到去犯。

column1: This is a crime so grave that it’s hard to name a punishment for it. Though I must add that we have always opposed the taking of thralls.
column2: 这是如此严重的罪行，以至于很难定下惩罚。不过我必须补充，我们一贯反对掳掠奴隶。

column1: This is a crime so grave that it’s hard to name a punishment for it. Perhaps it is appropriate to take them as thralls.
column2: 这是如此严重的罪行，以至于很难定下惩罚。或许将他们收为奴隶是合适的。

column1: These people are powerless and far from their home. It is unlikely that we will start a feud by treating them as we must.
column2: 这些人无力反抗，远离家园。按我们必须的方式对待他们，不大可能引发世仇。

column1: If we take too many foreign thralls, they may rebel.
column2: 如果我们接收太多外族奴隶，他们可能会反叛。

column1: We may suffer greatly, no matter how we punish them.
column2: 无论我们如何惩罚他们，都可能遭受严重损失。

column1: Their actions will make our women barren for two years.
column2: 他们的行为会让我们的妇女两年不育。

column1: They could have made our women barren for two years or more; luckily, we avoided that fate this time.
column2: 他们本可能让我们的妇女两年或更久不育；幸运的是，我们这次避开了那种命运。

column1: How many more refugees will be driven into our land?
column2: 还会有多少难民被驱赶到我们的土地上？

column1: Technically, the women have not defiled us. Take them as thralls, and kill only the men.
column2: 严格来说，妇女们并没有玷污我们。把她们收为奴隶，只杀掉男人。

column1: Ernalda is infinitely merciful, but the mysteries of the women’s sheds are among the holiest of her secrets. We dishonor her if we forget this.
column2: 厄娜尔达无限仁慈，但女圣棚的奥秘是她最神圣的秘密之一。如果我们忘记这一点，就是羞辱了她。

column1: Not even Eurmal would dream of committing such an offense.
column2: 就连尤尔马尔也不会梦到犯下这种冒犯。

column1: We have incurred the wrath of the Earth. Maran Gor will destroy our homes. Babeester Gor will chop off our heads.
column2: 我们已经招致大地的怒火。玛兰·格会摧毁我们的家园。巴贝斯特·格会砍下我们的头颅。

column1: I knew we should have placed booby traps around the women’s sheds.
column2: 我就知道应该在女圣棚周围设下陷阱。

column1: I told you there would be more refugees.
column2: 我告诉过你还有更多难民会来。

column1: I would feel better if I knew what Ernalda thinks of this.
column2: 如果我知道厄娜尔达对此怎么想，我会感觉好受些。

column1: It’s not their fault — they are foreigners, and don’t know any better.
column2: 这不是他们的错——他们是外乡人，不懂规矩。

column1: Can’t we gain somehow from them, to make up for our wound? Surely, if we enthrall them, merciful Ernalda will be satisfied.
column2: 难道我们不能从他们身上得到些什么，来弥补我们的创伤？当然，如果我们让他们为奴，仁慈的厄娜尔达一定会满意。

column1: We must atone for our laxity by building a temple to \x02\x02Voria, goddess of spring/Babeester Gor the Avenger\x02.
column2: 我们必须为懈怠赎罪，修建一座神庙献给 \x02\x02沃里亚，春之女神/复仇者巴贝斯特·格\x02。

column1: It is as we feared. When those foreigners defiled the women’s sacred sheds, the earth goddesses were affronted that we couldn’t take better care of their holy places. As a result, no children have been born during the last two seasons. I fear this condition may last another year or more.
column2: 正如我们所担心的。那些外乡人玷污女圣棚后，大地女神们因我们未能好好守护她们的圣地而愤怒。结果，过去两个季节都没有孩子出生。我担心这种情况可能还会持续一年或更久。

column1: sceneR019
column2: sceneR019

column1: Illator, noble of Tarsh, is back again. Now he’s accusing you of harboring Lunars, or some such. He says he’s been pursuing criminal enemies from the Battle of Falling Hills, and has reason to believe that at least one of them passed through your tula a while ago.
column2: 塔什的贵族伊拉托又来了。现在他指控你们窝藏月民之类的事。他说他一直在追捕来自落丘之战的罪犯敌人，有理由相信其中至少有一人不久前曾途经你们的图拉领地。

column1: Illator of Tarsh came and told us to hand over the Lunars we’d been hiding.
column2: 塔什的伊拉托来了，命令我们把藏匿的月民交出来。

column1: This is no longer a battlefield. You have no right to hunt them.
column2: 这里不再是战场。你没有权力追杀他们。

column1: We told him that he had no legal right to pursue even the Lunars for crimes committed in war.
column2: 我们告诉他，即使对月民在战争中所犯的罪行，他也没有合法权力追捕他们。

column1: After long discussion, in which many opposing precedents were cited, Illator conceded our point. He left shortly thereafter.
column2: 经过漫长讨论，引用了许多相反的先例后，伊拉托承认了我们的观点。不久后他就离开了。

column1: After long discussion, in which many opposing precedents were cited, Illator stalked out of our hall, his face reddened with anger.
column2: 经过漫长讨论，引用了许多相反的先例后，伊拉托怒气冲冲地走出我们的大厅，脸涨得通红。

column1: Lunars were here, but we sent them packing.
column2: 月民来过这里，但我们把他们打发走了。

column1: We told him we’d sent them packing.
column2: 我们告诉他，我们已经把他们打发走了。

column1: He describes the Lunars he is chasing. One of them matches your most recent group of Lunar visitors, and you tell him so. Illator flies into a rage, blaming you for protecting enemies of Orlanth. How do you respond?
column2: 他描述了他正在追捕的月民。其中一人与你最近接待的那批月民访客相符，于是你如实相告。伊拉托勃然大怒，指责你包庇奥兰斯的敌人。你如何回应？

column1: The enemies of Tarsh are not necessarily the enemies of Dragon Pass.
column2: 塔什的敌人未必是龙隘的敌人。

column1: Illator’s features darkened, and he soon took his leave of us.
column2: 伊拉托的脸色阴沉下来，不久便告辞离去。

column1: We had no way of knowing they were your enemies.
column2: 我们无从知道他们是你的敌人。

column1: Illator muttered uncomplimentary words, and soon took his leave of us.
column2: 伊拉托咕哝了几句不敬的话，不久便告辞离去。

column1: After all we’ve done for you, you have no right to get angry at us.
column2: 我们为你做了这么多，你没资格对我们发火。

column1: Illator apologized for his presumption. “For two seasons, I have chased these enemies, and I fear that my weariness has made me short-tempered.” As a token of apology, he gave us a silver ring.
column2: 伊拉托为自己的冒昧致歉。“两个季节以来，我一直在追捕这些敌人，恐怕是疲惫让我变得急躁了。”作为道歉的象征，他给了我们一枚银环。

column1: He describes the enemies he’s pursuing. None of them match the descriptions of your Lunar visitors. What do you tell him?
column2: 他描述了自己正在追捕的敌人。没有一个与你们那些月民访客的描述相符。你告诉他什么？

column1: Keep looking; your Lunars were not here.
column2: 继续找吧；你们的月民不在这儿。

column1: Disappointed, Illator continued on his way.
column2: 伊拉托失望地继续上路了。

column1: We saw one of your Lunars, and drove him off.
column2: 我们见过一个你们的月民，并且把他赶跑了。

column1: Illator flies into a rage, blaming you for protecting enemies of Orlanth. How do you respond?
column2: 伊拉托勃然大怒，指责你们包庇奥兰斯的敌人。你如何回应？

column1: Lunars? We haven’t seen any Lunars.
column2: 月民？我们没见过任何月民。

column1: We told him we hadn’t seen any Lunars.
column2: 我们告诉他，我们没见过任何月民。

column1: Illator thanked us for our honesty and composed a short poem of parting in our honor.
column2: 伊拉托感谢我们的诚实，并即兴作了一首短诗作为告别，以表敬意。

column1: Before he left, Illator composed a short poem referring to our dishonesty.
column2: 临行前，伊拉托作了一首影射我们不诚实的短诗。

column1: Some Lunars came by here, but we killed them.
column2: 有几个月民来过这里，但我们把他们杀了。

column1: We told him we’d killed the Lunars.
column2: 我们告诉他，我们杀了那些月民。

column1: He described the Lunars he was after. One of them matched our most recent group of Lunar visitors. We told them we’d killed his quarry. He rewarded us with a golden armband.
column2: 他描述了他在追捕的月民。其中一个与我们最近一批月民访客相符。我们告诉他我们杀了他追捕的目标。他赏了我们一只金臂环。

column1: We killed one of the Lunars you seek.
column2: 我们杀了一个你正在追捕的月民。

column1: His heart gladdened, Illator rewarded us with a headband of silver and emeralds. We feasted with him, and then he left.
column2: 伊拉托心情大好，赏了我们一条镶银绿宝石的头带。我们与他一同宴饮，然后他便离开了。

column1: Those Lunars are our thralls now.
column2: 那些月民现在是我们的奴隶了。

column1: We told Illator that the Lunars were our thralls.
column2: 我们告诉伊拉托，那些月民是我们的奴隶。

column1: Illator demands that you turn the thralls over to him, so that he may take them back to Tarsh for trial.
column2: 伊拉托要求你将奴隶交给他，好让他把他们带回塔什受审。

column1: The thralls are useful to us, and we will keep them.
column2: 这些奴隶对我们有用，我们要留着他们。

column1: Furthermore, we told him we would keep them.
column2: 而且，我们告诉他我们会留着他们。

column1: Illator seemed most displeased with our response. He said that we had chosen unwisely, and that we had not seen the last of him.
column2: 伊拉托对我们的回应似乎极为不满。他说我们做了不明智的选择，还说我们不会就此与他两清。

column1: If you want the thralls badly enough, you will pay a fair price for them.
column2: 如果你真的想要这些奴隶，那就出个公平的价钱买下他们。

column1: We demanded a fair price for them.
column2: 我们要求他出个公平的价钱。

column1: Illator paid for the thralls with a headband of silver and emeralds.
column2: 伊拉托用一条镶银绿宝石的头带付了奴隶的价钱。

column1: Illator negotiated shrewdly, and convinced us to release the thralls in exchange for a silver ring.
column2: 伊拉托精明地讨价还价，说服我们用奴隶换了一枚银环。

column1: If they are Lunar criminals, you may have them.
column2: 如果他们是月民罪犯，你可以带走他们。

column1: We gave him the Lunar criminals.
column2: 我们把月民罪犯交给了他。

column1: He said that he would tell his countrymen that we were a fair and honorable people.
column2: 他说他会告诉同胞，我们是公平而可敬的民族。

column1: Those thralls are worth somewhere between 1 and 5 cows.
column2: 那些奴隶价值大约1到5头牛。

column1: Those thralls are worth 10 cows.
column2: 那些奴隶价值10头牛。

column1: King Heort was known for pursuing vengeance against individual enemies after a battle.
column2: 赫欧特王以战后对个别敌人寻仇而闻名。

column1: The laws of crime do not apply to the battlefield; there, the laws of the sword apply.
column2: 犯罪法不适用于战场；那里适用的是刀剑法则。

column1: Foreigners are like tricksters; they are neither bound by our laws, or protected by them.
column2: 外人就像诡诈者；他们既不受我们的法律约束，也不受其保护。

column1: I resent that remark, \x01@\r.
column2: 我对那句话很不爽， \x01@\r.

column1: Tarsh is far away; Illator is unlikely to raid us.
column2: 塔什很远，伊拉托不太可能袭击我们。

column1: Illator is a mighty Wind Lord, and for all we know, has similarly powerful warriors in his search party.
column2: 伊拉托是一位强大的风之主君，而且据我们所知，他的搜索队里也有同样强悍的战士。

column1: Neither the Lunars or Tarshites mean much to Dragon Pass.
column2: 月民也好，塔什人也罢，对龙之隘口都没多大意义。

column1: We defile ourselves by keeping Chaotic Lunars, even as thralls. Give them to Illator, who will slay them.
column2: 留着混沌的月民——哪怕是当作奴隶——会玷污我们自己。把他们交给伊拉托，他会杀了他们。

column1: Courtesy demands that we treat Illator with honesty and respect.
column2: 礼数要求我们以诚实和尊重对待伊拉托。

column1: I told you that involving ourselves in foreign matters would lead to nothing but trouble.
column2: 我跟你说过，卷入外族事务只会带来麻烦。

column1: How dare this grinning monkey demand anything from us? The cheese I ate last night is more noble than he.
column2: 这只嬉皮笑脸的猴子怎么敢向我们提要求？我昨晚吃的奶酪都比他高贵。

column1: This is a matter for men, and Orlanth meant men to be harsh and quick.
column2: 这是男子汉的事，奥兰斯的意思是让男子汉变得冷酷而果断。

column1: Eurmal was less than a stickpicker, but he brought great changes to the world of the Storm Age.
column2: 欧尔马还不如一个拾柴人，但他给风暴时代的世界带来了巨大的改变。

column1: The weaponthanes, led by \x01Bq, complain that you have been favoring the lowly carls over them. “We are not being treated as honorable nobles,” they protest, “but like mere cottars, as servants of the farmers’ whims. We warriors look enviously at other clans; if a man risks his life for them, he can expect his proper due.”
column2: 由 \x01Bq领导的武器领主们抱怨你偏袒低贱的自由民，冷落他们。“我们没有被当作可敬的贵族对待，”他们抗议道，“反而像个佃农，成了农夫们随兴差遣的仆人。我们战士眼巴巴地看着别的部族；如果有人为他们卖命，就能得到应有的回报。”

column1: \x01Bq led a delegation of weaponthanes to complain that the carls were being favored over them.
column2: \x01Bq 率领一队武器领主前来抱怨自由民受到了偏袒。

column1: Assign cottars as servants to leading weaponthanes.
column2: 指派佃农给主要的武器领主做仆人。

column1: How many cottars do you assign?
column2: 你指派多少佃农？

column1: \x01Bq was happy with the offer and said that he hoped the ring would continue to treat the weaponthanes with respect. Behind \x01Bq’s back, many carls complained that the weaponthanes were getting puffed up with their own air.
column2: \x01Bq 对条件很满意，并表示希望长老会继续尊重武器领主。 \x01Bq背后，许多自由民抱怨武器领主们越来越自以为是了。

column1: We assigned some of the cottars to act as servants for the weaponthanes.
column2: 我们指派了一些佃农给武器领主做仆人。

column1: Compose a poem praising the weaponthanes and satirizing the carls.
column2: 作一首赞美武器领主、讽刺自由民的诗。

column1: \x01@N composed a poem praising the weaponthanes and satirizing the carls.
column2: \x01@N 作了一首赞美武器领主、讽刺自由民的诗。

column1: The poem became quite popular, and was soon recited in other tulas.
column2: 这首诗大受欢迎，很快就在其他图拉领地传诵开来。

column1: The poem fell on deaf ears. If anything, it seemed to upset the weaponthanes further.
column2: 这首诗歌对牛弹琴。非但如此，它似乎还进一步惹恼了武器领主们。

column1: Distribute rings and silver among the weaponthanes.
column2: 在武器领主中分发环饰和白银。

column1: We gave them rings and silver.
column2: 我们给了他们环饰和白银。

column1: How much do you distribute to them?
column2: 你分给他们多少？

column1: \x01Bq composed a praise poem, calling our chief a ring-giver.
column2: \x01Bq 创作了一首赞美诗，称我们的首领为赠环者。

column1: Give a feast in honor of the weaponthanes.
column2: 举办一场宴会，以向武器领主们致敬。

column1: We feasted in their honor.
column2: 我们设宴向他们致敬。

column1: How many cows do you slaughter for the feast?
column2: 你为宴会宰杀了多少头牛？

column1: The weaponthanes drank and laughed into the night. A few of the carls took part in the feast, though others muttered that we would starve ourselves just to pamper spoiled warriors.
column2: 武器领主们饮酒欢笑，直至深夜。少数自由民也参加了宴会，尽管其他人嘀咕说，我们为了娇惯骄兵悍将，就要让自己挨饿了。

column1: Persuade them that their grievances are exaggerated.
column2: 劝说他们，让他们觉得自己的不满被夸大了。

column1: We thought their grievances exaggerated, and tried to make them see this, too.
column2: 我们认为他们的不满被夸大了，并试图让他们也明白这一点。

column1: After much cajoling, the warriors laughed and agreed that they had been making much out of nothing.
column2: 经过好一番哄劝，战士们大笑起来，承认他们确实是小题大做了。

column1: They agreed that they may have tried too hard to make their point, and that things weren’t as bad as they’d made them out.
column2: 他们承认，自己或许太急于表明立场，而情况并没有他们描述的那么糟。

column1: The warriors remained grim-faced.
column2: 战士们依旧面色严峻。

column1: The carls aren’t in such a lovely mood, either.
column2: 自由民的心情也好不到哪儿去。

column1: I have to admit that the carls have been a wee bit prideful of late, and at the weaponthanes’ expense.
column2: 我得承认，自由民最近确实有点趾高气扬，而且还是以损害武器领主为代价的。

column1: We could give the weaponthanes something, but if we give them too much, we merely reverse the sense of grievance.
column2: 我们可以给武器领主一些东西，但如果给得太多，也只是把怨气颠倒过来而已。

column1: It is better to give a feast than to simply gift the weaponthanes. The carls can share in the feast, and will not be as slighted.
column2: 与其直接送礼给武器领主，不如举办一场宴会。自由民可以共享宴席，不会觉得受到冷落。

column1: King Heort laid down that those who risk their lives for the clan are its nobility, and deserve to be recognized as such.
column2: 赫尔特王规定：那些为氏族冒生命危险的人是氏族的贵族，理应得到相应的认可。

column1: The balance between happy carls and happy warriors is an eternal see-saw.
column2: 让自由民开心与让战士开心之间的平衡，就像一座永恒的跷跷板。

column1: Shaming them might work, but if it fails, they will be even more upset than before. Persuasion is less risky.
column2: 羞辱他们或许可行，但若失败，他们会比之前更愤怒。劝说风险较小。

column1: “You can’t heal Argmath by wounding Yorsar.”
column2: “用伤了约萨尔的法子，治不好阿格马斯。”

column1: The carls do not understand. A warrior’s honor is his most important possession.
column2: 自由民不懂。战士的荣誉是他最重要的财富。

column1: Violence was first invented by greed, then refined by revenge, anger, and hatred.
column2: 暴力最初由贪婪发明，后来被复仇、愤怒和仇恨精炼。

column1: Give them words, not goods.
column2: 给他们言语，不要给财物。

column1: If we belonged to a tribe, we would still have jealousies, but they would be directed outwards, not inwards.
column2: 如果我们属于某个部落，嫉妒依然存在，但矛头会向外，而非对内。

column1: Why do men care that others are doing better than they?
column2: 为何人们会介意别人过得比自己好？

column1: Make them happy again.
column2: 让他们重新高兴起来。

column1: Humor and respect are the best remedy for this grumbling illness.
column2: 幽默和尊重是治疗这种抱怨之疾的良药。

column1: Anything we try has the potential to make things worse. But they might listen to persuasion.
column2: 我们尝试的任何方法都可能让情况更糟。但他们或许会听从劝说。

column1: Chiefs are ring-givers. Let us give rings.
column2: 首领是赠环者。让我们赠出环饰吧。

column1: sceneR021
column2: sceneR021

column1: \x02\x07Red-Eye/the Mighty/the Stubborn/the Keen/the Rowdy/the Noisy/Scorpion-Killer\x02
column2: \x02\x07红眼/强者/固执者/锐利者/吵闹者/喧闹者/蝎子杀手\x02

column1: We agreed with him, and destroyed the herd.
column2: 我们同意了他的说法，消灭了那群牛。

column1: \x01@\x14 talked to him at great length, and he eventually agreed that the cattle were not contaminated.
column2: \x01@\x14 与他长谈之后，他最终同意那些牛并未受污染。

column1: We sent \x01@\x14 to talk to him. Angrily, he denounced us as liars and greedy abetters of Chaos.
column2: 我们派 \x01@\x14 去和他谈。他愤怒地指责我们是说谎者，是贪婪的混沌帮凶。

column1: We sent \x01@N to talk to him, and he eventually agreed that the cattle were not contaminated.
column2: 我们派 \x01@N 去和他谈，他最终同意那些牛并未受污染。

column1: We sent \x01@N to talk to him. Angrily, he denounced us as liars and greedy abetters of Chaos.
column2: 我们派 \x01@N 去和他谈。他愤怒地指责我们是说谎者，是贪婪的混沌帮凶。

column1: We showed him that he was mistaken. Gruffly, he apologized for his error.
column2: 我们向他证实他错了。他粗声粗气地为自己的错误道了歉。

column1: We tried to show him that he was mistaken, but he would have none of it.
column2: 我们试图向他证明他错了，但他完全听不进去。

column1: We sent him away.
column2: 我们把他打发走了。

column1: The Uroxi was so shocked by our refusal of his “help” that he only punched one carl on his way out of our tula.
column2: 那名乌洛希因我们拒绝他的“帮助”而震惊不已，以至于离开我们的图拉领地时，只打了自由民一拳。

column1: Conduct a ritual to test the herd’s health.
column2: 举行一场仪式，检验牛群的健康状况。

column1: Conduct a ritual to sense Chaos.
column2: 举行一场仪式，感知混沌。

column1: The magic of Uralda, the Cow Mother, will tell us if anything is wrong with the herd.
column2: 母牛女神乌拉尔达的魔法会告诉我们牛群是否有任何不妥。

column1: A lone warrior is of little concern to us.
column2: 一个孤身战士对我们无足轻重。

column1: Angering Storm Bulls is a good way to get into a fight.
column2: 激怒风暴公牛信徒是挑起战斗的好方法。

column1: If we push the Storm Bulls too far, we can expect an attack from a platoon of legendary berserkers. We could not survive such an attack.
column2: 如果我们把风暴公牛信徒逼得太紧，就会遭到一队传奇狂战士的攻击。我们无法在那种攻击下幸存。

column1: Couldn’t we just feast on the destroyed cows?
column2: 我们能不能就把那些被杀死的牛吃了？

column1: If we were part of a tribe, we wouldn’t be so afraid of fanatic Uroxi warriors.
column2: 如果我们是一个部落的一部分，就不会那么害怕狂热的乌洛希战士了。

column1: Kill the cows.
column2: 杀掉那些牛。

column1: Magic is only as reliable as the one who practices it.
column2: 魔法的可靠程度，取决于施法者本身。

column1: I told you Chaos was on the rise.
column2: 我告诉过你混沌正在抬头。

column1: “A kind word costs less than an apple.”
column2: “一句好话，比一个苹果还便宜。”

column1: If we had a bigger temple, broos would be afraid to come near us.
column2: 如果我们有一座更大的神殿，布鲁斯就不敢靠近我们了。

column1: Let’s leave the cows and see what happens. If broos come out, we could learn much by fighting them.
column2: 我们暂且不管那些牛，看看会发生什么。如果布鲁斯冒出来，与它们战斗能让我们学到不少东西。

column1: Anyone can be mistaken. Our own investigations might be mistaken.
column2: 任何人都可能犯错。我们自己的调查也可能有误。

column1: sceneR022
column2: sceneR022

column1: Confiscate the wine; warn of serious punishment next time.
column2: 没收葡萄酒；警告下次严惩。

column1: We confiscated the goods and let him off with a warning.
column2: 我们没收了货物，警告了他一番就放过了。

column1: The weaponthanes praised the clan ring for justly punishing this law-breaking carl.
column2: 武器领主们称赞氏族议会公正地惩罚了这个违法的自由民。

column1: The weaponthanes were unhappy; they said that we would never have been so lenient if the offense had been committed by one of them.
column2: 武器领主们很不高兴；他们说如果过错是由他们中的一员所犯，我们绝不会如此宽容。

column1: Forgive him; allow others to break the traditional rules.
column2: 原谅他；允许他人打破传统规则。

column1: We forgave him, and henceforth announced that all members of our clan could trade freely with outsiders.
column2: 我们原谅了他，并从此宣布氏族所有成员可以与外人自由交易。

column1: Our people were happy, but \x01@\x1A said that it would now be difficult to trade with others.
column2: 我们的人民很高兴，但 \x01@\x1A 说现在与其他人交易会变得困难。

column1: Shame him before his fellows.
column2: 在他的同伴面前羞辱他。

column1: We stood him up before his fellows, and held him out as an example of disobedience towards chosen leaders.
column2: 我们让他站在同伴面前，把他作为对当选领袖不服从的例证。

column1: The weaponthanes heaped extravagant praise on the clan ring for keeping the untrustworthy carls in their place. The carls resented this, and a chasm of distrust opened between warriors and farmers.
column2: 武器领主们对氏族议会大加赞赏，认为他们让不可信的自由民安分守己。自由民对此怨恨不已，战士与农夫之间出现了不信任的鸿沟。

column1: The carls were most affronted, and said that the clan ring had mistaken cruelty for justice.
column2: 自由民深感冒犯，称氏族议会将残忍误认为正义。

column2: 向胡马克特献祭，他是亡灵的敌人。

column2: 我们的神言者说，征兆不吉；胡马克特希望我们凭自己的力量击败他的亡灵敌人。

column2: 派遣一支大军去寻找并抗击亡灵。

column2: 我们沿着一条由 \x02\x03残肢断体/丢弃的武器/恶臭腐迹构成的踪迹\x02

column1: We came upon a massive encampment of undead. Outnumbered and demoralized, our men were routed, and many died in the retreat.
column2: 我们撞见了一个巨大的亡灵营地。寡不敌众且士气低落，我们的人马溃败了，许多人在撤退中丧生。

column1: Send scouts to learn where they came from.
column2: 派遣斥候去打探他们的来历。

column1: We sent scouts to learn where they came from.
column2: 我们派遣斥候去打探他们的来历。

column1: We followed the trail of the undead for many leagues to the west. We stopped to question the ducks we found living there.
column2: 我们沿着亡灵的踪迹向西追踪了许多里格。我们停下来，向居住在那里的鸭人询问情况。

column1: Our scouts either lost the trail or lost their nerve.
column2: 我们的斥候要么失去了踪迹，要么失去了胆量。

column1: We can only hope that they do not return.
column2: 我们只能希望他们不会回来。

column1: We hoped they would not bedevil us further.
column2: 我们希望他们不要再折磨我们。

column1: These are the zombies from the Upland Marsh the ducks warned us about. We must act, or risk being attacked again.
column2: 这就是鸭人警告过我们的高地沼泽僵尸。我们必须行动，否则可能再次遭到袭击。

column1: The ducks fight these creatures \x02\x03often/every season/all the time\x02, but whether they ever win or not, I do not know.
column2: 鸭人与这些生物作战 \x02\x03经常/每个季节/一直\x02，但他们是否曾经赢过，我不知道。

column1: If we gain the help of others and beat back the undead army, we will gain influence.
column2: 如果我们获得他人的帮助并击退亡灵大军，我们将获得影响力。

column1: We don’t have enough influence to guarantee that no other chieftains will oppose us at the moot.
column2: 我们没有足够的影响力来确保议会上没有其他酋长反对我们。

column1: How I wish we could convince other chieftains to help us, but I fear we are still on our own in this fight.
column2: 我多希望能说服其他酋长来帮助我们，但我担心这场战斗中我们仍然只能靠自己。

column1: The other chieftains of our tribe will give us a fair hearing.
column2: 我们部落的其他酋长会公平地听取我们的意见。

column1: By now, I \x02\x03expect/hope/believe\x02 that the other chieftains of our tribe will \x02\x03back us to/help us/be willing to join us to\x02 fight the undead.
column2: 到现在，我 \x02\x03期望/希望/相信\x02 我们部落的其他酋长会 \x02\x03支持我们/帮助我们/愿意加入我们来\x02 对抗亡灵。

column1: No matter how strong our arguments, our unpopularity will make it a challenge to rally other clans.
column2: 无论我们的论据多么有力，不受欢迎的处境都会使我们召集其他氏族变成挑战。

column1: The other clans will see that it is in their interest to destroy this menace, if we say that it is so.
column2: 如果我们说这是事实，其他氏族会明白消灭这个威胁符合他们的利益。

column1: This menace must be dealt with soon, for our own good and the good of everyone who lives near here.
column2: 这个威胁必须尽快解决，为了我们自己，也为了所有住在这附近的人好。

column1: This menace must be dealt with soon, for our own good and the good of everyone in our tribe.
column2: 这个威胁必须尽快解决，为了我们自己，也为了我们部落的每一个人好。

column1: Whatever we do, we better rebuild our fortifications and recruit more weaponthanes immediately.
column2: 无论我们做什么，最好立即重建防御工事并招募更多武器领主。

column1: Humakt is foe of the undead; perhaps a sacrifice to him will ward off the walking corpses.
column2: 胡马克特是亡灵的死敌；也许向他献祭能驱退行尸。

column1: Humakt is foe of the undead, but also a war god. Although a mighty sacrifice to him might do some good, he truly respects only those who go out and fight.
column2: 胡马克特是亡灵的死敌，但也是一位战神。尽管一场隆重的献祭可能有些好处，但他真正尊敬的只有那些亲自上阵战斗的人。

column1: The walking dead act with mindless determination. We must take active steps against them, or they will return.
column2: 行尸行动时带着无脑的决意。我们必须采取主动措施对付它们，否则它们会卷土重来。

column1: Until we \x02\x04defeat these zombies for good/smash every one these ghouls/hack them all to bits/destroy every corpse\x02, they will harass us, over and over and over again.
column2: 在我们 \x02\x04彻底击败这些僵尸/砸碎每一只食尸鬼/把它们全部砍成碎片/摧毁每一具尸体\x02之前，它们会一次又一次地骚扰我们。

column1: The undead are maybe Chaotic, maybe not. I prefer to err on the side of killing them.
column2: 亡灵或许是混乱的，或许不是。我宁可错杀也不放过。

column1: We must not rest until every zombie has been turned to ash.
column2: 在所有僵尸都化为灰烬之前，我们绝不能停歇。

column1: When will we \x02\x03stop delaying/gather a large force/mount an offensive\x02 and \x02\x03drive these rotting fiends out/burn their foul corpses to dust/smash their putrid warriors to pieces\x02?.
column2: 我们何时才能 \x02\x03停止拖延/集结一支大军/发起攻势\x02 并 \x02\x03把这些腐烂的恶魔赶出去/将它们污秽的尸体烧成灰/将它们腐烂的战士砸成碎片\x02？

column1: Let’s not all talk at once.
column2: 我们别同时一起说话。

column1: There is no time for talk. We must act at once, which means acting alone.
column2: 没有时间说话了。我们必须立刻行动，这意味着只能单独行动。

column1: We’ll humiliate ourselves in front of everyone if we lose against the undead.
column2: 如果我们输给亡灵，我们会在所有人面前蒙羞。

column1: We’re already \x02\x03disgraced/humiliated/dishonored\x02. We must fight back now, and win, no matter what.
column2: 我们已经 \x02\x03丢脸/受辱/名誉扫地\x02了。我们现在必须反击并获胜，不顾一切。

column1: We’re all going to die! Then rise again, as zombies! Then die again! Then rise again!
column2: 我们都得死！然后复活，变成僵尸！然后再死！再复活！

column1: Others should be shouldering these risks with us.
column2: 其他人应该和我们一起承担这些风险。

column1: The ducks warned us about this.
column2: 鸭人曾警告过我们这件事。

column1: The ducks certainly were \x02\x03right/correct/accurate\x02 about the undead threat.
column2: 鸭人关于亡灵威胁的说法无疑是 \x02\x03对的/正确的/准确的\x02 。

column1: We must appeal to the self-interest of the other clans to overcome our reputation and so rally them to their own defense.
column2: 我们必须诉诸其他氏族的自身利益，以克服我们的名声问题，从而召集他们进行自卫。

column1: We can hope that the other clans will now \x02\x03see/understand/consider\x02 the need for their own \x02\x03protection/defense/preservation\x02 and \x02\x03aid/help/stand with\x02 us against the undead.
column2: 我们可以希望其他氏族现在 \x02\x03看到/理解/考虑\x02 他们自身 \x02\x03保护/防御/存续\x02 的必要性，并 \x02\x03协助/帮助/支持\x02 我们对抗亡灵。

column1: The other clans will see the advantage in uniting to destroy this enemy that threatens us all.
column2: 其他氏族会看到联合起来消灭这个威胁我们所有人的敌人的好处。

column1: We must \x02\x03trade on our goodwill with/call together many/use every trick of persuasion we have with\x02 other clans so we can \x02\x03join forces/unite/stand together\x02 and defeat the undead.
column2: 我们必须 \x02\x03利用我们的善意与/召集众多/使用我们所有说服技巧与\x02 其他氏族合作，以便我们 \x02\x03联手/联合/团结一致\x02 并击败亡灵。

column1: Together, we found the undead encampment, and cut down the walking dead wherever they stood.
column2: 我们一同找到了亡灵营地，将行尸就地砍倒。

column1: They were no match for us. We brought the true death to all of the stinking monsters, though not without losing several of our own warriors.
column2: 它们不是我们的对手。我们将真正的死亡带给了所有恶臭的怪物，不过我们也损失了几名战士。

column1: Our god-talkers said that the signs were good; Humakt would punish all creatures who blurred the lines between life and death.
column2: 我们的神言者说征兆是吉兆；胡马克特会惩罚所有模糊生与死界限的造物。

column1: We came upon a massive encampment of undead. We annihilated them, though not without cost.
column2: 我们遇见一处庞大的亡灵营地。我们歼灭了它们，不过也付出了代价。

column1: Driving magical staves into the earth? I don’t like the sound of that.

column1: Their ritual curses the land.
column2: 她们的仪式诅咒了这片土地。

column2: 她们的仪式诅咒了这片土地。其影响可能远及远方。

column1: These women fit the description of no people I know of.
column2: 这些女人，样貌不像我所知的任何族人。

column1: We should do that thing, you know, where we call upon the … where we find out what — it could be quite … it’s just on the tip of my tongue…

column1: We should sacrifice to Orlanth. Give him at least ten cows.
column2: 我们该向奥兰斯献祭。至少给他十头牛。

column2: 绝不要相信巫女。她们的魔法又野又恶，毋庸置疑。

column2: 以法力低落为由婉拒。

column1: We declined, telling them at our magic was at a low ebb.
column2: 我们婉拒了，告诉他们我们的法力正值低落。

column1: Their earth priestess denounced us. “I can sense that your power is great. It is no offense to refuse our petition, but to falsely plead poverty is contemptible.”
column2: 她们的大地女祭司斥责我们：“我能感知你们的力量强大。拒绝我们的请求倒不算冒犯，但假意哭穷却令人不齿。”

column1: The priestess spent the night talking with our women before continuing her quest elsewhere in Dragon Pass.
column2: 女祭司整夜与我们族中的女子交谈，之后继续她在龙之隘口别处的求索。

column1: Promise to sacrifice to Orlanth as the ritual begins.
column2: 承诺在仪式开始时向奥兰斯献祭。

column1: How many cows do you sacrifice?
column2: 你献祭多少头牛？

column1: Many weeks later, news reached us of the disaster at Orlanth’s holy place. At the ritual, the dragon Aroka appeared, gobbling up several ranks of worshippers.
column2: 数周之后，奥兰斯圣地惨祸的消息传来。仪式上，飞龙阿洛卡现身，吞下了几排信徒。

column1: Send a few worshippers to the ritual.
column2: 派少量信徒去参加仪式。

column1: We sent a few worshippers to the ritual.
column2: 我们派了少量信徒去参加仪式。

column1: It took our worshippers four weeks to find their way to Orlanth’s holy place. It took another four weeks for the survivors to struggle their way back. At the ritual, the dragon Aroka had appeared, and gobbled up several ranks of worshippers.
column2: 我们的信徒花了四周才找到去奥兰斯圣地的路。幸存者又挣扎了四周才返回。仪式上，飞龙阿洛卡现身，吞下了几排信徒。

column1: Send many worshippers to the ritual.
column2: 派大量信徒去参加仪式。

column1: We sent many worshippers to the ritual.
column2: 我们派了大量信徒去参加仪式。

column1: It took our worshippers four weeks to find their way to Orlanth’s holy place. It took another four weeks for the survivors to struggle their way back. At the ritual, the dragon Aroka had appeared, gobbling up several ranks of worshippers.
column2: 我们的信徒花了四周才找到去奥兰斯圣地的路。幸存者又挣扎了四周才返回。仪式上，飞龙阿洛卡现身，吞下了几排信徒。

column1: There’s no sign of drought here. The mere thought of one sends chills up my spine.
column2: 这里毫无干旱的迹象。光是想想就让我脊背发凉。

column1: If we show appropriate generosity, we will gain the respect of clans both near and far.
column2: 若我们展示恰如其分的慷慨，便会赢得远近各氏族的敬重。

column1: Supporting them will deplete our own magic.
column2: 支援他们将耗尽我们自己的法力。

column1: The more worshippers we send, the more we deplete our own magic, which is at a low ebb.
column2: 我们送去的信徒越多，自己法力损耗就越大——目前正值低落。

column1: The more worshippers we send, the more we deplete our own magic, which is presently strong.
column2: 我们送去的信徒越多，自己法力损耗就越大——目前尚属强盛。

column1: The more worshippers we send, the more we deplete our own magic, which is at a low ebb. We would need to sacrifice nine cows to have the same effect as many worshippers.
column2: 我们送去的信徒越多，自己法力损耗就越大——目前正值低落。我们需要献祭九头牛才能达到与大量信徒相同的效果。

column1: The more worshippers we send, the more we deplete our own magic, which is presently strong. We would need to sacrifice nine cows to have a good effect on the ritual.
column2: 我们送去的信徒越多，自己法力损耗就越大——目前尚属强盛。我们需要献祭九头牛才能对仪式产生良好效果。

column1: Harmast Barefoot’s successful heroquest saved the world from Gbaji. Karsten Fardrosson’s spectacular failure caused stars to fall on his people.
column2: 哈马斯特·赤足成功的英雄探索拯救了世界免于格巴吉魔；卡斯滕·法德罗森惨烈的失败则让星辰坠落在他的人民头上。

column1: Couldn’t they do the less violent heroquest in which Orlanth captures Daga the drought god and puts him in a jar?
column2: 难道他们不能去做那个烈度较小的英雄探索——奥兰斯囚禁干旱神达加、把他塞进罐子的那一个？

column1: Whether or not the drought reaches us is out of our hands.
column2: 干旱是否降临到我们头上，非我们所能掌控。

column1: If we had a king, the king could decide how many worshippers to send.
column2: 如果我们有一位王，王就能决定派多少信徒去。

column1: The earth priestess is trying to sense if our magic is strong or not.
column2: 大地女祭司在试探我们的法力是否强盛。

column1: How exciting! Let’s send many worshippers!
column2: 太让人兴奋了！派大量信徒去吧！

column1: sceneR026
column2: sceneR026

column1: Your unhappy carls have grown so discontented that they put down their farm implements. They refuse to till the soil, feed the cattle, or weed the gardens until you address their grievances. “Time after time,” they complain, “you have acted against the interests of the farmers, the backbone of the clan. We will have no more of it.”
column2: 你们不满的自由民已怨声载道，竟撂下了农具。他们拒绝犁田、喂牛、锄园，直到你回应他们的怨情。“一次又一次，”他们抱怨道，“你行事总是损害农夫——氏族脊梁的利益。我们受够了。”

column1: The carls stopped work, and refused to start again until the ring addressed their grievances.
column2: 自由民停下了工作，并且拒绝重新开工，直到长老会回应他们的不满。

column1: Attempt the heroquest of Ernalda Feeds the Tribe.
column2: 尝试厄娜尔达哺育部落的英雄任务。

column1: The carls were glad to see that the clan still had Ernalda’s blessing, and went back to work. They said they were willing to wait and see how the clan would show Ernalda’s favor to them.
column2: 自由民很高兴看到氏族仍拥有厄娜尔达的祝福，便回去工作了。他们说愿意观望，看氏族将如何向他们展示厄娜尔达的恩惠。

column1: The carls said that this proved we had lost Ernalda’s favor. Then they went to their homes and refused to discuss the matter further.
column2: 自由民说这证明我们已失去厄娜尔达的恩惠。然后他们各自回家，拒绝再讨论此事。

column1: Dismiss some warriors.
column2: 遣散一些战士。

column1: To please them, we dismissed some warriors.
column2: 为取悦他们，我们遣散了一些战士。

column1: How many warriors do you dismiss?
column2: 你遣散多少战士？

column1: Do you wish to give each dismissed warrior a cow as compensation?
column2: 你是否愿意给每位被遣散的战士一头牛作为补偿？

column1: The carls were happy they had fewer mouths to feed, but unhappy that they had fewer cows.
column2: 自由民很高兴少了几张嘴要养，但又不高兴少了几头牛。

column1: The carls were happy they had fewer mouths to feed.
column2: 自由民很高兴少了几张嘴要养。

column1: But the remaining weaponthanes worried about their former companions.
column2: 但留下的武器领主担忧他们从前的同伴。

column1: Distribute goods to the farmers which have been set aside for the weaponthanes.
column2: 把原本预留给武器领主的货物分发给农夫们。

column1: The ring took from the weaponthanes to give to the carls.
column2: 长老会从武器领主那里取走物资，分给自由民。

column1: How many cows worth of trade goods do you take from the weaponthanes to give to the carls?
column2: 你从武器领主那里取走价值多少头牛的贸易货物，分给自由民？

column1: The warriors \x02\x02grumbled mightily/complained loudly\x02 at this redistribution.
column2: 战士们 \x02\x02大声抱怨/高声抗议\x02 这次重新分配。

column1: They said that they too, should put down their arms and refuse to fight next time we were raided. “Then we’d see our wealth come back to us, really quickly!” But no one believed their threat.
column2: 他们说，他们也应该放下武器，下次我们被袭击时拒绝作战。“那样我们就会看到财富马上回到我们手中！”但没人相信他们的威胁。

column1: One of the older weaponthanes quieted their complaints by pointing out that it was better to lose a little wealth, “for now, anyhow,” than be forced to raise arms against their clansmen.
column2: 一位年长的武器领主平息了他们的抱怨，指出失去一点财富——“至少暂时如此”——总比被迫对同族人动武要好。

column1: Order the warriors to force them back to work.
column2: 命令战士们强迫他们回去工作。

column1: The ring ordered the weaponthanes to force them back to work.
column2: 长老会命令武器领主强迫他们回去工作。

column1: When the carls saw that the warriors intended to follow their chieftain’s order, they returned to the fields.
column2: 当自由民看到战士们打算遵从他们首领的命令时，他们返回了田地。

column1: The warriors balked, refusing to use force against their own people.
column2: 战士们犹豫了，拒绝对自己的同胞使用武力。

column1: Replace the chief.
column2: 更换首领。

column1: To show how seriously the ring took their complaints, the chieftain stepped aside.
column2: 为表明长老会何等重视他们的不满，首领退让了。

column1: Trade for more cows.
column2: 交易更多牛只。

column1: The carls accepted our promise.
column2: 自由民接受了我们的承诺。

column1: To placate them, we promised to trade for more cows.
column2: 为安抚他们，我们承诺去交易更多牛只。

column1: The only thing for me to do is to prepare for the heroquest of Ernalda Feeds the Tribe. Or resign.
column2: 我唯一能做的就是为厄娜尔达哺育部落的英雄任务做准备。或者辞职。

column1: A failed heroquest would be as salt on the carls’ sores. I must resign.
column2: 失败的英雄任务会如同往自由民的伤口上撒盐。我必须辞职。

column1: The balm of cattle will heal these wounds. We can afford to look far and wide and bring home fine cows for the carls.
column2: 牛群的慰藉能治愈这些创伤。我们负担得起四处寻觅，为自由民带回上好的牛只。

column1: Even cows cannot solve all the carls’s grievances. I must resign.
column2: 即使牛群也无法解决自由民的所有不满。我必须辞职。

column1: This is no fit of pique. This is a grave crisis, one that threatens the very future of our clan.
column2: 这不是一时意气。这是一场严重的危机，威胁着我们氏族未来的存续。

column1: This is a grave crisis, one that threatens the very future of our clan. It requires heroic measures to make it better.
column2: 这是一场严重的危机，威胁着我们氏族未来的存续。需要英雄级的举措才能改善。

column1: This is no fit of pique. This is a grave crisis, one that can only truly be solved by the resignation of our chief.
column2: 这不是一时意气。这是一场严重的危机，唯有我们首领的辞职才能真正解决。

column1: This is a monumental crisis, one that can only truly be solved great action.
column2: 这是一场巨大的危机，唯有伟大的行动才能真正解决。

column1: Carls live and die for cows. If we increase the herds, they will see we take their complaints seriously.
column2: 自由民生与死皆系于牛群。如果我们增加畜群，他们就会看到我们认真对待他们的不满。

column1: We can well afford to increase the herds, which they will see as proof that we take their complaints seriously.
column2: 我们完全有能力增加畜群，他们会将此视为我们认真对待他们不满的证明。

column1: No point trying to buy their favor by enlarging the herd; we have little of value to trade for livestock.
column2: 试图通过扩大畜群来收买他们的好感毫无意义；我们没什么值钱的东西能用来交易牲畜。

column1: This incident reflects poorly on our leadership.
column2: 这一事件对我们领导层的形象不利。

column1: They must obey their chosen leaders. Force them to follow Heort’s Laws.
column2: 他们必须服从他们选出的领袖。强迫他们遵循赫尔特法令。

column1: Using force against our own carls would be unprecedented, and an outrage.
column2: 对我们的自由民用兵将是史无前例的，也是一种暴行。

column1: Carls will not be won over by shows of strength, but by heartfelt proof of our sincere interest in them.
column2: 自由民不会被武力展示所说服，而是需要我们真心关切他们的诚挚证明。

column1: If only we had paid attention to the carls’ beloved deity, Ernalda, then we would know what to do.
column2: 要是我们当初关注了自由民敬爱的神祇厄娜尔达，我们就知道该怎么做了。

column1: We could attempt the heroquest of Ernalda Feeds the Tribe, but heroquests are risky.
column2: 我们可以尝试厄娜尔达哺育部落的英雄任务，但英雄任务风险很大。

column1: We should attempt the heroquest of Ernalda Feeds the Tribe.
column2: 我们应该尝试厄娜尔达哺育部落的英雄任务。

column1: Now is not the time to heroquest.
column2: 现在不是进行英雄任务的时候。

column1: People who believe they suffer injustice enjoy nothing more than seeing injustice done to someone else.
column2: 那些自认为遭受不公的人，最喜欢看到不公施加在别人身上。

column1: Don’t add insult to injury by dishonoring the warriors.
column2: 不要因侮辱战士而雪上加霜。

column1: During the War of the Gods, Orlanth neglected his duties to his son Barntar the Plowman. The people went hungry, until Orlanth saw the error of his ways and humbled himself before Barntar.
column2: 众神之战期间，奥兰斯怠慢了对他儿子犁者巴恩塔的责任。人民忍饥挨饿，直到奥兰斯认识到自己的过错，在巴恩塔面前谦卑下来。

column1: We mustn’t be too downhearted. We let the clan down, but we can still make things right.
column2: 我们不必过于沮丧。我们让氏族失望了，但仍可挽回局面。

column1: I knew we should have listened to the carls back when their complaints seemed minor.
column2: 我早就知道，当初自由民的不满看似微小时，我们就该倾听。

column1: When ring-giver ignores earth-mother’s friend, no one partakes of Babeester’s bliss.
column2: 当赠环者忽视大地之母的朋友时，无人能分享巴贝斯特的福佑。

column1: sceneR027
column2: sceneR027

column1: A large number of our carls left for the \x01@! clan, taking cows with them.
column2: 大量我们的自由民前往 \x01@! 氏族，带走了牛只。

column1: Let them go.
column2: 随他们去吧。

column1: We had little choice but to let them leave.
column2: 我们别无选择，只能让他们离开。

column1: Offer to replace entire ring if they agree to stay.
column2: 提议更换整个长老会，如果他们同意留下。

column1: The ring stepped aside in favor of new candidates.
column2: 长老会让位给新的候选人。

column1: Most of the carls were sufficiently impressed by this gesture to give the clan another chance.
column2: 大多数自由民对这一姿态印象深刻，决定再给氏族一次机会。

column1: A few of the carls were sufficiently impressed by this gesture to give the clan another chance.
column2: 少数自由民对这一姿态印象深刻，决定再给氏族一次机会。

column1: Plead with them to stay.
column2: 恳求他们留下。

column1: The ring pleaded with them to reconsider.
column2: 长老会恳求他们重新考虑。

column1: Some of them did so; others left.
column2: 一些人这样做了；其他人则离开了。

column1: pleas fell on deaf ears.
column2: 恳求被当成了耳旁风

column1: Promise to perform the heroquest of Ernalda Feeds the Tribe.
column2: 承诺执行“埃尔纳达养育部落”英雄任务。

column1: Some of the carls were sufficiently impressed by this gesture to give the clan another chance.
column2: 一些自由民对这一姿态印象深刻，决定再给氏族一次机会。

column1: The carls said that this proved their point. They asked us how we expected them to stay in a clan that had lost Ernalda’s favor.
column2: 自由民说这证明了他们的观点。他们问我们，怎能期望他们留在已经失去埃尔纳达恩宠的氏族里。

column1: The carls sneered at our second heroquest failure. They said that this proved they were right to leave, for how could we expected them to stay when Ernalda so clearly turned her back to us?
column2: 自由民嘲笑我们第二次英雄任务失败。他们说这证明了他们离开是对的，因为埃尔纳达明显背弃了我们，我们怎能期望他们留下。

column1: “You can leave, but not with the cows.”
column2: “你们可以离开，但不准带走牛。”

column1: We told them that they were free to go, but that the cows belonged to our clan.
column2: 我们告诉他们可以自由离开，但牛属于我们的氏族。

column1: “What are you going to do to stop us from taking our cows?” the carls defiantly ask. Do you call on your warriors to prevent them from leaving with the livestock?
column2: “你们打算怎么阻止我们带走我们的牛？”自由民挑衅地问。你是否召来你的武士，阻止他们带着牲畜离开？

column1: We ordered our warriors to stop them from leaving with our cows.
column2: 我们命令武士阻止他们带着我们的牛离开。

column1: The warriors subjected the carls-turned-rustlers to a righteous beating, and only a few cattle were lost to us in the confusion.
column2: 武士们对这些变成盗牛贼的自由民施以正当的殴打，混乱中我们仅损失了几头牛。

column1: The weaponthanes balked, reminding us that the carls were our kin. Many harsh words were directed at the ring by carl and weaponthane alike.
column2: 武器领主们犹豫了，提醒我们自由民是我们的族人。自由民和武器领主都对长老会说了许多刻薄话。

column1: We backed down when the carls dared us to use force.
column2: 当自由民挑战我们使用武力时，我们退却了。

column1: People said the ring looked foolish, but they were also heard saying that it would have been worse had they insisted on using force.
column2: 人们说长老会看起来很愚蠢，但也听到有人说，如果他们坚持用武，情况会更糟。

column1: They have no right to those cows.
column2: 他们对那些牛没有权利。

column1: The carl is the backbone of the clan; we are disgraced.
column2: 自由民是氏族的脊梁；我们蒙受了耻辱。

column1: The carl is the backbone of the clan; we are disgraced unless we take giant steps to win them back.
column2: 自由民是氏族的脊梁；除非我们采取重大举措赢回他们，否则我们将蒙受耻辱。

column1: Mere words are unlikely to effect a reconciliation now.
column2: 如今仅凭言语不太可能实现和解。

column1: It is exceptionally rare for carls to become so disenchanted with their clan ring that they seek a new clan.
column2: 自由民对氏族议会如此失望以至于寻找新氏族，这种情况极其罕见。

column1: It is exceptionally rare for carls to leave a clan like this, we must match it with an exceptionally rare reaction.
column2: 自由民如此离开氏族极其罕见，我们必须以同样罕见的反应来回应。

column1: Even if we resolve this situation, we’ll be shamed in the eyes of other clans.
column2: 即使我们解决了这个局面，在其他氏族眼中我们也会蒙羞。

column1: If we resolve this by a heroquest, it will counterbalance the shame of having gotten to this point.
column2: 如果我们通过英雄任务解决此事，那将抵消走到这一步所蒙受的耻辱。

column1: We should all step down, admit our shame, and let a new ring start again.
column2: 我们都应该退位，承认耻辱，让新的长老会重新开始。

column1: We should attempt the heroquest of Ernalda Feeds the Tribe; things are so bad that any risk is worth it.
column2: 我们应该尝试“埃尔纳达养育部落”英雄任务；情况糟到任何风险都值得承担。

column1: We should have attempted the heroquest of Ernalda Feeds the Tribe before things got this bad.
column2: 我们本该在情况恶化到这种地步之前就尝试“埃尔纳达养育部落”英雄任务。

column1: We attempted the heroquest of Ernalda Feeds the Tribe before, and failed. Another failure will hurt all of us.
column2: 我们之前尝试过“埃尔纳达养育部落”英雄任务，但失败了。再次失败将伤害我们所有人。

column1: Although we should have attempted the heroquest of Ernalda Feeds the Tribe earlier, there is still a chance of success.
column2: 尽管我们本该更早尝试“埃尔纳达养育部落”英雄任务，但现在仍有成功的机会。

column1: Trying to heroquest now will merely pile one disaster on the other.
column2: 现在尝试英雄任务只会雪上加霜。

column1: Their joining the \x01@! clan will complicate marriage eligibility tremendously!
column2: 他们加入 \x01@! 氏族将极大地使婚姻资格复杂化！

column1: Perhaps we can find some treasure that will win back the love of the carls.
column2: 也许我们能找到一些财宝，赢回自由民的眷顾。

column1: This wouldn’t have happened if more of us knew how to read.
column2: 如果我们更多人识字，这件事就不会发生。

column1: The carls are right. The rest of you have been too arrogant, and should step down.
column2: 自由民是对的。你们其他人太傲慢了，应该退下。

column1: I’ve been telling you all along — we’re unfit to rule a cabbage patch!
column2: 我一直告诉你们——我们连一块白菜地都管不好！

column1: During the War of the Gods, Orlanth neglected his duties to his son Barntar the Plowman. But he mended his ways before it was too late.
column2: 在众神之战期间，奥兰斯忽视了他对儿子犁者巴恩塔的责任。但他及时改正了自己的行为。

column1: When ox-follower leads Uralda’s children, Orlanth’s bondsman must be loose.
column2: 当赶牛人带领乌拉达的儿女时，奥兰斯的仆从必须松开。

column1: Many of your warriors are leaving. They are tired of warning you to treat them with proper respect, they say. Now, they are acting. They will join the \x01@! clan. Next time they see you, it will be on the battlefield.
column2: 你们的许多武士正在离开。他们说，他们厌倦了一再警告你们要以适当的尊重对待他们。现在他们付诸行动了。他们将加入 \x01@! 氏族。下次见到你们，便是在战场上。

column1: Many of the weaponthanes packed up to leave, claiming that we had repeatedly slighted them.
column2: 许多武器领主收拾行装准备离开，声称我们一再轻视他们。

column1: Let them leave.
column2: 让他们走吧。

column1: We had no choice but to let them leave.
column2: 我们别无选择，只能让他们离开。

column1: Most of the warriors were sufficiently impressed by this gesture to give the clan another chance.
column2: 大多数武士对这一姿态印象深刻，决定再给氏族一次机会。

column1: A few of the warriors were sufficiently impressed by this gesture to give the clan another chance.
column2: 少数武士对这一姿态印象深刻，决定再给氏族一次机会。

column1: Attempt the Humakt the Champion heroquest.
column2: 尝试胡马克特冠军英雄任务。

column1: The weaponthanes were impressed by the heroquest. They took back their harsh words and agreed to continue to serve the clan.
column2: 武器领主们对英雄任务印象深刻。他们收回了自己的狠话，同意继续为氏族效力。

column1: The weaponthanes left, looking for a clan that enjoyed Humakt’s favor.
column2: 武器领主们离开了，去寻找一个享有胡马克特恩宠的氏族。

column1: The weaponthanes who were leaving were too polite to laugh at our failure, but said that they looked forward to serving a clan that enjoyed Humakt’s favor.
column2: 那些即将离开的武器领主很有礼貌，没有嘲笑我们的失败，但表示他们期待为一个享有胡马克特恩宠的氏族效力。

column1: “You can go, but take no clan property with you.”
column2: “你们可以走，但不准带走任何氏族财产。”

column1: We told them that they were free to go, but that our property was not.
column2: 我们告诉他们可以自由离开，但我们的财产不能带走。

column1: “These things are ours. They represent but a fraction of what we should take. Are you going to try to stop us?” they ask.
column2: “这些东西是我们的。它们不过是我们理应拿走的一小部分。你们打算阻拦我们吗？”他们问道。

column1: Do you call on your remaining loyal weaponthanes to prevent them from leaving with the goods?
column2: 你是否召集仍旧忠诚的武器领主，阻止他们带着货物离开？

column1: They said that it was only their due. We ordered our remaining warriors to stop them
column2: 他们说那是他们应得的。我们命令剩余的战士阻拦他们。

column1: Our warriors refused. Some were so affronted that they left, too.
column2: 我们的战士拒绝了。一些人愤愤不平，也离开了。

column1: Ultimately, the ring relented, and allowed them to take the property they claimed.
column2: 最终，长老会妥协了，允许他们拿走了声称的财产。

column1: I worked hard to trade for the things they’re so casually carting off!
column2: 我辛苦交易得来的东西，他们就这样大摇大摆地运走了！

column1: We have treated the warriors shamefully. I’m half-tempted to leave myself.
column2: 我们对待战士的方式令人羞愧。我自己都差点想离开。

column1: They have no faith in us, but their heritage still means something. If we all step down — which we should do anyway — most of them will come back.
column2: 他们对我们不抱信心，但血缘传承依然重要。如果我们全部退位——反正我们也该这么做——大部分人都会回来。

column1: They have no faith in us, but their heritage still means something. If we do something to honor that heritage most of them will return.
column2: 他们对我们不抱信心，但血缘传承依然重要。如果我们做些什么来尊重那份传承，大部分人都会回来。

column1: If we had learned the secrets of Humakti myths, then we would know what to do.
column2: 如果我们掌握了胡马克特神话的秘密，就会知道该怎么做。

column1: It is exceptionally rare for warriors to become so disenchanted with their clan ring that they seek a new clan.
column2: 战士对氏族议会如此失望以至于去投靠新氏族，这极其罕见。

column1: It is exceptionally rare for warriors to leave like this. It will take exceptionally rare action on our part to win them back.
column2: 战士这样离开极其罕见。我们这边也需要极其罕见的行动才能赢回他们。

column1: We should have learned the heroquest of Humakt the Champion. It would have honored the weaponthanes, and it would have helped us now.
column2: 我们本应学习冠军胡马克特的英雄任务。那本可向武器领主们表达敬意，现在也能帮到我们。

column1: We should attempt the heroquest of Humakt the Champion; things are so bad that any risk is justified.
column2: 我们应该尝试冠军胡马克特的英雄任务；情况已经糟到任何风险都值得冒。

column1: The heroquest of Humakt the Champion would have been easier if begun before we reached these sorry straits.
column2: 冠军胡马克特的英雄任务如果在我们陷入这种悲惨困境之前开始，本会更容易。

column1: We should have tried the heroquest of Humakt the Champion earlier, but we still have a chance of success.
column2: 我们本应更早尝试冠军胡马克特的英雄任务，但仍有成功的机会。

column1: Trying to heroquest now will only add catastrophe to humiliation.
column2: 现在尝试英雄任务只会给羞辱雪上加霜。

column1: We should all step down. And I’m tempted to strip my own insignia and set out for another clan.
column2: 我们都应该退位。而我自己也想剥下徽记，投奔另一个氏族。

column1: A new ring brings no guarantee of better leadership. The best way to honor the weaponthanes is to win at the Humakt the Champion heroquest.
column2: 新的长老会未必能带来更好的领导。向武器领主表达敬意的最佳方式，就是在冠军胡马克特的英雄任务中取胜。

column1: When Humakt severed his ties to his family, his brother Orlanth was offended. They fought for a long time, and wrecked many things. Before it was too late, they reconciled.
column2: 当胡马克特断绝与家族的联系时，他的兄弟奥兰斯感到冒犯。他们打了很久，毁掉了许多东西。在一切太晚之前，他们和好了。

column1: We don’t need warriors to defend our temples. The gods will do that for us.
column2: 我们不需要战士来守卫神庙。诸神自会替我们守护。

column1: The men squabble, but the women pay the price.
column2: 男人们争吵，女人们付出代价。

column1: Without swift swords, we are nothing.
column2: 没有锋利的刀剑，我们一无是处。

column1: With this stain on our reputation, we can forget about taking the throne in any of our lifetimes.
column2: 名声有了这个污点，我们这辈子都别想登上王座了。

column1: It will be good to have fewer warriors. We’ll be less tempted to raid.
column2: 少一些战士也好，这样我们就没那么想劫掠了。

column1: Bird-chirpings tie no blood-knots; only the finger-clasp, the forehead-knee, will do.
column2: 鸟鸣结不成血盟；唯有指握、触额触膝才行。

column2: sceneR029

column1: Arlesta, a priestess of Maran Gor, Mother of Earthquakes, pays you a visit. “You have done honor to Maran Gor, who is not often honored. Feared, yes; honored, no. It may be that we are prepared to give you a gift, should you continue to deserve such a thing.”
column2: 阿莱丝塔，地震之母玛兰·戈尔的女祭司，前来拜访你。“你们给玛兰·戈尔带来了荣耀，她并不常受尊荣。受畏惧，是的；受尊荣，不。也许我们准备给你们一份礼物，前提是你们继续值得如此。”

column1: A priestess of Maran Gor came to us, and hinted that she might have a gift of some sort to give us.
column2: 一位玛兰·戈尔的女祭司来到我们这里，暗示她也许有某种礼物要给我们。

column1: Ask Arlesta to be more specific about her gift.
column2: 请阿莱丝塔更具体地说明她的礼物。

column1: We asked her to be more specific about her gift.
column2: 我们请她更具体地说明她的礼物。

column1: “It is difficult to be less subtle than the Goddess of Shaking Earth,” she sniffed, “but you have succeeded.” At that, she abruptly departed.
column2: “比地震女神更难委婉可不容易，”她哼了一声，“但你们成功了。”说完，她突然离开了。

column1: Gift Arlesta with rings and silver.
column2: 以戒指和银币作为礼物赠与阿莱丝塔。

column1: We gave Arlesta gifts of rings and silver.
column2: 我们给了阿莱丝塔戒指和银币作为礼物。

column1: How many cows worth of goods do you give her?
column2: 你给她价值多少头牛的货物？

column1: After receiving our token of respect, she gave us Maran Gor’s gift: a clod of sacred earth that needed several clans’ god-talkers to work. She told us that it would make a rumbling noise when it was ready to use, and that it would bring the wrath of her mistress down on those who opposed our aims. But we would have to carefully decide when to use it, for it would work only once.
column2: 收到我们表示敬意的礼物后，她给了我们玛兰·戈尔的赠礼：一块需要好几个氏族的神言者共同运作的圣土之块。她告诉我们，当它准备就绪时会发出隆隆声，并能将女主人的愤怒降临到那些阻碍我们目标的人头上。但我们必须谨慎决定使用时机，因为它只能用一次。

column1: Invite Arlesta to preside over a sacrifice to Maran Gor.
column2: 邀请阿莱丝塔主持向玛兰·戈尔的献祭。

column1: We asked her to preside over a sacrifice to Maran Gor.
column2: 我们请她主持向玛兰·戈尔的献祭。

column1: After the ceremony, she gave us Maran Gor’s gift: a clod of sacred earth that needed several clans’ god-talkers to work. She told us that it would make a rumbling noise when it was ready to use, and that it would bring the wrath of her mistress down on those who opposed our aims. But we would have to carefully decide when to use it, for it would work only once.
column2: 仪式之后，她给了我们玛兰·戈尔的赠礼：一块需要好几个氏族的神言者共同运作的圣土之块。她告诉我们，当它准备就绪时会发出隆隆声，并能将女主人的愤怒降临到那些阻碍我们目标的人头上。但我们必须谨慎决定使用时机，因为它只能用一次。

column1: Offer to add a shrine to Maran Gor to your temple.
column2: 提议在你的神庙中增建一座玛兰·戈尔的神龛。

column1: We told her we would further honor her mistress by building a shrine to her in our temple.
column2: 我们告诉她，我们会在神庙中为她建一座神龛，以进一步尊崇她的女主人。

column1: Upon hearing this, she smiled a great, gap-toothed smile, and gave us Maran Gor’s gift: a clod of sacred earth that needed several clans’ god-talkers to work. She told us that it would make a rumbling noise when it was ready to use, and that it would bring the wrath of her mistress down on those who opposed our aims. But we would have to carefully decide when to use it, for it would work only once.
column2: 听闻此言，她咧嘴一笑，露出豁牙，将玛兰·戈尔的礼物赐予我们：一块需要数个氏族的神言者共同施法的神圣土块。她告诉我们，当土块即将生效时会发出隆隆声，并会将她主母的怒火倾泻到阻挠我们目标之人身上。但我们得谨慎决定何时使用它，因为仅能用一次。

column1: “The opportunity to pay homage to Maran Gor is gift enough.”
column2: “能向玛兰·戈尔致敬，这本身就是恩赐。”

column1: With exquisite and prudent politeness, we declined her gracious offer.
column2: 我们以细腻而审慎的礼节，婉拒了她慷慨的馈赠。

column1: Arlesta seemed pleased, though with her sharp-toothed smile, it was hard to be certain.
column2: 阿莱丝塔似乎颇为满意——尽管她尖牙毕露的笑容让人难以确定。

column1: If we enter into an agreement with this terrible goddess, it must be one which we are sure we can keep.
column2: 若要与此可怖的女神缔结协议，那必须是我们确信能够履行的协议。

column1: The favor of Maran Gor may bring us power, but it will also make others fear us.
column2: 玛兰·戈尔的恩惠或许能带给我们力量，但也会让旁人畏惧我们。

column1: The more Maran Gor’s priestesses like us, the more powerful her gift will be.
column2: 玛兰·戈尔的女祭司越喜欢我们，她的礼物就越强大。

column1: She likely intends to give us a Sacred Clod, which will bring an earthquake down on our enemies. The more cows we sacrifice now, the more powerful the earthquake.
column2: 她很可能打算赐予我们一块神圣土块，能引发地震摧毁敌人。我们献祭的牛只越多，地震就越猛烈。

column1: Maran Gor is Ernalda’s grim sister. She brings terrible destruction to those who incur the wrath of the Earth.
column2: 玛兰·戈尔是厄娜尔妲那位阴郁的姐妹。她会给招致大地怒火之人带来可怕的毁灭。

column1: The priestess will care more for sacrifice to her deity than for rings and silver.
column2: 比起指环与白银，女祭司更在意献祭给她的神祇。

column1: Maran Gor isn’t so bad. Eurmal stole her skirt once, and she didn’t kill him. Just dismembered him a couple of times.
column2: 玛兰·戈尔没那么糟。欧尔马特曾偷过她的裙子，她也没杀他——只是把他肢解了几回。

column1: Arlesta’s gift will not come without cost. If we refuse it, we must do so politely.
column2: 阿莱丝塔的礼物不会没有代价。若要拒绝，我们必须礼貌地拒绝。

column1: A king must be feared. Maran Gor’s favor can get us closer to the throne.
column2: 国王必须令人畏惧。玛兰·戈尔的恩惠能让我们离王座更近。

column1: Don’t trust her.
column2: 别相信她。

column1: “Roads are for the wise; the stupid should stay home.”
column2: “道路是给智者准备的；蠢人该待在家里。”

column1: Do whatever is necessary to get that gift.
column2: 不惜一切代价拿到那份礼物。

column1: Thunder-lizard’s mother is seldom a gold-thrower, preferring to drink life-ale.
column2: 雷蜥的母亲很少抛洒金粉，她更喜欢啜饮生命麦酒。

column1: They said that they would sooner intermarry with Beastfolk than with us. And the Beastfolk were their ancient enemies.
column2: 他们说，他们宁愿与兽人通婚也不愿与我们通婚。而兽人曾是他们的宿敌。

column1: They said that no mere trinkets, nor even cows, could redeem the blood we had spilled.
column2: 他们说，区区小玩意儿，甚至牛只，都无法赎回我们流下的血。
