column2: “你们所谓的珍宝连偿还你们流下的 \x01@! 血都不够！趁我们还未被迫背弃保护使者的誓言，滚出我们的视线！”

column1: They did not believe that \x01@\x12 did what we said it did.
column2: 他们不相信 \x01@\x12 能做到我们所说的。

column1: They said they would never join a tribe that would allow us to join it.
column2: 他们说他们绝不会加入一个允许我们加入的部落。

column1: The rest of the tribe refused them, and though our feud was settled, we left them with rankling resentment in their hearts.
column2: 部落的其他人拒绝了他们，虽然我们的世仇了结了，但我们让他们心中留下了怨恨。

column1: What do you propose calling your tribe?
column2: 你建议如何称呼你的部落？

column1: After many days of hard bargaining, we agreed, and the \x01@\x0E tribe was born.
column2: 经过多日艰难议价，我们达成了协议， \x01@\x0E 部落由此诞生。

column1: They said that they were glad to end the feud, but they did not want any other entanglements with us right now.
column2: 他们说很高兴结束世仇，但目前不想与我们有任何其他纠葛。

column1: Ending the feud is good enough for now.
column2: 结束世仇目前就足够了。

column1: Though we talked idly about tribes, both clans agreed that it was not the right time to consider tribal ties between our people.
column2: 虽然我们随意谈论了部落，但两个氏族都认为现在不是考虑我们人民之间部落关系的合适时机。

column1: Before leaving, we discussed tribes with them. They appeared to have no reservations about being part of the Colymar tribe.
column2: 离开前，我们与他们讨论了部落。他们似乎对成为科利马尔部落的一部分毫无保留。

column1: End the feud first with gifts, then talk about tribal things.
column2: 先用礼物结束世仇，再谈部落之事。

column1: Let’s not offend them with an offer worth less than fifty cows.
column2: 我们不要用价值不足五十头牛的提议冒犯他们。

column1: Peace, like anything valuable, can be purchased. Now that we have paid the price, we can talk and they will listen.
column2: 和平，如同任何宝贵之物，皆可购买。既然我们已付出代价，就可以交谈，他们会倾听。

column1: Gifts worth seven cows would be a minimum. Fifty cows would be good. A hundred would open their ears to tribe talk.
column2: 价值七头牛的礼物是底线。五十头牛不错。一百头牛会让他们愿意听部落之事。

column1: There is no guarantee that peace between our clans will lead to tribe-making. But we should try to talk to them.
column2: 不保证我们氏族之间的和平会导致部落建立。但我们应该试着与他们交谈。

column1: There is no guarantee that peace will mean they want to join our tribe. But there is no harm in asking.
column2: 不保证和平意味着他们想加入我们的部落。但问问也无妨。

column1: They have grievances with us, but none that can’t be overcome.
column2: 他们对我们有怨言，但并非无法克服。

column1: They have many grievances with us. We will have to be extraordinarily generous to sway their hearts.
column2: 他们对我们有很多怨言。我们必须极其慷慨才能打动他们的心。

column1: They dislike us, but if we can overcome their ill feelings they might listen to talk of tribe-making.
column2: 他们不喜欢我们，但如果我们能克服他们的恶感，他们或许会听部落建立的事。

column1: They are better disposed to us now. We should talk to them about making a tribe.
column2: 他们现在对我们态度更好了。我们应该和他们谈谈建立一个部落。

column1: They are better disposed to us now. We can see if they would like to join our tribe and find a more lasting peace.
column2: 他们现在对我们态度更好了。我们可以看看他们是否愿意加入我们的部落，寻求更持久的和平。

column1: They do not dislike us; they despise us. We must work hard to overcome their ill feelings towards us before making any other suggestion.
column2: 他们不是不喜欢我们；他们鄙视我们。在提出任何其他建议之前，我们必须努力克服他们对我们的恶感。

column1: They do not despise us; they dislike us. We must speak well and sway their opinion towards the benefits of life in a tribe.
column2: 他们不是鄙视我们；他们不喜欢我们。我们必须好好说话，说服他们看到部落生活的好处。

column1: Let’s offer them our magic, but give them as little as possible. Magic can’t be measured. How will they know?
column2: 让我们献上我们的魔法，但尽可能给得少。魔法无法衡量。他们怎么会知道？

column1: They should be approaching us, begging us to join a tribe with them.
column2: 他们应该主动来找我们，恳求我们加入他们的部落。

column1: I’d sooner eat grubs than stand up for these stickpickers at a tribal moot.
column2: 我宁可吃幼虫也不愿在部落大会上为这些拾柴人辩护。

column1: There’s something about that chieftain, he’s got this quality about him. No, more of a mood really. It’s hard to put into words.
column2: 那个酋长有些特别，他身上有种特质。不，更像是一种情绪。很难用言语表达。

column1: Boiling blood may be cooled by a gentle wind, but the same wind can fan the fire.
column2: 滚沸的热血可被和风吹冷，但同样的风也能扇起火焰。

column1: Stony hearts have no ears to listen.
column2: 石心无耳听。

column1: Orlanth so needed to make peace with Yelm that he brought him back from the dead.
column2: 奥兰斯如此需要与耶尔姆讲和，以至于将他从死者中带回。

column1: Generosity is the polish of the peace table.
column2: 慷慨是和平之桌的光泽。

column1: “Three things you must not boast about: your knowledge, the size of your herd, and the favor of Orlanth.”
column2: “三件事你不可吹嘘：你的知识，你畜群的大小，以及奥兰斯的眷顾。”

column1: need to decide what to do about Einarth’s prophecy that we will start a great tribe.
column2: 需要决定如何应对艾纳斯关于我们将建立一个伟大部落的预言。

column1: Try to start a tribe immediately.
column2: 立即尝试建立一个部落。

column1: Our emissaries began sounding out nearby clans.
column2: 我们的使者开始试探附近的氏族。

column1: Wait three years before starting the tribe.
column2: 等三年再开始建立部落。

column1: Our god-talkers felt that we should prepare for this great mission slowly, and begin tribe-making only when truly ready.
column2: 我们的神言者认为我们应该慢慢为这个伟大使命做准备，只有真正准备好时才开始建立部落。

column1: sceneR031
column2: sceneR031

column1: After the spell was cast, we saw no further signs of a curse.
column2: 法术后，我们再未看到诅咒的迹象。

column1: Perform a ritual of divination to identify the assailant.
column2: 执行占卜仪式以识别袭击者。

column1: To find who had done this, we performed an augury.
column2: 为了找出是谁干的，我们进行了占兆。

column1: We could not identify the attacker.
column2: 我们无法识别袭击者。

column1: We saw patterns in the entrails. First, a seed. Then, a stalk. Then, a man. Then, a man with an arrow. This meant the attacker was one of the plant people called Aldryami, or elves.
column2: 我们在内脏中看到了图案。先是种子，然后是茎秆，接着是一个人，再是一个持箭的人。这意味着袭击者是被称为阿尔德里亚米或精灵的植物人种之一。

column1: The Summons of Evil ritual had brought our ancient enemies to us.
column2: 召唤邪恶仪式将我们的宿敌带到了我们面前。

column1: We were once more bedeviled by our ancient enemies.
column2: 我们再次被宿敌困扰。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods for protection from unseen foes.
column2: 向诸神献祭以求得看不见的敌人的保护。

column1: Seeking protection from unseen foes, we sacrificed to the gods.
column2: 为寻求看不见的敌人的保护，我们向诸神献祭。

column1: Our god-talkers said that the gods would be watching out for us.
column2: 我们的神言者说诸神会保护我们。

column1: Our god-talkers could not say whether or not the gods would help us.
column2: 我们的神言者无法确定众神是否会帮助我们。

column1: Send a war party out to search for the assailant.
column2: 派出一支战团搜寻袭击者。

column1: We sent a party to track the attacker.
column2: 我们派出一队人追踪袭击者。

column1: We found no one. We did not even find a trace of an enemy’s passing.
column2: 我们谁也没找到。甚至没有发现敌人经过的痕迹。

column1: We spotted them from afar; our foes were the plant people called Aldryami, or elves.
column2: 我们远远地看见了他们；我们的敌人是被称为阿尔德里亚米或精灵的植物人。

column1: Do you attack them?
column2: 你要攻击他们吗？

column1: We chose not to attack them.
column2: 我们选择不攻击他们。

column1: Everyone celebrated the success of the Summons of Evil.
column2: 每个人都庆祝了“邪恶召唤”的成功。

column1: Their knowledge of the terrain, and their surprising ferocity, overwhelmed our war party. We mourned the dead.
column2: 他们对地形的了解以及惊人的凶残击溃了我们的战团。我们哀悼死者。

column1: Step up patrols.
column2: 加强巡逻。

column1: We stepped up our patrols.
column2: 我们加强了巡逻。

column1: The weaponthanes saw no further signs of the attacker.
column2: 武器领主们没有发现袭击者进一步的迹象。

column1: The carls are afraid to go near the woods.
column2: 自由民们不敢靠近树林。

column1: It’s hard to make peace with an enemy who shoots before he talks.
column2: 跟一个还没说话就放箭的敌人讲和是很难的。

column1: I can’t give good advice without knowing more of our foe.
column2: 在不了解更多敌人情况的前提下，我无法给出好建议。

column1: The attacker is no ordinary foe, for our patrols are excellent, and he eluded them as if they were nothing.
column2: 袭击者并非普通敌人，因为我们的巡逻队堪称卓越，而他却轻松躲过了他们，仿佛他们不存在一般。

column1: We should perform a divination.
column2: 我们应该进行一次占卜。

column1: Their stealth in the forest, the type of the arrow — these are important clues.
column2: 他们在森林中的隐秘行动、箭矢的类型——这些都是重要线索。

column1: That arrow is of elven manufacture. We’re dealing with the plant people, the Aldryami.
column2: 那支箭是精灵制造的。我们面对的是植物人，即阿尔德里亚米（精灵）。

column1: Our people will be dispirited if we do not take strong action.
column2: 如果我们不采取强硬行动，我们的人民会士气低落。

column1: Through the lung-food was the flesh-nail hammered.
column2: 通过肺食，肉钉被锤入。

column1: Why are the carls always coming running to us? Can’t they handle one little arrow on their own?
column2: 为什么自由民总是跑来找我们？他们连一支小箭都处理不了吗？

column1: We’re being attacked for clearing the forest.
column2: 我们因为清理森林而受到攻击。

column1: My heart pounds at the thought of battle with a mysterious foe.
column2: 一想到要与神秘敌人交战，我的心就怦怦直跳。

column1: The renowned prophet Einarth Milk-Eyes, who hails from a distant clan, returns.
column2: 来自遥远氏族的著名先知艾纳斯·奶眼回来了。

column1: Einarth Milk-Eyes, an old man from a faraway clan, comes to visit you. He is renowned as a prophet.
column2: 来自远方氏族的老人艾纳斯·奶眼前来拜访您。他以先知之名声名远扬。

column1: “A great kingdom I see before me. Its foundation, a tribe built of this tula’s timber.
column2: “我看见面前有一个伟大王国。它的根基，一个由这片图拉领地的木材建成的部落。

column1: I see a union of opposites, a marriage to the Queen of Feathers.
column2: 我看见对立之物的联合，一场与羽翼女王的联姻。

column1: “A golden tribe I see before me, a tribe built of this tula’s timber. I see rivals setting aside their differences, and a new unity in this land.
column2: “我看见面前有一个黄金部落，一个由这片图拉领地的木材建成的部落。我看见对手们搁置分歧，在这片土地上形成新的团结。

column1: I see triumph, if these clan halls contain sufficient wit and bravery.”
column2: 如果这些部族大厅拥有足够的智慧与勇气，我将看到胜利。”

column1: Einarth Milk-Eyes came to us
column2: 艾纳斯·奶眼来到我们这里

column1: again with a similar prophecy.
column2: 又一次带着相似的预言。

column1: with a prophecy.
column2: 带着一个预言。

column1: It seemed to mean that we should start a tribe.
column2: 这似乎意味着我们应该建立一个部落。

column1: End the feud with the \x01@! clan.
column2: 结束与 \x01@! 氏族的世仇。

column1: Gift Einarth.
column2: 赠礼给艾纳斯。

column1: We honored Einarth with gifts.
column2: 我们用礼物尊崇了艾纳斯。

column1: Einarth said that our generosity confirmed the truth of his prophecy.
column2: 艾纳斯说我们的慷慨证实了他预言的真相。

column1: Ignore the prophecy.
column2: 忽视这个预言。

column1: Immediately begin assembling a tribe.
column2: 立即开始组建部落。

column1: We took his words to heart, and decided it was time to assemble a tribe.
column2: 我们将他的话铭记在心，并决定是时候组建一个部落了。

column1: Offer him a place in your clan.
column2: 在你的氏族中为他提供一个位置。

column1: Once more, we offered him a home with us.
column2: 我们再次向他提供在我们这里的家。

column1: “You honor me again,” he said, “but I am still happy where I am.”
column2: “你又一次尊崇了我，”他说，“但我仍满足于目前所在之处。”

column1: We offered him a home with us.
column2: 我们向他提供在我们这里的家。

column1: “You honor me,” he said, “but I belong to a clan, and cannot forsake my duties to them.”
column2: “你尊崇了我，”他说，“但我属于一个氏族，不能抛弃对他们的职责。”

column1: Wait for a while, then assemble a tribe.
column2: 等一段时间，然后再组建部落。

column1: We decided to act on his words, but not in haste.
column2: 我们决定按他的话行事，但不急于一时。

column1: How many years do you decide to wait?
column2: 你决定等多少年？

column1: I trust Einarth.
column2: 我信任艾纳斯。

column1: Einarth is a great prophet. I would love the chance to learn from him.
column2: 艾纳斯是一位伟大的先知。我很想有机会向他学习。

column1: If Einarth trusts his prophecy enough to travel here to tell us, it must be true.
column2: 如果艾纳斯足够相信他的预言，以至于长途跋涉来告诉我们，那它一定是真的。

column1: We are not yet wealthy enough to sponsor a tribe.
column2: 我们还不够富有，无法赞助一个部落。

column1: We are wealthy enough to sponsor a tribe.
column2: 我们足够富有，可以赞助一个部落。

column1: I am not yet a skilled enough bargainer to broker the deals we would need to make.
column2: 我还不擅长谈判，无法促成我们需要达成的协议。

column1: I am confident that I can make the deals needed to create a tribe.
column2: 我有信心能达成创建部落所需的交易。

column1: I am afraid that I would make mistakes when laying down the laws governing our tribal obligations.
column2: 我担心在制定管理部落义务的法律时会犯错。

column1: Long have I studied the laws governing tribal obligations, in preparation for this day.
column2: 为迎接这一天，我已经研究部落义务的法律很久了。

column1: We’re not yet ready for the mantle of kingship.
column2: 我们还没准备好承担王权的重任。

column1: This may be what we’ve been waiting for.
column2: 这也许就是我们一直等待的。

column1: We have many enemies. It would be good to have many allies.
column2: 我们有很多敌人。有很多盟友会是好事。

column1: You heard the prophet! It is our destiny to lead!
column2: 你听到先知的话了！领导是我们的天命！

column1: Feathers? Queen? Does some poor thane get to marry a duck?
column2: 羽毛？女王？难道某个可怜的领主得娶一只鸭子吗？

column1: Uniting opposites — hmm, could that be the Uroxi making peace with the broos…no, that’s not it…
column2: 联合对立之物——嗯，会不会是乌洛希与布鲁斯讲和……不，不是这样……

column1: I don’t see any golden trees in our forests, but I won’t mention that to Einarth.
column2: 我在我们的森林里没看到任何金色树木，但我不会向艾纳斯提起这点。

column1: Peace means weddings. Weddings mean feasts. Feasts mean meat and ale. I like this Einarth fellow already!
column2: 和平意味着婚礼。婚礼意味着宴席。宴席意味着肉和麦酒。我已经喜欢上这个艾纳斯家伙了！

column1: Wit we have; bravery is another question.
column2: 智慧我们有；勇气是另一回事。

column1: Bravery we have; wit is another question.
column2: 勇气我们有；智慧是另一回事。

column1: We can be proud of what we have accomplished. But there are greater things ahead.
column2: 我们可以为我们所取得的成就感到自豪。但前方还有更伟大的事业。

column1: He speaks the truth.
column2: 他说的是实话。

column1: A tribe is strong where a clan is weak. Einarth tells us what we should already know.
column2: 一个部落强在氏族弱的地方。艾纳斯告诉我们本应已知的道理。

column1: I am not surprised that the gods have recognized our clan’s glory.
column2: 众神认可了我们氏族的荣耀，我并不惊讶。

column1: If we start a tribe, there will be rivalries, intrigue, war with other tribes, tragic bloodshed, and star-crossed love. Let’s do it!
column2: 如果我们建立部落，就会有竞争、阴谋、与其他部落的战争、悲惨的流血，以及命运多舛的爱情。就这么干吧！

column1: I don’t like the part about marrying a bird.
column2: 我不喜欢要娶一只鸟的那部分。

column1: I told you the day would come when our greatness would be recognized.
column2: 我告诉过你们，总有一天我们的伟大会被认可。

column1: A tribe? We left Heortland to escape the smothering grip of tribes!
column2: 部落？我们离开赫欧特兰就是为了逃离部落令人窒息的掌控！

column1: Marriage with the Queen of Feathers? Who?
column2: 与羽翼女王成婚？谁？

column1: This kingdom he speaks of would certainly be a new thing in Dragon Pass. And new isn’t always bad.
column2: 他说的这个王国在龙隘必定是新鲜事物。而新东西未必总是坏事。

column1: We ought to wait a few years, to be sure we’re really capable of starting a tribe.
column2: 我们应该等上几年，确保我们确实有能力建立一个部落。

column1: That poor old man. He has come so far, and looks so feeble. We must reward him.
column2: 那个可怜的老人。他走了这么远的路，看起来如此虚弱。我们必须奖励他。

column1: Once more that poor old man has come so far for us. He looks so weak. We must reward him.
column2: 那个可怜的老人再次为我们远道而来。他看起来如此虚弱。我们必须奖励他。

column1: There is no time to delay — let’s send out emissaries before Einarth even leaves.
column2: 没有时间耽搁了——我们在艾纳斯离开之前就派出使者。

column1: “I see the form of a kingdom in the mists before me. I see its beginning, a tribe grown on this tula’s lands. I see glory ahead — but there is a shadow, a dark space where I would expect to see the light of the tribe-making quest glowing brightly.”
column2: 我在面前的迷雾中看到一座王国的形态。我看到它的开端，一个在这片图拉领地上成长起来的部落。我看到前方的荣耀——但有一片阴影，一处黑暗的空间，而我本应看到建族试炼的光芒在那里明亮地闪耀。

column1: “I see the form of a great tribe in the mists before me. I see its beginning, the clan that lives on this tula’s lands. I see glory ahead — but there is a shadow, a dark space where I would expect to see the light of the tribe-making quest glowing brightly.”
column2: 我在面前的迷雾中看到一个伟大部落的形态。我看到它的开端，那个生活在这片图拉领地上的氏族。我看到前方的荣耀——但有一片阴影，一处黑暗的空间，而我本应看到建族试炼的光芒在那里明亮地闪耀。

column1: Einarth Milk-Eyes came to us with a prophecy. It seemed to mean that we should start a tribe, but first we must succeed at the tribe-making quest.
column2: 艾纳斯·奶眼带着一个预言来到我们这里。这似乎意味着我们应该建立一个部落，但首先我们必须成功完成建族试炼。

column1: Perform the “Making of the Storm Tribe” heroquest, where Orlanth and Ernalda form the first tribe.
column2: 进行“建立风暴部落”英雄任务，奥兰斯与厄娜尔达在那次任务中组成了第一个部落。

column1: To everyone’s great joy, our heroquest succeeded, and our clan readied itself for tribe-making in the near future.
column2: 令所有人无比欣喜的是，我们的英雄任务成功了，我们的氏族已准备好在不久的将来建立部落。

column1: Our heroquest succeeded, and everyone was glad to know that we would start tribe-making with a good and solid reputation.
column2: 我们的英雄任务成功了，每个人都很高兴知道我们将以良好而稳固的名声开始建族。

column1: Our heroquest succeeded, and the clan was relieved to start tribe-making with superior leaders.
column2: 我们的英雄任务成功了，氏族为能以卓越的领袖开始建族而感到宽慰。

column1: Our heroquest succeeded, and everyone looked forward to the days of tribe-making coming up soon.
column2: 我们的英雄任务成功了，每个人都期盼着即将到来的建族日子。

column1: To our shock and dismay, the heroquest failed. Everyone wondered what to do about the prophecy, and how soon we would be strong enough to attempt the heroquest again.
column2: 令我们震惊和沮丧的是，英雄任务失败了。每个人都在想该如何应对那个预言，以及我们要多久才能强大到再次尝试那个英雄任务。

column1: Wait until you are strong enough to attempt the “Making of the Storm Tribe” heroquest.
column2: 等你足够强大了再尝试“建立风暴部落”英雄任务。

column1: We decided to act on his words, but with proper preparation.
column2: 我们决定按照他的话行动，但要做好充分的准备。

column1: Wait until we have enough cows to sponsor a tribe before attempting a heroquest.
column2: 等到我们有足够的牛只来资助一个部落，再尝试英雄任务。

column1: We are wealthy enough to sponsor a tribe, if we can succeed at the heroquest.
column2: 只要我们能在英雄任务中成功，我们就足够富有来资助一个部落。

column1: There are still aspects to bargaining I would like to learn more about, before trying to deal with the trades necessary for tribe-making.
column2: 在尝试处理建族所需的交易之前，我还想多了解议价的一些方面。

column1: After we win the quest, I relish the chance to deal with all the other clans during tribe-making.
column2: 赢得任务之后，我很享受在建族过程中与所有其他氏族打交道的时机。

column1: We must build up our military strength so that we can back up a tribe-making attempt.
column2: 我们必须增强我们的军事力量，以便能够支持建族的尝试。

column1: We are strong enough to be a clan to contend with.
column2: 我们足够强大，是一个不容小觑的氏族。

column1: I could use more time and experience before becoming entangled in tribal law-speaking.
column2: 在被卷入部落法律的论说之前，我需要更多的时间和经验。

column1: We will succeed at the quest, and I will be ready to say the laws when we become a tribe.
column2: 我们会在任务中成功，当我族成为部落时，我将准备好宣说法条。

column1: Acting swiftly and decisively is one thing. Rushing into rash actions is another.
column2: 迅速果断地行动是一回事。匆忙冒进是另一回事。

column1: First we must find a devotee of Orlanth with sufficient skills to make it through the quest.
column2: 首先我们必须找到一位奥兰斯的信徒，具备足够的技能来完成这个任务。

column1: A bold prophecy calls for bold actions. We must heroquest as soon as possible.
column2: 大胆的预言需要大胆的行动。我们必须尽快进行英雄任务。

column1: We set aside magic for quests, and our trickster will strengthen our luck. We should start soon!
column2: 我们为任务预留了魔法，我们的诡术师将增强我们的运气。我们应该马上开始！

column1: Keep our trickster out of trouble until Sacred Time — when we can allot magic to quests and so succeed at this mission.
column2: 让我们的诡术师在神圣时间之前不要惹麻烦——那时我们可以为任务分配魔法，从而成功完成这一使命。

column1: Without a trickster on the ring to bolster our luck, I cannot say if our quest magic will be strong enough.
column2: 如果长老会中没有诡术师来增强我们的运气，我无法说我们的任务魔法是否足够强大。

column1: First someone must step aside and allow a trickster on the ring. Then we must allot magic for quests. Only then can we hope to succeed.
column2: 首先必须有人让位，让一位诡术师进入长老会。然后我们必须为任务分配魔法。只有这样我们才有希望成功。

column1: Send me to do this heroquest! I can set everyone to fighting, so that they will be weak, and we will be strong.
column2: 派我去做这个英雄任务！我可以让所有人都打起来，这样他们就会虚弱，而我们就会强大。

column1: A dangerous heroquest — great risks for great gains — or devastating losses — let’s start soon!
column2: 一个危险的英雄任务——巨大的风险换取巨大的收益——或者毁灭性的损失——我们尽快开始吧！

column1: I told you the day would come when those around us would see what we can do!
column2: 我告诉过你们，总有一天我们周围的人会看到我们能做什么！

column1: Heroquest? Then a tribe? Will we sink in the swamp of these entanglements?
column2: 英雄任务？然后建立部落？我们会陷入这些纠葛的沼泽中吗？

column1: Will we every really be strong enough to succeed at that heroquest?
column2: 我们真的能强大到在那个英雄任务中成功吗？

column1: We must show kindness to that poor old man, for travelling all this way just to tell us this news.
column2: 我们必须对那个可怜的老人表示善意，他不远千里来告诉我们这个消息。

column1: Don’t forget that it was Ernalda that led Orlanth to tribe-making.
column2: 别忘了，是厄娜尔达引导奥兰斯去建立部落的。

column1: We must show the other clans how our men were meant to lead them.
column2: 我们必须向其他氏族展示，我们的男人就是为领导他们而生的。

column1: This is no time to debate — let’s start the heroquest today.
column2: 现在不是争论的时候——我们今天就开始英雄任务。

column1: sceneR033
column2: sceneR033

column1: The roads connecting the clans are still plagued with bands of outlaws. At first they were attacking caravans and taking all the goods. Now they just kill traders and travelers for their own amusement.
column2: 连接各氏族的道路仍然受到亡命徒团伙的骚扰。起初他们袭击商队并抢走所有货物。现在他们只是为了取乐而杀死商人和旅人。

column1: Bandits continued to rob our trade caravans and began killing other travelers, too.
column2: 强盗继续抢劫我们的贸易商队，也开始杀死其他旅人。

column1: The roads that connect the clans have become infested with bandits. Men outlawed from various clans have banded together, and are ambushing traders. They’ve taken two shipments of goods in the last season. They’re probably attacking other clans, too.
column2: 连接各氏族的道路已经盗匪横行。各氏族中被剥夺法律保护的人聚集成伙，伏击商人。上个季节他们已劫走两批货物。他们很可能也在袭击其他氏族。

column1: Bandits robbed our trade caravans.
column2: 强盗抢劫了我们的贸易商队。

column1: Dispatch a war party to drive the bandits off.
column2: 派出战团驱逐强盗。

column1: We dispatched a war party to drive the bandits off.
column2: 我们派出了一个战团去驱逐强盗。

column1: Hearing our pounding hooves and the whicker of sword withdrawn from scabbard, the bandits fled for other parts. We saw to it that they left their loot behind them.
column2: 听到我们沉重的蹄声和拔剑出鞘的摩擦声，强盗们逃往别处。我们确保他们留下了赃物。

column1: The bandits outmaneuvered our war party. We drank the sour wine of defeat.
column2: 强盗以机动战术胜过我们的战团。我们饮下了失败的酸酒。

column1: Offer a reward to other clans for each bandit killed.
column2: 向其他氏族悬赏，每杀一名强盗给予奖赏。

column1: We offered wealth to the warriors of other clans, if they could demonstrate to us that they had slain the outlaws.
column2: 我们向其他氏族的战士提供财富，只要他们能向我们证明自己杀死了这些亡命徒。

column1: The other clans had little success in suppressing the bandits.
column2: 其他氏族在镇压强盗方面收效甚微。

column1: The weaponthanes of the other clans did not disappoint us, and safe trade was restored to the area.
column2: 其他氏族的武器领主没有让我们失望，该地区的安全贸易得以恢复。

column1: The weaponthanes of the other clans did not disappoint us when it came to suppressing the bandits, but their extortionate bargaining methods left much to be desired.
column2: 其他氏族的武器领主在镇压强盗方面没有让我们失望，但他们敲诈式的议价方法却不尽如人意。

column1: Sacrifice to Issaries for the protection of trade.
column2: 向伊萨里斯献祭以保护贸易。

column1: We sacrificed to Issaries, protector of trade.
column2: 我们向贸易的守护者伊萨里斯献祭。

column1: How much wealth do you sacrifice?
column2: 你献祭多少财富？

column1: The banditry did not cease.
column2: 强盗行为并未停止。

column1: The bandits went elsewhere, leaving us in peace.
column2: 强盗去了别处，让我们获得了安宁。

column1: Send an emissary to the bandits to buy them off.
column2: 派一名使者去贿赂强盗。

column1: We offered the bandit leader a payment if he would leave our traders be.
column2: 我们向强盗头目提供一笔酬金，条件是放过我们的商人。

column1: How much wealth do you offer for a year’s peace?
column2: 你愿为一年和平支付多少财富？

column1: The bandits liked the idea of receiving tribute, but held our trader’s face next to a flame until he agreed to increase the amount.
column2: 强盗喜欢收贡品的想法，但把我们的商人的脸凑近火焰，直到他同意增加金额。

column1: The bandits laughed at our offer. “Thank you for telling us how weak you are,” they said.
column2: 匪徒们嘲笑我们的提议。他们说：“多谢你告诉我们你们有多弱。”

column1: Send an emissary to the bandits to threaten them.
column2: 派一名使者去威胁匪徒。

column1: We sent an emissary to detail in precise terms the violence that would be done to them if they did not cease their activities.
column2: 我们派了一名使者，详细描述了若不停止活动，他们将会遭受何等暴力。

column1: The bandits were impressed by our poetic use of details, and left for parts unknown.
column2: 匪徒们被我们诗意的细节描述所打动，便离开去了未知之地。

column1: Sadly, the bandits’s mastery of the art of the threat outshone our own, and our warriors left, demoralized.
column2: 遗憾的是，匪徒们威胁的艺术胜过我们，我们的战士士气低落，离开了。

column1: We should do something about bandits. Otherwise, they’ll start stealing our sheep and cattle.
column2: 我们得对匪徒采取行动。否则他们会开始偷我们的牛羊。

column1: If the trade routes are impassable, we will suffer greatly.
column2: 如果商路不通，我们将损失惨重。

column1: Their position isn’t so strong that they’ll turn down a generous offer of tribute.
column2: 他们的地位并非稳固到会拒绝一份慷慨的贡品提议。

column1: The bandits are growing in strength. They’ll see a tribute offer as nothing more than an invitation to slit our throats.
column2: 匪徒正在壮大。他们会把贡品提议视为割我们喉咙的邀请。

column1: We must stomp on them now, before they get even \x02\x03bolder/stronger/fiercer\x02.
column2: 我们必须现在踩扁他们，趁他们还没变得更 \x02\x03大胆/强壮/凶猛\x02。

column1: They are \x02\x03tough/numerous/bad\x02 enough now that we should \x02\x03go to/engage/ask\x02 our neighbors for help.
column2: 他们现在已经 \x02\x03难缠/众多/恶劣\x02 到我们应该 \x02\x03去找/交战/请求\x02 邻族帮忙。

column1: Certainly, we can fight them. If we lose, however, more bandits will be attracted by our show of weakness.
column2: 当然，我们可以与他们战斗。但如果我们输了，更多的匪徒会被我们示弱所吸引。

column1: We can beat them.
column2: 我们可以打败他们。

column1: There are many bandits, and ambush is their specialty. They will make us fight on their terms.
column2: 匪徒人数众多，伏击是他们的专长。他们会逼我们按他们的方式战斗。

column1: As outlaws, they are not protected by Heort’s Laws. Putting a price on their heads might be unconventional, but it is not illegal.
column2: 作为法外之徒，他们不受赫尔特法令保护。悬赏他们的人头或许不合常规，但不违法。

column1: Putting a bounty on these bandits might be slower than a fight, but work better in the long run.
column2: 悬赏这些匪徒可能比直接战斗要慢，但长远来看效果更好。

column1: If we do pay tribute to the bandits, they’ll simply step up their attacks on our neighbors.
column2: 如果我们真的向匪徒进贡，他们只会加剧对我们邻邦的攻击。

column1: If we do not \x02\x03kill/drive off/get rid of\x02 these bandits, they will grow strong enough to attack our clan.
column2: 如果我们不 \x02\x03杀死/赶走/除掉\x02 这些匪徒，他们将变得足够强大来攻击我们的氏族。

column1: I will put the fear of the \x01@" clan into them!
column2: 我要让他们感受到 \x01@" 氏族的恐惧！

column1: Let me \x02\x04smash them down/crush them flat/slice them to ribbons/beat them stupid\x02!
column2: 让我 \x02\x04打倒/碾平/切碎/打傻\x02！

column1: I don’t think we’ll be able to find the bandits. I don’t think sacrificing will help much either, but it’s our best option.
column2: 我认为我们找不到那些匪徒。我也认为献祭不会有太大帮助，但这是我们最好的选择。

column1: Don’t attack them right away. At least warn them first.
column2: 不要立刻攻击他们。至少先警告他们。

column1: Sacrifice to Issaries.
column2: 向伊萨里斯献祭。

column1: Why not \x02\x04hire some of them as weaponthanes/hire them to harass our enemies/send a trade caravan out with poisoned food for them/call on Odayla to make the forest creatures harass them\x02?
column2: 何不 \x02\x04雇用其中一些作为武器领主/雇用他们骚扰我们的敌人/派出贸易商队，用有毒食物对付他们/召唤奥达拉让森林生物骚扰他们\x02？

column1: I knew we shouldn’t have outlawed all those people.
column2: 我早就知道我们不该把那些人都放逐。

column1: The silver-kingfishers dove beakwise into our sun-dusted river. Gagarth’s followers’ blade of speech is not Humakt’s sword.
column2: 翠鸟们喙朝下扎进了我们洒满阳光的河流。加加斯的追随者那言辞的刀锋不是胡玛克特的剑。

column1: Issaries is all the help we need.
column2: 伊萨里斯就是我们所需的一切帮助。

column1: Why not just burn the woods where they hide, killing bandits and elves in one step?
column2: 何不直接烧了他们躲藏的树林，把匪徒和精灵一举消灭？

column1: sceneR034
column2: sceneR034

column1: The outlaws you forgave have again shown their true colors. They attacked another of your young women, shaming her, and shaming your clan. They claim that they are still innocent of any crime, on the grounds that they were once more possessed by spirits at the time.
column2: 你宽恕的那些放逐者再次露出了真面目。他们袭击了你部族的另一名年轻女子，羞辱了她，也羞辱了你的氏族。他们声称自己仍然清白无辜，理由是当时他们又一次被恶灵附身。

column1: Two former outlaws again flouted our forgiveness by assaulting one of our young maidens. They claimed to have been possessed by spirits during the crime.
column2: 两名前放逐者再次藐视我们的宽恕，袭击了我们的一位年轻少女。他们声称犯罪时被恶灵附身。

column1: The outlaws you forgave have shown their true colors. They attacked one of your young women, shaming her, and shaming your clan. They claim that they are innocent of any crime, on the grounds that they were possessed by spirits at the time.
column2: 你宽恕的那些放逐者露出了真面目。他们袭击了你部族的一名年轻女子，羞辱了她，也羞辱了你的氏族。他们声称自己清白无辜，理由是当时被恶灵附身。

column1: Two former outlaws flouted our forgiveness by assaulting one of our young maidens. They claimed to have been possessed by spirits during the crime.
column2: 两名前放逐者藐视我们的宽恕，袭击了我们的一位年轻少女。他们声称犯罪时被恶灵附身。

column1: Declare them to have been possessed; compensate the victim.
column2: 宣布他们曾被附身；赔偿受害者。

column1: We agreed that they had been possessed, and were innocent of blame. We compensated the victim’s family.
column2: 我们同意他们曾被附身，并无过错。我们赔偿了受害者家属。

column1: Thanks to honeyed words and several ounces of silver, the victim’s family accepted the ring’s
column2: 多亏了甜言蜜语和几两白银，受害者家属接受了长老会的

column1: judgment.
column2: 判决。

column1: judgment, though other members of the clan were not so happy.
column2: 判决，尽管氏族其他成员并不那么高兴。

column1: The former outlaws became outlaws once again, shorn of Orlanth’s protection.
column2: 前放逐者再次沦为放逐者，失去了奥兰斯的庇护。

column1: Outlaw them; encourage victim’s family to take vengeance.
column2: 放逐他们；鼓励受害者家属复仇。

column1: We outlawed them, and advised the maiden’s family to seek personal vengeance against them.
column2: 我们放逐了他们，并建议少女的家人向他们寻仇。

column1: Vengeance was taken, and the stain of dishonor was lifted from the maid.
column2: 复仇已施，耻辱的污点从少女身上洗去。

column1: The outlaws evaded just vengeance, and slew \x01@\x03 members of the maid’s family.
column2: 放逐者避开了正义的复仇，并杀死了少女家的 \x01@\x03 名成员。

column1: Outlaw them; have clan’s war leader take vengeance.
column2: 放逐他们；由氏族的战争领袖复仇。

column1: They were outlawed. Once shorn of the protection of good society, they became the quarry of our war leader, \x01@\x17.
column2: 他们被放逐了。一旦失去善良社会的庇护，他们就成了我们战争领袖 \x01@\x17的猎物。

column1: Vengeance was taken, and the stain of dishonor was lifted from the clan.
column2: 复仇已施，耻辱的污点从氏族身上洗去。

column1: The outlaws evaded just vengeance.
column2: 放逐者避开了正义的复仇。

column1: Test them for signs of spirit possession.
column2: 测试他们是否有被恶灵附身的迹象。

column1: As unlikely as their story seemed, magical inquiries proved it to be true. They had been possessed. Still, many clan members were reluctant to believe the divination.
column2: 尽管他们的说法看似不可能，但魔法调查证明这是真的。他们确实被附身了。尽管如此，许多氏族成员仍不愿相信占卜的结果。

column1: As we expected, divination proved their tale of possession to be the sorriest of ruses.
column2: 正如我们所料，占卜证明他们附身的说辞是最拙劣的诡计。

column1: No one will begrudge us whatever compensation we pay to the maiden’s family.
column2: 无论我们向少女的家人支付多少补偿，都不会有人怨恨我们。

column1: They deserve outlawry. Once outlawed, anyone may kill them, without penalty. The maiden’s family will want to do so.
column2: 他们活该被放逐。一旦被放逐，任何人都可以杀死他们而不受惩罚。少女的家人也会想这么做。

column1: Every clan member’s honor is stained by this disgusting event.
column2: 每个氏族成员的荣誉都被这件恶心的事玷污了。

column1: They take us for fools if they expect us to believe in two separate spirit possessions.
column2: 如果他们认为我们会相信两次各自独立的恶灵附身，那他们把我们都当傻子了。

column1: They deserve outlawry. Once outlawed, anyone may kill them, without penalty. However, they have dishonored all of us, so the clan’s vengeance takes precedence.
column2: 他们活该被放逐。一旦被放逐，任何人都可以杀死他们而不受惩罚。然而，他们羞辱了我们所有人，所以氏族的复仇优先。

column1: We failed once before when we failed to outlaw them. We must do so now, and make sure they are killed this time.
column2: 我们之前失败过一次，没能放逐他们。我们现在必须这么做，并确保这次他们被杀死。

column1: We can test the truth of their tale.
column2: 我们可以检验他们故事的真假。

column1: We could try to test the truth of their tale, if we care.
column2: 我们可以试着检验他们故事的真假，如果我们愿意的话。

column1: The value of a divination depends on the skill of the diviner.
column2: 占卜的价值取决于占卜者的技艺。

column1: Our magic is weak. We cannot trust that we will be able to hear the gods correctly.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱。我们不能相信我们能正确听到神明的旨意。

column1: Our magic is weak. But I think we know what the answer would be anyway.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱。但我觉得反正我们也知道答案会是什么。

column1: Our magic is strong. Outlawing is harsh, a divination will tell us if it is the right thing to do.
column2: 我们的魔法强大。放逐是严厉的，占卜会告诉我们这样做是否正确。

column1: Why waste good magic on a divination, when we know very well what we need to do.
column2: 我们很清楚需要做什么，何必把好魔法浪费在占卜上。

column1: They are experienced warriors, and she comes from a family of carls. I will kill them.
column2: 他们是经验丰富的战士，而她出身自由民家庭。我会杀了他们。

column1: I kept my eye on those two, but blinked for minute. Let me restore my honor by killing them.
column2: 我一直盯着那两个，但眨眼了一分钟。让我杀了他们恢复荣誉。

column1: I will kill them. Slowly. Painfully.
column2: 我会杀了他们。慢慢地。痛苦地。

column1: We can’t completely dismiss the possibility that they were possessed, no matter how feeble their excuse seems.
column2: 我们不能完全排除他们被附身的可能性，无论他们的借口多么站不住脚。

column1: They must suffer before they die.
column2: 他们死前必须受苦。

column1: If they have been possessed, perhaps it means that the cursed sword Chaos Striker is buried somewhere on our tula.
column2: 如果他们曾被附身，也许意味着那把被诅咒的剑“混沌打击者”埋在我们领地的某处。

column1: Well…we never did find the Chaos Striker sword. Maybe they are just lying.
column2: 嗯……我们从未找到过混沌打击者剑。也许他们只是在撒谎。

column1: Right now, the feelings of the family are more important than our own.
column2: 此刻，家人的感受比我们自己的更重要。

column1: What happens if we outlaw them, and the spirits possess other of our menfolk?
column2: 如果我们放逐了他们，而恶灵又附身了我们其他族人，会怎样？

column1: They are dead already. The rest is detail.
column2: 他们已经是死人了。其余的都是细节。

column1: Priests from a number of nearby clans lodge a legal claim against you.
column2: 邻近数个氏族的祭司对你们提起了法律诉讼。

column1: “You have been sacrificing to Enemy Gods. You have angered the proper gods. Heler will not bring rain. Orlanth will not fight Valind. Until you are taught the error of your perfidious ways, all will suffer.”
column2: “你们一直在向敌对神祇献祭。你们激怒了正统神祇。赫勒不会再带来雨水。奥兰斯不会再与瓦林德作战。在你们被教导背信弃义之道的错误之前，所有人都将受苦。”

column1: “You have injured us greatly. You sacrificed to the trickster to avoid a curse, and he merely moved the curse to us, who did not deserve it. We demand that you renounce your perfidious ways.”
column2: “你们极大地伤害了我们。你们向恶作剧者献祭以规避诅咒，而他只是把诅咒转移到了我们身上，我们本不该承受。我们要求你们放弃背信弃义之道。”

column1: “You sacrificed to an Enemy God and angered the proper gods. You sacrificed to the trickster to avoid a curse, and he merely moved the curse to us, who did not deserve it. We demand that you renounce your perfidious ways.”
column2: “你向一位敌对神祇献祭，惹怒了正统神祇。你向恶作剧者献祭以避免诅咒，但他只是把诅咒转移到了我们这些无辜者身上。我们要求你放弃你背信弃义的行径。”

column1: “You have been sacrificing to Enemy Gods. You have angered the proper gods. You sacrificed to the trickster to avoid a curse, and he merely moved the curse to us, who did not deserve it. We demand that you renounce your perfidious ways.”
column2: “你一直在向敌对神祇献祭。你惹怒了正统神祇。你向恶作剧者献祭以避免诅咒，但他只是把诅咒转移到了我们这些无辜者身上。我们要求你放弃你背信弃义的行径。”

column1: Angry priests from other clans lodged a legal claim against us, claiming that our sacrifices were dangerous, and were harming them.
column2: 其他氏族的愤怒祭司对我们提起了法律诉讼，声称我们的献祭是危险的，并且对他们造成了伤害。

column1: Compensate your neighbors for the harm done to them.
column2: 赔偿你的邻居对他们造成的伤害。

column1: We agreed to compensate our neighbors for the harm done to them.
column2: 我们同意赔偿邻居对他们造成的伤害。

column1: How much wealth do you offer?
column2: 你出价多少财富？

column1: They departed, apparently satisfied.
column2: 他们离开了，显然很满意。

column1: They demanded more than we had offered.
column2: 他们要求的比我们提供的多。

column1: They demand twice as much as you have offered. Do you meet their demand?
column2: 他们要求你提供两倍的数额。你满足他们的要求吗？

column1: We paid them what they asked.
column2: 我们按他们的要求支付了。

column1: We refused them, and they left, muttering threats.
column2: 我们拒绝了他们，他们离开时嘟囔着威胁。

column1: Give them wealth to sacrifice to the proper gods.
column2: 给他们财富，让他们向正统神祇献祭。

column1: We gave them wealth to sacrifice as they wished.
column2: 我们给了他们财富，让他们随心献祭。

column1: How much total wealth do you offer?
column2: 你总共提供多少财富？

column1: They pronounced themselves satisfied with our offer, and said that the gods would be satisfied as well.
column2: 他们声称对我们的提议感到满意，并说神祇也会满意。

column1: They argued that they needed more to counter our unwise sacrifices, and our priests agreed to give it to them.
column2: 他们争辩说需要更多来抵消我们不智的献祭，我们的祭司同意给他们。

column1: Hold a feast for the priests.
column2: 为祭司们举办一场盛宴。

column1: We held a feast for the priests.
column2: 我们为祭司们举办了一场盛宴。

column1: They ate our food and drank our beer. Then they asked us what we would do to remedy their claim.
column2: 他们吃了我们的食物，喝了我们的啤酒。然后问我们打算如何补救他们的诉讼。

column1: Promise not to do it again.
column2: 承诺不再这样做。

column1: We told them we would discontinue the practices they abhorred.
column2: 我们告诉他们，我们将停止他们憎恶的做法。

column1: They pronounced themselves satisfied with our promise, but warned us not to err in this way again.
column2: 他们声称对我们的承诺感到满意，但警告我们不要再犯这样的错误。

column1: They told us that our promises were as empty as our heads, and refused to budge.
column2: 他们告诉我们，我们的承诺和我们的脑袋一样空洞，毫不让步。

column1: Refuse their claim.
column2: 拒绝他们的诉讼。

column1: We refused their claim.
column2: 我们拒绝了他们的诉讼。

column1: They said that they would tell all of Dragon Pass of our perfidy.
column2: 他们说，他们将把我们的背信弃义告诉整个龙隘。

column1: Let the tribal moot pass judgment.
column2: 让部落大会做出裁决。

column1: We told them we would be happy to argue the case at the next tribal moot.
column2: 我们告诉他们，我们很乐意在下次部落大会上辩论此案。

column1: The moot ruled in our favor, and held us blameless for our sacrificial practices.
column2: 议会裁定我们胜诉，认为我们的献祭做法无可指责。

column1: The moot ruled in the priests’ favor, and fined us.
column2: 议会裁定祭司们胜诉，并处罚了我们。

column1: I can probably convince them to take compensation for the harm done to them.
column2: 我或许能说服他们接受对他们所受伤害的赔偿。

column1: I can talk them into taking compensation, especially payment in the form of a sacrifice.
column2: 我可以说服他们接受赔偿，尤其是以献祭形式的支付。

column1: Given the harm we’ve done them, it will be hard to reach an amount of compensation we can accept.
column2: 考虑到我们对他们造成的伤害，很难达成我们能够接受的赔偿数额。

column1: I foresee endless negotiating if we just offer to compensate them directly.
column2: 如果我们只是直接提出赔偿，我预料会无休止的谈判。

column1: Precedents establish the amount of compensation owed in cases like this. I can get them to agree to a modest payment.
column2: 类似案例的赔偿金额由先例确定。我能让他们同意一笔适度的付款。

column1: Precedents establish the amount of compensation owed in cases like this. But they are angry, and may demand more than is their due.
column2: 类似案例的赔偿金额由先例确定。但他们很愤怒，可能会要求比应得更多。

column1: Precedents establish the amount of compensation owed in these cases. But our offenses are great, and they may demand more.
column2: 这些案例的赔偿金额由先例确定。但我们的过错很严重，他们可能会要求更多。

column1: To truly make up for the grievous harm we’ve done them, in a way that they will accept, we should go to the gods.
column2: 为了真正弥补我们对他们造成的严重伤害，以一种他们会接受的方式，我们应该求助于神祇。

column1: This can be resolved with noble words and a few well-placed pats on the back.
column2: 这可以用高贵的言辞和几记恰到好处的拍背来解决。

column1: A small amount of compensation will assuage their angry feelings.
column2: 少量赔偿就能平息他们的愤怒情绪。

column1: They have a serious grievance against us. It will be hard for me to simply talk them out of it.
column2: 他们对我们有严重的不满。我很难单靠劝说让他们放弃。

column1: There is no conflict between neighbors which cannot be resolved with a good feast.
column2: 邻里之间没有一场好盛宴解决不了的冲突。

column1: We must repent of our actions. Next thing you know, we’ll be sacrificing to Malia.
column2: 我们必须悔改我们的行为。你接着就知道，我们就要向玛利亚献祭了。

column1: It’s my fault that we sacrificed unwisely. I am dishonored.
column2: 我们献祭不智是我的错。我蒙受了耻辱。

column1: Give them 30 cows in compensation.
column2: 赔偿他们30头牛。

column1: We must all make a better effort to teach our children the secrets of the written word.
column2: 我们都必须更加努力地教导孩子书写文字的奥秘。

column1: Let us take this to the moot. Ah, to hear the verbal sallies of clashing lawspeakers!
column2: 让我们把这个提交给议会。啊，听听律法师们交锋时的唇枪舌剑！

column1: Apparitions have been seen rising out of the marsh.
column2: 有人看到鬼魂从沼泽升起。

column1: They’ll never help us build a temple now.
column2: 他们现在绝不会帮我们建造神庙了。

column1: Your call for wolf skins has been very successful. Perhaps too much so. You’re now drowning in the things. You have wolf blankets, wolf collars, wolf hide helmets, fur-covered ale flagons… and still, you have too many to use.
column2: 你对狼皮的征集非常成功。也许过于成功了。你现在被这些东西淹没了。你有狼皮毯子、狼皮项圈、狼皮头盔、毛皮覆盖的麦酒壶……而且你仍然有太多用不完。

column1: Many people came to sell us wolf skins. Too many, some said.
column2: 许多人来卖给我们狼皮。有些人说，太多了。

column1: Announce that you will buy no more wolf skins.
column2: 宣布你不再收购狼皮。

column1: We ended our offer to buy wolf skins
column2: 我们终止了收购狼皮的提议。

column1: Our neighbors grumbled loudly about losing the bounty.
column2: 我们的邻居大声抱怨失去了这笔赏金。

column1: Only buy half as many wolf-skins from now on.
column2: 从现在起只买一半数量的狼皮。

column1: We set a limit on how many we would buy from that day onwards. The limit was half of what we had been buying before.
column2: 我们设定了从那以后每日购买数量的上限。上限是我们之前购买量的一半。

column1: Our neighbors grumbled, but our own traders were no longer as worried about being broken by the bounty.
column2: 我们的邻居抱怨不已，但我们自己的商人不再担心被这笔赏金压垮了。

column1: Only buy a few wolf-skins from now on.
column2: 从现在起只买少量狼皮。

column1: We bought a few wolf skins from then on, but nothing near the amount we had been buying.
column2: 我们从那以后就只买少量狼皮，远不及我们之前购买的数量。

column1: Our neighbors grumbled about losing the bounty.
column2: 我们的邻居抱怨失去了赏金。

column1: We sent \x01@\x1A on a journey to sell excess wolf skins.
column2: 我们派 \x01@\x1A 去旅行销售多余的狼皮。

column1: \x01@\x1A took a small escort, and said that \x06 would try \x04 luck in the Holy Country, since it was obvious that nobody in Dragon Pass would buy wolf skins.
column2: \x01@\x1A 带了一小队护卫，并说 \x06 会去圣国试试 \x04 运气，因为显然龙隘没人会买狼皮。

column1: Spread the word that your efforts protect your neighbors from Telmori raiders.
column2: 传扬出去，你的努力保护了你的邻居免受泰尔莫里掠夺者的侵害。

column1: We made sure other clans knew that our efforts benefited them, also.
column2: 我们确保其他氏族也知道我们的努力同样令他们受益。

column1: Our neighbors said they were indebted to us for the timely warning.
column2: 我们的邻居说他们因这及时的警告而感激我们。

column1: Our neighbors gave little credence to our warnings.
column2: 我们的邻居对我们的警告不太相信。

column1: This wolf skin plan is \x02\x03draining/depleting/weakening\x02 our treasury.
column2: 这个狼皮计划正在 \x02\x03消耗/耗竭/削弱\x02 我们的国库。

column1: Although it is \x02\x03dangerous/probably pointless/possibly foolish\x02, I am willing to \x02\x03traipse around Dragon Pass/cover the land from high to low/go on a long trip\x02 and find buyers for our useless, extra skins.
column2: 尽管这 \x02\x03危险/可能无意义/或许愚蠢\x02，我愿意 \x02\x03在龙隘四处奔波/从高到低走遍这片土地/踏上长途旅程\x02 ，为我们那些无用多余的毛皮找到买主。

column1: I don’t think this is having any effect. Our patrols still report as many Telmori sightings as ever.
column2: 我不认为这有任何效果。我们的巡逻队报告的泰尔莫里目击数量仍跟往常一样。

column1: Our warriors are \x02\x03happy/pleased/content\x02 that we fight the wolfmen with \x02\x03traps instead of swords/hunters not weaponthanes/silver instead of their lives\x02. They’ll be upset if we stop now.
column2: 我们的战士们 \x02\x03高兴/满意/满足\x02 我们用 \x02\x03陷阱而非刀剑/猎人而非武器领主/白银而非他们的生命\x02来对付狼人。如果我们现在停下，他们会不高兴的。

column1: We have created an expectation of reward for the hunters of other tribes. They will resent us if we cut them off completely.
column2: 我们已经在其他部落的猎人中制造了对回报的期望。如果我们完全切断，他们会怨恨我们。

column1: By reducing the number of wolf men, we’re helping other tribes, too.
column2: 通过减少狼人的数量，我们也在帮助其他部落。

column1: I can make the other chieftains realize that they owe us for our campaign against the Telmori.
column2: 我能让其他酋长认识到他们因我们对泰尔莫里的征讨而欠我们人情。

column1: Even if this campaign against our ancient enemies is only symbolic, we do benefit magically.
column2: 即便这场针对我们宿敌的征讨只是象征性的，我们确实在魔法上受益。

column1: Einara Buttered-Bread fed the Six Red-Tailed Telmori until their stomachs burst. Then she cooked them for her clan.
column2: 黄油面包艾娜拉喂饱了六只红尾泰尔莫里，直到它们撑破肚皮。然后她把它们烹煮了给她的氏族吃。

column1: Odayla caught a wolf alive with his bare hands and took it home with him. When the sun rose in the morning, a young girl crept out of his cave and disappeared into the woods.
column2: 奥达拉徒手活捉了一只狼，带回了家。当清晨太阳升起时，一个年轻女孩从他的洞穴里爬出来，消失在树林中。

column1: Bad King Urgrain trapped wolves at night, and in the morning took the Telmori as thralls.
column2: 恶王乌格兰夜间设陷阱捕狼，清晨便将泰尔莫里人掳为奴隶。

column1: To a \x02\x02crisp/turn\x02 the beast-warmers did \x02\x03cook/bake/roast\x02 us; for what feast were we fattened?
column2: 在 \x02\x02酥脆/翻转\x02 的火上，兽皮取暖者们确实 \x02\x03烹煮/烘烤/炙烤\x02 了我们；我们被养肥，是为了哪场盛宴？

column1: We can’t stop now. The Telmori will out-breed us, then eat us.
column2: 我们现在不能停。泰尔莫里人会比我们繁殖得更快，然后吃掉我们。

column1: We must keep buying up wolf skins until no Telmori are left. The thought of their long teeth is keeping us awake at night.
column2: 我们必须继续收购狼皮，直到泰尔莫里人一个不剩。一想到他们那长长的獠牙，我们就夜不能寐。

column1: Someone’s bad thoughts have been \x02\x03souring the milk/making the fruit mushy/spoiling the bread\x02, but all you think about are wolves, wolves, wolves.
column2: 某人的恶念一直在 \x02\x03让牛奶变酸/让果实软烂/让面包腐坏\x02，可你满脑子想的都是狼、狼、狼。

column1: We have already \x02\x03festooned the walls/covered the altars/blanketed the floors\x02 of our temples with wolf fur. What more use can we gain from them?
column2: 我们已经用狼毛 \x02\x03装饰了墙壁/覆盖了祭坛/铺满了地板\x02 我们的神庙。我们还能从它们身上得到什么用处？

column1: Surely if we stop now, the Telmori will be motivated to peace.
column2: 如果我们现在停下来，泰尔莫里人肯定会萌生和平之意。

column1: \x01@\x1A came back, with great wealth for the clan.
column2: \x01@\x1A 回来了，为氏族带来了巨大财富。

column1: I have returned with great wealth for the clan, in exchange for our otherwise useless wolf pelts.
column2: 我带着为氏族换取的巨大财富回来了，换回了我们那些原本无用的狼皮。

column1: As I suspected, they were a rarity in the Holy Country.
column2: 正如我所料，它们在圣国颇为罕见。

column1: beg you, do not to submit to them again. We will be greatly aggravated if all our hard labor goes to decorate the hall of the \x01@! clan.”
column2: 恳求您，不要再向他们屈服。若我们所有的辛劳都只用来装饰 \x01@! 氏族的大厅，我们将大为恼火。”

column1: beseech you not to give in to them this time. We have toiled hard this year, and will be greatly vexed if our efforts only go to fill the bellies of the \x01@! clan.”
column2: 恳请您这次不要向他们让步。今年我们辛苦劳作，若我们的努力仅仅用来填饱 \x01@! 氏族的肚子，我们将十分愤懑。”

column1: entreat you to do whatever it takes to put an end to this. Why should we struggle all year just to watch the \x01@! clan walk away with what is ours by right?”
column2: 恳求您不惜一切代价终结此事。为何我们要辛苦一整年，却眼睁睁看着 \x01@! 氏族理直气壮地拿走属于我们的东西？”

column1: The carls asked if we would again pay tribute to the \x01@! clan.
column2: 自由民们问我们是否要再次向 \x01@! 氏族进贡。

column1: Do you make this payment?
column2: 你是否支付这笔贡品？

column1: Convince the carls that tribute is the only option.
column2: 说服自由民，进贡是唯一选择。

column1: We explained to the carls that tribute was the only option.
column2: 我们向自由民解释，进贡是唯一选择。

column1: They were far from convinced.
column2: 他们远未被说服。

column1: The carls could think of no other option.
column2: 自由民想不出其他办法。

column1: We launched a surprise attack against the \x01@! clan.
column2: 我们对 \x01@! 氏族发动了突袭。

column1: We scattered them like dust motes in the wind, and the question of tribute was dispersed on that same wind.
column2: 我们把他们像风中的尘埃一样驱散，进贡的问题也随那阵风消散了。

column1: We were beaten. Not long afterwards, we paid them tribute, with an additional penalty.
column2: 我们被打败了。不久之后，我们向他们支付了贡品，并附加了罚金。

column1: The only token Humakt accepts is blood.
column2: 胡马科特唯一接受的祭品是鲜血。

column1: We \x02\x03might be able to beat/could try to attack/have a chance against\x02 them, but with allies, our chance of winning would be greater and our risk lower.
column2: 我们 \x02\x03或许能击败/可以尝试攻击/有机会对抗\x02 它们，但有盟友相助，获胜的机会会更大，风险也更低。

column1: It will be harder to get the carls to accept the payment of tribute than to convince another clan to help us.
column2: 要让自由民接受纳贡，比说服另一个氏族来帮助我们更难。

column1: The carls will not like paying tribute, but they will like raiding during planting season even less.
column2: 自由民不会喜欢纳贡，但他们更不喜欢在播种季节袭击劫掠。

column1: The carls will not like paying tribute, but they will like raiding during harvest season even less.
column2: 自由民不会喜欢缴纳贡品，但他们更不喜欢在收获季节进行劫掠。

column1: Chinkis Mor, the elf warlord, demanded tribute from King Vingkot when Vingkot was weak. Vingkot became strong, and attacked the elves.
column2: 精灵军阀金基斯·莫尔在文戈特王弱小之时向他索要贡品。文戈特王强大之后，便攻击了精灵。

column1: Bad King Urgrain was once forced to pay tribute. He failed to fight back when his clan was strong, and so they became weak.
column2: 恶王乌格兰曾被迫缴纳贡品。他在自己氏族强大时未能反击，因此他们变得衰弱。

column1: The Surprising Tribe tried demanding tribute from Tragic King Errarth, seeking to drain his clan of its power before annihilating them.
column2: 惊奇部落曾试图向悲剧王埃拉思索要贡品，企图在歼灭他们之前耗尽氏族的实力。

column1: Ernalda wants us to find another way. \x02\x03But what that way is, remains a mystery/The priestesses strain their ears, listening for what that way might be/This I know, but I do not know what way she means\x02.
column2: 厄娜达希望我们另寻他法。 \x02\x03但那方法是什么，仍然是个谜/女祭司们侧耳倾听，想要聆听那方法为何/此事我知晓，但我不知她所指何意\x02。

column1: Kringle-klank did the peace-circles sing, as they clan-danced in their cow-holders.
column2: 克林格克兰克唱起了和平之环，他们在牛栏中跳起了氏族之舞。

column1: Grabby-Guts the Giant hand stole the sweat-bought grain-sacks.
column2: 夺肠巨人之手偷走了汗水换来的粮袋。

column1: Hungrier, smaller, weaker, poorer, gone.
column2: 更饥饿、更渺小、更虚弱、更贫穷、已消亡。

column1: \x02\x03This clan, these greedy/What we really need/The last time this happened, it just\x02 — what I mean to say is that \x02\x03they mean so much/to keep our heads up/hard work is not\x02 — you can’t blame them for it.
column2: \x02\x03这个氏族，这些贪婪的/我们真正需要的是/上次发生这事时，它只是\x02 ——我的意思是说 \x02\x03他们意义重大/让我们抬起头/辛勤劳作并不\x02 ——你无法责怪他们。

column1: Our children must be able to read, even though this part of our saga will be shameful.
column2: 我们的孩子必须能够阅读，即使我们传说中这部分的记载将蒙羞。

column1: If we had more scrolls, one might suggest a clever answer to this problem.
column2: 如果我们有更多卷轴，或许能有人提出一个巧妙的解决方案。

column1: We should sacrifice to Lhankor Mhy, to gain the wisdom to end this degrading tribute.
column2: 我们应当向兰科·莫尔献祭，以获得智慧来终结这屈辱的贡品。

column1: If we must go down, let us go down fighting!
column2: 如果我们注定要倒下，那就让我们战斗着倒下！

column1: Elves have been seen massing their forces north of Clearwine.
column2: 有报告称精灵在清酒镇以北集结兵力。

column1: If we don’t \x02\x03stop this nonsense/end this tribute/keep our goods and grain\x02, how will we ever get strong enough to defeat the elves?
column2: 如果我们不 \x02\x03制止这种胡闹/结束纳贡/保住我们的货物和谷物\x02，我们怎么可能变得足够强大来击败精灵？

column1: The grinning extortionists of the \x01@! clan are back. Last year, you gave them what you said was a one-time payment. “That’s what you think,” \x01B] chortles. Again they seek forty cows and eighty sheep.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的咧嘴狂笑的敲诈者又回来了。去年，你给了他们一笔你说是仅此一次的钱。“你以为是那样，” \x01B] 咯咯笑道。他们再次索要四十头牛和八十只羊。

column1: Nobles of the \x01@! clan came back and demanded tribute from us again.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的贵族回来了，再次向我们索要贡品。

column1: They agreed to help against the disreputable \x01@! clan.
column2: 他们同意帮忙对抗声名狼藉的 \x01@! 氏族。

column1: We scattered them like dust motes in the wind. The question of tribute was dispersed on that same wind.
column2: 我们将他们驱散如风中的微尘。贡品的问题也随着那阵风消散了。

column1: Offer them half as much, but acknowledge the payment as ongoing tribute, due after every harvest time.
column2: 给他们出一半的数目，但承认这是持续缴纳的贡品，每次收获季后应缴。

column1: They agreed to our proposal, and took the first payment immediately.
column2: 他们同意了我们的提议，并立即收取了第一笔款项。

column1: They agreed to our proposal but demanded some tribute now. They said they’d be back for the regular payment come Dark season.
column2: 他们同意了我们的提议，但要求现在缴纳部分贡品。他们说会在黑暗季回来收取常规款项。

column1: Pay them, “but this is absolutely the last time.”
column2: 付给他们，“但这绝对是最后一次。”

column1: We agreed to pay, but told them that they were receiving the last of our wealth.
column2: 我们同意支付，但告诉他们，他们正在接收我们最后的财富。

column1: We refused to pay them.
column2: 我们拒绝向他们支付。

column1: Not long after, they hit us in a surprise raid.
column2: 不久之后，他们发动了一次突袭。

column1: They did great damage to us, and again demanded tribute.
column2: 他们给我们造成了巨大损失，并再次索要贡品。

column1: What are we worrying about? It’s not like the tribute they’re asking is high.
column2: 我们在担心什么？他们要的贡品又不算高。

column1: The animals are sick. If we give them to \x01B], perhaps he will be poisoned and die.
column2: 牲口病了。如果我们把它们给 \x01B]，或许他会中毒而死。

column1: We have a chance against them, but with allies, our chance would be greater and our risk lower.
column2: 我们有机会对抗他们，但若有盟友，我们的机会会更大，风险更低。

column1: We need an ally to even dream of victory against the \x01@! clan.
column2: 我们甚至需要有一位盟友，才能梦想击败 \x01@! 氏族。

column1: Every time we pay tribute after saying we will not, the people become more dispirited.
column2: 每次我们说不会缴纳贡品却又交了之后，人民就更加沮丧。

column1: They are too rude to reason with.
column2: 他们粗鲁得无法与之讲道理。

column1: I’d sooner die than continue to pay them.
column2: 我宁愿死也不愿继续向他们纳贡。

column1: They have beaten us many times. We’d be fools to anger them again.
column2: 他们打败过我们多次。再去激怒他们就是傻瓜。

column1: They are puffed-up peacocks in need of a — a — kick in the groin. Let me spit on them, I beg of you!
column2: 他们就是一群趾高气扬的孔雀，需要——呃——往裆部踹一脚。让我朝他们吐口水吧，求您了！

column1: If we refuse to — that is, not in so many words, but if we indicate — we have to word it very carefully, but I think we can … Yes, definitely.
column2: 如果我们拒绝——也就是说，并非直接拒绝，而是暗示——我们必须措辞非常谨慎，但我觉得我们可以……是的，肯定行。

column1: Gifts paid unwillingly are not a sign of generosity.
column2: 不情愿地送出的礼物不是慷慨的象征。

column1: Ukkar Gra, King of the Basmoli, demanded tribute from King Vingkot when Vingkot was weak. Vingkot paid him, reserving his strength for other foes.
column2: 巴斯莫利之王乌卡尔·格拉，在文戈特王衰弱之时向他索要贡品。文戈特王给了他，保存实力以对付其他敌人。

column1: \x01@I has come back from an expedition into the Quivin Mountains. \x05 says \x06’s found the cave lair of a wyrm. Wyrms are dragon-like creatures the size of a small stead. \x01@I thinks this one is sitting on a mound of treasure.
column2: \x01@I 从一次进入奎文山脉的远征中回来了。 \x05 说 \x06发现了一条亚龙的洞穴巢穴。亚龙是类似龙的生物，大小相当于一个小型农庄。\x01@I认为这条亚龙正蹲在一堆财宝上。

column1: \x01@I came back from the mountains and told us that \x06 had found the lair of a wyrm.
column2: \x01@I  \x06 从山上回来告诉我们，他找到了亚龙的巢穴。

column1: Forbid anyone to disturb the wyrm.
column2: 禁止任何人打扰那条亚龙。

column1: We forbade anyone to disturb the wyrm.
column2: 我们禁止任何人打扰那条亚龙。

column1: Nobody was rash enough to disturb it.
column2: 没有人鲁莽到去打扰它。

column1: Send a party to give a gift of food to the wyrm.
column2: 派一队人给那条亚龙送去食物作为礼物。

column1: How many cattle do you feed him?
column2: 你喂他多少头牛？

column1: It greedily accepted our gift, and said that our generosity would be remembered.
column2: 它贪婪地接受了我们的礼物，并说我们的慷慨会被铭记。

column1: Send a party back to kill the wyrm and take the treasure.
column2: 派一支队伍回去杀死亚龙，夺取宝物。

column1: We sent a party to kill the wyrm and take the treasure.
column2: 我们派了一支队伍去杀死亚龙，夺取宝物。

column1: Who leads this mission?
column2: 谁领导这次任务？

column1: How many warriors do you send?
column2: 你派遣多少名战士？

column1: None of our warriors escaped unscathed. Some were killed; the rest, wounded.
column2: 我们的战士无一完好无损。有人阵亡；其余的都负了伤。

column1: Our heroic warriors slew the wyrm, though some were slain, and others were wounded. We gained a great pile of treasure, and celebrated our newfound wealth.
column2: 我们的英雄级战士杀死了亚龙，尽管也有战死和负伤。我们获得了一大堆宝物，庆祝我们新得的财富。

column1: The wyrm killed all but two of the party, including \x01@\x05.
column2: 亚龙杀死了队伍中除两人外的所有人，其中包括 \x01@\x05。

column1: Send \x01@t to take the treasure without killing the wyrm.
column2: 派 \x01@t 在不杀死亚龙的情况下夺取宝物。

column1: We sent \x01@t to take the treasure without killing the wyrm.
column2: 我们派 \x01@t 在不杀死亚龙的情况下夺取了宝物。

column1: \x01@t found the wyrm to be quite intelligent, although not quite intelligent enough. \x01@t taught it how to gamble, and beat it handily at dice.
column2: \x01@t 发现亚龙相当聪明，但还不够聪明。 \x01@t 教它如何赌博，并在掷骰子中轻松赢了它。

column1: \x01@t found the wyrm to be quite intelligent. So intelligent that, when \x01@t taught it how to gamble, it won handily, adding our clan’s wealth to its pile.
column2: \x01@t 发现亚龙相当聪明。聪明到当 \x01@t 教它赌博时，它轻松获胜，把我们氏族的财富添到了它的财堆里。

column1: Further, the wyrm warned us that we smelled like people who had angered dragonewts, and that we should mend our ways, or face annihilation.
column2: 此外，亚龙警告我们，我们闻起来像是得罪过龙人的家伙，并说我们应该改过自新，否则将面临毁灭。

column1: Trade \x01@I’s map to the lair to another clan.
column2: 将 \x01@I的巢穴地图交易给另一个氏族。

column1: We decided to trade away \x01@I’s map to the lair.
column2: 我们决定交易掉 \x01@I的巢穴地图。

column1: We sold the map for a goodly sum.
column2: 我们以可观的价格卖掉了地图。

column1: Later we heard that the warriors who bought the map were never seen again.
column2: 后来我们听说，买走地图的战士们再也没有出现过。

column1: Later we heard that the warriors who bought the map killed the wyrm, and greatly enriched their clan.
column2: 后来我们听说，买走地图的战士们杀死了亚龙，并大大充实了他们的氏族。

column1: Nobody seemed interested in the map.
column2: 似乎没有人对地图感兴趣。

column1: However, nobody seemed interested.
column2: 然而，似乎没有人感兴趣。

column1: Wyrms are nothing but savage and mindless beasts.
column2: 亚龙不过是野蛮无智的野兽。

column1: I’ve never seen a wyrm, but I understand that some of them are fairly intelligent.
column2: 我从未见过亚龙，但我了解到有些亚龙相当有智慧。

column1: We risk nothing by trying to sell the map.
column2: 我们尝试出售地图没有任何风险。

column1: I can get a good price for the map.
column2: 我能为地图卖个好价钱。

column1: Wyrms are the weakest of dragonkind. They are easy to kill.
column2: 亚龙是龙类中最弱小的。它们很容易杀死。

column1: Wyrms are tough opponents. Killing one requires great experience, bravery, and magic.
column2: 亚龙是难缠的对手。杀死一只需要丰富的经验、勇气和魔法。

column1: If you want anyone to come back alive, send at least seven weaponthanes along with a strong, crafty leader.
column2: 若想让任何人活着回来，至少派七名武器领主，再配上一名强大而狡诈的领袖。

column1: Our clan has always been a friend to dragonkind. Staying true to our heritage will enhance our magic.
column2: 我们氏族向来是龙类的朋友。坚守传承将增强我们的魔法。

column1: Our clan has always been a foe to dragonkind. Staying true to our heritage will enhance our magic.
column2: 我们氏族向来是龙类的敌人。坚守传承将增强我们的魔法。

column1: Our ancestors were neither friend nor foe to dragonkind. Staying true to our heritage will enhance our magic.
column2: 我们的祖先既非龙类的朋友也非敌人。坚守传承将增强我们的魔法。

column1: We will have to work hard to make up the loss if we send our farmers off on this wild wyrm-chase when the fields need attention.
column2: 如果我们在田地需要照看时派农夫去追猎亚龙，我们将不得不努力弥补损失。

column1: Wyrms follow the religion of the dragonewts. They hope to one day be reborn as dragons.
column2: 亚龙信奉龙人的宗教。它们希望有朝一日能转生为龙。

column1: I can get some of the wyrm’s treasure, and make a friend of him to boot. Don’t laugh!
column2: 我能弄到一部分亚龙的宝物，还能跟它交上朋友。别笑！

column1: Wyrms aren’t Chaotic, so we aren’t obligated to kill them. Of course, we’re not obligated to keep them alive, either…
column2: 亚龙并非混乱生物，所以我们没有义务杀死它们。当然，我们也没有义务让它们活着……

column1: We must leave it alone. We have no reason to kill the members of dragonkind, and much reason to avoid doing so.
column2: 我们必须不去招惹它。我们没有理由杀死龙类成员，而且有很多理由避免这样做。

column1: How grand our clan totem would look outfitted in wyrm’s horns!
column2: 我们的氏族图腾要是装上亚龙的角该多么气派！

column1: Little Aramarth learned to read the word “alynx” today.
column2: 小阿拉马斯今天学会了认读“alynx”这个词。

column1: Orlanth is a famed dragonslayer. We must emulate his ways.
column2: 奥兰斯是著名的屠龙者。我们必须效仿他的做法。

column1: Of course we must try to get its goods! It may have a great magical treasure for us!
column2: 当然我们必须设法得到它的财物！它可能为我们藏着一件强大的魔法宝物！

column1: All you men want to do is go into caves and kill things.
column2: 你们这些男人想做的就是钻进洞穴杀东西。
