column1: \x01@\x03 has been bitten by a poisonous snake. Efforts at healing have failed; \x04 limbs swell alarmingly.
column2: \x01@\x03 被毒蛇咬伤。治疗努力失败； \x04 的肢体肿胀得可怕。

column1: \x01@\x03 died from a snakebite, but not before composing an epic poem.
column2: \x01@\x03 死于蛇咬，但在死前创作了一首史诗。

column1: The clan ring gathers around \x01@\x03, who has been struck down again by an old injury. The healers say that the wound never fully healed, and that this time it will take \x04 life.
column2: 氏族议会聚集在 \x01@\x03周围，他再次被旧伤击倒。治疗者说伤口从未完全愈合，这次它将夺走 \x04 的生命。

column1: \x01@\x03 faces death bravely, saying that \x06 knows \x04 time has come. \x05 chants a death poem that \x06 wants remembered by the clan, then lapses into unconsciousness.
column2: \x01@\x03 勇敢地面对死亡，说 \x06 知道 \x04 的时刻到了。 \x05 吟唱了一首死亡之诗，希望 \x06 能被氏族铭记，然后陷入昏迷。

column1: Later that night, \x06 dies.
column2: 当晚晚些时候， \x06 死了。

column1: \x01@\x03 died from an old injury which suddenly worsened, but not before composing an epic poem.
column2: \x01@\x03 死于突然恶化的旧伤，但在死前创作了一首史诗。

column1: “It is the curse of the \x02\x06Sea People/Tusk Riders/Snake Mothers/People of the Spear/Newtlings/little beings of the forest\x02, from when my \x02\x03grandfather/grandmother/great-grandmother\x02 destroyed one of their shrines. I know that nothing can be done. But if you chant the verse I am about to give you, none of my own children will be struck by the curse.” And \x01@\x03 recites a poem of power and grace.
column2: “这是 \x02\x06海民/獠牙骑手/蛇母族/矛之民/蝾螈人/森林小生灵\x02的诅咒，源自我的 \x02\x03祖父/祖母/曾祖母\x02 摧毁了它们的一座神坛。我知道无可挽回。但如果你吟唱我将要给你的诗句，我自己的子女便不会遭受这诅咒。”于是 \x01@\x03 吟唱了一首充满力量与优雅的诗。

column1: \x05 will say nothing more of the curse, for fear that it would bring bad luck to \x04 children and the rest of the clan, but \x06 gives us a magnificent poem about the good things in \x04 own life, and says \x06 hopes we will remember \x08 well.
column2: \x05 不再提及这诅咒，唯恐给 \x04 孩子和氏族其余人带来厄运，但 \x06 给了我们一首壮美的诗，讲述 \x04 自己生命中的美好事物，并说 \x06 希望我们能铭记 \x08 于心。

column1: Then \x06 dies.
column2: 然后 \x06 死了。

column1: \x01@\x03 composed a final poem, then died from a curse that had affected \x04 father and grandmother.
column2: \x01@\x03 创作了最后一首诗，随后死于曾诅咒 \x04 父亲和祖母的诅咒。

column1: The ring gathers in sorrow around \x01@\x03, who was struck down by a weird Chaos monster \x02\x06that had the body of a giant snail and the head of a dragon/that looked like a deer but had the face of a troll/that had the body of a scorpion and a human head/that was hiding at the bottom of a pond/that was living inside one of our cows/that was lurking among the trees at the edge of our tula\x02.
column2: 长老会悲痛地围在 \x01@\x03身边，他被一只诡异的混沌怪物击倒， \x02\x06那怪物有巨型蜗牛的身体和龙的头颅/看起来像鹿却有着巨魔的面孔/有蝎子的身体和人类头颅/藏在一个池塘底部/寄居在我们的一头牛体内/潜伏在我们图拉边缘的树林中\x02。

column1: One of our \x02\x03Uroxi/Humakti/Elmali\x02 thanes killed the creature before it could get away, but \x01@\x03 is dying and the god-talkers say no healing spells or resurrection can save \x08. Even as the healers consult their lore, \x01@\x03 dies.
column2: 我们的一位 \x02\x03尤洛克斯追随者/胡马克蒂/埃尔马利\x02 持斧者在那生物逃走前杀死了它，但 \x01@\x03 正在死去，神言者说任何治疗法术或复活都无法拯救 \x08。就在治疗师查阅学识之际， \x01@\x03 死了。

column1: \x01@\x03 was attacked by a weird Chaos monster. We killed the creature, but there was no way to heal \x01@\x03, and \x06 died.
column2: \x01@\x03 被一只诡异的混沌怪物袭击。我们杀死了那生物，但无法治愈 \x01@\x03，于是 \x06 死了。

column1: Declare a private period of mourning.
column2: 宣布一段私密的哀悼期。

column1: We mourned privately for many nights and many days.
column2: 我们私下哀悼了许多个日夜。

column1: Prepare for the election of a king from another clan.
column2: 准备从另一个氏族选举一位国王。

column1: The other clans agreed to meet next season in a moot to elect a new king.
column2: 其他氏族同意下个季节召开会议选举新王。

column1: Sacrifice to \x01@\x08 in honor of \x01@\x03.
column2: 向 \x01@\x08 献祭以纪念 \x01@\x03。

column1: We sacrificed to \x01@\x08 in \x01@\x03’s honor.
column2: 我们向 \x01@\x08 献祭以纪念 \x01@\x03。

column1: The clan was glad to be certain that \x01@\x03 was in \x01@\x08’s hall.
column2: 氏族很高兴确定 \x01@\x03 在 \x01@\x08的大厅中。

column1: Select a member of your clan as candidate for king.
column2: 选择本氏族的一名成员作为国王候选人。

column1: Send emissaries to other clans to recite \x01@\x03’s poem.
column2: 派遣使者到其他氏族吟诵 \x01@\x03的诗。

column1: We made sure that other clans heard \x01@\x03’s poem.
column2: 我们确保其他氏族听到了 \x01@\x03的诗。

column1: They were as moved by it as we were.
column2: 他们和我们一样为之感动。

column1: They listened politely.
column2: 他们礼貌地听着。

column1: Send warriors to hunt Chaos creatures.
column2: 派遣战士猎杀混沌生物。

column1: Our warriors found a few bats that were the wrong color in a cave that hadn’t been there the season before. They said we had been lucky to find the creatures before they could grow any larger.
column2: 我们的战士在一个上个季节还不存在的洞穴里发现了几只颜色异常的蝙蝠。他们说幸运的是我们赶在它们长大之前找到了它们。

column1: Our hunters found three strange goats running in the woods near our sheep. They chased the goats and saw them shed their magical disguises. They were broo! We slew them and searched our tula for any other monsters, but could not find more.
column2: 我们的猎人在我们羊群附近的树林里发现了三只奇怪的山羊。他们追赶山羊，看到它们褪去了魔法伪装。它们是布鲁！我们杀死了它们，搜索了我们的图拉领地寻找其他怪物，但没有发现更多。

column1: Our warriors found a pool in the woods that was full of strange slime creatures. We attacked them with torches and with magic and killed them all before they could escape through their holes in the mud.
column2: 我们的战士在树林里发现了一个充满奇怪粘液生物的池塘。我们用火把和魔法攻击它们，在它们从泥洞逃走之前全部杀死。

column1: We found a pit in the wood that was full of horrible skulls, some of them human, all of them twisted and wrong. Our god-talkers blasted the pit with Orlanth’s lightnings and Urox’s magic and said that the evil spirits responsible for the horror had been destroyed.
column2: 我们在树林里发现了一个满是可怕头骨的坑洞，其中一些是人类头骨，全都扭曲变形。我们的神言者用奥兰斯的闪电和乌洛克斯的魔法轰击了坑洞，并说造成恐怖的恶灵已被摧毁。

column1: Our warriors and hunters searched the entire tula but could find no other monsters. We hoped for the best.
column2: 我们的战士和猎人搜索了整个图拉，但没有找到其他怪物。我们抱最好的希望。

column1: Our Uroxi and other god-talkers helped the warriors search, but we could not find any signs of Chaos.
column2: 我们的尤洛克斯追随者和其他神言者帮助战士搜索，但我们没有找到任何混沌的迹象。

column1: No one felt any easier when the warriors could find no sign of other Chaos beings, because no one understood where the creature that killed \x01@\x03 had come from.
column2: 战士们找不到其他混沌存在的迹象时，没有人感到轻松，因为没有人明白杀死 \x01@\x03 的怪物是从哪里来的。

column1: We searched the tula but could not find any other monsters.
column2: 我们搜索了图拉，但没有找到其他怪物。

column1: Where there is one monster, there may be more.
column2: 有一头怪物就可能还有更多。

column1: This monster was a freak. We are already strong against Chaos, and can afford to honor \x01@\x03 as \x06 deserves.
column2: 这头怪物是个异类。我们对混沌已经足够强大，能够以 \x06 应得的方式纪念 \x01@\x03 。

column1: Chaos has killed one of the best of us. If we are not careful, it could kill us all.
column2: 混沌杀死了我们中最优秀的一员。如果我们不小心，它可能会杀死我们所有人。

column1: I was proud to serve under \x01@\x03.
column2: 我很自豪曾在 \x01@\x03麾下效力。

column1: We are born of Earth, live in the wind, and by fire are transformed back into Earth.
column2: 我们生于大地，活在风中，经火转化回归大地。

column1: \x01@\x03 was an honorable Orlanthi. No greater words can be said.
column2: \x01@\x03 是一位可敬的奥兰提人。没有更高的赞誉了。

column1: Arrh! I hate Chaos!
column2: 啊！我痛恨混沌！

column1: I have not served a better \x01@\x15.
column2: 我从未侍奉过更好的 \x01@\x15。

column1: In the end, death tricks us all.
column2: 最终，死亡戏弄了我们所有人。

column1: “The best life is led by those who are good at what they do.”
column2: “最美好的生活属于那些精于本业之人。”

column1: \x01@\x03’s final words have humbled me.
column2: \x01@\x03的遗言让我谦卑。

column1: \x01@\x03 was a great \x01@\x15. \x03 greatness will not be reduced if we are less than extravagant in sacrificing in \x04 honor.
column2: \x01@\x03 曾是一位伟大的 \x01@\x15。 \x03 的伟大不会因为我们为纪念 \x04 而献祭时不够铺张而减损。

column1: When we lose the chief, we lose our eyes, our arms, our soul.
column2: 当我们失去酋长，我们便失去了眼睛、手臂和灵魂。

column1: We can change our luck. Our clan needs a female chief.
column2: 我们可以改变命运。我们的氏族需要一位女酋长。

column1: If it had not been a snake, it would have been an arrow or a sword. \x01@\x03’s days were numbered.
column2: 如果不是一条蛇，也会是一支箭或一把剑。 \x01@\x03的时日无多了。

column1: With that wound, \x01@\x03 is lucky \x06 livd as long as \x06 did..
column2: 受此伤， \x01@\x03 算幸运 \x06 活得像 \x06 一样久..

column1: If it had not been a Chaos monster, it would have been an arrow or a sword. \x01@\x03’s days were numbered.
column2: 如果不是混沌怪物，也会是一支箭或一把剑。 \x01@\x03的时日无多了。

column1: \x01@\x03 will be remembered as a \x07 of the sword who made peace when peace had to be made.
column2: \x01@\x03 将被铭记为一位刀剑 \x07 ，在必须和平时缔造和平。

column1: This is surely the first appearance of a whole plague of snakes!
column2: 这肯定是成灾蛇群的首现！

column1: Aiieeeeee! Wakboth the Devil! And \x01@\x03 dead!
column2: 哎呀呀呀呀！恶魔瓦克博斯！还有 \x01@\x03 死了！

column1: We can honor both \x01@\x03 and \x01@\x08 at this sad occasion.
column2: 在这悲伤的时刻，我们可以同时纪念 \x01@\x03 和 \x01@\x08 。

column1: Chaos can take even the best of us, no matter how vigilant we are.
column2: 混沌甚至能带走我们中最优秀的人，无论我们多么警惕。

column1: What a shame. What a tragedy.
column2: 真可惜。真是一场悲剧。

column1: What a shame that \x01@\x03 had to die to free \x04 kin from the curse.
column2: 真可惜， \x01@\x03 必须死去才能将 \x04 的族人从诅咒中解放出来。

column1: Chaos is really our worst foe. We will never be able to kill it. But we must try.
column2: 混沌确实是我们最可怕的敌人。我们永远无法杀死它。但我们必须尝试。

column1: These sorts of things happen. But that doesn’t make this any less tragic.
column2: 这种事时有发生。但这并不能减轻这场悲剧。

column1: What a tragedy. What a terrible tragedy.
column2: 真是一场悲剧。一场可怕的悲剧。

column1: sceneR041
column2: sceneR041

column1: Rumor has it that certain unmarried young men of the clan have been heading into the woods to visit a beautiful woman, one who doesn’t dress or act like an Orlanthi. It may even be that some married men have been with her, breaking the laws against adultery.
column2: 传言说氏族中某些未婚年轻男子一直前往树林，拜访一位美丽女子；这位女子穿着举止都不像奥兰瑟人。甚至可能有些已婚男子与她会面，违反了禁止通奸的法律。

column1: A beautiful woman appeared in the woods. Some said that she ensnared our men.
column2: 林中现出一位美人。有人说她蛊惑了我们的男人。

column1: Interrogate the menfolk to see who has been with her.
column2: 盘问男人们，看谁与她有染。

column1: We carefully questioned the menfolk to see if any of them had been with her.
column2: 我们仔细盘问了男人们，看是否有人与她有染。

column1: All of the menfolk steadfastly denied any contact with the woman of the woods.
column2: 所有男人都坚称从未接触过林中女子。

column1: Three men admitted to having been with the woman, who they say had “eyes that were impossible to resist.”
column2: 三名男子承认与那女子有染，称她有着“无法抗拒的眼神”。

column1: What do you do?
column2: 你怎么办？

column1: Admonish the men to be more careful.
column2: 告诫男人们要更加谨慎。

column1: We told them to use better judgment in the future.
column2: 我们告诫他们日后须明辨是非。

column1: They admitted that they had been foolish, and promised to learn from their mistake.
column2: 他们承认自己愚昧，并许诺从错误中吸取教训。

column1: Forgive them, for they were under a spell.
column2: 宽恕他们，毕竟他们是受了蛊惑。

column1: We forgave them, for they were obviously under a spell.
column2: 我们宽恕了他们，因为他们显然受了蛊惑。

column1: Perform a ritual to lift any curses they might be under.
column2: 举行仪式，解除他们可能身负的任何诅咒。

column1: We performed a ritual to lift any curses they have been under.
column2: 我们举行仪式，解除了他们身负的诅咒。

column1: The god-talkers said that the ritual had succeeded.
column2: 神言者称仪式已经成功。

column1: Perform the ritual dance of the Battle of Red Leaves.
column2: 跳起红叶之战的仪式之舞。

column1: We did the ritual dance of the Battle of Red Leaves.
column2: 我们跳起了红叶之战的仪式之舞。

column1: Dancing the Battle of Red Leaves succeeded in lifting the curse that had been put on several of our men, who should have known better.
column2: 跳红叶之战之舞成功解除了我们几名男子所受的诅咒——他们本该更清醒些。

column1: Our magicians could not determine if the dance was beneficial.
column2: 我们的法师无法判定这舞蹈是否有益。

column1: Although we defied our ancient enemies, the dance seemed to have little effect.
column2: 尽管我们违抗了宿敌，这舞蹈似乎收效甚微。

column1: Although we defied our ancient enemies by dancing the Battle of Red Leaves, it seemed to have little effect.
column2: 尽管我们以跳红叶之战之舞违抗了宿敌，这舞蹈似乎收效甚微。

column1: Remind the menfolk of the penalties for adultery.
column2: 提醒男人们通奸的惩罚。

column1: We reminded the men of the penalties for adultery.
column2: 我们提醒了男人们通奸的惩罚。

column1: Send a search party to capture the woman.
column2: 派出搜捕队去捉拿那女子。

column1: We sent searchers to capture her.
column2: 我们派出搜捕者去捉拿她。

column1: They could not find her, or any trace of her passing.
column2: 他们找不到她，也寻不见她经过的任何踪迹。

column1: Our best hunters searched long and hard, using their most powerful magics. They brought the woman back to us, tied with ropes. She would not speak to us. Our storytellers thought her some kind of kin to the aldryami, or elves.
column2: 我们最优秀的猎人竭尽全力搜寻，动用了最强大的魔法。他们用绳索将那女子绑了回来。她不肯对我们说话。我们的说书人认为她与阿尔德里亚米——或称精灵——有些亲缘。

column1: The elves are, of course, the ancient enemies of our clan.
column2: 精灵当然是我们氏族的宿敌。

column1: What do you do with her?
column2: 你如何处置她？

column1: Banish her from your lands.
column2: 将她驱逐出你的领地。

column1: We banished her from our lands.
column2: 我们将她驱逐出了领地。

column1: Kill her.
column2: 杀了她。

column1: We killed her.
column2: 我们杀了她。

column1: She died without showing fear.
column2: 她死去时毫无惧色。

column1: Give her gifts, and ask her to convey your goodwill to her people.
column2: 赠她礼物，请她向她的族人传达我们的善意。

column1: We gifted her, and asked her to convey our goodwill to her people.
column2: 我们赠她礼物，请她向她的族人传达我们的善意。

column1: How much wealth do you give her?
column2: 你赠予她多少财富？

column1: She warned us that our men had been dangerously infected, because we had offended the elves. She told us how to mix a potion to cure the infection before it showed itself. She also said that the trouble with the elves would get worse, if we weren’t careful.
column2: 她警告我们说，我们的人已被危险地感染了，因为我们冒犯了精灵。她告诉我们如何调配一种药水，在感染显现之前将其治愈。她还说，如果我们不小心，与精灵的麻烦会变得更糟。

column1: Send a search party to drive the woman off.
column2: 派出搜索队把那女人赶走。

column1: We sent searchers to drive her away.
column2: 我们派搜索队把她赶走了。

column1: “These are just rumors. Wait for facts.”
column2: “这些只是谣言。等有了事实再说。”

column1: We ignored the rumors.
column2: 我们无视了这些谣言。

column1: We know these \x02\x03woods/hills/lands\x02 as we know \x02\x03the lines on our palms/the shape of our faces/the toes on our feet\x02. If an outlaw woman hides here, we will find her.
column2: 我们了解这些 \x02\x03树林/山丘/土地\x02 就像我们了解 \x02\x03我们掌心的纹路/我们脸庞的轮廓/我们脚上的足趾\x02。如果有个法外女子藏在这里，我们定会找到她。

column1: To say I am an exceptional hunter is no empty boast. But I bet we will never find her.
column2: 说我是个非凡的猎人并非虚言。但我打赌我们永远找不到她。

column1: Trying to find a wood-nymph in the forest is like attempting to find one special grain of barley in a field.
column2: 森林里找林妖就像在田里找一粒特别的大麦。

column1: This is scarcely a matter for an individual of my great talents.
column2: 这几乎不是我这等才华之人该管的事。

column1: I will ask and ask and ask until the men tell the truth about this.
column2: 我会一遍遍地追问，直到男人们说出实情。

column1: I will subtly question the menfolk and determine what involvement they have had with this creature.
column2: 我会巧妙地盘问男人们，查明他们与这生灵有何瓜葛。

column1: This time, we should not waste any effort on the men. Their doom is worse than any punishment we could mete out.
column2: 这次，我们不应在男人身上浪费精力。他们的厄运比我们能施加的任何惩罚都要可怕。

column1: She is a wood nymph. If men were with her, they are \x02\x03in danger/doomed/in some kind of trouble\x02.
column2: 她是个林妖。如果有男人和她在一起，他们就 \x02\x03身处危险/注定遭殃/陷入了某种麻烦\x02。

column1: She is a wood nymph. If men were with her, she’ll have made their flesh soil for some terrible sprouting.
column2: 她是个林妖。如果有男人和她在一起，她定已让他们的血肉变成某种可怕萌芽的土壤。

column1: We know the dreadful penalty for cavorting with this nymph. We must find her and make her suffer.
column2: 我们很清楚与这林妖厮混的可怕代价。我们必须找到她，让她吃苦头。

column1: Our clan aided King Vingkot at the Battle of Red Leaves, where Chinkis Mor and his plant people were driven out of the Hills of Peace.
column2: 我们的氏族在红叶之战中援助了温科特王，金基斯·莫尔和他的植物人就是在那场战役中被逐出和平丘陵的。

column1: When King Vingkot drove Chinkis Mor and his plant people out of the Hills of Peace, they left huge thickets of poisonous bramble behind them.
column2: 当温科特王将金基斯·莫尔和他的植物人逐出和平丘陵时，他们留下了大片有毒的荆棘丛。

column1: The elves command the vines, roots, leaves, even the very buds of the lands they live in.
column2: 精灵们统御着他们所居之地的藤蔓、根须、叶片，甚至每一颗嫩芽。

column1: I sense no Chaos here.
column2: 我在此处未察觉到混沌。

column1: This is bad, but it is not Chaotic.
column2: 这很糟糕，但并非混沌之力所为。

column1: The elves may be our enemies, but at least they are not aligned with Chaos.
column2: 精灵或许是我们的敌人，但至少他们不与混沌为伍。

column1: A few of the men were with her; I feel it.
column2: 有几个男人跟她在一起过；我能感觉到。

column1: I sense that attraction overcame common sense in some of our men.
column2: 我感觉到，我们有些男人的理智被欲望冲昏了。

column1: I don’t know if there is any good outcome to this.
column2: 我不知道此事是否会有好结果。

column1: That \x02\x03dreadful/terrible/fearsome\x02 wood nymph \x02\x03is back/is here once again/has returned\x02 to seduce our men!
column2: 那个 \x02\x03可怖的/可怕的/令人胆寒的\x02 林妖 \x02\x03又回来了/再次来到了这里/已经返回\x02 来引诱我们的男人了！

column1: What a pack of worrying prudes! Our menfolk no doubt gave her a rougher time than she gave them!
column2: 真是一群自寻烦恼的假正经！我们的男人给她的苦头肯定比她给他们的多！

column1: Is this the same creature we banished from our lands? How dare she return with her perfidious ways!
column2: 这是我们驱逐出境的同一个生灵吗？她怎敢用她那背信弃义的方式回来！

column1: Men are so impulsive, and thus they bring harm to themselves and the clan.
column2: 男人如此冲动，因此给自己和氏族带来伤害。

column1: Why won’t these men ever learn?
column2: 这些男人怎么总也学不会？

column1: The \x02\x03rains have/baking sun has/elements have\x02 weathered our temples already. Repairs now will avoid greater costs in the future.
column2: \x02\x03雨水已经/炽阳已经/风雨已经\x02 侵蚀了我们的神庙。现在修缮可避免日后更大的代价。

column1: I told you the forests were dangerous!
column2: 我告诉过你们森林危险！

column1: I told you she would be back!
column2: 我告诉过你们她会回来！

column1: Humakt-necklaces she made of their heart-roads.
column2: 她用他们的心路做成了胡马克特项链。

column1: Flooded she their sense-shields with her eye-pools.
column2: 她用她的眼湖淹没了他们的感知之盾。

column1: The wood-nymphs are friends to what we call the elves, or plant people. They call themselves the Aldryami.
column2: 林妖们是我们称之为精灵或植物人的朋友。它们自称阿尔德里亚米。

column1: \x02\x03Hunt her down/Snare her/Find her\x02 and \x02\x03kill her/send her body-bits back to the elves/plant her corpse deep in the ground\x02.
column2: \x02\x03追捕她/诱捕她/找到她\x02 然后 \x02\x03杀死她/把她的身体碎块送回精灵那里/将她的尸体深埋地下\x02。

column1: sceneR042
column2: sceneR042

column1: “Anyone who had contact with the woman of the woods must come forward.”
column2: “任何与林中女子有过接触的人都必须站出来。”

column1: We told everyone who had contact with the woman of the woods to come forward.
column2: 我们命令所有与林中女子有过接触的人都站出来。

column1: No one did so.
column2: 没有人照做。

column1: Cast a curse-lifting spell on all of the men of the clan.
column2: 对氏族所有男性施放解除诅咒的法术。

column1: We cast a curse-lifting spell on all of the men of the clan.
column2: 我们对氏族所有男性施放了解除诅咒的法术。

column1: Nevertheless, more men died of the same terrible curse shortly thereafter. One of them was married.
column2: 然而，不久之后又有更多男性死于同样可怕的诅咒。其中一位已婚。

column1: The curse was not repeated.
column2: 诅咒没有再次出现。

column1: One married carl died of the curse, so we knew that he had committed adultery with the mysterious woman of the woods.
column2: 一名已婚的卡尔死于诅咒，于是我们知道他与那位神秘的林中女子犯了通奸。

column1: Cast a curse-lifting spell on all clan members.
column2: 对全体氏族成员施放解除诅咒的法术。

column1: We cast a curse-lifting spell on all of the people of the clan.
column2: 我们对氏族全体成员施放了解除诅咒的法术。

column1: One carl died of the curse. He was married; so we knew that he had committed adultery with the mysterious woman of the woods.
column2: 一名卡尔死于诅咒。他已婚；于是我们知道他与那位神秘的林中女子犯了通奸。

column1: Cast a curse-lifting spell on the men who admitted contact with the woman of the woods.
column2: 对承认与林中女子有接触的男性施放解除诅咒的法术。

column1: We cast a curse-lifting spell on the men who had met the woman of the woods.
column2: 我们对曾与林中女子见过面的男性施放了解除诅咒的法术。

column1: Sacrifice to Ernalda for help.
column2: 向厄纳尔达献祭以求帮助。

column1: We sacrificed to Ernalda for help.
column2: 我们向厄纳尔达献祭以求帮助。

column1: Why would anyone who had been with the woman deny it?
column2: 为什么任何与那女子有过接触的人会否认呢？

column1: Anyone who denies being with the nymph is making their own death seal.
column2: 任何否认与林妖相处的人都是在给自己签署死亡令。

column1: If any married men were with the woman, and admit to it, they are confessing to a crime that demands they be outlawed.
column2: 如果有已婚男性与那女子在一起，并且承认了，他们就是在供认一件需要被逐出氏族的罪行。

column1: Any married men who were with the woman are as good as outlawed already.
column2: 任何与那女子在一起的已婚男性已经几乎等同于被逐出氏族了。

column1: The people are distressed. They will be more distressed if we do nothing.
column2: 人们很痛苦。如果我们什么都不做，他们会更痛苦。

column1: Maybe there is a blessing with this curse; it would be good to turn flesh to soil.
column2: 也许这诅咒之中藏着祝福；将血肉化为土壤或许是好事。

column1: Maybe the curse won’t happen this time.
column2: 也许这次诅咒不会发生。

column1: Like the growth of weeds, a curse of the aldryami is fast and very difficult to stop. The folk name for the aldryami is “elves.”
column2: 阿尔德里亚米的诅咒如同野草生长，迅速且极难遏制。民间称阿尔德里亚米为“精灵”。

column1: Quickly, waste no time with who did what or when. Just cast a curse-lifting spell for everyone and avert disaster.
column2: 快，别浪费时间追究是谁做了什么、何时做的。直接对所有人施放祛咒法术，避免灾祸。

column1: If there are dishonorers of the marriage bed among the afflicted, Ernalda will be unlikely to help them.
column2: 如果受难者中有玷污婚姻之床的人，厄纳尔达不太可能帮助他们。

column1: All deaths are \x02\x03necessary/essential/mandatory\x02. Some are \x02\x03more shameful/less honorable/more ignoble\x02 than others.
column2: 所有死亡都是 \x02\x03必然/必需/强制\x02的。有些死亡 \x02\x03更为可耻/不那么体面/更加卑贱\x02 。

column1: To think, I was tempted to go with her, too.
column2: 想想看，我当时也差点跟她走了。

column1: If I see her, I will slay her.
column2: 若我见到她，必斩之。

column1: If we can cure the men, we win a victory over our ancient enemies, the Aldryami.
column2: 如果我们能治愈这些男人，就战胜了我们的宿敌——阿尔德里亚米。

column1: Counter-spells against foreign magic are unreliable, but it’s the best we can do. How I wish these foolish men had ignored her!
column2: 对抗外邦法术的反咒并不可靠，但这是我们最好的办法。我真希望那些蠢男人当初没理她！

column1: Every time this happens, our ancestor spirits are enraged. Our hatred of the Aldryami goes back — way, way back to before Time.
column2: 每次发生这种事，我们的祖先之灵都会震怒。我们对阿尔德里亚米的仇恨可以追溯——远在时间诞生之前。

column1: Let’s concentrate our magic on only those men who could be affected. That way it might succeed.
column2: 我们只把魔法集中在那些可能受影响的男人身上吧。这样或许能成功。

column1: Sometimes I wish all women could so afflict their men.
column2: 有时我希望所有女人都能这样折磨她们的男人。

column1: Sigh. It’s not their noses that these poor men are led around and astray with.
column2: 唉。这些可怜的男人可不是被牵着鼻子走错路的。

column1: Vingkot’s men were camped in the Hills of Peace. Wood women went among them, and planted the men with seeds. Hundreds died of the curse.
column2: 温科特的战士们曾在和平丘陵扎营。林间女子混入其中，在男人们体内播下种子。数百人死于诅咒。

column1: To have seen this once was bad enough. To see this again means I have lived long enough now, if not too long.
column2: 见过一次已经够糟了。再见一次，意味着我已活得够久，甚至太久了。

column1: It is bad to see a man die. But it is good that others learn not to prowl around like alynxes in heat, mating with women they cannot marry.
column2: 看着男人死去固然糟糕。但其他人能学会别像发情的艾林克斯猫那样四处游荡，与不能娶的女人交配，倒也是好事。

column1: It is terrible to see a man die this way again. Will the others ever learn not to jump on anything they see as if they were over-heated ducks?
column2: 再次看到男人这样死去实在可怕。其他人就学不会别像发情的鸭人那样见什么扑什么吗？

column1: I am tired of hearing complaints about my snoring. I have the right to snore when and where I please.
column2: 我听够了别人抱怨我打鼾。我有权在任何想打鼾的时间和地点打鼾。

column1: “When clothed, carls and nobles \x02\x03look and act profoundly different from/will not be confused with/may be distinguished from\x02 one another. Naked, they all seem lowly.”
column2: “穿上衣服时，自由民和贵族 \x02\x03看起来和行为举止截然不同/不会混淆/可以区分\x02 。赤身裸体时，他们都显得低贱。”

column1: Did you see — I saw it, I saw — how did — how…?
column2: 你看见了吗——我看见了，我看见了——怎么会——怎么……？

column1: Not again — how could they — why — oh, awful…
column2: 又来一次——他们怎么能——为什么——哦，太可怕了……

column1: When I get my hands on that creature, I’ll chop her up like a \x02\x03carrot/turnip/parsnip\x02.
column2: 等我抓到那个畜生，我要把她剁得像 \x02\x03胡萝卜/芜菁/欧洲萝卜\x02一样碎。

column1: sceneR043
column2: sceneR043

column1: Flash floods have put much of your tula underwater. Most of the herd was safely taken to higher ground, but you have lost livestock, goods, and buildings to the flood. The longer it continues, the more damage your tula will suffer.
column2: 山洪淹没了你的图拉领地的大部分地区。大多数牲畜已安全转移到高地，但你在洪水中损失了牲畜、物资和建筑。洪水持续越久，你的领地受损越重。

column1: Flood struck our lands.
column2: 洪水袭击了我们的土地。

column1: Offer help to neighboring clans who are in even worse shape than you.
column2: 向情况比你更糟的邻近氏族提供援助。

column1: We offered help to our neighbors.
column2: 我们向邻居提供了援助。

column1: How much in total do you give away?
column2: 你们总共赠送了多少？

column1: They accepted the little we gave them, and thanked us politely before returning to repairing the flood damage in their homes.
column2: 他们收下了我们施舍的微薄之资，礼貌道谢后便回去修补自家的洪灾损毁了。

column1: Perform the ritual dance of the Battle of Walking Waves.
column2: 表演行波之战的仪式舞蹈。

column1: We did dance of the Battle of Walking Waves, in which our clan helped King Vingkot stop the sea people.
column2: 我们跳了行波之战的舞蹈——在那场战役中，我们的氏族曾帮助温科特王阻止海民。

column1: Our magicians told us that the dance had little effect.
column2: 我们的法师告诉我们，舞蹈效果甚微。

column1: We sent our blue enemy back to the low places, where it belonged. The god-talkers said that our luck was restored as the waters fled.
column2: 我们把蓝色敌人赶回了它该待的低洼之地。神言者说，随着洪水退去，我们的运气也恢复了。

column1: We sacrificed to Ernalda for relief from the flood.
column2: 我们向厄纳尔达献祭，祈求缓解洪水。

column1: Eventually, the flood waters abated.
column2: 最终，洪水退去了。

column1: Sacrifice to Heler, the Rain God.
column2: 向雨神海勒尔献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to Heler, in hopes that he would end his rain.
column2: 我们向海勒尔献祭，希望他停雨。

column1: The god-talkers said that Heler was no longer angry, and that the flood would soon pass.
column2: 神言者说海勒尔不再愤怒，洪水很快会退去。

column1: Sacrifice to Orlanth.
column2: 向奥兰斯献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to Orlanth for relief from the flood.
column2: 我们向奥兰斯献祭，祈求缓解洪水。

column1: Wait out the flood.
column2: 等待洪水退去。

column1: We must work hard to rebuild our herds.
column2: 我们必须努力重建畜群。

column1: This loss is not serious enough to threaten the future of the clan.
column2: 这次损失尚不足以威胁氏族的未来。

column1: The forces of the sea are not our ancient enemies, but our ancestors fought them in the past.
column2: 海洋势力并非我们的宿敌，但我们的祖先曾与之交战。

column1: To give to our neighbors when we are suffering too would hearten our friends and stun our enemies.
column2: 在自己也遭难时向邻居施以援手，会鼓舞盟友，震慑敌人。

column1: Any good land is near water. Floods are a risk every farmer faces.
column2: 好地皆近水。洪水是每个农夫都要面对的风险。

column1: The rains have come and gone; the damage is done. Waiting is the best course.
column2: 雨来雨去，损害已成。等待是最好的策略。

column1: At the Battle of Walking Waves, our forebears helped King Vingkot to turn back the sea people who threatened to overrun the land.
column2: 在行波之战中，我们的祖先帮助温科特王击退了威胁要淹没大地的海民。

column1: Let’s challenge the other clans to a swimming competition.
column2: 我们向其他氏族挑战游泳比赛吧。

column1: I hate being damp.
column2: 我讨厌潮湿。

column1: Orlanth blew this rain onto us because he is dissatisfied with our clan ring. Some of us should quit.
column2: 奥兰斯把这场雨吹向我们，是因为他对我们的氏族议会不满。我们中该有人退出。

column1: See? If we all gather in one place, we are all struck by disaster at the same time.
column2: 看到了吗？如果我们都聚集在一处，灾难就会同时降临到所有人头上。

column1: The rain will help the forests grow back over us, if we don’t do something about all of these accursed elves.
column2: 如果我们不对这些该死的精灵采取行动，雨水就会助长森林，把我们都吞噬。

column1: Is there not some courtesy we could pay to our neighbors?
column2: 我们是否该向邻居表示一些礼节？

column1: All-Breaker destroys all things; its tide-claws rake us.
column2: “破万物”摧毁一切；它的潮汐利爪撕扯着我们。

column1: The great scribe Jalena was coming this way; I hope the floods will not detain her.
column2: 大抄写员贾莱娜正朝这里来；希望洪水不会耽搁她。

column1: To help our neighbors when we are suffering too would be an act worthy of a king.
column2: 在我们自身也受苦时帮助邻居，是配得上国王的行为。

column1: They were startled by our generosity, for we were as hard hit as they. Many poems were composed in our honor, some of them good ones.
column2: 他们被我们的慷慨惊到，因为我们和他们一样受灾严重。许多赞颂我们的诗歌被创作出来，其中一些是佳作。

column1: map
column2: 地图

column1: You have decided that now is the time to embark on the building of a tribe. You need to decide on a name for this new confederation of clans.
column2: 你已决定现在是时候开始建立一个部落。你需要为这个新的氏族联盟决定一个名字。

column1: Use divination to find a tribe name.
column2: 使用占卜来寻找部落名。

column1: \x02\x05Estanvali/Kultain/Locaem/Maboder/Sambari\x02
column2: \x02\x05埃斯坦瓦利/库尔泰/洛卡姆/马博德/桑巴里\x02

column1: The god-talkers all agreed that the signs suggested the name \x01A\x7F.
column2: 神言者们一致认为征象暗示的名字是 \x01A\x7F。

column1: We conducted a divination to pick a name for our tribe, which suggested we call ourselves the \x01A\x7F.
column2: 我们进行了一次占卜来为部落选名，结果建议我们自称 \x01A\x7F。

column1: Pick a new name for the tribe.
column2: 为部落选一个新名字。

column1: The name should make our enemies uneasy or afraid.
column2: 名字应让我们的敌人不安或恐惧。

column1: We don’t want to offend anyone, but we don’t want to seem weak, but — oh my, how can we decide?
column2: 我们不想冒犯任何人，但也不想显得软弱，但是——哦天哪，我们该怎么决定？

column1: Don’t come running for my help. Our clan is just good enough for me.
column2: 别跑来求我帮忙。我们氏族对我来说已经够好了。

column1: The name must show our leadership in forming the tribe.
column2: 名字必须展示我们在建立部落中的领导力。

column1: The name must encompass all that is good in the Orlanthi.
column2: 名字必须包含奥兰西族的一切美好品质。

column1: We should listen to what our tribe-mates have to say about the tribe name.
column2: 我们应该听听部落伙伴们对部落名的看法。

column1: We should find a name that brings all the clans together in a new way.
column2: 我们应该找一个以新方式将所有氏族凝聚在一起的名字。

column1: A good name will reflect the unity of the people.
column2: 一个好名字会体现人民的团结。

column1: The name should be peaceful, mellifluous, and easily remembered.
column2: 名字应平和、悦耳、易记。

column1: Me! Me! Name it after me!
column2: 我！我！以我命名！

column1: Politics. What a bore.
column2: 政治。真无聊。

column1: We should name it after our illustrious chief!
column2: 我们应该以我们杰出的酋长命名！

column1: Many tribes are named after their founder — the Colymar are but one example.
column2: 许多部落以其创始人命名——科利马氏只是其中之一。

column1: Many tribes are named after their founder, but there is no requirement to do so.
column2: 许多部落以其创始人命名，但并非必须如此。

column1: The gods will tell us what name we should use.
column2: 神会告诉我们该用什么名字。

column1: Just make up a name.
column2: 随便编个名字。

column1: Maybe our scrolls will tell us how to name a tribe.
column2: 也许我们的卷轴会告诉我们如何命名部落。

column1: Whatever we choose, someone won’t like it.
column2: 无论我们选什么，总会有人不喜欢。

column1: “A true name resounds through the ages like the roar of the wind in the forest.”
column2: “真名回荡万世，如林中风啸。”

column1: Bad King Urgrain named his tribe after himself, incurring the jealousy and anger of his tribe-mates.
column2: 恶王乌格兰以自己命名部落，招致了部落同伴的嫉妒和愤怒。

column1: Oh, let’s just call ourselves the He — I mean the Jare — the Kud — oh, never mind.
column2: 哦，我们干脆自称“赫”——我是说“贾尔”——“库德”——哦，算了。

column1: Our name should show the strength, courage and righteousness of our menfolk.
column2: 我们的名字应展现男性族人的力量、勇气和正义。

column1: The name should reflect the grace, intelligence and righteousness of our women.
column2: 名字应体现女性族人的优雅、智慧和正义。

column1: A good name will make a good tribe. Let the gods decide.
column2: 好名字造就好的部落。让神决定吧。

column1: If we make a new name, then kings and queens in the future will see that they serve the tribe, and not the other way around.
column2: 如果我们取一个新名字，未来的国王和王后会明白他们服务于部落，而非相反。

column2: 你目前拥有一个由 \x01@\x14 个氏族组成的部落雏形。你需要至少四个氏族才能成为一个真正的部落。你首先接近哪个邻近氏族？

column1: You need at least four clans to make up a tribe. Which neighboring clan do you approach first?
column2: 你需要至少四个氏族才能组成一个部落。你首先接近哪个邻近氏族？

column1: We arranged for a meeting a few weeks hence.
column2: 我们安排了数周后的会面。

column2: \x01@&以其熟练的厨师而闻名

column2: \x01@%以其土地丰饶而闻名

column1: \x01@,, known for its vineyard, and a holy site dedicated to Ernalda and Flamal
column2: \x01@,以其葡萄园和供奉厄纳尔达与弗拉马尔的神圣遗址而闻名

column1: \x01@#, known for reforming bandits and outlaws
column2: \x01@#以其改造强盗和亡命徒而闻名

column1: \x01@*, known for surviving pursuit by terrible foes
column2: \x01@*以其在可怕敌人的追捕中幸存而闻名

column1: \x01@-, known for its aggressive pursuit of trade
column2: \x01@-以其积极追求贸易而闻名

column1: \x01@\x1F, known for pottery and a fanatical attitude
column2: \x01@\x1F以其陶器和狂热态度而闻名

column1: \x01@(, known for a large boulder with war powers
column2: \x01@(以其具有战争力量的巨石而闻名

column1: \x01@), known for its collection of ancient texts
column2: \x01@)以其收集的古代文本而闻名

column1: \x01@ , known for a history of mad chieftains
column2: \x01@ 以其疯狂酋长的历史而闻名

column1: \x01@\x1E, known for hunting prowess
column2: \x01@\x1E以其狩猎技艺而闻名

column1: \x01@0, known for its reliance on raiding
column2: \x01@0以其依赖劫掠而闻名

column2: \x01@+以其谨慎规划而闻名

column1: \x01@., known for its hatred of Chaos
column2: \x01@.以其对混沌的憎恨而闻名

column1: \x01@', known for its large cattle herd
column2: \x01@'以其大群牛而闻名

column1: \x01@/, known for its tradition of female chieftains
column2: \x01@/以其女性酋长的传统而闻名

column1: \x01@\x1C, known for its early arrival in Dragon Pass
column2: \x01@\x1C以其早期抵达龙隘而闻名
