column2: \x01@\x1D其以埃尔马尔为主神

column1: We must seek clans whose leaders have been tested in the crucible of crisis.
column2: 我们必须寻找那些领导者在危机熔炉中经受考验的氏族。

column1: We must seek allies who are attuned to the powers of the Earth.
column2: 我们必须寻找那些与大地之力协调的盟友。

column1: We must seek allies dedicated to peace.
column2: 我们必须寻找致力于和平的盟友。

column1: We must seek clans who have been tested in war.
column2: 我们必须寻找在战争中被考验过的氏族。

column1: We must find dim-witted clans, who lose at gambling and often misplace valuable items.
column2: 我们必须找到愚笨的氏族，他们在赌博中输钱，并经常丢失贵重物品。

column1: We should seek friends who know the meaning of the word “loyalty.”
column2: 我们应该寻找懂得“忠诚”一词含义的朋友。

column1: The best allies are those who respect the rule of law.
column2: 最好的盟友是那些尊重法治的人。

column1: No point dealing with those too stubborn to know a good bargain when they see it.
column2: 与那些固执到连好买卖都认不出来的人打交道毫无意义。

column1: Be careful: joining our tribe won’t turn our enemies into friends.
column2: 小心：加入我们的部落不会把敌人变成朋友。

column1: Start with ground broken by the plow of friendship.
column2: 从友谊之犁翻开的土地开始。

column1: First, look to our friends and allies.
column2: 首先，看看我们的朋友和盟友。

column1: I’m looking forward to hunting on the other clans’ tulas.
column2: 我期待在其他氏族的图拉领地上狩猎。

column1: I have a bad feeling about this.
column2: 我对这件事有种不祥的预感。

column1: Now we carve the first heroic stanzas in a saga that will be remembered forever!
column2: 现在我们正在一部将永远被铭记的传说中刻下第一段英雄诗节！

column1: The crops are going to be bad this year. The carls say that a number of problems have combined to cause the crops to fail. Too much rain after planting rotted some of the seeds. Insects ate away at the young plants’ roots. An early frost killed more plants. These events have one result: you can expect a lean time until the next harvest.
column2: 今年的收成会很差。自由民们说，多种问题共同导致了歉收。播种后雨水过多，烂掉了一些种子。昆虫啃食了幼苗的根部。早霜又冻死了更多作物。这些事件只有一个结果：在下一次收获之前，你们将面临一段艰难的时期。

column1: The harvest was bad.
column2: 收成很差。

column1: Launch a raid to capture grain.
column2: 发动袭击抢夺粮食。

column1: We raided in search of grain. The food we gained cost us much goodwill among the other clans.
column2: 我们为寻找粮食发动了袭击。获得的食物让我们在其他氏族中损失了大量善意。

column1: We raided in search of grain. We lost not only the battle, but our neighbors’ goodwill.
column2: 我们为寻找粮食发动了袭击。不仅输掉了战斗，还失去了邻居们的善意。

column1: Offer help to neighboring clans.
column2: 向邻近氏族提供帮助。

column1: We sacrificed to Ernalda.
column2: 我们向厄纳尔达献祭。

column1: Ernalda heard our prayers, and blessed us so that we would not be hurt as badly by the poor harvest.
column2: 厄纳尔达听到了我们的祈祷，并赐福于我们，使我们不会因歉收而遭受重创。

column1: Ernalda heard our prayers.
column2: 厄纳尔达听到了我们的祈祷。

column1: The god-talkers were not sure that Ernalda had heard our prayers.
column2: 神言者们不确定厄纳尔达是否听到了我们的祈祷。

column1: The god-talkers said that Ernalda may have heard our prayers. Or maybe not.
column2: 神言者们说，厄纳尔达可能听到了我们的祈祷，也可能没有。

column1: Send a trade mission to distant clans to trade goods and cattle for grain.
column2: 派遣一支贸易使团前往遥远的氏族，用货物和牲畜交换粮食。

column1: We sent a trade mission to distant tulas, hoping to buy grain from them.
column2: 我们派遣了一支贸易使团前往遥远的图拉领地，希望能从他们那里购买粮食。

column1: Do you send \x01@\x14 on the mission?
column2: 你是否派 \x01@\x14 参加这次任务？

column1: Tough out the poor harvest.
column2: 挺过歉收的难关。

column1: We endured.
column2: 我们挺过来了。

column1: Send me on a trip. Surely there is good grain somewhere in Dragon Pass.
column2: 派我去一趟吧。龙之隘口某处肯定有好粮食。

column1: Our neighbors certainly won’t be expecting a raid during the harvest…
column2: 我们的邻居肯定想不到会在收获期间遭到袭击……

column1: Raiding our neighbors is not against Heort’s Law.
column2: 袭击邻居并不违反赫奥特律法。

column1: Our neighbors also suffer from a poor harvest. Raiding them would violate not Heort’s Law, but an unwritten law of decency.
column2: 我们的邻居也遭受着歉收之苦。袭击他们并不违反赫奥特律法，而是违反了不成文的体面法则。

column1: Our magic is at a low ebb. This is the cause of our misfortune.
column2: 我们的魔力处于低潮。这是我们不幸的根源。

column1: Sacrifice to Ernalda; the wizened plants will spring back to life.
column2: 向厄纳尔达献祭；枯萎的植物将重新焕发生机。

column1: When the harvest is bad, it is too late to sacrifice to Ernalda. Perhaps we should have done more at planting time.
column2: 收成不好时，再向厄纳尔达献祭已经太晚了。也许我们在播种时就该多下功夫。

column1: When the harvest is bad, it is too late to sacrifice to Ernalda. Perhaps we should have done more at planting time. Raiding will only mean a shortage of labor to take in what harvest we’ll have.
column2: 收成不好时，再向厄纳尔达献祭已经太晚了。也许我们在播种时就该多下功夫。袭击只会导致我们收获时劳动力短缺。

column1: The dragonewts have reason to hate us. Maybe their weird magic has caused this disaster.
column2: 龙人有理由恨我们。也许是他们诡异的魔法造成了这场灾难。

column1: The dragonewts have reason to respect us. Perhaps there are secrets of the Wyrm Friends’ Empire that could help us.
column2: 龙人有理由尊重我们。也许亚龙朋友帝国的秘密能帮助我们。

column1: Find grain.
column2: 寻找粮食。

column1: The flying staff of Theorben has been lost in the Quivini Mountains. It would make a fine piece of kingly regalia.
column2: 西奥本的飞行法杖遗失在奎维尼山脉。它会是一件很好的王权神器。

column1: We should find old accounts of farming in this region; maybe scrolls will tell us how to avoid bad harvests.
column2: 我们应该找到这个地区古老的农耕记录；也许卷轴会告诉我们如何避免歉收。

column1: You farm, sometimes the plants die. It is the way of things.
column2: 你耕种，有时植物会死。这是事物的规律。

column1: Mathkara blames herself for this, because she joked about our ancient enemies when she planted.
column2: 玛斯卡拉为此自责，因为她播种时拿我们的宿敌开了个玩笑。

column1: Our traders are back with horses and carts laden with grain. They say it took a long time, but finally they convinced a distant clan with great stockpiles of grain to sell it at a favorable price.
column2: 我们的商人回来了，马匹和马车满载粮食。他们说花了很长时间，但最终说服了一个有大量粮食储备的遥远氏族以优惠的价格出售。

column1: Your trade mission returns with empty carts and hungry horses. The poor harvest has laid low not only you and your neighbors, but most of Quviniland. Everywhere the traders went, they found people hoping to buy grain. Nowhere did they find clans willing to sell it.
column2: 你的贸易使团带着空车和饿马回来了。歉收不仅影响了你们和你们的邻居，还波及了奎维尼大部。商人所到之处，人们都想买粮。他们没有找到任何愿意卖粮的氏族。

column1: sceneR046
column2: sceneR046

column1: The ring has led the clan in cathartic mourning.
column2: 长老会引导氏族进行了宣泄式的哀悼。

column1: How do you do this?
column2: 你们如何做到？

column1: Give him wealth if he agrees to seek his fortune elsewhere.
column2: 如果他同意去别处谋生，就给他一些财物。

column1: How much do you give to him?
column2: 你给他多少？

column1: He agreed to do so.
column2: 他同意了。

column1: Give him travelling supplies and encourage him to seek his fortune elsewhere. Let him know he is lucky to receive even this.
column2: 给他旅途用品，鼓励他去别处谋生。让他知道能得到这些已经算是幸运了。

column1: He agreed to go.
column2: 他同意离开。

column1: Make him feel unwelcome.
column2: 让他感到不受欢迎。

column1: Find powerful holy warriors of Urox to scour your lands of Chaos taint.
column2: 寻找尤洛克斯的强大圣战士，清除你们土地上的混沌污染。

column1: We sought powerful holy warriors of Urox, hoping the would scour our lands of Chaos taint.
column2: 我们寻找尤洛克斯的强大圣战士，希望他们能清除我们土地上的混沌污染。

column1: The Storm Khans we found refused to come, citing worse Chaos problems in the Quivini Mountains.
column2: 我们找到的风暴可汗拒绝了，理由是奎维尼山脉有更严重的混沌问题。

column1: The Storm Khans came, broke a certain number of things, and consumed a great amount of food.
column2: 风暴可汗来了，打碎了一些东西，消耗了大量食物。

column1: They went away, and came back wounded and happy. They had slain many broos and a nest of creatures they called slime snakes.
column2: 他们离开了，回来时带着伤但很开心。他们杀死了许多布鲁斯和一窝他们称为粘液蛇的生物。

column1: They went away, but did not come back.
column2: 他们离开了，再也没有回来。

column1: Forbid all extreme and destructive mourning.
column2: 禁止一切极端和破坏性的哀悼。

column1: The ring forbade all destructive mourning.
column2: 长老会禁止了一切破坏性的哀悼。

column1: The people destroyed cattle and goods anyway, in secret.
column2: 人们还是秘密地毁掉了牲畜和财物。

column1: The people destroyed cattle and goods anyway, in secret mourning ceremonies.
column2: 人们还是在秘密的哀悼仪式中毁掉了牲畜和财物。

column1: The people grumbled and said that the ring was too proud to admit when things were going badly.
column2: 人们抱怨说，长老会太骄傲了，不肯承认情况糟糕。

column1: We sacrificed to Urox, foe of Chaos.
column2: 我们向混沌之敌尤洛克斯献祭。

column1: The god-talkers said that the Storm Bull would protect us from Chaos.
column2: 神言者说风暴公牛会守护我们免受混沌侵害。

column1: The god-talkers didn’t think the Storm Bull had received our sacrifice.
column2: 神言者认为风暴公牛没有接受我们的献祭。

column1: “We should have destroyed a few things to get his attention.”
column2: “我们本该毁掉些东西来引起它的注意。”

column1: Through ring members’ example, encourage extreme mourning behavior.
column2: 以环成员为表率，鼓励极端的哀悼行为。

column1: There’s nothing else to be done.
column2: 再没有别的办法了。

column1: I can convince even stubborn Storm Bulls to come here.
column2: 即便是最顽固的风暴公牛信徒，我也能说服他们来此。

column1: There is no victory against kinslaying! We must suffer! I myself shall \x02\x03slaughter the lambs/kill the piglets/slay the calves\x02 I raised by hand. \x02\x03Alas/Ai-ee/O, woe\x02!
column2: 弑亲之战绝无胜算！我们必须受苦！我本人要亲手 \x02\x03宰杀这些羊羔/杀死这些猪仔/屠杀这些牛犊\x02 。 \x02\x03啊/哎呀/呜呼，悲哉\x02！

column1: The people will despise us if we prevent them from mourning with true abandon.
column2: 倘若我们阻止民众纵情哀悼，他们会鄙视我们。

column1: Smash pots! Burn steads! Kill cattle! Throw yourselves on the ground! Only a frenzy of grief can save us.
column2: 砸锅罐！焚农庄！宰牲畜！匍匐于地！唯有疯狂的悲恸才能拯救我们。

column1: Cathartic mourning will clear everyone’s souls and lift their spirits. Then we can think clearly about how best to fight Chaos.
column2: 宣泄的哀悼能涤荡每个人的灵魂，振奋他们的精神。然后我们才能清醒思考如何最有效地对抗混沌。

column1: Now we can beseech Urox to help us.
column2: 如今我们可以恳求尤洛克斯助我们一臂之力了。

column1: The connection between Chaos and kinstrife is just a metaphor. We have nothing to worry about.
column2: 混沌与亲族纷争之间的联系不过是比喻。我们无需担忧。

column1: The connection between Chaos and kinslaying is not just poetic. We must take steps against Chaos. Alas, our magic is weak, so we are doomed!
column2: 混沌与弑亲之间的联系并非只是诗意的比喻。我们必须采取措施对抗混沌。唉，我们的魔法太弱，注定遭难！

column1: The connection between Chaos and kinslaying is not just poetic. We must take steps against Chaos. Our magic is strong, so sacrificing to Urox is the best option.
column2: 混沌与弑亲之间的联系并非只是诗意的比喻。我们必须采取措施对抗混沌。我们的魔法强大，因此向尤洛克斯献祭是最佳选择。

column1: His act gnaws at our hearth’s-heart!
column2: 他的恶行啃噬着我们家园的核心！

column1: The Chaos threat is bad. If we strike against it and fail, we’ll make it even worse. Unless we try the heroquest of Storm Bull against Wakboth the Devil.
column2: 混沌威胁很糟糕。如果我们出击却失败，情况会更糟。除非我们尝试风暴公牛对抗恶魔瓦克博斯的英雄任务。

column1: The Chaos threat is serious, but we can stamp it out if we act quickly and decisively.
column2: 混沌威胁很严重，但只要迅速果断行动，我们就能将其根除。

column1: If we kill him like he deserves, Chaos will be even stronger. So prepare yourselves for the worst.
column2: 如果我们以他应得的方式杀死他，混沌反而会更强。所以，做好最坏的打算吧。

column1: Chaos comes in the wake of kinstrife.
column2: 混沌在亲族纷争之后降临。

column1: Bad King Urgrain drank too much and fought with his cousin. When he slew the man, all manner of Chaos beasts came running towards him.
column2: 恶王乌格兰暴饮暴食，与表亲争斗。当他杀死那人时，各种混沌兽都朝他奔涌而来。

column1: The invitation to Chaos lurks in serious rivalry between kin, in the ale-jar, in hoarded anger.
column2: 对混沌的邀请潜伏在至亲间的激烈仇隙中，在酒坛中，在积压的怒火中。

column1: The elves will watch us fight off the threat of Chaos, then sweep down on us when we are weak.
column2: 精灵们会坐视我们击退混沌威胁，然后在我们虚弱时向我们发起突袭。

column1: Kinstrife attracts the undead. They can smell it.
column2: 亲族纷争会吸引亡灵。它们能嗅到这股气息。

column1: Minlinster’s mead-home became Urox’s foe-bringer.
column2: 明林斯特的蜜酒厅成了尤洛克斯的克敌之器。

column1: Mead-spilling pot smashing made Chaos confusion.
column2: 泼洒蜜酒、砸碎锅罐，制造了混沌的混乱。

column1: Destroy those dearest things that Chaos would taint and Chaos is thwarted.
column2: 毁掉混沌最想玷污的至爱之物，混沌便会被挫败。

column1: Just as long as you don’t burn down MY stead!
column2: 只要你别烧掉我的农庄就行！

column1: We must not encourage Chaos by allowing the people to do more damage.
column2: 我们不能放任人们造成更大破坏，以免助长混沌。

column1: What type of extreme mourning do you wish to encourage?
column2: 你希望鼓励何种极端的哀悼方式？

column1: Destroy livestock.
column2: 摧毁牲畜。

column1: We gave into the horror and madness. Ring members killed our precious livestock, to show that life with kinstrife is worth nothing.
column2: 我们屈服于恐惧与疯狂。环成员杀掉了我们珍贵的牲畜，以此表明有弑亲之罪的生命毫无价值。

column1: Destroy things.
column2: 毁坏财物。

column1: To show our dismay, we burned down our own steads.
column2: 为表悲恸，我们焚毁了自己的农庄。

column1: Hurt yourselves.
column2: 伤害自身。

column1: The ring members tore at their own flesh and bled upon the ground.
column2: 环成员撕裂自己的皮肉，让鲜血流淌于地。

column1: “That’s enough mourning.”
column2: “哀悼够了。”

column1: Weep piteously.
column2: 哀哭悲泣。

column1: The ring led us in piteous weeping.
column2: 环带领我们哀哭悲泣。

column1: Copious tears flowed.
column2: 泪如泉涌。

column1: We can mourn. That may be all we can do.
column2: 我们可以哀悼。或许我们只能如此。

column1: After we have mourned, strike back at Chaos.
column2: 哀悼之后，反击混沌。

column1: There are not enough tears
column2: 泪水远不足够。

column1: Once we are through grieving, we must seek out and destroy Chaos!
column2: 哀悼过后，我们必须找到并摧毁混沌！

column1: We must grieve, grieve shamelessly! Then we must seek out and destroy Chaos.
column2: 我们必须哀悼，不耻于哀悼！然后，我们必须找到并摧毁混沌。

column1: I knew that things couldn’t last.
column2: 我早知道事情不会长久。

column1: We mustn’t lose control. Self-mutilation attracts vampires and spirits.
column2: 我们不能失控。自残会招来吸血鬼和恶灵。

column1: You can mourn. I’m preparing for battle against Chaos.
column2: 你可以哀悼。我要准备迎战混沌了。

column1: Hair-tearing, arm-slicing, lamb-killing, stead-burning.
column2: 撕扯头发、割伤手臂、宰杀羊羔、焚烧农庄。

column1: How could our proud clan come to this?
column2: 我们骄傲的氏族怎会沦落至此？

column1: Whatever we do, spare our treasures!
column2: 无论做什么，请保全我们的珍宝！

column1: We can show our pain, yes, our sorrow. It’s bad, very bad.
column2: 我们可以展现痛苦，是的，我们的悲伤。很糟，非常糟。

column1: sceneR047
column2: sceneR047

column1: Your efforts to train the earthshakers as battle mounts have been successful! They’re ready to thunder across the landscape, striking fear into your foes and bringing cheer to your allies.
column2: 你训练地动者作为战骑的努力成功了！它们已准备好在战场上隆隆驰骋，让你的敌人心惊胆战，让你的盟友欢欣鼓舞。

column1: We succeeded in training the earthshakers as battle mounts.
column2: 我们成功将地动者训练成了战骑。

column1: Give them away.
column2: 将它们送走。

column1: Who do you give them to?
column2: 你要把它们送给谁？

column1: The dragonewts.
column2: 龙人。

column1: On a long and hazardous trek, we sought dragonewts. We found some impressive-looking specimens who looked like nobles, and presented the earthshakers to them. Their seeming leader hissed inscrutably. At length, he said, “You intention make good with us. But tie us in obligation now. Leave us.”
column2: 经过漫长艰险的跋涉，我们找到了龙人。我们找到了一些相貌不凡、看似贵族的龙人，将地动者献给了它们。它们那位看似首领的龙人发出难以捉摸的嘶嘶声。最后，它说道：“你之意，是与我等交好。但如今，是你强加义务于我等。离去。”

column1: Maran Gor priestesses
column2: 玛兰·戈尔女祭司们。

column1: We sought out the priestesses of shaking earth, in order to gift them with earthshakers.
column2: 我们寻到大地震颤的女祭司们，将地动者作为礼物赠予她们。

column1: The ducks.
column2: 鸭人。

column1: We gave the earthshakers to the ducks, who were much pleased with them. They ran about them, quacking and shaking their spears. The earthshakers looked longingly at their cabbages.
column2: 我们把地动者送给了鸭人，它们非常高兴。它们围着地动者跑来跑去，嘎嘎叫着，晃动长矛。地动者则渴望地望着它们的卷心菜。

column1: A neighboring clan
column2: 一个邻近的氏族。

column1: Which clan do you give the earthshakers to?
column2: 你要把地动者送给哪个氏族？

column1: In fact, they declared their feud with us over.
column2: 事实上，他们宣布与我们的世仇结束了。

column1: Plan to surprise your enemies with them.
column2: 计划用它们来突袭你的敌人。

column1: The warriors were eager to see them used on a raid.
column2: 武士们渴望看到它们在突袭中被使用。

column1: Night after night, our warriors planned and schemed the best ways to use the beasts. They agreed to draw straws for who would ride. Everyone was eager to see our enemies’ faces when the earthshakers appeared.
column2: 一夜又一夜，我们的武士们谋划着使用这些巨兽的最佳方式。他们同意抽签决定谁骑乘。每个人都急于看到当地动者出现时敌人脸上的表情。

column1: Sacrifice them to the gods.
column2: 将它们献祭给神明。

column1: We sacrificed them to \x01@\x07.
column2: 我们将它们献祭给了 \x01@\x07。

column1: Which clan do you trade them to?
column2: 你打算将它们交易给哪个氏族？

column1: How much wealth do you seek for them?
column2: 你为它们索要多少财富？

column1: They gave us our asking price.
column2: 他们按我们的要价付了。

column1: They gave less than we had asked.
column2: 他们付的比我们要价少。

column1: They would not buy the earthshakers.
column2: 他们不愿购买地动者。

column1: Use traders to spread word of these powerful new weapons.
column2: 利用商人散布这些强大新武器的消息。

column1: We let our neighbors know of these powerful new weapons.
column2: 我们让邻居知道了这些强大新武器。

column1: Our neighbors seemed impressed.
column2: 我们的邻居似乎印象深刻。

column1: These creatures are very valuable.
column2: 这些生物非常珍贵。

column1: I think the earthshakers will be useful for twenty years.
column2: 我认为地动者能使用二十年。

column1: I think the earthshakers will be useful for ten years, give or take.
column2: 我认为地动者能使用十年左右。

column1: The gift of these fabulous beasts could end a feud, or fortify an alliance.
column2: 赠予这些神奇的巨兽可以终结世仇，或巩固联盟。

column1: Our clan magic might increase if we sacrifice them.
column2: 如果献祭它们，我们的氏族魔法可能会增强。

column1: Our clan magic will increase if we sacrifice them.
column2: 如果献祭它们，我们的氏族魔法将会增强。

column1: We must keep these sword-headed creatures to strike at our foes.
column2: 我们必须留下这些剑头生物来打击我们的敌人。

column1: These violent creatures are holy to Ernalda’s violent sister, Maran Gor.
column2: 这些凶暴的生物是埃娜尔达的暴戾姐妹玛拉·戈尔的圣物。

column1: Let the other clans know we have them, so they will be afraid to raid us.
column2: 让其他氏族知道我们拥有它们，这样他们就不敢袭击我们。

column1: Let us save these creatures until we can trade them for something that might become a piece of royal regalia.
column2: 让我们保留这些生物，直到能用它们换到可能成为王室礼器的东西。

column1: Give them away, and get peace in return.
column2: 把它们送走，换取和平。

column1: These things eat plants, yes? Imagine them chomping down on a war party of perfidious plant-folk!
column2: 这些家伙吃植物，对吧？想象它们大口嚼碎一支背信弃义的植物人战队！

column1: They clearly belong to the dragonewts. Let’s return them to their rightful owners.
column2: 它们显然属于龙人。让我们把它们物归原主。

column1: These beasts, they’re so — so — you understand what I mean.
column2: 这些野兽，它们真是——真是——你懂我的意思。

column1: Ha! With these stomping beasts, we shall reduce the snivelling worms of the \x01@a clan to a thick, red paste!
column2: 哈！有了这些跺地巨兽，我们要把 \x01@a 氏族的鼻涕虫们碾成浓稠的红浆！

column1: Yes, let the traders boast to our foes. Our enemies should fear us even more now.
column2: 是的，让商人在敌人面前夸耀吧。我们的敌人现在应该更惧怕我们。

column1: Hah! I guess this was a good idea.
column2: 哈！我想这是个好主意。

column1: Yes!
column2: 没错！

column1: They won’t be much use in a skirmish, but if they charge, they’ll be deadly.
column2: 它们在散兵战中用处不大，但如果发起冲锋，将是致命的。

column1: They are shield and sword in one.
column2: 它们集盾与剑于一身。

column1: Now our horses aren’t good enough for the weaponthanes? Their arrogance knows no bounds!
column2: 怎么，我们的马现在配不上武器领主了？他们的傲慢真是毫无底线！

column1: Whoa.
column2: 哇哦。

column1: If you’d let me train them we could have them doing tricks. But no, you kept me well away from them.
column2: 如果当初你让我训练它们，我们本可以让它们表演把戏。但你没有，你把我远远隔开。

column1: I’m not certain that our ancestors would approve, but I think… I think it’s alright.
column2: 我不确定祖先们是否会赞成，但我觉得……我觉得还行。

column1: Now our enemies will learn what it’s like to fight against dragons!
column2: 现在我们的敌人将尝到与龙作战的滋味！

column1: sceneR048
column2: sceneR048

column1: Your efforts to train the earthshakers as beasts of burden have been successful! They can pull carts laden with goods as if they weighed nothing at all. They quickly and accurately plow deep furrows. They’ve also become quite skillful at nosing boulders out of land your carls are clearing.
column2: 你将地动者训练成驮兽的努力成功了！它们能拉动满载货物的货车，仿佛毫无重量。它们快速而精准地犁出深沟。它们还非常擅长将你们的自由民正在清理的土地上的巨石用鼻子拱开。

column1: Our efforts to train the earthshakers as beasts of burden proved successful.
column2: 我们将地动者训练成驮兽的努力证明是成功的。

column1: Change your clan name from \x01@" to “Earthshaker”
column2: 将你们的氏族名从 \x01@" 改为“地动者”

column1: From that day forward, we were known as the Earthshaker Clan.
column2: 从那天起，我们被称为地动者氏族。

column1: Earthshaker
column2: 地动者

column1: Earthshakers
column2: 地动者

column1: It was a little hard to tell, given their grim demeanor, but they seemed pleased with our gift.
column2: 鉴于他们严峻的神情，有点难以判断，但他们似乎对我们的礼物感到满意。

column1: The ducks
column2: 鸭人

column1: Keep them.
column2: 留下它们。

column1: The god-talkers said that Maran Gor was pleased that we returned her beasts.
column2: 神言者说玛拉·戈尔对我们归还她的巨兽感到高兴。

column1: There was no way to tell if Malia was pleased with the sacrifice, but our ancestors were outraged.
column2: 无从判断玛利亚是否对献祭满意，但我们的祖先感到愤怒。

column1: Everyone could tell that \x01@\x07 was happy with the sacrifice.
column2: 所有人都看得出来 \x01@\x07 对献祭感到满意。

column1: They would not buy the earthshakers.
column2: 他们不愿购买地动者。

column1: I think the earthshakers will live for sixty years.
column2: 我认为地动者能活六十年。

column1: I think the earthshakers will live for thirty years, give or take.
column2: 我认为地动者能活三十年左右。

column1: We should have trained them as war mounts.
column2: 我们本应该把它们训练成战骑。

column1: These creatures are holy to Ernalda’s violent sister, Maran Gor. Because we have tamed them, her priestesses may not want them.
column2: 这些生物是埃娜尔达的暴戾姐妹玛拉·戈尔的圣物。因为我们驯服了它们，她的女祭司可能不想要它们了。

column1: We must keep them, of course.
column2: 我们当然必须留下它们。

column1: The most famous clans are those with legendary names. These creatures can make us the Earthshakers, and we will be remembered forever.
column2: 最著名的氏族都有传奇性的名字。这些生物能让我们成为地动者，我们将永世铭记。

column1: Surely there are books that advise one on the best way to use domesticated earthshakers
column2: 肯定有书册指导人们如何最好地使用驯化的地动者。

column1: These beasts will bring us status within our tribe.
column2: 这些巨兽将提升我们在部落中的地位。

column1: These things eat plants, yes? We can bring captured plant-folk back here, and the earth beasts will dispose of them.
column2: 这些家伙吃植物，对吧？我们可以把抓到的植物人带回来，地兽会处理掉它们。

column1: It is good to keep them if we have much land to clear. Otherwise, it is better to get peace, silver, or the gods’ favor.
column2: 如果我们有大片土地需要清理，留着它们很好。否则，不如换取和平、白银或神明的恩宠。

column1: I have penetrated the secret of Gronan’s Rites of Kingship!
column2: 我已洞悉格罗南的王权仪式的秘密！

column1: “Earth cures drunkenness; plunge-wort cures worms. Barley soaks up bad magic.” Hmm, I’ve forgotten what oak is supposed to do.
column2: “泥土治醉酒；浸草治虫疾。大麦吸收坏魔法。”嗯，我忘了橡木是用来做什么的。

column1: Earth-beasts plucked the hurt-stones from all-Mother’s side.
column2: 地兽从万物之母的身侧拔出了伤痛之石。

column1: sceneR049
column2: sceneR049

column1: A small squad of magically mighty warriors from Tarsh launches a sneak raid against you, in an attempt to rescue Illator. They succeed, and many of your people are killed or wounded.
column2: 一小队来自塔什的魔法强兵突袭了我们，企图营救伊拉托。他们成功了，我们许多人死伤。

column1: Mighty raiders of Tarsh rescued Illator, killing many of our people in so doing.
column2: 塔什的强大袭击者救走了伊拉托，并在此过程中杀死了我们许多人。

column1: At least they didn’t take our cattle!
column2: 至少他们没抢走我们的牛只！

column1: Too late for ransom now.
column2: 现在要赎金已经太迟了。

column1: If we had more weaponthanes on patrol, this wouldn’t have happened.
column2: 要是我们有更多武器领主在巡逻，就不会发生这种事。

column1: The Tarshites went to a lot of trouble for this one man, trouble that is now ours.
column2: 塔什人为这一个人费了这么大的周折，如今这周折轮到我们头上了。

column1: The Tarshites showed loyalty to their own, and should be admired for it.
column2: 塔什人对他们自己的人展现了忠诚，这一点值得敬佩。

column1: There were several wind lords in the rescue party. It’s no wonder they were able to rescue Illator.
column2: 救援队里有好几个风领主。难怪他们能救走伊拉托。

column1: We should have killed him in the first place.
column2: 我们一开始就该杀了他。

column1: I admire their courage.
column2: 我敬佩他们的勇气。

column1: There’s not much we can do about this now.
column2: 现在我们对此也做不了什么。

column1: And I had lined up a lovely and talented young woman to marry Illator…
column2: 我还给伊拉托物色了一位可爱又有才华的年轻姑娘成婚……

column1: This wouldn’t have happened if Illator had been turned over to the women to guard.
column2: 要是当初把伊拉托交给女人看守，就不会发生这事。

column1: Humakt’s birds now feed, after the birds of the north freed their caged brother.
column2: 北方的飞鸟解救了它们笼中的兄弟，如今胡马克特的飞鸟得以饱餐。

column1: And we treated Illator almost as well as an honored guest…
column2: 我们几乎把伊拉托当作贵客款待……

column1: There’s no way we can track them down — the wind lords will be able to fly them all away.
column2: 我们不可能追上他们——风领主会带着所有人飞走。

column1: I told you keeping Illator hostage would be nothing but trouble.
column2: 我告诉过你，扣押伊拉托当人质只会招来麻烦。

column1: Story over.
column2: 故事到此为止。

column1: I admire their tactics, and would love to go up against them again someday.
column2: 我钦佩他们的战术，真想有朝一日再跟他们较量一番。

column1: Another band of Tarshite warriors attacks us, trying to rescue Illator. Again, they wound and kill our people, though the battle ends with Illator still in our custody.
column2: 又一队塔什武士袭击我们，企图营救伊拉托。他们再次杀伤我们的人，但战斗结束时伊拉托仍在我们手中。

column1: Once again raiders from Tarsh attacked and killed many of our people. They failed to rescue our Tarshite hostage, Illator.
column2: 塔什的袭击者又一次来袭，杀死了我们许多人。他们未能救出我们的人质伊拉托。

column1: A small but magically mighty squad of warriors from Tarsh launches a sneak raid against you, in an attempt to rescue Illator. Although many of your people are wounded, and some are killed, you drive the raiders back. Illator is still in your custody.
column2: 一小队来自塔什的魔法强兵突袭了我们，企图营救伊拉托。尽管我们许多人受伤，有些人阵亡，但我们击退了袭击者。伊拉托仍在我们手中。

column1: Mighty raiders of Tarsh attacked, killing many of our people in so doing. They did not succeed in their objective, which was rescuing our Tarshite hostage, Illator.
column2: 塔什的强大袭击者来袭，并在此过程中杀死了我们许多人。但他们未能达成目标——营救我们的人质伊拉托。

column1: Keep Illator in custody.
column2: 继续扣押伊拉托。

column1: Kill Illator and send word to his people that you’ve done it.
column2: 杀死伊拉托，并传话给他的族人你已经这么做了。

column1: We killed Illator and sent word to his people that there they no longer had anyone to rescue.
column2: 我们杀死了伊拉托，并传话给他的族人：他们再也没有人可以营救了。

column1: Let Illator go.
column2: 放走伊拉托。

column1: Not wishing to risk another attack, we released the prisoner.
column2: 不愿再冒被袭击的风险，我们释放了俘虏。

column1: Illator seemed amused by our decision. There was no denying his bravery.
column2: 伊拉托似乎对我们的决定感到好笑。他的勇气无可否认。

column1: Offer custody of Illator to another clan.
column2: 把伊拉托的监护权交给另一个部族。

column1: Which clan do you trade him to?
column2: 你把他交给哪个部族？

column1: What is the minimum amount of wealth you will accept for his ransom rights?
column2: 你愿意为赎他换来的权利接受的最低财富是多少？

column1: 5 cows
column2: 5头牛

column1: They offer you only \x01@\x03 cows worth of goods instead.
column2: 他们只愿意给你价值 \x01@\x03 头牛的东西。

column1: Do you settle for this amount?
column2: 你接受这个数目吗？

column1: They bargained shrewdly, but we settled for what they offered us.
column2: 他们讨价还价很精明，但我们接受了他们的出价。

column1: We could not agree on a fair ransom.
column2: 我们未能就合理的赎金达成一致。

column1: Ransom Illator.
column2: 赎走伊拉托。

column1: We parleyed with his people and made a ransom offer.
column2: 我们与他的族人谈判，提出了赎金条件。

column1: What is the minimum ransom you will accept?
column2: 你愿意接受的最低赎金是多少？

column1: 10 cows worth of goods
column2: 价值10头牛的货物

column1: 20 cows worth of goods
column2: 价值20头牛的货物

column1: 30 cows worth of goods
column2: 价值30头牛的货物

column1: They gave us a fair ransom.
column2: 他们给了我们一笔公平的赎金。

column1: If they are willing to send weaponthanes to rescue him, perhaps they are willing to pay for him.
column2: 如果他们愿意派武器领主来救他，或许他们也愿意为他出钱。

column1: Let him go. We made our point, and can now afford to act generously.
column2: 放他走吧。我们已经表明了态度，现在不妨表现得大度一些。

column1: I dimly remember something about using a third party to keep the hostage and negotiate a release…
column2: 我隐约记得关于利用第三方扣押人质并谈判释放的事……

column1: When a hostage is held and blood has been spilled, we can offer ransom-rights to another clan. The other clan then negotiates ransom, and cool heads win out.
column2: 当人质被扣押且已有流血事件，我们可以把赎金权交给另一个部族。由那个部族去谈判赎金，冷静的头脑能解决问题。

column1: When a hostage is held and blood spilled, we can offer ransom-rights to another clan. The other clan then negotiates ransom, and both parties owe it an obligation for its services.
column2: 当人质被扣押且已有流血事件，我们可以把赎金权交给另一个部族。那个部族随后谈判赎金，双方都欠它一份人情。

column1: We might improve our relations with the \x01@a clan by offering them his ransom-rights.
column2: 我们可以把赎金权交给 \x01@a 部族，以改善与他们的关系。

column1: Illator’s rescue party includes several wind lords. We were lucky to survive their onslaught this time.
column2: 伊拉托的救援队里有好几个风领主。这次我们能在他们的猛攻下幸存算走运了。

column1: It was only luck that let us \x02\x03drive off/stand up to/win against\x02 the Tarshites again. If they keep attacking, then we will lose, sooner or later.
column2: 我们这回能 \x02\x03击退/抵挡/战胜\x02 塔什人，纯粹靠运气。如果他们继续进攻，我们迟早会输。

column1: We fought them off once; we can do it again.
column2: 我们击退过他们一次，就能再击退一次。

column1: When will they \x02\x03realize/learn/admit\x02 they will not win against our mighty warriors?
column2: 他们什么时候才能 \x02\x03明白/学会/承认\x02 自己赢不了我们强大的武士？

column1: Kill him; he’s more trouble than he’s worth.
column2: 杀了他，他带来的麻烦多过他的价值。

column1: Killing a hostage will blacken our reputation throughout Dragon Pass.
column2: 杀死人质会让我们在整个龙之隘口名声扫地。

column1: Even though \x02\x03we took losses too/we suffered deaths too/we are counting our dead and wounded\x02, to kill a hostage like this will win us no favor with the other clans.
column2: 尽管 \x02\x03我们也损失惨重/我们也有人战死/我们正在清点死伤\x02，但这样杀死人质不会赢得其他部族的好感。

column1: The Tarshites are showing loyalty to their own, and should be admired for it.
column2: 塔什人对自己人展现了忠诚，这一点值得敬佩。

column1: These Tarshites surely are a \x02\x03determined/stubborn/loyal\x02 lot, aren’t they?
column2: 这些塔什人确实是一群 \x02\x03坚定/顽固/忠诚\x02 的家伙，不是吗？

column1: The hall is full of wounded. Let’s have no more carnage.
column2: 大厅里满是伤员。别再制造屠杀了。

column1: Once more our hall is full of the bleeding and maimed. Enough blood!
column2: 我们的厅堂再次挤满了流血和伤残的人。血够了！

column1: Is one hostage worth all this grief and sorrow?
column2: 一个人质值得这一切悲伤和痛苦吗？

column1: Let him go.
column2: 放他走。

column1: No one will start a tribe with us if we have enemies as powerful as this.
column2: 如果我们有如此强大的敌人，没有人愿意和我们建立氏族。

column1: If we get the tribe into a war with Tarsh, they’ll be the devil to pay at the next moot.
column2: 如果我们让部族卷入与塔什的战争，下次集会时他们会有大麻烦。

column1: The tribe will not want to be involved in this. It is \x02\x03ours alone to solve/our problem and only ours/up to us to act\x02.
column2: 部族不想卷入此事。这 \x02\x03只能由我们解决/是我们的问题，仅属于我们/取决于我们行动\x02。

column1: They’re bound to succeed sooner or later.
column2: 他们迟早一定会成功。

column1: It is only a matter of time before we are too weak to repel them.
column2: 我们变得太弱无法击退他们只是时间问题。

column1: Doom. Our doom, at the hands of the Tarshites.
column2: 厄运。我们的厄运，来自塔什人之手。

column1: I’ve never felt so alive as during that battle. Our combat prowess will surely improve if we continue to test our selves against them.
column2: 我从未像在那场战斗中那样感觉如此鲜活。如果继续与他们较量，我们的战斗技能肯定会提高。

column1: The Tarshites are worthy opponents, but getting a little predictable. Let Illator go, or ransom him, or something, so we can go out and find new foes!
column2: 塔什人是有价值的对手，但变得有点可预测了。放了伊拉托，或者要他赎金什么的，这样我们就能出去找新敌人了！

column1: These Tarshites must follow the wrong ways of worship, to be so cruel. Orlanth will be offended if we give in.
column2: 这些塔什人一定信奉了错误的崇拜方式才会如此残忍。如果我们屈服，奥兰斯会感到冒犯。

column1: We should question Illator closely, and learn the Tarshite battle magic.
column2: 我们应该仔细审问伊拉托，学习塔什人的战斗魔法。

column1: Their foreign worship gives them strengths we don’t know. Get rid of this Illator, and devote our time to learning more battle magic from our own gods.
column2: 他们的异教崇拜给了我们不知道的力量。处理掉这个伊拉托，把时间用来向我们自己的神学习更多的战斗魔法。

column1: Over the past few days, there have been several unsettling events. First Jarnesta cut into a cheese, and it bled. Then all of Korlmast’s cattle lost their horns.
column2: 过去几天发生了几件令人不安的事。先是贾内斯塔切奶酪时，奶酪流血了。然后科马斯特所有的牛都失去了角。

column1: Now \x01@\x03 has taken ill. \x05 has trouble breathing, as if Orlanth himself has cursed \x08, and \x06 keeps seeing the face of Illator of Tarsh.
column2: 现在 \x01@\x03 病倒了。 \x05 呼吸困难，仿佛奥兰斯本人诅咒了 \x08，而 \x06 一直看到塔什的伊拉托的脸。

column1: I cannot say if this is Illator’s curse, or a sending from his kinsmen in Tarsh. It was a mistake to kill an emissary to whom we’d given hospitality.
column2: 我说不清这是伊拉托的诅咒，还是他塔什亲属的派遣。杀死一个我们曾给予好客的使者是个错误。

column1: We god-talkers will deal with the curse as best we can.
column2: 我们神言者会尽力处理这个诅咒。

column1: sceneR050
column2: sceneR050

column1: Illator is back, with the cows you demanded of him. “I have driven these down all the way from Tarsh, because I am a man of my word,” he gasps. “Some of them died, and others are in bad condition. Take them, you stubborn rustics.” There are \x01@\x03 cows in the herd.
column2: 伊拉托回来了，带着你向他索要的牛。“我把这些牛一路从塔什赶下来，因为我是一个信守诺言的人，”他气喘吁吁地说。“有些死了，其他的状况很差。拿去吧，你们这些顽固的乡下人。”牛群中有 \x01@\x03 头牛。

column1: Illator of Tarsh finally brought us the cows he promised.
column2: 塔什的伊拉托终于给我们带来了他承诺的牛。

column1: Accept the cows; use healing magics on them.
column2: 接受牛；对它们施治疗魔法。

column1: We cast healing spells on the cows, so they would not die after their long journey.
column2: 我们对牛施了治疗法术，这样它们长途跋涉后就不会死。

column1: The magic of the god-talkers of Uralda saved the cows that had almost died in Illator’s care.
column2: 乌拉尔达神言者的魔法拯救了那些在伊拉托照料下几乎死去的牛。

column1: Despite our spells, some cows died shortly after Illator’s departure.
column2: 尽管我们施了法术，一些牛还是在伊拉托离开后不久就死了。

column1: Accept the cows; demand an apology for the “stubborn rustics” remark.
column2: 接受牛；要求为“顽固的乡下人”的言论道歉。

column1: We took the cows, but he made rude remarks to us, and we demanded satisfaction.
column2: 我们收了牛，但他对我们说了粗鲁的话，我们要求得到满意答复。

column1: Through gritted teeth he said, “You are correct. Neither ‘stubborn’ nor ‘rustic’ are the right words to describe you people.” Fortunately, honor is satisfied by an apology whether it is sincere or not, so we allowed him to depart unmolested.
column2: 他咬着牙说：“你们是对的。‘顽固’和‘乡下人’都不是描述你们这群人的恰当词语。”幸运的是，无论道歉是否真诚，荣誉都得到了满足，所以我们允许他平安离开。

column1: Half of the cows died shortly after Illator’s departure.
column2: 一半的牛在伊拉托离开后不久就死了。

column1: Illator was offended, and demanded a duel of honor.
column2: 伊拉托被冒犯了，要求进行荣誉决斗。

column1: Illator turns red and begins to shake. “You demand an apology? By Orlanth’s slicing blades, it is I who have been dishonored here! Appoint a champion, and we shall settle this matter on the duelling field!”
column2: 伊拉托脸色涨红，开始颤抖。“你们要求道歉？凭奥兰斯的利刃，是我在这里受辱！指定一个冠军，我们将在决斗场上解决此事！”

column1: Apologize to Illator
column2: 向伊拉托道歉

column1: To satisfy his honor, we withdrew our insult.
column2: 为了满足他的荣誉，我们收回了侮辱。

column1: Illator was satisfied, and left.
column2: 伊拉托满意了，然后离开了。

column1: Illator would not withdraw his demand for a duel.
column2: 伊拉托不肯撤回决斗要求。

column1: Designate \x01@\x0E as your champion.
column2: 指定 \x01@\x0E 为你的冠军。

column1: Designate a weaponthane as your champion.
column2: 指定一名武器侍卫为你的冠军。

column1: Accept the cows; lay on a feast in his honor.
column2: 接受牛；设宴款待他。

column1: We feasted in Illator’s honor.
column2: 我们设宴款待伊拉托。

column1: Although he was distant at first, our fine ale eventually loosened the line of Illator’s shoulders. He told us many wondrous stories of the Kingdom of Tarsh and its campaigns against the cruel Lunar Empire.
column2: 虽然起初他有些疏远，但我们上好的麦酒最终让伊拉托的肩膀放松下来。他给我们讲了许多关于塔什王国及其对抗残暴月之帝国的战役的奇妙故事。

column1: Demand healthy cows, not sickly ones.
column2: 要求健康的牛，而不是有病的。

column1: We demanded that he supply us with healthy cows, not sickly ones. He was offended, and demanded a duel to satisfy his honor.
column2: 我们要求他提供健康的牛，而不是有病的。他被冒犯了，要求进行荣誉决斗。

column1: Illator turns red and begins to shake. “I warned you that I would not be responsible for the condition of the cows! By Orlanth’s slicing blades, you have played me for a fool. Dishonored me! Appoint a champion, and we shall settle this matter on the duelling field!”
column2: 伊拉托脸色涨红，开始颤抖。“我警告过你们，我不会对牛的状况负责！凭奥兰斯的利刃，你们把我当傻子耍了。侮辱了我！指定一个冠军，我们将在决斗场上解决此事！”

column1: Demand more cows.
column2: 要求更多牛。

column1: We told him that the number of cows he brought us was insufficient.
column2: 我们告诉他，他带来的牛数量不够。

column1: Illator turns red and begins to shake. “Insufficient? Insufficient? I dragged these wretched beasts across the whole of Dragon Pass, and you have the temerity to ask for more? By Orlanth’s slicing blades, you have played me for a fool. Dishonored me! Appoint a champion, and we shall settle this matter on the duelling field!”
column2: 伊拉托涨红了脸，开始颤抖。“不够？不够？我拖着这些该死的畜生穿越了整个龙隘，你竟敢还要更多？以奥兰斯那切割之刃起誓，你把我当傻瓜耍了。让我蒙羞！派个勇士出来，我们在决斗场上解决这事！”

column1: In a ferocious fight, \x01@\x0E slew Illator.
column2: 在一场激烈的战斗中， \x01@\x0E 杀死了伊拉托。

column1: Half of the cows died shortly after Illator’s death.
column2: 伊拉托死后不久，一半的牛死了。

column1: In a single blow, Illator’s wind-howling sword split \x01@\x0E from skull to groin.
column2: 只一击，伊拉托那呼啸风剑就从颅顶到腹股沟劈开了 \x01@\x0E 。

column1: In a ferocious fight, \x01@\x08 slew Illator.
column2: 在一场激烈的战斗中， \x01@\x08 杀死了伊拉托。

column1: In a single blow, Illator’s wind-howling sword split \x01@\x08 from skull to groin.
column2: 只一击，伊拉托那呼啸风剑就从颅顶到腹股沟劈开了 \x01@\x08 。

column1: The cows are fine. They just need water, rest, and a bit of hay.
column2: 牛没事。它们只需要水、休息和一点干草。

column1: Illator is right; not all of those cows are healthy.
column2: 伊拉托是对的；那些牛并非全都健康。

column1: Without immediate attention, some of those cows will die.
column2: 如果不立刻处理，有些牛会死。

column1: Without immediate attention, half of those cows will die.
column2: 如果不立刻处理，一半的牛会死。

column1: We should have taken those round silver bits, I tell you.
column2: 我告诉你，我们本该收那些圆银币的。

column1: Don’t forget that, tired or not, Illator is a mighty Wind Lord.
column2: 别忘了，不管疲不疲惫，伊拉托可是个强大的风主。

column1: I can take him, if the need arises.
column2: 如果需要，我能对付他。

column1: Illator is a man of high rank in a great kingdom, and a warrior of renown. He is used to being treated with great respect.
column2: 伊拉托是一个伟大王国里的高爵之人，也是著名的战士。他习惯了被极大尊重地对待。

column1: Our magic is weak; healing spells on the cattle may be pointless.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱；对牛群施治愈术可能毫无意义。

column1: Our magic is strong; healing spells on the cattle will likely work.
column2: 我们的魔法很强；对牛群施治愈术很可能会奏效。

column1: This is a time for women’s wisdom, not men’s wisdom.
column2: 这是该用女性智慧的时候，而不是男性智慧。

column1: You’d better not be planning to use those mangy foreign cattle as a dowry.
column2: 你最好别打算用那些肮脏的外来牛当作嫁妆。

column1: I told you we should never have sent warriors to someone else’s war.
column2: 我告诉过你我们绝不该派战士去打别人的仗。

column1: I hear our neighbors to the south took silver bits for the warriors they sent to Tarsh, and have traded them for a piece of kingly regalia.
column2: 我听说我们南方的邻居为派往塔什的战士收了银币，并用它们换了一件王权神器。

column1: Orlanth’s-thane was road-drunk; exhaustion, his mead; ire, his brother.
column2: 奥兰斯之侍从沉醉于路途；疲惫是他的蜜酒，怒火是他的兄弟。

column1: I can fight if need be, but we cannot say he did not warn us.
column2: 必要时我可以战斗，但我们不能说他没有警告过我们。

column1: sceneR051
column2: sceneR051

column1: Argue that Orlmar is innocent.
column2: 主张奥尔马无罪。

column1: Do you distribute gifts among the ring members of the other clans?
column2: 你向其他氏族的环成员分发礼物吗？

column1: How much do you give to the other clans?
column2: 你给其他氏族多少？

column1: Do your warriors make a war-whooping display to show their support for your case?
column2: 你的战士们是否以战吼示威来支持你的诉讼？

column1: How many of them do so?
column2: 有多少人这样做？

column1: We disputed Orlmar’s guilt.
column2: 我们质疑奥尔马有罪。

column1: The moot decided that Orlmar was not guilty.
column2: 议会裁定奥尔马无罪。

column1: We did have to pay court costs.
column2: 我们确实必须支付诉讼费用。

column1: We were ordered to pay Eindgar Buttered-Bread’s inflated wergild.
column2: 我们被命令支付埃因加·黄油面包虚高的血偿金。

column1: Argue that you should pay, but less than what they ask.
column2: 主张你应该支付，但少于他们要求的数额。

column1: We conceded Orlmar’s guilt, but disputed the amount of compensation.
column2: 我们承认奥尔马有罪，但就赔偿金额提出异议。

column1: We won a
column2: 我们获得了

column1: substantial
column2: 大幅度的

column1: reduction in the wergild.
column2: 血偿金的削减。

column1: We were ordered to pay what Brandgor had originally asked of us.
column2: 我们被命令支付布兰德戈尔最初向我们索要的数额。

column1: Encourage chiefs of other clans to pressure Eindgar.
column2: 鼓动其他氏族的首领向埃因加施压。

column1: Do you give gifts to the chiefs of the other clans?
column2: 你向其他氏族的首领赠送礼物吗？

column1: How much do you give to the other chiefs?
column2: 你给其他首领多少？

column1: The other chiefs agreed to help our case.
column2: 其他首领同意帮助我们打这场官司。

column1: The other chiefs turned their backs on \x01@\x03.
column2: 其他首领背弃了 \x01@\x03。

column1: Remind other clans of their obligations to you.
column2: 提醒其他氏族他们对你的义务。

column1: Before the case was heard, we reminded other clans of all we had done for them.
column2: 在案件审理之前，我们提醒其他氏族我们为他们所做的一切。

column1: Settle for 40 cows before the case is heard.
column2: 在案件审理前以40头牛和解。

column1: We settled the case.
column2: 我们了结了此案。

column1: They agreed to settle out of court.
column2: 他们同意庭外和解。

column1: We can afford whatever wergild Eindgar demands.
column2: 无论埃因加要求多少血偿金，我们都付得起。

column1: The loss of a single cow is a grave blow to us.
column2: 损失一头牛对我们来说都是沉重打击。

column1: Now that they’ve been forced to the moot, they won’t settle for less than their new demand.
column2: 既然他们已被迫来到议会，他们不会接受低于新要求的和解。

column1: Hend provoked Orlmar; we don’t owe them so much as a cow hoof, let alone a cow.
column2: 亨德挑衅了奥尔马；我们连一只牛蹄子都不欠他们，更别说一头牛了。

column1: A young warrior of his rank is due a wergeld of 20 cows; Eindgar has increased the price because we forced this matter to the moot.
column2: 他这个等级的年轻武士应得20头牛的血偿金；埃因加提高了价格，因为我们把这件事闹到了议会。

column1: A young warrior of his rank is due a wergeld of 20 cows. However, Orlmar and his brother suffered compensating injuries in the incident, worth about 10 cows.
column2: 他这个等级的年轻武士应得20头牛的血偿金。然而，奥尔马和他的兄弟在此事件中也遭受了相应伤害，价值约10头牛。

column1: We have enough influence with the other chiefs to aid our cause, if we do not overplay our hand.
column2: 如果我们不过分炫耀，我们在其他首领面前有足够的影响力来帮助我们的事业。

column1: We owe the other clans more than they owe us. An attempt to sway things behind the scenes will probably hurt us.
column2: 我们欠其他氏族的比他们欠我们的多。试图在幕后左右局势很可能会伤害我们。

column1: We should never have let Orlmar outside the tula without his mother at his side.
column2: 我们本就不该让奥尔马在没有母亲陪伴的情况下离开图拉领地。

column1: Forty cows? That accursed Eindgar aims to break us!
column2: 四十头牛？那个该死的艾因德加想搞垮我们！

column1: We know that Orlmar did it; it would be wrong to argue otherwise.
column2: 我们知道是奥尔马干的；否认这一点是不对的。

column1: Our jabbering will not alter the verdict.
column2: 我们喋喋不休也改变不了裁决。

column1: After the case is over with, we must propose a treaty with the dragonewts.
column2: 案件结束后，我们必须提议与龙人缔结条约。

column1: The moot should pass a law that says all thanes must learn to read and write.
column2: 议会应通过一项法律，规定所有领主必须学会读写。

column1: This might have been cheaper if we’d settled earlier…
column2: 要是我们早点儿定居下来，也许会更便宜……

column1: sceneR052
column2: sceneR052

column1: A delegation of Beastfolk come to your clan to warn that you have gravely offended their people. “If you harm us any further, you will suffer,” says their leader, a Centaur. “Ironhoof will come back,” snorts their minotaur war leader. “And if that happens, you will surely be destroyed,” quacks their duck ally.
column2: 一群兽人使者来到你的部族，警告你们严重冒犯了他们的族人。“如果你们再伤害我们，你们就会遭殃。”他们的领袖，一位半人马说道。“铁蹄会回来的。”他们的牛头人战争领袖哼着鼻子说。“如果那样，你们肯定会被摧毁。”他们的鸭人盟友嘎嘎地说。

column1: A delegation of Beastfolk came to us and warned us that Ironhoof would come back if we offended them further.
column2: 一群兽人使者来到我们这里，警告我们说，如果我们再冒犯他们，铁蹄就会回来。

column1: We asked them to leave, and they did.
column2: 我们请他们离开，他们照做了。

column1: They did, but said we should remember their words carefully.
column2: 他们走了，但说我们应该仔细记住他们的话。

column1: Listen to them, but make no commitments.
column2: 倾听他们，但不要做出任何承诺。

column1: After we heard out their litany of complaints, they left.
column2: 在我们听完他们的一长串抱怨后，他们离开了。

column1: Offer them compensation.
column2: 向他们提供补偿。

column1: We offered them compensation.
column2: 我们向他们提供了补偿。

column1: Do you offer them:
column2: 你是否向他们提供：

column1: wealth
column2: 财富

column1: magical treasure
column2: 魔法宝物

column1: What treasures do you offer?
column2: 你提供什么宝物？

column1: We paid them a handsome settlement. The centaur told us that this was but a step on the road to peace between our peoples.
column2: 我们向他们支付了一笔可观的赔偿。半人马告诉我们，这仅仅是我们两族和平之路上的一步。

column1: The centaur told us that our payment to them was but a small step on the road to peace between our peoples.
column2: 半人马告诉我们，我们给他们的赔偿仅仅是我们两族和平之路上的小小一步。

column1: Then they departed.
column2: 然后他们就离开了。

column1: Promise not to offend them any further.
column2: 承诺不再冒犯他们。

column1: We promised not to offend them further.
column2: 我们承诺不再冒犯他们。

column1: They said we were saying the right words, but that only actions would ease their suspicions.
column2: 他们说我们说的话没错，但只有行动才能减轻他们的疑虑。

column1: Take them hostage.
column2: 扣押他们作为人质。

column1: We decided to take them hostage.
column2: 我们决定扣押他们作为人质。

column1: They fought furiously, with powerful magics. The duck was slain, but the centaur and minotaur became our prisoners.
column2: 他们激烈反抗，使用了强大的魔法。鸭人被杀死，但半人马和牛头人成了我们的囚犯。

column1: They fought furiously, with powerful magics. They slew many, including \x01@\x0E, before escaping.
column2: 他们激烈反抗，使用了强大的魔法。他们杀死了许多人，包括 \x01@\x0E，然后逃脱了。

column1: How much do you give to them?
column2: 你给他们多少？

column1: We paid them a handsome settlement.
column2: 我们向他们支付了一笔可观的赔偿。

column1: The centaur told us that our payment to them was but a small step on the road to peace between our peoples. Then they departed.
column2: 半人马告诉我们，我们给他们的赔偿仅仅是我们两族和平之路上的小小一步。然后他们就离开了。

column1: “War is made with bronze; peace is made with silver.”
column2: “战争靠青铜；和平靠白银。”

column1: Silver is good; treasures are better.
column2: 白银不错；宝物更好。

column1: If we want to avoid a war with a foe of unknown power, I’d offer sixty to eighty cows, or better yet, a treasure or two.
column2: 如果我们想避免与一个实力不明的敌人开战，我会提供六十到八十头牛，或者更好，一两件宝物。

column1: The ducks are Orlanthi, and follow a version of our laws. The other Beastfolk are complete strangers to our ways.
column2: 鸭人是奥兰迪人，遵循我们法律的一种变体。其他兽人则完全不了解我们的习俗。

column1: This Ironhoof is a legendary hero. We don’t want to invoke his wrath.
column2: 这个铁蹄是传说中的英雄。我们不想招致他的愤怒。

column1: Our neighbors are unlikely to aid us if we start a war with the beastfolk.
column2: 如果我们与兽人开战，我们的邻居不太可能帮助我们。

column1: These emissaries bristle with powerful magics.
column2: 这些使者浑身散发着强大的魔法。

column1: Because the beastfolk are our ancient enemies, giving in to them weakens our clan’s magic.
column2: 因为兽人是我们的宿敌，向他们让步会削弱我们部族的魔法。

column1: From the day that Ukkar Gra the Basmoli King first attacked our clan, the beastfolk have been our foes.
column2: 自从乌卡尔·格拉·巴索利王第一次攻击我们部族那天起，兽人就成了我们的敌人。

column1: We’re on the brink of disaster. We must disband the clan, so that those innocent of offenses against the beastfolk do not suffer with the guilty.
column2: 我们处于灾难边缘。我们必须解散部族，这样那些没有冒犯兽人的无辜者就不会与有罪者一起受苦。

column1: We must make a gesture of peace, or die. A genuine, generous gesture.
column2: 我们必须做出和平的姿态，否则就是死亡。一个真诚、慷慨的姿态。

column1: We can’t trust these strangers not to attack us even if we do pay them compensation. Better to spend our resources on temples, and trust to Orlanth to protect us.
column2: 我们不能相信这些陌生人即使我们支付了赔偿也不会攻击我们。最好把资源花在神庙上，依靠奥兰斯来保护我们。

column1: We can always breed more cows, but if we give away treasures, we’ll never regain them.
column2: 我们总能繁殖更多的牛，但如果送出了宝物，就再也拿不回来了。

column1: A war with the beastfolk will bring ruination upon this land. That doesn’t mean we must consider ourselves beneath them.
column2: 与兽人的战争会给这片土地带来毁灭。但这并不意味着我们必须认为自己比他们低贱。

column1: The tribe will not be happy until we settle this dispute with the beastfolk.
column2: 直到我们解决与兽人的争端，部落才会满意。

column1: sceneR053
column2: sceneR053

column1: As the beastfolk emissaries warned you, the beastfolk have risen up against your clan.
column2: 正如兽人使者警告你的那样，兽人已经起来反抗你的部族。

column1: Your constant harassment of the ducks has come to its fruition. The beastfolk have risen up against your clan.
column2: 你对鸭人的持续骚扰终于有了结果。兽人已经起来反抗你的部族。

column1: Bringing a huge force of ducks, minotaurs, and centaurs against you, supported by fox people and wasp people, they virtually destroy your clan. Almost all of your combatants are dead. Half of your non-combatants were slain or were taken as thralls. The victorious beastfolk destroyed your fortifications, drove off most of your livestock, and looted your steads and clan hall.
column2: 他们带来了一支由鸭人、牛头人和半人马组成的庞大军队，并得到狐人和黄蜂人的支援，几乎摧毁了你的部族。你的作战人员几乎全部阵亡。一半的非作战人员被杀或被俘为奴隶。获胜的兽人摧毁了你的防御工事，赶走了你的大部分牲畜，并洗劫了你的农庄和部族大厅。

column1: The entire ring, including the chief, died fighting the mighty army of beast warriors. In short, the future looks bleak for your clan. Should the survivors to seek membership in other clans, or soldier on, despite impossible odds?
column2: 包括酋长在内的整个议会成员都战死于那支强大的兽战士大军。简而言之，你们部族的未来黯淡无光。幸存者应该寻求加入其他部族，还是不顾渺茫希望继续战斗？

column1: Many ring members were slain fighting the enormous army of beast warriors. In short, the future looks bleak for your clan. Should the survivors to seek membership in other clans, or soldier on, despite impossible odds?
column2: 许多议会成员都战死于那支庞大的兽战士大军。简而言之，你们部族的未来黯淡无光。幸存者应该寻求加入其他部族，还是不顾渺茫希望继续战斗？

column1: The beast folk army came, and almost everyone died. Almost everything was taken from us.
column2: 兽人大军来了，几乎所有人都死了。我们几乎失去了一切。

column1: Disband the clan.
column2: 解散部族。

column1: Soldier on, despite impossible odds.
column2: 不顾渺茫希望，继续战斗。

column1: Despite impossible odds, we decided to soldier on.
column2: 尽管希望渺茫，我们决定继续战斗。

column1: When the Great Darkness came, and everything was dead, Orlanth did not give up. He went to the Underworld, and rescued Ernalda and the sun.
column2: 当大黑暗降临，万物寂灭时，奥兰斯没有放弃。他前往冥界，救出了厄纳尔达和太阳。

column1: They took our livestock, our goods, and our stored food. But they could not take our land.
column2: 他们夺走了我们的牲畜、货物和储备的食物。但他们夺不走我们的土地。

column1: Sometimes you must admit that there is nothing in your purse. Release the survivors to join other clans.
column2: 有时你必须承认口袋里一无所有。释放幸存者去加入其他部族。

column1: We don’t even have enough elders to run a proper society.
column2: 我们甚至没有足够的长老来维持一个正常的社会。

column1: I’ll be all right. I’ll learn to fight with the other arm.
column2: 我会没事的。我会学着用另一只手臂战斗。

column1: I can survive without a clan. I can become a wandering warrior of Urox.
column2: 没有氏族我也能活下去。我可以成为一个流浪的尤罗克斯战士。

column1: We have fewer cows, but also fewer mouths to feed.
column2: 我们的牛少了，但吃饭的嘴也少了。

column1: In trying to trick the beastfolk, we tricked ourselves.
column2: 本想欺骗兽人，结果却骗了我们自己。

column1: Our clan does not deserve to continue; we failed to defend the hearth.
column2: 我们的氏族不配延续下去；我们没能守护好炉灶。

column1: I don’t want to give up, but we are incapable of defending ourselves from other clans now.
column2: 我不想放弃，但我们现在无力抵御其他氏族。

column1: sceneR054
column2: sceneR054

column1: Dragonewt emissaries appear at your clan hall to warn you to avoid offending them further. “We wish avoid entanglements your world,” the high-status lizard man croaks. “But make impossible. Any more worse, we make all die. Made all die before when offense too great. Will again, you not stop.”
column2: 龙人使者出现在你的部族大厅，警告你不要进一步冒犯他们。“我们不想纠缠你们的世界，”那个高位蜥蜴人嘶哑地说道。“但你们让我们不得不插手。再糟糕下去，我们就让所有人都死。以前冒犯太过分的时候，我们就杀光过所有人。还会再这么做，你们挡不住。”

column1: Dragonewts came and threatened us.
column2: 龙人来了，威胁了我们。

column1: Make no promises.
column2: 不要做出任何承诺。

column1: We made them no promises.
column2: 我们没有对他们做出任何承诺。

column1: They left without further speech.
column2: 他们没再多说就离开了。

column1: Offer them gifts as a token of apology.
column2: 送他们礼物以示歉意。

column1: The dragonewt flared its scales and hissed. “No! No entangle! Will not take obligation!”
column2: 龙人竖起鳞片嘶嘶作响。“不！别纠缠！不会接受义务！”

column1: We promised not to offend them any further.
column2: 我们承诺不再进一步冒犯他们。

column1: Threaten them in return.
column2: 反过来威胁他们。

column1: We matched their threats with some of our own.
column2: 我们用同样的威胁回应了他们。

column1: One of them flared its frill at us, but they left without saying anything further.
column2: 其中一个向我们张开了颈扇，但他们没再多说就离开了。

column1: Perform the heroquest where Issaries reconciles Long-Tooth and Long-Nose.
column2: 执行伊萨里斯调和长牙与长鼻的英雄任务。

column1: The dragonewts waited while we performed our heroquest, and then turned and walked off without further ado.
column2: 龙人等着我们执行完英雄任务，然后转身离开，没有多话。

column1: The dragonewts waited outside the tula until the quest was over. When they learned the results, they flared their nostrils and growled. Then they left.
column2: 龙人在图拉领地外等到任务结束。得知结果后，他们喷了喷鼻息，发出低吼，然后离开了。

column1: We can afford to pay them to leave us alone.
column2: 我们付得起钱让他们不再打扰我们。

column1: Keep the payment low; we have few cows.
column2: 赔偿金额要低；我们的牛不多。

column1: Dragonewts like wealth as well as a normal person.
column2: 龙人和普通人一样喜欢财富。

column1: Never trade with a dragonewt. He might follow you around for life, resenting you for giving him a sense of obligation.
column2: 绝不要跟龙人做交易。他可能一辈子跟着你，因为觉得你给了他义务感而怨恨你。

column1: The Dragonkill War is not named for what happened to the dragons. It is named for what the dragons did.
column2: 屠龙战争不是以龙遭受了什么命名的。而是以龙做了什么命名的。

column1: A million soldiers went to the Dragonkill War. Ten soldiers came back.
column2: 百万士兵参加了屠龙战争。只有十名士兵回来了。

column1: Perhaps the indirect approach of “Issaries Reconciles Long-Tooth and Long-Nose” is best.
column2: 也许“伊萨里斯调和长牙与长鼻”这个间接方法最好。

column1: Heroquesting might be dangerous right now.
column2: 眼下执行英雄任务可能有危险。

column1: There’s an Issaries quest that might help, but we don’t fully understand the myths.
column2: 有一个伊萨里斯任务或许有用，但我们不完全理解那些神话。

column1: In the underworld, Issaries found two ancient and forgotten gods. He made peace between them, where no peace had been before.
column2: 在冥界，伊萨里斯找到了两个古老而被遗忘的神。他让它们之间达成了前所未有的和平。

column1: Tell them they can expect swift deaths if they are so foolish as to attack us.
column2: 告诉他们，如果他们愚蠢到攻击我们，很快就是死路一条。

column1: We need five cows worth of silver, and can’t tell the men why. Women’s magic, you know.
column2: 我们需要价值五头牛的银子，但不能告诉男人们原因。女人的魔法，你懂的。

column1: Our trader can calm snake-weather.
column2: 我们的商人能平息蛇怒之灾。

column1: First the mountain-snakes hissed, then they spat death-fire. These hazel-bearers speak without forked tongue.
column2: 先是山蛇嘶嘶作响，然后它们喷出了死亡之火。这些榛木杖使者说话不假。

column1: Give them cows, not magical treasures.
column2: 给他们牛，而不是魔法宝物。

column1: “No one knows what is going to happen next season, so go ahead and sleep.”
column2: “没人知道下一季会发生什么，所以放心睡吧。”

column1: Make peace with them, so we can make war with the elves.
column2: 跟他们讲和，这样我们就能跟精灵开战。

column1: Our inevitable battle with the dragonewts will be remembered for centuries.
column2: 我们与龙人不可避免的这场战斗将被铭记数百年。

column1: I told you we should treat the dragonewts with great respect, but nobody listened.
column2: 我告诉过你们应该对龙人保持极大的尊重，但没人听。

column1: We may be the clan ring, but we can’t make promises on behalf of every person in the clan.
column2: 我们也许是氏族议会，但不能代表氏族中的每个人做出承诺。

column1: sceneR055
column2: sceneR055

column1: The dragonewt emissaries warned you that they would “make all die,” and now they make good on their threat. An army of dragonewts, assisted by wyrms and dinosaurs, overrun your tula, devouring every man, woman and beast they can lay their claws on. The only survivors of the horrific onslaught are those who flee and hide. Only one in ten clan members is left alive. Most of your livestock have been eaten. Your fortifications were heavily damaged in the initial attack. The only hint of consolation is that the dragonewts didn’t bother to loot your steads.
column2: 龙人使者曾警告过你，他们会“让所有人都死”，现在他们兑现了威胁。一支由龙人组成的军队，在亚龙和恐龙的协助下，攻占了你的图拉领地，吞噬了他们爪子能够到的每一个男人、女人和野兽。这场可怕袭击中唯一的幸存者是那些逃跑和躲藏起来的人。每十个氏族成员中只有一人活了下来。你的大部分牲畜都被吃掉了。你的防御工事在最初的攻击中遭到严重破坏。唯一令人欣慰的是，龙人没有费心掠夺你的农庄。

column1: The entire ring, including the chief, died fighting the enormous army of dragonewts. In short, the future looks bleak for your clan. Should the survivors seek membership in other clans, or soldier on, despite impossible odds?
column2: 包括酋长在内的整个议会成员都死于与巨大龙人军队的战斗。简而言之，你的氏族前途黯淡。幸存者应该寻求加入其他氏族，还是不顾一切困难继续奋战？

column1: Many ring members were slain fighting the enormous army of dragonewts. In short, the future looks bleak for your clan. Should the survivors seek membership in other clans, or soldier on, despite impossible odds?
column2: 许多议会成员在与巨大龙人军队的战斗中阵亡。简而言之，你的氏族前途黯淡。幸存者应该寻求加入其他氏族，还是不顾一切困难继续奋战？

column1: An army of dragonewts attacked us and killed nearly everyone.
column2: 一支龙人军队袭击了我们，几乎杀光了所有人。

column1: They have eaten our livestock, our parents, and our children. But they could not eat our land.
column2: 他们吃掉了我们的牲畜、我们的父母和我们的孩子。但他们吃不掉我们的土地。

column1: In trying to trick the dragonewts, we tricked ourselves.
column2: 本想欺骗龙人，结果却骗了我们自己。

column2: sceneR056

column1: Find out if another clan made the skirt.
column2: 查明是不是另一个氏族做了那条裙子。

column1: We tried to find out if another clan was responsible for the Chaos hex.
column2: 我们试图查明是不是另一个氏族对混沌咒负责。

column1: Which neighboring clan do you investigate?
column2: 你调查哪个邻族？

column1: The women all denied having made the skirt.
column2: 女人们都否认做过那条裙子。

column1: The women of \x01@! all denied having made the skirt.
column2: \x01@! 的女人们都否认做过那条裙子。

column1: Interrogate the women of the clan.
column2: 审讯该氏族的女人。

column1: We asked the women of our clan if any of them had made the skirt.
column2: 我们询问了氏族的妇女，是否有人做了那条裙子。

column1: We sacrificed to Chalana Arroy.
column2: 我们向查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭。

column1: The healers said the omens were favorable, but uncertain.
column2: 治疗者说预兆有利，但不确定。

column1: The healers said the omens were unfavorable.
column2: 治疗者说预兆不利。

column1: Sacrifice to Urox.
column2: 向尤洛克斯献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to Urox.
column2: 我们向尤洛克斯献祭。

column1: The Storm Bull worshippers said the omens were unfavorable.
column2: 风暴公牛的信徒说预兆不利。

column1: Search for outlaws.
column2: 搜寻逃犯。

column1: We searched for outlaws.
column2: 我们搜寻了逃犯。

column1: We did not find any.
column2: 我们一个也没找到。

column1: It is very difficult to tell one clan’s bolt of cloth from another’s.
column2: 很难区分不同氏族的一匹布料。

column1: It is very difficult to tell one clan’s bolt of cloth from another’s, but of course I am an expert. That skirt was not made here.
column2: 很难区分不同氏族的一匹布料，但我当然是行家。那条裙子不是这里做的。

column1: It is very difficult to tell one clan’s bolt of cloth from another’s, but of course I am an expert. That skirt was made by one of us.
column2: 很难区分不同氏族的一匹布料，但我当然是行家。那条裙子是我们中某人做的。

column1: It is very difficult to tell one clan’s bolt of cloth from another’s, but of course I am an expert. That skirt was made by a member of Clan \x01@a.
column2: 很难区分不同氏族的一匹布料，但我当然是行家。那条裙子是 \x01@a氏族的一个成员做的。

column1: If we falsely accuse another clan’s women of being Chaotic, they have the right to take all of our cheese.
column2: 如果我们错误地指控另一个氏族的妇女是混沌信徒，他们有权拿走我们所有的奶酪。

column1: I can do little here, unless this be the work of outlaws. If so, I can hunt them down.
column2: 我在这里帮不上什么忙，除非这是逃犯所为。若是如此，我可以追捕他们。

column1: Another clan will be offended if we accuse them of Chaos, but grateful if we root out a genuine practitioner of Chaotic magics.
column2: 如果我们指控另一个氏族与混沌有关，他们会感到冒犯；但如果我们铲除真正的混沌法术施行者，他们会感激不尽。

column1: Either Chalana Arroy or Urox might be appropriate gods to sacrifice to.
column2: 向查拉娜·阿罗伊或尤洛克斯献祭都是合适的神祇。

column1: Chalana Arroy heals those sickened by Chaos; Urox avenges those slain by it.
column2: 查拉娜·阿罗伊治愈被混沌污染者；尤洛克斯为被其所杀者复仇。

column1: Sacrifice to my mistress, Chalana Arroy.
column2: 向我的女主人查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭。

column1: Let the Bad Wind, Urox, blow this Chaos taint away.
column2: 让恶风，尤洛克斯，吹走这混沌的污秽。

column1: Let’s not cause trouble in the tribe by accusing another clan of Chaos without any real proof of it.
column2: 我们不要在部落中惹麻烦，在没有确凿证据的情况下指控另一个氏族与混沌有关。

column1: Chaos is bad.
column2: 混沌是邪恶的。

column1: They agreed that we had the right to determine her fate, and we did so.
column2: 他们同意我们有权决定她的命运，我们便照做了。

column1: Brand her as a servant of Chaos and drive her off.
column2: 将她烙上混沌仆人的印记，然后赶走。

column1: We branded her a servant of Chaos and drove her off.
column2: 我们将她烙上混沌仆人的印记，然后赶走了她。

column1: Once outlawed, she was killed.
column2: 一旦被宣布为逃犯，她就被处死了。

column1: She may have infested the cattle, just like a broo does.
column2: 她可能已经感染了牛群，就像布罗那样。

column1: No doubt she has a horde of Chaos cultists waiting to overwhelm us.
column2: 毫无疑问，她有一大群混沌邪教徒在等着压垮我们。

column1: Once outlawed, she must die.
column2: 一旦被放逐，她必须死。

column1: If we banish her, it may make us a more inviting target for the minions of Chaos.
column2: 如果我们放逐她，这可能会让我们成为混沌爪牙眼中更具诱惑的目标。

column1: Our crops will lose fertility if we kill a clan member, even for a good reason.
column2: 如果我们杀死一名氏族成员，即使理由正当，我们的作物也会失去丰饶。

column1: I volunteer to kill her.
column2: 我自愿去杀死她。

column1: Everybody knows what this — it — I mean, I don’t have to say it.
column2: 大家都知道这——它——我的意思是，我不必说出来。

column1: sceneR057
column2: sceneR057

column1: How much compensation do you demand?
column2: 你要求多少补偿？

column1: Greater than normal for such a situation.
column2: 比这种情况下的普通标准更高。

column1: No more and no less than the precedents call for.
column2: 不多不少，恰如先例所要求的。

column1: Less than the precedents call for.
column2: 低于先例所要求的。

column1: They agreed to our demand.
column2: 他们同意了我们的要求。

column1: They refused us.
column2: 他们拒绝了我们。

column1: Try to get as many cows as you can for her.
column2: 尽量为她争取尽可能多的牛只。

column1: We can take what we want from them.
column2: 我们可以从他们那里拿走我们想要的东西。

column1: What is wrong with a girl and a fellow who love each other getting married?
column2: 一个女孩和一个彼此相爱的年轻人结婚，有什么不对？

column1: Deciding on marriages is the duty of the ring, not the individual.
column2: 决定婚姻是长老会的职责，而非个人。

column1: The \x01@! clan is near to a feud with us. If we allow the marriage, they will soften towards us. But other clans will see us as flouting tradition.
column2: the \x01@! 氏族与我们之间近乎世仇。如果我们允许这桩婚事，他们就会对我们缓和态度。但其他氏族会视我们为藐视传统。

column1: The carls will not want to lose labor by raiding during planting season, especially over one rash girl.
column2: 自由民们不想在播种季节因袭击而失去劳力，尤其只因一个鲁莽的姑娘。

column1: The carls will not want to lose labor by raiding during harvest season, especially over one rash girl.
column2: 自由民们不想在收获季节因袭击而失去劳力，尤其只因一个鲁莽的姑娘。

column1: Marriage is holy, but there is a right way and a wrong way to create a marriage bond.
column2: 婚姻是神圣的，但缔结婚约有着正确与错误的方式。

column1: We must show a rigid adherence to the correct laws here. Making a tribe is more important than one girl’s heart.
column2: 我们必须在此展现出对正确律法的严格遵循。缔造一个部落比一个女孩的心更重要。

column1: Shouldn’t we be paying homage to Kero Fin, the Mountain Mother?
column2: 难道我们不应该向山脉之母凯罗·芬致敬吗？

column1: One of our barley fields has begun to whisper forbidden secrets during the night.
column2: 我们的一块大麦田开始在夜间低语禁忌的秘密。

column1: \x02\x03At the end of/During/In the middle of\x02 Death Week, a gruesome delegation of your own dead warriors appears again in the clan hall.
column2: \x02\x03在死亡周结束时/在死亡周期间/在死亡周中期\x02 ，一队你自己的已故战士的骇人代表再次出现在部族大厅中。

column1: “You have \x02\x05humiliated/disgraced/dishonored/tarnished the good name of/shamed\x02 the clan. You \x02\x03persist in neglecting/still ignore/have forgotten\x02 the old ways. You will face \x02\x03catastrophe/ruin/tragedy\x02 unless you act in a manner worthy of your ancestors.”
column2: “你 \x02\x05羞辱了/使蒙羞/使丢脸/玷污了/使受辱\x02 氏族。你 \x02\x03持续忽视/仍然无视/已经忘却\x02 旧路。你将面临 \x02\x03灾难/毁灭/悲剧\x02 ，除非你行事无愧于你的祖先。”

column1: The ghosts of our dead warriors returned and scolded us again, saying that our actions shamed the clan.
column2: 我们已故战士的幽灵再次返回并责骂我们，说我们的行为使氏族蒙羞。

column1: In the middle of Death Week, a gruesome delegation appears in your clan hall. These are the insubstantial spirits of your own dead warriors.
column2: 死亡周中旬，一群可怖的代表团出现在你们的部族大厅。那是你们阵亡战士的无形魂魄。

column1: “You have shamed the clan. You have turned from the old ways. You will face nothing but doom and disaster until you act in a manner worthy of our ancestors.”
column2: “你们玷污了部族。你们背离了旧路。在你们以配得上先祖的方式行事之前，只会遭遇厄运与灾祸。”

column1: The ghosts of our dead warriors returned and told us that our actions shamed the clan.
column2: 我们阵亡战士的魂魄归来，告知我们的行为玷污了部族。

column1: Promise them that you will do better in the future.
column2: 向他们保证你日后会做得更好。

column1: We promised to do better in the future.
column2: 我们承诺日后会做得更好。

column1: “Orlanth became king of the gods by keeping all his promises. Do the same, and we will not see you again in your lifetime.”
column2: “奥兰斯通过信守所有诺言成为了众神之王。你也这样做，那么我们有生之年将不会再见到你。”

column1: “If your promises are empty, you may join us sooner than you think,” say the ghosts, before filing out of the hall.
column2: “如果你的诺言是空洞的，你可能会比你想象中更快加入我们，”幽灵们说完，列队走出了大厅。

column1: Sacrifice to Humakt for protection from ghosts.
column2: 向胡马克特献祭以获得对抗幽灵的保护。

column1: We sacrificed to Humakt.
column2: 我们向胡马克特献祭了。

column1: The god-talkers said that Humakt was as pleased with our sacrifice as he is unhappy with the undead, and promised to help us.
column2: 神言者说，胡马克特对我们的献祭感到满意，正如他对亡灵感到不满一样，并承诺会帮助我们。

column1: The god-talkers said that Humakt was grateful for our sacrifice, but that we should be able to handle our own ancestors.
column2: 神言者说，胡马克特感激我们的献祭，但我们应该能够处理自己的祖先。

column1: Sacrifice to these spirits.
column2: 向这些灵魂献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to them.
column2: 我们向他们献祭了。

column1: They pronounced themselves pleased with the respect we had shown them, and vanished.
column2: 他们宣称对我们所表示的尊敬感到满意，然后消失了。

column1: They said that we would even cheat the dead, and that they would be back to haunt us further.
column2: 他们说我们甚至会欺骗死者，并且他们会回来继续纠缠我们。

column1: Scold them for frightening their own people.
column2: 斥责他们惊吓自己的人民。

column1: We scolded them for frightening their own people.
column2: 我们斥责他们惊吓自己的人民。

column1: They seemed chastened, and admitted that they were not sure exactly what offenses we had committed against the heritage of our clan.
column2: 他们似乎被训诫了，承认他们并不确定我们究竟犯了什么冒犯氏族传承的罪行。

column1: They reacted with anger, and promised that they would soon be back, to take all of our luck and magic from us.
column2: 他们愤怒地回应，并承诺很快就会回来夺走我们所有的运气和魔法。

column1: Try to bind some of the spirits as magical servants.
column2: 尝试将一些灵魂束缚为魔法仆人。

column1: Our magicians tried to capture some of the ghosts to power their spells.
