column2: “这里的生活艰难。我们看到了你们一个敌人的下场，并想避免那样的命运。你们是希望以体面的和解结束我们无谓的战斗，还是让奥兰提人继续自相残杀，让我们的其他敌人旁观？”

column1: “Life here is difficult. We both have other enemies — bandits, dragonewts, beastfolk, Chaos creatures, and the like. Do you wish to come to an honorable settlement of our pointless fight, or shall the Orlanthi continue to spill each others’ blood, as our enemies look on?”
column2: “这里的生活艰难。我们双方都有其他敌人——强盗、龙人、兽人、混沌生物等等。你们是希望以体面的和解结束我们无谓的战斗，还是让奥兰提人继续自相残杀，让我们的敌人旁观？”

column1: “Life here could be better. We both have crafts to trade, young people to marry, and other enemies to fight. Why are we wasting time fighting each other, when we have so many other, more profitable, things to do?”
column2: “这里的生活本可以更好。我们都有手艺要交易、年轻人要婚配、还有别的敌人要打。为什么我们要浪费时间互相争斗，当有这么多其他更有益的事情可做？”

column1: “Life here is quite workable. There are enough Orlanthi to trade with, and plenty of good land for everyone to farm. Why not come to a responsible agreement and end our futile fight? Shall we gladden the hearts of our other enemies by fighting each other, instead of shedding their blood?”
column2: “这里的生活还算过得去。有足够多的奥兰提人可以交易，也有充足的良田供大家耕种。为什么不达成一个负责任的协议，结束我们徒劳的战斗？难道我们要通过互相争斗来取悦我们的其他敌人，而不是去放他们的血？”

column1: “We accept your offer of peace! Let us feast!”
column2: “我们接受你的和平提议！让我们宴饮吧！”

column1: We toasted them at our feast table. At length, they admitted that they had come to us to betray us, not to make peace. But they had been so moved by our open-hearted welcome that they would now support true reconciliation between our clans.
column2: 我们在宴席桌上向他们敬酒。最终，他们承认来此是为了背叛我们，而非媾和。但他们被我们开诚布公的欢迎深深打动，如今将支持我们氏族间的真正和解。

column1: We made plans for a peace parley.
column2: 我们制定了和平谈判的计划。

column1: We toasted them at our feast table. Together, we made plans for a peace parley on neutral ground.
column2: 我们在宴席桌上向他们敬酒。我们共同制定了在中立之地举行和平谈判的计划。

column1: “We are always ready to talk.”
column2: “我们随时愿意谈判。”

column1: \x01@N took the ring members aside and said, “They mean to betray us. I can feel it in my marrow.”
column2: \x01@N 将环成员拉到一边说：“他们想背叛我们。我骨子里能感觉到。”

column1: Together, we made plans for a peace parley on neutral ground.
column2: 我们共同制定了在中立之地举行和平谈判的计划。

column1: “We do not trust you. Begone.”
column2: “我们不信你。滚开。”

column1: We told them we did not trust them, and dismissed them from our presence.
column2: 我们告诉他们我们不相信他们，并将他们从我们面前打发走。

column1: Protesting their sincerity, they left.
column2: 他们抗议自己的真诚，然后离开了。

column1: “We will talk, but you must prove that we can trust you.”
column2: “我们会谈，但你必须证明我们可以信任你。”

column1: What proof do you demand?
column2: 你要求什么证明？

column1: A hostage.
column2: 一个人质。

column1: We demanded that they leave a hostage, to show that their intentions were honorable.
column2: 我们要求他们留下一名人质，以证明他们的意图是体面的。

column1: Protesting rather too much, they claimed great offense at our reasonable demand, and stalked off, promising a continuance of hostilities.
column2: 他们抗议得太过了，声称对我们合理的要求感到极大冒犯，然后大步离去，承诺继续敌对。

column1: A herd of 50 cows left with a neutral clan as peacebond.
column2: 一群五十头牛留给中立氏族作为和平保证金。

column1: They agreed to our demand. Together, we made plans for a peace parley on neutral ground.
column2: 他们同意了我们的要求。我们一起制定了在中立地点举行和平谈判的计划。

column1: Submission to a Lhankor Mhy ritual of truth.
column2: 接受兰科尔·穆伊的真理仪式。

column1: We demanded that they submit to a ritual of truth.
column2: 我们要求他们接受真理仪式。

column1: The ritual exposed them as base liars intending nothing but betrayal. We ran them off our land, and told them never to return.
column2: 仪式揭露了他们不过是卑鄙的骗子，一心只想着背叛。我们将他们赶出我们的土地，并告诉他们永远不许回来。

column1: “We’re not having problems with other enemies.”
column2: “我们和其他敌人没有麻烦。”

column1: They said that we should make peace because we were beset by many enemies, but we told them that we were not so afflicted.
column2: 他们说我们应该讲和，因为我们被众多敌人围攻，但我们告诉他们，我们并未受此困扰。

column1: They responded by listing the many enemies we had made, stating their case quite convincingly.
column2: 他们回应列举了我们结下的众多仇敌，说得相当有说服力。

column1: \x01@N took the ring members aside and said, “Their wrong arguments are too carefully crafted to be merely mistaken. They are lying, and mean to betray us.”
column2: \x01@N 将环成员拉到一旁说：“他们错误的论点精心雕琢，绝非仅仅是错误。他们在撒谎，打算背叛我们。”

column1: If we make peace with those scoundrels, our cows’ milk will dry up.
column2: 如果我们和那些恶棍讲和，我们牛只的奶都会干涸。

column1: If they offer us gifts, we should reciprocate.
column2: 如果他们送我们礼物，我们应该回礼。

column1: If they offer us gifts, that is good. We needn’t worry about impressing them by overdoing the reciprocal gifting.
column2: 如果他们送我们礼物，那是好事。我们不必担心回礼过重而让他们印象深刻。

column1: If they offer us gifts, we should impress them by giving even more in return.
column2: 如果他们送我们礼物，我们应该回赠更多来给他们留下深刻印象。

column1: We have the stronger force; it is no wonder that they now sue for peace.
column2: 我们兵力更强；难怪他们现在求和。

column1: They see what we can do with our stronger force; it is no wonder that, wisely, they now sue for peace.
column2: 他们看到了我们更强兵力能做到什么；难怪他们明智地现在求和。

column1: We have the weaker force; I wonder why they now sue for peace.
column2: 我们兵力较弱；我奇怪他们为什么现在求和。

column1: No Orlanthi would risk the grave dishonor brought about by a false promise of peace.
column2: 没有奥兰赛人会冒虚假和平承诺带来的严重不名誉风险。

column1: Since they are approaching us, we can rightly demand proof of their intentions.
column2: 既然他们在接近我们，我们完全有权要求他们证明意图。

column1: Since they are approaching us, we can rightly demand proof of their intentions. We can demand one of their noble youngsters as hostage, or a peacebond of cows left with another clan.
column2: 既然他们在接近我们，我们完全有权要求他们证明意图。我们可以要求他们的一名贵族子弟作为人质，或者将牛只作为和平保证金存在另一个氏族。

column1: Everyone thinks it’s a generous offer.
column2: 所有人都认为这是个慷慨的提议。

column1: Everyone thinks this offer is only our due, give our recent battle prowess.
column2: 所有人都认为这份提议只是我们应得的，鉴于我们最近的战斗勇武。

column1: If we feast them, they will be better disposed towards us when the real negotiations begin.
column2: 如果我们宴请他们，在真正谈判开始时，他们会对我们更友好。

column1: Feasting means drinking. Drinking often means fighting. Leave the celebration for a successful peace negotiation.
column2: 宴请意味着饮酒。饮酒常常意味着打架。把庆祝留到和平谈判成功之后吧。

column1: We could subject them to a ritual of truth, as proof of their intentions.
column2: 我们可以让他们接受真理仪式，作为他们意图的证明。

column1: They very subtly tested the strength of our magic as they approached us. Why would they do that, if their motives were good?
column2: 他们在接近我们时非常微妙地测试了我们魔法的强度。如果他们的动机是好的，为什么要这么做？

column1: King Heort made peace as often as he made war.
column2: 赫尔特大王既好战也好和。

column1: What costs us less — peace or hostility?
column2: 什么代价更小——和平还是敌对？

column1: How will our warriors prove their manhood, if they do not have the \x01@! to fight against?
column2: 如果我们的战士没有 \x01@! 可战，他们如何证明自己的男子气概？

column1: Perhaps we can forge a new tribe with them, now that they have come to their senses.
column2: 也许我们可以和他们缔造一个新部落，既然他们已经清醒过来。

column1: Perhaps we can forge a new tribe with them, now that they see what strong tribe-mates we’d make.
column2: 也许我们可以和他们缔造一个新部落，既然他们看到了我们会成为多么强大的部落伙伴。

column1: We have not yet revenged ourselves against them for the many slights they have given us. I say no peace!
column2: 我们还没有为他们对我们施加的诸多轻蔑而复仇。我说，不许求和！

column1: We must seize every chance for peace, for such opportunities are rare and precious.
column2: 我们必须抓住每一个和平机会，因为这样的机会稀少而珍贵。

column1: Look at how they come to us, seeking to end the bloodshed. We must hear them out.
column2: 看看他们是如何来寻求结束流血的。我们必须听他们说完。

column1: Refuse them, then raid them. How dare they come here like this?
column2: 拒绝他们，然后袭击他们。他们怎么敢就这样来这里？

column1: sceneR061
column2: sceneR061

column1: The \x01@! ring betrays you at their so-called peace parley. The meet is nothing but a pretense for a surprise assassination attempt against your leaders.
column2: \x01@! 长老会在他们所谓的和平谈判中背叛了你们。这次会面不过是伪装，企图突袭刺杀你们的领袖。

column1: The \x01@! betrayed us at their so-called peace parley.
column2: \x01@! 在他们所谓的和平谈判中背叛了我们。

column1: Fortunately, none of your people are seriously hurt.
column2: 幸运的是，你们的人没有受重伤。

column1: Fortunately, none of our people were seriously hurt.
column2: 幸运的是，我们的人没有受重伤。

column1: One is wounded in the attack.
column2: 有一人在袭击中受伤。

column1: One was wounded in the attack.
column2: 有一人在袭击中受了伤。

column1: \x01@\x17 are wounded in the attack.
column2: \x01@\x17 在袭击中受伤。

column1: \x01@\x17 were wounded in the attack.
column2: \x01@\x17 在袭击中受了伤。

column1: One is slain.
column2: 有一人被杀。

column1: One was slain.
column2: 有一人被杀了。

column1: \x01@\x0B are slain.
column2: \x01@\x0B 被杀。

column1: \x01@\x0B were slain.
column2: \x01@\x0B 被杀了。

column1: It was small consolation that we were given the peacebond.
column2: 我们拿到了和平保证金，但这只是小小的安慰。

column1: Do nothing for now.
column2: 暂且按兵不动。

column1: We bided our time, in spite of the indignant protests of our clansmen.
column2: 我们等待时机，尽管族人们愤慨抗议。

column1: Although we didn’t succeed in killing any of the \x01@! ring members, everyone was happy that we had struck the treacherous scum immediately.
column2: 尽管我们没能杀死任何一名 \x01@! 环成员，但所有人都很高兴我们立刻打击了那帮背信弃义的渣滓。

column1: Many were willing to condemn \x01@! treachery; none were willing to punish it.
column2: 许多人愿意谴责 \x01@! 的背叛，但没有人愿意惩罚它。

column1: Petition Orlanth to punish this ungodly treachery.
column2: 祈求奥兰斯惩罚这不敬神的背叛行径。

column1: We petitioned Orlanth to punish their ungodly treachery.
column2: 我们祈求奥兰斯惩罚他们不敬神的背叛行径。

column1: Soon, we heard that the \x01@! leaders had been visited by Orlanth’s spirits of reprisal. They were burnt by his harsh wind of justice. Some resigned from the \x01@! ring; others sacrificed to appease Orlanth’s wrath.
column2: 不久，我们听说 \x01@! 的领袖们遭到了奥兰斯复仇之灵的拜访。他们被他严酷的正义之风吹灼。一些人退出了 \x01@! 长老会，另一些人则献祭以平息奥兰斯的怒火。

column1: Alas, we heard no word that Orlanth heeded our request.
column2: 唉，我们没有听到任何奥兰斯理会我们祈求的消息。

column1: Spread word of \x01@! villainy.
column2: 传播 \x01@! 的恶行。

column1: We spread word of \x01@! villainy.
column2: 我们传播 \x01@! 的恶行。

column1: Their names were cursed throughout our corner of Dragon Pass.
column2: 他们的名字在我们龙之隘口这一带遭到诅咒。

column1: We gained nothing but a reputation for weakness and gullibility.
column2: 我们一无所获，只落得个软弱轻信的名声。

column1: We can well afford to buy vengeance from our neighbors.
column2: 我们完全负担得起从邻居那里买来复仇。

column1: We can’t afford to trade cows for vengeance.
column2: 我们负担不起用牛只换取复仇。

column1: It is forbidden to reward others for fighting one’s battles.
column2: 禁止因他人代战而给予酬劳。

column1: It is unusual to reward others for fighting one’s battles.
column2: 因他人代战而给予酬劳并不常见。

column1: It is unusual, but not unheard of, to reward others for fighting one’s battles.
column2: 因他人代战而给予酬劳虽不常见，但并非闻所未闻。

column1: We’re a war clan. It’s shameful to ask others to fight our battles.
column2: 我们是战争氏族。请他人代战是可耻的。

column1: We’re a peace clan. There’s no shame in paying others to fight our battles.
column2: 我们是和平氏族。花钱请人代战并无羞耻。

column1: We are strong. There is no honorable course but avenging ourselves against them on the field of valor.
column2: 我们实力强大。唯有在英勇战场上亲手复仇，方为荣誉之道。

column1: We are weak. We must become strong, and smash them then.
column2: 我们实力弱小。必须先变强大，再粉碎他们。

column1: Orlanth despises such breaches of hospitality, but he is a busy god. We must sacrifice at least fifteen cows to be sure of getting his attention.
column2: 奥兰斯鄙视这种背弃好客的行径，但他是个繁忙的神。我们至少得献祭十五头牛，才能确保引起他的注意。

column1: Raiding during planting season will compound our losses.
column2: 在播种季节劫掠会加剧我们的损失。

column1: Raiding during harvest time will compound our losses.
column2: 在收获季节劫掠会加剧我们的损失。

column1: The Unjust Emperor Yelm made promises of peace to Orlanth, but they were empty, and blew away in the wind of justice.
column2: 不义皇帝耶尔姆曾向奥兰斯许诺和平，但那都是空话，已被正义之风吹散。

column1: “A lie can kill, just like a knife can.”
column2: “谎言能杀人，就像刀能杀人一样。”

column1: Their clan magic will suffer as a result of this gross breach of hospitality.
column2: 由于这种严重背弃好客的行为，他们的氏族魔法将受损。

column1: Before we rush off to battle again, let the earth finish drinking the blood that is now spilt upon it.
column2: 在我们再次匆忙出战之前，先让大地饮尽此刻流淌的鲜血。

column1: We would be bad Orlanthi if we did not seek personal vengeance for this rank treachery.
column2: 倘若我们不为这等无耻背叛寻求个人复仇，那就不配做奥兰西人。

column1: Vengeance is the responsibility of the kin to the slain, not the entire clan.
column2: 复仇是死者亲属的责任，而非整个氏族。

column1: sceneR062
column2: sceneR062

column1: Adopt her into your clan.
column2: 将她收养入你的氏族。

column1: We adopted her as if she were our own daughter.
column2: 我们收养了她，视如己出。

column1: Offer to marry her to one of your high-ranking young men.
column2: 提议将她许配给你手下的一位高阶青年。

column1: We offered to marry her to a fine young fellow of noble rank.
column2: 我们提议将她许配给一位出身贵族的优秀青年。

column1: Offer to marry her to one of your young men, though not one of noble rank.
column2: 提议将她许配给你手下的一位青年，但并非贵族出身。

column1: We offered to marry her to a fine young fellow, though of humble rank.
column2: 我们提议将她许配给一位优秀青年，尽管出身卑微。

column1: “I cannot allow you to risk doubly insulting my father,” she says. “It is true that he will be very angry if you take me in. But if you take me and marry me below my station, he will be angry enough to start a war. It is not for myself that I object, but because I do not wish to be the cause of a conflict between clans.”
column2: “我不能让你冒双重侮辱我父亲的风险，”她说。“的确，你若收留我，他会非常愤怒。但若你收留我后又将我嫁低于身份的人，他会怒到发动战争。我反对并非为了自己，而是不愿成为氏族冲突的起因。”

column1: She told us that she couldn’t consent, because it would cause a war between our clan and that of her father.
column2: 她告诉我们她不能同意，因为这会导致我们氏族与她父亲氏族之间的战争。

column1: Send her on her way.
column2: 打发她上路。

column1: We sent her on her way.
column2: 我们打发她上路了。

column1: “I will remember your kindness always,” she hissed. It appeared that we had made an enemy, but what could one lone troublemaker do? And so she left our tula without incident.
column2: “我会永远记住你的‘善意’，”她嘶声道。看来我们树敌了，但一个孤零零的惹事精能做什么？于是她平安离开了我们的领地。

column1: Take her back to her father.
column2: 把她送回她父亲那里。

column1: We returned her to her father.
column2: 我们把她送回了她父亲那里。

column1: We took her back to her father, but he was suspicious of us and did not give us thanks.
column2: 我们把她送回了她父亲那里，但他对我们心存疑虑，没有道谢。

column1: His clan was grateful for the respect we showed them, and gave us a fine silver torc as a token of their gratitude.
column2: 他的氏族感激我们给予的尊重，赠送了一条精美的银环项链以表谢意。

column1: The \x01@! clan is poor; we have little to lose by helping her.
column2: The \x01@! clan is poor; we have little to lose by helping her.

column1: The \x01@! clan is prosperous; it would be bad to jeopardize our chances of trading with them.
column2: The \x01@! clan is prosperous; it would be bad to jeopardize our chances of trading with them.

column1: If it comes to a feud, we can beat them.
column2: 如果演变成世仇，我们能打败他们。

column1: If we are to start a feud, I’d rather do it with some other, weaker clan.
column2: 如果要挑起世仇，我宁愿选另一个更弱的氏族。

column1: As chieftain, her father has unlimited rights concerning her marriage.
column2: 作为酋长，她父亲对她的婚姻拥有无限权利。

column1: The precedents conflict. Her father, in concert with his ring, decides who she marries. But he should not marry her to one who has dishonored her.
column2: 先例冲突。她父亲与长老会共同决定她的婚配。但他不该把她嫁给那个使她受辱的人。

column1: The girl is right. The fact that her suitor has dishonored her outweighs her clan’s rights to choose her groom.
column2: 这姑娘说得对。求婚者使她受辱这一事实重于她氏族选择夫婿的权利。

column1: Her clan will be slighted if we aid her, and obligated to us if we return her to them.
column2: 如果我们帮助她，她的氏族会感到被轻视；如果我们把她送回去，他们则会欠我们人情。

column1: If she is of high rank, she deserves a groom of equal rank.
column2: 如果她出身高贵，她就该配一个同等地位的夫婿。

column1: There is something behind that girl’s eyes that I quite admire.
column2: 那姑娘眼神深处有一种我很欣赏的东西。

column1: Heinvar Humaktskin dishonored the daughter of Advast Hard-Mouth. To avoid a feud, he married the girl to Humaktskin, and thereby caused a worse feud with Clan Damasti, which sheltered her.
column2: 海因瓦尔·胡马科特斯金玷污了硬口阿德瓦斯特的女儿。为避免世仇，他将那姑娘嫁给了胡马科特斯金，结果却因此与庇护她的达马斯蒂氏族结下了更糟的世仇。

column1: I told you that the milk would curdle if you left it in jars with the image of Eurmal on them.
column2: 我告诉过你，如果把牛奶留在刻有尤尔马尔图案的罐子里，它会变酸。

column1: There’s something about this girl that reminds me of… Oh, what’s the word? It’s so annoying, sometimes I can get the words out, and other times they just don’t — don’t…
column2: 这姑娘身上有种东西让我想起……哦，那词是什么？真烦人，有时我能把话说清楚，有时就是说不——说不出来……

column1: She is a fine specimen of Orlanthi womanhood. The men of other clans do not deserve her, whether she is dishonored or not.
column2: 她是奥兰西女性的杰出典范。其他氏族的男人配不上她，无论她是否受辱。

column1: This allows us to gain a fine bride without paying a bride price. On the other hand, it means we don’t get a dowry… Never mind.
column2: 这样我们就能不付彩礼得到一位好新娘。另一方面，这意味着我们得不到嫁妆……算了。

column2: sceneR063

column1: An old woman who introduces herself as Leika brings a baby to you. She has been raising the child alone in the woods, so you can assume she has been outlawed from her clan for some reason. “I raised this girl in a shield, so that she will grow up to be a mighty warrior. It is time she had a clan, so I bring her to you. Her name is Kallyr.”
column2: 一位自称莱卡的老妇人带着一个婴儿来到你面前。她独自在林中抚养这孩子，因此可以猜测她因某种缘由被氏族放逐了。“我用盾牌养育这个女孩，让她成长为一位强大的战士。现在她该有个氏族了，所以我带她来找你。她的名字叫卡莉尔。”

column1: An outlaw woman brought us a baby she had raised in a shield. She told us that the babe, Kallyr, would one day be a mighty warrior.
column2: 一位被放逐的妇人带着她用盾牌养育的婴儿来到我们面前。她告诉我们，这个名叫卡莉尔的婴儿有朝一日会成为强大的战士。

column1: Adopt both the woman and the girl.
column2: 收留妇人和女孩两人。

column1: We adopted not only the girl, but the woman as well.
column2: 我们不仅收留了女孩，也收留了那个妇人。

column1: Leika was surprised and pleased by our generosity.
column2: 莱卡对我们的慷慨感到既惊讶又欣喜。

column1: Ask the woman why she is an outlaw.
column2: 询问妇人为何被放逐。

column1: We asked her why she was an outlaw.
column2: 我们问她为何被放逐。

column1: “My own outlawry is a long and sad story,” she said. “Let us say that it was a matter of wrong passion, and that I accept my punishment. This girl’s mother was also outlawed, and the child is the result of her shame. She is innocent of any blame, and needs a clan to grow up in.”
column2: “我自己的放逐是一段漫长而悲伤的故事，”她说，“就当作是错情的缘故吧，我接受惩罚。这女孩的母亲也被放逐了，孩子是她羞耻的产物。她没有任何过错，需要一个氏族来成长。”

column1: Recommend that she take the girl to another clan.
column2: 建议她把女孩带到另一个氏族去。

column1: Which other clan do you suggest?
column2: 你建议去哪个氏族？

column1: We told her to seek refuge from the \x01@! clan.
column2: 我们告诉她去向 \x01@! 氏族寻求庇护。

column1: She left without another word.
column2: 她一言不发地离开了。

column1: Take the girl in.
column2: 收留女孩。

column1: We did as the woman asked, and took the girl in.
column2: 我们按那妇人所求，收留了女孩。

column1: Leika thanked us, then returned to the woods.
column2: 莱卡谢过我们，然后返回了林中。

column1: Turn them away.
column2: 拒绝她们。

column1: We turned them away.
column2: 我们拒绝了她们。

column1: Leika is right. Kallyr will grow up to be a great warrior. I wish she was my daughter.
column2: 莱卡说得对。卡莉尔会成长为一名伟大的战士。我希望她是我的女儿。

column1: If a person is outlawed by another clan, it means nothing to us.
column2: 如果一个人被另一个氏族放逐，那对我们毫无意义。

column1: She is no kin to us; we are not obligated to take her in.
column2: 她与我们无亲无故，我们没有义务收留她。

column1: She is no kin to us; we are not obligated to take her in. That doesn’t mean, however, that the child should be deprived of proper society.
column2: 她与我们无亲无故，我们没有义务收留她。但这并不意味着这孩子应当被剥夺正常的社会生活。

column1: It is said that an infant cradled in a shield in the wilderness will grow up to be a mighty warrior. This might just be an old wives’ tale, though.
column2: 据说在荒野中用盾牌养育的婴儿会成长为强大的战士。不过，这可能只是个老妇人的传说。

column1: An infant cradled in a shield in the wilderness will grow up to be a mighty warrior, so the stories say.
column2: 在荒野中用盾牌养育的婴儿会成长为强大的战士，故事里是这么说的。

column1: The people might be heartened by a show of generosity, or offended that we have brought the taint of outlawry upon the clan.
column2: 人们可能会因慷慨之举而振奋，也可能会因我们给氏族招来放逐的污点而愤慨。

column1: The people will be heartened by a show of generosity.
column2: 人们会因慷慨之举而振奋。

column1: The people will be offended if we bring the taint of outlawry upon the clan.
column2: 如果我们将放逐的污点带入氏族，人们会愤慨。

column1: We must let the girl in; it would be sheer villainy to refuse her.
column2: 我们必须让女孩进来；拒绝她将是彻头彻尾的恶行。

column1: The babe is dishonored, and must suffer for her parents’ sins. This is harsh, but life is harsh, too.
column2: 这婴儿蒙受了耻辱，必须为父母之罪受苦。这很残酷，但生活也同样残酷。

column1: Etrig gave an axe to Brolarulf, and both parties prospered.
column2: 埃特里格赠予布罗拉鲁夫一把斧头，双方都因此兴旺。

column1: Wherever there is a dishonored woman, a dishonorable male lurks not far away.
column2: 凡有不名誉的女人之处，附近必有不名誉的男人。

column1: A girl born of a woman’s heedless lust is doomed to duplicate her mother’s sins.
column2: 因女人轻率的欲望而生的女孩，注定要重蹈她母亲的罪孽。

column1: “The best banquet is one you remember afterwards.”
column2: “最棒的宴席是事后仍能记起的那一场。”

column1: Of course we must let her in! What are we afraid of?
column2: 我们当然必须让她进来！我们在怕什么？

column1: To quote Oskul’s Saga, “From evil people, one can expect only evil.”
column2: 引用奥斯库尔传说：“从邪恶之人那里，只能期待邪恶。”

column1: Perhaps by the standards of ordinary clans, this baby will be a great warrior, but she will be hard pressed to eclipse the heroes of clan \x01@"!
column2: 或许以普通氏族的标尺来看，这个婴儿会成为伟大的战士，但她很难超越 \x01@"氏族的英雄们！

column1: Explorers found Humakt’s Raven Banner.
column2: 探索者发现了胡梅克特的渡鸦战旗。

column1: An exploration party returns with a legendary treasure of the First Age, Humakt’s Raven Banner. When carried into a fight, this battle standard guarantees victory in battle. However, it does so at great cost: the standard bearer is always killed.
column2: 一支探索队带回了一件第一纪元的传奇宝物——胡梅克特的渡鸦战旗。当它被带入战斗时，这面战旗能确保胜利。然而代价巨大：持旗者必死。

column1: Give it to an enemy or hostile group as a peace offering.
column2: 将其赠予一个敌人或敌对团体作为和平献礼。

column1: Which enemy do you give it to?
column2: 你赠予哪个敌人？

column1: We gave it to the Dragonewts, who accepted the banner but urged us not to force them into further obligations.
column2: 我们将其送给龙人，他们收下了战旗，但敦促我们不要强迫他们承担更多义务。

column1: We gave it to the Humakti. They were glad to see us making peace with them, and gave us reciprocal gifts.
column2: 我们将其送给胡梅克特信徒。他们很高兴看到我们与他们和解，并回赠了礼物。

column1: were glad to see us making peace with them, and ended their feud with us.
column2: 很高兴看到我们与他们和解，并结束了与我们氏族的世仇。

column1: were glad to see us making peace with them.
column2: 很高兴看到我们与他们和解。

column1: Our god-talkers were not pleased — they feared lasting damage to our clan’s magic and abilities by our making good with our ancient sworn enemies.
column2: 我们的神言者并不满意——他们担心与古老的死敌和解会对我氏族的魔法和能力造成持久损害。

column1: Give it to another clan.
column2: 赠予另一个氏族。

column1: Which clan do you give it to?
column2: 你赠予哪个氏族？

column1: They ended their feud with us.
column2: 他们结束了与我们氏族的世仇。

column1: They accepted the banner, though several of their weaponthanes gave us hard looks.
column2: 他们收下了战旗，尽管其中几位武器领主向我们投来了严厉的目光。

column1: Keep it.
column2: 留下它。

column1: We chose to keep Humakt’s Raven Banner and ponder its bittersweet blessing.
column2: 我们选择保留胡梅克特的渡鸦战旗，并思考这份苦乐参半的祝福。

column1: Return it to where it was hidden.
column2: 放回原隐藏处。

column1: Our explorers returned it to its ancient hiding place.
column2: 我们的探索者将其放回了古老的藏匿处。

column1: Trade it to another clan.
column2: 与另一个氏族交易。

column1: We decided to trade it away.
column2: 我们决定将其交易掉。

column1: 75 cows and 75 cows worth of goods
column2: 75头牛以及价值75头牛的货物

column1: 50 cows and 50 cows worth of goods
column2: 50头牛以及价值50头牛的货物

column1: 35 cows and 35 cows worth of goods
column2: 35头牛以及价值35头牛的货物

column1: We managed to get cattle and goods totalling \x01@\x16.
column2: 我们设法获得了总数达 \x01@\x16的牲畜和货物。

column1: We sold it for a goodly sum.
column2: 我们以一大笔钱把它卖掉了。

column1: The most they will offer you for the treasure is \x01@\x16, half in goods and half in cows. Do you accept their offer?
column2: 他们为这件宝物最多愿意出价 \x01@\x16，一半货物一半牛只。你接受他们的出价吗？

column1: We did not get the price we had hoped for.
column2: 我们没有得到期望的价格。

column1: Although it is always good to get more cows, our herds are currently large and healthy.
column2: 虽然多收牛总是好事，但我们的牧群目前又大又健康。

column1: We should trade it away; our herds are dwindling.
column2: 我们应该把它卖掉；我们的牧群在减少。

column1: It’s hard to say what we should ask for such a fabulous treasure.
column2: 很难说对这如此神奇的宝物我们该要什么价。

column1: Any smart trader would try to dicker us down no matter what our starting price, so we might as well start high.
column2: 不管我们开价多少，精明的商人都会设法压价，所以不如一开始就报高。

column1: If we keep the banner, we will have to use it sparingly. No warrior wants to go into combat if he is certain to die.
column2: 如果我们保留这面旗帜，就必须谨慎使用。没有战士愿意在必死无疑的情况下投入战斗。

column1: If we must give this treasure away, make sure we don’t send it to our enemies.
column2: 如果我们必须送出这件宝物，务必确保不要送给我们的敌人。

column1: This banner presents us with the chance to display generosity worthy of a king.
column2: 这面旗帜给了我们一个展现配得上王者慷慨的机会。

column1: One of the ten survivors of the Dragonkill War said that the man ordered to carry the Raven Banner into that battle dropped it early in the battle, thus ensuring victory for the dragons.
column2: 屠龙战争的十名幸存者之一说，奉命持渡鸦旗进入那场战斗的人在战斗初期就丢下了旗子，从而确保了龙族的胜利。

column1: Trade it for cows, or for peace.
column2: 用它换牛，或者换和平。

column1: With this treasure, we could safely march against the inhabitants of the Upland Marsh.
column2: 有了这件宝物，我们可以安全地向高地沼泽的居民进军。

column1: This treasure could give us permanent victory over the elves.
column2: 这件宝物能让我们永远战胜精灵。

column1: Are you all mad? Of course we should keep this legendary treasure!
column2: 你们都疯了吗？我们当然应该保留这件传说中的宝物！

column1: I told you we should be devoting as much effort as possible to exploration.
column2: 我告诉过你，我们应该把尽可能多的精力用于探索。

column1: You can sort this out; I promised to go admire Alsdaughter’s wedding outfit.
column2: 你来处理这事；我答应过要去欣赏艾尔斯德特的婚服。

column1: Another Tarshite raiding party has penetrated your defenses. Although few in number, they are mighty warriors with great magical powers. They bested your weaponthanes and are again seeking the Lunar thralls you refused to turn over to Illator.
column2: 又一支塔什袭击队突破了你的防线。虽然人数不多，但他们都是拥有强大魔法力量的勇猛战士。他们击败了你的武器领主，再次追索那些你拒绝交给伊拉托的月民奴隶。

column1: A Tarshite raiding party has penetrated your defenses. Although few in number, they are mighty warriors with great magical powers. They easily routed your weaponthanes and are advancing on your clan hall. They must seek the Lunar thralls you refused to turn over to Illator.
column2: 一支塔什袭击队突破了你的防线。虽然人数不多，但他们都是拥有强大魔法力量的勇猛战士。他们轻松击溃了你的武器领主，正向你的部族大厅逼近。他们必定是在追索那些你拒绝交给伊拉托的月民奴隶。

column1: Illator sent mighty warriors to take the Lunar thralls we refused him.
column2: 伊拉托派了勇猛战士来夺取我们拒绝给他的月民奴隶。

column1: Hand over the Lunars, then ambush the Tarshites on their way out of Dragon Pass.
column2: 交出月民，然后在塔什人离开龙之隘口的路上伏击他们。

column1: We gave them the thralls, planning to ambush them on their way out of Dragon Pass.
column2: 我们把奴隶交给了他们，计划在他们离开龙之隘口的路上伏击。

column1: Do you send your war leader to spearhead the ambush?
column2: 你派你的战争领袖去带头伏击吗？

column1: Our plan succeeded, and the thralls were recaptured.
column2: 我们的计划成功了，奴隶被夺了回来。

column1: They sniffed out our ambush, and bested us again.
column2: 他们识破了我们的伏击，再次击败了我们。

column1: Hand over the Lunars, with additional compensation.
column2: 交出月民，并额外赔偿。

column1: We gave them the Lunars, and compensation as well.
column2: 我们把月民交给了他们，还附上了赔偿。

column1: Hand over the Lunars.
column2: 交出月民。

column1: We gave them the Lunars.
column2: 我们把月民交给了他们。

column1: Kill the Lunars out of spite.
column2: 出于怨恨杀死月民。

column1: We could not hold the thralls, but we would not reward the aggression of the Tarshites. So we slew the Lunars ourselves.
column2: 我们留不住奴隶，但也不愿奖赏塔什人的侵略行为。于是我们亲手杀死了月民。

column1: The Tarshites were furious, but could do nothing but return to Tarsh, pronouncing dire threats.
column2: 塔什人暴怒不已，但只能返回塔什，同时发出可怕的威胁。

column1: Rally and fight them off.
column2: 集结起来击退他们。

column1: We rallied, and drove them off.
column2: 我们集结起来，击退了他们。

column1: We rallied, yet still they bested us, taking the Lunar thralls.
column2: 我们集结起来，但他们仍然击败了我们，带走了月民奴隶。

column1: The labor of those thralls is vital to our prosperity.
column2: 那些奴隶的劳作对我们的繁荣至关重要。

column1: It is good to have thralls, but it would be no great loss to give them up.
column2: 有奴隶固然好，但交出去也不算巨大损失。

column1: No thralls are worth this \x02\x03irritation/constant headache/repeated fighting\x02.
column2: 没有奴隶值得这样 \x02\x03恼怒/持续的头痛/反复的战斗\x02。

column1: It is customary, in a situation such as this, to kill the thralls.
column2: 在这种情况下，按习俗是杀死奴隶。

column1: We are outmatched; surrender the thralls and be done with it.
column2: 我们不是对手；交出奴隶，了结此事。

column1: They are \x02\x03mighty/strong/magic-strengthened\x02 where we are not; just surrender the thralls.
column2: 他们 \x02\x03强大/强壮/魔法强化\x02 而我们不是；干脆交出奴隶。

column1: Although they are tough opponents, we have a reasonable chance to beat them.
column2: 虽然他们是难缠的对手，但我们有相当机会打败他们。

column1: They are tough opponents, but we have enough weaponthanes to beat them.
column2: 他们是难缠的对手，但我们有足够的武器领主来击败他们。

column1: Don’t risk the few weaponthanes we have left defending mere thralls.
column2: 不要为了区区奴隶而拿我们仅剩的武器领主去冒险。

column1: We must appease them, or they will bring the wrath of their entire kingdom down on us.
column2: 我们必须安抚他们，否则他们会引动整个王国的怒火降临到我们头上。

column1: It matters little whether the Tarshites like us; they are too far away to send any larger force against us.
column2: 塔什人喜不喜欢我们无关紧要；他们离得太远，派不出更大的兵力来对付我们。

column1: It does not matter if the Tarshites like us; it does matter if we continue to waste fighters on this petty matter.
column2: 塔什人喜不喜欢我们不重要；但继续为这种小事浪费战士就很重要了。

column1: Our magic is strong enough to counter theirs.
column2: 我们的魔法足够强大，可以对抗他们的魔法。

column1: Their magic is stronger than ours.
column2: 他们的魔法比我们更强。

column1: They will kill the thralls if we give them up. We must protect them.
column2: 如果我们交出他们，他们会杀死奴隶。我们必须保护他们。

column1: They keep coming back for these people. Perhaps the thralls would be better off in Tarsh.
column2: 他们一直为这些人而来。也许奴隶们在塔什会过得更好。

column1: The women have manipulated us into this hopeless situation, and I for one will have no more of it!
column2: 女人们把我们操纵到了这无望的境地，我反正不想再掺和了！

column1: They must die in ambush, their last sight our proud, battle-howling faces.
column2: 他们必须在伏击中死去，最后映入眼帘的是我们骄傲的、战吼呼啸的脸庞。

column1: Is this conflict about thralls, or about warriors’ pride?
column2: 这场冲突是为了奴隶，还是为了战士的骄傲？

column1: Alynx-footed they crept. With alynx claws, they slashed.
column2: 他们像山猫般蹑足潜行。他们像山猫爪般撕扯。

column1: If we don’t appease the dragonewts, we’ll be facing another Dragonkill War.
column2: 如果我们不安抚龙人，我们将面临另一场屠龙战争。

column1: Pretend to give them back, then, attack later and take them all as thralls!
column2: 假装把他们还回去，然后稍后进攻，把所有人都抓来当奴隶！

column1: Beat these fighters off, then sacrifice the thralls to Eurmal, who will get a big laugh the next time the Tarshites attack.
column2: 击退这些战士，然后将奴隶献祭给尤尔马尔——等塔什人下次进攻时，他会开怀大笑。

column2: sceneR066

column1: Looks like you were wrong when you told that Uroxi warrior that your cows weren’t infested by Chaos. Baby broos spring from the still-living bodies of your cattle, and go on a rampage. Broos are the unspeakably nasty and fecund servants of Chaos. Obviously, you must hunt down and destroy the awful little things, before they become awful, big things. What else do you do?
column2: 看来你当初告诉那位尤洛克斯追随者，说你的牛没被混沌污染，是大错特错了。幼布鲁斯从你那些还活着的牛体内窜出，横冲直撞。布鲁斯是混沌那难以言喻、繁衍力惊人的仆从。显然，你必须追猎并摧毁这些可怕的小东西，免得它们长成可怕的大家伙。你还要做什么？

column1: Our cows turned out to be infested by broos.
column2: 我们的牛果然被布鲁斯污染了。

column1: Enact the “Elmal Guards the Stead” heroquest, where Elmal defeats Chaos monstrosities.
column2: 举行“艾尔玛守卫农庄”英雄探索——艾尔玛击败混沌怪物。

column1: To everyone’s relief, our heroquest succeeded, and our clan gained strength for the fight against Chaos.
column2: 令所有人松了口气的是，我们的英雄探索成功了，氏族在与混沌的战斗中获得了力量。

column1: Our heroquest succeeded, though we ignored the fight against Chaos in search of other rewards. Some feared that Chaos was still strong in our tula.
column2: 我们的英雄探索成功了，尽管我们为了寻求其他回报而忽略了对抗混沌。有人担心混沌在我们的领地上仍然强大。

column1: To our grave dismay, the heroquest failed. With cold in our bellies, we feared the coming of Chaos.
column2: 令我们深感沮丧的是，英雄探索失败了。我们心中冰凉，惧怕混沌降临。

column1: Enact the “Orlanth and Aroka” heroquest, to shield us from kinstrife and Chaos.
column2: 举行“奥兰斯与阿罗卡”英雄探索，为我们抵御亲族相残与混沌。

column1: Our heroquest succeeded, but some in the clan were uneasy at fighting kinstrife with a heroquest where Orlanth battles his own nephew.
column2: 我们的英雄探索成功了，但氏族中有人对用一场奥兰斯与亲侄战斗的英雄探索来对抗亲族相残感到不安。

column1: They went away, and came back wounded and happy. They had slain many broos and some jack o’bears.
column2: 他们离开了，回来后虽带伤却很高兴。他们杀死了许多布鲁斯和一些恶鬼熊。

column1: Sacrifice to Eurmal.
column2: 向尤尔马尔献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to Eurmal.
column2: 我们向尤尔马尔献祭了。

column1: The priests said Eurmal had taken our sacrifice, but had not heard our pleas.
column2: 祭司们说尤尔马尔接受了我们的献祭，但没有听到我们的祈求。

column1: The priests said that Eurmal had heard our pleas.
column2: 祭司们说尤尔马尔听到了我们的祈求。

column1: There was no sign that Urox had heard our pleas.
column2: 没有迹象表明乌洛克斯听到了我们的祈求。

column2: 祭司们认为乌洛克斯听到了我们的祈求。

column1: Stay calm, wait for further signs of Chaos taint.
column2: 保持冷静，等待混沌污染的进一步迹象。

column1: Storm Bull will be offended if we sacrifice cows to him; it would be like sacrificing his brothers.
column2: 若向暴风公牛献祭牛只，他会觉得受冒犯——那就像献祭他的兄弟。

column1: We can’t afford to sacrifice many cows.
column2: 我们献祭不了太多牛。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice generously.
column2: 我们能够慷慨献祭。

column1: I can convince Storm Khans to come here, no matter how unruly or unreasonable they might be.
column2: 不管风暴可汗们多么桀骜或不讲理，我都能说服他们来这里。

column1: The weaponthanes would accept aid from Uroxi warriors in this, the great fight against Chaos.
column2: 武器领主们会接受尤洛克斯追随者的援助，来参与这场对抗混沌的伟大战斗。

column1: I can convince the weaponthanes not to take slight at the presence of Storm Bulls, if you want to invite them.
column2: 如果你要邀请暴风公牛信徒，我能说服武器领主们不计较他们的在场。

column1: A failed heroquest could hurt us worse than the Chaos we’re fearing. We should try something else.
column2: 一场失败的英雄探索可能会比我们惧怕的混沌本身造成更严重的伤害。我们应该试试别的办法。

column1: Generous sacrifices work. Scanty sacrifices leave you poorer and in just as much trouble. We could fight Chaos directly, with help.
column2: 慷慨的献祭有效。吝啬的献祭只会让你更穷，麻烦依旧。我们可以在帮助下直接对抗混沌。

column1: A heroquest, if it works, will not only fight Chaos but increase our clan’s standing and dispel any rumors about this grievous lapse of judgment.
column2: 英雄探索如果成功，不仅能对抗混沌，还能提升氏族的声望，消除关于这次严重失策的谣言。

column1: We must do something to fight Chaos, lest it worsens. And we must repair our reputation, too, lest that sours.
column2: 我们必须做点什么来对抗混沌，免得它恶化。我们也必须修复名声，免得它败坏。

column1: Once Chaos is loose, all those nearby are endangered. We must fight and contain it now, before it spreads.
column2: 一旦混沌爆发，周围所有人都将遭殃。我们必须趁它尚未扩散，立刻战斗并遏制它。

column1: We should do something magical — either a sacrifice or heroquest.
column2: 我们应该做些魔法性的事情——无论是献祭还是英雄探索。

column1: We should do something magical.
column2: 我们应该做些魔法性的事情。

column1: Urox prefers sacrifices of cows, and is traditionally the foe of Chaos. Eurmal might be able to trick the Chaos creatures, I suppose…
column2: 乌洛克斯偏爱献祭牛只，且历来是混沌之敌。我想尤尔马尔或许能戏弄那些混沌生物……

column1: If we make it through the Elmal quest, we will have protection from Chaos for some time.
column2: 如果我们完成艾尔玛探索，就能在一段时间内获得对抗混沌的保护。

column1: The Orlanth and Aroka quest can shield us from kinstrife…which is form of Chaos…so it might ward directly against Chaos, too.
column2: 奥兰斯与阿罗卡的探索能让我们免受亲族相残……那是混沌的一种形态……所以也可能直接抵御混沌。

column1: Calling on my lord Urox is a last resort. Let’s find his earthly servants first.
column2: 召唤我主乌洛克斯是最后手段。我们先去找他在人间的仆从吧。

column1: Eurmal often tricks the minions of Chaos; let him do this for us.
column2: 尤尔马尔常戏弄混沌的爪牙；让他为我们做这件事。

column1: Chaos is not the only thing we have to worry about.
column2: 混沌不是我们唯一需要担心的事。

column1: Of course we must perform Elmal’s sacred quest.
column2: 当然，我们必须举行艾尔玛的神圣探索。

column1: Orlanth’s sacred quest might be able to help us with the aftermath of Chaos.
column2: 奥兰斯的神圣探索或许能在混沌的后续影响上帮助我们。

column1: Eurmal’s the one.
column2: 尤尔马尔是合适的人选。

column1: Tribute to the gods never goes ill.
column2: 向诸神献祭从不会有坏处。

column1: After Orlanth weakened him, Wakboth the Devil was pinned under a huge block by Storm Bull. The Block can still be seen, in the land of Prax.
column2: 在奥兰斯削弱恶魔瓦克博斯之后，暴风公牛用一块巨石压住了他。这块巨石至今仍可在普拉克斯之地看到。

column1: Algath argued that the cows were not infested, and now his fellows scorn him. We must urge them to be understanding.
column2: 阿尔加斯曾争辩说牛没有被污染，现在他的同伴们都鄙视他。我们必须劝他们要理解。

column1: Holy warriors of Urox come to your clan and pronounce you unwitting tools of Chaos, who have strengthened dark powers through ignorance and misrule. “We take no pleasure in this,” they say, “but if the land is to be protected from Chaos, you and your mistakes must be expunged from this world.” They then proceed to kill your warriors and leaders, to destroy your fortifications and steads, to loot your possessions and drive off your cattle. In short, the future looks bleak for your clan. Should the survivors seek membership in other clans, or soldier on, despite impossible odds?
column2: 乌洛克斯的圣战士们来到你的氏族，宣布你们是无意中为混沌效力的工具，因无知与治理不当助长了黑暗之力。“我们并不为此高兴，”他们说，“但若要保护这片土地免受混沌之害，你和你的错误必须从这世间抹除。”然后他们开始杀戮你的战士和首领，摧毁你的防御工事和农庄，劫掠你的财产，赶走你的牛群。简而言之，你的氏族前景暗淡。幸存者们是该寻求加入其他氏族，还是尽管希望渺茫也要继续坚持？

column1: Holy warriors of Urox came and ravaged our tula, killing many and destroying much. They said they had to do it to stop the rise of Chaos in the land.
column2: 尤洛克斯的圣战士来了，洗劫了我们的领地，杀了许多人，毁了许多东西。他们说这么做是为了阻止混沌在这片土地上崛起。

column1: They took our livestock, our goods, and our kin. But they could not take our land.
column2: 他们抢走了我们的牲畜、财物和族人，但他们夺不走我们的土地。

column1: They were right to destroy us.
column2: 他们毁灭我们是对的。

column1: I guess we learned not to fool with Uroxi, didn’t we? Don’t look at me that way!
column2: 我想我们学会了别招惹尤洛克斯追随者，对吧？别那样看着我！

column1: This is hopeless
column2: 这没希望了

column1: We must rely on the mercy of our kin in other clans.
column2: 我们必须依靠其他氏族亲戚的慈悲。

column1: If we try to live here now, we will be no better than outlaws.
column2: 如果现在还想住在这里，我们就跟流寇没什么两样。

column1: Our explorers return with an odd duck-person. His name is Redtail, and his people live in the Upland Marsh area. He brings a terrible warning: the undead of the marsh are on the move.
column2: 我们的探索者带回了一个奇怪的鸭人。他名叫红尾，族人住在高地沼泽地区。他带来了一个可怕的警告：沼泽的亡灵正在行动。

column1: Scouts from your clan bring a witness who bears a terrible warning. Redtail, a duck from the Upland Marsh area, says that the undead of the marsh are on the move.
column2: 你们氏族的斥候带回了一个目击者，他带来了可怕的警告。高地沼泽地区的鸭人红尾说，沼泽的亡灵正在行动。

column1: They are controlled by a centuries-old magician called Delecti. The ducks have always struggled to suppress the undead, but now they must also fight off raids launched by Orlanthi settlers. Taking advantage of their distraction, Delecti’s weird priestesses have begun to enlarge the marsh. If it continues to grow, all of Dragon Pass might be overrun by ghouls, zombies, and vampires.
column2: 它们被一个名叫德莱克提的百年法师控制着。鸭人一直在艰难地压制亡灵，但现在他们还不得不抵御奥兰斯移民发起的劫掠。趁他们分身乏术，德莱克提的怪异女祭司开始扩张沼泽。如果沼泽继续扩大，整个龙隘都可能被食尸鬼、僵尸和吸血鬼淹没。

column1: A duck came to warn us of the growth of the Upland Marsh, home to a kingdom of undead ruled by an undying magician named Delecti.
column2: 一只鸭人来警告我们高地沼泽正在扩张，那里是亡灵王国，由一名不死的法师德莱克提统治。

column1: Hire mercenaries to help the ducks.
column2: 雇佣佣兵去帮助鸭人。

column1: We decided to hire mercenaries to help the ducks.
column2: 我们决定雇佣佣兵去帮助鸭人。

column2: 你愿意花多少钱？

column1: Mercenaries willing to fight the undead were in short supply.
column2: 愿意与亡灵作战的佣兵很紧缺。

column1: We found fighters willing to battle the undead, and the ducks thanked us for our aid.
column2: 我们找到了愿意与亡灵作战的战士，鸭人感谢了我们的帮助。

column1: Sacrifice to Humakt, foe of the undead.
column2: 向胡马特献祭，他是亡灵之敌。

column1: We decided to sacrifice to Humakt, foe of the undead.
column2: 我们决定向胡马特献祭，他是亡灵之敌。

column1: Our priests did not think that our sacrifice had garnered Humakt’s favor.
column2: 我们的祭司认为我们的献祭并未赢得胡马特的恩惠。

column1: Our priests interpreted the signs and said that our sacrifice had been well-received.
column2: 我们的祭司解读了征兆，说我们的献祭已被悦纳。

column1: Send warriors to help the ducks.
column2: 派遣战士去帮助鸭人。

column1: Do you send your war leader with them?
column2: 你要不要派遣你们的战争领袖一起前往？

column1: How long should they stay, in seasons?
column2: 他们应该待多久，以季节计？

column1: \x01@\x10 led a group of warriors to help them fight the undead.
column2: \x01@\x10 率领一批战士去帮助他们对抗亡灵。

column1: We sent a group of warriors to help them fight the undead.
column2: 我们派遣了一批战士去帮助他们对抗亡灵。

column1: Tell other clans to stop raiding the ducks.
column2: 告诉其他氏族停止劫掠鸭人。

column1: We told other clans to stop raiding the ducks, lest they give comfort to the undead.
column2: 我们告诉其他氏族停止劫掠鸭人，以免他们助长了亡灵的气焰。

column1: Once they realized the effects of their raids, they agreed.
column2: 一旦他们意识到劫掠的后果，便同意了。

column1: They rebuffed us.
column2: 他们拒绝了我们。

column1: “We will raid the ducks whenever we like. If the undead weaken them, they make even easier targets.”
column2: “我们想什么时候劫掠鸭人就什么时候。如果亡灵削弱了他们，他们就更容易得手了。”

column1: Thank the duck for his report.
column2: 感谢那只鸭人带来的报告。

column1: We thanked the duck for the information he provided.
column2: 我们感谢了那只鸭人提供的信息。

column1: He said we were like the other featherless, full of talk but unwilling to actually do anything.
column2: 他说我们和其他没羽毛的家伙一样，只会说空话，不愿付诸行动。

column1: Release local ducks from their obligation to you; tell them to use freed resources against undead.
column2: 解除本地鸭人对你们的义务；告诉他们把腾出的资源用来对抗亡灵。

column1: We released the local ducks from their tribute obligation, telling them to instead use their resources against Delecti.
column2: 我们解除了本地鸭人的进贡义务，告诉他们转而把资源用来对抗德莱克提。

column1: They promised to continue the fight against Delecti’s undead in our name.
column2: 他们承诺以我们的名义继续对抗德莱克提的亡灵。

column1: Mercenaries probably want about eleven cows apiece to fight the undead.
column2: 佣兵大概每人要十一头牛才肯去对抗亡灵。

column1: Mercenaries will want ten cows apiece to fight the undead.
column2: 佣兵每人要十头牛才肯去对抗亡灵。

column1: We can spare some warriors now, to avoid a worse fight later.
column2: 我们现在可以抽调一些战士，避免日后更糟的战事。

column1: Though it might well prevent a worse fight later, we can’t afford to send a large force to aid the ducks now.
column2: 虽然这也许能避免日后更糟的战事，但我们现在派不出大部队去援助鸭人。

column1: So that’s where the zombies came from.
column2: 原来僵尸就是这么来的。

column1: This monster hates all living things. We must oppose him, for all our sakes.
column2: 这个怪物憎恨一切生灵。我们必须为了大家而反抗他。

column1: It might be hard to convince our neighbors to stop raiding the ducks. They won’t necessarily believe the story about Delecti.
column2: 要让我们的邻居停止劫掠鸭人可能很难。他们不一定相信德莱克提的故事。

column1: We can convince the other clans of the tribe to stop raiding the ducks, if it means protection from the undead.

column1: We can convince our neighbors to stop raiding the ducks, if it means protection from the undead.
column2: 只要意味着能抵御亡灵，我们就能说服邻居停止劫掠鸭人。

column1: We are lucky enough to ignore the situation without making it worse.
column2: 我们足够幸运，可以无视现状而不让情况恶化。

column1: We have used up all our luck of late. We can’t count on the whims of fortune to protect us from this threat.
column2: 我们最近已经耗尽了所有运气。不能指望命运的反复无常来保护我们免遭这个威胁。

column1: We won’t last long if Delecti turns our crop land into swamps.
column2: 如果德莱克提把我们的农田变成沼泽，我们撑不了多久。

column1: Delecti’s zombies have already attacked us.
column2: 德莱克提的僵尸已经袭击过我们了。

column1: Remember, Humakt scorns a bloodless sacrifice.
column2: 记住，胡马特鄙夷不见血的献祭。

column1: These ducks will think better of us if we release the local ducks from their tribute obligation to us.
column2: 如果我们解除本地鸭人的进贡义务，他们会对我们刮目相看。

column1: The duck was looking at me funny the whole time. I’m sure of it. You all noticed it, didn’t you?
column2: 那只鸭人一直怪异地盯着我。我很确定。你们都注意到了，对吧？

column1: In Ormad’s Saga, Asmund Grey-Locks learns that a large force of warriors can tilt legal decisions in his favor.
column2: 在《奥马德传说》中，灰发阿斯蒙德了解到，一支强大的战士队伍能让法律裁决对自己有利。

column1: Hunkered in carrion-shroud, the marsh-men advanced.
column2: 蜷在腐尸裹布中，沼泽人向前推进。

column1: I think the women’s magic has gone sour, and that’s what causes the dead to walk.
column2: 我觉得女人的魔法已经变质，那就是导致死者行走的原因。

column1: Good news! The warriors we sent to fight the undead have returned triumphant. They aided the ducks in repelling the forces of Delecti the Necromancer. The swamps have begun to shrink again, and sightings of walking corpses have decreased to normal levels. We definitely made the right decision!
column2: 好消息！我们派去对抗亡灵的战士凯旋而归。他们协助鸭人击退了死灵法师德莱克提的军队。沼泽开始再次缩小，目击行尸的次数已降至正常水平。我们绝对做出了正确的决定！

column1: After we lost the battle with undead, \x01@\x0F and the other chieftains challenged \x01@\x0B’s rule.
column2: 在输掉与亡灵的战斗后， \x01@\x0F 与其他酋长质疑了 \x01@\x0B的统治。

column1: “Better my regal posterior than your fat behind, \x01@\x0F.”
column2: “我高贵的臀部总好过你肥厚的屁股， \x01@\x0F。”

column2: \x01@\x0B 因 \x04 不忠而斥责了 \x01@\x0F 。

column1: The other chiefs seemed ill-satisfied by this response.
column2: 其他酋长对这个答复似乎并不满意。

column1: “One defeat does not end a reign.”
column2: “一次失败不会终结统治。”

column1: “We have all failed. We must fight them until we win, or die.”
column2: “我们都失败了。我们必须战斗至胜利，或战死。”

column1: Are you bluffing, or do you really want to fight the undead again?
column2: 你是在虚张声势，还是真的想再次与亡灵作战？

column1: bluffing
column2: 虚张声势

column1: The other chieftains enthusiastically agreed to fight again.
column2: 其他酋长热情地同意再次作战。

column1: fight the undead
column2: 与亡灵作战

column1: How many weaponthanes from each clan do you send?
column2: 每个部族派遣多少武器领主？

column2: 谁来率领这支战队？

column1: Your war leader
column2: 你的战争领袖

column1: Another chieftain
column2: 另一位酋长

column1: Again, the combined forces were slaughtered like sheep by the zombies and ghouls.
column2: 联军再次如羔羊般被僵尸和食尸鬼屠杀。

column1: \x01@\x0B was slain. The ghouls banged drums and howled, celebrating the chance to taste a monarch’s liver.
column2: \x01@\x0B 被斩杀。食尸鬼敲鼓嚎叫，庆祝得以品尝一位君王的肝脏。

column2: \x01@\x07 被斩杀。食尸鬼蹦跳着，互相抛掷 \x04 的头颅。

column2: \x01@\x0B 承认责任，提出放弃 \x04 王位。

column1: “You know, those undead are really tough.”
column2: “你知道，那些亡灵确实很难对付。”

column1: They’re just like the typical whining traders I have to deal with all the time.
column2: 他们就像我成天要应付的那些喋喋不休的商人。

column1: There is some bluster in \x01@\x0F’s words; don’t take \x08 entirely seriously.

column1: These rascals have no reason to complain!
column2: 这些无赖没理由抱怨！

column1: We cannot win against the undead if we do not field at least seventy-five men.
column2: 如果不上阵至少七十五人，我们无法战胜亡灵。

column1: While it would be best to have seventy-five men on the field, we could win with fewer.
column2: 虽然战场上最好有七十五人，但人少些我们也能赢。

column2: 普通战争领袖需要七十五人才能对付亡灵。我用五十人，甚至二十五人都能做到。

column1: They have plenty of reason to complain.
column2: 他们有很多理由抱怨。

column1: We can deal with this by bluffing them, or with dramatic forthrightness. A tempered response is wasted here.
column2: 我们可以虚张声势，或直截了当地应对。此处无须克制回应。

column1: Don’t say anything rash just because you feel that your honor is threatened.
column2: 不要因为觉得荣誉受威胁就说些鲁莽的话。

column1: Undead are an affront to Humakt.
column2: 亡灵是对胡马克特的侮辱。

column1: \x01@\x0F is well-respected, for \x04 clan maintains its temples well.
column2: \x01@\x0F 备受尊敬，因为 \x04 氏族的庙宇维护得很好。

column1: Leaden did the order-wand fall, tilting towards Ernalda’s feet.
column2: 沉重的权杖落下，歪向厄娜尔达的脚边。

column1: Whatever we do, we must not surrender the throne.
column2: 无论我们做什么，绝不能交出王座。

column1: Even my clansmen mutter behind my back. Perhaps they would rather lead the fight against the undead.
column2: 就连本氏族的族人也在背后嘀咕。也许他们更愿意领导对抗亡灵的战争。

column1: The people of my clan support me. A dramatic gesture will show up \x01@\x0F, and win back their favor.
column2: 氏族的人们支持我。一个戏剧性的举动会凸显 \x01@\x0F，并赢回他们的恩惠。

column2: sceneR070

column1: Once more, warriors who set off to the Upland March return as walking corpses. The carls are not so easily fooled this time. Several weaponthanes start hacking at the closest walking dead, while the rest are now wander about. Several of them \x02\x03shuffle in a small circle, singing one note over and over/stop and stare some runes on a wall, puzzled/stop and stand there, staring into the distance\x02.
column2: 再一次，出发前往高地沼泽的战士们回来时变成了行尸。自由民这次可没那么容易上当。几位武器领主开始砍杀最近的行尸，其余的行尸则四处游荡。其中几个 \x02\x03绕着小圈慢慢走，一遍又一遍地唱着一个音符/停下来，困惑地盯着墙上的符文/停下来站着，凝视远方\x02。

column1: Warriors again returned from the Upland Marsh as walking corpses.
column2: 战士们再次从高地沼泽返回，变成了行尸。

column1: Warriors from your clan have returned from a mission to the Upland Marsh area as walking corpses. The carls thought they were alive at first. This gave the corpses a chance to attack by surprise. A quick-thinking warrior distracted them, and everyone got to safety. The undead are now milling about in confusion. One of them is reciting a line from Oskul’s Saga, over and over.
column2: 你氏族的战士们结束高地沼泽地区的任务返回，却变成了行尸。自由民起初以为他们还活着。这给了行尸突袭的机会。一位反应敏捷的战士引开了它们，所有人都安全了。亡灵现在正困惑地四处乱转。其中一个正在一遍又一遍地背诵奥斯库尔传说的一段话。

column1: Warriors returned from the Upland Marsh as walking corpses.
column2: 战士们从高地沼泽返回，变成了行尸。

column1: We sent warriors to drive them off.
column2: 我们派出战士去驱赶它们。

column1: The undead were driven off.
column2: 亡灵被驱赶走了。

column1: The undead fought back fiercely, and we suffered losses.
column2: 亡灵猛烈反击，我们遭受了损失。

column1: Kill them, then compensate their families.
column2: 杀死它们，然后补偿它们的家人。

column1: We sent warriors to kill them.
column2: 我们派出战士去杀死它们。

column1: The undead were slain. Although their families grieved, they agreed there was nothing else we could have done.
column2: 亡灵被杀了。尽管他们的家人悲痛不已，但他们也同意我们别无选择。

column1: Kill them, then sacrifice to Humakt, foe of the undead.
column2: 杀了他们，然后献祭给亡灵之敌胡马克特。

column1: Then we sacrificed to Humakt, foe of the undead.
column2: 于是我们献祭给亡灵之敌胡马克特。

column1: The undead were slain.
column2: 亡灵被杀了。

column1: Threaten them with legal action if they don’t leave.
column2: 如果他们不离开，就以法律行动威胁他们。

column1: Our lawspeaker threatened them with legal action if they did not leave us alone.
column2: 我们的律法师以法律行动威胁他们，如果他们不离开我们。

column1: The gibbering undead had trouble responding, but eventually agreed to go away and trouble our clan no more.
column2: 胡言乱语的亡灵难以回应，但最终同意离开，不再骚扰我们的氏族。

column1: A clan’s warriors will come back from the dead if it has too few cows.
column2: 若氏族拥有的牛只太少，其战士将会从死者中归来。

column1: You can’t bargain with the dead!
column2: 你无法与死者议价！

column1: You can try bargaining with anything, even the undead. Question is, can they bargain back at you?
column2: 你可以尝试与任何事物议价，甚至包括亡灵。问题是，它们能与你还价吗？

column1: Just get rid of them quickly. We don’t other clans gossiping about how we can’t handle our own undead.
column2: 赶紧把他们处理掉。我们可不想其他氏族嚼舌根，说我们连自己的亡灵都搞不定。

column1: This is not a complicated issue. Kill them, and be done with it.
column2: 这不是什么复杂的问题。杀了他们，然后一了百了。

column1: \x02\x03Once more/Again/Yet again\x02, kill them, and be done with it.
column2: \x02\x03再一次/再次/又一次\x02，杀了他们，然后一了百了。

column1: They are dead, but they are dead Orlanthi. They are still bound by our laws.
column2: 他们是死者，但他们是死去的奥兰蒂人。他们仍需遵循我们的律法。

column1: They are dead Orlanthi. They are bound by our laws. At least, that’s what the common lore says is so.
column2: 他们是死去的奥兰蒂人，受我们律法约束。至少，传世常理是这么说的。

column1: There are precedents for pursuing legal cases against the undead. The problem is getting them to understand you.
column2: 对亡灵提起法律诉讼是有先例的。问题在于如何让他们理解你。

column1: Legal cases against the undead are fraught with problems. Just get rid of them.
column2: 对亡灵提起法律诉讼问题重重。干脆除掉他们吧。

column1: If we let them go and they ravage other clans, our reputation will suffer.
column2: 如果我们放他们走，让他们去劫掠其他氏族，我们的声誉会受损。

column1: If we kill them and sacrifice to Humakt, we’ll be seen as proper foes of the undead.
column2: 如果我们杀了他们并向胡玛克献祭，我们会被视为亡灵的正当敌人。

column1: We must kill them.
column2: 我们必须杀了他们。

column1: Of course we must kill them. Remuneration will make their families feel better.
column2: 我们当然必须杀了他们。给予补偿会让他们的家人好受些。

column1: We must build a temple to Eurmal at the earliest opportunity.
column2: 我们必须尽早修建一座献给欧鲁莫的神殿。

column1: They \x02\x03came from our homes/sat at our boards/were of our hearth\x02, yet now attack it. For this blasphemy, they must die.
column2: 他们 \x02\x03来自我们的家园/曾坐在我们宴席旁/曾是我们炉边之人\x02，而今却攻击它。因这亵渎之举，他们必须死。

column1: You surely know by now that Humakt scorns a bloodless sacrifice.
column2: 你此刻想必已知，胡玛克鄙夷不见血的献祭。

column1: Find out which line of the saga that one is mumbling. It could be an important clue.
column2: 弄清楚那人嘟囔的是传说里的哪一段。这可能是个重要线索。

column1: Why can’t we hire the ducks to keep our walking dead under control?
column2: 为什么我们不能雇佣鸭人来管控我们的行尸？

column1: We should send them to bother and frustrate an enemy.
column2: 我们应该派他们去骚扰和挫败某个敌人。

column1: Kill them, but don’t hurt their feelings.
column2: 杀了他们，但别伤及他们的感情。

column1: Sacrifice to Humakt is surely the only good option.
column2: 向胡玛克献祭无疑是唯一的好选择。

column1: They were doomed to this fate.
column2: 他们注定有此命运。

column1: We should check everyone who might have been near them; maybe being a walking corpse is contagious.
column2: 我们应该检查所有可能靠近过他们的人；也许行尸是能传染的。

column1: Aiee! I knew that walking corpses could spread their condition!
column2: 哎呀！我就知道行尸会传播他们的状况！

column1: Oh no! They’re back! We’re all going to \x02\x03end up as/wind up as/become\x02 the walking undead!
column2: 哦不！他们回来了！我们都将 \x02\x03最终成为/落得成为/变成\x02 行尸走肉！

column1: From the grave-mistress’ stead they wandered, soul-shorn.
column2: 从墓女主人的庄园而来，他们游荡着，灵魂已被剥离。

column1: Let me \x02\x03swing the swords/use the club/hurl the spear\x02 to bring down these vile creatures.
column2: 让我 \x02\x03挥剑/用棍棒/投掷长枪\x02 来击倒这些邪恶的生物。

column1: This could be the end of our clan if we do not act!
column2: 若不行动，这将是我族的末日！

column1: Oskul’s saga has always been one of my favorites…
column2: 奥斯库尔的传说一直是我最喜欢的故事之一……

column1: If we searched the scrolls, maybe we could gain magical protection against these undead.
column2: 如果我们查阅卷轴，或许能获得抵御这些亡灵的法术保护。

column1: The undead are easily fooled.
column2: 亡灵很容易被愚弄。

column1: They once \x02\x04laughed with us/sat at our boards/shared our mead/sang songs with us\x02. Kill them, that we grieve and go on.
column2: 他们曾 \x02\x04与我们一同欢笑/曾坐在我们宴席旁/曾共饮我们的蜜酒/曾与我们齐声歌唱\x02。杀了他们，让我们哀悼，然后继续前行。

column1: Act quickly to find new warriors; accept outlaws if necessary.
column2: 迅速行动寻找新战士；必要时接纳法外之徒。

column1: We sought new warriors wherever we could find them. We even approached bandits and outlaws.
column2: 我们想方设法寻找新战士，甚至向强盗和法外之徒伸出了手。

column1: Not even they would join a fighting force so vulnerable as ours.
column2: 就连他们也不愿加入像我们这样脆弱的战斗力量。

column1: How many do you want to take on?
column2: 你想接纳多少人？

column1: We took some of them on.
column2: 我们接纳了其中一些人。

column1: The new warriors joined our weaponthanes, who welcomed their aid.
column2: 新战士加入了我们的武器领主行列，他们欢迎这份助力。

column1: Build their morale with an inspirational poem.
column2: 用一首鼓舞人心的诗歌来提振他们的士气。

column1: The warriors \x02\x02could be heard repeating favorite verses for weeks afterwards/had spring in their steps as they returned to their duties\x02.
column2: 战士们 \x02\x02在之后的数周里，仍能听到他们反复吟诵钟爱的诗句/返回职责时步伐轻盈\x02。

column1: The warriors \x02\x02walked out before the chief finished/listened in stony silence\x02.
column2: 战士们 \x02\x02在首领讲完前就走了出去/沉默地聆听，面无表情\x02。

column1: Listen to them, but do nothing.
column2: 听听他们的话，但什么都不做。

column1: Send \x01@\x1A on a mission to find the best warriors available.
column2: 派遣 \x01@\x1A 执行任务，寻找可招募的最佳战士。

column1: We sent \x01@\x1A on a mission to find the best warriors available.
column2: 我们派遣了 \x01@\x1A 执行任务，寻找可招募的最佳战士。

column1: For how many seasons do you tell \x08 to stay out on the mission?
column2: 你让 \x08 在任务中待多少季？

column1: Take on new warriors only as qualified candidates come forward.
column2: 只有当合格的候选者出现时，才接纳新战士。

column1: We kept our eyes open for qualified warriors.
column2: 我们一直留意合格的战士。

column1: We took on a number of them.
column2: 我们接纳了其中一些人。

column1: We found only one new fighter.
column2: 我们只找到一名新的战士。

column1: More warriors will help us build up our herds again.
column2: 更多的战士将帮助我们重建畜群。

column1: Other clans will be sure to raid our herds if we don’t have enough weaponthanes.
column2: 如果我们没有足够的武器领主，其他氏族一定会来劫掠我们的畜群。

column1: The more time we spend looking, the better candidates we will find.
column2: 我们花在搜寻上的时间越多，找到的候选者就越优秀。

column1: If we continue to ignore the demands of the warriors, they might remove their ancestral insignia. A weaponthane can give no greater rebuke to his ring.
column2: 如果我们继续无视战士们的要求，他们可能会摘下祖先徽章。一位武器领主能给予其议会的最大斥责莫过于此。

column1: We should go among the other clans and find warriors who already have their own horses.
column2: 我们应该前往其他氏族，寻找那些已经拥有自己战马的战士。

column1: This is no time for poetry.
column2: 现在不是吟诗的时候。

column1: Some outlaws can fight. Sometimes that’s why they’re outlaws, they fight too well.
column2: 有些法外之徒能战斗。有时候，那正是他们被放逐的原因——他们太能打了。

column1: We will be attacked by other clans if we take on outlaws.
column2: 如果我们接纳法外之徒，将会受到其他氏族的攻击。

column1: We’ll just make things worse if we try to attract warriors and fail.
column2: 如果我们试图招募战士却失败了，只会让情况更糟。

column1: Don’t be hasty. We know what we’re doing.
column2: 别着急。我们知道自己在做什么。

column1: Precedent does not forbid us from forgiving outlaws, but we must remember that most such people were outlawed for good reason.
column2: 先例并不禁止我们宽恕法外之徒，但我们必须记住，这些人大多是因为正当理由才被放逐的。

column1: Our enemies won’t attack us if we’re too weak to fight back; it would be dishonorable.
column2: 我们的敌人不会因为我们弱到无力反击就来进攻；那是不荣誉的。

column1: We need to act, but if you like I can simply cheer the warriors up, for now.
column2: 我们必须行动，但如果你愿意，我现在可以先给战士们鼓鼓劲。

column1: We have no good reason not to treat this as a serious situation.
column2: 我们没有充分的理由不把这当作严重局面来对待。

column1: Outlaws can sometimes become good clansmen. But not always.
column2: 流放者有时能成为好族人。但并非总是如此。

column1: The carls are not worried about the lack of warriors. They are glad to have fewer mouths to feed.
column2: 自由民并不担心战士不足。他们反倒高兴能少几张嘴要喂。

column1: The carls are afraid of attacks. They want more weaponthanes too.
column2: 自由民害怕遭到袭击。他们也想要更多武器领主。

column1: Fewer warriors means fewer wounds to heal, but also more wounds.
column2: 战士少了，要治的伤就少了，但伤也会更多。

column1: Warriors are always worried that someone else is stronger.
column2: 战士们总是担心别人比自己更强。

column1: The rest of you should decide.
column2: 剩下的人该由你们来决定。

column1: Clan Ormandi forgave outlaws when it was desperate for warriors, not knowing they were vampires.
column2: 奥曼迪氏族在急需战士时赦免了流放者，却不知道他们是吸血鬼。

column1: The warriors are brave, but not stupid. They need help.
column2: 战士们很勇敢，但不愚蠢。他们需要帮助。

column1: Hire more warriors quickly, then increase the patrols to look out for zombies.
column2: 尽快招募更多战士，然后加强巡逻，提防僵尸。

column1: Why are we risking disaster by remaining defenseless?
column2: 我们为何要手无寸铁地冒险招致灾难？

column1: They would not complain unless there was good cause.
column2: 若不是有充分理由，他们不会抱怨。

column1: The thing about forgiving outlaws is that, well, you know…
column2: 赦免流放者这件事嘛，嗯，你知道的……

column1: This reminds me of that story of Vingkot. You know the one.
column2: 这让我想起那个温戈特的故事。你知道的那个。

column1: We’re certain about this, right?
column2: 我们对此确定无疑，对吧？

column1: Mice are getting into the grain stores. They have eaten more than the cost of a new alynx kitten.
column2: 老鼠溜进了粮仓。它们吃掉的粮食比买一只新猞猁幼崽的钱还多。

column1: Surely we have enough warriors. They are just greedy!
column2: 我们肯定有足够多的战士。他们只是贪心！

column1: There must be some way to support our weaponthanes more cheaply.
column2: 肯定有更省钱的办法来供养我们的武器领主。

column1: They are over-reacting. Things are not as bad as they say.
column2: 他们反应过度了。情况没有他们说的那么糟。

column1: Bad King Urgrain ignored the entreaties of his war leaders, who told him that his forces were too small to join the Battle of Kanda Fant. This is why all the tales of the Urgraini are tales of woe.
column2: 恶王乌格兰无视了他战争领袖们的恳求——他们告诉他兵力太少，不足以参加卡达·凡特之战。这就是为何所有关于乌尔格伦人的故事都是悲惨故事。

column1: It won’t take much to make the weaponthanes happy. But ignoring them would be very bad.
column2: 让武器领主们满意并不需要太多。但忽视他们则会非常糟糕。

column1: Dragon Pass is too dangerous to ignore the clan’s defense.
column2: 龙之隘口太过危险，不能忽视氏族的防御。

column1: Search three seasons.
column2: 搜寻三个季节。

column1: Just wait.
column2: 只管等待。

column1: Just do something.
column2: 只管做点什么。

column1: We need shrines to the children’s gods.
column2: 我们需要供奉儿童之神的圣坛。

column1: If we don’t sacrifice properly to the war gods, no army of weaponthanes will save us.
column2: 如果我们不向战争之神正确献祭，再多武器领主的军队也救不了我们。

column1: If we remain weak, our enemies might even plunder our temples!
column2: 如果我们保持虚弱，我们的敌人们甚至可能劫掠我们的神庙！

column1: I told you we had too few warriors.
column2: 我早就说过我们战士太少了。

column1: How can we crush our foes if we do not keep the clan strong?
column2: 若不保持氏族强大，我们怎能粉碎敌人？

column1: \x01@\x1A returned from \x04 recruiting mission with
column2: \x01@\x1A 从 \x04 招募任务归来，带回了

column1: I found only two new warriors.
column2: 我只找到两个新战士。

column1: 2 new weaponthanes.
column2: 2名新武器领主。

column1: I found us \x01@\x10 skilled fighters.
column2: 我为我们找到了 \x01@\x10 熟练的战士。

column1: \x01@\x10 new weaponthanes.
column2: \x01@\x10 新武器领主。

column1: sceneR072
column2: sceneR072

column1: The warriors come to you to once again protest their poor treatment by the clan ring. They remove their ancestral insignia. “We do not want our ancestors to see us so humbled and abused,” their spokesman says. “This is a gesture no Orlanthi takes lightly. If you ignore it, I do not know what we can do, and still maintain our honor as weaponthanes.
column2: 战士们来到你面前，再次抗议氏族议会对他们的苛待。他们摘下祖先徽章。“我们不想让祖先看到我们受此屈辱，”他们的发言人说道。“这个姿态，任何奥兰斯人都不会轻率对待。如果你无视它，我不知道我们还能做什么，同时还能保持我们身为武器领主的荣誉。”

column1: The weaponthanes complained that the ring had abused them, and removed their ancestral insignia.
column2: 武器领主们抱怨议会虐待了他们，并摘下了祖先徽章。

column1: Apologize profusely; promise to honor them in the future.
column2: 诚恳道歉；承诺将来会敬重他们。

column1: The ring apologized for its past actions, and promised to honor them in the future.
column2: 议会为其过去的行为道歉，并承诺将来会敬重他们。

column1: The weaponthanes were moved by the words of the chief, but said that actions were more eloquent than even the best-sounding rhetoric.
column2: 武器领主们被首领的话所感动，但表示行动比最动听的言辞更有说服力。

column1: The weaponthanes said that the time for words had passed.
column2: 武器领主们说，言词的时机已经过去了。

column1: Embark on a heroquest.
column2: 踏上英雄任务。

column1: We decided that a heroquest would fill them with pride.
column2: 我们决定，一次英雄任务能让他们充满自豪。

column1: Our god-talkers remind us that we only know one heroquest, so we will embark upon that one.
column2: 我们的神言者提醒我们，我们只知道一个英雄任务，所以我们将踏上那个任务。

column1: Which quest do you undertake?
column2: 你进行哪个任务？

column1: Elmal Guards the Stead, where Elmal loyally defends against monsters of the Darkness.
column2: 《埃尔马尔守卫家园》，埃尔马尔忠诚地抵御黑暗中的怪物。

column1: Humakt the Champion, where Orlanth and Humakt fight, but resolve their differences.
column2: 《冠军胡马克特》，奥兰斯与胡马克特战斗，但化解了分歧。

column1: The Making of the Storm Tribe, where Orlanth binds the clans into the first tribe.
column2: 《风暴部落的创立》，奥兰斯将各氏族凝聚成首个部落。

column1: Orlanth and Aroka, where Orlanth slays the Blue Dragon.
column2: 《奥兰斯与阿罗卡》，奥兰斯斩杀蓝龙。

column1: The weaponthanes were impressed by our success. They said that their earlier words should be forgotten, and that they would wear the clan regalia proudly.
column2: 武器领主们对我们的成功印象深刻。他们说该忘记之前的话，并将骄傲地佩戴氏族徽记。

column1: The weaponthanes said that it was plain the clan did not have the favor of the gods.
column2: 武器领主们说，显然氏族并未获得神的眷顾。

column1: The weaponthanes snorted derisively at this suggestion.
column2: 武器领主们对这个提议嗤之以鼻。

column1: Despite their dudgeon, some of the weaponthanes smiled, and agreed to resolve their differences in this unorthodox way.
column2: 尽管愤愤不平，一些武器领主还是露出了微笑，并同意以这种非常规方式化解分歧。

column1: Promise sacrifices to appease their ancestors.
column2: 承诺献祭以安抚他们的祖先。

column1: We sacrificed to appease their ancestors.
column2: 我们献祭以安抚他们的祖先。

column1: The warriors replaced their regalia, thanking us for this sign of respect.
column2: 战士们重新佩戴起徽记，感谢我们这份尊重的表示。

column1: But the god-talkers said that our ancestors were displeased to receive human sacrifice.
column2: 但神言者说，我们的祖先对接受人祭感到不悦。

column1: “What shames the ancestors is your incessant whining!”
column2: “让祖先蒙羞的是你们无休止的牢骚！”

column1: For their effrontery, they were scolded.
column2: 因为他们的无礼，他们被斥责了。

column1: They hung their heads in shame.
column2: 他们羞愧地垂下头。

column1: They said that they were glad that their ancestors could no longer hear the abuse they had to tolerate.
column2: 他们说，很高兴他们的祖先再也听不到他们不得不忍受的辱骂了。

column1: We must buy off their ancestors if we are to satisfy them.
column2: 我们必须收买他们的祖先，才能让他们满意。

column1: Of course I’ve removed my own insignia. Do you think I want my ancestors seeing this shameful development?
column2: 我当然已经摘掉了自己的徽记。你以为我想让祖先看到这耻辱的一幕吗？

column1: I’ve removed my own insignia in recognition of this shameful situation. Only a heroquest or a sacrifice will bring the matter to an honorable conclusion.
column2: 我摘下自己的徽记，以示对这场耻辱局面的承认。唯有英雄任务或献祭才能让此事体面收场。

column1: They flout their responsibility to obey chosen leaders!
column2: 他们公然蔑视服从选出的领袖这一责任！

column1: Their claims are not unjustified.
column2: 他们的诉求并非毫无道理。

column1: Their claims are not unjustified. A heroquest could restore their trust in us.
column2: 他们的诉求并非毫无道理。一次英雄任务可以重建他们对我们的信任。

column1: Their claims are justified. An apology may help, but the real solution is correct action in the future.
column2: 他们的诉求有道理。道歉或有帮助，但真正的解决之道在于未来的正确行动。

column1: Their claims are justified. We could promise better action in the future, but a heroquest now would reconcile them soonest.
column2: 他们的诉求有道理。我们可以承诺未来做得更好，但立即进行英雄任务能最快让他们和解。

column1: Shaming them is risky, but it just might work.
column2: 羞辱他们有风险，但或许可行。

column1: Apology will only work if it comes from the heart, and is followed by right actions.
column2: 道歉只有发自内心，并以正确的行动跟上，才会奏效。

column1: A heroquest would show them that we mean to change our ways for the better.
column2: 一次英雄任务能向他们表明，我们意在真正改过自新。

column1: I am glad that the carls are never this troublesome.
column2: 我很庆幸自由民从不这么麻烦。

column1: Elmal’s sacred quest could bring the weaponthanes and the clan back together.
column2: 埃尔马尔的神圣任务能让武器领主与氏族重归于好。

column1: The weaponthanes want respect. Sacrificing to their ancestors would begin to show that respect.
column2: 武器领主想要尊重。向他们的祖先献祭，就能开始展现这份尊重。

column1: The heroquest of Humakt the Champion might be used to heal the breach between the ring and weaponthanes.
column2: 勇者胡马克特的英雄任务或许能弥合长老会与武器领主之间的裂痕。

column1: The Storm Tribe quest would show the weaponthanes that we take them seriously.
column2: 风暴部落任务能让武器领主看到我们认真对待他们。

column1: The Orlanth and Aroka quest would make the weaponthanes strong, showing them we have their interests at heart.
column2: 奥兰斯与阿罗卡任务会让武器领主变得强大，表明我们真心把他们利益放在心上。

column1: Either the Storm Tribe quest or the Orlanth and Aroka quest would show the weaponthanes that we take their interests seriously.
column2: 风暴部落任务或奥兰斯与阿罗卡任务都能让武器领主看到我们认真对待他们的利益。

column1: Arm-wrestling will do the trick, and allows us to gamble as well. I bet on their champion!
column2: 扳手腕就能解决问题，还能顺便赌一把。我押他们的冠军！

column1: During the Storm Age, when Orlanth fought his brothers, he settled his differences with Kolat by arm-wrestling.
column2: 在风暴时代，当奥兰斯与他的兄弟们作战时，他就是通过扳手腕与科拉特了结分歧的。

column1: Make them shut up!
column2: 让他们闭嘴！

column1: We must show the ancestors that we have not lost our knack for generosity.
column2: 我们必须向祖先证明，我们没有失去慷慨的本事。

column1: Whatever you do, don’t insult them further.
column2: 无论你做什么，都别再进一步侮辱他们了。

column1: Wrath-mead was quick-drunk; cool reflection fell onto the blade-grass.
column2: 愤怒之蜜酒一口饮尽；冷静的反思落入剑草之中。

column1: A sincere apology is required here.
column2: 这里需要真诚的道歉。

column1: Abandon negotiations.
column2: 放弃谈判。

column1: \x02\x03Despite our/In spite of our/Although we had\x02 \x02\x06auspicious beginnings/seeming success/initial high hopes/similar ambitions/similar desires/good wishes on both sides\x02,
column2: \x02\x03尽管我们/尽管我们/虽然我们\x02 \x02\x06开端吉利/看似成功/起初期望很高/有类似雄心/有类似愿望/双方都心存善意\x02，

column1: when it came time to \x02\x03ask them to attend/request their presence at/get their promise to come to\x02 the confederation moot, they \x02\x03would not agree to do so/balked/refused us\x02.
column2: 但到了需要 \x02\x03请他们参加/请求他们出席/征得他们承诺参加\x02 联盟大会的时候，他们 \x02\x03却不肯同意/退缩了/拒绝了我们的请求\x02。

column1: They \x02\x04said that they were not quite ready to join a tribe yet/seemed disappointed in the negotiations, as if they expected much more/wished us better luck with other clans/said the idea was a good one, but the details of our negotiations did not satisfy their misgivings yet\x02.
column2: 他们 \x02\x04说自己还没完全准备好加入一个部落/似乎对谈判感到失望，仿佛期待更多/祝我们与其他氏族运气更好/说这个想法不错，但谈判的细节尚未打消他们的疑虑\x02。

column1: We realized we had \x02\x05blundered into a bad situation by mistake/no chance of winning them over/underestimated their greed/overestimated their fondness for us/a very poor chance of convincing them of anything\x02, and wisely withdrew our offer before we did our relations any more harm.
column2: 我们意识到我们 \x02\x05误入了糟糕局面/毫无赢得他们的希望/低估了他们的贪婪/高估了他们对我们的好感/几乎不可能说服他们任何事\x02，于是在进一步损害关系之前明智地撤回了提议。

column1: Accept the “20 cows worth of pots per year” requirement.
column2: 接受“每年价值20头牛的陶罐”的要求。

column1: We agreed that the clans of the tribe should buy as many pots as they specified.
column2: 我们同意了部落中的氏族应购买他们指定数量的陶罐。

column1: They offered to let us choose a different decoration each year.
column2: 他们提出每年让我们选择不同的花纹。

column1: Accept the “no other containers” requirement.
column2: 接受“不得有其他容器”的要求。

column1: We agreed that the tribe should use no containers but \x01@! containers.
column2: 我们同意了部落不得使用除 \x01@! 容器外的任何容器。

column1: They were pleased by our acceptance.
column2: 他们对我们的接受感到满意。

column1: Suggest a smaller number of pots per year.
column2: 建议减少每年的陶罐数量。

column1: We suggested that the clans should buy fewer pots each year than they first suggested.
column2: 我们建议各氏族每年购买的陶罐数量应少于他们最初提出的数量。

column1: Instead, they agreed to \x01@\x10 cows worth of pots each year.
column2: 结果，他们同意了每年价值 \x01@\x10 头牛的陶罐。

column1: They would not alter their proposal.
column2: 他们不愿修改自己的提议。

column1: Accept the tribal council requirement.
column2: 接受部落议会席位的要求。

column1: We promised them one seat on the tribal council.
column2: 我们承诺在部落议会中给他们一个席位。

column1: They were pleased to receive the seat.
column2: 他们对获得席位感到高兴。

column1: Give gifts.
column2: 赠送礼物。

column1: We gifted them.
column2: 我们赠予了他们礼物。

column1: They were unwilling to be in our debt, and gave reciprocal gifts of equal value.
column2: 他们不愿欠我们人情，回赠了同等价值的礼物。

column1: The \x01@! ring said that their clan was interested in joining the tribe.
column2: \x01@! 长老会说他们的氏族有意加入部落。

column1: They must have large and healthy herds to give so much time to their kiln.
column2: 他们能花这么多时间在窑炉上，必定拥有庞大健康的畜群。

column1: 20 cows a year worth of pots is a lot of pots.
column2: 每年价值20头牛的陶罐数量相当可观。

column1: Even if we buy fewer pots than they suggest, they will be worth less than we pay for them, because everyone in the area will be swimming in them.
column2: 即便我们买的陶罐比他们建议的少，这些罐子的价值也低于我们支付的价钱，因为整个地区所有人都将淹没在陶罐里。

column1: All these demands. And they will still be a thorn in our side at tribal moots.
column2: 所有这些要求。而且他们还会在部落大会上继续成为我们的麻烦。

column1: They have many brave warriors at their disposal; we should meet their demands.
column2: 他们拥有许多勇敢的战士可供调遣；我们应该满足他们的要求。

column1: Their warriors aren’t worth much, but they are already our allies. They’ll stand with us.
column2: 他们的战士不值一提，但他们已经是我们的盟友。他们会站在我们这边。

column1: They have few warriors of note. Ignore their demands now, and conquer them later.
column2: 他们没有几个值得一提的战士。现在无视他们的要求，日后征服他们。

column1: Our freedom-loving neighbors will rebel if forced to throw away all of their other containers.
column2: 我们热爱自由的邻居若被迫扔掉所有其他容器，就会反叛。

column1: They ask too much and they are already our enemies. We would be foolish to bring them into the tribe.
column2: 他们索求太多，且已是我们的敌人。若将他们纳入部落，实属愚蠢。

column1: If we make generous commitments on behalf of other clans, they may balk when it comes time to form a tribe.
column2: 若我们代表其他氏族做出慷慨承诺，到组建部落时他们可能会反悔。

column1: The woven basket is very important to the grain rituals of certain clans.
column2: 编织篮对某些氏族的谷物仪式至关重要。

column1: Their precious pots do not match the myths of many of the other clans, which require woven baskets. And the other clans are our friends.
column2: 他们珍贵的陶罐与许多其他氏族的神话不符——那些神话需要编织篮。而其他氏族是我们的朋友。

column1: Our barley plants will yield more if they know their grain is to be stored in such fine pots.
column2: 我们的大麦若知道谷物将存放在如此精美的陶罐中，收成会更丰。

column1: Yelm owned six pots made by Harana Ilor, goddess of harmony. Orlanth smashed five, and kept duck eggs in the sixth.
column2: 耶尔姆拥有和谐女神哈拉娜·伊洛尔制作的六个陶罐。奥兰斯打碎了五个，第六个用来装鸭蛋。

column1: We have been enemies. Can we be friends?
column2: 我们曾是敌人。能成为朋友吗？

column1: Their famous force of ghoul-fighters will make our tribe a bulwark against the unliving.
column2: 他们著名的食尸鬼战士部队将使我们的部落成为抵御亡灵的前哨。

column1: It is bad to raise one’s love of one’s own work above one’s love for Ernalda and her family.
column2: 若将自己工作的热爱凌驾于对厄娜尔达及其家人的爱之上，是不好的。

column1: Already they are trying to tell us how things will be, and not the other way around.
column2: 他们已经试图告诉我们事情该如何发展，而非反过来。

column1: I don’t understand this pot business. There must be a female mystery behind it.
column2: 我不明白这陶罐的事。背后必有女性奥秘。

column1: I find it hard to believe they have survived this long in Dragon Pass.
column2: 我很难相信他们能在龙之隘口存活这么久。

column2: 我想要王位，也配得上，而且我们负担得起。提名我。

column1: Even though I feel that I deserve the throne, it will be difficult for our clan to win this round of king-choosing.
column2: 尽管我觉得自己配得上王位，但本轮选王对我们氏族来说很难获胜。

column1: Though I am well qualified for the throne, the Vingan requirement stands in my way.
column2: 尽管我完全有资格登上王位，但温甘要求成了我的障碍。

column1: I am well qualified for the throne, and ready to rule the tribe. I would be honored to be chosen.
column2: 我完全有资格登上王位，并且准备好统治部落。如被选中，我深感荣幸。

column1: Your new tribe still needs to choose a king, one who is able to survive the kingship rites. The candidate must be able to lead and protect the people of the tribe; he or she must be strong and generous. Once a candidate is chosen, that candidate must complete the sacred rites unique to your tribe.
column2: 你的新部落仍需要选出一位国王，一位能通过王权仪式的国王。候选人必须能够领导和保护部落人民；他或她必须既强壮又慷慨。一旦选定候选人，该候选人必须完成你们部落独有的神圣仪式。

column1: The clans of the new tribe gathered once again to choose a king.
column2: 新部落的氏族再次聚集，以选出一位国王。

column1: Now that you have other clans wanting to join with you and become a tribe, you must choose a king. The king must be able to lead and protect the people of the tribe; he or she must be strong and generous. Once a candidate is chosen, that candidate must design and complete a sacred rite unique to your tribe. All future kings will have to undergo these rites as well.
column2: 既然有其他氏族希望加入你们并组成部落，你们必须选出一位国王。国王必须能够领导和保护部落人民；他或她必须既强壮又慷慨。一旦选定候选人，该候选人必须设计和完成你们部落独有的神圣仪式。所有未来的国王也都必须经历这些仪式。

column1: The clans of the new tribe gathered to choose a king.
column2: 新部落的氏族聚集以选出一位国王。

column1: Support a candidate from the clan most obligated to you.
column2: 支持一个最亏欠你们的氏族的候选人。

column1: We supported the candidate chosen by the \x01@! clan, which owed us more favors than any other.
column2: 我们支持了 \x01@! 氏族选择的候选人，该氏族欠我们的恩惠比任何其他氏族都多。

column1: Support a candidate from the strongest fighting clan.
column2: 支持一个来自最强战斗氏族的候选人。

column1: We said that the \x01@! clan had first right to the throne, because they had many well-equipped warriors.
column2: 我们说 \x01@! 氏族拥有王位的优先权，因为他们拥有许多装备精良的战士。

column1: To prove their generosity, the candidates of the other clans gave us many cows.
column2: 为证明他们的慷慨，其他氏族的候选人们给了我们许多牛。

column1: It is better to support a king and get cows, than to be a king and give cows.
column2: 支持一位国王并得到牛，总比当国王而给出牛要好。

column1: Only a rich clan can play the game of kings.
column2: 只有富有的氏族才能玩得起王者游戏。

column1: We can afford to pay the cows necessary to win support.
column2: 我们付得起赢得支持所需的牛。

column1: We are still wealthy enough to pay cows to garner support for our candidate.
column2: 我们仍然足够富有，可以拿出牛来为我们的候选人争取支持。

column1: Let’s save our herds and try for the kingship later.
column2: 让我们保留我们的牛群，以后再去争夺王权。

column1: To be a king, you must be generous. We are too poor to house the throne.
column2: 要成为国王，你必须慷慨。我们太穷了，坐不起王座。

column1: We will be looked down upon if we do not field a candidate.
column2: 如果我们不推举一位候选人，我们会被人看不起。

column1: It is rare for two consecutive kings to be chosen from the same clan.
column2: 连续两位国王从同一氏族选出是很少见的。

column1: It is rare for two consecutive kings to be chosen from the same clan. There is no point in waiting — let us seize the glory now!
column2: 连续两位国王从同一氏族选出是很少见的。等待毫无意义——现在就让我们抓住荣耀！

column1: We will have to wait until a more auspicious day to try for the kingship.
column2: 我们必须等到一个更吉利的日子再去争夺王位。

column1: The main reason to form a tribe is mutual protection, so we must provide the king.
column2: 组成部落的主要原因是相互保护，所以我们必须提供国王。

column1: The main reason to form a tribe is mutual protection, so we must support the \x01à.
column2: 组成部落的主要原因是相互保护，所以我们必须支持 \x01à.

column1: If the king thinks we were instrumental in his nomination, we will benefit from his rule.
column2: 如果国王认为我们在他的提名中起了重要作用，我们就会从他的统治中受益。

column1: The other clans owe us the throne.
column2: 其他氏族欠我们王位。

column1: We must repair our relations with the other clans before we can expect to take the throne.
column2: 我们必须先修复与其他氏族的关系，才能指望登上王位。

column1: Our candidate failed the rites. Now we must step aside and let another clan try.
column2: 我们的候选人未能通过仪式。现在我们必须退让，让另一个氏族尝试。

column1: We only select a nominee. The gods and spirits who oversee the rites of kingship truly choose the king.
column2: 我们只是选出一名提名人。真正挑选国王的是监督王权仪式的神灵和精魂。

column1: The gods who oversee the rites of kingship did not favor us for kingship last time. We must support another clan’s candidate now.
column2: 上次，监督王权仪式的诸神并未眷顾我们获得王权。现在我们只能支持另一个氏族的候选人。

column1: The best bull always wins.
column2: 最棒的公牛总会获胜。

column1: Allow me to test my eloquence!
column2: 让我试试我的口才！

column1: Hold a poetry contest, let the biggest wind-bag win!
column2: 举办一场诗歌比赛，让最能吹的人获胜！

column1: King Heort was rejected three times by his tribe before becoming king, and remaking the Storm Clans.
column2: 赫尔特国王在成为国王并重塑风暴氏族之前，曾被他的部落拒绝了三次。

column1: Choosing a Vingan queen would start the tribe off right, and fulfill our promise.
column2: 选择一位温甘女王可以让部落良好开端，并履行我们的承诺。

column1: The other clans think well enough of our clan, and of me. I would be honored to lead the tribe. Nominate me.
column2: 其他氏族对我们氏族和我都评价很高。若领导部落，我深感荣幸。请提名我。

column1: Even though I feel that I could lead the tribe, we must better our relations first.
column2: 尽管我觉得自己能够领导部落，但我们必须先改善关系。

column1: Clan \x01@!, famed for its robust pig herds, wants the following if they are to join your new tribe.
column2: 以其庞大的猪群闻名的 \x01@!氏族，如果他们要加入你的新部落，他们希望得到以下条件。

column1: Each clan of the tribe must sacrifice a dozen pigs to Mralota, the Pig Mother, each year, on her High Holy Day. A Pig Mother priestess must sit on the tribal council one year in four.
column2: 部落的每个氏族每年必须在猪母神姆拉洛塔的至高圣日向她献祭十二头猪。猪母神的女祭司每四年中必须有一年在部落议会中任职。

column1: The pig clan, Clan \x01@!, made many demands when asked to join our new tribe.
column2: 养猪氏族， \x01@!氏族，在被邀请加入我们的新部落时提出了许多要求。

column1: Clan \x01@! wants each clan of the tribe to sacrifice a dozen pigs to Mralota, the Pig Mother, each year. A Pig Mother priestess must sit on the tribal council one year in four.
column2: \x01@! 氏族希望部落的每个氏族每年向猪母神姆拉洛塔献祭十二头猪。猪母神的女祭司每四年中必须有一年在部落议会中任职。

column1: They said they would hold us to our promise.
column2: 他们说会要求我们履行承诺。

column1: Agree to provide acorns.
column2: 同意提供橡子。

column1: We agreed that each of the other clans should provide them with ten baskets of acorns a year.
column2: 我们同意其他氏族每年各向他们提供十筐橡子。

column1: They said their pigs would be much fatter and tastier.
column2: 他们说他们的猪会更肥更美味。

column1: Agree to Mralota sacrifices.
column2: 同意向姆拉洛塔献祭。

column1: We agreed that other clans should sacrifice to Mralota, the Pig Mother.
column2: 我们同意其他氏族应向猪母神姆拉洛塔献祭。

column1: How many pigs should each clan be obligated to sacrifice each year?
column2: 每个氏族每年应被要求献祭多少头猪？

column1: They said Mralota would be very pleased.
column2: 他们说姆拉洛塔会非常高兴。

column1: They said Mralota would be pleased.
column2: 他们说姆拉洛塔会很高兴。

column1: Allow a Mralota priestess on the tribal council every four years.
column2: 允许每四年有一位姆拉洛塔的女祭司进入部落议会。

column1: We agreed to allow a Mralota priestess on the tribal council every four years.
column2: 我们同意每四年允许一位姆拉洛塔的女祭司进入部落议会。

column1: They promised she would represent all the pig-tenders of the tribe.
column2: 他们承诺她会代表部落中所有养猪人。

column1: Demand that they use their wealth to aid poorer clans.
column2: 要求他们利用自己的财富帮助更贫穷的氏族。
