column1: We told them that they would be expected to use their wealth to aid poorer clans.
column2: 我们告诉他们，他们需用自己的财富接济更贫弱的氏族。

column1: What is the maximum they should expect to pay out each year?
column2: 他们每年最多该付多少？

column1: They agreed.
column2: 他们同意了。

column1: They agreed, but grudgingly.
column2: 他们同意了，但很不情愿。

column1: The \x01@! ring wanted to join our tribe.
column2: \x01@! 族想要加入我们的部落。

column1: Pigs, cows, they are all the same.
column2: 猪也好，牛也好，都一样。

column1: Even if we talk them into joining the tribe, they will do nothing but oppose us in tribal moots.
column2: 即便我们说服他们加入部落，他们到头来也只会在部落大会上与我们作对。

column1: What these people want more than anything is acceptance of their ways.
column2: 这些人最想要的，莫过于他们的习俗被接纳。

column1: We can easily afford to provide them with acorns. And I doubt they will be happy with less than 10 pigs per year, per clan.
column2: 我们完全拿得出橡子给他们。而且我怀疑，每年每个氏族少于十头猪他们不会满意。

column1: They might be less of a threat to us if we’re in the same tribe.
column2: 若同属一个部落，他们可能对我们威胁更小。

column1: This clan wisely uses its wealth to support its weaponthanes. We should do what is necessary to recruit them.
column2: 这个氏族明智地用财富供养武器领主。我们该尽力招揽他们。

column1: This clan foolishly squanders its wealth on squealing hogs. We should abandon negotiations.
column2: 这个氏族愚蠢地把财富挥霍在哼哼叫的猪身上。我们该放弃谈判。

column1: It is contrary to custom to allow a priestess of the Pig Mother a spot on the tribal council.
column2: 让猪母祭司在部落议会中占一席之地，是违背习俗的。

column1: Someone tell me why we should bring our enemies into the tribe. Do you know?
column2: 谁能告诉我，为何要把敌人引入部落？你知道吗？

column1: Better to have them in our tribe than in another tribe and escalating our feud.
column2: 让他们加入我们的部落，总好过加入另一个部落而加深世仇。

column1: They ask for strange things. Can we settle our feud by bringing them into the tribe, or should we just ignore them?
column2: 他们索要奇怪的东西。我们能通过吸纳他们入部落来化解世仇，还是干脆不理他们？

column1: They ask for many strange things. We must extract other concessions from them in return, or the other clans will reject the deal.
column2: 他们索要许多奇怪的东西。我们必须从他们那里换取其他让步，否则其他氏族会拒绝这笔交易。

column1: Their silly ways are insulting to our ancestors. Let them wallow in their slops.
column2: 他们愚蠢的做派侮辱了我们的祖先。让他们在泔水里打滚去吧。

column1: If we offer them a sacrifice of less than five pigs every year for each clan, they will be insulted.
column2: 如果我们每年每个氏族献祭少于五头猪，他们会觉得受辱。

column1: If we offer them a sacrifice of less than nine pigs every year for each clan, they will be insulted.
column2: 如果我们每年每个氏族献祭少于九头猪，他们会觉得受辱。

column1: Offend Esra, the grain goddess, to please Mralota, the pig goddess? Never!
column2: 为取悦猪神姆拉洛塔而冒犯谷神埃斯拉？绝不！

column1: Our feud is tiresome. But we will have new battles if we let the priestesses on the council.
column2: 世仇令人厌倦。但如果让祭司进入议会，我们会有新的争斗。

column1: We are forming a tribe for glory and renown. Not to suckle with dung-thanes.
column2: 我们组建部落是为了荣耀与声名，不是要和粪领主同流合污。

column1: Well, how much are they willing to give?
column2: 那么，他们愿意给多少？

column1: They deserve as much respect as any other honest clan.
column2: 他们应得到与其他正直氏族同等的尊重。

column1: Acorns for cows.
column2: 用橡子换牛。

column1: Pig.
column2: 猪。

column1: The gift of pig slop is generosity of a most affordable sort.
column2: 送猪泔水这种礼物，是最省钱的慷慨。

column1: Oh yes. I’ll be happy to give them my specialest acorns.
column2: 哦，是的。我很乐意给他们我最特别的橡子。

column1: We’d smell better if we stood alone.
column2: 如果我们独立于世，闻起来会更好些。

column1: Mrolata doesn’t even have legends of her own. They’re just Uralda’s stories with a different name.
column2: 姆罗洛塔连自己的传说都没有。那不过是乌拉达的故事换了个名字。

column1: Mralota, the Pig Mother, doesn’t even have any legends of her own. They’re just Uralda’s stories, changed a bit.
column2: 猪母姆拉洛塔连自己的传说都没有。那不过是乌拉达的故事，稍作改动而已。

column1: They ask for slops and leftovers. Their minds are in the mud.
column2: 他们索要泔水剩饭。他们的心思都在泥里。

column1: Our feud is futile. In a tribe, we can settle our differences and both come out ahead.
column2: 我们的世仇毫无意义。在部落里，我们可以化解分歧，双方都得利。

column1: Our emissaries were told of the conditions under which Clan \x01@! would join our tribe.
column2: 我们的使者得知了 \x01@! 氏族加入我部的条件。

column1: Allow them to contribute less to tribal warfare than other clans.
column2: 允许他们比其他氏族对部落战争贡献更少。

column1: We told them they could send fewer warriors to tribal wars than the other clans.
column2: 我们告诉他们，他们可以比其他氏族派出更少的战士参加部落战争。

column1: How many \x01@! warriors?
column2: 派多少 \x01@! 战士？

column1: They said that they would be better able to prepare victory feasts.
column2: 他们说，这样他们更能筹备胜利盛宴。

column1: We told them they would have to cook for the tribe at its moots and feasts.
column2: 我们告诉他们，他们必须在部落大会和盛宴上为部落做饭。

column1: Do you require them to supply more than their share of the ingredients for these feasts?
column2: 你是否要求他们为盛宴提供超过其份额的食材？

column1: They were most pleased to agree.
column2: 他们非常高兴地同意了。

column1: They grudgingly agreed.
column2: 他们勉强同意了。

column1: Require each clan to spend time growing their herbs and spices.
column2: 要求每个氏族花时间种植自己的草药和香料。

column1: We agreed that each clan should spend time growing their herbs and spices.
column2: 我们同意每个氏族应该花时间种植草药和香料。

column1: How much are they required to grow?
column2: 他们需要种多少？

column1: A token amount.
column2: 象征性的数量。

column1: Enough for the clan’s own use.
column2: 够氏族自用。

column1: Enough to trade.
column2: 够用来交易。

column1: They were happy that we’d agreed.
column2: 他们很高兴我们同意了。

column1: Support exploration.
column2: 支持探索。

column1: We agreed to support exploration in search of forgotten food plants.
column2: 我们同意支持探索，寻找被遗忘的食物植物。

column1: They said they could already almost taste the plants we’d find.
column2: 他们说，仿佛已经尝到了我们将找到的植物。

column1: The \x01@! ring agreed to our terms.
column2: \x01@! 族同意了我们的条件。

column1: Make them send thirty cows to each feast for every ten the rest of us send.
column2: 要求他们每场盛宴送三十头牛，而我们其余人每场送十头。

column1: Make them send twenty cows to each feast for every ten the rest of us send.
column2: 要求他们每场盛宴送二十头牛，而我们其余人每场送十头。

column1: If they want to join the tribe, let them show it by giving up their cows.
column2: 若他们想加入部落，让他们用交出牛来证明。

column1: Make them send fifteen cows to each feast for every ten the rest of us send.
column2: 要求他们每场盛宴送十五头牛，而我们其余人每场送十头。

column1: Our enemies will not join the tribe unless we are very generous to them.
column2: 除非我们非常慷慨，否则敌人不会加入部落。

column1: These stuffed hogs will be nothing but trouble for us in a tribe.
column2: 这些猪猡在部落里只会给我们带来麻烦。

column1: Although it seems like a demand, if we phrase it correctly, they will see the requirement to cook at our feasts as a privilege.
column2: 虽然听起来像要求，但如果我们措辞得当，他们会把在我们的盛宴上做饭视为特权。

column1: These belly-shakers are not worth our time. Let’s form a tribe without them, then conquer them.
column2: 这些摇肚皮的不值得我们花时间。我们先组建部落撇开他们，然后再征服他们。

column1: These belly-shakers are not worth much, but they are our allies. We could just ignore them for now.
column2: 这些摇肚皮的不怎么样，但他们是我们的盟友。我们可以暂且不理他们。

column1: In a tribe, any ally is a good ally.
column2: 在部落里，任何盟友都是好盟友。

column1: If they contribute less to tribal warfare, they must contribute more in some other area.
column2: 如果他们对部落战争贡献更少，就必须在其他方面贡献更多。

column1: We can let them send fewer warriors than the rest of us, but not so few that the other clans balk.
column2: 我们可以允许他们比其余人派出更少的战士，但不能少到其他氏族反对。

column1: Let them send seven warriors where the rest of us send ten.
column2: 让他们派出七名勇士，而我们其余人派出十名。

column1: They are our enemies. Perhaps we could change that.
column2: 他们是我们的敌人。或许我们可以改变这一点。

column1: Let them send seven warriors where the rest of us send ten. Agree to explore for new foods, which might benefit all.
column2: 让他们派出七名勇士，而我们其余人派出十名。同意探索新食物，这或许能让所有人受益。

column1: Exploration might also find herbs useful for magic, or useful treasures and secrets. The other clans will not see it as too costly a requirement.
column2: 探索还可能找到对魔法有用的草药，或有用的财宝与秘密。其他氏族不会认为这个要求代价太高。

column1: One plot of land out of five is not too much to turn over to growing herbs.
column2: 五块地中划出一块来种植草药，并不过分。

column1: One plot of land out of ten is not too much to turn over to growing herbs.
column2: 十块地中划出一块来种植草药，并不过分。

column1: The herbs they want us to grow will probably poison our crops.
column2: 他们要我们种的草药，很可能会毒害我们的庄稼。

column1: One plot of land out of twenty is not too much to turn over to growing herbs.
column2: 二十块地中划出一块来种植草药，并不过分。

column1: They’re a sick bunch.
column2: 他们是一群病秧子。

column1: Why should we trust what their cooks prepare? Better to prepare feast-food ourselves.
column2: 我们凭什么相信他们的厨子准备的食物？最好还是我们自己准备宴席食物。

column1: What they want most is to be able to pursue their cooking magics instead of fighting.
column2: 他们最想要的是能够钻研烹饪魔法，而不是打仗。

column1: If they really don’t want to fight, why force them?
column2: 如果他们真的不想打仗，何必强迫他们？

column1: I’m not sure I want to get mixed up with their cooking magic. Didn’t they try to poison Good King Oskul?
column2: 我不确定是否想卷入他们的烹饪魔法。他们不是曾试图毒害贤王奥斯库尔吗？

column1: Too fat.
column2: 太肥了。

column1: They want to find plants, we will find new treasures. Our interests coincide.
column2: 他们想找植物，我们会找到新财宝。我们的利益一致。

column1: This pastry is delicious! We must have this clan among us!
column2: 这糕点真美味！我们必须把这个氏族拉入我们中间！

column1: Why couldn’t the \x01@! heroquester enter the God Plane? Because she was too fat to leave her stead.
column2: 为什么那位 \x01@! 英雄探索者无法进入神界？因为她太胖了，离不开她的宅地。

column1: They eat and eat and have no stomachs for fighting! Let’s crush them!
column2: 他们只会吃吃吃，毫无战斗之心！让我们碾碎他们！

column1: The \x01@! clan, known for its rich crop yields, entertains your proposal for a new tribe.
column2: 以丰收闻名的 \x01@! 氏族，正在考虑你关于建立新部落的提议。

column1: We learned of the \x01@! demands for joining the new tribe.
column2: 我们得知了加入新部落的 \x01@! 条件。

column1: They want each clan of the new tribe to give them fertility magic every year.
column2: 他们要求新部落的每个氏族每年都向他们提供丰收魔法。

column1: They want a treasure.
column2: 他们想要一件财宝。

column1: Agree to give them fertility magic.
column2: 同意向他们提供丰收魔法。

column1: We agreed that the other clans should lend them fertility magic.
column2: 我们同意其他氏族应当借给他们丰收魔法。

column1: How much magic should each clan give them?
column2: 每个氏族应该给他们多少魔法？

column1: Some, but not a lot.
column2: 给一些，但不要太多。

column1: All a prosperous clan can spare.
column2: 所有富裕氏族能匀出来的全部。

column1: They thanked us for the offer.
column2: 他们感谢我们的提议。

column1: Agree to trade restrictions.
column2: 同意贸易限制。

column1: They seemed pleased.
column2: 他们似乎很满意。

column1: Demand favorable trade terms for other clans in the tribe seeking \x01@! grain.
column2: 要求为部落中寻求 \x01@! 谷物的其他氏族争取有利的贸易条件。

column1: We demanded favorable trade terms for other clans of the tribe seeking \x01@! grain.
column2: 我们要求为部落中寻求 \x01@! 谷物的其他氏族争取有利的贸易条件。

column1: They agreed, but didn’t seem very pleased by our request.
column2: 他们同意了，但似乎对我们的要求不太满意。

column1: Promise them a treasure.
column2: 承诺给他们一件财宝。

column1: To make the deal more attractive, we promised to give them a treasure.
column2: 为了让交易更有吸引力，我们承诺给他们一件财宝。

column1: They thanked us for\x01@\x01\x01@\x13.
column2: 他们因为\x01@\x01\x01@\x13向我们致谢。

column1: The \x01@! ring saw opportunities in our proposal.
column2: \x01@! 议会看到了我们提议中的机遇。

column1: They ask for many things. See to it that they give us plenty of grain for our cows, from now on.
column2: 他们索求甚多。从今往后，务必要让他们用大量谷物来换取我们的牛只。

column1: Ask them to trade \x01@\x19 Bushels of grain for 10 cows.
column2: 要求他们以 \x01@\x19 蒲式耳谷物交换10头牛。

column1: Ask them to trade \x01@\x14 Bushels of grain for 10 cows.
column2: 要求他们以 \x01@\x14 蒲式耳谷物交换10头牛。

column1: Ask them to trade \x01@\x15 Bushels of grain for 10 cows.
column2: 要求他们以 \x01@\x15 蒲式耳谷物交换10头牛。

column1: Ask them to trade \x01@\x16 Bushels of grain for 10 cows.
column2: 要求他们以 \x01@\x16 蒲式耳谷物交换10头牛。

column1: I, for one, want to learn their secrets. Let’s make an honest effort.
column2: 我个人很想学到他们的秘密。让我们诚心诚意地努力。

column1: Give them what they want, give them a treasure… just don’t give them a war treasure.
column2: 给他们想要的，给他们一件财宝……只是别给战争财宝。

column1: Give them what they want.
column2: 给他们想要的。

column1: Any deal we make with these enemies just makes them stronger.
column2: 与这些敌人达成的任何交易，都只会让他们更强大。

column1: We do not have what they want most, a treasure.
column2: 我们没有他们最想要的东西——一件财宝。

column1: Remember, if we give them a treasure, they get to keep it, even if no tribe is formed.
column2: 记住，如果我们给了他们一件财宝，即使部落没有建成，他们也照样保留。

column1: Since we can’t offer them a treasure, we will have to be extremely generous.
column2: 既然我们无法提供财宝，那就必须极为慷慨。

column1: I don’t trust them. We need allies, not foes.
column2: 我不信任他们。我们需要盟友，而不是敌人。

column1: If we give a little, I feel that they will join us. Our feud could be over soon.
column2: 如果我们稍作让步，我觉得他们会加入。我们的世仇或许很快就能了结。

column1: If we bring them into the tribe, we must work hard to end our feud.
column2: 如果我们将他们纳入部落，就必须努力终结我们的世仇。

column1: Other tribes will dislike the trade restrictions, but dislike is not hate.
column2: 其他部落会不喜欢贸易限制，但不喜欢不等于憎恨。

column1: If we give them all the fertility we can spare, their magic will rub off on us, and all will prosper.
column2: 如果我们把能匀出的丰收魔法全部给他们，他们的魔法也会影响到我们，所有人都将兴旺。

column1: We must be cautious with our clan fertility. Give them some, but not much.
column2: 我们必须谨慎对待氏族的丰收之力。给他们一些，但不要太多。

column1: Bringing them into the tribe might work out.
column2: 把他们拉进部落或许可行。

column1: Give them some magic; it will be worth it to end our feud.
column2: 给他们一些魔法；为了终结世仇，这值得。

column1: A token amount of our fertility will strengthen their magic greatly, without costing us dearly.
column2: 少量的丰收之力就能大大增强他们的魔法，而不会让我们付出太多代价。

column1: They are rich. It is worth it to give them a treasure, for we might learn their secrets of fertility.
column2: 他们很富有。给他们一件财宝是值得的，因为我们或许能学到他们丰收的秘密。

column1: They are rich. If they are in our tribe, we might learn their secrets of fertility.
column2: 他们很富有。如果他们加入我们的部落，我们或许能学到他们丰收的秘密。

column1: We could learn something from these enemies. I say we try to bring them into the tribe.
column2: 我们能从这些敌人身上学到东西。我说，我们应该尝试把他们拉进部落。

column1: They have been our enemies, but they keep faith with Barntar. I hate to admit it, but they’re good Orlanthi.
column2: 他们曾是我们的敌人，但他们坚守对巴恩塔的信仰。我虽然不愿承认，但他们是优秀的奥兰斯人。

column1: Give them a token amount of fertility, and demand a very favorable trade arrangement.
column2: 给他们象征性的一点丰收之力，同时要求非常有利的贸易安排。

column1: Give them a treasure; they will always be our friends.
column2: 给他们一件财宝；他们将永远是我们的朋友。

column1: Are we so desperate to make a tribe that we’ll join with our enemies?!
column2: 我们竟如此急于组建部落，以至于要和敌人联合吗？！

column1: They aim to make us their thralls. Break off negotiations, and abandon all efforts to make a tribe!
column2: 他们想让我们做他们的奴隶。中断谈判，放弃组建部落的一切努力！

column1: They’re acting calm, but they never expected us to ask them to join our tribe. Now we’ve got them!
column2: 他们故作镇定，但从未想过我们会邀请他们加入部落。现在我们有主动权了！

column1: I just can’t see it.
column2: 我就是看不出来。

column1: When your emissaries go to Clan \x01@!, it is the Earth Priestess, not the chief, who does the talking.
column2: 当你们的使者前往 \x01@!氏族时，说话的是大地女祭司，而不是酋长。

column1: “Everyone comes here to worship at our temple to Ernalda and Flamal, and to drink our holy wine. We are already respected and influential. To make it worthwhile to join a tribe, the other clans would have to fortify the temple against invaders. We would require the Ernalda and Asrelia seats on the tribal ring. We would specify a certain level of sacrifices to our goddess.”
column2: “人人都来我们的神庙朝拜厄纳尔达和弗拉马尔，饮用我们的圣酒。我们已是备受尊敬、举足轻重。要让我们加入某个部落值得，其他氏族必须加固神庙以抵御入侵者。我们需要部落议会中厄纳尔达和阿斯雷利亚的席位。我们要规定向女神献祭的一定标准。”

column1: Agree that other clans fortify the temple.
column2: 同意其他氏族加固神庙。

column1: We agreed that the other clans of the new tribe should help fortify the temple.
column2: 我们同意新部落的其他氏族应帮助加固神庙。

column1: What kind of fortifications do you offer them?
column2: 你们为他们提供何种防御工事？

column1: Fencing
column2: 栅栏

column1: A trench
column2: 壕沟

column1: A stone wall
column2: 石墙

column1: They said the goddesses and gods of the Earth would be pleased.
column2: 他们说大地女神与神明们会欣慰。

column1: Demand that they share their secret versions of the myths with other clans.
column2: 要求他们与其他氏族分享秘密版本的传说。

column1: Which do you want to learn?
column2: 你想学习哪一种？

column1: Ernalda Feeds the Tribe
column2: 厄纳尔达哺育部落

column1: Uralda’s Blessing
column2: 尤拉尔达的赐福

column1: both myths
column2: 两种传说

column1: They agreed to tell the tribe secrets of Ernalda.
column2: 他们同意告知部落关于厄纳尔达的秘密。

column1: They agreed to tell the tribe secrets of Uralda.
column2: 他们同意告知部落关于尤拉尔达的秘密。

column1: They agreed to tell the tribe secrets of Ernalda and Uralda.
column2: 他们同意告知部落关于厄纳尔达和尤拉尔达的秘密。

column1: They told us that the secrets were too holy to give out over a matter as prosaic as the founding of a tribe.
column2: 他们告诉我们，这些秘密过于神圣，不能因组建部落这等凡俗之事而传授。

column1: Reserve the tribal seats they want.
column2: 保留他们想要的部落席位。

column1: We promised them the Ernalda and Asrelia seats on the tribal ring.
column2: 我们承诺他们在部落议会中拥有厄纳尔达和阿斯雷利亚的席位。

column1: They seemed to regard this as their due.
column2: 他们似乎认为这是应得的。

column1: Specify sacrifices owed by the tribe’s other clans.
column2: 规定部落其他氏族应献祭的祭品。

column1: We agreed to specify sacrifices the other clans of the tribe would have to make at their temple.
column2: 我们同意规定部落其他氏族必须在他们神庙献祭的祭品。

column1: The priestess nodded and said it was good that we respected the Earth Mother.
column2: 女祭司点点头，说我们尊重大地母亲是好事。

column1: How much wealth is each clan obligated to sacrifice each year?
column2: 每个氏族每年需献祭多少财富？

column1: They said that the goddess would be pleased.
column2: 他们说女神会满意。

column1: The priestess \x02\x03praised our generosity/accepted our gifts/was pleased\x02.
column2: 女祭司 \x02\x03赞扬我们的慷慨/接受了我们的礼物/感到满意\x02。

column1: We should do everything we can to bring them into our clan. We will lose nothing by helping them, for we shall also gain Ernalda’s blessing.
column2: 我们应竭尽全力将他们纳入我们氏族。帮助他们我们不会有任何损失，因为我们还将获得厄纳尔达的赐福。

column1: If we will it, our feud could be over soon.
column2: 只要我们愿意，世仇很快就能了结。

column1: They most want heavy fortification of the temple.
column2: 他们最想要的是神庙的重型防御工事。

column1: If we don’t settle our feud, they’ll be nothing but trouble for us in the tribe.
column2: 若我们不解决世仇，他们在部落中只会给我们带来麻烦。

column1: No Orlanthi would attack the temple, but there are foreign and inhuman enemies nearby. Fortifying the temple is a good idea.
column2: 奥兰大人不会攻击神庙，但附近有异族和非人敌人。加固神庙是个好主意。

column1: No Orlanthi would attack the temple, and there are no foreign or inhuman enemies nearby. Fortifying the temple would be a waste of resources.
column2: 奥兰大人不会攻击神庙，附近也没有异族或非人敌人。加固神庙会是浪费资源。

column1: Give them the seats they want, they think predictably and will be good to have on the tribal council.
column2: 给他们想要的席位，他们的想法可预测，放在部落议事会上会有好处。

column1: They are our enemies, but in the sagas the worshippers of the Earth Mother are never fully evil, so I think we can win them over.
column2: 他们是我们的敌人，但在传说中，大地母亲的崇拜者从未完全邪恶，所以我认为我们能争取他们。

column1: Knowing the secret versions of the myths helps us when heroquesting.
column2: 知晓秘密版本的传说有助于我们进行英雄任务。

column1: Their magic is strong. Start by giving them gifts and they will warm to the idea.
column2: 他们的魔法强大。先送他们礼物，他们会慢慢接受这个想法。

column1: I don’t know whether it is better to have these foes inside the tribe, or out.
column2: 我不知道把这些敌人放在部落内好，还是部落外好。

column1: They may not wish to share their secret myths with the tribe, but they will not hold it against us if we ask.
column2: 他们可能不愿与部落分享秘密传说，但若我们提出请求，他们不会记恨我们。

column1: Flamal is the god of vegetation. He was married to Ernalda before Orlanth was.
column2: 弗拉马尔是植被之神。他在奥兰斯之前就娶了厄纳尔达。

column1: Their fortifications aren’t as good as I thought. No wonder they want help.
column2: 他们的防御工事没我想的那么好。难怪他们想要帮助。

column1: Yuck. I wouldn’t touch them with Eurmal’s Six Foot Pole.
column2: 呸。我甚至不想用尤尔玛的六尺竿碰他们。

column1: Ordinarily I wouldn’t trust them, but for the sacred cause of a tribe…
column2: 通常我不会信任他们，但为了部落的神圣事业……

column1: It is not necessarily crazy to fortify the temple. Trolls and Tusk Riders love to destroy Ernalda’s holy places.
column2: 加固神庙未必是疯狂之举。巨魔和獠牙骑手很喜欢摧毁厄纳尔达的圣地。

column1: We can trust them to do what’s right, especially if we are in the same tribe.
column2: 我们可以信任他们做正确的事，尤其当我们同属一个部落。

column1: I… I don’t know. This confuses me.
column2: 我……我不知道。这让我困惑。

column1: This is not the time to let our old feuds stop us from doing what is right.
column2: 现在不是让旧仇宿怨阻止我们做正确之事的时候。

column1: They think a lot of themselves, don’t they?
column2: 他们自视甚高，不是吗？

column1: The \x01@! ancestors were present when Ernalda first made gold.
column2: 厄纳尔达初次造出黄金时， \x01@! 祖先们都在场。

column1: Back when Ernalda created gold and all the other good things from the earth, our ancestors were great friends of the \x01@! ancestors.
column2: 在厄纳尔达从大地中创造出黄金和其他一切美好之物的时代，我们的祖先与 \x01@! 祖先们曾是挚友。

column1: If we let these women tell us what to do now, it won’t be long before they’re always telling us what to do.
column2: 要是我们现在听任这些女人对我们发号施令，用不了多久她们就会一直指挥我们。

column1: So now we are going to agree — willingly agree — to sacrifice and work for some other clan. I cannot condone it.
column2: 所以现在我们打算同意——心甘情愿地同意——为别的氏族献祭干活。我不能容忍。

column1: Let us make the amount of sacrifice as high as possible, so that they will be impressed by us.
column2: 让我们把献祭数额定得尽可能高，这样他们会对我们刮目相看。

column1: Don’t ask for the secret myths. You’ll learn truths you’re not prepared for.
column2: 别索要秘密传说。你会了解到你尚未准备好的真相。

column1: They look down on warriors, but they know they need us.
column2: 他们轻视战士，但他们知道需要我们。

column1: We spoke to \x01@\x13, chief of Clan \x01@!, to see if \x06 wanted to join our tribe. \x05 asked us what we had to offer \x08.
column2: 我们与 \x01@\x13交谈，他是 \x01@!氏族的酋长，想看看 \x06 是否愿意加入我们的部落。 \x05 问我们有什么可以提供的 \x08。

column1: “If you do not join the new tribe, you are the first clan it will crush.”
column2: “如果你不加入新部落，你将是它第一个碾压的氏族。”

column1: “Although it irks me to say so, your point has some merit,” \x01@\x13 mused.
column2: “虽然我很不情愿这样说，但你的观点有些道理，” \x01@\x13 若有所思地说。

column1: “Many have tried to crush us, and we are still here,” \x01@\x13 said, cleaning \x04 fingernails with the tip of \x04 knife. “Our enemies, where are they?”
column2: “很多人曾试图碾压我们，而我们依然在此，” \x01@\x13 一边说，一边用 \x04 刀尖清理着 \x04 指甲。“我们的敌人，他们在哪里？”

column1: “The other clans dislike you, but we honor you, and fought for your inclusion.”
column2: “其他氏族不喜欢你们，但我们尊重你们，并为你们的加入而战。”

column1: We told them that our clan fought for their inclusion, over the objections of the other clans.
column2: 我们告诉他们，我们的氏族不顾其他氏族的反对，为他们的加入而战。

column1: “It is good that someone in this Orlanth-cursed land is smart enough to pay us the honor we are due,” \x01@\x13 said.
column2: “在这片被奥兰斯诅咒的土地上，总算有人足够聪明，给予我们应得的荣誉，” \x01@\x13 说道。

column1: “Your craven efforts to curry favor are like a tapeworm in my stomach,” \x01@\x13 growled.
column2: “你那些卑躬屈膝的讨好行径就像我肚子里的绦虫，” \x01@\x13 咆哮道。

column1: “We’ll give you a treasure if you join.”
column2: “如果你们加入，我们会给你们一件宝物。”

column1: To show that our generosity extends even to the disreputable, we gave them a treasure.
column2: 为了证明我们的慷慨甚至惠及声名狼藉之徒，我们给了他们一件宝物。

column1: Which treasure do you give them?
column2: 你给他们哪件宝物？

column1: “It is good to get a gift without having to steal it,” \x01@\x13 reflected.
column2: “不用偷就能得到礼物，真好，” \x01@\x13 沉思道。

column1: “Your joining is inevitable. Join now, and get a seat on the council.”
column2: “你们加入是不可避免的。现在加入，就能在议会上得到一个席位。”

column1: We told them that they would have to join eventually, so they’d do best to join quickly and get a seat on the tribal council.
column2: 我们告诉他们，他们最终必须加入，所以最好尽快加入，并获得部落议会的一个席位。

column1: “I am tempted to say that the only inevitable thing is that a slit throat bleeds, but you do have a point,” \x01@\x13 philosophized.
column2: “我很想说唯一不可避免的事是喉咙被割开就会流血，但你确实有道理，” \x01@\x13 哲理地评论道。

column1: How do we persuade people who don’t want anything from us?
column2: 我们该如何说服那些从我们这里无所求的人？

column1: \x01@\x13 feigns indifference, but in fact the formation of a tribe has the hairs on the back of \x04 neck standing on end.
column2: \x01@\x13 假装漠不关心，但实际上部落的成立让 \x04 后颈的汗毛都竖了起来。

column1: The \x01@! clan has raided its neighbors many times, and done so fiercely.
column2: \x01@! 氏族曾多次劫掠邻族，且手段凶残。

column1: The \x01@! clan has reason to fear if a tribe forms without it.
column2: \x01@! 氏族有理由担心，如果部落没有它而形成。

column1: \x01@\x13 is no fool. \x05 knows that the \x01@! clan’s days as fierce raiders are finished if the other clans in the area unite.
column2: \x01@\x13不是傻瓜。\x05知道如果该地区的其他氏族联合起来，\x01@!氏族作为凶残劫掠者的日子就到头了。

column1: These shiftless bullies are not to be trusted.
column2: 这些懒惰的恶霸不可信任。

column1: We want our allies in our tribe.
column2: 我们希望我们的盟友加入我们的部落。

column1: They would like a treasure for nothing, but so would everyone.
column2: 他们想不劳而获得到宝物，但谁不想呢。

column1: I would say that we should offer them the trickster seat, but I am still hoping for that great honor myself.
column2: 我本想建议我们给他们欺诈者席位，但我自己还指望这份殊荣呢。

column1: Make them grovel like the dogs they are!
column2: 让他们像狗一样匍匐求饶！

column1: They seem rough and unsavory because their lives have disappointed them.
column2: 他们看似粗鲁讨厌，是因为生活令他们失望。

column1: If only we were as skeptical of this tribal foolishness as \x01@\x13 is.
column2: 要是我们能像 \x01@\x13 一样对这场部落闹剧保持怀疑就好了。

column1: Having these allies in the tribe is a good idea: they will support us to be king.
column2: 让这些盟友加入部落是个好主意：他们会支持我们成为国王。

column1: That one right there: he’s the one who tried to kill me last Fire season.
column2: 那边那个：他就是上次火季试图杀我的人。

column1: The sooner we get out of here the sooner we can stop worrying about guarding our horses.
column2: 我们越早离开这里，就越早不用操心看守马匹。

column1: They have no honor.
column2: 他们毫无荣誉可言。

column1: This can’t be a good idea.
column2: 这不可能是好主意。

column1: The truth is that they hate us as much as we hate them. Negotiating will just make it worse.
column2: 事实是他们恨我们就像我们恨他们一样。谈判只会让事情更糟。

column1: Whose idea was this?
column2: 这是谁的主意？

column1: Good clans have bad enemies. These scum are the worst, and we should keep them as enemies.
column2: 好氏族有坏敌人。这些人渣是最坏的，我们应该让他们继续当敌人。

column1: These ignorant bullies can’t be trusted.
column2: 这些无知的恶霸不可信。

column1: Tell them they deserve to be smashed!
column2: 告诉他们他们活该被粉碎！

column1: Sharp swords, blunt minds, black hearts. Scoundrels.
column2: 利剑，愚钝的头脑，黑心。恶棍。

column1: Hey! These guys make me look good!
column2: 嘿！这些家伙让我看起来不错！

column1: These bandits can add nothing to our clan’s proud traditions.
column2: 这些强盗对我们氏族骄傲的传统毫无增益。

column1: Ask these murderous scum about the Gagarth shrine hidden in their woods.
column2: 问问这些杀人的渣滓，关于藏在它们树林里的加加斯神殿。

column1: I feel sorry for their animals.
column2: 我为他们的动物感到难过。

column1: Their fields are in bad shape.
column2: 他们的田地状况很差。

column1: No one who farms as badly as these wretches belongs in our tribe.
column2: 像这些可怜虫那样糟糕耕种的人不配加入我们的部落。

column1: On its way to Dragon Pass, Clan \x01@! escaped pursuit by terrible foes. They have yet to fully recover from their losses.
column2: 在前往龙之关的途中， \x01@! 氏族摆脱了可怕敌人的追击。他们至今未能从损失中完全恢复。

column1: “Donate a treasure for the kingly regalia.”
column2: “为王权神器捐一件宝物。”

column1: We told them to donate a treasure for the kingly regalia.
column2: 我们告诉他们为王权神器捐一件宝物。

column1: What argument do you use to convince them to do this?
column2: 你用什么论点说服他们这样做？

column1: “It is a great honor to add a treasure to the regalia.”
column2: “为神器添上一件宝物是莫大的荣耀。”

column1: “Your clan is weak. It must prove its worth to the other clans.”
column2: “你的氏族很弱小。它必须向其他氏族证明自己的价值。”

column1: “Your clan magic will be strengthened through a tie to the tribal wyter.”
column2: “你们的氏族魔法将通过连接部落守护灵而得到增强。”

column1: They agreed to our request.
column2: 他们同意了我们的请求。

column1: They said they could not spare any of their treasures. All were needed in case their enemies came back.
column2: 他们说他们不能分出任何宝物。万一敌人回来，所有的都用得上。

column1: “Support our clan when we nominate a king.”
column2: “当我们提名国王时，支持我们氏族。”

column1: We told them that we would sponsor them, if they would in turn support us in the nomination of a king.
column2: 我们告诉他们，如果他们在国王提名中支持我们，我们就会支持他们。

column1: “Our clans have common interests.”
column2: “我们氏族有共同的利益。”

column1: “We’re doing you a favor by letting you join, and expect consideration in return.”
column2: “我们允许你们加入是给你们恩惠，期待得到回报。”

column1: “Your courage is well-known, and your support would legitimize any new king.”
column2: “你们的勇气众所周知，你们的支持会使任何新王具有合法性。”

column1: They said they would help us, and that it was good that we frankly told them why we wanted them in the clan. “We heard enough lies from the Pharaoh’s men,” their lawspeaker said.
column2: 他们说愿意帮助我们，并直言我们坦诚相告为何要他们加入氏族是件好事。“我们从法老手下那里听够了谎言，”他们的律法师说道。

column1: They politely declined our suggestion.
column2: 他们礼貌地婉拒了我们的建议。

column1: “Tell us the secrets of your deadly foes.”
column2: “告诉我们你们死敌的秘密。”

column1: We asked them to tell us the secrets of their deadly foes.
column2: 我们请他们告知其死敌的秘密。

column1: “You are admired; help us convince others to join the tribe.”
column2: “你们受人敬仰；帮我们说服其他人加入部落。”

column1: We told them that they were widely admired, and that their example would coax other clans to join us.
column2: 我们告诉他们，他们广受敬仰，他们的榜样能引诱其他氏族加入我们。

column1: They said they were uncomfortable with our admiration, yet would accept it as genuine.
column2: 他们说我们的敬仰令他们不自在，但仍愿当作真心接受。

column1: They told us that they had learned to distrust flattery back in Heortland.
column2: 他们告诉我们，在赫欧特兰他们就学会了不信任谄媚。

column1: “We have been running for a long time. It will be good to have the shelter of a tribe. We shall attend your moot of confederation.”
column2: “我们已经逃亡很久了。有个部落庇护将是好事。我们会参加你们的联盟集会。”

column1: The Hiord said that they would come to a confederation moot.
column2: 希奥德说他们会来参加联盟集会。

column1: I wouldn’t mind finding a way to stop fighting them.
column2: 我倒不介意找个法子停止与他们交战。

column1: Flattery is the grease of commerce.
column2: 谄媚是生意的润滑剂。

column1: Look at how they hold themselves. They are very skeptical.
column2: 瞧瞧他们那姿态。他们疑心很重。

column1: They’re so desperate we might be able to convince them to join, even though we are enemies.
column2: 他们如此绝望，我们或许能说服他们加入，即便我们本是敌人。

column1: We must know who their foes are.
column2: 我们必须知道他们的敌人是谁。

column1: We are better off raiding them than joining them.
column2: 我们与其加入他们，不如去劫掠他们。

column1: It’s not impossible to bring a feuding clan into your tribe.
column2: 把一个世仇氏族拉进部落并非不可能。

column1: It is somewhat underhanded, though not forbidden, to demand special favors for our clan from those we recruit to the tribe.
column2: 向我们征募来的人为我族索取特殊好处，虽不算禁止，却有些阴险。

column1: If we truly wish to bring them into the tribe, we must be bluntly honest.
column2: 如果我们当真想带他们入部落，就必须坦率直言。

column1: If we can bring them into the tribe, we might be able to settle our feud more easily.
column2: 如果我们能带他们入部落，或许能更容易化解世仇。

column1: Our allies know they are weak, and will appreciate the straight truth. They will help us in the tribe.
column2: 我们的盟友知道他们自己很弱小，会欣赏直截了当的真相。他们会在部落里帮助我们。

column1: Our allies know we are weak, and will appreciate the straight truth. They will help us in the tribe.
column2: 我们的盟友知道我们很弱小，会欣赏直截了当的真相。他们会在部落里帮助我们。

column1: If we try to bring them into the tribe and fail, they will hate us even more.
column2: 如果我们试图带他们入部落却失败了，他们会更加憎恨我们。

column1: Every king needs magical implements, or regalia, in order to complete the mystic rites to confirm his right to rule.
column2: 每位君王都需要魔法器物或冠冕徽记，才能完成神秘仪式以确认统治权。

column1: We are enemies. But they have darker enemies as well.
column2: 我们是敌人。但他们也有更险恶的敌人。

column1: They are weak now, but all clans were weak in the Darkness. They will grow.
column2: 他们现在很弱小，但黑暗时代所有氏族都弱小。他们会壮大。

column1: We have enough problems.
column2: 我们麻烦够多了。

column1: Given their problems, they do a good job of coping.
column2: 以他们的困境来看，他们应对得还算不错。

column1: They are not without honor.
column2: 他们并非毫无荣誉。

column1: They are good at fighting enemies, but can they feed themselves?
column2: 他们善于与敌人作战，但能养活自己吗？

column1: First we flatter and cajole. Now we order and demand. We could just be at home, taking care of ourselves.
column2: 先是奉承哄骗，现在又发号施令。我们还不如待在家里，顾好自己。

column1: We know they are good at being chased. The question is: can they give chase?
column2: 我们知道他们擅长逃跑。问题是：他们能追赶吗？

column1: The poem “\x01@!’s Flight From Belintar” is an inspiration to any red-blooded Orlanthi.
column2: 诗歌《\x01@!逃离贝林塔》激励着每一位热血奥兰斯人。

column1: “Don’t trust an acre sown too soon, or a son too early born.”
column2: “别信过早播种的田地，也别信过早降生的儿子。”

column1: Our feud could have been avoided in the first place. Let’s try to settle it.
column2: 我们的世仇当初本可避免。让我们设法化解它。

column1: Your emissaries approach Clan \x01@! with an offer of membership in the new tribe. They are well-known for their aggressive trading practices, and have many demands.
column2: 你们的使者接近氏族 \x01@! ，提出新部落成员资格。他们以激进的贸易手段闻名，且要求繁多。

column1: When asked to join our new tribe, the aggressive traders of Clan \x01@! had many demands.
column2: 当被邀请加入我们新部落时，氏族 \x01@! 的那些激进贸易者提出了许多要求。

column1: Agree to anti-banditry oath.
column2: 同意反劫掠誓言。

column1: We agreed to make an oath against bandits part of the rites of kingship.
column2: 我们同意将反劫掠誓言纳入王权仪式。

column1: They were pleased by our offer.
column2: 他们对我们提出的条件感到满意。

column1: Agree to guards for trade missions.
column2: 同意为贸易使团配备护卫。

column1: We agreed that each clan should send guards for \x01@! trade missions.
column2: 我们同意每个氏族应为 \x01@! 贸易使团派出护卫。

column1: How many warriors should each clan provide?
column2: 每个氏族应提供多少战士？

column1: The number of guards we suggested appeared to be acceptable to them.
column2: 我们提议的护卫人数似乎为他们所接受。

column1: We demanded that the king get a share of the proceeds from \x01@! trade.
column2: 我们要求国王从 \x01@! 贸易收益中分得一份。

column1: How big a share do you demand?
column2: 你要求多大一份？

column1: One cow in fifty.
column2: 每五十头牛中取一头。

column1: One cow in twenty.
column2: 每二十头牛中取一头。

column1: One cow in ten.
column2: 每十头牛中取一头。

column1: They seemed most displeased by our request, though they said they could agree if their other demands were met.
column2: 他们对我们的要求显得极为不悦，尽管表示若其他条件得到满足，他们可以同意。

column1: Give them the Issaries seat.
column2: 给他们伊萨里斯席位。

column1: We agreed that they should always occupy the Issaries seat on the tribal council.
column2: 我们同意他们应永久占据部落议会中的伊萨里斯席位。

column1: They were pleased with the offer, but seemed to think it was their due.
column2: 他们对这个提议很满意，但似乎认为这是他们应得的。

column1: “We must carefully examine the details of the entire matter, but it appears that we have the seeds of a profitable arrangement in our hands.”
column2: “我们必须仔细审视整件事的所有细节，但看来我们手中已有了一笔有利可图安排的雏形。”

column1: They want their baubles and gewgaws to be more valuable than food. Do not trust them.
column2: 他们想让那些小玩意和零碎比食物还值钱。别信他们。

column1: After all the cattle they have stolen from us, they smirk and whine about bandits.
column2: 在从我们这里偷了那么多牛之后，他们竟还嬉皮笑脸地抱怨劫匪。

column1: They forget that Orlanth was generous as well as cunning.
column2: 他们忘了奥兰斯既慷慨又狡黠。

column1: Be careful. They talk well, but they do not mean us well.
column2: 当心。他们能说会道，但并非心怀好意。

column1: They are the greatest traders in Dragon Pass. We can learn much from them.
column2: 他们是龙隘最伟大的商人。我们可以从他们身上学到很多。

column1: We have little chance of convincing our enemies to join the tribe. I don’t know that we should.
column2: 我们说服敌人加入部落的机会很渺茫。我不知道是否该试。

column1: Give them the oath, the seat, and two warriors per clan.
column2: 给他们誓言、席位，以及每族两名战士。

column1: Give them the oath, two warriors per clan, and at least 40 cows’ worth of gifts.
column2: 给他们誓言、每族两名战士，以及价值至少40头牛的礼物。

column1: Give them the oath, the seat, and six warriors per clan. Demand that they turn one twentieth of their proceeds over to the king.
column2: 给予他们誓言、席位，以及每个氏族六名武士。要求他们将二十分之一的收益上交国王。

column1: Give them the oath, six warriors per clan, and at least 40 cows’ worth of gifts. Demand that they turn one twentieth of their proceeds over to the king.
column2: 给予他们誓言、每个氏族六名武士，以及至少价值40头牛的礼物。要求他们将二十分之一的收益上交国王。

column1: Feuds aren’t forever. If they join our tribe, it will be easier to make peace.
column2: 世仇并非永恒。若他们加入我们的部落，和解会更易达成。

column1: Give them the oath, the seat, and four warriors per clan. Demand that they turn one twentieth of their proceeds over to the king.
column2: 给予他们誓言、席位，以及每个氏族四名武士。要求他们将二十分之一的收益上交国王。

column1: Give them the oath, four warriors per clan, and at least 40 cows’ worth of gifts. Demand that they turn one twentieth of their proceeds over to the king.
column2: 给予他们誓言、每个氏族四名武士，以及至少价值40头牛的礼物。要求他们将二十分之一的收益上交国王。

column1: An oath taken by the king during his royal rites is no trivial matter.
column2: 国王在王室仪式上立下的誓言并非小事。

column1: Other clans will wonder why we invite our enemies into the tribe.
column2: 其他氏族会怀疑我们为何将敌人邀入部落。

column1: Tribes are not always made of perfect allies.
column2: 部落并非总是由完美的盟友组成。

column1: Our proud warriors will not take kindly to being treated as mere servants.
column2: 我们骄傲的武士不会乐于被当作仆从对待。

column1: We have little to lose by demanding concessions. They are so calculating that they cannot properly hold a grudge.
column2: 我们要求让步没什么可损失的。他们如此精于算计，没法真正记恨。

column1: If we think we can settle our feud, maybe. Otherwise, never.
column2: 如果我们认为能解决世仇，或许可能。否则，绝不可能。

column1: If the king takes an anti-banditry oath, he must be prepared to keep it, or the tribal magic will be harmed.
column2: 若国王立下反劫掠誓言，他必须准备遵守，否则部落魔法将受损。

column1: Can jewels close an open wound? Does silver heal the sick?
column2: 宝石能愈合伤口吗？白银能治愈病患吗？

column1: It would be good to end our feud.
column2: 终结我们的世仇是好事。

column1: I don’t trust them. They think too much.
column2: 我不信任他们。他们想得太多。

column1: He would smile even wider with my axe in his head.
column2: 若我的斧子嵌进他脑袋，他会笑得更开。

column1: They are too smooth to be allowed to ply their wares outside the tribe.
column2: 他们太过圆滑，不该被允许在部落外兜售货物。

column1: Look at them carefully: they exhibit all of Issaries’ worst flaws.
column2: 仔细看他们：他们展现了伊萨里斯最糟糕的所有缺点。

column1: Our allies have been a great help to me. They will help our clan even more in the tribe.
column2: 我们的盟友对我帮助很大。在部落中他们将对我们的氏族帮助更大。

column1: The \x01@! clan is an important one. If we fail to strike a deal with them that the other clans can accept, we will lose the chance to form a tribe for a generation or more.
column2: 这个 \x01@! 氏族是一个重要氏族。若我们未能与他们达成其他氏族能接受的协议，我们将失去一代人甚至更久内组建部落的机会。

column1: Rich plunder here. We haven’t hit them hard enough yet.
column2: 这里战利品丰厚。我们还没把他们打够。

column1: How dare we ask them to give over to the king what they have earned by the sweat of their own brows?
column2: 我们怎敢要求他们将用自己汗水挣来的东西上交国王？

column1: I’ve had my doubts about starting a tribe. But I never thought we’d sink so low as to join with these slither-tongues.
column2: 我对组建部落一直心存疑虑。但我从未想过我们会沦落到与这些滑舌之流为伍。

column1: I don’t like the way he smiled at me.
column2: 我不喜欢他朝我笑的样子。

column1: Your emissaries approach Clan \x01@!, known for its guardianship of a holy rock with war powers, to ask if they want to join the new tribe.
column2: 你的使者接近以守护拥有战争力量的圣岩而闻名的氏族 \x01@!，询问他们是否愿意加入新部落。

column1: Clan \x01@!, on whose tula is found the War Rock, negotiated the terms under which they might join the new tribe.
column2: 在图拉领地内发现战争之岩的氏族 \x01@!，就他们可能加入新部落的条件进行了谈判。

column1: Demand loyalty pledges from shamans and the rock spirit.
column2: 要求萨满和岩石之灵宣誓效忠。

column1: We demanded that the rock spirit and its shamans pledge loyalty to the new tribe and its kings.
column2: 我们要求岩石之灵及其萨满向新部落及其国王宣誓效忠。

column1: Although reluctant at first, they finally agreed to this demand.
column2: 虽然起初不情愿，他们最终同意了这一要求。

column1: They not only refused this demand, but seemed much offended by it.
column2: 他们不仅拒绝了这一要求，而且似乎深感受辱。

column1: Negotiate sacrifices to War Rock.
column2: 谈判向战争之岩献祭的事宜。

column1: We argued over the sacrifices that each clan should give to the spirit of the War Rock.
column2: 我们就每个氏族应向战争之岩之灵献祭的祭品进行了争论。

column1: How many cows worth should each clan sacrifice each year?
column2: 每个氏族每年应献祭价值多少头牛的祭品？

column1: They accepted the sacrifices we suggested.
column2: 他们接受我们建议的祭品。

column1: They bargained shrewdly, and we agreed to greater sacrifices than we at first suggested.
column2: 他们精明地讨价还价，我们同意了比最初建议更大的祭品。

column1: Offer them a seat or seats on the council.
column2: 在议会中提供他们一个或多个席位。

column1: the Humakt seat
column2: 胡玛克特席位

column1: We offered them less than they had asked, but still convinced them that our offer was a good one.
column2: 我们提供的少于他们所求，但仍使他们相信我们的提议是好的。

column1: We offered them less than they had asked, which seemed to offend them.
column2: 我们提供的少于他们所求，这似乎触怒了它们。

column1: a Thunder Brothers seat
column2: 一个雷霆兄弟席位

column1: both seats
column2: 两个席位

column1: We offered them both the seats they sought.
column2: 我们提供了他们所求的两个席位。

column1: They were pleased to receive both seats.
column2: 他们对获得两个席位感到高兴。

column1: Respect shamans.
column2: 尊重萨满。

column1: We promised them better respect for shamans.
column2: 我们承诺给予萨满更多尊重。

column1: Is your respect for shamans unconditional?
column2: 你对萨满的尊重是无条件的吗？

column1: Yes, they should be treated the same as priests.
column2: 是的，他们应受到与祭司同等的待遇。

column1: They were pleased, and a little surprised, that we agreed to treat shamans as the equals of priests.
column2: 我们同意将萨满与祭司平等对待，他们既高兴又有些惊讶。

column1: No, they should be better respected, but priests are still more important.
column2: 不，他们应受到更多尊重，但祭司仍然更重要。

column1: Although we did not give them everything they wanted, they still seemed satisfied with the conditions of respect we proposed.
column2: 虽然我们没有给他们想要的一切，但他们似乎对我们提出的尊重条件感到满意。

column1: We would not concede that shamans were fully as important as priests, so they were displeased with us.
column2: 我们不肯承认萨满与祭司完全同等重要，因此他们对我们不满。

column1: No, they should receive tokens of respect only.
column2: 不，他们只应获得尊敬的象征。

column1: Although we did not give them everything they wanted, they still agreed to conditions of respect we proposed.
column2: 虽然我们没有给他们想要的一切，但他们仍同意了我们提出的尊重条件。

column1: We would not concede that shamans were nearly as important as priests, so they were displeased with us.
column2: 我们不肯承认萨满与祭司几乎同等重要，因此他们对我们不满。

column1: Their devotion to the War Rock is just an act; they don’t care about shamans any more than any other Orlanthi.
column2: 他们对战争之岩的虔诚只是做做样子；他们并不比其他奥兰斯人更关心萨满。

column1: They want respect for the Rock and their shamans more than they want to join our tribe.
column2: 他们想要岩石和他们的萨满得到尊重，胜过想要加入我们的部落。

column1: Our weaponthanes yearn to belong to a tribe that claims the War Rock as its own.
column2: 我们的武器领主渴望属于一个宣称拥有战争之岩的部落。

column1: Giving shamans the respect accorded to priests is contrary to tradition.
column2: 给予萨满等同于祭司的尊重违背传统。

column1: Giving shamans the respect accorded to priests is contrary to tradition. The other clans will not like it.
column2: 给予萨满等同于祭司的尊重违背传统。其他氏族不会喜欢这样。

column1: Negotiating with them will not be easy.
column2: 与他们谈判不会容易。

column1: Giving shamans the respect accorded to priests is contrary to tradition. The other clans will accept this provision only if it is well-laced with conditions.
column2: 给予萨满祭司般的尊重是违背传统的。其他氏族只有在附加诸多条件的情况下才会接受这项条款。

column1: They are our enemies, but they might actually want to join our tribe. They know we are not the worst of their enemies.
column2: 他们是我们的敌人，但他们或许真的想加入我们的部落。他们知道我们不是他们最坏的敌人。

column1: The other clans will be happy to respect shamans as if they were priests.
column2: 其他氏族会很乐意像尊重祭司一样尊重萨满。

column1: Sacrifices made to the War Rock are not wasted. Our warriors will win battle blessings.
column2: 向战争之岩献祭并非徒劳。我们的勇士将赢得战斗祝福。

column1: Sacrifices made to the War Rock are not wasted. Our warriors will win battle blessings. The bigger the sacrifice, the bigger the blessing.
column2: 向战争之岩献祭并非徒劳。我们的勇士将赢得战斗祝福。献祭越大，祝福越大。

column1: So that’s the vaunted War Rock? I’ve pulled more impressive stones out of the swamp.
column2: 那就是被吹嘘的战争之岩？我从沼泽里拔出来的石头都比这更壮观。

column1: If we win over the spirit of the War Rock, our martial deeds will be remembered for generations!
column2: 如果我们赢得战争之岩之灵的青睐，我们的战功将被世代传颂！

column1: If they credit our clan as giving ground to them, they will support us when the time comes to make one of our own a king.
column2: 如果他们承认是我们氏族让步于他们，那么轮到我们的人称王时，他们就会支持我们。

column1: I don’t mind respecting shamans — after all, they live alone and take care of themselves. But I balk at having to kowtow to a rock!
column2: 我不介意尊重萨满——毕竟他们独自生活，自食其力。但要我向一块石头叩头，那可不行！

column1: In Fulthamsaga, Fuldram Fulthamson made peace with his worst enemies and went on to become king.
column2: 在富尔萨姆传说中，富尔德拉姆·富尔萨姆森与他最凶恶的敌人和解，后来成为了国王。

column1: Promises are cheap. But promises to our enemy may not be worth much.
column2: 承诺不值钱。但向敌人做出的承诺可能更不值钱。

column1: No good their war god did them when the Dragons decided to eat their ancestors.
column2: 当巨龙决定吃掉他们祖先时，他们的战争之神可没帮上什么忙。

column1: They haven’t taken enough from us by raiding, now they want us to just give them our best things!
column2: 他们通过劫掠从我们这里拿走的还不够，现在还想让我们把最好的东西拱手相送！

column1: Ordinarily I’d say we should sacrifice as much as possible to their war god, and reap the benefits. But their war god does not love us.
column2: 通常我会说我们应该尽可能多地献祭给他们的战争之神，然后坐享其成。但他们的战争之神并不爱我们。

column1: Their war god is strong and might deserve respect, but the gods would turn away from us if we treated their shamans like priests.
column2: 他们的战争之神确实强大，或许值得尊敬，但如果我们对待他们的萨满如同祭司，众神就会背离我们。

column1: If they burn our steads again, I’ll vote to kick them out of the tribe.
column2: 如果他们再敢焚烧我们的农庄，我就投票把他们赶出部落。

column1: They talk better than they fight.
column2: 他们嘴上功夫比打仗厉害。

column1: I suppose it would be going too far to make their rock talk like a duck, wouldn’t it?
column2: 我想让他们的岩石像鸭子一样说话就太过分了，对吧？

column1: If they will join our tribe, we might be on the road to ending our feud.
column2: 如果他们愿意加入我们的部落，我们或许就能走上终结世仇之路。

column1: Their war god teaches them something of force. Nothing of honor.
column2: 他们的战争之神只教他们武力之道，丝毫不讲荣誉。

column1: I’m ready to bring them into the tribe and work at ending the feud if the rest of you are.
column2: 如果你们其余的人都同意，我也准备好接纳他们入部，并致力于终结世仇。

column1: I am too happy fighting them as enemies to give proper counsel. The rest of you need to weigh this carefully.
column2: 我太乐于与他们为敌作战了，无法给出恰当的建议。你们其余的人需要仔细权衡此事。

column1: The \x01@! clan had its tribe-making demands all written out before our emissaries even got there.
column2: \x01@! 氏族在我们的使者抵达之前就已经把他们的立部要求全部写好了。

column1: The \x01@! clan, known for its collection of old documents and its shrine to Lhankor Mhy, have anticipated your tribe-making mission.
column2: \x01@! 氏族以收藏古卷和建有兰卡·密神殿而闻名，他们已经预见到了你们的立部任务。

column1: To join the clan, the \x01@! want the other clans to donate wealth for the purchase of discovered documents, and for teaching people how to read. They wish to make literacy a requirement for all candidates for the throne. Finally, they wish to occupy the Lhankor Mhy seat on the tribal council in perpetuity.
column2: 为了加入部落， \x01@! 氏族希望其他氏族捐出财富，用于购买已发现的文献，以及教人识字。他们希望将读写能力作为所有王位候选人的必要条件。最后，他们希望永久占据部落议会中的兰卡·密席位。

column1: Agree that kings must be literate.
column2: 同意国王必须识字。

column1: We agreed that all kings of our future tribe would have to know how to read.
column2: 我们同意，我们未来部落的所有国王都必须识字。

column1: They promised to tutor anyone who wished to be king.
column2: 他们承诺辅导任何想当国王的人。

column1: Demand that they make a grand map for the whole tribe.
column2: 要求他们为整个部落绘制一幅大地图。

column1: We made them agree to make a large map, incorporating the exploration of all the clans of the tribe.
column2: 我们让他们同意绘制一幅大地图，囊括部落所有氏族的探索成果。

column1: They said they would be happy to compile such a map.
column2: 他们说很乐意编纂这样一幅地图。

column1: Dicker over the literacy and document-buying payments.
column2: 就识字和文献购置费用进行讨价还价。

column1: How much should each clan pay each year to their literacy and document fund?
column2: 每个氏族每年应为他们的识字和文献基金支付多少？

column1: How should they divide the wealth?
column2: 他们该如何分配这笔财富？

column1: Equally between documents and teaching people to read.
column2: 在文献和教人识字之间平分。

column1: Mostly on documents.
column2: 主要用于文献。

column1: Mostly on reading.
column2: 主要用于识字。

column1: They said they would take our offer under advisement.
column2: 他们说会考虑我们的提议。

column1: Give them the Lhankor Mhy seat.
column2: 把兰卡·密席位给他们。

column1: We agreed that they should sit in the Lhankor Mhy seat of the tribal council.
column2: 我们同意他们应占据部落议会中的兰卡·密席位。

column1: There is a legendary scroll telling the secrets of Uralda. Maybe this \x01@! plan could help us find it.
column2: 有一卷传说卷轴记载着乌拉达的秘密。也许这个 \x01@! 计划能帮我们找到它。

column1: Our enemies are not very good bargainers. They might join with us despite our feud.
column2: 我们的敌人不太擅长讨价还价。尽管有世仇，他们或许还是愿意加入我们。

column1: It would be disastrous to allow only the literate to become king. Most of the chieftains around here can’t read a single sigil!
column2: 只允许识字的人当国王将是灾难性的。这附近的酋长们大多连一个符文都不认得！

column1: To please these enemies, we would risk offending all the other clans.
column2: 为了取悦这些敌人，我们将冒着得罪所有其他氏族的风险。

column1: Talking with these pointy-heads never solves anything.
column2: 和这些尖脑袋的家伙谈话永远解决不了问题。

column1: If we weren’t trying to make a tribe, they might already have come begging us for peace.
column2: 要不是我们在组建部落，他们可能早已跑来乞求和平了。

column1: Their leaders lack skill but their warriors are mighty. I don’t know if we should try to bring them into the tribe or not.
column2: 他们的领袖缺乏技巧，但他们的战士却很勇猛。我不知道是否该尝试把他们纳入部落。

column1: They are not trying to take from us. They ask only to give us great opportunities.
column2: 他们不是想从我们这里索取什么。他们只是请求赐予我们绝佳的机会。

column1: Once in our tribe, they could turn the other clans against us by twisting the law.
column2: 一旦加入我们的部落，他们可能会通过歪曲法律来挑拨其他氏族反对我们。

column1: There are many old documents about plants I wish I was able to read.
column2: 有很多关于植物的古老文献，我真希望自己能读懂。

column1: I don’t trust them. There’s something they’re hiding from us. Something valuable.
column2: 我不信任他们。他们对我们隐瞒了某些东西。某些有价值的东西。

column1: Some of my best friends worship Lhankhor Mhy. But these blind sages are terrified of anything they don’t know already.
column2: 我最好的朋友中有些信奉兰卡·密。但这些盲目的贤者对任何他们尚未知晓的东西都怕得要命。

column1: “Demanding” that a bunch of Lhankor Mhys make a map is like ordering a fish to swim.
column2: “要求”一群兰科尔·米斯绘制地图，就如同命令鱼游泳。

column1: They will talk and talk and talk. Then we will fall asleep. Then Chaos creatures will sneak up on us, and kill us.
column2: 他们会说啊说啊说个不停。然后我们就会睡着。然后混沌生灵就会悄悄靠近我们，杀死我们。

column1: Finally, a clan that knows what is most important! They must lead our tribe!
column2: 终于，有个知道什么最重要的氏族了！他们必须领导我们的部落！

column1: Feuds can be ended, but the written word lives forever.
column2: 世仇可以终结，但文字永存。

column1: Their magic is not like ours, but it is strong.
column2: 他们的魔法不像我们的，但也很强大。

column1: Their magic is strong, but not good at adapting to this new land. They need us.
column2: 他们的魔法很强大，但不擅长适应这片新土地。他们需要我们。

column1: They are our enemies, and they are not good at changing.
column2: 他们是我们的敌人，而且不擅长改变。

column1: Just make sure they don’t teach all of the women to read and none of the men. Then we’d have no end of trouble.
column2: 只要确保他们别只教所有女人读书，男人一个都不教。那样我们就会麻烦不断。

column1: If we have a tribe, these old greybeards will make up all sorts of new rules and make us follow them.
column2: 如果我们有了部落，这些老家伙会编出各种新规，强迫我们遵守。

column1: If we had a good map, we could easily figure out where the zombies are hiding.
column2: 如果我们有张好地图，就能轻松搞清僵尸藏在哪里。

column1: Ask for the map, give them the seat, and promise ten cows a year to literacy, but not for documents.
column2: 要求地图，给他们席位，并承诺每年十头牛用于读写能力，但不得用于文件。

column1: Ask for the map and promise ten cows a year to literacy, but not for documents. In addition, give them at least 40 cows worth of goods.
column2: 要求地图，并承诺每年十头牛用于读写，但不得用于文件。此外，给他们至少价值四十头牛的货物。

column1: Maps made by people who forget that the world is always changing can be dangerous.
column2: 由那些忘记世界总是在变化的人绘制的地图可能很危险。

column1: About all they’re good for will be writing down our exploits.
column2: 他们大概只配记录我们的功绩。

column1: Ask them for the secrets of the Empire of Wyrm’s Friends.
column2: 向他们索要龙之友帝国的秘密。

column1: I don’t want these people anywhere near our tula.
column2: 我不希望这些人靠近我们的图拉领地。

column1: Your emissaries approach Clan \x01@!, known for its martial prowess and its ancient hatred of trolls, about joining your new tribe.
column2: 你的使者接近 \x01@!氏族，该氏族以武力和对巨魔的宿仇闻名，商讨加入你的新部落。

column1: The ferocious \x01@! clan made many demands when we sought to bring them into our tribe.
column2: 凶猛的 \x01@! 氏族在我们试图将他们纳入部落时提出了许多要求。

column1: They also demand that Clan \x01@+ expel its troll tavern keepers.
column2: 他们还要求 \x01@+ 氏族驱逐其巨魔酒馆老板。

column1: Agree that they lead tribal raids.
column2: 同意他们领导部落突袭。

column1: They grinned and said we would not be sorry.
column2: 他们咧嘴笑道，我们不会后悔的。

column1: We agreed that they should lead tribal raids.
column2: 我们同意他们应该领导部落突袭。

column1: Demand that \x01@! weaponthanes patrol tulas of other clans.
column2: 要求 \x01@! 武器领主巡逻其他氏族的图拉领地。

column1: In exchange for the things they wanted, we told them that they would have to assign their extra weaponthanes to patrol other clans.
column2: 作为对他们所求之物的交换，我们告诉他们必须指派多余的武器领主巡逻其他氏族。

column1: How many warriors must they send to each clan?
column2: 他们必须向每个氏族派遣多少战士？

column1: They acknowledged that they were the finest warriors, and would therefore be able to help other clans, but what were the other clans going to do to help them?
column2: 他们承认自己是最优秀的战士，因此能够帮助其他氏族，但其他氏族又准备如何帮助他们呢？

column1: Negotiate the amount other clans will pay to equip them.
column2: 协商其他氏族将支付的装备费用。

column1: We dickered over the amount other clans would pay to equip their warriors.
column2: 我们为其他氏族将支付的装备其战士的费用讨价还价。

column1: How much will each other clan pay each year?
column2: 每个其他氏族每年支付多少？

column1: They nodded curtly.
column2: 他们简短地点了点头。

column1: Make promises regarding the \x01@+ clan’s trolls.
column2: 就 \x01@+ 氏族的巨魔做出承诺。

column1: “Good riddance!” they said.
column2: “总算走了！”他们说。

column1: How much tribute will they pay annually?
column2: 他们每年将进贡多少？

column1: They were pleased at the prospect.
column2: 他们对这一前景感到满意。

column1: Promise that the \x01@+’s trolls will submit to ritual humiliation once a year.
column2: 承诺 \x01@+的巨魔每年接受一次仪式性羞辱。

column1: We promised that the \x01@+’s trolls would submit to ritual humiliation once a year.
column2: 我们承诺 \x01@+的巨魔将每年接受一次仪式性羞辱。

column1: They smiled at the prospect.
column2: 他们对此前景微微一笑。

column1: They said we were making a wise decision.
column2: 他们说我们做出了明智的决定。

column1: They’ve stamped their own fields flat. Too much war.
column2: 他们把自己的田地都踩平了。战争太多了。

column1: Fine, so long as they don’t drag their tribe into too many wars.
column2: 行，只要他们别把自己的部落拖入太多战争。

column1: Strong allies make stronger herds.
column2: 强大的盟友造就更强大的畜群。

column1: Give them ten cows a year to equip their weaponthanes.
column2: 每年给他们十头牛装备武器领主。

column1: We will have to promise much to convince them. It could still be worth it to end our feud.
column2: 我们得承诺很多才能说服他们。但终结世仇仍然值得。

column1: Give them twelve cows a year to equip their weaponthanes.
column2: 每年给他们十二头牛来装备武器领主。

column1: If we cannot give them both the seats they want, they will take it as an insult.
column2: 如果我们不能给他们两个想要的席位，他们会视作侮辱。

column1: They are harsh enemies, but we have the upper hand in our feud.
column2: 他们是难缠的敌人，但在世仇中我们占上风。

column1: This is better than suing for peace; we can seek peace with honor.
column2: 这比求和要好；我们可以有尊严地求和。

column1: We can offer only one of the seats they want.
column2: 我们只能提供他们想要的一个席位。

column1: The two seats they want are already taken. They will need extra encouragement to be interested in joining us.
column2: 他们想要的两个席位已被占据。他们需要额外的激励才会对加入我们感兴趣。

column1: They deserve both tribal council seats.
column2: 他们值得两个部落议会席位。

column1: They deserve these tribal council seats, but there is not room on the council now for both of them.
column2: 他们值得这些部落议会席位，但目前议会上没有同时容纳两者的空间。

column1: If we give in to the demands of a clan we’re feuding with, we’ll appear weak.
column2: 如果我们向世仇氏族的要求让步，就会显得软弱。

column1: There is no harm in giving them gifts. If they accept them instead of giving them back, we might be able to convince them to join the tribe.
column2: 给他们礼物并无害处。如果他们接受而不退回，我们或许能说服他们加入部落。

column1: Because their ancient enemies are the trolls, their clan magic will suffer if they join with a troll-loving clan.
column2: 因为他们的宿敌是巨魔，如果与喜爱巨魔的氏族联合，他们的氏族魔法将受损。

column1: Because we are a peace clan, we could benefit from an alliance with a War Clan.
column2: 因为我们是和平氏族，与战争氏族结盟对我们有利。

column1: It is bad enough that we are a war clan, without entering into an alliance with another one.
column2: 我们自己是战争氏族已经够糟了，再与另一个战争氏族结盟就更糟了。

column1: There’s no point in offering less than four cows a year. Their weaponthanes are used to rich gifts.
column2: 每年出价少于四头牛没有意义。他们的武器领主习惯了丰厚的礼物。

column1: If we can end our feud by bringing them into the tribe, I am not against this.
column2: 如果将他们纳入部落能终结世仇，我不反对。

column1: No games. Either we end our feud in a tribe or carry the fight to its end.
column2: 不是儿戏。要么我们在部落内终结世仇，要么战斗到底。

column1: They may know war, but they know little else. They will appreciate our guidance in the tribe.
column2: 他们可能懂战争，但其他所知甚少。他们会感激我们在部落中的指导。

column1: They would be a worthy addition to our tribe.
column2: 他们会是我们部落的宝贵新成员。

column1: Bah! They only think they’re tough.
column2: 呸！他们只是自以为很强硬。

column1: If we equip them, they will find treasures for us.
column2: 如果我们武装他们，他们会为我们找到财宝。

column1: Battle-music echoed in their trade-god’s words.
column2: 战歌回荡在他们交易之神的话语中。

column1: The real question is, how many eligible bachelors do they have?
column2: 真正的问题是，他们有多少适龄的单身汉？

column1: Whatever they want. It’s worth it to make sure they stay allied with us.
column2: 他们要什么都行。确保他们与我们结盟是值得的。

column1: If we leave them out of the tribe, we may never make peace.
column2: 如果我们把他们排除在部落之外，我们可能永远无法和平。

column1: I don’t want them patrolling our tula. I don’t want them in our tribe.
column2: 我不想让他们在我们的领地上巡逻。我不想让他们加入我们的部落。

column1: They are too stupid for words.
column2: 他们愚蠢得难以言喻。

column1: With them in a tribe, we will have to watch our backs. Without a tribe, we could just fight them honestly and openly.
column2: 让他们加入部落，我们就得提防背后。不加入部落，我们就能正大光明地与他们战斗。

column1: If our clan had their discipline, we could accomplish great things.
column2: 如果我们氏族有他们的纪律，我们就能成就伟业。

column1: They can be beaten.
column2: 他们是可以被打败的。

column1: Bastards!
column2: 杂种！

column1: Uh, hangover. Sorry.
column2: 呃，宿醉。抱歉。

column1: It’s bad that we’re always at war with each other, but in a tribe, they’ll agitate to be at war with everyone else.
column2: 我们总是彼此交战很糟糕，但在部落里，他们会煽动与所有其他人交战。

column1: The \x01@! chieftain thought that our offer of membership in the tribe was a trick.
column2: The \x01@! 酋长认为我们邀请他们加入部落是个诡计。

column1: “Your deeds are more likely to be remembered if you are part of a tribe.”
column2: “如果你是一个部落的一员，你的事迹更可能被铭记。”

column1: We told him that the deeds of tribes are better remembered than the deeds of clans.
column2: 我们告诉他，部落的事迹比氏族的事迹更易被铭记。

column1: Mad-Blood \x01@p said it is good to be remembered.
column2: 狂血 \x01@p 说能被铭记是好事。

column1: Mad-Blood \x01@p said that the \x01@! clan’s place in history was assured back when our clan’s ancestors were still a pack of dirty thralls.
column2: 狂血 \x01@p 说， \x01@! 氏族在历史上的地位早在我们的祖先还是一群肮脏的奴隶时就已经确定了。

column1: “Together, we will have protection from our foes.”
column2: “联合起来，我们将免受敌人的侵害。”

column1: We told him that a tribe fights foes better than a clan does.
column2: 我们告诉他，部落比氏族更善于打击敌人。

column1: Mad-Blood \x01@p said that it was good to crush foes.
column2: 狂血 \x01@p 说打倒敌人是好事。

column1: Mad-Blood \x01@p said that we might be his foes.
column2: 狂血 \x01@p 说我们可能是他的敌人。

column1: “A tribe can support heroquests more easily than a clan.”
column2: “部落比氏族更容易支持英雄任务。”

column1: We told him that a tribe can support heroquests more easily than a clan.
column2: 我们告诉他，部落比氏族更容易支持英雄任务。

column1: Mad-Blood \x01@p said that \x06 might go on a heroquest himself one day.
column2: 狂血 \x01@p 说 \x06 也许有一天会亲自进行一次英雄任务。

column1: Mad-Blood \x01@p said that heroquests were just the spirits tricking people.
column2: 狂血 \x01@p 说英雄任务不过是神灵在戏弄人。

column1: We told him that a clan facing hard times is better off in a tribe.
column2: 我们告诉他，一个面临艰难时期的氏族在部落中会过得更好。

column1: Mad-Blood \x01@p said that it was good to rely on others for food.
column2: 狂血 \x01@p 说依赖他人获取食物是件好事。

column1: Mad-Blood \x01@p said that it was bad to rely on others for food.
column2: 狂血 \x01@p 说，仰赖他人施舍食物可不好。

column1: \x01@p, their chief, \x02\x04praised our generosity over and over and over again/at first eyed our gifts suspiciously, then heaped them in the middle of the hall and lavished praise on us/told us we were lucky that they would agree to accept our gifts/insisted that we make three equal stacks of our gifts before even looking at them, but did accept them when we piled them up properly\x02.
column2: \x01@p他们的族长， \x02\x04一遍又一遍又一遍地称赞我们的慷慨/起初怀疑地打量我们的礼物，随后将它们堆在厅堂中央，对我们大加赞赏/告诉我们，我们很走运，他们愿意接受我们的礼物/坚持要求我们先把自己礼物码成均匀三堆才肯瞧上一眼，不过当我们码好之后，他们还是收下了\x02。

column1: Mad-Blood \x01@p tore at the gifts, biting cloth, smashing pots, and ruining everything \x06 could get \x04 hands on. Then \x06 sat on \x04 heels and gave a blood-curdling howl. One of the \x01@! weaponthanes told us that \x01@p had taken great offense at our gifts.
column2: 狂血 \x01@p 撕扯着礼物，咬碎布料，砸破陶罐，毁掉了 \x06 能抓到的 \x04 一切。然后 \x06 蹲坐在 \x04 脚跟上，发出一声令人毛骨悚然的嚎叫。其中一位 \x01@! 武器领主告诉我们， \x01@p 对我们的礼物大为光火。

column1: Our gifts offended Mad-Blood \x01@p.
column2: 我们的礼物冒犯了狂血 \x01@p。

column1: \x01@p at first refused the gifts, but after conferring with \x04 ring, thanked us for them instead. Then \x06 left the hall while \x04 thanes brought forth gifts of nearly identical value for us. They explained that their chief was not willing to be in our debt.
column2: \x01@p 首先拒绝了礼物，但在与 \x04 ring商议后，转而感谢了我们。随后 \x06 离开大厅，同时 \x04 领主们为我们带来了价值几乎相当的礼物。他们解释说，他们的酋长不愿欠我们人情。

column1: “Are these gifts a trick, a ruse?” said Mad-Blood \x01@p, the \x01@! chief. “I can be even craftier than you!” And \x06 gave us reciprocal gifts.
column2: “这些礼物是诡计、是圈套吗？”疯血 \x01@p说道，这位 \x01@! 酋长。“我甚至可以比你们更狡猾！”然后 \x06 给了我们回礼。

column1: We watched in silence as \x01@p gave our gifts a close inspection, patting some items and holding up others to sniff them deeply. At last, \x01@p grunted and snapped \x04 fingers. \x03 weaponthanes then gave us gifts in kind.
column2: 我们沉默地看着 \x01@p 仔细检查我们的礼物，拍打一些物品，又举起其他物品深深嗅闻。最后， \x01@p 咕哝一声，打了个响指 \x04 。 \x03 武器领主们随即给了我们等值的礼物。

column1: Mad-Blood \x01@p’s face contorted, and \x06 drove us angrily from \x04 hall.
column2: 疯血 \x01@p’s脸扭曲了，并且 \x06 愤怒地将我们赶出 \x04 大厅。

column1: Mad-Blood \x01@p’s rumored insanity has not prevented his people from amassing large and healthy herds.
column2: 疯血 \x01@p’s传闻中的疯狂并未阻止他的人民积累庞大而健康的畜群。

column1: The \x01@! herds are small, their animals scrawny.
column2: 这些 \x01@! 牧群规模不大，牲口也瘦骨嶙峋。

column1: Their leaders may be mad, but their weaponthanes are a force to be reckoned with. Better with us than against us.
column2: 他们的首领或许癫狂，但麾下的武器领主却是一股不可小觑的力量。与我们为伍好过与我们为敌。

column1: Thanks to a number of ferocious but rash attacks, the \x01@! have few good fighters left. They’re better ignored.
column2: 由于数次凶猛却鲁莽的进攻，这些 \x01@! 已所剩无几的好战士。最好别去理会他们。

column1: The craziest thing is that he doesn’t realize this is his chance to escape our wrath.
column2: 最疯狂的是，他竟未意识到这是他逃脱我们怒火的机会。

column1: \x01@p rules his clan by fear. He will not be remembered well.
column2: \x01@p 以恐惧统治他的氏族。他不会被人铭记。

column1: Bringing an enemy into our tribe is bad enough. Forming a tribe with our insane enemy is…crazy.
column2: 把一个敌人带入我们的部落已经够糟了。跟一个疯狂的敌人组成部落简直是……疯了。

column1: The \x01@! think ill of us. There is little point in negotiating with them.
column2: \x01@! 对我们评价不佳。跟他们谈判没什么意义。

column1: The \x01@! think highly of us. A few sensible words, and Mad-Blood will seem less mad.
column2: \x01@! 对我们评价很高。说几句明智的话，狂血就不会显得那么疯了。

column1: \x01@p is crazy, but we need allies in the tribe.
column2: \x01@p 是疯了，但我们在部落里需要盟友。

column1: He hates us, we hate him, he’s crazy, we’re not. Let’s get out of here.
column2: 他恨我们，我们恨他，他疯了，我们没疯。咱们离开这儿吧。

column1: Talking with \x01@p will only make him hate us more.
column2: 跟 \x01@p 交谈只会让他更恨我们。

column1: Many tribes form in order to better perform heroquests.
column2: 许多部落的形成是为了更好地执行英雄任务。

column1: The gods sometimes look after the insane.
column2: 众神有时会庇护疯子。

column1: The gods sometimes look after the insane. But that doesn’t mean we have to join with them.
column2: 众神有时会庇护疯子。但那不意味着我们必须跟他们联合。

column1: A hundred years from now, our descendants will be telling Bad King \x01@p stories.
column2: 一百年后，我们的子孙会讲述暴君 \x01@p 的故事。

column1: \x01@p’s mother probably ate witchweed when he was nursing.
column2: \x01@p的母亲在哺乳他时大概吃了巫草。

column1: If you think \x01@p is crazy, you should see his trickster.
column2: 如果你觉得 \x01@p 疯了，你应该看看他的诡术师。

column1: His clan is honorable. \x01@p is not.
column2: 他的氏族很体面。 \x01@p 不是。

column1: This is not good.
column2: 这不好。

column1: We have enough clans for the tribe. Maybe we don’t need to talk with this madman.
column2: 我们已经有足够多的氏族来组成部落了。也许我们没必要跟这个疯子谈。

column1: None of you can think of a really compelling reason for them to join a tribe, now can you?
column2: 你们谁也想不出一个真正有说服力的理由让他们加入部落，对吧？

column1: Maybe he’s smarter than he lets on.
column2: 也许他比表面上看起来更聪明。

column1: Hah! What a slug!
column2: 哈！真像只鼻涕虫！

column1: He’s insane.
column2: 他疯了。

column1: When I said that \x01@p was as crazy as a Tusk Rider, I was insulting the one on the pig.
column2: 当我说 \x01@p 跟獠牙骑士一样疯的时候，我是在侮辱那个骑猪的。

column1: Your emissaries speak to Clan \x01@!, the hunting clan, about the new tribe. They want the right to hunt in other clans’ tulas, sacrifices made annually to Odayla the Hunter, and a mutual oath of support between their clan and yours within the tribe.
column2: 你们的使者跟 \x01@!狩猎氏族谈论新部落的事。他们想要在其他氏族的图拉领地上狩猎的权利、每年向猎人奥达拉献祭，以及他们氏族与你们氏族在部落内互相支持宣誓。

column1: We asked Clan \x01@! what it would take to get them to join our tribe.
column2: 我们问 \x01@! 氏族，要怎样才能让他们加入我们的部落。

column1: Agree to mutual support oath.
column2: 同意互相支持宣誓。

column1: Both sides agreed to end the feud.
column2: 双方同意结束世仇。

column1: It was also agreed that both sides would set aside the feud, once we became a tribe.
column2: 双方也同意，一旦我们成为部落，就放下世仇。

column1: They asked that we swear by Humakt, god of oaths, and we did so.
column2: 他们要求我们以誓言之神胡马克特的名义发誓，我们照做了。

column1: Agree to Odayla sacrifices.
column2: 同意向奥达拉献祭。

column1: We agreed to specify sacrifices the other clans of the tribe would have to make to Odayla.
column2: 我们同意规定部落其他氏族必须向奥达拉献祭的事宜。

column1: They said that Odayla and the Lady of the Wild would smile on us.
column2: 他们说奥达拉和荒野女士会眷顾我们。

column1: Ask them to add one of their treasures to the tribal regalia.
column2: 请他们将一件宝物加入部落圣物。

column1: We asked them to add one of their clan treasures to the tribal regalia.
column2: 我们请他们将一件氏族宝物加入部落圣物。

column1: They agreed to do so.
column2: 他们同意了。

column1: They reluctantly agreed to do so.
column2: 他们勉强同意了。

column1: Cede them hunting rights.
column2: 让出狩猎权给他们。

column1: We agreed that they would have full rights to hunt on the other tulas of the tribe.
column2: 我们同意他们完全有权在部落其他图拉领地上狩猎。

column1: They said they would hunt so silently and skillfully that we’d never even notice them.
column2: 他们说他们会悄无声息、技巧高超地狩猎，我们甚至不会注意到他们。

column1: Sacrifices to Odayla will not be wasted; they will help us catch more game, too.
column2: 向奥达拉献祭不会白费；他们也会帮助我们猎获更多猎物。

column1: Asking for a treasure for the tribal regalia might make the other clans happier.
column2: 为部落圣物索要一件宝物也许会让其他氏族更高兴。

column1: It won’t be easy to get anything from them, now or later.
column2: 现在或以后，从他们那里得到任何东西都不容易。

column1: Too much blood to forgive so easily.
column2: 流血太多，没那么容易宽恕。

column1: If we bring them into the tribe we won’t be able to raid them as often.
column2: 如果把他们带入部落，我们就不能那么频繁地袭击他们了。

column1: Feuds can be just as important as tribes.
column2: 世仇有时跟部落一样重要。

column1: I don’t like them but that doesn’t mean we shouldn’t take this chance to make peace.
column2: 我不喜欢他们，但这不意味着我们不该抓住这个机会讲和。

column1: It would be good to have an ally at tribal moots.
column2: 在部落大会上有个盟友是好事。

column1: I’m not certain.
column2: 我不确定。

column1: Are the rest of you ready to work towards ending our feud?
column2: 你们其他人准备好努力结束我们的世仇了吗？

column1: Odayla is god of the hunt.
column2: 奥达拉是狩猎之神。

column1: Their hunting magic is good magic.
column2: 他们的狩猎魔法是好的魔法。

column1: If they really understood how to be Orlanthi, they wouldn’t all worship Odayla.
column2: 如果他们真的懂得如何做奥兰提人，就不会都崇拜奥达拉了。

column1: Sacrificing to Odayla will help us as well. It might be worth it.
column2: 向奥达拉献祭对我们也有帮助。也许值得。

column1: They’re asking for permission to just sneak onto our tula whenever they feel like it!
column2: 他们要求的是随时随地悄悄溜进我们领地的许可！

column1: If I am in your pocket, and you are in mine, who is wearing the pants?
column2: 如果我在你的口袋里，你也在我的口袋里，那谁在穿裤子呢？

column1: Oh yes. Let’s “support” each other. Mutually. Can’t wait to see this.
column2: 哦，是啊。让我们“互相支持”吧。有来有往。真等不及要看这出好戏了。

column1: Pah! What kind of warrior specializes in the slaying of animals?
column2: 呸！哪种战士会专精屠戮动物？

column1: What treasure could they possibly hope to add to the regalia? A vole skin? The tooth of a shrew?
column2: 他们还能希望往圣物里加什么宝物？一只田鼠的皮？一只鼩鼱的牙齿？

column1: We don’t need to be tied to these folks. They’re just hunters with delusions of grandeur.
column2: 我们不需要跟这些人绑在一起。他们不过是些狂妄自大的猎人而已。

column1: I once read a scroll that told of Odayla’s secrets of woodcraft. I wish I could remember it…
column2: 我曾读过一卷讲奥达拉林间技艺秘密的卷轴。真希望我能记得起来……

column1: The tribal temple must house the most impressive regalia in all of Dragon Pass.
column2: 部落神殿必须存放龙之谷最令人赞叹的圣物。

column1: They are weak. We should be fighting them, not begging them to join us.
column2: 他们很弱小。我们应该跟他们打仗，而不是求他们加入。

column1: We can trust them.
column2: 我们可以信任他们。

column1: Our clans will get along well in a tribe.
column2: 我们的氏族在部落里会相处融洽。

column1: If we are generous with the sacrifices, this is our chance to start making peace.
column2: 如果我们在献祭上慷慨大方，这就是我们开始讲和的机会。

column1: The \x01@! clan is known for its long-range planning, and for a tavern it maintains as part of its market. Its chief, \x01C\x18 was expecting you and has a list of demands prepared. \x05 wants the tribal hall to be built on \x01@! land. \x05 wants to host the confederation moot. \x05 wants the right to build and run taverns in other tulas. \x05 wants the new tribe to make peace with the trolls.
column2: 这个 \x01@! 氏族以长远规划著称，还因其市场内设的酒馆而闻名。其酋长 \x01C\x18 早已料到你的到来，并准备好了一纸要求。 \x05 希望部落大厅建在 \x01@! 领地上。 \x05 希望主办联盟大会。 \x05 希望在其他的图拉领地上建造并经营酒馆。 \x05 希望新部落与巨魔讲和。

column1: The careful planners of Clan \x01@! had many demands prepared for our emissaries.
column2: 氏族 \x01@! 的缜密规划者们为我们的使者准备了许多要求。

column1: The \x01@!’s chief, \x01C\x18, wants the tribal hall to be built on \x01@! land. \x05 wants to host the confederation moot. \x05 wants the right to build and run taverns in other tulas. \x05 wants the new tribe to make peace with the trolls.
column2: \x01@!的酋长 \x01C\x18希望部落大厅建在 \x01@! 领地上。 \x05 希望主办联盟大会。 \x05 希望在其他的图拉领地上建造并经营酒馆。 \x05 希望新部落与巨魔讲和。

column1: Agree to make peace with trolls.
column2: 同意与巨魔讲和。

column1: We agreed that the new tribe would make peace with the trolls.
column2: 我们同意让新部落与巨魔讲和。

column1: They were pleased, and said it would be a fine thing to return to the friendship trolls and humans once enjoyed before the Pharaoh came.
column2: 他们很满意，说能让巨魔和人类重新找回法老到来前曾有的友谊，实乃美事一桩。

column1: Allow them to build the tribal hall.
column2: 允许他们建造部落大厅。

column1: We let them build the tribal hall on their lands.
column2: 我们允许他们在自己的领地上建造部落大厅。

column1: \x01C\x18 showed us a rough sketch of \x04 plans for the building.
column2: \x01C\x18 向我们展示了一份 \x04 建筑规划的草图。

column1: Allow them to host the confederation moot.
column2: 允许他们主办联盟大会。

column1: We allowed them to host the confederation moot.
column2: 我们允许他们主办联盟大会。

column1: They promised it would be a grand event.
column2: 他们承诺那将是一场盛事。

column1: Let them build taverns on other clan’s tulas.
column2: 让他们在其他氏族的图拉领地上建造酒馆。

column1: We gave them license to build taverns on other clan’s tulas.
column2: 我们授予他们在其他氏族的图拉领地上建造酒馆的许可。

column1: They said we would find them a source of pleasure.
column2: 他们说我们会发现那里成了乐土。

column1: “Your answers are close enough to what we expected. We shall join you at the confederation moot.”
column2: “你们的答复与我们预想的相差无几。我们将在联盟大会上与你们会合。”

column1: Trolls are nothing more than animals. We’d be crazy to think of making “peace” with them.
column2: 巨魔不过是畜生。我们若是想跟他们讲什么“和平”，那简直是疯了。

column1: They talk as if we could be friends. But our feud has been nasty, and nastier because of their tricks.
column2: 他们说得好像我们能成朋友似的。可我们的世仇凶险缠斗，而他们的诡计更让这仇怨变本加厉。

column1: The things they ask for are more important than they seem.
column2: 他们所要求的东西远比表面上重要。

column1: We would have to give them everything they want to have any chance of success.
column2: 我们得满足他们的全部要求，才有任何成功的机会。

column1: Joining our tribe would be a sneaky way for them to wriggle out of their bad situation.
column2: 加入我们的部落，对他们来说是一条摆脱困境的狡诈捷径。

column1: I’m not sure we should bring them into our tribe, but I do know that our feud isn’t going as well for us as I’d like.
column2: 我不确定我们该不该接纳他们入部落，但我确实知道，眼下的世仇进展并不如我所愿。

column1: It is very unusual to allow one clan to earn wealth on another clan’s land.
column2: 允许一个氏族在另一个氏族的领地上牟利，这非常不寻常。

column1: The notion of peace with the trolls will make many of the other clan leaders uneasy.
column2: 与巨魔讲和的想法会让其他许多氏族首领感到不安。

column1: The trolls have been friendly with us already.
column2: 巨魔已经对我们表现出了友善。

column1: Things will not go well for us if we agree to their demands.
column2: 如果我们答应他们的要求，事情对我们会很不利。

column1: The trolls are our ancient enemies; making peace with them will harm our clan magic.
column2: 巨魔是我们的宿敌；与他们讲和会削弱我们的氏族魔法。

column1: The trolls hate the elves as much as our ancestors did. We could have worse friends.
column2: 巨魔像我们的祖先一样痛恨精灵。我们本可以结交更差的朋友。

column1: In a land ruled by rashness and violence, it is good to see a clan that plans ahead.
column2: 在一片由鲁莽和暴力统治的土地上，能看到一个提前规划的氏族，真是好事。

column1: I would prefer peace, but the warriors are still hungry to win our feud.
column2: 我宁愿讲和，但战士们仍渴望赢得世仇。

column1: If we can convince them to join the tribe, we may succeed in easing our feud.
column2: 如果我们能说服他们加入部落，或许能缓和我们的世仇。

column1: Make peace with the trolls. I hear they eat elves.
column2: 跟巨魔讲和吧。我听说他们吃精灵。

column1: If they build those … what I mean to say is … we’ve heard of them, back in history, but are they really what we…?
column2: 如果他们建造那些……我的意思是……我们在历史上听说过它们，但它们真的是我们……？

column1: Has self-importance so blinded you that you are willing to consort with troll-friends? A pox on the tribe, if so.
column2: 难道自负已经让你盲目到愿意与巨魔之友为伍了吗？若是如此，愿灾祸降于部落。

column1: I predict trouble here — tribe, ale, trolls. Not a good mix.
column2: 我预见到麻烦——部落、麦酒、巨魔。可不是什么好搭配。

column1: All the trolls really want is to be left alone, which I can certainly understand.
column2: 巨魔真正想要的就是别被打扰，我完全理解这点。

column1: Quit with them.
column2: 跟他们断绝关系。

column1: They are too greedy and grasping to be trusted.
column2: 他们太过贪婪攫取，不可信任。

column1: Tavern? Good. Trolls? Huh.
column2: 酒馆？不错。巨魔？哼。

column1: You can’t trust troll-lovers.
column2: 你不能信任爱巨魔的人。

column1: Their beer is good with me.
column2: 他们的啤酒我觉得不错。

column1: Let them have the tavern. Then we can piss in their beer vats and say the trolls did it.
column2: 让他们开酒馆吧。然后我们可以在他们的啤酒桶里撒尿，再说是巨魔干的。

column1: Well, I’d rather that we hosted the confederation moot, but if it’s important to them…
column2: 嗯，我宁愿由我们来主办联盟大会，但如果这对他们很重要……

column1: Creatures of darkness have no place in our tribe.
column2: 黑暗的造物在我们部落中没有位置。

column1: These troll-dung lovers have no place in our tribe.
column2: 这些爱巨魔粪的家伙在我们部落中没有位置。

column1: Our allies must be granted a place of honor.
column2: 我们的盟友必须得到尊荣之位。

column1: Your emissaries are able to interrupt the brawling of Clan \x01@!’s leaders long enough to ask them if they want to join your new tribe. They are as well-known for their hatred of Chaos as for their rashness and lack of forethought.
column2: 你的使者们设法在氏族 \x01@!首领们的混战中打断了足够长时间，问他们是否想加入你的新部落。他们以憎恶混沌著称，也以鲁莽和缺乏远见闻名。

column1: The idea of a tribe seems never to have occurred to them. “How would a tribe help us fight broos?”
column2: 部落这个想法似乎从未在他们脑中闪现过。“部落怎么帮我们打布鲁斯？”

column1: We asked the Chaos fighters of Clan \x01@! to join our new tribe.
column2: 我们邀请氏族 \x01@! 的混沌战士们加入我们的新部落。

column1: Their chief, \x01@p, asks, “Can you tell us yet how a tribe would help us fight broos?”
column2: 他们的酋长 \x01@p问：“你们现在能告诉我们部落怎么帮我们打布鲁斯了吗？”

column1: “Our magic will be stronger. Magic can crush Chaos.”
column2: “我们的魔法会变得更强。魔法能碾碎混沌。”

column1: We told them that the combined magic of a tribe would be strong against Chaos.
column2: 我们告诉他们，一个部落的联合魔法将对混沌产生强大的抵抗。

column1: “Your magic will strengthen us in our fight against Chaos.”
column2: “你们的魔法将增强我们对抗混沌的力量。”

column1: “Magic cannot crush Chaos. It takes strength and determination.”
column2: “魔法无法粉碎混沌。需要力量和决心才行。”

column1: “The fight against Chaos isn’t everything. There are cows to raise and seeds to sow.”
column2: “对抗混沌并非一切。还有牛要养，种子要播。”

column1: We told them that a tribe would help them with the herd and crops.
column2: 我们告诉他们，一个部落会在牲畜和庄稼上帮助他们。

column1: They nodded. “It’s important to raise bulls.”
column2: 他们点了点头。“养公牛很重要。”

column1: They snorted and laughed at us.
column2: 他们对我们嗤之以鼻，放声嘲笑。

column1: “We can share our maps, and better find where Chaos lurks.”
column2: “我们可以分享地图，更好地找到混沌潜伏之处。”

column1: We told them that a tribe could better explore in search of Chaos.
column2: 我们告诉他们，一个部落可以更好地探索以搜寻混沌。

column1: They looked pleased at this prospect.
column2: 他们对此前景显得很高兴。

column1: “We can sense where Chaos lurks without your maps!”
column2: “没有你们的地图，我们也能感知混沌潜伏在哪里！”

column1: “We will have more warriors to fight Chaos.”
column2: “我们将有更多战士去对抗混沌。”

column1: We told them that more warriors were always good in the fight against Chaos.
column2: 我们告诉他们，对抗混沌时，战士越多越好。

column1: “We would be happy to lead your warriors against Chaos.”
column2: “我们很乐意率领你们的战士去对抗混沌。”

column1: “Are you suggesting we aren’t strong enough to fight Chaos?”
column2: “你是暗示我们不够强壮，无法对抗混沌吗？”

column1: “If Chaos does not erupt in the meantime, we will be at this moot of yours.”
column2: “如果混沌在此期间没有爆发，我们会参加你们的这个集会。”

column1: If they fight Chaos all the time, when do they find time to raise healthy herds?
column2: 如果他们一直与混沌战斗，哪还有时间养出健康的畜群？

column1: Talk about fighting, then about magic.
column2: 先谈战斗，再谈魔法。

column1: These brutes are interested in little besides Chaos. If we gift them, they’ll think we’re serious about fighting Chaos, too.
column2: 这些野蛮人对混沌以外的事几乎不感兴趣。如果我们赠予礼物，他们就会认为我们也是认真要对抗混沌。

column1: Give them gifts so they will know we hate Chaos too, then get out of here.
column2: 给他们礼物，好让他们知道我们也憎恨混沌，然后离开这里。

column1: The omens all say that Chaos is strong now, and growing stronger. We may want them in the tribe.
column2: 所有征兆都显示混沌如今势强，且日益强大。我们也许需要他们加入部落。

column1: It’s good to have allies.
column2: 有盟友总是好事。

column1: Elmali know how to fight Chaos without destroying everything we touch.
column2: 艾尔玛利人知道如何与混沌战斗而不摧毁我们所触及的一切。

column1: With these allies in the tribe we could heroquest to eliminate Chaos from Dragon Pass.
column2: 有了这些盟友加入部落，我们可以进行英雄任务，从龙之隘口消灭混沌。

column1: Tell them the truth and find out if they’re smart enough to recognize it.
column2: 告诉他们真相，看看他们是否足够聪明能认清这一点。

column1: They are so obsessed with fighting Chaos that they lost three of their clan treasures to thieves.
column2: 他们太沉迷于对抗混沌，以至于丢了三个氏族宝物给窃贼。

column1: Fighting Chaos is all very well, but we don’t want clans with no sense of balance in our tribe.
column2: 对抗混沌固然很好，但我们不希望部落里有缺乏平衡感的氏族。

column1: It’s too bad they were outside the Pass during the Dragonkill: they would all have charged like fools and died in one bite.
column2: 可惜龙杀战争时他们不在隘口附近：否则他们都会像傻子一样冲锋，一口就被吞掉。

column1: Do not insult my glorious brothers!
column2: 不要侮辱我光荣的兄弟们！

column1: Some day maybe the crap will get knocked out of their heads.
column2: 说不定哪天他们脑袋里的粪会被敲出来。

column1: The Uroxi did not invent the fighting arts.
column2: 战斗技艺可不是乌洛希发明的。

column1: Even the unruly Storm Bull is central to our worship.
column2: 即使是不守规矩的风暴公牛也是我们崇拜的核心。

column1: Fighting Chaos is a holy mission. But if we can’t convince them that our warriors will help, forget it.
column2: 对抗混沌是一项神圣使命。但如果我们不能说服他们相信我们的战士能帮上忙，那就算了。

column1: They can help us against zombies and ghouls.
column2: 他们可以帮助我们对抗僵尸和食尸鬼。

column1: It’s always nice having more strong bulls around.
column2: 身边多几头强壮的公牛总是好事。

column1: They fight so much because that’s all they’re good for.
column2: 他们战斗得那么多，只是因为那点本事。

column1: The map argument is the strongest.
column2: 地图的论点是最有力的。

column1: I knew they’d be fighting when we got here.
column2: 我就知道我们到这儿时他们会在打架。

column1: Why would the proud Uroxi humble themselves by joining a tribe? And why would we ask them to?
column2: 为什么骄傲的乌洛希要自降身份加入一个部落？我们又为什么要邀请他们？
