column1: They’re proud that they can kill Chaos creatures that are even stupider than they are.
column2: 他们很自豪能杀死那些比他们还蠢的混沌生物。

column1: They know what’s important.
column2: 他们知道什么最重要。

column1: They think they’re great warriors because they charge without knowing where they’re going.
column2: 他们觉得自己是伟大的战士，因为他们在不知道往哪冲的情况下就冲锋了。

column1: Maybe we can talk them into helping with the tribe.
column2: 也许我们可以说服他们帮助部落。

column1: They forget that Orlanth conquered Urox.
column2: 他们忘了是奥兰斯征服了乌洛克斯。

column1: I can handle these brutes.
column2: 我能应付这些野蛮人。

column1: They breed good bulls. That’s the most I can say.
column2: 他们育出的公牛不错。这大概是我能给出的最高评价了。

column1: They’re stupid but they’re right: Chaos will overwhelm us if we don’t fight it together.
column2: 他们很蠢，但说得对：如果我们不共同对抗混沌，它就会压倒我们。

column1: “When a bad bull stomps your pasture, sharpen the knives.”
column2: “当恶牛践踏你的牧场时，把刀磨利。”

column1: They have the right idea, if they can remember that we could be friends in a tribe.
column2: 他们的想法是对的，只要他们能记住，我们可以在部落里成为朋友。

column1: Our enemies respect only force, not magic or common sense.
column2: 我们的敌人只尊重武力，不尊重魔法或常识。

column1: Clan \x01@! is known for its large cattle herds. Because of this, it is a popular target for raids by other local clans. Its chieftain, \x01@p, is skeptical when your emissaries approach \x08 about the new tribe. “We are wealthy, and the other clans are poor. If I were a suspicious \x07, I would think that this tribe is concocted merely so you can force us to share our wealth.”
column2: 氏族 \x01@! 以大群牛群闻名。因此，它常成为当地其他氏族袭击的目标。其酋长 \x01@p在你们的使者接近 \x08 谈论新部落时持怀疑态度。“我们富有，而其他氏族贫穷。如果我是一个多疑的 \x07，我会认为这个部落的组建只是为了逼我们分享财富。”

column1: We asked the prosperous Clan \x01@! to join our new tribe.
column2: 我们请富有的氏族 \x01@! 加入我们的新部落。

column1: \x01@p still wonders if this tribe is concocted merely so we can force \x08 to share \x04 clan’s wealth.
column2: \x01@p 仍然怀疑这个部落的组建只是为了逼 \x08 分享 \x04 氏族的财富。

column1: “The other clans will supply additional warriors to guard your herds.”
column2: “其他氏族将提供额外的战士来守卫你们的畜群。”

column1: We told them that the other clans would supply warriors to protect their herds.
column2: 我们告诉他们，其他氏族会提供战士保护他们的牲畜。

column1: How many warriors does each other clan supply?
column2: 每个其他氏族提供多少战士？

column1: They acknowledged that there was strength in numbers.
column2: 他们承认人多力量大。

column1: It seemed as if they had expected us to promise them a greater number of warriors.
column2: 他们似乎原本期待我们会承诺更多的战士数量。

column1: “You will be asked to help the other clans. That will cost you less than continued raiding.”
column2: “你们会被要求帮助其他氏族。这比不断遭受袭击的代价要小。”

column1: We told them that they would be asked to help others, but that it would be better than being raided all the time.
column2: 我们告诉他们，他们会被要求帮助别人，但这总比一直遭受袭击要好。

column1: What is the number of cows they must give to each clan annually?
column2: 他们每年必须给每个氏族多少头牛？

column1: They said that our logic was galling, yet also inescapable.
column2: 他们说我们的逻辑令人恼火，却又无法回避。

column1: They said that calling a bandit a king does not make him any less of a bandit.
column2: 他们说，把强盗称作国王，并不会让他少当一点强盗。

column1: “Wealth is fleeting. Founding a tribe wins you a place in history.”
column2: “财富转瞬即逝。创立一个氏族能让你在历史上留名。”

column1: We told them that participation in the tribe would seal their place in history.
column2: 我们告诉他们，加入部落将确保他们在历史上的地位。

column1: They said that they were moved by our eloquence.
column2: 他们说，他们被我们的口才打动了。

column1: They said that you can’t eat history.
column2: 他们说，历史又不能当饭吃。

column1: “Wealth is nothing without influence. Join us, and sit on the council.”
column2: “没有影响力，财富一文不值。加入我们，坐上议会席位。”

column1: We offered them a seat on the tribal council.
column2: 我们给他们提供了一个部落议会的席位。

column1: We offered them seats on the tribal council.
column2: 我们给他们提供了多个部落议会的席位。

column1: How many seats do you offer them?
column2: 你给他们几个席位？

column1: They said that our offer was attractive.
column2: 他们说我们的提议很有吸引力。

column1: They said that we had not convinced them that influence was worth much if it meant giving up cows. They did continue to listen to us, however.
column2: 他们说，如果影响力意味着放弃牛只，那他们并不觉得它有多大价值。不过他们还是继续听着我们说话。

column1: “We shall chew on your offer for a while. Expect us at your confederation moot.”
column2: “我们会好好考虑你的提议。在你们的联合大会上等着我们吧。”

column1: We must have them in our clan!
column2: 我们必须把他们拉进我们的部族！

column1: Although they are rich, they find it galling that the martial clans raid them, and that successful herders never get poems written about them.
column2: 尽管他们富有，但军事氏族袭击他们，而成功的牧人也从未被人写诗歌颂，这让他们感到屈辱。

column1: They think that a tribe has little to offer them.
column2: 他们认为一个部落给不了他们什么。

column1: Make them give ten cows to each clan, and offer them six warriors from each clan.
column2: 让他们给每个氏族十头牛，然后给他们每个氏族派六名战士。

column1: Make them give eight cows to each clan, and offer them four warriors from each clan.
column2: 让他们给每个氏族八头牛，然后给他们每个氏族派四名战士。

column1: Why bow and scrape to get them in our tribe, when we can just keep raiding them?
column2: 既然我们可以继续袭击他们，何必卑躬屈膝地拉他们入伙？

column1: The only way a rich herding clan gets into the poems and chronicles is through the influence it wields in a powerful tribe.
column2: 一个富有的牧人氏族要想被写进诗歌和编年史，唯一的途径就是在一个强大部落中施加影响力。

column1: In a tribe, their wealth would probably work against us.
column2: 如果在一个部落里，他们的财富可能会对我们不利。

column1: They already hate us. They will probably hate us more if we try to bully them into the tribe.
column2: 他们已经恨我们了。如果我们试图强迫他们加入部落，他们可能会更恨我们。

column1: You have to be rough with people like this, or they don’t listen to you.
column2: 对这种人就得强硬，否则他们不会听你的。

column1: These cowards know where they stand.
column2: 这些懦夫知道自己的位置。

column1: Tell them that they’ll have a central role in defeating the undead if they join us.
column2: 告诉他们，如果加入我们，他们将在击败亡灵的战斗中发挥核心作用。

column1: They will join, no matter what we say. It is inevitable.
column2: 无论我们说什么，他们都会加入。这是不可避免的。

column1: They’re destined to be the richest clan in Dragon Pass, but that doesn’t mean we should side with them.
column2: 他们注定会成为龙隘最富有的氏族，但这并不意味着我们应该站在他们一边。

column1: These folks certainly know the value of a cow!
column2: 这些人确实知道一头牛的价值！

column1: “No man is so wealthy that he will turn down a gift.”
column2: “再富有的人也不会拒绝一份礼物。”

column1: “Cows give milk and silver gives joy, but for settling feuds there’s nothing like sharpened bronze.”
column2: “牛给奶，银给欢，但解决世仇，没有什么比得上磨利的青铜。”

column1: I knew they’d be rude to our emissaries.
column2: 我就知道他们会对我们使者无礼。

column1: Told you they were richer than we are.
column2: 早告诉你他们比我们富。

column1: Surely they will listen to reason.
column2: 他们肯定会听道理的。

column1: These cowards would rather follow cattle than glory.
column2: 这些懦夫宁愿追随牛群也不愿追随荣耀。

column1: They know that we are the best at… well, I think they understand that. Right?
column2: 他们知道我们是最擅长的……嗯，我想他们明白的，对吧？

column1: Even I could not make them listen. They only have ears for the farting of their cows.
column2: 连我都无法让他们听进去。他们只听得见自己牛放的屁。

column1: They’ve been nothing but rude to us, but we are better than that.
column2: 他们对我们一直很无礼，但我们不屑于计较。

column1: Perhaps we can learn from them how to become wealthy.
column2: 也许我们可以向他们学习如何变得富有。

column1: They will take advantage of us more as tribe members, than if we kept ourselves apart from them.
column2: 如果他们成为部落成员，会比我们与他们保持距离时更多地利用我们。

column1: We need to become king of the tribe and then plunder these dung lords at will.
column2: 我们需要成为部落之王，然后随意掠夺这些粪堆领主。

column1: Talking with them is a waste of time.
column2: 跟他们谈话是浪费时间。

column1: They have forgotten the gods, they think only of riches.
column2: 他们忘记了神明，只想着财富。

column1: You dream if you think we can convince them of anything but the fact that we will raid them until they beg for mercy.
column2: 如果你认为我们能说服他们任何事情，那就是做梦——他们只知道我们会一直袭击他们，直到他们求饶。

column1: I hate seeing an enemy clan that has richer temples than we do.
column2: 我讨厌看到敌对的氏族拥有比我们更富丽堂皇的神殿。

column1: I don’t think we should join with them, but that doesn’t mean we should just keep killing them.
column2: 我认为我们不应该与他们联合，但这并不意味着我们应该一直杀他们。

column1: It’s enemies like this that force us to make a tribe.
column2: 正是这样的敌人迫使我们建立部落。

column1: Your emissaries approach the eccentric Clan \x01@!, known for its peculiar custom of favoring female chieftains. They seem interested in joining the tribe. They offer to give magical power to the other clans, and to share their many warriors as well. In return, they want the right to tutor the female children of the tribe’s thanes. Finally, they want a provision that one in four monarchs will be a queen who worships Vinga, the female warrior.
column2: 你的使者们走近了古怪的氏族 \x01@!，该氏族以偏爱女性酋长的奇特习俗而闻名。他们似乎对加入部落感兴趣。他们提出赐予其他氏族魔法力量，并分享他们的众多战士。作为回报，他们想要教导部落中侍卫们的女儿的权力。最后，他们想要一项规定：每四位君主中有一位必须是信仰文加——这位女战士的女王。

column1: We asked the eccentrics of Clan \x01@! to join our new tribe.
column2: 我们请求氏族 \x01@! 的古怪者们加入我们的新部落。

column1: Accept gift of magic.
column2: 接受魔法礼物。

column1: We accepted their gift of magic.
column2: 我们接受了他们的魔法礼物。

column1: “We will perform rituals during Sacred Time that will gift you with magic.”
column2: “我们将在神圣时间举行仪式，赐予你们魔法。”

column1: Accept warriors.
column2: 接受战士。

column1: We accepted their offer of warriors for the other clans’ use.
column2: 我们接受了他们提供战士供其他氏族使用的提议。

column1: How many \x01@! warriors do you propose to send to each clan?
column2: 你建议向每个氏族派遣多少 \x01@! 名战士？

column1: They agreed to the number of warriors we suggested.
column2: 他们同意了我们建议的战士数量。

column1: They said that we asked too much of them.
column2: 他们说我们要求太高了。

column1: Agree to tutoring of daughters.
column2: 同意教导女儿们。

column1: We agreed that they could tutor the daughters of thanes.
column2: 我们同意他们可以教导侍卫们的女儿。

column1: “The daughters of your thanes will be in good hands.”
column2: “你们侍卫们的女儿将会得到妥善照顾。”

column1: Agree to Vingan queens.
column2: 同意文加女王。

column1: We agreed that one monarch in four should be a Vingan queen.
column2: 我们同意每四位君主中应有一位是文加女王。

column1: “We know that our requests seem strange, but I promise you that you will not regret fulfilling them. Expect our full support at your confederation moot.”
column2: “我们知道我们的请求看似奇怪，但我向你们保证，满足它们你们不会后悔。在你们的联合大会上期待我们的全力支持。”

column1: Finally, a clan which wants to give us things and take little in return!
column2: 终于有一个氏族愿意给我们东西，而索求回报却很少！

column1: They want something important, and they’re not telling us what it is.
column2: 他们想要某样重要的东西，却没有告诉我们是什么。

column1: Of everything they ask, they most want the Vingan queens.
column2: 在他们的所有要求中，他们最想要的是文加女王。

column1: Don’t ask for more than four warriors for each clan.
column2: 不要要求每个氏族超过四名战士。

column1: Don’t ask for more than five warriors for each clan.
column2: 每个氏族索要的战士不要超过五人。

column1: They wouldn’t offer us their warriors unless they intended to settle our feud.
column2: 除非他们打算解决我们之间的世仇，否则不会向我们提供战士。

column1: The only way this could work is if the first king acts to end all feuds within the tribe.
column2: 唯一可行的办法，就是由第一位王来终结部落内所有的世仇。

column1: The other clans will be pleased with the novelty of female kings. It will be something to distinguish our history in the chronicles.
column2: 其他氏族会对女王的新鲜感感到满意。这将是在编年史中让我们历史与众不同的东西。

column1: The other clans will not be happy. How can we know there will always be a deserving female candidate?
column2: 其他氏族不会高兴。我们怎么知道总能找到合适的女性候选？

column1: Who knows what strange magics the Vingans know?
column2: 谁知道文加信徒懂得什么古怪的魔法？

column1: They mean it. They will give the tribe strong magic and warriors even though we have been feuding until now.
column2: 他们是认真的。哪怕我们一直有世仇，他们也会赐予部落强大的魔法和战士。

column1: Give them what they want, but first accept their gifts.
column2: 给他们想要的，但先接受他们的馈赠。

column1: This is no trick. We can make peace with them. But we mustn’t ask for more than four warriors for each clan.
column2: 这不是诡计。我们可以与他们和解。但每个氏族索要的战士不得超过四人。

column1: Yes, Vingan queens! Let us also have Trickster kings!
column2: 好啊，文加女王！让我们也有恶作剧之王！

column1: What sinister plan do they have? What odd ideas will their implant in our daughters’ minds?
column2: 他们有什么险恶计划？他们会在我们女儿的脑子里灌输什么怪念头？

column1: Finally, a clan with sensible proposals.
column2: 终于有一个提出合理提议的氏族了。

column1: We have been enemies until now. But maybe that can change.
column2: 我们一直是敌人。但也许这可以改变。

column1: It’s a trap, a trap, I tell you!
column2: 这是个陷阱，陷阱，我跟你说！

column1: Vingan queens?
column2: 文加女王？

column1: The \x01@! warriors will be welcome here.
column2: \x01@! 战士们在这里会受欢迎的。

column1: No, you send us your daughters!
column2: 不，你们把女儿送过来！

column1: Sending daughters to be tutored and having occasional Vingan queens is a small price to pay for peace.
column2: 送女儿去受训，偶尔有文加女王，这是为和平付出的小小代价。

column1: I can’t believe they’re just willing to give us these things. We have been enemies.
column2: 我不敢相信他们就这么愿意给我们这些东西。我们一直是敌人。

column1: Could work.
column2: 行得通。

column1: Why are they so eager to be in a tribe? Are they that weak?
column2: 他们为什么这么急于加入部落？他们有那么弱吗？

column1: They want to give us magic and warriors? They must be desperate to get out of our feud.
column2: 他们想给我们魔法和战士？他们一定是急于摆脱与我们的世仇。

column1: The other clans won’t be happy to have Vingan queens. We need to get as much as possible from them if we agree.
column2: 其他氏族不会乐意有文加女王。如果我们同意，必须从他们那里尽可能多捞好处。

column1: I had no idea they would be willing to help us with their magic.
column2: 我完全没想到他们愿意用魔法帮助我们。

column1: I said they’d want to have Vingan queens, didn’t I?
column2: 我说过他们会想要文加女王，不是吗？

column1: Nothing they suggest is offensive to the gods.
column2: 他们提出的任何建议都没有冒犯众神。

column1: We negotiated with Clan \x01@!, the first clan to settle in our immediate area, to see if we could bring them into our tribe.
column2: 我们与 \x01@!氏族谈判——他们是第一个定居在我们邻近地区的氏族——看看能否将他们纳入我们的部落。

column1: Agree to propitiate the cross spirit.
column2: 同意安抚十字精灵。

column1: We agreed to propitiate the spirit of the crossline stone.
column2: 我们同意安抚十字线石的精灵。

column1: They were willing to accept a token sacrifice every Sacred Time.
column2: 他们愿意在每个神圣时间接受象征性的献祭。

column1: They insisted on a large sacrifice every Sacred Time.
column2: 他们坚持在每个神圣时间进行大型献祭。

column1: Demand their magical blessings for entire tribe.
column2: 要求他们为整个部落赐予魔法祝福。

column1: They agreed to our demand, but said we would have to sweeten our offer.
column2: 他们同意了我们的要求，但表示我们必须加码我们的提议。

column1: They refused.
column2: 他们拒绝了。

column1: “This tribe of yours will be too big for us to bless each and every clan.”
column2: “你们这个部落太大了，我们没法为每个氏族都赐福。”

column1: Guarantee them a seat or seats on the council.
column2: 保证他们在议事会上有一个或多个席位。

column1: They grudgingly accepted the one seat we offered them.
column2: 他们勉强接受了我们提供的一个席位。

column1: They gratefully accepted the council seats we offered them.
column2: 他们感激地接受了我们提供的议事会席位。

column1: Promise to make war on Beastfolk.
column2: 承诺向兽人开战。

column1: We told them we would make war on the Beastfolk.
column2: 我们告诉他们，我们将向兽人开战。

column1: We also made certain that they understood just how high a price the tribe would be paying by prosecuting their war for them.
column2: 我们也确保他们明白，部落为他们发动战争将付出多么高昂的代价。

column1: Despite our careful arguments, they did not seem to appreciate just how high a price the tribe would be paying by prosecuting their war for them.
column2: 尽管我们仔细论证，他们似乎并未充分认识到部落为他们发动战争将付出多么高昂的代价。

column1: “It is our right, as one of the first clans to defeat the menace of the crossline, to take the forefront at this confederation moot. We shall be there.”
column2: “作为最早击败交叉线威胁的氏族之一，我们有权在这次联盟议会上占据前沿位置。我们必须在场。”

column1: The \x01@! wisdom is shown not by their early arrival, but by the size and health of their herds.
column2: \x01@! 的智慧不在于他们来得早，而在于他们牲畜的规模和健康程度。

column1: If they’re in a tribe with us, they won’t be allowed to steal our cows.
column2: 如果他们和我们同在一个部落，他们就不能偷我们的牛了。

column1: They want respect, above all. Even the fight against the enemies, the beastfolk, is a battle for respect.
column2: 他们最看重的是尊重。即便与敌人——兽人——的战斗，也是一场争夺尊重的战斗。

column1: Demand their blessings, then offer one seat and propitiate the cross spirit. If that doesn’t work, then promise them their war.
column2: 要求他们的祝福，然后提供一个席位并安抚十字精灵。如果不行，就承诺他们的战争。

column1: Demand their blessings, then offer two seats and propitiate the cross spirit. If that doesn’t work, then promise them their war.
column2: 要求他们的祝福，然后提供两个席位并安抚十字精灵。如果不行，就承诺他们的战争。

column1: Demand their blessings, then offer three seats and propitiate the cross spirit. If that doesn’t work, then promise them their war.
column2: 要求他们的祝福，然后提供三个席位并安抚十字精灵。如果不行，就承诺他们的战争。

column1: I don’t know if we can bargain with a hostile clan, but it’s worth a try. Offer a seat, demand their blessings, and propitiate the spirit. If that doesn’t work, then promise them their war.
column2: 我不知道能否与一个敌对的氏族谈判，但值得一试。提供一个席位，要求他们的祝福，并安抚精灵。如果不行，就承诺他们的战争。

column1: I don’t know if we can bargain with a hostile clan, but it’s worth a try. Offer two seats, demand their blessings, and propitiate the spirit. If that doesn’t work, then promise them their war.
column2: 我不知道能否与一个敌对的氏族谈判，但值得一试。提供两个席位，要求他们的祝福，并安抚精灵。如果不行，就承诺他们的战争。

column1: I don’t know if we can bargain with a hostile clan, but it’s worth a try. Offer three seats, demand their blessings, and propitiate the spirit. If that doesn’t work, then promise them their war.
column2: 我不知道能否与一个敌对的氏族谈判，但值得一试。提供三个席位，要求他们的祝福，并安抚精灵。如果不行，就承诺他们的战争。

column1: I’m not sure about this war against the beastfolk…
column2: 我对这场针对兽人的战争不太确定……

column1: I am not one to shirk a fight, but the beastfolk are dangerous enemies. We don’t even know how many of them there are!
column2: 我不是个临阵退缩的人，但兽人是危险的敌人。我们甚至不知道他们有多少人！

column1: I’d rather fight with them than against them.
column2: 我宁可和他们并肩作战，也不愿与他们为敌。

column1: The other clans will balk if we promise too much.
column2: 如果我们承诺太多，其他氏族会退缩的。

column1: They are worthy of a seat, but the other clans will balk if we promise them much more than that.
column2: 他们值得拥有一个席位，但如果我们承诺更多，其他氏族会犹豫。

column1: They are worthy of a seat or even two, but the other clans will balk if we promise them more.
column2: 他们值得拥有一两个席位，但如果我们承诺更多，其他氏族会犹豫。

column1: All they want is to rub our noses in their superiority.
column2: 他们只想让我们低头认输，显摆自己的优越。

column1: They think they’re better than us. We’ll have to make many concessions if we continue negotiating, but I don’t think it’s worth it.
column2: 他们觉得自己比我们强。如果继续谈判，我们得做出很多让步，但我觉得这不值得。

column1: They used up all their magic coming through the crossline. Their blessings are worthless.
column2: 他们穿越交叉线耗尽了所有魔法。他们的祝福毫无价值。

column1: Their blessings would be powerful.
column2: 他们的祝福会很强大。

column1: Gaining their blessings and propitiating their spirit could decide the future of our clan’s magic.
column2: 获得他们的祝福并安抚他们的灵能决定我们氏族魔法的未来。

column1: What are these dried-up old fools going to do to us? Tremble so heartily that we take pity on them?
column2: 这些干瘪的老傻瓜能对我们做什么？颤颤巍巍到让我们可怜他们？

column1: If only we could turn their hatred against the forest folk.
column2: 要是能把他们的仇恨引向森林民就好了。

column1: What could be more thrilling than a war against the beastfolk?
column2: 还有什么比对抗兽人更令人振奋的呢？

column1: They were first here. We are part of their fate, nothing more.
column2: 他们先到这里的。我们只是他们命运的一部分，仅此而已。

column1: Even if we get them into our tribe, how do we know they won’t just continue the feud?
column2: 就算我们把他们纳入部落，怎么知道他们不会继续世仇？

column1: No organization, not even a tribe, can prevent Orlanthi from avenging their kin.
column2: 没有任何组织，哪怕是部落，能阻止奥兰多人复仇。

column1: Any organization, even a tribe, can agree to do something stupid — like fight the Beastfolk.
column2: 任何组织，哪怕是部落，都可能同意干蠢事——比如对抗兽人。

column1: We can meet in Lhankor Mhy’s weather at the moot, rather than Humakt’s weather on the field.
column2: 我们可以在兰科·姆伊的天气下在议会上会面，而不是在胡马克特的天气下在战场上相见。

column1: If we give them seats on the council, they will support us when the time comes to pick a king.
column2: 如果我们在议会上给他们席位，到时候选国王时他们会支持我们。

column1: If we can end the feud, we look like kings. Let’s offer representation on the king’s council.
column2: 如果能结束世仇，我们就像国王一样。让我们在国王议会中提供代表席位。

column1: They took one of the dragonewt’s crosses! They are too brave, or crazy. We should have nothing to do with them!
column2: 他们夺了一根龙蜥人的十字架！他们太勇敢了，或者说疯了。我们不应该和他们有任何瓜葛！

column1: If we can get them into our tribe, they will start attending our temples.
column2: 如果我们能让他们加入部落，他们就会开始来我们的神庙。

column1: At last! A war worthy of our honor!
column2: 终于！一场配得上我们荣誉的战争！

column1: A fight broke out at a feast we held in honor of \x01@!. Similar incidents of disharmony affected others in our tribe.
column2: 我们为 \x01@!举办的一场宴会上爆发了斗殴。类似的不和谐事件也影响了部落中的其他人。

column1: Convince other clans in tribe to give up treasures for tribal regalia.
column2: 说服部落中的其他氏族为了部落圣物交出财宝。

column1: We tried to convince other clans that they needed to give up more, so that our tribal regalia would have strong magic.
column2: 我们试图说服其他氏族，他们需要交出更多，这样我们的部落圣物才会有强大的魔法。

column1: Who makes the argument?
column2: 谁来提出这个论点？

column1: Do you give up a treasure of your own?
column2: 你是否交出自己的财宝？

column1: Which treasure do you give up?
column2: 你交出哪件财宝？

column1: The other clans were not interested in adding to the tribal regalia.
column2: 其他氏族对扩充部落圣物不感兴趣。

column1: Explore in search of new items for the tribal regalia.
column2: 探索寻找新的部落圣物物品。

column1: We decided to send out a party in search of new treasures to add to the tribal regalia.
column2: 我们决定派出一队人寻找新的财宝来扩充部落圣物。

column1: Who leads this party?
column2: 谁来带领这队人？

column1: Do you try to recruit warriors from other clans to help?
column2: 你是否尝试从其他氏族招募战士来帮忙？

column1: We convinced \x01@\x17 warriors from other clans to join the mission.
column2: 我们说服了来自其他氏族的 \x01@\x17 名战士加入任务。

column1: No other clans would send warriors to support the mission.
column2: 没有其他氏族愿意派战士支援这次任务。

column1: How many warriors do you send from your own clan?
column2: 你从自己的氏族派出多少战士？

column1: How many seasons long is their mission?
column2: 他们的任务持续几个季节？

column1: Sacrifice to Orlanth the King.
column2: 向奥兰斯国王献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to Orlanth in his aspect as the Great Ruler.
column2: 我们向奥兰斯以其伟大统治者的形态献祭。

column1: The priests said that the sacrifice had been received by Orlanth, but that the magic of our tribe had not strengthened.
column2: 祭司说献祭已被奥兰斯接纳，但我们部落的魔法并未增强。

column1: The priests could not say whether or not the sacrifice had been received by Orlanth.
column2: 祭司无法确定献祭是否被奥兰斯接纳。

column1: Scold members of your clan who participated in the fight.
column2: 斥责参与斗殴的本氏族成员。

column1: We scolded those of our clan who had taken part in the fight.
column2: 我们斥责了参与斗殴的本氏族成员。

column1: People were pleased that we did this.
column2: 人们对我们这样做感到高兴。

column1: This did little to brighten the mood of the clan, or of the tribe.
column2: 这并没有给氏族或部落的情绪带来多少好转。

column1: Inspire clans to harmony at a special feast.
column2: 在特别宴会上激励各氏族走向和谐。

column1: People were pleased that \x01@\x0B did this.
column2: 人们对 \x01@\x0B 这样做感到高兴。

column1: This did little to brighten the mood of the tribe.
column2: 这并没有给部落的情绪带来多少好转。

column1: Scour Dragon Pass for stolen regalia.
column2: 在龙之隘口仔细搜索被偷的圣物。

column1: We sent out a party to search for the stolen regalia.
column2: 我们派出一队人搜索被偷的圣物。

column1: There is no problem that the right words cannot solve.
column2: 没有正确的话语解决不了的问题。

column1: We are lucky that no one was seriously injured. We could be sorting out legal claims for a generation.
column2: 我们很幸运没有人受重伤。否则我们可能要花一代人的时间来理清法律诉讼。

column1: There is no good reason for this disharmony.
column2: 这种不和谐没有充分的理由。

column1: There is no obvious reason for this disharmony. We must sacrifice to Orlanth for guidance.
column2: 这种不和谐没有明显的原因。我们必须向奥兰斯献祭以求得指引。

column1: Our tribal regalia is too meager to bind the clans together. We must add new and potent items to it.
column2: 我们的部落圣物太微薄，无法将各氏族凝聚在一起。我们必须添加新的强力物品。

column1: The theft of our tribal regalia has robbed us of our harmony. We must recover it.
column2: 部落圣物被盗，剥夺了我们的和谐。我们必须找回它。

column1: We will never have harmony until we have a set of tribal regalia which is truly magical. We must add great pieces of treasure to it.
column2: 除非我们拥有一套真正具有魔力的部落圣物，否则永远不会有和谐。我们必须添加重要的财宝。

column1: We will never have harmony until we recover the lost tribal regalia.
column2: 除非我们找回丢失的部落圣物，否则永远不会有和谐。

column1: Sacrifice to Orlanth. Let him sort this out.
column2: 向奥兰斯献祭。让他来解决。

column1: What’s the problem? We just had a bit of a tussle with those other people, that’s all.
column2: 有什么问题？我们只是和其他人有点小摩擦，仅此而已。

column1: When Bad King Urgrain lost his tribal regalia, he lost half his clans.
column2: 当恶王乌格兰丢失了他的部落圣物时，他失去了半数的氏族。

column1: I am sure there are texts that explain what to do in such a situation.
column2: 我相信有典籍解释在这种情况下该怎么做。

column1: The problem is with our tribal regalia.
column2: 问题出在我们的部落圣物上。

column1: Another feast!
column2: 又是一场宴会！

column1: this new treasure.
column2: 这件新财宝。

column1: these new treasures.
column2: 这些新财宝。

column1: I know the tribe was counting on me to find treasures we could use in the tribal regalia, but my search has failed. \x02\x02 We will have to get by as best we can/We will have to hope that the tribe’s spirit is strong enough to survive without enough regalia\x02.
column2: 我知道部族指望我找到可以用于部落圣物的宝藏，但我的搜寻失败了。 \x02\x02 我们只能尽力而为/我们只能希望部族的灵魂足够坚强，能在没有足够圣物的情况下生存下去\x02。

column1: I know the tribe was counting on me to recover our tribal regalia, but my search has failed. \x02\x02 We will have to get by as best we can/We will have to hope that the tribe’s spirit is strong enough to survive without enough regalia\x02.
column2: 我知道部族指望我找回我们的部落圣物，但我的搜寻失败了。 \x02\x02 我们只能尽力而为/我们只能希望部族的灵魂足够坚强，能在没有足够圣物的情况下生存下去\x02。

column2: 我们的氏族在其他酋长中评价良好。我们无需和解，也无需在赠礼上走极端。

column1: We have better things to do than argue over a girl — like improve our temples.

column1: Even the chieftains who seem to like us — secretly, they despise us.

column1: We cannot defile the sanctity of marriage!

column1: “She is one of ours now. You have no claim on her.”
column2: “她现在是我们的人了。你对她没有主张。”

column2: “我们来掰手腕，决定她属于哪个氏族。”

column2: 他同意我们的提议。

column2: \x01B_ 赢得了比赛。

column2: \x01B_ 说我们会后悔不遵守协议；现在我们要以血来偿还。

column1: “We shall keep her, but will negotiate compensation.”
column2: “我们会留下她，但愿意协商补偿。”

column1: We negotiated terms of compensation with \x01B_.
column2: 我们与 \x01B_协商了补偿条款。

column1: After many hours of hard bargaining, the least they will accept in compensation is \x01@\x1A cows worth of goods.
column2: 经过数小时的艰难议价，他们愿意接受的最低补偿是价值 \x01@\x1A 头牛的货物。

column1: “Your case is strong. You may take her back with you.”
column2: “你的案情有力。你可以把她带回去。”

column1: Our carls were unhappy that we would give her up so easily.
column2: 我们的自由民对我们如此轻易地交出她感到不满。

column1: The family she was staying with protested the ring’s decision and were angry for some time.
column2: 收留她的家族抗议长老会的决定，并且恼怒了一段时间。

column1: The young man we married her to was distraught. “We are just beginning to enjoy ourselves, and now you sunder us as though we were mated cattle!” he cried.
column2: 我们把她嫁给的年轻人心烦意乱。“我们才刚刚开始享受生活，现在你们就把我们拆散，好像我们是配种的牛一样！”他哭喊道。

column1: “She is married now. It is a done thing, and you must forget her.”
column2: “她已经结婚了。这是既成事实，你必须忘记她。”

column1: \x01B_ reluctantly agreed that what was done was done.
column2: \x01B_ 不情愿地同意生米已成熟饭。

column1: Offer them at least five cows for her.
column2: 至少出五头牛把她换来。

column1: Offer them at least ten cows.
column2: 至少出十头牛。

column1: Pay no heed to \x01B_’s threats. We can beat them on the field of battle.
column2: 别理会 \x01B_的威胁。我们可以在战场上打败他们。

column1: We are obligated to return her. There is no way around it.
column2: 我们有义务归还她。没有别的办法。

column2: 她合法地嫁给了我们的一位年轻人。他们现在不能把她从我们身边带走。

column1: They were once well-disposed towards us. We must find a peaceful solution to this problem.
column2: 他们曾经对我们很有好感。我们必须为这个问题找到一个和平的解决方案。

column1: In the time of Vingkot, the Idevlings and the Kikotlings went to war over a woman. She turned out to be a troublemaker who wished them both ill.
column2: 在温科特时代，伊德夫林人与基科特林人曾为一个女人开战。结果她是个挑事者，巴不得他们两败俱伤。

column1: She is ours now. They may not take her from us.
column2: 她现在是我们的人了。他们不能把她从我们身边带走。

column1: I would not give them a barrow full of rotting sheep carcasses!
column2: 我连一满坟的腐烂羊尸都不想给他们！

column1: We have a fine young woman, and she is what is important. She is worth at least forty cows.
column2: 我们有一位出色的年轻女子，这才是最重要的。她至少值四十头牛。

column1: If we make enemies now, it will be hard to form a tribe later.
column2: 如果现在结仇，日后就难以组成部落了。

column1: Assume that \x01C$ is dead; console her family.

column2: 我们以为 \x01C$ 已经死了，并安慰了她悲痛欲绝的家人。

column1: They were certain that she was still alive.
column2: 他们确信她还活着。

column1: We did not go there to look for her.
column2: 我们没有去那里找她。

column1: Her parents loudly condemned the judgment of the ring, and many of the clan supported them.

column2: 我们派了一支搜索队去荒野中寻找她。

column1: How many seasons should they search before they give up?
column2: 他们应该搜索几个季节才放弃？

column1: Send emissaries to nearby clans, looking for \x01C$.
column2: 向附近的氏族派出使者，寻找 \x01C$。

column1: We sent searchers to neighboring clans, looking for \x01C$.
column2: 我们向邻近的氏族派出搜索者，寻找 \x01C$。

column1: Do you accuse her of lying?
column2: 你指控她说谎吗？

column1: We did not press the issue.
column2: 我们没有追究此事。

column1: We have lost many warriors of late. We cannot afford to fight to rescue this girl, even if she is a thane’s daughter.
column2: 我们近来损失了许多战士。我们无法为救这个女孩而战斗，即使她是领主的女儿。

column1: Our weaponthanes will do whatever is necessary to rescue a thane’s daughter.
column2: 我们的武器领主将不惜一切代价救回领主的女儿。

column1: If another clan is implicated in her kidnapping, we have no choice but to initiate a blood feud against them.
column2: 如果另一个氏族卷入她的绑架案，我们别无选择，只能对他们发起血仇。

column1: If another clan is implicated in her kidnapping, we can initiate a legal claim against them.
column2: 如果另一个氏族卷入她的绑架案，我们可以对他们提起法律诉讼。

column1: We are not feuding with anyone. It cannot be one of our neighbors who did this thing.
column2: 我们没有与任何人结仇。不可能是我们的邻居干的。

column1: A divination ritual might tell us where she is, and save us from searching blindly.
column2: 一次占卜仪式或许能告诉我们她在哪里，省得我们盲目搜索。

column1: If our magic was strong, a divination ritual might tell us where she is, and save us from searching blindly. But our magic is weak.
column2: 如果我们的魔法够强，一次占卜仪式或许能告诉我们她在哪里，省得我们盲目搜索。但我们的魔法很弱。

column1: Our magic is strong. A divination ritual will tell us where she is, and save us from searching blindly.
column2: 我们的魔法很强。一次占卜仪式会告诉我们她在哪里，省得我们盲目搜索。

column1: It was the elves who took her.
column2: 是精灵带走了她。

column1: She has been claimed by the undead, and will no doubt come back to infect us with the contagion of the grave.
column2: 她已被亡灵据为己有，无疑会回来把坟墓的瘟疫传染给我们。

column1: The dragonewts wouldn’t do something like this.
column2: 龙人不会做这种事。

column1: They came for me, but took \x01C$ by mistake!
column2: 他们是冲我来的，但误抓了 \x01C$ ！

column1: We must not shame ourselves before Ernalda. Spare no effort to find her.
column2: 我们绝不能在艾尔纳达面前蒙羞。要不遗余力找到她。

column1: \x01C$ does not deserve to suffer for the ring’s decisions. We must find her.
column2: \x01C$ 不该因为长老会的决定而受苦。我们必须找到她。

column1: She’s one girl, and she may still be alive. We lose more warriors every time we fight.
column2: 她只是一个姑娘，也许还活着。我们每打一仗都会损失更多战士。

column1: “Dark looks turn to darker deeds.”
column2: “阴暗的眼神会酿成更阴险的恶行。”

column1: Someone knows.
column2: 有人知情。

column1: We searched everywhere, but didn’t find \x01C$. She is lost to us forever.
column2: 我们找遍了各处，但没有找到 \x01C$。她永远离开我们了。

column1: The search party sent to find \x01C$ came back without her.
column2: 派去找 \x01C$ 的搜索队回来了，没有找到她。

column1: The orphaned girl, Kallyr, the one you took in after an outlaw woman raised her in a shield, has grown up. She is now a fine young woman with ambitions to be a warrior. She has joined the warrior woman’s cult of Vinga. As you can see from the bruises on her sparring partners, she has a real talent for fighting, one that seems almost superhuman.
column2: 那个被遗弃的女孩卡莉尔——那个被法外女子在盾牌上抚养大的孩子——已经长大了。她现在是一位出色的年轻女子，有志成为一名战士。她加入了战士之女神温加的女神教团。正如你可以从她对练伙伴身上的淤青看到的那样，她有着真正的战斗天赋，几乎超凡脱俗。

column1: Kallyr, the girl raised in a shield, had become quite the young warrior.
column2: 那个在盾牌上长大的女孩卡莉尔，已经成为一位相当年轻的战士。

column1: Hold a feast in her honor.

column1: We held a feast in her honor.
column2: 我们为她举办了一场宴会。

column1: Our warriors were greatly pleased that Kallyr would stay among us.
column2: 我们的战士们非常高兴卡莉尔能留在我们中间。

column1: Make her work harder to earn your approval.
column2: 让她更努力地工作来赢得你的认可。

column1: We made her work even harder to please us.
column2: 我们让她更加努力地取悦我们。

column1: Kallyr was nothing if not eager to please.
column2: 卡莉尔若说有什么，那就是渴望取悦他人。

column1: Send her away to be trained under a famous holy warrior of Vinga.
column2: 送她去一位著名的温加圣武士那里训练。

column1: We sent her away to be trained under a famous holy warrior of Vinga.
column2: 我们送她去一位著名的温加圣武士那里接受训练。

column1: The warriors missed Kallyr, and said that they would have been more than capable of training her.
column2: 战士们想念卡莉尔，并说他们完全有能力训练她。

column1: Let her improve at her own pace.

column1: Test her mettle by sending her on an exploratory mission.

column2: 我们派她去执行一次侦察任务，考验了她的勇气。

column1: We could surely stand to learn more of the troll lands to the north, to see if the Uz trade god, Argan Argar, holds sway there.
column2: 我们当然可以多了解北方的巨魔领地，看看乌兹的贸易之神阿尔甘·阿尔加是否在那里掌权。

column1: The other warriors are jealous of her. Send her away, so there will be less grumbling.
column2: 其他战士嫉妒她。把她送走，这样抱怨就会少一些。

column1: Even the oldest and most grizzled of our weaponthanes adores Kallyr. They see her as flesh of their flesh.
column2: 就连我们最年长、最老练的武器领主也喜爱卡莉尔。他们视她为骨中骨、肉中肉。

column1: Hero’s blood flows in Kallyr’s veins. A hero must never be given the easy route.
column2: 英雄之血在卡莉尔的血管中流淌。英雄绝不能被给予坦途。

column1: If we send her to train with another clan, it will strengthen the ties between us.
column2: 如果我们送她去另一个氏族训练，会加强我们之间的联系。

column1: The other warriors are proud of Kallyr, and a feast in her honor would give them cheer.
column2: 其他战士为卡莉尔感到自豪，为她举办一场宴会将使他们欢欣鼓舞。

column1: Whatever you do, don’t let her learn magic. It’ll spoil her martial ardor.
column2: 无论你做什么，别让她学魔法。那会败坏她的尚武热忱。

column1: Her fighting skills are good, but she must learn magic if she is to truly be a hero.
column2: 她的战斗技巧不错，但如果要成为真正的英雄，她必须学习魔法。

column1: She must train under Taralarth Battle-Dancer of clan \x01@/. Taralarth is the greatest Vingan warrior in all of Dragon Pass.
column2: 她必须在 \x01@/氏族的塔拉拉斯·战斗舞者门下受训。塔拉拉斯是龙之隘口最强的温加战士。

column1: Away, that’s where she’d learn — not that she can’t learn here, you — don’t misunderstand me, I wasn’t saying that — fine, fine trainers we have here, yes.
column2: 离开这里，那才是她该学的地方——不是说她在这儿学不到，你——别误会，我不是那个意思——我们这儿有很好的训练师，是的。

column1: Let the girl be a girl. She will have plenty of time to be a hero later.
column2: 让女孩做女孩吧。她以后有的是时间当英雄。

column1: She is a great example to the others. She must learn to read, so that they will want to, also.
column2: 她是其他人的好榜样。她必须学会阅读，这样其他人也会想学。

column1: If she must go somewhere, make sure it is not to the north, where I just know she’ll be eaten by trolls.
column2: 如果她非要去什么地方，确保不是北方，我敢肯定她会在那里被巨魔吃掉。

column1: If I cannot toast Kallyr’s many fine qualities, I fear I shall burst a gall bladder!
column2: 如果我不能为卡莉尔的诸多美德举杯庆贺，我怕我会胆囊破裂！

column1: Divide and conquer, that’s what I always say.
column2: 分而治之，我一直这么说。

column1: Just send an Eurmal \x02\x02blessing/curse\x02 to each of these \x02\x03whiners/complainers/rebels\x02.
column2: 只需给每个 \x02\x03抱怨者/牢骚者/反叛者\x02送去一个欧尔玛的 \x02\x02祝福/诅咒\x02 。

column1: When one bull becomes weak, another replaces him.
column2: 一头公牛变弱时，另一头会取代它。

column1: All of my hopes are \x02\x04in ruins/for nothing, now/shattered/smashed\x02.
column2: 我所有的希望都 \x02\x04化为废墟/归于虚无/破碎/粉碎\x02。

column1: We were never meant for the mealy-mouthed ways of kings.
column2: 我们天生就不适应国王们委婉曲折的做法。

column1: There is no political problem that cannot be resolved with generous gift-giving.
column2: 没有什么是慷慨馈赠解决不了的政治问题。

column1: Threats or treats, threats or treats.
column2: 威胁还是贿赂，威胁还是贿赂。

column1: I will have to bring the more loyal chieftains back to my side, and so deprive the unhappiest of his support.
column2: 我必须把更忠诚的酋长们拉回我这边，从而剥夺那些最不满者得到的支持。

column1: So they think I have disgraced them, do they? Wait until I defeat them in battle — then they’ll know the bitter taste of dishonor!
column2: 所以他们觉得我让他们蒙羞了，是吗？等我击败他们——那时他们就会尝到耻辱的苦味！

column1: Again? Even if I were to rival King Heort himself, this \x02\x03gaggle/crowd/mob\x02 would not know it. I will give it up.
column2: 又一次？就算我能与赫尔特王本人相提并论，这群 \x02\x03乌合之众/暴民/乱民\x02 也不会知道。我放弃了。

column1: sceneR099
column2: sceneR099

column1: Let them keep the hostages.
column2: 让他们留着人质吧。

column1: We told them to keep the hostages.
column2: 我们告诉他们留着人质。

column1: Pay them the customary ransom of \x01A" cows.
column2: 按习俗支付 \x01A" 头牛作为赎金。

column1: We paid the ransom they demanded.
column2: 我们支付了他们要求的赎金。

column1: Our warriors rejoiced that their companions were alive and back with the clan.
column2: 我们的战士欢呼雀跃，因为他们的同伴活着回到了氏族。

column1: Send our clan trader to negotiate a lower ransom.
column2: 派我们氏族的商人去谈判降低赎金。

column1: We sent our trader to negotiate a lower ransom.
column2: 我们派商人去谈判降低赎金。

column1: They refuse to lower their ransom demand.
column2: 他们拒绝降低赎金要求。

column1: \x01@N bargains them down to a ransom of \x01@\x12 cows. Do you pay it?
column2: \x01@N 将赎金谈降到 \x01@\x12 头牛。你支付吗？

column1: Send a small group to rescue hostages.
column2: 派一小队人去营救人质。

column1: We sent a small war party to rescue the hostages.
column2: 我们派了一支小型战团去营救人质。

column1: Who leads the mission?
column2: 谁领导这次任务？

column1: Our warriors \x02\x04crept into the enemy tula at night and quietly brought out our kinfolk/snuck past the enemy patrols, found our kinfolk, and set them free/slid into the enemy tula as silently as ghosts, and rescued the hostages/set a brush fire near the enemy tula, and retrieved our kin during the ensuing confusion\x02.
column2: 我们的战士 \x02\x04趁夜潜入敌方图拉，悄悄带出了我们的族人/偷偷绕过敌方巡逻队，找到了我们的族人，将他们释放/像幽灵一样无声地滑入敌方图拉，救出了人质/在敌方图拉附近放了一场灌木火，在随后的混乱中找回了我们的族人\x02。

column1: They \x02\x03were able to get away without wetting their blades/had to fight a few farmers, and so got out easily/had to bruise a few weaponthanes on the way out, but made it home safely\x02.
column2: 他们 \x02\x03得以不沾刀血就脱身/不得不跟几个农夫交手，但轻松脱身/出去时不得不揍了几个武器领主，但仍安全到家\x02。

column1: We tried to rescue our kinfolk, but \x02\x04the enemy fought our every move towards their tula/enemy patrols spotted us and set their fighters upon us before we could get anywhere near their tula/although we slipped into the tula at night easily enough, we could not find the hostages we knew were there. Indeed, the enemy found us instead/we were discovered near the enemy’s clan hall, and had to fight to get free ourselves\x02.
column2: 我们试图营救我们的族人，但 \x02\x04敌人阻止了我们向图拉推进的每一步/敌方巡逻队发现了我们，在我们还没靠近图拉时就派兵攻击/我们虽然很容易就趁夜溜进了图拉，却找不到明知在那里的人质。实际上，反而是敌人发现了我们/我们在敌方部族大厅附近被发现，不得不杀出重围\x02。

column1: One of our weaponthanes took a stray shot, and died. Others were injured in the skirmishing.
column2: 我们的一名武器领主流矢中身，就此陨落。另有数人在散兵战中负伤。

column1: Do you want to try another way to get the hostages back?
column2: 你想试试其他法子要回人质吗？

column1: Our warriors, brought low, disturbed the rest of the clan so badly that no one could agree on what to do.
column2: 战士们的挫败令整个氏族人心惶惶，无人能就如何行动达成一致。

column1: \x01@\x05, the emissary, had long since left in disgust.
column2: \x01@\x05那位使者早已厌弃离去。

column1: Our warriors \x02\x04crept into the enemy tula at night and quietly kidnapped some thanes/snuck past the enemy patrols and grabbed some nobles/found crafters near the edge of the enemy tula, and took them hostage/set a brush fire near the enemy tula, and nabbed some of our enemy during the ensuing confusion\x02.
column2: 我们的战士们 \x02\x04趁夜潜入敌方图拉，悄然绑走了一些领主/溜过敌方巡逻队，掳走了几名贵族/在敌方图拉边界附近找到了工匠，将他们扣为人质/在敌方图拉附近引燃灌木火，趁混乱抓了几个敌人\x02。

column1: They \x02\x03were able to get back without wetting their blades/had only a few farmers to threaten, and so got out easily/had to bruise a few weaponthanes on the way out, but made it home safely\x02.
column2: 他们 \x02\x03兵不血刃便得以脱身/只需威胁几个农夫，轻松撤出/撤离时不得不打伤几名武器领主，但最终平安归来\x02。

column1: We seized \x01@\x10 hostages.
column2: 我们夺取了 \x01@\x10 人质。

column1: Do you:
column2: 你要：

column1: trade all of the hostages you hold for the two they hold?
column2: 用你手中所有的人质交换他们手中的那两人？

column1: They paid us the ransom we demanded for the extra hostages.
column2: 他们支付了我们为额外人质索要的赎金。

column1: They won through haggling what they could not win on the battlefield, and paid us less ransom than we demanded.
column2: 他们凭讨价还价赢得了战场上赢不了的东西，支付的赎金少于我们的要价。

column1: We tried to grab hostages, but \x02\x04the enemy fought our every move towards their tula/enemy patrols spotted us and set their fighters upon us before we could get anywhere near their tula/although we slipped into the tula at night easily enough, the enemy found us soon enough/we were discovered near the enemy’s clan hall, and had to fight\x02.
column2: 我们试图抓人质，但 \x02\x04敌人对我们的每一步逼近其图拉的行动都加以反击/敌方巡逻队发现了我们，在我们接近其图拉之前就派出战士截击/我们虽然夜间顺利潜入图拉，但很快被敌人发现/我们在敌方部族大厅附近暴露，不得不应战\x02。

column1: One of our warriors took a stray arrow, and died. Others were injured in the skirmishing, and we did not bring home any hostages.
column2: 我们的一名战士中流箭身亡，另有数人在散兵战中负伤，且未能带回任何人质。

column1: Do you want to try another way to get your hostages back?
column2: 你想试试其他法子救回人质吗？

column1: As much as we might like to, we can’t afford to pay ransom now.
column2: 尽管我们很想，但眼下付不起赎金。

column1: Pay the ransom and be done with it. We can well afford it.
column2: 付赎金了结此事。我们完全负担得起。

column1: I am confident that I can bargain down their ransom.
column2: 我有信心能压低他们的赎金要价。

column1: It will be easier to take \x01@! hostages than to recover our own.
column2: 抓 \x01@! 人质比赎回我们自己的人更容易。

column1: I am confident that I can lead a successful war party. It will be easier to take \x01@! hostages than to recover our own.
column2: 我有信心能带领一支成功的战团。抓 \x01@! 人质比赎回我们的人更容易。

column1: I am confident that I can lead a successful war party.
column2: 我有信心能带领一支成功的战团。

column1: If we don’t pay the ransom, the hostages might be adopted into the \x01@! clan. They might feel abandoned, and justified in taking revenge.
column2: 若不付赎金，人质可能会被收养进 \x01@! 氏族。他们可能感到被抛弃，有理由复仇。

column1: Relations between our two clans are poor. It will be hard to persuade them of anything.
column2: 我们两族之间关系恶劣，任何事都难以说服他们。

column1: Apart from a little raiding, relations between our two clans are good. They may be open to persuasion.
column2: 除了零星劫掠，我们两族关系尚可。他们或许愿意听从劝说。

column1: Our clan magic is weak. It is a bad time to take dramatic action.
column2: 我们的氏族魔法薄弱，不宜采取激烈行动。

column1: Our clan magic is strong. It is a good time to take action.
column2: 我们的氏族魔法强大，正是采取行动之时。

column1: Tell them that if they do not release the hostages, I will come over and drool on their old women, in a way they do not wish to be drooled upon.
column2: 告诉他们，若不放人，我就过去在他们老妇身上滴口水——用一种她们绝不愿被滴的方式。

column1: “The best equipment is common sense.”
column2: “最好的装备是常识。”

column1: sceneR100
column2: sceneR100

column1: An exploratory party was captured by gigantic bull-men, who took them as thralls. Only \x01@I was allowed to return, to warn us never to venture onto Beastfolk lands again.
column2: 一支探索队被巨大的牛头人俘虏，沦为奴隶。只有 \x01@I 被允许回来警告我们，永不再涉足兽人领地。

column1: \x01@I returns with terrible news. When exploring to the \x01@O, the exploratory party was ambushed by gigantic bull-men. They captured the party and declared them thralls. They let \x01@I go, in order to warn the clan that those lands are under the protection of the great Ironhoof, and that any who come there will be taken as thralls.
column2: \x01@I 带回噩耗。在探索 \x01@O时，探索队遭到巨大牛头人伏击。他们俘虏了队伍，宣布其为奴隶。他们放 \x01@I 归来，以警告氏族：那片土地受伟大的铁蹄庇护，任何踏入者都将被俘为奴。

column1: Alas, the gigantic bull-men still hold our exploration party as thralls.
column2: 唉，巨大的牛头人依然扣着我们的探索队为奴。

column1: Let the matter go.
column2: 就此作罢。

column1: People weren’t pleased that the ring had given up their kin to the beastfolk.
column2: 民众不满长老会将族人拱手让给兽人。

column1: Our ancestors were even less happy.
column2: 我们的祖先更为不满。

column1: We accepted the loss of our clan mates.
column2: 我们接受了失去族人的事实。

column1: Promise not to trespass on their territory if they return their prisoners.
column2: 承诺若他们归还俘虏，我们便不再侵犯其领地。

column1: Who do you choose as your emissary to the bull-men?
column2: 你选谁作为出使牛头人的使者？

column1: What is the value of the gifts you bring for the bull-men?
column2: 你为牛头人准备的礼物价值几何？

column1: How many guards do you send to accompany \x01@\x05?
column2: 你派多少护卫陪同 \x01@\x05？

column1: The emissary’s party did not return.
column2: 使团未能归来。

column1: The emissary returned with the lost clan members, having solemnly promised the bull-men that we would not trespass on their lands again.
column2: 使者带着失散的族人归来，已向牛头人郑重承诺不再侵犯他们的土地。

column1: The emissary’s party returned with none of the lost clan members. The bull-men said that they were lucky not to be taken as thralls themselves.
column2: 使团空手而归。牛头人说他们没被扣为奴隶已是万幸。

column1: Do you let the matter rest?
column2: 你要就此作罢吗？

column1: We grieved our lost clansmen, while hatred for the bull-men burned like coals in our hearts.
column2: 我们哀悼失落的族人，而对牛头人的仇恨如煤火般在胸中燃烧。

column1: Send a war party to rescue the prisoners.
column2: 派出战团营救俘虏。

column1: We found our people and succeeded in freeing them after a tough running battle with the bull-men and their allies.
column2: 我们找到了族人，在与牛头人及其盟友的一场激烈追击战后成功解救了他们。

column1: We fought a nasty running battle with the bull-men. Their allies pelted us with slingstones from the cover of the trees. Nearly all our warriors were killed or wounded and we never found our kinsmen.
column2: 与牛头人展开了一场惨烈的追击战。他们的盟友从树林掩护中向我们投掷投石。几乎我们所有的战士都阵亡或受伤，我们始终未能找到我们的族人。

column1: We had to admit that our clansmen were destined to serve the bull-men for good.
column2: 我们不得不承认，我们的族人注定要永远侍奉牛头人。

column1: Send a war party to take bull-man prisoners; then swap hostages.
column2: 派遣一支战团去俘虏牛头人；然后交换人质。

column1: We sent a small war party to take bull-men prisoner, so we would have prisoners to swap for our lost clan mates.
column2: 我们派出一支小战团去俘虏牛头人，这样我们就有俘虏来交换失踪的族人。

column1: We surprised a group of bull-men in the forest and took \x01@\x12 of them captive.
column2: 我们在森林中突袭了一群牛头人，俘虏了其中 \x01@\x12 。

column1: The fearsomely strong creatures did not stay captured for long, though. By the time we got back to our clan lands, all of them had escaped. In the process, they harmed many of our warriors.
column2: 不过，这些强得可怕的生物并未被囚禁多久。等我们回到氏族领地时，他们全都逃脱了。过程中，他们伤了我们不少战士。

column1: We failed to capture any bull-men. Many of our weaponthanes were killed or wounded.
column2: 我们没能抓到任何牛头人。许多武器领主阵亡或受伤。

column1: Warn other clans not to go to beastfolk territory.
column2: 警告其他氏族不要去兽人领地。

column1: We warned other clans not to go to the lands of the beastfolk.
column2: 我们警告其他氏族不要去兽人领地。

column1: Which clans do you warn?
column2: 你警告哪些氏族？

column1: Send \x01@\x18 to engage bull-men in drinking competition.
column2: 派遣 \x01@\x18 与牛头人进行饮酒比赛。

column1: We sent \x01@\x18 to engage the bull-men in a drinking competition.
column2: 我们派遣 \x01@\x18 与牛头人进行饮酒比赛。

column1: How many warriors do you send along with \x01@\x18?
column2: 你派多少战士随同 \x01@\x18？

column1: Our warriors came back without \x01@\x18. When asked what happened to \x08, the warriors would only shake their heads.
column2: 我们的战士们回来了， \x01@\x18没有回来。当问起 \x08发生了什么，战士们只是摇头。

column1: Neither \x01@\x18 or the warriors we sent along with \x08 came back.
column2: \x01@\x18 和我们派去随同 \x08 的战士都没有回来。

column1: The bull-men are called minotaurs. They are very tough, and very stubborn.
column2: 牛头人被称为牛头人。他们非常强悍，也非常顽固。

column1: They don’t really care about their territory. They just want ransom, like any human clan.
column2: 他们其实并不在乎自己的领土。他们只是想要赎金，像任何人类氏族一样。

column1: It sounds as if the bull-men value the sanctity of their land more than anything else.
column2: 听起来牛头人把土地的圣洁看得比什么都重要。

column1: Some beastfolk, the ducks for example, follow a strange version of Orlanthi custom. These bull-men, on the other hand, do not.
column2: 有些兽人，比如鸭人，遵循一种奇怪的奥兰斯风俗。但这些牛头人不一样，他们不遵守。

column1: There can be no accommodation with our ancient enemies.
column2: 与我们的宿敌不可能达成和解。

column1: Just because they’re a little bigger than we are doesn’t mean we can’t take them.
column2: 仅仅因为他们比我们大一点，并不意味着我们不能对付他们。

column1: It is always easier to take random prisoners than rescue hostages.
column2: 抓随机俘虏总是比营救人质容易。

column1: It is always easier to take random prisoners than rescue hostages. The question is: can we hold onto bull-man prisoners after we take them?
column2: 抓随机俘虏总是比营救人质容易。问题在于：我们抓到牛头人俘虏后能关住他们吗？

column1: We have already antagonized the beastfolk. It pains me to say this, but perhaps we should leave well enough alone.
column2: 我们已经激怒了兽人。我很难过这么说，但也许我们该就此罢手。

column1: We have shown friendship and an open hand to the beastfolk. Surely the bull-men will listen to reason.
column2: 我们曾向兽人展示友谊和开放的态度。牛头人肯定会听从道理的。

column1: Let’s not offend Ernalda by fighting in Sea season, and let’s also not offend the beastfolk.
column2: 我们不要在还魂季战斗冒犯厄尔纳尔达，也不要冒犯兽人。

column1: Let’s not offend Ernalda by fighting in Earth season, and let’s also not offend the beastfolk.
column2: 我们不要在土季战斗冒犯厄尔纳尔达，也不要冒犯兽人。

column1: Our clan magic is weak. It is a bad time to fight bull-men.
column2: 我们的氏族魔法很弱。现在不是与牛头人战斗的好时机。

column1: Our clan magic is strong. It is a good time to fight bull-men.
column2: 我们的氏族魔法很强。现在是与牛头人战斗的好时机。

column1: Before Alakoring was Alakoring Dragonbreaker, he negotiated with bull-men. He came with too few warriors, and they tried to make him a thrall.
column2: 在阿拉科林成为屠龙者阿拉科林之前，他曾与牛头人谈判。他带的战士太少，他们想把他变成奴隶。

column1: Let me lead the delegation. If anyone can talk sense into bull-men, it would be me.
column2: 让我带领使团。如果有人能让牛头人讲道理，那就是我。

column1: Bulls always think they run things. Don’t trust them.
column2: 公牛们总以为自己是老大。别相信他们。

column1: I hear these bull-heads are fond of drink. I’ll defeat them in a drinking contest and win back our hostages!
column2: 我听说这些牛头人喜欢喝酒。我会在饮酒比赛中打败他们，赢回我们的人质！

column1: They had ferocious nets! Big heads with wicked-looking horns! Our clansmen are doomed, doomed.
column2: 他们有凶猛的网！长着凶恶尖角的大脑袋！我们的族人完了，彻底完了。

column1: \x02\x03This is not going to be easy./We killed bull-men in the Storm Age. Let us slaughter them again./We cannot back down from beast-men.\x02
column2: \x02\x03这不会容易。/我们在风暴时代杀过牛头人。让我们再屠杀他们一次。/我们不能在兽人面前退缩。\x02

column1: sceneR101
column2: sceneR101

column1: A new clan arrived and wanted to claim some of our land as their own.
column2: 一个新氏族到来，想声称我们的一部分土地归他们所有。

column1: Drive them off by force.
column2: 用武力赶走他们。

column1: We decided to drive them off.
column2: 我们决定赶走他们。

column1: We drove them away.
column2: 我们赶走了他们。

column1: Hold a feast for them, then ask them to go.
column2: 为他们举办盛宴，然后请他们离开。

column1: We feasted them, then asked them to go.
column2: 我们宴请了他们，然后请他们离开。

column1: They said the \x01@* clan was grateful to us for our hospitality, and would seek land elsewhere.
column2: 他们说 \x01@* 氏族感激我们的好客，会去别处寻找土地。

column1: Later, we learned they had found a place to live in Dragon Pass.
column2: 后来，我们得知他们在龙隘找到了居住地。

column1: “Your generosity is no generosity at all!” they cried. “You feed us only to speed us on our way!” Reluctantly, they left our tula.
column2: “你们的慷慨根本不是慷慨！”他们喊道。“你们给我们吃的只是为了催我们上路！”他们不情愿地离开了我们的领地。

column1: Give them some of your lands, if they agree to an alliance.
column2: 如果同意结盟，就给他们一些土地。

column1: We ceded them some of our land.
column2: 我们割让了一些土地给他们。

column1: Offer to adopt them into your clan.
column2: 提议将他们收养进你的氏族。

column1: We offered to make them members of clan \x01@".
column2: 我们提议让他们成为 \x01@"氏族的成员。

column1: The people were not pleased that we were granting membership in the clan to strangers.
column2: 人们对于允许陌生人加入氏族并不高兴。

column1: The people welcomed them gladly.
column2: 人们欣然欢迎他们。

column1: Among the prominent \x01@* leaders were \x01@\x18.
column2: 在突出的 \x01@* 领导者中有 \x01@\x18。

column1: They said that although their clan had fallen on bad times, it could not turn its back on its history and ancestors. They could not join our clan.
column2: 他们说，尽管他们的氏族落难，但不能背弃自己的历史和祖先。他们不能加入我们的氏族。

column1: Persuade them to leave.
column2: 说服他们离开。

column1: We said that they should leave.
column2: 我们说他们应该离开。

column1: They said that they were tired, had escaped many enemies, and would make their stand here. They refused to leave.
column2: 他们说他们累了，已经逃过了许多敌人，要在这里坚守。他们拒绝离开。

column1: They agreed to look for better land elsewhere.
column2: 他们同意去别处寻找更好的土地。

column1: We may have much land, but we are far from wealthy. They must leave us to grow into our claim.
column2: 我们或许土地很多，但远谈不上富足。他们必须离开，好让我们发展自己的领地。

column1: Although we are wealthy, we will not stay that way by adopting every stray alynx that wanders into our pastures.
column2: 尽管我们富足，但如果收养每只流浪到我们牧场中的野猫，我们就无法保持富裕。

column1: They will be more tractable when we get some hot food into them.
column2: 等我们给他们些热食下肚，他们就会更顺从了。

column1: I’m not saying we should drive them off. But if we want to, we can crush the dirty jinxes with little trouble.
column2: 我并不是说应该赶走他们。但如果我们想，不费什么麻烦就能碾碎那些肮脏的晦气鬼。

column1: This clan of survivors brings with it many warriors for each carl. We could stand to increase our martial strength.
column2: 这个幸存者氏族带来的战士比每个自由民都多。增强我们的军事力量也不错。

column1: In the time of Vingkot, our ancestors encountered people in need, and adopted them into our clan.
column2: 在温戈特时代，我们的祖先曾遇到有需要的人，并将他们收养进我们的氏族。

column1: There are too many of them to turn into thralls, so I say drive the lawless scum away!
column2: 他们人数太多，无法全部变成奴隶，所以我说，赶走这些无法无天的渣滓！

column1: If we give them land, we are assured their gratitude. It would be good to have a proven ally as a neighbor.
column2: 如果我们给他们土地，就一定会得到他们的感激。有一位经得起考验的盟友做邻居是好事。

column1: There are too many weaponthanes among this ragged clan. Our carls will complain if they have to support even more people who grow nothing.
column2: 这个破衣烂衫的氏族里武器领主太多了。我们的自由民如果还要供养更多不事生产的人，会抱怨的。

column1: Feast them. Then, when they are drunk and full, draw weapons — oh, wait, that violates our sacred vows of hospitality. Feast them, then adopt them!
column2: 宴请他们。然后，等他们酒足饭饱，就拔刀——哦，等等，这违反了我们神圣的好客誓言。还是宴请他们，然后收养他们吧！

column1: I admire them. Despite the odds, they have proven that the hearth is where the people are.
column2: 我钦佩他们。尽管胜算渺茫，但他们证明了炉火所在就是家园所在。

column1: We will look bad if we decline to help them.
column2: 如果我们拒绝帮助他们，会显得很糟糕。

column1: We didn’t make a land claim only to give it all away.
column2: 我们声明土地不是用来送人的。

column1: Fleeing the god-king’s weather-of-points, luck-filled refugees found noble land-defenders.
column2: 逃离神王“尖芒天候”的幸运难民，遇到了高尚的土地捍卫者。

column1: No Orlanthi owes anything to any other Orlanthi…
column2: 没有哪个奥兰提人欠其他奥兰提人什么……

column1: Their magic must be strong, for they made it all this way in the face of enemy pursuit.
column2: 他们的魔法一定很强，才能在敌人的追击下一路走到这里。

column1: Wait until a clan with treasure to give us comes along. Then we’ll consider giving them land.
column2: 等到一个有财宝可以给我们的氏族来了再说。到那时我们再考虑给他们土地。

column1: What is the next clan you decide to approach?
column2: 你决定接下来去找哪个氏族？

column1: “We have enough clans.”
column2: “我们已经够多氏族了。”

column1: \x02\x03We agreed to meet soon to discuss the terms of making a tribe/We arranged for a meeting in the near future/We decided to meet very soon to talk about tribe-making\x02.
column2: \x02\x03我们同意不久后见面讨论组建部落的事宜/我们安排了不久后的会面/我们决定很快见面商讨组建部落的事\x02。

column1: Smaller tribes are better — there are fewer chances for disagreement.
column2: 小部落更好——分歧的机会更少。

column1: We have only \x01@\x18 clans in our tribe so far. A bigger tribe would be better for us all.
column2: 到目前为止，我们的部落只有 \x01@\x18 个氏族。更大的部落对我们所有人都更好。

column1: With \x01@\x18 clans in our tribe, we begin to have a chance of succeeding. But more wouldn’t hurt us, either.
column2: 部落中有 \x01@\x18 个氏族，我们开始有了成功的机会。但再多一些也无妨。

column1: \x01@\x18 clans in a tribe is a good, strong number to support and defend each other.
column2: \x01@\x18 部落中的氏族数量是一个很好、稳固的数字，足以互相扶持和防御。

column1: We must be careful not to grow so big that we cannot get along, and the tribe fail before it’s begun.
column2: 我们必须小心，不能长得太大以至于无法和睦相处，导致部落还没开始就失败。

column1: \x02\x02We have been making promises that will not be popular with all the members of the tribe./We must be careful not to give away too much, or we risk losing the tribe before it is born.\x02
column2: \x02\x02我们一直在做出一些不受部落所有成员欢迎的承诺。/我们必须小心不要给得太多，否则冒着部落还没诞生就失去它的风险。\x02

column1: Unless the members of the tribe are all our friends, we will have trouble convincing them of this plan.
column2: 除非部落的所有成员都是我们的朋友，否则我们要让他们信服这个计划会有困难。

column1: We need a clan that hates the elves as much as we do.
column2: 我们需要一个和我们一样痛恨精灵的氏族。

column1: We need warriors who are not afraid to die to destroy the unliving.
column2: 我们需要不惧死亡、以毁灭不死生物为目标的战士。

column1: We don’t need any more clans. We don’t want our own glory diluted too much.
column2: 我们不需要更多氏族了。我们不希望自己的荣耀被过度稀释。

column1: We need enough clans to make us famous for our tribe-making skills.
column2: 我们需要足够的氏族，让我们因组建部落的技巧而闻名。

column1: We need clans made up of heroes, the wind blazing through their hair!
column2: 我们需要由英雄组成的氏族，让狂风掠过他们的头发！

column1: It doesn’t matter who we choose. We are either fated to be a tribe, or not.
column2: 我们选谁并不重要。我们注定要么成为部落，要么不会。

column1: We must choose clans who will not betray us.
column2: 我们必须选择不会背叛我们的氏族。

column1: Really, if you ask me, the choice is obvious — oh, what was I thinking? The name of the clan was right on the tip of — pardon me?
column2: 真的，如果你问我，选择是显而易见的——哦，我在想什么？这个氏族的名字就在我嘴边——你说什么？

column1: Yes, good plan, I mean idea.
column2: 是的，好计划，我是说好主意。

column1: \x02\x06This whole effort is doomed./I still have a bad feeling about this./Now we’re trying to curry favor with every flea-bag group that calls itself a clan./I don’t think we need to tie ourselves up with any of them./Look how this ‘tribe’ idea sends us scurrying hither and thither, like supplicating weasels! How shameful!/Alliances are bad enough. Now we’re embroiling ourselves further in Orlanth-knows-what.\x02
column2: \x02\x06这整个努力注定失败。/我对这事还是有种不好的感觉。/现在我们正试图讨好每一个自称氏族的跳蚤窝。/我不认为我们需要和他们任何一个绑在一起。/看这“部落”主意让我们像乞求的黄鼬一样四处乱窜！多可耻！/联盟就已经够糟了。现在我们还在进一步卷入奥兰斯知道什么鬼东西。\x02

column1: Most of those clans think they’re better than us.
column2: 那些氏族多数认为他们比我们强。

column1: We must carefully weigh the demands of each clan, and choose those whose demands will not cause the others to balk.
column2: 我们必须仔细权衡每个氏族的要求，选择那些要求不会让其他氏族退缩的氏族。

column1: We must choose clans who value the written word.
column2: 我们必须选择重视文字书写的氏族。

column1: This is going well.
column2: 一切顺利。

column1: If we can create a huge tribe, the sagas will remember us forever!
column2: 如果能建立一个庞大的部落，传说将永远铭记我们！

column1: \x02\x03We must choose clans brimming with marriageable young men and women./In a tribe, every marriage and every child can help cement an alliance./We can form the tribe, but it will not be solid until blood-ties binds it tight.\x02
column2: \x02\x03我们必须选择充满可婚配年轻男女的氏族。/在部落中，每一场婚姻和每一个孩子都有助于巩固联盟。/我们可以组建部落，但除非血缘纽带将其紧紧联结，否则它不会稳固。\x02

column1: We must choose clans whose men are willing to listen to reason.
column2: 我们必须选择那些男人愿意讲道理的氏族。

column1: Which clans need our help the most?
column2: 哪些氏族最需要我们帮助？

column1: Let’s not give them all gifts to make them join us. Let’s ask some of them for gifts.
column2: 别全拿礼物讨好它们加入。找几个氏族，向它们要点礼物。

column1: Make sure we do not include clans whose women are harridans and shrews.
column2: 确保我们不包括那些女人泼辣凶悍的氏族。

column1: \x02\x03See to it that we approach clans willing to make peace with other tribes./If we can bring Peace Clans into the tribe, we will bring a new golden age to Dragon Pass./Our tribe should include our enemies, because then they will no longer be our enemies!\x02
column2: \x02\x03务必接触愿意与其他部落讲和的氏族。/如果我们能让和平氏族加入部落，龙之隘口将迎来新的黄金时代。/我们的部落应当容纳仇敌，因为那样它们就不再是我们的仇敌了！\x02

column1: Choose clans who respect the gods.
column2: 选择尊崇神明的氏族。

column1: “\x02\x06The clouds that move slowly are the farmer’s friends/When the heron hovers over the field, forgetfulness reigns/Kinship is stronger than kings, but crowns beat gowns/A queen is as good as a king, and better to look at/Where dragons rule, grow teeth and scales/You can hear an ancestor in every stone\x02.”
column2: “\x02\x06缓行的云是农人的朋友/苍鹭盘旋在田野上空时，健忘主宰一切/亲情强过王权，但冠冕胜过袍服/王后堪比国王，且更赏心悦目/在龙统治的地方，长出牙齿和鳞片/每块石头里都能听见祖先的声音\x02。”

column1: We must choose clans who are on good terms with the dragonewts.
column2: 我们必须选择与龙人关系和睦的氏族。

column1: Choose only clans who know the true meaning of generosity.
column2: 只选择懂得慷慨真义的氏族。

column1: Take on only clans with fierce warriors.
column2: 只接纳拥有勇猛战士的氏族。

column1: \x02\x05All clans have their strengths. Our task is to choose those that will be strongest together./Our tribe will be stronger if it mirrors Orlanth’s Storm Tribe. Any of our neighbors might deserve to join./Clans that believe in justice instead of simply getting their own way are rare, but with luck we will find them./The first king will settle all the feuds within the tribe, so that the tribe will start as friends./Seek friends who understand the lessons of the Storm.\x02
column2: \x02\x05所有氏族各有长处。我们的任务是挑选那些合力最强之辈。/如果我们的部落能仿效奥兰斯的风暴部落，它将更加强大。任何邻族都可能有资格加入。/信奉公正而非一味任性的氏族很罕见，但运气好的话我们会找到的。/初代王将平息部落内部所有世仇，使部落从一开始就亲如友邻。/寻找懂得风暴教诲的盟友。\x02

column1: \x02\x03In a tribe, no one has to starve./Our enemies do not deserve to join./Clans who respect the Earth Mother, that’s who we need.\x02
column2: \x02\x03在部落里，没有人会挨饿。/我们的仇敌不配加入。/我们需要的是尊重大地母亲的氏族。\x02

column1: \x02\x05A tribe will not change the facts of war and death./Seek clans who believe in war and Humakt will bless the tribe./Tribes mean war./A tribe is good. Allies in the tribe is even better./Seek clans who face the truth as bravely as they face danger.\x02
column2: \x02\x05部落改变不了战争与死亡的现实。/寻找信奉战争的氏族，胡马克特会赐福部落。/部落意味着战争。/部落很好。部落里有盟友则更好。/寻找能像直面危险一样勇敢面对真相的氏族。\x02

column1: \x02\x03Talk talk talk…/This will pay off when we are king, and can take whatever we want./Clans that can’t fight Chaos aren’t worth talking to.\x02
column2: \x02\x03空谈空谈空谈……/等我们当了王，能任意予取予求时，这些就会见成效。/不能对抗混沌的氏族，不值得与它们交谈。\x02

column1: \x02\x06If we choose only wise clans, we might not deserve the throne. Lucky for us there are plenty of idiots to choose from!/Let’s finish this off and get on to the feast!/I’ve visited all these clans. They have good points and bad points./Good to see the rest of you are taking your responsibilities so seriously./Next!/How many clans do we have already?\x02
column2: \x02\x06若我们只选择睿智的氏族，或许就不配坐上王位。幸好我们有足够多的蠢货可选！/我们赶紧收尾，去赴宴吧！/所有氏族我都走访过。它们各有好坏。/很高兴看到诸位如此认真尽责。/下一个！/我们已经有多少氏族了？\x02

column1: We were not able to convince enough of our neighbors to join us in making a tribe. The god-talkers said that the omens were turning bad, and that we should stop our efforts for now.
column2: 我们未能说服足够多的邻族共同组建部落。神言者说预兆正在转坏，我们应暂缓努力。

column1: We ceased our tribe-building activities.
column2: 我们中止了部落建设活动。

column1: We can try again some other year, when we are stronger and better respected.
column2: 我们可以等来年实力更强、更受敬重时再尝试。

column1: None of our neighbors wanted to join us in making a tribe.
column2: 没有一个邻族愿意与我们共建部落。

column1: We can try again some other year, when the clans who had agreed to form a tribe get over their disappointment.
column2: 我们可以等来年，等那些原本同意组建部落的氏族从失望中平复后再尝试。

column1: Though some of our neighbors wanted to join us in making a tribe, the others could not be convinced.
column2: 虽然有些邻族愿意与我们共建部落，但其余氏族未能被说服。

column1: The clans who had agreed to form a tribe with us were peevish and disappointed.
column2: 那些原本同意与我们一起组建部落的氏族既恼怒又失望。

column1: sceneR103
column2: sceneR103

column1: Priestesses of Esra destroyed more \x01@\x1F pots, protesting the tribal law that \x01@\x1F pots should be used whenever possible.
column2: 埃斯拉的女祭司打破了更多 \x01@\x1F 口陶罐，以抗议那条“尽可能使用陶罐”的部落法律 \x01@\x1F 。

column1: Priestesses of Esra destroyed pots belonging to the \x01@\x1F clan, protesting the tribal law that \x01@\x1F pots should be used whenever possible.
column2: 埃斯拉的女祭司打破了属于 \x01@\x1F 氏族的陶罐，以抗议那条“尽可能使用陶罐”的部落法律 \x01@\x1F 。

column1: At tribal moot, argue that priestesses should not be punished.
column2: 在部落大会上，主张不应惩罚女祭司。

column1: We went to the tribal moot to say that the priestesses of Esra should not be punished.
column2: 我们前往部落大会，主张不应惩罚埃斯拉的女祭司。

column1: How much in total do you distribute among the clans?
column2: 你总共在氏族之间分配了多少？

column1: The moot ruled that the grain priestesses had broken tribal law, and would have to be punished.
column2: 大会裁定谷物女祭司违反了部落法律，必须受到惩罚。

column1: At tribal moot, argue to strike down the pottery law.
column2: 在部落大会上，主张废除陶器法。

column1: We went to the tribal moot to argue that the pottery law should be struck down.
column2: 我们前往部落大会，主张应当废除陶器法。

column1: How much total wealth do you give the clans?
column2: 你总共给各氏族多少财富？

column1: The case was judged in our favor. The other clans were glad to see the pottery requirements go away.
column2: 裁决结果对我方有利。其他氏族很高兴看到陶器规定被废除。

column1: Pay what they ask.
column2: 满足它们的要求。

column1: They said we were just.
column2: 它们称赞我们公正。

column1: In what way do you punish them?
column2: 你打算如何惩罚她们？

column1: Scold them in public.
column2: 当众训斥她们。

column1: The chief grain-woman said our heads were made of clay.
column2: 首席谷仓女说我们的脑袋是泥做的。

column1: Forbid them from performing their rituals this year.
column2: 禁止她们今年举行仪式。

column1: The grain-women said that it would be the fault of the ring if Esra withheld her bounty.
column2: 谷仓女们声称，如果埃斯拉克扣收成，那就是长老会的过错。

column1: Fine their families.
column2: 处罚她们的家族。

column1: Although they were unhappy, their families were among those most able to afford a fine.
column2: 虽然它们不悦，但这些家族是最有能力支付罚款的。

column1: They ask for 30 cows in compensation from each clan.
column2: 它们要求每个氏族赔偿30头牛。

column1: Punish the priestesses.
column2: 惩罚女祭司。

column1: We chose to punish the priestesses.
column2: 我们选择惩罚女祭司。

column1: We don’t want to pay cows every time some minor deities’ devotees disagree with a tribal decision.
column2: 我们可不想每次某个小神祇的信徒反对部落决议就得赔牛。

column1: We are too unpopular to prevail at the moot.
column2: 我们在议会上太不受欢迎，无法获胜。

column1: The other clans will not listen to us at the moot. But if we can solve this ourselves, it might raise their opinion of us.
column2: 其他氏族在议会上不会听我们的。但如果我们自己能解决这件事，或许能提升他们对我们的看法。

column1: The other clans respect us; we can change things at the moot.
column2: 其他氏族尊重我们；我们可以在议会上改变局面。

column1: The other clans think well of us. We can try to change this law at the moot.
column2: 其他氏族对我们印象不错。我们可以尝试在议会上修改这条法律。

column1: A good scolding might shame the priestesses into doing what’s right.
column2: 一顿严厉训斥或许能让女祭司们羞愧而做正确的事。

column1: The Esra priestesses usually come from the wealthier families. We could fine them without causing undue hardship.
column2: 埃斯拉的女祭司通常出身富裕家庭。我们可以罚她们的款，而不至于造成过度困苦。

column1: Esra is the goddess of grain. If her priestesses are punished, our crops will fail.
column2: 埃斯拉是谷物女神。如果她的女祭司们受到惩罚，我们的庄稼就会歉收。

column1: If we punish the priestesses, they will resent it, become stubborn, and object again.
column2: 如果我们惩罚女祭司，她们会心怀怨恨，变得固执，再次反对。

column1: Punishing the priestesses will only increase their resentment and their objections.
column2: 惩罚女祭司只会增加她们的怨恨和反对。

column1: A \x02\x03pot/dish/jar\x02 is \x02\x03worth less/less valuable/cheaper\x02 than a scroll.
column2: 一个 \x02\x03罐子/盘/陶罐\x02 比 \x02\x03更不值钱/价值更低/更廉价\x02 胜过一张卷轴。

column1: The real question is: what do the dragonewts think?
column2: 真正的问题是：龙人怎么想？

column1: Women! Always causing trouble!
column2: 女人！总是惹麻烦！

column1: A few smashed pots is a small price for learning where the people are unhappy.
column2: 打碎几只罐子，换来了解民怨所在，代价很小。

column1: We cannot have people smashing things right and left, every time they change their minds about an agreement!
column2: 我们不能让人们每次对协议改变主意就到处打砸东西！

column1: sceneR104

column1: We heard them out, but said little.

column2: 牛比剑更有力量。

column2: 这全都是计谋，要我们交出牛和财宝！

column1: It is not too late to abandon this folly!
column2: 现在放弃这愚蠢之举还为时不晚！

column1: Like cattle to the fold, let them believe they can back out if they want to. Once we are a tribe, they will be pleased at the results, and the gate will be shut.

column1: Tell them that we must unite to smite our common undead foes!

column1: In a dream the other night, I saw sunshine gleaming on a crown, while a stone altar wept heroic tears. The gods are pleased that we hold the crown, but wish us to pay attention to the god-plane now. We must plan for a heroquest, soon.

column1: While watching the sky in the evening, I saw the clouds form a great crown, and a great altar. The crown fell towards the altar and blew apart! We must reverse this unsettling omen with something very magically potent — a heroquest, and soon.

column1: During a reverie recently, I beheld a large hall, ready for company, with food laid out and ale at hand. No one was there except Ernalda, who polished a crown and smiled, but then looked up and wept at the empty hall. I take it to mean that the gods would like us to visit them. We must pay attention to their wishes, and perform a heroquest soon.
column2: 最近一次恍惚中，我看见一座大厅，已为宾客备好，食物陈列，麦酒在手。那里空无一人，只有厄娜尔达在擦拭一顶王冠微笑，但她抬起头，看着空荡荡的大厅哭泣。我认为这意味着众神希望我们去拜访他们。我们必须留意他们的愿望，并尽快举行一场英雄追寻。

column1: Orlanth appeared in my dreams these last few nights, smiling and holding out a great crown. I believe we must prepare to take the throne when the next chance presents itself.
column2: 最近几夜，奥兰斯出现在我的梦中，微笑着捧出一顶巨大的王冠。我相信我们必须做好准备，当下一次机会出现时夺取王座。

column1: The smoke from the altar fires curls in rings lately. The grain brought in for sacrifice has of itself formed plaited circles. I saw seven alynx kittens playing in a ring — need we more omens to tell us that the time grows near when we must take the crown?
column2: 近来祭坛火焰的烟雾缭绕成环。带来献祭的谷物自己编成了辫状环。我看见七只艾林克斯幼崽围成一圈玩耍——我们还需要更多预兆来告诉我们夺取王冠的时刻即将到来吗？

column1: During a reverie recently, I beheld a large hall, full of good company, with food and ale at hand. Everyone was making merry, singing and dancing. Orlanth and Ernalda were there, laughing and pointing to the one empty chair, a chair with a crown on its seat. I take it to mean that the gods would like us to take the throne when the next chance comes.
column2: 在近日的一场梦境中，我望见一座大厅，满座高朋，食物与麦酒近在咫尺。众人欢歌起舞，尽情作乐。奥兰斯与厄娜尔达也在那里，笑着指向那把空着的椅子——椅座上放着一顶王冠。我想这意味着诸神希望我们在下一次机会来临时登上王位。
