column1: \x01@\x0B completed the rites of kingship. The celebration lasted for days.
column2: \x01@\x0B 完成了王权仪式。庆祝活动持续了数日。

column1: We have given away enough cows already. The gods will have to be satisfied with the sacrifices of others.
column2: 我们已经送出了够多的牛只。诸神只能满足于其他人的献祭了。

column1: Men and women now know of our generosity. The time has come for us to show it to the gods.
column2: 男女皆知我们的慷慨。现在该向诸神展示这份慷慨了。

column1: With a tribe comes war, and so it should be. Let the warriors celebrate now, for they will have to fight soon.
column2: 有部落就有战争，理当如此。让战士们尽情欢庆吧，因为他们很快就要上阵厮杀。

column1: Whatever we do, it is important that we show support for the tribe, and not just our own reputation.
column2: 无论我们做什么，重要的是展现对部落的支持，而非仅顾自己的名声。

column1: The tribal regalia is purely symbolic. We need not worry about it.
column2: 部落圣物纯粹是象征性的，我们不必操心。

column1: If we are willing to add to the tribal regalia, the other clans will follow our lead.
column2: 如果我们愿意向部落圣物添置宝物，其他部族就会效仿我们。

column1: It will be hard to convince the other clans to add to the tribal regalia. We will have to add to it ourselves.
column2: 很难说服其他部族向部落圣物添置宝物。我们必须自己动手。

column1: If we ask the other clans to add to the tribal regalia, they will be anxious to please. We need not add to it ourselves.
column2: 如果我们请其他部族向部落圣物添置宝物，他们会迫不及待地迎合。我们不必亲自动手。

column1: Everybody knows that a tribe is doomed to fail if its magical regalia is not strong enough.
column2: 人人都知道，如果一个部落的魔法圣物不够强大，它注定要失败。

column1: The last rites probably failed because the tribe’s regalia wasn’t strong enough.
column2: 上次仪式很可能失败，就是因为部落的圣物不够强大。

column1: This is going to be the best celebration ever!
column2: 这将是史上最棒的庆典！

column1: After his failed attempt to replicate his father’s rites of kingship, Urgrain Urgrainsson burned for seven days.
column2: 在试图重演他父亲的王权仪式失败后，乌格兰·乌格兰森焚烧了七天。

column1: These rites are awfully dangerous!
column2: 这些仪式简直危险至极！

column1: The regalia is the important thing here.
column2: 圣物才是关键。

column1: Perhaps one day I will undergo these rites!
column2: 或许有一天，我也会接受这些仪式！

column1: Soon after \x01@\x0B succeeds, we can begin building more temples for the entire tribe to use.
column2: \x01@\x0B 登基成功后，我们便可开始为整个部落建造更多神庙。

column1: This moment is so — so — so… momentous! No, that’s not exactly the word. Historical, that’s the word. Isn’t it?
column2: 这一刻真是——真是——真是……非同小可！不，这个词不太准确。历史性的，就是这个。对吧？

column1: our own \x01@\x0B
column2: 我们自己的 \x01@\x0B

column1: \x01@\x0B got ready for the rites of kingship.
column2: \x01@\x0B 为王权仪式做好了准备。

column1: Entertain influential thanes of other clans.
column2: 款待其他部族有威望的领主。

column1: We celebrated with influential thanes of other clans.
column2: 我们与其他部族有威望的领主一同欢庆。

column1: What is the value of the gifts and food you give to them?
column2: 你赠予他们的礼物和食物的价值是多少？

column1: The thanes were impressed by our generosity.
column2: 领主们对我们的慷慨印象深刻。

column1: The thanes said that our generosity was less than that of many other clans.
column2: 领主们说我们的慷慨不及许多其他部族。

column1: Entertain members of your clan who have served its interests well.
column2: 款待那些为你部族利益做出贡献的成员。

column1: We used the joyous occasion to reward those who served our clan well.
column2: 我们趁着喜庆时刻，奖赏了那些为部族效力的人。

column1: Our people were impressed by the generosity of the ring.
column2: 我们的人民对长老会的慷慨印象深刻。

column1: The people said that we had forgotten the meaning of generosity.
column2: 人民说我们已经忘记了慷慨的含义。

column1: The people seemed to think they were due even more gifts.
column2: 人民似乎认为他们应得更多礼物。

column1: We decided to lend our magic to aid \x01@\x0B.
column2: 我们决定借出我们的魔法来帮助 \x01@\x0B。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods to aid \x01@\x0B.
column2: 向众神献祭以帮助 \x01@\x0B。

column1: We sacrificed to the gods so that \x01@\x0B might perform well in the rite of kingship.
column2: 我们向众神献祭，以便 \x01@\x0B 能在王权仪式中表现良好。

column1: \x01@\x0B attempted the rites of kingship, and was killed by \x02\x07an inhuman hero/mist that howled/a word no one can remember/whirling spirits/ancestral spirits/an unseen blade/birds from the sun\x02. After a time of mourning, we would have to pick a new candidate.
column2: \x01@\x0B 尝试了王权仪式，并被 \x02\x07非人英雄/嚎叫的迷雾/无人记得的话语/旋转的精灵/先祖之灵/无形的刀刃/来自太阳的鸟\x02杀死。哀悼期过后，我们必须挑选新的候选人。

column1: Spread the board, and open the kegs. Let the musicians play! Do not let my tests be marred by parsimony.
column2: 摆好宴席，打开酒桶。让乐师们演奏！不要让我的考验因吝啬而受损。

column1: In sacrifices, be generous to the gods, for it will be worse to have their ill-will than not to call on them at all.
column2: 在献祭中，对众神要慷慨，因为惹来他们的恶意比根本不召唤他们更糟糕。

column1: We all know what the rites are, and I am ready.
column2: 我们都知道仪式是什么，我已经准备好了。

column1: The moment is getting nearer, I can feel my strength rise like gathering storm clouds.
column2: 时刻越来越近，我能感觉到我的力量如聚集的暴风云般升腾。

column1: Let us give magic, not cows.
column2: 让我们给予魔法，而非牛只。

column1: We have many choices. We can give to others, to our own, or to the gods.
column2: 我们有很多选择。我们可以给予他人、给予我们自己、或给予众神。

column1: The people are discontented. Please them before pleasing others.
column2: 人民不满。在取悦他人之前先取悦他们。

column1: Strengthen our bonds with our allies, so they do not become our foes.
column2: 加强我们与盟友的联系，以免他们变成我们的敌人。

column1: Of course we can use magic to cause the rites to fail. Magic is the highest form of politics.
column2: 当然我们可以用魔法让仪式失败。魔法是最高形式的政治。

column1: History tells us that clans who fail to elect their preferred candidate sometimes spoil the rites. But it is easy to detect, and brings dishonor.
column2: 历史告诉我们，未能选出心仪候选人的氏族有时会破坏仪式。但这很容易被发现，并带来耻辱。

column1: Other clans have not yet forgiven us. We should continue to curry favor.
column2: 其他氏族尚未原谅我们。我们应该继续讨取欢心。

column1: Our relations with the other clans are poor. This would be a good time to improve them.
column2: 我们与其他氏族的关系不佳。现在是改善它们的好时机。

column1: Our relations with the other clans are strong. We can afford to turn our attentions elsewhere.
column2: 我们与其他氏族的关系牢固。我们可以将注意力转向别处。

column1: Our own people are neglected. Do not let their discontent grow.
column2: 我们的人民被忽视了。不要让他们的不满滋长。

column1: Our people are content, so please the gods instead.
column2: 我们的人民满意，所以转而取悦众神。

column1: \x02\x03Vingkot’s descendants all used his sword and helm in their kingship rites, until the regalia was lost/This is the most important ritual the tribe can perform together/Uvuli Urgrainsdottir used magic to prevent her husband from doing what her beloved brother could not\x02.
column2: \x02\x03Vingkot的后裔都在王权仪式中使用他的剑与头盔，直到仪礼失窃/这是部落能共同进行的最重要的仪式/乌武莉·乌格兰斯多蒂尔使用魔法阻止她的丈夫去做她深爱的兄弟未能做到的事\x02。

column1: I don’t see why the other clans didn’t just choose to disband the tribe.
column2: 我不明白其他氏族为什么不干脆选择解散部落。

column1: It is easier for kings who inherit the rites than for the one who invents them.
column2: 对于继承仪式的国王来说，比发明它们的人更容易。

column1: This day should be chronicled, so that people will know of it three hundred years from now.
column2: 这一天应当被载入史册，以便三百年后的人们仍能知晓。

column1: Lavish gift-giving will help the other clans forget recent events.
column2: 慷慨赠礼将帮助其他氏族忘记最近的事件。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods.
column2: 向众神献祭。

column1: Why should \x01@\x0B succeed? Why did no one choose me?
column2: 为什么 \x01@\x0B 应当成功？为什么没人选择我？

column1: Put me in charge of the feasting!
column2: 让我负责宴席！

column1: sceneR108
column2: sceneR108

column1: A dispute broke out between the pig priestesses and the grain priestesses.
column2: 猪神女祭司与谷物女祭司之间爆发了争执。

column1: Compensate the grain priestesses.
column2: 补偿谷物女祭司。

column1: We compensated the grain priestesses.
column2: 我们补偿了谷物女祭司。

column1: The Mralota priestesses were affronted, and the Esra priestesses complained that the pig-worshippers were still hogging the shed.
column2: 姆拉洛塔女祭司们感到受辱，而埃斯拉女祭司们抱怨说猪崇拜者们还在霸占棚屋。

column1: Encourage the opposed priestesses to find agreement.
column2: 鼓励对立的女祭司们寻求一致。

column1: We encouraged the opposed priestesses to find agreement.
column2: 我们鼓励了对立的女祭司们寻求一致。

column1: After several heated exchanges, and several calmer discussions, they were able to resolve their dispute.
column2: 经过几次激烈交锋和几次冷静讨论，她们得以解决争端。

column1: The Esra women said the Mralota women were pig-headed. The Mralota women said that the Esra women had rotten toes.
column2: 埃斯拉妇女说姆拉洛塔妇女顽固如猪。姆拉洛塔妇女说埃斯拉妇女脚趾腐烂。

column1: Scold the pig priestesses of your clan.
column2: 责骂你氏族的猪神女祭司。

column1: We scolded our pig priestesses.
column2: 我们责骂了我们的猪神女祭司。

column1: The Mralota women said that they were right, and that we had offended their goddess. Now they would not only hamper the Esra rituals, but would limit their own magic, as well.
column2: 姆拉洛塔妇女说她们是对的，我们冒犯了她们的女神。现在她们不仅会妨碍埃斯拉的仪式，还会限制她们自己的魔法。

column1: Urge the pig priestesses of Clan \x01@$ to preach humility.
column2: 敦促 \x01@$ 氏族的猪神女祭司宣扬谦卑。

column1: We urged the pig priestesses of Clan \x01@$ to preach humility.
column2: 我们敦促了 \x01@$ 氏族的猪神女祭司宣扬谦卑。

column1: The Mralota priestesses of Clan \x01@$ agreed to speak to our Mralota priestesses, and to urge restraint.
column2: \x01@$ 氏族的姆拉洛塔女祭司同意与我们的姆拉洛塔女祭司交谈，并敦促克制。

column1: The \x01@$ priestesses rebuffed us, saying that our pig women were only demanding what they had long been deprived of.
column2: \x01@$ 女祭司们驳回了我们，说我们的猪妇女只是在要求她们长期被剥夺的东西。

column1: “This is not a matter for the ring.”
column2: “这不关长老会的事。”

column1: We left this matter to the fertility priestesses.
column2: 我们将此事交由丰饶女祭司处理。

column1: The arguing priestesses agreed that it was none of our affair, but that is all they agreed upon.
column2: 争吵的女祭司们同意这不关我们的事，但这也是她们唯一同意的事。

column1: The Mralota women are a little full of themselves lately, but it is nothing that should concern us.
column2: 姆拉洛塔妇女最近有点自以为是，但这不值得我们担忧。

column1: Our Mralota women are under the influence of their counterparts in the \x01@$ clan.
column2: 我们的姆拉洛塔妇女受到 \x01@$ 氏族同行的影响。

column1: The pig women and the grain women can be reconciled.
column2: 猪妇女和谷物妇女可以和解。

column1: Everyone is in a sour mood. Reconciliation will be difficult.
column2: 每个人都心情不好。和解会很困难。

column1: I can convince the \x01@$ priestesses to step in on our behalf.
column2: 我能说服 \x01@$ 女祭司代表我们介入。

column1: If this dispute continues, our pig magic will be strong, but our crop magic will be weak.
column2: 如果这场争执继续，我们的猪魔法会变强，但我们的作物魔法会变弱。

column1: We must act decisively or these squabbles will ruin all our fertility.
column2: 我们必须果断行动，否则这些争吵将毁掉我们所有的丰饶。

column1: This is silly. Why have we let this go on for so long?
column2: 这太蠢了。我们为何让它持续这么久？

column1: We have to stop this now. Or we will never solve it.
column2: 我们现在必须制止它。否则我们永远解决不了。

column1: The carls are all offended by the overweening pride of the pig women.
column2: 自由民全都被猪女人们那傲慢自大的气焰激怒了。

column1: The pig priestesses must understand their place. But the longer this goes on, the harder that will be.
column2: 猪神女祭司必须认清自己的位置。但事态拖得越久，这事就越难办。

column1: Arrrgh! Make it stop!
column2: 啊——！让它停下！

column1: I’m going to grab one of those silly pig sticks and use it. Hard.
column2: 我非得抓起一根那蠢猪棍，狠狠用上一番。

column1: Gifts will quiet the offended tongues of the grain women.
column2: 礼物能让那些被冒犯的谷物女人们闭上嘴。

column1: Supporting the grain women will give comfort to the elves.
column2: 支持谷物女人们会让精灵感到安慰。

column1: This is getting out of hand.
column2: 这事快要失控了。

column1: We’re never going to solve this, are we?
column2: 我们永远解决不了这事，对吧？

column1: Anger must be turned to understanding.
column2: 愤怒必须转化为理解。

column1: Nothing we say will end this dispute.
column2: 我们说什么都不会结束这场争端。

column1: Uh-oh. Them again.
column2: 呃哦。又是他们。

column1: At this rate, we’ll be facing kinstrife.
column2: 照这样下去，我们将面临同族相争。

column1: Some of our Mralota priestesses left the tribe and went back to Heortland, where they said they would be treated right. The people weren’t sure they were sorry to see them go.
column2: 我们的一些姆拉洛塔女祭司离开了部族，回到了赫奥特兰，她们说在那里会受到公正对待。族人们也不确定是否对她们的离去感到遗憾。

column1: How big a gift do you send with your emissary?
column2: 你派使者送去多大的礼物？

column1: Find a few new cottars to tend the gardens.
column2: 找几个新佃农来照料园子。

column1: We looked for new cottars to tend the gardens.
column2: 我们找过新佃农来照料园子。

column1: Which clan do you approach in search of cottars?
column2: 你去找哪个氏族寻找佃农？

column1: We found no one willing to be adopted into our tribe as a cottar.
column2: 我们没找到愿意加入我们部族当佃农的人。

column1: Stop growing the herbs.
column2: 别再种那些草药了。

column1: We stopped growing the herbs.
column2: 我们已经停止种植草药。

column1: Scold the carls for their constant complaining.
column2: 责骂自由民们没完没了的抱怨。

column1: We scolded the carls for their constant complaining.
column2: 我们责骂了自由民们没完没了的抱怨。

column1: The carls laughed with embarrassment. “Indeed, we have vexed you greatly, and with little cause. We shall try to carry on in the loving spirit of Ernalda.”
column2: 自由民尴尬地笑了。“确实，我们惹您大怒了，却没什么缘由。我们会努力以埃纳尔达的仁爱精神继续干下去。”

column1: The carls bore our reprimand with frost-trimmed silence.
column2: 自由民以寒霜般的沉默承受了我们的训斥。

column1: “Come now. You exaggerate the threat to the crops.”
column2: “得了吧。你们夸大了对庄稼的威胁。”

column1: We told the carls that they were exaggerating.
column2: 我们告诉自由民，他们夸大其词了。

column1: The carls laughed with embarrassment. “Perhaps we have let the principle of the thing become too important. You are right; it is just a little extra work.”
column2: 自由民尴尬地笑了。“或许我们把这事的原则看得太重了。您说得对；不过是多了一点活计。”

column1: The carls shook with embarrassment. “You may be right; it is just a little extra work. But the principle of this thing is what matters.”
column2: 自由民羞愧得发抖。“您或许是对的；不过是多了一点活计。但这件事的原则才是要紧的。”

column1: Despite this matter, the carls are in good spirits. They will respond to reason.
column2: 尽管出了这事，自由民们情绪不错。他们会听从道理的。

column1: The carls see this as just the latest in a long series of slights. It will be hard to appease them.
column2: 自由民认为这只是长期一系列轻慢中的最新一桩。很难安抚他们。

column1: The carls are jealous of the praise that the weaponthanes have been getting of late.
column2: 自由民嫉妒武器领主们近来得到的赞誉。

column1: We cannot force the weaponthanes to root about in dirt.
column2: 我们没法逼武器领主们在泥地里刨土。

column1: Our crops will fail unless we tend to this crisis immediately!
column2: 我们的庄稼会歉收，除非我们立即处理这场危机！

column1: Our grain crops are more important than these spice plants.
column2: 我们的谷物比这些香料植物更重要。

column1: We grow only a token amount of these herbs. The carls greatly exaggerate the work involved.
column2: 我们只种植少量象征性的这些草药。自由民大大夸大了其中涉及的工作。

column1: Growing the herbs is some work, but it scarcely prevents the carls from tending to the crops.
column2: 种植草药确实有点活计，但几乎不妨碍自由民照料庄稼。

column1: We agreed to grow too many of these \x01@& plants.
column2: 我们同意种植了太多这些 \x01@& 植物。

column1: Esra is the grain goddess. There is no herb goddess.
column2: 埃斯拉是谷物女神。没有草药女神。

column1: I’ve seen them out there, they’re leaning, they’re chewing, it’s really quite a … I don’t have to spell it out for you, do I?
column2: 我在那儿见过她们，她们倚着，嚼着，那实在相当……我得给你明说吗，不用吧？

column1: Just stop growing them. Who cares about the stupid tribe?
column2: 就别种了。谁在乎那蠢部族？

column2: sceneR110

column1: Southerners come to your tula looking for the present location of the \x01@* clan. They say that they’re agents of the Pharaoh, the tyrannical ruler your people fled when you came to this land. They appear to be sorcerers; at the very least, those strange implements they carry are probably magical weapons.
column2: 南方人来到你的图拉领地，寻找 \x01@* 氏族当前的位置。他们自称是法老，那个你们族人逃到这片土地时所躲避的暴虐统治者的代理人。他们似乎是巫师；至少，他们携带的那些奇怪器具很可能是魔法武器。

column1: The implements emit a low thrumming
column2: 那些器具发出低沉嗡鸣

column1: sound.
column2: 声。

column1: sound, the likes of which you have never heard.
column2: 声，是你从未听过的那种。

column1: The Pharaoh’s sorcerers came to us looking for the \x01@* clan, which we had adopted into ours.
column2: 法老的巫师来找我们，寻找 \x01@* 氏族，那氏族已被我们吸纳。

column1: The Pharaoh’s sorcerers came to us looking for the \x01@* clan.
column2: 法老的巫师来找我们，寻找 \x01@* 氏族。

column1: “Die now, sorcerous scum!”
column2: “去死吧，巫师渣滓！”

column1: We attacked them.
column2: 我们攻击了他们。

column1: Although a wailing bolt of evil magic killed one of our warriors without leaving a mark, we slew the sorcerers before they could wreak any further harm.
column2: 尽管一道哀嚎的邪恶魔法箭矢杀死了我们一名战士，没留下任何伤痕，但我们还是赶在巫师们造成更多伤害之前杀死了他们。

column1: Do you keep their thrumming implements?
column2: 你要保留他们的嗡嗡法器吗？

column1: With their strange implements, they slew some and wounded others.
column2: 用他们的奇怪器具，他们杀死了一些人，打伤了一些人。

column1: A stray mystic bolt thrown by one of the sorcerers destroyed\x01@\x01\x01@\x14.
column2: 一个巫师发出的一枚游荡秘术矢摧毁了\x01@\x01\x01@\x14。

column1: We drove them off, but at great cost.
column2: 我们击退了他们，但代价惨重。

column1: The sorcerers gave us a bow of thanks and left.
column2: 巫师们向我们鞠躬致谢后离开了。

column1: The sorcerers point their thrumming implements at you.
column2: 巫师们将他们的嗡嗡法器指向你。

column1: They threatened us with their sorcerous implements.
column2: 他们用巫术工具威胁我们。

column1: Wait and see.
column2: 等着瞧。

column1: Then one of them told the leader that we were telling the truth. They left without uttering another word.
column2: 然后其中一个告诉首领我们在说实话。他们没再多说一句就离开了。

column1: “It is none of your affair, barbarian trash,” their leader replied. “Consider yourself lucky that it is not you that we seek.”
column2: “这不关你的事，蛮族废物，”他们的首领回答，“算你走运，我们找的不是你。”

column1: They are rigidly devoted to their mission. No conciliation is possible here.
column2: 他们僵化地忠于自己的使命。这里不可能有任何和解。

column1: There are only three of them. What are we waiting for?
column2: 他们就三个人。我们还在等什么？

column1: They would not swagger in here so confidently if they had not the power to back up their bravado.
column2: 要是没有实力撑腰，他们怎敢如此嚣张地闯进来。

column1: They have come a long way to find our clansmen. Let them go back empty-handed.
column2: 他们远道而来寻找我们族人。让他们空手而归。

column1: They are sorcerers. They use a kind of magic that all good Orlanthi abhor.
column2: 他们是巫师。他们所用的魔法，是所有正直的奥兰斯人所憎恶的。

column1: They are sorcerers. They use a type of magic that all good Orlanthi abhor. Our magic is strong, so we must fight them.
column2: 他们是巫师。他们所用的魔法，是所有正直的奥兰斯人所憎恶的。我们的魔法强大，所以必须与他们战斗。

column1: They are sorcerers. They use a type of magic that all good Orlanthi abhor. Alas, our magic is weak, so we cannot fight them now.
column2: 他们是巫师。他们所用的魔法，是所有正直的奥兰斯人所憎恶的。可惜我们的魔法弱小，现在不能与他们战斗。

column1: When dealing with sorcerers, lying is always an option.
column2: 对付巫师，撒谎总是一个选项。

column1: These hounds of the Pharaoh are searching for our new clansmen!
column2: 这些法老的走狗正在寻找我们新加入的族人！

column1: Tell them what they want to know. It’s not as if they’re vampires.
column2: 告诉他们想知道的就是。又不是吸血鬼。

column1: Sorcerers are as bad as vampires, but they die easier.
column2: 巫师和吸血鬼一样坏，但更容易死。

column1: They’re going to kill us all!
column2: 他们会杀死我们所有人！

column1: Our magic is powerless against sorcery, we’re all going to die!
column2: 我们的魔法敌不过巫术，我们都要死了！

column1: I have a bad feeling about those strange objects they carry.
column2: 我对他们带的那些奇怪物件有种不祥的预感。

column1: The swimmer’s “Emptied” come sniffing for life-water. We should show them theirs.
column2: 游泳者的“空壳”来嗅生命之水了。我们该让他们见识一下自己的。

column1: Don’t betray our tribe mates. Kill these dogs of the Pharaoh.
column2: 不要背叛我们的族伴。杀掉这些法老的走狗。

column1: The sorcerers point their strange implements at you.
column2: 巫师们将他们怪异的器具指向了你。

column1: The sorcerers thanked us for the information, and left.
column2: 巫师们感谢我们提供的信息，然后离开了。

column1: Then one of them told the leader that we were lying.
column2: 然后其中一人告诉首领我们在撒谎。

column1: We attacked at the same moment that the leader cried to his men to attack us.
column2: 我们在首领命令手下攻击我们的同一瞬间发起了攻击。

column1: They attacked us.
column2: 他们攻击了我们。

column1: Do you keep their humming implements?
column2: 你们保留了它们嗡鸣的器具吗？

column1: Everyone rejoiced that we had killed the enemies of our new clansmen. We hoped that they would be the last of the Pharaoh’s lackeys who would dare to come to Dragon Pass.
column2: 所有人都为杀死了新族人敌人的胜利而欢欣。我们希望这是法老走狗最后一次胆敢踏足龙之隘口。

column1: We put the southerner’s strange objects in a safe place, though our god-talkers said that no good could come of them.
column2: 我们把南方人的怪异物件存放在安全处，尽管我们的神言者说它们不会带来任何好事。

column1: What are they doing?
column2: 他们在做什么？

column1: Hold steady, we can fool them still.
column2: 稳住，我们还能骗到他们。

column1: Hah, we can tell these sorcerors anything at all and they will fall for it.
column2: 哈，我们对这些巫师说什么他们都会上当。

column1: They’re not going to fall for it…
column2: 他们不会上当的…

column1: Those must be magical objects they’re pointing at us — bad magic!
column2: 他们指向我们的那些一定是魔法物件——坏魔法！

column1: The swimmer’s Emptied come sniffing for life-water. We should show them theirs.
column2: 游泳者的空壳来嗅生命之水了。我们该让他们见识一下自己的。

column1: Our tribe continued to be beset by bandits.
column2: 我们部落继续受到匪徒侵扰。

column1: Our tribe was beset by bandits.
column2: 我们部落遭到了匪徒侵扰。

column1: Find bandit leader and make a deal.
column2: 找到匪首，达成交易。

column1: We sought out the bandit leader, in order to make a deal with him.
column2: 我们寻到了匪首，为的是与他做一笔交易。

column1: How much are you prepared to give to him?
column2: 你准备给他多少？

column1: Do you ask other clans to do the same?
column2: 你是否要求其他氏族也这样做？

column1: The bandits were pleased by the offer we made them, and left for parts unknown.
column2: 匪徒对我们提出的条件很满意，便离开了，去向未知。

column1: The bandits said they could steal more from us than we were offering them as compensation.
column2: 匪徒说，他们能从我们这里偷到比我们提出的赔偿更多的钱。

column1: Find the bandit leader and threaten him.
column2: 找到匪首，威胁他。

column1: We found the bandit leader, and threatened him.
column2: 我们找到了匪首，并威胁了他。

column1: The bandits said that our poetry was crude and lacking in meter.
column2: 匪徒说我们的诗歌粗糙，缺乏韵律。

column1: Organize inter-clan patrols to fight the bandits.
column2: 组织氏族间巡逻队来打击匪徒。

column1: We decided to organize weaponthanes from our own and other clans of the tribe to fight the bandits.
column2: 我们决定从本氏族和部落其他氏族中组织武器领主来打击匪徒。

column1: The bandits were soundly defeated. Those who we did not slay on the spot fled like rippling squirrels, and were not seen again.
column2: 匪徒被彻底击败。未被当场格杀者如波浪般逃窜的松鼠，再不见踪影。

column1: The bandits ambushed our war party, inflicting heavy damage on the fleeing weaponthanes.
column2: 匪徒伏击了我们的队伍，给溃逃的武器领主造成重创。

column1: Do you ask other clans of the tribe to contribute to sacrifices?
column2: 你是否要求部落其他氏族为献祭出力？

column1: Our priests said that our sacrifices had not been well-received.
column2: 我们的祭司说，我们的献祭没有受到欢迎。

column1: How many warriors do you send to fight the bandits?
column2: 你派多少战士去打击匪徒？

column1: The bandits were soundly defeated. Those we did not slay on the spot fled like rippling squirrels, and were not seen again.
column2: 匪徒被彻底击败。未被当场格杀者如波浪般逃窜的松鼠，再不见踪影。

column1: Bargaining with bandits is \x02\x03giving chickens to the fox/a sign of how weak we think we are/doomed to fail\x02.
column2: 与匪徒议价就像是 \x02\x03给狐狸送鸡/暴露我们对自己的弱小认知/注定失败\x02。

column1: We will have to give the bandits at least \x01@\x1A cows; otherwise, they can make more by robbing us.
column2: 我们至少得给匪徒 \x01@\x1A 头牛；否则他们靠抢劫能得到更多。

column1: There are too many bandits, and they know the wild country too well. It will be hard to beat them.
column2: 匪徒太多，又对野外过于熟悉。很难击败他们。

column1: There are too many small, roving bands of bandits for one clan to slay them all. But each clan could slay the ones nearest it, and so defeat the horde.
column2: 匪徒的小股流窜队伍太多，单个氏族无法全部击杀。但每个氏族可以消灭最临近自己的那一伙，从而击败整个匪帮。

column1: We can smash the bandits, and they should know it.
column2: 我们能粉碎匪徒，他们理应清楚这点。

column1: Why haven’t we cleared out the forest yet? \x02\x03The fighters are eager to use these scoundrels for practice/The warriors look forward to an easy victory/The weaponthanes want these bandits for sword practice\x02.
column2: 为什么我们还没扫清森林？ \x02\x03战士们渴望拿这些恶棍练手/战士们期待一场轻松胜利/武器领主想用这些匪徒练剑\x02。

column1: The other clans will become restless if we cannot stop the banditry.
column2: 如果我们不能制止匪患，其他氏族会变得不安。

column1: If this keeps up, we face bandits outside and dissent within.
column2: 再这样下去，我们外有匪患，内有分歧。

column1: Which is worse? To lose goods by bandits, or lose grain by sending our farmers to war when they should be working the fields?
column2: 哪个更糟？被匪徒抢走财物，还是在本应下地干活时派农夫去打仗而损失粮食？

column1: When Gagarth stole from Orlanth, Orlanth did not wait to act.
column2: 当加加斯偷了奥兰斯的东西，奥兰斯没有坐视不管。

column1: The chronicles often tell of clans who act swiftly and well on behalf of their tribe, yet incur only rancor from their kings.
column2: 编年史常记载那些为部落迅速妥善行动，却只招来国王怨恨的氏族。

column1: How were we to know that being the royal clan was so difficult?
column2: 我们怎么知道成为王族竟如此艰难？

column1: Emboldened by crown-tarnish, the bounty-thieves night-crept.
column2: 因王冠蒙尘而胆大妄为，劫匪们趁夜潜行。

column1: Gold-hunters roam when gold-dispenser sleeps.
column2: 赏金猎人游荡于散金者沉睡之时。

column1: “There is no victory without a good woman’s arms to return to.”
column2: “没有好女人的怀抱可归，便无胜利可言。”

column1: “Do not \x02\x03offer your finger to the wasp/wake the bear by pulling brambles from its fur/make a roar without teeth to back it\x02.”
column2: “不要 \x02\x03把手指伸给黄蜂/从熊毛里拔荆棘而惊醒熊/在没有牙齿支撑时发出怒吼\x02。”

column1: Crush the thieving swine!
column2: 碾碎这些偷窃的猪猡！

column1: We will need everyone’s swords to cut down these weeds — it is time to get rid of these vermin once and for all!
column2: 我们需要所有人的剑来砍倒这些杂草——是时候彻底铲除这些害虫了！

column1: We must take arms against these bandits \x02\x03again and again/over and over/as often as we must\x02, and wipe their stain from the forest for good.
column2: 我们必须拿起武器对抗这些匪徒 \x02\x03一次又一次/反复/尽其所能\x02，永远洗去他们在森林中的污迹。

column1: Issaries will help us.
column2: 伊萨里斯会帮助我们。

column1: If we ignore these bandits now, they will breed like trollkin and make us poorer.
column2: 如果我们现在忽视这些匪徒，他们会像小巨魔一样繁殖，让我们更穷。

column1: Why should Issaries listen to our pleas, when we bungle in our own tactics against the bandits?
column2: 当我们自己对匪徒的战术都搞砸时，伊萨里斯凭什么听我们的祈求？

column1: Two spirit-talkers seek audience with the ring to see if you have any need of their services. Spirit-talkers are Orlanthi, but they wander around in the wilderness, with ties to no single clan. Their magic is a little different from the kind you’re used to; they deal with spirits, not gods. They are Strangers, meaning that they are not of your clan, but can be trusted to follow normal customs and beliefs.
column2: 两名灵语者求见长老会，询问你是否需要他们的服务。灵语者是奥兰斯人，但他们在荒野中游荡，不与任何单一氏族绑定。他们的魔法与你习惯的略有不同；他们与灵打交道，而非神祇。他们是陌生人，意味着不属于你的氏族，但可以信任他们会遵循通常的习俗和信仰。

column1: Spirit-talkers showed up and asked if we needed anything from them.
column2: 灵语者出现，问我们是否需要他们做什么。

column1: “Begone! You are strange and weird!”
column2: “滚开！你们古怪又诡异！”

column1: The older spirit-talker said, “The strangest thing you will see is in a reflecting pool.”
column2: 年长的灵语者说：“你会在倒影池中见到最奇怪的东西。”

column1: “Heal our wounded.”
column2: “治愈我们的伤者。”

column1: We asked them to heal our wounded.
column2: 我们请求他们治愈我们的伤者。

column1: The older spirit-talker shakes his rattle, tastes the air, and says, “Hrm. The healing spirits seem to be pleased this day. The healing will cost you \x01@\x1A cows worth of silver.”
column2: 年长的灵语者摇晃着响板，品尝空气，说道：“嗯。治愈之灵今天似乎很高兴。治疗将花费你价值 \x01@\x1A 头牛的银子。”

column1: “Protect us from the undead.”
column2: “保护我们免受亡灵侵袭。”

column1: We asked them for protection from the undead.
column2: 我们请求他们提供对抗亡灵的保护。

column1: The older spirit-talker shakes his rattle, tastes the air, and says, “That will cost you \x01@\x19 cows worth of silver.”
column2: 年长的灵语者摇晃着响板，品尝空气，说道：“那将花费你价值 \x01@\x19 头牛的银子。”

column1: They danced around, shook their rattles, and went into convulsions. Several hours later, they told us that we were now safe from undead.
column2: 他们四处跳舞，摇晃响板，陷入抽搐。几小时后，他们告诉我们，我们现在已不受亡灵威胁。

column1: “Sell us a Spirit Fetch or two.”
column2: “卖给我们一两个精魂护符。”

column1: We asked them to sell us Spirit Fetches.
column2: 我们请求他们卖给我们精魂护符。

column1: We changed our minds when we learned how high the price was.
column2: 当我们得知价格有多高时，我们改变了主意。

column1: The older spirit-talker rummages about in his bag, and withdraws a number of small fetishes made from twigs, grass, stones and animal hide. “I have \x01@\x14 fetishes I can spare, and will charge you only 15 cows worth of silver for each one.”
column2: 年长的灵语者在他的袋子里翻找，取出若干用树枝、草、石块和兽皮制成的小护符。“我有 \x01@\x14 个可以匀出的护符，每个只收你价值15头牛的银子。”

column1: The older spirit-talker rummages about in his bag, and withdraws a small fetish made from twigs, grass, stones and animal hide. “I have 1 fetish I can spare, and will charge you only 15 cows worth of silver for it.”
column2: 年长的灵语者在他的袋子里翻找，取出一个用树枝、草、石块和兽皮制成的小护符。“我有一个可以匀出的护符，只收你价值15头牛的银子。”

column1: How many fetishes do you want?
column2: 你想要多少个护符？

column1: We added the Spirit Fetch to our treasures.
column2: 我们将精魂护符加入我们的宝库。

column1: We added the Spirit Fetches to our treasures.
column2: 我们将精魂护符们加入我们的宝库。

column1: “We need no spirit-talking, but we shall feed you.”
column2: “我们不需要灵语，但我们会款待你们。”

column1: We did not want anything from them, but gave them hospitality.
column2: 我们并不想从他们那里得到什么，但还是给予了他们好客款待。

column1: The old one told us we would be rewarded for our generosity.
column2: 那位老人告诉我们，我们的慷慨将得到回报。

column1: We can certainly afford to pay them for their services.
column2: 我们当然付得起他们的服务费。

column1: We can’t afford to pay them.
column2: 我们付不起他们的费用。

column1: They are not quite like normal people, and not quite foreigners.
column2: 他们既不完全像普通人，也不完全是异乡人。

column1: They are not quite like normal people, and not quite foreigners. We still owe them courtesy and hospitality.
column2: 他们既不完全像普通人，也不完全是异乡人。我们仍应对他们保持礼貌和好客。

column1: They are sorcerers! Cast them out!
column2: 他们是巫师！把他们赶出去！

column1: Spirit-talkers aren’t sorcerers or anything bad like that. They talk to spirits, including our own ancestor spirits.
column2: 灵语者不是巫师或任何那样的坏东西。他们与灵交谈，包括我们自己的祖先之灵。

column1: A Spirit Fetch is a magical item that replenishes our magic after we use it up.
column2: 精魂护符是一种魔法物品，可以在我们用尽魔力后补充我们的魔法。

column1: We are threatened by undead, and can use their help.
column2: 我们受到亡灵的威胁，可以利用他们的帮助。

column1: I can certainly use help in healing our many wounded.
column2: 我当然需要帮助来治愈我们众多的伤者。

column1: Spirit-talkers have awesome powers, since they can call on a vast array of spirits. We can’t risk offending them.
column2: 灵语者拥有令人敬畏的力量，因为他们能召唤大量的灵。我们不能冒犯他们的风险。

column1: Spirits are worthy of reverence, just as gods are. Gods are greater than spirits, that is all.
column2: 灵值得敬畏，正如神祇一样。神比灵更伟大，仅此而已。

column1: Even if they weren’t planning to fleece us — which they are — we can’t afford their outrageous prices.
column2: 即使他们没有打算宰我们（事实上他们就是），我们也付不起他们离谱的价格。

column1: You don’t suppose they can contact dragon spirits, do you?
column2: 你不会认为他们能联系龙灵吧？

column1: These mangy tomcats aren’t worthy of our time, much less our silver.
column2: 这些肮脏的公猫不值得我们的时间，更不用说我们的银子了。

column1: Spirits shook the Moss-Soles as wind rattles a roof.
column2: 灵撼动着苔藓脚族，如同风摇响屋顶。

column1: Your explorers return to report an encounter with very strange foreigners. The foreigners wore odd clothes and spoke in a peculiar way. They were warriors, and showed no fear when they met our explorers. They identified themselves as the Black Horse Troop, and said they served a hero named Sir Ethilrist. The strangest thing about them, though was their horses. Examined up close, these weren’t horses at all, but grotesque and monstrous beasts — possibly things of Chaos!
column2: 你们的探索者归来报告，遇到了一群非常奇怪的异乡人。他们穿着古怪的衣物，说话方式奇特。他们是战士，见到我们的探索者时毫无惧色。他们自称是黑马部队，效忠于一位名叫埃瑟里斯特爵士的英雄。最奇怪的是他们的坐骑。凑近细看，那根本不是马，而是狰狞可怖的怪兽——或许是混沌之物！

column1: Our explorers met foreign warriors who rode on monsters shaped like horses.
column2: 我们的探索者遇到了骑着形似马匹的怪兽的异乡战士。

column1: Invite them to your tula.
column2: 邀请他们来你的领地。

column1: We sought them out, and invited them to our tula.
column2: 我们找到了他们，邀请他们来我们的领地。

column1: Sir Ethilrist’s men seemed surprised and amused by our offer of hospitality, and promised to take us up on it, one day.
column2: 埃瑟里斯特爵士的手下对我们提供的好客之举既惊讶又觉得有趣，并承诺有朝一日会来接受款待。

column1: Leave well enough alone.
column2: 不惹事为好。

column1: Make war on them.
column2: 向他们开战。

column1: We organized a war party to fight them.
column2: 我们组织了一支战队去讨伐他们。

column1: Do you send:
column2: 你派出的是：

column1: A large force from your clan only.
column2: 仅由你部族派出的大军。

column1: A large force from all clans.
column2: 由所有部族派出的大军。

column1: The Black Horse Troop proved to be a terrible foe. There were many of them. They were very skilled, and their magic was strong. Still, we drove them back, though the cost was high. We lost \x01@\x14 and many warriors.
column2: 黑马部队原来是一支可怕的敌人。他们人数众多，技艺高超，魔法强大。即便如此，我们还是击退了他们，但代价高昂。我们损失了 \x01@\x14 和许多战士。

column1: The Black Horse Troop proved to be a terrible foe. There were many of them. They were very skilled, and their magic was strong. They smashed us utterly. We lost \x01@\x14 and many warriors.
column2: 黑马部队原来是一支可怕的敌人。他们人数众多，技艺高超，魔法强大。他们彻底击溃了我们。我们损失了 \x01@\x14 和许多战士。

column1: See if they wish to trade treasures.
column2: 看看他们是否愿意交易宝物。

column1: We sought them out, and asked if they wanted to trade treasures.
column2: 我们找到他们，询问是否愿意交易宝物。

column1: They agree to trade with you, in the name of friendship between the troop and your people.
column2: 他们同意与你交易，以表示部队与你部族之间的友谊。

column1: They offer you your choice of the following:
column2: 他们提供以下物品供你选择：

column1: The Bit of Kargzant
column2: 卡格赞特马嚼

column1: The Silver Lips of Anriar
column2: 安里亚银唇

column1: We were pleased to have established good relations with strangers who had such powerful magic.
column2: 我们很高兴能与如此强大的异乡人建立良好关系。

column1: They responded angrily to our offer
column2: 他们对我们的出价愤怒回应

column1: of a Spirit Fetch. “We do not need this useless shamanic trash!” they exclaimed.
column2: 灵魂唤引。“我们不需要这无用的萨满垃圾！”他们喊道。

column1: of our Dragon Cart. “We do not need this broken down piece of trash!” they exclaimed.
column2: 我们的龙车。“我们不需要这破铜烂铁！”他们喊道。

column1: of Dwarf Food. “We do not need this worthless stuff!” they exclaimed.
column2: 矮人食品。“我们不需要这毫无价值的东西！”他们喊道。

column1: They responded angrily to our offer. “We do not need this insulting, useless trash!” they exclaimed.
column2: 他们对我们的出价愤怒回应。“我们不需要这侮辱人的无用垃圾！”他们喊道。

column1: We left without making a trade.
column2: 我们没做成交易就离开了。

column1: They did not, but thanked us (in an odd, foreign way) for asking.
column2: 他们没有，但用一种古怪的异乡方式感谢我们的询问。

column1: Warn other clans about them.
column2: 向其他部族警告他们。

column1: We warned other clans about them.
column2: 我们向其他部族警告了他们。

column1: They thanked us for the warning.
column2: 他们感谢我们的警告。

column1: Few believed our story.
column2: 几乎没人相信我们的话。

column1: No foreigner can withstand the onslaught of Orlanthi warriors, pure-hearted and true.
column2: 没有异乡人能抵挡奥尔兰赛战士的冲击，他们心地纯洁、信念坚定。

column1: Our tribe is strong. Working together, we can defeat anyone.
column2: 我们的部族很强大。团结一致，我们能击败任何人。

column1: As newcomers to our lands, we owe them hospitality.
column2: 作为新来我们土地的人，我们理应对他们好客。

column1: We owe these foreigners nothing.
column2: 我们什么都不欠这些异乡人。

column1: Although we could stand to improve our relations with our neighbors, they may be skeptical of our warnings.
column2: 尽管我们可以改善与邻居的关系，但他们可能对我们的警告持怀疑态度。

column1: We will cement our good relations with our neighbors by warning them of this potential menace.
column2: 我们将通过警告邻居这个潜在威胁来巩固友好关系。

column1: We’d be mad to attack this group in any season — and reckless to attack them in Sea season, when we would be better off planting.
column2: 在任何季节攻击这群人都是疯了——尤其在海季攻击更是鲁莽，那时我们本该播种。

column1: We’d be mad to attack this group — and reckless to attack them in Earth season, when we would be better off reaping.
column2: 攻击这群人是疯了——在地季攻击更是鲁莽，那时我们本该收获。

column1: He who chases the wolf before it howls feels its bite.
column2: 在狼嚎之前就追上去的人，会尝到被咬的滋味。

column1: If they are powerful foreigners, they may have treasures the like of which we have never seen!
column2: 如果他们是有势力的异乡人，可能拥有我们从未见过的珍宝！

column1: Foreigners will know new jokes; I am tired of the old ones. Especially the one about Eurmal and the sheep.
column2: 异乡人应该知道些新笑话；老笑话我都听腻了。尤其是那个关于尤尔马尔和羊的。

column1: Save our strength for fighting zombies.
column2: 把力气留着打僵尸。

column1: Foreigners are ignorant and easy to cheat.
column2: 异乡人愚昧无知，容易欺骗。

column1: By making war for no reason, we risk the integrity of the throne.
column2: 无缘无故开战，我们会危及王座的完整。

column1: If these prove to be the terrible enemies we think they are, we could win respect by defeating them alone.
column2: 如果这群人真是我们想的那种可怕敌人，独自击败他们就能赢得尊敬。

column1: While exploring in the mountains to the northwest, your people find a disused mine shaft. A hunch made \x01@I take them a long way into it. As they descended into its depths, they heard sounds. Before proceeding much further, they decided to come back home for advice.
column2: 在西北方的山脉中探索时，你们的人发现了一个废弃矿井。一个直觉让 \x01@I 带他们深入其中。当他们下到深处时，听到了声响。在继续深入之前，他们决定回家寻求建议。

column1: While exploring around that bizarre statue-covered mountain, your people find a disused mine shaft. A hunch made \x01@I take them a long way into it. As they descended into its depths, they heard sounds. Before proceeding much further, they decided to come back home for advice.
column2: 在探索那座遍布怪异雕像的山时，你们的人发现了一个废弃矿井。一个直觉让 \x01@I 带他们深入其中。当他们下到深处时，听到了声响。在继续深入之前，他们决定回家寻求建议。

column1: Our explorers found an old mine in the mountains. When they went deep into it, they heard sounds and returned home to tell us.
column2: 我们的探索者在山中找到一个旧矿井。当他们深入其中时，听到了声响，便回家告诉我们。

column1: Investigate the sounds.
column2: 调查那些声响。

column1: We decided to find out what the sounds were.
column2: 我们决定查明那些声响是什么。

column1: Who leads the exploration party?
column2: 谁率领探索队伍？

column1: Perform a divination ritual.
column2: 进行占卜仪式。

column1: We performed a divination ritual.
column2: 我们进行了占卜仪式。

column1: The Knowing God told our priests and priestesses that the sounds were made by dwarfs, and pale people who act like dwarfs. The dwarfs are everyone’s enemies, because they want not only to stop everything from changing, but to go back to the days before Orlanth’s father Umath made a place for himself in the world.
column2: 全知之神告诉我们的男女祭司，那些声响是矮人和一些行为像矮人的苍白之人发出的。矮人是一切人的敌人，因为他们不仅想阻止一切变化，还想回到奥尔兰特的父亲乌玛斯在世上为自己开辟领地之前的时代。

column1: The Knowing God told our priests and priestesses that the sounds were made by \x02\x06voracious trolls/cruel beastfolk/bug-like Chaos creatures/smoke people/wind spirits/an underground river\x02.
column2: 全知之神告诉我们祭司们，那些声响是由 \x02\x06贪婪的巨魔/残暴的兽人/虫样的混沌生物/烟雾人/风灵/地下河\x02发出的。

column1: If we went there, the result would be \x02\x06disaster/good magic/boredom/bad magic/a paradoxical discovery/great good fortune\x02.
column2: 如果我们去了那里，结果将是 \x02\x06灾难/好魔法/无聊/坏魔法/一个矛盾的发现/巨大的好运\x02。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods for protection from underground mysteries.
column2: 向众神献祭，以求庇护免受地下奥秘之害。

column1: We elected to sacrifice to the gods for protection from underground mysteries.
column2: 我们选择向众神献祭，以求庇护免受地下奥秘之害。

column1: Which god do you sacrifice to?
column2: 你向哪位神献祭？

column1: The god-talkers thought that the gods had not heard us. Some of the people said that we were fools to sacrifice every time we found a hole in the ground.
column2: 神言者们认为众神没有听到我们的祈求。有些人说我们每在地上发现一个洞就献祭，真是愚蠢。

column1: Sell the information to another clan.
column2: 将情报卖给另一个氏族。

column1: We decided to sell the information to another clan.
column2: 我们决定将情报卖给另一个氏族。

column1: Which clan do you sell it to?
column2: 你把它卖给哪个氏族？

column1: Stay away.
column2: 远离。

column1: We decided to stay away from it.
column2: 我们决定远离它。

column1: Why would anyone want to pay for such vague information?
column2: 为什么会有人愿意为这样含糊的情报付钱？

column1: We could get a couple of cows for this information.
column2: 我们能用这情报换来几头牛。

column1: We could get four cows for this information.
column2: 我们能用这情报换来四头牛。

column1: We could get six cows for this information.
column2: 我们能用这情报换来六头牛。

column1: How can we estimate the risk, when we don’t know what sorts of things are lurking in the mine?
column2: 当我们不知道矿井里潜伏着什么时，我们怎么估计风险？

column1: If we share this information with another clan, they might like us a little better.
column2: 如果我们与另一个氏族分享这情报，他们也许会稍微喜欢我们一点。

column1: It is a good day to perform a divination.
column2: 今天是进行占卜的好日子。

column1: There are many malign spirits about these days. If we perform a divination, they might pose as the Knowing God and give us bad information.
column2: 近日有许多恶灵出没。如果我们进行占卜，它们可能假扮全知之神，给我们错误的信息。

column1: Ah sure, send a large party of our farmers off during Sea season. Then wonder where the food is, come harvest time.
column2: 啊，当然啦，在海季派出一大群农夫。然后到收获时，才纳闷食物在哪。

column1: Ah sure, send a large party of our farmers off during Earth season. Then wonder why the grain-sacks hang limp in Dark time.
column2: 啊，当然啦，在地季派出一大群农夫。然后到暗季，才纳闷为什么粮袋瘪着。

column1: I’ll go!
column2: 我去！

column1: Both the trolls and the dwarfs live in the earth.
column2: 巨魔和矮人都住在地下。

column1: We must perform a divination ritual before proceeding further.
column2: 在继续前进之前，我们必须举行一次占卜仪式。

column1: Curiosity is like an alynx. If you do not scratch it under the chin, it will claw you.
column2: 好奇心就像一只獭猫。如果你不挠它下巴，它就会抓你。

column1: There could be Chaos in need of smiting down there.
column2: 下面可能有混沌需要诛灭。

column1: Sounds beneath the earth? How intriguing!
column2: 地底下的声响？多么引人入胜啊！

column1: Gods protect us from this awful news!
column2: 诸神保佑我们免受这可怕消息的困扰！

column1: I told you that exploring never gets us anything — except more stupid questions!
column2: 我告诉过你，探索从不会给我们带来什么——除了更多愚蠢的问题！

column1: \x01CK, an accomplished holy warrior of Elmal, comes to your clan looking for your aid in a great heroquest. “Our people are cursed by fighting and dissension. Hendriki fight Heortlanders. People in Dragon Pass squabble. Differences are more important than similarities. I wish to go to the realm of the gods, so that Orlanth may fight me. Then people will be loyal and united again. I need your magic to help me.”
column2: \x01CK一位艾尔玛的成就神圣武士，来到你的氏族，寻求你在一次伟大英雄任务中的帮助。“我们的族人被争斗与分歧所诅咒。亨德里基人攻打赫奥特兰人。龙隘的人们争吵不休。差异比相似更重要。我希望前往神域，让奥兰斯与我战斗。这样人们才能再次忠诚团结。我需要你的魔法来帮助我。”

column1: The Elmali holy warrior \x01CK approached us, seeking our support for his heroquest.
column2: 艾尔玛的神圣武士 \x01CK 来到我们面前，寻求我们对他英雄任务的支持。

column1: Do as \x01CK asks.
column2: 按照 \x01CK 的要求去做。

column1: We did as he asked, and lent our ritual support to his quest.
column2: 我们如他所愿，为他的任务提供了仪式上的支持。

column1: Recruit other clans to share the magical burden of support.
column2: 招募其他氏族分担支持所需的魔法负担。

column1: \x01CK was pleased; he said that we spared him the necessity of approaching other clans, too.
column2: \x01CK 感到满意；他说我们让他免除了还得去找其他氏族的必要。

column1: The other clans refused us. \x01CK departed, swearing gore-spattered vengeance on the cowards in Dragon Pass who did not understand the need for unity between Orlanthi.
column2: 其他氏族拒绝了我们。 \x01CK 离开了，发誓要对龙隘那些不理解奥兰蒂之间需要团结的懦夫施加血溅复仇。

column1: “We cannot help you, our magic is weak.”
column2: “我们无法帮助你，我们的魔法很弱。”

column1: We refused him, because our magic was weak.
column2: 我们拒绝了他，因为我们的魔法很弱。

column1: \x01CK flew into a rage, claiming we were liars.
column2: \x01CK 勃然大怒，声称我们是骗子。

column1: \x01CK flew into a rage. “You lie! Your magic is strong. I can feel it like metal on the back of my tongue! You have the magic, yet you will not give it to me! No one will give it to me!”
column2: \x01CK 勃然大怒。“你撒谎！你们的魔法很强。我能感觉到，就像舌尖上的金属味！你们有魔法，却不愿给我！谁也不愿意给我！”

column1: He picked up \x01@\x10 and threw \x08 through the clan hall wall. Swearing gore-spattered vengeance on the cowards of Dragon Pass who did not understand the need for unity between Orlanthi, he departed.
column2: 他捡起 \x01@\x10 并将 \x08 扔穿了部族大厅的墙壁。他离开了，发誓要对龙隘那些不理解奥兰蒂之间需要团结的懦夫施加血溅复仇。

column1: We did not pursue him; even though he was too crazy to follow the hospitality rules, we were better than that.
column2: 我们没有追赶他；尽管他疯到不遵守好客规则，但我们比那更好。

column1: \x01CK flew into a rage, insulting our magic and leaving without enjoying our hospitality.
column2: \x01CK 勃然大怒，侮辱我们的魔法，没有享受我们的款待就离开了。

column1: \x01CK flew into a rage. “You stinking Dragon Pass folk are all alike! Boastful and proud, yet without a piss-pot’s worth of magic between the lot of you!” He stalked out of the hall without touching the lavish meal we had prepared for him.
column2: \x01CK 勃然大怒。“你们这些臭龙隘人都是一个德行！吹嘘又傲慢，可你们所有人加在一起连一尿壶的魔法都不值！”他大步走出大厅，碰都没碰我们为他准备的丰盛餐食。

column1: “We cannot help you; it is too risky.”
column2: “我们无法帮助你；这太冒险了。”

column1: “Your idea is foolish, \x01CK.”
column2: “你的想法很愚蠢， \x01CK。”

column1: Our fertility will remain strong no matter what you choose to do.
column2: 无论你选择做什么，我们的丰饶将保持强盛。

column1: Although the people he seeks to unite are all Orlanthi, there are great differences between them.
column2: 尽管他试图团结的人都是奥兰蒂，但他们之间存在着巨大的差异。

column1: Although the people he seeks to unite are all Orlanthi, there are great differences between them. I do not think even a heroquest can succeed here.
column2: 尽管他试图团结的人都是奥兰蒂，但他们之间存在着巨大的差异。我认为即使是一次英雄任务也不可能在这里成功。

column1: If we enlist our neighbors and \x01CK succeeds, they will be grateful. If he fails, they will blame us for involving them.
column2: 如果我们招募邻居们，而 \x01CK 成功了，他们会感激我们。如果他失败了，他们会因为我们将他们卷入而责怪我们。

column1: Our popularity is such that our neighbors would sooner follow the advice of a one-legged hop-toad.
column2: 我们的声望高到邻居们宁愿听一只独腿蟾蜍的话。

column1: Our popularity is enough to overcome any doubts or misgivings our neighbors hold.
column2: 我们的声望足以消除邻居们的任何怀疑或顾虑。

column1: Our magic is strong. We can help him.
column2: 我们的魔法很强大。我们可以帮他。

column1: Our magic is weak. We would only hinder him.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱。我们只会拖累他。

column1: If helping \x01CK robs us of our fertility for the year, we have enough stored food to get by.
column2: 如果帮助 \x01CK 让我们失去当年的丰饶，我们还有足够的存粮撑过去。

column1: If helping \x01CK robs us of our fertility for the year, we will starve.
column2: 如果帮助 \x01CK 让我们失去当年的丰饶，我们会饿死。

column1: Supporting a heroquest is like joining a war; one must balance the possibility of great reward with the certainty of great risk.
column2: 支持英雄任务如同参战；必须在巨大回报的可能与巨大风险的确凿之间权衡。

column1: He is a great hero! We must support him.
column2: 他是个大英雄！我们必须支持他。

column1: Isn’t the main Elmali heroquest about getting the dung kicked out of you?
column2: 埃尔马利的主要英雄任务不就是让人揍得屁滚尿流吗？

column1: You can see the chronicle of his wondrous adventures written on his flesh!
column2: 你能看到他身上刻写的奇妙冒险编年史！

column1: If we don’t help him, he might get violent.
column2: 如果我们不帮他，他可能会动粗。

column1: It is a sacred duty to help heroes meet gods.
column2: 帮助英雄面见神祇是神圣的职责。

column1: He’s come all this way. It would be wrong to refuse him.
column2: 他一路跋涉而来。拒绝他是不对的。

column1: \x01CK has quite a temper. I doubt he will be able to reconcile anyone.
column2: \x01CK 脾气很暴躁。我怀疑他能否调和任何人。

column1: \x01CK has not come back from his heroquest. We must assume he was destroyed in the realm of the gods. This is bad news for us all; the magic we gave him is lost forever, and can’t be used to fatten our livestock or protect our crops.
column2: \x01CK 他还没有从英雄任务中回来。我们必须假定他已在神域被毁灭。这对我们所有人都是坏消息；我们给他的魔法永远失去了，无法用来养肥牲畜或保护庄稼。

column2: sceneR116

column1: While on an exploration and trade mission north of our tula, your people are approached by a trio of dwarfs who wish to trade with Orlanthi clans. Referring to their leader, they say, “Isidilian say we not yet reached schedule point where unauthorized may trade with outsider humans. But we individuals with own souls, not just parts of machine. We wish prove such, and enter trade immediately.” Your explorers come back to ask what to do.
column2: 在我们的领地以北执行探索和贸易任务时，你们的人遇到三个想与奥兰斯氏族贸易的矮人。他们指着首领说：“伊西迪利安说我们尚未到达允许未授权者与外界人类贸易的计划节点。但我们是有自己的灵魂的个体，不只是机器零件。我们希望证明这一点，并立即开始贸易。”你们的探索者回来请示该怎么做。

column1: Dwarfs of Dwarf Mine wanted to trade with us, even though their leader did not want them to.
column2: 矮人矿井的矮人想和我们贸易，尽管他们的首领不让他们这么做。

column1: Do not go back to meet them.
column2: 不要回去见他们。

column1: We gave up the chance to meet them again.
column2: 我们放弃了再次见他们的机会。

column1: Report them to Isidilian’s functionaries.
column2: 向伊西迪利安的官吏举报他们。

column1: We went to Dwarf Mine to report them to Isidilian’s functionaries.
column2: 我们去了矮人矿井，向伊西迪利安的官吏举报他们。

column1: “Is good you respect schedule,” they said. “Broken daughters recycled, affirmative affirmative. In exchange for service, us grant silver.”
column2: “你们尊重计划是好事，”他们说，“损坏的女儿们已回收，确认确认。作为服务交换，我们赐予白银。”

column1: Suggest another clan they might trade with.
column2: 建议另一个他们可以贸易的氏族。

column1: “Thank all. Seek smooth functioning,” the dwarf replied.
column2: “感谢所有。追求顺畅运作，”矮人回答。

column1: Trade normal goods with them.
column2: 与他们交易普通货物。

column1: We decided to trade normal goods with them.
column2: 我们决定与他们交易普通货物。

column1: Who leads the trading party?
column2: 谁带领贸易队？

column1: How many warriors do you send to guard \x01@\x05?
column2: 你派多少战士护卫 \x01@\x05？

column1: “We wish trade dwarf food for good things,” they say.
column2: “我们想用矮人食品换好东西，”他们说。

column1: What quantity of trade goods do you want to exchange for dwarf food?
column2: 你想用多少数量的贸易货物交换矮人食品？

column1: We gained a number of round metal cylinders containing what the dwarfs said was food. When our trading party tried to trade it to another clan on the way home, they were laughed at. “Who wants dwarf food?” the other traders said. “How do you even get it open?” We came home and put the cylinders away. \x01@\x14 finally smashed the containers open, and said the food tasted like dry leaves and sand.
column2: 我们获得了一些圆柱形金属罐，里面装着矮人所说的食物。当我们的贸易队在回家路上试图将其卖给另一个氏族时，他们遭到了嘲笑。“谁要矮人食品？”其他商人说，“你们怎么打开它？”我们回到家，把罐子收了起来。 \x01@\x14 终于砸开了容器，说食物尝起来像干树叶和沙子。

column1: In the middle of the transaction, the traders were attacked by other dwarfs.
column2: 交易进行中，商人们遭到其他矮人攻击。

column1: In the middle of the transaction, the renegade traders are attacked by other dwarfs.
column2: 交易进行中，叛逃的商人们遭到其他矮人攻击。

column1: Flee.
column2: 逃跑。

column1: We ran away, and lost the goods we had laid out for their inspection.
column2: 我们逃跑了，损失了摆出来给他们检查的货物。

column1: Try to recover the goods you’ve given the traders.
column2: 试图找回你已交给商人的货物。

column1: We tried to recover the goods we had laid out for their inspection. One of our warriors was hit by a strange missile fired by the dwarf enemies. We fled without the goods.
column2: 我们试图找回摆出来给他们检查的货物。我们的一名战士被矮人敌人发射的奇怪投掷物击中。我们空手逃走了。

column1: Fight the other dwarfs.
column2: 与那些矮人战斗。

column1: We fought back against the attackers.
column2: 我们对攻击者进行了反击。

column1: We drove them back, and concluded the deal. We gained a number of round metal cylinders containing what the dwarfs said was food. When our trading party tried to trade it to another clan on the way home, they were laughed at. “Who wants dwarf food?” the other traders said. “How do you even get it open?” We came home and put the cylinders away. \x01@\x14 finally smashed the containers open, and said the food tasted like dry leaves and sand.
column2: 我们击退了他们，完成了交易。我们获得了一些圆柱形金属罐，里面装着矮人所说的食物。当我们的贸易队在回家路上试图将其卖给另一个氏族时，他们遭到了嘲笑。“谁要矮人食品？”其他商人说，“你们怎么打开它？”我们回到家，把罐子收了起来。 \x01@\x14 终于砸开了容器，说食物尝起来像干树叶和沙子。

column1: They felled almost the entire trading party. Only \x01@\x05 escaped to tell the tale.
column2: 他们几乎杀光了整个贸易队。只有 \x01@\x05 逃回来讲述经过。

column1: Trade treasures with them.
column2: 与他们交易宝物。

column1: We decided we would trade treasures with them.
column2: 我们决定与他们交易宝物。

column1: Which treasure do you trade?
column2: 你交易哪件宝物？

column1: They gave us a treasure they called the Magnet of Mostal. They said that it would even things out, so that everything would be predictable and good.
column2: 他们给了我们一件宝物，称为莫斯塔尔磁铁。他们说这能平衡一切，让所有事物都可预测且良好。

column1: We ran away, and lost the treasure we had laid out for their inspection.
column2: 我们逃跑了，损失了摆出来给他们检查的宝物。

column1: We tried to recover the treasure we had laid out for their inspection. One of our warriors was hit by a strange missile fired by the dwarf enemies. We fled without the treasure.
column2: 我们试图找回摆出来给他们检查的宝物。我们的一名战士被矮人敌人发射的奇怪投掷物击中。我们空手逃走了。

column1: We drove them back, and concluded the deal. They gave us a treasure they called the Magnet of Mostal. They said that it would even things out, so that everything would be predictable and good.
column2: 我们击退了他们，并达成了交易。他们给了我们一件名为“莫斯塔尔磁铁”的宝物。他们说这能让一切平衡，使万物变得可预测且美好。

column1: There is no danger here. They want to be individuals, like us.
column2: 这里没有危险。他们想成为像我们一样的个体。

column1: Who knows what wondrous goods these strange beings might have to offer?
column2: 谁知道这些奇怪的家伙可能带来什么奇妙的货物？

column1: Better stick to trading treasures. Who knows what these strange beings consider valuable?
column2: 最好还是交易宝物。谁知道这些奇怪的生物觉得什么有价值？

column1: They are breaking the laws of their people, but their laws mean nothing to us.
column2: 他们在触犯自己族人的律法，但他们的律法对我们毫无意义。

column1: They are breaking the laws of their people, and we must assume that they will be harshly punished if caught.
column2: 他们在触犯自己族人的律法，我们必须假设一旦被抓，他们会被严惩。

column1: We could gain the favor of a powerful foreign king by reporting them to Isidilian.
column2: 我们可以向伊西迪利安告发他们，从而赢得一位强大异族国王的恩惠。

column1: We could gain the favor of a powerful foreign king by reporting them to Isidilian. Or of another clan, by giving them an opportunity.
column2: 我们可以向伊西迪利安告发他们，从而赢得一位强大异族国王的恩惠。或者给他们一个机会，赢得另一个氏族的恩惠。

column1: The omens are good.
column2: 征兆吉利。

column1: The omens are bad.
column2: 征兆凶险。

column1: Whatever you do, don’t trade for dwarf food. Legend has it that their food is inedible, and stored in jars no one but the dwarfs can open.
column2: 不管你做什么，千万别交易矮人食品。传说他们的食物难以下咽，而且装在只有矮人才能打开的罐子里。

column1: It is all a plot to kill and eat us.
column2: 这一切都是个阴谋，要杀死并吃掉我们。

column1: Dwarfs hate elves. We must curry favor with Isidilian.
column2: 矮人憎恨精灵。我们必须讨好伊西迪利安。

column1: The \x01@! clan is strong in the worship of the gods. Let them take this opportunity.
column2: \x01@! 氏族在敬奉神明方面力量强大。让他们抓住这个机会。

column1: Why do we always have to deal with weird little non-humans who try to act like people? They should be glad we don’t just take their ridiculous toys.
column2: 为什么我们总要跟那些试图装得像人的古怪小个子非人类打交道？他们该庆幸我们没直接抢走他们那些可笑的玩具。

column1: What a chance for adventure!
column2: 多好的冒险机会啊！

column1: Trading as a proof of having souls? If only that were all that was required, we could all be certain.
column2: 以交易来证明拥有灵魂？要是只需要这样就能确定，那我们都能肯定了。

column1: Why not?
column2: 为什么不呢？

column1: Dwarves are great builders — maybe they have something that can help us build new temples.
column2: 矮人是伟大的建造者——也许他们有什么东西能帮我们建造新的神殿。

column1: Divorces are not uncommon in Orlanthi society. What is uncommon is the screaming rancor that marks the divorce of \x01CO and \x01CP. \x01CP, who is kin to several ring members of the \x01@! clan, insists that \x01CO return her dowry — the exact ten cows she brought with her. Since they were married a decade ago, and those specific cows have long since departed for the land of the dead, her insistence is less than reasonable.
column2: 离婚在奥兰瑟社会中并不罕见。罕见的是 \x01CO 和 \x01CP离婚时那种尖刻的怨恨。 \x01CP是 \x01@! 氏族几位长老会成员的亲属，坚持要求 \x01CO 归还她的嫁妆——确切来说是她带来的十头牛。既然他们十年前就结婚了，而那些特定的牛早已前往死者之地，她的坚持就不太合理了。

column1: \x01CO and \x01CP got divorced. \x01CP made unreasonable claims on him for a settlement.
column2: \x01CO  \x01CP 离婚了。 \x01CP 对他提出了不合理的要求作为补偿。

column1: Argue that she is misusing the law.
column2: 争辩说她滥用了法律。

column1: Our lawspeaker argued that she was misusing the law.
column2: 我们的律法师争辩说她滥用了法律。

column1: When \x01CP realized that she was flouting the sacred laws of Orlanth out of mere spite, she retracted her demands, and settled for a reasonable dowry repayment.
column2: 当 \x01CP 意识到自己只是出于恶意而藐视奥兰斯的神圣律法时，她收回了要求，并接受了一笔合理的嫁妆赔偿。

column1: \x01CP was affronted, and left for clan \x01@!, promising that they would take vengeance against us.
column2: \x01CP 感到受辱，便前往 \x01@!氏族，扬言要向我们复仇。

column1: We made sure that she received a fair settlement regardless.
column2: 我们确保她无论怎样都得到了公平的补偿。

column1: \x01CP’s kin spoke to her, and she quietly withdrew her outrageous claim.
column2: \x01CP的亲属找她谈了话，她悄悄收回了离谱的要求。

column1: The \x01@! ring was affronted, and promised to support \x01CP’s claims by force of arms if necessary. She soon left us, and moved back in with them.
column2: \x01@! 长老会感到受辱，并承诺必要时以武力支持 \x01CP的要求。她很快离开了我们，搬回去和他们同住。

column1: Chide her for making preposterous demands.
column2: 责备她提出荒谬的要求。

column1: We chided her for making preposterous demands.
column2: 我们责备她提出荒谬的要求。

column1: When \x01CP realized that she was bringing upon herself the disapproval of the rest of the clan, she retracted her demands, and settled for a reasonable dowry repayment.
column2: 当 \x01CP 意识到自己正在招致氏族其他成员的不满时，她收回了要求，并接受了一笔合理的嫁妆赔偿。

column1: Help him pay her twice the original dowry.
column2: 帮他付给她双倍的原始嫁妆。

column1: To settle the dispute, the ring repaid her dowry, and \x01CO repaid it again.
column2: 为解决争端，长老会偿还了她的嫁妆， \x01CO 又偿还了一遍。

column1: \x01CP accepted our offer.
column2: \x01CP 接受了我们的提议。

column1: Keep the ring out of this mess.
column2: 让长老会置身事外。

column1: The ring stayed out of the matter.
column2: 长老会未介入此事。

column1: Only a few days later, \x01CP returned to the \x01@! clan, taking the ten cows she was legally due.
column2: 仅几天后， \x01CP 回到了 \x01@! 氏族，带走了她依法应得的十头牛。

column1: It’s normal to get your dowry back when a marriage ends. But one cow is more or less the same as any other for this purpose.
column2: 婚姻结束时拿回嫁妆是正常的。但就这点而言，一头牛跟另一头牛基本上没什么区别。

column1: Give her twice the dowry. That should end their ceaseless conflict.
column2: 给她双倍嫁妆。这应该能结束他们没完没了的冲突。

column1: She doesn’t really want the cows. She wants to punish \x01CO for disappointing her.
column2: 她其实不想要那些牛。她想惩罚 \x01CO 让她失望。

column1: She is cleverly exploiting a flaw in Heort’s Law. \x01CO is obligated to do as she asks.
column2: 她巧妙地利用了赫奥特律法的一个漏洞。 \x01CO 有义务按她说的做。

column1: Any reasonable person would agree that her claim is absurd, but she has a legal right to make it.
column2: 任何理性的人都会同意她的要求很荒谬，但她在法律上有权提出。

column1: I believe I can out-argue her.
column2: 我相信我能辩过她。

column1: I believe I can out-argue her, and keep our name clear in the tribe.
column2: 我相信我能辩过她，并让我们在部落中保住名声。

column1: This foolish dispute has made us the laughing-stock of the entire tribe.
column2: 这场愚蠢的争端让我们成了整个部落的笑柄。

column1: I have no idea how to solve this problem.
column2: 我不知道该怎么解决这个问题。

column1: Her kin will end up burning one of our steads. I can smell the smoke already.
column2: 她的族人最终会烧掉我们的一座农庄。我已经闻到烟味了。

column1: I told you they’d make a terrible couple.
column2: 我早说过他们不是一对好夫妻。

column1: Twice the dowry is too small a price to pay for ten years of loutish behavior.
column2: 为十年粗暴无礼的行径付双倍嫁妆，代价并不算大。

column1: She has humiliated him daily for ten years. Let us now humiliate her.
column2: 十年来她天天羞辱他。现在让我们羞辱她。

column2: sceneR118

column1: A group of refugees come to our tula, seeking help. They seem to be Orlanthi. “We sought land to the west of here, and were captured and enslaved by cruel horse nomads. Loving freedom, we escaped. Yet our escape has cost us much. We beg you to aid us.”
column2: 一群难民来到我们的领地，寻求帮助。他们看起来是奥兰斯人。“我们在西边寻找土地，却被残酷的马背游牧者俘虏为奴。热爱自由的我们逃了出来。然而这场逃亡让我们付出了巨大代价。我们恳求你们伸出援手。”

column1: Refugees came seeking aid. They said they had escaped from cruel horse nomads.
column2: 难民前来求助。他们说自己是逃出残酷马背游牧者之手的。

column1: Refugees came seeking aid. They said they had escaped from the Horse-Spawn.
column2: 难民前来求助。他们说自己是逃出那可恶马裔的。

column1: Adopt them as family.
column2: 接纳他们为族人。

column1: We adopted them as family.
column2: 我们接纳他们为族人。

column1: Do you make them carls or cottars?
column2: 你要让他们成为自由民还是佃农？

column1: We were sure our ancestors, who had adopted the “Stick People” during the Darkness, would be pleased.
column2: 我们确信，那些在黑暗时代接纳了‘棍人’的祖先们会感到欣慰。

column1: Some said that our ancestors, who had enthralled the “Stick People” during the Darkness, would be displeased.
column2: 有人说，在黑暗时代奴役了‘棍人’的祖先们会不高兴。

column1: We said they would be thralls.
column2: 我们说他们将为奴隶。

column1: They try to run away.
column2: 他们试图逃跑。

column1: Do you chase them?
column2: 你要追捕他们吗？

column1: They ran away.
column2: 他们逃走了。

column1: Some folk said that our ancestors, who had adopted the “Stick People” during the Darkness, would be unhappy.
column2: 有人说，在黑暗时代接纳了‘棍人’的祖先们会不高兴。

column1: We knew that our ancestors, who had enthralled the “Stick People” during the Darkness, would be pleased.
column2: 我们知道，在黑暗时代奴役了‘棍人’的祖先们会感到欣慰。

column1: Send them to a neighboring clan.
column2: 将他们送到邻近的氏族去。

column1: Which other clan?
column2: 送到哪个氏族？

column1: We sent them to the \x01Ý.
column2: 我们将他们送到了 \x01Ý.

column1: People complained about the ring’s lack of kindness.
column2: 人们抱怨长老会缺乏仁慈。

column1: The people complained that the clan ring had stupidly passed up a chance to take thralls to work in our fields.
column2: 人们抱怨氏族议会愚蠢地错过了一次抓奴隶来干农活的机会。

column1: People said that the ring had made the right decision, since these folk were not our kin.
column2: 人们说氏族议会做出了正确的决定，因为这些人并非我们的亲族。

column1: We conducted a divination ritual.
column2: 我们进行了一次占卜仪式。

column1: The Knowing God told our priests that no one was looking for the refugees any more.
column2: 全知之神告诉我们的祭司，已经没人再追查这些难民了。

column1: The Knowing God told our priests that the horse nomads would come looking for their thralls, and would bring many warriors to help them.
column2: 全知之神告诉我们的祭司，马背游牧者会来找回他们的奴隶，并且会带来许多战士帮他们。

column1: We can afford to take on more carls.
column2: 我们养得起更多自由民。

column1: We can’t afford to take on more carls, we don’t have enough cows that they can tend some.
column2: 我们养不起更多自由民，我们没有足够的牛只让他们照料。

column1: These people are Orlanthi, and should be treated as such.
column2: 这些人是奥兰斯人，就应当如此对待。

column1: Our people have a long tradition of taking remnant peoples and adopting them as our own.
column2: 我们氏族有悠久的传统，收留残民并接纳他们为自己人。

column1: Our ancestors took people like this as thralls, and so should we.
column2: 我们的祖先曾把这样的人收为奴隶，我们也该这么做。

column1: This situation is of no magical significance .
column2: 这种情况没有任何魔法意义。

column1: If we adopt them, in the traditions of our ancestors, our clan magic will be strengthened.
column2: 如果我们按照祖先传统接纳他们，我们的氏族魔法将会得到增强。

column1: If we enthrall them, in the traditions of our ancestors, our clan magic will be strengthened.
column2: 如果我们按照祖先传统奴役他们，我们的氏族魔法将会得到增强。

column1: Good thing we came to this part of Dragon Pass instead of heading west!
column2: 幸好我们来了龙隘的这片区域，而不是往西走！

column1: We shouldn’t fear the cruel Horse-Spawn.
column2: 我们不应惧怕那残酷的马裔。

column1: We must adopt them!
column2: 我们必须接纳他们！

column1: These refugees must have ended up in the territory of the Horse-Spawn.
column2: 这些难民一定是落入了马裔的地盘。

column1: If we take these people in, the horse people will do us great harm.
column2: 如果我们收留这些人，马上民族会给我们带来大祸。

column1: The fight with the horse people will be glorious!
column2: 与马人的战斗将充满荣耀！

column1: Of course we must help them.
column2: 我们当然必须帮助他们。

column1: sceneR119
column2: sceneR119

column1: There are \x01@\x1A rebel clans. How much do you distribute among them?
column2: 有 \x01@\x1A 个反叛氏族。你打算在他们之间分配多少？

column1: Our words were well-received.
column2: 我们的话得到了良好回应。

column1: The rebels rejected our arguments.
column2: 反叛者拒绝了我们的话。

column1: Fight the rebels.
column2: 与反叛者开战。

column1: We massed our forces against the rebels.
column2: 我们集结兵力对抗反叛者。

column1: Together, we planned to force the king to abdicate.
column2: 我们共同谋划，要迫使国王退位。

column1: Let both sides fight, wait for advantage.
column2: 让双方相斗，坐等渔利。

column1: We bided our time.
column2: 我们静待时机。

column1: Try to mediate the dispute.
column2: 尝试调解争端。

column1: We tried to find conciliation between the two sides.
column2: 我们试图在双方之间斡旋和解。

column1: How much wealth do you give to each of the other chieftains?
column2: 你打算给其他每位酋长多少财富？

column1: We convinced the clans to stop insulting one another and work to make things better.
column2: 我们说服了各氏族停止相互辱骂，齐心协力改善局面。

column1: We found that people were more interested in insulting one another than in working to make things better.
column2: 我们发现人们更热衷于互相辱骂，而不是努力改善局面。

column1: We don’t have enough cows to engage in diplomacy now.
column2: 我们现在没有足够的牛只来进行外交。

column1: We have more than enough cows to make a diplomatic effort.
column2: 我们有足够多的牛只来进行外交斡旋。

column1: The number of cows we own has nothing to do with this.
column2: 我们拥有牛只的数量与此无关。

column1: No one ever gets hurt in fights within the tribe.
column2: 在部落内部的争斗中从未有人受伤。

column1: The rebels are stronger than the loyalists.
column2: 反叛者比忠顺派更强。

column1: The loyalists are stronger than the rebels.
column2: 忠顺派比反叛者更强。

column1: Our misrule caused this strife.
column2: 我们治理不善才导致了这场纷争。

column1: Our misrule caused this strife. Yet eloquent words and great generosity can still preserve the throne.
column2: 我们治理不善才导致了这场纷争。然而，雄辩的话语和慷慨的馈赠仍能保住王位。

column1: If we mass against the rebels now, then we’ll be fighting instead of planting. Find a better way to end this.
column2: 如果我们现在集结兵力对抗反叛者，就会耽误春耕。找更好的办法来了结此事吧。

column1: If we join the rebels against the king, then we’ll be fighting instead of planting. Find a better way to end this.
column2: 如果我们加入反叛者一起对抗国王，就会耽误春耕。找更好的办法来了结此事吧。

column1: If we mass against the rebels now, we’ll be fighting instead of reaping. Find a better way to end this.
column2: 如果我们现在集结兵力对抗反叛者，就会耽误秋收。找更好的办法来了结此事吧。

column1: True heroes.
column2: 真正的英雄。
