column2: 无论你做什么，确保那女孩不死，因为是我们，我们该为残忍抛弃她而受责——为什么，为什么我们总做不对事？

column1: They think she’s lying, and tell her so, but she just shakes her head and walks away, leaving the emissaries with the \x01@! ring members.
column2: 他们觉得她在说谎，便直接告诉她，但她只是摇摇头走开，留下使者们和 \x01@! 戒指成员在一起。

column1: Ask the \x01@! chieftain to interrogate her.
column2: 请 \x01@! 酋长审问她。

column1: We decided that we had done what could be done.
column2: 我们决定已经做了力所能及的事。

column1: Their chieftain thanked us for the warning.
column2: 他们的酋长感谢我们的警告。

column1: Their chieftain scolded us for slandering one of their young women.
column2: 他们的酋长责骂我们诽谤他们的一位年轻女子。

column1: Demand the right to cast truth magic on her.
column2: 要求对她施放真相魔法的权利。

column1: We demanded the right to cast truth magic on her.
column2: 我们要求对她施放真相魔法的权利。

column1: Their chieftain was greatly insulted by this request.
column2: 他们的酋长因这个请求深感受辱。

column1: Their chieftain agreed that we had the right.
column2: 他们的酋长同意我们有权这样做。

column1: They’re hiding something. They’re all hiding something.
column2: 他们在隐瞒什么。他们全都在隐瞒什么。

column1: We are stronger than they are, though they are loathe to admit it because of our feud.
column2: 我们比他们强大，尽管他们因为世仇而不愿承认。

column1: We are weaker than they are, and they know it. They look for reasons to continue our feud.
column2: 我们比他们弱，而他们知道这一点。他们在找理由延续世仇。

column1: We are stronger than they are.
column2: 我们比他们强大。

column1: We are weaker than they are.
column2: 我们比他们弱小。

column1: We have no right to cast truth magic on her.
column2: 我们没有权利对她施放真相魔法。

column1: We have the right to ask to cast truth magic on her.
column2: 我们有权请求对她施放真相魔法。

column1: We have the right to ask to cast truth magic on her, but I doubt they will agree to it because of our feud.
column2: 我们有权请求对她施放真相魔法，但我怀疑他们会因世仇而不同意。

column1: We have the right to ask to cast truth magic on her. However, it is common for people to take offense when this right is exercised.
column2: 我们有权请求对她施放真相魔法。然而，当这项权利被行使时，人们常常感到冒犯。

column1: Settle this without fighting. We need to get our crops in the ground.
column2: 不动刃解决这事。我们得把庄稼种下地。

column1: Settle this without fighting. We need to get our grain harvested.
column2: 不动刃解决这事。我们得把谷物收割完。

column1: “No one is so good that there is no bad in her, nor so bad that she is free from good.”
column2: “没有一个人好到毫无恶处，也没有一个人坏到毫无善念。”

column1: sceneR131
column2: sceneR131

column1: Kallyr returns to your clan after spending three years under the tutelage of the region’s greatest holy warrior of Vinga. A new sense of confidence and command has replaced the childlike exuberance you used to know.
column2: 卡莉尔在地区最伟大的温加神圣战士的指导下度过了三年，回到了你的氏族。一种新的自信和统帅气概取代了你曾熟悉的孩童般的活力。

column1: Kallyr returned from her training.
column2: 卡莉尔结束了训练归来。

column1: She told us a tale of Orlanth that she had learned, “\x01@\r.”
column2: 她给我们讲了一个她学到的奥兰斯故事：“\x01@\r.”

column1: Parts of Kallyr’s knowledge were new to us.
column2: 卡莉尔知识中的一部分对我们是全新的。

column1: Kallyr told us the tale of Orlanth’s Lightbringers Quest. She told it better than any of our god-talkers, but she had not learned any secret parts we didn’t already know.
column2: 卡莉尔给我们讲了奥兰斯光明使者追寻的故事。她讲得比我们任何神言者都好，但她没有学到任何我们不知道的秘密部分。

column1: Tell her that she must not be prouder than her elders.
column2: 告诉她，她不得比她的长辈更骄傲。

column1: We told her that she must not be prouder than her elders.
column2: 我们告诉她，她不得比她的长辈更骄傲。

column1: She replied that, since we had shown our pride to be beyond measure, there was little chance of her outshining us in that area.
column2: 她回答说，既然我们的傲慢已无人能及，她在这方面恐怕难以超越我们。

column1: Test her mettle by sending her to lead a raid.
column2: 派她率领劫掠队，考验她的胆识。

column1: We sent her to lead a raid.
column2: 我们派她率领劫掠队。

column1: Everyone praised Kallyr, and said they would follow her anywhere.
column2: 人人都称赞卡莉尔，说愿意追随她到天涯海角。

column1: Everyone criticized themselves for failing to live up to Kallyr’s high standard.
column2: 人人都自责未能达到卡莉尔的高标准。

column1: Welcome her, but make no great fuss.
column2: 欢迎她，但不要大张旗鼓。

column1: We welcomed her.
column2: 我们欢迎了她。

column1: We don’t need to raid for cows. Perhaps an exploratory mission…
column2: 我们不需要为牛只而劫掠。也许派一支探险队……

column1: Kallyr is a great warrior now. The last thing she wants is for us to fawn over her.
column2: 卡莉尔已是伟大的战士。她现在最不想要的就是我们对她阿谀奉承。

column1: Kallyr feels she now deserves to be treated as an equal.
column2: 卡莉尔认为自己理应受到平等对待。

column1: Kallyr knows she will be an invaluable member of our society, and we should honor her as such.
column2: 卡莉尔深知自己将成为我们社会中不可或缺的一员，我们应当以此礼遇她。

column1: The other warriors will be jealous if we make a fuss over her.
column2: 若我们对她大加追捧，其他战士会心生嫉妒。

column1: Let Kallyr prove herself without taking hands away from planting our fields.
column2: 让卡莉尔证明自己，不必从田里抽调人手。

column1: Let Kallyr prove herself without taking hands away from bringing in the crops.
column2: 让卡莉尔证明自己，不必从收割中抽调人手。

column1: Queen Ingban first distinguished herself by finding the Climbing Sand.
column2: 英班女王最初正是因发现“攀爬沙”而崭露头角。

column1: She is no longer a child. She has learned her lessons well, and needs no more from us.
column2: 她已不再是孩子。她学有所成，无需我们再多指导。

column1: Send her in search of dragonewt secrets.
column2: 派她去探寻龙秘。

column1: Send her in search of ancient scrolls.
column2: 派她去搜寻古代卷轴。

column1: Maybe I should step aside, and let her take my place on the ring.
column2: 也许我该退位，让她接替我进入长老会。

column1: Send her in search of appointments for our temples.
column2: 派她去为我们神庙的神职任命奔走。

column1: She is everything we hoped.
column2: 她正是我们所期待的样子。

column1: Send her in search of secret stories of the gods.
column2: 派她去搜寻神明的隐秘故事。

column1: You promised all of the other clans of the tribe that you would fight them, if necessary, rather than give up the throne. They have deemed it necessary. The warriors of every other clan are massing on the battlefield against you. Their warriors outnumber yours \x01@\x13 to 1.
column2: 你曾向部落所有其他氏族承诺，必要时你会与他们开战，也绝不放弃王位。如今他们认为时机已到。每个氏族的战士都在战场上集结，与你为敌。他们的战士数量是你的 \x01@\x13 倍。

column1: The other clans prepared to attack us and force \x01@\x0B to step down.
column2: 其他氏族准备攻击我们，逼迫 \x01@\x0B 退位。

column1: Fight to win; surrender only if all the warriors are killed.
column2: 战斗至胜；除非所有战士战死，否则绝不投降。

column1: We fought them.
column2: 我们与他们战斗。

column1: Before the battle, \x01@\x10 says, “Remember that clod of earth we got from the Maran Gor priestess? We must be able to use it, because I hear it rumbling.”
column2: 战前， \x01@\x10 说道：“还记得我们从玛兰·戈尔女祭司那里得来的那块土块吗？我们一定用得着它，因为我听见它在隆隆作响。”

column1: Do you use the Sacred Clod in the upcoming battle?
column2: 你会在即将到来的战斗中使用神圣土块吗？

column1: Fight to win; surrender only if half the warriors are killed.
column2: 战斗至胜；除非一半战士战死，否则绝不投降。

column1: Sneering at the overwhelming odds, \x01@\x0B led our thundering warriors into battle. Warrior after warrior fell beneath the rebel swords.
column2: 面对压倒性的劣势， \x01@\x0B 嗤笑一声，率领我们雷霆般的战士冲入战场。战士一个接一个倒在叛军的剑下。

column1: Fight until honor is satisfied, then renounce the throne.
column2: 战斗到荣誉得以满足，然后放弃王位。

column1: The other clans were glad that \x01@\x0B was not willing to throw away the lives of tribal warriors for \x04 own pride.
column2: 其他氏族很高兴 \x01@\x0B 不愿为 \x04 自己的骄傲而牺牲部落战士的生命。

column1: Whatever happens, we are bound to lose the throne. Let us lose no more than that.
column2: 无论如何，我们都会失去王位。那就仅此而已吧。

column1: This is no longer a matter of law. It will be resolved only by force of arms.
column2: 这已不是律法能解决的问题。只有武力才能决出结果。

column1: We have no hope of winning.
column2: 我们毫无胜算。

column1: If we can win, our victory will be legendary.
column2: 若能取胜，我们的胜利将成为传奇。

column1: If we put on a valiant show, the other clans will respect us a little, at least.
column2: 若能英勇一战，至少其他氏族会多一分尊重。

column1: Giving up the throne will weaken our clan magic.
column2: 放弃王位会削弱我们的氏族魔法。

column1: Like Bad King Urgrain facing the wrath of the Seven Uroxi, we have no good choice before us.
column2: 如同恶王乌格兰面对七位尤洛克斯追随者的怒火，我们面前没有好选择。

column1: Let this be a time of Endings.
column2: 让此刻成为终结之时。

column1: If we are not willing to die today, we do not have warrior’s hearts.
column2: 若我们今日不敢赴死，便不配拥有战士之心。

column1: Better to be a fool in the land of the living than a fool in the halls of the dead.
column2: 在生者之地做傻瓜，也好过在死者之厅做傻瓜。

column1: No crown is worth dying for.
column2: 没有王冠值得为之赴死。

column1: Ready the shields, saddle the horses, polish your swords! We shall fight a good battle, and win, no matter the cost!
column2: 备好盾牌，鞍上战马，磨利刀剑！我们要好好打一仗，赢得胜利，不计代价！

column1: I cannot just step down as easily as if alighting from some horse. If we show them we are not weak, then I can resign honorably.
column2: 我不能像下马一样轻易退位。若让他们看出我们并不软弱，我就能体面地退位。

column1: More than three-quarters of your warriors are dead.
column2: 超过四分之三的战士已阵亡。

column1: Do you disband the clan?
column2: 你要解散氏族吗？

column1: Despite this terrible loss, we chose to soldier on.
column2: 尽管遭受如此惨重的损失，我们仍选择继续前行。

column1: After losing the throne, we went to the moot where a new king would be chosen.
column2: 失去王位后，我们前往议会，那里将选出新国王。

column1: Give gifts to other clans.
column2: 赠予其他氏族礼物。

column1: Which clans do you gift?
column2: 你要赠礼给哪些氏族？

column1: We gave gifts to other clans.
column2: 我们赠予了其他氏族礼物。

column1: This gesture seemed to help repair our clan’s tattered reputation.
column2: 这一姿态似乎有助于修复我们氏族破碎的名声。

column1: Humbly abstain from choosing a new king.
column2: 谦逊地放弃推选新国王。

column1: We did not participate in the choice.
column2: 我们没有参与推选。

column1: This was seen as a sign of new humility, and other clans spoke well of us for the first time in a long while.
column2: 这被视为一种新的谦卑之举，其他氏族长久以来首次对我们说了好话。

column1: Support \x01@G.
column2: 支持 \x01@G。

column1: Support \x01@F.
column2: 支持 \x01@F。

column1: We supported \x01@F, who had been the most vocal of our opponents.
column2: 我们支持了 \x01@F，他是我们最激烈的反对者之一。

column1: The elders of other clans quietly questioned our motives, suspecting that something underhanded was afoot.
column2: 其他氏族的族长们暗自质疑我们的动机，怀疑其中有见不得人的勾当。

column1: Attempt to find a compromise candidate.
column2: 试图找一个折中候选人。

column1: We tried to find a compromise candidate.
column2: 我们试图找一个折中候选人。

column1: The candidate.
column2: 候选人。

column1: It is a bad time for politics, or gift-giving in general.
column2: 眼下不是搞政治或送礼的好时机。

column1: They may hate us, but we are still rich. And it is cows who choose kings.
column2: 他们或许恨我们，但我们依然富有。而牛只才是决定国王的人。

column1: They do not trust us.
column2: 他们不信任我们。

column1: Our lack of influence makes us honest brokers, with no stake in the outcome.
column2: 我们缺乏影响力，反而让我们成为诚实的中间人，对结果没有利害关系。

column1: We must have our fighters war-whoop for a candidate, so they do not think us completely humbled.
column2: 我们必须让战士为某位候选人发出战吼，以免他们认为我们已彻底屈服。

column1: No law forbids us from supporting our candidate of choice.
column2: 没有法律禁止我们支持自己选中的候选人。

column1: No law forbids us from supporting our candidate of choice. Common sense, however, suggests a show of prudence.
column2: 没有法律禁止我们支持自己选中的候选人。但常识告诉我们，应当表现谨慎。

column1: We should give cows away, to build our reputation for another day.
column2: 我们应当赠送牛只，为日后积攒声誉。

column1: The other chieftains wish us to do nothing. They will give us some credit for wisdom if we fulfill this expectation.
column2: 其他酋长希望我们按兵不动。若顺从这一期望，他们会认可我们的明智。

column1: Our reputation is so poisoned that any candidate we support is doomed to lose. You know, we could use this to our advantage…
column2: 我们的名声已败坏至此，任何我们支持的候选人都注定落败。你明白，我们可以利用这一点……

column1: To think that we gave up the throne so that these puking babes could fight over it!
column2: 想想我们放弃了王位，竟让这些乳臭未干的小儿来争抢！

column1: We must impress them with our generosity.
column2: 我们必须以慷慨打动他们。

column1: We have to make them like us again.
column2: 我们必须让他们重新喜欢我们。

column1: \x01@F masterminded our downfall, and is certain to win. We must support \x08, or lose further favor in \x04 eyes.
column2: \x01@F 策划了我们的败落，且必胜无疑。我们必须支持 \x08，否则会在 \x04 眼中更加失宠。

column1: Our best choice will be to let the other clans choose \x01@F without getting involved.
column2: 我们最好的选择是让其他氏族自行选择 \x01@F ，不介入其中。

column1: sceneR134
column2: sceneR134

column1: The day of battle is upon us.
column2: 战斗之日已至。

column1: We went to war against the \x01Á.
column2: 我们曾与……开战 \x01Á.

column1: Commit as little as possible to the battle.
column2: 尽可能少地投入战斗。

column1: Our clan held back from the worst of the fighting.
column2: 我方氏族避开了最惨烈的战斗。

column1: Volunteer for an assignment that is risky, but not too risky.
column2: 请缨执行一项风险适中但不至于过大的任务。

column1: We sought an assignment of moderate risk.
column2: 我们寻求了一项风险适中的任务。

column1: Volunteer to give magical aid instead of risking warriors.
column2: 请缨提供魔法援助，而非让战士冒险。

column1: Other clans jeered that our magic was weak, and would be of little help.
column2: 其他氏族嘲讽我们的魔法虚弱，无甚助益。

column1: Other clans said that our magic was strong, and would be of great help.
column2: 其他氏族称我们的魔法强大，大有助益。

column1: Volunteer to spearhead the attack.
column2: 请缨担任突击先锋。

column1: We volunteered to spearhead the attack.
column2: 我们自愿担任突击先锋。

column1: \x05 said we would spearhead the attack.
column2: \x05 声称我们将担任突击先锋。

column1: \x05 spared our clan the worst of the fighting.
column2: \x05 让我方氏族免于最惨烈的战斗。

column1: Before the battle, \x01@\x10 says, “Remember that clod of earth we got from the Maran Gor priestess? We must have enough clans to use it, because I hear it rumbling.”
column2: 战前， \x01@\x10 说道：“还记得我们从玛兰·戈尔女祭司那里得到的土块吗？我们必须凑够氏族来使用它，因为我听到它在隆隆作响。”

column1: The \x01@< forces were bested. Enemy thunderbolts fell all around us. \x01Á overran tulas of our tribe, looting them.
column2: \x01@< 的军队被击败。敌方的雷霆在我们周围落下。 \x01Á 攻占了我们部落的图拉领地，将其劫掠一空。

column1: Our tula was among those ravaged.
column2: 我们的领地也惨遭蹂躏。

column1: Thanks to the merciful mother Ernalda, our tula was spared their depredations.
column2: 感谢仁慈的母亲埃尔纳尔达，我们的领地幸免于他们的掠夺。

column1: Thunderbolts lashed all about us, thrown by friends and foes alike. We lost good warriors, but helped our tribe carry the day. We were given a generous share of the spoils.
column2: 雷霆在我们四周肆虐，敌我双方皆在投掷。我们失去了优秀的战士，但帮助部落赢得了胜利。我们分得了丰厚的战利品。

column1: The worst of the fighting was some distance from us. We heard the crack of lightning and felt the rumble of thunder from the great magics that were loosed on the battlefield that day. Only one of our people was killed. We were given but a token share of the spoils.
column2: 最惨烈的战斗离我们有一段距离。我们只听到闪电的爆裂声和那天战场上释放的宏大魔法所引发的雷鸣。仅有一名族人阵亡。我们只得到象征性的战利品份额。

column1: How much do you wish to sacrifice to the gods of war?
column2: 你愿向战神献祭多少？

column1: Our magic rained down on the battlefield, and helped bring victory to the warriors. Our efforts were recognized with an appropriate share of the spoils.
column2: 我们的魔法如雨般倾泻在战场上，助战士们赢得胜利。我们的付出得到了相应份额的战利品作为认可。

column1: Our magics were not strong enough. The \x01@< forces were bested. \x01Á overran tulas of our tribe, looting them.
column2: 我们的魔法不够强大。 \x01@< 的军队被击败。 \x01Á 攻占了我们部落的图拉领地，将其劫掠一空。

column1: We can’t afford to sacrifice enough cows to be of any use.
column2: 我们献祭的牛只数量不足以派上用场。

column1: If our magic is strong, we have the cows to sacrifice.
column2: 若我们的魔法强大，我们自有牛只可供献祭。

column1: The other clans will be obligated to us if we bear the brunt of the risk.
column2: 若我们承担主要风险，其他氏族便会欠我们人情。

column1: We are likely to win this battle. We should spearhead it, so that we get the best share of the spoils.
column2: 我们很可能赢得这场战斗。应当打头阵，以便获得最佳战利品份额。

column1: We are unlikely to win this battle. We should be neither cowardly nor foolhardy.
column2: 我们不太可能赢得这场战斗。既不应怯懦，也不应鲁莽。

column1: If we petition them, the gods will favor us over the \x01Á.
column2: 若我们向他们祈求，众神会眷顾我们，胜过 \x01Á.

column1: Our magic is weak; the gods will ignore our petitions.
column2: 我们的魔法虚弱；众神会无视我们的祈求。

column1: You know how I feel.
column2: 你明白我的感受。

column1: Honor. Duty. Death.
column2: 荣誉。职责。死亡。

column1: I suppose it’s too late to talk this out with the \x01Á…
column2: 我想现在与……商谈为时已晚 \x01Á…

column1: This is a time for heroes!
column2: 这是英雄的时代！

column1: Charge!
column2: 冲锋！

column1: \x02\x02This does not look good/I think we can hold them off\x02.
column2: \x02\x02形势不妙/我想我们能挡住他们\x02。

column1: We lost good warriors, but led our tribe to carry the day. The insignia of our clan was the last thing that many of the beastmen saw in this life. We were given a generous share of the spoils. Since the Beastfolk are poor, this was a generous share of not very much.
column2: 我们失去了优秀的战士，但带领部落赢得了胜利。许多兽人在此生中最后看到的是我们氏族的徽记。我们分得了丰厚的战利品。不过由于兽人群落贫穷，这丰厚的份额其实也不多。

column1: The \x01@< forces were bested. The Beastfolk overran tulas of our tribe, looting them and killing as many people as they could.
column2: \x01@< 的军队被击败。兽人群落攻占了我们部落的图拉领地，大肆劫掠，尽可能多地杀戮。

column1: We lost good warriors, but helped our tribe carry the day. We were given a generous share of the spoils. But the Beastfolk were poor, and what good is it to have a generous share of not very much?
column2: 我们失去了优秀的战士，但帮助部落赢得了胜利。我们分得了丰厚的战利品。但兽人群落贫穷，分到一份丰厚的微不足道之物又有何用？

column1: Only one of our people was killed. We were given but a token share of what few spoils there were.
column2: 仅有一名族人阵亡。我们只得到了那点可怜战利品中象征性的一份。

column1: Our magic rained down on our inhuman foes, and helped bring victory to the warriors. Our efforts were recognized with an appropriate share of the spoils, though, being Beastfolk, the spoils were slim.
column2: 我们的魔法倾泻在非人宿敌身上，助战士们赢得胜利。我们的付出得到了相应份额的战利品作为认可，不过由于对方是兽人群落，战利品微薄。

column1: Our magics were not strong enough. The Beastfolk magics found our magicians and killed or hurt them. On the battlefield, \x01@< forces were bested. The Beastfolk overran tulas of our tribe, looting them and killing as many people as they could.
column2: 我们的魔法不够强大。兽人的魔法发现了我们的法师，杀害或伤害了他们。在战场上， \x01@< 部队被击败。兽人席卷了我们部落的图拉领地，大肆劫掠，尽可能多地屠戮民众。

column1: We can’t afford to sacrifice enough cows to counter the dread magic of the Beastfolk.
column2: 我们无法献祭足够的牛只来对抗兽人那可怕的魔法。

column1: We have many cows to sacrifice. Surely our inhuman foes do not have anything so valuable to give to whatever gods they revere.
column2: 我们有很多牛只可以献祭。那些非人的敌人肯定拿不出如此珍贵的东西献给他们所崇拜的无论什么神祇。

column1: Everyone is afraid of the Beastfolk. The other clans will be obligated to us if we are the closest to the fight.
column2: 所有人都害怕兽人。如果我们是最靠近战斗的氏族，其他氏族就会欠我们人情。

column1: Although everyone is afraid of the Beastfolk, I think we can beat them. We should spearhead it, so that we get the best share of the spoils.
column2: 虽然每个人都害怕兽人，但我认为我们能击败他们。我们应该带头出击，这样就能分到最好的战利品。

column1: Everyone is afraid of the Beastfolk, and rightly so. If we fight, we should do so expecting to die.
column2: 所有人都害怕兽人，这理所当然。如果要打，我们应当抱着必死的决心。

column1: If we petition them, the gods will favor us over the Beastfolk.
column2: 如果我们向神明祈求，神明会眷顾我们而非兽人。

column1: When the dragons ate all the people in Dragon Pass, they did not eat the Beastfolk.
column2: 当年巨龙吃光了龙之隘口的所有人，却没有吃兽人。

column1: Don’t forget that we could use the Sacred Clod — it will let us take risks we would not otherwise dare!
column2: 别忘了我们可以用神圣土块——它能让我们冒原本不敢冒的风险！

column1: We must lead by example, inspiring our tribe-mates to fight bravely, exhorting them to a grand victory!
column2: 我们必须以身作则，激励族人们勇敢战斗，鼓舞他们取得辉煌的胜利！

column2: sceneR136

column1: The Horse-Spawn fought with fiery arrows and lances, atop strange horses able to leap great heights. We lost good warriors, but led our tribe to carry the day. The insignia of our clan was the last thing that the haughty Horse-Spawn saw in this life. We were given a generous share of the spoils.
column2: 马裔骑着能高高跃起的异马，以火箭和骑枪作战。我们失去了优秀的战士，但带领氏族赢得了胜利。我们氏族的徽记，是那些高傲的马裔此生所见到的最后一样东西。我们分到了丰厚的战利品。

column1: The Horse-Spawn fought with fiery arrows and lances, atop strange horses able to leap great heights. The \x01@< forces were bested. The terrible horse-riders showed particular skill at killing clan and tribal leaders. They overran tulas of our tribe, looting them and enslaving the carls.
column2: 马裔骑着能高高跃起的异马，以火箭和骑枪作战。 \x01@< 部队被击败。那些可怕的骑手在屠戮氏族和部落首领方面尤为擅长。他们席卷了我们部落的图拉领地，劫掠一空并奴役了自由民。

column1: The Horse-Spawn fought with fiery arrows and lances, atop strange horses able to leap great heights. We lost good warriors, but helped our tribe carry the day. We were given a generous share of the spoils.
column2: 马裔骑着能高高跃起的异马，以火箭和骑枪作战。我们失去了优秀的战士，但帮助氏族赢得了胜利。我们分到了丰厚的战利品。

column1: The Horse-Spawn fought with fiery arrows and lances, atop strange horses able to leap great heights. Only one of our people was killed. We were given but a token share of the spoils.
column2: 马裔骑着能高高跃起的异马，以火箭和骑枪作战。我们只有一人阵亡。但只分到了象征性的战利品。

column1: The Horse-Spawn fought with fiery arrows and lances, atop strange horses able to leap great heights. The \x01@< forces were bested. The terrible horse-riders showed particular skill at killing clan and tribal leaders; thankfully, our own leaders were far from the fray. They overran tulas of our tribe, looting them and enslaving the carls.
column2: 马裔骑着能高高跃起的异马，以火箭和骑枪作战。 \x01@< 部队被击败。那些可怕的骑手在屠戮氏族和部落首领方面尤为擅长；所幸，我们自己的首领远离了战团。他们席卷了我们部落的图拉领地，劫掠一空并奴役了自由民。

column1: The Horse-Spawn fought with fiery arrows and lances, atop strange horses able to leap great heights. Our magic rained down upon them, and helped bring victory to the warriors. Our efforts were recognized with an appropriate share of the spoils.
column2: 马裔骑着能高高跃起的异马，以火箭和骑枪作战。我们的魔法如雨般倾泻在他们头上，帮助战士们取得了胜利。我们的努力得到了认可，分到了应得的战利品。

column1: Our magics were not strong enough. The \x01@< forces were bested. The Horse-Spawn overran tulas of our tribe, looting them.
column2: 我们的魔法不够强大。 \x01@< 部队被击败。马裔席卷了我们部落的图拉领地，大肆劫掠。

column1: To gain the favor of the gods, you must sacrifice wealth. We don’t have enough cows to do that.
column2: 要获得神明的恩惠，你必须献祭财富。我们没有足够的牛只来做到这一点。

column1: We have many cows to sacrifice. The horse people have no cows; surely that makes our gods stronger than theirs.
column2: 我们有很多牛只可以献祭。马上民族没有牛；这肯定让我们的神比他们的神更强大。

column1: The Horse-Spawn are known to fight strangely and well, from horseback. The other clans will be obligated to us if we spearhead the fight against them.
column2: 马裔以骑术精湛、战法怪异著称。如果我们带头对抗他们，其他氏族就会欠我们人情。

column1: The Horse-Spawn are known to fight strangely and well, from horseback. Nevertheless, I think we can beat them. We should lead the fight and get the best share of the spoils.
column2: 马裔以骑术精湛、战法怪异著称。尽管如此，我认为我们能击败他们。我们应该领导战斗，分到最好的战利品。

column1: The Horse-Spawn are known to fight strangely and well, from horseback. If we fight, we should do so expecting to die.
column2: 马裔以骑术精湛、战法怪异著称。如果要打，我们应当抱着必死的决心。

column1: If we petition them, the gods will favor us over the horse people.
column2: 如果我们向神明祈求，神明会眷顾我们而非马上民族。

column1: Our magic is weak. The other clans will laugh if we boast of our magical prowess.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱。如果我们吹嘘自己的魔法造诣，其他氏族会笑话的。

column1: We have no ancient stories or ancestral proverbs about these Horse-Spawn. It makes me nervous.
column2: 我们没有关于这些马裔的古老故事或祖先谚语。这让我不安。

column1: Don’t forget to bring out the Sacred Clod — it will let us take risks we would not otherwise dare!
column2: 别忘了拿出神圣土块——它能让我们冒原本不敢冒的风险！

column1: We must lead the charge and bring our glorious tribe to a grand victory!
column2: 我们必须带头冲锋，带领我们光荣的氏族走向伟大的胜利！

column2: sceneR137

column1: We lost good warriors, but led our tribe to carry the day. The insignia of our clan was the last thing that many of the trolls saw in this life. We were given a generous share of the spoils. Unfortunately, much of the troll treasure turned out to be useless lead coins.
column2: 我们失去了优秀的战士，但带领氏族赢得了胜利。我们氏族的徽记，是许多巨魔此生所见到的最后一样东西。我们分到了丰厚的战利品。不幸的是，巨魔的财宝大多是毫无用处的铅币。

column1: The \x01@< forces were bested. The trolls overran tulas of our tribe, looting them and taking as many people as they could. Our storytellers told us that the captives and the battlefield dead would likely end up in troll cookpots.
column2: \x01@< 部队被击败。巨魔席卷了我们部落的图拉领地，大肆劫掠并尽可能多地掳走人口。我们的故事讲述者告诉我们，俘虏和战场上的死者很可能会成为巨魔锅中的食物。

column1: We lost good warriors, but helped our tribe carry the day. We were given a generous share of the spoils. But the troll treasure turned out to be mostly useless lead coins, and what good is it to have a generous share of worthless garbage?
column2: 我们失去了优秀的战士，但帮助部落赢得了胜利。我们分到了丰厚的战利品。但巨魔的宝藏大多是没用的铅币，分到一堆毫无价值的垃圾又有什么意义呢？

column1: Only one of our people was killed. We were given but a token share of the spoils. Even those who spearheaded the battle complained that the troll riches were mostly useless lead coins.
column2: 我们只有一人阵亡。我们只分到了象征性的战利品。即使是冲锋陷阵的人也抱怨说巨魔的财富大多是没用的铅币。

column1: Our magic rained down on our inhuman foes, and helped bring victory to the warriors. Our efforts were recognized with an appropriate share of the spoils. Unfortunately, troll treasure is mostly made up of worthless lead coins, so we sacrificed more wealth than we gained.
column2: 我们的魔法如雨般落在非人的敌人头上，帮助战士们取得了胜利。我们的付出得到了相应份额的战利品的认可。不幸的是，巨魔的宝藏大多由毫无价值的铅币组成，所以我们牺牲的财富多于收获。

column1: Our magics were not strong enough. The night-soaked troll magics found our magicians and killed or hurt them. On the battlefield, \x01@< forces were bested. The trolls overran tulas of our tribe, looting them and taking as many people as they could. Our storytellers told us that the captives and the battlefield dead would likely end up in troll cookpots.
column2: 我们的魔法不够强大。暗夜浸染的巨魔魔法找到了我们的法师，杀死或打伤了他们。战场上， \x01@< 军队被击败。巨魔横扫了我们部落的图拉领地，洗劫一空，尽可能多地掳走人口。我们的讲故事人告诉我们，俘虏和战死者多半会变成巨魔锅中的肉食。

column1: We have many cows to sacrifice. The hungry trolls have probably eaten all of their cows already, if they even know enough to raise them.
column2: 我们有很多牛可供献祭。那些饥饿的巨魔大概早已吃光了他们自己的牛——如果他们懂得养牛的话。

column1: Do not think that the spoils will be great. Trolls consider lead coins to be as good as cows.
column2: 别以为战利品会很丰厚。巨魔认为铅币和牛一样值钱。

column1: The trolls are fearsome opponents who know neither honor nor pity. The other clans will be obligated to us if we spearhead the fight against them.
column2: 巨魔是可怕的对手，既不懂荣誉也不知怜悯。如果我们带头对抗他们，其他氏族会欠我们人情。

column1: The trolls are fearsome opponents who know neither honor nor pity. That doesn’t mean we can’t beat them. We should lead the fight and get the best share of the spoils.
column2: 巨魔是可怕的对手，既不懂荣誉也不知怜悯。但这不代表我们打不赢他们。我们应该带头作战，拿到最好的那份战利品。

column1: The trolls are fearsome opponents who know neither honor nor pity. If we fight, we should do so expecting to die.
column2: 巨魔是可怕的对手，既不懂荣誉也不知怜悯。若要作战，就应当做好赴死的准备。

column1: If we petition them, the gods will favor us over these grunting minions of darkness.
column2: 如果我们向他们祈求，众神会眷顾我们，胜过这些黑暗的咕噜小卒。

column1: The trolls are a fearsome nocturnal race whose gods and heroes often fought Orlanth during the Storm Age.
column2: 巨魔是可怕的夜行种族，其神祇与英雄常在风暴时代与奥兰斯作战。

column1: The founders of our clan fought against the forces of Boztakang, cruel lord of trolls.
column2: 我们氏族的创立者曾与巨魔的残酷领主博兹塔康的势力作战。

column1: We must kill them all or end our days as troll-meat.
column2: 我们必须杀光他们，否则自己终将成为巨魔的口粮。

column1: Our ancestors are with us.
column2: 我们的祖先与我们同在。

column1: We must use the Sacred Clod — it will let us take risks we would not otherwise dare!
column2: 我们必须使用神圣土块——它能让我们冒平日不敢冒的风险！

column1: For the ancestors! For the glory of the tribe!
column2: 为了祖先！为了部落的荣耀！

column2: sceneR138

column1: The time has come to make war on the
column2: 开战的时刻已到，讨伐

column1: rebel clan which has
column2: 那个曾……的叛乱氏族

column1: \x01@\x08 rebel clans who have
column2: \x01@\x08 那些曾……的叛乱氏族

column1: One clan musters to help us with the fight.
column2: 有一个氏族集结兵力来协助我们作战。

column1: \x01@\r clans muster to help with the fight.
column2: \x01@\r个氏族集结兵力来协助作战。

column1: The time has come to make good on that promise.
column2: 履行那个承诺的时刻到了。

column1: One other clan joins us and the royal clan for the battle.
column2: 另一个氏族加入我们和王室氏族一同参战。

column1: \x01@\r clans join your clan and the royal clan for the battle.
column2: \x01@\r个氏族加入你们的氏族和王室氏族一同参战。

column1: “Attack them by surprise.”
column2: “发动突袭。”

column1: We proposed attacking the rebels before they were ready for us.
column2: 我们提议在叛军准备好之前发起进攻。

column1: We came upon the rebels before they were prepared and fell upon them, killing many. With fewer warriors to protect them, the rebel clans had little choice but to submit to the superior strength of the loyalist forces.
column2: 我们在叛军尚未准备就绪时杀到，向他们猛扑过去，杀死许多人。由于保护他们的战士减少，叛军各氏族别无选择，只能向优势的忠君势力屈服。

column1: “Fight an honest, straightforward battle.”
column2: “堂堂正正地打一场。”

column1: “Fight an honest, straightforward battle,” we said, and joined the usual pre-battle hubbub: boasts, insults, personal challenges, rival calls to the gods, and displays of magical prowess.
column2: “堂堂正正地打一场，”我们说道，然后加入了战前常见的热闹：夸耀、辱骂、个人挑战、向神明的对抗呼号，以及魔法力量的展示。

column1: As fighting time draws near, \x01@\x10 says, “Remember that clod of earth we got from the Maran Gor priestess? We must have enough clans to use it, because I hear it rumbling.”
column2: 战斗时刻临近， \x01@\x10 说道：“还记得我们从玛兰·戈尔女祭司那里得到的那个土块吗？我们必须有足够的氏族才能使用它，因为我听到了它的隆隆声。”

column1: “Give the rebels one last chance to surrender.”
column2: “给叛军最后一次投降的机会。”

column1: We said that we should give the rebels one last chance to surrender.
column2: 我们说过应该给叛军最后一次投降的机会。

column1: How much do you offer to the rebels?
column2: 你打算向叛军提供多少？

column1: The rebels said that only a fight would settle their grievances.
column2: 叛军说只有一战才能解决他们的怨愤。

column1: The rebels agreed to make peace.
column2: 叛军同意讲和。

column1: “There are too many of them. We’re joining the winning side.”
column2: “他们人数太多。我们要加入胜算更大的一方。”

column1: We decided that the rebels had a better chance of winning, so we joined them.
column2: 我们认定叛军胜算更大，于是加入了他们。

column1: A large number of cows might turn rebels back into loyalists.
column2: 一大群牛或许能让叛军变回忠臣。

column1: Ten cows for each chieftain might turn rebels back into loyalists. Twenty cows would assure it.
column2: 每位酋长十头牛或许能让叛军变回忠臣。二十头牛则一定能做到。

column1: Fifteen cows for each chieftain might turn rebels back into loyalists. Thirty cows would assure it.
column2: 每位酋长十五头牛或许能让叛军变回忠臣。三十头牛则一定能做到。

column1: Orlanth assures that rightful kings always win.
column2: 奥兰斯保证正义的国王总是获胜。

column1: The rebels have a better chance of winning than we do.
column2: 叛军的胜算比我们大。

column1: Our forces are evenly matched. I cannot predict who will win.
column2: 我们的兵力旗鼓相当。我无法预测谁将获胜。

column1: I am confident that we will beat the rebels.
column2: 我有信心我们能击败叛军。

column1: A sneak attack would be considered a bold move, in the tradition of the great king Urgrain.
column2: 突袭会被视为一次大胆的行动，合乎伟大的乌格伦国王的传统。

column1: A sneak attack would not be unprecedented.
column2: 突袭并非没有先例。

column1: A sneak attack would not be unprecedented, but it would not be honorable, either. The custom is to allow for a period of boasts, war-whoops and displays before honest battle is joined.
column2: 突袭并非没有先例，但同样也不光彩。习俗是在堂堂正正交战前，留出一段夸耀、战吼和展示的时间。

column1: If we give these rebels one last chance to surrender, we could delay fighting until after the crops are in the ground.
column2: 如果我们给这些叛军最后一次投降的机会，我们就可以把战斗推迟到庄稼下地之后。

column1: If we give these rebels one last chance to surrender, we could delay fighting until after the crops are harvested.
column2: 如果我们给这些叛军最后一次投降的机会，我们就可以把战斗推迟到庄稼收割之后。

column1: If the rules mean you must die, change the rules.
column2: 如果规则意味着你必须死，那就改变规则。

column1: Kings come and go. The only constant is the death that follows them around.
column2: 国王来了又去。唯一不变的，是跟随他们左右的死亡。

column1: The rebels have the tougher fight. We must join them, for Orlanth does not esteem the foreordained victor.
column2: 叛军打的是更艰苦的仗。我们必须加入他们，因为奥兰斯并不尊崇那命定的胜利者。

column1: We shall crush these obstreperous clans, the sooner the better.
column2: 我们要碾碎这些桀骜不驯的氏族，越快越好。

column1: If we move quickly and boldly, we can turn the tide of favor back our way.
column2: 如果我们迅速而大胆地行动，就能让恩惠的潮水重新倒向我们这边。

column2: sceneR139

column1: one clan
column2: 一个氏族

column1: \x01Ck clans
column2: \x01Ck 氏族

column1: What do you recommend to the other clans?
column2: 你向其他氏族推荐什么？

column1: Ask Orlanth if he approves of our actions.
column2: 询问奥兰斯他是否赞同我们的行动。

column1: We said that we should appeal to Orlanth, to see if our actions pleased him.
column2: 我们说过应当向奥兰斯求助，看看我们的行动是否令他满意。

column1: Our priests told us that Orlanth was displeased with us for failing to obey our chosen leaders.
column2: 我们的祭司告诉我们，奥兰斯因我们未能服从所选领袖而不悦。

column1: Fight an honest, straightforward battle.
column2: 打一场光明正大的仗。

column1: We said “Fight an honest, straightforward battle,” and joined the usual pre-battle hubbub: boasts, insults, personal challenges, rival calls to the gods, and displays of magical prowess.
column2: 我们说了“打一场光明正大的仗”，然后加入了战前常见的喧嚣：夸耀、辱骂、个人决斗、向诸神的竞争性呼告以及展示魔法威能。

column1: \x01@\x0B agreed that \x04 position was impossible, and abdicated the throne.
column2: \x01@\x0B 同意 \x04 的处境不可维持，于是逊位。

column1: Despite their insults, we told them we would do the same.
column2: 尽管他们侮辱我们，我们告诉他们我们也会这么做。

column1: The rebel leaders scorned us, saying that our ring must be entirely composed of Eurmali. “A more dishonorable suggestion we have never heard. We fight to protest misrule, yet you suggest we begin a new reign with the gravest of offenses?”
column2: 叛军首领嘲笑我们，说我们的法环必定全由尤尔玛利组成。“我们从未听过如此不名誉的建议。我们起兵是为了抗议暴政，而你却建议我们用最严重的罪行开启新统治？”

column1: Despite their insults, we told them we would stay and fight alongside them.
column2: 尽管他们侮辱我们，我们告诉他们我们会留下和他们并肩战斗。

column1: Our comrades have blood in their nostrils; it will be hard to turn them towards conciliation.
column2: 我们的战友鼻孔里还带着血腥味；很难让他们转向和解。

column1: Our comrades respect our judgment; we can turn them towards conciliation.
column2: 我们的战友尊重我们的判断；我们能使他们转向和解。

column1: Our comrades respect our judgment; we can turn them towards conciliation. \x01@\x0B is certain to welcome such an overture.
column2: 我们的战友尊重我们的判断；我们能使他们转向和解。 \x01@\x0B 必定欢迎这样的示好。

column1: If we take the battlefield, we will die like squirrels.
column2: 如果我们踏上战场，就会像松鼠一样死去。

column1: Our forces are so much stronger than those of the loyalists that we must be careful not to slaughter them by fighting too vigorously.
column2: 我们的兵力远强于保皇派，必须小心不要因作战过于猛烈而屠戮他们。

column1: We will probably lose this fight.
column2: 我们很可能会输掉这场战斗。

column1: I expect that we will win this fight.
column2: 我预计我们会赢得这场战斗。

column1: As rebels, we have the disadvantage, so the rules governing our actions are less strict.
column2: 作为叛乱者，我们处于劣势，因此约束我们行为的规则不那么严格。

column1: \x01@\x0B’s misrule has surely offended Orlanth as sorely as it has \x04 subjects.
column2: \x01@\x0B's的暴政无疑深深冒犯了奥兰斯，也冒犯了 \x04 臣民。

column1: If we act against Orlanth’s wishes, our clan magic will suffer.
column2: 如果我们违背奥兰斯的意愿，我们的氏族魔法就会受损。

column1: It may seem dishonorable, but there is a way to end this in our favor, a way that involves spilling only one person’s blood…
column2: 这或许有失荣誉，但有一种方法能让我们得利，一种只需流一人之血的方法……

column1: “It would be bad if a war broke out within the tribe.”
column2: “部族内部爆发战争会很糟糕。”

column1: \x01@\x0B agreed that a war would be very bad, and abdicated the throne.
column2: \x01@\x0B 同意战争非常糟糕，并退位让贤。

column1: What do you tell the discontented nobles of the other clan?
column2: 你对另一氏族心怀不满的贵族说什么？

column1: “Let the matter rest, for now.”
column2: “暂且让此事搁置吧。”

column1: We told the other discontented nobles to let the matter rest.
column2: 我们告诉其他心怀不满的贵族，让此事搁置。

column1: “We will give you many cows if you step down.”
column2: “如果你退位，我们会给你许多牛只。”

column1: \x01@\x0B said that our gesture of generosity would help the tribe to begin anew, with a new monarch.
column2: \x01@\x0B 说我们的慷慨姿态将有助于部族在新君主带领下重新开始。

column1: “You have flouted the laws of King Heort.”
column2: “你蔑视了赫奥特国王的法律。”

column1: \x01@\x0B said that our grasp of the precedents was overwhelming. “I had no idea that I had broken so many of the hallowed laws of our people.” \x05 abandoned the throne.
column2: \x01@\x0B 说我们对先例的掌握令人折服。“我竟不知自己破坏了这么多我们族人的神圣法律。” \x05 放弃了王位。

column1: “You tried to govern well, but the people do not love you.”
column2: “你试图好好治理，但人民并不爱你。”

column1: \x01@\x0B said that what we gave voice to was an unfortunate truth, and agreed to step down.
column2: \x01@\x0B 说我们道出的是一个不幸的事实，并同意退位。

column1: “Your reign has weakened the magic of all the clans.”
column2: “你的统治削弱了所有氏族的魔法。”

column1: \x01@\x0B said that \x06 had lost the favor of the gods and spirits, and would step down.
column2: \x01@\x0B 说 \x06 已失去神明与神灵的恩宠，将会退位。

column1: We can afford to make a payment that will ease \x01@\x0B from the throne.
column2: 我们能够支付一笔补偿，让 \x01@\x0B 顺利退位。

column1: In a true war within the tribe, many would die.
column2: 在部族间的真正战争中，许多人会死去。

column1: The people are unhappy, but their mood may yet change.
column2: 人民并不快乐，但他们的情绪或许还会改变。

column1: Our magic is strong; we can’t argue that the tribe’s magic is weak.
column2: 我们的魔法强大；我们不能争论说部族的魔法弱小。

column1: Bad King Urgrain was asked to step down thirteen times, but only left his throne when his clan grabbed spears and forced him from it.
column2: 恶王乌格兰被要求退位十三次，但直到他的氏族拿起长矛将他赶下王座，他才离开。

column1: The other clans of the tribe join together to bring a claim against you at the tribal moot. You are accused of using magic to hinder the \x01@! candidate, \x01@J, during \x04 rites of kingship.
column2: 部落的其他氏族联合起来，在部落大会上对你提出指控。你被控在王权仪式 \x04 期间使用魔法阻挠 \x01@! 候选人 \x01@J。

column1: \x01@J is shocked and angered; your magic could have killed \x08.
column2: \x01@J 感到震惊和愤怒；你的魔法本可能杀死 \x08。

column1: \x01@J’s clan is overcome with rage; your magic slew their candidate for the throne.
column2: \x01@J的氏族怒不可遏；你的魔法杀死了他们的王位候选人。

column1: The other clans brought us before a tribal moot for using magic against \x01@J during the rites of kingship.
column2: 其他氏族因我们在王权仪式期间对 \x01@J 使用魔法而将我们带到了部落大会面前。

column1: Compensate \x01@J’s clan.
column2: 赔偿 \x01@J的氏族。

column1: We admitted fault, and compensated \x01@J’s clan.
column2: 我们承认了过错，并赔偿了 \x01@J的氏族。

column1: Pay twice the requested compensation.
column2: 支付所要求赔偿的两倍。

column1: They seemed pleased with our generosity.
column2: 他们似乎对我们的慷慨感到满意。

column1: Pay half of the requested compensation.
column2: 支付所要求赔偿的一半。

column1: “\x01@J seemed unfit to rule.”
column2: “\x01@J 似乎不适合统治。”

column1: Before the moot, we argued that \x01@J had been unfit to rule.
column2: 在议会之前，我们争辩说 \x01@J 不适合统治。

column1: How much wealth do you give to other clans before the case is judged?
column2: 在案件裁决之前，你给其他氏族多少牛只？

column1: How many of your warriors make a war-whooping display to show their support for your case?
column2: 有多少战士以战吼示威，表示支持你的讼案？

column1: The other clans said that we were wrong to do what we did, but that no real harm had been done.
column2: 其他氏族说我们做错了，但并没有造成实际伤害。

column1: The other clans agreed that we had kept an unworthy candidate from the throne.
column2: 其他氏族同意我们阻止了一个不称职的王位候选者。

column1: The other clans said that we had behaved like crazy foreigners, not like good Orlanthi.
column2: 其他氏族说我们的行为像疯狂的异乡人，不像正直的奥兰斯崇拜者。

column1: “The precedents allow us to take such action.”
column2: “先例允许我们采取这样的行动。”

column1: Before the moot, we argued that legal precedents us allowed us to use magic to challenge a candidate for the throne during the rites.
column2: 在议会之前，我们争辩说法律先例允许我们在仪式中使用魔法挑战王位候选者。

column1: The other clans could not refute our interpretation of the Laws of Heort. They did not like what we had done, but could not say that it was illegal.
column2: 其他氏族无法驳斥我们对赫奥特律法的解释。他们不喜欢我们的所作所为，但不能说那是违法的。

column1: “It is not we who kept \x01@J from the throne, but the gods.”
column2: “阻止 \x01@J 登上王位的不是我们，而是神明。”

column1: We argued that the gods had judged \x01@J and found him wanting, so no blame could be attached to us.
column2: 我们争辩说，神明已审判 \x01@J ，并认为他不合格，因此我们不能受到指责。

column1: The other clans could not refute the arguments of our priests. How can magic granted by the gods be bad?
column2: 其他氏族无法驳斥我们祭司的论点。神明赐予的魔法怎么会是邪恶的呢？

column1: “We merely put \x01@J to the test required by the rites. \x05 passed, so no harm is done.”
column2: “我们只是让 \x01@J 接受了仪式要求的考验。 \x05 通过了，所以没有造成伤害。”

column1: Our argument was like so: “We merely put \x01@J to the test required by the rites. \x05 passed, so no harm is done.”
column2: 我们的论点如下：“我们只是让 \x01@J 接受了仪式要求的考验。 \x05 通过了，所以没有造成伤害。”

column1: The other clans could not refute the arguments of our priests. We were merely ensuring the integrity of the rites.
column2: 其他氏族无法驳斥我们祭司的论点。我们只是确保了仪式的完整性。

column1: The other clans will see the rightness of our cause. There is no need to give them cows.
column2: 其他氏族会认清我们事业的正确性。没有必要给他们牛只。

column1: We should send \x01@\x17 warriors to war-whoop at the moot. There is nothing to fear at home.
column2: 我们应派遣 \x01@\x17 名战士到议会进行战吼。在领地没什么可担心的。

column1: If we argue that the precedents allow this, we will be laughed out of Dragon Pass.
column2: 如果我们争辩说先例允许这样做，我们会被笑出龙隘。

column1: Arguing that the precedents support us will require considerable twisting of Heort’s Law.
column2: 主张先例支持我们将需要对赫奥特律法进行相当程度的扭曲。

column1: The best argument is that we were merely putting \x01@\x0B to a proper test.
column2: 最好的论点是：我们只是让 \x01@\x0B 接受了适当的考验。

column1: Arguing that the precedents support us will require considerable twisting of Heort’s Law. Fortunately, I am up to the task.
column2: 主张先例支持我们将需要对赫奥特律法进行相当程度的扭曲。幸运的是，我胜任这项任务。

column1: Everyone will agree that \x01@J was unfit to rule.
column2: 所有人都会同意 \x01@J 不适合统治。

column1: Our tribe-mates are suspicious of us already. Perhaps it will be better to admit fault right away.
column2: 同部落的人已经对我们起疑了。也许立即认错会更好。

column1: The other clans hold us in high regard. We should be able to persuade them that our actions were right.
column2: 其他氏族对我们很敬重。我们应该能够说服他们我们的行为是正确的。

column1: We did not kill the candidate. We merely brought \x01@J to the attention of Orlanth. Our god did the rest.
column2: 我们没有杀死候选者。我们只是让 \x01@J 引起了奥兰斯的注意。剩下的事由我们的神明来完成。

column1: Reassure \x01@\x0B with a gift.
column2: 用礼物安抚 \x01@\x0B 。

column1: We showed our loyalty with a gift.
column2: 我们用一份礼物表达了忠诚。

column1: Reassure \x01@\x0B with a poem of praise.
column2: 用一首赞美诗安抚 \x01@\x0B 。

column1: We gave voice to our loyalty, in a poem of praise.
column2: 我们用一首赞美诗发出了忠诚之声。

column1: Say little; leave as quickly as possible.
column2: 少说为妙；尽快离开。

column1: We said little, and left as soon as we could.
column2: 我们几乎没说什么，并尽快离开了。

column1: We left as soon as we could, and sent heralds to the other clans.
column2: 我们尽快离开了，并向其他氏族派去了传令官。

column1: Tell \x01@\x0B \x06 misinterprets your actions.
column2: 告诉 \x01@\x0B \x06 曲解了你的行为。

column1: Men bring war. Cows bring peace.
column2: 男人带来战争。牛只带来和平。

column1: The secret of winning a duel is to be the first to strike.
column2: 赢得决斗的秘诀是先发制人。

column1: Poetry can speak the language of peace, or thump out the drumbeat of war.
column2: 诗歌既能诉说和平之言，也能擂响战鼓。

column1: Slap this fool on the side of the head.
column2: 给这傻瓜耳刮子。

column1: There is nothing like a war within the tribe to reward the valorous and punish the weak.
column2: 没有什么比部落内部战争更能奖赏勇者、惩罚弱者了。

column1: The members of the mysterious Black Horse Troop take your clan up on its invitation to visit your tula. You lay on a feast for these weird foreigners. Their monstrous steeds are frightening to many of your people. Their manners are not quite right, but they act like people you can trust. Their leader, Sir Ethilrist, seems particularly pleased by your hospitality. “In my many years, we have met and killed many types of people. We have found that most are not friendly to outsiders. Even fewer are friendly to outsiders as warlike and formidable as myself. Your hospitality is remarkable, even for Orlanth-worshippers.”
column2: 神秘的黑马部队成员接受了你们氏族的邀请，前来拜访你们的图拉领地。你们为这些古怪的异乡人设宴款待。他们那骇人的坐骑吓得许多族人胆寒。他们的举止不太合规矩，但行事作风像是可信之人。他们的首领埃瑟里斯特爵士似乎对你们的款待格外满意：“我多年以来，遇到过并杀过许多种人。我发现大多数人对异乡人不友善。对像我这样好战而令人生畏的异乡人友善者更是寥寥。你们的好客之心实在卓绝，即便对于奥兰斯崇拜者而言也是如此。”

column1: We hosted Sir Ethilrist and his Black Horse Troop at our tula.
column2: 我们在领地上款待了埃瑟里斯特爵士和他的黑马部队。

column1: Ask for nothing.
column2: 什么也不索取。

column1: We asked them for nothing.
column2: 我们什么也没向他们索求。

column1: But as he left, Sir Ethilrist insisted on gifting us. “You must take one of our treasures, friendly ones.”
column2: 但临走时，埃瑟里斯特爵士执意要赠礼给我们。“友善之人，你们必须收下我们的一件宝物。”

column1: Ethilrist offers you your choice of the following:
column2: 埃瑟里斯特让你从以下宝物中挑选：

column1: The Bit of Kargzant, which will help bind your tribe together
column2: 卡格赞特马嚼，有助于凝聚部落

column1: We chose the Bit of Kargzant.
column2: 我们选择了卡格赞特马嚼。

column1: The Silver Lips of Anriar, which helps persuade people
column2: 安里亚银唇，有助于说服他人

column1: We chose the Silver Lips of Anriar.
column2: 我们选择了安里亚银唇。

column1: Sir Ethilrist seemed secretly amused at our choice.
column2: 埃瑟里斯特爵士似乎对我们的选择暗自觉得好笑。

column1: Ask him for help with a raid.
column2: 请他协助一次突袭。

column1: We asked Ethilrist for his help on a raid. He said we did not understand what we asked, but that he would help us if we really wanted him to.
column2: 我们请埃瑟里斯特协助一次突袭。他说我们并不清楚自己在请求什么，但如果我们真想要他帮忙，他会出手。

column1: “You do not know what you ask for,” he says. “If you truly want us to, we will raid one of your neighbors for you. But I warn you that the results will surprise you, and that we will take all of the loot. Do you truly want to be known as the clan that loosed the Black Horse Troop on a rival?”
column2: “你不知道你要求的是什么，”他说。“如果你真的希望我们这样做，我们可以为你劫掠一个你的邻居。但我警告你，结果会让你吃惊，而且我们会拿走所有战利品。你真的想让别人知道你是那个把黑马部队放出去对付对手的部族吗？”

column1: Withdraw your request.
column2: 撤回你的请求。

column1: Something in his tone caused us to reconsider, and we withdrew our request.
column2: 他语气中的某些东西让我们重新考虑，于是我们撤回了请求。

column1: Sir Ethilrist showed the ghost of a grim smile, and said, “That is best.” He thanked us for our hospitality, and the Black Horse Troop left the tula.
column2: 埃瑟里斯特爵士露出一丝冷笑，说道：“那样最好。”他感谢我们的热情款待，然后黑马部队离开了图拉领地。

column1: “Yes, this is how we wish to be known.”
column2: “是的，这正是我们希望被人所知的方式。”

column1: “Then which of your neighbors do you wish us to raid for you?”
column2: “那么你希望我们为你劫掠哪个邻居？”

column1: They slew every warrior. They took every carl and every child to be sold as thralls. They burned every stead. Every cow, every horse, every sheep, every pig was slaughtered and fed to their monstrous steeds. They placed strange implements in the temple and drained it of magic. They took the fertility from the land, and stole the spirits from the air.
column2: 他们杀死了每一个战士。他们带走了每一个自由民和每一个孩子，卖作奴隶。他们烧毁了每一处农庄。每一头牛、每一匹马、每一只羊、每一头猪都被宰杀，喂给了他们那些可怕的战马。他们在神庙里放置了奇怪的器具，吸干了其中的魔法。他们从土地中夺走了丰饶，从空气中偷走了神灵。

column1: They thanked us for the opportunity, then rode off with their new thralls, to the west. They told all they met that we were their friends.
column2: 他们感谢我们给了他们这个机会，然后带着新得的奴隶策马向西而去。他们告诉所有遇到的人我们是他们的朋友。

column1: Ask him to train some of your weaponthanes.
column2: 请他训练一些你的武器领主。

column1: We asked if they would train some of our weaponthanes.
column2: 我们问他们是否愿意训练我们的一些武器领主。

column1: Sir Ethilrist thought for a moment, and then agreed.
column2: 埃瑟里斯特爵士思考了片刻，然后同意了。

column1: How many weaponthanes do you send for training?
column2: 你派多少武器领主去接受训练？

column1: Ask if they know any useful stories of Orlanth.
column2: 问问他们是否知道任何关于奥兰斯的实用故事。

column1: We asked if they knew any useful stories of Orlanth.
column2: 我们问他们是否知道任何关于奥兰斯的实用故事。

column1: “I have heard many stories of many gods over the centuries,” Sir Ethilrist said. “But I do not wish to upset my gracious hosts by asking them which Orlanth they wish to hear about. I have met many Orlanthi, and before I sl… ah, ahem. At any rate, you can be certain that the stories I know are all foreign and strange, and no good to you.”
column2: “几个世纪以来，我听过许多关于许多神祇的故事，”埃瑟里斯特爵士说。“但我不想因为询问我的好客主人们想听哪个奥兰斯的故事而惹恼他们。我见过很多奥兰斯人，在我杀…啊，咳咳。无论如何，你们可以确定我知道的故事都是外来的、陌生的，对你们没什么用。”

column1: Offer to trade treasures with them.
column2: 提议与他们交易宝物。

column1: We asked if they wanted to trade treasures.
column2: 我们问他们是否愿意交易宝物。

column1: They agreed to trade us the Bit of Kargzant.
column2: 他们同意与我们交易卡格赞特马嚼。

column1: They agreed to trade us the Silver Lips of Anriar.
column2: 他们同意与我们交易安里亚银唇。

column1: Sir Ethilrist agreed to the exchange.
column2: 埃瑟里斯特爵士同意了交换。

column1: They frighten the carls. We should have no more to do with them.
column2: 它们让自由民感到恐惧。我们不应再与他们有瓜葛。

column1: If they were successful warriors, they’d have a permanent tula by now. They have nothing worth trading for.
column2: 如果他们是有成就的战士，他们现在应该有了一个永久的图拉领地。他们没什么值得交易的东西。

column1: Perhaps they would be willing to trade treasures with us.
column2: 也许他们会愿意与我们交易宝物。

column1: They are too strange to be of any help on a raid. Good Orlanthi fighting tactics will probably destroy them.
column2: 他们太奇怪了，在一次劫掠中帮不上忙。好的奥兰斯战斗战术可能会摧毁他们。

column1: Perhaps they have fighting secrets they might teach our weaponthanes.
column2: 也许他们有一些战斗秘诀可以教给我们的武器领主。

column1: We could send our weaponthanes to be trained by these dangerous men, but there is a good chance none would return.
column2: 我们可以派我们的武器领主去接受这些危险人物的训练，但他们极有可能一个都回不来。

column1: We might be looked down upon by others if we use these foreigners against other Orlanthi.
column2: 如果我们利用这些外人对付其他奥兰斯人，可能会被他人看不起。

column1: To hear them talk, it is clear they have won many great battles. Let us use them against our foes.
column2: 听他们说话，显然他们赢得过许多伟大战役。让我们用他们来对付我们的敌人。

column1: To hear them talk, it is clear they have slaughtered many unsuspecting foes. It would be wrong to loose them against even our worst enemies.
column2: 听他们说话，显然他们屠杀过许多毫无防备的敌人。即使是对付我们最坏的敌人，放出他们也是不对的。

column1: They may know secret stories of Orlanth that are only told in foreign places.
column2: 他们可能知道一些只有在外地才会讲述的关于奥兰斯的秘密故事。

column1: These people are not Orlanthi. Even if they know stories of Orlanth, they will get the details wrong.
column2: 这些人不是奥兰斯人。即使他们知道奥兰斯的故事，细节也会弄错。

column1: They may be foreigners, but they are great servants of Death.
column2: 他们也许是外乡人，但他们是死亡的伟大仆从。

column1: With their help, we can crush those who dare to bully us!
column2: 有了他们的帮助，我们可以碾碎那些胆敢欺凌我们的人！

column1: He could kill the lot of us, with nothing but a sharpened eyelash.
column2: 他可以用一根磨尖的眼睫毛杀死我们所有人。

column1: We must hear foreign Orlanth-tales!
column2: 我们必须听听外来的奥兰斯传说！

column1: Good hosts don’t ask for anything from their guests.
column2: 好客的主人不会向客人索取任何东西。

column1: I told you it was a good idea to invite them here.
column2: 我告诉过你邀请他们来这里是个好主意。

column1: One of the warriors we sent to train under Sir Ethilrist returned. He said that he learned many strange things and fought in many terrible fights, against many unearthly foes. He is glad to be home so he can forget all that. The other \x01@\x0B warriors were killed while fighting for Sir Ethilrist.
column2: 我们送去埃瑟里斯特爵士麾下接受训练的战士中有一个回来了。他说他学到了许多奇怪的东西，参加许多可怕的战斗，对抗许多非人的敌人。他很高兴回到家，这样他就能忘记这一切。其他 \x01@\x0B 战士在为埃瑟里斯特爵士作战时被杀死了。

column1: \x01Cn of the warriors we sent to train under Sir Ethilrist returned. They said that they learned many strange things and fought in many terrible fights, against many unearthly foes. They are glad to be home so they can forget all that. The other \x01@\x0B warriors were killed while fighting for Sir Ethilrist.
column2: \x01Cn 我们送去埃瑟里斯特爵士麾下接受训练的战士中有一部分回来了。他们说学到了许多奇怪的东西，参加许多可怕的战斗，对抗许多非人的敌人。他们很高兴回到家，这样他们就能忘记这一切。其他 \x01@\x0B 战士在为埃瑟里斯特爵士作战时被杀死了。

column1: None of the warriors we sent to train under Sir Ethilrist returned. Instead, he sent us a strange note which is hard to read. It seems to say that our weaponthanes were all too fragile for the training methods of the Black Horse Troop, and that they are all now dead.
column2: 我们送去埃瑟里斯特爵士麾下接受训练的战士一个也没有回来。相反，他给我们送来了一张难以辨认的奇怪便条。上面似乎说我们的武器领主对于黑马部队的训练方法来说都太过脆弱，现在全都死了。

column1: None of the warriors we sent to train under Sir Ethilrist returned. Instead, he sent us a strange note which is hard to read. It seems to say that our weaponthanes are happier with the Black Horse Troop, and will not be back. They send loot they have won in battle, to compensate us for the loss.
column2: 我们派去在埃瑟里斯特爵士麾下训练的战士无一人返回。相反，他寄来一张难以辨认的奇怪便条。上面似乎说我们的武器领主在黑马部队过得更快乐，不会再回来了。他们送来在战斗中夺得的战利品，作为对我们的补偿。

column1: sceneR144
column2: sceneR144

column1: Your explorers stumble across a bizarre sight to the northwest. It is a huge mountain face with a number of huge doors. Enormous statues sit outside, as if watching visitors. The big metal cylinders pointing out of the mountain face might be weapons of some kind. There is no sound coming from inside the mountain.
column2: 你的探险者在西北方偶然发现一处奇景。那是一面巨大的山壁，上面有数扇巨大的门。门外矗立着巨大的雕像，仿佛在注视来访者。从山壁中伸出的巨大金属圆柱可能是某种武器。山内没有任何声音传出。

column1: Our explorers found doors and gigantic statues on the side of a mountain.
column2: 我们的探险者在一座山的侧面发现了门和巨大的雕像。

column1: Continue to explore the area, in search of a back entrance.
column2: 继续探索该区域，寻找后门入口。

column1: We decided to keep exploring the area, in hopes of finding a back entrance.
column2: 我们决定继续探索该区域，希望能找到后门入口。

column1: The explorers saw a mine shaft, the one that they found on an earlier expedition, but it was bricked over. Clearly, the dwarves did not want any more surprise visitors.
column2: 探险者看到了一处矿井竖井——就是先前探险中发现的那个——但已被砖石封堵。显然，矮人不希望再有意外访客。

column1: Force the doors open.
column2: 强行破门。

column1: We tried to force the doors open.
column2: 我们试图强行破门。

column1: No matter how hard we pushed and pulled, no matter what kind of magic we used, the doors would not open.
column2: 无论我们如何推拉，无论使用何种魔法，大门纹丝不动。

column1: Knock on the doors.
column2: 敲门。

column1: We knocked on the doors.
column2: 我们敲了门。

column1: We thought for a moment that we heard a sound inside, but no one answered our knocks and shouts.
column2: 有那么一刻我们似乎听到里面有声响，但没人回应我们的敲门和喊叫。

column1: We left the area.
column2: 我们离开了该区域。

column1: Tell other clans about this place.
column2: 将此地告知其他氏族。

column1: We spread the news to other clans.
column2: 我们将消息散布给其他氏族。

column1: Which clans do you tell?
column2: 你要告知哪些氏族？

column1: They thanked us for the news.
column2: 他们感谢我们带来的消息。

column1: There could be magical cows inside!
column2: 里面可能有魔法牛只！

column1: Looks like an old ruin. Nothing of value there.
column2: 看上去像是一处古老废墟。没什么值钱的东西。

column1: No doubt this is a treasure trove, if only we can find our way in.
column2: 这无疑是个宝库，只要我们能找到进去的路。

column1: This is Dwarf Mine, home to those strange foreigners of the same name. Isidilian, King of the Dwarfs, was an ally of the Empire of Wyrm’s Friends.
column2: 这是矮人矿井，是那些同名异乡人的家园。矮人王伊西迪利安曾是龙之友帝国的盟友。

column1: If there are people inside, they’re foreigners, so we’re allowed to knock the door down.
column2: 如果里面住着人，那都是外乡人，所以我们有权把门砸开。

column1: If we don’t know who lives there, we must treat them with the courtesy we would expect ourselves.
column2: 如果我们不知道谁住在那里，就必须以我们期望他人对待自己的礼节相待。

column1: We could just be awakening another enemy, which we need like holes in the head.
column2: 我们可能只是唤醒另一个敌人，而这正是我们最不需要的，就像头上多个窟窿。

column1: Other clans will be offended if we interrupt them just to tell them that we’ve found a place we know nothing about.
column2: 如果我们仅仅为了告诉他们我们发现了一处一无所知的地方而打扰其他氏族，他们会感到不快。

column1: Other clans are always happy to learn the latest rumors about our strange new land.
column2: 其他氏族总是乐于得知关于我们这片陌生新土地的最新传闻。

column1: Surely there is great adventure to be had in the dungeon-like corridors of this ancient complex!
column2: 在这座古老建筑迷宫般的走廊里，必定有伟大的冒险在等待！

column1: If we had good maps from ancient times, we’d know how to get into this place.
column2: 如果我们有古代的好地图，就会知道如何进入这个地方。

column1: “When at an unknown door, only the rash rely on luck.”
column2: “面对未知之门，唯有莽撞者依赖运气。”

column1: We spent several weeks looking for another way into that cliff side. We couldn’t find one.
column2: 我们花了数周时间寻找另一条进入那片悬崖的路，但一无所获。

column1: sceneR145
column2: sceneR145

column1: The exploration party you sent to the disused mine returns to report a remarkable series of events. They fell down a hole in the shaft and found themselves in the middle of a community of Mostali, or dwarfs. (There were humans there, too, ones who acted just like dwarfs.) The underground kingdom is called Dwarf Mine. The dwarfs told your explorers that they were “ahead of schedule,” which seemed to please them. They even gained an audience with the King of the Dwarfs, Isidilian. After Isidilian asked them many questions, they were allowed to leave.
column2: 你派往废弃矿山的探险队返回，报告了一系列非凡事件。他们掉进矿井的一个洞里，发现自己置身于一个莫斯塔利（即矮人）聚居地之中。（那里也有人类，行为举止与矮人无异。）这个地下王国名叫矮人矿井。矮人告诉你的探险者，他们“提前于日程表”，这似乎令矮人们很高兴。他们甚至得以觐见矮人王伊西迪利安。伊西迪利安问了他们许多问题之后，才允许他们离开。

column1: Our explorers came back to report that they had visited the underground kingdom of the dwarfs.
column2: 我们的探险者返回报告，他们造访了矮人的地下王国。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods for protection from dwarfs.
column2: 向众神献祭以求庇护，抵御矮人。

column1: We sacrificed to the gods for protection from dwarfs.
column2: 我们向众神献祭，以求庇护，抵御矮人。

column1: The omens suggested that the gods had heard our plea.
column2: 征兆显示众神已听到我们的祈求。

column1: The omens were bad. The priests suggested that we had chosen the wrong god to sacrifice to.
column2: 征兆不祥。祭司们建议我们选错了献祭的神祇。

column1: The omens were bad. The priests said that the dwarfs must have very powerful magic.
column2: 征兆不祥。祭司们说矮人必定拥有非常强大的魔法。

column1: Send a trade delegation.
column2: 派遣贸易使团。

column1: We sent traders to Dwarf Mine.
column2: 我们向矮人矿井派出了商人。

column1: The traders spoke to the dwarfs, who spoke haltingly and seemed concerned only for something they called “the schedule.” Again and again the dwarfs suggested that our traders would soon be allowed to open negotiations. Then they would hum and say that the time was not yet right. Finally, \x01@\x05 gave up and came home.
column2: 商人与矮人交谈，矮人说话吞吞吐吐，似乎只关心他们所谓的“日程表”。矮人一再表示，不久就会允许我们的商人开始谈判。然后他们会沉吟片刻，说时机未到。最终， \x01@\x05 放弃并返回家园。

column1: Send gifts to Isidilian.
column2: 向伊西迪利安赠送礼物。

column1: We sent gifts to Isidilian.
column2: 我们向伊西迪利安赠送了礼物。

column1: How many warriors do you send along?
column2: 你派遣了多少战士同行？

column1: Our party did not meet with the Dwarf King; something called “the schedule” seemed to forbid it. However, Isidilian sent word through a pale, dwarf-like human ambassador that he was pleased by the gift.
column2: 我们的队伍未能见到矮人王；某种叫做“日程表”的东西似乎禁止了此事。不过，伊西迪利安通过一位苍白、矮人似的人类大使传来口信，说他对礼物感到满意。

column1: Spread the news to other clans.
column2: 将消息散布给其他氏族。

column1: We told other clans about these strange foreigners.
column2: 我们把这些古怪的异乡人的消息告诉了其他氏族。

column1: Which other clans do you tell?
column2: 你要告知哪些其他氏族？

column1: They were grateful for the news. Some viewed the discovery as a good omen. Others thought it meant disaster.
column2: 他们对消息表示感谢。一些人认为这个发现是好兆头。另一些人则觉得这意味着灾祸。

column1: Send \x01@t to take a treasure from them.
column2: 派遣 \x01@t 从他们那里夺取一件宝物。

column1: We sent \x01@t to try to take a treasure from them.
column2: 我们派遣 \x01@t 试图从他们那里夺取一件宝物。

column1: \x01@t returned with a valuable treasure, the Voss Varainu Tapestry.
column2: \x01@t带回了一件珍贵的宝物——沃斯·瓦莱努挂毯。

column1: Two of the warriors we sent did not return.
column2: 我们派出的战士中有两人未能归来。

column1: The warrior we sent did not return.
column2: 我们派出的那位战士未能归来。

column1: \x01@t returned with \x04 life, but not the life of the warrior we sent along. \x05 did not return with a treasure, either.
column2: \x01@t 带着 \x04 生命归来，却不是我们一并派出的那位战士的生命。 \x05 也没有带回任何宝物。

column1: \x01@t returned with \x04 life, but not the lives of half of those we sent along. \x05 did not return with a treasure, either.
column2: \x01@t 带着 \x04 生命归来，却不是我们一并派出的一半人的生命。 \x05 也没有带回任何宝物。

column1: Neither \x01@t nor the warrior we sent along on \x04 mission were ever seen again.
column2: 无论是 \x01@t 还是我们派去执行 \x04 任务的战士，都再未现身。

column1: Neither \x01@t nor the warriors we sent along on \x04 mission were ever seen again.
column2: 无论是 \x01@t 还是我们派去执行 \x04 任务的战士们，都再未现身。

column1: Cows eat dwarfs, who are deadly afraid of them.
column2: 牛吃矮人，而矮人极度畏惧牛。

column1: We can’t be giving out cows every time we find a mountain full of crazy foreigners.
column2: 我们不能每次发现一座满是疯外族的山时就分发牛只。

column1: The dwarfs may not be Orlanthi, but everyone is happy to get a gift.
column2: 矮人也许不是奥兰斯人，但收到礼物谁都高兴。

column1: We must make trade arrangements with them, before the other clans discover them.
column2: 我们必须赶在其他氏族发现他们之前，与他们达成贸易安排。

column1: Legend has it that dwarfs consider generosity and trading to be heretical.
column2: 传说中矮人视慷慨与贸易为异端。

column1: Dwarfs can be fearsome opponents. They have peculiar and powerful weapons.
column2: 矮人可以是可怕的对手。他们拥有奇特而强大的武器。

column1: Heort said that it was the responsibility of all good Orlanthi to steal treasures from dwarfs.
column2: 赫奥特说过，所有正直的奥兰斯人的责任就是从矮人那里偷取宝物。

column1: They are foreigners, and we can’t expect them to behave well.
column2: 他们是外族，我们不能指望他们行为得体。

column1: They are foreigners, and we can’t expect them to behave well. Our neighbors will appreciate good warning.
column2: 他们是外族，我们不能指望他们行为得体。我们的邻居会感激恰当的警告。

column1: The first few moments of contact between dwarfs and Orlanthi will determine relations between our peoples for a long time to come.
column2: 矮人与奥兰斯人最初接触的片刻，将决定我们两族之间未来长久的关系。

column1: The first few moments of contact between dwarfs and Orlanthi will determine relations between our peoples for centuries to come.
column2: 矮人与奥兰斯人最初接触的片刻，将决定我们两族之间未来数世纪的关系。

column1: The dwarf’s dead god Mostal was foe to Orlanth.
column2: 矮人的死亡之神莫斯塔尔是奥兰斯的敌人。

column1: The dwarf’s dead god Mostal was foe to Orlanth, because Mostal hated change, and Orlanth is the son of change.
column2: 矮人的死亡之神莫斯塔尔是奥兰斯的敌人，因为莫斯塔尔憎恨变化，而奥兰斯乃变化之子。

column1: Dwarfs are said to be ancient enemies of the perfidious elves.
column2: 据说矮人是背信弃义的精灵的宿敌。

column1: No more gifts to weird foreigners!
column2: 别再给古怪的外族送礼了！

column1: I told you dwarfs would show up sooner or later!
column2: 我告诉过你矮人迟早会出现！

column2: sceneR146

column1: Warriors from another clan sneak onto your tula at night and set fire to a stead. A few people are burned, but no one is killed. The stead is burned beyond repair, and the goods of the clan members who live there are destroyed.
column2: 另一个氏族的战士趁夜潜入你的领地，纵火烧毁了一座农庄。有几个人被烧伤，但无人丧命。农庄烧得无法修复，住在那里的氏族成员的财物也被毁。

column1: Warriors from another clan set fire to a stead, destroying it and causing injuries to the people inside it.
column2: 另一个氏族的战士纵火烧毁了一座农庄，导致屋内人员受伤。

column1: Perform a divination to identify the culprit.
column2: 进行一次占卜以找出肇事者。

column1: We performed a divination to identify the culprit.
column2: 我们进行了一次占卜以找出肇事者。

column1: The priests and priestesses examined the signs and sat for a long time with leather sheets over their heads. The Knowing God told them that the stead burners were from the \x01@! clan. They were sent by \x01CP, who thinks she was wronged by us in her recent divorce settlement.
column2: 祭司们审视了征兆，头上盖着皮革坐了很久。全知之神告知他们，纵火烧庄者来自 \x01@! 氏族。他们是奉 \x01CP之命而来，她认为自己在最近的离婚裁决中受了我们的委屈。

column1: The priests and priestesses examined the signs and sat for a long time with leather sheets over their heads. The Knowing God told them that the stead burners were from the
column2: 祭司们审视了征兆，头上盖着皮革坐了很久。全知之神告知他们，纵火烧庄者来自

column1: They were sent by \x02\x05an angry priest/crazy shamans/jealous ancestor spirits/a cruel war chief/a troublemaking Eurmali\x02 because we \x02\x06have too many cows/don’t plant the crops in straight lines/raid our neighbors too ferociously/claim too much land/have the wrong ancient enemies/tell incorrect stories about the gods.\x02
column2: 他们是奉 \x02\x05愤怒的祭司/疯狂的萨满/嫉妒的祖先之灵/残忍的战争首领/爱惹事的尤尔马里\x02 之命而来，因为我们是 \x02\x06拥有太多牛只/不将作物种成直线/过于凶猛地劫掠邻居/宣称过多土地/有错误的宿敌/讲述关于诸神的不正确故事。\x02

column1: Demand compensation.
column2: 要求赔偿。

column1: We demanded compensation from them.
column2: 我们向他们要求赔偿。

column1: The \x01@! ring listened to our claim, and spoke to their people. They discovered that \x01CP sent the stead burners. She did this because she considered herself wronged by us during her recent divorce settlement.
column2: \x01@! 议会听取了我们的申诉，并与他们的人民商议。他们发现是 \x01CP 派出了纵火烧庄者。她这么做是因为她认为自己在最近的离婚裁决中受了我们的委屈。

column1: The \x01@! ring listened to our claim, and weighed the evidence from the divination we performed.
column2: \x01@! 议会听取了我们的申诉，并权衡了我们占卜所得的证据。

column1: They compensated us for the damage done to the stead, and for the burns suffered by our people.
column2: 他们赔偿了我们农庄的损失以及族人遭受的烧伤。

column1: The \x01@! ring rejected our claim.
column2: \x01@! 议会驳回了我们的申诉。

column1: A raid was in order.
column2: 一场突袭是合宜的。

column1: Raid them, even though it is Sea season.
column2: 突袭他们，尽管眼下是海季。

column1: \x02\x03Some of the carls muttered worriedly about the crops for the upcoming year/Some of the carls fretted about having a short harvest come Earth season./Once the excitement died down, the carl began to worry about how little grain they’d planted.\x02
column2: \x02\x03一些自由民忧心忡忡地嘀咕着来年的收成/一些自由民担心地季到来时收成不足。/兴奋消退后，自由民开始担忧他们种下的谷物实在太少。\x02

column1: Raid them, even though it is Earth season.
column2: 突袭他们，尽管眼下是地季。

column1: \x02\x03Some of the carls muttered worriedly that they weren’t able to harvest enough food for the upcoming year./Some of the carls grumbled that they hadn’t had time to gather in all of the harvest, and that lean times were ahead./Once the thrill of raiding passed, the carls remembered that they had not had time to do a thorough harvest and they lamented hungry times to come.\x02
column2: \x02\x03一些自由民忧心地嘀咕他们没能为来年收获足够的粮食。/一些自由民抱怨说他们没来得及收完全部庄稼，苦日子就在前头。/突袭的刺激过后，自由民想起他们没时间彻底收割，于是哀叹即将到来的饥饿时光。\x02

column1: Make a claim against them at a tribal moot.
column2: 在部落大会上向他们提出申诉。

column1: We made a claim against them at a tribal moot.
column2: 我们在部落大会上向他们提出了申诉。

column1: I suspect \x01CP, who left us for the \x01@! clan when we did not support her absurd divorce demands. Her former husband lived in that stead.
column2: 我怀疑是 \x01CP，当初我们未支持她那荒谬的离婚要求，她便离我们而去投靠了 \x01@! 氏族。她的前夫就住在那个农庄。

column1: We should perform a divination, but examine its results carefully. Our magic is weak, and so we may misunderstand the answer the gods give us.
column2: 我们应该进行一次占卜，但要仔细审视其结果。我们的魔法很弱，因此我们可能会误解诸神给予的答案。

column1: We should perform a divination. Our magic is strong, and so we will easily be able to understand the answer the gods give us.
column2: 我们应该进行一次占卜。我们的魔法强大，因此我们将能轻易理解诸神给予的答案。

column1: Find the culprit, and ask for restitution. Don’t get involved with raiding now, when we must plant the crops.
column2: 找到肇事者，并要求赔偿。现在不要卷入掠夺，我们必须种植庄稼。

column1: Find the culprit, and ask for restitution. Don’t get involved with raiding now, when we must harvest the crops.
column2: 找到肇事者，并要求赔偿。现在不要卷入掠夺，我们必须收割庄稼。

column1: The \x01@\x02 clan is famous for wanting to impose its rule on others. It will take more than a burned stead to quell our love of freedom!
column2: \x01@\x02 氏族以想要将统治强加于他人而闻名。要平息我们对自由的热爱，可不止烧掉一个农庄那么简单！

column1: It is \x01CP, taking her revenge on us. Because this is private vengeance, the \x01@! ring will give us fair hearing.
column2: 是 \x01CP在向我们复仇。因为这是私人复仇， \x01@! 戒环会给予我们公正的听证。

column1: This is all part of some clan’s perfidious scheming for the throne.
column2: 这全是某个氏族为夺取王位而进行的背信弃义的阴谋的一部分。

column2: sceneR147

column1: The owners of the escaped thralls you adopted come to you demanding their return.
column2: 你收养的逃跑奴隶的物主们来找你，要求归还他们。

column1: The owners of the escaped thralls you took as your own come to you demanding their return.
column2: 你占为己有的逃跑奴隶的物主们来找你，要求归还他们。

column1: In halting tradetalk, they tell you that they are the Grazers, the rightful lords of these lands. They have no plans to enthrall you, at least for the moment. But they do intend to reclaim the property you have stolen from them.
column2: 他们用结巴的贸易语告诉你，他们是放牧者，是这些土地的合法领主。他们目前至少没有奴役你的计划。但他们确实打算收回你从他们那里偷走的财产。

column1: The haughty horse nomads who called themselves
column2: 那些自称为……的傲慢的马背游牧者

column1: Grazers
column2: 放牧者

column1: Grazers, but we know as the Horse-Spawn,
column2: 放牧者，但我们称之为马裔，

column1: came to reclaim the refugees we had
column2: 来要回我们曾……

column1: adopted.
column2: 收养的。

column1: enthralled.
column2: 奴役的。

column1: Attack the Grazers immediately.
column2: 立即攻击放牧者。

column1: Even these few horse-riders proved to be ferocious enemies. They fought with fiery arrows and lances. Their peculiar horses leapt through our tula like giant grasshoppers, falling among us where we least expected them. We killed the horses and their riders, but at great cost. They wore jewelry, which we added to our wealth.
column2: 就连这少数几名骑手也证明是凶猛的敌人。他们用火矢和长矛作战。他们怪异的马匹像巨型蚱蜢一样跃过我们的领地，从我们最意想不到的地方扑向我们。我们杀死了马匹和骑手，但代价惨重。他们佩戴珠宝，我们将其纳入了财富。

column1: Even these few horse-riders proved to be ferocious enemies. They fought with fiery arrows and lances. Their peculiar horses leapt through our tula like giant grasshoppers, falling among us where we least expected them. Many of our warriors were slain or wounded. The Grazers snatched up some of our leaders, taking \x01Cq away with them.
column2: 就连这少数几名骑手也证明是凶猛的敌人。他们用火矢和长矛作战。他们怪异的马匹像巨型蚱蜢一样跃过我们的领地，从我们最意想不到的地方扑向我们。我们的许多战士阵亡或负伤。放牧者掳走了我们的一些首领，将 \x01Cq 掳走了。

column1: Give the thralls back.
column2: 把奴隶还回来。

column1: We decided to return the thralls.
column2: 我们决定归还奴隶。

column1: The Grazers congratulated us on our wisdom.
column2: 放牧者恭维我们的智慧。

column1: Our own people grumbled that we made people kin and then made them not kin, as if the sacred bonds of kinship meant nothing to us.
column2: 我们自己的人抱怨我们让人成为亲族，又让人不再是亲族，仿佛神圣的亲族纽带对我们毫无意义。

column1: The carls grumbled that we gave away our property without care for the extra work they would now have to do.
column2: 自由民抱怨我们随意送掉财产，却不考虑他们现在要额外干的活。

column1: Refuse to return them.
column2: 拒绝归还。

column1: We refused to return them.
column2: 我们拒绝归还。

column1: “Low people all fools,” they said. “You pay price for is stupid.”
column2: “低贱之人全是蠢货，”他们说。“付出代价是愚蠢的。”

column1: “We sent your thralls to another clan.”
column2: “我们把你们的奴隶送到了另一个氏族。”

column1: We told them we sent the thralls to another clan.
column2: 我们告诉他们我们把奴隶送到了另一个氏族。

column1: They called us liars, and again demanded the return of their thralls.
column2: 他们骂我们是骗子，再次要求归还他们的奴隶。

column1: They swallowed our deception.
column2: 他们相信了我们的谎言。

column1: “Then tell which clan you sent our thralls,” the Grazer leader demands.
column2: “那就告诉我们，你把我们的奴隶送到了哪个氏族，”放牧者首领要求道。

column1: Refuse to name a clan.
column2: 拒绝说出氏族名。

column1: Name a clan.
column2: 说出一个氏族名。

column1: Tell them we sent the thralls to:
column2: 告诉他们我们把奴隶送到了：

column1: They seemed to share a joke with their horses, then rode off towards the \x01Cr tula.
column2: 他们似乎跟马儿开了个玩笑，然后骑马朝着 \x01Cr 领地驰去。

column1: “We’ve never seen these thralls of yours.”
column2: “我们从没见过你们的这些奴隶。”

column1: We told them we’d never seen their thralls.
column2: 我们告诉他们我们从没见过他们的奴隶。

column1: They swallowed our deception, and left our tula.
column2: 他们相信了我们的谎言，离开了我们的领地。

column1: It’s too bad the refugees couldn’t tell us much about their captors. But it’s clear these riders are foreigners.
column2: 可惜难民没能告诉我们多少关于俘获者的事。但很明显这些骑手是外族人。

column1: Those are the mangiest horses I’ve ever seen!
column2: 我从没见过这么癞皮的马！

column1: Those are fine horses.
column2: 那是些好马。

column1: There is something peculiar about those horses.
column2: 那些马有点古怪。

column1: It is against the law to lie, even to foreigners.
column2: 说谎是违背律法的，即使是对外族人。

column1: These people are foreigners. We owe them nothing.
column2: 这些人是外族人。我们不欠他们什么。

column1: These people are foreigners. We owe them nothing. We do owe obligations to our Orlanthi neighbors.
column2: 这些人是外族人。我们不欠他们什么。但我们确实欠奥兰斯族邻居情分。

column1: The gods and spirits favor us.
column2: 神与灵眷顾我们。

column1: We have called upon the gods and spirits many times of late. They are tired of hearing our pleas.
column2: 近来我们多次向神明与灵祈求。他们已听厌了我们的请愿。

column1: I’d rather lie than get kicked in the head by a great big horse.
column2: 我宁可说谎也不愿被一匹大马踢中脑袋。

column1: Bulls — strong! Horses — weak!
column2: 公牛——强壮！马——弱小！

column1: These haughty horse nomads enslave our people. They must feel the wind of Orlanth’s justice upon them!
column2: 这些傲慢的马背游牧者奴役我们的人民。他们必须感受到奥兰斯正义之风吹拂在他们身上！

column1: Dirty \x01@6 scum, that’s what they are.
column2: 肮脏的 \x01@6 渣滓，他们就是这样的人。

column1: I wonder if these people are literate.
column2: 我好奇这些人是否识字。

column1: If you want to kill and loot, get up early.
column2: 要想杀人劫掠，就得早起。

column1: If we had a tribe, we could make war on them.
column2: 如果我们有一个部落，就能向他们开战。

column1: I’ve been thinking about that attack a few weeks ago. We know the Horse-Spawn take thralls, so \x01Cq might still be alive. The Horse-Spawn live somewhere to the west. We should send explorers after them until we find their lands and discover what has happened to our clansmen.
column2: 我一直在想几周前那次袭击。我们知道马裔会掳走奴隶，所以 \x01Cq 可能还活着。马裔生活在西边的某处。我们应该派出探索者追踪他们，直到找到他们的领地，查明我们的族人遭遇了什么。

column2: sceneR148

column1: The shepherds of your clan are invited to participate in a fighting kite festival. They stamp the borders between the clans in a way that expresses Orlanth’s battling, stormy nature through friendly competition. The festival takes place over several days. Competitors use sharp edges on their kites to try to cut the strings of the other kiters. The clan that wins the most matches is thought to have the favor of Orlanth.
column2: 你们的氏族牧人受邀参加斗风筝节。他们通过友好的竞技在氏族间进行边境踩踏仪式，以此展现奥兰斯好斗又暴烈的本质。节庆持续数日。参赛者利用风筝的利刃割断对手的风筝线。赢得最多比赛的氏族被认为获得了奥兰斯的恩惠。

column1: Our shepherds took part in the fighting kite festival.
column2: 我们的牧人参加了斗风筝节。

column1: Concentrate on winning the contest.
column2: 集中精力赢得比赛。

column1: We concentrated on winning the contest.
column2: 我们集中精力赢得了比赛。

column1: Give gifts to the other clans.
column2: 向其他氏族馈赠礼物。

column1: We gave gifts to the other clans.
column2: 我们向其他氏族馈赠了礼物。

column1: How much do you give to the \x01@\x10 neighboring clans?
column2: 你愿意赠予 \x01@\x10 邻近氏族多少礼物？

column1: They expressed gratitude for our great generosity, and gave gifts in return.
column2: 他们感激于我们极大的慷慨，并回赠了礼物。

column1: They expressed gratitude for our generosity.
column2: 他们感激于我们的慷慨。

column1: Throw an elaborate feast for the other clans.
column2: 为其他氏族举办一场盛大的宴会。

column1: We threw an elaborate feast when the festival reached our own tula.
column2: 当节庆来到我们自己的图拉领地时，我们举办了一场盛大的宴会。

column1: Talk peace with the other clans.
column2: 与其它氏族进行和平谈判。

column1: We said that it was time to formalize the peace between us.
column2: 我们表示是时候让我们之间的和平正式化了。

column1: The other chieftains said that peace was good.
column2: 其他酋长说和平是好事。

column1: The other chieftains said that the border-stamping was more than enough peace, though they did not think less of us for making the suggestion.
column2: 其他酋长说边境踩踏仪式带来的和平已经足够了，不过他们并没有因我们提出这个建议而看低我们。

column1: Talk tribe-making with the other clans.
column2: 与其它氏族商讨建立部落。

column1: We used this as a chance to argue for the formation of a tribe.
column2: 我们借此机会为建立部落而争辩。

column1: Although no chieftain committed immediately to the suggestion, most seemed in some way interested.
column2: 尽管没有酋长立刻对这个提议做出承诺，但大多数人似乎都有些兴趣。

column1: Although there was no agreement on the need for a tribe, no one thought ill of us for suggesting it.
column2: 尽管大家没有就建立部落的必要性达成一致，但也无人因我们的提议而产生恶感。

column1: Our shepherds cut the most kites, and we won the contest. The other clans saw that we had the favor of Orlanth.
column2: 我们的牧人割断了最多的风筝，我们赢得了比赛。其他氏族看到我们得到了奥兰斯的恩惠。

column1: Our neighbors are in a good mood, and we have no feuds with them. We don’t need to give them cows.
column2: 我们的邻邦心情不错，我们与他们也没有世仇。我们不需要给他们牛只。

column1: This is an excellent opportunity to show our generosity. We can slaughter cows for a feast, or give them away.
column2: 这是展现我们慷慨的绝佳时机。我们可以宰牛设宴，或干脆将牛只赠出。

column1: Good relations mean good trading.
column2: 良好的关系意味着良好的贸易。

column1: We should raid them as soon as this festival is done; they won’t expect it.
column2: 我们应当节庆一结束就袭击他们；他们肯定料不到。

column1: This tradition shows that we respect each other’s borders, and can pay tribute to Orlanth’s competitive nature without shedding blood.
column2: 这个传统表明我们彼此尊重边界，并且能以不流血的方式向奥兰斯好斗的本性致敬。

column1: This is a good chance to improve our relations with our neighbors, with little risk of insulting them.
column2: 这是个改善我们与邻邦关系的良机，且几乎不会冒犯到他们。

column1: Who cares about fighting kites?
column2: 谁在乎斗风筝啊？

column1: If we win the contest, our clan magic will be stronger.
column2: 如果我们赢得比赛，我们的氏族魔法就会更强。

column1: Trying harder will not give us a better chance of winning.
column2: 再努力也不会增加我们获胜的机会。

column1: If we throw a feast, tradition requires that we slaughter many cows.
column2: 如果我们设宴，传统要求我们宰杀许多牛。

column1: When Orlanth tamed his unruly brothers, he did not fight with peaceful Kolat. Instead, their brightly-colored kites fought.
column2: 当奥兰斯驯服他那群桀骜不驯的兄弟时，他并未与平和的科拉特交手。相反，是双方色彩鲜艳的风筝在空中缠斗。

column1: If only we had the string from the first kite Orlanth made!
column2: 要是我们能有奥兰斯制作的第一只风筝上的线就好了！

column1: If we had a shrine to Vinga, we would not need border-stampings to protect us. Our women would be able to fight!
column2: 如果我们有一座供奉维加的圣坛，我们就不需要靠边境踩踏仪式来保护自己。我们的女人也能战斗！

column1: Like knifed swallows the air-flowers sailed, visiting Orlanth’s fleeces.
column2: 那些“天空之花”如同被刀锋划过的燕子般飘航，拜访了奥兰斯的云絮。

column1: sceneR149
column2: sceneR149

column1: They claim that they make the best food in all of Dragon Pass, and wish to prove it.
column2: 他们声称自己能做出巨龙隘口最好的食物，并想证明这一点。

column1: Offer to judge food cooked by others.
column2: 主动提出评判他人烹制的食物。

column1: We volunteered to serve as judges.
column2: 我们自愿担任评委。

column1: Who wins the contest?
column2: 谁赢了比赛？

column1: Everyone had to agree with us. They said the only possible fault with the \x01@! dishes was that there weren’t enough of them.
column2: 所有人都不得不认同我们的评判。他们说 \x01@! 菜肴唯一的缺点是不够多。

column1: Treat the event as a festival for your peoples’ enjoyment.
column2: 将此事当作一场让民众享乐的节日。

column1: We told our people to drink up and eat well.
column2: 我们告诉族人尽情饮用，吃好喝好。

column1: They did so, and many toasts were made to the wisdom and generosity of the ring.
column2: 他们照做了，众人频频举杯，赞颂长老会的智慧与慷慨。

column1: The people seemed to be in a stormy mood, and the fine foods prepared by the other clans did little to leaven their agitated tempers.
column2: 民众似乎情绪不佳，其他氏族准备的精致美食也未能平息他们的躁动。

column1: Try to win the contest.
column2: 尝试赢得比赛。

column1: We accepted their challenge.
column2: 我们接受了他们的挑战。

column1: We won the contest, and the other clans composed poems in honor of our cooking skills.
column2: 我们赢得了比赛，其他氏族还作诗赞颂我们的厨艺。

column1: The tasters enjoyed our food, but we did not win the contest.
column2: 品尝者很喜欢我们的食物，但我们没能赢得比赛。

column1: Our food was ridiculed by the other clans.
column2: 我们的食物遭到了其他氏族的嘲笑。

column1: Use magic to help win the contest.
column2: 使用魔法来赢得比赛。

column1: We used our magics to help us prepare food for the contest.
column2: 我们运用魔法为比赛准备食物。

column1: Sound out other chieftains about starting a tribe.
column2: 试探其他酋长关于建立部落的意向。

column1: The assembled chiefs said that we sought a tribe only because we had ambitions to be kings.
column2: 聚集的酋长们说，我们寻求建立部落不过是因为我们有当国王的野心罢了。

column1: The carls are in a good mood.
column2: 自由民心情绪好。

column1: The carls should be urged to celebrate.
column2: 应当鼓励自由民们尽情欢庆。

column1: The use of our clan magic for a mere cooking contest is frivolous and wasteful.
column2: 将我们的氏族魔法用在一场小小的烹饪比赛上，实属轻浮和浪费。

column1: The warriors have suffered many indignities of late. Allow them to make merry now.
column2: 战士们近来蒙受了许多屈辱。让他们此时尽情作乐吧。

column1: Although it seems merely jolly, this event could help improve relations with other clans.
column2: 虽然这看起来只是寻欢作乐，但这个活动有助于改善与其他氏族的关系。

column1: The other clans are likely to listen to us if we propose the formation of a tribe.
column2: 如果我们提议建立部落，其他氏族很可能会听从我们。

column1: The other clans do not love us, and are unlikely to listen to us if we propose the formation of a tribe.
column2: 其他氏族不喜欢我们，如果我们提议建立部落，他们也不太可能听从我们。

column1: Our magic is strong enough; we can rely on Ernalda’s blessing in the preparation of this feast.
column2: 我们的魔法足够强大；我们可以依靠埃娜尔达的祝福来准备这场盛宴。

column1: If we tried to use magic now, the spirits might spoil our dishes out of spite.
column2: 如果我们现在尝试使用魔法，那些精灵可能会出于怨恨而搞砸我们的菜肴。

column1: It would be cheating to use magic in a cooking contest!
column2: 在烹饪比赛中使用魔法是作弊行为！

column1: The other clans are probably using magic to prepare their food.
column2: 其他氏族大概是用魔法来准备食物的。

column1: What could be holier to Ernalda than the nourishment of the people? It would be an insult to her not to use magic.
column2: 对埃尔纳尔达来说，还有什么比滋养人民更神圣的呢？不用魔法反而是对她的侮辱。

column1: This is not a mere cooking contest! It is the founding moment of the greatest tribe that the Orlanthi have ever known!
column2: 这可不只是一场烹饪比赛！这是奥尔兰提人历史上最伟大部落的奠基时刻！

column1: If only we knew the secrets of dragonewt food!
column2: 要是我们知道龙人食物的秘密就好了！

column1: I volunteer for an eating contest!
column2: 我自愿参加大胃王比赛！

column1: The undead hate the smell of good food.
column2: 亡灵讨厌美味食物的气味。

column1: Of course we should try to win!
column2: 我们当然应该尽力取胜！

column1: Silly.
column2: 愚蠢。

column1: Perhaps someday we can bring the clans together and share all our books.
column2: 也许有一天我们能团结所有氏族，共享我们所有的书籍。

column1: This is the way the clans should always get along.
column2: 这才是氏族之间应有的相处之道。

column1: “Full bellies make long friends.”
column2: “肚饱才能交长久。”

column1: Win it.
column2: 赢下它。
