column2: 最好的事情是我们不用为此花一分钱。

column1: More food!
column2: 更多食物！

column1: I suppose cooking is something you could be proud of.
column2: 我觉得烹饪确实值得骄傲。

column1: The rest of you enjoy yourselves. I’m sizing up their weaponthanes.

column1: As we bided our time, the fighting between loyalists and rebels turned into a full-fledged war.
column2: 在我们等待时机之际，忠诚派和叛乱派之间的冲突演变成了一场全面战争。

column1: Join the rebels.
column2: 加入叛乱派。

column1: Quit the tribe.
column2: 退出部落。

column1: We quit the tribe.
column2: 我们退出了部落。

column1: Our people worried about what would happen next.
column2: 我们的人民担心接下来会发生什么。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods for peace within the tribe.
column2: 向众神献祭，祈求部落内部的和平。

column1: We sacrificed to the gods for peace within the tribe.
column2: 我们向众神献祭，祈求部落内部的和平。

column1: The priests and priestesses told us that the signs were not good. They said that the gods can only do so much to correct the folly of man.
column2: 祭司们告诉我们，征兆并不吉利。他们说，众神在纠正人类的愚蠢方面能做的也有限。

column1: We tried to mediate the dispute.
column2: 我们试图调解这场争端。

column1: Both loyalists and rebels called us fools, saying that it was too late for words.
column2: 忠诚派和叛乱派都骂我们是傻瓜，说现在动嘴已经太迟了。

column1: Now that things have gotten out of hand, the chieftains will be ready to talk.
column2: 既然事情已经失控，酋长们就该准备好谈判了。

column1: Rebels and loyalists alike think of us as cowards, opportunists, or both.
column2: 叛乱派和忠诚派都把我们看作懦夫、投机分子，或者两者都是。

column1: Rebels and loyalists alike think of us as cowards, opportunists, or both. They resent us all the more, because each side needs our help desperately.
column2: 叛乱派和忠诚派都把我们看作懦夫、投机分子，或者两者都是。他们更加憎恨我们，因为双方都急需我们的帮助。

column1: We will be destroyed, whatever side we join.
column2: 无论我们加入哪一边，都会被毁灭。

column1: The rebels will probably win.
column2: 叛乱派很可能会赢。

column1: We are legally bound to join the rebels.
column2: 我们在法律上有义务加入叛乱派。

column1: We are a people of law. Yet we are often left without the means to enforce those laws.
column2: 我们是遵从法律的民族。然而，我们常常没有执行那些法律的手段。

column1: There is a magic solution.
column2: 有一个魔法般的解决办法。

column1: The gods have great power, but they cannot alter the folly of man.
column2: 众神拥有伟大的力量，却无法改变人类的愚蠢。

column1: Maybe it’s not too late to avoid this bloodshed during the time Ernalda set aside for us to work our fields.
column2: 趁着埃尔纳尔达为我们留出耕耘田地的时间，也许现在避免这场流血还不算太晚。

column1: Loyalty is the most important virtue.
column2: 忠诚是最重要的美德。

column1: If only we had acted earlier in the name of peace!
column2: 要是我们早点以和平的名义行动就好了！

column1: I’ve said all along that a tribe was a foolish idea, doomed to end in a bad way. Let us be free of it, now.
column2: 我一直都说部落是个愚蠢的主意，注定没有好下场。现在就让我们摆脱它吧。

column1: We must put our faith in Orlanth, the first and greatest king.
column2: 我们必须相信奥兰斯——第一位也是最伟大的国王。

column1: It is never too late to make peace.
column2: 谋求和平永远不嫌晚。

They also insist that you must pay 5 cows each to the other clans of the tribe, as a penalty for flouting the terms of tribal confederation. Finally, they insist on being allowed to rebuild their tavern.
column2: 你的女人烧了他们的酒馆，你却毫无作为。他们要求赔偿20头牛。他们还坚持你必须向部落的其他氏族各支付5头牛，作为藐视部落联盟条款的罚金。最后，他们坚持要求允许他们重建酒馆。

column1: although you paid damages, you did not let them rebuild when your women burned their tavern. They insist that you must pay 5 cows each to the other clans of the tribe, as a penalty for flouting the terms of tribal confederation. Of course, they also insist on being allowed to rebuild their tavern.
column2: 尽管你支付了赔偿，但当你的女人烧了他们的酒馆时，你却不让他们重建。他们坚持你必须向部落的其他氏族各支付5头牛，作为藐视部落联盟条款的罚金。当然，他们也坚持要求允许他们重建酒馆。

column1: Compensate them and pay the fine they suggest.
column2: 赔偿他们并支付他们提出的罚金。

column1: “Taverns are bad. No clan should have one.”
column2: “酒馆不是好东西。没有氏族该开酒馆。”

column1: Before the moot, we said: “Taverns are bad. No clan should have one.”
column2: 在大会之前，我们说：“酒馆不是好东西。没有氏族该开酒馆。”

column1: The other clans said that we had not proved that taverns were bad. We were ordered to pay the compensation and fine, and had to allow the rebuilding of the tavern.
column2: 其他氏族说我们没能证明酒馆不是好东西。我们被命令支付赔偿和罚金，并且必须允许重建酒馆。

column1: “The tavern causes trouble between our men and women.”
column2: “酒馆在我们的男人和女人之间惹麻烦。”

column1: Before the moot, we said: “The tavern causes trouble between our men and women.”
column2: 在大会之前，我们说：“酒馆在我们的男人和女人之间惹麻烦。”

column1: The other clans said problems between men and women began back in the Godtime, even before Orlanth first wooed Ernalda. The taverns caused problems in their tulas, too, but they did not complain about it. Nor did they complain about paying compensation when their women burned taverns. We were ordered to pay the compensation and fine, and had to allow the rebuilding of the tavern.
column2: 其他氏族说男女之间的麻烦从神代就开始了，甚至在奥兰斯第一次追求埃尔纳尔达之前。酒馆在他们的图拉领地上也惹麻烦，但他们并没有抱怨。当他们的女人烧了酒馆时，他们也没有抱怨支付赔偿的事。我们被命令支付赔偿和罚金，并且必须允许重建酒馆。

column1: “The tavern drains too much wealth from us.”
column2: “酒馆从我们这里榨走了太多财富。”

column1: Before the moot, we argued: “The tavern drains too much wealth from us.”
column2: 在大会之前，我们争辩说：“酒馆从我们这里榨走了太多财富。”

column1: “The tavern ruined our clan magic.”
column2: “酒馆毁掉了我们的氏族魔法。”

column1: Our herds are dwindling. Careful not to pay more in gifts to the others than we would in compensation.
column2: 我们的畜群正在减少。小心别在礼物上花得比赔偿更多。

column1: We are wealthy now, and should spend our wealth to get rid of that tavern. If we let them rebuild it, we will lose many cows over the long run.
column2: 我们现在很富有，应该花钱摆脱那家酒馆。如果我们让他们重建，长期下去我们会损失很多头牛。

column1: Although they dare not say it, the other chieftains want to get rid of the taverns on their tulas, too.
column2: 虽然他们不敢说出来，但其他酋长也想除掉自家图拉领地里的酒馆。

column1: The other chieftains can see that we are being asked to pay compensation twice over. They will fear such a thing might happen to them, and help us renegotiate this tavern trouble.
column2: 其他酋长能看出我们正在被要求支付双倍补偿。他们会担心自己也可能遭遇这种事，于是帮助我们重新协商这起酒馆纠纷。

column1: Taverns are contrary to custom, but we put them into our terms of tribal confederation.
column2: 酒馆有违习俗，但我们将其纳入了部落联盟的条款。

column1: Taverns are contrary to custom; the sinister Dragon Empire had them.
column2: 酒馆有违习俗；邪恶的龙帝帝国曾有酒馆。

column1: Taverns are contrary to custom, and interfere with the sacred relationship between men and women.
column2: 酒馆有违习俗，还会干扰男女之间的神圣关系。

column1: We may not like it, but we did agree to having taverns during tribal confederation.
column2: 我们或许不喜欢，但在部落联盟期间，我们确实同意了设立酒馆。

column1: The other chieftains think that we are troublemakers; we are unlikely to get a fair hearing.
column2: 其他酋长认为我们是惹是生非的人；我们不太可能得到公正的听证。

column1: We have proven ourselves to the tribe again and again. They will support us, even if our claim is weak.
column2: 我们一次又一次地向部落证明了自己。他们会支持我们，即使我们的诉求并不充分。

column1: We have proven ourselves to the tribe again and again. They will follow us if we argue that all taverns should be eliminated.
column2: 我们一次又一次地向部落证明了自己。如果我们主张应当铲除所有酒馆，他们会追随我们。

column1: Their god-talkers will know that our magic is strong, so we can’t argue that it is weak.
column2: 他们的神言者知道我们的魔法强大，所以我们不能硬说它薄弱。

column1: Their god-talkers will know that our magic is weak, and no one can say for sure that the tavern did not cause this.
column2: 他们的神言者知道我们的魔法薄弱，而且没人能肯定酒馆没有造成这件事。

column1: What! These rogues mean to bamboozle us into paying twice — nothing for them now, I say, and nothing ever again!
column2: 什么！这些恶棍想糊弄我们付双倍钱——我说，现在一文不给，以后也一文不给！

column1: If the tavern is rebuilt, it will be reburned.
column2: 如果酒馆重建，它会被再次烧毁。

column1: The taverns are fine. The women are the ones who need to be put in their place.
column2: 酒馆没问题。需要被管好的女人。

column1: At a tribal moot, the \x01@! clan announced that their alliance with us was over, and that they were leaving the tribe. They blamed us, in part, for their decision to leave.
column2: 在一次部落大会上， \x01@! 部族宣布他们与我们的联盟结束，他们要离开部落。他们把离开的决定部分归咎于我们。

column1: At a tribal moot, the \x01@! clan announced that they were leaving the tribe. They blamed us, in part, for their decision to leave.
column2: 在一次部落大会上， \x01@! 部族宣布他们要离开部落。他们把离开的决定部分归咎于我们。

column1: “Good riddance to bad cabbage!”
column2: “谢天谢地总算走了！”

column1: “Good riddance to bad cabbage!” we said.
column2: “谢天谢地总算走了！”我们说道。

column1: They questioned the legitimacy of our ancestors, and then told us that they intended that the place of our next meeting should be a battlefield.
column2: 他们质疑了我们祖先的正统性，然后告诉我们，他们打算让我们下次会面的地方变成一个战场。

column1: Offer them gifts if they will stay.
column2: 如果他们愿意留下，就赠送礼物给他们。

column1: We offered them gifts if they would agree to stay.
column2: 我们提出如果他们同意留下，就赠送礼物。

column1: Our generosity made them reconsider their decision, and they remained in the tribe.
column2: 我们的慷慨让他们重新考虑了自己的决定，于是他们留在了部落中。

column1: They said that our offer was a starving cow, delivered late.
column2: 他们说我们的馈赠是一头瘦牛，还姗姗来迟。

column1: Persuade them that it is in their best interests to remain.
column2: 说服他们留下来符合他们自身的最佳利益。

column1: We said that they would be better off within the tribe than outside it.
column2: 我们说他们留在部落内比在外面更好。

column1: Our wise words caused them reconsider their decision, and they remained in the tribe.
column2: 我们明智的话语让他们重新考虑了自己的决定，于是他们留在了部落中。

column1: They said that our clan still maintained its love of empty words. They would not be persuaded.
column2: 他们说我们部族还是老样子，只会说空话。他们不会被说服。

column1: Threaten them with raids if they leave.
column2: 威胁他们说如果离开就会遭到袭击。

column1: We told them that they would be raided if they left.
column2: 我们告诉他们，如果离开就会遭到袭击。

column1: They became quiet. Their features reddened. They agreed to remain in the tribe.
column2: 他们安静下来，脸色涨红。他们同意留在部落中。

column1: They said that they would find a new tribe, one that would tear our tribe to ribbons.
column2: 他们说他们会找到一个新部落，一个能把我们部落撕成碎片的部落。

column1: Wish them well.
column2: 祝他们一切顺利。

column1: We wished them well.
column2: 我们祝他们一切顺利。

column1: They thanked us, and said they hoped the place of our next meeting would not be a battlefield.
column2: 他们感谢了我们，并说希望我们下次会面的地方不是战场。

column1: We won’t deserve the Ten Year Ring if our tribe disintegrates around us.
column2: 如果我们的部落在我们身边分崩离析，我们就不配拥有十年之环。

column1: It is all a ruse to extort cows from us — cows we can ill-afford to give.
column2: 这全是敲诈我们牛只的诡计——而这些牛我们根本给不起。

column1: No one can remain angry when newly-acquired cows are mooing in his stead.
column2: 当新到手的牛在他地盘上哞哞叫时，没人能继续愤怒下去。

column1: If they are without a tribe, they are vulnerable. This is our best argument.
column2: 如果他们没有部落，他们就很脆弱。这是我们的最佳论据。

column1: It is illegal for them to leave unless their chief carries a sheep three times around the tribal hall.
column2: 除非他们的酋长扛着一头羊绕部落大厅三圈，否则他们离开是非法的。

column1: If they leave, all of the conditions their clan imposed on the tribe at confederation are forgotten. We must decide if it is in our advantage for them to leave.
column2: 如果他们离开，他们部族在联盟时施加给部落的所有条件都将被遗忘。我们必须判断让他们离开是否对我们有利。

column1: If they leave, our tribe will find it harder to win wars.
column2: 如果他们离开，我们的部落将更难赢得战争。

column1: Good riddance to bad cabbage!
column2: 谢天谢地总算走了！

column1: In the game of tribes, you can’t have winners unless you also have losers.
column2: 在部落的游戏里，有赢家就必然有输家。

column1: The moss that grows on the trees on their tula has affected their judgment.
column2: 他们图拉领地上树木长出的苔藓影响了他们的判断。

column1: It would be disastrous to allow them to leave!
column2: 允许他们离开将是灾难性的！

column1: If this is their decision, we must honor it.
column2: 如果这是他们的决定，我们必须尊重。

column1: Every clan has the right to do what they think is best for themselves, whether we agree or not.
column2: 每个部族都有权利做他们认为对自己最有利的事，无论我们同意与否。

column1: With such disloyal thoughts and words, why should we wish them to stay in the tribe?
column2: 怀着如此不忠的想法和言辞，我们为什么还希望他们留在部落里？

column1: This is a direct insult to our leadership, and we must take strong measures against them.
column2: 这是对我们领导力的直接侮辱，我们必须对他们采取强硬手段。

column1: Announce a heroquest.
column2: 宣布一场英雄探索。

column1: All of the clans said that this would be a good thing.
column2: 所有部族都说这是一件好事。

column1: Give gifts to all clans.
column2: 向所有部族赠送礼物。

column1: How much do you distribute among the tribe?
column2: 你在部落中分发多少（牛只）？

column1: The complaining clans had scarcely taken their gifts when their grumbling began anew.
column2: 抱怨的部族刚接过礼物，他们的怨声就又开始响起。

column1: Give gifts to dissatisfied clans.
column2: 向不满的部族赠送礼物。

column1: Those who had loyally served complained that disloyalty was rewarded and fealty ignored.
column2: 那些忠诚效力的部族抱怨说，不忠得到了奖赏，而忠诚却被忽视。

column1: Tell the chiefs of the dissatisfied clans to rein in their warriors, or else.
column2: 告诉不满部族的酋长们约束好他们的武士，否则后果自负。

column1: The complaining chieftains were silent, but seemed to collude among one another for ill purpose.
column2: 抱怨的酋长们沉默了，但似乎彼此之间在密谋不轨。

column1: “There is nothing wrong with a little friendly fighting.”
column2: “友好切磋一下没什么问题。”

column1: Some of the clans seemed mollified by this answer.
column2: 一些部族似乎对这个回答感到缓和。

column1: Propose a war to unite the clans.
column2: 提议发动一场战争来团结各部落。

column1: Who do you propose to make war on?
column2: 你提议向谁开战？

column1: Beastfolk
column2: 兽人

column1: The Horse-Spawn
column2: 马裔

column1: All agreed to a war, when the next Fire season came.
column2: 众人一致同意，待下一个火之季来临便开战。

column1: Kings are measured by their generosity. Thankfully, we are able to give.
column2: 君王以慷慨来衡量。幸好，我们尚能施予。

column1: We are \x02\x03kingly/rich/wealthy\x02 enough to answer one complaint directly. Gift them.
column2: 我们 \x02\x03仁慈/富裕/富足\x02 得足以直接回应一项怨言。赠礼给他们。

column1: Kings are measured by their generosity, but we are poor. We must give only what we absolutely need to give.
column2: 君王以慷慨来衡量，但我们贫困。只能给出绝对必要之物。

column1: If we must give them gifts, part with the least amount we can spare.
column2: 若必须赠礼，就拿出我们能省下的最少部分。

column1: A little veiled threat never hurt anyone.
column2: 略加威胁，从未伤人。

column1: They posture and complain, but must know that a genuine fight with the loyal clans would do them no good.
column2: 他们虚张声势、满口抱怨，但一定明白与忠诚氏族真刀真枪地干对他们没好处。

column1: If we war with the grumblers, we will lose. We must find an outside enemy, like the trolls.
column2: 若与抱怨者开战，我们会输。必须找一个外部敌人，比如巨魔。

column1: If we war with the grumblers, we will lose. We must find an outside enemy, like the \x01Á.
column2: 若与抱怨者开战，我们会输。必须找一个外部敌人，比如 \x01Á.

column1: If we war with the grumblers, we will lose. We must find an outside enemy, like the Beastfolk.
column2: 若与抱怨者开战，我们会输。必须找一个外部敌人，比如兽人。

column1: If fight an outside enemy and win, the tribe will reunite. If we lose, they will at least be consumed for a while with hatred for our common foe.
column2: 若与外部敌人交战并获胜，部落将重新团结。若落败，他们至少也会因仇恨共同敌人而消停一阵。

column1: They will be insulted by gifts.
column2: 赠礼只会侮辱他们。

column1: Give generously, but shrewdly.
column2: 慷慨但精明地给予。

column1: A successful heroquest could quell the complainers and give heart to the loyal clans.
column2: 一场成功的英雄任务能平息抱怨者，并给忠诚氏族以鼓舞。

column1: The clans who have been taking the blows of the grumblers will be affronted if do not we reward them, as well.
column2: 那些一直承受抱怨者打击的氏族，若我们不同样嘉奖他们，定会感到冒犯。

column1: There is a chance that these passions will defuse of their own accord.
column2: 这些怒火或许会自行平息。

column1: There is a small chance that these passions will defuse on their own, but a quest is more likely to reconcile these angry hearts.
column2: 这些怒火自行平息的机会微乎其微，但一次任务更有可能调和这些愤怒的心。

column1: There is a chance that these passions will defuse of their own accord. But it is a small one.
column2: 这些怒火或许会自行平息，但几率很小。

column1: A quest would make each clan contribute and each clan benefit. If we succeed, that is.
column2: 一次任务能让每个氏族贡献力量，每个氏族获益——前提是我们成功。

column1: The clans need a common goal — or at least something to distract them from their squabbling.
column2: 氏族需要一个共同的目标——或至少能分散他们对争吵的注意力。

column1: Each clan will contribute to the quest, and, if we succeed, the tribe will become some greater thing than the clans in it.
column2: 每个氏族都将为任务贡献，而一旦成功，部落将超越内部各氏族，成为更伟大的存在。

column1: We need something to overshadow these petty complaints.
column2: 我们需要能盖过这些琐碎抱怨的东西。

column1: This grumbling is just letting off a little beer-induced steam.
column2: 这些咕哝不过是借着酒劲儿撒气罢了。

column1: Sometimes a fighter needs a stern word, well-placed.

column1: I told you we should have taken strong action to quell these dissenters.

column1: “How dare you suggest such villainy! Begone!”
column2: “你怎敢提出如此恶行！滚开！”

column1: We sent the dastardly swine on their way.
column2: 我们把这卑鄙的猪猡赶走了。

column2: 他们走时说要痒我们十四夜。我们有些人痒了，其他人没有。

column2: “弄瘸他们的马要多少钱？”

column2: 我们无法满足他们的最低要价，被迫谢绝了他们的提议。

column2: 我们试图讨价还价，但他们咬定价格不松口。

column1: Decline their offer.
column2: 谢绝他们的提议。

column2: 我们谢绝了他们的提议。

column2: 灵魂之伤，可如刀剑般深。

column2: 驱使灵魂攻击敌族，与用剑刃沾染他们鲜血相比，并无更恶。当然，敌族可不这么看。

column1: If they ever find out that we withered their sword-arms, they will hate us bitterly.
column2: 一旦他们发现是我们枯萎了他们的持剑之臂，便会恨我们入骨。

column2: 若我们枯萎了他们的持剑之臂，他们就无法劫掠我们，而我们劫掠他们时便拥有了优势。

column1: If nearby clans hear that we have chastised these crude shamans, they will think us honorable and good.
column2: 若邻近氏族听说我们惩戒了这些粗野的萨满，他们会认为我们光荣而良善。

column1: Our magic is strong. \x01@! divinations will not point towards us.
column2: 我们的魔法强大。 \x01@! 占卜术无法指向我们。

column1: Our magic is weak. \x01@! divinations may point towards us.
column2: 我们的魔法弱小。 \x01@! 占卜术可能指向我们。

column1: There is no worse thing we can do to them than make their crops fail.
column2: 我们能对他们做的最恶之事，莫过于让他们的庄稼绝收。

column1: This could start an endless cycle of attacks by spirits!
column2: 这可能会引发灵魂攻击的无尽循环！

column1: We should only give them wealth \x02\x02after/once\x02 we know their curses have succeeded.
column2: 我们只应在 \x02\x02得知他们的诅咒成功后/一旦\x02 得知他们的诅咒成功，再给他们财富。

column1: “A spirit’s curse is but a gnat’s bite to the devout man.”
column2: “虔诚者眼中，灵魂的诅咒不过蚊蚋之叮。”

column1: Spirit-talkers are frequently willing to bargain.
column2: 灵语者通常愿意议价。

column1: The revenge we bought from the shamans has borne fruit. \x01@!’s crops have failed.
column2: 我们从萨满那里买来的复仇已结出果实。 \x01@!的庄稼绝收了。

column1: They performed a divination, and blame us for sending bad spirits against them.
column2: 他们进行了一次占卜，并指责我们派恶灵对付他们。

column1: They performed a divination to find who had sent bad spirits against them, but do not seem to suspect us.
column2: 他们进行了一次占卜以查明是谁派恶灵对付他们，但似乎并未怀疑我们。

column1: Shamans return to your tula. “You are prosperous now. You may not know this, but it is partly our doing. You treated us politely, and we told the spirits hereabouts not to disturb you. We told some of them of your generosity, and the great deeds of your ancestors. The life of a shaman is a hard one, and…” The shaman’s voice trails off expectantly.
column2: 萨满们返回你的领地。“你们如今繁荣昌盛。你们可能不知，但这其中也有我们的功劳。你们待我们以礼，我们便告知此地的灵魂不要打扰你们。我们还将你们的慷慨与先祖们的伟业告知了其中一些灵魂。萨满的生活艰辛，而……”萨满的声音期待地低了下去。

column1: Shamans came to our tula and took credit for our prosperity.
column2: 萨满们来到我们的领地，将我们的繁荣归功于自己。

column1: Give them a share of your clan magic.
column2: 赐予他们一部分氏族魔法。

column1: We gave them a share of our clan magic.
column2: 我们赐予了他们一部分氏族魔法。

column1: The lead shaman said, “We are shamans. Magic is something we have no shortage of. Here,” he continued, waving his wrist as if tying an invisible knot, “it is so common to us that we shall give you some more. We appreciate your gesture, nonetheless.” He continued to stand before us, expectation in his voice and eyes.
column2: 首席萨满说道：“我们是萨满。魔法是我们从不短缺之物。喏，”他继续道，挥动手腕仿佛在打一个无形的结，“这对我们而言太过平常，我们愿多赠予你们一些。不过，我们仍感激你们的心意。”他继续站在我们面前，声音与眼神中充满期待。

column1: Give them a treasure.
column2: 赐予他们一件宝物。

column1: Which treasure do you give to them?
column2: 你赐予他们哪件宝物？

column1: We offered them a Spirit Fetch, which seemed to offend them.
column2: 我们赠予他们一件灵魂唤引，但这似乎冒犯了他们。

column1: “Fools! Idiots! If you don’t value what we’ve given you, we can take it back.”
column2: “蠢货！白痴！若你们不珍视我们赐予之物，我们大可收回。”

column1: We gave them the treasure known as\x01@\x01\x01@\x14. They thanked us profusely, and said they would continue to urge the spirits to aid us.
column2: 我们将名为\x01@\x01\x01@\x14的宝物赐予了他们。他们感激不尽，并表示将继续劝导灵魂助佑我们。

column1: Give them hospitality and send them on their way.
column2: 以好客款待他们，然后送他们上路。

column1: We gave them hospitality and sent them on their way.
column2: 我们以好客款待了他们，然后送他们上路。

column1: The shamans noisily and enthusiastically ate our food and drank our drinks. When it became clear to them that we intended to gift them no further, the lead shaman shook his head. “How sad ingratitude is,” he said, departing. “How disappointed the spirits will be.”
column2: 萨满们喧闹而热情地吃喝我们的食物与饮品。当他们明白我们无意再赠予时，首席萨满摇了摇头。“忘恩负义何其可悲，”他边说边离去，“灵魂该有多失望啊。”

column1: Give them wealth.
column2: 赐予他们财富。

column1: They waited expectantly for our gift. When they saw what we chose to give them, they seemed less than pleased. “How unfortunate,” said the lead shaman, departing. “We have lost our bet with the spirits. You are as miserly as they said you would be.”
column2: 他们期待地等待着我们的赠礼。看到我们选择给予之物时，他们似乎并不太满意。“真不幸，”首席萨满说道，转身离去，“我们与灵魂打赌输了。你们正如他们所说那般吝啬。”

column1: They thanked us profusely, and said they would continue to urge the spirits to aid us.
column2: 他们感激不尽，并表示将继续劝导灵魂助佑我们。

column1: “Our struggle has been hard. We saw no spirits aid us.”
column2: “我们的奋斗一直艰难。我们未见任何灵魂相助。”

column1: We told them, “Our struggle has been hard. We saw no spirits aid us.”
column2: 我们告诉他们：“我们的奋斗一直艰难。我们未见任何灵魂相助。”

column1: The lead shaman waggled his head mournfully. “The spirits will not be pleased to hear that you doubt them.” He departed, reciting a famous poem about a proud clan whose prosperity did not last.
column2: 首席萨满悲恸地摇着头。“灵魂听到你们怀疑他们，不会高兴的。”他背诵着一首关于某个骄傲氏族繁荣未能持久的著名诗篇，转身离去。

column1: Our cows are fat and happy because of our hard work, not due to the efforts of a pair of scraggly strangers.
column2: 我们的牛只肥壮欢快，是因为我们的辛勤劳作，而非两个邋遢陌生人的努力。

column1: We are prosperous. We can afford to reward them.
column2: 我们繁荣昌盛。我们负担得起奖赏他们。

column1: Our prosperity is due to the shrewd bargaining of our traders, not the invisible spritings of the spirits.
column2: 我们的繁荣得益于商人的精明议价，而非灵魂那看不见的幽影把戏。

column1: We can afford to spare a treasure.
column2: 我们还能匀出一件宝物。

column1: They are Strangers, not Foreigners. We can expect them to respect our laws of hospitality.
column2: 他们是陌客，而非外族人。我们可以期望他们尊重我们的好客律法。

column1: Our crops are plentiful because the carls break their backs to plant and weed and harvest them. I see no spirits laboring on our behalf.
column2: 我们的庄稼丰收，是因为自由民们弯腰弓背地播种、除草、收割。我未见任何灵魂为我们劳作。

column1: Our bins are overflowing with grain. What matter if they do not quite deserve it? Give anyway.
column2: 我们的粮仓堆满了谷物。即便他们并不完全应得，那又何妨？照给不误。

column1: It is always hard to tell what things are attributable to the actions of spirits, and which to the labor of men and women.
column2: 哪些归于灵魂之作为，哪些归于男女之辛劳，向来难以分辨。

column1: Maybe they helped us, maybe they didn’t. But they can definitely harm us if we offend them.
column2: 也许他们帮了我们，也许没有。但若我们冒犯他们，他们定能加害我们。

column1: King Urgrain’s lands were prosperous for a week. Then shamans came and took credit, and he beheaded them. That was the beginning of the end for Bad King Urgrain.
column2: 恶王乌格兰的领地繁荣了一周。随后萨满前来邀功，他便斩了他们的首。这便是恶王乌格兰末路的开端。

column1: This is nothing more than barefooted, stink-breathed extortion!
column2: 这不过是光脚臭嘴的敲诈勒索！

column1: What better object for our generosity than the spirits?
column2: 还有什么比献给灵体更能彰显我们慷慨的呢？

column1: Share our wealth, not our treasures.
column2: 分享我们的财富，而非我们的宝物。

column1: But what have they done to keep the elves away?
column2: 但他们又做了什么来阻止精灵靠近？

column1: Our ancestral spirits were beset by hostile spirits sent by those shamans, but managed to drive them all away.
column2: 我们的先祖之灵曾遭那些萨满派来的敌意灵体围攻，但最终将它们全部驱离。

column1: They say the shrine we built to house them served as a strong fortress against the attack.
column2: 据说我们为安置它们而建的圣所，在袭击中充当了坚固堡垒。

column2: 神言者将皮毡蒙在头上，终于告诉我们它将会在 \x02\x06林间空地/树丛中/大锅里/朋友中间/雷暴时/一堆金币旁\x02被找到。他们说任何试图寻回它的人都将安然无恙。

column2: 我们向诸神献祭，以求护佑免遭偷窃。

column1: They never returned.

column1: Treasures come and treasures go. The important thing is that they circulate through the world, encouraging good trading.
column2: 宝物来去如流水。重要的是它们在世间流通，促进良好的贸易。

column1: Our warriors are only willing to take reasonable risks to recover this treasure. There are more important things to protect.
column2: 我们的战士只愿意冒合理的风险去寻回这件宝物。有更重要的东西需要守护。

column1: If we had better patrols, this never would have happened.
column2: 若我们的巡逻队更得力些，这事本不会发生。

column1: The gods cannot protect us from what has already happened, for they are as bound by Time as the rest of us.
column2: 众神无法护我们免于已然发生之事，因他们和我们一样受制于时间。

column1: Our magic is strong. If we perform a divination, our god-talkers will correctly understand the sendings of the gods.
column2: 我们的法术强盛。若进行占卜，神言者必能正确领会诸神的启示。

column2: 我们的法术微弱。若进行占卜，神言者很可能混淆诸神传达的真相。

column1: Our fields need our attention — we should lure the treasure home, not send good farmers off to pursue it.
column2: 田地需要我们的照看——我们应引诱宝物回家，而非让好农夫们追出去。

column1: A magical treasure must be treated like it was a chieftain held prisoner by enemies!
column2: 一件魔法宝物，必须像对待被敌人囚禁的酋长一样慎重！

column1: You have to admire their spunk, stealing it right from under our noses like that.
column2: 你不得不佩服他们的胆量，竟敢就这样从我们眼皮底下偷走它。

column1: If the gods cannot help us with this theft, they can protect us from future ones.
column2: 若诸神无法助我们应对此次失窃，他们至少能护佑我们免于未来的窃案。

column1: Of course we must try to recover it! Otherwise, they’ll come and steal more treasures from us!
column2: 当然必须设法寻回！否则他们会再来偷走更多宝物！

column1: Offer a reward. Even if we fail to recover\x01@\x01\x01@\x14, people will know that we are prosperous.
column2: 提供悬赏。即使我们未能寻回\x01@\x01\x01@\x14，人们也会知晓我们繁荣昌盛。

column1: Temples provide solace at a time of loss.

column2: 族人们说，是时候解救被马裔奴役的同胞了。

column2: 你首次召集外部战士队伍的行动失败了。你的族人仍然希望你做些什么来解救他们被奴役的同胞。

column2: 族人们问，他们仍被马裔扣押的同胞该如何处理。

column2: 一支侦察队返回报告，他们看到了被马裔带走的氏族成员。他们未被马背游牧者发现，并且知道如何返回那个关押我们族人为奴的马裔营地。

column1: Explorers found the encampment where Horse-Spawn held our people as thralls.
column2: 侦察者找到了马裔关押我们族人为奴的营地。

column1: Hire warriors from other clans to rescue your clan members.

column1: The hired warriors were successful.

column1: and some of our clansmen were returned to us.

column2: 任务成功了，

column2: 派遣一支营救队去解救马裔定居点中的所有奴隶。

column1: We sent a rescue party to free all thralls held by the Horse-Spawn.
column2: 我们派遣了一支营救队去解救所有被马裔关押的奴隶。

column1: and some of our clansmen were returned to us. Other thralls were freed as well, and they promised to praise us to their clan chieftains. Some of our warriors were wounded, but none were killed or taken to be thralls.
column2: 我们的一些族人回到了我们身边。其他奴隶也被释放了，他们承诺会向他们的氏族酋长赞扬我们。我们的一些战士受了伤，但无人被杀或被俘为奴。

column1: and the rest of our people were returned to us. Other thralls were freed as well, and they promised to praise us to their clan chieftains. Some of our warriors were wounded, but none were killed or taken to be thralls.
column2: 其余族人都回到了我们身边。其他奴隶也被释放了，他们承诺会向他们的氏族酋长赞扬我们。我们的一些战士受了伤，但无人被杀或被俘为奴。

column1: The mission failed. Some of our warriors returned to tell us that the others had been taken as thralls. The leader of the mission, \x01@\x14, was taken as a thrall, too.
column2: 任务失败了。我们的一些战士回来告诉我们，其他人已被抓为奴隶。任务的领导者 \x01@\x14也被抓为奴隶。

column1: Tell the clan that you can’t risk losing any more people.
column2: 告诉氏族，你不能冒险再失去更多人了。

column1: The ring said that they could not afford to risk further losses, and would not send a rescue party.
column2: 长老会说他们无法承受更多的损失，不会派遣营救队。

column1: The people were not encouraged by these words, but accepted them as true.
column2: 人们听到这些话并未受到鼓舞，但接受这是事实。

column1: The people wept and wailed when they heard this.
column2: 人们听到后哭泣哀嚎。

column1: “We will rescue them when we are stronger.”
column2: “等我们更强大了再去救他们。”

column1: The people said that they looked forward to the day when we would smash the Horse-Spawn and rescue our people from their shameful state of servitude.
column2: 人们说他们期待有一天我们能粉碎马裔，将我们的族人从可耻的奴役状态中解救出来。

column1: We can’t afford to pay someone else to do this for us.
column2: 我们付不起钱让别人替我们做这件事。

column1: We can afford to pay someone else to do this for us.
column2: 我们付得起钱让别人替我们做这件事。

column1: We have enough wealth now to make good on our promise.
column2: 我们现在有足够的财富来兑现我们的承诺。

column1: Our herds are fat, our storehouses are full. We can tray again to attract good fighters to rescue our kin.
column2: 我们的畜群肥壮，粮仓丰满。我们可以再次尝试吸引优秀的战士来营救我们的亲人。

column1: No outside warrior will risk his life for any number of cows.
column2: 没有外族战士会为了任何数量的牛只冒生命危险。

column1: No outside warrior will risk his life for less than six cows.
column2: 没有外族战士会为了少于六头牛冒生命危险。

column1: No outside warrior will risk his life for less than five cows.
column2: 没有外族战士会为了少于五头牛冒生命危险。

column1: No outside warrior will risk his life for less than four cows.
column2: 没有外族战士会为了少于四头牛冒生命危险。

column1: No outside warrior will risk his life for less than three cows.
column2: 没有外族战士会为了少于三头牛冒生命危险。

column1: The Horse-Spawn are perhaps our most dangerous foes.
column2: 马裔也许是我们最危险的敌人。

column1: It will be easier to rescue a few prisoners than to free all of them.
column2: 解救少数囚犯比解救全部要容易。

column1: We will be lucky to find our kin, luckier still if we can free them.
column2: 能找到我们的亲人已是幸运，若能解救他们则更是万幸。

column1: We cannot rely on outside help, we must \x02\x03fight/rescue our clansmen/take care of our own\x02, ourselves.
column2: 我们不能依赖外部帮助，我们必须 \x02\x03战斗/营救我们的族人/照顾好我们自己\x02。

column1: The Horse-Spawn legally own our people now, by right of conquest.
column2: 根据征服权，马裔现在合法地拥有我们的族人。

column1: If we make idle promises, we are poor leaders.
column2: 如果我们做出空洞的承诺，我们就是糟糕的领袖。

column1: The people were willing to wait once, but we cannot expect their patience to last forever.
column2: 人们愿意等待一次，但我们不能指望他们的耐心永远持续。

column1: We must act, not talk.
column2: 我们必须行动，而不是空谈。

column1: \x02\x04We have proven ourselves as good leaders/In other matters, we have earned the people’s trust/Our decisions have proven right before/We are known for our good judgment\x02. The people will \x02\x03follow us/obey us/comply with our decision here\x02, even if they do not like what we propose.
column2: \x02\x04我们已经证明自己是优秀的领袖/在其他事务上，我们赢得了人们的信任/我们的决策以往都是正确的/我们以判断力著称\x02。人们会 \x02\x03跟随我们/服从我们/遵从我们在此的决定\x02，即使他们不喜欢我们的提议。

column1: Other clans will feel obligated to us if we free their people from the Horse-Spawn.
column2: 如果我们从马裔手中解救出其他氏族的族人，那些氏族将对我们心存感激。

column1: The Horse-Spawn deserve to lose all their thralls. Even our foes will admire us, if we can rescue everyone.
column2: 马裔活该失去所有奴隶。如果我们能救出所有人，连我们的敌人都会敬佩我们。

column1: Better to rescue \x02\x03our own/our clansmen/our kin\x02 first, then mount a \x02\x03larger/serious/better-armed\x02 campaign later.
column2: 最好先救回 \x02\x03我们自己/我们的族人/我们的亲属\x02 ，然后再发动一场 \x02\x03更大规模/认真/装备更好的\x02 战役。

column1: Our clan magic is strong. It will give us an advantage against the Horse-Spawn, who have strange and powerful magics of their own.
column2: 我们的氏族魔法很强大。这会让我们在面对马裔时占据优势，他们自己也拥有奇特而强大的魔法。

column1: Our clan magic is weak. We will be at a disadvantage against the Horse-Spawn, who possess strange and powerful magics of their own.
column2: 我们的氏族魔法很弱小。我们在面对马裔时会处于劣势，他们自己拥有奇特而强大的魔法。

column1: The people are understandably upset — but raiding right now will mean neglecting our fields and that will mean a hungry year for us all.
column2: 人们感到不满是可以理解的——但现在出征意味着荒废我们的田地，那将意味着我们所有人都要挨饿一年。

column1: If we had a bigger temple, foreigners would \x02\x03fear holding our people as thralls/not dare to take our kin as thralls/think twice before stealing our kinfolk\x02 .
column2: 如果我们有一座更大的神殿，外族人就会 \x02\x03害怕奴役我们的人民/不敢掳走我们的族人/在窃取我们的亲属之前三思\x02 。

column1: It is better to die than to allow our people to live as thralls.
column2: 与其让我们的族人沦为奴隶，不如战死。

column1: It is better to live as a thrall than to die in battle.
column2: 与其战死沙场，不如苟且为奴。

column1: \x02\x03But how can we say/But what do you measure/But where do we\x02…? What I mean to say is \x02\x03that it is easy to say/that it’s hard to find/that we really don’t know\x02… \x02\x02Yes, that’s it./Not that I want to offend any of you, but before we speak we must establish…\x02
column2: \x02\x03但我们怎能说/可我们拿什么衡量/却又何处寻\x02…？我的意思是 \x02\x03说起来容易/但难以找到/我们真不知\x02… \x02\x02对，就是这样。/并非有意冒犯诸位，但在开口之前，我们得先定下…\x02

column1: In Airvant’s Saga, Airvant resists pressure to fight a superior foe, while his former wife leads her clan to destruction.
column2: 在艾尔万特传说中，艾尔万特抵抗压力，不与强敌交手，而他前妻则带领她的氏族走向毁灭。

column1: The clans reluctantly agreed to outlaw \x01@\x0B for refusing to obey the tribal moot, and \x06 was soon found and killed.
column2: 各部落不情愿地同意将 \x01@\x0B 逐出法外，因他拒绝服从部落大会，而 \x06 很快被发现并杀死。

column1: \x01@\x0B gave us many cows.
column2: \x01@\x0B 给了我们许多牛。

column1: “You can’t expel us! We quit!”
column2: “你们不能驱逐我们！我们自己走！”

column1: We proudly left the moot before any proceedings against us began.
column2: 在对我们的任何诉讼开始前，我们骄傲地离开了议会。

column1: We are wealthy enough to make our own justice.
column2: 我们足够富有，可以自行伸张正义。

column1: If we offend the tribe, they will expel us and then raid us. We will have to find another tribe quickly, or face eradication.
column2: 如果我们冒犯了部落，他们会驱逐我们，然后袭击我们。我们得迅速找到另一个部落，否则将面临灭绝。

column1: It is true that we have sometimes infringed on royal prerogatives, but this expulsion order is unjust.
column2: 诚然，我们有时侵犯了王室特权，但这次驱逐令是不公正的。

column1: We must beg forgiveness.
column2: 我们必须乞求宽恕。

column1: Our dreams are like smoke up a smoke-hole!
column2: 我们的梦想如同从烟孔升起的烟雾！

column1: They can’t expel us! We quit!
column2: 他们不能驱逐我们！我们自己走！

column1: If you do not trust a man you wish to do you good, speak well of him. But lies and treachery deserve nothing but the same in return.
column2: 如果你不信任一个你想对你好的人，那就说他的好话。但谎言和背叛只配得到同样的回报。

column2: 其他领主同意王冠应由他们中的一人佩戴，并同意与我们并肩作战。下一个火季，战斗就将打响。

column2: 其他领主同意 \x01@" 氏族一次又一次地证明了它配得上王位，并同意与我们并肩作战。下一个火季，战斗就将打响。

column1: We are bears in a tribe of mice. Everyone knows that!
column2: 我们是在老鼠部落里的熊。谁都知道！

column1: Surely it is the turn of another clan to claim the throne.
column2: 当然该轮到另一个氏族来要求王位了。

column1: The people must have a monarch they can take pride in.
column2: 人民必须有一位他们可以为之骄傲的君主。

column1: \x01@\x0B is unjust.
column2: \x01@\x0B 是不公正的。

column1: Strangers sneak into the chieftain’s stead during the in the night, their faces painted, their clothes bearing the insignia of no clan.
column2: 陌生人在夜间潜入酋长的庄园，脸上涂着颜料，衣服上没有氏族徽记。

column1: \x01@\x0B attacked them, and they cut \x08 down, like the rabid beast \x06 was.
column2: \x01@\x0B 攻击了他们，他们砍倒了 \x08 ，就像杀死疯兽 \x06 一样。

column1: How many outlaws do you seek?
column2: 你们要追捕多少法外之徒？

column1: How much (in trade goods) do you offer to each outlaw?
column2: 你为每个法外之徒提供多少（以货物计算）？

column1: They did not wish to believe us, but we told them the truth, and they had no choice but to accept our account as true.
column2: 他们不愿相信我们，但我们告诉了他们真相，他们别无选择，只能接受我们的说法是真话。

column1: Wait for a better opportunity for revenge.
column2: 等待更好的复仇机会。

column1: We waited, and bided our time.
column2: 我们等待着，静候时机。

column1: There are outlaws living in the woods around here.
column2: 这附近的林子里住着一些法外之徒。

column1: There are many warriors who are hot for battle against an unjust foe.
column2: 有许多战士渴望与不义的敌人一战。

column1: Our political situation is not so good. Other clans may be reluctant to believe our tale.
column2: 我们的政治局势不大好。其他氏族可能不愿相信我们的话。

column1: The other clans know we are honorable. They will support us at the moot, or in war.
column2: 其他氏族深知我们体面。无论在议会上还是战场上，他们都会支持我们。

column1: Let us shed no more blood.
column2: 我们不要再流血了。

column1: Give \x01@\x0B a taste of \x04 own villainy!
column2: 让 \x01@\x0B 尝尝 \x04 自己的恶行滋味！

column1: This stain on our tribe will not be washed away by talking. Only the cleansing rain of battle will make us clean.
column2: 我们氏族身上的污点，光靠言语是洗不掉的。只有战斗的净化之雨才能让我们洁净。

column1: If true, this is hardly behavior worthy of a king.
column2: 若果真如此，这哪配得上一位国王的所为。

column1: The final rebellion against Bad King Urgrain began when he sent outlaws to kill Magnus Bare-Arms.
column2: 对恶王乌格兰的最终反叛，始于他派出歹徒刺杀马格努斯·裸臂。

column1: Maybe we’d better wait…
column2: 或许我们最好等等…

column1: Offer them 25 cows worth of silver.
column2: 给他们价值25头牛的银子。

column1: We offered them half of what they asked.
column2: 我们给了他们要价的一半。

column1: They reluctantly parted with the treasure, complaining that we bargained too shrewdly for the honest traders of the \x01@! clan.
column2: 他们不情愿地交出了宝物，抱怨我们这些 \x01@! 氏族的诚实商贩讨价还价太精明了。

column1: Offer them 50 cows worth of silver.
column2: 给他们价值50头牛的银子。

column1: We gave them the silver they asked for.
column2: 我们给了他们索要的银币。

column1: They praised our boldness and good judgment.
column2: 他们称赞我们的勇敢与明智。

column1: Politely decline their offer.
column2: 礼貌地拒绝他们的提议。

column1: Suggest another clan that might be interested.
column2: 推荐另一个可能感兴趣的氏族。

column1: We sent them elsewhere.
column2: 我们把他们打发去了别处。

column1: Which clan do you suggest?
column2: 你推荐哪个氏族？

column1: They thanked us for the suggestion.
column2: 他们感谢我们的建议。

column1: Trade treasure for treasure.
column2: 以宝换宝。

column1: We traded them our \x01@\x14 for it.
column2: 我们用我们的 \x01@\x14 换取了它。

column1: I know what this treasure is. It will protect our sheep from illness.
column2: 我知道这件宝物是什么。它能保护我们的羊群免受疾病。

column1: Treasure for treasure is the fairest trade.
column2: 以宝换宝是最公平的交易。

column1: Give them the full amount of silver.
column2: 给他们全额银币。

column1: Give them half the silver they ask for.
column2: 给他们索要的一半银币。

column1: I am uncertain. Send them elsewhere.
column2: 我不确定。打发他们去别处。

column1: They’re trying to put one over on us.
column2: 他们想糊弄我们。

column1: This treasure will help us against our ancient enemies.
column2: 这件宝物能帮助我们对抗宿敌。

column1: This must be one of the legendary and peculiar weapons of the dwarfs.
column2: 这一定是矮人传说中的奇特武器之一。

column1: How much are we willing to pay to satisfy our curiosity? That is the real question.
column2: 为了满足好奇心，我们愿意付多少钱？这才是真正的问题。

column1: If it is from the dwarfs, it is certainly magical.
column2: 如果来自矮人，那必定具有魔力。

column1: If it is magical, why do they not tell us what it is?

column1: Your exploration party is taken prisoner by trolls. Unable to escape, they’re left to their own devices, without advice from the ring. The trolls drag them into the presence of their leader, the terrifying Cragspider. The explorers can tell just from her presence that she’s immensely powerful — and quite displeased to learn that they exist.

column2: 我们必须攻击她。虽然我们会死，但这将增强我们的氏族魔法。

column1: Trollkin were found in the grain bins again.
column2: 小巨魔又在粮仓里被发现了。

You’re familiar with these creatures from the old country — they’re trollkin, the stunted and sometimes simple-minded offspring that most trolls are cursed with.
column2: \x01Bl 发现一群小巨魔在自己的农庄粮仓里乱翻。他们吃掉了一些谷物，还糟蹋了更多。你对这些来自旧国的生物很熟悉——他们是小巨魔，大多数巨魔受诅咒而生下的发育迟缓、有时头脑简单的后代。

column1: Trollkin were found in the grain bins.

column1: Take them as thralls.

column2: 他们可能有用，可以用来 \x02\x03泼洒粪便/收集牛粪作燃料/冲洗猪\x02。

column2: 如果我们收他们为奴隶，他们会惊扰羊群。

column2: 所有神祇中，只有欧尔马会对小巨魔的礼物感到高兴。

column1: They might be able to perform simple but unpleasant chores.

column1: If we can’t make good use of them, the crafters might.

column2: 不管是不是小巨魔，他们是有智力的生物，应该得到自由！

column1: Trollkin are not notably smart creatures after all. Drive them far, far away this time, so that they are hopelessly lost.
column2: 小巨魔毕竟不是特别聪明的生物。这次把他们赶得远远的，让他们彻底迷路。
