column2: 释放矮人，让他们去攻打他们的敌人——精灵。

column1: Everything dies, except your reputation.
column2: 万物皆亡，唯名声不死。

column1: An alliance with the dwarfs might help us seek and keep the crown.
column2: 与矮人结盟可能有助于我们寻求并保有王冠。

column1: sceneR165
column2: sceneR165

column1: Explorers from your clan find the body of a dragonewt warrior lying in a stream bed just inside the boundaries of the tula. Some of them have heard that it is possible to make magical armor from the hide of a dragonewt. However, they don’t want to touch or move the body without first seeking advice from the ring.
column2: 你们氏族的探险者在图拉地界内的一条溪床里发现了一具龙人战士的尸体。有些人听说过龙人的皮可以制作魔法护甲。但他们不想在征求长老会意见之前触碰或移动尸体。

column1: Explorers from our clan found the body of a dragonewt warrior lying in a stream bed.
column2: 我们氏族的探险者在一条溪床里发现了一具龙人战士的尸体。

column1: Destroy the body.
column2: 销毁尸体。

column1: We destroyed the body.
column2: 我们销毁了尸体。

column1: The carls who burned the body swore that it smelled like \x02\x04chicken/fish/butter/cinnamon\x02.
column2: 焚烧尸体的自由民发誓说它闻起来像 \x02\x04鸡肉/鱼肉/黄油/肉桂\x02。

column1: Which other clan do you give it to?
column2: 你把它送给哪个氏族？

column1: Leave it alone.
column2: 别管它。

column1: We left it alone.
column2: 我们没管它。

column1: We let the body rot where it lay. Some of the carls swore that it smelled like \x02\x04chicken/fish/butter/cinnamon\x02.
column2: 我们让尸体在原地腐烂。有些自由民发誓说它闻起来像 \x02\x04鸡肉/鱼肉/黄油/肉桂\x02。

column1: 15 cows worth of goods
column2: 价值15头牛的物品

column1: 25 cows worth of goods
column2: 价值25头牛的物品

column1: The most they offer you for the treasure is \x01@\x17. Do you accept their offer?
column2: 他们为这件宝物出的最高价是 \x01@\x17。你接受这个出价吗？

column1: Try to make magical armor from its hide.
column2: 尝试用它的皮制作魔法护甲。

column1: We decided to make magical armor from its hide.
column2: 我们决定用它的皮制作魔法护甲。

column1: It was difficult to skin the dragonewt corpse without destroying the hide, but our tanners and magicians managed the task.
column2: 在不毁坏皮革的情况下剥龙人的皮很困难，但我们的制革匠和法师还是完成了任务。

column1: Who gets to wear the armor?
column2: 谁穿这件护甲？

column1: The god-talkers performed a ritual so that \x01@\x05 could draw upon the magic of the armor. It shaped itself to \x04 body, and they said nobody else would be able to wear it.
column2: 神言者举行了一场仪式，以便 \x01@\x05 能够汲取护甲的魔力。护甲自动贴合在 \x04 身体上，他们说没有其他人能穿上它。

column1: We attuned the armor to \x01@\x05.
column2: 我们将护甲调谐到 \x01@\x05。

column1: The dragonewt corpse was too difficult to skin, and we ruined it so that it could not be made into armor.
column2: 龙人的尸体太难剥皮，我们把它毁了，无法做成护甲。

column1: We should get cows for this.
column2: 我们应该为此要几头牛。

column1: Its presence will give the cows the frothing and sliding disease.
column2: 它的存在会让牛患上口吐白沫、滑倒的疾病。

column1: We should demand fifteen cows for it.
column2: 我们应该为此索要十五头牛。

column1: We should demand twenty cows for it.
column2: 我们应该为此索要二十头牛。

column1: We should ask twenty-five cows for it.
column2: 我们应该为此索要二十五头牛。

column1: Remember what happened in the Dragonkill War.
column2: 记住屠龙战争中发生了什么。

column1: We’re having trouble with some of our neighbors. We should improve relations by giving the body to one of them.
column2: 我们正和几个邻居闹矛盾。应该把尸体送给他们中的一个来改善关系。

column1: You can’t make magical armor out of a dragonewt corpse. That’s an old wive’s tale.
column2: 你没法用龙人的尸体做魔法护甲。那是老太婆的传说。

column1: It is difficult to make the armor. If you tear the skin of the torso, or any of the tattoos, the hide is useless.
column2: 制作这种铠甲很难。一旦划破躯干的皮肤或任何一处纹身，这张兽皮就没用了。

column1: Dragonewt armor is difficult to make, but makes its wearer very powerful.
column2: 龙人铠甲很难制作，但能让穿戴者变得非常强大。

column1: Leave it alone. It might spread disease.
column2: 别管它。可能会传播疾病。

column1: Dragonewts make all the other strange foreigners look normal by comparison.
column2: 龙人让其他所有奇怪的异邦人相比之下都显得正常了。

column1: A little generosity would not go awry.
column2: 一点点慷慨总不会出错。

column1: I don’t think the dragonewts like having their hides turned into armor…
column2: 我觉得龙人可不喜欢自己的皮被做成铠甲……

column1: sceneR166
column2: sceneR166

column1: \x02\x03Luena/Jessa/Urasandra\x02
column2: \x02\x03卢埃纳/耶萨/乌拉桑德拉\x02

column1: Approach the trolls and see if they want to trade.
column2: 接近巨魔，看看他们是否想交易。

column1: We decided we should try to trade with them.
column2: 我们决定应该试着和他们交易。

column1: Who leads the trade party?
column2: 谁带领交易队伍？

column1: The trolls were willing to trade with us.
column2: 巨魔愿意和我们交易。

column1: What do you want to trade?
column2: 你想交易什么？

column1: They dealt fairly with us.
column2: 他们和我们公平交易。

column1: They dealt fairly with us, and we made a small profit.
column2: 他们和我们公平交易，我们获得了一点小利。

column1: But our ancestors, who had fought trolls in the Storm Age, were unhappy.
column2: 但我们那些在风暴时代曾与巨魔战斗过的祖先们并不高兴。

column1: The trolls refused to deal with us.
column2: 巨魔拒绝与我们交易。

column1: “You bad to trolls,” they said, “so go away.”
column2: “你们对巨魔不好，”他们说，“所以走开。”

column1: Assemble other clans for a joint raid.
column2: 召集其他氏族进行联合奇袭。

column1: We decided to assemble other clans for a joint raid.
column2: 我们决定召集其他氏族进行联合奇袭。

column1: The other clans refused to participate. They said we could not be trusted with the lives of their warriors, or the division of the spoils. By the time they had finished deciding, it was too late to intercept the caravan.
column2: 其他氏族拒绝参与。他们说信不过我们把族中勇士的生命托付给我们，也信不过我们的战利品分配。等他们做完决定时，拦截那支商队已为时太晚。

column1: It was agreed that we would raid the trolls together.
column2: 大家一致同意我们将一起奇袭巨魔。

column1: The raiders of the united clans slashed through the caravan of giant bugs, gaining good loot.
column2: 联合氏族的奇袭者杀穿了那支巨虫商队，获得了丰厚的战利品。

column1: \x01@\x05 found it difficult to restrain the warriors of the many clans. They attacked haphazardly, and the defending trolls made short work of them. They were terrified by awful spirits, and attacked by demons of darkness. Some of our own warriors were killed; many were wounded.
column2: \x01@\x05 发现很难约束众多氏族的战士。他们胡乱进攻，防守的巨魔轻而易举地击溃了他们。他们被可怕的邪灵吓得要命，又遭到黑暗魔鬼的袭击。我们的一些战士阵亡了；许多人身负重伤。

column1: \x01@\x05 was among the slain.
column2: \x01@\x05 在阵亡者中。

column1: We thanked her for her interesting report.
column2: 我们感谢她带来了有趣的报告。

column1: Offer gifts to the trolls.
column2: 向巨魔赠送礼物。

column1: We offered gifts to the trolls.
column2: 我们向巨魔赠送了礼物。

column1: The trolls were surprised by our generosity. “You good to trolls,” they said. “Trolls say thanks.”
column2: 巨魔被我们的慷慨所打动。“你们对巨魔好，”他们说，“巨魔说谢谢。”

column1: Raid the caravan.
column2: 奇袭商队。

column1: We decided to raid them.
column2: 我们决定奇袭他们。

column1: Our raiders slashed through the caravan of giant bugs, gaining much good loot.
column2: 我们的奇袭者杀穿了那支巨虫商队，获得了许多丰厚的战利品。

column1: Our warriors found the caravan too well defended. They were terrified by awful spirits, and attacked by demons of darkness. Some were killed; many were wounded.
column2: 我们的战士们发现那支商队防守太严。他们被可怕的邪灵吓得要命，又遭到黑暗魔鬼的袭击。一些战士阵亡了；许多人身负重伤。

column1: It is always good to trade.
column2: 交易总是好的。

column1: We have treated the trolls with respect. They should be willing to trade with us.
column2: 我们以尊重相待巨魔。他们应该愿意和我们交易。

column1: We have shown the trolls that we are their foes. Of course they will not trade with us.
column2: 我们向巨魔展现了我们是他们的敌人。他们当然不会和我们交易。

column1: This clumsy caravan is ripe for the taking!
column2: 这支笨拙的商队，简直是唾手可得！

column1: If we bring in other clans, we are more likely to succeed, but we will get a smaller share of the loot.
column2: 如果我们带上其他氏族，会更容易成功，但我们将分到更小份额的战利品。

column1: Trolls are inhuman, but if we wish to please them, they will probably accept gifts.
column2: 巨魔并非人类，但如果我们想取悦他们，他们很可能会接受礼物。

column1: If we ask other clans to join in with us, we are likely to get nothing but insults.
column2: 如果我们要求其他氏族加入我们，很可能只会换来侮辱。

column1: The other clans are waiting for us to lead them.
column2: 其他氏族正等待我们带领他们。

column1: The war clouds move west. It is a good time for battle.
column2: 战云向西移动。现在是战斗的好时机。

column1: The war clouds move east. It is a bad time for battle.
column2: 战云向东移动。现在是战斗的坏时机。

column1: Will troll-booty make up for lost crops? I think not!
column2: 巨魔的战利品能弥补失去的收成吗？我觉得不能！

column1: The trolls were the enemy of our ancestors. We must raid the trolls to honor our ancestors!
column2: 巨魔是我们祖先的敌人。我们必须奇袭巨魔，以荣耀我们的祖先！

column1: We must not rest until we have heard a troll song about our generosity.
column2: 我们绝不能休息，直到听到一首关于我们慷慨的巨魔之歌。

column1: Trade is the answer.
column2: 交易就是答案。

column1: The trolls will rue the day they approached the \x01@" tula!
column2: 巨魔会为它们接近 \x01@" 图拉领地的那一天追悔莫及！

column1: It is too risky. Do nothing.
column2: 风险太大。什么都不做。

column1: To find the best choice, we must first decide what we want.
column2: 要想找到最佳选择，我们必须先决定自己想要什么。

column1: While foraging for berries in the bush, women of the clan encounter a talking fox. In halting Tradetalk, it tells them that it will protect them from the spirits of the wood if the clan agrees not to clear any more of the forest for the next five years. The clan must also agree to stop hunting foxes for that period. The fox warns that the spirits will be very angry if the clan doesn’t comply. It tells them it will be waiting for them the next day, when they have talked to the other “two-legs.”
column2: 氏族的女人们在灌木丛中寻找浆果时，遇到了一只说话的狐狸。它用磕磕巴巴的贸易语告诉她们，如果氏族同意未来五年不再砍伐林地，它就会保护她们免受林中灵体的侵扰。氏族还必须同意在那段时间内不再狩猎狐狸。狐狸警告说，如果氏族不遵守，灵体会非常愤怒。它告诉她们，等她们和其他“两条腿的”商量过后，它会在第二天等她们答复。

column1: Women found a talking fox in our woods. It wanted us to make an agreement not to hunt foxes or clear any more forest.
column2: 女人们在我们的树林里遇到了一只说话的狐狸。它想让我们达成协议，不再狩猎狐狸或砍伐林地。

column1: Agree not to clear land.
column2: 同意不清除土地。

column1: We told the fox we would let the forest be.
column2: 我们告诉狐狸我们会让森林保持原样。

column1: The fox said that this would satisfy the tree spirits, but not the spirits of its ancestors.
column2: 狐狸说这会满足树灵，但满足不了它祖先的灵体。

column1: Agree not to hunt foxes.
column2: 同意不狩猎狐狸。

column1: We told the fox that we would not hunt its kin.
column2: 我们告诉狐狸我们不会狩猎它的同类。

column1: The fox said that this would satisfy the spirits of its ancestors, but not the tree spirits.
column2: 狐狸说这会满足它祖先的灵体，但满足不了树灵。

column1: Agree to both conditions.
column2: 同意两个条件。

column1: We agreed to both conditions.
column2: 我们同意了两个条件。

column1: The fox said that we would never know the full measure of disaster we had avoided.
column2: 狐狸说我们永远不会知道自己避免了多大的灾难。

column1: Tell people to avoid the fox.
column2: 让人们避开那只狐狸。

column1: We told our people to avoid the fox.
column2: 我们告诉我们的人避开那只狐狸。

column1: We thought we did the right thing, and it appears we did. The fox seemed to have vanished, and we could not see any ill effects from ignoring the fox’s threats.
column2: 我们以为自己做了正确的事，看来我们确实做对了。那只狐狸似乎消失了，我们也看不到忽视狐狸威胁带来了任何不良影响。

column1: We thought we did the right thing, but our clan magic suffered greatly, and we had to admit that we should have paid more attention to the fox’s threats.
column2: 我们原以为做了正确的事，但氏族魔法严重受损，不得不承认当初该更留意那只狐狸的威胁。

column1: There is no harm in curtailing our hunting of foxes.
column2: 减少猎狐并无害处。

column1: The fox pelts we take each year provide us with warmth, and are valuable in trade.
column2: 我们每年获得的狐皮不仅能御寒，也是珍贵的贸易品。

column1: If we stop hunting foxes, we will not only lose the chance to take fox pelts. There will be more foxes, and they will eat other small game animals we would otherwise catch.
column2: 若停止猎狐，我们不仅失去获得狐皮的机会。狐狸还会增多，吃掉我们本可捕获的其他小猎物。

column1: Foxes don’t talk. It’s all some kind of trick.
column2: 狐狸不会说话。这全是某种把戏。

column1: Talking animals are strong spirit-friends. Its threat could be very real.
column2: 会说话的动物是强大的灵魂之友。它的威胁可能是真的。

column1: Talking animals are strong spirit-friends. We must assume its threat is real.
column2: 会说话的动物是强大的灵魂之友。我们必须假设它的威胁是真的。

column1: We can’t agree to leave the land uncleared — the people will starve!
column2: 我们不能同意不清理土地——人民会挨饿的！

column1: We have plenty of land cleared already.
column2: 我们已经清理了足够多的土地。

column1: We can’t agree to leave the land uncleared; we need to grow more food to feed our people.
column2: 我们不能同意不清理土地；我们需要种植更多粮食来养活族人。

column1: At the moment, we have enough farmland to support our people.
column2: 目前，我们有足够的农田养活族人。

column1: Its pelt would make a fine collar decoration.
column2: 它的毛皮可以做成漂亮的领饰。

column1: We must agree to its demands. The undead are our real enemies, and we can’t afford angry spirits distracting us from that fact.
column2: 我们必须同意它的要求。亡灵才是我们真正的敌人，我们经不起被愤怒的精灵分散对事实的注意力。

column1: It might just be bluffing.
column2: 它可能只是在虚张声势。

column1: sceneR168
column2: sceneR168

column1: Thanes from the \x01@! clan come to lodge a claim against you. Unlike most other clans in the area, their main god is the sun deity, Elmal. In their tradition, it is Elmal who is the exemplar of the good chieftain. Elmali clans still worship Orlanth and the other gods, and their laws are otherwise similar to yours. These thanes are here to complain that thanes of your clan disrupted their holy ceremonies and lobbed dirt clods at their temple.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的乡绅前来向你提出控诉。与当地大多数氏族不同，他们的主神是太阳神埃尔马尔。在他们的传统中，埃尔马尔是贤明酋长的典范。埃尔马尔部族仍然崇拜奥兰斯和其他神祇，其法律在其他方面也与你们相似。这些乡绅是来投诉你们氏族的乡绅扰乱了他们的神圣仪式，并向他们的神庙投掷土块。

column1: Thanes from an Elmal clan came to complain that our thanes disrupted their holy ceremonies and lobbed dirt clods at their temple.
column2: 一个埃尔马尔氏族的乡绅前来投诉，说我们的乡绅扰乱了他们的神圣仪式，并向他们的神庙投掷土块。

column1: Allow them to lob dirt clods at your temple.
column2: 允许他们向你们的庙宇投掷土块。

column1: We allowed them to lob dirt clods at our temple.
column2: 我们允许他们向我们的庙宇投掷土块。

column1: They did so with great relish, and then pronounced our claim settled.
column2: 他们兴致勃勃地这样做了，然后宣布我们的索赔已了结。

column1: Compose a poem of apology.
column2: 写一首道歉诗。

column1: We composed a poem of apology to them.
column2: 我们为他们写了一首道歉诗。

column1: They were moved by our verses, and said that they considered the matter closed.
column2: 他们被我们的诗句所打动，并表示认为此事已了结。

column1: Our poem only offended them further. “Slippery words cannot conceal your contempt for our god!” they cried. They said that they would make sacrifices to Elmal, and that we would suffer ill-fortune as a result.
column2: 我们的诗反而进一步得罪了他们。“花言巧语掩盖不了你们对我们神的轻蔑！”他们喊道。他们说他们会向埃尔马尔献祭，因此我们将遭遇厄运。

column1: They were satisfied by our offer, and said that they considered the claim settled.
column2: 他们对我们的提议感到满意，并表示认为索赔已了结。

column1: “We expected little from you blowhard cottar-kin,” said the lead thane. “You offer even less than we expected.” They cursed us and left quickly while the ring restrained our hotheads from violating the guesting ritual.
column2: “我们对你这些自吹自擂的佃农亲戚本就没抱什么期望，”为首的乡绅说。“你们给的甚至比我们期望的还少。”他们诅咒了我们，然后迅速离开，同时长老会制止了我们中的冲动者违反宾客仪式。

column1: “Elmal must always be subordinate to Orlanth.”
column2: “埃尔马尔必须永远从属于奥兰斯。”

column1: “Elmal must always be subordinate to Orlanth,” we said.
column2: “埃尔马尔必须永远从属于奥兰斯，”我们说道。

column1: This seemed to greatly offend the Elmali thanes. They said that they would make sacrifices to Elmal, and that we would suffer ill-fortune as a result.
column2: 这似乎极大地触怒了埃尔马尔部族的乡绅。他们说他们会向埃尔马尔献祭，因此我们将遭遇厄运。

column1: “Take your claim to the moot, if you want.”
column2: “如果你们愿意，就把你们的索赔提交到议会吧。”

column1: We told them to take their claim to the moot, if they wanted.
column2: 我们告诉他们，如果他们愿意，就把索赔提交到议会。

column1: And they did.
column2: 他们照做了。

column1: How much total wealth do you distribute among the other clans before the case is judged?
column2: 在案件裁决之前，你在其他氏族之间分配多少总财富？

column1: The other clans agreed that what our thanes had done was in the tradition of Orlanth, for Orlanth bested Elmal the first time they met. They said that the subservience of Elmali to Orlanthi should be renewed every so often.
column2: 其他氏族一致认为，我们的乡绅所作所为符合奥兰斯的传统，因为奥兰斯第一次相遇时就战胜了埃尔马尔。他们说埃尔马尔部族对奥兰斯氏的从属关系应当每隔一段时间重新确认。

column1: The other clans said that we had offended the Elmali for no good reason. “Although Elmal is subservient to Orlanth, there is no need to rub the poor fellows’ noses in it.” We were levied a fine of ten cows.
column2: 其他氏族说我们无缘无故地冒犯了埃尔马尔部族。“尽管埃尔马尔从属于奥兰斯，但没必要往可怜家伙们的鼻子上抹灰。”我们被处以十头牛的罚金。

column1: They want respect, not goods.
column2: 他们要的是尊重，不是财物。

column1: A tangible gift shows greater respect than do pretty words.
column2: 实在的礼物比漂亮话更能显示尊重。

column1: If we lose at the moot, they will fine us fifty cows.
column2: 如果我们在议会上败诉，他们将罚我们五十头牛。

column1: Elmal must always be subordinate to Orlanth.
column2: 埃尔马尔必须永远从属于奥兰斯。

column1: Elmal must always be subordinate to Orlanth, or so our laws say. The \x01@! laws are different, however.
column2: 埃尔马尔必须永远从属于奥兰斯，至少我们的法律是这么说的。然而， \x01@! 的法律有所不同。

column1: If we lose at the moot, they will fine us twenty cows.
column2: 如果我们在议会上败诉，他们将罚我们二十头牛。

column1: If we lose at the moot, they will fine us ten cows.
column2: 如果我们在议会上败诉，他们将罚我们十头牛。

column1: If they want to get along, let them sue for peace.
column2: 如果他们想和睦相处，就让他们求和吧。

column1: They’re brave to come here and whine, when we can smash them like dogs.
column2: 他们敢来这里发牢骚，真是够勇敢的，毕竟我们可以像打狗一样揍扁他们。

column1: They think they can swagger in and order us around because they have more warriors than we do.
column2: 他们以为仗着比我方多几个战士就能大摇大摆进来对我们发号施令。

column1: I’d rather not apologize.
column2: 我宁愿不道歉。

column1: The other clans all feel as we do about Elmal’s subservience to Orlanth.
column2: 其他氏族对埃尔马尔从属于奥兰斯一事与我们感受相同。

column1: The other clans all feel as we do about Elmal’s subservience to Orlanth. That means the Elmali are likely to be offended at a moot, no matter how the ruling goes.
column2: 其他氏族对埃尔马尔从属于奥兰斯一事与我们感受相同。这意味着无论裁决如何，埃尔马尔部族在议会上都可能感到受冒犯。

column1: The damage is done. Where our clans are concerned, there has been far worse.
column2: 损害已经造成。就我们氏族而言，还有比这更糟的情况。

column1: They will hurt our magic if we don’t apologize. But they will still hate us no matter what we do.
column2: 如果我们不道歉，他们会伤害我们的魔法。但无论我们做什么，他们仍然会恨我们。

column1: Our magic will suffer if we let them lob dirt at our temple.
column2: 如果我们让他们往我们的神庙扔脏东西，我们的魔法会受损。

column1: Our magic will suffer if we let them lob dirt at our temple. But we weakened the Elmali magic by doing the same to them.
column2: 如果我们让他们往我们的神庙扔脏东西，我们的魔法会受损。但我们也对他们做了同样的事，削弱了埃尔马尔魔法。

column1: Our magic will suffer if we let them lob dirt at our temple. But if we offend them, they could call on Elmal to curse us, which might be worse.
column2: 如果我们让他们往我们的神庙扔脏东西，我们的魔法会受损。但如果我们冒犯了他们，他们可能召唤艾尔玛诅咒我们，那可能更糟。

column1: Oh dear. This is bad.
column2: 哦天哪。这很糟糕。

column1: I am ashamed of what our brothers and sisters have done.
column2: 我为我们的兄弟姐妹们所做的事感到羞耻。

column1: I am ashamed of our clansmen, but we cannot allow our enemies to violate the temple.
column2: 我为我们的族人感到羞耻，但我们不能允许敌人亵渎神庙。

column1: This is bad. But they’ve done worse.
column2: 这很糟糕。但他们的所作所为更恶劣。

column1: It’s good to see Elmal getting picked on, instead of Eurmal.
column2: 看到艾尔玛被欺负而不是欧尔玛，倒是件好事。

column1: One rank offense to the gods does not undo another!
column2: 对神明的一等冒犯并不能抵消另一等冒犯！

column1: The gods’ shrines should never be dragged into our feuds. But we can’t let them violate our own temple.
column2: 神明的圣殿绝不应被卷入我们的世仇。但我们不能让他们亵渎我们自己的神庙。

column1: Let us make war on them!
column2: 让我们向他们开战吧！

column1: It’s too bad we violated their temple. That was going too far.
column2: 太糟糕了，我们亵渎了他们的神庙。那做得太过分了。

column1: They’re lucky we even let them on our tula.
column2: 我们让他们踏上我们的领地，他们已经够幸运了。

column1: Elmali and Orlanthi alike honor the sacred traditions of the poet’s muse.
column2: 埃尔马尔与奥兰斯人同样尊崇诗人缪斯的神圣传统。

column1: Pour them Orlanth’s word-mead.
column2: 为他们斟上奥兰斯的言语蜜酒。

column1: Don’t waste a good poem on these wretches.
column2: 别把好诗浪费在这些可怜虫身上。

column1: Elmal is Orlanth’s loyal thane. We must treat our allies with respect.
column2: 艾尔玛是奥兰斯的忠诚侍从。我们必须尊重我们的盟友。

column1: Our allies deserve better than this.
column2: 我们的盟友理应得到比这更好的待遇。

column1: Scum.
column2: 渣滓。

column1: The king would be happiest if we fix this situation ourselves.
column2: 如果我们自己解决这个局面，国王会最高兴。

column1: It’s true that Elmal walks behind Orlanth, but that is no excuse for such disruptive acts by our weaponthanes. We must make amends.
column2: 诚然艾尔玛行在奥兰斯之后，但这不能成为我们的武器领主们如此破坏行为的借口。我们必须弥补过错。

column1: If they are wise, they will not keep pulling the tail of this tribal tiger but will accept our apology.
column2: 如果他们明智，就不会继续拉扯这只部族老虎的尾巴，而是接受我们的道歉。

column1: Ducks came and demanded compensation for kinsmen they said we slew.
column2: 鸭人来了，要求为据称被我们杀害的族人提供赔偿。

column1: Pay a carl’s wergild for each dead duck.
column2: 为每只死去的鸭人支付一个自由民的血偿金。

column1: We paid a carl’s wergild for each dead duck.
column2: 我们为每只死去的鸭人支付了一个自由民的血偿金。

column1: The ducks squawked, but accepted the payment.
column2: 鸭人嘎嘎叫了一阵，但接受了赔偿。

column1: Pay a cottar’s wergild for each dead duck.
column2: 为每只死去的鸭人支付一个佃农的血偿金。

column1: We paid a cottar’s wergild for each dead duck.
column2: 我们为每只死去的鸭人支付了一个佃农的血偿金。

column1: The ducks squawked mightily, but accepted the payment.
column2: 鸭人拼命嘎嘎叫，但接受了赔偿。

column1: Pay a thane’s wergild for each dead duck.
column2: 为每只死去的鸭人支付一个领主级血偿金。

column1: We paid a thane’s wergild for each dead duck.
column2: 我们为每只死去的鸭人支付了一个领主级血偿金。

column1: The ducks pronounced themselves satisfied with our justice.
column2: 鸭人宣称对我们的公正裁决感到满意。

column1: Reject their claim.
column2: 驳回他们的要求。

column1: We rejected their claim.
column2: 我们驳回了他们的要求。

column1: Predictably, they were outraged.
column2: 不出所料，他们暴跳如雷。

column1: Demand tribute from them.
column2: 向他们索要贡品。

column1: We demanded tribute from them.
column2: 我们向他们索要贡品。

column1: After much squawking and shaking of tiny fists, they gave in to our demands.
column2: 在大量嘎嘎叫和挥舞小拳头之后，他们屈服于我们的要求。

column1: They refused to pay, and threatened war with the beastfolk if we pursued them.
column2: 他们拒绝支付，并威胁说如果我们继续逼迫，他们就要与兽人开战。

column1: Offer to pay in cattle.
column2: 提议用牛只支付。

column1: “Cows can’t live in the marsh. Silver! I said silver and I mean silver! What do you take us for?” The ducks went on for a while in this vein before calming down a bit.
column2: “牛不能在沼泽里活。银币！我说的是银币，就是银币！你把我们当什么了？”鸭人在这个调调上继续了一会儿才稍稍平静下来。

column1: We are poor. Pay as little as possible.
column2: 我们很穷。尽可能少付。

column1: We have enough cows to pay what justice demands.
column2: 我们有足够的牛只来支付公正所要求的数额。

column1: They are lying. The ducks killed were probably thralls.
column2: 他们在撒谎。被杀的那些鸭人很可能是奴隶。

column1: We cannot afford a thane’s wergild for each slain duck.
column2: 我们付不起每只被杀鸭人的领主级血偿金。

column1: They want to be respected as proper Orlanthi, which means getting the full wergild we would pay for slain humans.
column2: 他们希望作为正宗的奥兰斯人受到尊重，这意味着要得到我们为被杀死的人类所支付的全额血偿金。

column1: They want to be respected as proper Orlanthi, which means getting the full wergild we would pay for slain humans. But we can’t afford a thane’s wergild for each slain duck.
column2: 他们希望作为正宗的奥兰斯人受到尊重，这意味着要得到我们为被杀死的人类所支付的全额血偿金。但我们付不起每只被杀鸭人的领主级血偿金。

column1: The ducks are no threat to us.
column2: 鸭人对我们没有威胁。

column1: The ducks are no threat to us. Their cousins, the beastfolk, are a different matter.
column2: 鸭人对我们没有威胁。但他们的亲戚兽人，则是另一回事。

column1: The ducks are no threat to us. On the other hand, their cousins, the beastfolk, could fall upon our tula and destroy us.
column2: 鸭人对我们没有威胁。但另一方面，他们的亲戚兽人可能袭击我们的领地并摧毁我们。

column1: They are foreigners, and we can mistreat them if we want to.
column2: 他们是外族人，如果我们想，我们可以虐待他们。

column1: They seem oddly familiar with our ways.
column2: 他们似乎对我们的方式异常熟悉。

column1: They are Orlanthi, but their versions of proper customs are peculiar.
column2: 他们是奥兰斯人，但他们版本的正统习俗很奇怪。

column1: The ducks claim to be descended from a great, vanished Empire called Ganderland.
column2: 鸭人声称是一个名为刚德兰的伟大已消失帝国的后裔。

column1: They are protecting the interests of their clan, as any human thanes would do.
column2: 他们在保护自己氏族的利益，就像任何人族领主都会做的那样。

column1: We have already done them harm. Do not threaten them further.
column2: 我们已经伤害了他们。不要再威胁他们了。

column1: Certainly, I helped kill their thanes. They were annoying me with that infernal squawking of theirs.
column2: 当然，我帮忙杀了他们的领主。他们那该死的嘎嘎叫声烦死我了。

column1: I see male ducks are as vainglorious and vexing as male humans.
column2: 我发现公鸭和人族男人一样虚荣又烦人。

column1: If we don’t give them what they want, they’ll send minotaurs after us!
column2: 如果我们不给他们想要的东西，他们会派牛头人来追我们！

column1: How can… this is a bad situation, but we cannot admit… to the contrary, we should take this… take situation and…
column2: 怎么可能……这是个糟糕的局面，但我们不能承认……相反，我们应该抓住这……抓住局面并且……

column1: Demand that he explain why he was outlawed.
column2: 要求他解释为何被剥夺法权。

column1: We demanded that he explain why he was outlawed. Orlkensor would not say.
column2: 我们要求他解释为何被剥夺法权。奥尔肯索不肯说。

column1: Orlkensor shakes his head sadly and says that he has taken a vow not to speak of this. He turns to leave.
column2: 奥尔肯索悲伤地摇摇头，说他已发誓不谈此事。他转身离开。

column1: He took his leave of us.
column2: 他向我们告辞了。

column1: Stop him.
column2: 拦住他。

column1: We stopped him from leaving.
column2: 我们阻止了他离开。

column1: Later, when they had time to grumble, the warriors complained that we should have respected Orlkensor’s obviously honorable desire to remain silent.
column2: 后来，当人们有时间抱怨时，战士们说我们本该尊重奥肯索·铜骨那明显体面的沉默意愿。

column1: Find another clan to take him in.
column2: 找另一个氏族收留他。

column1: Which other clan do you approach?
column2: 你去找哪个氏族？

column1: Give him quarters in \x01@\x05’s stead.
column2: 让他住在 \x01@\x05的地盘。

column1: We took him in, and he joined \x01@\x05’s household.
column2: 我们收留了他，他加入了 \x01@\x05的家庭。

column1: The people were happy with the ring’s decision.
column2: 人民对长老会的决定感到满意。

column1: Orlkensor Bronzebones
column2: 奥肯索·铜骨

column1: Give him quarters in the chief’s hall.
column2: 让他住在酋长大厅。

column1: We gave him quarters in the chief’s hall.
column2: 我们让他住在酋长大厅。

column1: We heard some grumbling from the other weaponthanes, who said that Orlkensor had not worked for this honor.
column2: 我们听到其他武器领主有些抱怨，说奥肯索没有为这份荣誉付出努力。

column1: Carls and warriors both criticized the ring for a shortage of compassion. They said that if \x01@\x05 thought he deserved our aid, the clan leaders should have freely given it.
column2: 自由民和战士都批评长老会缺乏同情心。他们说如果 \x01@\x05 认为他值得我们援助，氏族领袖本应慷慨给予。

column1: He can’t be trusted. He means to harm us, somehow.
column2: 他不可信。他想以某种方式伤害我们。

column1: He must have killed someone, or committed some gross act of adultery.
column2: 他一定杀了人，或者犯了某种严重的通奸罪。

column1: People sometimes get outlawed for no good reason.
column2: 人们有时会被无缘无故地放逐。

column1: People sometimes get outlawed for no good reason. Orlkensor probably offended his chieftain.
column2: 人们有时会被无缘无故地放逐。奥肯索大概得罪了他的酋长。

column1: Orlkensor carries himself as a true warrior. The weaponthanes will be offended if he is not treated well.
column2: 奥肯索举止像个真正的战士。如果对他不好，武器领主们会感到冒犯。

column1: Orlkensor carries himself as a true warrior. The weaponthanes will be offended if he is not treated well. Or, on the other hand, if he is treated better than they.
column2: 奥肯索举止像个真正的战士。如果对他不好，武器领主们会感到冒犯。或者反过来，如果待他比他们更好，也会如此。

column1: When Oskul the Brave slew the seven Weeping Nights, he aroused the jealousy of Bad King Urgrain, who then outlawed him.
column2: 当勇敢的奥克苏尔斩杀七个哭泣之夜时，他激起了恶王乌格兰的嫉妒，于是乌格兰放逐了他。

column1: \x01@\x05 is not a ring member. \x05 shouldn’t be making decisions for the clan.
column2: \x01@\x05 不是长老会成员。 \x05 不该为氏族做决定。

column1: When we act in a kindly manner, we earn the love and honor of the goddess Chalana Arroy.
column2: 当我们以仁慈的方式行事时，我们会赢得女神查拉娜·阿罗伊的爱与荣耀。

column1: Why does he come running for another clan? He should exult in his opportunity, for now he can experience freedom from all entanglements.
column2: 他为什么跑到另一个氏族来？他本应庆幸自己的机遇，因为现在他可以摆脱一切羁绊获得自由。

column1: He will not bring trouble, but his enemies will.
column2: 他不会带来麻烦，但他的敌人会。

column1: When Humakt was without a clan, Orlanth adopted him.
column2: 当胡马特没有氏族时，奥兰斯收留了他。

column1: He was honor-wreathed, as the redvine encircles a tree trunk.
column2: 他身披荣誉，犹如红藤缠绕树干。

column1: I trust \x01@\x05.
We have enough weaponthanes right now, but we could give him a good introduction elsewhere.
column2: 我们现在有足够的武器领主，但我们可以给他写一封好的推荐信去别处。

column1: We can always use an extra weaponthane.
column2: 我们总是能多用一个武器领主。

column1: sceneR171
column2: sceneR171

column1: A Uroxi warrior came to demand that Orlkensor Bronzebones fight him to the death.
column2: 一位乌洛希战士前来要求奥肯索·铜骨与他决斗至死。

column1: Ask Orlkensor why the Uroxi seeks him.
column2: 问奥肯索为什么乌洛希要找他。

column1: We asked Orlkensor why the Uroxi sought him.
column2: 我们问奥肯索为什么乌洛希要找他。

column1: “I am grateful to you for taking me in. But please do not ask me more. I have sworn not to speak of this.”
column2: “我感激你们收留我，但请不要再问了。我发誓不提此事。”

column1: Ask the Uroxi why his honor is besmirched.
column2: 问乌洛希为何他的荣誉受玷污。

column1: We asked the Uroxi what Orlkensor had done to besmirch his honor.
column2: 我们问乌洛希奥肯索做了什么玷污他的荣誉。

column1: “It is not your business,” the Uroxi said. “It is between the defiler and me.”
column2: “这不关你的事，”乌洛希说，“这是亵渎者与我之间的事。”

column1: Demand that Orlkensor fight the Uroxi.
column2: 命令奥肯索与乌洛希决斗。

column1: We demanded that Orlkensor fight the Uroxi.
column2: 我们命令奥肯索与乌洛希决斗。

column1: “I can see that I cannot fulfill both my oath to you and my oath to Ernalda. This fight is inevitable.” And he left the clan hall to fight the Uroxi.
column2: “我看得出我无法同时履行对你的誓言和对埃尔纳尔达的誓言。这场战斗不可避免。”说完他离开部族大厅去与乌洛希战斗。

column1: Orlkensor refused to fight. “If I break my vow to Ernalda, how can you trust me to honor my vow to you?”
column2: 奥肯索拒绝战斗。“如果我违背对埃尔纳尔达的誓言，你们怎能相信我会遵守对你们的誓言？”

column1: Suggest that they resolve their differences peacefully.
column2: 建议他们和平解决分歧。

column1: We suggest that they resolve their differences peacefully.
column2: 我们建议他们和平解决分歧。

column1: This won a sad look from Orlkensor and crazed laughter from the Uroxi.
column2: 这换来了奥肯索悲伤的目光和乌洛希癫狂的大笑。

column1: Use force to drive the Uroxi off.
column2: 用武力赶走乌洛希。

column1: We used force to drive the Uroxi off.
column2: 我们用武力赶走了乌洛希。

column1: Enraged, the Uroxi fought off the warriors we sent to drive him away.
column2: 暴怒的乌洛希击退了我们派去驱赶他的战士。

column1: He wounded some of our fighters, and then said he would leave.
column2: 他伤了我们几名战士，然后说他会离开。

column1: He killed some of our fighters and wounded others. Then said he would leave.
column2: 他杀了我们几名战士又伤了其他人，然后说他会离开。

column1: “Orlkensor should not consider our dispute settled,” the Uroxi said. “I will not violate the sanctity of your clan hall by going in to get him now. But I shall get him. That I swear, by Urox’s horns.”
column2: “奥肯索别以为我们的争端就此了结，”乌洛希说，“我不会闯入你们部族大厅的圣地现在就去抓他，但我一定会抓到他。我以乌洛克斯之角发誓。”

column1: Neither man is about to waver.
column2: 两人都不肯退让。

column1: If we offend the Uroxi, we could have trouble with all of the Storm Bulls in Dragon Pass.
column2: 如果我们冒犯乌洛希，可能会与龙隘的所有风暴公牛信徒结下仇怨。

column1: How could we know that Orlkensor would turn out to be a rat?
column2: 我们怎么可能知道奥肯索到头来是个鼠辈？

column1: In the short time he has been here, Orlkensor has proven himself worthy.
column2: 来到这里的短短时间里，奥肯索已经证明了自己值得信赖。

column1: We must find the peaceful way.
column2: 我们必须找到和平之道。

column1: Let us sweep this yawping bully from our lands!
column2: 让我们把这个大呼小叫的恶霸赶出我们的土地！

column1: The feud between the Alkanar and Red Hay clans began with a personal dispute between two thanes.
column2: 阿尔卡纳氏族与红干草氏族之间的世仇始于两位领主之间的私人争端。

column1: We will not understand this until it is over, if then.
column2: 我们恐怕要到事情结束才能明白，或许那时也未必。

column1: The Storm Bull is all bluff and no bite.
column2: 风暴公牛全是虚张声势，没有真本事。

column1: He looks like a worthy foe!
column2: 他看起来像个值得一战的对手！

column1: All the Storm Bulls in the valley will attack us if this Uroxi is killed!
column2: 如果这个乌洛希被杀，山谷里所有风暴公牛信徒都会来攻击我们！

column1: This dispute is over the love of a woman.
column2: 这场争端源于对一个女人的爱。

column1: After this is over, we should give gifts to the Uroxi.
column2: 这件事结束后，我们应该给乌洛希送礼。

column1: Orlkensor is one of us now.
column2: 奥尔肯索现在是我们的一员了。

column1: This is always the way it ends.
column2: 结局总是如此。

column1: Uh-oh. Make sure he doesn’t… wait, don’t let him…
column2: 哎呀。确保他别……等等，别让他……

column1: Storm Bulls need to remember their place.
column2: 风暴公牛们需要记住自己的位置。

column1: Oh no. Oh no!
column2: 哦不。哦不！

column1: As good Orlanthi… well, it’s not easy to say what we should do.
column2: 作为正直的奥兰希人……嗯，很难说我们应该怎么做。

column1: If we’re lucky, this will just be a temporary misunderstanding.
column2: 如果我们运气好，这只是一个暂时的误会。

column1: We wouldn’t have this kind of problem any more if we could learn how to speak with the Dragonewts.
column2: 如果我们学会与龙人交谈，就不会再有这种问题了。

column1: “A found sword is a friend. A falling rock is an enemy, even to itself.”
column2: “拾到的剑是朋友。滚落的石头是敌人，连对它自己也是。”

column1: Stupid bully.
column2: 愚蠢的恶霸。

column1: Why doesn’t anyone listen to me before we have these problems?
column2: 为什么在出问题之前没人听我的？

column1: Whew. For a second there, I thought he was after me.
column2: 呼。刚才那一瞬，我还以为他在追我。

column1: Sometimes the bulls have to fight, and nothing else will do.
column2: 有时公牛们必须战斗，别无他法。

column1: Fight!
column2: 战斗！

column1: Our people watched in dismay as the two fought a furious battle. Each dealt terrible blows to the other.
column2: 我们的人民沮丧地看着两人激战。双方都给对方造成了可怕的创伤。

column1: Then the Uroxi drove his sword through Orlkensor’s heart, slaying Orlkensor. “Now my Valensta’s honor is restored,” the Uroxi muttered, and left our tula without a further word.
column2: 接着乌洛希将剑刺入奥尔肯索的心脏，杀死了奥尔肯索。“现在我的瓦伦斯塔的荣誉恢复了，”乌洛希低语道，然后一言不发地离开了我们的领地。

column1: Then Orlkensor disarmed the Uroxi. He gave the man a chance to relent, but the Uroxi would not. So Orlkensor dropped his own sword, leapt upon the furious Storm Bull, and snapped his neck. “I have broken my vow,” Orlkensor said, “and will not curse you by staying, as an oath-breaker, among you.” He left immediately, despite all of our pleading. He was heading west.
column2: 随后奥尔肯索解除了乌洛希的武装。他给了那人一个让步的机会，但乌洛希不肯。于是奥尔肯索丢下自己的剑，扑向狂暴的风暴公牛，拧断了他的脖子。“我违背了誓言，”奥尔肯索说，“不会作为一个背誓者留在你们中间，诅咒你们。”尽管我们百般恳求，他还是立刻离开了。他朝西边走去。

column1: sceneR172
column2: sceneR172

column1: A dwarf invasion force comes to your tula and destroys it. Your brave warriors fall before the hail of magical fire from their legendary implements of destruction. The dwarfs complete their carnage calmly and without remorse, killing warriors and non-combatants alike.
column2: 一支矮人入侵部队来到你的领地并将其摧毁。你勇敢的战士倒在他们传奇毁灭武器发出的魔法弹雨之下。矮人冷静而无悔地完成了屠杀，不分战士与非战斗人员。

column1: A dwarf army came to our tula and destroyed nearly everything.
column2: 一支矮人军队来到我们的领地，摧毁了几乎所有东西。

column1: For all we know, they have poisoned the land. Our clan is no more.
column2: 据我们所知，他们已毒害了这片土地。我们的氏族不复存在。

column1: If only we had treated the dwarfs as we wished to be treated ourselves!
column2: 要是我们曾像希望被对待那样对待矮人就好了！

column1: They took our livestock, our goods, and our stored food. But they have not taken our heritage, or bound the spirits of our ancestors. We must soldier on.
column2: 他们夺走了我们的牲畜、货物和储存的食物。但他们没有夺走我们的传承，也没有束缚祖先之灵。我们必须继续坚持下去。

column1: And I thought Humakt was efficient in the dealing of death!
column2: 我还以为胡马克特在杀戮中效率高超呢！

column1: If we are alive, we are not defeated.
column2: 只要我们还活着，就没有被打败。

column1: Bulls from other clans will raid us soon. Better to offer our few remaining cows, than have them taken from us.
column2: 其他氏族的公牛们很快就会来袭击我们。不如献出我们仅剩的几头牛，总比被他们抢走好。

column1: In trying to trick the dwarfs, we tricked ourselves.
column2: 在试图欺骗矮人时，我们欺骗了自己。

column1: They didn’t destroy everything. We did our best to defend our home.
column2: 他们没有摧毁一切。我们尽力保卫了家园。

column1: When Chaos came, Vinga did not give up. She fought, even though everything seemed hopeless.
column2: 当混沌来临时，文嘉没有放弃。她战斗了，尽管一切看似绝望。

column1: sceneR173
column2: sceneR173

column1: A huge force of trolls, led by the legendary Cragspider the Firewitch, descend on your tula. They kill everyone in sight, combatants and noncombatants alike. Cragspider proves to be a fearsome foe; her bolts of flame alone are responsible for killing perhaps a third of your people. The troll warriors who accompany her do their share of killing, too. A few brave survivors witness the aftermath from a vantage point in the forest. The trolls loot your steads, and round up your livestock. They slaughter the animals and throw the carcasses onto large wagons. They do the same with the corpses of the slain. The corpses that do not fit on the wagon are devoured by the trolls, on the spot.
column2: 一支庞大的巨魔部队，由传奇人物火巫克拉格斯派德率领，降临在你的领地。他们杀死视线内所有人，不分战斗人员与非战斗人员。克拉格斯派德被证明是可怕的敌人；仅她的火焰箭矢就杀死了大约三分之一的子民。随行的巨魔战士也尽了自己的杀戮之责。少数勇敢的幸存者从森林中的有利位置目睹了这一切。巨魔洗劫了你们的农庄，圈起了你们的牲畜。他们屠杀动物，将尸体扔上大车。对被杀者的尸体也如法炮制。装不上车的尸体当场被巨魔吞食。

column1: Trolls came and laid waste to our tula. Almost everyone was killed.
column2: 巨魔来了，将我们的领地夷为废墟。几乎所有人都被杀死了。

column1: They have taken almost all of our food. How can we possibly continue?
column2: 他们夺走了我们几乎所有的食物。我们怎么可能继续下去？

column1: If only we had treated the trolls as we wished to be treated ourselves!
column2: 要是我们曾像希望被对待那样对待巨魔就好了！

column1: They took all of our food, and the lives of three out of four of our people. But they have not taken our heritage, or bound the spirits of our ancestors. We must soldier on.
column2: 他们夺走了我们所有的食物，以及四分之三族人的生命。但他们没有夺走我们的传承，也没有束缚祖先之灵。我们必须继续坚持下去。

column1: We must all vow vengeance on the trolls, and live only to slay them. We will be destroyed, but we will take enemies with us.
column2: 我们所有人都必须发誓向巨魔复仇，活着只为杀死他们。我们将被毁灭，但我们会拉上敌人陪葬。

column1: Almost every cow, every sheep, every horse and every pig — gone. Gone!
column2: 几乎每一头牛、每一只羊、每一匹马和每一头猪——都没了。都没了！

column1: Making Cragspider herself angry enough to come down all the way from the north to personally wipe us out — that’s quite an accomplishment!
column2: 让克拉格斯派德本人愤怒到一路从北方南下亲自消灭我们——这可真是了不起的成就！

column1: We tried to defend the hearth, and we failed. We do not deserve to continue.
column2: 我们试图保卫炉火，但我们失败了。我们不配继续存在。

column1: sceneR174
column2: sceneR174

column1: Factions appeared among the weaponthanes, who squabbled over the division of loot from a raid.
column2: 武器领主中出现了派系，为一次突袭的战利品分配而争吵。

column1: Give the bravos three quarters of the loot.
column2: 把战利品的四分之三给那些好斗者。

column1: We awarded the bulk of the loot to the complaining faction.
column2: 我们将大部分战利品判给了抱怨的一方。

column1: We persuaded the veterans that they had indeed taken the cream of the loot in the past, although they had not meant to do so. Both sides agreed that the matter was over and done with.
column2: 我们说服了老兵们，他们过去确实拿走了战利品的精华，尽管并非有意为之。双方都同意此事就此了结。

column1: The young warriors were satisfied, but the veterans were sorely aggrieved. They grumbled for a long time afterwards.
column2: 年轻战士们满意了，但老兵们深感委屈。此后他们抱怨了很久。

column1: Let them work it out themselves.
column2: 让他们自己解决。

column1: We let them resolve the matter themselves.
column2: 我们让他们自行解决此事。

column1: Weaponthanes on both sides of the dispute were ashamed that their squabble had reached the ears of the ring. They pledged to behave properly in the future.
column2: 争端双方的武器领主都因争吵传到了长老会耳中而羞愧。他们承诺今后会守规矩。

column1: The squabbling factions could not agree, and each demanded that the ring resolve the dispute.
column2: 争吵的派系无法达成一致，各自要求长老会解决争端。

column1: Order that the loot be shared equally.
column2: 下令平分战利品。

column1: We ordered that the loot be shared equally.
column2: 我们下令平分战利品。

column1: The warriors recognized the justice of our decision.
column2: 武士们认可我们裁决的公正。

column1: Both sides of the dispute were displeased. The young warriors said that they had been shorted in the past, and the veterans said that they should be compensated for having to endure the insults of the bravos.
column2: 争端双方都不满意。年轻武士说他们过去一直吃亏，老战士则说他们忍受了那些暴徒的侮辱，理应得到补偿。

column1: Punish both sides; confiscate all of the loot.
column2: 惩罚双方；没收全部战利品。

column1: To show them that squabbling would not be tolerated, the chieftain took all of the loot.
column2: 为了让他们明白争吵不会被容忍，酋长拿走了所有战利品。

column1: Both sides took the rebuke as it was intended. They said that we were right to remind them of dignity and honor, and they pledged to behave properly in the future.
column2: 双方领会了训诫的本意。他们说我们提醒他们尊严与荣誉是对的，并承诺今后会守规矩。

column1: This united both sides. Unfortunately, it united them in feeling that the ring was unjust.
column2: 这反而让双方团结起来。不幸的是，他们团结在认为长老会不公的共识上。

column1: Punish complainers by giving the veterans three quarters of the loot.
column2: 惩罚抱怨者，把战利品的三分之二给老战士。

column1: We punished the complainers by giving the veterans three quarters of the loot.
column2: 我们惩罚了抱怨者，把战利品的三分之二给了老战士。

column1: They were chastened, and admitted that their grievances were exaggerated and harmful to the unity of the clan.
column2: 他们受到了训诫，承认自己的抱怨夸大其词，损害了氏族的团结。

column1: This decision only aggravated the grievance of the young warriors. They said it was proof that we favored the slow over the swift.
column2: 这个决定只会加剧年轻武士的不满。他们说这证明我们偏爱迟钝者而非敏捷者。

column1: This dispute has little to do with young and old; it is more about petty personality conflicts.
column2: 这场争执与年龄大小关系不大；更多是琐碎的性格冲突。

column1: The warriors are already discontented. If we allow this to continue, things will get much worse.
column2: 武士们已经心怀不满。如果我们任由事态发展，情况会更糟。

column1: This is a trifling matter. If we involve ourselves, we will probably make it worse.
column2: 这是小事一桩。如果我们插手，很可能让事情更糟。

column1: Back in the Storm Age, King Vingkot placed a shattered clan under our protection. That clan was called the Nalda Bin.
column2: 回到风暴时代，王温格科特将一个破碎的氏族置于我们的保护之下。那个氏族叫纳尔达·宾。

column1: Honey is sweeter than blood.
column2: 蜂蜜比血更甜。

column1: The weaponthanes will respond to strict discipline.
column2: 武器领主会对严格纪律做出回应。

column1: Eurmal had a scab, and he picked at it until it fell off and transformed into a terrible enemy.
column2: 尤尔马尔有个痂，他不停地抠，直到痂脱落，变成了一个可怕的敌人。

column1: Give the young brats a good swat.
column2: 好好教训那些小崽子一顿。

column1: The brave young warriors are always subtly abused by the more cautious, older fighters.
column2: 勇敢的年轻武士总是被更谨慎的年长战士暗中打压。

column1: It’s my fault, isn’t it?
column2: 是我的错，对吧？

column1: This sort of thing is bound to happen.
column2: 这种事迟早会发生。

column1: If we had more Vingan warriors, this would never happen.
column2: 如果我们有更多温干战士，这种事绝不会发生。

column1: Punish the complainers.
column2: 惩罚抱怨者。

column1: P
column2: P

column1: sceneR175
column2: sceneR175

column1: A woman whose insignia corresponds to no local clan comes to you with a proposal. “I am Saraska Bright-Eyes, and it has been prophesied that I will unite the tribes and make this the land called Saraska. I will be Queen of the Kings, the Peaceful Hero, the Great Uniter. I know that your people helped make a tribe when there were only clans, so I now seek your aid in making a kingdom where there are only tribes.”
column2: 一位徽记不属于本地任何氏族的女子来找你，提出一个建议。“我是萨拉斯卡·亮眼，预言说我将统一诸部族，使这片土地成为名为萨拉斯卡的王国。我将成为众王之王、和平英雄、伟大统一者。我知道你们的族人曾帮助过在只有氏族时建立部族的事，所以现在我寻求你们的帮助，在只有部族时建立王国。”

column1: She concludes with an impromptu ritual asking the gods to favor us and her plan.
column2: 她以一个即兴仪式作为结尾，祈求诸神眷顾我们和她的计划。

column1: A woman called Saraska Bright-Eyes came to us and said she would unify the tribes of Dragon Pass.
column2: 一位名叫萨拉斯卡·亮眼的女子来到我们面前，说她将统一龙隘的诸部族。

column1: We conducted a divination.
column2: 我们进行了一次占卜。

column1: The god-talkers said that the omens surrounding this Saraska Bright-Eyes were all bad. She did not have the favor of the gods; the prophecies she speaks of refer to someone who is not yet born.
column2: 神言者们说，围绕这位萨拉斯卡·亮眼的征兆全是凶兆。她没有得到诸神的恩惠；她所说的预言指的是一个尚未出生的人。

column1: They could not say if her luck would rub off on those who helped her or opposed her.
column2: 他们说不上她的运气是否会波及帮助她或反对她的人。

column1: The god-talkers said that the omens surrounding Saraska Bright-Eyes were good. She might well be the subject of the prophecies about a true kingdom of Orlanth in Dragon Pass.
column2: 神言者们说，围绕萨拉斯卡·亮眼的征兆是吉兆。她很可能是关于龙隘将出现一个真正的奥兰斯王国的预言所指之人。

column1: This could be our chance to align ourselves with destiny, by supporting her kingdom-building.
column2: 这可能是我们顺应天命的机会，通过支持她建立王国。

column1: Receive her politely, but promise nothing.
column2: 礼貌地接待她，但什么也不承诺。

column1: We promised her nothing.
column2: 我们没有对她做出任何承诺。

column1: She said that we would see the truth of her words soon enough.
column2: 她说我们很快会看到她的预言成真。

column1: “Come back when you’ve won the support of other clans.”
column2: “等你赢得其他氏族的支持再回来。”

column1: We told her to come back when she had won the support of other clans.
column2: 我们告诉她，等她赢得其他氏族的支持再回来。

column1: She said that she would do this. “You will have to beat your shields loudly, for me to notice you, when the other clans rally around me and proclaim my kingdom.”
column2: 她说她会这么做。“当其他氏族聚集在我周围，宣告我的王国时，你们得使劲敲响你们的盾牌，我才会注意到你们。”

column1: Saraska seemed satisfied that we were supporting her cause in a way we knew best.
column2: 萨拉斯卡似乎对我们以最擅长的方式支持她的事业感到满意。

column1: I have not Seen her at all. So she could succeed or fail.
column2: 我完全没有预见到她的未来。所以她可能成功也可能失败。

column1: We can’t trust this woman.
column2: 我们不能信任这个女人。

column1: She is sincere.
column2: 她很真诚。

column1: Saraska is sincere. But there is something amiss about her.
column2: 萨拉斯卡是真诚的。但她身上有些不对劲。

column1: This is not the way we do things here in Dragon Pass.
column2: 这不是我们在龙隘行事的规矩。

column1: What she suggests is contrary to local tradition. But all traditions were innovations, once.
column2: 她的建议违背了当地传统。但所有传统都曾经是创新。

column1: Let us see how she attempts to make a kingdom — we can always take over after her.
column2: 让我们看看她如何尝试建立王国——我们总可以在她之后接手。

column1: If the prophecies say it is so, it is so.
column2: 如果预言如此说，那便是如此。

column1: Our magic is weak. If we conduct a divination, our god-talkers may misinterpret the signs.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱。如果我们进行占卜，我们的神言者可能会误解征兆。

column1: Our magic is strong, and our god-talkers are wise. They will find the truth.
column2: 我们的魔法强大，我们的神言者睿智。他们会找到真相。

column1: Our ancestors once served loyally under a king who was an immortal troll.
column2: 我们的祖先曾忠诚地侍奉一位不朽的巨魔国王。

column1: It is bad enough that we are part of a tribe, let alone a kingdom.
column2: 我们属于一个部落就已经够糟了，更不用说一个王国了。

column1: We cannot throw away the achievements of our grandfathers and grandmothers, by submerging our holy tribe into a useless kingdom!
column2: 我们不能将我们神圣的部落淹没在一个无用的王国中，从而抛弃我们祖辈的成就！

column1: So bright-shining were her eyes, that her brow was star-limned.
column2: 她的双眼如此明亮，眉宇间仿佛绘着星辰。

column1: We must at least give her a chance to make her case.
column2: 我们至少该给她一个机会陈述她的理由。

column1: This reminds me of that prophecy about making something new.
column2: 这让我想起那个关于创造新事物的预言。

column1: She may be the one in that weird prophecy we heard once, that said we’d end up in Orlanth’s Hall.
column2: 她可能就是那个我们曾听过的古怪预言中提到的人，预言说我们最终会进入奥兰斯的大殿。

column1: She sounds like the one in that odd prophecy we heard once.
column2: 她听起来就像我们曾听过的那个古怪预言中的人。

column1: I would like to believe this is the woman in that odd prophecy we heard once. Perform a divination first, then hear her out.
column2: 我宁愿相信这就是那个古怪预言中的女人。先进行一次占卜，再听她说完。

column1: I would like to believe this is the woman in that odd prophecy we heard once. She could show us the way to even greater glory!
column2: 我宁愿相信这就是那个古怪预言中的女人。她或许能指引我们走向更伟大的荣耀！

column1: Remember Saraska, the woman who claimed that she was destined to be ruler of a great kingdom in Dragon Pass? She was unable to convince any of the tribes to help her.
column2: 还记得萨拉斯卡吗？那个自称命中注定要成为龙之隘口伟大王国统治者的女人。她未能说服任何部落帮助她。

column1: The last we heard of Saraska, she marched off in a high rage with a rag-tag band of followers, insisting that she would make a great kingdom someday.
column2: 我们最后一次听到萨拉斯卡的消息，她带着一群乌合之众怒不可遏地离去，坚称自己终将建立一个伟大的王国。

column1: Our recent political upheavals caused us to neglect the concerns of Saraska, the woman who claimed a destiny as Queen of Dragon Pass.
column2: 近来的政治动荡让我们忽略了萨拉斯卡的诉求，就是那个自称命运注定成为龙之隘口女王的女子。

column1: She was unable to keep the support of the tribes who were willing to help her, nor could she overcome the ill-will of the tribes who opposed her.
column2: 她既无法保住那些愿意帮助她的部落的支持，也克服不了反对她的部落的敌意。

column1: The last we heard of Saraska, she disappeared into the woods with a band of loyal followers, insisting that she would make a great kingdom someday.
column2: 我们最后一次听到萨拉斯卡的消息，她带着一群忠诚的追随者消失在森林中，坚称自己终将建立一个伟大的王国。

column1: sceneR176
column2: sceneR176

column1: We heard that the terrible Praxian hero Jaldon Goldentooth was cutting a swath through Dragon Pass, and heading our way.
column2: 我们听说可怕的普拉克斯英雄贾尔顿·金牙正在龙之隘口大杀四方，正朝我们这边而来。

column1: Offer tribute to Goldentooth if he will bypass your tula.
column2: 如果金牙愿意绕开你的领地，就向他进贡。

column1: We decided to offer tribute to Goldentooth.
column2: 我们决定向金牙进贡。

column1: How many warriors do you send to accompany \x01@\x05?
column2: 你派遣多少战士护送 \x01@\x05？

column1: How much are you prepared to offer him?
column2: 你准备向他献上多少？

column1: Goldentooth said that he was inclined to kill us, but that his sable riders needed loot in order to follow him to his final destination. He agreed not to attack our tula.
column2: 金牙说他本想杀死我们，但他的黑貂骑手需要战利品才能跟随他前往最终目的地。他同意不进攻我们的领地。

column1: Unfortunately, the other clans of Dragon Pass thought of us as betrayers.
column2: 不幸的是，龙之隘口的其他氏族视我们为背叛者。

column1: The delegation never returned.
column2: 使团再也没有回来。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods, so that Goldentooth will attack elsewhere.
column2: 向众神献祭，让金牙去攻打别处。

column1: We sacrificed to the gods, so that Goldentooth would attack elsewhere.
column2: 我们向众神献祭，让金牙去攻打别处。

column1: The omens were good.
column2: 征兆是吉兆。

column1: The god-talkers said that the omens were bad.
column2: 神言者说征兆是凶兆。

column1: But we got lucky.
column2: 但我们运气好。

column1: But our luck turned out bad after all.
column2: 但我们的运气终究还是变坏了。

column1: Send a force to fight Goldentooth before he arrives.
column2: 在金牙抵达之前派遣一支部队去迎战。

column1: We sent a force to fight Goldentooth before he arrives.
column2: 我们在金牙抵达之前派遣了一支部队去迎战。

column1: Our war party was destroyed to a man.
column2: 我们的战团全军覆没。

column1: Send noncombatants to a distant clan.
column2: 将非战斗人员送到一个遥远的氏族去。

column1: We sent our noncombatants away.
column2: 我们送走了非战斗人员。

column1: Set traps throughout the tula to thwart Goldentooth’s invasion.
column2: 在整个领地设置陷阱，以挫败金牙的入侵。

column1: We prepared ourselves by laying traps for Goldentooth’s horde.
column2: 我们布置陷阱，为金牙的大军做好准备。

column1: Goldentooth’s horde ravaged our tula. They slew many warriors, and some noncombatants. They smashed our fortifications and took a quarter of our herds. They even killed some of our children.
column2: 金牙的大军洗劫了我们的领地。他们杀死了许多战士和一些非战斗人员。他们摧毁了我们的防御工事，抢走了四分之一的畜群。他们甚至杀害了我们的一些孩子。

column1: Goldentooth’s horde ravaged our tula. They slew many warriors. They smashed our fortifications and took a quarter of our herds.
column2: 金牙的大军洗劫了我们的领地。他们杀死了许多战士。他们摧毁了我们的防御工事，抢走了四分之一的畜群。

column1: The damage would have been much worse had not the clan ring led the defense. \x01@\x13 sacrificed \x08self so the rest of us could drive off Jaldon.
column2: 若非氏族议会领导了防御，损失会惨重得多。 \x01@\x13 牺牲了 \x08自己，我们其余人才得以击退贾尔顿。

column1: We mourned \x08 but had no time to waste on elaborate funeral rites.
column2: 我们哀悼 \x08 ，但没有时间浪费在繁复的葬礼仪式上。

column1: One ring member suffered grievous wounds.
column2: 一名议会成员身负重伤。

column1: \x01@\x06 ring members suffered grievous wounds.
column2: \x01@\x06 议会成员身负重伤。

column1: We can’t afford to offer a generous tribute.
column2: 我们负担不起丰厚的贡品。

column1: We can afford to offer a generous tribute.
column2: 我们负担得起丰厚的贡品。

column1: We should immediately dispatch a force to head Goldentooth off.
column2: 我们应当立即派遣一支部队去拦截金牙。

column1: Goldentooth is a legendary slayer of men. This may be the most terrible battle we have ever faced.
column2: 金牙是传说中的屠戮者。这可能是我们面临过的最可怕的战斗。

column1: Goldentooth is a legendary slayer of men. If he comes here, many of us will die.
column2: 金牙是传说中的屠戮者。如果他来到这里，我们许多人都会死。

column1: Our time is best used to lay traps, and prepare for the most terrible battle we have ever faced.
column2: 我们的时间最好用来布置陷阱，为有史以来最可怕的战斗做准备。

column1: The gods have little influence over the actions of our enemies.
column2: 众神对我们敌人的行动影响甚微。

column1: The gods have little influence over the actions of our enemies. Perhaps Ernalda could help us, a little.
column2: 众神对我们敌人的行动影响甚微。也许厄娜尔达能帮我们一点忙。

column1: Is there no end to our woes? A horrible foe in Sea season, when we should be planting our crops.
column2: 我们的苦难何时才到头？海季里来了个可怕的敌人，而这时本该是播种的时候。

column1: Is there no end to our woes? A horrible foe in Earth season, when we should be bringing in our crops.
column2: 我们的苦难何时才到头？地季里来了个可怕的敌人，而这时本该是收获的时候。

column1: Goldentooth has been killed several times throughout history, but always returns to kill again.
column2: 金牙在历史上曾被杀死过多次，但总是归来继续杀戮。

column1: There is no bargaining with an avatar of death.
column2: 与死亡的化身没有议价的余地。

column1: We must spend our precious time finding refuge for those who cannot fight.
column2: 我们必须花费宝贵的时间为那些不能战斗的人寻找避难所。

column1: This Goldentooth is not all he is said to be.
column2: 这个金牙并不像传闻中那样。

column1: We should not wait until Goldentooth brings the fight to us. We should take it to him.
column2: 我们不应该坐等金牙将战斗带到我们面前。我们应该主动出击。

column1: We brought this on ourselves, somehow.
column2: 不知怎的，这是我们自找的。

column1: Golden — Goldentooth? Jaldon Goldentooth? Oh. Oh my.
column2: 金牙——金牙？贾尔顿·金牙？哦。哦老天。

column1: We are doomed.
column2: 我们完了。

column1: sceneR177
column2: sceneR177

column1: The number of clans in our tribe dwindled until we could no longer support our agreements, and the tribe fell apart.
column2: 我们部落中的氏族数量不断减少，直到我们无法再履行盟约，部落就此瓦解。

column1: Once again, the number of clans in our tribe dwindled until we could no longer support our agreements, and the tribe fell apart.
column2: 又一次，我们部落中的氏族数量不断减少，直到我们无法再履行盟约，部落就此瓦解。

column1: We were without a tribe, and wondered what to do.
column2: 我们失去了部落，不知该如何是好。

column1: Now you are without a tribe. The carls say that their herds will be subject to raiding without the protection of a tribe. The weaponthanes are worried, too.
column2: 如今你们失去了部落。自由民说，没有部落保护，他们的牲畜会遭劫掠。武器领主们也很担忧。

column1: The only other tribe of the region is the \x01Á.
column2: 该地区唯一的另一个部落是 \x01Á.

column1: The people feel hopeless. “What use is there in our joining a tribe,” they lament, “when tribes shift out from under us like sand under a wheel?”
column2: 人们感到绝望。“我们加入部落又有什么用？”他们哀叹，“部落像车轮下的沙子一样从我们脚下流走？”

column1: Everyone fears what the next step will be, though everyone knows what it is.
column2: 每个人都害怕下一步会怎样，尽管人人都知道那是什么。

column1: Ask to join the \x01@= tribe.
column2: 请求加入 \x01@= 部落。

column1: We asked to join the \x01@= tribe.
column2: 我们请求加入 \x01@= 部落。

column1: How much total wealth do you distribute among the \x01@\x0E \x01@= clans before your petition is heard?
column2: 在你们的请愿被受理之前，你们在 \x01@\x0E \x01@= 氏族中共分配了多少财富？

column1: Ask to join the \x01@E tribe.
column2: 请求加入 \x01@E 部落。

column1: We asked to join the \x01@E tribe.
column2: 我们请求加入 \x01@E 部落。

column1: How much total wealth do you distribute among the \x01@\x0E \x01@E clans before your petition is heard?
column2: 在你们的请愿被受理之前，你们在 \x01@\x0E \x01@E 氏族中共分配了多少财富？

column1: Beg to rejoin your old tribe.
column2: 乞求重新加入你们原来的部落。

column1: We begged to rejoin our old tribe.
column2: 我们乞求重新加入原来的部落。

column1: They laughed and jeered, but said they would hear our claim.
column2: 他们嘲笑讥讽，但说会听我们的请求。

column1: They would only take us back if they would give half of our wealth to them
column2: 他们只会在我们把一半财富交给他们的前提下重新接纳我们。

column1: They demand that you take half of your wealth and distribute it among the other clans. Do you agree?
column2: 他们要求你们取出一半财富分给其他氏族。你们同意吗？

column1: We agreed, and returned to the fold, our reputation sullied. We were called The Foolish Clan. Our ancestor spirits refused to talk to our priests for many weeks.
column2: 我们同意了，回归了部落，但名声受损。我们被称为“愚者氏族”。我们的祖先之灵连续数周拒绝与祭司交谈。

column1: We refused to.
column2: 我们拒绝了。

column1: They said they didn’t want a clan of stickpickers in their tribe.
column2: 他们说他们不想要一群拾柴人氏族加入他们的部落。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors said that the apple skins were cloudy, and that the geese flew east. None of our god-talkers could say what this meant…
column2: 我们的祖先之灵说苹果皮浑浊不清，大雁向东飞去。我们的神言者无人能说出这意味着什么……

column1: The spirits of our ancestors told us to petition the \x01@\x01 tribe, and offer each clan twenty cows.
column2: 我们的祖先之灵告诉我们向 \x01@\x01 部落请愿，并向每个氏族献上二十头牛。

column1: The god-talkers said that the voices of our ancestors mumbled, the sheep entrails were rotten, and the flames refused to burn clearly. They said the gods were turning their backs on us.
column2: 神言者说祖先的声音含混不清，羊的内脏腐烂了，火焰不肯明亮地燃烧。他们说神明正在背弃我们。

column1: Our leaders saw little choice but to disband the clan. Our people scattered, seeking adoption into other clans. Thus ends the saga of the \x01@" clan.
column2: 我们的领袖别无选择，只能解散氏族。我们的人民四散，寻求被其他氏族收养。 \x01@" 氏族的传说就此终结。

column1: Continue as a solitary clan.
column2: 作为独立氏族继续存在。

column1: We decided to continue as a solitary clan.
column2: 我们决定作为独立氏族继续存在。

column1: They rejected our petition, on the grounds that our leadership was weak.
column2: 他们拒绝了我们的请愿，理由是领导力薄弱。

column1: They rejected our petition, on the grounds that our kennings were incomprehensible.
column2: 他们拒绝了我们的请愿，理由是我們的隐喻令人费解。

column1: They rejected our petition, on the grounds that our cows were scrawny and our fields festooned with weeds.
column2: 他们拒绝了我们的请愿，理由是牛只瘦弱，田里杂草丛生。

column1: They rejected our petition, saying that they had no need of pedants who knew everything about the law and nothing about life.
column2: 他们拒绝了我们的请愿，说他们不需要那些精通法律却对生活一无所知的学究。

column1: They rejected our petition, on the grounds that our weaponthanes were undisciplined and our record of victory questionable.
column2: 他们拒绝了我们的请愿，理由是武器领主缺乏纪律，胜利记录存疑。

column1: They rejected our petition. After we had left the tribal hall and the tula of its host, their children pelted us with rotten vegetables.
column2: 他们拒绝了我们的请愿。我们离开部落大厅和主人领地后，他们的孩子向我们投掷腐烂的蔬菜。

column1: We are poor, but must act as if we are rich.
column2: 我们很穷，但必须表现得富有。

column1: We are wealthy, and must be willing to show it.
column2: 我们很富有，也必须乐意展示出来。

column1: We are still wealthy, and must use it before we grow poorer.
column2: 我们依然富有，必须在变穷之前利用它。

column1: If we show our generosity, another tribe will adopt us.
column2: 如果我们展示慷慨，另一个部落会收养我们。

column1: If we give each of its clans ten cows, another tribe will adopt us.
column2: 如果我们给每个氏族十头牛，另一个部落会收养我们。

column1: If we give each of its clans twenty cows, another tribe will adopt us.
column2: 如果我们给每个氏族二十头牛，另一个部落会收养我们。

column1: Without a tribe, we \x02\x03are an easy target for anyone who wants to pick on us/will be raided into oblivion/cannot hope to defend ourselves well\x02.
column2: 没有部落，我们 \x02\x03是任何人都可以轻易欺负的目标/会被劫掠直至消亡/无法很好地自卫\x02。

column1: We should petition the \x01Á.
column2: 我们应该向……请愿 \x01Á.

column1: There is no point in petitioning anyone, we are too small and weak to be welcome in a tribe.
column2: 向任何人请愿都没有意义，我们太小太弱，不会被部落欢迎。

column1: Our magic is strong. A divination will yield a clear answer.
column2: 我们的魔法很强大。一次占卜会给出清晰的答案。

column1: Our magic is weak. A divination will yield us nothing more than a bunch of vague and irrelevant images.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱。占卜只会给我们一堆模糊且无关的图像。

column1: Our magic is poor. Save it for convincing another tribe to let us join them.
column2: 我们的魔法很差。留着它用于说服另一个部落接纳我们吧。

column1: Without a tribe, our granaries will be looted, and our fields burned.
column2: 没有部落，我们的粮仓会被洗劫，田地会被焚烧。

column1: I have many convoluted arguments I can use to convince another tribe to accept us.
column2: 我有很多复杂的论据可以用来说服另一个部落接受我们。

column1: Maybe the gods could help us. Even Eurmal might be useful now.
column2: 也许神明能帮助我们。就连欧尔玛现在都可能派上用场。

column1: Now we are back the way we were meant to be.
column2: 现在我们回到了我们本应如此的状态。

column1: If we hadn’t started this whole tribe business, there would be no tribes, and we wouldn’t be in this spot. What fools we were!
column2: 如果我们当初没有开启这整个部落的麻烦事，就不会有部落存在，我们也不会落到这步田地。我们多傻啊！

column1: Now I’ll just have to go my own way, won’t I?
column2: 现在我只能走自己的路了，不是吗？

column1: I told you it was a bad idea to quit the tribe.
column2: 我告诉过你，脱离部族是个坏主意。

column1: I told you we won’t find another home.
column2: 我告诉过你，我们找不到另一个家园。

column1: I knew we were fated for obscurity.
column2: 我就知道我们注定默默无闻。

column1: If we must disband, then the other clans will clamor to adopt our people, I just know it.
column2: 如果必须解散，其他氏族肯定会争着接纳我们的人，我敢肯定。

column1: If only we were dragonewts. We could reincarnate into new bodies, and everything would be fine.
column2: 要是我们是龙人就好了。我们可以转生到新身体里，一切都会好起来。

column1: If only we knew dragonewt magics, our divinations would be certain to be right.
column2: 要是我们懂龙人魔法就好了，我们的占卜就肯定准确。

column1: Without a tribe, we are nothing.
column2: 没有部族，我们什么都不是。

column1: \x02\x04We are cursed/We are luckless/It is hopeless/We are soon to be dead\x02.
column2: \x02\x04我们被诅咒了/我们不走运/没有希望了/我们很快就要死了\x02。

column1: We are doomed now.
column2: 我们这下完蛋了。

column1: We should just \x02\x03humble/abase/mortify\x02 ourselves and \x02\x04beg/plead/implore them/grovel\x02 until our old tribe takes us back in.
column2: 我们不如 \x02\x03谦卑/卑微/自贬\x02 自己，然后 \x02\x04乞求/恳求/哀求他们/匍匐在地\x02 ，直到老部族重新接纳我们。

column1: Oh, whatever is to become of us?
column2: 哦，我们到底会变成什么样？

column1: \x02\x03Who is going to want us/How will we survive/Are we doomed\x02?
column2: \x02\x03谁会要我们/我们怎么活下去/我们注定灭亡吗\x02？

column1: sceneR178
column2: sceneR178

column1: The thanes of the \x01@! clan threatened us with war between our tribe and their new tribe if we did not pay them thirty cows.
column2: 氏族的 \x01@! 领主威胁我们，如果不付三十头牛，就在我们的部族和他们的新部族之间开战。

column1: Call their bluff.
column2: 虚张声势而已。

column1: We said they were bluffing.
column2: 我们说他们在虚张声势。

column1: They said we would soon learn whether or not their threats carried weight.
column2: 他们说我们很快就会知道他们的威胁是否有分量。

column1: Pay them, then arrange for a surprise attack on the \x01Á.
column2: 付给他们，然后安排一次突袭 \x01Á.

column1: We paid them what they asked, then went to the moot to argue for a surprise attack on the \x01Á.
column2: 我们付了他们要的数目，然后去议会主张突袭 \x01Á.

column1: Refuse them, then arrange for a surprise attack on the \x01Á.
column2: 拒绝他们，然后安排一次突袭 \x01Á.

column1: We refused to pay them. After they left, we went to the moot to argue for a surprise attack on the \x01Á.
column2: 我们拒绝付钱。他们离开后，我们去议会主张突袭 \x01Á.

column1: Try to negotiate their demand downwards.
column2: 试着讨价还价，把要求压低。

column1: We dickered with them.
column2: 我们和他们讨价还价。

column1: They’re willing to settle for \x01@\x19 cows. Do you agree to pay?
column2: 他们愿意接受 \x01@\x19 头牛。你同意付吗？

column1: We paid less than they at first demanded.
column2: 我们付的比他们最初要求的少。

column1: We refused to pay.
column2: 我们拒绝付钱。

column1: They left, chortling threats at us.
column2: 他们离开时，得意地朝我们发出威胁。

column1: They refused to reconsider their demands. Do you agree to pay 30 cows?
column2: 他们拒绝重新考虑要求。你同意付30头牛吗？

column1: “Your new tribe is weak. If you attack us, we will destroy you.”
column2: “你们的新部族很弱。如果你们攻击我们，我们会把你们消灭。”

column1: “Your new tribe is weak,” we told them. “If you attack us, we will destroy you.”
column2: “你们的新部族很弱，”我们告诉他们，“如果你们攻击我们，我们会把你们消灭。”

column1: They disagreed with this statement, in most vivid terms.
column2: 他们用最激烈的言辞反驳了这种说法。

column1: Thirty cows mean little to us. Pay them and be done with it.
column2: 三十头牛对我们来说不算什么。付给他们，一了百了。

column1: Let me haggle with them. I can reduce their price.
column2: 让我跟他们谈。我能压下他们的价。

column1: They will never attack us.
column2: 他们绝不会攻击我们。

column1: If we do not fight back when we are threatened, we will be shamed.
column2: 如果受到威胁却不反击，我们会蒙羞。

column1: We have a good chance of beating their tribe.
column2: 我们很有机会打败他们的部族。

column1: If we pay them, they will not expect an attack immediately afterwards. That will be the best way to beat them.
column2: 如果我们付了钱，他们不会想到紧接着就会遭到攻击。那将是打败他们的最佳方式。

column1: They may or may not be able to convince their new tribe-mates to help them raid us.

column1: They are but crawling maggots, easily crushed.
column2: 他们不过是爬行的蛆虫，一捏就碎。

column2: 骗他们以为事情了结，然后攻击他们，这不对。

column1: The trick is to, well, trick them.
column2: 诀窍就是，嗯，骗他们。

column2: 在乌尔格兰成为昏君之前，他带着他的氏族从弯曲杖部族到了奥格德部族。他威胁奥格德人，结果奥格德人杀了他许多战士。

column1: Surely they will settle for less than thirty cows.
column2: 他们肯定愿意接受少于三十头牛的数目。

column1: We must show them that thirty cows is but a pittance to us.
column2: 我们必须让他们明白，三十头牛对我们来说不过是小意思。

column1: Whatever we do, we must show proper respect for the gods.
column2: 无论我们做什么，都必须对神表示应有的敬意。

column1: We will lose far more from fighting than by meeting their demands.
column2: 打仗的损失远比满足他们的要求大得多。

column1: There is something about this in Oskul’s Saga, if only I could remember it…
column2: 奥斯库尔传说里提到过这事，要是我能想起来就好了……

column1: Tell them they have bought their own deaths.
column2: 告诉他们，他们是在自寻死路。

column1: A war broke out within the tribe between rebels and loyalists.

column2: 部族内部爆发了你的氏族与部族其他部分之间的战争。

column1: Abdicate the throne.
column2: 让出王位。

column1: \x01@\x0B abdicated the throne.
column2: \x01@\x0B 让出了王位。

column1: The fighting stopped, so that the jostling for position could begin.
column2: 战斗停止了，以便开始争夺地位。

column1: Call on the gods to punish the disloyal clans.
column2: 祈求神明惩罚不忠的氏族。

column1: Our priests called on the gods to punish the disloyal clans.
column2: 我们的祭司祈求神明惩罚不忠的氏族。

column2: 祭司告诉我们， \x01@\x07 没有给我们任何回应祈祷的迹象。

column1: Fight them, but only after hiring weaponthanes from another tribe to help.
column2: 跟他们打，但得先从另一个部族雇佣武器领主来帮忙。

column2: 你去找哪个部族？

column1: We sought weaponthanes from the \x01@E tribe to fight for us.
column2: 我们到 \x01@E 部族寻求武器领主为我们而战。

column1: How much are you prepared to offer each warrior?
column2: 你准备给每个战士多少报酬？

column1: How many weaponthanes do you seek?
column2: 你找多少武器领主？

column1: We hired many willing warriors.
column2: 我们雇佣了许多愿意作战的战士。

column1: We found few warriors.
column2: 我们只找到少数战士。

column1: No warriors came to our aid.
column2: 没有战士前来援助。

column1: As the conflict draws nigh, \x01@\x10 says, “Remember that clod of earth we got from the Maran Gor priestess? We must have enough clans to use it, because I hear it rumbling.”
column2: 随着冲突临近， \x01@\x10 说道：“还记得我们从玛兰·戈尔女祭司那里得到的那块泥土吗？我们必须凑够足够的氏族来使用它，因为我听到它在隆隆作响。”

column1: The battle was joined.
column2: 战斗打响了。

column1: The rebels overwhelmed our loyalist forces, driving us back and killing many.
column2: 叛乱者压倒了我们的忠臣部队，把我们击退，杀了很多人。

column1: The rebels overwhelmed us, driving us back and killing many.
column2: 叛乱者压倒我们，把我们击退，杀了很多人。

column1: “You win. I surrender the throne.”
column2: “你赢了。我交出王位。”

column1: Launch a quick strike to demoralize the rebels.
column2: 发动一次快速打击，瓦解叛军士气。

column1: We fought to demoralize the rebels.
column2: 我们战斗是为了瓦解叛军士气。

column1: How many warriors do you send to accompany loyalist fighters?
column2: 你派出多少战士与忠诚派战士同行？

column1: Striking quickly and valiantly, our warriors drove back the rebel leaders. But the rebels rallied, taking advantage of their superior force. Our forces were attacked from all sides, and were almost all slain.
column2: 我们战士迅速勇猛地出击，击退了叛军首领。但叛军重整旗鼓，凭借兵力优势反扑。我军四面受敌，几乎全军覆没。

column1: The leaders of the loyalists then seized \x01@\x0B, cursing \x08 for incompetence, and for losing the favor of the gods.
column2: 忠诚派首领们随后抓住了 \x01@\x0B，斥责 \x08 无能，丧失了诸神的眷顾。

column1: The leaders of our clan then seized \x01@\x0B, cursing \x08 for incompetence, and for losing the favor of the gods.
column2: 我们氏族首领们随后抓住了 \x01@\x0B，斥责 \x08 无能，丧失了诸神的眷顾。

column1: Lead an all-out war against the rebels.
column2: 对叛军发动全面战争。

column1: As the conflict nears, \x01@\x10 says, “Remember that clod of earth we got from the Maran Gor priestess? We must have enough clans to use it, because I hear it rumbling.”
column2: 随着冲突临近， \x01@\x10 说道：“还记得我们从玛兰·戈尔女祭司那里得到的那块土块吗？我们必须有足够多的氏族来用它，因为我听到它在隆隆作响。”

column1: The rebels overwhelmed our loyalist forces. They drove us back, killing many. Our clan suffered terrible losses.
column2: 叛军击溃了我们的忠诚派部队。他们击退我们，杀死多人。我氏族损失惨重。

column1: The rebels overwhelmed our forces. They drove us back, killing many. We suffered terrible losses.
column2: 叛军击溃了我们的部队。他们击退我们，杀死多人。我们损失惨重。

column1: “You have won. I surrender the throne.”
column2: “你们赢了。我交出王座。”

column1: No outside warrior will risk his life for less than ten cows. That’s a steep price we may not need to pay.
column2: 没有外族战士愿意为少于十头牛卖命。这个代价太高，我们或许不必支付。

column1: Three cows for each outside warrior should do the trick.
column2: 每个外族战士三头牛就能搞定。

column1: If we must fight, let us fight without mercy.
column2: 若必须战，那就毫不留情地战。

column1: There is no point in hiring fewer than twenty outside warriors.
column2: 雇佣少于二十名外族战士毫无意义。

column1: A small, swift strike has perhaps the best chance of success — yet the worst consequences if we fail.
column2: 一场小型快速突袭或许成功率最高——但一旦失败，后果也最严重。

column1: A small, swift strike has perhaps a slim of success. We will lose any larger battle.
column2: 一场小型快速突袭或许成功希望渺茫。如果打大规模战役，我们必败。

column1: The \x01Á might let us hire warriors from them.
column2: \x01Á 也许能让我们从他们那里雇佣战士。

column1: The gods might punish disloyal clans.
column2: 诸神或许会惩罚不忠的氏族。

column1: Orlanth the King might punish disloyal clans.
column2: 奥兰斯王或许会惩罚不忠的氏族。

column1: Orlanth the King might punish disloyal clans, but it is more likely that he will expect us to deal with this matter ourselves. Only a sacrifice of fifty or more cows would get his attention.
column2: 奥兰斯王或许会惩罚不忠的氏族，但更可能的是，他会期待我们自行处理此事。只有献祭五十头或更多牛，才能引起他的注意。

column1: The best victory is one that costs the fewest lives.
column2: 最好的胜利是牺牲最少生命的胜利。

column1: \x01@\x0B, if you are given a choice between abdication and death, make it easier for the rest of us, and choose death.
column2: \x01@\x0B如果你必须在退位与死亡之间选择，那就让我们其他人轻松些，选死亡吧。

column1: Discard the crown, for all crowns are trash.
column2: 丢掉王冠吧，因为所有王冠都是垃圾。

column1: We don’t deserve the throne, after letting things get so bad.
column2: 把局面搞成这样，我们不配拥有王座。

column1: Bad King Urgrain killed all those who rebelled against him, until his clan consisted of two cows, a trickster, and his donkey.
column2: 恶王乌格兰杀光了所有反抗他的人，直到他的氏族只剩下两头牛、一个骗子和他的驴。

column1: Abdication will be painful and humiliating, but it is the only peaceful course.
column2: 退位将痛苦而屈辱，但这是唯一的和平之路。

column1: This is the stuff that sagas are made of!
column2: 这正是传说诞生的素材！

column1: The gods know we have obeyed Orlanth’s laws.
column2: 诸神知道我们遵守了奥兰斯的律法。

column1: Fools! Now they’ll pay.
column2: 蠢货！现在他们要付出代价。

column1: Fight.
column2: 战斗。

column1: These rebellious fools do not realize that the rest of the tribe wishes to avoid trouble. A quick blow will restore them to their senses.
column2: 这些叛乱的蠢货不明白部落其他人都想避祸。一次快速打击就能让他们清醒。

column1: The gods will support me, and will show these disloyal curs that they have forfeited their blessings!
column2: 诸神将支持我，并让这些不忠的狗东西明白，他们已经失去了神的恩赐！

column1: If I must fight them, to a man, I will. If I must spend cattle on finding warriors to aid me, I will. I will not meekly cede the throne! I vow to make this cost the rebels more than it costs me.
column2: 若必须与他们一战，我将战斗到底，一个不留。若须花费牲畜招募战士助我，我也在所不惜。我不会懦弱地让出王座！我发誓要让叛军付出比我更大的代价。

column1: It seems that only a few clans remain loyal, and they will probably cast their lot with the rebels soon enough. I must step down, and so avoid a tribal blood-letting.
column2: 看来只有少数几个氏族仍保持忠诚，而且他们很可能很快就会倒向叛军。我必须退位，以免部族流血。

column1: It seems that no other clan but my own remains loyal. They will probably desert me soon enough. I must step down, and so avoid a tribal blood-letting.
column2: 看来除了我自己的氏族，没有其他氏族保持忠诚。他们很快大概就会抛弃我。我必须退位，以免部族流血。

column1: If we must fight them, to a man, we will. If we must spend cattle on finding warriors to aid us, we will. I will not meekly cede the throne! This will cost the rebels more than it costs us.
column2: 若必须与他们一战，我们将战斗到底，一个不留。若须花费牲畜招募战士助我，我们也做得到。我不会懦弱地让出王座！这将让叛军付出比我们更大的代价。

column1: The gods will support me. They will show these disloyal curs that I alone have their favor!
column2: 诸神将支持我。他们将让这些不忠的狗东西明白，只有我拥有他们的眷顾！

column1: The battle was joined. We won, showing the rebels that \x01@\x0B still retained Orlanth’s favor. The rebel chieftains begged forgiveness, and we granted it to them. Rebel and loyalist alike joined the victory feast, and all old grievances were buried with the slain.
column2: 战斗开始了。我们获胜，向叛军表明 \x01@\x0B 仍保有奥兰斯的眷顾。叛军首领乞求宽恕，我们应允了他们。叛军与忠诚派一同参加了胜利盛宴，所有旧怨都与阵亡者一同埋葬。

column1: Alarmed at the growth of the Colymar tribe, the other clans are gathering themselves into tribes.
column2: 由于科利马尔部落的崛起，其他氏族正在联合组成部落。

column1: “By helping to start a new tribe, you changed the face of Dragon Pass.” Afraid of your tribe’s power, the other clans are gathering themselves into tribes.
column2: “通过帮助建立新部落，你改变了龙隘的面貌。” 由于惧怕你部落的力量，其他氏族正在联合组成部落。

column1: Finally, the

column1: It was already Fire season, so we immediately prepared for war.
column2: 当时已经是火季，所以我们立刻备战。

column1: Fight immediately.
column2: 立即战斗。

column1: Wait until next Fire season.
column2: 等到下一个火季。

column1: The other clans would not fight the \x01Á because \x02\x07their magic was too strong/the omens were not good/they had done nothing to harm us/they were not the worst of our enemies/their ancestors had fought bravely during the Battle of Kanda Fant/they had the forces of destructive Earth on their side/their ruler had bested seven trolls during the rites of kingship\x02.

column1: Attempt an alliance with another tribe.

column1: We sought an alliance with the \x01@\n.
column2: 我们寻求与\x01@\n的联盟。

column1: We readied our plans to win over the \x01@\n.
column2: 我们准备好了计划来赢得 \x01@\n。

column1: We suggested to the other clans that we seek an alliance with the \x01@\n.
column2: 我们建议与其他部族寻求与\x01@\n结盟。

column1: We convinced them that it would be good to do so.
column2: 我们说服了他们，这么做是好的。

column1: We convinced the other clans in our tribe that it would be good to ally with the \x01@\n.
column2: 我们说服了我们部落的其他氏族，与\x01@\n结盟是好事。

column1: Convey the news to the other clans of the tribe.
column2: 向部落的其他氏族传达消息

column1: We conveyed the news to the other clans of the tribe.
column2: 我们已将消息传达给部落其他氏族

column1: They decided that the best course of action was to wait.
column2: 他们认定，当前上策唯有等待。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods for protection from new tribes.
column2: 向诸神献祭，以求得庇护免受新部落的侵害

column1: We sacrificed to the gods for protection from new tribes.
column2: 我们向诸神献祭，以求得庇护免受新部落的侵害。

column1: The god-talkers said that the omens were bad. The gods want us to fight our own fights with the other tribes, and will not intercede in disputes between those who worship them well.
column2: 神言者说征兆不祥。诸神要我们亲自与其他部落作战，不会干预那些虔诚敬奉者之间的纷争。

column1: The god-talkers said that the omens were good. If the other tribes tried to harm us, our magics would be strong.
column2: 神言者说征兆吉利。若其他部落试图加害我们，我们的魔法将会强大。

column1: Which tribe do you warn them against?
column2: 你警告他们防范哪个部落？

column1: They thanked us for our kindly warning.
column2: 他们感谢我们善意的警告。

column1: They thanked us for the warning, but said they did not wish to be beholden to us further. Or, that is what their frantic hissing seemed to mean.
column2: 他们感谢我们的警告，但说不想再欠我们人情。或者说，他们急促的嘶嘶声似乎是这个意思。

column1: They almost insulted us in the way they brushed off our warning.
column2: 他们几乎是以侮辱的方式无视了我们的警告。

column1: We are strong, and should prove it on the battlefield.
column2: 我们强大，应在战场上证明这一点。

column1: We must build up our forces before seeking battle.
column2: 我们必须先积蓄力量，再寻求战斗。

column1: In a place where there are so many elder races and other strange things, it is good to have some inhumans on your side.
column2: 在这样一个拥有众多古老种族和其他奇异事物的地方，身边有些非人是好事。

column1: A friend is always better than an enemy.
column2: 朋友总好过敌人。

column1: An alliance with one tribe will lead to a war with the others.
column2: 与一个部落联盟会导致与其他部落的战争。

column1: We should strengthen our magic through sacrifice, in case war breaks out between tribes.
column2: 我们应通过献祭增强魔法，以防部落间爆发战争。

column1: We could strengthen our magic through sacrifice, but if the gods are displeased, they might take some of our magic away from us.
column2: 我们可以通过献祭增强魔法，但若诸神不悦，他们可能会从我们这里夺走部分魔法。

column1: Sacrifice is good, but it is Ernalda, Issaries and Chalana Arroy we should seek aid from. If we ask the war gods for what we should provide ourselves, they will be offended.
column2: 献祭是好的，但我们应该向厄娜尔达、伊萨里斯和查拉娜·阿罗伊寻求帮助。如果我们向战争之神祈求我们自己应提供的东西，他们会发怒。

column1: Farmers wait and see how their crops grow. We should wait too, especially in this season when we must tend to those crops.
column2: 农夫们观望庄稼长势。我们也该等待，尤其在这个必须照料庄稼的季节。

column1: After Bad King Urgrain’s reign, the night came and all the tribes fell apart. Oskul created a new tribe, and then others formed out of Oskul-fear.
column2: 恶王乌格兰统治之后，黑夜降临，所有部落分崩离析。奥斯库尔建立了一个新部落，随后其他部落因对奥斯库尔的恐惧而形成。

column1: With the help of one of the new tribes, we can rid the forests of the elves, once and for all!
column2: 借助一个新部落的帮助，我们可以一劳永逸地清除森林中的精灵！

column1: We should tell the dragonewts about this!
column2: 我们应该把这件事告诉龙人！

column1: We must also tell the dragonewts about this!
column2: 我们还必须把这件事告诉龙人！

column1: The balance has swung too far towards friendship and negotiation. It is time to make some death.
column2: 平衡已过度偏向友谊与谈判。是时候制造死亡了。

column1: War, war, war!
column2: 战争，战争，战争！

column1: If we don’t attack them, they’ll attack us.
column2: 我们若不攻击他们，他们就会攻击我们。

column1: Either we attack them, or they attack us. It is all the same.
column2: 要么我们攻击他们，要么他们攻击我们。结果都一样。

column1: Good Ernalda, preserve us!
column2: 仁慈的厄娜尔达，保佑我们！
