column2: 小巨魔奴隶们再次制造了比其价值更大的麻烦。他们顽固、自私，还以骚扰羊群和其他动物为乐。自由民坚持要求你立刻除掉这些可憎的生物。

column1: The trollkin thralls caused trouble again, to no one’s great surprise.
column2: 小巨魔奴隶又惹了麻烦，对此没人感到意外。

column1: The trollkin you’ve taken as thralls prove to be nothing but trouble. They’re nasty, they’re vicious, and they don’t follow orders. Lately they’ve taken off to sneaking off and worrying the sheep. The carls demand that you get rid of these loathsome creatures immediately.
column2: 你收为奴隶的小巨魔结果只是麻烦。他们卑劣、恶毒，还不服从命令。最近他们又溜出去骚扰羊群。自由民要求你立刻除掉这些可憎的生物。

column1: The trollkin thralls caused trouble.
column2: 小巨魔奴隶惹了麻烦。

column1: Put their heads on pikes along your boundary lines.
column2: 把他们的脑袋插在边界线上的尖桩上。

column1: We killed them and stuck their heads on pikes along our boundary lines.
column2: 我们杀了他们，把他们的脑袋插在边界线上的尖桩上。

column1: We saw no more trollkin after that.
column2: 那之后我们再也没有见过小巨魔。

column1: The god-talkers said that the signs were good. Eurmal liked our gift of trollkin.
column2: 神言者说预兆很好。尤尔马尔喜欢我们献上的小巨魔。

column1: The god-talkers said that the signs were hard to read. It is not always possible to tell if the gods like every gift you give to them.
column2: 神言者说预兆难以解读。并非总能知道诸神是否喜欢你献上的每件礼物。

column1: What is the minimum price (in goods) you will accept for them?
column2: 你愿意接受的最低价格（以货物计）是多少？

column1: The carls will be happy if you drive them off.
column2: 如果你赶走它们，自由民会高兴。

column1: The carls will be happy if you kill them.
column2: 如果你杀死它们，自由民会高兴。

column1: The carls will be happy if you not only kill them, but make sure that these accursed things never come here again.
column2: 如果你不仅杀死它们，还确保这些该死的东西再也不会回来，自由民会高兴。

column1: The trolls will hate us if we hurt the trollkin.
column2: 如果我们伤害小巨魔，巨魔会憎恨我们。

column1: Trolls show little affection for trollkin, and might not mind if we mistreat them.
column2: 巨魔对小巨魔没什么感情，或许不介意我们虐待它们。

column1: Trolls use and abuse trollkin themselves. What will they care what we do with these pests?
column2: 巨魔自己也会利用和虐待小巨魔。他们会在乎我们对这些害虫做什么？

column1: Trolls consider the trollkin to be pests, and might admire us if we show that we know how to ward them off.
column2: 巨魔认为小巨魔是害虫，如果我们表现出知道如何驱赶它们，他们可能会赞赏我们。

column1: As long as we do not tell another clan of our problems with these thralls, we can sell them in good conscience.
column2: 只要我们不告诉其他氏族我们与这些奴隶的问题，我们就可以心安理得地卖掉它们。

column1: If we sell these thralls to another clan, and they cause problems there, the other clan may make a claim against us.
column2: 如果我们把这些奴隶卖给另一个氏族，而他们在那里造成麻烦，那个氏族可能会向我们索赔。

column1: Don’t sell these thralls to another clan — we know very well the damage they will cause.
column2: 别把这些奴隶卖给其他氏族——我们很清楚他们会造成的损害。

column1: The trolls have reason to dislike us already. We must be cautious.
column2: 巨魔已经有理由不喜欢我们了。我们必须谨慎。

column1: The trolls may dislike us, but the goodwill of our carls is far more important.
column2: 巨魔可能不喜欢我们，但我们自由民的好感要重要得多。

column1: We have shown good faith to the trolls. Perhaps, in this instance, they are capable of understanding that their offspring have wronged us.
column2: 我们已经向巨魔表达了善意。也许这一次，他们能够理解是他们的后代冒犯了我们。

column1: The trolls do not hate us. They may understand that if we kill the trollkin, it is the last thing we do, not the first.
column2: 巨魔并不恨我们。他们或许明白，如果我们杀死小巨魔，那是我们最后的手段，而非首选。

column1: The gods don’t much care what you sacrifice to them, as long as you sacrifice.
column2: 神明并不太在意你献祭什么，只要你献祭就行。

column1: The gods will not appreciate a worthless sacrifice.
column2: 神明不会欣赏毫无价值的献祭。

column1: They are living creatures, they have belonged to us for a time, and they have some value. The gods will consider them an acceptable sacrifice now, even if they would not before.
column2: 他们是活物，曾属于我们一段时间，并且有一定价值。即使以前不行，现在神明会认为他们是可接受的献祭。

column1: They have some worth now. Use them for a sacrifice, or for a ward against further trollkin.
column2: 现在他们有些价值了。要么用来献祭，要么用来作为抵御更多小巨魔的护符。

column1: Sacrifice them to Eurmal.
column2: 把他们献祭给尤尔马尔。

column1: The true test of mercy is whether you show it to those who will not thank you for it.
column2: 仁慈的真正考验，在于你是否对那些不会感激你的人施以仁慈。

column1: Why those — \x02\x03dirty, I mean filthy/despicable/nasty\x02 — those — \x02\x03ugly/thick-headed/greedy\x02…!
column2: 为什么那些—— \x02\x03肮脏的，我是说污秽/卑鄙/下流\x02 ——那些—— \x02\x03丑陋/愚蠢/贪婪\x02……！

column1: This wouldn’t have happened, if it weren’t for the women spending all of their time in that holy shed of theirs. They just go there to plot against us.
column2: 要不是女人们整天待在她们那神圣的小棚屋里，这事就不会发生。她们去那里就是为了密谋对付我们。

column1: We wouldn’t have this problem, if the men would just do their duty by the women and do their duty for the clan.
column2: 要是男人们履行对女人的职责，为氏族尽本分，我们就不会有这个麻烦。

column1: The trolls will attack us for \x02\x02no cause/the slightest of reasons\x02. They are \x02\x03dishonorable/untrustworthy/ignoble\x02, unlike our dragonewt friends.
column2: 巨魔会 \x02\x02无缘无故/为了一点小事\x02就攻击我们。他们 \x02\x03不光彩/不值得信任/卑劣\x02，不像我们的龙族朋友。

column1: cow
column2: 母牛

column1: Pay both refund and compensation.
column2: 既退还货款又支付补偿。

column1: They thanked us for resolving the problem quickly and without argument.
column2: 他们感谢我们迅速且无争议地解决了问题。

column1: Refund the price.
column2: 退还货款。

column1: We refunded the price, but did not pay compensation.
column2: 我们退还了货款，但没有支付补偿。

column1: They made no secret of their displeasure as they left.
column2: 他们离开时毫不掩饰自己的不悦。

column1: “If you cannot control your thralls, that is not our legal responsibility.”
column2: “如果你们管不住自己的奴隶，那并非我们的法律责任。”

column1: “If you cannot control your thralls,” we said, “that is not our responsibility.”
column2: “如果你们管不住自己的奴隶，”我们说道，“那并非我们的责任。”

column1: We convinced them that the legal precedents were on our side. Although they were not happy to do so, they admitted that the fault was not ours.
column2: 我们说服他们，法律先例站在我们这边。尽管他们不情愿，但还是承认错不在我们。

column1: We cited many legal precedents to support our cause, but they cited many more that reinforced their position. Honor gave us little choice but to pay what they wished.
column2: 我们引用了许多法律先例来支持我们的立场，但他们引用了更多来强化他们的主张。出于荣誉，我们别无选择，只能支付他们要求的金额。

column1: “Sacrifice the things; you’ll get more from the gods than from us.”
column2: “把这些东西献祭掉；你们从神明那里得到的会比从我们这里得到的多。”

column1: “Sacrifice the things,” we said, “You’ll get more from the gods than from us.”
column2: “把这些东西献祭掉，”我们说道，“你们从神明那里得到的会比从我们这里得到的多。”

column1: We convinced them that the gods would take the trollkin as sacrifices. They left, discussing which god should reap this unexpected benefit.
column2: 我们说服他们，神明会接受小巨魔作为祭品。他们离开了，讨论着该让哪位神明收获这份意外之喜。

column1: They argued that the gods would be offended by such a useless sacrifice, and could not be swayed.
column2: 他们争辩说，如此无用的祭品会触怒神明，无法被说服。

column1: “If you’re so sure you’re right, why don’t you take it to the moot?”
column2: “如果你那么确定自己是对的，为什么不提交到议会？”

column1: “If you’re so sure you’re right,” we said, “why don’t you take it to the moot?”
column2: “如果你那么确定自己是对的，”我们说道，“为什么不提交到议会？”

column1: Insulted, they said they would do exactly that. When time for a moot came, they were laughed at by the other clans for making such a fuss over a petty matter. We were seen as clever, and they were seen as fools.
column2: 他们受辱，说他们一定会这么做。到了议会的时候，其他氏族嘲笑他们为一件小事大惊小怪。我们被视为聪明，他们则被视为傻瓜。

column1: The payment may be fair, but the compensation is not.
column2: 付款可能合理，但补偿不合理。

column1: Four times not very much is still not very much.
column2: 四倍的不多仍然不多。

column1: They’re lying; those are perfectly good trollkin, and they caused no harm.
column2: 他们在撒谎；那些小巨魔明明好好的，没有造成任何伤害。

column1: We should never have traded the trollkin to them — and we should not try to trade trollkin again.
column2: 我们当初就不该把小巨魔交易给他们——而且我们以后也不该再尝试交易小巨魔。

column1: Are we responsible for every calf we sell, or for each grain of wheat?
column2: 难道我们要为我们卖出的每头牛犊或每粒小麦负责吗？

column1: We are not required to take the trollkin back, but maybe there is a way to solve everyone’s problem here.
column2: 我们没有义务收回小巨魔，但也许有办法解决所有人的问题。

column1: If we have to fight, we can beat their weak and puny soldiers.
column2: 如果我们必须战斗，我们能打败他们软弱无力的士兵。

column1: As much as we welcome a chance to pound another clan, a fight over trollkin is…well…not exactly heroic.
column2: 虽然我们很乐意找机会痛扁另一个氏族，但为了一群小巨魔打架……呃……实在算不上英雄壮举。

column1: Better settle.
column2: 最好还是和解。

column1: They are stronger than we are. Do we really want to fight against bad odds for a dispute over trollkin?
column2: 他们比我们强。我们真的要为了争夺小巨魔这种破事去以弱敌强吗？

column1: A clever tongue or a jingling purse is the best way to settle this matter.
column2: 巧舌如簧或鼓鼓钱袋才是解决此事的最佳途径。

column1: There are precedents that would support us, and precedents that would support them.
column2: 既有支持我们的先例，也有支持他们的先例。

column1: If they take this to the moot, they will be laughed at.
column2: 要是他们闹到议会上，只会被人嘲笑。

column1: There are precedents that would support us, and precedents that would support them. But these carls are probably untutored in the law, and I can out-argue them.
column2: 既有支持我们的先例，也有支持他们的先例。但这些自由民大概不懂法律，我能辩得过他们。

column1: They are offended, but they will not start a feud over such a petty matter.
column2: 他们虽然感到冒犯，但还不至于为了这点小事就结下世仇。

column1: Better to smooth relations between our clans than to insist on being right in this matter.
column2: 与其在这件事上固执己见，不如缓和两族之间的关系。

column1: They will happiest if we can show them a way to get rid of the trollkin without losing face.
column2: 如果我们能给他们一个不失体面地处理掉小巨魔的办法，他们才会最满意。

column1: They regard us as honest and trustworthy. They will give a fair hearing to our arguments.
column2: 他们认为我们诚实可靠，会公正地听取我们的论据。

column1: They regard us with ill will. They will not listen to reason.
column2: 他们对我们心怀敌意，不会听我们讲道理。

column1: Let me convince them to sacrifice the trollkin. If that fails, we will sacrifice the trollkin ourselves.
column2: 让我去说服他们献祭小巨魔。如果不行，我们就自己动手献祭。

column1: Sacrificing trollkin to Eurmal might go with or against the one making the sacrifice, but at least the trollkin would not bother any of us afterwards.
column2: 把小巨魔献祭给欧尔玛，结果可能对献祭者有利也可能不利，但至少往后那些小巨魔不会再烦扰我们任何人。

column1: It’s possible that the gods wouldn’t want to receive these creatures, but it’s certain that we don’t want them.
column2: 众神或许不愿接纳这些造物，但我们确定不想要它们。

column1: We can argue that the trollkin have acquired value through trade, and that the gods will take them as they would any other form of wealth.
column2: 我们可以主张这些小巨魔通过交易获得了价值，众神会像接受其他财富一样接受它们。

column1: We can’t pay them back. We must save our wealth in case \x02\x03the nose-ring of Oskul Oskulsson/Esra’s grain thresher/Vinga’s magic arrow\x02 turns up.
column2: 我们无力偿还他们。必须保住财富，以防 \x02\x03奥克苏尔·奥克苏尔森的鼻环/埃斯拉的脱粒机/文伽的魔法箭\x02 出现。

column1: What is worthy in a sacrifice is not the value of the goods, but the honesty of the worshipper’s intentions.
column2: 献祭的价值不在于祭品的贵重，而在于献祭者心意的真诚。

column1: If it cannot be taught to read, it is an animal. We are not responsible for the actions of livestock we trade; why should we be with trollkin?
column2: 如果教不会它认字，那就是个畜生。我们不必为自己交易的牲畜负责，凭什么要对小巨魔负责？

column1: What do you do with the returned trollkin?
column2: 你们打算怎么处置退回来的小巨魔？

column1: Then we had to decide what to do with the returned trollkin.
column2: 然后我们得决定怎么处置退回来的小巨魔。

column1: You heard what they said. If we take them as thralls, they’ll worry the sheep.
column2: 你听见他们说的了。要是收为奴隶，它们会惊扰羊群。

column1: We should not trade them. It will ruin our trading reputation.
column2: 我们不该交易它们。这会毁了我们做生意的名声。

column1: Just kill them, I tell you. Kill them.
column2: 直接杀了它们，我跟你说。杀了它们。

column1: Just. Kill. The. Trollkin.
column2: 直接。杀了。那些。小巨魔。

column1: We have long opposed the taking of thralls. This is why we sold them as… thralls. Hmm, perhaps we are being punished for inconsistency.
column2: 我们一直反对蓄奴。所以我们才把它们当作……奴隶卖掉了。嗯，也许我们正因言行不一而受到惩罚。

column1: Our ancestors took worthy thralls. I don’t think they would care what we do with such worthless things.
column2: 我们的先祖会收有价值的奴隶。我觉得他们才不在乎我们怎么处置这些没用的东西。

column1: We do not wish to offend the trolls, but then, we do not wish to offend our carls, either.
column2: 我们既不想得罪巨魔，也不想得罪自家的自由民。

column1: They are living creatures, and have acquired value through trade. The gods will consider them an acceptable sacrifice now, even if they would not before.
column2: 它们是活物，又通过交易获得了价值。即便以前不行，现在众神也会视它们为可接受的祭品。

column1: They might be able to perform simple but unpleasant chores, if we keep them far from the animals.
column2: 要是让它们离牲畜远点，或许能做些简单但脏累的杂活。

column1: Don’t even think about letting one of those things near our grain bins!
column2: 想都别想放那种东西靠近我们的粮仓！

column1: I suppose I already mentioned that the curse that causes trolls to give birth to trollkin children was laid by the Chaos fiend Gbaji.
column2: 我想我提过了，让巨魔生下小巨魔的诅咒是由混沌魔鬼格巴吉降下的。

column1: Eurmal’s waiting! Don’t offend him by not sacrificing these dee-lightful creatures to him!
column2: 欧尔玛正等着呢！别不把这些可爱的小东西献祭给他而惹恼他！

column1: I told you we should have killed them.
column2: 我早说该杀了它们。

column1: We have been afflicted by our own version of the trollkin curse.
column2: 我们也遭受了自家版本的小巨魔诅咒。

column1: Once trollkin show up, you can never get rid of them.
column2: 小巨魔一旦出现，就永远甩不掉了。

column1: We must somehow recoup our losses!
column2: 我们总得想法弥补损失！

column1: They cannot help being trollkin.
column2: 它们生来就是小巨魔，这也没办法。

column1: A dragonewt appears at your boundaries and demands the return of his old body. “You have something of mine,” it hisses. “My old body. Come here to recover it. Give now — both of us avoid entanglement.”
column2: 一个龙人出现在你的领地边界，要求归还它的旧身躯。“你们有我的东西，”它嘶嘶地说，“我的旧身躯。我来取回。现在交出来——你我皆免纠缠。”

column1: A dragonewt came and asked for its old body back.
column2: 来了个龙人，要讨回它的旧身躯。

column1: Attack the dragonewt.
column2: 攻击龙人。

column1: We attacked him.
column2: 我们攻击了它。

column1: It fought viciously, with weird and powerful magic. It slew some of our warriors, and wounded others. The other warriors fell back, and allowed it to retreat.
column2: 它凶猛搏斗，使出了古怪而强大的魔法。它杀了我们几个武士，还打伤了一些。其余武士退却，让它逃走了。

column1: It fought viciously, with weird and powerful magic. Our warriors fought back valiantly, with good Orlanth-granted magic. One of them was slain, but he managed to knock the dragonewt over as he fell, so that the others could pierce it with their swords.
column2: 它凶猛搏斗，使出了古怪而强大的魔法。我们的武士英勇还击，用上了欧兰斯赐予的强大魔法。一名武士阵亡，但他倒下时成功撞倒了那个龙人，好让其他人用剑刺穿它。

column1: What do you do with the body?
column2: 你们打算怎么处理尸体？

column1: Both the carls and weaponthanes expressed alarm that we would let “another stinking dragonewt corpse” clutter up the tula. They demanded that we find some other thing to do with the body.
column2: 自由民和武器领主都对“让另一具臭烘烘的龙人尸体”堆在图拉上表示震惊。他们要求我们另找地方处理尸体。

column1: Which clan do you offer it to?
column2: 你打算把它送给哪个氏族？

column1: What is the minimum price you’ll accept for it?
column2: 你愿意接受的最低价格是多少？

column1: It was difficult to skin the dragonewt corpse without destroying the hide, but our magicians managed the task.
column2: 要剥下龙人尸体而不损坏皮子很难，但我们的法师还是完成了任务。

column1: To avoid another visit by the dragonewt, we burned the body. Its smell reminded us of \x02\x04chicken/fish/butter/cinnamon\x02.
column2: 为了避免龙人再度来访，我们焚烧了尸体。它的气味让我们想起 \x02\x04鸡肉/鱼/黄油/肉桂\x02。

column1: Offer it compensation instead of the body.
column2: 向它提供补偿，而不是尸体。

column1: We offered it compensation instead of the body.
column2: 我们向它提供了补偿，而不是尸体。

column1: “No!” the dragonewt roared. “Not come for trade entanglement. Come for body back!”
column2: “不！”龙人咆哮道。“不是为交易纠缠而来。是为取回身体！”

column1: “We don’t have your body.”
column2: “我们没有你的身体。”

column1: “We don’t have your body,” we told it.
column2: “我们没有你的身体，”我们告诉它。

column1: It asks you who has it.
column2: 它问你们谁拿走了身体。

column1: Refuse to say.
column2: 拒绝回答。

column1: We refused to tell the dragonewt who had it.
column2: 我们拒绝告诉龙人是谁拿走了身体。

column1: It departed, promising stern action.
column2: 它离开了，扬言要采取严厉行动。

column1: Tell the truth.
column2: 说实话。

column1: It departed, heading in the direction of the \x01@\x0E tula.
column2: 它离开了，朝 \x01@\x0E 图拉领地的方向而去。

column1: Tell him you are not sure where it is.
column2: 告诉它你不确定身体在哪儿。

column1: We said that we really had no idea exactly where the body was.
column2: 我们说我们确实不清楚身体到底在何处。

column1: It flared its crest and hissed, “You not lie, exactly — but you not truthful either.” It departed, promising stern action.
column2: 它竖起头冠咝咝地说：“你没说谎，确切地说——但你也没说实话。”它离开了，扬言要采取严厉行动。

column1: Name a different clan than the one that has it.
column2: 说出一个不同于实际持有者的氏族名字。

column1: We said that the \x01Ý had it.
column2: 我们说是 \x01Ý 拿走了身体。

column1: “You lie,” it said. “Mystic connection to old body, I have. I know it here.”
column2: “你在撒谎，”它说。“我与旧身体有神秘联系。我知道它在这里。”

column1: “We have it, but we’re not going to give it to you.”
column2: “我们拿着它，但我们不会把它还给你。”

column1: We told it that we had the body, but refused to surrender it.
column2: 我们告诉它我们拿走了身体，但拒绝交出。

column1: Let the dragonewt have its old body.
column2: 让龙人拿回它的旧身体。

column1: We returned the fabulous suit of magical armor to its original owner.
column2: 我们将那套神奇的法术盔甲归还给了原主。

column1: We showed the dragonewt where we had found its body. It was still there, untouched.
column2: 我们指给龙人看发现它身体的地方。它还在那里，原封未动。

column1: We gave it the scraps of skin that were left after our failed attempt to turn its hide into magical armor.
column2: 我们把试图将它的皮制成法术盔甲失败后剩下的碎皮给了它。

column1: Whether it was pleased or displeased, we could not tell. It departed without a further word.
column2: 无论它是高兴还是不满，我们都无法分辨。它一言不发地离开了。

column1: Insist that it compensate you for the body.
column2: 坚持让它为身体补偿你。

column1: We insisted that it compensate us first.
column2: 我们坚持要它先补偿我们。

column1: “My body!” it hissed. “Not yours! Mine!” It flared its crests at us.
column2: “我的身体！”它咝咝道。“不是你的！是我的！”它对我们竖起了头冠。

column1: Dragonewt skins are valuable. Demand something for it.
column2: 龙人的皮值钱。为此索要些回报。

column1: One dragonewt skin was valuable. Two dragonewt skins might still be worth something. But too many dragonewt skins are worthless.
column2: 一张龙人皮值钱。两张龙人皮或许还值点钱。但太多张龙人皮就一文不值了。

column1: We can probably beat a lone dragonewt.
column2: 我们大概能打败一个落单的龙人。

column1: We might beat a lone dragonewt. It might cost us lives, though.
column2: 我们也许能打败一个落单的龙人。不过可能会付出生命代价。

column1: We might beat a lone dragonewt. It will cost us lives to do so.
column2: 我们也许能打败一个落单的龙人。这样做会让我们付出生命代价。

column1: We might beat a lone dragonewt. But then other dragonewts might come and… well, remember what happened in the Dragonkill War.
column2: 我们也许能打败一个落单的龙人。但随后其他龙人可能会来……嗯，还记得屠龙战争里发生的事吧。

column1: If we keep playing keep-away with the dragonewt and its body, we had better be prepared for the consequences.
column2: 如果我们继续跟龙人和它的身体玩捉迷藏，最好为后果做好准备。

column1: What are we doing? If we want a war with the dragonewts, let us prepare and then declare so, openly.
column2: 我们在干什么？如果我们想跟龙人开战，那就准备妥当，然后公开宣战。

column1: We are obligated to see to the body’s return.
column2: 我们有义务确保身体归还。

column1: We owe no obligations to those who do not follow our laws — especially inhuman ones.
column2: 对于那些不遵守我们律法的人——尤其是非人异类——我们不承担任何义务。

column1: How would we feel if we learned that the dragonewts were desecrating the corpses of our kin?
column2: 如果得知龙人亵渎我们同胞的遗体，我们会作何感想？

column1: Do we really want to be known as the Harasses Dragonewts Clan?
column2: 我们真的想落个“骚扰龙人氏族”的名声吗？

column1: Don’t we have better things to do — real deals to make, other clans to raid, pastures to tend?
column2: 难道我们没有更重要的事要做——谈真正的交易、袭击其他氏族、照料牧场？

column1: Our magic is weak compared to the dragonewt’s.
column2: 我们的法术跟龙人相比很弱。

column1: Dragonewt magic is strong, but ours is stronger still.
column2: 龙人的法术很强，但我们的更强。

column1: Kill it, skin it, and let me dress up in the hide! I bet I can make the tail move.
column2: 杀了它，剥了皮，让我穿上那层皮！我赌我能让尾巴动起来。

column1: I wonder if burning dragonewt makes for multi-colored flames?
column2: 我在想焚烧龙人会不会产生五彩火焰？

column1: If we kill this one, we can make magical armor out of it.
column2: 如果我们杀了这个，就能用它制作法术盔甲。

column1: If we kill this one, we can make magical armor out of it, too.
column2: 如果我们杀了这个，也能用它制作法术盔甲。

column1: Do not give it away. Get something for it.
column2: 别把它送回去。要换点东西。

column1: We found it. We have it. Get something for it.
column2: 我们找到的。我们拿着呢。要换点东西。

column1: Is it a woman or a man? I can’t tell.
column2: 它是女人还是男人？我分不清。

column1: We must not offend the gods of the dragonewts.
column2: 我们绝不能冒犯龙人的神祇。

column1: Is it a man or a woman? I can’t tell.
column2: 它是男人还是女人？我分不清。

column1: The man-snake came and requested his life-tunic.
column2: 那蛇人来了，索要他的生命之衣。

column1: We must do everything we can to satisfy our scaly friend.
column2: 我们必须竭尽全力让我们的鳞甲朋友满意。

column1: It is hard to tell what a dragonewt thinks or feels, but I don’t think we’d like to have to keep looking for our body if we died.
column2: 很难判断龙人在想什么或感受什么，但我想如果我们死了，肯定也不希望还得一直找自己的遗体。

column1: Do the honorable thing, and tell it about its old body, and let it go.
column2: 做体面的事——告诉它旧身体的下落，让它带走。

column1: What will it do if finds out we really don’t know where the body is?
column2: 如果它发现我们真的不知道身体在哪，它会怎么做？

column1: Your emissaries approach the leadership of the \x01@! clan, which worships the sun god Elmal as their chief god. You ask them if they wish to join your new tribe. “There is often tension between Elmal clans and Orlanth clans, who do not respect us properly. A pledge of respect for Elmal must be contained in the new tribe’s rites of kingship. Each clan must sacrifice to Elmal each holy season. We must be guaranteed two seats on the tribal council, in perpetuity.”
column2: 你的使者们接近 \x01@! 氏族的领导层，这个氏族崇拜太阳神埃尔马尔作为他们的主神。你问他们是否愿意加入你的新部落。“埃尔马尔氏族与奥兰斯氏族之间时常存在紧张关系，后者对我们缺乏应有的尊重。新部落的王权仪式中必须包含对埃尔马尔的尊重誓言。每个神圣季节，每个氏族都必须向埃尔马尔献祭。我们必须获得部落议会中的两个席位，永久保留。”

column1: We talked to \x01@! leaders to see if they wanted to join our new tribe.
column2: 我们与 \x01@! 部族的领袖们交谈，看他们是否愿意加入我们的新部落。

column1: The \x01@! wants a pledge of respect for Elmal contained in the new tribe’s rites of kingship. They want clan to sacrifice to Elmal each holy season. They two seats on the tribal council, guaranteed, in perpetuity.”
column2: \x01@! 希望在王权仪式中加入对埃尔马尔的尊崇誓言。他们要求氏族每个神圣季节向埃尔马尔献祭。他们要保证在部落议会中永久拥有两个席位。

column1: Agree to pledge in rites of kingship.
column2: 同意在王权仪式中宣誓。

column1: We agreed to a pledge of respect for Elmal in the rites of kingship.
column2: 我们同意在王权仪式中加入尊崇埃尔马尔的誓言。

column1: They said it was a good beginning for showing proper respect for Elmal.
column2: 他们说，这对于向埃尔马尔表达应有敬意而言，是个良好的开端。

column1: Agree to sacrifice to Elmal.
column2: 同意向埃尔马尔献祭。

column1: We agreed that the other clans would sacrifice to Elmal.
column2: 我们同意其他氏族将向埃尔马尔献祭。

column1: How much wealth will each clan sacrifice to Elmal each year?
column2: 每个氏族每年需向埃尔马尔献祭多少财富？

column1: It was clear that they had expected a larger sacrifice.
column2: 很明显，他们原本期望更多的献祭。

column1: They were pleased with our promise.
column2: 他们对我们的承诺感到满意。

column1: Demand that they teach their sun magic to warriors of the other clans.
column2: 要求他们将太阳魔法传授给其他氏族的战士。

column1: We demanded that they teach their sun magic to warriors of the other clans.
column2: 我们要求他们将太阳魔法传授给其他氏族的战士。

column1: They weren’t happy, but agreed in principle.
column2: 他们虽不情愿，但原则上同意了。

column1: “We have looked with care upon your proposal, and have concluded that the sun is bright upon it. May Elmal shine on the confederation moot.”
column2: “我们仔细审视了你们的提议，认为太阳的光辉照耀其上。愿埃尔马尔照耀联盟大会。”

column1: They are wealthy, and would make a worthy addition to our tribe.
column2: 他们很富有，会成为我们部落宝贵的成员。

column1: They are poor, and we are wasting our time with them.
column2: 他们很穷，我们是在浪费时间与他们周旋。

column1: Our allies should not be hard to convince.
column2: 说服我们的盟友应该不难。

column1: We would need to sacrifice much to Elmal each year to convince these enemies to join our tribe.
column2: 我们需要每年向埃尔马尔献祭大量祭品，才能说服这些敌人加入我们的部落。

column1: We must give them exactly what they want or agree to large sacrifices, as many as a dozen cows per year.
column2: 我们必须完全满足他们的要求，或者同意大量的献祭，每年多达十几头牛。

column1: They would make powerful friends, or terrible foes.
column2: 他们可能成为强大的朋友，或可怕的敌人。

column1: They are weaker than we are. We’d have to spend all of our time rescuing them.
column2: 他们比我们弱小。我们将不得不把所有时间都花在援救他们上。

column1: Orlanth clans often clash with Elmal clans, it is true.
column2: 奥兰斯氏族常与埃尔马尔氏族发生冲突，这确实不假。

column1: Orlanth clans often clash with Elmal clans, and with good reason. Elmal must remain the loyal thane, and may not usurp Orlanth’s privileges.
column2: 奥兰斯氏族常与埃尔马尔氏族发生冲突，而且有充分的理由。埃尔马尔必须保持忠诚侍从的身份，不得僭夺奥兰斯的特权。

column1: Orlanth clans often clash with Elmal clans, because they are unjust. We have as much right to worship as they.
column2: 奥兰斯氏族常与埃尔马尔氏族发生冲突，是因为他们不公正。我们同样有权进行崇拜。

column1: You would think that Elmal’s light would lead them away from their clan’s saga of foolish errors.
column2: 你会以为埃尔马尔的光芒会指引他们远离其氏族那充满愚蠢错误的传说。

column1: The other clans will not understand if we strain to please these difficult people.
column2: 如果我们费力讨好这些难以相处的人，其他氏族不会理解。

column1: The other clans will want Elmali magic.
column2: 其他氏族会想要埃尔马尔魔法。

column1: The other clans will not want to sacrifice too much to Elmal.
column2: 其他氏族不愿向埃尔马尔献祭太多。

column1: The other clans will not want to sacrifice too much to Elmal. Four cows or less is no great issue, but after that their grumbling will steadily increase.
column2: 其他氏族不愿向埃尔马尔献祭太多。四头牛或更少倒没什么大问题，但超过这个数，他们的抱怨就会稳步增加。

column1: To convince our enemies to join the tribe, we would have to promise much. And that will hurt our chances at the confederation moot.
column2: 要说服我们的敌人加入部落，我们必须做出许多承诺。而这将损害我们在联盟大会上的机会。

column1: Of course, we are also Elmali, so we already know the fighting magics of the sun god.
column2: 当然，我们也是埃尔马尔信徒，所以我们早已熟知太阳神的战斗魔法。

column1: Their magic isn’t as powerful as they think it is.
column2: 他们的魔法并不像他们想象的那么强大。

column1: Our best warriors will get better if we learn the Elmali spells.
column2: 如果我们学会埃尔马尔法术，我们最优秀的战士会变得更强。

column1: They think they are the only clan who understands Elmal’s ways. This blindness hurts them more than it hurts us.
column2: 他们以为自己是唯一理解埃尔马尔之道的氏族。这种盲目损害他们更甚于损害我们。

column1: There is no finer clan in all of Dragon Pass. Aside from ours, of course.
column2: 龙之隘口没有比他们更优秀的氏族了。当然，除了我们之外。

column1: I hate seeing my god’s bright ways twisted so strangely by this dangerous clan.
column2: 我憎恨看到我神的明亮之道被这个危险的氏族扭曲得如此奇怪。

column1: Elmal guarded Orlanth’s hearth when the Great Darkness fell upon the world, and Orlanth had to reawaken the gods killed by Chaos.
column2: 当大黑暗降临世间，奥兰斯必须重唤醒被混沌杀死的众神时，埃尔马尔守护了奥兰斯的炉灶。

column1: It would be unusual to have two Elmal clans in the same tribe. But it could work to our advantage.
column2: 同一个部落中有两个埃尔马尔氏族并不寻常。但这对我们可能有利。

column1: They’re very arrogant for a clan that forgot to teach its thanes how to read.
column2: 对于一个忘记教其侍从识字的氏族来说，他们太傲慢了。

column1: The other clans may not ever want an Elmali king.
column2: 其他氏族可能永远不希望有一位埃尔马尔国王。

column1: Having another Elmal clan in the tribe could help us hold the kingship.
column2: 部落中有另一个埃尔马尔氏族可以帮助我们保住王权。

column1: Make sure that there is a reason for the tribe to want them, as well as reasons for them to want the tribe.
column2: 确保部落有理由需要他们，同时他们也有理由想要加入部落。

column1: Our feud doesn’t have to be forever. Let’s get them into the tribe and sort it out.
column2: 我们的世仇不必永远持续下去。让他们加入部落，然后慢慢解决吧。

column1: I told you they’d want to compose the rites of kingship.
column2: 我告诉过你，他们会想要制定王权仪式。

column1: I can’t forget the reasons we are feuding, but I know that gifting them could help make things better.
column2: 我无法忘记我们结仇的原因，但我知道馈赠礼物或许有助于改善局面。

column1: They are too proud to know what is best for them. I don’t know if that means we should bring them into the tribe or leave them in the cold.
column2: 他们过于骄傲，以至于不知什么对他们最有利。我不知道这意味着我们应该接纳他们入部落，还是该把他们晾在一边。

column1: No matter what we do, they will work against us.
column2: 无论我们做什么，他们都会与我们作对。

column1: We shouldn’t even be talking to these people — they follow the wrong god. Are we to become Elmal-worshippers, too?
column2: 我们甚至不该和这些人交谈——他们信奉错了神。难道我们也要变成埃尔马尔的崇拜者吗？

column1: We are just inviting their rivalry. We do not need another Elmali clan to contend with.
column2: 我们这是在招来他们的竞争。我们不需要再应付另一个埃尔马尔氏族。

column1: If we can bring them into the tribe, we will have to fight them less.
column2: 如果我们能让他们加入部落，我们就得少与他们争斗。

column1: Our enemies aren’t stupid.
column2: 我们的敌人并不愚蠢。

column1: I hate to say it, but I think we should forget our feud. For now.
column2: 我讨厌这么说，但我想我们应该忘记我们的世仇。至少暂时如此。

column1: The one whispering in the back just called me a stickpicker!
column2: 后面那个嘀咕的家伙刚才叫我拾柴人！

column1: sceneR186
column2: sceneR186

column1: Ducks came and said they wanted to join our tribe.
column2: 鸭人来了，说他们想加入我们的部落。

column1: They left, their heads hung low. They said they hoped we would one day see the merits of their case.
column2: 他们垂头丧气地离开了。他们说希望有一天我们能明白他们请求的合理性。

column1: Decline their request; tell this funny story at the moot.
column2: 拒绝他们的请求；在议会上讲这个趣事。

column1: \x01@\x01 told this as a funny story to entertain the moot.
column2: \x01@\x01 将此作为趣闻在议会上讲述。

column1: Leaders of the other clans wept with laughter, and wanted \x01@\x01 to travel to all of their tulas to tell the story to those who had not heard it.
column2: 其他氏族的首领们笑得流泪，想要 \x01@\x01 前往他们所有的图拉领地，将这个故事讲给没听过的人听。

column1: The leaders of the other clans did not find the story all that funny. “Although of course ducks cannot join human tribes, there is no reason to laugh at them for wanting to do so.”
column2: 其他氏族的首领们并不觉得这故事有多好笑。“虽然鸭人当然不能加入人类部落，但他们有此意愿，也没有理由嘲笑。”

column1: How much wealth do you tell the ducks to give to each clan?
column2: 你告诉鸭人要给每个氏族多少财富？

column1: They balked at the size of the gifts we suggested, and withdrew their request. “You don’t wish to help us,” they wailed. “You merely wish to swindle us!”
column2: 我们提议的礼物规模让他们踌躇不前，于是他们撤回了请求。“你们并非真心相助，”他们哀号道，“你们只是想骗我们！”

column1: The other clans were swayed by our praise of the ducks.
column2: 其他氏族被我们对鸭人的赞扬所打动。

column1: There were some legal objections, but we proposed a compromise, and the ducks entered into a special treaty with the tribe.
column2: 存在一些法律上的异议，但我们提出了折中方案，于是鸭人与部落签订了一项特别条约。

column1: Allied with our tribe
column2: 与我们部落结盟

column1: The other clans laughed us out of the moot. The ducks thanked us for making an honest effort on their behalf. “You are good, even if your tribe-mates are not.”
column2: 其他氏族将我们嘲笑出了议会。鸭人感谢我们为他们所做的真诚努力。“你们是好人，尽管你们的族人不是。”

column1: We responded thus: “It is traditional to offer a treasure to a possible sponsor.”
column2: 我们如此回应：“按传统，应向可能的赞助者献上宝物。”

column1: They gave us a tube made of rolled-up, dried marshweed. They said it was a Tube of Truth-Seeking, and that it would aid us in making divinations.
column2: 他们给了我们一个用卷起的干沼草制成的管子。他们说这是求真管，能助我们进行占卜。

column1: They said that it was not their way to buy their place in a tribe.
column2: 他们说，购买部族中的席位并非他们的作风。

column1: They said they had given us enough already.
column2: 他们说已经给了我们足够的东西。

column1: “It is traditional to offer gifts to a possible sponsor.”
column2: “按传统，应向可能的赞助者献上礼物。”

column1: We responded thus: “It is traditional to offer gifts to a possible sponsor.”
column2: 我们如此回应：“按传统，应向可能的赞助者献上礼物。”

column1: They gave us treasure.
column2: 他们给了我们宝物。

column1: It would be unseemly to extort gifts from them at a time like this.
column2: 在这种时候向他们勒索礼物，有失体统。

column1: They should give us gifts, or even a treasure.
column2: 他们应该给我们礼物，甚至一件宝物。

column1: If their first gift isn’t good enough, ask them for another.
column2: 如果他们的第一件礼物不够好，再向他们要一件。

column1: What use could these scrawny creatures be to us?
column2: 这些瘦削的生物对我们有什么用？

column1: The ducks can be quite effective fighters.
column2: 鸭人可以是相当有效的战士。

column1: The ducks can be ferocious fighters, especially against the undead. There are many holy warriors of Humakt among them.
column2: 鸭人可以是凶猛的战士，尤其对抗亡灵时。他们中许多人是胡玛克特的圣战士。

column1: If they give us more than 15 cows, we are legally bound to speak for them at the moot.
column2: 如果他们给我们超过15头牛，法律上我们就必须在议会上为他们发言。

column1: I don’t think I’ve ever heard of a tribe with ducks in it.
column2: 我想我从没听说过有鸭人加入的部落。

column1: This is so unusual, maybe it has something to do with that feathery queen prophecy we were given. We should try to get them in.
column2: 这太不寻常了，也许与我们得到的那个羽毛女王预言有关。我们应该争取让他们加入。

column1: A tribe with ducks in it is unheard-of. It will be extremely difficult to convince the other clans to accept them.
column2: 有鸭人的部落闻所未闻。要说服其他氏族接纳他们极其困难。

column1: We have no special quarrel with the ducks, but the \x01@\x1C clan does. We swore to make war on the beastfolk as part of our tribal confederation. Oh, this is just too ludicrous.
column2: 我们与鸭人并无特殊过节，但 \x01@\x1C 氏族有。我们曾宣誓作为部落联盟的一部分对兽人开战。哦，这真是太荒谬了。

column1: We have no special quarrel with the ducks, but the \x01@\x1C clan does. The ducks are fools to try and join a tribe with such an obvious enemy.
column2: 我们与鸭人并无特殊过节，但 \x01@\x1C 氏族有。鸭人想加入一个拥有如此明显敌人的部落，真是愚蠢。

column1: We are well-respected. The others will give a fair hearing to a petition on behalf of the duck clan, should we choose to make it.
column2: 我们很受敬重。若我们选择提交请愿，其他氏族会公正地听取为鸭人氏族所做的陈词。

column1: We are not well-respected. If we petition on behalf of the ducks, we will be laughed at.
column2: 我们不受敬重。若我们为鸭人请愿，会被嘲笑。

column1: Our ancestors reviled the beastfolk. They will surely punish us if we consider such an outlandish proposal.
column2: 我们的祖先曾痛斥兽人。若我们考虑如此怪异的提议，他们必然降罚。

column1: Making friends with traditional enemies is a quick way to lose blessings and respect.
column2: 与传统敌人交友是快速失去祝福和敬重的途径。

column1: Our traditional enemies are the beastfolk. We tolerate the ducks, risking our ancestors’s disapproval, but a grudging tolerance is as far as we should go.
column2: 我们的传统敌人是兽人。我们容忍鸭人已是冒着祖先不悦的风险，但勉强的容忍就是我们该做的一切。

column1: Ducks…feathers…let me find my scrolls to see if the ducks have queens…
column2: 鸭人……羽毛……让我找找卷轴，看看鸭人是否有女王……

column1: There are many Humakti among them. I like these ducks better than many of the human clans in our tribe.
column2: 他们中有许多胡玛克特信徒。比起我们部落中的许多人类氏族，我更喜欢这些鸭人。

column1: Oh, the moot will rock with laughter to hear of this \x02\x03flat-footed/tail-end-up/cockeyed\x02 proposal!
column2: 哦，议会听到这个 \x02\x03笨拙的/尾巴翘起的/歪斜的\x02 提议，会笑得前仰后合！

column1: We must have them in our tribe.
column2: 我们必须让他们加入我们的部落。

column1: Let us make japes at the expense of these absurd quackers!
column2: 让我们拿这些荒谬的呱呱叫的家伙开涮吧！

column1: Refuse them if we must, but do not humiliate them.
column2: 必要的话可以拒绝他们，但不要羞辱他们。

column1: If our petition is likely to fail anyway, let us wring as much as many gifts from them as we can. We can speak for them without fear that they will actually be accepted.
column2: 如果我们的请愿无论如何都可能失败，那就尽可能从他们那里榨取礼物。我们可以为他们发言，而不用担心他们真的会被接纳。

column1: \x02\x03Instarya/Ellyr/Doranda\x02
column2: \x02\x03因斯塔里亚/艾尔利尔/多兰达\x02

column1: Ask their kinfolk if they could have done it.
column2: 问问他们的族人，他们是否可能做了那事。

column1: The ring asked their kinfolk if they could have done it.
column2: 长老会询问了他们的族人，他们是否可能做了那事。

column1: Exonerate them.
column2: 宣告他们无罪。

column1: They were exonerated.
column2: 他们被宣告无罪。

column1: They thanked us for being wise enough to see the truth.
column2: 他们感谢我们足够明智，看清了真相。

column1: Not long afterwards, they were afflicted by boils and were cut by unseen winds. We saw that they had indeed been guilty of the crimes, despite the absolution we had given them. They knew then that they were outlaws, and did not need to be asked to leave.
column2: 不久之后，他们遭受疖子之苦，被无形之风割伤。我们看到他们确实犯了罪，尽管我们已给予赦免。他们于是知道自己成了亡命徒，不需被要求离开。

column1: Interrogate them.
column2: 审问他们。

column1: The ring interrogated them.
column2: 长老会审问了他们。

column1: They steadfastly proclaimed their innocence.
column2: 他们坚定地宣称自己无罪。

column1: They seemed sincere in this.
column2: 他们在这点上似乎很真诚。

column1: We outlawed them.
column2: 我们宣布他们为不法之徒。

column1: There is no point in interrogating them; they will simply deny the offense.
column2: 审问他们毫无意义；他们只会矢口否认罪行。

column1: I don’t think I could tell a lie from an honest profession of the truth.
column2: 我觉得我无法分辨谎言与真诚的实话。

column1: Allow me to interrogate them. If they are guilty, I will ferret out their lies. If they speak truth, I shall prove them blameless.
column2: 请允许我来审问他们。若他们有罪，我会揪出他们的谎言。若他们说真话，我会证明他们清白。

column1: It is useless to ask the opinions of others. Everyone has gossip, but no one really knows what happened.
column2: 询问他人意见毫无用处。人人都在传谣，但无人真正知晓实情。

column1: It is hard to separate gossip from truth when talking to witnesses.
column2: 与目击者交谈时，很难将流言与真相区分开。

column1: I am a good judge of character. I can separate gossip from truth when talking to witnesses.
column2: 我善于判断他人品性。与目击者交谈时，我能区分流言与真相。

column1: This matter is too small and too personal to yield to divination.
column2: 此事过于细微私密，占卜难以奏效。

column1: If we exonerate the guilty, or outlaw the innocent, our clan magic will suffer.
column2: 若我们赦免有罪者，或流放无辜者，氏族魔法将受损。

column1: Our magic is weak. False spirits may impersonate those of our ancestors.
column2: 我们的魔法太弱。伪灵可能冒充祖先之灵。

column1: Our magic is strong. The spirits of our ancestors will speak clear and true.
column2: 我们的魔法强大。祖先之灵将清晰而真实地言说。

column1: They cannot have done such a terrible thing.
column2: 他们不可能做出如此可怕之事。

column1: We are doomed to make the wrong decision, whatever we do.
column2: 无论我们怎么做，都注定要做出错误决定。

column1: They are innocent.
column2: 他们无罪。

column1: Errarth, the Tragic King, judged adulterers innocent. The next day, his newborn child was killed by a stray arrow.
column2: 悲剧之王埃拉尔斯判定通奸者无罪。次日，他新生的孩子被流矢射死。

column1: the daughter of a thane, is causing trouble for the ring. She seems to do nothing but agitate against your decisions. She has convinced the carls that you favor the weaponthanes, and the weaponthanes that you favor the carls. She says that you have dishonored clan ancestors, that your rulings are unjust, and that your management of the clan’s wealth leaves much to be desired.
column2: 一位领主之女，正在给长老会制造麻烦。她似乎除了煽动反对你的决定之外什么都不做。她让自由民相信你偏袒武器领主，又让武器领主相信你偏袒自由民。她说你侮辱了氏族祖先，你的裁决不公，你对氏族财富的管理令人不敢恭维。

column1: the irritating one, is again causing trouble for the ring. Once again, she seems to do nothing but agitate against your decisions. She has convinced the carls that you favor the weaponthanes, and the weaponthanes that you favor the carls. She says that you have dishonored clan ancestors, that your rulings are unjust, and that your management of the clan’s wealth leaves much to be desired.
column2: 那个惹人厌的家伙，又在给长老会制造麻烦。她似乎除了煽动反对你的决定之外什么都不做。她让自由民相信你偏袒武器领主，又让武器领主相信你偏袒自由民。她说你侮辱了氏族祖先，你的裁决不公，你对氏族财富的管理令人不敢恭维。

column1: who left with the other troublemakers when we split the clan, is back. “Their ring was even more stupid and foolish than you, I could not stay with such imbeciles. Furthermore, no one would listen to my wise council.” She starts in afresh prodding and poking at the ring’s decisions. Until she returned, the carls and weaponthanes were content enough with other, and the clan was content with the ring. Now everyone is grumbling — some agree with \x01Bs, some bad-mouth the ring for letting her within eyesight of our tula.
column2: 那个在我们分裂氏族时与其他捣乱者一同离开的家伙，回来了。“他们的长老会比你们更愚蠢更无知，我无法与这样的白痴待在一起。而且，没人听我的明智建议。”她开始重新挑刺，攻击长老会的决定。在她回来之前，自由民和武器领主彼此还算满意，氏族也对长老会满意。如今人人都在抱怨——有人赞同 \x01Bs，有人骂长老会竟然让她踏入我们的领地视线之内。

column1: \x01Bs did nothing but speak out against the ring.
column2: \x01Bs 除了公开反对长老会，什么也没做。

column1: Yet again, \x01Bs spent much time speaking out against the ring.
column2: 又一次， \x01Bs 花了很多时间公开反对长老会。

column1: \x01Bs returned from the new clan she had joined. To no one’s surprise, she immediately started sowing discord among the clan members.
column2: \x01Bs 她从加入的新氏族回来了。不出众人所料，她立刻开始在氏族成员中散播不和。

column1: Ignore the situation.
column2: 无视此局面。

column1: The ring did nothing to counter her cutting words.
column2: 长老会未采取任何行动反驳她的刻薄言辞。

column1: Offer her compensation in exchange for her silence.
column2: 向她提供补偿以换取她的沉默。

column1: The ring offered her compensation in exchange for her silence.
column2: 长老会向她提供补偿以换取她的沉默。

column1: She howled with outrage. “This offer proves your mendacity. You fear the truth! Well, I love the truth, and nothing will stop me from saying whatever I think is right!”
column2: 她愤怒地吼道：“此提议证明了你们的虚伪。你们害怕真相！哼，我爱真相，没有什么能阻止我说出我认为正确的话！”

column1: The chieftain outlawed her.
column2: 首领将她放逐了。

column1: Her few supporters complained vociferously about this harsh measure, until even those who had disliked her felt sorry for her and angry at the ring.
column2: 她为数不多的支持者大声抗议这项严厉措施，直到连那些原本不喜欢她的人都为她感到难过，并对长老会感到愤怒。

column1: Although she had some supporters among the people, surprisingly few of them argued against the chieftain’s harsh decision.
column2: 虽然她在民众中有一些支持者，但出乎意料地很少有人反对首领的严厉决定。

column1: We tried to outlaw her, but she won her legal case.
column2: 我们试图放逐她，但她赢得了诉讼。

column1: We launched a legal case against her, but \x01Bs showed an amazing \x02\x02legal mind/grasp of Heort’s laws\x02,
column2: 我们对她提起了诉讼，但 \x01Bs 展现了惊人的 \x02\x02法律头脑/对赫尔特法令的掌握\x02，

column1: arguing that \x02\x03we had no justice/our lawspeaker had not followed proper procedure/the case had no merit\x02. \x01@\x0C tried to
column2: 辩称 \x02\x03我们没有公正/我们的律法师未遵循正当程序/此案毫无依据\x02。 \x01@\x0C 试图

column1: and eventually \x06 had to concede the case. \x01Bs’s supporters threw her a feast, declaring she should be the new clan lawspeaker.
column2: 最终 \x06 不得不认输。 \x01Bs的支持者为她举办了宴会，宣称她应该成为新的氏族律法师。

column1: Persuade her that her words harm the unity of the clan.
column2: 说服她，让她明白自己的言论损害了氏族的团结。

column1: We told her that her words were harmful to the unity of the clan.
column2: 我们告诉她，她的言论损害了氏族的团结。

column1: She told us that our poor leadership was harmful to the clan, and that her honesty was the only thing preventing a violent revolt.
column2: 她告诉我们，我们糟糕的领导力对氏族有害，而她的诚实是阻止暴力叛乱的唯一因素。

column1: Threaten her with outlawry.
column2: 以放逐威胁她。

column1: We threatened her with outlawry.
column2: 我们以放逐威胁她。

column1: She laughed and said that such an action would only prove our cowardice and lack of proper justice. She continued with a threat of her own: the people of our clan would rise up to defend her against such an unjust ruling.
column2: 她大笑说，此举只会证明我们的怯懦和缺乏公正。她随后以自己的威胁回敬：我们氏族的人民会起来保护她，反抗这种不公正的裁决。

column1: Try to marry her off to another clan.
column2: 试图将她嫁给另一个氏族。

column1: We sought a husband for her among the other clans.
column2: 我们在其他氏族中为她寻找丈夫。

column1: Which clan do you try to marry her into?
column2: 你试图将她嫁入哪个氏族？

column1: But \x01Bs would not hear of marrying him. “I cannot leave my home clan when it is in the grip of idiots and scoundrels,” she said. “Besides, the one you try to marry me to looks like a trollkin and smells like a broo.”
column2: 但 \x01Bs 不愿嫁给他。“我不能离开我的氏族，当它被蠢货和恶棍掌控之时，”她说，“而且，你们想让我嫁的那个人长得像个小巨魔，闻起来像个布罗。”

column1: After much cajoling, she was persuaded to marry the fellow.
column2: 经过多次哄劝，她终于被说服嫁给了那家伙。

column1: The people of clan \x01@! knew of \x01Bs, and said that they feared that any children she bore would be as lawless and unruly as she.
column2: 氏族 \x01@! 的人们知晓了 \x01Bs，并说他们担心她生下的任何孩子都会像她一样无法无天、桀骜不驯。

column1: She’s lonely, that’s all.
column2: 她只是孤单罢了。

column1: She is consumed by spite, and no one knows why. Her parents did their best to raise her properly.
column2: 她被怨恨吞噬，无人知晓缘由。她的父母已尽力将她好好养育。

column1: She is consumed by spite, and no one knows why. It is unlikely that any argument will satisfy her.
column2: 她被怨恨吞噬，无人知晓缘由。任何说辞都难以令她满意。

column1: She is consumed by spite, and no one cares why by now. No argument will satisfy her, no clan will welcome her.
column2: 她被怨恨吞噬，事到如今也没人在乎缘由了。没有说辞能令她满意，没有氏族会欢迎她。

column1: She is extremely popular among the weaponthanes.
column2: 她在武器领主中极受欢迎。

column1: Everyone says that the weaponthanes love her, but I can think of no particular weaponthanes who do.
column2: 人人都说武器领主们爱戴她，但我想不出哪个具体的武器领主是如此。

column1: We can’t outlaw her just for speaking her mind.
column2: 我们不能仅仅因为她直言不讳就放逐她。

column1: People are often outlawed for purely political reasons.
column2: 人们常常因纯粹的政治原因而被放逐。

column1: She shows disrespect for chosen leaders. We are well within our rights to outlaw her.
column2: 她表现出对当选领袖的不敬。我们完全有权放逐她。

column1: She still shows disrespect for chosen leaders. We are done with polite ways to handle her.
column2: 她依然对当选领袖不敬。我们已经受够了用温和的方式处理她。

column1: The people will be very upset if we outlaw her.
column2: 如果我们放逐她，民众会非常不安。

column1: Her complaints are unjustified.
column2: 她的抱怨毫无道理。

column1: Her complaints are unjustified. Nonetheless, the mood of the people will continue to deteriorate if we do not take strong action.
column2: 她的抱怨毫无道理。然而，如果我们不采取强硬行动，民众的情绪会继续恶化。

column1: Her complaints are still unjustified. Nonetheless, the mood of the people will continue to deteriorate if we do not take strong action.
column2: 她的抱怨依然毫无道理。然而，如果我们不采取强硬行动，民众的情绪会继续恶化。

column1: Her complaints are unjustified, but the mood of the people will continue to deteriorate if we do not take strong action. We must outlaw her.
column2: 她的抱怨毫无道理，但如果我们不采取强硬行动，民众的情绪会继续恶化。我们必须放逐她。

column1: Her complaints are still unjustified, and the mood of the people may lift if we take action. Outlaw her.
column2: 她的抱怨依然毫无道理，而如果我们采取行动，民众的情绪或许会好转。放逐她。

column1: The carls adore her, as they love good weather at harvest time.
column2: 自由民们崇拜她，就像喜爱丰收时节的好天气一样。

column1: She says the carls love her, but secretly they wish she would shut her mouth.
column2: 她说自由民们爱戴她，但暗地里他们巴不得她闭嘴。

column1: Errarth, the Tragic King, failed to act against an enemy in his own clan. That enemy turned out to be mad; she triggered an avalanche, and many of Errarth’s tribe were buried.
column2: 悲剧之王埃拉斯，未能对自己氏族中的一个敌人采取行动。那敌人后来疯了；她引发了雪崩，埃拉斯部落的许多人被掩埋。

column1: She must understand that her actions hurt us all.
column2: 她必须明白自己的行为伤害了我们所有人。

column1: Oh, she doesn’t really mean any harm by her words. I rather admire her gumption!
column2: 哦，她的话其实并非存心伤人。我倒很欣赏她的胆识！

column1: I know! Let’s let her sit on the ring with us!
column2: 我知道了！让她和我们一起坐进长老会吧！

column1: Her furious opposition to us could prevent us from forming a tribe.
column2: 她对我们的激烈反对可能阻止我们组建部落。

column1: Give her something pretty. That will silence her, or at least show our generosity.
column2: 给她些漂亮的东西。那会让她安静下来，或至少显示我们的慷慨。

column1: Give her something valuable. Maybe that will silence her, or at least show our generosity.
column2: 给她些值钱的东西。或许那会让她安静下来，或至少显示我们的慷慨。

column1: Even an entire, new clan at her disposal did not impress her!
column2: 即便拿出整个新氏族供她支配，也没能打动她！

column1: Valensta, a young noblewoman from the \x01@! clan, comes to enquire about the fate of a “noble friend of our clan.” Although she is reluctant to say his name, eventually she identifies him as Orlkensor, the warrior you adopted after Valensta’s clan outlawed him. Your warriors tell her that Orlkensor was slain by a Uroxi warrior. Valensta breaks down, sobbing that the worst possible thing has happened. The Uroxi who killed Orlkensor was her husband, Vingulf.
column2: 瓦伦斯塔，一位来自 \x01@! 氏族的年轻贵族女子，前来询问“我们氏族的一位贵族朋友”的命运。虽然她不愿说出他的名字，但最终她确认那人是奥克森索——那个在瓦伦斯塔的氏族放逐他之后，你们收养的武士。你们的武士告诉她，奥克森索被一名乌洛希武士所杀。瓦伦斯塔崩溃了，哭诉着最糟糕的事情发生了。杀死奥克森索的乌洛希人正是她的丈夫，温古尔夫。

column1: Valensta, a young noblewoman from the \x01@! clan, comes to enquire about the fate of Orlkensor. When we told her that he was slain by a Uroxi warrior, she sobbed. The killer was her husband, Vingulf.
column2: 瓦伦斯塔，一位来自 \x01@! 氏族的年轻贵族女子，前来询问奥克森索的命运。当我们告诉她，他被一名乌洛希武士所杀时，她抽泣起来。凶手是她的丈夫，温古尔夫。

column1: Console her.
column2: 安慰她。

column1: We did our best to console her.
column2: 我们尽力安慰了她。

column1: She left, wreathed in sorrow.
column2: 她离开了，满心悲伤。

column1: Insist that Vingulf apologize for his harsh words.
column2: 坚持要求温古尔夫为他刻薄的言辞道歉。

column1: We insisted that Vingulf apologize for his harsh words. But he merely insulted Orlkensor further.
column2: 我们坚持要求温古尔夫为他刻薄的言辞道歉。但他只是进一步侮辱了奥克森索。

column1: He heaps further insults on Orlkensor’s memory.
column2: 他对奥克森索的记忆又加上了更多的侮辱。

column1: Challenge Vingulf to a duel.
column2: 向温古尔夫挑战决斗。

column1: Who fights the duel?
column2: 谁去决斗？

column1: \x01@\x05 challenged him to a duel.
column2: \x01@\x05 向他提出了决斗挑战。

column1: Vingulf charged \x01@\x05 like a wild beast crashing out of the forest. \x01@\x05 circled him, forcing him to adopt a more cautious stance.
column2: 温古尔夫像一头冲出森林的野兽一样冲向 \x01@\x05 。 \x01@\x05 绕着他转圈，迫使他采取更谨慎的姿势。

column1: Take the silver and go.
column2: 收下银子，然后离开。

column1: She fell on the ground, weeping and wailing. Finally, she recovered herself enough to say, “I know that none believe me, save for dear, slain Orlkensor. But we were the best of friends, and no more. I would never dare commit such a grievous sin against Ernalda, and against my husband.”
column2: 她跌倒在地，哀哭不止。终于，她勉强平复自己，说道：“我知道没人相信我，除了已故的、亲爱的奥尔克森索。但我们只是最好的朋友，仅此而已。我绝不敢对埃尔纳尔达，以及对我的丈夫，犯下如此严重的罪行。”

I swear to you by Ernalda’s apron that Orlkensor was my dear friend, and nothing more. Vingulf’s hatred of Orlkensor was without reason. Tell me where he was headed, I beseech you.”
column2: 她泪如雨下。“被杀的那个人，温古尔夫，是我的丈夫。他被对正直的奥尔克森索的嫉妒吞噬。我以埃尔纳尔达的围裙发誓，奥尔克森索只是我亲爱的朋友，仅此而已。温古尔夫对奥尔克森索的仇恨毫无缘由。求求你，告诉我他朝哪个方向去了。”

column1: A very strange group of explorers comes to your tula. They’re looking for something called an inn, and want to know if you can change the gold coins of the northern empire into silver ones. They seem also to be requesting your hospitality for the night. Along with a strangely-attired Vingan warrior, there’s a duck, a dragonewt, and two very strange beings — a tall human with skin darker than you’ve seen on any man before, and an inhuman beastman, the like of which you’ve never laid eyes on.
column2: 一群非常奇怪的探险者来到你的图拉领地。他们在寻找一个叫“客栈”的地方，并想知道你能不能把北方帝国的金币兑换成银币。他们似乎也在请求你收留他们过夜。除了一个衣着古怪的文加战士，还有一只鸭子、一个龙人，以及两个非常奇异的生物——一个高个子人类，皮肤比你见过的任何男人都要黑，还有一个非人的兽人，你从未见过的那种。

column1: Strange explorers came to our tula.
column2: 奇怪的探险者来到了我们的图拉领地。

column1: They fought back with odd and powerful magics. Although we were merely fighting to get rid of them, they struck to kill. We lost a warrior, and four others were injured. The strange group soon gave up and retreated in a disorderly fashion.
column2: 他们用奇特而强大的魔法反击。虽然我们只是想驱逐他们，他们却下了杀手。我们损失了一名战士，另有四人受伤。这伙奇怪的家伙很快就放弃了抵抗，混乱地撤退了。

column1: We gave them hospitality. But they failed to behave properly.
column2: 我们款待了他们。但他们的行为很不得体。

column1: These guests don’t know the rules of hospitality. The beastman fondles married women in an untoward way, and the dragonewt flings darts at one of your sheep and chuckles in a demented manner. When urged to teach her companions how to act, the Vingan threatens you.
column2: 这些客人不懂好客之道。那个兽人不恰当地抚摸已婚妇女，龙人朝你的一只羊投掷飞镖并疯癫地咯咯笑。当你敦促那位文加人教导她的同伴如何行为得当时，她威胁了你。

column1: Put up with their bad behavior until they go away.
column2: 忍受他们的恶劣行为直到他们离开。

column1: We put up with their bad behavior until they went away.
column2: 我们忍受了他们的恶劣行为，直到他们离开。

column1: We decided to kill them.
column2: 我们决定杀了他们。

column1: As expected, they had many odd and powerful magics. They killed some warriors, and wounded others. But there were too many brave fighters against them, and one by one they were slain — except for the dragonewt, who ran away early in the fighting. We rooted through their belongings and found much good loot, including things that seemed to be magical treasures.
column2: 不出所料，他们拥有许多奇特而强大的魔法。他们杀死了几名战士，并打伤了其他人。但勇敢的战士人数远多于他们，他们一个接一个地被杀死——除了那个龙人，他在战斗初期就逃跑了。我们翻查了他们的物品，找到了许多好战利品，包括一些似乎是魔法宝物的东西。

column1: There was a large leg-bone in bronze, which might have been part of a dead god. There was a small brooch of red leather, in the shape of a mask. There was a cloak that had a picture of a lizard on it, and a mirror in the shape of an eye.
column2: 有一根巨大的青铜腿骨，可能是一位死去神灵的一部分。有一个红色皮革制成的小胸针，形状像面具。有一件斗篷上面画着一只蜥蜴，还有一面眼睛形状的镜子。

column1: We gained the God Bone, the Red Leather Mask, the Shimmering Cloak, and the Eye Mirror.
column2: 我们获得了神骨、红皮面具、闪光斗篷和眼之镜。

column1: They fought back with odd and powerful magics. Many of our warriors fell back, blood running from their ears. Many of these later died. Others lay wounded. We slew the duck, but the others retreated in an orderly fashion. They didn’t even leave his body behind for us to loot.

column1: An Orlanthi who would travel with such strange companions is mad, and probably no Orlanthi at all.
column2: 一个会跟这种古怪同伴同行的奥兰提人怕是疯了，或许根本就不是奥兰提人。

column1: These are all beyond the protection of the law. They will behave wrongly. Orlanth would want us to kill them.
column2: 这些人全都不受法律保护。他们行事邪恶。奥兰兹会希望我们杀掉他们。

column1: They are dangerous. Another clan won’t appreciate our sending them.
column2: 他们很危险。把他们送到另一个部落，那个部落不会感激我们。

column1: They are weird and troubling. We owe it to our neighbors to kill them.
column2: 他们又古怪又麻烦。我们有责任杀死他们，好让邻居安宁。

column1: Our magic is strong. We can beat them.
column2: 我们的魔法很强。我们能打败他们。

column1: Our magic is weak. We shouldn’t anger them.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱。我们不该激怒他们。

column1: Their presence will bless the crops.
column2: 他们的存在会保佑庄稼。

column1: Bad King Urgrain employed weird outcasts such as these to punish members of his tribe who spoke out against him.
column2: 恶王乌格兰曾雇佣这类古怪的被驱逐者，来惩罚部落中敢于公开反对他的人。

column1: Do not anger them, but do not let them stay!
column2: 不要激怒他们，但也不要让他们留下！

column1: They are dripping with booty!
column2: 他们浑身都是战利品！

column1: I can hardly wait to search their corpses for valuable treasures!
column2: 我简直等不及要搜刮他们的尸体找值钱宝物了！

column1: We should kill them, except that there is a dragonewt among them. Let’s welcome them, instead.
column2: 我们本该杀了他们，但他们当中有一个龙人。不如还是欢迎他们吧。

column1: The warriors are already proud, as Orlanthi should be. They need no pampering.
column2: 战士们已经很自豪了，正像奥兰提人应有的样子。他们不需要奉承。

column1: Our relations with the bride’s clan are already as good as could be hoped.
column2: 我们与新娘部落的关系已经好得不能再好了。

column2: 我们与新娘部落的关系没有应有的那么好。

column1: Bless them, but do not give up too much magic.
column2: 祝福他们，但不要给出太多魔法。

column2: 他们会回报我们的祝福，给我们带来巨大的好运。

column2: 在莱巴思与奥尔弗雷达的婚礼上，悲剧之王埃拉思向他每一位祖先的灵致了祝酒词，唯有一位除外。

column1: It took Orlanth a long time to understand Ernalda’s blessing, but when he did, he was very happy.

column1: Praise is due to the warriors.
column2: 应当赞扬战士们。

column1: The carls deserve their share of glory.
column2: 自由民们理应分享荣耀。

column1: This is no time for politics. This is a time for the bride and groom.
column2: 现在不是谈政治的时候。这是新郎新娘的时刻。

column2: 这看起来是一场普通而欢乐的婚礼。但底下潜伏着亡灵那可怕的恶臭！

column1: The bride’s clan would be a good clan to found a tribe with.
column2: 新娘的部落是个适合结盟建立新部落的好部落。

column2: 通奸是对社区的罪行，也是对诸神的冒犯。如果她的指控属实，她并不是唯一受害的一方。

column1: If her husband has broken his marriage vows, one could argue that he is in breach of a pact. The precedents are contradictory, but her claim has some merit.
column2: 如果她的丈夫违背了婚誓，可以认为他违反了契约。先例虽有矛盾，但她的主张有一定道理。

column1: Our clans are friendly. We can rule honestly, without worrying about how it will affect our relations with her clan.
column2: 我们的氏族关系友好。我们可以公正裁决，不必担心这会如何影响与她的氏族的关系。

column1: Her clan is already displeased with us.
column2: 她的氏族已经对我们不满了。

column1: Relations between our clans are strained. Perhaps we should pay, whatever the merits of her case.
column2: 我们氏族之间的关系紧张。也许我们应该赔偿，无论她的案件有何理由。

column2: 我们的魔法很弱。我们的法师无法正确解读征兆。

column1: If we fail to outlaw an adulterer, our clan magic will suffer.
column2: 如果我们未能将通奸者定为非法，我们的氏族魔法将受损。

column1: Outlaw him!
column2: 宣布他为非法！

column1: Send her packing!
column2: 把她打发走！

column1: I told you it would never last.
column2: 我告诉过你这不会长久。

column1: Pay her.
column2: 赔偿她。

The young woman Eonislara was found out in the forest, making love with Korol, a notorious poet and troublemaking warrior of the \x01@! clan. Korol left without a formal farewell. Eonislara is unmarried, so her actions are not an offense against the gods. But she is betrothed to Jorator, a young thane of the \x01@a clan, and the wedding is scheduled for next season.

column1: Let marriage proceed as if nothing has happened.
column2: 让婚礼照常进行，好像什么都没发生过。

column1: Raid the \x01@a clan.

column2: 我们庆祝粗鲁的乔拉托所在的氏族受挫。

column2: 我们把发生的事告诉了乔拉托，但劝他继续婚礼。

column1: Jorator said that Eonislara was a fine young woman, and that if the gods condoned this behavior, he could do no less.
column2: 乔拉托说欧尼斯拉拉是个好姑娘，如果神灵宽恕这种行为，他也不能做得更少。

column1: Jorator angrily refused to honor his betrothal. “I thought I was marrying a good maiden, not a wild and dirty alynx!” When our people heard this, they were outraged.
column2: 乔拉托愤怒地拒绝履行婚约。“我以为我要娶的是一位好姑娘，而不是一只野性难驯的肮脏山猫！”我们的人听到后，非常愤慨。

column1: A marriage is like any other trade. A bargain is a bargain.
column2: 婚姻就像任何其他交易。协议就是协议。

column1: A marriage is like any other trade. You must tell your trading partner the facts, so he will not complain later.
column2: 婚姻就像任何其他交易。你必须告知交易伙伴事实，这样他日后才不会抱怨。

column1: Eonislara has done nothing wrong.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉没有做错任何事。

column1: Eonislara has done nothing wrong; nor has the otherwise disreputable Korol. It would be absurd to marry her to him.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉没有做错任何事；同样地，那个名声不好的科罗尔也没有。把她嫁给他会显得荒谬。

column1: Jorator’s clan is allied to ours. Korol’s clan is on the cusp of a feud with us.
column2: 乔拉托的氏族是我们的盟友。科罗尔的氏族与我们之间的关系正濒临世仇。

column1: This is juicy gossip, but we need to plant our fields more than anything else right now.
column2: 这是个劲爆的八卦，但我们现在最需要的是耕种田地。

column1: This is juicy gossip, but we need to harvest our crops more than anything else right now.
column2: 这是个劲爆的八卦，但我们现在最需要的是收割庄稼。

column1: Surely Jorator will forgive her.
column2: 乔拉托肯定会原谅她的。

column1: Eonislara loves Korol, not Jorator.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉爱的是科罗尔，不是乔拉托。

column1: We must increase patrols, and lay traps for skunks.
column2: 我们必须增加巡逻，并为臭鼬设下陷阱。

column1: Korol’s poetry is fine indeed: “More snakes live in the mountains than any old fool thinks.”
column2: 科罗尔的诗歌确实一般：“山里的蛇比任何老傻瓜想的都多。”

column1: Eonislara is wise. It is good to have a point of comparison before accepting the yoke of marriage.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉很明智。在接受婚姻的枷锁之前有个比较对象是好事。

column1: Korol has talked many of his hotheaded kinfolk out of unwise revenge.
column2: 科罗尔劝阻了许多冲动的族人放弃不明智的复仇。

column1: Let’s just hope Korol didn’t impregnate her.
column2: 只希望科罗尔没让她怀孕。

column1: Eonislara’s desires are not important. This is a matter between clans.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉的欲望不重要。这是氏族之间的事。

column1: If we allow the marriage, she will betray good Jorator.
column2: 如果我们同意这桩婚事，她会背叛好心的乔拉托。

column1: Korol will cause trouble for Jorator if we allow the marriage.
column2: 如果我们同意这桩婚事，科罗尔会给乔拉托找麻烦。

column1: This story will be told behind Jorator’s back. It would be rude not to inform him.
column2: 这个故事会在乔拉托背后流传。不告知他是不礼貌的。

column1: The marriage between Eonislara and Jorator was a fine affair. Jorator’s clan hosted us, impressing us with their hospitality and generosity.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉和乔拉托的婚礼办得很不错。乔拉托的氏族招待了我们，他们的好客与慷慨让我们印象深刻。

column1: Oh, I do love weddings.
column2: 哦，我确实喜欢婚礼。

column1: We convinced them to part with it for less.
column2: 我们说服了他们以更低的价格成交。

column1: We could not meet their offer.
column2: 我们无法满足他们的要价。

column1: They refused to bargain.
column2: 他们拒绝讨价还价。

column1: Try to haggle their price down.
column2: 试着把他们的价格砍下来。

column1: We tried to reduce the price they were asking.
column2: 我们试图降低他们要的价钱。

column1: Forty cows is far too low a price for such a fabulous item!
column2: 四十头牛对于这样一件绝妙的物品来说太便宜了！

column1: The price they ask is fair.
column2: 他们要的价钱是公道的。

column1: The price they ask is fair, but we might be able to bargain them down.
column2: 他们要的价钱是公道的，但我们或许能砍下价来。

column1: The price they ask is fair, but I sense that they wish to quickly dispose of their goods. They will settle for less.
column2: 他们要的价钱是公道的，但我感觉他们想尽快脱手。他们会接受更低的价格。

column1: We can easily take them.
column2: 我们可以轻松拿下他们。

column1: We can easily take them. A chipmunk could easily take them.
column2: 我们可以轻松拿下他们。连花栗鼠都能轻松拿下他们。

column1: A more honest pair of traders I have never seen.
column2: 我从未见过比这更诚实的一对商人。

column1: There is something not quite right about this situation…
column2: 这情况有点不太对劲……

column1: They are thieves.
column2: 他们是小偷。

column1: We must find who they stole the treasure from, and return it to them.
column2: 我们必须找到他们从谁那里偷了宝物，然后归还回去。

column1: This is a useful magical treasure.
column2: 这是一件有用的魔法宝物。

column1: This is a useful magical treasure. They are not uncommon, as such things go.
column2: 这是一件有用的魔法宝物。这种东西并不罕见。

column1: It is valuable, but not magical.
column2: 它很值钱，但并非魔法物品。

column1: If only they had the fabled sword, Chaos Striker.
column2: 要是他们有那把传说中的剑“混沌打击者”就好了。

column1: Squeeze them and see what rancid juices pour out.
column2: 榨干他们，看看能挤出什么酸腐的汁水。

column1: It’s stolen, which means we can steal it from them.
column2: 它是偷来的，所以我们可以再从他们那里偷走。

column1: This treasure might be useful, but we know that our own wealth is precious.
column2: 这件宝物或许有用，但我们知道自己的财富同样珍贵。

column1: It would be unseemly to haggle.
column2: 讨价还价有失体面。

column1: This fabulous \x01@\x14 would be worth it at twice the price!
column2: 这件绝妙的 \x01@\x14 即使价格翻倍也值得！

column1: There’s something that… it’s just a nagging little — but it would be unfair to — no, I’ll not say it.
column2: 有些事……只是隐隐揪心——但那样会不公平——不，我不说了。

column2: sceneR198

column1: Give it back.
column2: 把它还回去。

column1: We gave it back.
column2: 我们还了回去。

column1: The priestesses said they were pleased by our honesty.
column2: 女祭司们说她们对我们的诚实感到满意。

column1: Give it to them, but only in exchange for something.
column2: 可以把东西给他们，但必须换点什么。

column1: How much do you want for it?
column2: 你们想要多少钱？

column1: We said we would give it to them for \x01@\x17 cow’s worth of goods or cattle.
column2: 我们说我们可以用价值 \x01@\x17 头牛的货物或牲口换给他们。

column1: They called us thieves, and said that Uralda would dry up our cows’ udders if we did not give them what was rightfully theirs.
column2: 他们叫我们小偷，还说如果不归还本该属于他们的东西，乌拉尔达会让我们的母牛干奶。

column1: They grudgingly agreed to compensate us for the treasure.
column2: 他们不情愿地同意为这件宝物补偿我们。

column1: “Let’s have a contest of magic, and see if the gods want you to have it.”
column2: “来一场魔法较量吧，看看神明是否想让你们得到它。”

column1: We said, “Let’s have a contest of magic, and see if the gods want you to have it.”
column2: 我们说：“来一场魔法较量吧，看看神明是否想让你们得到它。”

column1: Our priestesses dropped a seed onto dry and barren earth, and so did theirs.
column2: 我们的女祭司把一颗种子播在干涸贫瘠的土里，她们也一样。

column1: Our seed sprouted, and theirs did not. They left without the treasure, although they were slow to congratulate us on our superior connection to the gods.
column2: 我们的种子发芽了，她们没有。她们空手离开了，尽管她们迟迟不愿祝贺我们与神明的联系更紧密。

column1: Their seed sprouted, and ours did not. We admitted that we could not return the treasure to them because we did not have it anymore. They said we were worse than the devious thieves who stole it, and left the tula in great ire.
column2: 她们的种子发芽了，我们的没有。我们承认无法归还宝物，因为它已经不在了。她们说我们比偷走它的狡猾小偷更可恶，然后怒气冲冲地离开了图拉。

column1: Offer them compensation instead.
column2: 改为向他们提供补偿。

column1: They said that the treasure was crucial to their clan magic, and would not accept any other substitute for it.
column2: 他们说这件宝物对他们的氏族魔法至关重要，不接受任何其他替代品。

column1: They said that Esra, the grain goddess, would punish us by taking the goodness from our fields.
column2: 他们说谷物女神埃斯拉会夺走我们田野的沃土来惩罚我们。

column1: Tell them we no longer have it.
column2: 告诉他们我们不再拥有它了。

column1: We told them that their ancestors needed to sniff further, for the treasure was no longer at our tula.
column2: 我们告诉他们说，他们的祖先需要再仔细嗅探，因为宝物已经不在我们的领地上。

column1: They said that we were definitely fools, possibly thieves, and certainly liars. “Now you add insulting our ancestors to our grievance against you!” they exclaimed.
column2: 他们说我们绝对是傻瓜，可能是小偷，肯定是说谎者。“现在你们又侮辱我们的祖先，这加剧了我们的不满！”他们喊道。

column1: Their leader said, “If you bought it, then you had to suspect it was stolen or else you are idiots. Now you say you no longer have it? You are fools and you are cursed.” She said that if ever the treasure returned, so would they.
column2: 他们的首领说：“如果你们买下了它，那你们就应该怀疑它是偷来的，否则你们就是白痴。现在你们说不再拥有它了？你们是傻瓜，你们被诅咒了。”她说如果宝物一旦重现，他们就会回来。

column1: They said that if ever the treasure returned, so would they.
column2: 他们说如果宝物一旦重现，他们就会回来。

column1: We need more cows.
column2: 我们需要更多的牛。

column1: Ask for forty cows.
column2: 索要四十头牛。

column1: The value of this treasure is forty cows.
column2: 这件宝物的价值是四十头牛。

column1: The value of this treasure is forty cows, but our right to it is in doubt. Ask for sixteen cows.
column2: 这件宝物的价值是四十头牛，但我们拥有它的权利存疑。索要十六头牛。

column1: The value of this treasure is forty cows, but our right to it is in doubt. Ask for eleven cows.
column2: 这件宝物的价值是四十头牛，但我们拥有它的权利存疑。索要十一头牛。

column1: Ernalda priestesses are supposed to be peaceful, so they’re no threat to us.
column2: 厄纳尔达女祭司本应是和平的，所以他们对我们没有威胁。

column1: Possession is the essence of the law.
column2: 占有是法律的本质。

column1: We can argue that we didn’t know it was stolen.
column2: 我们可以辩称不知道它是偷来的。

column1: We knew that it was stolen.
column2: 我们知道它是偷来的。

column1: We knew then that it was stolen, and we know now that it was stolen.
column2: 我们当时知道它是偷来的，现在也知道它是偷来的。

column1: They are on good terms with us. Even if we keep the treasure, that won’t change.
column2: 他们与我们关系良好。即使我们保留宝物，也不会改变这一点。

column1: They dislike us already. Keeping the treasure could be a mistake.
column2: 他们已经不喜欢我们了。保留宝物可能是个错误。

column1: They dislike us even more now. Keeping the treasure is a mistake.
column2: 他们现在更加不喜欢我们了。保留宝物是个错误。

column1: Our magic is strong. Challenge them to a duel of fertility.
column2: 我们的魔法强大。向他们挑战生育决斗。

column1: Our magic is weak. If we challenge them, we will probably lose.
column2: 我们的魔法弱小。如果我们挑战，很可能会输。

column1: Don’t listen to any threats they might make. The priestesses of clan \x01@a couldn’t tell wheat from barley if it was growing out of their ears.
column2: 不要理会他们可能发出的任何威胁。氏族 \x01@a 的女祭司们就算大麦小麦从她们耳朵里长出来也分不清。

column1: They could curse us if we don’t act virtuously.
column2: 如果我们不正直行事，他们可能会诅咒我们。

column1: They may have cursed already. We could remedy this by acting virtuously.
column2: 他们可能已经下了诅咒。我们可以通过正直行事来弥补。

column1: Ernalda made gold, and it turned everyone greedy.
column2: 厄纳尔达创造了黄金，这让每个人都变得贪婪。

column1: I bet we could win a fertility duel, so it won’t matter that it isn’t here at the tula right now.
column2: 我打赌我们能赢下生育决斗，所以宝物目前不在领地这事无关紧要。

column1: Let’s say we don’t have it. That way, they will look all over Dragon Pass for it, and we will have time to trade it for something better.
column2: 就说我们没有它。这样他们就会找遍龙隘，我们就有时间用它换更好的东西。

column1: We must do what they want. They are priestesses.
column2: 我们必须按他们说的做。她们是女祭司。

column1: They think they’re better than us.
column2: 她们觉得自己比我们强。

column1: Get something in return for it, at least.
column2: 至少要从它身上换取一些回报。

column1: A contest of magic would be thrilling indeed!
column2: 一场魔法竞赛确实会令人兴奋！

column1: It turned out to be a bad idea, trying to sell\x01@\x01\x01@\x18 to the \x01@! clan. Their Ernalda priestesses insisted it was theirs, and they simply took it. Many of them wanted to just kill us for our audacity, but I managed to talk our way out of it.
column2: 事实证明，试图把\x01@\x01\x01@\x18 卖给 \x01@! 氏族是个坏主意。他们的厄纳尔达女祭司坚持说那是她们的，然后就直接拿走了。她们中许多人想直接杀了我们以惩罚我们的放肆，但我设法用话脱了身。

column2: sceneR199

column1: Dwarfs come to your tula to deliver a warning. “Much offense have you given to the schedule. Unacceptable, unacceptable. Vermin not be permitted to further harm schedule. Interfere no further, or we force to kill, kill, kill. Present calculations guess we kill eight in ten your people, we attack. Also kill eight in ten animal matter, take eight in ten plant matter, destroy eight in ten buildings. Would mean end of your clan. Not want to do it, for time loss would also harm schedule. By you keep going this way, you worse harm to schedule than us kill you. Understand?”
column2: 矮人来到你的领地发出警告。“你们严重冒犯了日程。不可接受，不可接受。不允害虫继续伤害日程。不得再干涉，否则我们强制杀戮，杀戮，杀戮。当前计算预估我们杀死你们十分之八人口，我们便攻击。也杀死十分之八动物物质，拿走十分之八植物物质，摧毁十分之八建筑。这将意味着你们氏族的终结。不想这样做，因为时间损失也会伤害日程。但你们继续这样下去，你们对日程造成的伤害比我们杀死你们更甚。明白吗？”

column1: Dwarfs promised war if we did not improve relations with them.
column2: 矮人扬言，如果我们不改善与他们的关系，就会开战。

column1: “What we told on Orlanthi, this supposed to be minor insult. We not care. Schedule not permit time to be insulted. Only important thing is: just stop what you doing, so we not kill you.” Then they departed.
column2: “我们对奥兰提人所讲的，这本是微不足道的冒犯。我们不在乎。日程不允许有时间被冒犯。唯一重要的是：停止你们的所作所为，这样我们就不会杀死你们。”然后他们离开了。

column1: We listened, but promised nothing.
column2: 我们听了，但没有做出任何承诺。

column1: They left without further word.
column2: 他们一言不发地离开了。

column1: They accepted, saying “These resources partway compensate harm to schedule.” Then they left.
column2: 他们接受了，说“这些资源部分补偿了对日程的伤害。”然后离开了。

column1: They refused, saying “These resources not enough compensate harm to schedule. Just stop what is you doing, so we not kill you.” Then they departed.
column2: 他们拒绝了，说“这些资源不足以补偿对日程的伤害。停止你们的所作所为，这样我们就不会杀死你们。”然后离开了。

column1: Which treasures do you offer them?
column2: 你向他们提供哪些宝物？

column1: They accepted our offer of treasure.
column2: 他们接受了我们提供的宝物。

column1: treasure
column2: 宝物

column1: “Words not matter. Words not cost resources,” the main dwarf said. Action, this what matter. Take no more actions to harm schedule, you not be eight in ten killed. End of speak.” Then they left.
column2: “话语不重要。话语不消耗资源，”为首的矮人说。“行动，这才重要。不再采取伤害日程的行动，你们就不会被杀死十分之八。言尽于此。”然后他们离开了。

column1: They fought without emotion, using strange magic wands that belched fire and felled many. Many were hurt, but none were killed. We caught them and took them as prisoners.
column2: 他们毫无感情地战斗，使用奇怪的魔杖喷出火焰，击倒了许多人。许多人受伤，但无人死亡。我们抓住了他们并把他们关押为俘虏。

column1: Who leads the party to inform the dwarfs of the ransom demand?
column2: 谁带队去通知矮人关于赎金的要求？

column1: How much ransom do you demand?
column2: 你要求多少赎金？

column1: We sent \x01@\x05, with a guard of \x01@\x06 warriors, to demand ransom from the dwarfs.
column2: 我们派 \x01@\x05带领 \x01@\x06 名战士的护卫队去向矮人索要赎金。

column1: They met our demands. We arranged to swap prisoners for wealth.
column2: 他们答应了我们的要求。我们安排了用财富交换俘虏。

column1: They fought without emotion, using strange magic wands that belched fire and felled many. Some were slain, many others wounded. We had to let them retreat, or they would have felled many more.
column2: 他们毫无情感地作战，使用奇怪的法杖喷出火焰，击倒了许多人。有人被杀，更多人受伤。我们不得不让他们撤退，否则他们会杀死更多人。

column1: We can afford to compensate them.
column2: 我们赔得起他们。

column1: We can’t afford to compensate them.
column2: 我们赔不起他们。

column1: They don’t really mean it.
column2: 他们并不是当真的。

column1: They’re serious; they mean to kill us all if we offend them again.
column2: 他们是认真的；如果我们再冒犯他们，他们就要杀光我们。

column1: They’re serious; they mean to kill us all if we offend them again. Give them silver; it is what they will like the best.
column2: 他们是认真的；如果我们再冒犯他们，他们就要杀光我们。给他们银子；这是他们最想要的。

column1: We can take these three runts.
column2: 我们能对付这三个矮崽子。

column1: We can take these three runts, even though they probably have dangerous dwarf weapons.
column2: 我们能对付这三个矮崽子，尽管他们很可能带着危险的矮人武器。

column1: We can take these three runts. What we can’t take is the entire dwarf nation descending upon us.
column2: 我们能对付这三个矮崽子。但我们对付不了整个矮人国度的怒火。

column1: We can take these three runts. What we can’t take is the entire dwarf nation descending on us with their terrible, fire-breathing weapons.
column2: 我们能对付这三个矮崽子。但我们对付不了整个矮人国度带着他们那可怕的喷火武器杀过来。

column1: If we mend our ways without making embarrassing admissions, we will save ourselves and preserve our honor.
column2: 如果我们不改过自新，又不做出令人难堪的认错，就能保全自己，也保住我们的荣誉。

column1: We can use our strong magic against these three, if that seems wise.
column2: 如果我们觉得明智的话，可以用我们强大的魔法对付这三个。

column1: Our magic is weak now, and the weapons of the dwarfs are of legendary power.
column2: 我们的魔法现在很弱，而矮人的武器拥有传说般的力量。

column1: The dwarf schedule has been laid out since before the beginning of time. They seek to use it to end all change in the world.
column2: 矮人的日程从时间开始之前就已经定好。他们想用它来终结世间一切变化。

column1: What liars! I bet they can only kill seven in ten of us!
column2: 撒谎精！我赌他们十个人里最多只能杀七个！

column1: The wounding abilities of dwarf weapons are legendary. Let us not test them.
column2: 矮人武器的杀伤力是传奇性的。我们别去试了。

column1: Offer cows or silver; do not offer a treasure.
column2: 献牛或银子，不要献宝物。

column1: Give promises, not cows.
column2: 许下承诺，而不是献牛。

column1: The dwarfs are yet another enemy people, and they don’t really worship gods.
column2: 矮人是又一个敌对民族，他们并不真正崇拜神祇。

column1: We must at least insult them a little!
column2: 我们至少得骂他们两句！

column1: It is too late. Our destruction is assured.
column2: 太迟了。我们注定灭亡。

column2: sceneR200

column1: Trollkin come to the tula to deliver a message from the trolls. “Ooh, ah. Mistress Cragspider says, ‘You have ann—ann—ann—bothered the trolls enough. Any further ann—ann—ann—botherment and she mad at you, so she kill you all. Personally maybe even. That’s not exactly what she said. I forget exactly what she said. But main thing is, she kill you if you not stop bothering trolls.” Timidly, another one adds: “Also please personal message from us do not kill messengers please.”
column2: 小巨魔们来到图拉，传达巨魔的消息。“呜，啊。岩蛛女主人说：‘你们已经——已经——已经——惹够巨魔了。再有任何——任何——惹事，她就生你们的气，所以她会杀掉你们所有人。也许还是亲自动手。她原话不是这样说的。我忘记她原话怎么说了。但重点是，如果你们不停止惹巨魔，她就会杀了你们。’”胆怯地，另一个补充道：“还有，请收下我们个人的消息——不要杀信使，求求了。”

column1: Trollkin came to deliver a message from Cragspider, leader of the trolls. She warned us that she was considering destroying us.
column2: 小巨魔们前来传达巨魔领袖岩蛛的消息。她警告我们她正在考虑消灭我们。

column1: Promise not to offend Cragspider any further.
column2: 承诺不再冒犯岩蛛。

column1: We promised not to offend Cragspider any further.
column2: 我们承诺不再冒犯岩蛛。

column1: The trollkin said they would convey this message to their leader.
column2: 小巨魔们说他们会把这个消息传达给他们的女主人。

column1: Release the trollkin from their chains.
column2: 解开小巨魔们的锁链。

column1: We released the trollkin from their chains.
column2: 我们解开了小巨魔们的锁链。

column1: They thanked us and said we were more merciful than their mistress. “Her warning no lie though! Be careful, or your brains end up in soup for her dinner table!”
column2: 他们感谢我们，说我们比他们的女主人仁慈。“不过她的警告不是假的！小心点，否则你们的脑子就会变成她餐桌上的汤料！”

column1: Send tribute to Cragspider.
column2: 向岩蛛进贡。

column1: How much do you give to her?
column2: 你给她多少？

column1: Which treasures do you offer her?
column2: 你献上哪些宝物？

column1: Do you send a delegation to deliver the treasure personally?
column2: 你是否派一支使团亲自送上宝物？

column1: We sent a delegation to deliver it to Cragspider.
column2: 我们派了一支使团将宝物送到岩蛛那里。

column1: They did not see Cragspider, but one of her attendants. The attendant, named Ukkur, received our peace-gift. “Thank you for your tasty gift,” Ukkur said. “We not so ready to eat you now. But you far from having proved yourselves. Go now, and not be troll enemies.”
column2: 他们没有见到岩蛛，只见到她的一名侍从。这名侍从名叫乌库尔，收下了我们的和平礼物。“谢谢你们美味的礼物，”乌库尔说，“我们现在不那么着急吃你们了。但你们远未证明自己。走吧，不要成为巨魔的敌人。”

column1: We never saw the delegation, or the treasure, again. \x01@\x14 said that Cragspider had probably destroyed them all in a fit of rage.
column2: 我们再也没见过那支使团和那批宝物了。 \x01@\x14 说岩蛛可能在一怒之下把他们全毁了。

column1: The trollkin left with gifts for Cragspider.
column2: 小巨魔们带着给岩蛛的礼物离开了。

column1: Take them prisoner.
column2: 俘虏他们。

column1: We took them prisoner.
column2: 我们俘虏了他们。

column1: What do you do with them?
column2: 你打算怎么处置他们？

column1: Make them thralls.

column2: 对巨魔来说，唯一比一个巨魔崽更可牺牲的，就是三个巨魔崽。

column2: 巨魔是黑暗生物，永远是我们之敌。

column2: 以自由之名释放巨魔崽！要不就囚禁它们，献祭给尤尔马尔。

column1: Look at how the collars chafe their little necks!
column2: 看那项圈磨破了它们的小脖子！

column1: He who promises much and gives little will die in a grand stead.

column1: Release them, and earn the gratitude of the trolls.

column2: 如果树强敌，无人愿与我们结盟。

column1: Argue for this.
column2: 支持此议。

column2: “萨拉斯卡的计划有利有弊。”

column1: The other clans hooted down Saraska and \x01@\x0B, scolding them for their rank foolishness.
column2: 其他氏族嘘声赶走萨拉斯卡和 \x01@\x0B，斥责他们的极度愚蠢。

column1: We have many cows, so we can play the game of politics.
column2: 我们牛只众多，因此玩得起政治游戏。

column1: The game of politics is for richer clans.
column2: 政治游戏是给更富有的氏族玩的。

column1: Saraska’s kingdom will make our cows healthier.
column2: 萨拉斯卡的王国会让我们的牛更加健壮。

column1: Saraska and \x01@\x0B have nothing but good intentions.
column2: 萨拉斯卡和 \x01@\x0B 只有好意。

column1: Saraska is too trusting, and \x01@\x0B is too greedy.
column2: 萨拉斯卡太轻信，而 \x01@\x0B 太贪婪。

column2: 在议会上，我们说：“她应该接受考验，以证明她魔法的力量。”

column1: The other clans agreed with us; Saraska would have to prove herself to us. “I am prepared to do so,” Saraska said, “because the prophecies say it will be so.” She strode confidently outside the tribal hall. All murmured that this was a good omen indeed, that she had the favor of Orlanth. “Orlanth, I call on you to recognize my right to rule! Ernalda, I call on you to recognize my bounty and goodness! Lhankor Mhy, I call on you to recognize my love for the law!”

column1: The other clans thought our insistence foolish. “Do the prophecies not say Saraska is bound to be our queen?” they said, enraptured by her oratory. It was decided that we would seek confederation with the other tribes.
column2: 其他氏族认为我们的坚持是愚蠢的。“难道预言不是说了萨拉斯卡注定要成为我们的女王吗？”他们说着，被她的演说所迷住。最终决定我们将寻求与其他部族结盟。

column1: “We must make Saraska’s kingdom.”

column1: The other clans agreed that we would bring Saraska’s kingdom into being. It was decided that we would seek confederation with the other tribes. Our own clan was selected to lead the delegation to the \x01Á.
column2: 其他氏族同意我们将促成萨拉斯卡的王国。最终决定我们将寻求与其他部族结盟。我们自己的氏族被选中领导代表团前往 \x01Á.

column1: We are not rich enough to be persuasive.
column2: 我们不够富有，无法说服他人。

column1: There is nothing so persuasive as a gift of cows.
column2: 没有什么比赠送牛只更有说服力的了。

column1: Saraska is the most admirable person I have ever had the honor of meeting.
column2: 萨拉斯卡是我有幸遇见的最令人敬佩的人。

column1: Saraska is certainly sincere.
column2: 萨拉斯卡无疑是真诚的。

column1: Saraska is sincere, but there is something wrong about her. My gut tells me that she is deluded.
column2: 萨拉斯卡是真诚的，但她身上有些不对劲。我的直觉告诉我她受了迷惑。

column1: I’ve talked to the warriors of the other clans, and they seem uncertain about this.
column2: 我和其他氏族的战士们谈过，他们似乎对此不确定。

column1: We must follow Saraska, because she has the prophecies behind her.
column2: 我们必须追随萨拉斯卡，因为她有预言作为后盾。

column1: It is strange to want a kingdom, when life is still so hard here, and people so scattered.
column2: 奇怪的是，在生活仍如此艰难、人们如此分散之时，却渴望一个王国。

column1: There are many poems about kingdoms that started too soon, and crumbled into dust.
column2: 有许多诗歌讲述那些过早建立、又化为尘土的王国。

column1: Everyone in the clan will hate us if we don’t support her.
column2: 如果我们不支持她，氏族里的每个人都会憎恨我们。

column1: Our reputation in the tribe is poor. It will be hard for us to persuade the others of anything.
column2: 我们在部落中名声很差。要说服其他人任何事情都会很困难。

column1: Our reputation in the tribe is good. Our words will be weighed fairly.
column2: 我们在部落中名声很好。我们的话会得到公正的衡量。

column1: Her main argument is that her rule is mandated by the gods.
column2: 她的主要论点是，她的统治是众神所命。

column1: Her main argument is that her rule is mandated by the gods. If she does not prove this, we are fools to follow her.
column2: 她的主要论点是，她的统治是众神所命。如果她无法证明这一点，追随她就是愚蠢之举。

column1: The rest of the tribe hates us, so we should decide what we want to happen, and argue the opposite.
