column2: 我们或许想给，但给不了。

column1: We can afford to help a son of our clan.
column2: 我们承受得起帮助氏族的一个儿子。

column1: We are not legally obligated to help him.
column2: 我们没有法律义务帮助他。

column1: He has no use for anything but warriors.
column2: 他除了战士什么都用不上。

column1: If we give him wealth, he can hire mercenaries to help him fight.
column2: 如果我们给他财富，他可以雇佣佣兵帮他作战。

column1: Jaldon is a legendary enemy. Derik will probably die, as will any we send to help him.
column2: 贾尔顿是传奇般的敌人。德里克很可能战死，我们派去帮助他的人也一样。

column1: If we do nothing, we will be shamed. We can send a few fighters.
column2: 如果我们无所作为，就会蒙羞。我们可以派几个战士去。

column1: We can’t spare any fighters now.
column2: 我们现在抽不出任何战士。

column1: Jaldon is a legendary enemy. I think Derik has legend in him too, and could beat Jaldon.
column2: 贾尔顿是传奇般的敌人。但我觉得德里克身上也有传奇色彩，他能击败贾尔顿。

column1: Jaldon is a legendary enemy. I think Derik has legend in him too, and could beat Jaldon. But when heroes clash, ordinary folk die.
column2: 贾尔顿是传奇般的敌人。但我觉得德里克身上也有传奇色彩，他能击败贾尔顿。不过英雄相争时，凡人会丧命。

column1: Derik will need the aid of the gods to battle a foe so great as Jaldon Goldentooth.
column2: 德里克需要神明的帮助才能与贾尔顿·金牙这样强大的敌人作战。

column1: Derik will need the aid of our war gods to battle a foe so great as Jaldon Goldentooth.
column2: 德里克需要我们的战争之神的帮助才能与贾尔顿·金牙这样强大的敌人作战。

column1: Jaldon is immortal, but that doesn’t mean he can’t be killed. He’s been killed several times. The problem is that he never stays killed.
column2: 贾尔顿是不朽的，但这并不意味着他不能被杀死。他已经被杀过好几次了。问题是他从来不会一直死着。

column1: It would be dishonorable to refuse to fight.
column2: 拒绝战斗是不光彩的。

column1: Jaldon is not evil. He is our enemy, and we must slay him, but that does not make him evil.
column2: 贾尔顿并非邪恶。他是我们的敌人，我们必须杀死他，但这并不代表他就是邪恶的。

column1: We must save our resources for the climactic battle against the elves.
column2: 我们必须把资源留到与精灵的决战中。

column1: The sable riders are doomed to fail, because they never learn to read.
column2: 黑貂骑手注定失败，因为他们从不学会阅读。

column1: Derik will win, but will be badly wounded.
column2: 德里克会赢，但会受到重伤。

column1: We must sacrifice to the gods.
column2: 我们必须向神明献祭。

column1: If we help Derik, Jaldon will slay him, then come back and finish us off!
column2: 如果我们帮助德里克，贾尔顿会杀了他，然后回来把我们赶尽杀绝！

column1: You have declared war against the \x01Á. The day of the battle is upon you.
column2: 你对 \x01Á. 宣战了。战斗之日已经来临。

column1: The \x01Á has declared war against you. The day of the battle is upon you.
column2: \x01Á 对你宣战了。战斗之日已经来临。

column1: The day of the battle against the \x01Á came upon us.
column2: 与 \x01Á 的战斗之日来临了。

column1: The god-talkers said we were likely to win the battle.
column2: 神言者说我们很可能赢得战斗。

column1: The god-talkers said we were likely to lose the battle.
column2: 神言者说我们很可能输掉战斗。

column1: The god-talkers said that the signs were confused, and it was hard to say who would win.
column2: 神言者说征兆混乱，难以说谁会赢。

column1: Fight boldly.
column2: 勇敢地战斗。

column1: We fought boldly.
column2: 我们勇敢地战斗了。

column1: Fight cautiously.
column2: 谨慎地战斗。

column1: We fought cautiously.
column2: 我们谨慎地战斗了。

column1: Fight cleverly.
column2: 巧妙地战斗。

column1: We fought cleverly.
column2: 我们巧妙地战斗了。

column1: We sacrificed to the gods.
column2: 我们向神明献祭了。

column1: The priests said that the gods favored us.
column2: 祭司们说神明眷顾我们。

column1: The priests said that the signs were bad. The gods were refusing to take sides in a battle between Orlanthi.
column2: 祭司们说征兆不好。神明拒绝在奥兰斯人之间的战斗中偏袒任何一方。

column1: We sued for peace.
column2: 我们求和了。

column1: This is a battle that will be sung of for years — and our names must be foremost in the songs!
column2: 这是一场将传唱多年的战斗——我们的名字必须响彻歌谣！

column1: The gods will favor our boldness when we ask them. Then we will lead on the field of battle and shine in our glory!
column2: 当我们祈求时，神明会眷顾我们的勇猛。届时我们将在战场上率领众人，在荣耀中闪耀！

column1: We should not take the chance that \x01@\x0B will rebuff an offer of peace.
column2: 我们不应该冒险让 \x01@\x0B 拒绝和谈的提议。

column1: An offer of peace, even at this fateful hour, could prevent bloodshed and make our name as negotiators.
column2: 即使在这命运攸关的时刻，提出和平提议也能避免流血，并让我们作为谈判者成名。

column1: I’m glad this has nothing to do with the carls.
column2: 我很高兴这与自由民无关。

column1: If we lose, we will have to pay reparations.
column2: 若我们战败，就必须支付赔款。

column1: There is no dishonor in seeking the aid of the gods.
column2: 寻求诸神助益并无耻辱。

column1: There is no dishonor in seeking the aid of the gods. On the other hand, there is no guarantee that, in a fight between Orlanthi, they will grant such aid.
column2: 寻求诸神助益并无耻辱。但另一方面，在奥朗斯人之间的战斗中，并不保证他们会赐予这种助益。

column1: A clever plan grants the best results if we win, and exacts the highest toll if we lose.
column2: 一个巧妙的计划若获胜则带来最佳结果，若失败则索取代价最高。

column1: A clever victory would grant the greatest credit to our rule.
column2: 一场巧妙的胜利将为我们统治赢得最大的声望。

column1: There is no point in seeking the aid of the gods.
column2: 寻求诸神助益毫无意义。

column1: Our magic is strong. Divinations and sacrifices are likely to succeed.
column2: 我们的魔法强大。占卜和献祭很可能成功。

column1: Our magic is weak. Divinations and sacrifices are likely to fail.
column2: 我们的魔法薄弱。占卜和献祭很可能失败。

column1: Our magic is strong. Divinations are likely to succeed. As are sacrifices, if we gift the gods with at least twenty-five cows.
column2: 我们的魔法强大。占卜很可能成功。献祭亦如此，若我们赠予诸神至少二十五头牛。

column1: Suing for peace will increase the fertility of our fields.
column2: 求和将增加我们田地的丰饶。

column1: We could try suing for peace, so we could go home and tend our crops. But a war is more likely than a peace by now.
column2: 我们可以尝试求和，这样就能回家照料庄稼。但事到如今，战争比和平更可能发生。

column1: Better wounded pride than wounded flesh.
column2: 宁可伤自尊，也不伤血肉。

column1: Bold bullying is best.
column2: 大胆欺凌最为上策。

column1: A sword need not be stupid.
column2: 剑不必愚蠢。

column1: “\x02\x04’Tis easier to mend the barn than to build a new one/The fiercest alynxes must learn to sleep together in their den/Fight boldly, die nobly/Roar like bears, plot like snakes, and fight like Storm Bulls\x02.”
column2: “\x02\x04修补谷仓比新建一座更容易/最凶猛的艾林克斯猫也得学会在巢穴中共眠/勇敢战斗，高贵赴死/如熊般咆哮，如蛇般谋划，如风暴公牛般战斗\x02。”

column1: It is not too late to make peace!
column2: 此刻言和，为时未晚！

column1: Frontal assault was good enough for our ancestors, and it is good enough for us.
column2: 正面强攻对我们的祖先来说足够好，对我们来说也足够好。

column1: We will suffer losses, that is sure. Let’s lose as few kinfolk as possible.
column2: 我们必遭损失，这毋庸置疑。让我们尽可能少失去族人。

column1: The battle was joined. Priests from both sides rained thunder down on the battlefield. We charged our foemen boldly, our battleshouts ringing in their ears. Their line broke, and we fell among them, driving the enemy into the mud. We suffered only light losses. \x01@\x0B surrendered, and paid reparations to us. Our clan claimed a royal share of the loot.
column2: 战斗开始了。双方祭司向战场降下雷霆。我们勇敢地冲向敌人，战吼在他们耳边回荡。他们的阵线崩溃了，我们冲入敌阵，将敌人赶入泥泞。我们只遭受了轻微损失。 \x01@\x0B 投降，并向我们支付赔款。我们的氏族分得了战利品中王家的一份。

column1: The battle was joined. Priests from both sides rained thunder down on the battlefield. We charged boldly, and our battleshouts echoed off our enemies’ burnished shields. We fell upon them, but their line held. They advanced implacably, driving us into the mud, and slaying many and wounding more. There was no choice but to surrender, and pay reparations.
column2: 战斗开始了。双方祭司向战场降下雷霆。我们勇敢冲锋，战吼在敌人锃亮的盾牌上回荡。我们扑向他们，但他们的阵线坚守住了。他们无情地推进，将我们赶入泥泞，杀死许多，伤者更多。别无选择，只能投降并支付赔款。

column1: The battle was joined. Priests from both sides rained thunder down on the battlefield. We made our foemen come to us, keeping tight discipline and providing them few opportunities to hurt us. They crashed against us again and again, but our line held.
column2: 战斗开始了。双方祭司向战场降下雷霆。我们保持严密纪律，让敌人来攻，几乎不给他们伤害我们的机会。他们一次又一次冲击我们，但我们的阵线坚守住了。

column1: The battle was joined. Priests from both sides rained thunder down on the battlefield. We made our foemen come to us, their battleshouts shrieking all about us. They fell upon us, and our line broke. With wind-fleet feet they pursued us into the trees and gullies, slaying many and wounding more. We had no choice but to surrender, and pay reparations.
column2: 战斗开始了。双方祭司向战场降下雷霆。我们让敌人来攻，他们的战吼在我们四周尖啸。他们扑向我们，我们的阵线崩溃了。他们以风驰电掣之速追入树林和沟壑，杀死许多，伤者更多。我们别无选择，只能投降并支付赔款。

column1: The battle was joined. Priests from both sides rained thunder down on the battlefield. We engaged our foemen with an ingenious feint, sending our main force to flank them by surprise. We fell among them on all sides, driving the enemy like sheep to the slaughter. We suffered only light losses.
column2: 战斗开始了。双方祭司向战场降下雷霆。我们以精妙的佯攻与敌人交战，派遣主力出其不意地侧击。我们从四面八方冲入敌阵，如驱羊群般将敌人赶向屠戮。我们只遭受了轻微损失。

column1: They gave us what we asked for, with stony glares. Several of them spit at us, barely missing our feet.
column2: 他们以冰冷的怒视给了我们索要之物。其中有几人朝我们吐唾沫，几乎吐到我们脚上。

column1: They gave us less than we asked for.
column2: 他们给得比我们要求的少。

column1: They refused us. They said the only way they would give tribute to cold and heartless folk like ourselves would be if they were dead, and we had slaughtered them as they stood there.
column2: 他们拒绝了。他们说，要向像我们这样冷酷无情的人进贡，唯一的办法就是他们死了，而我们当场屠杀了他们。

column1: Some of the people were ashamed that we had not offered help, while the greediest were sorry that we didn’t press our temporary advantage.
column2: 部分民众因我们未曾施以援手而感到羞愧，而最贪婪的那些人则遗憾我们没有利用暂时的优势。

column1: We helped them with gifts.
column2: 我们以礼物帮助他们。

column1: What do you give them?
column2: 你们给他们什么？

column1: Their gratitude was unrestrained.
column2: 他们感激不尽。

column1: They accepted the gifts, but grudgingly, and only, they said, because they were hardly in a position to refuse. They still suspected us and our motives.
column2: 他们接受了礼物，但态度勉强，并且说只是因为几乎没有拒绝的余地。他们仍然怀疑我们和我们的动机。

column1: They thanked us, but they seemed preoccupied with their recent loss.
column2: 他们向我们道谢，但似乎心系最近遭受的损失。

column1: They accepted the gifts, but said that they were still suspicious of us and our motives.
column2: 他们接受了礼物，但说仍然怀疑我们和我们的动机。

column1: They believed our tale.
column2: 他们相信了我们的说法。

column1: They said we were snakes.
column2: 他们说我们是蛇。

column1: Helping our enemies would be a noble thing to do. But I’m not set on it.
column2: 帮助我们的敌人是件高尚之举，但我并不执着于此。

column1: Surely we can afford to help our allies. They would do as much for us.
column2: 我们当然有能力帮助盟友。他们也会为我们做同样的事。

column1: We aren’t exactly wealthy ourselves. We can’t help them.
column2: 我们自己也不算富裕。我们帮不了他们。

column1: We can afford to help them, assuming we want to.
column2: 只要愿意，我们负担得起帮助他们的代价。

column1: Now that they are weak, we can demand tribute. They will be afraid that we will raid them.
column2: 如今他们虚弱，我们可以要求进贡。他们会害怕我们劫掠他们。

column1: We are not obligated to help them.
column2: 我们没有义务帮助他们。

column1: If our alliance is to count for anything, we should help them now.
column2: 如果我们的联盟要有任何意义，我们现在就应该帮助他们。

column1: We will gain their esteem by helping them when they are in trouble.
column2: 在他们困难时施以援手，我们将赢得他们的尊敬。

column1: We will gain their esteem by helping them; if we threaten them, we will gain their hatred.
column2: 帮助他们，我们会赢得尊敬；威胁他们，只会招来仇恨。

column1: Against trolls, Orlanthi should stick together.
column2: 面对巨魔，奥兰赛人理应团结一致。

column1: The beastfolk would kill us all, if they could, just as they tried to kill our ancestors.
column2: 兽人若能做到，会杀死我们所有人，正如他们曾试图杀死我们祖先那样。

column1: I have heard there are shamans in the area who seek out clans who have just been raided. They offer to send bad spirits against the enemies of those who hire them.
column2: 我听说这个地区有萨满，专找刚遭劫掠的部族。他们提供恶灵，去攻击雇佣者的敌人。

column1: Let them rot.
column2: 让他们腐烂去吧。

column1: Bad King Urgrain sent trolls against King Voskath. Then Voskath sent elves against King Urgrain.
column2: 恶王乌格兰派巨魔攻打沃斯卡斯王。随后沃斯卡斯王派精灵攻打乌格兰王。

column1: This is an excellent chance to get two foes at one anothers’ throats.
column2: 这是让两个仇敌互相撕咬的绝佳机会。

column1: Make sure they know who visited this fate upon them, so they will fear us.
column2: 确保他们知道是谁降下这命运，这样他们就会畏惧我们。

column1: Blame it on someone else, or they’ll take vengeance on us!
column2: 把罪责推到别人头上，否则他们会向我们复仇！

column1: We must help them!
column2: 我们必须帮助他们！

column1: We expected this sort of thing to happen when we decided to resettle this area. They should have expected it, too.
column2: 我们决定重新定居这片区域时，就预料到会发生这种事。他们也应该预料到。

column1: Let’s raid them when they’re weak.
column2: 趁他们虚弱时袭击他们。

column1: We will get no better chance to display our generosity.
column2: 再也没有更好的机会来展现我们的慷慨了。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors told me they averted a curse sent by enemy shamans.
column2: 祖先之灵告诉我，他们挡下了敌方萨满施放的诅咒。

column1: “Ernalda will smile on us if we make peace.”
column2: “若我们缔造和平，厄尔纳尔达会向我们微笑。”

column1: We said, “Ernalda will smile on us if we make peace.”
column2: 我们说：“若我们缔造和平，厄尔纳尔达会向我们微笑。”

column1: \x01@\x0B said that we needed the blessings of Ernalda. \x05 agreed to make an alliance in the goddess’ name.
column2: \x01@\x0B 说我们需要厄尔纳尔达的赐福。 \x05 同意以女神之名缔结联盟。

column1: \x01@\x0B said that we had no right to invoke the Earth Mother, when we made tribes only for our own gain.
column2: \x01@\x0B 说我们无权召唤大地母亲，因为我们组建部族仅仅是为了自身利益。

column1: “Make peace, or we will make war.”
column2: “要么议和，要么开战。”

column1: We said: “Make peace, or we will make war.”
column2: 我们说：“要么议和，要么开战。”

column1: Make war.
column2: 开战。

column1: We decided to make war.
column2: 我们决定开战。

column1: The other clans agreed to this, because the \x01Á said we were not trustworthy, and obviously harbored plans to make war on us.
column2: 其他部族同意了这一点，因为 \x01Á 说我们不可信，而且显然对我们怀有开战的计划。

column1: We let the matter rest.
column2: 我们让这件事就此作罢。

column1: Some of the weaponthanes muttered that a weak tribe was worse than a strong clan.
column2: 一些武器领主嘀咕说，一个弱小的部族还不如一个强大的氏族。

column1: “We must unite against the inhumans.”
column2: “我们必须联合起来对抗非人。”

column1: We said: “We must unite against the inhumans.”
column2: 我们说：“我们必须联合起来对抗非人。”

column1: \x01@\x0B said that the inhumans were indeed a mighty threat. \x05 agreed to make peace with us.
column2: \x01@\x0B 说非人确实是一个巨大的威胁。 \x05 同意与我们议和。

column1: \x01@\x0B rejected our request for alliance. “The threat of the inhumans is less than is feared,” \x06 said.
column2: \x01@\x0B 拒绝了我们的联盟请求。“非人的威胁并不像人们担心的那么大，” \x06 说道。

column1: “We must unite against the other tribes.”
column2: “我们必须联合起来对抗其他部族。”

column1: We said: “We must unite against the other tribes.”
column2: 我们说：“我们必须联合起来对抗其他部族。”

column1: \x01@\x0B said that this was a good plan.
column2: \x01@\x0B 说这是个好计划。

column1: “Should we make immediate war on another tribe?”
column2: “我们应当立即向另一个部族开战吗？”

column1: “No, let others merely fear us for now.”
column2: “不，暂时只让其他部族畏惧我们就好。”

column1: We decided to wait before declaring war on anyone.
column2: 我们决定在向任何人宣战之前先等待。

column1: \x01@\x0B rejected our argument. “It is bad enough to have tribes. If we keep on like this, soon we will have a kingdom, and why would we want that?”
column2: \x01@\x0B 反驳了我们的论点。“有部族就已经够糟了。如果继续这样下去，很快我们就会有个王国，那有什么好？”

column1: “With peace, we can enforce the laws of Orlanth.”
column2: “有了和平，我们可以推行奥兰斯的律法。”

column1: We said: “With peace, we can spread the laws of Orlanth.”
column2: 我们说：“有了和平，我们可以传播奥兰斯的律法。”

column1: \x01@\x0B said that the laws were important, and by agreeing to follow them together, we would win the favor of Orlanth.
column2: \x01@\x0B 说律法很重要，通过共同遵守，我们将赢得奥兰斯的青睐。

column1: \x01@\x0B said that the laws of Orlanth were important, but that the freedom of Orlanth was important, too.
column2: \x01@\x0B 说奥兰斯的律法很重要，但奥兰斯的自由也同样重要。

column1: They will respond well to threats.
column2: 他们对威胁反应良好。

column1: It is hard to know what they want.
column2: 很难知道他们想要什么。

column1: They only made a tribe because we did, because they were afraid. They will not be anxious to deal with us.
column2: 他们只因我们组建部族才跟着做，因为他们害怕。他们不会急于与我们打交道。

column1: Make peace only with those who fear you.
column2: 只与畏惧你的人和谈。

column1: When peace fails, war wins.
column2: 和平失败时，战争就赢了。

column1: People fear inhumans more than they fear one another.
column2: 人们对非人的恐惧超过了对彼此的恐惧。

column1: Peace agreements between tribes are not long-lasting.
column2: 部族间的和平协议不会持久。

column1: The best argument we have is that an alliance would help uphold the laws of Orlanth.
column2: 我们最好的论据是，联盟有助于维护奥兰斯的律法。

column1: If we fail to win peace, our reputation will suffer.
column2: 如果我们未能赢得和平，我们的声誉会受损。

column1: Our best argument is protection from a common foe.
column2: 我们最好的论据是抵御共同的敌人。

column1: Ernalda smiles on the peacemaker.
column2: 厄尔纳尔达向缔造和平者微笑。

column1: If we make peace in Ernalda’s name, and then break the peace, our fertility will suffer.
column2: 若我们以厄尔纳尔达之名缔造和平，随后又破坏和平，我们的丰饶将受损。

column1: We must argue for peace in Ernalda’s name. We mustn’t break the peace, or our fertility will suffer.
column2: 我们必须以厄尔纳尔达之名争取和平。我们绝不能破坏和平，否则我们的丰饶将受损。

column1: Talk of peace during Sea season is good. Talk of war is not.
column2: 海季谈论和平是好的。谈论战争则不好。

column1: Talk of peace during Earth season is good. Talk of war is not.
column2: 地季谈论和平是好的。谈论战争则不好。

column1: King Voskath made peace with Bad King Urgrain, but Urgrain broke the peace. Urgrain’s lawspeakers were tongue-tied for a year after that.
column2: 沃斯卡斯王与恶王乌格兰议和，但乌格兰破坏了和平。自那以后，乌格兰的律法师一年之内都张口结舌。

column1: Peace is good, if you are the first one to break it.
column2: 如果你是第一个破坏和约的人，和平就是好事。

column1: We must not make vows we are not prepared to honor.
column2: 我们绝不能许下不准备履行的誓言。

column1: Everyone knows what a terrible threat the elves pose!
column2: 谁都知道精灵构成了多么可怕的威胁！

column1: War is inevitable. Let us embrace it.
column2: 战争不可避免。让我们拥抱它吧。

column1: Laws are meant to be followed.
column2: 律法理应被遵守。

column1: A well-phrased threat never hurt anybody.
column2: 巧言威胁从未伤害过任何人。

column1: sceneR211
column2: sceneR211

column1: \x01Bs returns from the \x01@! tula. She brings her dowry back with her, and more wealth besides. “They treated me intolerably,” she complains. “The man you married me to was worse than an ox, and his kin all stank wretchedly. Their clan is almost as badly ruled as this one. Its ring competes with ours for sheer stupidity. Divorce was the only option.” She then asks what has happened in her absence, and immediately starts ridiculing the ring for decisions taken while she was away.
column2: \x01Bs 从 \x01@! 图拉领地归来。她带回了自己的嫁妆，还有更多财富。“他们对我无法忍受，”她抱怨道，“你们把我嫁的那个男人连牛都不如，他的亲戚全都臭不可闻。他们的氏族统治得几乎跟这个一样糟。他们的长老会在愚蠢程度上跟我们的不相上下。离婚是唯一的选择。”然后她询问自己不在时发生了什么，并立刻开始嘲笑长老会在她离开期间做出的决定。

column1: “A large part of the clan is gone! I don’t blame them, they went looking for better leadership, I’m sure.”
column2: “氏族的一大半都不在了！我不怪他们，他们去找更好的领导了，我敢肯定。”

column1: She finally concludes, “And I see that the ring isn’t even competent enough to have a full seven members.”
column2: 她最后说，“我还看到，长老会连凑齐七个成员的本事都没有。”

column1: \x01Bs divorced her husband in clan \x01@! and returned to us. She immediately began to insult the ring and question its decisions.
column2: \x01Bs 在氏族 \x01@! 与丈夫离婚，回到了我们身边。她立刻开始侮辱长老会，质疑其决定。

column1: The ring decided that her behavior was best ignored.
column2: 长老会决定，她的行为最好不予理睬。

column1: She laughed scornfully. “The fools in the \x01@! clan tried the same tack with me, but I have taken a vow to all the gods to speak the truth wherever I find it. And the truth is that you are fools.”
column2: 她轻蔑地大笑。“ \x01@! 氏族的蠢货们对我用过同样的招数，但我已向所有神明起誓，无论在哪里发现真相都要说出来。而真相就是，你们都是蠢货。”

column1: Although it was expected that her supporters among the people would rail against this decision, no one would speak on her behalf.
column2: 虽然人们预料她的人民中的支持者会强烈反对这个决定，但没有人愿意为她说话。

column1: She told us that we were pus-filled boils on the backside of Dragon Pass, and that her red-hot honesty was the only available lance.
column2: 她告诉我们，我们是龙隘臀部的脓包，而她灼热的诚实是唯一的刺刀。

column1: Shuffle the ring a bit.
column2: 对长老会稍作调整。

column1: \x01@\x03 generously offered to resign from the ring, saying that another could take \x04 place.
column2: \x01@\x03 慷慨地提出要从长老会辞职，说别人可以取代 \x04 的位置。

column1: \x01Bs seemed surprised, but said, “One measly ring member is probably not enough to make a difference, and any replacement is likely to be as idiotic as \x01@\x03. But I am a fair woman, and will give \x08 a chance.”
column2: \x01Bs 似乎很惊讶，但说：“区区一个长老会成员大概不足以改变什么，而且任何替代者都可能跟 \x01@\x03一样愚蠢。但我是个公平的女人，会给 \x08 一个机会。”

column1: Try to marry her off to yet another clan.
column2: 试图把她嫁给另一个氏族。

column1: But \x01Bs would not hear of marrying him. “He looks like even more of a slack-jawed cretin than the last husband you tried to foist upon me,” she said. “And the clan you seek to marry me reeks of lawlessness and the love of Chaos.” The members of the \x01@! ring were most affronted by her words.
column2: 但 \x01Bs 根本不愿嫁给他。“他看起来比你们之前硬塞给我的那个丈夫更像一个嘴歪眼斜的傻瓜，”她说，“而你们想把我嫁过去的那个氏族，散发着一股无法无天和爱慕混沌的臭气。” \x01@! 长老会的成员们被她的言辞深深冒犯了。

column1: After much cajoling, she finally admitted to the fine qualities of the groom and his clan.
column2: 经过一番哄劝，她终于承认了新郎及其氏族的优秀品质。

column1: The people of clan \x01@! had heard of the trouble \x01Bs caused in the last clan she married into. They said that they would sooner marry their menfolk to scorpions than to her.
column2: 氏族 \x01@! 的人们听说了 \x01Bs 在她上一个嫁入的氏族惹出的麻烦。他们说，他们宁可把自己的男人们嫁给蝎子，也不愿娶她。

column1: She is the victim of some tragic curse.
column2: 她是某个悲剧诅咒的受害者。

column1: The weaponthanes are glad to have her back.
column2: 武器领主们很高兴她回来了。

column1: She claims support among the weaponthanes, but they do not seem overjoyed to see her back.
column2: 她声称得到武器领主们的支持，但他们似乎并不因为她的归来而欣喜若狂。

column1: She claims support among the weaponthanes, but they would be happy never to lay eyes upon her again.
column2: 她声称得到武器领主们的支持，但他们宁愿再也不用看到她。

column1: She shows disrespect for chosen leaders, and our previous efforts to deal with her have failed. None can blame us for outlawing her.
column2: 她表现出对当选领袖的不敬，我们之前处理她的努力都失败了。没有人能因为我们放逐她而指责我们。

column1: The carls are glad to welcome her back, as they are happy to see the green return during Sea season.
column2: 自由民们很高兴欢迎她回来，就像他们乐于在海季看到绿意回归一样。

column1: Those who say the carls are glad to see her do not know the carls well.
column2: 那些说自由民们很高兴见到她的人，并不了解自由民。

column1: Tragic King Errarth failed to outlaw his nephew, Jotarth, and Jotarth made war on him.
column2: 悲剧王埃拉思未能放逐他的侄子乔塔思，而乔塔思对他发动了战争。

column1: I hope this causes a war, somehow.
column2: 我希望这能引发一场战争，不知怎的。

column1: I told you she’d be back.
column2: 我告诉过你们她会回来的。

column1: Maybe she’s right about us. Maybe we are all fools.
column2: 也许她对我们说的没错。也许我们都是蠢货。

column1: sceneR212
column2: sceneR212

column1: Jerensta, an explorer of the \x01@! clan, reports a strange sight she saw while searching the Quivin Mountains for treasure. “I saw a man and a woman, frozen into the ice. They held one another as lovers, with expressions so sad I do not think I shall ever recover from looking upon their faces. The man wore the insignia of your clan, so I felt obligated to bring you this news. The woman bore \x01@a insignia.”
column2: \x01@! 氏族的探索者杰伦斯塔报告了她在奎文山脉搜寻宝藏时看到的一幅奇异景象。“我看到一男一女，冻结在冰中。他们如恋人般相拥，表情如此悲伤，我觉得我永远无法从看到他们的面容中恢复过来。那男人佩戴着你们氏族的徽记，所以我觉得有责任把这条消息带给你们。那女人佩戴着 \x01@a 的徽记。”

column1: An explorer from another clan said that she had seen a man and a woman frozen in the ice high up in the Quivini Mountains, and that the man wore our clan insignia.
column2: 另一个氏族的探索者说，她在奎维尼山脉高处的冰中看到一男一女，那男人佩戴着我们氏族的徽记。

column1: We took no further action.
column2: 我们没有采取进一步行动。

column1: Reward her for the information.
column2: 酬谢她提供的信息。

column1: We rewarded the explorer for her information.
column2: 我们酬谢了那个探索者提供的信息。

column1: What do you give her?
column2: 你给她什么？

column1: Although she did not say so, she seemed to expect more than we gave her.
column2: 虽然她没有明说，但她似乎期望的比我们给的多。

column1: She thanked us for our consideration.
column2: 她感谢我们的关照。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods in their memory.
column2: 向诸神献祭以纪念他们。

column1: We sacrificed to the gods in their memory.
column2: 我们向诸神献祭以纪念他们。

column1: The god-talkers said that they heard the bold, ringing voice of Orlkensor, and the sorrow-wracked voice of Valensta, echoing in the woods not long after our sacrifice was made.
column2: 神言者说，在我们献祭后不久，他们听到奥肯索尔那雄浑洪亮的声音，以及瓦伦斯塔那充满悲伤的声音，在树林中回荡。

column1: The god-talkers waited for a sign that the gods would honor Orlkensor and Valensta, but saw none.
column2: 神言者等待着神会尊荣奥肯索尔和瓦伦斯塔的征兆，但什么也没看到。

column1: Send a mission to pay last respects.
column2: 派遣一个使团去致以最后的敬意。

column1: We sent a mission to pay last respects.
column2: 我们派遣了一个使团去致以最后的敬意。

column1: We found the spot the explorer told us about. The bodies belonged to the former outlaw Orlkensor and Valensta, the woman who claimed that she loved him only as a friend. We let the ice on the mountain’s bosom be their grave.
column2: 我们找到了探索者所说的地点。尸体属于前逃犯奥肯索和瓦伦斯塔——那个自称只把他当朋友的女人。我们让山峦怀抱的冰雪成为他们的坟墓。

column1: We could not find the spot the explorer told us about.
column2: 我们未能找到探索者所说的地点。

column1: Send a mission to recover the bodies.
column2: 派出队伍回收尸体。

column1: We sent a mission to recover the bodies.
column2: 我们派出了队伍回收尸体。

column1: We found the spot the explorer told us about. The bodies belonged to the former outlaw Orlkensor and Valensta, the woman who claimed that she loved him only as a friend.
column2: 我们找到了探索者所说的地点。尸体属于前逃犯奥肯索和瓦伦斯塔——那个自称只把他当朋友的女人。

column1: There were not enough of us to hack through the ice. We had to leave the two tragic lovers frozen to the mountain’s bosom.
column2: 我们人手不足，无法凿开冰层。只得让这对悲惨的恋人永远冻结在山峦的怀抱中。

column1: It is not a good time for a sacrifice.
column2: 现在不是献祭的好时机。

column1: We should sacrifice to the gods, and reward Jerensta well.
column2: 我们应向众神献祭，并好好酬赏杰伦斯塔。

column1: Jerensta expects no return for her efforts on our behalf.
column2: 杰伦斯塔为我们出力，不图回报。

column1: It would be offensive not to give Jerensta at least ten cows. Then we can proceed.
column2: 不给杰伦斯塔至少十头牛会很失礼。然后我们再继续行事。

column1: First we must thank Jerensta with at least five cows for her news.
column2: 首先，我们必须用至少五头牛来感谢杰伦斯塔带来的消息。

column1: Warriors who brave the Quivini Mountains will surely be eaten by frost demons.
column2: 胆敢闯入奎维尼山脉的勇士，定会被冰霜恶鬼吞噬。

column1: The warriors loved Orlkensor, and wish to honor his memory.
column2: 战士们深爱着奥肯索，希望能纪念他。

column1: It is not a good time to risk lives with a dangerous expedition.
column2: 现在不是用危险的远征去冒险的好时机。

column1: The warriors loved Orlkensor, and are ready to take reasonable risks to honor his memory.
column2: 战士们深爱着奥肯索，愿意冒合理的风险来纪念他。

column1: Orlkensor was a good and gentle man.
column2: 奥肯索是个善良温和的人。

column1: Orlkensor was an honorable warrior who respected the truth.
column2: 奥肯索是个尊崇真理、可敬的战士。

column1: Orlkensor was outlawed for no good reason. He respected the law.
column2: 奥肯索被放逐毫无缘由。他尊重律法。

column1: Even the good must die, as Eurmal taught Grandfather Mortal.
column2: 正如尤尔马尔教导凡人祖父的那样，就连善人亦难免一死。

column1: Does no one care that Orlkensor was likely an adulterer?
column2: 难道没人介意奥肯索很可能是奸夫吗？

column1: I am sure that Orlkensor and Valensta did nothing dishonorable while her husband lived.
column2: 我确信，在瓦伦斯塔的丈夫在世时，奥肯索与她并未做过任何可耻之事。

column1: sceneR213
column2: sceneR213

column1: A squabble has broken out between factions in the clan. One group, calling itself the First People, claims descent from the founders of the tribe. The others claim descent from the Nalda Bin, the remnant people
column2: 氏族内派系间爆发了争执。一方自称“先民”，声称是部落创始者的后裔。另一方则自称是纳尔达·宾的后裔——那个被遗民的族群，

column1: the founders adopted before the dawn of time, back in the Storm Age.
column2: 创始者在黎明时代之前、风暴时代就已收养的遗民。

column1: the founders took as thralls before the dawn of time, back in the Storm Age. Of course, their long-ago children were born as free members of the clan, and so the two peoples became one.
column2: 创始者在黎明时代之前、风暴时代就掳为奴隶的族群。当然，他们很久以前的子女出生时已是氏族的自由成员，因此两族融为了一体。

column1: But the Nalda Bin say that their ancestors get fewer sacrifices than the ancestors of the founders. Further, they say that the First People get the best grazing lands and the healthiest animals.
column2: 但纳尔达·宾声称，他们的祖先获得的献祭少于创始者们的祖先。他们还称先民占据了最好的牧场和最健壮的牲畜。

column1: A squabble broke out between those who claimed descent from the founders of the tribe, and those whose ancestors were the remnant people adopted into the tribe during the Storm Age.
column2: 争执在自称部落创始者后裔的人，与祖先是在风暴时代被收养入族的遗民之间爆发了。

column1: Let tempers cool on their own.
column2: 让怒气自行平息。

column1: We decided to let tempers cool on their own.
column2: 我们决定让怒气自行平息。

column1: The squabbling stopped.
column2: 争执停止了。

column1: Redistribute land and herds to favor the Nalda Bin.
column2: 重新分配土地和畜群，以偏袒纳尔达·宾。

column1: We redressed the grievances of the remnant people.
column2: 我们纠正了遗民的不满。

column1: This displeased the descendants of the clan founders.
column2: 这触怒了氏族创始者的后裔。

column1: Sacrifice to the ancestors of the Nalda Bin.
column2: 向纳尔达·宾的祖先献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to the ancestors of the Nalda Bin.
column2: 我们向纳尔达·宾的祖先献祭。

column1: The god-talkers said that the ancestors of the Nalda Bin had smiled on us.
column2: 神言者说，纳尔达·宾的祖先向我们微笑了。

column1: The god-talkers said that the Nalda Bin ancestors continued their slumber, unaware of the homage we paid them.
column2: 神言者说，纳尔达·宾的祖先仍在沉睡，对我们的敬奉毫不知情。

column1: Scold the people for dividing into factions.
column2: 训斥民众，不该分裂成派系。

column1: We scolded the people for dividing into factions.
column2: 我们训斥了民众，不该分裂成派系。

column1: Both sides praised us for our strong words. “We have forgotten that our first loyalty is to the clan, and that we prosper together or suffer together.” They pledged to forget their old jealousies and work together.
column2: 双方都称赞我们的严厉言辞。“我们忘了，首要忠诚应归于氏族，要么一起繁荣，要么一起受苦。”他们发誓抛却旧怨，协力同心。

column1: Each side was offended that we had not reserved our hottest words for the other.
column2: 双方都因我们没有把最激烈的话留给对方而恼怒。

column1: Tell the Nalda Bin that the First People are entitled to preferential treatment.
column2: 告诉纳尔达·宾，先民有权享有优待。

column1: We told the Nalda Bin that the First People were entitled to preferential treatment.
column2: 我们告诉纳尔达·宾，先民有权享有优待。

column1: The Nalda Bin were forced to concede that our interpretation of clan traditions was correct.
column2: 纳尔达·宾被迫承认我们对氏族传统的解读是正确的。

column1: The Nalda Bin refused to concede that our interpretation of clan traditions was correct.
column2: 纳尔达·宾拒绝承认我们对氏族传统的解读是正确的。

column1: Of course the First People get the best cows and the lushest pastures.
column2: 当然先民得到最好的牛和最茂盛的牧场。

column1: If there is a preference for the First People, it is just coincidence.
column2: 如果说先民受到偏爱，那也纯属巧合。

column1: Unless the First People are given what they want, our clan will split in two!
column2: 除非先民得到他们想要的，否则我们的氏族就要一分为二！

column1: Unless the Nalda Bin are given what they want, our clan will split in two!
column2: 除非纳尔达·宾得到他们想要的，否则我们的氏族就要一分为二！

column1: This is less about bloodlines than about poor morale in general.
column2: 这与其说是血统问题，不如说是普遍的士气低落。

column1: This has more to do with general respect than with specific complaints.
column2: 这更多关乎普遍的尊重，而非具体的抱怨。

column1: If we want to see this pointless bickering go on and on, just redistribute things. Pretty soon everyone will be counting the squeals of the pig litters, and arguing over that.
column2: 如果想看到这场无谓的争吵无休无止，那就重新分配吧。很快每个人都会数猪仔的叫声，并为此争吵不休。

column1: If we want to keep this quarrel going, remind the Nalda Bin that they are second-best.
column2: 如果想维持这场争吵，就提醒纳尔达·宾他们是二等公民。

column1: There are times when a good scolding improves discipline.
column2: 有时候，一顿好训能改善纪律。

column1: Shame them all, and shame them equally.
column2: 让他们都蒙羞，而且要一视同仁。

column1: The Nalda Bin were taken into the clan as thralls.
column2: 纳尔达·宾是作为奴隶被接纳进氏族的。

column1: The Nalda Bin were taken into the clan as equals.
column2: 纳尔达·宾是作为平等者被接纳进氏族的。

column1: The Nalda Bin were taken into the clan as equals. We must treat their descendants as such.
column2: 纳尔达·宾是以平等身份被纳入氏族的。我们必须同样对待他们的后代。

column1: The Nalda Bin were taken into the clan as thralls. The First People have always been entitled to preferential treatment.
column2: 纳尔达·宾是作为奴隶被纳入氏族的。先民始终有权享有优待。

column1: Of course we must respect everyone’s ancient ancestors.
column2: 当然，我们必须尊重所有人的远古祖先。

column1: Of course we must respect everyone’s ancient ancestors. But we need not respect their descendants, who are engaging in pointless quibbling.
column2: 当然，我们必须尊重所有人的远古祖先。但不必尊重他们的后代，这些人正纠缠于无谓的争论。

column1: Some problems are best solved through neglect.
column2: 有些问题最好置之不理。

column1: When the people are foolish, a reprimand is in order.
column2: 当民众愚昧时，理应予以训斥。

column1: Sacrifice will benefit all.
column2: 献祭将惠及众人。

column1: It has been a long time since we called upon the spirits of the early thralls. They may not hear our prayers.
column2: 我们很久没有召唤早期奴隶的魂灵了。他们可能听不到我们的祈祷。

column1: A sacrifice will act as a balm to sore tempers.
column2: 献祭可抚慰愤怒的情绪。

column1: A sacrifice will \x02\x03soften the hearts/cool the fever/ease the worries\x02 of the Nalda Bin, and they will stop \x02\x03inflaming/provoking/inciting\x02 the First People, and this quarrel will \x02\x03blow away on the breeze/fade away/dampen down and die out\x02.
column2: 献祭将 \x02\x03软化内心/降温退热/缓解忧虑\x02 纳尔达·宾的心，他们便会停止 \x02\x03激怒/挑衅/煽动\x02 先民，这场争执将 \x02\x03随风消散/渐渐平息/降温熄灭\x02。

column1: The Nalda Bin \x02\x03started/came to us/joined us\x02 as our thralls. But the children of thralls are full members of the clan.
column2: 纳尔达·宾 \x02\x03起初是/来投靠/加入我们\x02 作为我们的奴隶。但奴隶的子女已是氏族的正式成员。

column1: The Storm Age was a time before time, when \x02\x03the existing clans were sundered/all the clans fell apart/many old clans were smashed\x02, and new ones arose from their ruins.
column2: 风暴时代是时间之前的时间，那时 \x02\x03现有的氏族被分裂/所有氏族分崩离析/许多古老氏族被粉碎\x02，新的氏族从废墟中崛起。

column1: People should rely on themselves, not on spirits who have been dead since before time began.
column2: 人应当依靠自己，而非那些在时间开始前就已死去的魂灵。

column1: It is good to see the women, who married into these bloodlines, fighting as if they were born into them. It means their marriages are strong.
column2: 看到嫁入这些血脉的女子像生来就在其中一般奋力战斗，是件好事。这意味着她们的婚姻牢固。

column1: Favor the meek and downtrodden.
column2: 眷顾温顺与被践踏者。

column1: Bloodlines may have been mixed up over the last thirteen hundred years.
column2: 过去一千三百年里，血脉可能早已混杂。

column1: Bloodlines have surely been mixed up over the centuries. Remind them that we are one clan, now.
column2: 千百年来，血脉必然已经混杂。提醒他们，我们现在是一个氏族。

column1: Why are the women fighting over the men’s ancestors? It is stupid.
column2: 女人们为何要为了男人的祖先争斗？这很愚蠢。

column1: sceneR214
column2: sceneR214

column1: A band of wandering musicians requests permission to play at your clan market. Their representative is a beastman who introduces himself as Hairball, and speaks Tradetalk as well as it can be spoken. “My master, Bundalini, promises an exciting and remarkable performance, one that will bring other clans from all over Dragon Pass. You will prosper from all of the trade opportunities, and our fee for playing is a very reasonable ten cows. An opportunity to hear Bundalini’s All-Skeleton band comes only once in a generation!” In addition to Bundalini the giant, the party includes two minotaurs and a host of walking skeletons.
column2: 一伙流浪乐师请求在你族集市演奏。他们的代表是个自称海波尔的兽人，能说一口流利的贸易语。“我家主人邦达利尼保证献上一场激动人心的精彩表演，会引来龙隘各地其他氏族。你们将因所有贸易机会而繁荣，我们的演奏费用仅为十头牛，十分合理。聆听邦达利尼全骷髅乐队的机会，一代人只有一次！”除了巨人邦达利尼，队伍还包括两名牛头人和一群行走骷髅。

column1: A band of very strange musicians asked for permission to play at our clan market.
column2: 一伙非常古怪的乐师请求在我们氏族集市演奏。

column1: Accept the offer.
column2: 接受提议。

column1: We accepted the offer.
column2: 我们接受了提议。

column1: Decline the offer.
column2: 拒绝提议。

column1: We declined the offer.
column2: 我们拒绝了提议。

column1: Hairball sighed, but left without further argument.
column2: 海波尔叹了口气，但没再争辩便离开了。

column1: The minotaurs offered stout resistance while Hairball and Bundalini retreated. No one was harmed on either side.
column2: 牛头人们奋力抵抗，而海波尔和邦达利尼撤走了。双方均无人受伤。

column1: Suggest another clan they might ask.
column2: 建议他们去询问另一个氏族。

column1: Agree to attend.
column2: 同意出席。

column1: Decline the invitation
column2: 拒绝邀请。

column1: Tell them to come back later.
column2: 告诉他们稍后再来。

column1: We told them to come back later.
column2: 我们告诉他们稍后再来。

column1: They left, the sound of the giant’s bass drum slowly fading in the distance.
column2: 他们离开了，巨人低音鼓的声音渐渐消失在远方。

column1: They’re too expensive; send them on their way.
column2: 他们太贵了；打发他们走。

column1: The carls could use a diversion from their life of toil.
column2: 自由民需要一些消遣来摆脱劳苦生活。

column1: There’s something sinister about these strange musicians…
column2: 这些古怪乐师身上有股邪气……

column1: We could gain great trade opportunities by hosting their concert.
column2: 主办他们的音乐会可带来巨大贸易机会。

column1: If we try to fight them, they will slay us all.
column2: 如果我们试图与他们战斗，他们就会杀光我们所有人。

column1: Our warriors could use some rollicking music to bring them cheer.
column2: 我们的战士需要一些欢快的音乐来振奋精神。

column1: Let’s not risk it.
column2: 我们还是别冒险了。

column1: They are not Orlanthi, so we must drive them off.
column2: 他们不是奥兰斯人，所以我们必须赶走他们。

column1: They are not Orlanthi, so they cannot be trusted to behave properly.
column2: 他们不是奥兰斯人，无法信任他们会举止得体。

column1: Although they are not Orlanthi, this Hairball creature knows the correct greetings. Perhaps, if we allow them to play for us, they will behave properly.
column2: 虽然他们不是奥兰斯人，但这个叫海波尔的家伙懂得正确的问候礼。也许，如果我们允许他们为我们演奏，他们会举止得体。

column1: When in doubt, delay.
column2: 心存疑虑时，就拖延。

column1: Another clan might thank us for sending this band to them.
column2: 其他氏族可能会感谢我们把这支乐队送去。

column1: Another clan might thank us for sending this band to them, so long as we choose a clan that trusts us.
column2: 只要我们选择一个信任我们的氏族，其他氏族可能会感谢我们把这支乐队送去。

column1: Bad King Urgrain whipped a poet, and that poet wrote the sagas that preserve his name in infamy.
column2: 恶王乌格兰鞭打了一位诗人，而那位诗人写下了传说，让他的名字遗臭万年。

column1: A worse blasphemy I cannot conceive of!
column2: 我想不出还有比这更重的亵渎了！

column1: I cannot wait to hear them play!
column2: 我等不及听他们演奏了！

column1: By Orlanth’s smiting klanth, I can’t believe that we are even considering a request made by undead monsters!
column2: 以奥兰斯惩戒之杖起誓，我简直不敢相信我们竟在考虑不死怪物提出的请求！

column1: They are but tootlers and thumpers. They cannot hope to compete with my own full-throated singing.
column2: 他们不过是些吹吹打打的家伙。休想与我本人的引吭高歌相比。

column1: We mustn’t let the expenditure of a mere ten cows keep us from enjoying a wondrous entertainment!
column2: 我们绝不能让区区十头牛的花费阻止我们享受一场奇妙的娱乐！

column1: If others come from miles around, the eligible young men of Dragon Pass will see our fair and marriageable maidens.
column2: 如果其他人从方圆数里赶来，龙隘的未婚青年就会看到我们美丽且适婚的少女。

column1: Other clans will think we’re crazy if we host this freakish event.
column2: 要是我们主办这场怪诞活动，其他氏族会觉得我们疯了。

column1: sceneR215
column2: sceneR215

column1: Bundalini and His All-Skeleton Band play at your clan market, and the booming sound of the giant’s drum attracts the curious from all of Dragon Pass. A festival atmosphere ensues, and people from many clans come to trade, to talk, to swap gossip, and to forget old slights.
column2: 邦达利尼和他的全骷髅乐队在你们的氏族市场上表演，巨人鼓声的轰鸣吸引了龙之隘口各地的好奇者。节日气氛随之而来，来自许多氏族的人们前来交易、交谈、交换流言，并忘却旧日嫌隙。

column1: Bundalini’s All-Skeleton Band played, and people came from all over.
column2: 邦达利尼的全骷髅乐队演奏了，人们从四面八方赶来。

column1: Challenge members of other clans to tests of skill and strength.
column2: 挑战其他氏族成员，较量技艺与力量。

column1: We challenged members of other clans to tests of skill and strength.
column2: 我们挑战了其他氏族成员，较量技艺与力量。

column1: We won the most contests, and the others celebrated our prowess.
column2: 我们赢得了大部分比试，其他人颂扬我们的勇武。

column1: Encourage your people to enjoy the event.
column2: 鼓励你的人民享受这场盛会。

column1: We did nothing but enjoy the event.
column2: 我们除了享受盛会，什么也没做。

column1: The people were happy.
column2: 人们很高兴。

column1: Forge new trade arrangements.
column2: 缔结新的贸易协议。

column1: We decided to forge new trade arrangements.
column2: 我们决定缔结新的贸易协议。

column1: We made some good deals, which promised to pay off in the next few seasons.
column2: 我们达成了一些不错的交易，有望在未来几个季节获得回报。

column1: We did not make the deals we wanted to make.
column2: 我们没有达成想要的交易。

column1: Who do you gift?
column2: 你赠予谁礼物？

column1: What do you give to the other clans?
column2: 你送给其他氏族什么？

column1: They celebrated our generosity.
column2: 他们赞颂我们的慷慨。

column1: Seek advantageous marriages.
column2: 寻求有利的联姻。

column1: We sought advantageous marriages.
column2: 我们寻求了有利的联姻。

column1: We did not arrange any.
column2: 我们未能促成任何联姻。

column1: See if others want to start a tribe.
column2: 看看是否有人想组建一个部落。

column1: We tested other leaders to see if they wanted to make a tribe.
column2: 我们试探了其他领袖，看他们是否想组建一个部落。

column1: The time seemed to be right for tribemaking.
column2: 组建部落的时机似乎已经成熟。

column1: We agreed to begin negotiating with the other clans in a few short weeks.
column2: 我们同意在短短几周内开始与其他氏族谈判。

column1: The time did not seem right for tribemaking.
column2: 组建部落的时机似乎尚未成熟。

column1: Now is not the time for gifts.
column2: 现在不是送礼的时候。

column1: It is a good time to prove our generosity.
column2: 现在是证明我们慷慨的好时机。

column1: People want to have a good time. Now is not the time for trade.
column2: 人们想好好乐一乐。现在不是做买卖的时候。

column1: This is a good time to seek new trade arrangements.
column2: 现在是寻求新贸易协议的好时机。

column1: Our warriors wish to prove their abilities.
column2: 我们的战士渴望证明自己的能力。

column1: The warriors are dispirited. We should carouse with them, and forget other cares.
column2: 战士们士气低落。我们应该和他们一起畅饮狂欢，忘却其他烦恼。

column1: It is a good time to seek advantageous marriages.
column2: 现在是寻求有利联姻的好时机。

column1: In this festive atmosphere, we can seek to improve our position without incurring the spite of others.
column2: 在这节日氛围中，我们可以在不招致他人怨恨的情况下提升自己的地位。

column1: If we lose contests of skill and strength, our clan magic will weaken.
column2: 如果我们输掉技艺与力量的比试，我们的氏族魔法会削弱。

column1: Winning contests of skill and strength will strengthen our clan magic.
column2: 赢得技艺与力量的比试将增强我们的氏族魔法。

column1: Seek better deals when we trade our grain.
column2: 在交易我们的谷物时争取更好的价格。

column1: The carls are unhappy. We should celebrate with them, so that they know they are more important than other clans.
column2: 自由民们不高兴。我们应该和他们一起庆祝，让他们知道他们比其他氏族更重要。

column1: During Tragic King Errarth’s last days, as the poison seeped through his body, music was the only pleasure that could ease his fevered mind.
column2: 在悲剧王埃拉思的最后日子里，当毒液渗透他的身体时，音乐是唯一能缓解他狂躁思绪的快乐。

column1: Don’t talk to me unless you’re here to tell me I can kill them all.
column2: 除非你来告诉我可以杀光他们，否则别跟我说话。

column1: So many choices … I don’t — trade, on one hand, and then challenges, they’d be fun, but… generosity, that’s a … what do the rest of you think?
column2: 这么多选择……我不——贸易，一方面，然后挑战，那会很有趣，但是……慷慨，那是……你们其他人怎么看？

column1: With the protection of a tribe, the temples will be safer.
column2: 有了部落的保护，神庙会更安全。

column1: This peaceful and happy time offers us a good chance to sound out other leaders, and see if it is a good time to make a tribe.
column2: 这段和平快乐的时光给了我们试探其他领袖的好机会，看看是不是组建部落的好时机。

column1: Challenges! Yes!
column2: 挑战！没错！

column1: You’ve all gone mad. Mad!
column2: 你们都疯了。疯了！

column1: sceneR216
column2: sceneR216

column1: A delegation from a clan far to the south, in the Holy Country, comes to seek your friendship. Their clan is called the Lead Breaker clan. “We have a magical treasure that we wish to give to you for safe-keeping. It is called the Iron Spike. In exchange for this service, we give you a tapestry and a silver necklace. When we come to reclaim the Spike, we will give you more silver and an even more valuable tapestry.”
column2: 一个来自遥远南方圣国的氏族代表团前来寻求你们的友谊。他们的氏族叫做破铅氏族。“我们有一件魔法宝物，想交给你们保管。它叫铁刺。作为这份托管的交换，我们给你们一张挂毯和一条银项链。等我们回来取回铁刺时，会给你们更多银子和更值钱的挂毯。”

column1: A delegation from the Holy Country came to give us gifts and ask us to commit a treasure of theirs for safe-keeping.
column2: 一个来自圣国的代表团前来赠送礼物，并请求我们保管他们的宝物。

column1: Agree to keep the spike for them.
column2: 同意为他们保管铁刺。

column1: We agreed to keep the treasure, which they called the Iron Spike.
column2: 我们同意保管那件他们称为铁刺的宝物。

column1: The Lead Breakers thanked us for our friendship. They promised to return for the Iron Spike soon, bringing the gifts due us.
column2: 破铅氏感谢我们的友谊。他们承诺很快会回来取走铁刺，并带来应给我们的礼物。

column1: Ask if they serve the Pharaoh.
column2: 询问他们是否为法老效力。

column1: We asked if they served the Pharaoh.
column2: 我们询问他们是否为法老效力。

column1: \x01@N took the other ring members aside and said, “I think they are not telling the truth.”
column2: \x01@N 把其他戒指成员拉到一边说：“我觉得他们没说实话。”

column1: We gave them hospitality. They said we were gracious hosts, and again asked us to keep the treasure for them.
column2: 我们款待了他们。他们称赞我们是好客的主人，再次请求我们为他们保管宝物。

column1: They praise you for your hospitality, and again press you to accept the treasure for safe-keeping.
column2: 他们称赞你的好客，再次恳求你接受宝物代为保管。

column1: Again we refused. They said they would seek out another clan for the great boon they had to offer.
column2: 我们再次拒绝了。他们说会去找另一个氏族，给予他们能提供的巨大恩惠。

column1: Give them reciprocal gifts.
column2: 回赠他们礼物。

column1: We gave them reciprocal gifts. They said we were gracious hosts, and again asked us to keep the treasure for them.
column2: 我们回赠了他们礼物。他们称赞我们是好客的主人，再次请求我们为他们保管宝物。

column1: We sent them on their way.
column2: 我们送他们上路了。

column1: They said it was sad that we could not be friends. They said they would seek out another clan for the great boon they had to offer.
column2: 他们说我们不能成为朋友真是太遗憾了。他们说会去找另一个氏族，给予他们能提供的巨大恩惠。

column1: Accept their gifts, and be done with it.
column2: 收下他们的礼物，就此了结。

column1: We must let them know that we can give gifts, too.
column2: 我们必须让他们知道，我们也能送礼。

column1: The gifts they give us are very valuable.
column2: 他们给我们的礼物非常贵重。

column1: The gifts they give us are very valuable. Imagine how great the reward will be if we do what they ask!
column2: 他们给我们的礼物非常贵重。想象一下，如果我们照他们说的做，回报会有多大！

column1: We are obligated to give them reciprocal gifts.
column2: 我们有义务回赠他们礼物。

column1: They were content to remain in the land we felt obligated to flee.
column2: 他们满足于留在我们觉得必须逃离的土地上。

column1: They were content to remain in the land we felt obligated to flee. We can assume they are well-disposed towards our enemy, the Pharaoh.
column2: 他们满足于留在我们觉得必须逃离的土地上。我们可以假定他们对我们敌人的法老怀有好感。

column1: An invasion from the Holy Country could come at any time.
column2: 圣国的入侵随时可能到来。

column1: We have little to fear from them.
column2: 我们无须惧怕他们。

column1: We have little to fear from them. It will be hard for them to mount an effective raid all the way from the Holy Country.
column2: 我们无须惧怕他们。他们要从圣国一路发动有效的袭击并不容易。

column1: It is always good to have allies.
column2: 有盟友总是好事。

column1: It is hard to say what good the Lead Breakers could do for us.
column2: 很难说破铅者能为我们带来什么好处。

column1: If we hold the treasure, we will benefit from its magic.
column2: 如果我们持有那件宝物，就能受益于它的魔力。

column1: They’re offering a magic weapon to use against our ancient enemies, the trolls! We must accept.
column2: 他们献出一件魔法武器，用来对付我们的宿敌——巨魔！我们必须接受。

column1: I have heard of this Iron Spike. It is a weapon to use against trolls.
column2: 我听说过这柄铁刺。它是用来对付巨魔的武器。

column1: We can take their treasure and then trade it away.
column2: 我们可以收下他们的宝物，然后转手交易掉。

column1: If they serve the Pharaoh, they serve a tyrant and a usurper!
column2: 如果他们侍奉法老，那他们就是在侍奉一个暴君和篡位者！

column1: If they serve the Pharaoh, do not ally with them. The other clans hate the Pharaoh, and will keep us from the throne.
column2: 如果他们侍奉法老，就不要与他们结盟。其他氏族憎恨法老，会阻挠我们登上王位。

column1: If we ally with the Lead Breakers, we could intermarry with them.
column2: 如果我们与破铅者结盟，就可以与他们通婚。

column1: They come offering peace. Let us toast them.
column2: 他们带来和平的提议。让我们向他们敬酒。

column1: They have given us gifts. It would be rude to refuse them.
column2: 他们赠予我们礼物。拒绝是无礼的。

column1: Let us take this treasure, and see what it does!
column2: 让我们收下这件宝物，看看它有什么作用！

column1: sceneR217
column2: sceneR217

column1: Allow Rangoron to try to steal the plow.
column2: 允许兰戈隆去偷那把犁。

column1: We allowed Rangoron to try to do so.
column2: 我们允许兰戈隆去尝试这样做。

column1: Rangoron crept into the tula of the \x01@% clan late at night, but was discovered. They plunged their swords into his back and thighs, but still he escaped. When word of his failure reached Ostlana’s mother Veoslina, she prevented any further contact between Rangoron and her daughter.
column2: 兰戈隆深夜潜入 \x01@% 氏族的图拉领地，却被发觉。他们刺穿了他的背部和双腿，但他还是逃脱了。失败的消息传到奥斯特拉娜的母亲维奥斯莉娜耳中后，她阻止了兰戈隆与她女儿的一切往来。

column1: Rangoron crept into the tula of the \x01@% clan late at night, and crept out with the plow. He presented it to Ostlana’s mother Veoslina, who then permitted the marriage.
column2: 兰戈隆深夜潜入 \x01@% 氏族的图拉领地，带着犁悄悄溜出。他将犁献给奥斯特拉娜的母亲维奥斯莉娜，她于是同意了婚事。

column1: Ask Ostlana’s ring to reconsider the terms of marriage.
column2: 请求奥斯特拉娜的议会重新考虑婚约条件。

column1: We asked the girl’s ring to reconsider the terms of marriage.
column2: 我们请求那姑娘的议会重新考虑婚约条件。

column1: Over the objections of Ostlana’s mother, who was a member of the \x01@a ring, it was decided that a normal bride price and dowry would suffice. The marriage would go ahead, with no thefts or feuds.
column2: 奥斯特拉娜的母亲是 \x01@a 议会的成员，尽管她反对，最终决定以普通的彩礼和嫁妆即可。婚事继续进行，无需盗窃或世仇。

column1: Ostlana’s mother was a member of the \x01@a ring, and they would not gainsay her.
column2: 奥斯特拉娜的母亲是 \x01@a 议会的成员，他们不会反驳她。

column1: Help Rangoron steal the plow.
column2: 协助兰戈隆偷犁。

column1: We decided to help Rangoron to steal the plow.
column2: 我们决定协助兰戈隆偷犁。

column1: How many warriors do you send with him?
column2: 你派多少武士随他同去？

column2: 帮手

column1: crept into the tula of the \x01@% clan late at night, and crept out with the plow. He presented it to Ostlana’s mother Veoslina, who then permitted the marriage.
column2: 深夜潜入 \x01@% 氏族的图拉领地，带着犁悄悄溜出。他将犁献给奥斯特拉娜的母亲维奥斯莉娜，她于是同意了婚事。

column1: They thanked us for the warning, and said they would bring their plow to bless our fields when planting time next came. Rangoron said that we had betrayed him, and told the other weaponthanes that we were not fit to rule.
column2: 他们感谢我们发出警告，并说待到下一个播种时节，他们将带着自己的犁来祝福我们的田地。兰戈隆说我们背叛了他，还告诉其他武器领主，说我们不配统治。

column1: Rangoron’s sword-mates said that they respected his impulsiveness, but not his judgment. The clan ring had done the right thing, they said.
column2: 兰戈隆的剑伴们说，他们尊重他的冲动，但不认可他的判断。他们说氏族议会做得对。

column1: Rangoron’s sword-mates heard his complaint with sympathetic ears. The clan ring had denied him his rights of valor, they said.
column2: 兰戈隆的剑伴们同情地倾听他的抱怨。他们说，氏族议会剥夺了他凭勇武应得的权利。

column1: “Rangoron, you must not court the daughter of a treacherous person.”
column2: “兰戈隆，你绝不能追求一个背信弃义之人的女儿。”

column1: We told Rangoron not to court the daughter of a treacherous person.
column2: 我们告诉兰戈隆不要追求一个背信弃义之人的女儿。

column1: Rangoron was disappointed, for he had formed a great attachment to the clever Ostlana. Despite that, he conceded that Ostlana’s kin were nothing but trouble, and that the match would end in sorrow.
column2: 兰戈隆很失望，因为他已对聪慧的奥斯特拉娜产生了深厚感情。尽管如此，他承认奥斯特拉娜的亲属只会带来麻烦，这门亲事终将酿成悲伤。

column1: Rangoron seemed to reluctantly agree to our command. But then he tried to steal the plow anyway.
column2: 兰戈隆似乎不情愿地服从了我们的命令。但之后他还是试图偷那把犁。

column1: Rangoron deserves a chance to test his valor.
column2: 兰戈隆值得一个证明自己勇武的机会。

column1: Rangoron is popular among the weaponthanes. They will be pleased if we help him win his clever bride.
column2: 兰戈隆在武器领主中很受欢迎。如果我们帮他赢得他聪慧的新娘，他们会很高兴。

column1: The plow will be well-guarded. Alone, Rangoron has less than half a chance of success.
column2: 那把犁守卫森严。兰戈隆独自成功的机会不到一半。

column1: Alone, he has little chance. But if we send just a single warrior to help him…
column2: 独自一人，他机会渺茫。但如果我们只派一名武士协助他……

column1: If Rangoron steals the plow, they will launch a claim against us at the moot.
column2: 如果兰戈隆偷了那把犁，他们会在议会上向我们提出索赔。

column1: If we refuse Rangoron, we risk dissension in the ranks.
column2: 如果我们拒绝兰戈隆，就会冒队伍内部分裂的风险。

column1: That so-called magic plow doesn’t even work.
column2: 那把所谓的魔法犁根本不起作用。

column1: Orlanth performed many great deeds to win the love of Ernalda.
column2: 奥兰斯为赢得厄娜尔达的爱，完成了许多伟大功业。

column1: Marriages should end wars, not start them.
column2: 婚姻应终结战争，而非引发战争。

column1: Who cares about a stupid plow, anyway?
column2: 谁在乎一把愚蠢的犁呢？

column1: What a great and romantic tale this shall make!
column2: 这将成为一个多么伟大而浪漫的故事啊！

column1: How would we like it if others stole our treasures?
column2: 如果别人偷了我们的宝物，我们作何感想？

column1: It’s not as if she’s asking him to raid a dragonewt lair.
column2: 她又没让他去袭击龙人巢穴。

column1: I refuse to abuse our ally’s trust.
column2: 我拒绝滥用盟友的信任。

column1: Dumb idea.
column2: 蠢主意。

column1: Cheating our allies is as bad as raiding them during the harvest.
column2: 欺骗盟友和在大丰收时袭击他们一样恶劣。

column1: They agreed that they had been at fault for allowing bad spirits to infest their wine. They paid the compensation we asked.
column2: 他们承认自己有过错，让恶灵侵染了他们的酒。他们支付了我们要求的赔偿。

column1: They said that there were no bad spirits in the wine when they traded it to us, and denied us compensation.
column2: 他们说把酒卖给我们时，酒里没有恶灵，并拒绝赔偿。

column1: Take it to the moot.
column2: 提交议会裁决。

column2: 我们倒掉了剩下的疯酒。

column2: 喝过酒的人尖叫着逃离地上的水坑。就连我们中没喝过酒的人，也觉得看到泥泞中有怪异的身影盘绕 \x01@\x12 随即踢开那些身影。

column1: Sacrifice to gods for protection from bad spirits.
column2: 向神明献祭，祈求免受恶灵侵害。

column1: We sacrificed to the gods for protection from bad spirits.
column2: 我们向神明献祭，祈求免受恶灵侵害。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were good. The gods would protect us against bad spirits.
column2: 神言者说征兆是好的。众神将庇佑我们免受恶灵侵害。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were confusing. Perhaps the gods had not heard our pleas.
column2: 神言者说征兆令人困惑。或许众神未曾听到我们的祈求。

column1: Send for shamans to exorcise bad spirits.
column2: 派人去请萨满驱除恶灵。

column1: We sent for shamans to exorcise bad spirits.
column2: 我们派人去请萨满驱除恶灵。

column1: No shamans came.
column2: 没有萨满前来。

column1: We found shamans willing to perform an exorcism.
column2: 我们找到了愿意施行驱魔仪式的萨满。

column2: 他们索要 \x01@\x1A 头牛作为报酬。你同意吗？

column1: We agreed to their price. They went off into the hills to perform ceremonies, and came back to tell us that the spirits were gone.
column2: 我们同意了他们的要价。他们前往山里举行仪式，然后回来告诉我们恶灵已去。

column1: We would not pay their price. They warned us that spirits were circling all around us, and meant us great harm.
column2: 我们不愿支付他们的要价。他们警告说，恶灵正盘绕在我们四周，将给我们带来大祸。

column1: We could not meet their price. They told us that we were practically guaranteed harm from the spirits circling all around us.
column2: 我们无法满足他们的要价。他们告诉我们，恶灵盘绕在我们四周，我们几乎必遭其害。

column1: Use trickster magic to send the spirits elsewhere.
column2: 使用诡术魔法将恶灵送往别处。

column1: We used trickster magic to send the spirits elsewhere.
column2: 我们使用诡术魔法将恶灵送往别处。

column1: “It is always hard to know how well trickster magic has worked,” \x01@\x14 said.
column2: “诡术魔法是否奏效，总是很难说清。” \x01@\x14 说道。

column1: You can never find a shaman when you need one.
column2: 需要萨满的时候永远找不到一个。

column2: 我能给我们找到一位萨满。

column2: 我们的损失折合 \x01@\x06 头牛。

column2: 我们的损失折合 \x01@\x07 头牛。

column1: Our damages equal \x01@\x08 cows.
column2: 我们的损失折合 \x01@\x08 头牛。

column1: Our damages equal \x01@\t cows.
column2: 我们的损失折合 \x01@\t 头牛。

column1: Forget compensation. We must do something about this spirit infestation.
column2: 忘了赔偿吧。我们必须处理这鬼灵作祟的事。

column1: Our own magic is strong. We need not rely on shamans.
column2: 我们自己的魔法足够强大。无需依赖萨满。

column1: Our own magic is weak. We should seek outside help.
column2: 我们自己的魔法太弱。应当寻求外部帮助。

column1: Our own magic is strong. We should sacrifice to the gods — but not Eurmal, who never solves a problem without causing more trouble.
column2: 我们自己的魔法足够强大。应当向众神献祭——但不包括尤尔马尔，他从不解决问题而不惹出更多麻烦。

column1: I can send the spirits elsewhere.
column2: 我能把恶灵送往别处。

column1: I tried some of that wine, and it didn’t affect me a bit. I’ll drink the rest, if you want.
column2: 我尝过那种酒，对我毫无影响。如果你们愿意，我把剩下的都喝了。

column1: Bad King Urgrain deliberately provoked the spirits of his ancestors, to prove he was a king among kings. He came to regret this.
column2: 恶王乌格兰故意挑衅他祖先的灵魂，以证明自己是万王之王。他后来为此追悔莫及。

column1: Bad spirits are harbingers of the undead!
column2: 恶灵是亡灵的先兆！

column1: It would be interesting to see trickster magic at work.
column2: 看看诡术魔法如何运作，倒是有趣。

column1: They refused to consider this, and said we were foul plant-lovers.
column2: 他们拒绝考虑此事，还说我们是肮脏的植物爱好者。

column1: We approached the elves, and told them that they were not entitled to take over a temple they had not built. We urged them to agree to our proposal.
column2: 我们找到精灵，告诉他们无权占据一座并非他们建造的圣殿。我们敦促他们接受我们的提议。

column1: The elves would not listen to reason, and departed dissatisfied, the matter unresolved.
column2: 精灵不听道理，不满地离开了，问题悬而未决。

column1: The elves agreed to limit their use of the temple, and both sides of the dispute said they were satisfied with its resolution.
column2: 精灵同意限制使用圣殿，争执双方均对解决方案表示满意。

column1: We did not involve ourselves in the matter.
column2: 我们没有介入此事。

column1: Find elves and tell them you support their demands.
column2: 找到精灵，告诉他们你支持他们的诉求。

column1: We sought out the elves and told them we supported their demands.
column2: 我们找到精灵，告诉他们我们支持他们的诉求。

column1: They thanked us for not interfering with their rights.
column2: 他们感谢我们没有干涉他们的权利。

column1: Offer the elves compensation instead of temple rights.
column2: 向精灵提供补偿，而非让出圣殿使用权。

column1: We sought out the elves and offered them compensation instead of temple rights.
column2: 我们找到精灵，向他们提供补偿，而非让出圣殿使用权。

column1: “Have what we need. Nothing we wish more than access to Flamal’s powers.”
column2: “给我们所需之物。我们只求能触及弗拉马尔的力量，别无他愿。”

column1: Send a war party to attack the petitioning elves.
column2: 派出战团攻击请愿的精灵。

column1: We sent a war party to find and kill elves.
column2: 我们派出战团去寻找并杀死精灵。

column1: Who leads the party?
column2: 由谁率领战团？

column1: The elves melted into the forest, and we hurt none of them. On the way back home, they ambushed us, as if they came from nowhere. Many were hurt, and \x01@\x05 was killed.
column2: 精灵遁入森林，我们未伤及任何一个。归途中，他们仿佛凭空出现般伏击了我们。许多人受伤， \x01@\x05 阵亡。

column1: There’s only one good thing to say about elves: they don’t steal cows.
column2: 关于精灵只有一点好处：他们不偷牛。

column1: When elves are involved, no conciliation is possible.
column2: 一旦牵扯到精灵，绝无和解可能。

column1: Conciliation is better than fighting.
column2: 和解胜过争斗。

column1: The elves are our friends. We can convince them to compromise.
column2: 精灵是我们的朋友。我们能说服他们让步。

column1: The elves hate us. We couldn’t convince them that the sky is blue.
column2: 精灵憎恨我们。就算说天是蓝的，他们也不会信。

column1: What threat can a bunch of walking plants offer us?
column2: 一群会走的植物能构成什么威胁？

column1: The elves are terrifying opponents. In their native forest, one band of elves can defeat an army of vicious trolls.
column2: 精灵是可怕的对手。在它们本族的森林里，一支精灵队伍就能击败一支凶残的巨魔大军。

column1: The elves are terrifying opponents. If we wish to fight them, the war party must be led by someone proficient at both combat and magic.
column2: 精灵是可怕的对手。若要与之作战，战团须由精通战斗与魔法的人统帅。

column1: We are not obligated to help.
column2: 我们没有义务帮忙。

column1: Our allies are right to come to us for help. We have some choices…
column2: 盟友来向我们求助是对的。我们有一些选择……

column1: We have no quarrel with the elves.
column2: 我们与精灵并无过节。

column1: The elves are our ancient enemies.
column2: 精灵是我们的宿敌。

column1: The elves are our ancient enemies. Our clan magic will suffer if we aid them.
column2: 精灵是我们的宿敌。若帮助他们，我们的氏族魔法将受损。

column1: Flamal, who was killed and then came back, loves elves more than us. If we harm the elves, our fertility could suffer.
column2: 弗拉马尔——曾死去又复生——爱精灵胜过爱我们。若伤害精灵，我们的丰饶可能受损。

column1: Flamal, who was killed and then came back, loves elves more than us. If we harm the elves, our fertility could suffer. If we raid during Sea season, our crops will suffer.
column2: 弗拉马尔死而复生，他爱精灵胜过爱我们。若我们伤害精灵，我们的丰饶便会受损。若我们在海季劫掠，我们的收成便会遭殃。

column1: Flamal, who was killed and then came back, loves elves more than us. If we harm the elves, our fertility could suffer. If we raid during Earth season, our crops will suffer.
column2: 弗拉马尔死而复生，他爱精灵胜过爱我们。若我们伤害精灵，我们的丰饶便会受损。若我们在地季劫掠，我们的收成便会遭殃。

column1: Flamal, who was killed and then came back, loves elves more than us. It is unlikely that he is paying attention to this dispute, though.
column2: 弗拉马尔死而复生，他爱精灵胜过爱我们。不过他不太可能在意这场争端。

column1: It is unlikely that Flamal is paying attention to this dispute. We must think of our crops, and avoid fighting during Sea season.
column2: 弗拉马尔不大可能在意这场争端。我们必须为收成着想，避免在海季作战。

column1: It is unlikely that Flamal is paying attention to this dispute. We must think of our crops, and avoid fighting during Earth season.
column2: 弗拉马尔不大可能在意这场争端。我们必须为收成着想，避免在地季作战。

column1: Flamal is the god of vegetation. Some say he was married to Ernalda before she married Orlanth.
column2: 弗拉马尔是植物之神。有人说他在厄纳尔达嫁给奥兰斯之前曾与她结为夫妻。

column1: Why can’t elves and humans worship Flamal together?
column2: 为何精灵与人类不能一同崇拜弗拉马尔？

column1: Flamal is a male fertility deity, unlike all of those weeping earth goddesses. We must honor him.
column2: 弗拉马尔是男性丰饶神，与那些哭泣的大地女神不同。我们必须尊崇他。

column1: Do we fear the brazen turnip-men? I say we do not!
column2: 我们难道害怕那些厚颜无耻的萝卜人吗？我说不！

column1: This is the moment we’ve been waiting for. The final reckoning. The time when the elves all die!
column2: 这是我们等待已久的时刻。最终的清算。精灵们尽数灭亡之时！

column1: Well, the weaponthanes of the \x01@a clan assembled a war party and drove the elves off.
column2: 嗯， \x01@a 氏族的武器领主们集结了一支战团，将精灵驱赶走了。

column1: Well, the elves suddenly dropped their demands and melted back into the woods. Just goes to show you can never tell what elves are going to do.
column2: 嗯，精灵们突然放弃了他们的要求，悄悄退回林中。这恰恰说明你永远无法预料精灵会做什么。

column1: Kill him.
column2: 杀了他。

column1: We said that we had killed him, and would not pay wergild.
column2: 我们说自己确实杀了他，但拒不支付血偿金。

column2: \x01A| 痛斥我们拒绝遵从正法。

column1: Pay wergild.
column2: 支付血偿金。

column2: 我们支付了血偿金。

column1: “We didn’t kill him.”
column2: “我们没有杀他。”

column1: We denied killing him.
column2: 我们否认杀了他。

column1: We let him go.
column2: 我们放他走了。

column1: The people grumbled that our generosity would be mistaken for soft-headedness.
column2: 人们抱怨说我们的慷慨会被误以为是软弱。

column1: We convinced them to pay more than the customary ransom.
column2: 我们说服他们支付了高于惯例的赎金。

column1: They convinced us to let them pay less than the customary ransom.
column2: 他们说服我们允许他们支付低于惯例的赎金。

column1: Take him as a thrall.
column2: 把他收为奴隶。

column1: We took him as a thrall.
column2: 我们把他收为奴隶。

column1: He was unhappy with his fate; we told him that thieves can expect to have things taken from them, including precious freedom.
column2: 他对自己的命运感到不满；我们告诉他，盗贼应当预料到自己也会失去东西，包括宝贵的自由。

column1: He was trying to steal our cows!
column2: 他当时正试图偷我们的牛！

column1: If we ransom him, we can turn theft into advantage.
column2: 若我们收取赎金，便可将偷窃化为好处。

column1: We cannot tolerate theft.
column2: 我们不能容忍偷窃。

column1: If we beat him and let him go to tell the tale, thieves will fear us, whether they are \x01@# thieves or outlaw bandits.
column2: 若是揍他一顿再放他出去传话，无论他们是 \x01@# 窃贼还是无法无天的匪徒，都会畏惧我们。

column1: He is an Orlanthi, so we cannot harm or enthrall him.
column2: 他是奥兰斯信徒，所以我们不能伤害或奴役他。

column1: He did not give the proper greetings, and I think that means we can do whatever we want.
column2: 他没有行恰当的问候礼，我认为这意味着我们可以为所欲为。

column1: He did not give the proper greetings, and clearly meant to take from us. We can dispose of him as we want.
column2: 他没有行恰当的问候礼，而且显然意图夺取我们的东西。我们可以随意处置他。

column1: A thrall is easy to take but hard to keep.
column2: 抓个奴隶容易，但看住难。

column1: One less \x01@! is one less enemy.
column2: 少一个 \x01@! 就少一个敌人。

column1: His clan is trouble and always has been.
column2: 他的氏族向来是麻烦。

column1: His clan is part of our tribe. If we deal harshly with him, they will wonder why they are in a tribe.
column2: 他的氏族是我们部落的一部分。若我们严厉处置他，他们会质疑自己为何要留在部落里。

column1: If, in emulation of our ancestors, we take him as a thrall, our clan magic will benefit.
column2: 若效仿先祖，将他收为奴隶，我们的氏族魔法将受益。

column1: If we flout the traditions of our ancestors and take him as a thrall, our clan magic will suffer.
column2: 若我们蔑视先祖的传统，将他收为奴隶，我们的氏族魔法将受损。

column1: He’s done no harm to us — we don’t need to harm him.
column2: 他没有伤害我们——我们不必伤害他。

column1: We don’t have to kill him. He’ll know better than to sneak around our steads again.
column2: 我们不必杀他。他以后会知道不该再在我们的农庄附近鬼鬼祟祟。

column1: The dew-treader came, making theft-thoughts.
column2: 那个踏露者来了，心里盘算着偷窃之念。

column1: We must show we are better than he is.
column2: 我们必须展示我们比他更高尚。

column1: This nose-dripping is not worth killing.
column2: 这个流鼻涕的家伙不值得杀。

column1: He is in league with the elves.
column2: 他与精灵勾结。

column1: Our allies will know he was trying to steal from us and pay ransom so that we don’t kill him.
column2: 我们的盟友将会得知他曾试图偷窃我们，并支付赎金以免被杀。

column1: “It is clear, then, that your entire clan sanctioned the murder of our priestess. You shall suffer for this. I swear it, and our rock swears it.”
column2: “那么显然，你们整个氏族都认可了杀害我们女祭司的行径。你们必将为此受难。我发誓，我们的岩石也发誓。”

column1: The signs were unclear.
column2: 征兆并不清晰。

column1: Convince them that their spirit is wrong.
column2: 说服他们，他们的岩石精灵出错了。

column1: We told them that their rock spirit was wrong.
column2: 我们告诉他们，他们的岩石精灵出错了。

column1: They were affronted at first, but gradually conceded that the spirits, even a spirit so great as their rock spirit, can sometimes be wrong. “We still think she did it,” they said, “but will seek further proof before demanding her death.”
column2: 他们起初感到冒犯，但逐渐承认，精灵（即使伟大如他们的岩石精灵）偶尔也会出错。“我们仍然认为她做了那事，”他们说，“但在要求处死她之前，会寻求更多证据。”

column1: \x01@( warriors slew her soon after she left the boundaries of our tula.
column2: \x01@( 勇士们在她离开我们图拉领地边界后不久便将她杀死。

column1: We can’t afford compensation.
column2: 我们付不起补偿。

column1: Compensate them and be done with it.
column2: 补偿他们，就此了结。

column1: It will be very hard to convince them that their spirit is wrong.
column2: 要说服他们相信他们的精灵出错了，会非常困难。

column1: They’re not so tough.
column2: 他们没那么强悍。

column1: They’re renowned for the martial powers their rock spirit grants them.
column2: 他们以岩石精灵赋予的战斗力量而著称。

column1: Orlanthi kill each other all the time. What’s the fuss?
column2: 奥兰西人整天自相残杀，有什么好大惊小怪的？

column1: We owe a wergild of twenty cows.
column2: 我们欠下二十头牛的血偿金。

column1: There’s a big difference between an honest killing and a secret murder. The former can be wiped clean by the payment of wergild, where the latter demands outlawry, and thus death, for the guilty.
column2: 光明正大的杀人跟暗地里行凶是大不相同的。前者可以靠支付血偿金抹干净，而后者则要求对凶手处以放逐，也就是死路一条。

column1: If we simply ask them to leave, it will push them closer to a feud with us.
column2: 如果我们只是请他们离开，只会把他们推得更近，可能跟我们结下世仇。

column1: Asking them to leave, or questioning the honesty of their spirit, will push them towards a feud with us.
column2: 要求他们离开，或者质疑他们精魂的诚实，都会促使他们与我们结下世仇。

column1: Their rock is very powerful.
column2: 他们的岩石非常强大。

column1: Our magic is strong. A divination will reveal all.
column2: 我们的魔法很强。一次占卜就能揭示一切。

column1: Our magic is weak. A divination will merely muddy the waters.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱。一次占卜只会把水搅浑。

column1: Our gods are infallible. This is not true of spirits, or those who interpret the signs they give.
column2: 我们的神从不犯错。但精魂不是这样，那些解读精魂给出征兆的人也不是这样。

column1: To think — a murderer in our midst!
column2: 想不到——我们中间竟有个杀人犯！

column1: Bad King Urgrain killed a spirit-talker who told him the shades were unhappy with his rule. Then he came down with the gout.
column2: 恶王乌格兰杀了一个精魂交谈者，那人告诉他，阴魂对他统治不满。然后他就得了痛风。

column1: It does not matter if she is innocent. We must outlaw her to make peace in the tribe.
column2: 她是否清白并不重要。我们必须放逐她，才能在部落中求得和平。

column1: We must outlaw her, or there will be no more marriages between our clans.
column2: 我们必须放逐她，否则我们氏族之间就再不会有通婚了。

column1: Priests and thanes from the \x01@! clan come to request the right to adopt Voballa, the young child of carls Vanartha and Robasart. “A document written during the First Age says that a great hero of the Knowing God will be born one day in Dragon Pass, and that she will have a mark upon her forehead, like so. This babe has the same mark upon its forehead. We ask that you allow us to raise the child, as we are uniquely qualified to initiate her into the secrets of Lhankor Mhy.”
column2: \x01@! 氏族的祭司和乡绅前来请求收养沃巴拉——自由民瓦纳撒和罗巴萨特的小女儿。“第一纪元时写的一份文书说，有一天会在龙之隘口诞生一位全知之神的伟大英雄，她额头上会有这样一个标记。这婴孩额头上就有同样的标记。我们请求允许我们抚养这孩子，因为我们具备独一无二的条件，可以引领她踏上兰科·米的秘仪之路。”

column1: Priests and thanes from the \x01@! clan come to request the right to adopt a baby, one they said would grow up to become a great hero of the Knowing God.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的祭司和乡绅前来请求收养一个婴儿，他们说这婴儿长大后会成为全知之神的伟大英雄。

column1: Allow the adoption.
column2: 允许收养。

column1: We granted their request.
column2: 我们同意了他们的请求。

column1: They were grateful, and said that all of Dragon Pass would one day be grateful to us, too.
column2: 他们很感激，并说有朝一日整个龙之隘口都会感激我们。

column1: Grant their request, in exchange for a gift of knowledge.
column2: 同意他们的请求，换取一份知识礼物。

column1: We granted their request, in exchange for a gift of knowledge.
column2: 我们同意了他们的请求，换取了一份知识礼物。

column1: They said they would be happy to tell us the tale of “\x01@\r” in return for the baby.
column2: 他们说很高兴用“\x01@\r”的故事来换这个婴儿。

column1: Grant their request, in exchange for a gift of magic.
column2: 同意他们的请求，换取一件魔法礼物。

column1: We granted their request, in exchange for a gift of magic.
column2: 我们同意了他们的请求，换取了一件魔法礼物。

column1: They said they would be happy to give us magic in return for the baby.
column2: 他们说很高兴用魔法来换这个婴儿。

column1: Grant their request, in exchange for an end to the feud between your clans.
column2: 同意他们的请求，换取你们氏族之间世仇的终结。

column1: We told them we would grant them their request in exchange for an end to the feud between us.
column2: 我们告诉他们，我们愿意同意他们的请求，以换取我们之间的世仇终结。

column1: “We would hate there to be any chance that Voballa could inadvertently be harmed in a feud.”
column2: “我们不想让沃巴拉在世仇中有丝毫可能被无意伤害。”

column1: They said the signs weren’t right for this.
column2: 他们说征兆不适合这么做。

column1: The \x01@! priests mumbled among themselves. The eldest sighed and said, “Much as we would wish to agree to this, the signs are not good for ending the feud in this way. Of course, we are still interested in the adoption.”
column2: \x01@! 祭司们低声相互议论。最年长的叹了口气说：“尽管我们很想同意这件事，但征兆不利于用这种方式结束世仇。当然，我们对收养仍然感兴趣。”

column1: Let them raise her, but not as a member of their clan.
column2: 让他们抚养她，但不能作为他们氏族的成员。

column1: We said they could raise her, but not as a member of their clan.
column2: 我们说他们可以抚养她，但不能作为他们氏族的成员。

column1: They said they would be happy to raise her. She would be not only a treasure to our clans, but to all of Dragon Pass.
column2: 他们说他们会很高兴抚养她。她不仅会成为我们氏族的珍宝，也会是整个龙之隘口的珍宝。

column1: Refuse their request.
column2: 拒绝他们的请求。

column1: We refused their request.
column2: 我们拒绝了他们的请求。

column1: The \x01@! priests said we lacked respect for the Knowing God, but the people were happy that we had not given Vanartha and Robasart’s child away.
column2: \x01@! 祭司们说我们缺乏对全知之神的尊敬，但族人们很高兴我们没有把瓦纳撒和罗巴萨特的孩子送走。

column1: Their prophecy was not woven by Kev. They are mistaken.
column2: 那个预言不是凯夫编织的。他们弄错了。

column1: If we grant their request, we might heal the feud between our clans.
column2: 如果我们同意他们的请求，或许能弥合我们氏族之间的世仇。

column1: If we grant their request, they will like us better.
column2: 如果我们同意他们的请求，他们会更喜欢我们。

column1: Helping them will foster harmony in the tribe.
column2: 帮助他们将促进部落的和谐。

column1: Helping them will foster harmony in the tribe. If we refuse, they they may rethink membership in the tribe.
column2: 帮助他们将促进部落的和谐。如果我们拒绝，他们可能会重新考虑是否留在部落内。

column1: Our enemies are humbling themselves by coming to us. This is a choice moment — we should make the best of it.
column2: 我们的敌人屈尊前来求我们。这是个关键时刻——我们应该好好利用。

column1: If we are going to consider our enemies’ unusual request, at least ask for magic, or a gift of knowledge. Don’t give anything away.
column2: 如果我们打算考虑敌人不寻常的请求，至少索要魔法或知识礼物。别白给。

column1: We should ask for magic, or a gift of knowledge.
column2: 我们应该索要魔法或知识礼物。

column1: Our magic is already strong. We should ask for knowledge that we can use when we heroquest.
column2: 我们的魔法已经很强。我们应该索要那些能在英雄探索时用到的知识。

column1: Our magic is weak; let us secure their blessings.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱，让我们确保他们的祝福。

column1: Vanartha and Robasart will be sad to lose their child, especially to the enemy camp.
column2: 瓦纳撒和罗巴萨特会因失去孩子而悲伤，尤其是孩子落入敌营。

column1: Vanartha and Robasart will be sad to lose their child, even to a heroic destiny.
column2: 瓦纳撒和罗巴萨特会因失去孩子而悲伤，哪怕是为了英雄的命运。

column1: Vanartha and Robasart will be sad to lose their child, but the carls will understand the importance of Voballa’s heroic destiny.
column2: 瓦纳撒和罗巴萨特会因失去孩子而悲伤，但自由民们能理解沃巴拉英雄命运的重要性。

column1: Vanartha and Robasart will be sad to lose their child, and the carls support them, heroic destiny or no heroic destiny.
column2: 瓦纳撒和罗巴萨特会因失去孩子而悲伤，而自由民们支持他们，不管有没有英雄命运。

column1: How can we even think of listening to our foes? Say the word and I will chop through them like a knife through paper!
column2: 我们怎能考虑聆听敌人之言？您一声令下，我就如刀切纸般将他们斩碎！

column1: What kind of hero sits around reading scrolls all day?
column2: 整天坐着读卷轴的算什么英雄？

column1: Of course we must grant this request.
column2: 我们当然必须答应这个请求。

column1: They have a document that says it. But can we trust them or their interpretation?
column2: 他们有文件这样写。但我们能相信他们或其解读吗？

column1: They have a document that says it. It must be so.
column2: 他们有文件这样写。那必然如此。

column1: This will end in sorrow for Voballa.
column2: 这对沃巴拉来说将以悲伤收场。

column1: Hey, if I’d known about this prophecy, I could have made them a baby with that mark a long time ago!
column2: 嘿，要是我早知道这个预言，我早就给他们造一个带那印记的娃娃了！

column1: If these book men got out more often, they’d know that distinctive markings aren’t always as distinctive as you think.
column2: 要是这些书呆子多出门走走，他们就会知道特征印记并不总像你以为的那么有特征。
