column1: Eonislara turned out to be pregnant. Her kinfolk were embarrassed.
column2: 结果欧尼斯拉拉怀孕了。她的族人很尴尬。

column1: Encourage Jorator to marry her.
column2: 鼓励乔拉托娶她。

column1: “Eonislara has a child by my blood?” Jorator exclaimed. “We must renew our betrothal. It will grow up to be a brave warrior, I am sure!” We were pleased by his response. But then Eonislara began to cry, “I cannot begin a marriage on a falsehood. The child is not Jorator’s, but springs from the loins of the poet Korol.” At first Jorator turned red and made as if to throw us out of his stead. Eonislara’s wailing increased, and Jorator’s heart softened. He and Eonislara spent some time alone together, away from everyone’s opinions, and in the end they agreed to marry.
column2: “欧尼斯拉拉怀了我的血脉？”乔拉托惊呼道，“我们必须重订婚约。这孩子长大必成勇猛战士，我确信！”我们对他的回应感到欣慰。但欧尼斯拉拉开始哭泣：“我不能以谎言开始婚姻。孩子不是乔拉托的，而是来自诗人科罗尔的腰胯。”起初乔拉托涨红了脸，作势要赶我们出他的宅院。欧尼斯拉拉的哭喊声更大了，乔拉托心软了。他和欧尼斯拉拉独处了一段时间，远离所有人的意见，最终他们同意结婚。

column1: “Your proposal is absurd and offensive! I know that the child is not mine, and will not be fooled into marriage with a promise-breaker! She told me that she would be mine alone!”
column2: “你的提议荒谬无礼！我知道孩子不是我的，我不会被一个背誓者骗入婚姻！她曾对我说她只属我一个人！”

column1: Raid the \x01@! clan.
column2: 突袭 \x01@! 氏族。

column1: We bested rude Jorator’s clan. Yet our people did not cheer; they said we made private things into clan things, and embarrassed everyone.
column2: 我们击败了粗鲁的乔拉托的氏族。但族人没有欢呼；他们说我们把私事变成了氏族之事，令所有人难堪。

column1: We did not best rude Jorator’s clan. The people were unhappy; not only had we launched a pointless battle, but we had lost as well.
column2: 我们未能击败粗鲁的乔拉托的氏族。人们很不快；我们不仅发动了一场无谓的战斗，而且还输了。

column1: Raid the \x01@! clan, even though it is Sea season.
column2: 突袭 \x01@! 氏族，即使现在是海季。

column1: Raid the \x01@! clan, even though it is Earth season.
column2: 突袭 \x01@! 氏族，即使现在是地季。

column1: We decided to let the matter rest.
column2: 我们决定不再追究此事。

column1: The people said they were glad to see the end of what should have been kept a private matter in the first place.
column2: 人们说，看到这本该首先是私事的事情完结，他们很高兴。

column1: Encourage Korol to marry her.
column2: 鼓励科罗尔娶她。

column1: “The thick-skulls came and trod upon the law-twigs,” Korol said. “I am not obligated to forge marriage-metal just because she is child-round. If I were ring-bound each time a girl was filled by my loin-fruit, I would already be twenty-times married.”
column2: “那些厚头骨跑来踩断了律法之枝，”科罗尔说，“我没有义务仅仅因为她肚子圆了就锻造婚姻之铁。要是每次姑娘被我腰胯之果填满我就得被长老会束缚，我早就结婚二十次了。”

column1: “A stupid thing said twice is twice-stupid,” Korol said. “I would not forge marriage-metal before, and will not now. If this happened each time a girl was filled by my loin-fruit, I would already be twenty-times married.”
column2: “蠢话说了两遍就是双倍蠢，”科罗尔说，“我以前不会锻造婚姻之铁，现在也不会。要是每次姑娘被我腰胯之果填满都这样，我早就结婚二十次了。”

column1: We bested lecherous Korol’s clan. Yet our people did not cheer; they said we made private things into clan things, and embarrassed everyone.
column2: 我们击败了好色的科罗尔的氏族。但族人没有欢呼；他们说我们把私事变成了氏族之事，令所有人难堪。

column1: We did not best lecherous Korol’s clan. The people were unhappy; not only had we launched a pointless battle, but we had lost as well.
column2: 我们未能击败好色的科罗尔的氏族。人们很不快；我们不仅发动了一场无谓的战斗，而且还输了。

column1: Leave this matter to her kinfolk.
column2: 把这件事留给她的族人处理。

column1: We left the matter to her kinfolk.
column2: 我们把这件事交给了她的族人。

column1: People were happy that the ring did not interfere.
column2: 人们很高兴长老会没有干涉。

column1: Scold Eonislara for being careless.
column2: 责骂欧尼斯拉拉粗心大意。

column1: The ring scolded Eonislara for being careless.
column2: 长老会责骂欧尼斯拉拉粗心大意。

column1: The people were amazed that the clan leaders blamed her for having a child outside marriage. They said that their leaders were making new and stupid rules, and forgetting traditional ways.
column2: 人们很惊讶，氏族首领竟因她婚姻外有子而责备她。他们说首领们在制定愚蠢的新规矩，忘记了传统之道。

column1: Some kind-hearted folks were even sorrier for Eonislara, for having known Korol and then learning he was killed.
column2: 一些好心人更为欧尼斯拉拉感到难过，她曾与科罗尔相好，后来又得知他被杀了。

column1: Scold her kinfolk for being unreasonable.
column2: 责骂她的族人无理取闹。

column1: The ring scolded her kinfolk for being unreasonable.
column2: 长老会责骂她的族人无理取闹。

column1: The people were happy that the clan leaders had said these things, for no blame should attach to a woman for a child born outside of marriage.
column2: 人们很高兴氏族首领说了这些话，因为婚姻之外生的孩子不应该归咎于女人。

column1: Eonislara’s carelessness will dry up the cows’ udders.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉的粗心大意会让牛的乳房干涸。

column1: Who cares?
column2: 谁在乎？

column1: It will be easier to force Korol to marry her than to force Jorator.
column2: 强迫科罗尔娶她比强迫乔拉托更容易。

column1: It will be easier to force Jorator to marry her than to force Korol.
column2: 强迫乔拉托娶她比强迫科罗尔更容易。

column1: Jorator’s clan is too strong for us to force him into marriage.
column2: 乔拉托的氏族太强大，我们无法强迫他结婚。

column1: We can convince Jorator’s clan to force him to honor his betrothal.
column2: 我们可以说服乔拉托的氏族强迫他履行婚约。

column1: Everyone involved in this has a different opinion. There’s no way to make things right.
column2: 此事中每个人意见都不同。没法把事情摆平。

column1: We must marry her to Korol.
column2: 我们必须把她嫁给科罗尔。

column1: Eonislara has not broken the law.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉没有违法。

column1: Eonislara has broken neither law nor custom.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉既没有违法也没有违俗。

column1: Eonislara has broken neither law nor custom. This is a private matter, and should remain so.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉既没有违法也没有违俗。这是私事，也应保持为私事。

column1: If we try to force a marriage, we will offend the unwilling groom’s clan.
column2: 如果我们试图强迫婚姻，我们会冒犯不情愿新郎的氏族。

column1: Jorator’s clan dislikes us more than Korol’s clan.
column2: 乔拉托的氏族比科罗尔的氏族更不喜欢我们。

column1: Korol’s clan dislikes us more than Jorator’s clan.
column2: 科罗尔的氏族比乔拉托的氏族更不喜欢我们。

column1: Jorator’s clan may be difficult to convince of anything.
column2: 乔拉托的氏族可能很难被说服去做任何事。

column1: Unless Jorator is just stupid, he should be willing to marry Eonislara.
column2: 除非乔拉托就是个蠢货，否则他应该愿意娶欧尼斯拉拉。

column1: Why are we bothering with this trifle when it’s time to plant our crops?
column2: 正值播种时节，我们为什么还要为这点小事操心？

column1: Why are we bothering with this trifle when it’s harvest time?
column2: 正值收获时节，我们为什么还要为这点小事操心？

column1: Good King Oskul was born outside the marriage bond.
column2: 贤王奥斯库尔生于婚姻之外。

column1: Eonislara’s kin are being unreasonable. They need a good talking to.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉的亲族太不讲理了。他们需要好好被训斥一顿。

column1: The only vow broken here was Jorator’s vow to marry her.
column2: 这里唯一被违背的誓言，是乔拉托要娶她的誓言。

column1: A child is no reason to force a marriage.
column2: 一个孩子不足以成为强制结婚的理由。

column1: Scold no one.
column2: 谁也不许责骂。

column1: What nonsense! You’d think she was accused of killing a dragonewt or something.
column2: 简直胡闹！说得好像她被指控杀了某种龙人似的。

column1: We should be worried about improving our temples instead.
column2: 我们更应该操心的是修缮我们的神庙。

column1: sceneR224
column2: sceneR224

column1: Jorator of clan \x01@!, to whom you married the young woman Eonislara, demands compensation. “Eonislara promised that she would dally with no other before our marriage, yet now she is puffed up with the child of some accursed seducer! I have been cheated, and demand the return of the bride price as penalty!”
column2: 氏族 \x01@!的乔拉托——你把年轻女子欧尼斯拉拉嫁给了他——要求补偿。“欧尼斯拉拉曾承诺在我们婚前不会与他人私通，可现在她却被某个该死的勾引者搞大了肚子！我被骗了，要求退回彩礼作为惩罚！”

column1: Jorator of clan \x01@!, to whom you married the young woman Eonislara, demands compensation. “I thought you made up the story of Eonislara and Korol to put me off the marriage, since Eonislara promised she would dally with no other before we wed. Yet now she is puffed up with child, and I see the story was true! I am cheated, and demand the return of the bride price as penalty!”
column2: 氏族 \x01@!的乔拉托——你把年轻女子欧尼斯拉拉嫁给了他——要求补偿。“我本以为你编造欧尼斯拉拉和科罗尔的故事是为了阻止我结婚，因为欧尼斯拉拉承诺过婚前不会与他人私通。可现在她肚子大了，我才知道那故事是真的！我被骗了，要求退回彩礼作为惩罚！”

column1: Jorator came to complain that his bride Eonislara had broken a promise to stay faithful to him before they were married. He wanted her bride price back.
column2: 乔拉托来抱怨说，他的新娘欧尼斯拉拉违背了婚前对他保持忠贞的承诺。他想要回彩礼。

column1: Advise Eonislara to divorce him.
column2: 建议欧尼斯拉拉与他离婚。

column1: We told Eonislara that she should divorce him.
column2: 我们告诉欧尼斯拉拉，她应该与他离婚。

column1: Eonislara agreed that Jorator was being unreasonable. She came back to us. Jorator stalked off, threatening reprisals.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉同意乔拉托是在无理取闹。她回到了我们身边。乔拉托气冲冲地走了，扬言要报复。

column1: Eonislara said that her husband was being unreasonable, but that she did not yet wish a divorce. The people were sad that she chose to stay with a fool.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉说她丈夫在无理取闹，但她还不想离婚。人们为她选择留在一个傻瓜身边而难过。

column1: Refund the bride price.
column2: 退还彩礼。

column1: He departed, seemingly satisfied. Eonislara’s kin said she was embarrassed by Jorator’s behavior.
column2: 他离开了，似乎心满意足。欧尼斯拉拉的亲族说，乔拉托的行为让她很尴尬。

column1: When we returned home and told the story of his foolishness, the people laughed and jeered. They were proud that we had not given into his absurd bullying.
column2: 当我们回到家，讲起他那些蠢事时，人们大笑并嘲笑他。他们为我们没有屈从于他那荒谬的欺凌而感到自豪。

column1: Try to mollify him, but do not pay him.
column2: 设法安抚他，但不付钱给他。

column1: We tried to mollify him without paying him.
column2: 我们试图安抚他，但没有给他钱。

column1: At last, he admitted that Eonislara had committed no real offense against him, and promised to raise the child as if it were his kin.
column2: 最后，他承认欧尼斯拉拉并没有真正对他构成冒犯，并承诺把这个孩子当成自己的亲族来抚养。

column1: Jorator would not be moved from his anger.
column2: 乔拉托的愤怒无法平息。

column1: “Your claim is without legal foundation.”
column2: “你的要求没有法律依据。”

column1: We told him that his claim was without legal foundation.
column2: 我们告诉他，他的要求没有法律依据。

column1: Jorator was forced to admit that there was no shame in pregnancy outside the marriage bond, and that any promise-breaking between him and Eonislara was a private matter, now that they were kin.
column2: 乔拉托被迫承认，婚姻之外的怀孕并无羞耻可言，而且他与欧尼斯拉拉之间的任何背约行为，既然现在已是亲族，就只是私事。

column1: Jorator refused to admit that his claim did not conform to the law. He stubbornly refused to listen to reason.
column2: 乔拉托拒绝承认他的要求不符合法律。他顽固地拒绝听从道理。

column1: She broke a promise. We must return the bride price.
column2: 她违背了诺言。我们必须退还彩礼。

column1: Eonislara has broken no laws. She was not his bride when she laid with Korol.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉没有犯任何罪。她与科罗尔同寝时还不是他的新娘。

column1: Jorator is stupid. We already explained this to him once.
column2: 乔拉托是个蠢货。我们早就跟他解释过一遍了。

column1: Eonislara is now kin to Jorator, and there can be no crimes between kin. This is not a matter for clans at all.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉现在是乔拉托的亲族，亲族之间不可能有罪行。这根本不是氏族之间的事。

column1: There is no end to this man’s stupidity. Eonislara is now his kin; there are no crimes between kin. His own clan will tell him as much.
column2: 这个人的愚蠢没完没了。欧尼斯拉拉现在是他的亲族；亲族之间没有犯罪。他自己的氏族会告诉他这一点的。

column1: His clan might be offended if we do not please him.
column2: 如果我们不让他满意，他的氏族可能会被激怒。

column1: Why is he bringing this up again? Even his own clan thinks he is an idiot. But for Eonislara’s sake…
column2: 他为什么又提起这事？连他自己的氏族都觉得他是个白痴。但看在欧尼斯拉拉的份上……

column1: All of Jorator’s supporters are kin to him. No one else from his clan is here to lend weight to his claim.
column2: 乔拉托的所有支持者都是他的亲族。他的氏族里没有其他人来这里为他的要求撑腰。

column1: Jorator is a fearsome magician. He will send curses upon us if we do not please him.
column2: 乔拉托是个可怕的法师。如果我们不让他满意，他会对我们降下诅咒。

column1: She should divorce him, and let us raise the babe. We haven’t enough children to work the fields when we are old.
column2: 她应该离婚，让我们来养孩子。我们还没有足够的孩子在我们年老时耕种田地。

column1: Eurmal launched a lawsuit against the Bird God for painting his arm white. Everyone laughed.
column2: 欧尔马尔对鸟神提起了诉讼，指控鸟神把他的胳膊涂成了白色。所有人都笑了。

column1: He is a fool, but treat him gently.
column2: 他是个傻瓜，但要对他温和些。

column1: It is sad that Eonislara is married to a buffoon. She should divorce him.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉嫁给一个小丑，真是可怜。她应该跟他离婚。

column1: She made a vow to him, and broke it. We are dishonored if we do not repudiate her.
column2: 她对他立下了誓言，却违背了。如果我们不与她划清界限，我们便会蒙羞。

column1: It is never too soon to end a bad match.
column2: 结束一段糟糕的姻缘，永远不嫌太早。

column1: Unlike temple-building, this is not a matter for clans.
column2: 与修建神庙不同，这不是氏族之间的事。

column1: Refund the bride price? Never!
column2: 退还彩礼？绝不！

column1: Any threats he makes will be empty ones.
column2: 他做出的任何威胁都将是空话。

column1: There is a humorous incident like this in Oskul’s Saga… or is it Harmast’s Saga?
column2: 在奥斯库尔的传说中……或是哈马斯特的传说中，有过这样一件趣事。

column1: Eonislara had a fine baby boy. He looks a little like Korol the Poet, but more like Eonislara. Despite all the tempest surrounding their betrothal, Jorator dandles the baby on his knee like any other father.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉生下了一个健康的男婴。他长得有点神似诗人科罗尔，但更像欧尼斯拉拉。尽管订婚风波曾如风暴般喧嚣，乔拉托还是像所有父亲一样，将婴儿放在膝上轻轻逗弄。

column1: Eonislara had a fine baby boy. He looks much like Eonislara’s male kin, with maybe just a hint of Korol the Poet’s chin.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉生下了一个健康的男婴。他长得酷似欧尼斯拉拉的男性亲属，下巴或许带着一丝诗人科罗尔的痕迹。

column1: Eonislara had a fine baby boy. He looks just like Korol the Poet.
column2: 欧尼斯拉拉生下了一个健康的男婴。他简直就是诗人科罗尔的翻版。

column1: A trickster from the \x01@! clan comes to \x02\x05deride/jeer at/mock/sneer at/taunt\x02 you. He has a couple of warriors from his clan with him to discourage you from attacking him.
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的 \x02\x05诡术师\x02 嘲笑/讥讽/愚弄/嗤笑/嘲弄你。他还带了同族的几名战士同行，以防你攻击他。

column1: “I hear your heroquesters \x02\x05tripped and fell at the portal of the gods/get all dressed to go and then have to stay at home/are a sorry, inept lot/can’t buckle their braces correctly, let alone enter the god-plane/were unable to enter the realm of the gods\x02!”
column2: “我听说你们的英雄探索者 \x02\x05在神域门口绊倒摔跤/穿戴整齐准备出发却只能困守家中/是一群可怜又无能的家伙/连背带都系不紧，更别说进入神域了/根本进不了众神领域\x02！”

column1: He scoffs, “You are \x02\x05a sorry excuse for Orlanthi/miserable wretches/clumsy, foolish oafs/spirit-lacking and god unblessed/unhappy rogues\x02, aren’t you?”
column2: 他嗤笑道：“你们这群 \x02\x05奥兰提的可怜虫/可悲的废物/笨手笨脚的蠢货/失魂落魄、不受神明眷顾者/倒霉的恶棍\x02，不是吗？”

column1: He capers about, doing a little dance and drooling on his tunic. “Well, in exchange for something valuable I will bless you with trickster magic, so that you will not be so laughably incompetent next time you quest!” He wants goods worth at least ten cows in exchange for Eurmal’s blessing.
column2: 他蹦蹦跳跳地耍弄着，跳了一支小舞，口水淌到袍子上。“这样吧，只要你们拿点值钱的东西来换，我就用诡术魔法赐福你们，免得下次探索时还这般可笑无能！”他想要价值至少十头牛的财物，以换取尤尔马尔的祝福。

column1: A trickster came to laugh at us, and to offer us a blessing that would help us on our next heroquest.
column2: 一名诡术师跑来嘲笑我们，还说能赐予我们祝福，帮助我们下次英雄探索。

column1: Demand an apology.
column2: 要求他道歉。

column1: We demanded an apology. He apologized in such a way as to magnify the insult.
column2: 我们要求他道歉。他倒是对此道了歉，方式却让侮辱变本加厉。

column1: “Certainly, I would be happy to apologize,” he says. “I am sorry that I reminded you that you are pathetic maggots. It pains me to think of the vastness of your incompetence, and the great dishonor your foolishness brings on all the Orlanthi of Dragon Pass.”
column2: “当然，我很乐意道歉，”他说。“我很抱歉提醒了你们，你们不过是一群可怜虫。一想到你们那无边无际的无能，想到你们的愚蠢给龙隘所有奥兰提人带来的莫大耻辱，我就心痛。”

column1: Suffer the insult.
column2: 忍气吞声。

column1: We silently suffered the insult.
column2: 我们默默忍下了侮辱。

column1: Haggle over the price.
column2: 讨价还价。

column1: We dickered with him over the price.
column2: 我们与他讨价还价。

column1: He will accept no less than \x01@\x1A cows worth. Do you agree to his price?
column2: 他至少接受价值 \x01@\x1A 头牛的财物。你同意他的要价吗？

column1: He offered us a better price, and we took it.
column2: 他给了我们一个更合适的价格，我们接受了。

column1: We refused his price, but he didn’t go away, he just stood there and grinned expectantly.
column2: 我们拒绝了他的要价，但他没有离开，只是站在那里，咧嘴笑着，等着我们。

column1: He will accept no less than \x01@\x1A cows worth, which you do not have. Do you agree to add cows to meet his price?
column2: 他至少接受价值 \x01@\x1A 头牛的财物，但你手头不够。你同意再添些牛只来凑足这个价格吗？

column1: He offered us a better price, and we made it up with cattle and goods.
column2: 他给了我们一个更合适的价格，我们用牲畜和财物凑齐了。

column1: Our efforts to haggle caused him to increase his price.
column2: 我们的讨价还价反而让他抬高了要价。

column1: Your haggling causes him to increase his price, to \x01@\x1A cows worth. Do you agree to his price?
column2: 你的讨价还价让他把要价涨到了 \x01@\x1A 头牛的财物。你同意他的要价吗？

column1: We took him up on his offer anyway.
column2: 我们最终还是接受了他的条件。

column1: Now he will accept no less than \x01@\x1A cows worth, which you do not have. Do you agree to add cows to meet his price?
column2: 现在他至少接受价值 \x01@\x1A 头牛的财物，但你手头不够。你同意再添些牛只来凑足这个价格吗？

column1: Politely decline his offer.
column2: 礼貌地拒绝他的提议。

column1: We politely declined his offer.
column2: 我们礼貌地拒绝了他的提议。

column1: He chortled through his nose and left.
column2: 他哼哼着鼻子笑着离开了。

column1: Rudely decline his offer.
column2: 粗暴地拒绝他的提议。

column1: We rudely declined his offer.
column2: 我们粗暴地拒绝了他的提议。

column1: He made noises like a bird, removed his boot and smelled it, and then departed.
column2: 他发出鸟叫般的声音，脱下靴子闻了闻，然后离开了。

column1: Take him up on his offer.
column2: 接受他的提议。

column1: We took him up on his offer.
column2: 我们接受了他的提议。

column1: He thanked us for the goods we gave him, and said we would think of him on our next heroquest.
column2: 他感谢我们给了他财物，并说我们下次英雄探索时会想起他的。

column1: We wounded the trickster and one of his guardians, and they ran off. Our honor was satisfied.
column2: 我们打伤了那个诡术师和他的一个护卫，他们逃走了。我们的荣誉得到了维护。

column1: They were ready for our blows. They struck us several times, and escaped without injury.
column2: 他们早已防备我们的攻击。他们打了我们几下，毫发无损地逃脱了。

column1: Ten cows is too much to pay for something that may not even exist.
column2: 十头牛的代价太高，为了一件也许根本不存在的东西。

column1: We can afford his boon, if we want it.
column2: 如果愿意，我们负担得起他的恩赐。

column1: I can convince him to better that price.
column2: 我能说服他降低价格。

column1: Never bargain with a trickster.
column2: 永远别跟诡术师讨价还价。

column1: It’s hard to tell whether trickster magic works or backfires.
column2: 很难说诡术魔法是生效还是起反作用。

column1: Maybe his \x02\x03questionable magic/dubious offer/unknown blessing\x02 is worth the price he’s asking.
column2: 也许他那 \x02\x03可疑的魔法/靠不住的提议/未知的祝福\x02 值他开出的价码。

column1: It is illegal to deal with another clan’s trickster.
column2: 与别的氏族的诡术师打交道是违法的。

column1: A trickster is a natural outlaw, unless he has the protection of a clan chief.
column2: 诡术师天生就是法外之徒，除非他得到氏族酋长的庇护。

column1: A trickster is a natural outlaw, unless he has the protection of a clan chief. This fellow, of course, is protected by the \x01@! chief.
column2: 诡术师天生就是法外之徒，除非他得到氏族酋长的庇护。当然，这家伙受到了 \x01@! 酋长的庇护。

column1: We may \x02\x03hate his words and his offer/deride the way he comes to sneer at us/get sick at the very sight of him\x02, but don’t offend him. That may offend the \x01@! chief.
column2: 我们或许 \x02\x03憎恶他的言辞和提议/嘲弄他前来讥讽我们的方式/一见到他就感到恶心\x02，但别冒犯他。那可能会冒犯到 \x01@! 酋长。

column1: We can take them.
column2: 我们能对付他们。

column1: If they get offended when we attack their trickster, we can fight them off.
column2: 如果我们攻击他们的戏弄者时他们被激怒，我们可以击退他们。

column1: Better stop at rudeness.
column2: 最好止步于无礼。

column1: The people are offended by his mockery.
column2: 人民被他的嘲弄冒犯了。

column1: The people are offended by his mockery. They will be upset with us if we do not abuse him.
column2: 人民被他的嘲弄冒犯了。如果我们不辱骂他，他们会对我们不满。

column1: The people are enraged by his continued mockery. They expect us to make him make amends.
column2: 人民被他持续的嘲弄激怒了。他们希望我们让他做出补偿。

column1: The people are discouraged by his reappearance. They want us to try this blessing of his, if only to get rid of him.
column2: 人民因他再次出现而气馁。他们希望我们试试他的祝福，只要能摆脱他就行。

column1: The people would like to see us get onto the god-plane. They aren’t willing to part with wealth for this, though.
column2: 人民希望看到我们进入神域。不过他们不愿为此舍弃财富。

column1: Tricksters have powerful magic.
column2: 戏弄者拥有强大的魔法。

column1: Tricksters have powerful magic, but even they cannot always predict how it will work.
column2: 戏弄者拥有强大的魔法，但连他们也未必总能预测魔法会如何生效。

column1: Tricksters have powerful but unreliable magic. He seems pretty confident, though.
column2: 戏弄者拥有强大但不可靠的魔法。不过，他似乎相当自信。

column1: If we could trust his magic not to veer off in some unpredictable way, I’d say we could accept his offer.
column2: 如果我们能相信他的魔法不会以某种不可预测的方式偏离，我会说我们可以接受他的提议。

column1: He will probably continue to annoy us until we either succeed at a heroquest or accept Eurmal’s blessing. I ask you, which is cheaper?
column2: 他大概会一直烦扰我们，直到我们成功完成英雄任务或接受尤尔马尔的祝福。我问你，哪个更划算？

column1: Me! Me! I am the only trickster you should trust.
column2: 我！我！你们唯一该信任的戏弄者就是我。

column1: He’s giving me the evil eye! I can feel it!
column2: 他在给我施加恶毒之眼！我能感觉到！

column1: Why are you all looking at me funny? Would you give ME ten cows if I offered Eurmal’s blessing for our quests? I don’t think so!
column2: 你们为什么都奇怪地看着我？如果我提出用尤尔马尔的祝福来祝我们的任务，你们会给我十头牛吗？我可不信！

column1: Yeah, yeah. The sacred society of Eurmal devotees and all that. Secret sign, special song. Uh-huh.
column2: 是啊，是啊。尤尔马尔信徒神圣协会，还有那些。秘密记号，特别歌曲。嗯哼。

column1: Isn’t that just like a man?

column2: 在我们准备献祭时，混沌生物吃掉了一些我们牛只。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were good; Urox would aid us in our battle.
column2: 神言者说吉兆显现；乌洛克斯将在战斗中帮助我们。

column1: The god-talkers said that Urox must be helping others who were worse beset by Chaos.
column2: 神言者说乌洛克斯一定在帮助其他被混沌侵扰更甚的人。

column2: 寻求其他氏族的帮助。

column2: 我们寻求了其他氏族的帮助。

column2: 当我们与其他酋长交谈时，混沌生物吃掉了一些我们孩童。

column2: 一个氏族

sent warriors to aid us. A total of \x01@\x06 weaponthanes came.
column2: 派来武士援助我们。共有 \x01@\x06 名武器领主前来。

column1: No other clan agreed to help us.
column2: 没有其他氏族同意帮助我们。

column1: Send for Uroxi warriors.
column2: 召唤乌洛希武士。

column1: We sent for Uroxi warriors.
column2: 我们召唤了乌洛希武士。

column1: While we waited for word to get to them, the Chaos creature ate some of our horses.
column2: 在我们等待消息传到他们那里时，混沌生物吃掉了一些我们马匹。

column1: \x01@\x18 great holy warriors of Urox came to aid us.
column2: \x01@\x18 乌洛克斯的伟大的圣战士们前来援助我们。

column1: They said we should call on the Storm Bull for his aid.
column2: 他们说我们应该召唤风暴公牛前来援助。

column1: None of them heeded our call.
column2: 没有一人回应我们的呼唤。

column1: The Uroxi refused to help us, because we had not respected them before now. “Maybe now you will realize how important we are,” they said.
column2: 乌洛希拒绝帮助我们，因为我们此前从未尊重过他们。“也许现在你们会意识到我们有多重要，”他们说。

column1: This thing is a grave threat to us, but we must not sacrifice more cows than it would eat.
column2: 这东西对我们构成严重威胁，但我们不能献祭比它吃掉的更多的牛只。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice generously to Urox.
column2: 我们负担得起慷慨地向乌洛克斯献祭。

column1: Get the children to the temples! Hurry!
column2: 把孩子送到神庙去！快！

column1: We must not fail this time. We must not.
column2: 这次我们绝不能失败。绝不能。

column1: We must send for Uroxi warriors.
column2: 我们必须召唤乌洛希武士。

column1: The Uroxi are well-disposed towards us, and live to fight Chaos. They will come.
column2: 乌洛希对我们抱有好感，他们生来就为对抗混沌而战。他们会来的。

column1: Although the Uroxi live to fight Chaos, we have slighted them in the past. They might not help us.
column2: 尽管乌洛希生来就为对抗混沌而战，但我们过去曾怠慢过他们。他们可能不会帮助我们。

column1: We don’t need to prepare. We must fight it immediately!
column2: 我们不需要准备。我们必须立刻战斗！

column1: The longer we wait, the more harm it will do.
column2: 我们等得越久，它造成的伤害就越大。

column1: We can’t hope to defeat it alone.
column2: 我们不可能单独击败它。

column1: Other clans might help us. If there is Chaos abroad in Dragon Pass, it is in everyone’s interests to fight it.
column2: 其他氏族也许会帮助我们。如果混沌在龙之隘口肆虐，那么对抗混沌符合所有人的利益。

column1: If there is Chaos abroad in Dragon Pass, it is in everyone’s interests to fight it. But our neighbors dislike us, which might blind them to this obvious truth.
column2: 如果混沌在龙之隘口肆虐，那么对抗混沌符合所有人的利益。但我们的邻居不喜欢我们，这可能会让他们对这一显而易见的真相视而不见。

column1: If there is Chaos abroad in Dragon Pass, it is in everyone’s interests to fight it. Our neighbors are our friends, and will help us.
column2: 如果混沌在龙之隘口肆虐，那么对抗混沌符合所有人的利益。我们的邻居是我们的朋友，会帮助我们。

column1: We must try everything. We cannot fail!
column2: 我们必须尝试一切办法。我们不能失败！

column1: Can we survive? We must try.
column2: 我们能幸存吗？我们必须尝试。

column1: Urox will expect us to shift for ourselves.
column2: 乌洛克斯会指望我们自食其力。

column1: A monster so fierce can only be beaten with divine aid.
column2: 如此凶猛的怪物只能靠神力才能击败。

column1: The more cows we sacrifice to Urox, the more likely it is he will hear us. Sacrifice ten cows, at least.
column2: 我们向乌洛克斯献祭的牛只越多，他就越有可能听见我们。至少献祭十头牛。

column1: Sacrifice, plead for help, whatever it takes.
column2: 献祭、乞求帮助，无论付出什么代价。

column1: Why can we not kill this beast?!
column2: 我们为什么不能杀死这头野兽？！

column1: The more cows we sacrifice to Urox, the more likely it is he will hear us. Sacrifice twenty-five cows, at least.
column2: 我们向乌洛克斯献祭的牛只越多，他就越有可能听见我们。至少献祭二十五头牛。

column1: If we can’t kill it this time, we must sacrifice to Urox immediately to fight off Chaos.
column2: 如果我们这次杀不死它，就必须立即向乌洛克斯献祭，以击退混沌。

column1: We have many enemies, but our worst enemy is Chaos.
column2: 我们有很多敌人，但我们最大的敌人是混沌。

column1: Wakboth… the Devil…
column2: 瓦克博斯……恶魔……

column1: This could be the end. But we will keep fighting!
column2: 这可能是终结。但我们会继续战斗！

column1: This is in no way my fault.
column2: 这绝不是我的错。

column1: Oh no. Not again. Find the Storm Bulls, find the Storm Bulls!
column2: 哦不。又来了。找到风暴公牛信徒，找到风暴公牛信徒！

column1: Sacrifice to Urox. Seek out Uroxi warriors.
column2: 向乌洛克斯献祭。寻找乌洛希武士。

column1: It could be worse. It could be a gigantic undead creature.
column2: 情况本可能更糟。它可能是一头巨大的不死生物。

column1: Well, we’ll really be in trouble if we kill it and then it comes back to life, won’t we.
column2: 嗯，如果我们杀死它然后它又复活了，那我们可真要麻烦了，不是吗。

column1: This is bad.
column2: 这可糟了。

column1: We are being punished for making war on our neighbors!
column2: 我们正在因对我们邻居发动战争而受到惩罚！

column1: If we had a tribe, it would be easier to get help from our neighbors.
column2: 如果我们有一个部落，从邻居那里获得帮助会更容易。

column1: We must kill it. We can kill it! Come on!
column2: 我们必须杀死它。我们能杀死它！来吧！

column1: Kill!
column2: 杀！

column1: Uh-oh.
column2: 哎呀。

column1: I was afraid this was going to happen.
column2: 我就怕会发生这种事。

column1: Run away!
column2: 快跑！

column1: I think this is what I Saw. The poor sheep!
column2: 我想这就是我所预见到的。可怜的羊啊！

column1: \x01@\x14 found out that all the maps in Dragon Pass were jumbled up.
column2: \x01@\x14 发现龙之隘的所有地图都混乱了。

column1: Apologize to other clans for ruining all the maps.
column2: 向其他氏族道歉，因为弄乱了所有地图。

column1: We apologized to other clans for ruining all the maps.
column2: 我们向其他氏族道歉，因为弄乱了所有地图。

column1: They said that our forthrightness was admirable, and that everyone knows that heroquesting is risky.
column2: 他们说我们的坦率值得钦佩，人人都知道英雄任务是有风险的。

column1: They said that we had harmed them greatly, and that no mere apology would suffice.
column2: 他们说我们严重伤害了他们，仅道歉是不够的。

column1: Blame another clan for ruining maps.
column2: 责怪另一个氏族弄乱了地图。

column1: Which clan do you blame?
column2: 你责怪哪个氏族？

column1: No one believed us. They called us obvious liars. They cursed us once for jumbling up the maps, and twice for lying about it.
column2: 没人相信我们。他们说我们是明显的骗子。他们一次诅咒我们弄乱地图，两次诅咒我们撒谎。

column1: We ignored the problem, as best we could, but word got around to the other clans that our failed heroquest had caused the mess. Our neighbors cursed us for trying to hide our guilt.
column2: 我们尽可能无视了这个问题，但消息传到了其他氏族，说我们失败的英雄任务造成了混乱。邻居们诅咒我们试图隐瞒罪责。

column1: Sacrifice to Issaries, the traveling god.
column2: 向旅行之神伊萨里斯献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to Issaries, the traveling god.
column2: 我们向旅行之神伊萨里斯献祭。

column1: Before our eyes, the lines on the maps wriggled and shifted, until they were right again. The people rejoiced.
column2: 在我们眼前，地图上的线条扭动移动，直到恢复正确。人们欢欣鼓舞。

column1: The maps remained jumbled. The other clans performed divinations which revealed that our failed heroquest was responsible for this disaster.
column2: 地图仍然混乱。其他氏族进行占卜，揭示出我们失败的英雄任务是这场灾难的原因。

column1: They held it against us for many seasons.
column2: 他们为此记恨了我们许多季节。

column1: Sacrifice to Lhankor Mhy, the knowing god.
column2: 向全知之神兰克尔莫献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to Lhankor Mhy, the knowing god.
column2: 我们向全知之神兰克尔莫献祭。

column1: We can’t afford any sacrifices now.
column2: 我们现在负担不起任何献祭。

column1: We can afford a generous gift to the gods.
column2: 我们能够向众神献上丰厚的礼物。

column1: If we do nothing to correct this, and we are held responsible, all of Dragon Pass will revile us.
column2: 如果我们不纠正此事，并被追究责任，整个龙之隘都会唾弃我们。

column1: If we apologize for causing this, we will be admired for our forthrightness.
column2: 如果我们为此道歉，我们会因坦率而受到钦佩。

column1: This was caused by our failed heroquest, and everyone will know it.
column2: 这是我们失败的英雄任务造成的，人人都会知道。

column1: This problem was caused by our failed heroquest, and everyone will know it. We must sacrifice to correct it.
column2: 这个问题是我们失败的英雄任务造成的，人人都会知道。我们必须献祭来纠正它。

column1: A failed Lhankor Mhy heroquest caused this. We must petition his rival, Issaries, to correct it.
column2: 失败的兰克尔莫英雄任务导致了此事。我们必须祈求他的对手伊萨里斯来纠正。

column1: A failed Issaries heroquest caused this. We must petition his rival, Lhankor Mhy, to correct it.
column2: 失败的伊萨里斯英雄任务导致了此事。我们必须祈求他的对手兰克尔莫来纠正。

column1: The failed Vinga Trailblazer heroquest caused this. We should petition either Issaries or Lhankor Mhy to correct it.
column2: 失败的温加开拓者英雄任务导致了此事。我们应祈求伊萨里斯或兰克尔莫来纠正。

column1: What does it matter if we cannot explore? We should pay more attention to our fields, and less to faraway places.
column2: 如果我们无法探索，那又有什么关系？我们应该多关注田地，少关心远方。

column1: Only the Knowing God can right this terrible error.
column2: 只有全知之神才能纠正这个可怕的错误。

column1: Only the Traveling God can find the right paths again.
column2: 只有旅行之神才能重新找到正确的道路。

column1: The people will be pleasantly surprised by a royal apology, and will admire us for it.
column2: 人民会因一次诚恳的道歉而惊喜，并会因此钦佩我们。

column1: It’s the cursed elves, trying to keep us from burning down their noisome forests!
column2: 是那些该死的精灵，想阻止我们烧掉他们恶臭的森林！

column1: This is some awful spell unleashed by the scheming sorceresses of the \x01@/ clan!
column2: 这是 \x01@/ 氏族诡计多端的女巫释放的可怕法术！

column1: At last! The maps have righted themselves again, and once more we can safely explore the lands around us.
column2: 终于！地图再次自行恢复正确，我们又能安全探索周围的土地了。

column2: 大面包的萨满回来找我们要更多的牛。

column1: The shamans of the spirit that calls itself Grandbread return, demanding cows. “You have not yet seen the terrible knowledge-stealing powers of our dread spirit patron. Pay us \x01@\x18 cows and escape from being made stupid.”
column2: 自称大面包的灵魂的萨满回来了，索要牛只。“你们还没见识过我们可怕灵魂庇护者的窃取知识之力。付给我们 \x01@\x18 头牛，以免变得愚蠢。”

column1: Shamans of Grandbread came back and asked us for cows again.
column2: 大面包的萨满回来又找我们要牛。

column1: A couple of shamans come to threaten you with bad magic if you do not pay them five cows. “We met a new and powerful spirit that calls itself Grandbread. It says it is a spirit of knowledge, and that it will steal your knowledge from you if you do not please us, its first worshippers.”
column2: 几个萨满前来威胁你，如果你不付给他们五头牛，就会施加恶咒。“我们遇到了一个自称大面包的强大新灵魂。它说它是知识之灵，如果你不取悦我们这些它的首批信徒，它就会偷走你的知识。”

column1: Shamans tried to get us to give them cows by threatening us with the power of Grandbread, a bad new knowledge spirit.
column2: 萨满试图用大面包的力量威胁我们交出牛只，那是个糟糕的新知识之灵。

column1: Their spirit patron might have been powerful, but these shamans were not. When we charged them, they ran and fell. They were easily killed.
column2: 他们的灵魂庇护者或许很强大，但这些萨满不是。当我们冲向他们时，他们逃跑跌倒，被轻易杀死。

column1: The shamans were easy to kill, but with his dying breath, one of them called on Grandbread to curse us.
column2: 萨满很容易杀死，但其中一个在临死前呼唤大面包诅咒我们。

column1: Our god-talkers said they felt a tugging at their minds, and a malign presence that must be the spirit that called itself Grandbread.
column2: 我们的神言者说他们感到思想被拉扯，还有一股恶意的存在，必定是那个自称大面包的灵魂。

column1: It hurt their heads, and the heads of the wise people of our clan.
column2: 它弄痛了他们的头，以及我们氏族智者们的头。

column1: After that day, people forgot things that they had known before, and gave stupid answers to questions others asked them.
column2: 从那天起，人们忘记了以前知道的事情，并对他人的提问给出愚蠢的回答。

column1: We paid them.
column2: 我们付了。

column1: We did not pay them.
column2: 我们没有付。

column1: Sacrifice for protection from Grandbread’s magic.
column2: 献祭以求免受大面包魔法的侵害。

column1: We sacrificed for protection from Grandbread’s magic.
column2: 我们献祭以求免受大面包魔法的侵害。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were bad. \x01@\x07 had not heard our pleas.
column2: 神言者说征兆不好。 \x01@\x07 没有听到我们的祈求。

column1: The god-talkers said that the signs were good. \x01@\x07 sent magic to fortify us against Grandbread’s powers.
column2: 神言者说征兆良好。 \x01@\x07 送出魔法来加固我们，以抵御大面包的力量。

column1: We visited the clan they claimed to have harmed.
column2: 我们拜访了他们声称受到伤害的氏族。

column1: The people there were milling around with blank eyes. When we asked them questions, they said stupid things. They said they dimly remembered refusing to pay a couple of shamans who served a new spirit called Bigbread, or something like it.
column2: 那里的人们眼神空洞地四处游荡。当我们问他们问题时，他们尽说些蠢话。他们说依稀记得曾拒绝支付酬劳给几个萨满，这些萨满侍奉一个叫做“大面包”或类似名字的新灵体。

column1: The people there said they had been visited by crude shamans, and refused to pay them. Instead, they sacrificed to \x02\x04Ernalda/Lhankor Mhy/Issaries/Chalana Arroy\x02 for protection, and bested the spirit when it came to infest their minds.
column2: 那里的人们说，他们曾被粗野的萨满造访，并拒绝支付酬劳。相反，他们向 \x02\x04厄纳尔达/兰科尔·姆伊/伊萨里斯/查拉娜·阿洛伊\x02 献祭以求庇护，并在那灵体前来侵蚀他们心智时击败了它。

column1: The god-talkers said they felt a tugging at their minds, and a malign presence that must be the spirit that called itself Grandbread. They drove it off, and were unharmed by its magic.
column2: 神言者说他们感到心智被拉扯，还有一种恶意的存在，必定是那自称为大面包的灵体。他们驱走了它，并未受其魔法所伤。

column1: The god-talkers said they felt a tugging at their minds, and a malign presence that must be the spirit that called itself Grandbread.
column2: 神言者说他们感到心智被拉扯，还有一种恶意的存在，必定是那自称为大面包的灵体。

column1: Even five cows is too much to spare.
column2: 连五头牛都太多，拿不出来。

column1: Five cows is not too much to pay to get rid of these pests.
column2: 花五头牛除掉这些害虫并不算多。

column1: We cannot afford to keep buying them off with cows. Drive them away, and be done with this.
column2: 我们负担不起一直用牛打发他们。赶走他们，就此了结。

column1: Even one cow is one cow too many for these grubby oafs.
column2: 对这些肮脏的蠢货来说，哪怕一头牛都太多了。

column1: If we pay them, they’ll just keep coming back for more.
column2: 如果我们付钱给他们，他们只会不断回来要更多。

column1: See? Here they come again, sniffing around for more of our cattle.
column2: 看？他们又来了，到处嗅着想要更多我们的牛。

column1: They did no lasting damage on their prior visit, but that doesn’t mean they could never hurt us.
column2: 他们先前造访时并未造成持久伤害，但那并不意味着他们永远无法伤害我们。

column1: Why do they ask for less this time? Their terrible god is maybe not so terrible at all.
column2: 为什么他们这次要的更少？他们那可怕的神也许根本没那么可怕。

column1: I don’t know about their magic, but if it comes down to a normal fight, we can easily kill these hog-shaped outlaws.
column2: 我不知道他们的魔法如何，但如果只是一场普通战斗，我们可以轻易杀死这些猪一样的歹徒。

column1: The other clans will thank us if we nip this threat in the bud.
column2: 如果我们能将威胁扼杀在萌芽中，其他部族会感激我们。

column1: Grandbread is a terrifying Chaos god!
column2: 大面包是一个可怕的混沌之神！

column1: Grandbread isn’t a spirit. He’s an old, dead god from a Lhankor Mhy story.
column2: 大面包不是灵体。他是来自兰科尔·姆伊故事中的一个古老、已死的神。

column1: Grandbread is an old, dead god from the Lhankor Mhy heroquest we failed.
column2: 大面包是来自我们失败的那次兰科尔·姆伊英雄探索中的一个古老、已死的神。

column1: Grandbread is an old, dead god from the Lhankor Mhy heroquest we failed. Our failure must have given power to a spirit that now claims his name.
column2: 大面包是来自我们失败的那次兰科尔·姆伊英雄探索中的一个古老、已死的神。我们的失败必定赐予了一个灵体力量，这个灵体现在冒用他的名字。

column1: Grandbread is a dead god from the Lhankor Mhy heroquest we failed. That failure must have given power to a spirit which has taken his name. Kill its worshippers now, before it gains more of them.
column2: 大面包是来自我们失败的那次兰科尔·姆伊英雄探索中的一个已死之神。那次失败必定赐予了一个灵体力量，它夺取了他的名字。现在趁它还没获得更多信徒，杀掉它的崇拜者。

column1: Grandbread ate knowledge like it was food. He tried to pound the truth into meal, cook it into loaves of bread, and devour it.
column2: 大面包像吃食物一样吞噬知识。他试图将真理捣碎成粉，烤成面包，然后吞食。

column1: Pay them, pay them, or it will make us stupid!
column2: 付给他们，付给他们，否则它会让我们变蠢！

column1: Let this spirit come! Our god-talkers will wrestle it to the ground and bind it to our service!
column2: 让这个灵体来吧！我们的神言者会将它摔倒在地，绑来为我们效力！

column1: We should get some sort of protection against this fearful Grandbread.
column2: 我们应该获得某种防护来对抗这个可怕的大面包。

column1: Knowledge-eater gobbles words before they are even spoken, but he will find bronze an unpleasant meal.
column2: 知识吞噬者在话语出口之前就将它们吞咽，但他会发现青铜是一道不愉快的菜肴。

column1: If others learn that we are frightened by fat shamans, we will never gain the throne.
column2: 如果别人知道我们被肥胖的萨满吓住，我们将永远无法获得王位。

column1: This would never have happened if we’d done the Uralda heroquest.
column2: 如果我们完成了乌拉尔达英雄探索，这事绝不会发生。

column1: If it steals our knowledge, clans will clash out of ignorance.
column2: 如果它偷走了我们的知识，部族之间会因为无知而冲突。

column2: sceneR229

column1: Your traders again \x02\x03encountered/skirmished with/were accosted by\x02 Saraska’s bandits. The self-proclaimed future Queen of Dragon Pass is reduced to highway robbery. Our traders escaped unharmed, but lost some goods while fleeing.
column2: 你们的商人再次 \x02\x03遭遇/与……发生小规模冲突/被……搭讪\x02 萨拉斯卡的匪帮。这位自封的龙之隘口未来女王已沦落到拦路抢劫的地步。我们的商人逃脱时未受伤，但慌乱中损失了一些货物。

column1: Bandits, led by Saraska, chased our traders again.
column2: 由萨拉斯卡带领的匪帮再次追赶我们的商人。

column1: Your traders are pursued by bandits while traveling between tulas. The leader of the bandits is the self-styled future Queen of Dragon Pass, Saraska, now reduced to brigandage. The traders escaped unharmed, but lost some goods while fleeing.
column2: 你们的商人在不同图拉领地间旅行时遭到匪帮追击。匪帮头目是自封的龙之隘口未来女王萨拉斯卡，如今沦落为强盗。商人们逃脱时未受伤，但慌乱中损失了一些货物。

column1: Bandits, led by Saraska, chased our traders.
column2: 由萨拉斯卡带领的匪帮追赶了我们的商人。

column1: Ignore her.
column2: 别理会她。

column1: We paid her no mind.
column2: 我们没把她放在心上。

column1: Offer her tribute if she goes away.
column2: 如果她离开，就向她进贡。

column1: We sent a delegation to offer her tribute.
column2: 我们派遣了一个使团向她进贡。

column1: What tribute do you offer her?
column2: 你向她进献什么贡品？

column1: She haughtily refused to accept our tribute. “Although you sightless fools do not see it, I am ordained by the gods to be your queen. I will not leave my kingdom, or my subjects.”
column2: 她傲慢地拒绝接受我们的贡品。“虽然你们这些盲目的蠢货看不到，但众神已指定我做你们的王后。我不会离开我的王国，也不会离开我的臣民。”

column1: Send a war party to drive her bandits off.
column2: 派一支战团去驱赶她的匪帮。

column1: We sent a war party against her.
column2: 我们派了一支战团去对付她。

column1: Led by \x01@\x05, our proud fighters found the bandits and drove them off. As she fled, Saraska said we would regret our effrontery when the prophecies came true, and she reigned over us as queen.
column2: 在 \x01@\x05的带领下，我们骄傲的战士们找到匪帮并将他们赶走。逃跑时，萨拉斯卡说当预言成真、她加冕为我们的王后时，我们会对自己的无礼感到后悔。

column1: Saraska’s warriors ambushed our own, and wounded many. She said she would not kill us, for she wanted us to live to see her crowned, so that we would regret opposing her.
column2: 萨拉斯卡的战士伏击了我们的人，打伤了许多人。她说她不会杀死我们，因为她想让我们活着看到她加冕，这样我们就会后悔反对她。

column1: Send a war party to kill Saraska.
column2: 派一支战团去杀死萨拉斯卡。

column1: Led by \x01@\x05, our proud fighters found the bandits and fought them off. \x01@\x05 pursued Saraska into a gorge, where she fell from her horse. \x01@\x05 advanced upon her and drew \x04 sword. As she died, Saraska said the gods would resurrect her, and that she would still be queen.
column2: 在 \x01@\x05的带领下，我们骄傲的战士找到了强盗并击退了他们。 \x01@\x05 追逐萨拉斯卡进入峡谷，她从马上摔落。 \x01@\x05 逼近她并拔出 \x04 剑。她临死时说诸神会复活她，她仍将是女王。

column1: Saraska’s warriors attacked us from ambush, wounding \x01@\x05 and many others. She said she would not kill us, for she wanted us to live to see her crowned, so that we would regret opposing her.
column2: 萨拉斯卡的战士伏击了我们，打伤了 \x01@\x05 和许多人。她说不会杀我们，想让我们活着看她加冕，这样我们就会后悔反对她。

column1: Threaten her with death if she does not halt her banditry.
column2: 威胁她若不停止劫掠就处死她。

column1: We sent a delegation to threaten her with death if would not halt her banditry.
column2: 我们派了使团去威胁她若不停止劫掠就处死她。

column1: She paid no heed to our threats. “I have no other destiny than to be queen of all of these lands, to rule a great kingdom. The worms will not eat me until that destiny is fulfilled, and none of your unperceiving bluster cannot change that.”
column2: 她对我们的威胁不予理会。“我此生唯一的命运，就是成为这片土地的女王，统治一个伟大的王国。在那个命运实现之前，蛆虫不会啃食我，你们那些盲目的虚张声势改变不了什么。”

column1: We can afford to pay tribute, but take care that the tribute does not exceed what we could expect her to take from us.
column2: 我们能承担贡品，但注意不要让贡品超过她可能从我们这里抢走的数量。

column1: We can’t afford tribute.
column2: 我们付不起贡品。

column1: If we give one cow, she will want two. And if we give two, she might raid us for four.
column2: 如果我们给一头牛，她就会要两头。而如果我们给两头，她可能会来抢走四头。

column1: Don’t even think of giving one sickly calf to that has-been!
column2: 想都别想给那个过气的人一头病弱的小牛犊！

column1: She will listen to reason.
column2: 她会听从道理。

column1: She will never give up.
column2: 她永远不会放弃。

column1: She still believes that she will be queen, and that her motley gang of bandits are the foundation of a great new kingdom. She will never listen to reason.
column2: 她仍然相信自己会成为女王，而她那群乌合之众的匪帮正是伟大新王国的基础。她永远不会听从道理。

column1: She is still rambling on and on about a kingdom, and will chew on anyone’s ear about how she is meant to be queen.
column2: 她还在喋喋不休地谈论王国，会逮着任何人的耳朵说她要成为女王。

column1: Rumor is that she bores her bandits stiff with this talk of a kingdom. But they tolerate her because she is growing mad, and the madder she gets, the better brigand she is.
column2: 传言说，她用这番王国论调让匪帮们听得厌烦透顶。但他们都容忍她，因为她正渐渐疯癫，而她越疯，就越是个好强盗。

column1: She is protected by the prophecies that say she will be queen. We cannot act against her.
column2: 她受到预言保护，预言说她将成为女王。我们不能对她动手。

column1: She is acting like an outlaw, and so can be treated as one.
column2: 她行事像个法外之徒，因此也可以被当作法外之徒对待。

column1: \x02\x02Are we tired of hearing about Saraska yet/Are we sick of losing our hard-won wealth to her buffoons\x02? Make an end of her.
column2: \x02\x02我们听厌了萨拉斯卡的传闻吗/我们受够了她的小丑抢走我们辛苦得来的财富吗\x02？让她了结吧。

column1: It’s too risky to fight bandits in territory they know well.
column2: 在他们熟悉的地盘上跟强盗作战太冒险了。

column1: I’m not sure we can beat her, but we could out-bluff her.
column2: 我不确定能打败她，但我们可以虚张声势唬住她。

column1: Saraska is no military leader, and her bandits are a rag-tag lot. We can beat them.
column2: 萨拉斯卡不是军事领袖，她的匪帮也是一群乌合之众。我们能打败他们。

column1: The weaponthanes need the exercise.
column2: 武器领主需要锻炼。

column1: I’m ashamed that we have not settled with these pathetic bandits already.
column2: 我很惭愧我们还没收拾掉这群可悲的强盗。

column1: I’ll do it.
column2: 我来办。

column1: She is the future queen of this land; this great destiny will give her the magic needed to defeat us.
column2: 她是这片土地未来的女王；这伟大命运会赋予她击败我们所需的魔法。

column1: She has always claimed to be the ordained queen of the land, but the low fate she has now reached shows that her magic is weak.
column2: 她一直声称自己是这片土地受命的女王，但她如今沦落的低微命运正说明她的魔法很弱。

column1: She is queen of nothing but stupid luck. It’s time for her luck to run out.
column2: 她不过是愚蠢运气加身的女王罢了。是时候让她的运气耗尽了。

column1: The crops need our attention — ignore her for now, keep the farmers at work in the fields.
column2: 庄稼需要我们照料——先别管她，让农夫们在田里干活。

column1: Before he was killed by Oskul, Bad King Urgrain was reduced to banditry.
column2: 在被奥斯库尔杀死之前，恶王乌格兰也曾沦为强盗。

column1: She is but a nuisance. There is no need to kill her.
column2: 她不过是个麻烦。没必要杀了她。

column1: End it.
column2: 了结它。

column1: Eurmal gnaws her soul.
column2: 厄玛尔在啃噬她的灵魂。

column1: Talking is better than killing.
column2: 谈话胜过杀戮。

column1: I am glad she did not marry any of our handsome young bachelors.
column2: 我很高兴她没有嫁给我们任何一位英俊的年轻单身汉。

column1: How sad. \x02\x02To be convinced that one has a great destiny, yet to see that destiny mysteriously slip away/To be incapable of admitting error, and so be mired deeply in it\x02.
column2: 真可悲。 \x02\x02坚信自己拥有伟大命运，却眼睁睁看着那命运神秘地溜走/无法承认错误，因此深陷其中无法自拔\x02。

column1: If we act against her, she will become queen, and make our destruction her first order of business.
column2: 如果我们对她动手，她就会成为女王，并把毁灭我们当作首要任务。

column1: She’s not really going to become queen of anything, is she?
column2: 她不会真的成为什么女王吧，会吗？

column1: Humor the poor wretch with a \x02\x03bolt of fine cloth or two/small herd of cows/few silver rings\x02.
column2: 用 \x02\x03一两匹好布/一小群牛/几枚银戒指\x02来哄哄这个可怜虫。

column1: We must kill her, or she might raid the dragonewts, and bring their wrath upon us all.
column2: 我们必须杀了她，否则她可能会袭击龙人，把他们的怒火引到我们所有人身上。

column1: Drive her off, or she will \x02\x03come and take/plot how to steal/get her crew to rob\x02 our treasures.
column2: 赶走她，否则她就会 \x02\x03过来拿走/密谋偷窃/让她的手下抢走\x02 我们的财宝。

column1: sceneR230
column2: sceneR230

column1: \x02\x03Elendra/Natalla/Felesta\x02
column2: \x02\x03埃伦德拉/纳塔拉/费莱斯塔\x02

column1: \x01@\x0B accepted our alliance gladly, and Saraska said that the prophecies had predicted that we would waver, but finally tread upon the true path.
column2: \x01@\x0B 高兴地接受了我们的联盟，萨拉斯卡说过预言曾预测我们会犹豫，但最终会踏上正途。

column1: We had to try to convince the other clans of this.
column2: 我们必须设法说服其他氏族相信这一点。

column1: The other clans would not agree to peace.
column2: 其他氏族不会同意和平。

column1: Make war on them before they make war on you.
column2: 在他们对你开战之前先对他们开战。

column1: We told the other clans that we should make war on the \x01Á before the \x01Á made war on us.
column2: 我们告诉其他氏族，我们应该在 \x01Á 对我们开战之前先对 \x01Á 开战。

column1: They agreed that this was a good idea.
column2: 他们同意这是个好主意。

column1: The other clans did not think it wise to rush into battle.
column2: 其他氏族认为仓促开战并非明智之举。

column1: Some of our weaponthanes joined with weaponthanes from other clans, to prepare themselves and their battle magics for the attack we knew would come.
column2: 我们的一些武器领主与其他氏族的武器领主联合，为即将到来的攻击淬炼自身与战斗魔法。

column1: We thanked \x01@\x01 and prepared for an attack.
column2: 我们感谢 \x01@\x01 并准备迎击。

column1: Wait for further developments.
column2: 等待事态进一步发展。

column1: We waited to see what would happen.
column2: 我们静观其变。

column1: We have no hope of surviving a war.
column2: 我们毫无希望在战争中幸存。

column1: If we cannot stop a war, we must prepare for one.
column2: 若无法阻止战争，就必须为之备战。

column1: Surprise and preparation are better weapons than delay and subterfuge.
column2: 奇袭与准备胜于拖延与诡计。

column1: Don’t go rushing into battle now, when we need to sow our crops.
column2: 现在不要急于开战——我们还得播种。

column1: Don’t go rushing into battle now, when we need to harvest our crops.
column2: 现在不要急于开战——我们还得收割。

column1: Before striking at Bad King Urgrain, Oskul said, “It is better to act than to wait.”
column2: 在打击恶王乌格兰之前，奥斯库尔说：“行动胜于等待。”

column1: We must help \x01@\x01 to find a just peace.
column2: 我们必须帮助 \x01@\x01 寻找公正的和平。

column1: If I were king, and \x01@\x01 talked to my enemies, I’d outlaw her.
column2: 若我为王，而 \x01@\x01 与敌人交谈，我便将她放逐。

column1: I’m coming to doubt Saraska’s interpretation of the prophecies.
column2: 我开始怀疑萨拉斯卡对预言的解读。

column1: There is no way to look good in this situation.
column2: 在这种局面下，怎么都显得不好看。

column1: She wore her righteousness-cloak, sparkled in her courage-jewels.
column2: 她披着正义之袍，勇气之珠宝闪耀。

column1: Saraska is doomed, and will doom many others before she is done.
column2: 萨拉斯卡在劫难逃，而在此之前她将拖累许多人。

column1: Better to know now, than be surprised later.
column2: 现在知晓，总好过日后措手不及。

column1: “A central authority will make our laws enforceable.”
column2: “中央权威能让我们的法律得以执行。”

column1: We told them, “A central authority will make our laws enforceable.”
column2: 我们告诉他们：“中央权威能让我们的法律得以执行。”

column1: They said that it was good to have laws, but even better to have an authority strong enough to obey the laws. They agreed to help make Saraska’s kingdom.
column2: 他们说有法律固然好，但有一个强大到足以遵守法律的权威则更好。他们同意协助建立萨拉斯卡的王国。

column1: They laughed and jeered. “We came to Dragon Pass to make our own fortunes, and to escape the oppressive laws of others. We are Orlanthi, and we love freedom!”
column2: 他们大笑并嘲讽。“我们来龙隘是为了发自己的财，逃离他人的压迫法律。我们是奥兰斯人，我们热爱自由！”

column1: “A kingdom will bring prosperity.”
column2: “王国将带来繁荣。”

column1: We told them, “A kingdom will bring prosperity.”
column2: 我们告诉他们：“王国将带来繁荣。”

column1: They said it would be good to be prosperous. They agreed to help make Saraska’s kingdom.
column2: 他们说繁荣是好事。他们同意协助建立萨拉斯卡的王国。

column1: They frowned and wrinkled their foreheads. They said they did not see how a kingdom would enrich them.
column2: 他们皱眉蹙额，说看不出王国如何让他们致富。

column1: “In a kingdom, our cows will be safe from raiding.”
column2: “在王国里，我们的牛只将免遭劫掠。”

column1: We told them, “In a kingdom, our cows will be safe from raiding.”
column2: 我们告诉他们：“在王国里，我们的牛只将免遭劫掠。”

column1: They said it would be good to worry only about foreign enemies, and not about trouble from other Orlanthi. They agreed to help make Saraska’s kingdom.
column2: 他们说只担心外敌、不顾及奥兰斯同胞间的麻烦是件好事。他们同意协助建立萨拉斯卡的王国。

column1: They spit and rattled their swords. They said that if they could not be raided by their neighbors, that also meant they could not raid their neighbors. “The first would be good, but the second would be bad,” they said. They refused to help make Saraska’s kingdom.
column2: 他们吐唾沫并晃动刀剑。他们说如果不能被邻居劫掠，那也意味着不能劫掠邻居。“前者好，后者糟，”他们说。他们拒绝协助建立萨拉斯卡的王国。

column1: “Saraska is a great leader.”
column2: “萨拉斯卡是伟大的领袖。”

column1: We told them, “Saraska is a great leader.”
column2: 我们告诉他们：“萨拉斯卡是伟大的领袖。”

column1: They said that her royal attributes were obvious, and that they would be pleased to bow down to her. They agreed to help make a kingdom for her.
column2: 他们说她的王者气质显而易见，很乐意向她俯首称臣。他们同意协助为她建立王国。

column1: They scoffed and jeered, saying, “We have not seen any evidence of Saraska’s so-called great qualities. We hear a lot of hot wind blowing by, but where is the action?” They refused to make a kingdom for her.
column2: 他们嗤笑嘲讽，说：“我们没看到萨拉斯卡所谓优秀品质的任何证据。听到的只有一阵阵热风，行动在哪里？”他们拒绝为她建立王国。

column1: “Saraska’s magic will carry us all to greatness.”
column2: “萨拉斯卡的魔法将带领我们所有人走向伟大。”

column1: We told them, “Saraska’s magic will carry us all to greatness.”
column2: 我们告诉他们：“萨拉斯卡的魔法将带领我们所有人走向伟大。”

column1: They said that they had already heard stories of the great magic that surrounded Saraska, and knew that the prophecies commanded them to build a kingdom for her.
column2: 他们说早已听闻环绕萨拉斯卡的强大魔法传闻，知道预言命令他们为她建立王国。

column1: They said that they did not wish to seem impious, but they had seen no evidence of Saraska’s magic. Before we could say anything, Saraska stepped forward and said, “Proof I am prepared to offer,” Saraska said, “For the gods themselves support my claims.” She strode confidently outside the tribal hall. It had been a clear day, but now glorious dark clouds rolled up. All murmured that this was a good omen indeed, that she had the favor of Orlanth. “Orlanth, I call on you to recognize my right to rule! Ernalda, I call on you to recognize my bounty and goodness! Lhankor Mhy, I call on you to recognize my love for the law!”
column2: 他们说不愿显得不虔诚，但尚未看见萨拉斯卡魔法的证据。我们还未开口，萨拉斯卡便走上前说：“证据我准备好提供了，”萨拉斯卡说，“因为众神本身支持我的主张。”她自信地大步走出部落大厅。原本晴朗的日子，此刻壮丽的乌云涌起。众人低语，这确是好兆头，她得到了奥兰斯的恩宠。“奥兰斯，我呼唤你承认我的统治权！厄纳尔达，我呼唤你承认我的丰饶与仁善！兰科·米，我呼唤你承认我对律法的热爱！”

column1: “With three tribes, we can make a kingdom,” Saraska said. “The others will come after I am crowned. They will come willingly, or by force if need be. Now I must prepare myself for the rites, to create a great Crown Test and pass it.”
column2: “有了三个部落，我们就能建立一个王国，”萨拉斯卡说。“其他部落在加冕之后会来的。他们要么自愿，要么在必要时被武力带来。现在我必须为仪式做准备，创设一场伟大的王冠试炼并通过它。”

column1: Don’t give them anything.
column2: 什么都不给他们。

column1: We can afford to give them gifts; it will help Saraska’s cause.
column2: 我们送得起礼物；这有助于萨拉斯卡的事业。

column1: I am not sure how a kingdom would bring us prosperity.
column2: 我不确定王国如何给我们带来繁荣。

column1: No one will join a new kingdom if it does not promise prosperity.
column2: 若不承诺繁荣，没人会加入一个新王国。

column1: Our best argument is that a kingdom will bring prosperity.
column2: 我们最好的论据是王国会带来繁荣。

column1: In a kingdom, our cows will be safe from raiding.
column2: 在王国里，我们的牛只将免遭劫掠。

column1: The warriors will never support a kingdom where they are no longer allowed to raid one another.
column2: 战士们绝不会支持一个禁止他们彼此劫掠的王国。

column1: We are a people of laws, yet have no way to enforce those laws.
column2: 我们是一个拥有法律的民族，却无法执行那些法律。

column1: We are a people of laws, yet have no way to enforce those laws. Sadly, many of the folk in Dragon Pass like it this way.
column2: 我们是崇尚法律的民族，却无法执行那些法律。可悲的是，龙之谷的许多民众偏偏喜欢这样。

column1: Our best argument is that a central authority will make our laws enforceable.
column2: 我们最好的论点是，中央权威能让我们的法律得以执行。

column1: Saraska is a great leader.
column2: 萨拉斯卡是一位伟大的领袖。

column1: We say that Saraska is a great leader, but this may be hard to prove.
column2: 我们说萨拉斯卡是位伟大的领袖，但这可能很难证明。

column1: Our best argument is that Saraska is a great leader.
column2: 我们最好的论点是，萨拉斯卡是位伟大的领袖。

column1: Saraska’s magic will carry us all to greatness.
column2: 萨拉斯卡的魔法将带领我们所有人走向辉煌。

column1: They may want proof of Saraska’s magic.
column2: 他们可能想看到萨拉斯卡魔法的证明。

column1: Our best argument is that Saraska’s magic is very powerful.
column2: 我们最好的论点是，萨拉斯卡的魔法非常强大。

column1: When Oskul told the other outlawed thanes that he was favored by the gods, they said that they would fight with him to destroy Bad King Urgrain.
column2: 当奥斯库尔告诉其他被放逐的领主他被神明眷顾时，他们说愿意与他并肩作战，摧毁恶王乌格兰。

column1: Our best argument is that Saraska will destroy the elves.
column2: 我们最好的论点是，萨拉斯卡将摧毁精灵。

column1: I told you that one day we’d be standing before another tribe’s moot, helping realize a great prophecy.
column2: 我告诉过你，总有一天我们会站在另一个部落的集会上，帮助实现一个伟大的预言。

column1: Our best argument is that a kingdom will enable us to teach all our children to read.
column2: 我们最好的论点是，建立王国后我们就能教会所有孩子识字。

column1: Although you opposed it, people from your tribe have won the acceptance of other tribes for Saraska’s new kingdom.
column2: 尽管你反对过，但你部落的人已经为萨拉斯卡的新王国赢得了其他部落的接纳。

column1: Saraska won the support of other kings, including our own. She said she was readying the royal rites that would inaugurate her rule over the new kingdom.
column2: 萨拉斯卡赢得了其他国王的支持，包括我们自己的国王。她说她正在准备王权仪式，以宣告她对这新王国的统治。

column1: Argue that she has not proven her leadership abilities.
column2: 辩称她尚未证明自己的领导能力。

column1: We said that she had not proven herself.
column2: 我们说过她尚未证明自己。

column1: The kings did not want to hear our arguments, but our well-chosen words forced them to take heed. People from all the tribes murmured agreement as we said that it was deeds, not words, that made a leader. Saraska turned red and began to shake. She demanded that the kings have us slain. The people were shocked. They threw clods of earth at her, saying that her actions were less than her words. She was driven off, and the people cheered us for unmasking a false leader before she took the throne of thrones. Everyone said that this incident proved it was not the time for a kingdom.
column2: 国王们不愿听我们的辩词，但我们精挑细选的话语迫使他们不得不注意。当我们说出“成就领袖的是行动而非言语”时，所有部落的人都低声附和。萨拉斯卡脸涨得通红，开始发抖。她要求国王们处死我们。民众震惊了。他们朝她投掷土块，说她的行为配不上她的言辞。她被赶走了，民众为我们欢呼，因为我们揭穿了一个假领袖，让她没能登上王位之座。所有人都说，这件事证明现在还不是建立王国的时候。

column1: The kings demanded our silence. The people jeered us. They would not be moved from their disastrous course.
column2: 国王们要求我们闭嘴。民众嘲笑我们。他们不会从灾难性的道路上回头。

column1: Demand that she prove her magic.
column2: 要求她证明自己的魔法。

column1: We said that she had not proven her magic.
column2: 我们说过她尚未证明自己的魔法。

column1: People were embarrassed that we had spoken out. “When she undergoes the rites of kingship, her magic will be tested.”
column2: 我们说出那话让众人难堪。“当她举行王权仪式时，她的魔法自然会受到考验。”

column1: We held our tongues.
column2: 我们缄口不言。

column1: Quietly prepare for war.
column2: 悄悄备战。

column1: We quietly readied ourselves for war.
column2: 我们悄悄做好了战争准备。

column1: I have given Saraska my oath. But not all the kings have.
column2: 我已经向萨拉斯卡宣誓效忠。但并非所有国王都这么做了。

column1: Their pledges of loyalty are sincere. Our distrust of the great Saraska is shameful.
column2: 他们的效忠誓言是真诚的。我们对伟大的萨拉斯卡抱持怀疑是可耻的。

column1: Something bad will come of this.
column2: 此事必将带来厄运。

column1: We have no choice but to quit the tribe.
column2: 我们别无选择，只能离开部落。

column1: Our chosen leaders have decided to bow down to Saraska. There is nothing proper we can do to stop this.
column2: 我们选出的领袖决定向萨拉斯卡低头。我们无法采取任何正当手段阻止此事。

column1: Everyone says she is a great leader.
column2: 人人都说她是一位伟大的领袖。

column1: Leadership is about what you do, not about what you say.
column2: 领导力在于你做了什么，而非说了什么。

column1: If we speak out against Saraska, we could get ourselves in trouble.
column2: 如果我们公开反对萨拉斯卡，可能会惹上麻烦。

column1: Leadership is about what you do, not about what you say. They do not want to hear us now, but when they are finished, they will be glad we spoke out.
column2: 领导力在于你做了什么，而非说了什么。他们现在不想听我们说话，但等事情结束后，他们会庆幸我们说出了口。

column1: Everyone says her magic is strong, and that prophecies proclaim her kingdom.
column2: 人人都说她的魔法强大，预言也宣告了她的王国。

column1: Everyone talks about her magic, but I haven’t seen any sign of it.
column2: 人人都谈论她的魔法，但我并未看到任何迹象。

column1: Her magic may not be as strong as she says. But we will get a chance to see this during the royal rites, and should say nothing about this now.
column2: 她的魔法或许不像她说的那样强大。但我们在王权仪式上会有机会见证，现在不必多言。

column1: The first king was Vingkot, son of Orlanth.
column2: 第一位国王是奥兰斯之子温戈特。

column1: Let’s quit the tribe. If bad things happen when Saraska takes the throne, they’ll beg us to come back. If good things happen, we can beg to be let back in.
column2: 我们离开部落吧。如果萨拉斯卡登基后出了坏事，他们会求我们回来。如果出了好事，我们可以求着回去。

column1: Trust no one but your sword.
column2: 除了你的剑，谁也别信。

column1: It is always good to be prepared.
column2: 有备总是无患。

column1: Saraska will lead us against the undead of Upland Marsh.
column2: 萨拉斯卡将带领我们对抗高地沼泽的亡灵。

column1: Saraska’s kingdom will make advantageous marriages easier to find.
column2: 萨拉斯卡的王国会让联姻更容易找到好对象。

column1: You’re all just upset because it is a woman who will lead us.
column2: 你们之所以心烦，不过是因为领导我们的是个女人。

column1: We’ve received word about Saraska and her Crown Test. She underwent a ritual of her own devising, and was struck down and killed by a thunderbolt. We were right about her all along, and a delegate from our old tribe has come to say so. We will be welcomed back and recognized for our wisdom, if we choose to rejoin the tribe.
column2: 我们收到了关于萨拉斯卡和她王冠试炼的消息。她执行了自己设计的一种仪式，结果被一道雷霆劈死了。我们一直是对的，原部落派来了一位代表，承认了这一点。如果我们选择重返部落，我们将受到欢迎，我们的智慧也会得到认可。

column1: We received word that Saraska failed her Crown Test. We were right about her all along, and a delegate from our old tribe came to urge us to rejoin the tribe.
column2: 我们收到消息，萨拉斯卡的王冠试炼失败了。我们一直是对的，原部落派来了一位代表，敦促我们重返部落。

column1: Rejoin.
column2: 重返部落。

column1: The tribe welcomed us back with a three-day feast, featuring many toasts to our virtues.
column2: 部落以三天的盛宴欢迎我们回来，席间多次举杯赞颂我们的美德。

column1: Stay independent.
column2: 保持独立。

column1: We chose not to rejoin so foolish a tribe.
column2: 我们选择不重返如此愚蠢的部落。

column1: Rejoining the tribe will make trade so much easier.
column2: 重返部落会让交易方便得多。

column1: We are bound by our decision if we want to save face.
column2: 如果我们要保全面子，就必须遵守自己的决定。

column1: Their admission of error is enough welcome back for us.
column2: 他们承认错误，对我们来说已经足够表示欢迎了。

column1: Do we want to rejoin a tribe that cannot listen to wise counsel?
column2: 我们真的想重返一个听不进明智劝告的部落吗？

column1: Our clan is better off in a tribe that can recognize and correct its lapses of judgment.
column2: 我们氏族在能够识别并纠正自身判断失误的部落中会更好。

column1: Her magic was not as strong as everyone thought.
column2: 她的魔法并不像大家想的那么强大。

column1: I knew her magic was not as strong as she said. But ours will be better if we are part of a tribe.
column2: 我知道她的魔法不像她说的那么强大。但若我们加入部落，我们的魔法会更强。

column1: I told you they’d beg us to come back.
column2: 我早就说过他们会求我们回去。

column1: The undead still fear our tribe. We should rejoin.
column2: 亡灵仍然畏惧我们部落。我们应该重新加入。

column1: A tribe allows us to arrange many advantageous marriages. We would be fools to refuse this apology.
column2: 一个部落让我们能安排许多有利的联姻。拒绝这个道歉，我们就是傻瓜。
