column1: Say nothing.
column2: 什么也别说。

column1: We said nothing.
column2: 我们什么也没说。

column1: Everyone agreed to make war on them when Fire season next came.
column2: 大家都同意在下一个火季来临时对他们开战。

column1: They thank you for the warning, and say that all would be forgiven if you come back and fight on their side.
column2: 他们感谢你的警告，并说如果你回来和他们并肩作战，一切都会被原谅。

column1: Rejoin your old tribe.
column2: 重新加入你的旧部落。

column1: We rejoined our old tribe.
column2: 我们重新加入了旧部落。

column1: We decided to attack the \x01Á before they attacked us.
column2: 我们决定在 \x01Á 攻击我们之前先发制人。

column1: We refused to switch sides yet again.
column2: 我们拒绝再次倒戈。

column1: “Send a delegation to badger the \x01Á into peace on our terms.”
column2: “派遣代表团去纠缠 \x01Á ，迫使他们按照我们的条件讲和。”

column1: We told them to send a delegation to badger the \x01Á into peace on our terms.
column2: 我们告诉他们派遣代表团去纠缠 \x01Á ，迫使他们按照我们的条件讲和。

column1: It was agreed that we should give them one last chance before making war.
column2: 大家同意在开战前再给他们最后一次机会。

column1: The delegates our tribe sent were rebuffed. Our former tribe-mates gave them curses and insults to communicate to us.
column2: 我们部落派出的代表遭到了拒绝。我们以前的部落同胞用诅咒和辱骂来传达他们的意思。

column1: The other clans said that they were glad we harbored no soft spot for our former tribe. We had no doubts that the next Fire season would bring war.
column2: 其他氏族表示很高兴我们对旧部落毫不心慈手软。我们毫不怀疑下一个火季将带来战争。

column1: “We will go and badger the \x01Á into peace on our terms.”
column2: “我们将去纠缠 \x01Á ，迫使他们按照我们的条件讲和。”

column1: We said we would go and badger the \x01Á into peace on our terms.
column2: 我们说过要去纠缠 \x01Á ，迫使他们按照我们的条件讲和。

column1: It was agreed that we give them one last chance. When our delegates went to our old tribe, they were rebuffed. Our former tribe-mates cursed us, and said we were fools.
column2: 大家同意再给他们一次机会。当我们的代表前往旧部落时，遭到了拒绝。我们以前的部落同胞诅咒我们，说我们是傻瓜。

column1: We are new to this tribe, and do not know its ways.
column2: 我们刚加入这个部落，不了解它的规矩。

column1: We are new to this tribe. Custom dictates that we go along with them, until we win their respect.
column2: 我们刚加入这个部落。习俗要求我们顺从其行事，直到赢得他们的尊重。

column1: Sometimes you can win a war by talking.
column2: 有时候靠交谈就能赢得战争。

column1: If we go to talk to our old tribe, they will heap scorn on our heads.
column2: 如果我们去找旧部落谈话，他们会把轻蔑泼在我们头上。

column1: If we go to talk to our old tribe, they will heap scorn on our heads. Delegates from another clan might have some chance of success.
column2: 如果我们去找旧部落谈话，他们会把轻蔑泼在我们头上。来自其他氏族的代表或许还有一些成功的机会。

column1: Let us show our martial fervor.
column2: 让我们展示战斗的热忱。

column1: The tribe’s other weaponthanes wonder if they can trust us in battle. Let us show them that they can.
column2: 部落的其他武器领主怀疑在战场上是否信任我们。让我们向他们证明可以。

column1: We must warn our old tribe; they were our friends, and we should not shed their blood.
column2: 我们必须警告旧部落；他们曾是我们的朋友，我们不应该流血相向。

column1: We must avert a war.
column2: 我们必须避免战争。

column1: In the First Age, the Northern Horse People stood against the way Orlanth wanted things. The Heortlings made war on them.
column2: 在第一纪元，北方马族反对奥兰斯所期望的秩序。希奥廷人对他们发动了战争。

column1: We will prove ourselves on the field of battle, and all of our weapons will be given legendary names!
column2: 我们将在战场上证明自己，我们所有的武器都将获得传奇之名！

column1: Threaten our old tribe.
column2: 威胁我们的旧部落。

column1: Saraska’s kingdom will welcome the dragonewts, so that people and dragons will live again in harmony.
column2: 萨拉斯卡的王国将欢迎龙人，让人与龙再次和谐共存。

column1: A third tribe has agreed to join us in bringing about Saraska’s kingdom. Saraska will perform the rites of kingship next season.
column2: 第三个部落已经同意加入我们，共同缔造萨拉斯卡的王国。萨拉斯卡将在下一季举行王权仪式。

column1: sceneR234
column2: sceneR234

column1: It is time to fight for Saraska’s kingdom. Among the other clans of your tribe, you take the field against the \x01Á.
column2: 是时候为萨拉斯卡的王国而战了。在你的部落其他氏族中，你率军讨伐 \x01Á.

column1: We attacked the \x01Á, in the name of Saraska’s new kingdom.
column2: 我们以萨拉斯卡新王国的名义攻击了 \x01Á, 。

column1: \x01Á surprises you with an attack on your tribal hall. The object of their attack is clearly Saraska; despite the prophecies, they want to destroy her kingdom before it is born. The clans of your tribe rush to meet them on the battlefield. There is no time for an orderly plan of battle.
column2: \x01Á 突袭了你们的部落大厅。他们的攻击目标显然是萨拉斯卡；尽管有预言，他们仍想在她的王国诞生之前毁灭它。你部落的各个氏族匆忙赶往战场迎敌。没有时间制定周密的作战计划。

column1: The \x01Á attacked us, seeking to destroy Saraska’s new kingdom before its birth.
column2: \x01Á 攻击了我们，试图在萨拉斯卡的新王国诞生之前摧毁它。

column1: Fight as honor demands, no less and no more.
column2: 按照荣誉的要求战斗，不多不少。

column1: We fought no less than, and no more than, honor demanded.
column2: 我们战斗得恰如荣誉所要求，不多不少。

column1: Our warriors fought well, taking opportunities to press ahead when they came, and retreating when necessary. They felled a number of our foes, and won the respect of our fellows without seeking undue risks.
column2: 我们的战士战斗出色，抓住时机推进，必要时撤退。他们击倒了许多敌人，没有冒不必要的风险就赢得了同伴的尊重。

column1: Our warriors fought well, taking opportunities to press ahead when they came, and retreating when necessary. Unfortunately, many of them were trapped in a ravine, and some were slain. Others were wounded. Such are the fortunes of war.
column2: 我们的战士战斗出色，抓住时机推进，必要时撤退。不幸的是，许多人被困在峡谷中，一些被杀死，另一些负伤。这就是战争的命运。

column1: We decided that it was best to risk as little as possible in this war.
column2: 我们决定在这场战争中最好尽量减少风险。

column1: We feinted and evaded. We made warlike noises. We retreated before it was necessary, and avoided risky attacks, no matter how tempting they seemed. Some of the other warriors spoke ill of us, but we started the battle as we ended it — with no warriors dead, and none badly wounded.
column2: 我们佯攻和规避。发出好战的呐喊。在必要时之前就撤退，避免任何冒险攻击，无论它们看起来多么诱人。其他一些战士对我们说三道四，但我们开始战斗时和结束时一样——没有战士阵亡，也没有人重伤。

column1: We feinted and evaded, making warlike noises but retreating before it was necessary. We avoided risky attacks, no matter how tempting. Still, the ferocious weaponthanes of the \x01@! clan trapped some of our fighters in a ravine, and slew them.
column2: 我们佯攻和规避，发出好战的呐喊但在必要时之前就撤退。我们避免任何冒险攻击，无论多么诱人。尽管如此， \x01@! 氏族的凶猛武器领主将我们的一些战士困在峡谷中并杀死了他们。

column1: Fight without quarter.
column2: 毫不留情地战斗。

column1: We fought without quarter.
column2: 我们毫不留情地战斗。

column1: Our warriors were second to none in ferocity and bravery. We felled many of our foes. We showed no mercy, and those of us who fell received none. We drew blood, and we shed blood.
column2: 我们的战士在凶猛和勇武方面首屈一指。我们砍倒了许多敌人。我们不施怜悯，倒下者也得不到怜悯。我们染血，我们也流血。

column1: Our warriors charged into the fray, shouting to the war gods and warning their foes that they would receive no mercy. Courage was with them that day, but luck was not. Warrior after warrior fell beneath the blades of our foes. Many died. Many more were wounded.
column2: 我们的战士冲入战团，向战争之神呐喊，警告敌人他们不会得到怜悯。那天他们虽有勇气，却无运气。战士一个接一个倒在敌人的刀锋下。许多人阵亡。更多人负伤。

column1: Argue for surrender.
column2: 主张投降。

column1: We argued for surrender.
column2: 我们主张投降。

column1: Saraska cursed us as cowards. She spurred her horse onwards and into the battle. The others of our tribe followed her. Honor gave us no choice but to follow.
column2: 萨拉斯卡诅咒我们是懦夫。她策马向前冲入战斗。部落中的其他人跟随她。荣誉让我们别无选择，只能跟上。

column1: Sacrifice to the war gods before battle begins.
column2: 战斗开始前向战争之神献祭。

column1: Before we did so, we sacrificed to the gods.
column2: 在此事之前，我们向诸神献祭。

column1: The god-talkers said that the omens were bad. The gods did not favor Saraska.
column2: 神言者说征兆不祥。诸神不眷顾萨拉斯卡。

column1: The god-talkers said that omens were unclear.
column2: 神言者说征兆不明。

column1: The gods will understand that we cannot afford to sacrifice to them.
column2: 诸神会理解我们无力向他们献祭。

column1: If ever an occasion demanded a generous sacrifice, it is this one.
column2: 如果说有哪个场合需要慷慨献祭，那就是现在。

column1: What would we rather see punctured — our pride, or our flesh?
column2: 我们更愿意看到什么被戳破——我们的骄傲，还是我们的身体？

column1: Saraska is in no mood to surrender.
column2: 萨拉斯卡无意投降。

column1: Saraska is in no mood to surrender. If she rides into battle, the others will follow.
column2: 萨拉斯卡无意投降。如果她冲入战斗，其他人会跟上。

column1: We are not a war clan. We do not kill things, we grow things.
column2: 我们不是一个战争氏族。我们不杀生，我们种植。

column1: Fight without quarter!
column2: 不留活口地战斗！

column1: The greater risks we take, the greater honor we gain. If we win, that is. If we lose, we will suffer more.
column2: 我们冒的风险越大，获得的荣誉越大。当然，前提是我们赢了。如果输了，我们将承受更多痛苦。

column1: The others will admire us if we fight without quarter, and will jeer at us if we fight cautiously.
column2: 如果我们不留活口地战斗，其他人会钦佩我们；如果谨慎战斗，他们会嘲笑我们。

column1: It is a good time to sacrifice to the gods.
column2: 现在是向诸神献祭的好时机。

column1: It is a bad time to sacrifice to the gods.
column2: 现在不是向诸神献祭的好时机。

column1: Are we sure that the gods favor Saraska?
column2: 我们确定诸神眷顾萨拉斯卡吗？

column1: There is no help for it. The crops will suffer from war.
column2: 无可奈何。庄稼会因战争而受损。

column1: Any fight worth fighting is worth fighting to the death.
column2: 任何值得一战的战斗都值得战至死亡。

column1: They will rue the day they aligned themselves against Saraska!
column2: 他们会后悔与萨拉斯卡为敌的日子！

column1: Shed as little blood as possible.
column2: 尽可能少流血。

column1: The sky is shot with russet clouds, as it was the day Tragic King Errarth was slain.
column2: 天空布满赤褐色的云层，正如悲剧王埃拉思被杀死的那天一样。

column1: O woe, what an awful day!
column2: 唉，多可怕的一天！

column1: By Orlanth’s klanth, it could not be a better day!
column2: 以奥兰斯的克兰斯起誓，今天再好不过了！

column1: I knew it would come to this.
column2: 我早知道会这样。

column1: sceneR235
column2: sceneR235

column1: The time has come for Saraska to undergo the Crown Test. She has created a set of magical rites that combine elements from the kingship rites of each tribe, including yours. It is a time of celebration, for this event will be remembered for all of history. There is also a sense of apprehension, for the Crown Test is sometimes dangerous, and, even though the prophecies are said to foreordain her success, some can’t help but worry about Saraska.
column2: 萨拉斯卡接受王冠试炼的时刻到了。她创造了一套魔法仪式，融合了每个部落（包括你们）的王权仪式元素。这是庆祝的时刻，因为这一事件将被载入史册。同时也有一种担忧，因为王冠试炼有时是危险的，尽管预言据说注定她会成功，但有些人还是忍不住为萨拉斯卡担心。

column1: The time came for Saraska’s Crown Test.
column2: 萨拉斯卡的王冠试炼时刻到了。

column1: What is the total value of the gifts and food you give away?
column2: 你赠送的礼物和食物的总价值是多少？

column1: The thanes accused us of being opportunists and schemers.
column2: 家臣们指责我们是机会主义者和阴谋家。

column1: Our people celebrated throughout the day. Many toasts were made in honor of the ring.
column2: 我们的人民整天庆祝。多次举杯向长老会致敬。

column1: The people were cheerless, and drank so little that the ring was saddened.
column2: 人们无精打采，喝得很少，让长老会感到忧伤。

column1: Lend your magic to aid Saraska.
column2: 借出你的魔法以协助萨拉斯卡。

column1: We decided to lend our magic to aid Saraska.
column2: 我们决定借出魔法以协助萨拉斯卡。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods in honor of Saraska.
column2: 向诸神献祭以向萨拉斯卡致敬。

column1: Secretly use your magic to hinder Saraska.
column2: 秘密使用你的魔法阻碍萨拉斯卡。

column1: The people are in a good mood. There is no need to cheer them up.
column2: 人们情绪很好。无需让他们振奋。

column1: The people are in a bad mood. They could use some cheering up.
column2: 人们情绪不佳。他们需要一些振奋。

column1: The warriors are in good spirits. They don’t need encouragement to drink and celebrate.
column2: 战士们士气高昂。他们不需要鼓励就会喝酒庆祝。

column1: The warriors are dispirited. We should celebrate with them, and do them honor.
column2: 战士们士气低落。我们应该与他们一同庆祝，以示敬意。

column1: We are already well respected in Dragon Pass, and can turn our thoughts to other matters.
column2: 我们在龙之隘口已经备受尊敬，可以转向其他事务。

column1: Our name is reviled throughout Dragon Pass. We must repair our tattered reputation.
column2: 我们的名声在整个龙之隘口遭到唾弃。我们必须修复我们破败的声誉。

column1: If prophecy dictates that Saraska will be queen, we needn’t use up our clan magic to support her. She will pass the Crown Test.
column2: 如果预言注定萨拉斯卡会成为女王，我们就不必耗尽氏族魔法来支持她。她会通过王冠试炼。

column1: We can sacrifice to the gods, gaining both the normal benefits of sacrifices, and the respect of our tribe-mates.
column2: 我们可以向诸神献祭，既获得献祭的正常好处，又得到部落同伴的尊重。

column1: When he took the throne, Good King Oskul said, “My Crown Test was hunting and killing Bad King Urgrain.”
column2: 贤王奥斯库尔登基时说：“我的王冠试炼就是猎杀恶王乌格兰。”

column1: If we improve our relations with others, our trade opportunities will increase.
column2: 如果我们改善与其他人的关系，我们的贸易机会就会增加。

column1: Good relations mean that our legal claims will be honestly entertained.
column2: 良好的关系意味着我们的法律诉讼将得到公正的审理。

column1: Let’s turn our magic against her, and see if those prophecies are really true.
column2: 让我们把魔法用来对付她，看看那些预言是否真的应验。

column1: After she passes the Crown Test, Saraska will lead the new kingdom against the loathsome elves.
column2: 通过王冠试炼后，萨拉斯卡将领导新王国对抗可憎的精灵。

column1: How can anyone even suggest that we would use bad magic against Saraska? She would pass the Crown Test, and then destroy us!
column2: 怎么会有人居然建议我们用恶魔法对付萨拉斯卡？她会通过王冠试炼，然后摧毁我们！

column1: After she passes the Crown Test, Saraska will lead us to a new era of healing and compassion.
column2: 通过王冠试炼后，萨拉斯卡将带领我们进入一个疗愈与同情的新时代。

column1: After she passes the Crown Test, Saraska will announce a great new temple building campaign.
column2: 通过王冠试炼后，萨拉斯卡将宣布一项宏伟的新神庙建造运动。

column1: After she passes the Crown Test, Saraska will forge a grand alliance with the dragonewts.
column2: 通过王冠试炼后，萨拉斯卡将与龙人缔结伟大的联盟。

column1: Something bad is going to happen.
column2: 将有坏事发生。

column1: \x01@\x01 is sent by his fellow warriors to speak to the ring. They want to quit the tribe. “We joined the tribe so that we would be strong in battle and prosperous in peace. Yet the tribe has brought us nothing but dishonor. We have tasted bitter defeat, and seen gross misrule. It is better to face the dangers of Dragon Pass as an independent clan than to heap shame upon the traditions of our ancestors.”
column2: \x01@\x01 他被战友们派去向长老会发言。他们想要脱离部落。“我们加入部落是为了在战斗中强大、在和平中繁荣。然而部落带给我们的只有耻辱。我们尝尽了惨痛的失败，目睹了严重的治理不当。与其给祖先的传统蒙羞，不如作为一个独立氏族面对龙隘的危险。”

column1: The warriors said that the tribe had brought us nothing but shame, and that we should leave it.
column2: 战士们说部落带给我们的只有耻辱，我们应该离开。

column1: Compose a poem detailing the successes of the tribe.
column2: 创作一首诗歌，详述部落的成功事迹。

column1: We composed a poem detailing the successes of the tribe.
column2: 我们创作了一首诗歌，详述部落的成功事迹。

column1: Our poem reminded them of the past glories of the tribe, and the great future that lay ahead of it. \x01@\x01 withdrew his complaint, and said that we had honored the warriors by giving them a fair hearing.
column2: 我们的诗歌让他们回想起部落昔日的荣光以及即将到来的伟大未来。 \x01@\x01 撤回了他的抱怨，并说我们通过给予战士们公平的听证而尊重了他们。

column1: “\x01@N’s kennings are usually better, \x04 choice of words bolder,” \x01@\x01 said. “Accept it; the tribe is weak inspiration for poetry because the tribe is weak. We must quit the tribe.”
column2: “\x01@N的迂回语通常更好， \x04 的措辞更大胆，” \x01@\x01 说道。“承认吧；部落是写诗的无趣灵感，因为部落本身太弱。我们必须脱离部落。”

column1: The warriors cheered our decision.
column2: 战士们为我们的决定欢呼。

column1: Tell other chieftains that your warriors are dissatisfied.
column2: 告诉其他酋长，你们的战士们心怀不满。

column1: We told the other chieftains that our warriors were dissatisfied.
column2: 我们告诉其他酋长，我们的战士们心怀不满。

column1: To prove our worth to them, they gave us gifts.
column2: 为了向他们证明我们的价值，他们给了我们礼物。

column1: When the warriors saw these gifts, they were chastened. “Our words were over-hasty,” \x01@\x01 said. “The generosity of the other chieftains shows that there is much honor in our tribe, and that we were wrong to say we should quit.”
column2: 当战士们看到这些礼物，他们感到惭愧。“我们的话过于草率，” \x01@\x01 说道。“其他酋长的慷慨表明我们的部落还有很多荣誉，我们说要脱离部落是错的。”

column1: When the warriors saw these gifts, they were thoughtful. “The other chieftains want us to stay, but are careful not to strain themselves lifting goods onto the gifting-cart. We wait and see if they better deserve our comradeship in the future.”
column2: 当战士们看到这些礼物，他们若有所思。“其他酋长希望我们留下，但他们小心翼翼避免在往礼车上搬货物时太费力。我们等着看，他们未来是否更配得上我们的同志情谊。”

column1: The other chieftains told us that we should better discipline our warriors. “You should give them more gifts, so that they do not bother you with foolish complaints.”
column2: 其他酋长告诉我们，我们应该更好地管束我们的战士。“你们应该给他们更多礼物，这样他们就不会用愚蠢的抱怨来烦你们。”

column1: “Things will get better.”
column2: “情况会好起来的。”

column1: We told them that things would get better.
column2: 我们告诉他们情况会好起来的。

column1: The warriors were convinced by our argument. \x01@\x01 withdrew his complaint, saying that they would give the tribe another chance to prove its worth to us.
column2: 战士们被我们的辩解说服了。 \x01@\x01 撤回了他的抱怨，说他们会给部落再一次机会来向我们证明其价值。

column1: “Your arguments are weak,” \x01@\x01 said. “Not because you argue poorly, but because the tribe itself is weak. You yourselves must realize that there is no good choice but to quit.”
column2: “你们的辩解很无力，” \x01@\x01 说道。“不是你们辩解得不好，而是部落本身太弱。你们自己必须意识到，除了脱离，别无良策。”

column1: Without a tribe, our cattle will be more vulnerable to raiding.
column2: 没有部落，我们的牛群将更容易遭受袭击。

column1: Do what the warriors say.
column2: 照战士们说的做。

column1: The warriors are coming to us before it is too late. We can still fix things.
column2: 战士们来找我们还为时未晚。我们还能补救。

column1: The warriors are very dissatisfied. Talk will not fix things. Only a sign of generosity from the tribe will do.
column2: 战士们非常不满。空谈无济于事。只有部落表现出的慷慨才行。

column1: A show of generosity will appease the warriors.
column2: 展示慷慨能够平息战士们的怒气。

column1: An argument is quickly forgotten, but a good poem is remembered forever.
column2: 争论很快被遗忘，但一首好诗却永垂不朽。

column1: When all the world was gone, and every man was alone, Heort went out upon the world.
column2: 当整个世界消逝，每个人孤身一人时，海尔特走出了世界。

column1: There is no surer token of reconciliation than a generous gift.
column2: 没有比慷慨的礼物更可靠的和解标志了。

column1: Sever our ties with this dishonorable tribe.
column2: 断绝与这个可耻部落的联系。

column1: We never should have joined a tribe in the first place.
column2: 我们当初就不该加入部落。

column1: If we quit the tribe, our old tribe-mates will attack us!
column2: 如果我们脱离部落，我们之前的部落同伴会攻击我们！

column1: We cannot give up now, and throw away everything we’ve built.
column2: 我们现在不能放弃，不能抛弃我们所建立的一切。

column1: We’ve been carrying this woebegone collection of clans since the day we joined!
column2: 自从加入那天起，我们一直背负着这个愁眉苦脸的氏族集合体！

column1: sceneR237
column2: sceneR237

column1: War is inevitable. The upheavals caused by Saraska’s claims will not end until she and her allies are defeated on the battlefield. Or so you tell your warriors as you prepare to attack. Among the other clans of your tribe, you take the field against the \x01Á.
column2: 战争不可避免。萨拉斯卡的主张所引发的动乱，除非她和她的盟军在战场上被击败，否则不会结束。或者，当你准备进攻时，就这样告诉你的战士们。在你的部落其他氏族中，你率军出征对抗 \x01Á.

column1: We attacked the \x01Á, to put to an end the dangerous plans of the false leader, Saraska.
column2: 我们进攻了 \x01Á, 以终结那位虚假领袖萨拉斯卡的危险计划。

column1: The \x01Á attacked us, in support of Saraska’s new kingdom.
column2: \x01Á 进攻了我们，支援萨拉斯卡的新王国。

column1: Our warriors fought well, taking opportunities to press ahead when they came, and retreating when necessary. They felled a number of our foes, and won the respect of our fellows without taking undue risks.
column2: 我们的战士们作战勇猛，抓住时机推进，必要时撤退。他们击倒了大量敌人，没有冒不必要的风险就赢得了同伴的尊重。

column1: Our warriors fought well, taking opportunities to press ahead when they came, and retreating when necessary. Unfortunately, many of them were boxed in by cruel Saraska’s warriors, and were hacked down. Some were slain; others were wounded.
column2: 我们的战士们作战勇猛，抓住时机推进，必要时撤退。不幸的是，许多人被残忍的萨拉斯卡的战士们包围，被砍倒。一些被杀，另一些受伤。

column1: We feinted and evaded. We made warlike noises. We retreated before it was necessary, and avoided risky attacks, no matter how tempting they seemed. Some of the other warriors spoke ill of us, but we started the battle as we ended it — with no warriors dead, and none seriously wounded.
column2: 我们佯攻并规避。我们发出战争喧嚣。我们在必要时之前就撤退，避免了冒险攻击，无论它们看起来多么诱人。其他一些战士说我们坏话，但我们以同样的方式开始和结束战斗——没有战士阵亡，也没有人重伤。

column1: We feinted and evaded, making warlike noises. We retreated before it was necessary, and avoided risky attacks, no matter how tempting. Still, the ferocious weaponthanes of the \x01@! clan trapped some of our fighters in a gully, and slew them. Others were wounded.
column2: 我们佯攻并规避，发出战争喧嚣。我们在必要时之前就撤退，避免了冒险攻击，无论多么诱人。然而， \x01@! 氏族的凶猛武器领主将我们的一些战士困在沟壑中并杀死了他们。另一些受伤。

column1: Our warriors were second to none in ferocity and bravery. We felled many of our foes. We showed no mercy, and those of us who fell received none. We drew blood, and we shed it.
column2: 我们的战士在凶猛和勇敢上无人能及。我们砍倒了众多敌人。我们毫不留情，那些倒下的人也未得到怜悯。我们流血，也令敌人流血。

column1: The other clans agreed that this was the best option. We swore to support Saraska and help make her kingdom. She accepted our pledge of fealty, and said she would go to seek another tribe to join with us.
column2: 其他氏族一致认为这是最佳选择。我们宣誓支持萨拉斯卡，并助她建立王国。她接受了我们的效忠誓言，并表示将去寻找另一个部落与我们联合。

column1: The other clans refused to surrender. They promised to fight Saraska, who sought to steal their freedom from them. Honor gave us no choice but to fight with the rest of our tribe.
column2: 其他氏族拒绝投降。他们发誓要与企图剥夺他们自由的萨拉斯卡作战。荣誉让我们别无选择，只能与部落其余人一同战斗。

column1: The god-talkers said that the omens were good. The gods did not favor Saraska after all.
column2: 神言者说征兆吉利。诸神终究并不眷顾萨拉斯卡。

column1: The god-talkers said that omens were bad. The gods surely favored Saraska.
column2: 神言者说征兆不祥。诸神显然眷顾萨拉斯卡。

column1: If Saraska is false, there is no need to sacrifice to assure her doom. If she is true, no sacrifice will aid us.
column2: 若萨拉斯卡是假的，无需献祭来确保她的覆灭。若她是真的，任何献祭也帮不了我们。

column1: Saraska’s fate may be in the hands of the gods, but if sacrifice will protect our warriors, we should do it.
column2: 萨拉斯卡的命运或许掌握在诸神手中，但如果献祭能保护我们的战士，我们就该去做。

column1: The others will mock us if we suggest surrender now.
column2: 如果现在提议投降，其他人会嘲笑我们。

column1: The others respect us. They will consider surrender if we advise it.
column2: 其他人尊重我们。如果我们建议投降，他们会考虑。

column1: They will rue the day they aligned themselves with Saraska!
column2: 他们会后悔与萨拉斯卡结盟的那一天！

column1: When Lokamayadon usurped the rightful worship of Orlanth, everything went bad. But Harmast Barefoot risked all to quest for the hero Arkat, who destroyed the usurper.
column2: 当洛卡玛亚顿篡夺了奥兰斯合法的崇拜时，一切便变得糟糕。但哈马斯特·赤足冒着一切风险去寻找英雄阿尔卡特，后者摧毁了篡位者。

column1: Saraska is the worst of tyrants. The only way to assure her death is to fight without quarter.
column2: 萨拉斯卡是最残暴的暴君。确保她死亡的唯一方法就是毫不留情地战斗。

column1: We don’t want to be mocked by others. Then again, we don’t want to die in droves, either.
column2: 我们不想被他人嘲笑。但话说回来，我们也不想成群地死去。

column1: There is a time to fight, that time is now. Even peace clans must be ready to defend themselves with honor!
column2: 战斗有时，此刻正是其时。即便是和平氏族也必须准备好以荣誉自卫！

column1: I feel the wrath of Orlanth singing in my blood!
column2: 我感到奥兰斯的怒火在血脉中歌唱！

column1: It is time to rid the world of this pest.
column2: 是时候将这种害虫从世间清除了。

column1: Warriors of our clan were present when Saraska was brought down to meet her inevitable fate.
column2: 当萨拉斯卡被击倒，迎来她不可避免的宿命时，我们氏族的战士在场。

column1: sceneR238
column2: sceneR238

column1: Near death, the hero Derik Furman is borne into your clan hall. “He slew Jaldon Goldentooth, the great Praxian incarnation of death, and buried him beneath a cairn of skulls. But the blows Jaldon dealt to him took their toll soon after he did so, and Derik has not regained consciousness since. Since you were not willing to aid him in his fight, we ask that you help him now.”
column2: 英雄德里克·弗曼濒临死亡，被抬进你们的部族大厅。“他杀死了贾尔顿·金牙——伟大的普拉克斯死亡化身，并将其埋葬在颅骨石冢之下。但贾尔顿给他造成的创伤在他完成此事后不久便发作，德里克自此再未恢复意识。既然你们当初不愿在战斗中援助他，我们现在请求你们此刻帮助他。”

column1: Near death, the hero Derik Furman is borne into your clan hall. “He slew Jaldon Goldentooth, the great Praxian incarnation of death, and buried him beneath a cairn of skulls. But the blows Jaldon dealt to him took their toll soon after he did so, and Derik has not regained consciousness since.”
column2: 英雄德里克·弗曼濒临死亡，被抬进你们的部族大厅。“他杀死了贾尔顿·金牙——伟大的普拉克斯死亡化身，并将其埋葬在颅骨石冢之下。但贾尔顿给他造成的创伤在他完成此事后不久便发作，德里克自此再未恢复意识。”

column1: Derik Furman’s warriors brought him into our clan hall, gravely wounded. He had slain Jaldon Goldentooth.
column2: 德里克·弗曼的战士们将他重伤抬入我们的部族大厅。他杀死了贾尔顿·金牙。

column1: The mercenaries your gifts helped hire were instrumental in defeating Jaldon’s Praxian raiders.
column2: 你们馈赠所雇佣的佣兵在击败贾尔顿的普拉克斯袭击者中发挥了关键作用。

column1: The warriors you sent were instrumental in defeating Jaldon’s Praxian raiders.
column2: 你们派去的战士在击败贾尔顿的普拉克斯袭击者中发挥了关键作用。

column1: All of them were slain.
column2: 他们全部阵亡。

column1: Half of them were slain. The others were wounded.
column2: 他们半数阵亡。其余人受伤。

column1: A third of them were slain. The others were wounded. They considered themselves lucky to be back at all
column2: 他们三分之一阵亡。其余人受伤。他们觉得自己能回来已是幸运。

column1: A quarter of them were slain. The others were wounded. They considered themselves lucky to be back.
column2: 他们四分之一阵亡。其余人受伤。他们觉得自己能回来已是幸运。

column1: They all returned, but each of them had suffered serious wounds.
column2: 他们全部归来，但每人都受了重伤。

column1: The magic you lent them was instrumental in defeating Jaldon’s nomad shamans.
column2: 你们借出的魔法在击败贾尔顿的游牧萨满中发挥了关键作用。

column1: Send for Chalana Arroy priestesses to heal Derik.
column2: 派人去找查拉娜·阿罗伊女祭司来医治德里克。

column1: We sent for Chalana Arroy priestesses to heal Derik.
column2: 我们派人去找查拉娜·阿罗伊女祭司来医治德里克。

column1: There were no priestesses to be found; Jaldon’s raids had wounded hundreds of people, so no healers could be spared for the one who had laid him to rest. Derik remained unconscious for close to a season.
column2: 找不到女祭司；贾尔顿的袭击让数百人受伤，因此没有治疗者能匀给这位安葬死亡化身的人。德里克昏迷了近一个季节。

column1: Priestesses were hard to find; Jaldon’s raids had wounded hundreds of people, so they were in great demand. But we found one healer willing to treat the one who had laid death’s champion to rest. Derik regained consciousness a few days after the treatment. Within a week, he was able to stand. Within two weeks, he was able to spar with his warrior companions.
column2: 女祭司很难找；贾尔顿的袭击让数百人受伤，因此她们极为抢手。但我们找到一位愿意治疗这位安葬死亡化身之人的治疗者。德里克在治疗后几天恢复了意识。一周之内，他能站立。两周之内，他能与战友对练。

column1: Tell Derik’s followers to take him elsewhere.
column2: 告诉德里克的追随者带他去别处。

column1: We told Derik’s followers to take him elsewhere.
column2: 我们告诉德里克的追随者带他去别处。

column1: They did so, although it made them unhappy. Our warriors complained that we had no honor.
column2: 他们照做了，尽管很不情愿。我们的战士抱怨我们没有荣誉。

column1: Tend to Derik as he recovers.
column2: 在德里克康复期间照料他。

column1: We tended to him as he recovered. He remained unconscious for close to a season.
column2: 我们在其康复期间照料了他。他昏迷了近一个季节。

column1: Tend to Derik; allow his followers to stay here until he recovers.
column2: 照料德里克；允许他的追随者留在这里直到他康复。

column1: We tended to Derik, and allowed his followers to stay until he recovered.
column2: 我们照料了德里克，并允许他的追随者留下直到他康复。

column1: Derik remained unconscious for close to a season. During that time, his many followers ate heartily.
column2: 德里克昏迷了近一个季节。在那段时间里，他的众多追随者吃掉了大量食物。

column1: Try to magically heal Derik.
column2: 尝试用魔法治疗德里克。

column1: We tried to magically heal Derik.
column2: 我们尝试用魔法治疗德里克。

column1: His condition showed no improvement. He remained unconscious for close to a season.
column2: 他的状况毫无起色。他昏迷了将近一个季节。

column1: He regained consciousness a few days later. Within a week, he was able to stand. Within two weeks, he was able to spar with his warrior companions.
column2: 几天后他恢复了意识。一周内他就能站立。两周内，他已能与战友对练。

column1: The carls are afraid that Derik’s companions will misbehave.
column2: 自由民担心德里克的同伴会惹是生非。

column1: The carls are afraid that Derik’s companions will misbehave, but I think it is just harmless grumbling.
column2: 自由民担心德里克的同伴会惹是生非，但我认为那不过是无害的抱怨。

column1: The carls are in a bad mood already, and will be displeased to see Derik’s scruffy companions eating us out of house and home.
column2: 自由民本已心情不佳，看到德里克那帮邋遢的同伴把咱们吃个精光，肯定会不高兴。

column1: Derik caused much death; no Chalana Arroy priestesses will help him.
column2: 德里克造成了大量死亡；没有查拉娜·阿罗伊女祭司会帮他。

column1: Jaldon’s raids wounded many; all of our neighbors’ Chalana Arroy priestesses will be busy tending to them.
column2: 贾尔登的袭击伤了许多人；我们所有邻居的查拉娜·阿罗伊女祭司都会忙于照料他们。

column1: Throughout Dragon Pass, Chalana Arroy priestesses will be busy tending to those wounded by Jaldon’s raids. Still, we can convince one to come to heal the one who slew death’s champion.
column2: 整个龙隘的查拉娜·阿罗伊女祭司都会忙于照料被贾尔登袭击所伤的人。不过，我们仍能说服一位来医治那位斩杀了死亡勇士的人。

column1: The warriors will be furious if we send Derik elsewhere.
column2: 如果我们把德里克送到别处，战士们会怒不可遏。

column1: The warriors will be glad if we entertain Derik’s companions while he recovers.
column2: 如果我们在他恢复期间款待德里克的同伴，战士们会很高兴。

column1: If we raid someone while Derik recovers, his thirty worthy companions will help us fight.
column2: 如果我们在德里克恢复期间袭击某人，他那三十位可敬的同伴会帮我们作战。

column1: Derik was wounded by a manifestation of death; he will not recover.
column2: 德里克被死亡的化身所伤；他无法康复。

column1: Magical healing is the only way.
column2: 魔法治疗是唯一的办法。

column1: Our magic is strong. We should try to heal him ourselves.
column2: 我们的魔法很强。我们应该自己试着治疗他。

column1: Our magic is weak. There is no point in trying to heal him ourselves.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱。自己尝试治疗毫无意义。

column1: In the battle between Humakt and Wakboth, the Devil bit the Sword God in half, and cast the pieces aside. This wound would have killed anyone lesser than Humakt, and even he was not able to fight any more that day.
column2: 在胡马克特与瓦克博斯的战斗中，魔鬼将剑神咬成两半，并将碎片丢弃。这伤势足以杀死任何不如胡马克特者，就连他那天也无法再战。

column1: Let us make no more war.
column2: 让我们不再开战。

column1: Don’t let those mischievous bulls of his cause any trouble.
column2: 别让他那些顽劣的蛮牛惹麻烦。

column1: Jaldon was an undead monster. We must do all we can for the one who slew him.
column2: 贾尔登是不死怪物。我们必须为斩杀他的人竭尽全力。

column1: It is a good thing Jaldon was not a woman, or Derik would not have beaten him.
column2: 幸好贾尔登不是女人，否则德里克打不过他。

column1: Send for priestesses.
column2: 派人去请女祭司。

column1: We should have done more when he asked us for help.
column2: 他向我们求助时，我们本应做得更多。

column1: sceneR239
column2: sceneR239

column1: Derik, now recovered from his wounds, prepares to leave. “I can never thank you properly for all you have done for me. When I was a child, this clan protected me. When my battle with Jaldon made me weaker than a child, you brought me back to health. We go now, down to Prax, where we will take the battle to the nomads. But before we leave, I wish to give you a gift. What shall it be?”
column2: 德里克伤愈后准备离开。“我永远无法恰当地感谢你们为我所做的一切。小时候，这个氏族保护了我。当与贾尔登的决斗让我比孩童还虚弱时，你们让我恢复健康。现在我们出发，前往普拉克斯，将战火引向游牧民。但在离开前，我想赠你们一份礼物。想要什么？”

column1: Derik left us, but before he went he offered us a gift.
column2: 德里克离开了我们，但走之前他主动提出赠礼。

column1: Ask for a treasure.
column2: 索要一件宝物。

column1: We asked for a treasure.
column2: 我们索要了一件宝物。

column1: Derik gave us a Hunting Horn, one which would help us find what we sought.
column2: 德里克给了我们一只狩猎号角，它能帮助我们找到所追寻之物。

column1: Ask for cattle.
column2: 索要牛只。

column1: We asked for cattle.
column2: 我们索要了牛只。

column1: “I have no cattle to give,” Derik said. “But I aim to create a new tribe, the horse people, and we will raid the raiders. When we do so, I will see that some of the spoils are spent to buy you cattle.”
column2: “我没有牛可以给，”德里克说，“但我计划创建一个新部落——骑马民族，我们要劫掠那些劫掠者。届时，我会确保将部分战利品用于为你们购买牛只。”

column1: Ask for magic.
column2: 索要魔法。

column1: We asked for magic.
column2: 我们索要了魔法。

column1: Magic he gave us.
column2: 他给了我们魔法。

column1: Ask for silver.
column2: 索要白银。

column1: We asked for silver.
column2: 我们索要了白银。

column1: Silver he gave us.
column2: 他给了我们白银。

column1: “You have given us enough of a gift already, by destroying Jaldon.”
column2: “你们已经给了我们足够的礼物，那就是消灭贾尔登。”

column1: We said, “You have given us enough of a gift already, by destroying Jaldon.”
column2: 我们说：“你们已经给了我们足够的礼物，那就是消灭贾尔登。”

column1: Tears appeared in the great warrior’s eyes. “Clan of my birth, again you honor me.” He dried his eyes and extemporized a song. He sang it in an unearthly voice, and it was about our clan and his love for us. It was not long before clans throughout Dragon Pass were singing this song. Most of them changed it so that it was about their clans, but they still knew which clan the song was really about.
column2: 伟大战士的眼中涌出泪水。“生我养我的氏族，你们再次给予我荣耀。”他擦干眼泪，即兴创作了一首歌。他用超凡的嗓音唱了出来，歌词是关于我们的氏族和他对我们的爱。不久，整个龙隘的氏族都在传唱这首歌。大多数氏族将其改为关于他们自己的氏族，但他们仍知道这首歌真正唱的是哪个氏族。

column1: Cows! Ask for cows!
column2: 牛！要牛！

column1: He is a raider. He has no cows with him.
column2: 他是个劫掠者。他身边没有牛。

column1: He is a raider. He has no cows with him. After a while, he may be able to send us some.
column2: 他是个劫掠者。他身边没有牛。过一段时间，他或许能送一些给我们。

column1: Think of silver as an easily-portable cow that does not moo.
column2: 把白银看作是不会哞哞叫、便于携带的牛。

column1: A treasure owned by a mighty warrior would help us greatly.
column2: 一位强大战士拥有的宝物能大大帮助我们。

column1: I have heard that Derik is very successful in catching those he chases, even when they hide. Perhaps his treasure would allow us to do the same.
column2: 我听说德里克在追捕目标时非常成功，即便他们躲藏起来。或许他的宝物能让我们也做到同样的事。

column1: He has already done enough for Dragon Pass, by slaying one of its worst enemies.
column2: 他通过杀死龙隘最凶恶的敌人之一，已经为龙隘做得够多了。

column1: He is a great warrior. Maybe he has mighty magic.
column2: 他是一位伟大的战士。也许他拥有强大的魔法。

column1: By defeating the champion of death, he gained great magic. It would be good if we could get him to share it with us.
column2: 通过击败死亡勇士，他获得了强大的魔法。如果他能与我们分享，那就太好了。

column1: Before Orlanth went on the Lightbringers Quest, he called his kings and heroes and priests together. He gave them sacred gifts, and they gifted him with magical tools.
column2: 在奥兰斯踏上光明使者追寻之前，他召集了他的诸王、英雄和祭司。他赠予他们神圣的礼物，他们也回赠他魔法工具。

column1: Ask for a treasure; it’s the best deal.
column2: 要一件宝物；这是最划算的。

column1: Ask for an elf-smashing treasure.
column2: 要一件能砸碎精灵的宝物。

column1: His blessing alone would edge us closer to the crown.
column2: 仅凭他的祝福就能让我们更接近王冠。

column1: Cows are the only useful gift.
column2: 牛只是唯一有用的礼物。

column1: We need Derik’s war-like, masculine magic, to counteract all of the simpering female magic we get around here.
column2: 我们需要德里克那好战、阳刚的魔法，来抵消我们这里处处可见的娇柔女性魔法。

column1: I told you he’d give us gifts if we treated him right.
column2: 我告诉过你，如果我们对他好，他就会给我们礼物。

column1: Derik Furman, who was born into our clan but now leads his own tribe, has fulfilled his promise, and sent us five milk cows. His thane, Varmath Rhinobane, said we could expect the same next Fire season.
column2: 德里克·弗曼，生于我们的氏族，但如今领导着自己的部落，兑现了承诺，送来了五头奶牛。他的领主瓦马斯·犀牛灾说，下个火之季我们还能期待同样的礼物。

column1: sceneR240
column2: sceneR240

column1: Comfort Derik.
column2: 安慰德里克。

column1: We tried to comfort Derik.
column2: 我们试图安慰德里克。

column1: He said, “I will not be comforted until I am a man, and I have brought the raiders low.”
column2: 他说：“在我成为一个男人、把袭击者击垮之前，我不会接受安慰。”

column1: Compose a poem in honor of the slain.
column2: 创作一首诗悼念死者。

column1: We composed a poem in honor of the slain.
column2: 我们创作了一首悼念死者的诗。

column1: The people praised our poem, which gave them some cheer in a time of mourning.
column2: 人们称赞我们的诗，在哀悼之时给了他们些许慰藉。

column1: \x01@N could not properly capture the sorrow of this event, and did not share our poem with the others.
column2: \x01@N 未能恰当捕捉此事的悲伤，便没有将我们的诗与他人分享。

column1: The god-talkers said that the signs were unclear.
column2: 神言者说征兆不明。

column1: The god-talkers said that Derik would grow to be strong and wise. He would leave us, and would become known as a great hero. He would bring death to a deathbringer, laying him under a cairn of skulls. He would found a new people, a nation of outsiders, and would bring honor to the clan.
column2: 神言者说德里克将会长大，变得强大而智慧。他会离开我们，成为闻名遐迩的伟大英雄。他会给一个带来死亡者带去死亡，将他埋葬在头骨堆成的石冢之下。他会创建一个新的民族，一个外来者的国度，并为氏族带来荣誉。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods for protection from Praxians.
column2: 向众神献祭以求保护免受普拉克斯人的侵害。

column1: We sacrificed to the gods for protection from Praxians.
column2: 我们向众神献祭以求保护免受普拉克斯人的侵害。

column1: The god-talkers said that the signs were unclear. It was hard to know if the gods had heard our entreaties.
column2: 神言者说征兆不明。很难知道众神是否听到了我们的恳求。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were good. The gods would shield us from desert raiders.
column2: 神言者说征兆良好。众神会庇护我们免受沙漠袭击者的侵害。

column1: Send a war party to kill Sable Riders.
column2: 派遣一支战团去杀死黑貂骑手。

column1: We sent a war party to kill Sable Riders.
column2: 我们派遣了一支战团去杀死黑貂骑手。

column1: They scoured Dragon Pass for the raiders, but they were not to be found.
column2: 他们搜遍龙之隘口寻找袭击者，却一无所获。

column1: They found and battled the desert raiders.
column2: 他们找到并迎战了沙漠袭击者。

column1: Our fierce warriors shouted the names of the slain as they pulled the nomads from their beasts and cut their throats. We recovered the loot they had pillaged, and more.
column2: 我们凶猛的战士高喊着死者的名字，将游牧民从他们的坐骑上拽下，割开他们的喉咙。我们夺回了他们抢掠的财物，甚至更多。

column1: Our fierce warriors shouted the names of the slain as they charged the nomads. From atop their peculiar beasts, the raiders slashed at our fighters, wounding some. They fled, and we could not give proper chase to them.
column2: 我们凶猛的战士高喊着死者的名字冲向游牧民。袭击者从他们奇异的坐骑上挥砍我们的战士，伤了一些人。他们逃走了，我们未能有效追击。

column1: We are too poor to sacrifice.
column2: 我们太穷了，无法献祭。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice.
column2: 我们负担得起献祭。

column1: The Sable Riders are our friends. How could they do this to us?
column2: 黑貂骑手是我们的朋友。他们怎么能这样对我们？

column1: Sable Riders are tough opponents, who strike and run. The leader of the war party must be a good hunter, as well as a good fighter.
column2: 黑貂骑手是难缠的对手，打了就跑。战团的首领必须既是好猎手，也是好战士。

column1: Send our best hunter and six weaponthanes to kill Sable Riders.
column2: 派出我们最好的猎手和六名武器领主去杀死黑貂骑手。

column1: We must comfort Derik by burying him in a mound of earth for sixteen days.
column2: 我们必须通过将德里克埋入土丘十六天来安慰他。

column1: Revenge.
column2: 复仇。

column1: The people are disheartened. We must do something to cheer them up.
column2: 人们灰心丧气。我们必须做点什么让他们振作起来。

column1: The people are disheartened. We must do something to cheer them up. We should try a poem, for a failed poem doesn’t carry the consequences of a failed raid.
column2: 人们灰心丧气。我们必须做点什么让他们振作起来。我们应该尝试一首诗，因为一首失败的诗不会像一次失败的袭击那样带来后果。

column1: We should sacrifice.
column2: 我们应该献祭。

column1: It is a good time to sacrifice, or conduct a divination.
column2: 现在是献祭或进行占卜的好时机。

column1: It is a bad time to sacrifice, or conduct a divination.
column2: 现在是献祭或进行占卜的坏时机。

column1: Our ancestors cry for blood!
column2: 我们的祖先渴求鲜血！

column1: The carls feel sad for Derik, but let’s not get carried away. We still have to plant the crops.
column2: 自由民为德里克感到难过，但我们别太激动。我们还得播种庄稼。

column1: The carls feel sad for Derik, but let’s not get carried away. We still have to harvest the crops.
column2: 自由民为德里克感到难过，但我们别太激动。我们还得收割庄稼。

column1: Derik will achieve his vengeance, and become a great hero in doing so.
column2: 德里克将实现他的复仇，并因此成为伟大的英雄。

column1: The Praxians, led by death’s champion, Jaldon Goldentooth, helped start the Dragonkill War. Jaldon brought 100,000 warriors from Prax to destroy the dragonewt nesting places.
column2: 在死亡化身贾尔顿·金牙的率领下，普拉克斯人协助发动了屠龙战争。贾尔顿从普拉克斯带来了十万勇士，去摧毁龙人的巢穴。

column1: Comfort him.
column2: 安慰他。

column1: Kill Sable Riders!
column2: 杀死黑貂骑手！

column1: Praxians are enemies of the dragonewts, and so must die!
column2: 普拉克斯人是龙人的敌人，所以他们必须死！

column1: Vengeance brings nothing but more vengeance.
column2: 复仇只会带来更多的复仇。

column1: A family traveling without protection? They were doomed.
column2: 一个没有保护的家族上路？他们注定灭亡。

column1: Our sacrifices would be stronger if our temples were better.
column2: 如果我们的神庙更好，我们的献祭会更强大。

column1: Elmal, the Defender, will grant us strength.
column2: 守护者埃尔玛尔会赐予我们力量。

column1: Track them, kill them.
column2: 追踪他们，杀死他们。

column1: Derik the Praxian-Hater
column2: 德里克·恨帕克西安者

column1: sceneR241
column2: sceneR241

column1: Derik, whose family was slain by Sable Riders, became a singleminded young warrior, unpopular with the older \x01@\x17s.
column2: 德里克，其家人被黑貂骑手杀害，变成了一个一心一意的年轻战士，不受年长 \x01@\x17们喜欢。

column1: Praise Derik’s pride and stubbornness.
column2: 赞扬德里克的骄傲和固执。

column1: We praised Derik’s pride and stubbornness.
column2: 我们赞扬了德里克的骄傲和固执。

column1: The other \x01@\x17s realized that what they saw as Derik’s faults were in fact his virtues.
column2: 其他 \x01@\x17们意识到，他们曾视为德里克缺点的东西，实际上正是他的美德。

column1: The \x01@\x17s grumbled.
column2: \x01@\x17们抱怨道。

column1: Scold Derik for his pride and stubbornness.
column2: 责备德里克的骄傲和固执。

column1: We scolded Derik for his pride and stubbornness.
column2: 我们责备了德里克的骄傲和固执。

column1: Derik said he would try to be more like us from now on. The other \x01@\x17s thought they would be happy to see him humbled, but instead they were ashamed, and blamed us for scolding him.
column2: 德里克说，从今以后他会努力变得更像我们。其他 \x01@\x17们本以为看到他被羞辱会高兴，但他们反而感到羞愧，并责怪我们训斥了他。

column1: Derik laughed grimly, and said, “Do not trouble yourselves with me, for I will not be with you much longer.” The \x01@\x17s were offended by his impertinence.
column2: 德里克苦笑着，说道：“不必为我烦心，因为我与你们相处的时间不多了。” \x01@\x17们被他的无礼冒犯了。

column1: Send Derik on a raid against Sable Riders.
column2: 派德里克去袭击黑貂骑手。

column1: We sent Derik on a raid against Sable Riders.
column2: 我们派德里克去袭击黑貂骑手。

column1: How many warriors accompany him?
column2: 有多少战士与他同行？

column1: Tell the \x01@\x17s to let him be.
column2: 告诉 \x01@\x17们随他去吧。

column1: We told the \x01@\x17s to let him be.
column2: 我们告诉 \x01@\x17们随他去了。

column1: They remembered that pride is an Orlanthi virtue, and not a fault. They promised to cease their grumbling, and look to Derik as a model of good behavior.
column2: 他们记起骄傲是奥兰斯美德，而非缺点。他们承诺停止抱怨，并将德里克视为良好行为的典范。

column1: We reminded them that pride is an Orlanthi virtue, and not a fault. We discovered that the warriors were unhappy about many other things; their true quarrels were with the clan ring.
column2: 我们提醒他们，骄傲是奥兰斯美德，而非缺点。我们发现战士们对许多其他事情感到不满；他们真正的争执是针对氏族议会。

column1: Derik’s behavior has offended everyone!
column2: 德里克的行为冒犯了所有人！

column1: The complaints of the \x01@\x17s are not serious.
column2: \x01@\x17们的抱怨并不严重。

column1: The \x01@\x17s are really upset about other things.
column2: \x01@\x17们对别的事情真的很不满。

column1: Derik does not display the proper virtues of humility and obedience.
column2: 德里克并未展现出谦逊与服从的应有美德。

column1: Pride is an Orlanthi virtue.
column2: 骄傲是奥兰斯美德。

column1: Derik is young, but he is determined. He is ready to lead.
column2: 德里克虽然年轻，但意志坚定。他已准备好领导。

column1: Derik is young, but determined and skillful. He is ready to lead; his hatred of the Sable Riders will assure success.
column2: 德里克虽然年轻，但意志坚定且技艺精湛。他已准备好领导；他对黑貂骑手的仇恨将确保胜利。

column1: The \x01@\x17s are forgetting what it is like to be young. Also, they lack Derik’s passion for vengeance.
column2: \x01@\x17们忘记了年轻是什么样子。而且，他们缺乏德里克那样的复仇激情。

column1: Why are we troubling ourselves with \x01@\x17 squabbles during Sea season?
column2: 我们为何要在海之季为 \x01@\x17 们的争吵自寻烦恼？

column1: Why are we troubling ourselves with \x01@\x17 squabbles during Earth season?
column2: 我们为何要在地季为 \x01@\x17 们的争吵自寻烦恼？

column1: After his initiation, Orlanth was not content with the way that things were. He felt he too deserved a part of the leadership of the world, but his desires were refused by the Emperor.
column2: 在成年礼之后，奥兰斯并不满足于现状。他觉得自己也应分得世界领导权的一部分，但他的愿望被皇帝拒绝了。

column1: His hatred is like a disease inside him.
column2: 他的仇恨就像他体内的疾病。

column1: It is good to see a fine young bull testing himself and others.
column2: 看到一头优秀的年轻公牛考验自己和他人，是件好事。

column1: Condemn his pride and stubbornness! Next thing you know, young Orlanthi will become rebellious and violent!
column2: 谴责他的骄傲和固执！接下来，年轻的奥兰斯人就会变得叛逆和暴力！

column1: He must stop and learn to read. That will teach him wisdom.
column2: 他必须停下来学习阅读。那会教他智慧。

column1: Fuelled by hate-heat, his heart-fires burn.
column2: 被仇恨之热所驱动，他的心中之火在燃烧。

column1: The other clans will not make a tribe with us if we are known for indulging troublemakers.
column2: 如果我们以纵容惹事者而闻名，其他氏族就不会与我们结为部落。

column1: Let him prove himself on a daring raid!
column2: 让他通过一次大胆的袭击证明自己！

column1: We look at what has happened, and afterwards we say it was destiny.
column2: 我们审视所发生的事，事后才说这是命运。

column1: Derik is back, triumphant. He led our warriors to a Sable Rider encampment, where he slew many and pillaged their goods. None of our warriors were so much as scratched in the fight.
column2: 德里克回来了，大获全胜。他带领我们的战士来到一处黑貂骑手的营地，在那里他斩杀多人，并掠夺了他们的财物。我们的战士在战斗中毫发无伤。

column1: Derik is back, elated. He and our
column2: 德里克回来了，兴高采烈。他和我们的

column1: warriors snuck up on a Sable Rider encampment
column2: 战士们悄悄靠近一处黑貂骑手的营地

column1: warrior snuck up on a Sable Rider encampment
column2: 战士悄悄靠近一处黑貂骑手的营地

column1: and caused much mischief before sneaking away again. They cut the traces on the Sable Riders’ mounts, and scattered their herd animals. They punched holes in waterskins and loosened every knot they could find. No one saw them, and they managed to steal a few goods while they were there.
column2: 造成了许多恶作剧，然后才悄悄溜走。他们割断了黑貂骑手坐骑的缰绳，驱散了他们的牧群。他们在水囊上戳洞，并解松了他们能找到的每一个绳结。没人看见他们，他们还趁机偷了一些财物。

column1: sceneR242
column2: sceneR242

column1: Derik Single-Path, who has distinguished himself in many raids, comes before the clan ring and says that he is leaving. “I thank you for raising me and making me a good Orlanthi. Now I must move on, for I have become as strong as I can among a clan of Dragon Pass. I must go out into the world and find new tests for myself, so I can strengthen my powers against the misbegotten raiders of Prax. I ask now for your blessing, before I go.”
column2: 德里克·单径，在多场袭击中表现卓著，来到氏族议会前说他即将离开。“感谢你们养育了我，使我成为一个优秀的奥兰斯人。现在我必须前行，因为在龙之山峰的氏族中我已变得足够强大。我必须走向世界，为自己寻找新的考验，以便增强我的力量，对抗普拉克斯那些卑劣的侵袭者。在离开之前，我请求你们的祝福。”

column1: Derik Single-Path told us he was leaving to seek new challenges.
column2: 德里克·单径告诉我们他要离开去寻找新的挑战。

column1: Give Derik a parting gift.
column2: 给德里克一份临别礼物。

column1: We gave him a parting gift.
column2: 我们给了他一份临别礼物。

column1: What do you give him?
column2: 你给他什么？

column1: He thanked us for our generosity. “Perhaps one day we will meet again,” he said.
column2: 他感谢我们的慷慨。“也许有一天我们会再相见，”他说。

column1: Give him permission to leave.
column2: 允许他离开。

column1: We gave him permission to leave.
column2: 我们允许他离开。

column1: “Perhaps one day we will meet again,” he said.
column2: “也许有一天我们会再相见，”他说。

column1: Persuade him to stay.
column2: 劝说他留下。

column1: We tried to convince him to stay.
column2: 我们试图说服他留下。

column1: “I am flattered that you want me to remain,” he said, “but the name you have given me, Single-Path, tells the story. I have a different path to walk than the rest of you. Perhaps, one day, that path will cross yours again.” Then he took his leave of us.
column2: “你们想让我留下，我很荣幸，”他说，“但你们赐予我的名字——单径，已说明了一切。我有与众不同的道路要走。也许有一天，那条路会与你们的交汇。”然后他辞别了我们。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods to protect Derik on his travels.
column2: 向众神献祭，以保护德里克旅途平安。

column1: We sacrificed to the gods to protect Derik on his travels.
column2: 我们向众神献祭，以保护德里克旅途平安。

column1: He thanked us for our generosity. “The things I will do, I will do not only for vengeance, but to honor you and honor our gods,” he said. “Perhaps one day we will meet again, and I will have accomplishments to share with you.”
column2: 他感谢我们的慷慨。“我所做之事，不仅为复仇，更为尊崇你们与我们的神明，”他说，“或许有朝一日我们重逢，届时我必有功业与你们分享。”

column1: Give him a parting magical blessing.
column2: 赐予他临别魔法祝福。

column1: We gave him a parting magical blessing.
column2: 我们赐予了他临别魔法祝福。

column1: How great a blessing?
column2: 祝福何等深厚？

column1: A token blessing.
column2: 象征性的祝福。

column1: A small blessing.
column2: 微小的祝福。

column1: A generous blessing.
column2: 慷慨的祝福。

column1: All of your clan magic.
column2: 倾尽氏族全部魔法。

column1: He thanked us for our generosity. “Your blessings will aid me in my journey. It will be a long one, because I do not know exactly what I am looking for. Perhaps, after I find it, I will come back here and tell you what it was.” Then he took his leave of us.
column2: 他感谢我们的慷慨。“你们的祝福将助我旅途。这旅途漫长，因我尚不明所寻之物。或许寻得之后，我会回到此地，告知你们那是什么。”随后他辞别了我们。

column1: He is going away. We’ll never see any benefit from the gifts we give him.
column2: 他就要走了。我们赠予他的礼物永无回报。

column1: Although we’ll never see any benefit from the gifts we give him, we’re rich enough to make the gesture anyway.
column2: 尽管我们赠他的礼物永无回报，但我们足够富足，仍可作此表示。

column1: He wants to stay, and forget this silly crusade against the nomads.
column2: 他想留下，忘却这场对抗游牧民的愚蠢征讨。

column1: It will be hard to convince him to stay. He knows his destiny is elsewhere.
column2: 说服他留下会很难。他知道自己的命运在别处。

column1: It will be impossible to convince him to stay. He knows his destiny is elsewhere.
column2: 说服他留下绝无可能。他知道自己的命运在别处。

column1: A lone traveler faces many dangers in untamed Dragon Pass.
column2: 独行旅人在未经驯服的龙之隘口将面临诸多危险。

column1: Although he is headstrong and not always obedient, the people have come to love his pride and fervor. The more generous we are with him, the happier they will be.
column2: 尽管他固执且不总顺从，但民众已爱上他的骄傲与热忱。我们待他越慷慨，他们便越欢喜。

column1: He will need powerful magic to achieve his lofty goals.
column2: 他需要强大的魔法来实现其崇高目标。

column1: If we sacrifice to the gods, they will protect Derik and bless us at the same time.
column2: 若我们向众神献祭，他们将护佑德里克并同时赐福我们。

column1: When Orlanth began his great journey, many friends came to see him off, wishing him well and giving him their prayers and hopes.
column2: 当奥兰斯踏上伟大征途时，众多友朋前来送行，祝他安好，献上祈祷与期盼。

column1: Like a troll coin, he’ll be back.
column2: 如同巨魔钱币，他定会归来。

column1: I wish I was going with him!
column2: 真希望我与他同行！

column1: He should seek the help of the dragonewts, who ate many foul Praxians during the Dragonkill War.

column1: They offer you \x01@\x1A cows. Do you accept?
column2: 他们向你献上 \x01@\x1A 头牛。你接受吗？

column1: They offered us fair compensation, and we accepted it.
column2: 他们给出了合理的赔偿，我们接受了。

column1: The compensation they offered us was niggardly, and we rejected it.
column2: 他们提出的赔偿十分吝啬，我们拒绝了。

column1: They refused to raise their offer.
column2: 他们拒绝提高报价。

column1: They refused to discuss our case against them.
column2: 他们拒绝讨论我们的控诉。

column1: Demand that the \x01Á join in a war against a third tribe.
column2: 要求 \x01Á 加入对第三方部落的战争。

column1: The \x01Á said that they would not be pushed into an all-out war.
column2: \x01Á 表示他们不会被推入全面战争。

column1: Ignore the breach of the peace.
column2: 无视和平协议被违反。

column1: We ignored this breach of the peace.
column2: 我们无视了这次对和平的破坏。

column1: Our warriors said that friends who smiled while stabbing you in the back were worse than no friends at all.
column2: 我们的战士说，笑着在背后捅刀的朋友比没有朋友更糟。

column1: Make war on the \x01Á.
column2: 向……开战 \x01Á.

column1: We decided to make war on them.
column2: 我们决定向他们开战。

column1: When do you declare war?
column2: 你何时宣战？

column1: Next Fire season.
column2: 下一个火之季。

column1: Any cows they offer us will have the mange.
column2: 他们献上的任何牛都会长疥癣。

column1: We should seek compensation.
column2: 我们应该寻求赔偿。

column1: They didn’t really mean it.
column2: 他们并非有意。

column1: Alliances are bad for trade.
column2: 联盟不利于贸易。

column1: A war could gain us good loot.
column2: 战争能让我们获得上好战利品。

column1: A war could gain us good loot. But of course the risks are higher than for a legal claim.
column2: 战争能让我们获得上好战利品。但当然，风险比法律诉讼更高。

column1: You could interpret our peace agreement to say that they are allowed to raid us.
column2: 我们可以将和平协议解释为允许他们劫掠我们。

column1: We are clearly in the right.
column2: 我们明显理直。

column1: They have violated the peace agreement we made with them. But among our people, peace agreements do not last long.
column2: 我们违反了与他们达成的和平协议。但在我们族人中，和平协议维持不久。

column1: If we wage war with another tribe at our side, we are more likely to win than if we make war on the \x01Á.
column2: 若我们与另一个部落并肩作战，胜算比单独向……开战更大。 \x01Á.

column1: The \x01Á are anxious to end their peace with us. The raid was a deliberate blow, one we must meet aggressively.
column2: \x01Á  渴望结束与我们的和平。这次袭击是蓄意的一击，我们必须积极回击。

column1: The \x01Á are mostly well-disposed to us. This is the action of a disobedient clan.
column2: \x01Á  大多对我们怀有好感。这是一个不听话氏族的行为。

column1: We must find a peaceful way out of this, and go home and tend to our fields.
column2: 我们必须找到和平的出路，然后回家照料我们的田地。

column1: It is better to wound pride than flesh.
column2: 伤自尊胜于伤皮肉。

column1: Peace arrangements only last so long.
column2: 和平安排只能维持那么久。

column1: We cannot tolerate an attack upon the royal clan.
column2: 我们不能容忍对王族的攻击。

column1: Many poems will be written about the war this will spark.
column2: 这场战争将引发许多诗篇。

column1: Orlanth was rejected every time by the Emperor, until the War of the Gods began.
column2: 奥兰斯每次都被皇帝拒绝，直到众神之战开始。

column1: “Never look up in battle, lest the magicians enchant you, and turn you suddenly into a hog.”
column2: “战斗中绝不要抬头，以免法师对你施咒，突然把你变成一头猪。”

column2: sceneR247

column1: We went to \x01@!’s market, and saw Bundalini and His All-Skeleton Band perform.
column2: 我们去了  \x01@! 的市场，观看了邦达利尼和他的全骷髅乐队的表演。

column1: We made some good deals.
column2: 我们做成了一些好买卖。

column1: We did not make the deals we wanted to make. Still, we had a good time dancing.
column2: 我们没有做成想要的买卖。不过，我们跳舞跳得很开心。

column1: How much total wealth do you distribute?
column2: 你分配的总财富是多少？

column1: They celebrated our gratitude.
column2: 他们感激我们的谢意。

column1: Join the challenges.
column2: 参加挑战。

column1: We participated in challenges of skill and strength.
column2: 我们参加了技巧和力量的挑战。

column1: We did not arrange any marriages, though it seemed that we came close.
column2: 我们没有安排任何婚姻，尽管我们似乎差点就安排了。

column1: Warn everyone that Bundalini is dangerous.
column2: 警告所有人，邦达利尼是危险的。

column1: We warned everyone that Bundalini was dangerous.
column2: 我们警告了所有人邦达利尼是危险的。

column1: They laughed at us. “Everyone can see that he is just a performer,” they said, “and that his walking skeletons are as tame as can be.”
column2: 他们嘲笑我们。“所有人都能看出他只是一个表演者，”他们说，“而且他的行走骷髅驯服得不能再驯服了。”

column1: The time did not seem right for tribemaking, though our neighbors treated us with courtesy.
column2: 时机似乎不适合结盟，尽管我们的邻居对我们以礼相待。

column1: We were not clever enough to let Bundalini play at our market. Let us at least show we are generous.
column2: 我们不够聪明，没让邦达利尼在我们的市场上表演。至少让我们表现出慷慨吧。

column1: Bundalini is a monster, I tell you! A monster!
column2: 邦达利尼是个怪物，我告诉你！一个怪物！

column1: I’ll be on guard duty.
column2: 我会站岗放哨。

column1: Everyone is laughing at us, because we turned Bundalini away from our own market.
column2: 所有人都在嘲笑我们，因为我们把邦达利尼从自己的市场赶走了。

column1: Orlanth made a type of instrument which had not been seen, ever. When people heard it they laughed out loud. This was part of Orlanth’s plan, for there was not enough laughter in the world.
column2: 奥兰斯制造了一种前所未见的乐器。人们听到它时放声大笑。这是奥兰斯计划的一部分，因为世界上没有足够的欢笑。

column1: Ha ha! We were fools not to let Bundalini play for us! Let’s make merry!
column2: 哈哈！我们真是傻瓜，没让邦达利尼为我们表演！让我们尽情欢乐吧！

column1: If you don’t warn them that fearsome, undead-loving giants are dangerous, then I will!
column2: 如果你不警告他们那些可怕、热爱不死生物的巨人是危险的，那我就去！

column1: But then \x01@\x01, our chieftain, drew a dagger and threatened Bundalini with it.
column2: 但随后  \x01@\x01，我们的酋长，拔出一把匕首威胁邦达利尼。

column1: But then \x01@\x01, of our clan ring, drew a dagger and threatened Bundalini with it.
column2: 但随后  \x01@\x01，我们氏族议会的一员，拔出一把匕首威胁邦达利尼。

column1: “I know you are a demon set to devour us all! Well, not everyone here is a blind, stupid idiot, more interested in hearing tootling and banging than in opposing the living dead! Not everyone here is a complete, drooling cretin! You shall not devour the people of the \x01@" clan, for we are wiser than these other dolts! Eat them if you want, but know that you will never eat us!”
column2: “我知道你是一个恶魔，要吞噬我们所有人！好吧，这里并非每个人都是瞎了眼、愚蠢的白痴，只对听吹吹打打感兴趣，却反对对抗不死生物！这里并非每个人都是完全流口水的低能儿！你休想吞噬  \x01@"  氏族的人民，因为我们比这些蠢货更聪明！你想吃他们就吃吧，但你永远别想吃我们！”

column1: The delegation from the Holy Country returns to reclaim the Iron Spike. These representatives of the far-off Lead Breakers clan bring the gifts they promised: a tapestry even more valuable than the one they gave you before, and plenty more silver.
column2: 来自圣国的代表团回来收回铁刺。这些来自遥远的破铅者氏族的代表带来了他们承诺的礼物：一幅比之前给你们的更珍贵的挂毯，以及更多的白银。

column1: The delegation from the Holy Country returned to reclaim the Iron Spike, bearing the gifts they had promised.
column2: 来自圣国的代表团回来收回铁刺，带来了他们承诺的礼物。

column1: Attack them and take the gifts.
column2: 攻击他们，拿走礼物。

column1: We attacked them and took the gifts.
column2: 我们攻击了他们，拿走了礼物。

column1: These Lead Breakers offered us little resistance, for they were talkers, not fighters. One of them wounded \x01@\x12 with magic, but our people were otherwise unhurt. We took the gifts and drove them off.
column2: 这些破铅者几乎没有抵抗，因为他们是说客，不是战士。其中一人用魔法伤了  \x01@\x12 ，但除此之外我们的人没有受伤。我们拿走了礼物，把他们赶走了。

column1: Return the Iron Spike.
column2: 归还铁刺。

column1: We returned it to them, and accepted the gifts.
column2: 我们把它还给了他们，并接受了礼物。

column1: Our people were happy.
column2: 我们的人民很高兴。

column1: Threaten to attack them if they don’t hand over the gifts.
column2: 威胁说如果他们不交出礼物就攻击他们。

column1: We threatened to attack them unless they handed over the gifts. They said they served the Pharaoh, who would harm us if we did not return the Spike.
column2: 我们威胁说除非他们交出礼物，否则就攻击他们。他们说他们侍奉法老，如果我们不归还铁刺，法老就会伤害我们。

column1: “I warn you, the repercussions will be terrible if you mistreat us,” he says. “The Pharaoh needs the Spike back, and you do not wish to experience his displeasure.”
column2: “我警告你，如果你虐待我们，后果将非常可怕，”他说。“法老需要拿回铁刺，你不想体验他的不悦。”

column1: “Actually, we don’t have the Spike any more.”
column2: “实际上，我们不再拥有铁刺了。”

column1: We said we did not have it.
column2: 我们说我们没有它。

column1: One of them looked at the stone on his ring.
column2: 其中一人看了看他戒指上的宝石。

column1: “We know that you lie,” they said, departing. “You will regret this.”
column2: “我们知道你在撒谎，”他们说着离开了。“你会后悔的。”

column1: “You have given away something very valuable, something that did not belong to you. You will regret this, I assure you,” he said. Then they left.
column2: “你送出了一件非常珍贵的东西，一件不属于你的东西。你会后悔的，我向你保证，”他说。然后他们离开了。

column1: Return the Spike.
column2: 归还铁刺。

column1: We returned it.
column2: 我们归还了它。

column1: “It is good that you have reconsidered. Although you do not deserve it, we will still give you the gifts we promised, because we Lead Breakers are civilized Orlanthi.” They gifted us and left. The weaponthanes said it looked as if we had given in to their threats.
column2: “你们重新考虑是好事。虽然你们不配，但我们仍会给你们承诺的礼物，因为我们破铅者是文明的奥兰斯人。”他们给了我们礼物后离开了。武器领主们说我们看起来像是屈服于了他们的威胁。

column1: “We don’t have it any more.”
column2: “我们不再拥有它了。”

column1: We said we didn’t have it any more.
column2: 我们说我们不再拥有它了。

column1: They said we were lying. They said they served the Pharaoh, who would harm us if we did not give them the Spike.
column2: 他们说我们撒谎。他们说他们侍奉法老，如果我们不给他们铁刺，法老就会伤害我们。

column1: “You lie,” he says. “Did you think we would come with no way of knowing if you had the spike? I warn you, the repercussions will be terrible if you do not give it to us, immediately. The Pharaoh does not like unneeded delays.”
column2: “你在撒谎，”他说。“你以为我们会在不知道你是否拥有尖峰的情况下前来吗？我警告你，如果你不立刻把它交给我们，后果会很严重。法老不喜欢不必要的拖延。”

column1: “We’re still not giving it to you.”
column2: “我们还是不会交给你。”

column1: We refused to give it up.
column2: 我们拒绝交出。

column1: “Very well,” they said, departing. “You will regret this.”
column2: “很好，”他们说着离开了。“你们会后悔的。”

column1: “We have the spike, but we’re not going to give it to you.”
column2: “我们有尖峰，但我们不会交给你。”

column1: We said to them, “We have the spike, but we’re not going to give it to you.”
column2: 我们对他们说：“我们有尖峰，但我们不会交给你们。”

column1: They said they served the Pharaoh, who would harm us if we did not return the Spike.
column2: 他们说他们效忠于法老，如果我们不归还尖峰，法老就会伤害我们。

column1: “Indeed you do,” he says. “I warn you, the repercussions will be terrible if you do not give it to us, immediately. The Pharaoh does not like unneeded delays.”
column2: “你们确实有，”他说。“我警告你们，如果不立刻把它交给我们，后果会非常严重。法老不喜欢不必要的拖延。”

column1: Remain steadfast in your refusal.
column2: 保持拒绝的决心。

column1: Again we refused to give it up.
column2: 我们再次拒绝交出。

column1: “It is odd that you say you have the Spike, when you do not. You have given away something very valuable, something that did not belong to you. You will regret this, I assure you.” Then they left.
column2: “你们说你们有尖峰，其实并没有，这很奇怪。你们送掉了一件非常珍贵的东西，一件不属于你们的东西。我向你们保证，你们会后悔的。”然后他们离开了。

column1: Offer them compensation for it.
column2: 向他们提供补偿。

column1: They said they did not want compensation. They wanted the Spike, and nothing else.
column2: 他们说他们不要补偿。他们只想要尖峰，其他什么都不要。

column1: “I am afraid we must turn down your offer,” he purrs. “We come only for the Spike. It is of little use to you, but of great use to us.”
column2: “恐怕我们必须拒绝你的提议，”他低声说道。“我们只为尖峰而来。它对你们没什么用，但对我们却很有用。”

column1: “We’re keeping it anyway.”
column2: “我们无论如何都要留着它。”

column1: “You saucy, dishonorable creatures!” their leader said, departing. “You will regret this, I promise you.”
column2: “你们这些无礼、不光彩的家伙！”他们的首领说着离开了。“我向你们保证，你们会后悔的。”

column1: They thanked us, and gave us the gifts they had promised. The people were happy.
column2: 他们感谢了我们，并给了我们承诺的礼物。人们很高兴。

column1: “You don’t have it, do you?” their leader thundered. “You have given away something very valuable, something that did not belong to you. You will regret this, I assure you,” he said. Then they left.
column2: “你们没有它，对吧？”他们的首领怒吼道。“你们送掉了一件非常珍贵的东西，一件不属于你们的东西。我向你们保证，你们会后悔的，”他说。然后他们离开了。

column1: Promises made to clans from the Holy Country are not binding.
column2: 对圣国的氏族做出的承诺没有约束力。

column1: We made a promise to them. They are in the right.
column2: 我们向他们做出了承诺。他们是占理的一方。

column1: There’s something they aren’t telling us about the Spike.
column2: 关于尖峰，他们有些事情没告诉我们。

column1: They could have powerful battle magic.
column2: 他们可能拥有强大的战斗魔法。

column1: They cannot defend themselves against us.
column2: 他们无法抵御我们。

column1: We can beat them, and they know it.
column2: 我们能打败他们，他们也知道这一点。

column1: The Pharaoh has brought strange new magics to the Holy Country.
column2: 法老将奇怪的新魔法带到了圣国。

column1: Losing a great weapon against the trolls seems like a blow against our ancestors.
column2: 失去一件对抗巨魔的强大武器似乎是对我们祖先的打击。

column1: The people will be happy to get those gifts.
column2: 人们会很高兴得到那些礼物。

column1: The people will be happy to get those gifts. They will be even happier if they can keep the treasure, too.
column2: 人们会很高兴得到那些礼物。如果他们还能保留宝物，那就更高兴了。

column1: Orlanth helped Grandmother Turtle by fighting off the birds that hurt her. He did not collect on his debt then, but reserved it to be a return gift for the future.
column2: 奥兰斯赶走了伤害乌龟祖母的鸟儿，帮助了她。他当时没有索要回报，而是将它留作将来的回礼。

column1: They worship the same gods as we, and so should be treated properly.
column2: 他们和我们信仰同样的神灵，所以应该受到妥善对待。

column1: What I meant to say back when the — so what if it’s not what we’re talking about now, I finally figured out what I wanted to — all right, all right, what are we talking about now?
column2: 我当初想说的是——就算不是我们现在在谈的又怎样，我终于搞明白我想说什么了——好了好了，我们现在在说什么来着？

column1: They need the Spike more than we do.
column2: 他们比我们更需要尖峰。

column1: Take the gifts and keep the Spike. If we use the gifts to build up our temples, the gods will understand.
column2: 收下礼物，保留尖峰。如果我们用这些礼物来修建神庙，神灵会理解的。

column1: They serve the Pharaoh; the Iron Spike is a weapon to use against the spirit of our old ruler, the Only Old One.
column2: 他们效忠法老；铁刺是用来对付我们旧统治者唯一古老者灵魂的武器。

column1: When the gods hand you a treasure, hang onto it.
column2: 当神灵赐予你宝物时，要牢牢抓住它。

column1: I’m afraid hanging onto the Spike will just cause more trouble.
column2: 恐怕留着尖峰只会带来更多麻烦。

column1: We made a mistake getting rid of the Spike. Now the Pharaoh will attack us.
column2: 我们丢掉尖峰是个错误。现在法老会来攻击我们。

column1: The Pharaoh is stupid enough to send us his treasure and now he thinks he can get it back? Oh no.
column2: 法老蠢到把他的宝物送给我们，现在还以为能要回去？哦不。

column1: A huge troll, who identifies herself as Umulguk, seeks permission to enter your tula as a guest. She knows that you guard an item known as the Iron Spike, and wants to warn you that possession of this item marks you out as a great foe of the trolls. If you give her the Spike, that will show that you meant no harm to her people.
column2: 一位自称乌穆尔古克的巨大巨魔请求作为客人进入你们的领地。她知道你们守护着一件名为铁刺的物品，并想警告你们，拥有这件物品会让你们成为巨魔的大敌。如果你把尖峰交给她，这表示你们无意伤害她的族人。

column1: A huge troll named Umulguk warned us that having the Iron Spike meant we were enemies of the trolls. She said we should give her the Spike.
column2: 一位名叫乌穆尔古克的巨大巨魔警告我们，拥有铁刺意味着我们是巨魔的敌人。她说我们应该把尖峰交给她。

column1: Ask something in return for it.
column2: 要求她给予回报。

column1: In return for it, she offered a set of Lead Eyes, which would speed the spirits of our warriors when they died.
column2: 作为回报，她提供了一套铅眼，可以加速我们战士死后灵魂的进程。

column1: She offers a set of Lead Eyes, which will speed the spirits of your warriors when they die.
column2: 她提供了一套铅眼，可以加速你们战士死后灵魂的进程。

column1: Do you take them?
column2: 你要收下吗？

column1: We didn’t want them.
column2: 我们不想要。

column1: She growled deep in her massive throat but remained motionless. Then she repeated her demand.
column2: 她在巨大的喉咙深处发出低吼，但一动不动。然后她重复了她的要求。

column1: We attacked her.
column2: 我们攻击了她。

column1: She threw off the first few warriors who ran at her. Then she drew her weapons. No one would fight her after that, and she slowly walked away.
column2: 她甩开了最初几个冲向她战士。然后她抽出武器。之后没人再敢与她战斗，她慢慢地走开了。

column1: She killed the first few warriors who ran at her. Then she drew her weapons. No one would fight her after that, and she slowly walked away.
column2: 她杀死了最初几个冲向她战士。然后她抽出武器。之后没人再敢与她战斗，她慢慢地走开了。

column1: Give her the Spike.
column2: 把尖峰交给她。

column1: We gave it to her.
column2: 我们把它交给了她。

column1: She said that the trolls would remember what we had done for them.
column2: 她说巨魔会记住我们为他们所做的一切。

column1: Thank her for the warning.
column2: 感谢她的警告。

column1: We thanked her for the warning.
column2: 我们感谢了她的警告。

column1: She departed unhappily, saying that a warning was no good if you ignored it.

column1: We conducted our own divination.
column2: 我们进行了自己的占卜。

column1: \x01D\x08 cursed us for wasting time and doubting the superior Chaos-detecting abilities of his clan.
column2: \x01D\x08 他诅咒我们浪费时间，并怀疑他氏族卓越的混沌探测能力。

column1: Our god-talkers said that their god-talkers were wrong. They had misread the signs. Our people were blameless.
column2: 我们的神言者说他们的神言者错了。他们误解了征兆。我们的人民是无辜的。

column1: Our god-talkers said that the signs were unclear. They did not say that there was a Chaos cultist among us, but then they did not say there was not.
column2: 我们的神言者说征兆不明确。他们没有说我们之中有混沌崇拜者，但也没有说没有。

column1: Have the clan ring conduct the questioning.
column2: 让氏族议会进行审问。

column1: The clan ring interrogated the people instead.
column2: 氏族议会反而审问了民众。

column1: Everyone denies being a Chaos cultist. No one seems to be lying. But \x01D\x08 scolds you: “Of course you think they’re innocent. Whoever it is has been lying to you forever! You’re either stupid, or deliberately harboring Chaos! Others will know of your treachery!” He stomped away.
column2: 每个人都否认是混沌崇拜者。似乎没有人撒谎。但是 \x01D\x08 谴责你：“你当然认为他们是无辜的。不管是谁，一直在对你撒谎！你要么是愚蠢，要么是故意窝藏混沌！其他人会知道你的背叛！”他跺脚离开了。

column1: Have \x01@\x15 conduct the questioning.
column2: 让 \x01@\x15 进行审问。

column1: We had \x01@\x15 conduct the questioning.
column2: 我们让 \x01@\x15 进行了审问。

column1: He said that there was no Chaos among us. He and \x01D\x08 argued for a long time.
column2: 他说我们之中没有混沌。他和 \x01D\x08 争论了很久。

column1: Finally \x01D\x08 admitted that \x01@\x15’s magic was greater than his, and that he must have been wrong when he said there was a Chaos cultist among us. He left to look for the culprit somewhere else.
column2: 最终 \x01D\x08 承认 \x01@\x15的法力比他强，他一定是在说我们之中有混沌崇拜者时错了。他离开去别处寻找罪犯。

column1: He said he still thought there was a Chaos cultist among us, but would not fight another Uroxi over this difference of opinion. His clan would take necessary measures, \x01D\x08 said, taking his leave of us.
column2: 他说他仍然认为我们之中有混沌崇拜者，但不会因这个意见分歧与另一位尤洛克斯争斗。他的氏族将采取必要措施， \x01D\x08 说着，向我们告辞。

column1: Let \x01D\x08 interrogate people.
column2: 让 \x01D\x08 审问民众。

column1: We let him do so.
column2: 我们让他这么做了。

column1: After lengthy interrogation sessions, \x01D\x08 concludes that \x01@\x01 is the culprit! \x01@\x01 swears that the accusation was unjust. “\x01D\x08 is crazy!” \x06 protests.
column2: 经过长时间的审讯， \x01D\x08 得出结论 \x01@\x01 是罪犯！ \x01@\x01 发誓指控不公。“\x01D\x08 疯了！” \x06 抗议道。

column1: Outlaw \x01@\x01.
We outlawed \x01@\x01, horrified that a minion of Chaos had been among us for so many years.
column2: 我们放逐了 \x01@\x01，惊恐于一个混沌爪牙竟在我们中间这么多年。

column1: Refuse to accept \x01D\x08’s judgment.
column2: 拒绝接受 \x01D\x08的判决。

column1: We refused to believe that \x01@\x01 was a minion of Chaos.
column2: 我们拒绝相信 \x01@\x01 是混沌爪牙。

column1: “It is clear, then, that you harbor Chaos deliberately,” \x01D\x08 said. “You should know this, foul ones: when the just vengeance of the Cleansing Wind comes, it comes without warning.”
column2: “那么很明显，你们是故意窝藏混沌，” \x01D\x08 说道。“你们该知道这个，肮脏的东西：当净化之风的正义复仇降临，它是不告而来的。”

column1: The Uroxi have no quarrel with us. We needn’t fear their immediate wrath, even if we deny \x01D\x08.
column2: 乌洛希与我们无冤无仇。即使我们否认 \x01D\x08，也无需害怕他们立即的怒火。

column1: I have heard it said that the Uroxi already regard us as unwitting accomplices of Chaos.
column2: 我听说乌洛希已经把我们视为混沌的无知帮凶。

column1: We do not wish to anger all the Uroxi of Dragon Pass.
column2: 我们不想激怒龙隘的所有乌洛希。

column1: Together, the Uroxi warriors of Dragon Pass could destroy our entire clan.
column2: 龙隘的乌洛希战士联合起来能摧毁我们整个氏族。

column1: Our worst foe is Chaos!
column2: 我们最凶恶的敌人是混沌！

column1: Uroxi are not known for careful questioning.
column2: 乌洛希不以审慎盘问著称。

column1: He has already decided someone is guilty. Do not trust him.
column2: 他已经认定某人有罪。别信他。

column1: Remember, if we offend \x01D\x08, we offend his clan, as well.
column2: 记住，如果我们冒犯 \x01D\x08，也就冒犯了他的氏族。

column1: Give \x01D\x08 what he wants. We need his clan on our side in tribal affairs.
column2: 给 \x01D\x08 他想要的。在部落事务中我们需要他的氏族站在我们这边。

column1: \x01D\x08’s clan is already hostile to us. We do not want to risk a feud.
column2: \x01D\x08的氏族已经对我们怀有敌意。我们不想冒世仇的风险。

column1: \x01D\x08’s clan is on good terms with us. We can stand up for what is right without risking a feud.
column2: \x01D\x08的氏族与我们关系良好。我们可以坚持正确的事而不冒世仇风险。

column1: He is picking on us because of our feud.
column2: 他找我们麻烦是因为我们的世仇。

column1: If their divination says one of us is a cultist of Thanatar, they must be right.
column2: 如果他们的占卜说我们中有人是萨纳塔的信徒，那他们一定是对的。

column1: In a divination, the gods are infallible. But the priests who attract their attention and interpret the signs they send are not.
column2: 在占卜中，众神是无误的。但那些吸引他们注意并解释他们所传征兆的祭司们却并非如此。

column1: Urox is the foe of Chaos. When he fights for us, he is the Cleansing Wind. When he bullies us, he is the Bad Wind.
column2: 乌洛克斯是混沌之敌。当他为我们而战时，他是净化之风。当他欺凌我们时，他是恶风。

column1: Let me talk some sense into him. There are no Chaos cultists here.
column2: 让我去跟他讲讲道理。这里没有混沌信徒。

column1: Pay no mind to his bluster.
column2: 别理会他的虚张声势。

column1: Beneath his earth-pounders Chaos-Scourer trod Enkand the Splitter. On his head-spikes Vostoo the Grand was gored.
column2: 在他踏碎大地的脚下，混沌扫荡者踩碎了分裂者恩坎德。在他的头刺上，大沃斯托被顶穿。

column1: Just do whatever he says.
column2: 照他说的做就是了。

column1: The culprit is a woman, no doubt.
column2: 罪犯是个女人，毫无疑问。

column2: sceneR257

column1: \x01D\t, a member of the \x01@! clan ring, comes seeking your help again. “That terrible walktapus is still stalking our tula, attacking our cattle. One of our children was taken and we fear for the rest. Some of our weaponthanes are still recovering from injuries, and the rest are too small a force to defeat this thing. Help us hunt and slay this dread beast.”
column2: \x01D\t， \x01@! 氏族议会的一名成员，又来寻求你的帮助。“那可怕的步行章鱼仍在我们的图拉领地上出没，袭击我们的牛群。我们有个孩子被掳走了，我们担心其余孩子。我们的一些武器领主还在养伤，剩下的人手不足以击败这东西。帮我们猎杀这头恐怖野兽。”

column1: We did it as a favor to them.
column2: 我们帮他们作为恩惠。

column1: Do it in exchange for a treasure.
column2: 以交换一件宝物为条件去做。

column1: We did it in exchange for a treasure.
column2: 我们以交换一件宝物为条件做了。

column1: Do it in exchange for wealth.
column2: 以交换财富为条件去做。

column1: We did it in exchange for wealth.
column2: 我们以交换财富为条件做了。

column1: Do it in honor of Urox, foe of Chaos.
column2: 为了荣耀混沌之敌乌洛克斯而做。

column1: We did it in honor of Urox, foe of Chaos.
column2: 我们为了荣耀混沌之敌乌洛克斯而做了。

column1: Turn her down.
column2: 拒绝她。

column1: We turned her down.
column2: 我们拒绝了她。

column1: She said that she was sorry to have troubled us. “I suppose you can’t always assume that every clan is truly dedicated to the fight against Chaos.”
column2: 她说她很抱歉打扰了我们。“我想你也不能总假定每个氏族都真正致力于对抗混沌。”

column1: How many do you send with \x01@\x05?
column2: 你派多少人跟 \x01@\x05一起？

column1: We sent \x01@\x05, along with \x01@\x06 warriors.
column2: 我们派了 \x01@\x05，和 \x01@\x06 名战士一起。

column1: They did not find the walktapus.
column2: 他们没有找到步行章鱼。

column1: They found the walktapus hiding under some fallen trees. It made a weird screeching sound, then burst through the log’s rotten wood, hurling itself at the hunting party.
column2: 他们发现步行章鱼藏在一堆倒下的树下。它发出诡异的尖叫声，然后冲破腐烂的木头，向狩猎队猛扑过来。

column1: The walktapus slew \x01@\x19 of our warriors, then charged into the brush with surprising speed. \x01@\x05 would not allow them to follow it, and called off the hunt.
column2: 步行章鱼杀死了我们 \x01@\x19 名战士，然后以惊人的速度冲进灌木丛。 \x01@\x05 不允许他们追击，并取消了狩猎。

column1: Our warriors fell upon it, hacking furiously. We cut it to bits. Then \x01@! sages carefully burned each of the pieces, saying that the creatures were thought to be able to regrow themselves. The sages made sure that no one breathed in the oily smoke from the burning creature’s meat.
column2: 我们的战士扑向它，疯狂砍杀。我们把它砍成碎片。然后 \x01@! 的贤者们小心地焚烧每一块，说这种生物被认为能自行再生。贤者们确保没有人吸入那燃烧怪物血肉冒出的油性烟雾。

column1: Later, \x01@\x01 gave us a fine hunting alynx in return for our aid.
column2: 后来， \x01@\x01 给了我们一只上好的狩猎山猫作为我们帮助的回报。

column1: They gave us a fine hunting alynx.
column2: 他们给了我们一只上好的狩猎山猫。

column1: Later, \x01@\x01 asked which treasure we wanted in return for our aid.
column2: 后来， \x01@\x01 问我们想要哪件宝物作为援助的回报。

column1: a Bell of Uralda, which rings with the power of the Earth rune
column2: 一只乌拉尔达之钟，它响着大地符文的魔力

column1: They gave us a Bell of Uralda, which rang with the power of the Earth rune.
column2: 他们给了我们一只乌拉尔达之钟，它响着大地符文的魔力。

column1: a fine hunting alynx
column2: 一只上好的狩猎山猫

column1: a Garland of Reeds, which ensures friendship with the elves
column2: 一个芦苇花环，确保与精灵的友谊

column1: They gave us a Garland of Reeds, to ensure friendship with the elves.
column2: 他们赠予我们一个芦苇花环，以确保与精灵的友谊。

column1: a jar of Three-Bean Broth, a beverage trading partners find pleasing
column2: 一罐三豆汤，一种贸易伙伴喜爱的饮品

column1: They gave us a jar of Three-Bean Broth, a beverage trading partners find pleasing.
column2: 他们赠予我们一罐三豆汤，一种贸易伙伴喜爱的饮品。

column1: They gave us goods worth \x01@\x15 cows.
column2: 他们赠予我们价值 \x01@\x15 牛只的货物。

column1: Our god-talkers said that Urox would be pleased by this action undertaken in his name.
column2: 我们的神言者说，乌罗克斯会因以他之名行此事而喜悦。

column1: The \x01@! clan was also quite pleased, needless to say.
column2: 当然， \x01@! 氏族也相当满意。

column1: We are poor; let’s not ask for anything fancy.
column2: 我们很穷；别要求什么花哨的东西。

column1: We are \x02\x03well-off/prosperous/rich\x02, and \x02\x03do not need their wealth/do not need to do this for reward/can afford to be generous to them\x02.
column2: 我们 \x02\x03小康/富足/殷实\x02，并且 \x02\x03无需他们的财富/无需为此求取报酬/有能力慷慨待之\x02。

column1: They are a prosperous clan.
column2: 他们是一个兴旺的氏族。

column1: They are a prosperous clan, and have gathered many interesting treasures.
column2: 他们是一个兴旺的氏族，并积攒了许多有趣的宝物。

column1: They are a prosperous clan, and I’d hate to see us fumble the chance to impress them and gain some of their wealth.
column2: 他们是一个兴旺的氏族，我不愿看到我们错失机会，去打动他们并获取他们部分财富。

column1: They are a prosperous clan, and have gathered many interesting treasures. I particularly covet their Three-Bean Broth.
column2: 他们是一个兴旺的氏族，并积攒了许多有趣的宝物。我尤为垂涎他们的三豆汤。

column1: Our fighters will be proud to defeat a thing of Chaos.
column2: 我们的战士会以击败混沌之物而自豪。

column1: We can’t risk losing any of our warriors.
column2: 我们不能冒险损失任何战士。

column1: Our fighters will be proud to defeat a thing of Chaos. Send at least nine of them.
column2: 我们的战士会以击败混沌之物而自豪。派至少九人前往。

column1: Our fighters are eager now to defeat this thing of Chaos. Send at least nine of them.
column2: 我们的战士现在急于击败这混沌之物。派至少九人前往。

column1: Our fighters will try again to crush this thing of Chaos, if you tell them to. Send at least nine of them.
column2: 若你下令，我们的战士会再次尝试粉碎这混沌之物。派至少九人前往。

column1: Our fighters will be proud to defeat a thing of Chaos. Send at least nine of them, and send \x01@\x08 to lead them.
column2: 我们的战士会以击败混沌之物而自豪。派至少九人前往，并派 \x01@\x08 带领他们。

column1: They will like us better if we help them.
column2: 若我们帮助他们，他们会更喜欢我们。

column1: They are feuding with us, but Chaos threatens everyone.
column2: 他们正与我们结仇，但混沌威胁着所有人。

column1: In tribal affairs, it is always good to have another clan owe you a favor.
column2: 在部落事务中，让另一个氏族欠你一份恩惠总是好的。

column1: They definitely need help. And they have been willing to help us when we need it.
column2: 他们确实需要帮助。而且在我们需要时，他们也乐于相助。

column1: It is better to please a god than to please one’s neighbor.
column2: 取悦神明胜于取悦邻人。

column1: If we defeat the walktapus in the name of Urox, our clan magic will get stronger.
column2: 若我们以乌罗克斯之名击败步行章鱼，我们的氏族魔法就会变强。

column1: Send me to lead the party. I will smash the Chaos beast.
column2: 派我带领队伍。我会砸烂这混沌野兽。

column1: Send me to lead the party. I will smash the Chaos beast this time.
column2: 派我带领队伍。这次我会砸烂这混沌野兽。

column1: Send me to lead the party. I will smash the Chaos beast this time, and dance on its grave.
column2: 派我带领队伍。这次我会砸烂这混沌野兽，并在其坟头起舞。

column1: Send me to lead the party. I will tickle the walktapus under its many arms.
column2: 派我带领队伍。我会搔挠步行章鱼的许多触腕之下。

column1: They have a treasure that makes them elf-friends. Let Chaos eat them.
column2: 他们有一件让他们成为精灵之友的宝物。让混沌吞噬他们吧。

column1: \x01D\t is a wise woman. We must help her.
column2: \x01D\t是一位智慧的女性。我们必须帮助她。

column1: They breed fine hunting alynxes.
column2: 他们培育优良的狩猎山猫。

column1: I have heard that a walktapus is a fairly common Chaos monster — and very, very dangerous.
column2: 我听说步行章鱼是一种相当常见的混沌怪物——而且非常非常危险。

column1: We \x02\x03didn’t have much luck/didn’t do much good/didn’t look so brave and victorious\x02 last time we tried to help.
column2: 我们 \x02\x03上次尝试帮助时运气不佳/没起什么作用/看起来不那么勇敢和胜利\x02 。

column1: Refusing to help our own allies? That sounds like Bad King Urgrain.
column2: 拒绝帮助自己的盟友？那听起来像是恶王乌格兰的行径。

column1: They are enemies, it is true. But this is bad. Maybe we should help.
column2: 他们确实是敌人。但这次情况很糟。也许我们应该帮忙。
