column2: sceneR258

column1: \x01D\r, the willful child of well-liked carls, has a history of making trouble. But now he has done the unthinkable. He has desecrated your \x01@\x14 temple, throwing cow dung all over the holy shrines. When asked why he would do such a thing, he only shrugs. His parents are beside themselves with shame and anger.
column2: \x01D\r，一位受人喜爱的自由民家的任性孩子，素来惹是生非。但如今他做了不可想象之事。他亵渎了你们 \x01@\x14 的神庙，将牛粪扔满圣坛。当被问及为何如此时，他只是耸肩。他的父母羞愧愤怒得难以自持。

column1: The god-talkers conduct the usual rites to restore the balance of the temple.
column2: 神言者举行常规仪式，以恢复神庙的平衡。

column1: \x01D\r, the willful child of well-liked carls, desecrated the \x01@\x14 temple.
column2: \x01D\r，一位受人喜爱的自由民家的任性孩子，亵渎了 \x01@\x14 神庙。

column1: The god-talkers conducted rites to restore the balance of the temple.
column2: 神言者举行了仪式，以恢复神庙的平衡。

column1: Conduct an additional, powerful temple-purification ritual.
column2: 额外举行一个强大的神庙净化仪式。

column1: We conducted another, more powerful ritual to make sure the temple was purified.
column2: 我们举行了另一个更强大的仪式，以确保神庙被净化。

column1: How much do you sacrifice in the course of the ritual?
column2: 在仪式过程中，你们献祭多少？

column1: The god-talkers said that the temple had been properly purified.
column2: 神言者说神庙已被恰当净化。

column1: The god-talkers said that the temple was not fully purified. We would have to suffer the indignation of the gods.
column2: 神言者说神庙并未完全净化。我们将不得不承受神明的愤怒。

column1: Outlaw him, and see to it that he is killed.
column2: 将他逐出氏族，并确保他被处死。

column1: Who kills him?
column2: 谁杀他？

column1: We outlawed him, and sent \x01@\x05 to kill him.
column2: 我们将他逐出氏族，并派 \x01@\x05 去杀他。

column1: \x01@\x05 did kill him, and was thereafter shunned by the people of the clan. They said that \x01D\r was not yet initiated into adulthood, and therefore not responsible for his actions.
column2: \x01@\x05 确实杀死了他，此后被氏族众人排斥。他们说 \x01D\r尚未成年受礼，因此不对其行为负责。

column1: We outlawed him.
column2: 我们将他逐出氏族。

column1: Although the people were horrified by what he had done, they were also horrified by our harsh punishment. They said that he was not yet initiated into adulthood, and therefore not responsible for his actions. His parents left the clan in order to look after him; a boy alone would not last long in the wilds of Dragon Pass.
column2: 尽管人们对他所做之事感到惊骇，但他们也对我们严厉的惩罚感到惊骇。他们说他还未完成成年受礼，因此不对其行为负责。他的父母离开氏族以照顾他；一个男孩独自一人在龙之隘口的荒野中活不了多久。

column1: Send for shamans to see if the boy is possessed.
column2: 派人去请萨满，看看这男孩是否被附身。

column1: We sent for shamans to see if the boy is possessed.
column2: 我们派人请来萨满，看看那男孩是否被附身了。

column1: We found shamans willing to test him for spirit possession.
column2: 我们找到了愿意为他测试是否被恶灵附身的萨满。

column1: Shamans heed your call. For the low price of \x01A$ cows, they will test the boy.
column2: 萨满响应了你的召唤。只需 \x01A$ 头牛的低廉价格，他们就会测试那个男孩。

column1: They said that he was not possessed. He was just a very bad child.
column2: 他们说他没有被附身。他只是个非常坏的孩子。

column1: They said he was possessed.
column2: 他们说他是被附身的。

column1: An argument has broken out within the tribe. Central to the tribal regalia is an ancient and legendary weapon known as the Black Spear. Some clans are claiming that the spear is too useful to be kept only for ceremonies; it should be used by a powerful war clan to hunt and fight. Others say it is too risky to use the spear; if it is damaged, the spirit of the tribe will be wounded, maybe even destroyed.
column2: 部族内部爆发了一场争论。部落圣物的核心是一把名为“黑矛”的古老传奇武器。一些氏族声称，这把矛太有用了，不能只用于仪式；应该交给一个强大的战争氏族，用于狩猎和战斗。另一些人则说，使用这把矛风险太大；如果它被损坏，部落的灵魂就会受伤，甚至可能被摧毁。

column2: 这长枪在召唤我们，利用我们来铸就它自身的命运。

column1: Leave the spear in the temple, where it belongs.
column2: 将长枪留在庙中，那里才是它的归宿。

column1: Enough foolish yammer!
column2: 够了，别再愚蠢地抱怨了！

column1: \x01@\x0B has hidden the much-disputed Black Spear in the wilderness. All who find it during the next year will join a new clan, the Black Spear Clan, which will be part of your tribe. That clan will forever after possess the spear. Some of your weaponthanes and more adventurous farmers want to go join the hunt for the Black Spear, and join the new clan.
column2: \x01@\x0B 已将备受争议的黑矛藏匿于荒野。凡在接下来一年内寻得者，都将加入一个新氏族——黑矛氏族，该氏族将成为你们部落的一部分。此后该氏族将永远持有长枪。你们的一些武器领主和好冒险的农夫想要加入搜寻黑矛的行列，并加入新氏族。

column1: In accordance with the words of your tribal spirit, you have hidden the Black Spear in the wilderness, announcing that any who find it will join a new clan, the Black Spear Clan, which will be part of your tribe. That clan will forever after possess the spear. Much to your surprise, some of the weaponthanes and more adventurous farmers of your royal clan want to search for the spear and hoping to leave the royal clan for the Black Spear clan.
column2: 遵照你们氏族之灵的指示，你们已将黑矛藏匿于荒野，并宣告凡寻得者将加入一个新氏族——黑矛氏族，该氏族将成为你们部落的一部分。此后该氏族将永远持有长枪。令你们大为惊讶的是，你们王室氏族中的一些武器领主和好冒险的农夫想要搜寻长枪，并希望离开王室氏族加入黑矛氏族。

column1: We hid the Black Spear, and said that whoever found it would be part of the new Black Spear Clan. Much to our surprise, some of our warriors and carls wanted to search for the spear.
column2: 我们将黑矛藏起，并宣称任何找到它的人都将成为新黑矛氏族的一员。令我们大为惊讶的是，我们的一些战士和自由民想要搜寻长枪。

column1: Forbid them to go.
column2: 禁止他们前往。

column1: We would not let them go.
column2: 我们不会放他们走。

column1: They were unhappy, but respected the commands of the chief.
column2: 他们虽不快，但尊重酋长的命令。

column1: They would not heed the chief’s command.
column2: 他们不愿听从酋长的命令。

column1: \x01@\x1A weaponthanes and \x01@\x19 warriors went off to seek the spear, even though we said they could not.
column2: \x01@\x1A 武器领主和 \x01@\x19 战士们出发寻找长枪，尽管我们说过不准。

column1: \x01@\x1A weaponthane and \x01@\x19 warriors went off to seek the spear, even though we said they could not.
column2: \x01@\x1A 武器领主和 \x01@\x19 战士们出发寻找长枪，尽管我们说过不准。

column1: Let them go, with your blessings.
column2: 让他们去吧，带着你们的祝福。

column1: We let them go, with our blessings.
column2: 我们放他们去了，带着我们的祝福。

column1: One weaponthane
column2: 一名武器领主

column1: \x01@\x1A weaponthanes
column2: \x01@\x1A 武器领主们

column1: and \x01@\x19 warriors went off to seek the spear.
column2: 和 \x01@\x19 战士们出发寻找长枪。

column1: We let them go.
column2: 我们放他们去了。

column1: “The Black Spear clan will be poor for many years.”
column2: “黑矛氏族将贫困多年。”

column1: We told them: “The Black Spear clan will be poor for many years.”
column2: 我们告诉他们：“黑矛氏族将贫困多年。”

column1: They found no merit in our words. They said that the Black Spear Clan would be a heroic and magical clan, and that heroes were meant to struggle against great odds.
column2: 他们不认为我们的话有道理。他们说黑矛氏族将是一个英雄而神奇的氏族，而英雄注定要在巨大逆境中奋斗。

column1: They weighed the possible glory of a new clan against the difficult realities of life in Dragon Pass. They elected to remain with us. The people were gladdened by their decision.
column2: 他们权衡了新氏族可能的荣耀与龙隘地区生活的艰辛现实。他们选择留下与我们同在。人民为他们的决定感到欣慰。

column1: “The royal clan is more prestigious than the Black Spear Clan.”
column2: “王室氏族比黑矛氏族更尊贵。”

column1: We told them: “The royal clan is more prestigious than the Black Spear Clan.”
column2: 我们告诉他们：“王室氏族比黑矛氏族更尊贵。”

column1: They rejected our argument. They said that the crown comes and goes, but the legendary Black Spear would always be a part of the Black Spear Clan.
column2: 他们驳回了我们的论点。他们说王冠来去无常，但传奇的黑矛将永远是黑矛氏族的一部分。

column1: They agreed that they sought possible glory, when there was certain glory already in our clan. They laughed and said that they had forgotten themselves. The people were glad that they did not wish to leave.
column2: 他们承认自己追求可能的荣耀，而我们氏族已有确定的荣耀。他们笑着说自己忘了本分。人们很高兴他们不愿离开。

column1: The Black Spear clan will have more cows than any other!
column2: 黑矛氏族将比其他氏族拥有更多牛只！

column1: A new clan will be poor for many years. I can persuade them to stay.
column2: 一个新氏族将穷困多年。我能说服他们留下。

column1: If we give our blessings, all the warriors will leave.
column2: 如果我们赐予祝福，所有武士都会离开。

column1: More warriors will leave us if we give our blessings.
column2: 如果我们赐予祝福，会有更多武士离开我们。

column1: Only a few warriors want to go, but everyone wants them to be given the chance to do what they want.
column2: 只有少数武士想走，但人人都希望给他们机会去做想做的事。

column1: The Black Spear clan will soon eclipse even our clan in prestige.
column2: 黑矛氏族很快就会在威望上超越我们氏族。

column1: Better the crown than the Black Spear.
column2: 王冠胜过黑矛。

column1: Let me talk to them. The royal clan is more prestigious than the Black Spear Clan.
column2: 让我和他们谈谈。王室氏族比黑矛氏族更有威望。

column1: The Black Spear became a powerful symbol of our hatred of the Pharaoh.
column2: 黑矛成为了我们仇恨法老的强大象征。

column1: What a pile of bull!
column2: 放屁！

column1: If my knee wasn’t acting up, I’d join the search for the spear myself.
column2: 要不是我的膝盖不给力，我自己就去找长枪了。

column1: They’ll be scratching like chickens if they go.
column2: 他们要是去了，会像小鸡一样乱抓。

column1: We cannot stop them from leaving if they truly want to leave.
column2: 如果他们真心想走，我们拦不住。

column1: We must give them our blessings, or the Black Spear clan will grow powerful and take vengeance against us.
column2: 我们必须赐予祝福，否则黑矛氏族会壮大起来，向我们复仇。

column1: If we are to create a new clan in our tribe, we want to maintain good relations with that clan.
column2: 如果我们要在部落里建立一个新氏族，我们想与之保持良好关系。

column1: We’ll live.
column2: 我们会活下去。

column1: Wandering around in the wilderness without the clan’s magic to protect them? They’re zombie bait!
column2: 没有氏族魔法的保护在荒野游荡？他们是活死人的诱饵！

column1: Hail the heroes!
column2: 向英雄致敬！

column1: Like Umath and Orlanth, they must make a place of their own.
column2: 如同乌玛斯和奥兰斯，他们必须开创自己的地盘。

column1: We must be big enough to let them go.
column2: 我们必须足够大度，让他们离开。

column1: I would rather not lose our warriors. But perhaps it must be so.
column2: 我宁愿不失去我们的武士。但或许事已至此。

column1: If we ever hope to hold the kingship, we must act like kings.
column2: 如果我们还想保住王权，就必须行事如王。

column1: The people are afraid and angry, wanting to know what the ring is going to do about this continued threat to their children.
column2: 人们又怕又怒，想知道长老会打算如何应对这个持续威胁他们孩子的危险。

column1: He has two puncture wounds on his neck, and has lost a great deal of blood. The people are afraid that a vampire is loose in the area.
column2: 他脖子上有两个穿刺伤口，失血过多。人们害怕有吸血鬼在这片区域出没。

column1: \x02\x03We presumed that the vampire had moved on to other tulas./We hoped that this was the last we would hear of vampires./We decided to wait until we were faced with a foe we could strike.\x02
column2: \x02\x03我们假定那吸血鬼已经去了其他图拉领地。/我们希望这是最后一次听到吸血鬼的消息。/我们决定等待，直到面对一个我们可以打击的敌人。\x02

column1: Do nothing more.
column2: 不再采取行动。

column1: Sacrifice to Humakt for protection from undead.
column2: 向胡马克特献祭以求抵御亡灵。

column1: We sacrificed to Humakt for protection from undead.
column2: 我们向胡马克特献祭以求抵御亡灵。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were good; Humakt had heard our pleas.
column2: 神言者说征兆良好；胡马克特已听到我们的祈求。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were unclear; they could not say that Humakt had heard our pleas.
column2: 神言者说征兆不明；他们无法断言胡马克特听到了我们的祈求。

column1: Sacrifice to Urox for protection from Chaos.
column2: 向尤洛克斯献祭以求抵御混沌。

column1: We sacrificed to Urox for protection from Chaos.
column2: 我们向尤洛克斯献祭以求抵御混沌。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were good; Urox had heard our pleas.
column2: 神言者说征兆良好；尤洛克斯已听到我们的祈求。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were unclear; they could not say that Urox had heard our pleas.
column2: 神言者说征兆不明；他们无法断言尤洛克斯听到了我们的祈求。

column1: Send warriors to hunt the vampire.
column2: 派遣武士猎杀吸血鬼。

column1: We sent warriors to hunt the vampire.
column2: 我们派遣武士猎杀吸血鬼。

column1: We did not find the vampire.
column2: 我们没有找到吸血鬼。

column1: Our warriors found the vampire. It was a woman from the \x01@! clan. They backed her into a patch of briars. She used strange, howling magics on us, and all were burned by her spells.
column2: 我们的武士找到了吸血鬼。她是一个来自 \x01@! 氏族的女人。他们把她逼进一片荆棘丛。她对我们使用了诡异嚎叫的魔法，所有人都被她的咒语灼伤。

column1: \x01@\x05 and the others fell to the ground, and the vampire escaped.
column2: \x01@\x05 其他人倒在地上，吸血鬼逃走了。

column1: We can’t afford to sacrifice now.
column2: 我们现在承受不起献祭。

column1: We really can’t spare the cows right now. Sacrifice goods instead.
column2: 我们现在实在匀不出牛只。改用货物献祭。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice as much as we need to, to stop this menace.
column2: 我们能承受所需的任何献祭，以阻止这个威胁。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice again, but if you kill the vampire, then we won’t need to sacrifice for this at all.
column2: 我们可以再次献祭，但如果你们杀了吸血鬼，那我们就完全不需要为此献祭了。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice generously. Do so, and keep the vampire from scaring away our trade.
column2: 我们承担得起丰厚的献祭。就这样做，别让吸血鬼吓跑我们的商队。

column1: We really can’t spare the goods for an adequate sacrifice. Sacrifice cattle instead.
column2: 我们实在匀不出足够的货物进行适当的献祭。改用牲畜献祭。

column1: They say vampires are \x02\x03soft, but devious in a fight/weak, but hard to track/unpredictable when cornered\x02.
column2: 他们说吸血鬼 \x02\x03身体柔软，但战斗时狡诈/弱小但难以追踪/被困时难以预测\x02。

column1: They say vampires are hard to track. If this one preys on little boys, it shouldn’t be able to stand against true warriors — if we find it.
column2: 他们说吸血鬼难以追踪。如果这个专挑小男孩下手，那么它应该无法对抗真正的武士——只要我们能找到它。

column1: Now we know that vampires are hard to track, and tricky to fight. Better the known enemy than the unknown.
column2: 现在我们知道吸血鬼难以追踪，战斗也棘手。已知的敌人总好过未知的。

column1: They say that vampires are weak, but tricky. If we find it, we must be extra alert.
column2: 他们说吸血鬼虽然弱小，但诡计多端。如果我们找到它，必须格外警惕。

column1: If this vampire preys on little boys, it shouldn’t be able to stand against true warriors — if we find it. We must send only a few weaponthanes, so that it does not sense our approach.
column2: 如果这个吸血鬼专挑小男孩下手，它应该无法对抗真正的武士——只要我们能找到它。我们只需派几个武器领主，以免它察觉我们的接近。

column1: This vampire preys on children, which means it will shy away from a true fight. We need to send a few weaponthanes skilled in hunting and tracking, so that we can sneak up on it.
column2: 这个吸血鬼以儿童为食，这意味着它会回避真正的战斗。我们需要派几个精通狩猎和追踪的武器领主，这样我们可以悄悄接近它。

column1: We must \x02\x03hunt it/find it/seek it\x02 again. This time we will take a few weaponthanes with magic skills, too.
column2: 我们必须 \x02\x03再次猎杀它/找到它/追寻它\x02 。这次我们还会带上几个有魔法技能的武器领主。

column1: Cure the boy first, or the people will be afraid of what he might become. Then, go after the vampire.
column2: 先治好那个男孩，否则人们会害怕他变成什么。然后再去追捕吸血鬼。

column1: The parents of the clan want us to do more to protect their children from this threat.
column2: 氏族的父母们希望我们做更多事来保护他们的孩子免受这种威胁。

column1: The parents of the clan demand to know what we are going to do to protect their children. We must do something!
column2: 氏族的父母们要求知道我们打算如何保护他们的孩子。我们必须做点什么！

column1: If we don’t kill this vampire, or drive it off, we can expect some very angry carls.
column2: 如果我们不杀死这只吸血鬼，或把它赶走，可以预料会有一些非常愤怒的自由民。

column1: We don’t know for sure it is a vampire.
column2: 我们并不确定那是一只吸血鬼。

column1: It will go away on its own, now that it’s well-fed.
column2: 既然它已经饱餐一顿，它自己就会离开。

column1: Some say vampires are undead; some say they are Chaos creatures.
column2: 有人说吸血鬼是亡灵，有人说它们是混沌生物。

column1: Undead or Chaos creature — what does it matter? It still \x02\x03threatens us all/is a menace to our children/lurks in the woods\x02.
column2: 亡灵也好混沌生物也罢——那又有什么区别？它仍然 \x02\x03威胁着我们所有人/是我们孩子的祸害/潜伏在森林里\x02。

column1: Both Urox and Humakt despise vampires, because they are undead creatures of Chaos.
column2: 乌洛克斯和胡马克特都憎恶吸血鬼，因为它们是混沌的亡灵生物。

column1: Both Urox and Humakt despise the undead, and those who ignore the undead.
column2: 乌洛克斯和胡马克特都憎恶亡灵，也憎恶那些无视亡灵之人。

column1: If Humakt frowns upon us, sacrifice to Urox.
column2: 如果胡马克特对我们皱眉，就向乌洛克斯献祭。

column1: If Urox fails to bless us, sacrifice to Humakt.
column2: 如果乌洛克斯不赐福我们，就向胡马克特献祭。

column1: Ask Humakt’s or Urox’s blessings, do not try to fight again without their backing.
column2: 祈求胡马克特或乌洛克斯的赐福，没有他们的支持就不要再次开战。

column1: Both Urox and Humakt despise vampires, because they are undead creatures of Chaos. Sacrifice ten cows to either god.
column2: 乌洛克斯和胡马克特都憎恶吸血鬼，因为它们是混沌的亡灵生物。向任意一位神明献祭十头牛。

column1: Both Urox and Humakt despise vampires, because they are undead. They also despise those who ignore the undead.
column2: 乌洛克斯和胡马克特都憎恶吸血鬼，因为它们是亡灵。他们也憎恶那些无视亡灵之人。

column1: If Humakt frowns upon us, sacrifice ten cows to Urox.
column2: 如果胡马克特对我们皱眉，就向乌洛克斯献祭十头牛。

column1: If Urox fails to bless us, sacrifice ten cows to Humakt.
column2: 如果乌洛克斯不赐福我们，就向胡马克特献祭十头牛。

column1: Sacrifice ten cows to Humakt or Urox to gain their attention and their blessing. Do not try to fight again without their backing.
column2: 向胡马克特或乌洛克斯献祭十头牛，以获得他们的关注和赐福。没有他们的支持就不要再次开战。

column1: I sniff the stench of Chaos! Let us sacrifice to the Cleansing Wind!
column2: 我嗅到了混沌的恶臭！让我们向净化之风献祭！

column1: The mighty Storm Bull will now support us in battling this accursed thing!
column2: 强大的风暴公牛现在将支持我们，与这受诅咒的东西战斗！

column1: The state of undeath is an abomination to Humakt, Lord of Death.
column2: 亡者状态是对死亡之主胡马克特的憎恶。

column1: Humakt is most likely to aid those \x02\x03who take up arms against the undead themselves/who are willing to die/who hate undeath, and do not fear death themselves\x02.
column2: 胡马克特最可能帮助那些 \x02\x03自己拿起武器对抗亡灵之人/愿意赴死之人/憎恶亡灵而自身不畏死亡之人\x02。

column1: We must perform a preventive ritual for the boy, then we can think what to do about the vampire.
column2: 我们必须先对那男孩进行一次预防仪式，然后才能考虑如何对付吸血鬼。

column1: Vampires serve the Chaos god Vivamort, who teaches them to infect others with their unliving magic.
column2: 吸血鬼侍奉混沌神维瓦莫特，此神教导它们用不死魔法感染他人。

column1: Look up, look down, look behind yourself. Vampires are masters of deception.
column2: 抬头看、低头看、回头看身后。吸血鬼是欺骗大师。

column1: Let me lead the search party! I will personally cut the head off this accursed thing!
column2: 让我来带领搜索队！我要亲手砍下这受诅咒东西的脑袋！

column1: We must search \x02\x04and search/every treetop/the whole tula/the woods\x02 until we find this \x02\x03creature/monster/fiend\x02! I will personally \x02\x03run my sword through it/cleave it in two/chop it to bits\x02!
column2: 我们必须搜索 \x02\x04再搜索/每棵树梢/整个图拉领地/森林\x02 ，直到找到这 \x02\x03生物/怪物/恶魔\x02！我要亲手 \x02\x03用剑刺穿它/把它劈成两半/把它剁成碎片\x02！

column1: We will have to prepare ourselves more thoroughly this time, but we cannot give up trying to kill this vampire now!
column2: 这次我们必须更充分地准备，但我们不能放弃杀死这只吸血鬼的努力！

column1: Cure the boy first, of course. Then deal with the vampire.
column2: 当然，先治好那男孩。然后再对付吸血鬼。

column1: As all the fighters stared, the head kept on shrieking, and the body blackened the grass it fell on. The remains gradually shrivelled up, and the terrible head fell silent. Our warriors were only too glad to leave that ghastly site, and returned home as quickly as pride would let them.
column2: 当所有战士都盯着看时，那颗头颅仍在尖叫，尸体把倒下的草地熏黑了。残骸逐渐枯萎，恐怖的头颅终于沉寂。我们的战士很乐意离开那可怕的现场，以自尊所能允许的最快速度返回家中。

column1: Kallyr comes to the ring again to propose a dangerous mission. “In the Holy Country there are a people called the Kitori. They are humans, but live like trolls and worship troll gods. One of their great heroes is Warlan Darkbreath. column1: While exploring in the \x01@O, your exploration party is attacked by a bandit gang led by a powerful shaman named \x01D\x1B. He captures a member of the party and demands an outrageous ransom of 10 cows worth of goods for the explorer \x01D\x1C, who is a carl.
column2: 在 \x01@O探索时，你的探索队遭到一伙强盗袭击，为首的是名叫 \x01D\x1B的强大萨满。他俘虏了一名队员，并索要10头牛价值的赎金来换回这名身为自由民的探索者 \x01D\x1C。

column1: A bandit shaman named \x01D\x1B captured the carl \x01D\x1C and demanded an outrageous ransom for his return.
column2: 一个名叫 \x01D\x1B 的强盗萨满抓住了自由民 \x01D\x1C ，并索要一笔高昂的赎金来换他回来。

column1: Let \x01D\x1B keep \x01D\x1C.
column2: 让 \x01D\x1B 留着 \x01D\x1C吧。

column1: The clan did not act against him.
column2: 氏族没有对他采取行动。

column1: Our carls didn’t like it that we left \x01D\x1C to his fate, and wondered why were afraid of \x01D\x1B.
column2: 我们的自由民不喜欢我们弃 \x01D\x1C 于不顾，他们不明白我们为何害怕 \x01D\x1B。

column1: Offer five cows for his return.
column2: 出五头牛换他回来。

column1: We offered him five cows for \x01D\x1C’s return.
column2: 我们出了五头牛换取 \x01D\x1C的归来。

column1: Who leads the delegation to his camp?
column2: 谁率领代表团前往他的营地？

column1: The shaman danced around \x01@\x05 with his rattle and made unpleasant noises. Then he returned \x01D\x1C to us, and we left his presence.
column2: 萨满拿着响板绕着 \x01@\x05 跳舞，发出不悦的声音。然后他把 \x01D\x1C 还给了我们，我们离开了他的地盘。

column1: Pay what \x01D\x1B asks.
column2: 按 \x01D\x1B 的要求付钱。

column1: We paid what he asked.
column2: 我们按他要求的付了钱。

column1: The shaman danced around \x01@\x05 with his rattle and made unpleasant chortling noises. Then he returned \x01D\x1C to us, and we left his presence.
column2: 萨满拿着响板绕着 \x01@\x05 跳舞，发出不悦的咯咯笑声。然后他把 \x01D\x1C 还给了我们，我们离开了他的地盘。

column1: Recruit warriors from other clans to join a war party against \x01D\x1B.
column2: 从其他氏族招募战士，组成讨伐队攻打 \x01D\x1B。

column1: We decided to recruit warriors from other clans to join a war party against him.
column2: 我们决定从其他氏族招募战士，组成讨伐队攻打他。

column1: \x01@\x11 of our neighbors were willing to send five warriors each.
column2: \x01@\x11 我们的邻族每族愿意各派五名战士。

column1: No one was willing to help us.
column2: 没人愿意帮助我们。

column1: Seek the blessings of your clan spirits before fighting the shaman.
column2: 在与萨满交战前，先寻求氏族之灵的祝福。

column1: We sought the blessings of our ancestral spirits before fighting the shaman.
column2: 在与萨满交战前，我们寻求了祖先之灵的祝福。

column1: What do you sacrifice to them?
column2: 你向他们献祭什么？

column1: Our ancestral spirits spoke to our god-talkers. They said they would aid us against the spirits who served \x01D\x1B the Bandit.
column2: 我们的祖先之灵向神言者说话了。他们说他们会帮助我们对峙那位侍奉 \x01D\x1B 的强盗萨满。

column1: The god-talkers could not contact our ancestral spirits.
column2: 神言者无法联系到我们的祖先之灵。

column1: Send a war party to liberate \x01D\x1C.
column2: 派出讨伐队解救 \x01D\x1C。

column1: We sent a war party to liberate \x01D\x1C.
column2: 我们派出讨伐队解救 \x01D\x1C。

column1: \x01@\x05 fell upon \x01D\x1B and the bandits and scattered them. \x05 rescued \x01D\x1C.
column2: \x01@\x05 袭击了 \x01D\x1B 和那伙强盗，击溃了他们。 \x05 救出了 \x01D\x1C。

column1: Our war party fell upon \x01D\x1B and his bandits and scattered them. We rescued \x01D\x1C.
column2: 我们的讨伐队袭击了 \x01D\x1B 和他的强盗，击溃了他们。我们救出了 \x01D\x1C。

column1: \x01D\x1B escaped. From a distance, he screamed that he was going to curse us.
column2: \x01D\x1B 逃走了。他在远处尖叫着说要诅咒我们。

column1: \x01@\x05 seized \x01D\x1B and
column2: \x01@\x05 抓住了 \x01D\x1B 并

column1: threw him on the ground, then jumped on him until he was dead.
column2: 把他摔在地上，然后踩在他身上直到他死去。

column1: stabbed him till \x01D\x1B’s life-blood stained the ground.
column2: 刺向他，直到 \x01D\x1B的生命之血浸透土地。

column1: knocked him against a tree until he did not move any more.
column2: 把他撞到树上，直到他一动不动。

column1: thumped him on the head, then ran a sword through \x01D\x1B’s chest.
column2: 重击他的头部，然后用剑刺穿 \x01D\x1B的胸膛。

column1: \x01@\x05 was seized by invisible spirits. \x05 attacked a tree and then swung at a boulder as \x01D\x1B and the bandits escaped.
column2: \x01@\x05 被无形的灵体抓住了。 \x05 攻击了一棵树，然后挥剑劈向巨石，与此同时 \x01D\x1B 和那伙强盗逃走了。

column1: Our war party were seized by invisible spirits, and attacked one another as \x01D\x1B and his bandits escaped.
column2: 我们的讨伐队被无形的灵体抓住了，在 \x01D\x1B 和他的强盗逃走时，他们互相攻击。

column1: \x01@\x05 then stabbed himself repeatedly and quickly bled to death.
column2: \x01@\x05 然后反复刺向自己，很快失血而死。

column1: \x01@\x05 was pierced from all sides by \x04 possessed comrades’ swords and quickly bled to death.
column2: \x01@\x05 被 \x04 被附身的同伴从四面八方刺中，很快失血而死。

column1: We don’t have enough cows to be paying any ransom.
column2: 我们没有那么多牛来支付赎金。

column1: Better to lose a little wealth than risk our warriors’ lives.
column2: 损失一点财富总比拿战士的生命冒险好。

column1: We can’t just keep losing farmers or cattle to this bandit, shaman or no shaman.
column2: 我们不能再让这个强盗——不管他是不是萨满——抓走我们的农夫或牛只了。

column1: Every time this happens, the carls grow more \x02\x04anxious/uneasy/dispirited/troubled\x02.
column2: 每次发生这种事，自由民就变得越来越 \x02\x04焦虑/不安/沮丧/困扰\x02。

column1: Ten cows isn’t too much to pay. \x01D\x1C is a fine and merry fellow.
column2: 十头牛不算太多。 \x01D\x1C 是个善良又快乐的好伙计。

column1: The proper ransom for a fellow of \x01D\x1C’s rank is five cows.
column2: 对于 \x01D\x1C这种身份的人来说，合适的赎金是五头牛。

column1: The other clans might listen to us if we show how \x01D\x1B threatens their welfare.
column2: 如果我们能证明 \x01D\x1B 威胁到其他氏族的利益，他们也许愿意听我们的话。

column1: The longer this \x02\x03continues/drags on/goes on\x02, the \x02\x03worse/lower/poorer\x02 our reputation grows.
column2: 这事 \x02\x03持续/拖延/进行的时间越长\x02，我们声誉就变得越 \x02\x03糟糕/低下/卑劣\x02 。

column1: \x01D\x1B is not much of a threat.
column2: \x01D\x1B 算不上什么威胁。

column1: Shamans can be dangerous.
column2: 萨满可能很危险。

column1: I have heard of this \x01D\x1B. He has powerful magic. We cannot defeat him without help.
column2: 我听说过这事 \x01D\x1B。他拥有强大的魔法。没有帮助，我们无法击败他。

column1: It is time to stop this \x01D\x1B fellow. But we must prepare carefully and well, so we don’t have to do it again.
column2: 是时候阻止那家伙 \x01D\x1B 了。但我们必须精心准备，以免再干一次。

column1: Our weaponthanes are \x02\x03proud and bold/strong and quick/valiant and brave\x02, but even they \x02\x03require/admit to needing/are glad to request\x02 help in \x02\x03overcoming/defeating/vanquishing\x02 this shaman.
column2: 我们的武器领主 \x02\x03骄傲而大胆/强壮而敏捷/英勇而果敢\x02，但即便是他们也 \x02\x03需要/承认需要/乐意请求\x02 帮助，来 \x02\x03克服/击败/征服\x02 这个萨满。

column1: The clans are fed up with the rampant banditry in these parts. They will help us, if we ask them.
column2: 部族们受够了此地猖獗的匪患。如果我们开口，他们会帮助我们。

column1: There is little banditry around here; the other clans won’t see this as their problem.
column2: 这里没什么匪患；其他部族不认为这是他们的问题。

column1: \x01D\x1B will settle for less.
column2: \x01D\x1B 将满足于更少。

column1: Even if we pay \x01D\x1C’s proper ransom, \x01D\x1B will think it his license to steal our carls.
column2: 即使我们支付 \x01D\x1C应得的赎金， \x01D\x1B 也会认为这是掠夺我们自由民的特许状。

column1: We can’t seem to \x02\x04defeat/vanquish/beat/kill\x02 \x01D\x1B. What are we doing wrong?
column2: 我们似乎无法 \x02\x04打败/征服/击倒/杀死\x02 \x01D\x1B。我们做错了什么？

column1: Our neighbors dislike us. They might be more willing to help \x01D\x1B than to help us.
column2: 我们的邻居不喜欢我们。他们可能更愿意帮助 \x01D\x1B 而不是我们。

column1: Our neighbors are our loyal friends. They will help us against the bandit shaman.
column2: 我们的邻居是我们忠实的朋友。他们会帮助我们对抗匪首萨满。

column1: Our clan spirits can fight \x01D\x1B’s spirits.
column2: 我们氏族之灵能与 \x01D\x1B的灵体战斗。

column1: Our magic is weak; we will not be able to contact our clan spirits.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱；我们将无法联系氏族之灵。

column1: We can’t just keep losing carls to \x01D\x1B, we must end this menace once and for all.
column2: 我们不能继续任由 \x01D\x1B劫掠自由民，必须一劳永逸地结束这一威胁。

column1: Even a powerful shaman \x02\x03has a weak point/can be hurt somewhere/must have a blind spot\x02. We must just \x02\x03discover/find out/ascertain\x02 what that spot is.
column2: 即便是强大的萨满 \x02\x03也有弱点/总有个地方可以被伤害/必定存在盲点\x02。我们必须 \x02\x03发现/找出/确认\x02 那个弱点所在。

column1: The other carls don’t like \x01D\x1C. Leave him there.
column2: 其他自由民不喜欢 \x01D\x1C。让他待在那里。

column1: The other carls will be dispirited if we abandon \x01D\x1C.
column2: 如果我们抛弃 \x01D\x1C，其他自由民会灰心丧气。

column1: The carls will lose their \x02\x04faith in/respect for/regard for/esteem for\x02 the ring if we don’t make and end of this \x02\x03miserable/shameful/sorry\x02 situation.
column2: 如果我们不终结这 \x02\x03糟糕/可耻/可悲\x02 的局面，自由民将失去对长老会的 \x02\x04信任/尊敬/尊重/敬重\x02 。

column1: What? Are we some kind of strange market where \x01D\x1B goes every time he needs cows?
column2: 什么？难道我们是某种奇怪的市场，每当他 \x01D\x1B 需要牛就来找我们？

column1: \x01D\x1B is becoming a giant thorn in our sides. It’s time we just took him out.
column2: \x01D\x1B 正成为我们的眼中钉肉中刺。是时候除掉他了。

column1: Our clan spirits have a right to know what has happened.
column2: 我们的氏族之灵有权知道发生了什么。

column1: \x01D\x1C is a resourceful fellow; he will escape on his own.
column2: \x01D\x1C 是个足智多谋的家伙；他会自己逃脱。

column1: I volunteer to lead the war party!
column2: 我自愿率领战帮！

column1: \x01D\x1C was a good fellow, and I shall mourn his passing. We cannot afford to risk warriors or throw away our precious wealth.
column2: \x01D\x1C 曾是个好汉，我将哀悼他的逝去。我们不能再冒险牺牲武士或挥霍宝贵的财富。

column1: The carls \x02\x04are eager for us to/want us to/hope we will/pray for us to\x02 get \x01D\x1C back, but \x02\x03they’re no match for a/they cannot stand up to this/they are not trained to fight a\x02 shaman themselves.
column2: 自由民 \x02\x04渴望我们/希望我们/期盼我们/祈祷我们\x02 把 \x01D\x1C 弄回来，但 \x02\x03他们打不过一个/他们无法对抗这个/他们未经训练无法对付\x02 萨满。

column2: sceneR266

column1: The carls and the cottars are fighting again. The carls accuse the cottars of grazing their sheep on cattle lands. The cottars reply that they cannot feed their sheep on nothing but rocks and sand.
column2: 自由民和佃农又在争斗。自由民指责佃农在牧牛地上放羊。佃农反驳说，他们没法用岩石和沙子喂羊。

column1: Carls and cottars argued over grazing land again.
column2: 自由民和佃农又为牧场争吵了。

column1: The carls and the cottars are fighting. The carls complain that the cottars are herding sheep onto their grazing lands. The cottars complain that the carls expect them to feed their sheep on nothing but rocks and sand.
column2: 自由民和佃农在争斗。自由民抱怨佃农把羊赶到他们的牧场上。佃农抱怨自由民指望他们只用岩石和沙子喂羊。

column1: Carls and cottars argued over grazing land.
column2: 自由民和佃农为牧场争吵。

column1: Compose a poem about harmony between carls and cottars.
column2: 创作一首关于自由民与佃农之间和谐的诗。

column1: \x01@N composed a poem about harmony between carls and cottars.
column2: \x01@N 创作了一首关于自由民与佃农之间和谐的诗。

column1: Both groups agreed that the poem was a fine one, and did them honor. They agreed to live up to its ideals in the future.
column2: 双方一致认为这首诗是佳作，为他们增光。他们同意未来依其理想行事。

column1: \x01@N’s effort was not one of \x04 best poems.
column2: \x01@N的努力并非 \x04 最佳诗作之一。

column1: Let them argue.
column2: 让他们吵去吧。

column1: We let them argue.
column2: 我们让他们吵。

column1: Sacrifice to Uralda, the Cow Mother and Nevala, the Sheep Mother.
column2: 向乌拉尔达——母牛女神，和内瓦拉——绵羊母亲献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to Uralda and the Sheep Mother.
column2: 我们向乌拉尔达和绵羊母亲献祭。

column1: Both groups were honored by the sacrifice, and pledged to resolve their differences in a friendly manner.
column2: 双方因献祭而感到荣幸，并承诺以友善方式解决分歧。

column1: Each group complained that their goddess should have received a better share of the sacrifice.
column2: 每一方都抱怨自己的女神本该获得更好的献祭份额。

column1: Scold the carls.
column2: 斥责自由民。

column1: Ring members scolded the carls.
column2: 长老会成员斥责了自由民。

column1: The carls admitted that they had been pressing the cottars unfairly, and agreed to give them their fair share of grazing land.
column2: 自由民承认他们曾不公平地压迫佃农，并同意给予他们应得的牧场份额。

column1: The carls said we unfairly abused them, and complained that the ring was unjust.
column2: 自由民说我们不公地虐待他们，并抱怨长老会不公正。

column1: Scold the cottars.
column2: 训斥佃农。

column1: Ring members scolded the cottars.
column2: 长老会成员训斥了佃农。

column1: The cottars said that they were in the right, and no amount of scolding could hide the fact that we favored the cow herders over the sheep folk.
column2: 佃农说他们有理，再怎么训斥也掩盖不了我们偏袒牧牛人而非牧羊人的事实。

column1: The cottars admitted that their grievances were exaggerated, and said that they would henceforth show their Orlanthi pride in a way that did not weaken the harmony of the clan.
column2: 佃农承认他们的不满有些夸大，并表示今后会以不削弱氏族和谐的方式展示他们的奥兰提自豪感。

column1: A little rivalry between carls and cottars is normal.
column2: 自由民与佃农之间有点竞争是正常的。

column1: The carls have been mistreating the cottars.
column2: 自由民一直在虐待佃农。

column1: The cottars unfairly accuse the carls.
column2: 佃农不公正地指责自由民。

column1: Poetry never settled a dispute.
column2: 诗歌从未解决过争端。

column1: An inspiring poem might \x02\x04lift everyone’s spirits/calm their ruffled feathers/bridge their differences/restore harmony\x02.
column2: 一首鼓舞人心的诗歌或许 \x02\x04能提振所有人的精神/安抚他们焦躁的情绪/弥合他们的分歧/恢复和谐\x02。

column1: Sheep and cattle graze differently, on different kinds of land. There is no real reason to fight.
column2: 羊和牛以不同方式在不同类型的土地上吃草。没有真正的理由争斗。

column1: Again? This is a sign of other problems in the clan.
column2: 又来了？这是氏族存在其他问题的征兆。

column1: Scolding either side or both sides will just irritate everyone further. A good poem is the only way.
column2: 训斥任何一方或双方只会让每个人更加恼火。一首好诗是唯一办法。

column1: This dispute arises because the carls and cottars are dispirited for other reasons.
column2: 这场争端是因为自由民和佃农因其他原因而情绪低落。

column1: The real solution will involve more land and more cows, but we could try to cheer them up meanwhile.
column2: 真正的解决方案需要更多土地和更多牛，但在此期间我们可以试着让他们高兴起来。

column1: A scolding for either side of this debate will shut them up, for a little while.
column2: 对辩论任何一方的训斥能让他们闭嘴一会儿。

column1: The people are often cheered when we sacrifice to their patron goddesses.
column2: 当我们向他们的守护女神献祭时，人们往往会高兴起来。

column1: Sacrificing to their goddesses will cheer the people more than poetry or scoldings.
column2: 向女神们献祭会比诗歌或训斥更让人民高兴。

column1: Sacrificing to their goddesses will cheer the people more than poetry or scoldings. Also, it will bring us divine favor.
column2: 向女神们献祭会比诗歌或训斥更让人民高兴。此外，它还会为我们带来神圣恩惠。

column1: A sacrifice to their respective goddesses might cheer them up, if the sacrifices are equally divided.
column2: 如果献祭平均分配，向各自的女神献祭或许能让他们高兴起来。

column1: Whether or not a sacrifice to their goddesses will quiet everyone down, it will bring us divine favor.
column2: 无论向女神献祭能否让所有人安静下来，它都会为我们带来神圣恩惠。

column1: Sacrifice to Uralda and forget those petty sheep-folk!
column2: 向乌拉尔达献祭，忘了那些渺小的牧羊人吧！

column1: This \x02\x03quarrel/argument/dispute\x02 is \x02\x03keeping us from important matters, like raiding/just farmer’s drivel/a waste of our time\x02.
column2: 这场 \x02\x03争吵/争论/纠纷\x02 正 \x02\x03阻碍我们处理重要事务，比如掠夺/不过是农夫的无稽之谈/浪费我们的时间\x02。

column1: It’s not as if it were a dispute between priestesses of Ernalda and Esra. Let them work the insults out of their system.
column2: 这又不是厄尔纳达和埃斯拉的女祭司之间的纠纷。让他们互相骂个够吧。

column1: Let me talk both sides into uniting against the \x02\x02crafters/hunters\x02.
column2: 让我说服双方联合起来对抗 \x02\x02工匠/猎人\x02。

column1: Just sell off half the sheep and half the cattle. That will show them who is in charge around here.
column2: 干脆卖掉一半的羊和一半的牛。这会让它们知道这里谁说了算。

column1: Lock the chief complainers in the pigsty until they learn to get along.
column2: 把主要抱怨者锁在猪圈里，直到他们学会和睦相处。

column1: Distribution of land is the clan ring’s responsibility.
column2: 土地分配是氏族议会的责任。

column1: \x01@\x05 found the camp of the cursed Horse-Spawn, and motioned the warriors to creep up upon it.
column2: \x01@\x05 找到了被诅咒的马裔的营地，并向战士们示意悄悄靠近。

column1: The Horse-Spawn somehow heard us approach, and took the field to repel us. They fought furiously, and we saw the magic of their high-leaping, fire-hoofed horses. Some were killed, and many were wounded. A horse leapt upon \x01@\x05 and crushed \x04 legs; it was lucky \x06 was not slain.
column2: 马裔不知怎地听到了我们靠近，遂列阵击退我们。他们激战不休，我们目睹了他们那种高高跃起、蹄踏火焰的马匹的魔法。有人被杀，多人受伤。一匹马跃向 \x01@\x05 ，踩碎了 \x04 的腿；幸好 \x06 未被杀死。

column1: \x05 leapt upon the horse before the Horse-Spawn could react.
column2: \x05 在马裔反应过来之前跃上了马背。

column1: Although the horse leaped and bucked at first, \x01@\x05 managed to control it, and we escaped from the Horse-Spawn encampment with their arrows and curses falling all around us. One of our warriors was killed, and two more were wounded. But we gained this great magical horse.
column2: 尽管那马起初又跳又蹶， \x01@\x05 还是设法控制了它，我们在马裔的箭矢与诅咒中逃离了他们的营地。我们的一名战士被杀，还有两人受伤。但我们已经得到了这匹伟大的魔法马匹。

column1: The beast ran into the heart of the Horse-Spawn camp, with \x01@\x05 on its back. The warriors hesitated, and the Horse-Spawn surrounded them. Some were killed, and many were wounded before they could escape.
column2: 那畜牲跑进了马裔营地深处，背上驮着 \x01@\x05 。战士们犹豫了，马裔包围了他们。一些人被杀，许多人受伤后才得以逃脱。

column1: The cursed Horse-Spawn had moved on, and \x01@\x05 could not find their camp.
column2: 被诅咒的马裔已经转移， \x01@\x05 找不到他们的营地。

column1: Horse-Spawn steeds are not normal creatures.
column2: 马裔的战马不是普通生物。

column1: The leader of this party must be good with animals, for this horse is one of the magnificent, magical beasts called Goldeneyes.
column2: 这支队伍的领队必须擅长驯兽，因为这匹马是被称为金眼马的壮丽魔法野兽之一。

column1: We should pay outside warriors three cows each.
column2: 我们应该每个外族战士付三头牛。

column1: We should pay outside warriors two cows each.
column2: 我们应该每个外族战士付两头牛。

column1: The Horse-Spawn are not as tough as the stories say.
column2: 马裔并不像传闻中那么难缠。

column2: 马裔很棘手。派出队伍会有风险。

column1: This should be theft by stealth, not a full-scale raid.
column2: 这应该是偷窃行动，而非全面袭击。

column1: This should be theft by stealth, not a full-scale raid. We should send neither too few or too many warriors — seven of them, say. The leader must be a good hunter, as well as a good fighter.
column2: 这应该是偷窃行动，而非全面袭击。我们派出的战士既不应太少也不应太多——比方说七个人。领队必须既是好猎人，也是好战士。

column1: There is no point in seeking outside warriors; none of our neighbors wish to see us prosper.

column1: We are well-respected, so it will not be hard to find outside warriors to help us.

column1: The horse will be easy to catch.
column2: 那匹马容易捕获。

column1: The powerful magics of the Horse-Spawn make them one of our most dangerous foes.
column2: 马裔的强大魔法使他们成为我们最危险的敌人之一。

column1: We will need the favor of the gods in order to have a hope of succeeding against the Horse-Spawn.
column2: 我们需要诸神的恩惠才有希望成功对抗马裔。

column1: The carls would love us to get that horse, but I fear it will be at the cost of our crops.
column2: 自由民们会希望我们得到那匹马，但我担心这会以我们的庄稼为代价。

column1: The carls would love us to get that horse, but I fear it will be at the cost of our harvest.

column1: The Horse-Spawn claim to be descended from centaurs, and kin to horses.
column2: 马裔声称是半人马的后裔，与马匹为亲族。

column1: Having a Horse-Spawn steed would allow us to maneuver better on the battlefield.

column1: The weaponthanes will be discouraged if we do not do this.

column2: 我们可以用一匹魔法马匹来对抗亡灵。

column1: Refuse her.

column2: 我听说过亚龙把穿甲的勇士咬成两段。

column1: If we lead the hunting party, we’ll have more control over what happens to our warriors.

column1: If we lead the hunting party, we can lead all the warriors, and make sure we win.
column2: 如果我们领导狩猎队伍，就能统领所有勇士，确保我们获胜。

column1: Our ancestors steered clear of anything involving dragons, or dragonkin. So should we.
column2: 我们的祖先对任何涉及龙或龙裔的事都敬而远之。我们也该如此。

column1: One of the giant reptiles called earthshakers galumphs onto your tula, intent on eating your crops. \x01D% manages to herd it away from the barley, but now it’s crashed into a stead.
column2: 一头被称为地动者的巨型爬行动物笨重地踏上你的领地，意图啃食你的庄稼。 \x01D% 设法把它从大麦田引开，但如今它又撞进一座农庄。

column1: An earthshaker came onto our lands and destroyed a stead.
column2: 一头地动者来到我们的土地上，摧毁了一座农庄。

column1: Give it hay to eat.
column2: 给它干草吃。

column1: We gave it hay to eat.
column2: 我们给了它干草吃。

column1: It ate a large amount of hay, and then wandered off.
column2: 它吃了大量干草，然后走开了。

column1: Send warriors to fight it.
column2: 派战士去战斗。

column1: We sent warriors to fight it.
column2: 我们派战士去战斗。

column1: They did not hurt it much, but they made it go away.
column2: 他们没怎么伤到它，但把它赶走了。

column1: It smashed at them with its huge, spiked tail. Many were wounded.
column2: 它用巨大的、带刺的尾巴猛击他们，许多人受了伤。

column1: They were unable to land a blow solid enough to cut through its thick hide, so they withdrew.
column2: 他们无法打出足够结实的重击来切开它厚实的皮，于是撤退了。

column1: Send warriors to herd it away.
column2: 派战士去把它赶走。

column1: We sent warriors to herd it away.
column2: 我们派战士去把它赶走。

column1: It ignored their cries, and their clattering of swords on shields.
column2: 它无视他们的喊叫和刀剑敲击盾牌的声响。

column1: Their cries and their clattering of swords on shields startled the creature, which ran across the tula, smashed into another stead, and then settled down again to graze on a nearby patch of weeds.
column2: 他们的喊叫和刀剑敲击盾牌的声响惊动了这头野兽，它跑过领地，撞进另一座农庄，然后在附近一片杂草丛中停下来继续吃草。

column1: Use magic to drive it off.
column2: 使用魔法驱赶它。

column1: We used magic to drive it off.
column2: 我们使用魔法驱赶它。

column1: It got up and thundered away, without hurting anything.
column2: 它站起来，轰隆跑开，没有损坏任何东西。

column1: It paid no attention to our spells.
column2: 它对我们的咒语毫不在意。

column1: Wait it out.
column2: 等待它自行离开。

column1: We waited for it to leave.
column2: 我们等它自己离开。

column1: It ate a large amount of our crops before wandering away.
column2: 它在离开前吃了我们大量庄稼。

column1: It will soon leave on its own, without hurting anything.
column2: 它很快就会自己离开，不会损坏任何东西。

column1: It will eat our crops if we don’t get rid of it.
column2: 如果我们不赶走它，它会吃掉我们的庄稼。

column1: We cannot afford to \x02\x03keep feeding/give handouts to/support\x02 this beast.
column2: 我们负担不起 \x02\x03一直喂食/施舍/供养\x02 这头野兽。

column1: We can easily get rid of it by feeding it, but then it will want to come back.
column2: 我们很容易就能用喂食把它弄走，但之后它还会想回来。

column1: We can try \x02\x04clanging our shields in its face/waving torches at it/poking it with spears/shouting and yelling at it\x02, but these beasts are very dense — it may not even notice.
column2: 我们可以尝试 \x02\x04在它面前敲盾牌/朝它挥舞火把/用矛戳它/朝它大喊大叫\x02，但这些野兽非常迟钝——它可能根本注意不到。

column1: Every time it smashes a stead, we lose about ten cows worth of materials and lost work.
column2: 每次它撞毁一座农庄，我们就会损失大约十头牛价值的材料和工时。

column1: Every time it lumbers onto our tula, we lose goods and the carls spend the rest of the day talking about it instead of working.
column2: 每次它笨重地踏上我们的领地，我们都会损失物资，自由民们剩下的时间都在谈论它而不是干活。

column1: The warriors won’t be happy if they get hit by that tail.
column2: 战士们如果被那条尾巴击中，是不会高兴的。

column1: The warriors are wondering if they couldn’t try some new tactics out on the beast.
column2: 战士们想知道是否可以对这头野兽尝试一些新战术。

column1: The warriors want to fight \x02\x03brave fighters/a real battle/with equals\x02, not \x02\x03stab at/slaughter/risk their limbs with\x02 some \x02\x03dumb/slow-witted/impervious\x02 animal.
column2: 战士们想与 \x02\x03勇敢的战士/真正的战斗/势均力敌的对手\x02作战，而不是 \x02\x03刺戳/屠杀/用肢体冒险\x02 某个 \x02\x03愚蠢/反应慢/刀枪不入\x02 的动物。

column1: Our magic is strong; our spells will succeed against it.
column2: 我们的魔法强大，咒语能成功对付它。

column1: Our magic is weak; spells will not succeed against it.
column2: 我们的魔法弱小，咒语无法成功对付它。

column1: The farmers will be upset if it eats their crops.
column2: 如果它吃掉庄稼，农夫们会不满。

column1: Not again! The farmers are already unhappy at losing good grain to this beasts’ belly.
column2: 又来了！农夫们已经因为好谷物进了这野兽的肚子而不高兴了。

column1: The carls wonder aloud how such a \x02\x03dim/slow/stupid\x02 creature can \x02\x03outwit/defeat/ignore\x02 our supposedly tough and brave weaponthanes.
column2: 自由民大声质疑，如此 \x02\x03迟钝/缓慢/愚蠢\x02 的畜生怎么能 \x02\x03智胜/击败/无视\x02 我们理应强悍勇敢的武器领主。

column1: Our grain bins are full. We can afford to lose a bit to vermin — especially when the vermin is bigger than a stead.
column2: 我们的粮仓是满的，损失一点给害兽也能承受——尤其是当这害兽比一座农庄还大的时候。

column1: Our grain bins are empty. Any loss of crops could be disastrous.
column2: 我们的粮仓是空的，任何庄稼损失都可能是灾难性的。

column1: These creatures are sacred to Ernalda’s vengeful sister, Maran Gor.
column2: 这些生物是埃娜尔达复仇的姐妹——玛兰·戈尔——的神圣造物。

column1: Just \x02\x04give it a good poke/yell in its ear/thump it on its snout/give it a good shove\x02.
column2: 只要 \x02\x04狠狠戳它一下/冲它耳朵喊一声/在它鼻子上敲一下/用力推它一把\x02。

column1: There are many kinds of earthshakers. Some are intelligent, and cast spells. Others are terrible carnivores, and some eat only plants. They are sacred to Maran Gor, Ernalda’s vengeful sister.
column2: 地动者有很多种。有些有智慧，能施法术。另一些是可怕的食肉动物，还有些只吃植物。它们为Maran Gor所珍视，她是Ernalda的复仇之妹。

column1: This earthshaker is obviously the plant-eating kind. But it is still a danger to our crops and sheds.
column2: 这只地动者显然是食草类。但它对我们的庄稼和棚屋仍然是威胁。

column1: Some say that Maran Gor \x02\x03created the earthshakers from the Sacred Mud/found the earthshakers in a hidden crevasse far away from here/discovered the earthshakers in a steaming jungle in some other realm\x02, but no one agrees if the story is true or not.
column2: 有人说Maran Gor \x02\x03用神圣污泥创造了地动者/在远离此地的隐藏裂缝中发现了地动者/在另一个领域的蒸汽丛林中发现了地动者\x02，但没人相信这个传闻是真是假。

column1: It’s a magnificent creature — don’t hurt it!
column2: 这是一只宏伟的生物——别伤害它！

column1: We can outrun that spiky tail.
column2: 我们能跑赢那条尖刺尾巴。

column1: I have heard stories of undead earthshakers, although I am fairly sure this is not one of them.
column2: 我听说过不死地动者的故事，尽管我很确定这只不是其中之一。

column1: If we had a nice big temple to Maran Gor this sort of thing wouldn’t happen.
column2: 如果我们有一座宏伟的神庙供奉Maran Gor，这种事情就不会发生。

column2: sceneR273

column1: The \x01Á sought to make peace with our tribe.
column2: 那 \x01Á 试图与我们的部落和平相处。

column1: “Make peace if they sacrifice to strengthen our magic.”
column2: “如果它们献祭来强化我们的魔法，就讲和。”

column1: Before the moot, we said: “Make peace if they sacrifice to strengthen our magic.”
column2: 议会之前，我们说过：“如果它们献祭来强化我们的魔法，就讲和。”

column1: The other clans agreed with us.
column2: 其他氏族同意我们。

column1: The other clans disagreed.
column2: 其他氏族不同意。

column1: They said it was stupid to make peace with the \x01Á. The delegation members were greatly affronted when our chieftains rejected them.
column2: 他们说与 \x01Á. 讲和是愚蠢的。当我们的酋长拒绝他们时，代表团成员感到极大的冒犯。

column1: They decided to ask them for treasures.
column2: 他们决定向他们索要财宝。

column1: They decided to ask them for cows.
column2: 他们决定向他们索要牛只。

column1: They decided to ask them to make war on another tribe.
column2: 他们决定要求他们对另一个部落开战。

column1: “Make peace if they give a treasure to each clan.”
column2: “如果它们给每个氏族一件财宝，就讲和。”

column1: Before the moot, we said: “Make peace if they give a treasure to each clan.”
column2: 议会之前，我们说过：“如果它们给每个氏族一件财宝，就讲和。”

column1: They decided to ask them to sacrifice to strengthen their clan magic.
column2: 他们决定要求他们献祭以强化他们的氏族魔法。

column1: “Make peace if they give cows to each clan.”
column2: “如果它们给每个氏族牛只，就讲和。”

column1: Before the moot, we said: “Make peace if they give cows to each clan.”
column2: 议会之前，我们说过：“如果它们给每个氏族牛只，就讲和。”

column1: “Our two tribes should ally to make war on another tribe.”
column2: “我们两个部落应该结盟，对另一个部落开战。”

column1: Which other tribe do you suggest to attack?
column2: 你建议攻击哪个其他部落？

column1: “They are swine. We should never make peace with them!”
column2: “他们是猪猡。我们绝不应与他们讲和！”

column1: At the moot, we said: “They are swine. We should never make peace with them!”
column2: 在议会上，我们说道：“他们是猪猡。我们绝不应与他们讲和！”

column1: The other clans agreed that the \x01Á were in many ways pig-like.
column2: 其他氏族同意， \x01Á 在很多方面像猪一样。

column1: The other clans agree that the \x01Á are in many ways pig-like.
column2: 其他氏族都认为 \x01Á 在许多方面像猪。

column1: When do you make war?
column2: 你们何时开战？

column1: Right away.
column2: 立刻。

column1: We decided to make immediate war on them.
column2: 我们决定立刻对他们开战。

column1: We decided to make war on them when Fire season next came.
column2: 我们决定等到下次火之季来临再对他们开战。

column1: Refuse their offer of peace.
column2: 拒绝他们的和平提议。

column1: We refused their offer of peace.
column2: 我们拒绝了他们的和平提议。

column1: The other clans did not agree with us. They thought it would be good to make peace with the \x01Á.
column2: 其他氏族并不赞同我们。他们认为与我们讲和是好事 \x01Á.

column1: They decided to ask them to sacrifice to strengthen our magic.
column2: 他们决定请求他们献祭以强化我们的魔法。

column1: We could not reach an agreement. There would be no peace between our tribes.
column2: 我们未能达成一致。我们部落之间将无和平可言。

column1: We reached an agreement, and made pledges of peace between our tribes.
column2: 我们达成了一致，并在部落间立下了和平誓言。

column1: They agreed to sacrifices, and the magic of all our clans was strengthened.
column2: 他们同意献祭，我们所有氏族的魔法都得到了强化。

column1: They gave each clan a treasure, a small tub of lotion called Heort’s Balm.
column2: 他们赐予每个氏族一件宝物，一小罐名为“希尔特香膏”的油膏。

column1: They said it should be dabbed on the forehead of our lawspeaker when arguing legal precedent.
column2: 他们说在辩论法律先例时，应将其涂抹在律法师的前额上。

column1: They gave each clan fifteen cows.
column2: 他们赐予每个氏族十五头牛。

column1: We decided to make immediate war on our foes.
column2: 我们决定立即向敌人开战。

column1: We decided to wage this war when Fire season next came.
column2: 我们决定在下一个火季来临时发动这场战争。

column1: They could not reach an agreement. There would be no peace between our tribes.
column2: 他们未能达成一致。我们部落之间将无和平可言。

column1: They reached an agreement.
column2: 他们达成了一致。

column1: The \x01Á agreed to sacrifices, and the magic of all our clans was strengthened.
column2: \x01Á 同意献祭，我们所有氏族的魔法都得到了强化。

column1: The \x01Á gave each clan a treasure, a small tub of lotion called Heort’s Balm. They said it should be dabbed on the forehead of our lawspeaker when arguing legal precedent.
column2: \x01Á 赐予每个氏族一件宝物，一小罐名为“希尔特香膏”的油膏。他们说在辩论法律先例时，应将其涂抹在律法师的前额上。

column1: The \x01Á gave each clan fifteen cows.
column2: \x01Á 赐予每个氏族十五头牛。

column1: We could use some more cows.
column2: 我们还能多用些牛。

column1: We have lots of cows, so we don’t need more. I have heard of the treasure they will likely offer; it is also a herd-growing treasure. We should ask for magic, instead.
column2: 我们已有许多牛，所以不需要更多。我听说过他们可能会提供的宝物；那也是一件能增长畜群的宝物。我们应该转而要求魔法。

column1: Treasures are valuable trade goods.
column2: 宝物是珍贵的贸易品。

column1: It is always good for two tribes to make war against another tribe, if you are one of the two.
column2: 两个部落对另一个部落开战总是好事——只要你是那两个之一。

column1: Peace is good — while it lasts.
column2: 和平是好事——只要它持续。

column1: Our tribe-mates resent our political maneuvering. They’re not likely to follow our lead.
column2: 我们的同胞憎恶我们的政治操纵。他们不太可能听从我们的领导。

column1: They should sacrifice for us.
column2: 他们应该为我们献祭。

column1: Our magic is already strong. Ask for a treasure, instead.
column2: 我们的魔法已经够强了。改为要求一件宝物吧。

column1: Ernalda will be offended if we make peace in Sea season by making war.
column2: 若我们在海之季通过开战来求和，厄纳尔达会感到冒犯。

column1: Ernalda will be offended if we make peace in Earth season by making war.
column2: 若我们在地之季通过开战来求和，厄纳尔达会感到冒犯。

column1: It would be a bitter irony if a peace agreement led to war.
column2: 若一纸和约反倒引向战争，那将是苦涩的讽刺。

column1: Peace is only good if it also brings death.
column2: 和平只有在也带来死亡时才是好的。

column1: You can never have too many cows.
column2: 牛永远不嫌多。

column1: The other members of our tribe hate us and will do the opposite of what we say. We should suggest the thing we least want.
column2: 我们部落的其他成员憎恨我们，会做与我们所言相反的事。我们应该提出我们最不想要的东西。

column1: They aren’t fit to clean our toenails!
column2: 他们连给我们洗脚趾甲都不配！

column1: We don’t need them!
column2: 我们不需要他们！

column1: Strangers show up and request hospitality. “We are from the distant East,” they say. “We are explorers, and we wish to learn about the peoples of this region so that we can report back to the scholars from our home country. If you would be willing to speak to us, we could give you something in return.”
column2: 陌生人出现并请求好客。“我们来自遥远的东方，”他们说。“我们是探险者，希望了解这片地区的各个民族，以便回去向祖国的学者报告。如果你们愿意与我们交谈，我们可以给予你们一些回报。”

column1: Strangers who said they were from the east requested hospitality.
column2: 自称来自东方的陌生人请求好客。

column1: They fought back, using weird implements to cast shrieking spells that hurt our ears and made us bleed. Their magic killed many, and gave a strange shaking disease to others. When we were overwhelmed, and could no longer fight, they admitted they were not from the east, but from the south. They had come at the behest of the Pharaoh, to punish us for depriving him of the Iron Spike. “Let all of Dragon Pass know that the Pharaoh’s reach is long, and his just fury unquenchable,” they said. Then they departed.
column2: 他们反击了，使用怪异的器具施放刺耳的咒语，刺痛我们的耳朵并让我们流血。他们的魔法杀死许多人，还让其他人患上奇怪的颤抖病。当我们被压制、无法再战斗时，他们承认自己并非来自东方，而是来自南方。他们是奉法老之命前来惩罚我们剥夺他的铁刺。“让整个龙之隘口都知道，法老的手伸得很长，他正义的怒火永不熄灭，”他们说。然后他们离开了。

column1: Give them hospitality, then ask them for cows.
column2: 给予他们好客，然后向他们索要牛只。

column1: We invited them into our hall.
column2: 我们邀请他们进入自己的厅堂。

column1: They seemed to enjoy our hospitality. As the evening wore on, and a spirit of friendliness seemed to grow between us, we asked them for cows. The one who did most of the talking smiled. “We have something to give you,” he said, “but it is not cows.”
column2: 他们似乎享受了我们的好客。随着夜色渐深，一种友好的气氛似乎在我们之间滋长，我们向他们索要牛只。那个主要说话的人微笑道：“我们有东西要给你们，”他说，“但不是牛。”

column1: Give them hospitality, then ask them for stories of Orlanth and Ernalda.
column2: 给予他们好客，然后向他们索要奥兰斯和厄纳尔达的故事。

column1: They seemed to enjoy our hospitality. As the evening wore on, and a spirit of friendliness seemed to grow between us, we asked them to tell us stories of Ernalda and Orlanth. The one who did most of the talking smiled. “We have something to give you,” he said, “but it is not tales.”
column2: 他们似乎享受了我们的好客。随着夜色渐深，一种友好的气氛似乎在我们之间滋长，我们请他们讲述厄纳尔达和奥兰斯的故事。那个主要说话的人微笑道：“我们有东西要给你们，”他说，“但不是传说。”

column1: Give them hospitality, then offer them gifts.
column2: 给予他们好客，然后向他们赠送礼物。

column1: They seemed to enjoy our hospitality. As the evening wore on, and a spirit of friendliness seemed to grow between us, we told them we wished to offer them gifts. The one who did most of the talking smiled. “There are only two things we want from you,” he said, “Your blood, and your fear.”
column2: 他们似乎享受了我们的好客。随着夜色渐深，一种友好的气氛似乎在我们之间滋长，我们告诉他们想赠送礼物。那个主要说话的人微笑道：“我们只想要你们的两样东西，”他说，“你们的血，和你们的恐惧。”

column1: They attacked us, using weird implements to cast shrieking spells that hurt our ears and made us bleed. Their magic killed many, and gave a strange shaking disease to others. When we were overwhelmed, and could no longer fight, they admitted they were not from the east, but from the south. They had come at the behest of the Pharaoh, to punish us for depriving him of the Iron Spike. “Let all of Dragon Pass know that the Pharaoh’s reach is long, and his just fury unquenchable,” they said. Then they departed.
column2: 他们攻击了我们，使用怪异的器具施放刺耳的咒语，刺痛我们的耳朵并让我们流血。他们的魔法杀死许多人，还让其他人患上奇怪的颤抖病。当我们被压制、无法再战斗时，他们承认自己并非来自东方，而是来自南方。他们是奉法老之命前来惩罚我们剥夺他的铁刺。“让整个龙之隘口都知道，法老的手伸得很长，他正义的怒火永不熄灭，”他们说。然后他们离开了。

column1: A gift of cows would seal the friendship between our distant peoples.
column2: 赠送牛只可以巩固我们两个遥远民族之间的友谊。

column1: I wouldn’t turn down an offer of more cows, but we don’t need them.
column2: 我不会拒绝更多的牛，但我们不需要它们。

column1: They don’t have any cows with them. They’re explorers; how can they give us cows?
column2: 他们身边没有牛。他们是探险者，怎么能给我们牛呢？

column1: If they are from the east, why do they speak Tradetalk with a southern accent?
column2: 如果他们是东方来的，为什么说贸易语带着南方口音？

column1: Kill them and take their things!
column2: 杀了他们，拿走他们的东西！

column1: These men are warriors. The only thing they plan to tell their “scholars” is the state of our defenses.
column2: 这些人是武士。他们唯一打算告诉“学者”的，是我们防御的状况。

column1: If they do mean us harm, it is better to surprise than be surprised.

column2: 故事可以非常强大。

column2: 他们没有给我们攻击他们的理由。

column2: 我很惊讶这些人是东方来的。他们和我在故事中期待的样子完全不同。

column2: 你注意到他说话时指关节扭动的方式了吗？如果他说的是真话，那我就是兰考尔·姆伊的女儿。

column1: Attack or be attacked, that’s what I say.
column2: 要么进攻，要么被攻击，我就是这么说的。

column1: We must impress these foreigners with our generosity.
column2: 我们必须以慷慨打动这些外乡人。

column1: They’re agents of the Pharaoh come to kill us with evil sorcery!
column2: 他们是法老的走狗，来用邪恶巫术杀死我们的！

column1: Greet people with peace in your heart, and prosperity will be yours.
column2: 以心中和平迎接他人，繁荣将属于你。

column1: We must learn how they worship Orlanth and Ernalda.
column2: 我们必须了解他们如何崇拜奥兰斯和厄纳尔达。

column1: Showing no regard for the laws of hospitality, they attacked us. They used weird implements to cast shrieking spells that hurt our ears and made us bleed. Their magic killed many, and gave a strange shaking disease to others. They concentrated their dread spells on our ring members, and slew \x01@\x1A, \x01@\x19, and \x01@\x18 with their painful noises. When we were overwhelmed, and could no longer fight, they admitted they were not from the east, but from the south. They had come at the behest of the Pharaoh, to punish us for depriving him of the Iron Spike. “Let all of Dragon Pass know that the Pharaoh’s reach is long, and his just fury unquenchable,” they said. Then they departed.
column2: 他们全然不顾好客之法，袭击了我们。他们用奇异的器具施放刺耳的咒语，伤我们耳朵，令我们流血。他们的魔法杀死了许多人，又让其他人染上奇怪的颤抖之病。他们将可怕的咒语集中加诸我们的议会成员，用那痛苦之声杀死了 \x01@\x1A、 \x01@\x19和 \x01@\x18 。待我们被击垮、无力再战之时，他们承认自己并非来自东方，而是来自南方。他们是奉法老之命而来，惩罚我们夺走了他的铁刺。“让龙之隘口全境皆知，法老之手伸得很长，他公正的怒火永不熄灭。”他们说完便离去了。

column2: 他们就侮辱 \x01D8一事道了歉，并赠送礼物以示诚意。

column1: They claimed to be offended by our accusation of poor hospitality. “\x01D8 is a fool, and you are fools to be pressing his claim!” their lawspeaker cried.
column2: 他们声称被我们指责待客不周所冒犯。“\x01D8 是个蠢货，你们竟坚持他的主张，更是蠢货！”他们的律法师喊道。

column1: No poem ever solved a problem.
column2: 从没有一首诗解决过问题。

column1: A well-phrased satire stings longer than a sword; its bite can linger for generations.
column2: 一首措辞巧妙的讽刺诗比剑刺得更久；它的尖刻能延续数代。

column1: It will be hard to beat them on the battlefield.
column2: 在战场上击败他们会很困难。

column1: \x01D8 and his fellow weaponthanes are not really offended.
column2: \x01D8 和他手下的武器领主们并未真正被冒犯。

column1: \x01D8 and his fellow weaponthanes are offended.
column2: \x01D8 和他手下的武器领主们被冒犯了。

column1: \x01D8 holds this insult close to his bosom. It will be hard to convince him to give it up.
column2: \x01D8 将此侮辱深藏于心。要说服他放下很难。

column1: \x01D8 holds this insult close to his bosom. It will be hard, but not impossible, to convince him to give it up.
column2: \x01D8 将此侮辱深藏于心。要说服他放下很难，但并非不可能。

column1: This could lead to a feud.
column2: 这可能导致一场世仇。

column1: Relations between our clans are poor, and they are daring us to make things worse.
column2: 我们两族之间的关系本就糟糕，他们是在激我们让事情变得更糟。

column1: Relations between our clans have been good. This must be some kind of misunderstanding.
column2: 我们两族之间的关系一直很好。这一定是某种误会。

column1: Our allies are not always happy with us, but we should be able to trust them.
column2: 我们的盟友并不总对我们满意，但我们应当能信任他们。

column1: Don’t interrupt the planting — a poem is as good a raid for now.
column2: 别打断播种——眼下，一首诗跟一场劫掠一样管用。

column1: Don’t interrupt the harvest — a poem is as good a raid for now.
column2: 别打断收获——眼下，一首诗跟一场劫掠一样管用。

column1: A poem, a poem! A scurrilous poem!
column2: 来首诗，来首诗！一首下流的讽刺诗！

column1: I’d sooner punch a man in the face than insult him with a clever kenning.
column2: 我宁愿一拳揍在对方脸上，也不愿用巧妙的比喻来侮辱他。

column1: They can’t have meant to insult him.
column2: 他们不可能是故意侮辱他。

column1: The hole-rags fed us worm-food, showing all they were honor-shriven.
column2: 那些破布洞们招待我们虫粮，显露出他们全是失格之人。

column1: Wouldn’t the elves just love it if we fell to fighting amongst ourselves?
column2: 精灵们难道不乐见我们自相争斗吗？

column1: Tell them that we have many clever brides, but they will not marry bad hosts.
column2: 告诉他们我们有很多聪慧的新娘，但她们不会嫁给坏东道。

column1: Don’t talk about raiding our allies. Talk with them first.
column2: 别谈劫掠我们的盟友。先跟他们谈谈。

column1: The thrall \x01D; reported that the carl \x01D< had been slain by a centaur.
column2: 奴隶 \x01D; 报告说自由民 \x01D< 被一名半人马杀害了。

column2: 为 \x01D<谱写一首颂诗。

column1: We composed a poem in honor of \x01D<.
column2: 我们为 \x01D<谱写一首颂诗。

column1: \x01@N’s poem was moving, and everyone said that \x01D<’s spirit would be honored to hear it.
column2: \x01@N的诗作感人至深，所有人都说 \x01D<的英灵听到它必感荣耀。

column2: \x01@N 悲痛欲绝，未能恰当地吟诵 \x04 的诗作，效果全失。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors told us that \x01D< was not slain by a centaur, but secretly murdered by \x01D;.
column2: 我们的祖先之灵告诉我们， \x01D< 并非被半人马所杀，而是被 \x01D;秘密谋害。

column1: Console \x01D<’s family.
column2: 慰问 \x01D<的家人。

column1: We consoled \x01D<’s family.
column2: 我们慰问了 \x01D<的家人。

column1: His kinfolk thanked the clan ring for their words of sympathy.
column2: 他的族人感谢氏族议会的慰问之言。

column1: His kinfolk were seized by grief, and would hear no words of sympathy.
column2: 他的族人被悲痛攫住，听不进任何慰问之言。

column1: Outlaw \x01D; for secret murder.
column2: 以秘密谋杀罪将 \x01D; 放逐。

column1: We outlawed \x01D; for secret murder.
column2: 我们以秘密谋杀罪将 \x01D; 放逐。

column1: Do you see to it that he is then killed?
column2: 你是否确保他随后被处死？

column1: A weaponthane was sent to kill him. The people were glad when he returned with \x01D;’s blood on his tunic.
column2: 一名武器侍从被派去杀他。当他回来时，外衣上沾着 \x01D;的血，人们很高兴。

column1: The people said that the ring should not have allowed the treacherous one to live.

column1: Sacrifice to the gods to speed \x01D<’s spirit to the realm of the dead.

column1: We sacrificed to the gods to speed \x01D<’s spirit to the realm of the dead.
column2: 我们向众神献祭，以加速 \x01D<的灵魂前往死者国度。

column1: As the god-talkers placed the sacrifice in the temple, it bled. \x01D<’s spirit was heard to cry, “\x01D; killed me!”
column2: 当神言者将祭品放入神庙时，它流血了。听到 \x01D<的灵魂哭喊：“\x01D; 杀了我！”

column2: 人们很高兴我们做了这个姿态。

column1: Send a war party to hunt centaurs.
column2: 派遣一支战团去猎杀半人马。

column1: We sent a war party to hunt centaurs.
column2: 我们派遣了一支战团去猎杀半人马。

column1: We did not find any centaurs.
column2: 我们没有找到任何半人马。

column1: We found centaurs and did battle with them.
column2: 我们找到了半人马并与他们交战。

column1: We slew \x01@\x11 of them, all the while shouting \x01D<’s name, so his spirit could hear that we had avenged him.
column2: 我们杀死了 \x01@\x11 个，同时一直呼喊 \x01D<的名字，这样他的灵魂就能听到我们为他报了仇。

column1: They used their horse-halves to fight unfairly, running around us faster than we could strike at them. They wounded some of us, and killed others.
column2: 他们利用自己的马身半部不公平地战斗，绕着我们从我们攻击不及的速度跑动。他们伤了我们一些人，杀了另一些人。

column1: \x01@\x05, who led the party, was among the slain.
column2: \x01@\x05领导战团者亦被杀。

column1: We should be trading with the beastfolk, not fighting them.
column2: 我们应该与兽人贸易，而不是与他们战斗。

column1: The beastfolk already wish us harm. Let’s not make things worse.
column2: 兽人已经想伤害我们了。别让事情变得更糟。

column1: The beastfolk have been friendly in the past. Why would they do such a thing?
column2: 兽人过去一直很友好。他们为什么会做这种事？

column1: There is something odd about the way \x01D; tells his story.
column2: \x01D; 讲述故事的方式有些古怪。

column1: The centaurs will surely destroy us if we try to fight them.
column2: 如果我们试图与半人马战斗，他们一定会毁灭我们。

column1: Our warriors are anxious to avenge \x01D<’s death.
column2: 我们的战士急于为 \x01D<之死复仇。

column1: The centaurs will be hard to find. We must send a skilled hunter to lead the war party.
column2: 半人马很难找到。我们必须派一名熟练的猎人领导战团。

column1: We must send a skilled hunter to lead the war party, and at least six warriors to accompany him.
column2: 我们必须派一名熟练的猎人领导战团，并至少六名战士陪同他。

column1: A poem is the best way to ensure that \x01D< is remembered.
column2: 创作一首诗是确保 \x01D< 被铭记的最佳方式。

column1: The people are sad. We must do something to bring them cheer.
column2: 人们很悲伤。我们必须做点什么让他们高兴起来。

column1: What’s the point of a divination? We know what happened. Sacrifice instead.
column2: 占卜有什么用？我们知道发生了什么。不如献祭。

column1: Our magic is weak. There is little point in performing a sacrifice.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱。进行献祭没什么意义。

column1: \x01D; is lying. He killed \x01D< himself.
column2: \x01D; 在撒谎。他亲手杀害了 \x01D< 。

column1: Sacrifice in aid of \x01D<’s spirit, and we will all be rewarded.
column2: 献祭以帮助 \x01D<的灵魂，我们将得到回报。

column1: We must build another temple, to increase the chances that the gods will hear us in times like these.
column2: 我们必须再建一座神庙，以增加在这样的时刻众神听到我们的机会。

column1: We must console his kinfolk.
column2: 我们必须慰问他的族人。

column1: “A son is a blessing, but if his father is dead, he was born late.”
column2: “儿子是福，但如果父亲已死，他就出生得太晚了。”

column1: The others of our tribe will not like it if we provoke a war with the beastfolk.
column2: 如果我们挑起与兽人的战争，我们部落的其他人不会喜欢。

column1: A poem costs less than a sacrifice.
column2: 一首诗的花费比献祭少。

column1: Tusk Riders killed a woman and wounded two others.
column2: 獠牙骑手杀了一个女人，伤了另外两人。

column2: 他们杀了一些牛，弄脏了尸体。

column1: Tusk Riders killed some cattle, fouling the carcasses.
column2: 獠牙骑手杀了一些牛，弄脏了尸体。

column1: They desecrate the temple to \x01@\x14.
column2: 他们亵渎了供奉 \x01@\x14的神庙。

column1: Tusk Riders desecrated the temple to \x01@\x14.
column2: 獠牙骑手亵渎了供奉 \x01@\x14的神庙。

column1: We told the people that Dragon Pass was a dangerous place, and that such raids were to be expected.
column2: 我们告诉人们龙隘是个危险之地，这样的袭击是意料之中的。

column1: Offer to pay Tusk Riders to attack another clan.
column2: 提议付钱给獠牙骑手让他们攻击另一个氏族。

column1: We decided to offer payment if they would attack another clan.
column2: 我们决定如果他们愿意攻击另一个氏族，就提供酬劳。

column1: Who leads the delegation to parley with the Tusk Riders?
column2: 谁率领代表团与獠牙骑手谈判？

column1: How much payment are you prepared to offer?
column2: 你准备提供多少酬劳？

column1: Which clan do you want them to attack?
column2: 你想让他们攻击哪个氏族？

column1: We did not find any Tusk Riders.
column2: 我们没有找到任何獠牙骑手。

column1: \x01@\x05 found the Tusk Riders, and parleyed with them.
column2: \x01@\x05 找到了獠牙骑手，并与他们谈判。

column1: Later, we heard that they had done so, burning several steads and trampling some fields.
column2: 后来，我们听说他们确实这样做了，烧了几个农庄，踩踏了一些田地。

column1: They said that they would definitely attack us again, and rode off.
column2: 他们说他们肯定会再次袭击我们，然后骑马离开了。

column1: They attacked the delegation, saying “We can attack you and still take the tribute.”
column2: 他们袭击了代表团，说：“我们既能袭击你们，还能拿走贡品。”

column1: We slew \x01@\x11 of them, toppling them from their giant boars and crushing their throats under our boots. Our swords pierced them many times.
column2: 我们杀死了 \x01@\x11 个，将他们从巨大的野猪背上掀下来，用靴子踩碎他们的喉咙。我们的剑多次刺穿他们。

column1: They ran us down with their gigantic boars, killing some and wounding others. They fled into the woods, laughing obscenely.
column2: 他们用巨大的野猪冲倒我们，杀死了一些，伤了另一些。他们逃进树林，猥亵地大笑着。

column1: Offer tribute to the Tusk Riders.
column2: 向獠牙骑手进献贡品。

column1: We decided to offer them tribute.
column2: 我们决定向他们进贡。

column1: How much tribute are you prepared to offer?
column2: 你准备进贡多少？

column1: They agreed not to attack us any more.
column2: 他们同意不再攻击我们。

column1: They said that they would enjoy attacking us again, and rode off.
column2: 他们说很乐意再次袭击我们，然后策马而去。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods for aid against Tusk Riders.
column2: 向神明献祭，祈求助我们对抗獠牙骑手。

column1: We sacrificed to the gods for aid against Tusk Riders.
column2: 我们向神明献祭，祈求助我们对抗獠牙骑手。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were good. If we fought the Tusk Riders, \x01@\x07 would aid us.
column2: 神言者说吉兆显现。若我们与獠牙骑手作战， \x01@\x07 将助我们一臂之力。

column1: The god-talkers said that \x01@\x07 had helped us, but perhaps not enough to guarantee victory against the Tusk Riders.
column2: 神言者说 \x01@\x07 已施以援手，但或许不足以确保战胜獠牙骑手。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were poor; \x01@\x07 had not heard our pleas.
column2: 神言者说凶兆显现； \x01@\x07 未垂听我们的祈求。

column1: Send a war party to hunt for Tusk Riders.
column2: 派出战团猎杀獠牙骑手。

column1: We sent a war party to hunt for them.
column2: 我们派出战团猎杀他们。

column1: We found Tusk Riders and did battle with them.
column2: 我们发现了獠牙骑手并与他们交战。

column1: Those giant boars they ride are intelligent, and tell the Tusk Riders what to do.
column2: 他们骑的那些巨型野猪很聪明，会指挥獠牙骑手行动。

column1: We are too poor to pay tribute, or to sacrifice.
column2: 我们太穷了，无力进贡或献祭。

column1: We can pay tribute, or sacrifice, if that is what the rest of you think wise.
column2: 我们可以进贡或献祭，如果诸位觉得这样明智的话。

column1: Tusk Riders are easy to out-bargain.
column2: 獠牙骑手很容易被议价压过。

column1: Tusk Riders are easy to out-bargain, except for the fact that they are easily tempted to violence.
column2: 獠牙骑手很容易被议价压过，只是他们很容易受暴力诱惑。

column1: Tusk Riders are tough, but not invulnerable.
column2: 獠牙骑手很强悍，但并非无懈可击。

column1: Send at least eight warriors to kill Tusk Riders, and at least four to bargain with them.
column2: 至少派八名战士去杀獠牙骑手，至少派四名去与他们谈判。

column1: Send at least ten warriors to kill Tusk Riders, and at least five to bargain with them.
column2: 至少派十名战士去杀獠牙骑手，至少派五名去与他们谈判。

column1: Sending Tusk Riders to attack another clan is not seen as a sign of friendship.
column2: 让獠牙骑手去攻击另一个氏族，并不会被视为友谊的表示。

column1: The magic of the Tusk Riders is greater than that of the dragonewts and beastfolk combined.
column2: 獠牙骑手的魔法比龙人和兽人的魔法加起来还要强大。

column1: Sacrificing to the gods will strengthen our clan magic.
column2: 向神明献祭将增强我们的氏族魔法。

column1: Sacrificing to Orlanth or another war god will strengthen our clan magic.
column2: 向奥兰斯或另一位战争之神献祭将增强我们的氏族魔法。

column1: Sacrificing to Orlanth or another war god will strengthen our clan magic. Then we can attack the Tusk Riders, and have a good chance of winning.
column2: 向奥兰斯或另一位战争之神献祭将增强我们的氏族魔法。这样我们就能攻击獠牙骑手，并有很大胜算。

column1: Sending a large party of our farmers off during Sea season will mean a lean harvest, later.
column2: 在海季派出一大群农夫外出，意味着日后收成会减少。

column1: Sending a large party of our farmers off during Earth season will mean a long, hungry year.
column2: 在地季派出一大群农夫外出，意味着将迎来漫长、饥馑的一年。

column1: Tusk Riders are half human, half troll, and all nasty.
column2: 獠牙骑手一半是人、一半是巨魔，而且全都凶恶至极。

column1: Let me at them!
column2: 让我去会会他们！

column1: I yearn to place my boot upon a tusk rider’s throat.
column2: 我渴望把靴子踩在一个獠牙骑手的喉咙上。

column1: I can’t believe they — didn’t we — what about increasing — increasing — I hate Tusk Riders!
column2: 我真不敢相信他们——我们不是——不如增加——增加——我恨獠牙骑手！

column1: They desecrated the temple. The gods will surely aid us in destroying them.
column2: 他们亵渎了神殿。神明定会助我们消灭他们。

column1: Your explorers encounter a woman from Heortland while mapping the \x01@O. Her name is \x01D>, and she is fleeing from her homeland. “I slew an agent of the Pharaoh, who sought to tell chosen Orlanthi chieftains how to interpret the laws of our people. Although my act was just, and supported by the spirits of our ancestors, the leaders were too afraid of the Pharaoh to stand up for what is right. They outlawed me, and sent pursuers to kill me. I think I have outdistanced my pursuers, but would be lying if I said I was sure of that.” The explorers were moved by her words, and brought her here, suggesting that you should give her asylum.

column1: Explorers found the warrior \x01D>, who fled from the injustice of the Pharaoh, and said we should give her asylum.
column2: 探险者发现了战士 \x01D>，她因不堪法老的不公而逃亡，并说我们应该给予她庇护。

column1: Adopt her as a weaponthane in the \x01Cc’s household.

column1: The people were proud to see a foe of the Pharaoh honored in such a fashion.

column1: Adopt her as a weaponthane.

column2: 这是取悦祖先的好机会。从这位萨满手中买下这些奴隶，让他们干活。

column2: 那些奴隶看起来不太健康。让他们下地干活会要了他们的命。

column1: Whatever we say to her will be the wrong thing.
column2: 无论我们对她说些什么，都会是错的。

column2: 除非我们按全价买下，否则她会诅咒我们，让我们的牙龈流血！

column1: Reject these unhealthy thralls.
column2: 拒绝这些不健康的奴隶。

column1: We must remember never to marry into this crazy clan.
column2: 我们必须记住，永远不要和这个疯氏族联姻。

column2: 我们从那个古怪萨满手里买来的那些奴隶，果然是一桩赔本买卖。我们接手时他们就有病，而且一天比一天病重。即便给了一些休息和好食物，他们还是一个个虚弱死去，一个不剩。

column1: Those are indeed fine horses.

column2: 这案子听起来很复杂。双方都有先例支持。

column1: He who promises nothing disappoints no one.
column2: 什么也不许诺的人，不会让任何人失望。

column1: Bad King Urgrain took gifts from two clans, then ruled against both.

column1: Why do they give us horses, and not wine?

column1: \x01BX complains that, while he was a guest at the \x01@! market, he was bullied and insulted by a pair of their weaponthanes. “They called us stickpickers, lichen eaters, and rag-wearers. They said that our men are too friendly with our sheep, because our women do not bear looking at. They said that Chalana Arroy cries whenever we use the word ‘mercy’, and that Humakt spits whenever we say ‘honor’.”
column2: \x01BX 抱怨道，他在 \x01@! 市场做客时，被他们的一对武器领主欺凌侮辱。“他们叫我们拾柴人、地衣食客、穿破布的人。他们说我们的男人与羊太过亲昵，因为我们的女人不堪入目。他们说我们每次用‘慈悲’这个词，查拉娜·阿洛伊就会哭泣；我们每次说‘荣誉’，胡马克特就会吐唾沫。”

column1: \x01BX was bullied and insulted by a pair of \x01@! weaponthanes at their clan market.
column2: \x01BX 在 \x01@! 氏族的市场上，被一对武器领主欺凌侮辱。

column1: Convince \x01BX to forget these insults.
column2: 说服 \x01BX 忘记这些侮辱。

column1: The ring said that \x01BX should forget their insults.
column2: 长老会说 \x01BX 应该忘记那些侮辱。

column1: “They did not simply insult us!” \x01BX cried. “They said the gods despised us! We must punish them for this vile calumny!”
column2: “他们不只是侮辱我们！” \x01BX 哭喊道。“他们说众神鄙视我们！我们必须惩罚他们的恶毒诽谤！”

column1: The ring did nothing about this.
column2: 长老会对此无动于衷。

column1: We had more important things to worry about than marketplace chatter.
column2: 我们有比市井闲话更重要的事要操心。

column1: The people resented the ring’s attitude. “If you are not willing to defend the clan’s honor,” they said, “who else is?”
column2: 族人对长老会的态度感到愤懑。“如果你们不愿捍卫氏族的荣誉，”他们说，“那还有谁愿意？”

column1: The people were happy to have avenged their insults.
column2: 族人们很高兴为侮辱复了仇。

column1: The raid was unsuccessful, so we were doubly shamed.
column2: 袭击没有成功，于是我们受尽双重耻辱。

column1: Send for shamans to curse them.
column2: 召来萨满诅咒他们。

column1: We sent for shamans to curse them.
column2: 我们召来了萨满诅咒他们。

column1: The least they will accept is \x01@\x13 cows.
column2: 他们最少愿意接受 \x01@\x13 头牛。

column1: They will not lower their price.
column2: 他们不肯降低要价。

column1: We decided that the price of the curse was too rich for us.
column2: 我们认定诅咒的代价对我们来说太高了。

column1: We waited to hear that they suffered humiliating effects from the curse, but we got no such news.
column2: 我们等待着听闻他们遭受诅咒的屈辱后果，却没有听到任何消息。

column1: Threaten them with a raid.
column2: 用袭击威胁他们。

column2: 我们用袭击威胁了他们。

column2: 他们同意不想因为这种事面对袭击。他们让侮辱人的武器领主撤回言论，并没收了他们的银戒指。他们将戒指作为礼物送给了我们。

column1: They said they looked forward to being raided by us, for then they could prove that the gods laughed at our martial prowess.
column2: 他们表示期待被我们袭击，因为那样他们就能证明众神嘲笑我们的战斗能力。

column1: Shamans will be too hard to find.
column2: 萨满太难找了。

column1: Raid the scoundrels!
column2: 袭击那些恶棍！

column1: We will beat them if we raid them, and cow them if we threaten them.
column2: 如果我们袭击他们，就能打败他们；如果我们威胁他们，就能吓住他们。

column1: They are stronger than we are. It will take luck to beat them, and a confident tongue to intimidate them.
column2: 他们比我们强大。打败他们需要运气，恐吓他们需要自信的言辞。

column1: If we do not challenge these insults, we are admitting that they are true.
column2: 如果我们不挑战这些侮辱，就等于承认它们是真的。

column1: The people will be disheartened if we do nothing.
column2: 若我们无所作为，族人将心灰意冷。

column1: If we threaten them, and they insult us further, the people will be even unhappier.
column2: 若我们威胁他们，而他们进一步侮辱我们，族人会更加不满。

column1: Shamans are crazy. They’d curse us just as soon as look at us.
column2: 萨满都疯了。他们一看见我们就想诅咒我们。

column1: This is a job for shamans.
column2: 这是萨满的活。

column2: 查拉娜·阿罗伊当然不会每次我们一说“仁慈！”就哭泣。我们应……不能被这种胡言乱语冒犯。

column1: At least they did not accuse us of being overfond of our horses!
column2: 至少他们没有指责我们太爱马！

column1: Don’t you think that if we get all upset it will lend credence to the sheep accusation?
column2: 你不觉得我们若惊慌失措，反而会让关于羊的指控显得可信吗？

column1: Do not let foolish words distract us from our true enemies: the elves.
column2: 不要让蠢话分散我们对真正敌人的关注：精灵。

column1: That pack of inbred moss-lickers say that we are eaters of lichen? They must die!
column2: 那帮近亲繁殖的舔苔者说我们是吃地衣的？他们必须死！

column1: The worm-tongues held up a capture-glass, and insulted what they saw within.
column2: 虫舌们举起一面捕捉镜，侮辱了镜中所见。

column1: Do not injure the good women of clan \x01@! because they are cursed with stupid men.
column2: 不要伤害 \x01@! 氏族的好女人们，因为她们被蠢男人诅咒了。

column1: \x01@\x14, a trader from the northern kingdom of Tarsh, is touring Dragon Pass in search of carls willing to leave their clans for farming opportunities in his homeland. The carls of your clan listen to him with great interest. “There is much good land, ready for the taking. You will be safe from raids, and safe from the many inhumans, monsters, and foreigners who bedevil you here in Dragon Pass. Our king has declared that every new farmer who settles our lands will get a herd of 30 cows.”
column2: \x01@\x14一位来自北方塔什王国的商人，正在龙之隘口游历，寻找愿意离开氏族前往他故乡耕种谋生的自由民。你氏族的自由民饶有兴致地听他讲话。“那里有大量良田，等着开垦。你们将免受劫掠，免受那些在龙之隘口折磨你们的众多非人、怪物和外乡人的侵扰。我们的国王已经宣布，每个在我们土地上定居的新农夫都将获得30头牛的畜群。”

column1: \x01@\x14, a trader from the northern kingdom of Tarsh, tried to convince some of our carls to leave us for farming opportunities in his homeland.
column2: \x01@\x14一位来自北方塔什王国的商人，试图说服我们的一些自由民离开我们去他故乡耕种。

column2: 说服自由民， \x01@\x14的条件中暗藏陷阱。

column2: \x01@N 说 \x01@\x14的条件中一定有隐藏陷阱。

column1: The carls agreed, and would not go with \x01@\x14. They praised \x01@N’s sharp eye for chicanery. We decided that he was exaggerating, making a loan of cows sound like a gift.
column2: 自由民同意了，不愿跟 \x01@\x14走。他们称赞 \x01@N对欺诈的敏锐眼光。我们断定他夸大了，把牛只的借贷说得像馈赠。

column1: The carls disagreed, and said that \x01@\x14’s offer was an honest one.
column2: 自由民不同意，说 \x01@\x14的条件是诚实的。

column1: \x01@\x1A carls and their families left with \x01@\x14. Those left behind were sad to see them go.
column2: \x01@\x1A 自由民及其家人带着 \x01@\x14离开了。留下的人看着他们离去，心中悲戚。

column1: Convince carls that they will be cut off from their ancestors if they go.
column2: 说服自由民，让他们明白如果离开，就会与祖先断绝联系。

column2: \x01@N 说他们如果离开，就会与祖先断绝联系。

column1: The carls agreed that \x01@N was right, and said they would not separate themselves from the spirits of their ancestors.
column2: 自由民同意 \x01@N 说得对，表示不会与祖先的英灵分离。

column1: The carls said their ancestors would understand if they left to seek opportunity.
column2: 自由民说，如果离开去寻求机会，祖先会理解的。

column1: Encourage some carls to go.
column2: 鼓励一些自由民离开。

column2: 长老会鼓励一些自由民离开。

column1: The people were unhappy; they said it seemed the ring members were pushing our kinfolk away.
column2: 人们很不满；他们说环成员似乎是在赶走我们的亲人。

column1: The people toasted the ring members; they said they were generous, because they were willing to give people the freedom to seek their own way.
column2: 人们向环成员敬酒；他们说环成员很慷慨，愿意给予人们自由去寻找自己的道路。

column1: \x01@\x1A carls said they would take their families to farm in Tarsh.
column2: \x01@\x1A 自由民说他们会带着家人去塔什务农。

column1: However, it turned out that no one wanted to go to Tarsh.
column2: 然而，结果没人愿意去塔什。

column1: Forbid carls to go.
column2: 禁止自由民离开。

column1: The ring said that no one could go to Tarsh.
column2: 长老会说任何人都不准去塔什。

column1: The people were unhappy; they said the clan ring wanted to keep them poor, stupid, and obedient.
column2: 人们很不满；他们说氏族议会想让他们保持贫穷、愚蠢和顺从。

column1: The people toasted the ring members; they said they were wise, because they were willing to fight to keep the clan together.
column2: 人们向环成员敬酒；他们说环成员很明智，因为他们愿意战斗来维持氏族的团结。

column1: Tell carls they are free to go, but that you wish them to stay.
column2: 告诉自由民他们可以自由离开，但你希望他们留下。

column2: \x01@N 说如果自由民想离开，氏族不会阻拦，但他们应该留下。

column2: 自由民被 \x01@N的话语打动；他们说很高兴拥有决定的自由，并且决定留下与我们在一起。

column1: Our carls would never leave us.
column2: 我们的自由民永远不会离开我们。
