column1: There are already too many carls for the weaponthanes to defend. Let some of them leave.
column2: 自由民已经太多，武器领主无力守卫。让其中一些人离开吧。

column1: \x01@\x14 is a cunning salesman.
column2: \x01@\x14 是个狡猾的说客。

column1: \x01@\x14 is a cunning salesman; he exaggerates the benefits of his proposal.
column2: \x01@\x14 是个狡猾的说客；他夸大了他提议的好处。

column1: Although \x01@\x14 is a cunning salesman, I can show how he exaggerates the benefits of his proposal.
column2: 虽然 \x01@\x14 是个狡猾的说客，但我要指出他是如何夸大他提议的好处的。

column1: If others see that our carls are anxious to leave, our reputation will suffer.
column2: 如果别人看到我们的自由民急于离开，我们的声誉会受损。

column1: We must let them know they are free, but also that we want them to stay.
column2: 我们必须让他们知道他们是自由的，但我们也希望他们留下。

column1: If they go, the carls will be cut off from the spirits of their ancestors.
column2: 如果他们走了，自由民就会与祖先的英灵断绝联系。

column1: Let me talk to the carls. I can explain to them that they will be cut off from the spirits of their ancestors if they go.
column2: 让我去跟自由民谈谈。我可以向他们解释，如果离开，就会与祖先的英灵断绝联系。

column1: When Bad King Urgrain lost the Chalice of Ernalda, his carls wished to desert him. He said he would hunt them down and kill them if they did. So they stayed, but plotted his downfall.
column2: 当恶王乌格兰丢失了厄娜尔达圣杯时，他的自由民想要抛弃他。他说如果他们敢走，他就会追捕并杀死他们。于是他们留下来了，但密谋推翻他。

column1: Thirty cows is quite an offer. There must be a catch to it.
column2: 三十头牛可是个大价钱。这里面一定有蹊跷。

column1: No one offers thirty cows out of goodness and generosity.
column2: 没人会出于善良和慷慨就白白给予三十头牛。

column1: I told you the Tarshites would try to steal our carls.
column2: 我告诉过你们，塔什人试图偷走我们的自由民。

column1: What would Orlanth want us to do?
column2: 奥兰斯会希望我们怎么做？

column1: If they really want to leave, we can’t stop them. Let’s at least get credit for letting them do what they want.
column2: 如果他们真的想离开，我们拦不住。至少让他们做自己想做的事，我们还能落个好名声。

column1: Apologize for an error made in the heat of the moment.
column2: 为一时的冲动所犯的错误道歉。

column1: \x01@\x0B apologized for an error made in the heat of the moment.
column2: \x01@\x0B 为一时的冲动所犯的错误道歉。

column1: The chieftains said that it took a wise leader to admit fault, and renewed their pledges of fealty to \x01@\x0B.
column2: 酋长们说，承认错误需要明智的领袖，并重新向 \x01@\x0B宣誓效忠。

column1: The chieftains said that words were good, but actions were better. They said they would watch to see if \x01@\x0B’s judgment improved in the seasons to come.
column2: 酋长们说，言语虽好，行动更佳。他们说会在未来的季节里观察 \x01@\x0B的判断是否有所改善。

column1: The chieftains agreed that the \x01@\x0B was not at fault for a decision made while under the influence of hostile spirits.
column2: 酋长们一致认为， \x01@\x0B 在敌对神灵影响下做出的决定，不应归咎于他。

column1: The chieftains said, “You have proven your villainy. If you are going to lie to us, you should at least try to lie well. This deception would not fool an uninitiated shepherd boy. You must step down, or we will take the throne from you.”
column2: 酋长们说：“你已经证明了你的恶行。如果你要对我们撒谎，至少应该撒得像样一点。这种欺骗连一个未受启蒙的牧羊少年都骗不了。你必须退位，否则我们将夺走你的王座。”

column1: “You have proven your villainy,” the chieftains say. “If you are going to lie to us, you should at least try to lie well. This deception would not fool an uninitiated shepherd boy. You must step down, or we will take the throne from you.”
column2: “你已经证明了你的恶行，”酋长们说。“如果你要对我们撒谎，至少应该撒得像样一点。这种欺骗连一个未受启蒙的牧羊少年都骗不了。你必须退位，否则我们将夺走你的王座。”

column1: Step down.
column2: 退位。

column1: Scold them for their disloyalty.
column2: 斥责他们的不忠。

column1: \x01@\x0B scolded them for their disloyalty.
column2: \x01@\x0B 斥责他们的不忠。

column1: The chieftains cowered and apologized for questioning their chosen leader.
column2: 酋长们畏缩了，为质疑他们选定的领袖而道歉。

column1: The chieftains said that pride was a virtue but arrogance was not, and promised more trouble if \x01@\x0B did not mend \x04 ways.
column2: 酋长们说骄傲是美德，但傲慢不是，并承诺如果 \x01@\x0B 不改 \x04 方式，会有更多麻烦。

column1: Tell them you will think about what they have said.
column2: 告诉他们你会考虑他们所说的话。

column1: \x01@\x0B said that \x06 would consider their words.
column2: \x01@\x0B 说 \x06 会考虑他们的话。

column1: Legally, we must renounce the throne.
column2: 从法理上说，我们必须放弃王位。

column1: Tell them they are disloyal. If they attack us, so much the better! Then we will beat them, and prove them unworthy!
column2: 告诉他们他们不忠。如果他们攻击我们，那更好！然后我们会打败他们，证明他们不配！

column1: They are disloyal!
column2: 他们不忠！

column1: Tell them they are disloyal. If they attack us, so much the better! Then we shall all die defending our honor, and leave behind a glorious legend!
column2: 告诉他们他们不忠。如果他们攻击我们，那更好！然后我们将战死捍卫荣誉，留下光荣的传说！

column1: They are very angry, but beneath it all they hope that the \x01@\x0B will redeem \x08self.
column2: 他们非常愤怒，但在内心深处，他们希望 \x01@\x0B 会挽救 \x08自我。

column1: It is better to say nothing than to say something stupid.
column2: 什么都不说比说蠢话要好。

column1: There is a time to thunder, and a time to retreat. This is a time to retreat.
column2: 有怒吼的时候，也有撤退的时候。现在是撤退的时候。

column1: If we succeed in cowing them, we will be feared and respected. An apology is more likely to work, though.
column2: 如果我们成功地吓住他们，我们就会被敬畏和尊重。不过，道歉更可能奏效。

column1: I thought we really were confused by bad magic.
column2: 我以为我们确实被邪恶魔法搞糊涂了。

column1: No one was testing \x01@\x0B for spirit possession in the heat of the moment. No one can prove us wrong if we make this claim.
column2: 在激动时刻没有人测试 \x01@\x0B 是否被附身。如果我们这样声称，没人能证明我们错了。

column1: Bad King Urgrain was confronted by the chieftains of his tribe. Urgrain said he would apologize to them after he chopped their heads off.
column2: 恶王乌格兰被他部落的酋长们质问。乌格兰说他会在砍掉他们的头之后向他们道歉。

column1: We have done wrong, and must admit it.
column2: 我们做错了，必须承认。

column1: We mustn’t scold them. It would be impolite.
column2: 我们不应责骂他们。那是不礼貌的。

column1: \x01@\x0B must step down, to avoid a war.
column2: \x01@\x0B 必须退位，以避免战争。

column1: I thought it was the right thing to do. I was wrong, and must apologize and make amends.
column2: 我以为那是正确的事。我错了，必须道歉并弥补。

column1: I thought it was the right thing to do, and am the only one to blame. I must step down to make room for wiser heads.
column2: 我以为那是正确的事，而且唯有我该负责。我必须退位，为更明智的人让路。

column1: Our magic is weak. Perhaps that is why we were confused.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱。也许这就是我们困惑的原因。

column1: Our magic is strong. They will not believe me if I claim we suffered bad magic.
column2: 我们的魔法很强。如果我声称我们中了邪恶魔法，他们不会相信。

column1: All this is very pertinent. I must reflect on these matters.
column2: 这一切都切中要害。我必须反思这些事。

column1: How dare they presume to defy our leadership!
column2: 他们竟敢胆大妄为挑战我们的领导！

column1: Apologize for making a terrible mistake.
column2: 为犯下可怕的错误道歉。

column1: We apologized for making a terrible mistake.
column2: 我们为犯下可怕的错误道了歉。

column1: They said we had shown that we were proud, but not arrogant, and welcomed our words of contrition.
column2: 他们说我们表现出骄傲，而非傲慢，并欢迎我们的忏悔之言。

column1: They said that actions were more important than words. They would be watching us to see if we behaved properly in the future.
column2: 他们说行动比言语更重要。他们会观察我们未来是否行为得当。

column1: They said we were wise to change to our ways.
column2: 他们说我们改变行为方式是明智的。

column1: The other clans agreed that it was not our fault that we had fallen prey to hostile spirits.
column2: 其他氏族同意我们成为敌对精灵的牺牲品不是我们的错。

column1: The other clans said we were not only liars, but poor liars. They expelled us from the tribe. The people took this as a terrible blow.
column2: 其他氏族说我们不仅是骗子，还是拙劣的骗子。他们将我们逐出部落。人们将此视为沉重打击。

column1: How much total wealth do you give to the \x01@\x14 clans in the tribe?
column2: 你总共给部落中的 \x01@\x14 氏族多少财富？

column1: They said that our gifts were generous, and showed true contrition.
column2: 他们说我们的礼物很慷慨，展现了真正的忏悔。

column1: They said we could not erase a great offense with a few gifts. They would be watching us to see if we behaved properly in the future.
column2: 他们说我们不能用几件礼物抹去严重的冒犯。他们会观察我们未来是否行为得当。

column1: The people were unhappy, and said that we had disgraced ourselves.
column2: 人们很不高兴，说我们让自己蒙羞。

column1: We must either quit, or give each clan 50 cows. It is the law.
column2: 我们要么退出，要么给每个氏族五十头牛。这是法律。

column1: The chief is responsible for the decisions we make.
column2: 酋长为我们做出的决定负责。

column1: They will be offended if we offer them gifts.
column2: 如果我们送礼物，他们会感到被冒犯。

column1: They are very angry, and very suspicious.
column2: 他们非常愤怒，也非常怀疑。

column1: Our offense is great, but not so great that a generous gift will not erase it.
column2: 我们的冒犯很大，但还没大到一份慷慨礼物无法抹去的地步。

column1: They want an apology.
column2: 他们想要道歉。

column1: They are our friends, and will forgive us this one lapse.
column2: 他们是我们的朋友，会原谅我们这一次过失。

column1: No one was testing us for spirit possession in the heat of the moment. No one can prove us wrong if we make this claim.
column2: 在激动时刻没有人测试我们是否被附身。如果我们这样声称，没人能证明我们错了。

column1: Although no one can prove us wrong if we say we were under a spell, they will be very suspicious.
column2: 虽然如果我们说中了咒，没人能证明我们错了，但他们会很怀疑。

column1: The Ofrandlings fought beside Bad King Urgrain almost until the end. They threw themselves on Oskul’s mercy, and Oskul embraced them.
column2: 奥弗兰德人几乎战斗到最后一刻，始终站在恶王乌格兰一边。他们乞求奥斯库尔的怜悯，奥斯库尔接纳了他们。

column1: There’s a perfectly good justification for what we did. I knew it when I went to sleep last night, but now I have forgotten it.
column2: 我们的所作所为有一个完全充分的理由。昨晚入睡时我还记得，但现在我忘了。

column1: Better to try and fail than to try nothing and fail.
column2: 尝试而失败总比什么都不尝试而失败好。

column1: If we all knew how to read, things like this wouldn’t happen.
column2: 如果我们都识字，这种事就不会发生。

column1: If we leave the tribe, we can never rule it.
column2: 如果我们离开部落，就永远无法统治它。

column1: Though the clan followed my course, I am the only to one blame, and must step down to make room for wiser heads.
column2: 虽然氏族遵循了我的路线，但只有我该负责，必须退位，为更明智的人让路。

column1: No offense is so great that a gift of cattle cannot smooth it over.
column2: 没有牛群礼物无法平息的冒犯。

column1: How dare they castigate us! We must quit this shallow tribe, and find our glorious destiny elsewhere!
column2: 他们竟敢斥责我们！我们必须离开这个浅薄的部落，去别处寻找我们光荣的命运！

column1: Again, prominent thanes of the other clans of the tribe come to \x02\x03enlist your support/make a proposal to you/ask you to join them\x02.
column2: 再一次，部落其他氏族的重要领主前来 \x02\x03争取你的支持/向你提出建议/请求你加入他们\x02。

column1: Prominent thanes of the other clans of the tribe come to make a proposal to you.
column2: 部落其他氏族的重要领主前来向你提出建议。

column1: Hear them out, but do nothing.
column2: 听他们说完，但什么也不做。

column1: They wheedled and made speeches at us for a very long afternoon. Finally, they gave up and left.
column2: 他们花了一整个下午对我们又是哄骗又是演讲。最终，他们放弃了，离开了。

column1: “Wage war against our enemies.”
column2: “向我们的敌人开战。”

column1: We suggested that we make war against our enemies.
column2: 我们提议向我们的敌人开战。

column1: “Wage war against the discontented clans.”
column2: “向那些不满的氏族开战。”

column1: We agreed to petition the king together at the first opportunity.
column2: 我们同意一有机会就一同向国王请愿。

column1: The thanes of the other clans said that the harm done by \x01@\x0B’s attempt to make a false kingdom was impossible to exaggerate. They did not say what further action they would take.
column2: 其他氏族的领主们说 \x01@\x0B企图建立虚假王国所造成的危害再怎么夸大也不为过。他们没有说明下一步会采取什么行动。

column1: This animosity will increase the number of \x02\x03two-headed/sick and spindly/six-legged\x02 calves born to our cows.
column2: 这种敌意会增加我们牛群中产出 \x02\x03双头/病弱/六腿\x02 牛犊的数量。

column1: The wise leader always reserves judgment.
column2: 明智的领袖总是保留判断。

column1: It was a terrible mistake for \x01@\x0B to try to make a false kingdom. But except for this, \x06 has made good decisions.
column2: \x01@\x0B 试图建立虚假王国是一个可怕的错误。但除此之外， \x06 做出了明智的决定。

column1: Will these thanes ever stop their complaining? They sound like carls and cottars bickering over a patch of grass.
column2: 这些领主什么时候才能停止抱怨？他们听起来就像自由民和佃农为了一块草地争吵。

column1: When \x01@\x0B tried to make a false kingdom, it was the worst in a long chain of bad decisions.
column2: 当 \x01@\x0B 试图建立虚假王国时，那是连串糟糕决策中最恶劣的一个。

column1: \x01@\x0B has not listened to the clans in this tribe, else \x06 would have tended to their complaints long ago.
column2: \x01@\x0B 没有倾听部落中其他氏族的声音，否则 \x06 早就处理他们的抱怨了。

column1: Bad King Urgrain was given every opportunity to rule wisely, but he punished those kind enough to point out his flaws.
column2: 恶王乌格兰本有各种机会明智地统治，但他却惩罚那些好心指出他缺点的人。

column1: Thrones are made to be overturned.
column2: 王座生来就是要被推翻的。

column1: Kings and Queens are made to be overthrown.
column2: 国王和女王生来就是要被推翻的。

column1: Better to talk than to make war.
column2: 交谈胜过开战。

column1: Better to make war than to talk.
column2: 开战胜过交谈。

column1: Haven’t we had enough war and conquest?
column2: 我们难道还没有受够战争和征服吗？

column1: Knife-words prised Ernalda-tears from the rule-torc.
column2: 利刃般的话语从统治项圈中撬出了埃娜尔达之泪。

column1: When the Wyrm’s Friends committed crimes against the dragons, the dragonewts rose up to smite them.
column2: 当亚龙之友对龙族犯下罪行时，龙人奋起痛击他们。

column1: If we convince \x01@\x0B to step aside, we can seize the crown ourselves.
column2: 如果我们说服 \x01@\x0B 让位，我们就可以自己夺取王冠。

column1: What better chance will we have to take the throne for ourselves?
column2: 我们还能有更好的机会为自己夺取王位吗？

column1: This is a sign that the reign of \x01@\x0B is to end. We must be ready for ours to begin.
column2: 这是一个征兆，表明 \x01@\x0B 的统治即将终结。我们必须为我们的统治开始做好准备。

column1: \x01@\x14, the devotee of Eurmal on our clan ring, gave away a herd of our cows.
column2: \x01@\x14我们氏族议会中尤尔马尔的信徒，送走了我们的一群牛。

column1: The ring accepted the trickster’s actions.
column2: 长老会接受了恶作剧者的行为。

column1: The most reliable and stalwart carls were upset by the ring’s decision. The more reckless young carls were furious.
column2: 最可靠坚定的自由民对长老会的决定感到不安。更鲁莽的年轻自由民则愤怒不已。

column1: “It’s the trickster’s religious duty to betray us.”
column2: “背叛我们是恶作剧者的宗教义务。”

column1: The ring members told the people, “It’s the trickster’s religious duty to betray us.”
column2: 环成员告诉人们：“背叛我们是恶作剧者的宗教义务。”

column1: The people told the ring members, “You are crazy.”
column2: 人们告诉环成员：“你们疯了。”

column1: What argument do you use?
column2: 你用什么论点？

column1: “\x01@\x14 broke the law; if you take the cows, you are breaking it, too.”
column2: “\x01@\x14 违反了法律；如果你拿走牛，你也在违法。”

column1: They said that tricksters could never be trusted, and returned the cattle to us.
column2: 他们说恶作剧者永远不可信任，并把牛还给了我们。

column1: They said that they could not be blamed if we were betrayed by our trickster, and refused to return the cattle.
column2: 他们说如果被我们的恶作剧者背叛，他们不能受到责备，并拒绝归还牛。

column1: “We are your friends; do not take advantage of us in this way.”
column2: “我们是你们的朋友；不要这样利用我们。”

column1: They returned the cattle in the name of friendship.
column2: 他们以友谊的名义归还了牛。

column1: They said that if we were really friends, we would not try to withdraw a gift.
column2: 他们说如果我们真是朋友，就不会试图收回礼物。

column1: “We will do you two favors later if you do us this favor now.”
column2: “如果你们现在帮我们这个忙，我们以后会帮你们两次恩惠。”

column1: They said that they would take the favors and return the cows.
column2: 他们说他们接受恩惠并归还牛。

column1: They said they would sooner have cows now than promises later.
column2: 他们说他们宁愿现在得到牛，而不是未来的承诺。

column1: Punish \x01@\x14.
What is a fitting price for \x01@\x14 to pay?
column2: 什么是 \x01@\x14 应当付出的合适代价？

column1: Withdraw the chief’s protection from \x01@\x14.
column2: 撤销酋长对 \x01@\x14的保护。

column1: Now that \x01@\x14 is no longer protected, do you have \x08 killed?
column2: 既然 \x01@\x14 不再受保护，你是否让人杀死 \x08 ？

column1: Who kills \x08?
column2: 谁杀死 \x08？

column1: The carls were glad to see \x08 gone, but said it would be better if we’d killed \x08.
column2: 自由民很高兴看到 \x08 离开了，但说如果我们杀死了 \x08会更好。

column1: Remove \x01@\x14 from the ring.
column2: 将 \x01@\x14 从长老会中移除。

column1: We removed \x01@\x14 from the clan ring.
column2: 我们将 \x01@\x14 从氏族议会中移除。

column1: The people said it was good to punish \x08, but that this was not enough punishment.
column2: 人们说惩罚 \x08是好事，但这还不够惩罚。

column1: “They were really funny-looking cows.”
column2: “那些牛看起来真的很滑稽。”

column1: The ring told the people, “They were really funny-looking cows.”
column2: 长老会对人们说：“那些牛看起来真的很滑稽。”

column1: The people told the ring, “You are all crazy. With such foolish leaders, our clan is doomed.”
column2: 人们对长老会说：“你们都疯了。有这种愚蠢的领袖，我们的氏族完蛋了。”

column1: They said it was dishonorable to withdraw a gift.
column2: 他们说收回礼物是不光彩的。

column1: Then they said they did not want to be raided, and returned the cows.
column2: 然后他们说他们不想被袭击，于是归还了牛。

column1: “Because you are dishonorable, it will be a pleasure to repel your puny raid,” they said, and departed.
column2: “因为你们不光彩，击退你们可怜的袭击将是一种乐趣，”他们说道，然后离开了。

column1: The people did not like to see the chief impoverished in this way, but were glad to see \x08 take proper responsibility for the trickster \x06 had protected.
column2: 人们不喜欢看到酋长如此被削弱，但很高兴看到 \x08 为恶作剧者 \x06 所保护的人承担了适当责任。

column1: Come to think of it, there is something wrong with those cows.
column2: 仔细想想，那些牛有点问题。

column1: They are taking fifty cows! Fifty! It is too great a loss to bear!
column2: 他们拿走了五十头牛！五十头！损失太大了，无法承受！

column1: It is more important to get the cows back than to punish \x01@\x14.
column2: 把牛要回来比惩罚 \x01@\x14更重要。

column1: Tell them what the law is, and they will give the cows back.
column2: 告诉他们法律是什么，他们就会归还牛。

column1: Maybe they will give the cows back if we promise them two great favors later.

column2: 人民爱戴 \x01@t，但不想卷入世仇。

column1: Eurmal’s japes often made fights worse. Once, for example, he helped the dwarfs kill many elves with the thing called Death, and he did it for a laugh.
column2: 尤尔马尔的玩笑常常让冲突恶化。例如，他曾利用名为“死亡”的东西帮助矮人杀死许多精灵，而这一切只为了取乐。

column1: Of course I was right to ridicule him.
column2: 我当然有理由嘲弄他。

column1: The funny one makes me laugh! \x01DC is a turd, and deserves to be mocked!
column2: 这个滑稽鬼让我发笑！ \x01DC 是个废物，活该被嘲笑！

column1: Whenever Eurmal and Urox agree on something, there is reason to worry.
column2: 每当尤尔马尔和乌洛克斯达成一致，就该担心了。

column1: The best solution is to take \x01@t off the ring for a couple of years.
column2: 最好的办法是把 \x01@t 从长老会除名几年。

column1: A fight! We must see a fight!
column2: 打一架！我们一定要看打架！

column1: \x01@t is bound to get us into worse trouble than this.
column2: \x01@t 肯定会给我们惹上比这更大的麻烦。

column1: sceneR295
column2: sceneR295

column1: The men of the \x01@! clan arrive at the boundaries of your tula, pulling a cart loaded down with grain. They seem unhappy. When asked what is happening, they explain that they are paying off a bet. “Your clan-mate, \x01@t, was gambling with our chieftain. All night long \x06 lost. \x05 lost at every game \x06 played, and went further and further into debt.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的人来到我们领地边界，拉着一辆装满粮食的马车。他们看上去很不高兴。问起缘由，他们解释说是在偿还赌债。“你们氏族的人， \x01@t，曾与我们酋长赌博。整晚 \x06 都在输。 \x05 每场都输 \x06 玩过，债务越来越深。”

column1: Then on the last game of dice, \x06 won everything back and more. We suspect \x06 used trickster magic, but will pay our debt, because we are an honorable clan.”
column2: 然后在最后一局骰子中， \x06 赢回了所有甚至更多。我们怀疑 \x06 使用了恶作剧魔法，但我们会偿还债务，因为我们是体面的氏族。”

column1: \x01@t won a bet with the \x01@! chieftain, and won much grain.
column2: \x01@t 赢了一场与 \x01@! 酋长的赌局，赢了很多粮食。

column1: Allow them to keep the grain.
column2: 让他们留下粮食。

column1: We told them to keep the grain.
column2: 我们告诉他们留下粮食。

column1: They seemed offended. “Do you believe that we are so poor that we cannot afford to make good on our bets? Take your winnings, and humiliate us no further!”
column2: 他们似乎被冒犯了。“你们以为我们穷得连赌债都还不起吗？拿走你们的赢利，别再羞辱我们了！”

column1: Give them a reciprocal gift.
column2: 回赠他们一份礼物。

column1: We gave them a gift in return.
column2: 我们回赠了他们一份礼物。

column1: They seemed pleased that we honored them in this way. \x01@t asked them if they wanted to gamble some more, but they declined.
column2: 他们似乎很高兴我们如此尊重他们。 \x01@t 问他们是否想再赌几局，但他们拒绝了。

column1: Graciously accept \x01@t’s winnings.
column2: 宽厚地接受 \x01@t的赢利。

column1: They left our tula with their empty cart, shaking their heads sorrowfully.
column2: 他们拉着空车离开了我们的领地，悲伤地摇着头。

column1: Tell them that \x01@t is a trickster.
column2: 告诉他们 \x01@t 是个恶作剧者。

column1: They scowled and thanked us for the information.
column2: 他们皱起眉头，感谢我们提供这个消息。

column1: Maybe we can give them a reciprocal gift.
column2: 也许我们可以回赠他们一份礼物。

column1: With that much grain coming in, we can afford to give them a reciprocal gift.
column2: 有了这么多粮食进账，我们承担得起回赠一份礼物。

column1: The only honorable thing is to refuse to take their grain.
column2: 唯一体面的做法是拒绝收他们的粮食。

column1: Refusing to accept their grain would dishonor them. We would be saying that they cannot afford to pay their debts.
column2: 拒绝收他们的粮食会让他们蒙羞。那无异于说他们偿还不起债务。

column1: Refusing to accept their grain would dishonor them. Giving a reciprocal gift would not.
column2: 拒绝接受他们的谷物会让他们蒙羞。回赠礼物则不会。

column1: The people are delighted with \x01@t’s winnings. They will be disappointed if we give them back.
column2: 族人对 \x01@t赢得的战利品感到欣喜。如果我们还回去，他们会失望的。

column1: They are our friends, and we must take care not to offend them.
column2: 他们是我们的朋友，我们必须小心不要冒犯他们。

column1: That grain is blighted.
column2: 那些谷物感染了枯萎病。

column1: That’s a lot of grain!
column2: 那是很多谷物！

column1: That’s enough grain to feed a hundred people for a year!
column2: 那些谷物足以养活一百人一整年！

column1: That’s enough grain to feed a hundred people for a year. They will suffer without it.
column2: 那些谷物足以养活一百人一整年。没有它，他们会受苦。

column1: In gambling as well as in trade, a bargain is a bargain.
column2: 赌博也好，贸易也罢，成交就是成交。

column1: Let me tell them I am a trickster, so they will know how I hoodwinked them!
column2: 让我告诉他们我是个恶作剧者，这样他们就知道我是如何欺骗他们的了！

column1: It would be dishonest not to tell them that \x01@t is a trickster.
column2: 不告诉他们 \x01@t 是个恶作剧者是不诚实的。

column1: Praise Orlanth! Praise Ernalda! Praise bountiful Eurmal!
column2: 赞美奥兰斯！赞美埃尔纳尔达！赞美慷慨的尤尔马尔！

column1: Let’s put ourselves in their boots. We could not easily lose that much grain.
column2: 让我们设身处地想一想。我们不可能轻易损失那么多谷物。

column1: Do not allow their generosity to outshine ours!
column2: 别让他们的慷慨胜过我们的！

column1: sceneR296
column2: sceneR296

column1: Traders from the \x01@! clan arrive with a huge, mouldering, moth-eaten book. They claim that someone in your clan has agreed to purchase it. There is some confusion over who this might be, until \x01DD steps forward and claims the book. “This book has all sorts of information in it, dating all the way back to the Empire of Wyrm’s Friends. It has many poems and stories, all of great usefulness. They are selling it to us for a mere 80 cows.”
column2: \x01@! 氏族的商人带着一本巨大、发霉、虫蛀的书到来。他们声称你氏族中有人同意购买它。大家困惑于这人是谁，直到 \x01DD 走上前认领了这本书。“这本书包含各种各样的信息，可以追溯到龙之友帝国时期。它有许多诗歌和故事，都很有用。他们只卖给我们80头牛。”

column1: Allow the purchase.
column2: 允许购买。

column1: We accepted this agreement, and acquired the book.
column2: 我们接受了这个协议，获得了这本书。

column1: Inside the book, we found the myth of “\x01@\r.”
column2: 在书中，我们发现了“\x01@\r”的神话。

column1: Our god-talkers were disappointed, as they already knew its secrets.
column2: 我们的神言者很失望，因为他们已经知道了其中的秘密。

column1: After much discussion, they agreed that it would be good if they expressed their esteem for us with a generous gift of \x01@\x1A cows.
column2: 经过大量讨论，他们同意，如果能以 \x01@\x1A 头牛作为慷慨礼物来表达对我们的敬意，那将很好。

column1: They said they would give serious consideration to the giving of a reciprocal gift, and then departed.
column2: 他们说会认真考虑回赠礼物的事，然后离开了。

column1: Our god-talkers were glad to gain more secret knowledge.
column2: 我们的神言者很高兴获得了更多秘密知识。

column1: Call off the purchase.
column2: 取消购买。

column1: We called off the purchase.
column2: 我们取消了购买。

column1: Take the book by force.
column2: 武力夺取这本书。

column1: We took the book by force.
column2: 我们武力夺取了这本书。

column1: Try to renegotiate the price.
column2: 尝试重新协商价格。

column1: We tried to renegotiate the price.
column2: 我们尝试重新协商价格。

column1: They agree to sell it for forty cows.
column2: 他们同意以四十头牛出售。

column1: They agreed to sell it to us at a fairer price.
column2: 他们同意以更公平的价格卖给我们。

column1: They said that a member of the ring had agreed to this price, and that we were rank tergiversators. We did not know what this meant, but were fairly sure it was an insult. \x01DD confirmed that it was an insult, and added that \x06 agreed with it. \x05 would not explain further.
column2: 他们说长老会的一名成员已经同意了这一价格，而我们是一群可耻的变节者。我们不知道这意味着什么，但相当确定这是一种侮辱。 \x01DD 确认这是一种侮辱，并补充说 \x06 也同意这一评价。 \x05 不愿进一步解释。

column1: \x01DD is mad if \x06 thinks we can afford to pay eighty cows for a book.
column2: \x01DD 如果 \x06 认为我们付得起八十头牛买一本书，那真是疯了。

column1: Eighty cows is a fair price for a rare treasure such as this.
column2: 八十头牛对于这样一件稀有珍宝来说是公道的价格。

column1: Eighty cows is too much to pay.
column2: 八十头牛付得太多了。

column1: A fair price would be forty cows.
column2: 公道的价格应该是四十头牛。

column1: We are bound by \x01DD’s promise.
column2: 我们受 \x01DD的承诺约束。

column1: If we attempt to dicker, we will offend them.
column2: 如果我们试图讨价还价，会冒犯他们。

column1: A request for a reciprocal gift allows them to decrease the price without feeling that we renege on our promises.
column2: 要求回赠礼物可以让他们降低价格，同时不会觉得我们食言。

column1: Reading too much weakens your sword-arm.
column2: 读书太多会削弱你的剑臂。

column1: They are weak. Let’s just take it.
column2: 他们很弱。直接抢吧。

column1: We can easily overpower these feeble types, but their clan as a whole is stronger than ours.
column2: 我们可以轻易制服这些弱者，但他们的氏族整体比我们强。

column1: They dislike us already; if we offend them, it will make things worse.
column2: 他们已经不喜欢我们了；如果我们冒犯他们，情况会更糟。

column1: They are our friends; we can afford to annoy them a little.
column2: 他们是我们的朋友；我们稍微惹恼他们一下也没什么。

column1: From the book, we can learn the secrets of Poetry. It also might contain powerful myths of the gods that we do not know.
column2: 从这本书中，我们可以学到诗歌的秘密。它还可能包含我们所不知道的强大神明神话。

column1: If this book is so important, they should have sent strong warriors to guard it.
column2: 如果这本书如此重要，他们本应派强大的战士来守护它。

column1: Ancient stories have power, for they tell us what to expect when we enter the realm of the gods.
column2: 古老的故事具有力量，因为它们告诉我们进入神域时会遇到什么。

column1: We must not embarrass our friend \x01DD, even if \x06 made promises \x06 shouldn’t have made.
column2: 我们绝不能让我们朋友 \x01DD难堪，即使 \x06 做出了 \x06 本不该做出的承诺。

column1: Eighty cows! I think I feel a fit of apoplexy coming on…
column2: 八十头牛！我觉得我快要中风了……

column1: Eighty cows is too much to pay, but this is still a valuable treasure.
column2: 八十头牛付得太多，但这仍然是一件珍贵的宝物。

column1: sceneR297
column2: sceneR297

column1: \x01DE, a weaponthane of your clan, reports a terrifying encounter with skeletal creatures in the forest bordering your tula. “They were like skeletons, yet also like birds, and they had fangs!” Without consulting with the other ring members, \x01@\x05 rallies four weaponthanes and heads out to do battle with the things.
column2: \x01DE你氏族的一名武器领主报告说，在与你们领地接壤的森林中遭遇了可怕的骷髅生物。“它们像骷髅，却又像鸟，还有獠牙！”没有与其他长老会成员商议， \x01@\x05 召集了四名武器领主出发去与那些东西战斗。

column1: \x01DE was attacked by skeletal, winged monsters in the forest. \x01@\x05 took weaponthanes out to do battle with them.
column2: \x01DE 在森林中被骷髅般的飞行怪物袭击。 \x01@\x05 带领武器领主出去与它们战斗。

column1: Sacrifice to Humakt to strengthen \x01@\x05’s hand.
column2: 向胡马克特献祭以增强 \x01@\x05的力量。

column1: We sacrificed to Humakt to strengthen \x01@\x05’s hand.
column2: 我们向胡马克特献祭以增强 \x01@\x05的力量。

column1: The god-talkers said the omens were good; Humakt heard our pleas.
column2: 神言者说征兆良好；胡马克特听到了我们的祈求。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs could not be read. We did not know if Humakt accepted our sacrifice.
column2: 神言者说征兆无法解读。我们不知道胡马克特是否接受了我们的献祭。

column1: \x01@\x05 and the four weaponthanes returned triumphant. They told us how they slew the monsters.
column2: \x01@\x05 四位武器领主凯旋而归。他们向我们讲述了如何斩杀怪物。

column1: We knew that Humakt had heard us, after all.
column2: 我们终于知道，胡马克特听到了我们的祈求。

column1: We knew it would have been much worse if Humakt had not been on our side.
column2: 我们知道，要是没有胡马克特站在我们这边，情况会更糟。

column1: \x01@\x05 was slain, too.
column2: \x01@\x05 也被杀了。

column1: Only \x01@\x05 was spared injury.
column2: 只有 \x01@\x05 毫发无伤。

column1: The people bemoaned the fact that Humakt had not heard our pleas.
column2: 人们哀叹胡马克特没有回应我们的祈求。

column1: Send others to join the fight.
column2: 派其他人加入战斗。

column1: We sent others to join the fight.
column2: 我们派了其他人加入战斗。

column1: With their help, \x01@\x05 slew the monsters. The people cheered.
column2: 在他们的帮助下， \x01@\x05 杀死了怪物。人们欢呼起来。

column1: The monsters were too terrible for our warriors. They overwhelmed them and killed them all.
column2: 怪物对我们的战士来说太可怕了。它们击溃了战士们，将他们全部杀死。

column1: The monsters were too terrible for our warriors. They killed \x01@\x1A of them, and wounded everyone else.
column2: 怪物对我们的战士来说太可怕了。它们杀了 \x01@\x1A 个，其余全部受伤。

column1: Only \x01@\x05 was spared, though \x06 suffered injuries.
column2: 只有 \x01@\x05 幸免，尽管 \x06 受了伤。

column1: Though \x01@\x05 suffered injuries, \x04 life was spared
column2: 尽管 \x01@\x05 受了伤， \x04 的性命得以保全

column1: Send someone to take over from \x01@\x05 in leading the fight.
column2: 派个人去接替 \x01@\x05 指挥战斗。

column1: We sent someone to take over from \x01@\x05 in leading the fight.
column2: 我们派了人去接替 \x01@\x05 指挥战斗。

column1: \x01@\x14 led our fierce fighters in slaying the monsters. The people cheered \x08. \x01@\x05 seemed troubled, but, when questioned, would admit to no hard feelings. “The important thing is that the undead were slain, not who they were slain by.”
column2: \x01@\x14 带领我们勇猛的战士屠杀了怪物。民众为 \x08欢呼。 \x01@\x05 似乎有些困扰，但被问及时却不愿承认有任何不满。“重要的是亡灵被杀了，而不是被谁杀的。”

column1: The monsters were too terrible for our warriors.
column2: 怪物对我们的战士来说太过可怕。

column1: \x01@\x05 was among the slain. These words were on \x04 lips when \x06 died: “If only you had allowed me to lead…”
column2: \x01@\x05 是阵亡者之一。 \x06 临终时 \x04 嘴边的话是：“要是你当初让我指挥……”

column1: After nightfall, \x01@\x14 died of \x04 wounds.
column2: 入夜后， \x01@\x14 因 \x04 伤而亡。

column1: Send more warriors, and someone to take over from \x01@\x05 in leading the fight.
column2: 再派些战士，以及一个人去接替 \x01@\x05 指挥战斗。

column1: How many more fighters do you send?
column2: 你要再派多少战士？

column1: We sent more warriors, and told \x01@\x14 to take over from \x01@\x05 in leading the fight.
column2: 我们派了更多战士，并命令 \x01@\x14 接替 \x01@\x05 指挥战斗。

column1: Though \x01@\x05 suffered injuries, \x04 life was spared.
column2: 尽管 \x01@\x05 受了伤，但 \x04 保住了性命。

column1: A few hours later, \x01@\x14 died of \x04 wounds.
column2: 几小时后， \x01@\x14 因 \x04 伤而亡。

column1: Wait for \x01@\x05 to return.
column2: 等待 \x01@\x05 归来。

column1: \x01@\x05 and the four weaponthanes returned triumphant. They told us how they slew the monsters. The people cheered.
column2: \x01@\x05 四位武器领主凯旋而归。他们讲述了如何杀死那些怪物。民众欢呼雀跃。

column1: The monsters were too terrible for \x01@\x05’s brave warriors. Two were wounded, and two were slain.
column2: 怪物对 \x01@\x05的勇敢战士而言太过可怕。两人负伤，两人战死。

column1: I wish we could afford to sacrifice, but we can’t.
column2: 我希望我们能承担得起献祭，但我们不能。

column1: A sacrifice can’t hurt.
column2: 献祭总没有坏处。

column1: \x01@\x05 hates the undead so much; \x06 will be shamed if we send someone to replace \x08.
column2: \x01@\x05 憎恨亡灵至极； \x06 若我们派人替换 \x08，将会感到羞耻。

column1: \x01@\x05 will be fine.
column2: \x01@\x05 会没事的。

column1: \x01@\x05 is doomed!
column2: \x01@\x05 注定要完蛋！

column1: No one ever lost a fight by sending too few fighters.
column2: 没有人因为派出的战士太少而输掉战斗。

column1: \x01@\x05 is not the best one to lead this fight.
column2: \x01@\x05 并非领导这场战斗的最佳人选。

column1: Send me to lead the fight.
column2: 派我来领导战斗。

column1: Send me to lead the fight, and send more warriors with me.
column2: 派我来领导战斗，并多派些战士与我同行。

column1: Our magic is strong; Humakt will hear our prayers.
column2: 我们的魔法强大；胡玛克特将听见我们的祈祷。

column1: Our magic is weak; we cannot make Humakt hear us.
column2: 我们的魔法薄弱；我们无法让胡玛克特听见我们。

column1: The carls are no friends of the undead, but they want nothing to do with this.
column2: 自由民并非亡灵的朋友，但他们不愿与此事有任何瓜葛。

column1: These skeleton things sound like harpies, which are Chaos creatures. \x01@\x05 is not strong enough; I must take over.
column2: 这些骷髅似的东西听起来像哈比，它们是混沌生物。 \x01@\x05 不够强大；我必须接手。

column1: As a devotee of Humakt, foe of the undead, it is my duty to lead this fight.
column2: 作为胡玛克特的信徒、亡灵之敌，领导这场战斗是我的职责。

column1: Sacrifice to the god who hates these creatures.
column2: 向憎恨这些生物的神献祭。

column1: The more warriors we send, the more dead we will have on our hands.
column2: 派出越多的战士，我们手上就会沾上越多的死者。

column1: If only \x01@\x05 had asked me to go, too!
column2: 要是 \x01@\x05 也让我去就好了！

column1: It is not good to be obsessed with only one enemy, as \x01@\x05 is.
column2: 只执着于一个敌人是不好的，就像 \x01@\x05 那样。

column1: We must support \x01@\x05 to the fullest extent possible. Every last flying bone must be crushed into powder.
column2: 我们必须全力支持 \x01@\x05 。每一根飞行的骨头都必须碾成粉末。

column1: Shower Humakt with gifts, so he will know how we esteem him.
column2: 向胡玛克特慷慨献礼，让他知晓我们何等敬重他。

column1: They will do it if you gift each warrior with five cows worth of goods.
column2: 如果你赠予每位战士价值五头牛的货物，他们会照办。

column1: How many do you hire?
column2: 你雇佣多少人？

column1: They reported success in their attack. They wounded many of our foes.
column2: 他们报告说攻击成功，击伤了我们许多敌人。

column1: Make peace with the \x01@! clan.
column2: 与 \x01@! 氏族议和。

column1: We decided to make peace with the \x01@! clan.
column2: 我们决定与 \x01@! 氏族议和。

column1: Bad King Urgrain hired his weaponthanes out to the highest bidders for any attack on anyone or anything. When the warriors discovered they’d been hired to attack their own steads, they quit their service.
column2: 恶王乌格兰将自己的武器领主们出租给出价最高者，用于攻击任何人或任何事。当这些武士发现他们被雇来攻击自己的农庄时，便辞去了职务。

column1: Nobles from the \x01@! clan come in their formal finery to tell you that they intend to kill as many of you as they can. “Because we have told you this, it won’t be secret murder, which is a crime. We will kill you legally, which you deserve because you have offended us in countless ways. No longer can we allow your insults and transgressions against us to go unanswered. We will answer them in blood.”
column2: 来自 \x01@! 部落的贵族们身着正式盛装前来告诉你，他们打算尽可能多地杀死你们。“因为我们告诉了你这一点，就不会是秘密谋杀——那是一种罪行。我们会合法地杀死你们，这是你们应得的，因为你们用无数方式冒犯了我们。我们不能再允许你们对我们的侮辱和侵犯不加回应。我们将用鲜血回应。”

column1: The nobles haughtily ignored our words. “Only blood will wash away the memory of your past insults,” they said, as they departed.
column2: 贵族们傲慢地无视了我们的言语。“只有鲜血才能洗去你们过去侮辱的记忆，”他们说完便离去了。

column1: The poem was not memorable.

column2: 创作一首诗，将他们描绘成蠢货。

column1: We composed a poem portraying them as fools.
column2: 我们创作了一首诗，将他们描绘成蠢货。

column1: The poem was not as funny as we had hoped.

column1: We composed a poem praising their honor.
column2: 我们创作了一首诗赞美他们的荣誉。

column1: The nobles were moved to tears by \x01@N’s eloquent history of their clan. They said they would call off their feud, but warned us that any further bad actions on our part would erase the beauty of the poem we had made for them that day.
column2: 贵族们被 \x01@N对他们部落往事富有文采的叙述感动落泪。他们说会取消世仇，但警告我们，若我们今后再有不良行为，就会抹去那天我们为他们所作诗歌的美好。

column1: The nobles listened to \x01@N’s opening verses, but then spit and shook their fists. “Your words are insufficient,” they said. “Only blood will wash away the memory of your past insults.” Then they departed.
column2: 贵族们听了 \x01@N的开篇诗节，但随后吐口水并挥舞拳头。“你们的言语不够，”他们说，“只有鲜血才能洗去你们过去侮辱的记忆。”然后他们离去了。

column1: Do nothing, for now.
column2: 暂时什么都不做。

column1: Offer them gifts.
column2: 向他们献上礼物。

column1: We offered them gifts.
column2: 我们向他们献上了礼物。

column1: What do you offer?
column2: 你献上什么？

column1: They were affronted. “This paltry sum does not begin to erase the assaults your people have made upon our honor!” They departed, stamping their boots upon the ground.
column2: 他们被冒犯了。“这点微薄之资根本不足以抹去你们族人对我们荣誉的侵犯！”他们跺着靴子离开了。

column1: They accepted the gift. “This gesture of respect is long overdue.
column2: 他们接受了礼物。“这份尊敬的姿态早该有了。

column1: We will postpone our feud — for now.”
column2: 我们暂且推迟世仇——就现在。”

column1: If they feud with us, we will lose a few cows. If we make peace with them, we will lose many cows.
column2: 若他们与我们结仇，我们只会损失几头牛。若我们与他们讲和，我们则会损失许多牛只。

column1: They’ll be insulted if we offer them cows.
column2: 如果我们送他们牛，他们会觉得受辱。

column1: Stolen cows cause feuds. Gifts of cows end them.
column2: 偷牛引发世仇；赠牛终结世仇。

column1: They’ll be insulted if we offer them less than twenty-five cows.
column2: 如果我们给的牛不足二十五头，他们会觉得受辱。

column1: For every twenty-five cows we give them, a past wrong will be forgotten.
column2: 每给他们二十五头牛，过去的冤仇就会被遗忘。

column1: Nothing will come of this.
column2: 这不会有什么结果。

column1: The people are worried; we must give them \x02\x03courage/reassurance/heart\x02.
column2: 族人们很担忧；我们必须给予他们 \x02\x03勇气/安慰/信心\x02。

column1: Poems never do anything.
column2: 诗歌从来无用。

column1: A good poem could \x02\x03win respect from other clans/inflame their already-hot hearts/inspire the people to defend their hearth\x02.
column2: 一首好诗或许能 \x02\x03赢得其他氏族的尊重/点燃他们已然炽热的心/激励族人守护他们的家园\x02。

column1: A well-phrased poem could rally our people, gain support from other clans, or turn hate to love.
column2: 一首措辞精妙的诗能团结我们的族人，争取其他氏族的支持，或将仇恨化为爱意。

column1: It is easier to compose a hateful poem than an amusing one. Harder still to turn hard hearts soft.
column2: 写一首怨毒的诗比写一首诙谐的诗容易。而让铁石心肠变柔软则更难。

column1: It would be good if others thought them villains, and sided with us.
column2: 如果别人视他们为恶徒，站到我们这边，那就好了。

column1: We must show generosity and justice to stop this feud before it gets started.
column2: 我们必须展现慷慨与公正，在仇怨开始之前就将其阻止。

column1: When Bad King Urgrain was mighty, he started no feud he did not end. But when he fell from Orlanth’s favor, his many feuds ended him.
column2: 恶王乌格兰强盛之时，他所挑起的世仇无不终结。但当他失宠于奥兰斯，他众多的世仇终结了他。

column1: Ernalda said, “Don’t poke at the wasp’s nest without a net on your head and gloves on your hands.”
column2: 厄娜尔达说过：“不要在没有网兜头和手套手时去捅黄蜂窝。”

column1: Odayla prefers to grapple with the bear he sees, than to hunt a wolf hiding in the underbrush.
column2: 奥达拉更愿与他所见之熊搏斗，而非猎杀藏在灌木丛中的狼。

column1: They are so \x02\x04condescending/pretentious/smug/haughty\x02; it will be \x02\x04hilarious/amusing/fun/easy\x02 to humiliate them.
column2: 他们如此 \x02\x04居高临下/装腔作势/自鸣得意/傲慢\x02；羞辱他们将 \x02\x04极其可笑/很有意思/很好玩/很容易\x02 。

column1: If we can end this trouble before it goes any further, the rest of the tribe will look up to us.
column2: 如果我们能在事态扩大前解决这麻烦，部落的其他人会敬重我们。

column1: A feud within our tribe might tear the tribe apart, and we would stand alone again, as we were meant to be.
column2: 部落内部的世仇可能撕裂整个部落，而我们又将孤立无援，正如我们本应如此。

column1: If we don’t end this feud right now, they could turn the entire tribe against us!
column2: 如果我们不立刻终结这场世仇，他们可能会让整个部落与我们为敌！

column1: We have done \x02\x03unforgivable/horrible/awful\x02 things to them, it is true.
column2: 我们确实对他们做了 \x02\x03不可饶恕/可怕/糟糕\x02 的事，这是真的。

column1: \x02\x04What a disaster it will be/There will be terrible trouble/We can look forward to sad misfortune/I see calamity ahead\x02 if this continues.
column2: \x02\x04如果继续下去，那将是多大的灾难/将会有可怕的麻烦/我们只能期待悲惨的不幸/我预见前方有灾祸\x02 。

column2: 武器领主们灰心丧气，因为听任此事发生，我们羞辱了我们的守护神。

column1: Attack another clan.
column2: 攻击另一个氏族。

column1: The people were glad that we had struck against our treacherous foes.
column2: 族人们很高兴我们打击了背信弃义的敌人。

column2: 战士们后悔未能对这些背信弃义的敌人施以重击。

column2: 族人们听闻我们伤害了一个无辜氏族，感到不快。

column2: 族人们听闻我们攻击了一个无辜氏族，感到不快，并认为我们蒙受耻辱的失利是罪有应得。

column2: 我们在他们的氏族议会前提出了诉讼。

column1: They denied that they had slain our horses.
column2: 他们否认杀害了我们的马匹。

column2: \x01@N曾与他们争论我们的案子，认为他们在撒谎。

column2: \x01@N曾与他们争论我们的案子，认为他们说的是实话。

column2: 将诉讼提交议会。

column1: We took our claim to the moot.
column2: 我们将诉讼提交给了议会。

column1: We sacrificed to Elmal Horse-Friend for protection from horse-killers.
column2: 我们向马友埃尔玛献祭，以求免受杀马者之害。

column1: The god-talkers said that the signs were good; Elmal would protect us from such attacks in the future.
column2: 神言者说征兆良好；埃尔玛将保护我们免受此类攻击。

column1: The god-talkers could not promise that Elmal had heard our pleas.
column2: 神言者无法保证埃尔玛已听到我们的祈求。

column2: 失去马匹已是坏事。我们不应再屠杀牛只雪上加霜。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice a few cows to gain protection against horse-slayers.
column2: 我们承担得起献祭几头牛来获得对抗杀马者的庇护。

column2: 如果我们献祭后仍然损失更多马匹，那就马牛两失。不如让他们赔偿我们。

column1: The law is useless in such situations.
column2: 在这种情况下法律毫无用处。

column1: I tell you, conduct a divination to identify the scoundrels who keep slaying our horses, then lodge a legal claim against them.
column2: 我告诉你，举行占卜指认那些不断杀害我们马匹的恶棍，然后对他们提出法律诉讼。

column1: First, divination to identify the scoundrels who keep killing our horses. Then, if they are in our tribe, we can lodge a claim against them at the moot.
column2: 先占卜，找出那些不断杀害我们马匹的恶徒。然后，如果他们在我们部落里，我们就可以在议会上对他们提起诉讼。

column1: The cowardly clan \x01@a did this! We must smash them!
column2: 懦弱的 \x01@a 部族干的！我们必须粉碎他们！

column1: \x02\x03The feculent cowards/My sword-song sings that the spineless/I know in my belly that the gutless wonders of\x02 clan \x01@a did this, as part of their feud against us. We must \x02\x03destroy/kill/smash\x02 them!
column2: \x02\x03肮脏懦弱的/我的剑歌吟唱，毫无骨气的/我心知肚明，没胆的\x02\x01@a氏族干了这事，作为他们对我们的世仇的一部分。我们必须 \x02\x03消灭/杀死/粉碎\x02 他们！

column1: The clan \x01@a did this, as part of their feud against us. We must \x02\x03build up our strength/amass a large fighting force/wait until we are stronger then they are\x02, and then smash them.
column2: \x01@a 部族干了这事，作为他们对我们的世仇的一部分。我们必须 \x02\x03积蓄力量/集结大军/等到我们比他们强大\x02，然后粉碎他们。

column1: It would be disastrous to attack or accuse the wrong clan.
column2: 攻击或指控错误的部族将是灾难性的。

column1: Divinations never lie.
column2: 占卜从不说谎。

column1: Divinations are only as good as the diviner. Sacrifices are only as strong as the magic of the god-talkers who make them.
column2: 占卜的好坏取决于占卜者。献祭的强弱取决于进行献祭的神言者的魔力。

column1: A sacrifice will keep the horse-slayers away. A divination will reveal them, so we can deal with them ourselves.
column2: 一次献祭会让杀马者远离。一次占卜会揭露他们，这样我们就能亲自处理他们。

column1: Our magic is weak. It is a bad time for sacrifices and divinations.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱。现在不是进行献祭和占卜的好时机。

column1: Find a peaceful way to solve this, or wait until after planting time.
column2: 找到和平解决的办法，或者等到种植季节之后。

column1: Find a peaceful way to solve this, or wait until after harvest time.
column2: 找到和平解决的办法，或者等到收获季节之后。

column1: Elmal is the Horse-Friend, the Loyal Thane, and the benevolent Winter Sun.
column2: 艾尔玛是马之友、忠诚侍从，以及仁慈的冬日太阳。

column1: Elmal as Horse-Friend will help us protect our steeds.
column2: 作为马之友的艾尔玛会帮助我们保护我们的坐骑。

column1: Elmal as Loyal Thane will help us avenge this insult.
column2: 作为忠诚侍从的艾尔玛会帮助我们报复这一侮辱。

column1: Our patron god, Elmal, is also friend and protector to horses.
column2: 我们的守护神艾尔玛也是马的朋友和保护者。

column1: Our patron god, Elmal, cannot deny us if we entreat him wisely.
column2: 我们的守护神艾尔玛，如果我们明智地恳求他，他不会拒绝我们。

column1: Our patron god, Elmal, will lead us to victory when we avenge this insult.
column2: 我们的守护神艾尔玛会带领我们走向胜利，当我们报复这一侮辱时。

column1: Elmal will protect us from this outrage, but perhaps we should fight our foes directly.
column2: 艾尔玛会保护我们免受这一暴行的侵害，但也许我们应该直接与敌人战斗。

column1: At least they didn’t kill cows.
column2: 至少他们没有杀牛。

column1: I told you \x02\x04our steeds were in peril/to watch out for sneaky horse-killers/our enemies would hurt our horses/our horses were in danger\x02.
column2: 我告诉过你 \x02\x04我们的坐骑处于危险中/小心鬼鬼祟祟的杀马者/我们的敌人会伤害我们的马/我们的马处于危险中\x02。

column1: Night-skulks cut the life-ribbons of the Elmal-friends.
column2: 夜游者割断了艾尔玛之友的生命之带。

column1: We must \x02\x03strike daringly/react quickly/act boldly\x02.
column2: 我们必须 \x02\x03大胆出击/迅速反应/勇敢行动\x02。

column1: \x01Bl, a young, energetic farmer, on the road to prosperity, asks the clan council for help. He claims that his stead is haunted. Objects move about. Wailing noises come from nowhere. \x01Bl’s wife and child have even seen an apparition. The people are afraid that their steads will be haunted, too.
column2: \x01Bl一个年轻有活力的农夫，正走在致富之路上，向氏族议会求助。他声称他的农庄闹鬼。物体四处移动。不知从何处传来哀号声。 \x01Bl的妻子和孩子甚至看到了幽灵。人们害怕自己的农庄也会闹鬼。

column1: The young farmer \x01Bl reported that his stead was haunted.
column2: 年轻的农夫 \x01Bl 报告说他的农庄闹鬼。

column1: Build \x01Bl a new stead.
column2: 建造 \x01Bl 一个新农庄。

column1: We built \x01Bl a new stead.
column2: 我们建造了 \x01Bl 一个新农庄。

column1: Even as we raised the timbers of the new stead, we heard the groaning of the ghost. It had moved, following poor \x01Bl’s family. The half-built stead was abandoned.
column2: 就在我们竖起新农庄的木料时，我们听到了鬼魂的呻吟。它已经移动了，跟着可怜的 \x01Bl一家。那个建了一半的农庄被废弃了。

column1: Our priests could not say what was causing the haunting.
column2: 我们的祭司说不出是什么导致了闹鬼。

column1: Launch a legal claim against the ghost.
column2: 对鬼魂提起法律诉讼。

column1: We launched a legal claim against the ghost.
column2: 我们对鬼魂提起了法律诉讼。

column1: The ghost would not respond to \x01@N’s legal arguments.
column2: 鬼魂不会回应 \x01@N的法律论点。

column1: Resign yourselves to the haunting.
column2: 逆来顺受，忍受闹鬼。

column1: The ring took no further action, and the people were afraid.
column2: 长老会没有采取进一步行动，人们很害怕。

column1: Send for shamans to banish the ghost.
column2: 派人请萨满来驱逐鬼魂。

column1: We sent for shamans to banish the ghost.
column2: 我们派人请萨满来驱逐鬼魂。

column1: Shamans came and said they would banish the ghost for the low price of \x01@\x10 cows.
column2: 萨满来了，说他们愿意以 \x01@\x10 头牛的低价驱逐鬼魂。

column1: Shamans come and say they will banish the ghost for the low price of \x01@\x10 cows worth of goods.
column2: 萨满来了，说他们愿意以价值 \x01@\x10 头牛的货物的低价驱逐鬼魂。

column1: We accepted the arrangement. They danced around \x01Bl’s stead, banged on a drum, and ate a brew of moss and lichens. Their eyes rolled back in their heads, and they spoke to the ghost.
column2: 我们接受了这个安排。他们在 \x01Bl的农庄周围跳舞，敲着鼓，吃了一种苔藓和地衣酿的饮料。他们的眼睛翻白，对着鬼魂说话。

column1: The bangings of the ghost stopped. The shamans said they had banished it.
column2: 鬼魂的撞击声停止了。萨满说他们已经驱逐了它。

column1: We decided that their price was too rich for us.
column2: 我们认定他们的要价对我们来说太高了。

column1: Before leaving, one of the shamans said, “I’m surprised a spirit would make its home among such a miserly clan.”
column2: 离开前，其中一个萨满说：“我很惊讶一个灵魂会在如此吝啬的氏族里安家。”

column1: We had to admit even their lower price was too rich for us.
column2: 我们不得不承认，即使他们降了价，对我们来说还是太高了。

column1: We could not afford to pay even this lower price. Before leaving, one of the shamans said, “I’m surprised a spirit would make its home among such a poverty-ridden clan.”
column2: 我们连这个更低的价格都付不起。离开前，其中一个萨满说：“我很惊讶一个灵魂会在如此贫穷的氏族里安家。”

column1: We attacked the \x01@!.
column2: 我们攻击了 \x01@!。

column1: The warriors regretted their failure to strike hard against these ghost-loving foes.
column2: 战士们懊悔未能对这些爱幽灵的敌人施以重击。

column1: They said that we had proven ourselves their enemies, and that no amount of legal jabber would convince them to release the ghost from service to them. “You are lucky we only send ghosts against you, instead of the deadly mercenaries of the \x01@/ clan.”
column2: 他们说我们已经表明自己是他们的敌人，无论我们在法律上如何喋喋不休，都无法说服他们将幽灵从对他们的服务中释放出来。“你们算走运，我们只派幽灵对付你们，而不是 \x01@/ 氏族的致命雇佣兵。”

column1: Drop the claim.
column2: 放弃主张。

column1: We dropped the claim.
column2: 我们放弃了主张。

column1: Take the claim to the moot.
column2: 将主张提交议会。

column1: How much wealth do you distribute among the other clans before the case is judged?
column2: 在案件裁决前，你向其他氏族分发多少财富？

column1: When in doubt, send for shamans.
column2: 若有疑虑，便召萨满。

column1: Horvator Farsee once conducted a case against a spirit, so there may be precedents for outlawing the ghost. First, we should learn why it is here.
column2: 远视者霍瓦托曾审理过一桩针对灵体的案件，因此可能有将幽灵定为非法的先例。首先，我们应弄清它为何在此。

column1: A new stead will make him happy.
column2: 一座新的宅园会让他高兴。

column1: It never hurts to try different solutions to a problem.
column2: 尝试不同的解决方案从无害处。

column1: We must know more of the situation. Every time we try and fail, the people will grow more fearful.
column2: 我们必须了解更多情况。每次我们尝试并失败，人们就会更加恐惧。

column1: Exorcism is not a specialty of the gods we worship. We must figure out what is going on.
column2: 驱魔并非我们所崇拜的神祇的专长。我们必须弄清楚发生了什么。

column1: Our magic is strong. A divination will point to the correct course of action.
column2: 我们的魔法很强。一次占卜将指明正确的行动方向。

column1: Our magic is weak. A divination will waste time and disappoint the people.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱。占卜只会浪费时间，让人民失望。

column1: The carls want a peaceful answer to this problem, so that the ghost will not interfere with planting.
column2: 自由民希望和平解决这个问题，以免幽灵干扰播种。

column1: The carls want a peaceful answer to this problem, so that the ghost will not interfere with the harvest.
column2: 自由民希望和平解决这个问题，以免幽灵干扰收获。

column1: \x01Bl must have forgotten the name of one of his ancestors. Let us make sport of his foolishness.
column2: \x01Bl 一定忘记了他某个祖先的名字。让我们取笑他的愚蠢吧。

column1: Spirits are all around us, and can be as troublesome and selfish as real people.
column2: 灵体无处不在，它们可以像真人一样麻烦和自私。

column1: If we resign ourselves to this haunting, we invite all manner of undead monsters to dine on our bones.
column2: 如果我们屈服于这次闹鬼，就会引来各种不死怪物啃噬我们的骨头。

column2: sceneR302

column1: Weaponthanes of your clan return from a sudden trip into the woods, dragging with them three captured elves, one of whom is severely wounded.
column2: 你们氏族的武器领主从一次突入林中的行程归来，拖拽着三名俘虏的精灵，其中一人伤势严重。

column1: \x05 sent the weaponthanes on the mission. “Now, finally, we shall have our final confrontation with the accursed elves! They will come here to rescue the hostages, and then we shall burn them all, as if they were nothing more than dry twigs!”
column2: \x05 派武器领主去执行任务。“现在，终于，我们将与被诅咒的精灵进行最终对决！他们会来这里营救人质，然后我们将把他们全部烧掉，仿佛他们不过是干枯的树枝！”

column1: Prepare for an elf attack.
column2: 准备迎接精灵攻击。

column1: We prepared for an elf attack.
column2: 我们准备了迎接精灵攻击。

column1: Release the elves.
column2: 释放精灵。

column1: We released the elves.
column2: 我们释放了精灵。

column1: Send a delegation to the elf camp to negotiate ransom for the prisoners.
column2: 派遣代表团前往精灵营地，就人质赎金进行谈判。

column1: We sent a delegation to the elf camp to negotiate ransom for the prisoners.
column2: 我们派遣了代表团前往精灵营地，就人质赎金进行谈判。

column1: Who guards \x01@\x05?
The delegation found no elves.
column2: 代表团没有找到精灵。

column1: The elves offer \x01@\x0E baskets of healing herbs in exchange for the prisoners.
column2: 精灵提供 \x01@\x0E 篮治疗草药交换俘虏。

column1: Reject the offer.
column2: 拒绝提议。

column1: We did not like the dried-up leaves they offered us.
column2: 我们不喜欢他们提供的干枯叶子。

column1: The elves slipped into the woods. As the delegation returned to our lands, they were attacked from a distance, by arrows.
column2: 精灵溜进了树林。当代表团返回我们的土地时，他们遭到了远处弓箭的袭击。

column1: \x01@\x05 and \x04 guardian dodged the arrows, and were unharmed.
column2: \x01@\x05 而 \x04 守护者避开了箭矢，毫发无伤。

column1: \x01@\x05 and \x04 guardians dodged the arrows, and were unharmed.
column2: \x01@\x05 而 \x04 守护者们避开了箭矢，毫发无伤。

column1: Many of \x01@\x05’s guardians were picked off. The rest managed to slip through the underbrush to safety.
column2: \x01@\x05的许多守护者被逐一击倒。其余人设法穿过灌木丛逃到了安全地带。

column1: \x01@\x05’s guardian was slain in the first volley. \x01@\x05 managed to crawl through the underbrush to safety.
column2: \x01@\x05的守护者在第一轮齐射中被杀。 \x01@\x05 设法爬过灌木丛逃到了安全地带。

column1: All but one of \x01@\x05’s guardians were slain.
column2: \x01@\x05的守护者除一人外全部被杀。

column1: The elves may be reluctant to talk to us, now that we’ve hacked that fellow’s arms off.
column2: 既然我们已经砍掉了那个家伙的胳膊，精灵们可能不愿意和我们交谈了。

column1: It’s hard to negotiate with elves, because it’s hard to find them.
column2: 与精灵谈判很困难，因为很难找到他们。

column1: Elves have many magical herbs to trade; some of these herbs have healing properties.
column2: 精灵有许多神奇草药可供交易；其中一些草药具有治疗功效。

column1: Elves are no worry. We can easily beat them.
column2: 精灵不足为虑。我们可以轻易击败他们。

column1: Elves can be deadly opponents.
column2: 精灵可能是致命的对手。

column1: In their native woods, one elf can fight like four men.
column2: 在故乡的森林中，一个精灵能顶四个男人。

column1: In their native woods, one elf can fight like four men. They will not fight us on our chosen ground.
column2: 在故乡的森林中，一个精灵能顶四个男人。他们不会在我们选定的战场与我们作战。

column1: The stories about the elves’ great healing herbs are lies.
column2: 关于精灵神奇治疗草药的传言是谎言。

column1: By striking against the elves, we emulate our ancestors, and strengthen our clan magic.
column2: 通过打击精灵，我们效仿先祖，并增强我们的氏族魔法。

column1: Elves fight with stealth and subterfuge. They will do something bad to us when we least expect it.
column2: 精灵以隐秘和诡计作战。他们会在我们最意想不到的时候对我们不利。

column1: Elves fight with stealth and subterfuge and carry grudges for a long, long time. They have already done bad things to us and will now, no doubt, do more.
column2: 精灵以隐秘和诡计作战，并怀恨在心很久很久。他们已经对我们做过坏事，现在无疑会做得更多。

column1: It can’t hurt just to talk to them.
column2: 只是和他们谈谈并无害处。

column1: Curse you all! You’re talking about me as if I’m not even here! It’s not the first time one of us has done something independently of the ring! The important thing is this: elves must die!
column2: 诅咒你们所有人！你们在谈论我，好像我根本不在这里！我们中有人未经长老会自行其是，这也不是第一次了！重要的是：精灵必须死！

column1: No one will join a tribe with us if the elves are threatening to make war on us.
column2: 如果精灵威胁要对我们开战，就没有人会加入我们的部落。

column1: The elves will cause our fields to become overgrown with trees! They’ll plant things inside us, which will burst forth through our skin!
column2: 精灵会让我们的田地长满树木！他们会在我们体内种东西，然后从我们的皮肤里爆出来！

column1: A \x01@\x14 cannot start a fight and then withdraw. \x01@\x15 must follow through.
column2: \x01@\x14 不能挑起争斗然后退缩。 \x01@\x15 必须坚持到底。

column1: The written word makes up for people’s short memories. A perusal of our clan history would show us that we faced this problem before.
column2: 文字弥补人们短暂的记忆。翻阅我们的氏族历史会发现，我们之前就曾面临过这个问题。

column1: Whatever else we do, we had better bolster our defenses and hire more weaponthanes. The Aldryami won’t take this act lightly.
column2: 无论我们做什么，最好还是加强防御，雇佣更多武器领主。精灵不会轻易放过此事。

column1: Nobles from the \x01@! clan come in their formal finery to tell you that they intend to kill as many of you as they can. “Because we have told you this, it is not secret murder, which is a crime. We will kill you legally, which you deserve because \x01@\x17 killed all four sons of our chief for no reason. We have thought well of you in the past, but this transgression is too terrible to go unanswered.”
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的贵族们身着华丽正装前来，告诉你他们打算尽可能多地杀死你们。“因为我们告知了你们，这就不是秘密谋杀——那是犯罪。我们会合法地杀死你们，这是你们应得的，因为 \x01@\x17 毫无理由地杀光了我们首领的四个儿子。我们过去一直对你们心怀善意，但这次冒犯太过严重，不能不予以回应。”

column1: Nobles from the \x01@! clan warned us that they were starting a feud against us, because \x01@\x17 had killed all four sons of their chief for no reason.
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的贵族警告我们，他们将要与我们开战，因为 \x01@\x17 毫无理由地杀光了他们首领的四个儿子。

column1: Apologize for \x01@\x17’s actions.
column2: 为 \x01@\x17的行为道歉。

column1: We apologized for \x01@\x17’s actions.
column2: 我们为 \x01@\x17的行为道了歉。

column1: The nobles grudgingly accepted words of contrition, but warned us that deeds mattered more than words. Should we ever slight them in any way, they would fight the fiercest feud ever waged by an Orlanthi clan.
column2: 贵族们勉强接受了我们的忏悔之词，但警告我们说行动比言语更重要。一旦我们有任何冒犯他们的举动，他们就会发动奥兰斯氏族有史以来最激烈的血仇。

column1: The nobles haughtily ignored our words. “Only blood can pay for the deaths of the chief’s four sons,” they said, as they departed.
column2: 贵族们傲慢地无视了我们的言辞。“只有鲜血才能偿还首领四个儿子的死，”他们说完便离去了。

column1: Compose a poem praising the memory of the slain.
column2: 创作一首诗悼念死者。

column1: We composed a poem praising the memory of the slain.
column2: 我们创作了一首诗悼念死者。

column1: The nobles were moved to tears by \x01@N’s eloquent account of their slain chief-sons. They said they would call off their feud, but warned us that any further bad actions on our part would erase the beauty of the poem we had made for them that day.
column2: 贵族们被 \x01@N对他们已故首领之子充满感染力的叙述感动得落泪。他们说会放弃这场血仇，但警告我们，如果我们再有不良行为，就会抹去我们那天为他们所作的诗篇的美好。

column1: The nobles listened to \x01@N’s opening verses, but then spit and shook their fists. “Your words are insufficient. Only blood can pay for the deaths of the chief’s four sons,” they said, as they departed.
column2: 贵族们听了 \x01@N的开篇诗句，但随后啐了一口，挥舞着拳头。“你们的言辞不够。只有鲜血才能偿还首领四个儿子的死，”他们说完便离去了。

column1: The people were not unhappy to keep their cows, but muttered angrily that the ring did nothing to avoid feuding.
column2: 人们对保住牛只并无不满，但愤怒地咕哝着说长老会没有采取任何措施避免血仇。

column1: Offer them wergild.
column2: 向他们支付血偿金。

column1: We offered them wergild. They said we should pay as if each of the four boys was a chief.
column2: 我们提出了血偿金。他们表示，我们应当按照每个男孩都是首领来支付。

column1: “Because these killings were so cruel, because you have robbed our chief of all his sons at once, because you have broken us with sorrow, you must pay wergild as if each slain boy was a chief. We demand forty cows for each of the four boys.”
column2: “因为这些杀戮如此残忍，因为你们一次夺走了我们首领的所有儿子，因为你们用悲伤击垮了我们，你们必须按照每个被杀男孩都是首领来支付血偿金。我们要求四个男孩每人四十头牛。”

column1: They said that there would be no feud. The people mourned the loss of such a large number of cows.
column2: 他们说不会有血仇了。人们为损失如此大量的牛只而悲痛。

column1: Offer them half of what they ask.
column2: 给他们要求的一半。

column1: We offered them half of this amount.
column2: 我们给了他们这个数额的一半。

column1: With some reluctance, they accepted this offer, and said that there would be no feud. The people were unhappy to lose so many cows.
column2: 他们有些不情愿地接受了这个提议，并说不会有血仇了。人们对失去这么多牛很不高兴。

column1: They were affronted. “This paltry sum does not begin to wash away the blood \x01@\x17 has spilled!” They departed, stamping their boots upon the ground.
column2: 他们被冒犯了。“这点小钱根本洗不净 \x01@\x17 溅洒的鲜血！”他们跺着靴子离开了。

column1: Offer them a quarter of what they ask.
column2: 给他们要求的四分之一。

column1: We offered them ten cows for each boy.
column2: 我们提出每个男孩十头牛。

column1: Refuse them outright.
column2: 直接拒绝他们。

column1: “It does not surprise us,” they said. “We expect you to pay in blood.” And then they departed.
column2: “这并不让我们意外，”他们说，“我们预料到你们会用血来偿还。”然后他们离去了。

column1: Outlaw \x01@\x17.
We outlawed \x01@\x17 for this terrible breach of peace and decency.
column2: 我们因 \x01@\x17 严重破坏和平与体面而将其放逐。

column1: Tell them you are ready to fight.
column2: 告诉他们你准备好战斗。

column1: We told them that we were ready to fight.
column2: 我们告诉他们，我们已准备好战斗。

column1: They said they were too.
column2: 他们说他们也准备好了。

column1: Don’t offer a wergild we can’t afford to pay.
column2: 不要支付我们无力承担的血偿金。

column1: We can’t afford to pay wergild.
column2: 我们付不起血偿金。

column1: We can afford to pay a reasonable wergild.
column2: 我们付得起合理的血偿金。

column1: They are wealthy, and can afford to hire mercenaries to attack us.
column2: 他们很富有，雇得起佣兵来攻击我们。

column1: They weren’t our boys. We had no legal responsibility to keep them alive.
column2: 他们不是我们的孩子。我们没有法律义务保护他们的性命。

column1: We must pay them wergild.
column2: 我们必须支付他们血偿金。

column1: They will probably demand much more than the normal wergild, because \x01@\x17’s action was so cruel.
column2: 他们可能会要求远超正常血偿金的数额，因为 \x01@\x17的行为如此残忍。

column1: If there must be war, we are ready.
column2: 如果非战不可，我们已做好准备。

column1: They are weak; we can withstand their assaults.
column2: 他们很弱；我们能抵挡他们的攻击。

column1: They are strong; we will suffer if they feud with us.
column2: 他们很强；如果他们与我们结仇，我们会遭殃。

column1: \x01@\x17 has put us in an impossible situation.
column2: \x01@\x17 让我们陷入了不可能的境地。

column1: These people were once our friends.
column2: 这些人曾经是我们的朋友。

column1: They are using this as a pretext to strike against \x01@\x0B’s throne. Ignore them.
column2: 他们正以此为由攻击 \x01@\x0B的王座。别理他们。

column1: They have baleful, secret magics to use against us.
column2: 他们有恶毒的秘密魔法来对付我们。

column1: Death claims all, including chief-sons.
column2: 死亡夺走一切，包括首领之子。

column1: There must be a way to make peace.
column2: 一定有办法达成和平。

column1: Why must we all suffer for something only one of us has done?
column2: 为什么只有一个人做的事，却要我们所有人承受？

column1: As a child, the one who would become Bad King Urgrain was subject to violent rages. People said he would overcome them, but they got worse when he seized the crown.
column2: 那个后来成为恶王乌格兰的人，小时候就常怒不可遏。人们说他能克服，但当他夺下王冠后，情况变得更糟。

column1: The little bastards deserved it.
column2: 那些小崽子活该。

column1: I didn’t kill them for no reason; I killed them to start a war. We’re getting soft and weak.
column2: 我杀他们并非无缘无故；我杀人是为了挑起战争。我们正变得软弱无力。

column1: Another delegation of the clan’s prominent women complain to the ring that their rights are still not being respected. “The men have grown ill-tempered and insulting. They \x02\x07denigrate our secret women’s magic/refuse to perform their progenitive duties/dishonor our female ancestors/refuse to avenge slights against us by other clans/trade for jewelry instead of food/claim that Vinga is not a complete goddess/recite poems in which women are the villains\x02. Something must be done to curb their improper behavior.”
column2: 族中另一批显赫女性向长老会投诉，称她们的权利仍未得到尊重。“男人们变得脾气暴躁、出言不逊。他们 \x02\x07诋毁我们秘密的女性巫术/拒绝履行生育职责/侮辱我们的女祖先/拒绝为其他氏族对我们的轻慢复仇/用交易换来首饰而非食物/声称温伽并非完整的女神/吟诵以女性为反派角色的诗歌\x02。必须采取行动遏制他们的不当行为。”

column1: Women gathered before the ring and said the men were still not behaving properly.
column2: 女人们聚集在长老会面前，说男人们仍未端正举止。

column1: A delegation of the clan’s prominent women complain to the ring that their rights are not being respected. “The men have grown ill-tempered and insulting. They \x02\x07denigrate our secret women’s magic/refuse to perform their progenitive duties/dishonor our female ancestors/refuse to avenge slights against us by other clans/trade for jewelry instead of food/claim that Vinga is not a complete goddess/recite poems in which women are the villains\x02. Something must be done to curb their improper behavior.”
column2: 族中一批显赫女性向长老会投诉，称她们的权利未得到尊重。“男人们变得脾气暴躁、出言不逊。他们 \x02\x07诋毁我们秘密的女性巫术/拒绝履行生育职责/侮辱我们的女祖先/拒绝为其他氏族对我们的轻慢复仇/用交易换来首饰而非食物/声称温伽并非完整的女神/吟诵以女性为反派角色的诗歌\x02。必须采取行动遏制他们的不当行为。”

column1: Women gathered before the ring and said the men were not behaving properly.
column2: 女人们聚集在长老会面前，说男人们举止不当。

column1: Hold a feast in honor of the women.
column2: 举办一场盛宴以向女性致敬。

column1: We held a feast in honor of the women.
column2: 我们举办了一场盛宴以向女性致敬。

column1: The men toasted the women, and all was forgotten.
column2: 男人们向女性敬酒，一切不快都被遗忘。

column1: The men toasted the women, but as the evening wore on the insincerity of their toasts became all the more apparent. Men and women alike left the feast in a worse temper than when they arrived.
column2: 男人们向女性敬酒，但随着夜色渐深，他们敬酒中的虚情假意愈发明显。男女双方离开盛宴时，心情比来时更糟了。

column1: Sacrifice to female ancestors.
column2: 向女祖先献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to the spirits of female ancestors.
column2: 我们向女祖先的英灵献祭。

column1: The women were pleased by this honor, and said they would give the men another chance to correct their behavior.
column2: 女人们对这份敬意感到欣慰，表示愿意再给男人们一次改过自新的机会。

column1: The men sneered at the ring for attempting to please the women. An argument broke out, and both men and women left the ceremony in an even fouler temper than before.
column2: 男人们嘲笑长老会试图讨好女人。争执爆发，男女双方离开仪式时，情绪比之前更加恶劣。

column1: Scold the men for their improper behavior.
column2: 斥责男人们的不当行为。

column1: Members of the clan ring scolded the men for their improper behavior.
column2: 氏族议会的成员斥责了男人们的不当行为。

column1: The men argued that they were falsely accused, and that \x01DO was stirring up trouble where there was no trouble to be found. “She is always speaking against us, finding offense where none is intended. To apologize for something we have not done would be dishonorable. You have been fooled by her poison words, and make the entire clan seem foolish.”
column2: 男人们争辩说他们被冤枉了， \x01DO 分明是在无事生非、挑起争端。“她总是与我们作对，在无人有意冒犯之处挑刺。为我们没做过的事道歉，那是有失体面。你们被她的毒言蛊惑，让整个氏族显得愚不可及。”

column1: The men said that they did not realize that the women were insulted, and promised to show them more respect in the future.
column2: 男人们说他们并未意识到女人们受到了冒犯，并承诺今后会更加尊重她们。

column1: The men argued that they were falsely accused, and that \x01DO was stirring up trouble where there was no trouble to be found. “She is always speaking against us, finding offense where none is intended. To apologize for something we have not done would be dishonorable. You have been fooled by her poison words, and make the entire clan seem foolish.” This only made the women more upset.
column2: 男人们争辩说他们被冤枉了， \x01DO 分明是在无事生非、挑起争端。“她总是与我们作对，在无人有意冒犯之处挑刺。为我们没做过的事道歉，那是有失体面。你们被她的毒言蛊惑，让整个氏族显得愚不可及。”这番话只让女人们更加气愤。

column1: The ring members said that this was not their concern.
column2: 长老会成员表示这并非他们分内之事。

column1: The women grumbled and gave the ring sour looks as they left. One of the girls stuck out her tongue at \x01DP.
column2: 女人们离去时嘟嘟囔囔，向长老会投来怨毒的目光。有个女孩朝 \x01DP吐了吐舌头。

column1: The women grumbled and gave the ring sour looks as they left. One of the girls stuck out her tongue at the ring before slipping out the doorway.
column2: 女人们离去时嘟嘟囔囔，向长老会投来怨毒的目光。有个女孩在溜出门前朝长老会吐了吐舌头。

column1: Remove \x01DO from ring.
column2: 将 \x01DO 逐出长老会。

column1: \x01DO was removed from the clan ring.
column2: \x01DO 被逐出了氏族议会。

column1: The women were affronted; they said that they respected \x01DO, and would heed her words even though she had been taken off the ring.
column2: 女人们感到受辱；她们说她们尊敬 \x01DO，即使她被逐出长老会，也会听从她的言辞。

column1: Urge \x01DO to curb her criticism of the men.
column2: 敦促 \x01DO 收敛她对男人们的批评。

column1: The other ring members urged \x01DO to curb her criticism of the men.
column2: 其他长老会成员敦促 \x01DO 收敛她对男人们的批评。

column1: \x01DO admitted that her complaints were, by and large, without foundation. She told the women this, and they also withdrew their criticisms of the men.
column2: \x01DO 承认她的投诉大体上并无根据。她将此事告知女人们，她们也收回了对男人们的批评。

column1: \x01DO would not withdraw her complaints against the men. She promised to hector them even more sternly in the days to come.
column2: \x01DO 不肯撤回她对男人们的投诉。她保证日后会更加严厉地训斥他们。

column1: If we ignore them, the problem will solve itself.
column2: 如果我们不理睬，问题会自行解决。

column1: The fires of discontent have been fanned by \x01DO and her constant criticism of the men.
column2: 不满之火被 \x01DO 及其对男人们的不断批评所煽起。

column1: The fires of discontent have been fanned by \x01DO and her constant criticism of the men. It will be hard to convince her to relent.
column2: 不满之火被 \x01DO 及其对男人们的不断批评所煽起。很难说服她让步。

column1: There are no laws governing the way men should treat women.
column2: 没有法律规定男人该如何对待女人。

column1: Men should show proper respect for women.
column2: 男人应当对女人表现出应有的尊重。

column1: The \x02\x03grievances/complaints/accusations\x02 of the women are \x02\x03justified/valid/legitimate\x02.
column2: 女人们的 \x02\x03怨言/投诉/指控\x02 是 \x02\x03正当的/合理的/有根据的\x02。

column1: Their complaints are warranted. The men are in a bad mood, which moves them to act improperly.
column2: 她们的投诉是有道理的。男人们心情不佳，从而举止不当。

column1: The grievances of the women are legitimate; the men are even crabbier than they were before, and it shows in their treatment of the women.
column2: 女人们的怨言是正当的；男人们比之前更加暴躁，这在他们对待女人的态度上显露无疑。

column1: Hold a feast, and let them forget their irritation in good food and strong ale.
column2: 举办一场盛宴，让她们在美食与烈酒中忘却烦躁。

column1: Remind the men that it takes woman and man to make a family, and families to make a clan.
column2: 提醒男人们，家庭需要男女共同组建，而氏族需要家庭来构成。

column1: A scolding will make the men feel worse, and then they will act worse. We should encourage \x01DO to still her tongue, so that the men and women can begin to speak pleasantly to one another again.
column2: 责骂会让男人们心情更糟，行为也会更恶劣。我们应当鼓励 \x01DO 管住舌头，这样男女才能重新愉快交谈。

column1: Perhaps time off from the ring will bring relief from \x01DO’s constant criticism, which only feeds everyone’s ill-feelings.
column2: 远离 \x01DO不断的批评，或许能让长老会消停一阵，因为那只会助长所有人的不满。

column1: We are cursed by the baleful red moon.
column2: 我们被不祥的红月诅咒了。

column1: When he made the laws, King Heort said, “Men are not superior to women, and women are not superior to men. Each must respect the other.”
column2: 赫尔特王制定法律时说：“男人不优于女人，女人也不优于男人。彼此必须相互尊重。”

column1: Bad King Urgrain often set the men and women of his clan against each other by putting events in the worst possible light.
column2: 恶王乌格兰常常以最坏的角度解读事件，挑拨氏族中的男女对立。

column1: \x02\x04Ha ha/Hoo hoo/oh! OH! oh/Hee hee hee\x02!
column2: \x02\x04哈哈/呼呼/哦！哦！哦/嘻嘻嘻\x02！

column1: The bulls must be yoked.
column2: 公牛必须套上轭。

column1: They are right! The men have committed gross offenses against the women!
column2: 他们说得对！男人们严重冒犯了女人们！

column1: When will the men atone for their transgressions against the women?
column2: 男人们何时才能为他们对女人的过错赎罪？

column1: Women, don’t let a feast or a sacrifice fool you! The men must make up for their wrongs.
column2: 女人们，别让宴会或献祭蒙骗你们！男人们必须弥补他们的错误。

column1: \x01DO is always causing trouble! When was the last time she gave good advice?
column2: \x01DO 总是惹麻烦！她上一次给出好建议是什么时候？

column1: \x01DO does not want to see the women of the clan enjoying the men!
column2: \x01DO 不愿看到氏族的女人们享受男人们的陪伴！

column1: \x01DO has gone too far this time — it pains me to sit on the ring with her.
column2: \x01DO 这次太过分了——与她一起坐在长老会上让我痛苦。

column1: Give them nothing! They are ungrateful wretches!
column2: 什么也别给他们！他们是不知感恩的贱人！

column1: Again? How dare they even think to complain about the men!
column2: 又来？他们怎么敢抱怨男人们！

column1: Scold the women, scold them for their audacity, scold them I say!
column2: 责骂女人们，骂她们放肆，我说骂她们！

column1: The men have been rather rude of late.
column2: 男人们近来相当粗鲁。

column1: “To love a false woman is like slipping on ice, but men are treacherous, too.”
column2: “爱上虚伪的女人如同在冰上滑倒，但男人同样背信弃义。”

column1: “A tongue with a sharp edge is as dangerous as a sword.”
column2: “利舌如剑般危险。”

column1: The men and women must arm-wrestle!
column2: 男人们和女人们必须掰手腕！

column1: Even before Orlanth laid eyes on Ernalda, men and women have quarrelled.
column2: 早在奥兰斯见到埃尔纳达之前，男女之间就已争吵不休。

column1: Men and women have squabbled since time began. And they will still be quarrelling long after all of us are gone to our ancestors.
column2: 从时间之初男女就互相争吵。在我们所有人回归祖先之后很久，他们仍会继续争吵。

column1: Quarrels flare up, then die down, then flare up again. It is the way of things.
column2: 争吵爆发，然后平息，然后再次爆发。世事如此。

column1: A feast, a feast!
column2: 宴会，宴会！

column1: The mood between the men and women is much improved. Although the women were at first offended by our removal of \x01DO from the clan ring, they now admit that many of her complaints about the behavior of the men were greatly exaggerated.
column2: 男女间的气氛大为改善。尽管女人们起初因我们罢免 \x01DO 的氏族议会席位而恼怒，但如今她们承认，她关于男人行为的许多抱怨都被大大夸大了。

column1: Relations between the men and the women improved.
column2: 男女关系改善了。

column1: Another delegation of the clan’s prominent men complain to the ring that their rights are still not being respected. “The women have grown ill-tempered and insulting. They \x02\x07use up clan magic with secret women’s rites/taunt us as we attempt to perform our progenitive duties/dishonor our male ancestors/scold us as cowards when we swear off vengeful acts/will not let us adorn ourselves with jewelry/claim that Vinga is as great a god as Orlanth/recite poems in which men are fools\x02. Something must be done to curb their improper behavior.”
column2: 氏族的又一批显要男性向长老会抱怨说他们的权利仍未被尊重。“女人们变得脾气暴躁且无礼。她们 \x02\x07用秘密的女性仪式消耗氏族魔法/在试图履行生育职责时嘲笑我们/羞辱我们的男性祖先/当我们发誓放弃复仇行为时骂我们是懦夫/不让我们佩戴珠宝/声称温加和奥兰斯一样伟大/背诵男人是傻瓜的诗篇\x02。必须采取措施约束她们的不当行为。”

column1: Men gathered before the ring and said the women were still not behaving properly.
column2: 男人们聚集在长老会前，说女人们仍行为不当。

column1: A delegation of the clan’s prominent men complain to the ring that their rights are not being respected. “The women have grown ill-tempered and insulting. They \x02\x07use up clan magic with secret women’s rites/taunt us as we attempt to perform our progenitive duties/dishonor our male ancestors/scold us as cowards when we swear off vengeful acts/will not let us adorn ourselves with jewelry/claim that Vinga is as great a god as Orlanth/recite poems in which men are fools\x02. Something must be done to curb their improper behavior.”
column2: 氏族的又一批显要男性向长老会抱怨说他们的权利未被尊重。“女人们变得脾气暴躁且无礼。她们 \x02\x07用秘密的女性仪式消耗氏族魔法/在试图履行生育职责时嘲笑我们/羞辱我们的男性祖先/当我们发誓放弃复仇行为时骂我们是懦夫/不让我们佩戴珠宝/声称温加和奥兰斯一样伟大/背诵男人是傻瓜的诗篇\x02。必须采取措施约束她们的不当行为。”

column1: Men gathered before the ring and said the women were not behaving properly.
column2: 男人们聚集在长老会前，说女人们行为不当。

column1: Hold a feast in honor of the men.
column2: 举行一场宴会以向男人们致敬。

column1: We held a feast in honor of the men.
column2: 我们举行了一场向男人们致敬的宴会。

column1: The women toasted the men, and all was forgotten.
column2: 女人们向男人们敬酒，一切都被遗忘了。

column1: The women toasted the men, but as the evening wore on the wicked irony of their toasts became all the more apparent. Men and women alike left the feast in a worse temper than when they arrived.
column2: 女人们向男人们敬酒，但随着夜色渐深，她们敬酒中恶毒的讽刺变得愈发明显。男女们离开宴会时，脾气比来时更糟。

column1: Sacrifice to male ancestors.
column2: 向男性祖先献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to the spirits of male ancestors.
column2: 我们向男性祖先的灵魂献祭。

column1: The men were pleased by this honor, and said they would give the women another chance to correct their behavior.
column2: 男人们对此荣誉感到高兴，并表示会给女人们另一次改正行为的机会。

column1: The women sneered at the ring for attempting to please the men. An argument broke out, and both men and women left the ceremony in an even fouler temper than before.

column1: Trade with other outsiders is the exclusive purview of the clan ring.
column2: 与其他外族的交易是氏族议会的专属权限。

column1: Bad King Urgrain insisted on trading for the clan. In his arrogance, he insulted other traders who made sure he got only weevily wheat and sickly cows in return for his goods.
column2: 恶王乌格兰坚持要为氏族交易。出于傲慢，他侮辱了其他商人，那些商人便确保他只能用货物换来满是象鼻虫的小麦和病弱的牛只。

column1: It’s nice to see someone else in trouble for once.
column2: 难得看到别人倒霉，真不错。

column1: “The best of us have our faults; the worst are not without worth.”

column1: Traders from the \x01@! clan come to complain about the outcome of a recent trade deal. “\x01@\r traded your cows for our sheep. column1: Please allow me to go! I shall come back with a grand epic of adventure among the dragon-kin!
