column1: If only we valued literacy as much as these savage dragonewts!
column2: 要是我们像这些野蛮的龙人一样重视读写能力就好了！

column1: I’m back from my sojourn among the dragonewts! I wish I could put my experiences into words — and mayhaps one day I shall succeed — but for now all I can say is that there are more mysteries, and strange ways of thinking in this world than I ever would have dreamed of. Do not worry; I am well. Better than ever, in fact. But please never ask me why the dragonewts wanted my poetry.
column2: 我结束了在龙人中的暂居回来了！我希望能将经历诉诸言语——或许有一天我会成功——但眼下我只能说，这世上有比我曾梦想过的更多的奥秘和奇特的思维方式。别担心；我很好。事实上，比以往都好。但请永远不要问我龙人为何想要我的诗歌。

column1: If I tell anyone, even in my sleep, disaster will befall Dragon Pass. Oh, and I nearly forgot — they have given us much gold and silver jewelry, as payment for my services!
column2: 如果我告诉任何人，即使在睡梦中，灾难便会降临龙隘。噢，我差点忘了——他们给了我们许多金银首饰，作为我服务的报酬！

column1: The dragonewts came back with \x01@\x10’s bones.
column2: 龙人带着 \x01@\x10的骨头回来了。

column1: We could not understand what had happened to \x08. All they would say was,
column2: 我们无法理解 \x08遭遇了什么。他们只肯说：

column1: They said,
column2: 他们说：

column1: “We sorry poem destroyed \x08.” They gave us gold and silver trinkets in compensation for our ring member’s death.
column2: “我们抱歉诗歌毁灭了 \x08。”他们给了我们金银小饰物作为环成员死亡的补偿。

column1: During Death Week, a grim delegation appears in your clan hall; these are the spirits of your illustrious ancestors. They have a complaint to make. “Whenever the clan ring deliberates, there is a part of us that hears what you say. We hear you tally up how many cows you have, what your relations are with your neighbors, and whether you are stronger than clans you might feud with. That is all well and good. But what we can no longer stand to hear are the foolish proverbs that \x01@\x10 continually resorts to when \x06 has nothing else to say! ‘Fish cannot swim in a frozen river!’ ‘I-forget is the name of the heron who hovers over the feast!’ ‘It is always better to be alive, for the dead keep no cows!’ What are these supposed to mean? They mean nothing! If we hear one more stupid proverb, we will go crazy!”
column2: 在死亡周期间，一群阴沉的使者出现在您的部族大厅中；他们是您荣耀祖先的灵魂。他们有话要投诉。“每当氏族议会商议时，我们都有一部分能听到你们所说的话。我们听到你们盘点自己有多少头牛，与邻邦关系如何，以及是否比可能结怨的氏族更强大。这些倒都没问题。但我们再也无法忍受的是， \x01@\x10 在 \x06 无话可说时不断搬出的那些愚蠢谚语！‘鱼不能在冰封的河流中游泳！’‘我忘了是盘旋在盛宴上方的苍鹭的名字！’‘活着总是更好，因为死人没有牛！’这些到底是什么意思？毫无意义！如果我们再听到一句愚蠢的谚语，我们就要疯了！”

column1: The spirits of our ancestors complained that \x01@\x10 spoke in foolish proverbs.
column2: 我们先祖的灵魂抱怨说， \x01@\x10 总是说些愚蠢的谚语。

column1: Have \x01@\x10 explain the meaning of \x04 various proverbs to them.
column2: 让 \x01@\x10 向它们解释 \x04 各种谚语的含义。

column1: We told \x01@\x10 to explain the meaning of \x04 various proverbs to them.
column2: 我们告诉 \x01@\x10 向它们解释 \x04 各种谚语的含义。

column1: The spirits admitted that many of \x01@\x10’s sayings had understandable meanings, once they were properly explained. They went back to the halls of the dead.
column2: 灵魂们承认，一旦得到恰当的解释， \x01@\x10的许多话语都有可理解的含义。它们返回了死者之厅。

column1: The spirits were restless during \x01@\x10’s fumbling explanations. They disappeared, groaning.
column2: 在 \x01@\x10笨拙的解释过程中，灵魂们变得不安。它们呻吟着消失了。

column1: Order \x01@\x10 to apologize.
column2: 命令 \x01@\x10 道歉。

column1: \x01@\x10 apologized to them.
column2: \x01@\x10 向它们道了歉。

column1: The spirits accepted \x01@\x10’s apology, and went back to the halls of the dead.
column2: 灵魂们接受了 \x01@\x10的道歉，返回了死者之厅。

column1: The spirits were restless during \x01@\x10’s fumbling speech. \x05 grew nervous and blurted out another proverb, saying “It is good to be modest, but not so modest that you forget to talk well and be wise.” The spirits disappeared, groaning.
column2: 在 \x01@\x10笨拙的发言中，灵魂们变得不安。 \x05 变得紧张，脱口而出另一句谚语：“谦逊是好事，但不要谦逊到忘记言谈得体、智慧明达。”灵魂们呻吟着消失了。

column1: Remove \x01@\x10 from clan ring.
column2: 将 \x01@\x10 从氏族议会中移除。

column1: We removed \x01@\x10 from clan ring.
column2: 我们将 \x01@\x10 从氏族议会中移除。

column1: The spirits thanked us for ensuring their rest, and disappeared.
column2: 灵魂们感谢我们确保了它们的安息，然后消失了。

column1: Sacrifice to them.
column2: 向它们献祭。

column1: They accepted the sacrifice, and said they would return to the halls of the dead, and bother us no more.
column2: 它们接受了献祭，并表示将返回死者之厅，不再打扰我们。

column1: They said, “Your sacrifice is not enough to compensate for the pain of listening to \x01@\x10’s incessant nattering!” Then they returned to the halls of the dead.
column2: 它们说：“你们的献祭不足以补偿聆听 \x01@\x10喋喋不休的痛苦！”然后它们返回了死者之厅。

column1: Scold your ancestors for frightening the people for no good reason.
column2: 训斥你的祖先无缘无故惊吓族人。

column1: We scolded them for frightening the people for no good reason.
column2: 我们训斥它们无缘无故惊吓族人。

column1: “No good reason?” they said. “No good reason? We have a dozen good reasons: ‘With no sons, there are no boundary stones!’ ‘Tell tales to clever young women at night-time, for too many eyes are open during the day!’ Need we recite a hundred more?” Then they vanished.
column2: “无缘无故？”它们说，“无缘无故？我们有一打好理由：‘没有儿子，就没有界石！’‘在夜间给聪明的年轻女子讲故事，因为白天睁眼太多！’需要我们再背诵一百条吗？”然后它们消失了。

column1: They agreed that they had wasted the clan’s magic to manifest themselves in this manner. They promised not to do it again.
column2: 它们同意它们浪费了氏族的魔法以这种方式现身。它们承诺不会再这样做。

column1: Eventually, the spirits went away, though not after terrifying the children and the horses.
column2: 最终，灵魂们离开了，尽管是在吓坏了孩子和马匹之后。

column1: As our ancestors, they should understand that the living need cows more than the dead.
column2: 作为我们的祖先，它们应当明白活人比死者更需要牛。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice to them.
column2: 我们负担得起向它们献祭。

column1: Those aren’t our ancestors. They don’t look anything like us.
column2: 那些不是我们的祖先。它们看起来一点也不像我们。

column1: We owe respect and obedience to the spirits of our ancestors.
column2: 我们应当对祖先之灵表示尊重和服从。

column1: They are our ancestors. They should not be frightening the people.
column2: 它们是我们的祖先。它们不应该惊吓族人。

column1: Even a spirit appreciates a generous gift.
column2: 即使是灵魂也欣赏慷慨的礼物。

column1: Every five cows worth of goods we give them increases the chances of our pleasing them.
column2: 我们每给他们价值五头牛的货物，就增加了我们取悦他们的机会。

column1: If we give them what they want, they will just keep coming back and demanding more.
column2: 如果我们给它们想要的，它们就会不断回来索要更多。

column1: If we do not please them, they could curse us with ill-fortune.
column2: 如果我们不取悦它们，它们可能会用厄运诅咒我们。

column1: Every time they come back, they drain more of our clan magic. If we do not please them, they could curse us with ill-fortune.
column2: 每次它们回来，都会消耗我们更多的氏族魔法。如果我们不取悦它们，它们可能会用厄运诅咒我们。

column1: I often get the urge to swat \x01@\x10 myself.
column2: 我经常有种想拍打 \x01@\x10 自己的冲动。

column1: Bad King Urgrain offended the spirits of his ancestors, who then killed his cattle and ridiculed him at the moot.
column2: 恶王乌格兰冒犯了他祖先的灵魂，它们随后杀死了他的牛群，并在议会上嘲笑他。

column1: If troublesome ghosts ride the rafters aloft, I can convince them to wander elsewhere.
column2: 如果烦人的鬼魂盘旋在高处的椽梁上，我能说服它们去别处游荡。

column1: Some of \x01@\x10’s sayings make sense, but often they have no relevance to the situation at hand.
column2: \x01@\x10的一些说法有道理，但通常与当前情况毫无关系。

column1: Do not drink ale with a stupid bear.
column2: 不要和愚蠢的熊一起喝麦芽酒。

column1: While our ancestors are here, we must get them to give us a boon to use against the elves.
column2: 趁着我们的祖先在此，我们必须让它们赐予我们一件可以对付精灵的恩惠。

column1: It is bad to be visited by ghosts, even ghosts of our own lineage.
column2: 被鬼魂造访是不好的，即使是我们自己血脉的鬼魂。

column1: Excuse me. I am going home to my own stead until this is over.
column2: 失陪了。我要回自己的农庄去，等这事结束再回来。

column1: Hey, ask the ancestors if they already heard this proverb: “All is not well inside rusty old helmets.”
column2: 嘿，问问祖先们是否已经听过这句谚语：“生锈旧头盔里可不太平。”

column1: Yeah, \x01@\x10 you’ve got some explaining to do!
column2: 是啊， \x01@\x10 你可得解释解释了！

column1: Oh, this should be good!
column2: 哦，这下可有好戏看了！

column2: sceneR312

column1: Two unknown people come to you seeking temporary refuge. They seem to be foreigners; they do not know the proper greetings, and speak only the trade language. Their clothes are tattered, and it is hard to say where they come from. “We need food, place to stay. Will fight. Fight bravely for you, especially from horseback. Will stay for ten, fifteen seasons, no more.”
column2: 两个陌生人来寻求临时庇护。他们似乎是外国人；不懂正确的问候礼，只会说贸易通用语。衣衫褴褛，难以判断来自何处。“我们需要食物，住处。会战斗。为你们英勇作战，尤其擅长骑马。会待十、十五季，不会更久。”

column1: Foreign warriors sought refuge among us.
column2: 外国战士曾在我们当中寻求庇护。

column1: Allow a volunteer to sponsor them as guests.
column2: 允许一名志愿者以宾客身份担保他们。

column1: The ring said that they would allow a volunteer to sponsor them as guests.
column2: 长老会说，他们会允许一名志愿者以宾客身份担保他们。

column1: One of the wealthy farmers stepped forward, and said he would sponsor the foreigners. He conducted a Guest Ceremony, agreeing that he and his kinfolk would be responsible for their actions. The foreigners praised his generosity.
column2: 一名富裕农夫站了出来，表示愿意担保这些外国人。他举行了宾客仪式，同意自己及族人将对他们的行为负责。外国人称赞了他的慷慨。

column1: No one would sponsor them. The foreigners understood what this meant, and left without any further talk.
column2: 无人愿意担保他们。外国人明白了这意味着什么，没有再多说就离开了。

column1: Ask them what kind of people they are.
column2: 问他们是什么人。

column1: We asked them to tell us what kind of people they were.
column2: 我们请他们说明自己的身份。

column1: They said they were Grazers. We did not know what this meant at first, until \x01@N said, “They mean that they are Horse-Spawn.” They were among the worst kinds of foreigners. The Horse-Spawn said that they meant us no harm, and that they were exiles, victims of an unjust ruling by the Horse-Spawn king.
column2: 他们自称放牧者。起初我们不明白这意指何物，直到 \x01@N 说道：“他们是说自己是马裔。”他们属于最恶劣的那类外国人。马裔声称对我们并无恶意，他们是流放者，因马裔国王的不公裁决而受害。

column1: They said, “We just wanderers, people without land. Honorable, and mean no harm. When we say this is true, is true.”
column2: 他们说：“我们只是流浪者，无地之人。诚实，无害。我们说是真的，就是真的。”

column1: Have the chief sponsor them as guests.
column2: 让酋长以宾客身份担保他们。

column1: Offer to initiate them as Orlanthi.
column2: 提议接纳他们为奥兰斯信徒。

column1: We offered to initiate them as Orlanthi.
column2: 我们提议接纳他们为奥兰斯信徒。

column1: They said they did not seek new gods. They merely wished a place to stay for a few seasons. Some of the people murmured unhappily at this response.
column2: 他们说不寻求新神祇，只希望暂住几个季节。一些族人对此回答不满，低声抱怨。

column1: They left without argument.
column2: 他们未争辩便离开了。

column1: Soon we heard that they blamed us for sending suspicious foreigners their way.
column2: 不久我们听说，他们责怪我们把可疑的外国人引向他们。

column1: They thanked us for sending much-needed mercenaries their way.
column2: 他们感谢我们把急需的雇佣兵引向那里。

column1: They don’t look like they can fight.
column2: 他们看起来不像是能打仗的样子。

column1: We have enough warriors already.
column2: 我们已经有足够多的战士了。

column1: We could use more warriors.
column2: 我们能用上更多战士。

column1: They have muscles under those rags, and carry themselves like brave fighters.
column2: 那些破布下面有肌肉，举止也像是勇敢的战士。

column1: The laws of hospitality demand that we help helpless foreigners.
column2: 好客法则要求我们帮助无助的外国人。

column1: They do not know the proper greetings. We can’t expect them to behave properly.
column2: 他们不懂正确的问候礼。我们不能指望他们行为得体。

column1: They are not Orlanthi. It would be very unusual to make them Orlanthi.
column2: 他们并非奥兰斯信徒。将他们转变为奥兰斯信徒会非常不寻常。

column1: Our neighbors will hate us if we make foreigners our guests.
column2: 如果我们收外国人为宾客，邻族会憎恨我们。

column1: I would be proud to adopt them.
column2: 我会为接纳他们而自豪。

column1: Our ancestors weren’t known for adopting strangers.
column2: 我们的祖先并不以接纳陌生人闻名。

column1: The omens are good; we can afford to take risks.
column2: 征兆良好；我们承担得起风险。

column1: The omens are bad; it is not a good time to take risks.
column2: 征兆不佳；现在不是冒险的好时机。

column1: Some of the people are fearful of strangers.
column2: 一些族人对陌生人感到恐惧。

column1: Foreigners talk funny, and are easy prey for pranks. Let us welcome them!
column2: 外国人说话好玩，容易成为恶作剧的对象。我们欢迎他们吧！

column1: If we are to make them guests, we will have to perform a Guest Ceremony. Someone will have to sponsor them; that person and his kin must take full responsibility for the guests’ actions.
column2: 若要收他们为宾客，我们必须举行宾客仪式。需要有人担保他们；担保人及其族人必须对宾客的行为负全责。

column1: They mean to strangle us in our beds!
column2: 他们是想在床上勒死我们！

column1: Ask them if they know where we might steal a good treasure.
column2: 问他们是否知道哪里可以偷到好财宝。

column1: If we don’t adopt them, one of our enemies will.
column2: 如果我们不接纳他们，我们的某个敌人会接纳。

column1: They must be brought to the worship of the proper gods.
column2: 必须引导他们崇拜正统神祇。

column1: Having foreign guests here will make other clans nervous, and prevent them from making marriages with us.
column2: 留下外国宾客会使其他部族紧张，从而阻止他们与我们联姻。

column1: The remaining foreigner we took in as a guest has left. He thanked us for sheltering him, and said he would speak well of us.
column2: 我们收为宾客的那个外国人已经离开。他感谢我们给予庇护，并说会为我们美言。

column1: Those foreigners we took in as guests have left. They thanked us for sheltering them, and said they would speak well of us.
column2: 我们收为宾客的那些外国人已经离开。他们感谢我们给予庇护，并说会为我们美言。

column1: While exploring in the \x01@O, members of your clan encounter a drooling, wild-eyed hermit, dressed in a suit of bark. He froths at the mouth, dances a little jig, and then says, “Ah! You are from the \x01@" clan. The spirits have whispered things about you. You are headed for doom — doom, I say! \x02\x07Your children will grow beards!/Snakes will infest your tula!/A two-headed calf will be born to one of your cows!/A blue boar will cause disquiet among your hogs!/One of your steads will be haunted by a restless spirit!/Drought will strike your lands!/Dragonewts will conduct a mysterious ritual on your tula!\x02 This will be but the first of many catastrophes to befall you! The only way to stop this is to sacrifice a thrall to Kolat, the spirit-herding god. If you do not have a thrall, you must sacrifice a treasure. If you do not have a treasure, you must sacrifice ten cows. If you do not have ten cows, you must sacrifice five horses.”
column2: 在 \x01@O探索时，你氏族的成员遇到一个流着口水、目光狂野、穿着树皮外衣的隐士。他口吐白沫，跳了段小舞，然后说：“啊！你们是 \x01@" 部族的。精灵们曾对我低语过你们的事。你们正走向厄运——厄运，我说！ \x02\x07你们的孩子会长胡子！/蛇会 infest 你们的图拉领地！/你们的某头母牛会生出双头牛犊！/一头蓝野猪会在你们的猪群中引起骚动！/你们的某个农庄会被不安的鬼魂作祟！/干旱会降临你们的土地！/龙人会在你们的图拉领地上举行神秘仪式！\x02 这仅仅是降临在你们身上的众多灾难中的第一个！阻止这一切的唯一办法是向灵魂放牧之神科拉特献祭一名奴隶。如果没有奴隶，就必须献祭一件宝藏。如果没有宝藏，就必须献祭十头牛。如果没有十头牛，就必须献祭五匹马。”

column1: Explorers met a bark-clad shaman, who made dire predictions, and said we should sacrifice to Kolat, the spirit-herding god.
column2: 探索者遇到一位树皮裹身的萨满，他做出了可怕的预言，并说我们应向灵魂放牧之神科拉特献祭。

column1: The people did not mind that we chose to keep our cows instead of listening to a frothing stranger.
column2: 族人们并不在意我们选择保留牛只而非听从一名口吐白沫的陌生人。

column1: The people worried that the ring might not know how to recognize a true \x02\x02omen/oracle\x02.
column2: 人们忧心忡忡，担心长老会或许不懂得如何辨识真正的 \x02\x02预兆/神谕\x02。

column1: Sacrifice five horses to Kolat.
column2: 向科拉特献祭五匹马。

column1: We sacrificed five horses to Kolat.
column2: 我们向科拉特献祭了五匹马。

column1: The god-talkers could not say whether Kolat had received our sacrifice, because Orlanth’s brother is not one of the gods we usually worship, and they did not know which signs to look for.
column2: 神言者无法判断科拉特是否接纳了我们的献祭，因为奥兰斯的兄弟并非我们通常供奉的神祇，他们也不知该寻找哪些征兆。

column1: Sacrifice ten cows to Kolat.
column2: 向科拉特献祭十头牛。

column1: We sacrificed ten cows to Kolat.
column2: 我们向科拉特献祭了十头牛。

column1: Sacrifice a thrall to Kolat.
column2: 向科拉特献祭一名奴隶。

column1: We sacrificed a thrall to Kolat.
column2: 我们向科拉特献祭了一名奴隶。

column1: Sacrifice a treasure to Kolat.
column2: 向科拉特献祭一件宝物。

column1: Which treasure?
column2: 哪件宝物？

column1: We sacrificed\x01@\x01\x01@\x14 to Kolat.
column2: 我们向科拉特献祭了\x01@\x01\x01@\x14 。

column1: His predictions of doom are empty wind.
column2: 他那套灾难预言不过是空穴来风。

column1: Don’t sacrifice cows.
column2: 不要献祭牛只。

column1: We can’t afford to sacrifice ten cows.
column2: 我们承担不起献祭十头牛的代价。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice ten cows.
column2: 我们能承担献祭十头牛的代价。

column1: A treasure is much more valuable than the other things Kolat wants from us.
column2: 与科拉特向我们索要的其他东西相比，一件宝物贵重得多。

column1: We have many treasures. We can trade one to Kolat, in exchange for good fortune.
column2: 我们拥有许多宝物。可以拿出一样与科拉特交换，换取好运。

column1: Don’t sacrifice horses.
column2: 不要献祭马匹。

column1: We can’t afford to sacrifice five horses.
column2: 我们承担不起献祭五匹马的代价。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice five horses.
column2: 我们能承担献祭五匹马的代价。

column1: We must do as the barkman says!
column2: 我们必须照树皮人说的做！

column1: Only a fool ignores a shaman’s prophecy.
column2: 只有傻瓜才会无视萨满的预言。

column1: Kolat is a distant god.
column2: 科拉特是一位遥远的神祇。

column1: Not every frothing madman you meet in the woods is a powerful seer.
column2: 你在林子里遇到的每个口吐白沫的疯子，不都是强大的先知。

column1: This fellow is just a frothing madman, not a seer of any kind.
column2: 这家伙不过是个口吐白沫的疯子，根本不是什么先知。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice a thrall; we have too many mouths to feed anyway.
column2: 我们能承担献祭一名奴隶的代价；反正我们吃饭的嘴太多了。

column1: We can’t afford to sacrifice any of our thralls; we need them to work in the fields.
column2: 我们承担不起献祭任何奴隶的代价；我们需要他们在田里干活。

column1: Kolat is Orlanth’s brother, the God of Winds, and the Master of Spirits. He is not a god we normally worship.
column2: 科拉特是奥兰斯的兄弟、风神与灵魂之主，并非我们通常供奉的神祇。

column1: Kolat is not as important as Orlanth.
column2: 科拉特没有奥兰斯那么重要。

column1: We must do anything possible to avert this doom!
column2: 我们必须竭尽所能来避免这场灾祸！

column1: Every clan in Dragon Pass suffers catastrophes every day. Sacrifices to a distant god aren’t worthwhile.
column2: 龙之隘口的每个部族每天都在遭遇灾祸。向遥远的神祇献祭得不偿失。

column1: When a god asks for a sacrifice, it is impious to refuse.
column2: 神明索要献祭时，拒绝便是不敬。

column1: For no reason should we go sacrificing treasures!
column2: 无论如何我们都不该去献祭宝物！

column1: sceneR314
column2: sceneR314

column1: \x01@! warriors kidnap \x01D^, daughter of the chief, and take her back to their tula.
column2: \x01@! 武士们绑架了 \x01D^，酋长的女儿，并将她带回他们的图拉领地。

column1: \x01@! warriors kidnapped \x01D^, the daughter of the chief, and took her back to their tula.
column2: \x01@! 武士们绑架了 \x01D^，酋长的女儿，并将她带回了他们的图拉领地。

column1: Hire mercenaries to rescue \x01D^.
column2: 雇佣佣兵去营救 \x01D^。

column1: We decided to hire mercenaries to rescue \x01D^.
column2: 我们决定雇佣佣兵去营救 \x01D^。

column1: Warriors of the \x01@a clan will do it if you gift each of them with five cows. How many do you hire?
column2: \x01@a 氏族的武士们愿意干这事，只要您赠予每人五头牛。您要雇佣多少人？

column1: They rescued \x01D^, and also wounded many of our \x01@! foes. The people rejoiced.
column2: 他们救出了 \x01D^，还重创了许多我们的 \x01@! 仇敌。人们欢呼雀跃。

column1: Ransom her.
column2: 支付赎金赎回她。

column1: We decided to pay ransom for her safe return.
column2: 我们决定支付赎金，换取她平安归来。

column1: They demand the unusually high ransom of 20 cows for her return. This is the equivalent of the wergild paid for the death of a noble.
column2: 他们为释放她索要高得离谱的赎金——二十头牛。这相当于一名贵族身亡的血偿金。

column1: Pay it.
column2: 支付。

column1: We paid a heavy price for her return, but at least we got her back.
column2: 我们为她的归来付出了沉重代价，但至少找回了她。

column1: Negotiate their demand down.
column2: 压低他们的要价。

column1: The lowest ransom they will accept is \x01@\x1A cows.
column2: 他们愿意接受的最低赎金是 \x01@\x1A 头牛。

column1: Return home empty-handed.
column2: 两手空空地回家。

column1: The price they demanded was too great, so we returned home empty-handed. The people lamented the loss of the chief’s clever daughter.
column2: 他们要价太高，所以我们两手空空地回了家。人们哀叹失去了酋长那聪慧的女儿。

column1: We could not meet even the lower ransom, so we returned home empty-handed. The people lamented the loss of the chief’s clever daughter.
column2: 我们连压低后的赎金也付不起，于是两手空空地回了家。人们哀叹失去了酋长那聪慧的女儿。

column1: Angered by your attempts to bargain with them, they increase their demand. Now the lowest ransom they will accept is \x01@\x1A cows.
column2: 他们被你还价的企图激怒，提高了要价。现在他们愿意接受的最低赎金是 \x01@\x1A 头牛。

column1: We could not meet this greater ransom demand, so we returned home empty-handed. The people lamented the loss of the chief’s clever daughter.
column2: 我们连这更高额的赎金也付不起，于是两手空空地回了家。人们哀叹失去了酋长那聪慧的女儿。

column1: Send a war party to rescue \x01D^.
column2: 派出战团去营救 \x01D^。

column1: Our enemies defeated us, and we did not rescue \x01D^. The people were demoralized.
column2: 我们的敌人击败了我们，我们没有救出 \x01D^。人们士气低落。

column1: The people lamented the loss of the chief’s daughter.
column2: 人们哀叹失去了酋长的女儿。

column1: We can’t afford to pay ransom or hire mercenaries.
column2: 我们付不起赎金，也雇不起佣兵。

column1: We can afford to pay ransom or hire mercenaries.
column2: 我们能付得起赎金，也雇得起佣兵。

column1: It will be hard to find mercenaries.
column2: 很难找到佣兵。

column1: Mercenaries will cost us five cows apiece.
column2: 佣兵每人要价五头牛。

column1: We will get her back!
column2: 我们一定要把她抢回来！

column1: We should hire mercenaries; we can’t beat them ourselves.
column2: 我们应该雇佣佣兵；我们自己打不过他们。

column1: We can beat them, or bully them into a favorable peace arrangement.
column2: 我们能打败他们，或者逼他们签下有利的和约。

column1: We should expect to pay a ransom of 20 cows for the daughter of a chief.
column2: 为酋长的女儿，我们预计要支付二十头牛的赎金。

column1: The proper ransom would be about 5 cows.
column2: 合理的赎金大约五头牛。

column1: If they are allowed to keep her, we will be remembered for generations as fools and cowards.
column2: 如果任由他们扣留她，后世几代人都将把我们视为蠢货和懦夫。

column1: Pay the ransom, or hire others to go raiding for us. It’s planting time, and we must get the seed sown.
column2: 要么支付赎金，要么雇别人替我们去劫掠。现在是播种时节，我们必须把种子播下去。

column1: Pay the ransom, or hire others to go raiding for us. It’s harvest time, and we must get the crops in.
column2: 要么支付赎金，要么雇别人替我们去劫掠。现在是收获时节，我们必须把庄稼收回来。

column1: Feuds are all-too-common since the migration to lawless Dragon Pass.
column2: 自从迁徙到无法无天的龙之隘口以来，世仇屡见不鲜。

column1: The only ransom we should give them is a punch in the face.
column2: 我们应该给他们的唯一赎金就是一记耳光。

column1: It is no good to rescue \x01D^ without addressing the real cause of the problem, which is the rift between our clans.
column2: 若不解决真正的问题——我们氏族间的裂痕，救回 \x01D^ 也无济于事。

column1: War is better than peace.
column2: 战争胜过和平。

column1: The people will fear us when they see how many mercenaries our wealth will buy.
column2: 当人们看到我们的财富能雇来多少佣兵时，他们就会畏惧我们。

column1: That poor girl must be terrified!
column2: 那可怜的女孩一定吓坏了！

column1: Whatever we do will be the wrong thing.
column2: 无论我们做什么都是错的。

column1: My daughter! We must get her back.
column2: 我的女儿！我们必须把她夺回来。

column1: Our warriors rescued \x01D^. The people celebrated a great victory over our enemies.
column2: 我们的战士救回了 \x01D^。人们欢庆对敌大胜。

column1: We recently heard the fate of our chief’s daughter, \x01D^, taken by the \x01@! clan.
column2: 我们最近听说了酋长之女 \x01D^的命运，她被 \x01@! 氏族掳走。

column1: They say that she died of a fever, but we will never know if that is the truth or not.
column2: 他们说她死于热病，但我们永远无从知晓这是否属实。

column1: They swear that she ran away from them, and were surprised to learn that she was not with us already.
column2: 他们发誓说她从他们那里逃走了，并惊讶地得知她并未回到我们身边。

column1: Our chief is mourning \x01D^ as dead.
column2: 我们的酋长正哀悼 \x01D^ 如已逝。

column1: sceneR315
column2: sceneR315

column1: \x01D_, one of the most promising young god-talkers of Ernalda in your clan, has been neglecting her duties of late. She often disappears for hours at a time. Her uncle follows her one day, and discovers that she’s been going into the forest to talk and laugh with a spirit. When word of her activities spreads, some of the people are concerned.
column2: \x01D_，你们氏族中厄娜尔达最有前途的年轻神言者之一，近来一直疏忽职责。她常常一次消失数小时。一天她的叔父跟踪她，发现她一直去森林里与一个灵魂又说又笑。当她的行为传开后，有些人感到担忧。

column1: \x01D_’s uncle found out that she was sneaking off into the forest to speak with a spirit.
column2: \x01D_的叔父发现她正偷偷溜进森林与一个灵魂交谈。

column1: \x01D_, one of the most promising young god-talkers of Ernalda in your clan, has again been neglecting her duties and disappearing for hours at a time. Her uncle follows her once more, and confirms that she goes to the forest to talk and laugh with a spirit. When word of her activities spreads, some of the people are concerned.
column2: \x01D_，你们氏族中厄娜尔达最有前途的年轻神言者之一，再次疏忽职责，一次消失数小时。她的叔父再一次跟踪她，并确认她去了森林与一个灵魂又说又笑。当她的行为传开后，有些人感到担忧。

column1: \x01D_’s uncle found out that she was sneaking off into the forest to speak with that spirit again.
column2: \x01D_的叔父发现她正偷偷溜进森林再次与那个灵魂交谈。

column1: Despite being forbidden to do so, \x01D_, is still neglecting her duties and slipping into the forest to visit with a spirit. When word of her activities spreads, some of the people are concerned.
column2: 尽管被禁止这样做， \x01D_仍在疏忽职责，溜进森林拜访一个灵魂。当她的行为传开后，有些人感到担忧。

column1: \x01D_’s uncle found out that she was sneaking off into the forest to speak with that spirit, even though she was forbidden from doing this.
column2: \x01D_的叔父发现她正偷偷溜进森林与那个灵魂交谈，尽管她被禁止这样做。

column1: Convince the people that there is no harm in it.
column2: 说服人们这并无害处。

column1: The ring members told the people that there was no harm in this.
column2: 长老会成员告诉人们这并无害处。

column1: The people were glad to hear this.
column2: 人们听到这很高兴。

column1: They were skeptical.
column2: 他们持怀疑态度。

column1: Forbid her to visit the spirit.
column2: 禁止她探访那个灵魂。

column1: We forbade her to visit the spirit.
column2: 我们禁止她探访那个灵魂。

column1: She was sad to abandon this spirit, which she called \x02\x04Green Needle/Wise Leaf/Treeheart/Flit\x02, and considered a friend. She did it, though, because she was a loyal daughter of the clan.
column2: 她悲伤地放弃了这个灵魂，她称它为 \x02\x04绿针/智叶/树心/飞掠\x02，并视其为朋友。但她还是这样做了，因为她是氏族的忠诚女儿。

column1: She said she would abandon her visits with the spirit.
column2: 她说她会放弃与灵魂的会面。

column1: Sacrifice to the spirit.
column2: 向灵魂献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to the spirit.
column2: 我们向灵魂献祭了。

column1: Our god-talkers said that we had probably made a mistake, because the signs were all bad. This spirit meant us harm, and now we had given it strength.
column2: 我们的神言者说我们很可能犯了错，因为所有征兆都不好。这个灵魂对我们怀有恶意，而我们现在给了它力量。

column1: Our god-talkers saw many good omens after the sacrifice was made.
column2: 献祭完成后，我们的神言者看到了许多好兆头。

column1: Send for shamans to capture the spirit.
column2: 派人召唤萨满来捕捉这个灵魂。

column1: We sent for shamans to capture the spirit.
column2: 我们派人召唤萨满来捕捉这个灵魂。

column1: Shamans came and said they would try to capture the spirit for the low price of \x01@\x10 cows.
column2: 萨满来了，说他们会以低价 \x01@\x10 头牛尝试捕捉这个灵魂。

column1: Shamans come and say they will try to capture the spirit for the low price of \x01@\x10 cows. The price must be paid whether they succeed or not.
column2: 萨满来了，说他们会以低价 \x01@\x10 头牛尝试捕捉这个灵魂。无论成功与否，都得支付这笔费用。

column1: We can not meet their lower price of \x01@\x13 cows, and must send them on their way.
column2: 我们付不起他们更低的要价 \x01@\x13 头牛，只能打发他们走。

column1: We can not meet their price of \x01@\x10 cows, and must send them on their way.
column2: 我们付不起他们要价 \x01@\x10 头牛，只能打发他们走。

column1: Send for shamans to drive off the spirit.
column2: 派人召唤萨满来驱走这个灵魂。

column1: We sent for shamans to drive off the spirit.
column2: 我们派人召唤萨满来驱走这个灵魂。

column1: Shamans came and said they would drive off the spirit for the low price of \x01@\x10 cows.
column2: 萨满来了，说他们会以低价 \x01@\x10 头牛驱走这个灵魂。

column1: Shamans come and say they will drive off the spirit for the low price of \x01@\x10 cows. The price must be paid whether they succeed or not.
column2: 萨满来了，说他们会以低价 \x01@\x10 头牛驱走这个灵魂。无论成功与否，都得支付这笔费用。

column1: We agreed to pay them.
column2: 我们同意付给他们。

column1: They went out into the forest and stayed all day. Then they came back with a little cage made of sticks, sheep gut, and shiny rocks. They handed it to us, and said that it was a captured spirit, and that we should treat it as a treasure.
column2: 他们走进森林待了一整天。然后带回一个小笼子，用树枝、羊肠和闪亮的石头做成。他们把它递给我们，说这是一个被俘的灵魂，我们应该把它当作宝物。

column1: They went out into the forest and stayed all day. They came back empty-handed.
column2: 他们走进森林待了一整天。空手而归。

column1: They disappeared into the forest. They came back a few hours later, saying that the spirit had been banished.
column2: 他们消失在森林中。几小时后回来，说那个灵魂已被驱逐。

column1: It will cost more to capture the spirit, but a captured spirit is a kind of treasure.
column2: 捕捉灵魂花费更多，但被俘的灵魂是一种宝物。

column1: You can’t trust spirits; they are outside Heort’s Laws.
column2: 你不能信任灵魂；它们不受赫尔特法令管辖。

column1: Sacrifice to the spirit, and it will give us a gift.
column2: 向灵魂献祭，它会给我们一份礼物。

column1: Sacrifice to the spirit, and it will give us a gift. Do not give it more than six cows, for it can gift us only so much.
column2: 向精魂献祭，它便会赐我们礼物。不要给它超过六头牛，因它只能赠与我们那么多。

column1: Shamans can drive it off.
column2: 萨满能驱走它。

column1: The spirit is harmful, but I can convince the people otherwise, if you want.
column2: 精魂有害，但如果你愿意，我能说服民众相信相反。

column1: The spirit will do us no harm.
column2: 精魂不会伤害我们。

column1: You never can be too sure where spirits are concerned.
column2: 涉及精魂之事，永远不能太过笃定。

column1: The world is full of spirits. Some are good; others are bad. Most of them have their own selfish goals, just like people.
column2: 世间满是精魂。有些善良，有些邪恶。大多数都有自私的目标，就像人一样。

column1: If you turn a ghost into a treasure, you are still haunted.
column2: 就算你把幽灵变成财宝，你仍受其困扰。

column1: A captured spirit would be most useful!
column2: 一个被俘的灵魂会大有用处！

column1: Capture it.
column2: 捕捉它。

column1: I told you she was off visiting spirits.
column2: 我告诉过你她出门拜访精魂去了。

column1: Ghosts, o ghosts, wander astray, find not your forms, find not your homes.
column2: 幽灵啊，幽灵，四处游荡，寻不着形貌，寻不着家园。

column1: sceneR316
column2: sceneR316

column1: The children of the clan are again growing beards! The people are angry and worried. They know it is a curse of some kind, and don’t like it happening again.
column2: 氏族的孩子们又开始长胡子了！人们既愤怒又担忧。他们知道这是某种诅咒，不愿看到它再次发生。

column1: Once again, we suffered the curse that caused our children to grow beards.
column2: 我们再次遭受了使孩子们长胡子的诅咒。

column1: The children of the clan, boys and girls alike, have begun to grow beards! The people are worried. They say it must be a curse of some kind.
column2: 氏族的孩子们，无论男孩女孩，都开始长胡子了！人们很担忧。他们说这一定是某种诅咒。

column1: We suffered a curse, and our children, both boys and girls, began to grow beards.
column2: 我们遭受了诅咒，我们的孩子，无论男女，都开始长胡子。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors said that the curse was laid by tricky shamans, who hoped we would then pay them to remove it.
column2: 我们祖先之灵说这诅咒是狡诈的萨满所施，他们指望我们付钱请他们解除。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors were unclear about the cause of the curse, but suggested that Eurmal was behind it.
column2: 我们祖先之灵对诅咒的原因并不清楚，但暗示尤尔玛尔是幕后黑手。

column1: They laughed at us and said that no one would marry our bearded children when they grew up.
column2: 他们嘲笑我们，说等我们长胡子的孩子长大，没人会娶他们。

column1: Take the matter to the moot.
column2: 将此事提交议会。

column1: We took the matter to the tribal moot.
column2: 我们将此事提交了部落大会。

column1: Eventually, the beards fell out on their own.
column2: 最终，胡子自行脱落了。

column1: They said that they had laid no curse on us.
column2: 他们说不曾对我们施咒。

column1: We raided the clan that had cursed us.
column2: 我们袭击了诅咒我们的那个氏族。

column1: The people were happy to have struck against the ones who sent bad magic against our children. Once we bested them in a raid, the children’s beards fell out of their own accord.
column2: 人们很高兴打击了向孩子施放恶咒的人。我们在一场袭击中击败他们后，孩子们的胡子便自行脱落了。

column1: The people were displeased that we had failed to harm the ones who sent bad magic against our children. Later, the children’s beards fell out of their own accord.
column2: 人们因我们未能伤害向孩子施放恶咒的人而不快。后来，孩子们的胡子自行脱落了。

column1: The god-talkers said Eurmal had taken our sacrifice, but had not heard our pleas. The people were sad and angry, and spent much time comforting the weeping children.
column2: 神言者说尤尔玛尔收下了我们的献祭，却没有听到我们的祈求。人们悲伤而愤怒，花了很多时间安慰哭泣的孩子。

column1: The god-talkers said that Eurmal had taken our sacrifice. And, very quickly, the children’s beards turned grey and fell out in large clumps on the ground. The priests gathered them and burned the hair on the altar to dispel any lingering bad magic.
column2: 神言者说尤尔玛尔收下了我们的献祭。很快，孩子们的胡子变灰，大块大块落到地上。祭司们收集起来，在祭坛上焚烧毛发以驱散任何残留的恶咒。

column1: Send for shamans, then rough them up.
column2: 召来萨满，然后揍他们一顿。

column1: We told shamans to come to break the curse.
column2: 我们叫萨满来解除诅咒。

column1: When they arrived, we said that we knew they had laid the curse, and we beat them.They fled, and the people laughed. Once we did this, the children’s beards fell out of their own accord.
column2: 他们到达后，我们说知道是他们施的咒，然后打了他们。他们逃走了，人们大笑。我们这样做后，孩子们的胡子便自行脱落了。

column1: When they arrived, we said that we knew they had laid the curse, and we attacked them. The shamans loosed terrible spirits who confused us and sickened our warriors. They escaped, warning us that many worse curses would soon befall us. Not long after, the children’s beards fell out of their own accord.
column2: 他们到达后，我们说知道是他们施的咒，便攻击了他们。萨满释放了可怕的精魂，使我们困惑并使我们的战士生病。他们逃走了，警告我们很快会有更糟的诅咒降临。不久之后，孩子们的胡子自行脱落了。

column1: Send for shamans to break the curse.
column2: 召萨满来解除诅咒。

column1: We sent for shamans to break the curse.
column2: 我们召了萨满来解除诅咒。

column1: Shamans came and said they would break the curse for the low price of \x01@\x10 cows.
column2: 萨满来了，说他们会以 \x01@\x10 头牛的便宜价钱解除诅咒。

column1: Shamans come and say they will break the curse for the low price of \x01@\x10 cows.
column2: 萨满来了，说他们会以 \x01@\x10 头牛的便宜价钱解除诅咒。

column1: They smeared foul-smelling ointments on the faces of the children, causing some of the younger ones to weep. They danced about and rolled on the ground. They then told the children to wash their faces in the creek. They said the beards would not come back.
column2: 他们把难闻的药膏涂在孩子们脸上，使一些年幼的孩子哭了起来。他们四处跳舞，在地上打滚。然后叫孩子们去小溪里洗脸。他们说胡子不会再长回来了。

column1: The least they will accept is \x01@\x13 cows. Do you accept?
column2: 他们最少愿意接受 \x01@\x13 头牛。你接受吗？

column1: We reached a fairer price, and so they proceeded with the curse-breaking.
column2: 我们谈成了更合理的价格，于是他们开始解除诅咒。

column1: We decided that their price was too rich for us. Eventually, the beards fell out on their own.
column2: 我们觉得他们的价格太贵了。最终，胡子自行脱落了。

column1: Even their lowest price was too rich for us. Everyone worried, until the beards fell out of their own accord some time later.
column2: 即便是最低价我们也觉得太贵。大家都很担忧，直到一段时间后胡子自行脱落。

column1: They will not lower their price. Do you accept?
column2: 他们不肯降价。你接受吗？

column1: Their price was too rich for us. Everyone worried, until the beards fell out of their own accord some time later.
column2: 他们的价格我们觉得太贵。大家都很担忧，直到一段时间后胡子自行脱落。

column1: They smeared foul-smelling ointments on the faces of the children, causing some of the younger ones to weep. They danced about and rolled on the ground. They then told the children to wash their faces in the creek.
column2: 他们把难闻的药膏涂在孩子们脸上，使一些年幼的孩子哭了起来。他们四处跳舞，在地上打滚。然后叫孩子们去小溪里洗脸。

column1: The shamans said they had driven away the beard-growing spirits for the moment, but could not guarantee that they would stay away. They did not know who had sent the spirits, if anyone.
column2: 萨满说他们暂时赶走了生须精魂，但无法保证它们不会回来。他们不知道是谁派来的这些精魂——如果真有人派的话。

column1: The lowest price they offer is \x01@\x13 cows. Do you accept?
column2: 他们开出的最低价是 \x01@\x13 头牛。你接受吗？

column1: We reached a fairer price, and so they proceeded with the curse-breaking ceremony.
column2: 我们谈到了更公平的价格，于是他们进行了破咒仪式。

column1: They would not lower their price, which was too rich for us. Everyone worried, until the beards fell out of their own accord some time later.
column2: 他们不肯降价，要价太高我们负担不起。人人都在担忧，直到后来胡子自行脱落。

column1: “The beards will fall out if we are patient.”
column2: “只要我们耐心等待，胡子自会脱落。”

column1: Goats have beards! Perhaps they are turning into goats!
column2: 山羊有胡子！也许他们正在变成山羊！

column1: They didn’t turn into goats last time. Perhaps they are only turning into \x02\x03sheep/rats/wolves\x02.
column2: 他们上次没变成山羊。也许他们只会变成 \x02\x03绵羊/老鼠/狼\x02。

column1: We could beat \x01@\x08 until \x06 gets Eurmal to relent!
column2: 我们可以痛打 \x01@\x08 直到 \x06 让尤尔马尔心软！

column1: We should wait and see what happens.
column2: 我们应该观望一下。

column1: We saw this before. We don’t need to panic, but it would be good to know who did this, so we can seek revenge at our leisure.
column2: 我们以前见过这种事。不必惊慌，但最好弄清楚是谁干的，这样我们日后可以慢慢复仇。

column1: We could send for shamans to end this absurdity soon, or just wait, and it will go away on its own.
column2: 我们可以请萨满来尽快终结这场闹剧，或者只是等待，它自己会消失。

column1: We could send for the shamans that did this, and force them to fix it for free. Or just wait.
column2: 我们可以请来制造这件事的萨满，逼他们免费解决。或者只是等待。

column1: We will not fall prey to this shamanistic ruse.
column2: 我们不会落入这种萨满伎俩的圈套。

column1: \x02\x03A sacrifice to Eurmal is always tricky business./The Trickster God is so unpredictable…/Sacrifice to Eurmal makes my stomach queasy.\x02 Still, we must try.
column2: \x02\x03向尤尔马尔献祭总是一件棘手的差事。/恶作剧之神如此难以捉摸……/向尤尔马尔献祭让我胃里翻腾。\x02 不过，我们必须一试。

column1: We must conduct a divination to see who is to blame for this.
column2: 我们必须进行一次占卜，看看该怪谁。

column1: Shamanic curses are always annoying, and often short-lived.
column2: 萨满的诅咒总是令人恼火，而且往往持续不长。

column1: If Eurmal can cure it, Eurmal probably caused it.
column2: 如果尤尔马尔能治好，那大概就是尤尔马尔造成的。

column1: Wheat is bearded. Perhaps they are turning into elves!
column2: 小麦有芒。也许他们正在变成精灵！

column1: They did not turn into elves last time. So \x02\x03our fears were unfounded/this is not elf-related/these beards do not signify wheat\x02.
column2: 他们上次没变成精灵。所以 \x02\x03我们的担心是没道理的/这与精灵无关/这些胡子不代表小麦\x02。

column1: Just wait. The carls need to tend the fields — we can always raid next season.
column2: 等待吧。自由民需要照料田地——我们总可以在下一季突袭。

column1: Just wait. The carls need to cut the grain — we can always raid next season.
column2: 等待吧。自由民需要收割谷物——我们总可以在下一季突袭。

column1: Beards are \x02\x03salutary/good/beneficial\x02. They are holy symbols of Lhankor Mhy, the knowing god.
column2: 胡须是 \x02\x03有益的/好的/有利的\x02。它们是全知之神兰科·米的圣物。

column1: Don’t trust shamans; they deal with spirits of the dead.
column2: 不要相信萨满；他们与亡灵之魂打交道。

column1: All diseases and curses are sent by bad spirits, or enemy gods. Sometimes bad spirits do the bidding of mortal men.
column2: 所有疾病和诅咒都是恶灵或敌对神祇降下的。有时恶灵会听从凡人的命令行事。

column1: The spirits will do what they want with us; there is no point doing anything about it.
column2: 神灵想对我们做什么就做什么；对此做任何事都没有意义。

column1: The shamans are doing this themselves, to drum up business.
column2: 萨满们自己搞的鬼，为了招揽生意。

column1: \x02\x03This is a dull, dull problem./I feel sad for the children, but really, what great deed would help them? None./There is nothing interesting to do here.\x02
column2: \x02\x03这是个枯燥、枯燥的问题。/我为孩子们感到难过，但说真的，有什么伟大的事迹能帮到他们？没有。/这里没什么有趣的事可做。\x02

column1: I wonder if their hair will turn grey soon?
column2: 不知道他们的头发会不会很快变白？

column1: If the beards get long, I volunteer to braid them.
column2: 如果胡子变长了，我自愿给它们编辫子。

column1: Get shamans to send this curse back to wherever it came from.
column2: 让萨满把这个诅咒送回它来的地方。

column1: Don’t look at me! I wish I’d thought of it!
column2: 别看我！我希望我也能想到这招！

column1: Don’t look at me! I didn’t arrange this!
column2: 别看我！这不是我安排的！

column1: My friend Eurmal must be feeling neglected lately.
column2: 我的朋友尤尔马尔最近一定感到被冷落了。

column1: Maybe Eurmal means for us to trade them as exotic thralls!
column2: 也许尤尔马尔的意思是要我们把它们当作奇异的奴隶贩卖！

column1: The Trickster might do this. Or not. But he might be able to cure it, I think.
column2: 恶作剧者可能会干这事。也可能不是。但他也许能治好，我想。

column1: It is one thing for the boys to become virile ahead of the normal time, but no one will marry our young women if they are bearded!
column2: 男孩们提前发育是一回事，但如果我们的年轻女子长了胡子，就没人会娶她们了！

column1: Our poor, poor children are doomed!
column2: 我们可怜的孩子们完蛋了！

column1: How can we be sure this is just like the last time?
column2: 我们怎么能确定这次和上次一样？

column1: If we had the great sword Chaos Striker, spirits would be afraid to interfere with us.
column2: 如果我们有伟大的剑“混沌打击者”，神灵们就不敢来干涉我们了。

column1: We still have not gotten Chaos Striker, the famous sword, which would protect us against this sort of thing.
column2: 我们仍然没有拿到那把著名的剑“混沌打击者”，它能保护我们免受此类事情侵害。

column1: Our children awoke yesterday morning with hair on their pillows, and not on their faces! Those dreadful beards that appeared so suddenly are gone.
column2: 我们的孩子们昨天早上醒来时，头发在枕头上，不在脸上！那些突然出现的可怕胡子不见了。

column1: At least, they fell out for most of the children. There were \x01@\x19 little boys whose hair stayed on their faces.
column2: 至少，大部分孩子都脱落了。还有 \x01@\x19 个小男孩的胡子还留在脸上。

column1: Our healers finally calmed the boys down, and the \x01@\x19 were very \x02\x03quiet and subdued/sorry and melancholy/well behaved\x02 all day.
column2: 我们的治疗者终于让男孩们平静下来， \x01@\x19 整天都 \x02\x03安静而顺从/难过而忧郁/表现良好\x02 。

column1: Finally, their beards fell out this morning, too.
column2: 终于，他们的胡子今天早上也脱落了。

column1: All the children are laughing and playing again.
column2: 所有的孩子又笑又玩。

column1: The beards on the children fell out of their own accord.
column2: 孩子们脸上的胡子自行脱落了。

column1: sceneR317
column2: sceneR317

column1: \x02\x06Red Creek/Ardling/Zethnos/Tarsavi/Vathari/Vengasting\x02
column2: \x02\x06红溪/阿德林/泽斯诺斯/塔萨维/瓦塔里/文加斯廷\x02

column1: \x01Dc again asked for us to aid him in taking vengeance against the men who had killed his father many years before.
column2: \x01Dc 再次请求我们帮助他向多年前杀死他父亲的人复仇。

column1: \x01Dc wanted vengeance against the men who had killed his father many years before.
column2: \x01Dc 想要向多年前杀死他父亲的人复仇。

column1: Allow \x01Dc to pursue private vengeance against them.
column2: 允许 \x01Dc 向他们实施私人复仇。

column1: We allowed \x01Dc to pursue private vengeance against them.
column2: 我们允许 \x01Dc 向他们实施私人复仇。

column1: Demand wergild for the slaying of \x01Dc’s father.
column2: 为杀害 \x01Dc父亲索要血偿金。

column1: We sent a delegation to demand wergild for the slaying of \x01Dc’s father.
column2: 我们派出代表团，为杀害 \x01Dc父亲索要血偿金。

column1: They said we were even more foolish asking again.
column2: 他们说我们再次询问更加愚蠢。

column1: “Do you think we no longer understand the law?”
column2: “你们以为我们不再懂律法了吗？”

column1: The \x01@! lawspeaker said that their clan should not be liable for actions taken so long ago, when \x01Df and \x01Dg belonged to another, faraway clan. Furthermore, the two men had changed since they burned \x01De. “They have renounced their brutal ways, and are now as judicious and honorable as any Orlanthi thane.”
column2: \x01@! 律法师说，他们的氏族不应该为如此久远以前的行动负责，当时 \x01Df 和 \x01Dg 隶属于另一个遥远的氏族。此外，那两个男人自从烧毁 \x01De后已经改变了。“他们已经摒弃了残暴的行径，如今和任何奥兰斯乡绅一样明智而可敬。”

column1: They said we were foolish to even ask. Our people were dissatisfied, but none more so than \x01Dc.
column2: 他们说我们竟然询问真是太蠢了。我们的人民感到不满，但最不满的是 \x01Dc。

column1: \x01Dc was kept from his quarry, and the people were disappointed for him.
column2: \x01Dc 被阻止接近他的猎物，人民为他感到失望。

column1: Tell \x01Dc that it is not the right time for vengeance.
column2: 告诉 \x01Dc 现在不是复仇的时候。

column1: We told \x01Dc that it was not the right time for vengeance.
column2: 我们告诉 \x01Dc 现在不是复仇的时候。

column1: He said he would ask us again later.
column2: 他说他以后会再问我们。

column1: \x01Dc fought valiantly during the raid. \x01Df and \x01Dg were now old, and ran from the battlefield when they saw him. He pursued them, slaying each at the same instant, with a sword in his right hand and an axe in his left. The people howled in glee, for he had won his vengeance against his father’s killers.
column2: \x01Dc 在袭击中英勇战斗。 \x01Df 和 \x01Dg 如今年迈，看到他时从战场逃跑。他追击他们，右手持剑，左手持斧，同时将两人斩杀。人们欢快地嚎叫，因为他终于向杀父仇人报了仇。

column1: Defying the clan ring, he said he would wait no longer. He left, and no one had any doubt that he would take his vengeance. Indeed, we soon learned that he had.
column2: 他违抗氏族议会，说不再等待。他离开了，没有人怀疑他会复仇。果然，我们很快得知他已经得手。

column1: Living cows are more useful than dead enemies.
column2: 活着的牛比死掉的敌人更有用。

column1: People eventually forget old grudges.
column2: 人们最终会忘记旧怨。

column1: \x01Dc will keep asking until we satisfy him.
column2: \x01Dc 会一直要求直到我们满足他。

column1: \x01Dc will keep asking until we satisfy him — or he may take matters into his own hands, no matter what we say.
column2: \x01Dc 会一直要求直到我们满足他——或者他会自行其是，不管我们说什么。

column1: \x01Dc will not ask us forever. Sooner or later he will seek his own revenge.
column2: \x01Dc 不会永远问我们。迟早他会自行复仇。

column1: We have good cause to demand wergild.
column2: 我们有充分的理由要求血偿金。

column1: The people sympathize with \x01Dc’s cause, but will not be so happy if it leads us into trouble.
column2: 人民同情 \x01Dc的诉求，但如果这给我们带来麻烦，他们就不会那么高兴了。

column1: This is far more important to him than it is to us. Let him proceed with his revenge on his own, if we are prepared to deal with whatever results.
column2: 这事对他远比对我们重要。如果我们准备好承担任何后果，就让他自己去复仇吧。

column1: Tell \x01Dc not to raise this matter during planting time! Or tell him to take care of it himself.
column2: 告诉 \x01Dc 不要在种植时节提起此事！或者让他自己处理。

column1: Tell \x01Dc not to raise this matter during harvest time! Or tell him to take care of it himself.
column2: 告诉 \x01Dc 不要在收获时节提起此事！或者让他自己处理。

column1: In the sagas, personal grudges often turn into full-fledged feuds between clans.
column2: 在传说中，个人恩怨常常演变成氏族间的全面世仇。

column1: Bad King Urgrain’s nephew insulted one of his mother’s cousins in another clan. Their quarrel grew to include their clans, and caused many weaponthanes on each side to die, before they ever came to blows themselves.
column2: 恶王乌格兰的侄子侮辱了另一个氏族中他母亲的一位表亲。他们的争吵扩大到氏族之间，导致双方许多武器领主丧命，而他们两人自己还未交手。

column1: Wergild was given to us as a way to atone for the blood we must shed. When wergild fails, more blood is spilled.
column2: 血偿金作为补偿我们不得不流下的鲜血的方式被赐予我们。当血偿金失败，更多的鲜血就会流淌。

column1: “Set out on the journey when the time is right, but do not wait for a perfect day or you will sit home all your life.”
column2: “时机合适就出发，但不要等待完美的一天，否则你会终生坐在家中。”

column1: How \x02\x03often can we deny his request/many more times will put him off/soon can we go into battle\x02?
column2: 我们还能 \x02\x03多少次拒绝他的请求/还要推脱他多少次/很快就能投入战斗\x02？

column1: Vengeance is the right of every Orlanthi.
column2: 复仇是每一位奥兰斯人的权利。

column1: Vengeance is the right of every Orlanthi. We’ll get it this time.
column2: 复仇是每一位奥兰斯人的权利。这次我们就要实现它。

column1: Vengeance brings death, and is therefore good.
column2: 复仇带来死亡，因此是好事。

column1: It is always the same. The bulls fight, then we lose our cows.
column2: 总是这样。公牛相斗，然后我们失去奶牛。

column1: If they pay us wergild, we can add a silver inlay to the altar of our temples.
column2: 如果他们支付血偿金，我们就可以在神庙的祭坛上添加银嵌饰。

column1: If we raid them, be sure to bring back goods and cattle to pay for that silver inlay for the altar.
column2: 如果我们袭击他们，务必带回货物和牛只，以支付祭坛的银嵌饰。

column1: We aren’t going to get anything for the temple out of this, are we?
column2: 我们不会从这件事中得到任何用于神庙的东西，对吧？

column1: \x01Dc would not be so vengeful if he had a clever bride to occupy his time.
column2: \x01Dc 如果有一位聪慧的新娘占据他的时间，他就不会如此复仇心切了。

column1: Let him do it himself.
column2: 让他自己做吧。

column1: We can’t put him off forever.
column2: 我们不可能永远推脱他。

column1: The \x01@! sent a delegation to demand wergild for the deaths of their two weaponthanes.
column2: \x01@! 派遣了一个代表团，要求为他们两位武器领主的死亡支付血偿金。

column1: Agree to their demand.
column2: 同意他们的要求。

column1: They said that justice had been done, and departed. Our people complained that they paid a heavy price for \x01Dc’s private vengeance.
column2: 他们说正义已实现，然后离开了。我们的人民抱怨说，他们为 \x01Dc的私人复仇付出了沉重代价。

column1: They denounced us as unjust, and promised that we would suffer for it. Our people toasted \x01Dc for his determination, and the clan ring for its support of him.
column2: 他们指责我们不义，并承诺我们会为此受苦。我们的人民举杯祝贺 \x01Dc 的坚定，以及氏族议会对他的支持。

column1: Offer them twenty cows instead. Remind them that \x01Dc never received wergild for his father’s death.
column2: 改为向他们提供二十头牛。提醒他们 \x01Dc 从未因其父亲之死获得血偿金。

column1: We offered them half as many cows.
column2: 我们向他们提供了半数牛只。

column1: They grudgingly agreed to this. The people grumbled for a while about the price paid for \x01Dc’s private vengeance, but soon went on to grumble about other things.
column2: 他们勉强同意了。人民抱怨了一阵为 \x01Dc的私人复仇付出的代价，但很快转而抱怨其他事情。

column1: They stood firm in their demand for forty cows.
column2: 他们坚持要求四十头牛。

column1: We can afford the wergild, if we want to pay it.
column2: 如果我们想支付，我们承担得起血偿金。

column1: They are determined to have the full forty cows.
column2: 他们决心要整整四十头牛。

column1: Maybe I can talk them into settling for less.
column2: 也许我能说服他们接受少一些。

column1: They have no real case against us.
column2: 他们对我们并没有什么正当理由。

column1: They have a case against us, but we also had a case against them.
column2: 他们对我们有指控，但我们对他们也有指控。

column1: They have more of a case against us than we had against them.
column2: 他们对我们的指控比我们对他们的指控更严重。

column1: The people will not like losing their cows.
column2: 族人不会喜欢失去他们的牛。

column1: In the sagas, full-fledged feuds between clans can continue for many years.
column2: 在传说中，氏族间全面爆发的宿敌之争可能持续多年。

column1: \x01Dc did no more than exercise his rights.
column2: \x01Dc 仅仅是行使了自己的权利。

column1: Death for death — as it should be.
column2: 以命偿命——本该如此。

column1: Keep the cows.
column2: 留下牛。

column1: We should keep our precious cattle, and never mind their threats.
column2: 我们应该保留我们宝贵的牛，别理会他们的威胁。

column1: Since we lacked the cattle, we refused them.
column2: 由于我们没有牛，便拒绝了他们。

column1: They denounced us as unjust, and promised that we would suffer for it. The people toasted \x01Dc for his determination, and the clan ring for its support of him.
column2: 他们谴责我们不公，并承诺我们必将为此受苦。族人举杯为 \x01Dc 的决心庆祝，也为氏族议会支持他而庆祝。

column1: While clearing some forest, your carls find an ancient cart decorated with dragon insignia. It is very old.
column2: 在清理一片森林时，你们的自由民发现了一辆装饰着龙纹徽记的古老马车。它非常古老。

column1: We found a very old cart with dragon insignia on it.
column2: 我们发现了一辆非常古老的马车，上面有龙纹徽记。

column1: We broke the cart into pieces and scattered them in the forest.
column2: 我们把马车砸碎，散落在森林中。

column1: Our ancestors were pleased that we remembered their hatred of all dragon-things.
column2: 我们的祖先很高兴我们记得他们对一切龙裔之物的仇恨。

column1: Give it away.
column2: 把它送人。

column1: They were grateful for the gift.
column2: 他们对这份礼物心怀感激。

column1: Leave it where you found it.
column2: 留在发现它的地方。

column1: We left it where we found it.
column2: 我们把它留在发现它的地方。

column1: We could tell that our ancestors approved.
column2: 我们能看出祖先们认可了。

column1: Put it on display.
column2: 把它展示出来。

column1: We put it on display.
column2: 我们把它展示了出来。

column1: Clans who once cooperated with dragons admired our new treasure. Those who had fought against dragons in the past were displeased with us.
column2: 曾与龙合作的氏族赞赏我们的新宝藏。那些过去曾与龙作战的氏族则对我们不满。

column1: What is the minimum amount of goods you will accept for it?
column2: 你愿意接受的最低货物数量是多少？

column1: 25 cows
column2: 25头牛

column1: 30 cows
column2: 30头牛

column1: Test it to see if it is magical.
column2: 测试它是否有魔力。

column1: Our god-talkers tested it to see if it was magical. They
column2: 我们的神言者测试了它是否有魔力。他们

column1: Our god-talkers
column2: 我们的神言者

column1: said it had no magic in it.
column2: 说它没有魔力。

column1: said it must have magic in it, but could not figure out what sort.
column2: 说它一定有魔力，但弄不清是哪种。

column1: It is good to trade.
column2: 适合交易。

column1: We don’t need to trade it away.
column2: 我们不需要把它交易出去。

column1: We can trade this for much-needed goods.
column2: 我们可以用这个交换急需的货物。

column1: If we give it away, our relations with the recipient will improve.
column2: 如果我们把它送人，与受赠者的关系将会改善。

column1: We must test it to see if it is magical.
column2: 我们必须测试它是否有魔力。

column1: Our ancestors fought against the Dragon Empire. If we destroy this relic of that time, our clan magic will be strengthened.
column2: 我们的祖先曾与龙之帝国作战。如果我们毁掉那个时代的这件遗物，我们的氏族魔法将会增强。

column1: Our ancestors ignored the Dragon Empire. If we ignore this relic of that time, our clan magic will be strengthened.
column2: 我们的祖先曾无视龙之帝国。如果我们无视那个时代的这件遗物，我们的氏族魔法将会增强。

column1: Our ancestors supported the Dragon Empire. If we proudly display this relic of that time, our clan magic will be strengthened.
column2: 我们的祖先曾支持龙之帝国。如果我们自豪地展示那个时代的这件遗物，我们的氏族魔法将会增强。

column1: Two hundred years ago, the empire of dragon friends was destroyed by the very dragons it courted.
column2: 两百年前，龙友帝国被它所讨好巴结的龙摧毁。

column1: Put it by the temple!
column2: 把它放在神庙旁！

column1: I doubt that it is magical. It is just an old cart.
column2: 我怀疑它是否有魔力。只是一辆旧马车而已。

column1: What a wonderful discovery!
column2: 多么奇妙的发现！

column1: If we disturb it, the dragonewts will come and destroy us!
column2: 如果我们惊扰它，龙人会来毁灭我们！

column1: What a grand gift this will make!
column2: 这将是一件多么贵重的礼物！

column1: If it is valuable, we should keep it.
column2: 如果它很珍贵，我们应该保留它。

column1: We must see it if it magical before we do anything else.
column2: 在采取其他行动之前，我们必须先确认它是否有魔力。

column1: What use could a relic of the stupid dragon friends be?
column2: 愚蠢的龙友的遗物能有什么用？

column1: Led by thanes of the \x01@! clan, some of the clans of your tribe launch an action at the moot. They want you expelled from the tribe. At the moot, it seems like every clan has a long litany of complaints against you, some more serious than others.
column2: 在 \x01@! 氏族的领主们带领下，你们部落的某些氏族在议会上发起动议。他们想要将你们逐出部落。在议会上，似乎每个氏族都对你们有一长串控诉，有些比另一些更严重。

column1: At the tribal moot, the \x01@! clan said we should be expelled from the tribe.
column2: 在部落大会上， \x01@! 氏族说我们应该被逐出部落。

column1: Answer each charge, point by point.
column2: 逐条回应每一项指控。

column1: We answered each charge, point by point.
column2: 我们逐条回应了每一项指控。

column1: Deluged in a flurry of detailed arguments, our tribemates admitted that the grounds to expel us did not seem so clear as before. They decided not to expel us after all, but told us to treat them with better respect in the future.
column2: 陷入一连串详细论证的我们族胞承认，驱逐我们的理由似乎不像之前那么明确了。他们最终决定不驱逐我们，但告诉我们以后要对他们更尊重些。

column1: The other clans complained our flurry of detailed arguments missed the main point. We were trying to turn boulders into grains of sand, they said. We were expelled from the tribe.
column2: 其他氏族抱怨我们一连串的详细论证没有抓住重点。他们说我们试图把巨石变成沙粒。我们被逐出了部落。

column1: Beg forgiveness.
column2: 乞求宽恕。

column1: We begged forgiveness.
column2: 我们乞求了宽恕。

column1: Our tribemates decided not to expel us after all, but told us to treat them with better respect in the future.
column2: 我们的族胞最终决定不驱逐我们，但告诉我们以后要对他们更尊重些。

column1: Our pleas and gifts were in vain. We were expelled from the tribe.
column2: 我们的恳求和礼物都是徒劳。我们被逐出了部落。

column1: Denounce your opponents as scoundrels.
column2: 谴责你的对手是无赖。

column1: We denounced our opponents as scoundrels.
column2: 我们谴责对手是无赖。

column1: Members of the other clans joined us in denouncing those who tried to get us expelled. The people were proud of \x01@N’s stirring condemnation of their actions.
column2: 其他氏族的成员加入了我们，共同谴责那些试图驱逐我们的人。族人为 \x01@N对他们行为的激动人心的谴责感到自豪。

column1: Have the chief step down.
column2: 让首领下台。

column1: The \x01@! thanes said that they would withdraw their complaint against us for the moment, but that they would renew it if we did not improve our relations with the rest of the tribe.
column2: \x01@! 的领主们说他们会暂时撤回对我们的投诉，但如果我们不改善与部落其他氏族的关系，他们会重新提起投诉。

column1: “You tried that the last time,” the others said. They insisted that the case go forward.
column2: “你们上次就试过了，”其他人说道。他们坚持继续推进案件。

column1: We quit the tribe before they could expel us.
column2: 在他们驱逐我们之前，我们退出了部落。

column1: Nobody tried to persuade us to stay.
column2: 没有人试图劝我们留下。

column1: What are they talking about? We haven’t done anything to offend them.
column2: 他们在说什么？我们没做任何冒犯他们的事。

column1: We should answer each charge, point by point.
column2: 我们应该逐条回应每一项指控。

column1: I’d still like to know the exact things they are accusing us of.
column2: 我仍然想知道他们具体指控我们什么。

column1: Although we could answer each charge point by point, they are right; we have committed many offenses against the rest of the tribe.
column2: 虽然我们可以逐条回应每一项指控，但他们是对的；我们确实对部落其他氏族犯下了许多过错。

column1: We have committed many offenses against the rest of the tribe. All we can do now is reform, after begging for their tolerance.
column2: 我们对部落其他氏族犯下了诸多罪行。如今我们只能乞求他们的容忍，然后改过自新。

column1: It would be foolish to answer each charge point by point unless someone can do it brilliantly. Of course, I am that person.
column2: 逐条回应每项指控是愚蠢的，除非有人能巧妙地做到。当然，我就是那个人。

column1: As with any other moot, we must war-whoop to show our willingness to fight them.
column2: 与任何集会一样，我们必须用战吼来表明我们愿意与他们一战。

column1: We will be vulnerable without a tribe.
column2: 没有部落，我们将脆弱不堪。

column1: The warriors of the other clans do not look like they are going to war-whoop.
column2: 其他氏族的战士们看起来并不打算发出战吼。

column1: The warriors of the other clans do not look like they are going to war-whoop. Maybe we shouldn’t, either.
column2: 其他氏族的战士们看起来并不打算发出战吼。也许我们也不该这么做。

column1: Whatever we argue, we must give them gifts.
column2: 无论我们如何辩解，都必须向他们赠送礼物。

column1: Whatever we argue, we must give them gifts. Extremely generous gifts.
column2: 无论我们如何辩解，都必须向他们赠送礼物。极为丰厚的礼物。

column1: Forgiveness is better than denunciation.
column2: 宽恕胜过谴责。

column1: I hate to recommend it, but we still haven’t tried weeping, wailing, groveling, and tearing our hair out.
column2: 我讨厌提出这个建议，但我们还没试过哭泣、哀号、跪地求饶、撕扯自己的头发。

column1: They won’t care now whether this chief steps down or not. Perhaps we could settle the case by trying to meet and match their arguments.
column2: 现在他们不会在意这个酋长是否下台。或许我们可以通过试图与他们的论点针锋相对来解决此事。

column1: I guess I shouldn’t have \x02\x04put bees in their outhouses/mooned their cattle/put pebbles in their boots/thrown all that dung at them\x02.
column2: 我想我不该 \x02\x04在他们屋外茅厕里放蜜蜂/用屁股对着他们的牛/往他们靴子里放石子/把那些粪都扔向他们\x02。

column1: We have done nothing without good cause.
column2: 我们做每件事都有充分的理由。

column1: They’re going to throw us out anyway, so we might as well retain our dignity and quit.
column2: 反正他们也要赶我们走，不如保持尊严，自己退出。

column1: This is a disaster! We must beg forgiveness!
column2: 这是一场灾难！我们必须乞求宽恕！

column1: What a \x02\x03catastrophe/calamity/debacle\x02! We must throw ourselves on the ground, at their mercy, and plead for forgiveness!
column2: 多么 \x02\x03的大灾难/大祸/惨败\x02！我们必须匍匐在地，任由他们发落，恳求原谅！

column1: Tribes are \x02\x02foolish/stupid\x02 anyway.
column2: 部落本来就 \x02\x02愚蠢/愚昧\x02 。

column1: We are guilty of nothing. This is all a bunch of nothing, whipped up by scheming \x01@! tongues.
column2: 我们什么也没做错。这一切都是子虚乌有，不过是那些诡计多端的 \x01@! 舌头煽动起来的。

column1: Just tell me the complaints, I can answer each and every one of them.
column2: 告诉我他们有哪些抱怨，我每条都能回应。

column1: Is it really that bad? I am prepared to atone for what they see as my misdeeds.
column2: 真的有那么糟吗？我准备为他们眼中的我的过失而赎罪。

column1: How dare they conspire against us!
column2: 他们竟敢阴谋对付我们！

column1: Even if I were to convince them otherwise, this taint on our clan would linger. I must resign.
column2: 即便我能说服他们相信并非如此，这份污点仍会玷污我们的氏族。我必须辞职。

column1: Why do want to belong a tribe where our supposed allies stab in us the back? Let’s leave this ill-mannered throng!
column2: 为什么想加入一个所谓的盟友会在背后捅刀子的部落？让我们离开这群无礼之徒！

column1: The forest seems to be claiming your cropland at a surprisingly fast rate, no doubt because of your Summons of Evil ritual. No one ever sees the forest moving, or notices rapid growth, but every morning the fields are full of saplings and the edge of the forest seems to have crept closer. The carls are quite perturbed by this, and say it is time to deal with our ancient enemy.
column2: 森林似乎正以惊人的速度侵占你们的农田，这无疑是因为你使用了“召唤邪恶仪式”。没人看到森林移动，也没注意到快速生长的迹象，但每天早晨田野里都长满树苗，森林的边缘似乎又逼近了一些。自由民对此相当不安，说该对付我们古老的敌人了。

column1: The forest is still creeping up on your cropland at an alarming rate. The carls curse every new day — they see their labored-over fields growing with saplings and swear that the woods are crowding closer. They blame the Aldryami.
column2: 森林仍以惊人的速度向你们的农田逼近。自由民每天都在诅咒——他们看到自己辛苦耕耘的田野长出树苗，发誓说树林正在挤过来。他们指责阿尔德里亚米。

column1: The forest seems to be claiming your cropland at a surprisingly fast rate. No one ever sees the forest moving, or notices rapid growth, but every morning the fields are full of saplings and the edge of the forest seems to have crept closer. The carls are quite perturbed by this, and say it is the work of the elves.
column2: 森林似乎正以惊人的速度侵占你们的农田。没人看到森林移动，也没注意到快速生长的迹象，但每天早晨田野里都长满树苗，森林的边缘似乎又逼近了一些。自由民对此相当不安，说是精灵干的。

column1: The forest began to reclaim the land we had cleared.
column2: 森林开始重新占据我们清理过的土地。

column1: The farmers complained that the ring wasn’t listening to \x01@\x01.
column2: 农夫们抱怨说长老会没有听取 \x01@\x01。

column1: The farmers complained that the ring wasn’t going to have to chop down all those trees.
column2: 农夫们抱怨说长老会不会需要砍掉所有那些树。

column1: Sacrifice to propitiate Aldrya, goddess of the elves.
column2: 献祭以安抚精灵女神阿尔德里亚。

column1: We sacrificed to propitiate Aldrya, goddess of the elves.
column2: 我们献祭以安抚精灵女神阿尔德里亚。

column1: The god-talkers said they could not tell whether the elf goddess had accepted our sacrifice, for she is an unfamiliar deity, and they did not know what signs to look for.
column2: 神言者说他们无法判断精灵女神是否接受了我们的献祭，因为那是位陌生的神祇，他们不知道该寻找什么征兆。

column1: But they could tell that our ancestors had noticed the sacrifice, for our clan magic suffered greatly.
column2: 但他们能看出我们的先祖注意到了这次献祭，因为我们的氏族魔法严重受损。

column1: Seek out elves for a peace negotiation.
column2: 寻找精灵进行和平谈判。

column1: We sought out elves for a peace negotiation.
column2: 我们寻找精灵进行和平谈判。

column1: We found some elves, but they refused to even consider a negotiation. “The only peace will be when you cease clearing land, and go back to Heortland. And we know that will never be.” Whether these elves spoke for the rest or not, we had no way of telling.
column2: 我们找到了一些精灵，但他们甚至拒绝考虑谈判。“唯一的和平就是你们停止开垦土地，返回赫奥特兰。而我们知道那永远不会发生。”这些精灵是否代表其他精灵，我们无从得知。

column1: We found no elves.
column2: 我们没找到任何精灵。

column1: Send a war party to punish the elves.
column2: 派出战团去惩罚精灵。

column1: We assembled a war party to punish the elves.
column2: 我们组建了一支战团去惩罚精灵。

column1: \x01@\x05 thought \x06 saw some movement in the forest, and heard mocking laughter, but the party did not encounter any elves that they could fight with.
column2: \x01@\x05 以为 \x06 看到了林中有动静，还听到了嘲弄的笑声，但战团没有遇到任何可以与之战斗的精灵。

column1: We saw no trace of elves.
column2: 我们没有看到精灵的踪迹。

column1: Tell the carls to hack down the new growth every morning.
column2: 命令自由民每天早上砍掉新长出的树苗。

column1: We told the carls to hack down the new growth every morning.
column2: 我们命令自由民每天早上砍掉新长出的树苗。

column1: They did so, but had less time for their other work.
column2: 他们照做了，但干其他活的时间就少了。

column1: The carls will not stand to see their fields turned into a forest. We must act, and act quickly.
column2: 自由民无法忍受看到自己的田地变成森林。我们必须行动，而且得快。

column1: If the carls think we have \x02\x03surrendered to the elves/given up/abandoned their interests\x02, how can we expect them to stay loyal?
column2: 如果自由民认为我们已经 \x02\x03向精灵投降/放弃/抛弃了他们的利益\x02，我们还能指望他们保持忠诚吗？

column1: If we can make peace with them, maybe we can trade with them.
column2: 如果我们能和他们讲和，或许还能与他们交易。

column1: The elves have good reason to hate us.
column2: 精灵有充分的理由憎恨我们。

column1: It’s \x02\x03difficult/near impossible/tricky\x02 to negotiate with \x02\x03those who have every reason to despise you/those with whom you have little in common/those who want nothing from you, but that you go away\x02.
column2: 与 \x02\x03那些有充分理由鄙视你的人/与你几乎毫无共同之处的人/除了你滚远点之外别无所求的人\x02谈判是 \x02\x03困难的/近乎不可能的/棘手的\x02 。

column1: We’ll teach those elves a lesson!
column2: 我们要给那些精灵点颜色看看！

column1: The elves are dangerous and tricky foes; in a deep forest, a dozen elves can hold off an army of trolls.
column2: 精灵是危险而狡猾的敌人；在密林深处，十几个精灵就能拖住一支巨魔大军。

column1: The weaponthanes do not want to traipse around the woods again, looking for nothing.
column2: 武器领主们不想再在林子里瞎逛，漫无目的地搜寻。

column1: Sending our warriors to fight will-o’-the-wisps depresses the weaponthanes and angers the carls. Try some other solution.
column2: 派我们的战士去追捕鬼火会让武器领主们沮丧，也会激怒自由民。试试别的办法吧。

column1: Elves are elusive at the best of times. If they are \x02\x02behind/causing\x02 this, they will expect us to look for them — we have no chance of finding them.
column2: 精灵在最好的时候都难以捉摸。如果他们 \x02\x02在背后/正在制造\x02 这一切，他们也会料到我们会去找他们——我们根本不可能找到他们。

column1: Elves are \x02\x04puzzling/evasive/baffling/frustrating\x02, even when you do find them. And if they don’t want to be found, \x02\x03nothing will reveal them/they won’t be found/they could stand two feet away and you’d never see them\x02.
column2: 精灵 \x02\x04令人费解/难以捉摸/令人困惑/让人灰心\x02，即使你找到了他们。而如果他们不想被发现， \x02\x03什么也无法暴露他们/就根本找不到他们/他们可以站在两英尺外而你永远也看不见\x02。

column1: We can’t afford to let the forest reclaim our crop land.
column2: 我们承受不起让森林重新吞噬我们的农田。

column1: We can’t afford to let the forest reclaim our crop land, and we can ill afford to raid when the remaining fields need us so!
column2: 我们承受不起让森林重新吞噬我们的农田，也承受不起在剩下的田地如此需要我们时去劫掠！

column1: If the carls spend their time hacking down the new growth, they won’t have time for their other duties.
column2: 如果自由民把时间都用来砍伐新生的树苗，他们就没空干其他活了。

column1: The carls aren’t thrilled about spending their time chopping down little trees, but they feel better at taking some action against this threat.
column2: 自由民对于花时间砍小树并不热衷，但能用实际行动对抗这个威胁，让他们感觉好受些。

column1: If the elves don’t want to talk to us, no amount of hunting them is going to find them.
column2: 如果精灵不愿与我们交谈，再怎么追捕他们也找不到。

column1: You can make peace with people you can see and understand. How can we begin to understand such invisible foes?
column2: 你可以与你能看见、能理解的人讲和。我们又怎能开始理解如此无形的敌人呢？

column1: The goddess of the elves is Aldrya.
column2: 精灵的女神是阿尔德里亚。

column1: The goddess of the elves is Aldrya. If we sacrifice to her, the elves will know it, and know we seek peace.
column2: 精灵的女神是阿尔德里亚。如果我们向她献祭，精灵会知道，也会知道我们在寻求和平。

column1: We could sacrifice again, I suppose, but it didn’t appear to work the last time. But with elves, who knows?
column2: 我想我们可以再次献祭，但上次似乎没什么用。不过对精灵来说，谁知道呢？

column1: The elves are our ancient enemies. If we sacrifice to their goddess, our clan magic will weaken.
column2: 精灵是我们的宿敌。如果向他们的女神献祭，我们的氏族魔法就会削弱。

column1: Sacrifices to foreign deities are a waste of time and goods. If we can’t contact the elf goddess, we can at least hack at their handiwork.
column2: 向异神献祭纯粹浪费时间和财物。既然我们无法联系上精灵女神，至少可以砍掉他们的造物。

column1: This is not the best way the Summons of Evil could have turned out, but we must still fight back.
column2: 这并非邪恶召唤能造成的最坏结果，但我们仍然必须反击。

column1: The weaponthanes have \x02\x03to do things they’d rather not do/arduous work to do at times/to work hard\x02. Why shouldn’t the carls?
column2: 武器领主们 \x02\x03有时也得做他们不愿做的事/承担艰苦的工作/辛苦劳作\x02。为什么自由民就不行？

column1: Elves don’t fight fair, but if you manage to catch them they are weak and spindly.
column2: 精灵不按常理出牌，但如果你能抓到他们，他们其实又弱又细。

column1: Although they resemble men, elves are really plants. They hate and fear mankind, because we clear and burn their forests.
column2: 虽然精灵长得像人，但他们其实是植物。他们憎恨和惧怕人类，因为我们清理并焚烧他们的森林。

column1: Our deities \x02\x03preside/rule/are in charge of\x02 tamed plants. So we \x02\x03have no clear channel/don’t have an easy way/find it hard to\x02 communicate with the forest.
column2: 我们的神祇 \x02\x03主管/统治/掌管\x02 被驯化的植物。所以我们 \x02\x03没有清晰的渠道/没有容易的办法/发现很难\x02 与森林沟通。

column1: This is it. The accursed elves are finally close enough we can chop them all down like kindling.
column2: 就是现在。那些可恶的精灵终于够近了，我们可以把他们像柴火一样全砍倒。

column1: It seems like I’m \x02\x03always sounding the alarm for/repeatedly calling your attention to/forever warning you of\x02 elven evil, but only now do you see \x02\x03that we must fight them, always./what devious enemies they are!/how serious the problem is!\x02
column2: 看来我 \x02\x03一直在为精灵的邪恶拉响警报/反复提醒你们注意/永远在警告你们提防\x02 它们，但直到现在你们才明白 \x02\x03我们必须永远与他们战斗。/他们是多么阴险的敌人！/问题有多严重！\x02

column1: I did something to offend the elves, didn’t I?
column2: 我是不是做了什么冒犯精灵的事？

column1: We must make peace with them.
column2: 我们必须与他们讲和。

column1: Aldrya may be the goddess of our enemies, but she is not an enemy god.
column2: 阿尔德里亚也许是我们敌人的女神，但她并非敌对之神。

column1: If we all knew how to read, we could read \x02\x02scrolls/books\x02 that would tell us what to do in such situations.
column2: 如果我们都识字，就能阅读 \x02\x02卷轴/书籍\x02 ，它们会告诉我们这种情况下该怎么做。

column1: \x01@\t was found dead, a victim of secret murder.
column2: \x01@\t被发现死了，是暗杀的牺牲品。

column1: Blame bandits.
column2: 怪罪到匪徒头上。

column1: We blamed outlaws for the crime.
column2: 我们把罪行嫁祸给了逃犯。

column1: Do you send a war party to punish the outlaws?
column2: 你会派一支战团去惩罚逃犯吗？

column1: We sent a war party to punish the outlaws.
column2: 我们派了一支战团去惩罚逃犯。

column1: We did not find any outlaws to punish.
column2: 我们没有找到任何逃犯来惩罚。

column1: We found outlaws and did battle with them.
column2: 我们找到了逃犯，并与他们交战。

column1: We slew \x01@\x11 of them, and drove the others off. The people rejoiced in our vengeance against \x01@\t’s slayers.
column2: 我们杀了他们中的 \x01@\x11 ，把其余的都赶走了。人民因我们对 \x01@\t的凶手复仇而欢欣鼓舞。

column1: The bandits ambushed \x01@\x05, and many were hurt. Some were slain.
column2: 匪徒伏击了 \x01@\x05，很多人受了伤。有些人被杀了。

column1: \x01@\x05, who led the party, was among them.
column2: \x01@\x05带领队伍的人，也在其中。

column1: Blame the \x01@a clan.
column2: 责怪 \x01@a 氏族。

column1: We blamed the \x01@a clan.
column2: 我们责怪了 \x01@a 氏族。

column1: We raided them; the people roared for vengeance.
column2: 我们袭击了他们；人民怒吼着要求复仇。

column1: The people cheered when they knew we had taken our vengeance.
column2: 人民得知我们已复仇时欢呼起来。

column1: The people lamented when they learned that \x01Dp’s killers had beaten us.
column2: 人民得知 \x01Dp的凶手击败了我们时哀叹不已。

column1: Launch a legal claim against them.
column2: 对他们提起法律诉讼。

column1: They denied involvement in \x01@\t’s murder. The people were outraged by their lies.
column2: 他们否认参与杀害 \x01@\t。人民对他们的谎言义愤填膺。

column1: Do you now take the matter to the moot?
column2: 你现在要将此事提交议会吗？

column1: We took the matter to the moot.
column2: 我们将此事提交了议会。

column1: Our messengers said that other clans would send emissaries in several weeks’ time.
column2: 我们的使者说其他氏族将在几周后派遣代表。

column1: The god-talkers studied the signs given us by the spirits of our ancestors, and concluded that \x01@\t had been slain by outlaws.
column2: 神言者研究了祖先之灵给我们的征兆，并得出结论： \x01@\t是被流寇杀害的。

column1: Hold a normal funeral for \x01@\t.
column2: 为 \x01@\t举行普通的葬礼。

column1: There was much lamenting at the funeral.
column2: 葬礼上哀声一片。

column1: The people were heartened by this tribute to our slain friend.
column2: 人民因这次对我们死难朋友的致敬而感到振奋。

column1: The people said that the ring was just trying to make them forget. They did not want forgetfulness; they wanted vengeance.
column2: 人民说长老会只是想让他们忘记。他们不愿忘记；他们想要复仇。

column1: Hold an especially lavish funeral feast for \x01@\t.
column2: 为 \x01@\t举行特别丰盛的葬礼宴席。

column1: We held an especially lavish funeral feast for \x01@\t.
column2: 我们为 \x01@\t举行了特别丰盛的葬礼宴席。

column1: We went to do battle with the \x01@a clan; the people roared for vengeance.
column2: 我们去与 \x01@a 氏族作战；人民怒吼着要求复仇。

column1: Bandits and outlaws are always causing trouble.
column2: 土匪和流寇总是惹是生非。

column1: I don’t care who we take vengeance against, as long as we take it against someone!
column2: 我不在乎我们找谁复仇，只要我们能找人复仇就行！

column1: We are strong. We can take vengeance against whoever deserves it.
column2: 我们很强。我们可以向任何应得复仇的人复仇。

column1: We are weak. We must bide our time, and celebrate \x01@\t’s life.
column2: 我们很弱。我们必须等待时机，并纪念 \x01@\t的一生。

column1: Divination will reveal all.
column2: 占卜将揭示一切。

column1: Our magic is weak; a divination will yield misleading results.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱；占卜会得出误导性的结果。

column1: The carls are deeply upset, and doubly upset to face this trouble during planting season.
column2: 自由民深感不安，在播种季节遇上这种麻烦更是不悦。

column1: The carls are deeply upset, and doubly upset to face this trouble during harvest season.
column2: 自由民深感不安，在收获季节遇上这种麻烦更是不悦。

column1: One death should not bring about others.
column2: 一人之死不应招致更多死亡。

column1: This death is good, for it will lead to other deaths.
column2: 这次死亡是好事，因为它将导致更多死亡。

column1: Bandits! Bandits!
column2: 土匪！土匪！

column2: sceneR322

column1: Your carls get a rude shock while helping a cow give birth; the calf has two heads! The people are very frightened. The attending priestess of Uralda immediately destroys the deformed creature.
column2: 你们的自由民在帮助母牛生产时受到了极大的惊吓；小牛有两个头！人民非常恐惧。在场的乌拉尔达祭司立即摧毁了这个畸形生物。

column1: A two-headed calf was born; the people saw it as an ill omen.
column2: 一头双头小牛诞生了；人民视之为不祥之兆。

column1: Sacrifice to Uralda for protection from deformed cattle.
column2: 向乌拉尔达献祭以求护佑，免受畸形牛的困扰。

column1: We sacrificed to Uralda for protection from deformed cattle.
column2: 我们向乌拉尔达献祭以求护佑，免受畸形牛的困扰。

column1: The god-talkers said that Uralda had heard our pleas.
column2: 神言者说乌拉尔达听到了我们的祈祷。

column1: The god-talkers said that we had failed to please benevolent Uralda.
column2: 神言者说我们未能取悦仁慈的乌拉尔达。

column1: The god-talkers said that Urox had heard our pleas.
column2: 神言者说尤洛克斯听到了我们的祈祷。

column1: The god-talkers said that we had failed to please great Urox.
column2: 神言者说我们未能取悦伟大的尤洛克斯。

column1: Send for shamans to scare away bad spirits.
column2: 派人去请萨满来驱赶恶灵。

column1: We sent for shamans to scare away bad spirits.
column2: 我们派人去请萨满来驱赶恶灵。

column1: Shamans came and said they would scare away bad spirits for the low price of \x01@\x13 cows.
column2: 萨满来了，说他们愿意以低价 \x01@\x13 头牛来驱赶恶灵。

column1: Shamans come and say they will scare away bad spirits for the low price of \x01@\x13 cows.
column2: 萨满来了，说他们愿意以低价 \x01@\x13 头牛来驱赶恶灵。

column1: They went out into the woods. They returned at nightfall, covered in pine needles and smelling of smoke. They said the spirits would no longer bother us.
column2: 他们走进树林。夜幕降临时回来，浑身松针，散发着烟味。他们说那些恶灵不会再打扰我们了。

column1: The least they will accept is \x01@\x13 cows. Do you accept their price?
column2: 他们最少接受 \x01@\x13 头牛。你接受他们的价钱吗？

column1: We reached a fairer price, and so they proceeded with their rituals.
column2: 我们谈到了更合理的价格，于是他们进行了仪式。

column1: We could not meet their lower price of \x01@\x13 cows, and had to send them on their way.
column2: 我们无法满足他们更低的价格 \x01@\x13 头牛，只好送他们上路。

column1: We could not meet their price, and had to send them on their way.
column2: 我们无法满足他们的价格，只好送他们上路。

column1: Send for Uroxi warriors to scour your lands of Chaos.
column2: 派人去请尤洛克斯追随者战士来扫荡你们土地上的混沌。

column1: We sent for Uroxi warriors to scour our lands of Chaos.
column2: 我们派人去请尤洛克斯追随者战士来扫荡我们土地上的混沌。

column1: No Uroxi came.
column2: 没有尤洛克斯追随者前来。

column1: Uroxi came and said they would scour our lands of Chaos for the low price of 10 cows.
column2: 尤洛克斯追随者来了，说他们愿意以低价10头牛来扫荡我们土地上的混沌。

column1: Storm Bulls come and say they will scour your lands of Chaos for the low price of 10 cows.
column2: 风暴公牛来了，说他们愿意以低价10头牛来扫荡你们土地上的混沌。

column1: They tramped around our tula for several days, and then came back and said that the Chaos which had grown an extra head on that calf had been defeated. They left, proudly singing a vulgar song.
column2: 他们在我们的领地上走了好几天，然后回来说，让那小牛长出一个额外脑袋的混沌已经被击败。他们离开了，高傲地唱着庸俗的歌。

column1: They tramped around our tula for several days, and then came back and told us that we were stupid, and that there was no Chaos around. They said we could take heart, because they were keeping the cows they gave them, which would be used in the fight against Chaos.
column2: 他们在我们的领地上走了好几天，然后回来说我们很蠢，周围根本没有混沌。他们说我们可以放心，因为他们留下了给他们的牛，这些牛将用于对抗混沌。

column1: We reached a fairer price, and so they proceeded with their scouring.
column2: 我们谈到了更合理的价格，于是他们开始了扫荡。

column1: They tramped around our tula for several days, and then came back and said that the Chaos which had grown an extra head on that calf was defeated. They left, proudly singing a vulgar song.
column2: 他们在我们的领地上走了好几天，然后回来说，让那小牛长出一个额外脑袋的混沌已经被击败。他们离开了，高傲地唱着庸俗的歌。

column1: They tramped around our tula for several days, and then came back and told us that we were stupid, and that there was no Chaos around. They said we could take heart, because they were keeping the cows we gave them, which would be used in the fight against Chaos.
column2: 他们在我们的领地周围转了好几天，然后回来说我们很蠢，周围根本没有混沌。他们叫我们放心，因为他们留下了我们给的牛，这些牛将用于对抗混沌。

column1: At least Ernalda warned of this, and we have been preparing for the possibility.
column2: 至少埃娜尔达对此发出了警告，我们一直在为此做准备。

column1: At least Ernalda warned of this. It was probably caused by Chaos, and the Storm Bulls can best deal with it.
column2: 至少埃娜尔达对此发出了警告。这很可能是混沌引起的，风暴公牛信徒最擅长处理它。

column1: This happens sometimes. It is not always Chaos.
column2: 这种情况有时会发生。不一定总是混沌。

column1: We can hire someone to help us.
column2: 我们可以雇人来帮忙。

column1: It would be good to see my proud Uroxi comrades again, yet also good to sacrifice to our Chaos-stomping god.
column2: 能再次见到我自豪的尤洛克斯追随者同伴固然很好，但向我们的踏碎混沌之神献祭也不错。

column1: Shamans are strangers, and can’t always be trusted.
column2: 萨满是陌生人，不能总是信任他们。

column1: Sacrifice to Uralda.
column2: 向尤拉尔达献祭。

column1: It’s not like it’s a three-headed cow. Now that would be cause for concern.
column2: 又不是三头牛。那才值得担忧。

column1: We must show that we are willing to spend any amount to protect the people from Chaos.
column2: 我们必须表明愿意不惜一切代价保护人民免受混沌侵害。

column1: These evil spirits might next cause disease in our children.
column2: 这些恶灵接下来可能会让我们的孩子染上疾病。

column1: Our lives are ruled by omens, both good and bad.
column2: 我们的生活受征兆主宰，无论吉凶。

column1: Oh, to tramp the woods with doughty Uroxi warriors!
column2: 啊，和勇敢的尤洛克斯信徒战士一起在林间跋涉！

column1: I like shamans better than troublemaking Uroxi.
column2: 比起惹是生非的尤洛克斯信徒，我更喜欢萨满。

column1: If only we had a scroll to tell us what to do about two-headed calves!
column2: 要是我们有卷轴告诉我们该怎么处理双头牛犊就好了！

column1: Why, the problem is often in cases such as this that it is difficult to figure out why exactly we …
column2: 哎呀，问题往往就在这种情况下，很难弄清楚为什么我们……

column1: I don’t think this is really any big problem.
column2: 我不认为这真的是什么大问题。

column1: A two-headed calf isn’t good, but that doesn’t mean it’s Chaotic.
column2: 双头牛犊不好，但这并不意味着它是混沌的。

column1: Don’t take any chances.
column2: 不要冒险。

column1: Can’t the rest of you handle these barn stall tragedies?
column2: 你们其余人就不能处理这些牛棚里的悲剧吗？

column1: Some of the greatest dragonewt heroes had two heads.
column2: 龙人英雄中最伟大的一些就有两个头。

column1: It is only a short step from two-headed calves to broos and zombies running loose among our herds.
column2: 从双头牛犊到布鲁斯和僵尸在我们的畜群中横冲直撞，只有一步之遥。

column1: Priestesses of Chalana Arroy from many different clans have gathered together to pay homage to their goddess. As part of their devotions, they are traveling to various tulas and offering to heal the sick and the wounded. They ask only that you promise to aid them in the future, when your help is needed. The more people they heal, the greater the favor they will ask. The people are honored by their visit.
column2: 来自许多不同氏族的查拉娜·阿罗伊女祭司聚集在一起向他们的女神致敬。作为虔诚的一部分，她们正前往各个图拉领地，提供治疗病人和伤者的服务。她们只要求你承诺将来在需要时帮助她们。她们治愈的人越多，要求的恩惠就越大。人民对她们的来访感到荣幸。

column1: Priestesses of Chalana Arroy said they would heal our sick and wounded in exchange for a future favor.
column2: 查拉娜·阿罗伊的女祭司说她们会治疗我们的病人和伤者，以换取未来的一个恩惠。

column1: Ask them to heal all of your sick and wounded.
column2: 请她们治疗你所有的病人和伤者。

column1: We asked them to heal all of our sick and wounded.
column2: 我们请她们治疗了我们所有的病人和伤者。

column1: They did so, and the people rejoiced.
column2: 她们照做了，人民欢欣鼓舞。

column1: The priestesses departed, reminding us that they would one day come back to ask for a favor in return.
column2: 女祭司们离开了，提醒我们她们总有一天会回来要求回报恩惠。

column1: Ask them to heal half of your sick and wounded.
column2: 请她们治疗一半的病人和伤者。

column1: We asked them to heal half of our sick and wounded.
column2: 我们请她们治疗了一半的病人和伤者。

column1: They did so, and the people were pleased. The priestesses departed, reminding us that they would one day come back to ask for a favor in return.
column2: 她们照做了，人民感到满意。女祭司们离开了，提醒我们她们总有一天会回来要求回报恩惠。

column1: Ask them to heal only a few people.
column2: 请她们只治疗几个人。

column1: We asked them to heal only a few people.
column2: 我们请她们只治疗了几个人。

column1: They did so and departed, reminding us that they would one day come back to ask for a favor in return.
column2: 她们照做了然后离开，提醒我们她们总有一天会回来要求回报恩惠。

column1: The priestesses said nothing, but the people saw that they were displeased, and so were displeased in turn.
column2: 女祭司们什么也没说，但人们看出她们不高兴，于是也不高兴起来。

column1: Decline their offer; give them gifts.
column2: 拒绝她们的提议；送给她们礼物。

column1: We declined their offer, and offered them gifts in return.
column2: 我们拒绝了她们的提议，并回赠了礼物。

column1: They declined our gifts, saying that it was not yet the time. The priestesses said little else, but the people saw that they were displeased, and so were displeased in turn.
column2: 她们拒绝了我们的礼物，说时候未到。女祭司们没再多说什么，但人们看出她们不高兴，于是也不高兴起来。

column1: We must be careful not to promise a favor if we do not know what that favor will be.
column2: 我们必须小心，如果不知道这个恩惠是什么，就不要承诺。

column1: In general, it is bad to promise a favor when you do not know what that favor will be.

column1: They thanked us in the name of their unyielding god.
column2: 他们以他们那不屈之神的名义向我们道谢。

column2: 他们在我们的土地上徘徊多日，却未找到他们寻找的怪物。不过他们是不错的客人，几乎没有打扰我们。

column1: Give permission; give them gifts.
