column2: 我们同意了，并赠予他们礼物。

column1: They praised us as an honorable clan.
column2: 他们称赞我们是光荣的氏族。

column1: They found spectres and ghouls everywhere, and put them to the sword. We knew that our lands were haunted, but had no idea just how much danger our people were in. We were overjoyed that they vanquished the undead on our tula.
column2: 他们发现遍地都是幽魂和食尸鬼，便将它们尽数斩杀。我们知道我们的土地闹鬼，但完全没想到族人竟身处如此巨大的危险之中。他们歼灭了我们的领地上的亡灵，我们欣喜若狂。

column1: Give them permission and sacrifice to Humakt.
column2: 允许他们，并向胡马特献祭。

column2: 我们同意了，并向胡马特献祭。

column1: They praised us as a wise and honorable clan.
column2: 他们称赞我们是明智而光荣的氏族。

column2: 他们发现遍地都是幽魂和食尸鬼，便将它们尽数斩杀。我们知道我们的土地闹鬼，但完全没想到族人竟身处如此巨大的危险之中。我们欣喜若狂。

column1: Give them permission.
column2: 允许他们。

column1: They scolded us, saying that it was one thing for us to foolishly expose ourselves to danger, yet another to threaten our neighbors through inaction. “When the undead turn you into walking corpses, you will attack the tulas that border yours, and then we will have to come and kill you. You are dishonorable vermin. You might as well be undead already.” Then they departed. The people were afraid, although whether they feared the undead more than the Humakti themselves was hard to say.
column2: 他们斥责我们，说我们愚蠢地置身险境是一回事，但通过不作为危害邻居则是另一回事。“等亡灵把你们变成行尸，你们就会攻击相邻的领地，那时我们就得来杀掉你们。你们是不光彩的害虫。你们简直已经是亡灵了。”然后他们离开了。人们很害怕，尽管很难说他们更怕亡灵还是更怕胡马特人自己。

column1: Please, no gifts or sacrifices this time.
column2: 这次请不要送礼或献祭。

column1: We can afford to be generous.
column2: 我们经得起慷慨大方。

column1: It is one thing to give away wealth, but another thing to give it away for nothing.
column2: 施舍财富是一回事，白白浪费又是另一回事。

column1: They’re not so tough. The ghosts and ghouls will eat them alive.
column2: 他们没那么厉害。幽灵和食尸鬼会活活把他们吃掉。

column1: They are great warriors.
column2: 他们是伟大的战士。

column1: They are great warriors. We don’t want them angry at us.
column2: 他们是伟大的战士。我们不想让他们对我们发怒。

column1: Humakti are known for their fanatical loathing of the undead.
column2: 胡马特人以对亡灵狂热的憎恨著称。

column1: Humakti are known for their loathing of the undead, and sometimes for scorning those who do not share it.
column2: 胡马特人以憎恨亡灵著称，有时也鄙视那些不共担此恨的人。

column1: If we sacrifice to Humakt, they will be pleased.
column2: 如果我们向胡马特献祭，他们会高兴。

column1: If we sacrifice to Humakt, they will be likelier to succeed.
column2: 如果我们向胡马特献祭，他们更有可能成功。

column1: If we sacrifice to Humakt, they will be likelier to succeed; they will honor us, too.
column2: 如果我们向胡马特献祭，他们更有可能成功；他们也会尊敬我们。

column1: Humakt was once Orlanth’s brother, but he severed his kinship ties in order to command the weapon called Death.
column2: 胡马特曾是奥兰斯的兄弟，但他为了掌握名为“死亡”的武器而切断了血缘纽带。

column1: The threat they name is real. We must aid them through sacrifice.
column2: 他们提到的威胁是真实的。我们必须通过献祭来帮助他们。

column1: Humakt has heard our prayers. These warriors ask to do us a great favor.
column2: 胡马特听到了我们的祈祷。这些战士请求帮我们一个大忙。

column1: How can we refuse them?
column2: 我们怎能拒绝他们？

column1: Undead are Chaotic, and I can smell Chaos. If I didn’t smell them, they aren’t here.
column2: 亡灵是混沌的，我能闻到混沌。如果我没闻到它们，它们就不在此处。

column1: Eurmal said that Humakt was once a sword, but became Orlanth’s brother. Humakt, offended, stuffed him in a barrel. Without food, Eurmal grew thin enough to squeeze through the barrel-slats.
column2: 欧尔马尔说胡马特曾是一把剑，后来成了奥兰斯的兄弟。胡马特被冒犯，把他塞进一个桶里。没有食物，欧尔马尔变得很瘦，足以从桶板间挤出来。

column1: The undead are known to spread disease.
column2: 众所周知，亡灵会传播疾病。

column1: If they are such great heroes, why do they travel in packs?
column2: 如果他们真是如此伟大的英雄，为何要结伴而行？

column1: The last time we faced a problem like this, I had exactly the right — no, I’m sorry, I was thinking of the last problem.
column2: 上一次我们面对这样的问题时，我正好有正确的——不，抱歉，我在想上一个问题。

column1: We must exterminate the undead; it must be the ghouls and living corpses who are scaring the dragonewts away.
column2: 我们必须消灭亡灵；一定是那些食尸鬼和活尸把龙人吓跑了。

column1: The spirits of your most illustrious ancestors materialize in your clan hall. “You have done honor to us, and to the history of the clan. The wise and judicious rule of the clan ring strengthens our magic, so now we wish to honor you with a reciprocal gift.”
column2: 你最杰出的祖先之灵显现在你的部族大厅中。“你们为我们、为氏族历史带来了荣耀。氏族议会的明智而审慎的统治增强了我们的魔法，因此现在我们希望回赠一份礼物来向你们致敬。”

column1: The spirits of our ancestors appeared and offered us a gift.
column2: 我们的祖先之灵显现，赠予我们一份礼物。

column1: Ask for joy.
column2: 请求欢乐。

column1: We asked them for joy.
column2: 我们向他们请求欢乐。

column1: “We are pleased to grant it to you,” they said. The room filled with bright light and the sound of distant music, and that night the ale we drank tested better than ale had ever tasted. The people were merry.
column2: “我们很乐意赐予你们。”他们说。房间里充满了明亮的光芒和遥远的音乐声，那晚我们喝的麦芽酒尝起来比以往任何时候都好。人们欢快无比。

column1: “Magic you shall have,” they said, and vanished.
column2: “你们将得到魔法。”他们说，然后消失了。

column1: Ask for wisdom.
column2: 请求智慧。

column1: “Grant us wisdom,” we said.
column2: “请赐予我们智慧。”我们说。

column1: “Wisdom you shall have,” said our ancestors, who then vanished.
column2: “你们将得到智慧。”我们的祖先说，然后消失了。

column1: They were affronted. “We are your ancestors, yet our gifts are not good enough for you?” They vanished, and the people were disheartened.
column2: 他们被冒犯了。“我们是你们的祖先，而我们的礼物对你们来说还不满足吗？”他们消失了，人们沮丧不已。

column1: “Grant luck to the leaders of our war parties.”
column2: “赐予我们战团领袖好运。”

column2: 我们请求他们赐予我们战团领袖好运。

column2: “他们会得到好运。”我们的祖先说，然后消失了。

column1: Luck in battle is more important than anything.
column2: 战斗中的好运比什么都重要。

column2: 战斗中好运很重要，但我想如果你们其余人真的认为我们应该接受不同的恩惠，我们可以接受。

column1: Luck in battle is crucial; we can’t afford to lose more warriors.
column2: 战斗中好运至关重要；我们不能再失去更多战士了。

column1: They don’t really want us to ask for anything; it is a gesture, nothing more.
column2: 他们其实并不想要我们索取任何东西；这只是一个姿态，仅此而已。

column1: It is good to be wise.
column2: 聪明是好事。

column1: We must accept this offer, whichever boon we pick. Otherwise they will be gravely offended.
column2: 我们必须接受这个提议，无论我们选择哪种恩惠。否则他们会非常生气。

column1: Let the people reap the rewards of this most auspicious visitation.
column2: 让人民收获这次最吉祥到访的奖赏。

column1: The people are already happy; this is why we have been granted this visit. Let us take a different boon.
column2: 人民已经很高兴了；这正是我们获得这次访问的原因。让我们接受另一种恩惠。

column1: Let them strengthen our clan magic.
column2: 让他们加强我们的氏族魔法。

column1: We still tell the stories of our valiant ancestors, all the way back to the days when Orlanth made the first tribes, and Vingkot was the first king.
column2: 我们仍在传颂我们英勇祖先的故事，一直追溯到奥兰斯建立最初部落、温科特成为首位国王的时代。

column1: We don’t need any help from our ancestors!
column2: 我们不需要祖先的任何帮助！

column2: \x01@\r说“严重地”。懂了吗？“严重地！”

column1: I told you if you listened to me we’d be so popular that the spirits of our ancestors would come back to thank us.

column1: Battle fortune!
column2: 战斗好运！

column1: The men will quickly waste any advantages we gain in battle; let us gain wisdom instead.

column1: Members of the cult of Elmal, loyal thane and horse friend, approach you with an offer. As part of their homage to their god, they wish to perform a ritual to improve the bloodlines of all of the horses of Dragon Pass. They’re willing to perform this ritual for you. A drunken trickster seems to figure somehow in the ritual, which they insist must be performed in secret in a stead full of your best horses.
column2: 埃尔马尔信仰的成员，忠诚的侍从和马的朋友，向你们提出一个提议。作为他们向神致敬的一部分，他们希望举行一个仪式来改善龙隘所有马匹的血统。他们愿意为你们举行这个仪式。一个喝醉的恶作剧者似乎以某种方式参与了仪式，他们坚持仪式必须在你们最好的马匹所在的农庄秘密进行。

column1: Elmal cultists offered to perform a horse ritual for us.

column1: We accepted their offer.

column1: They seemed displeased for some reason.

column2: 接受他们的提议；给他们回礼。

column2: 我们接受了他们的提议，并给了他们礼物。

column1: “You, we cannot tell,” they said. They then pointed to the trickster who was with them, drunk and wearing a horse costume. “Him, he does not want to know.” Some of them laughed, and the trickster looked nervous.
column2: “你，我们不能告诉，”他们说。然后他们指着和他们一起的恶作剧者，他喝醉了，穿着马戏服。“他，他不想知道。”他们中的一些人笑了，恶作剧者看起来很紧张。

column1: They said it was too bad that we did not wish to honor Elmal.

column1: They gathered up our horses and went into the stead. We heard banging noises and a muffled cry. Finally they came out, thanked us for helping them honor Elmal, and departed.
column2: 他们聚集了我们的马，走进了农庄。我们听到了撞击声和一声闷叫。最后他们出来了，感谢我们帮助他们尊崇埃尔马尔，然后离开了。

column1: Their ritual is a powerful one; we are lucky to get this offer.

column2: 埃尔马尔仪式对马不好。

column1: We can’t afford to gift them today, so let’s owe them a favor.

column1: We can afford a generous reciprocal gift.
column2: 我们能负担得起丰厚的回礼。

column1: This is their holy duty. They’ll be offended if we offer them anything in return.

column1: Ho-hum.

column2: 不要问他们的秘密仪式，免得冒犯他们。

column1: Just as Uralda is the bountiful cow mother, Nevala is the ewe goddess.

column1: Cultists of Uralda, mother of cows, come to you and offer to perform a ritual to honor their goddess. The ritual will make your cows healthier and more fertile. Although they do so to honor Uralda, it is also clear that they want you to offer something in exchange for their ritual services.
column2: 乌拉尔达——奶牛之母——的信徒前来觐见，提议举行仪式以尊崇他们的女神。仪式将使您的奶牛更健康、更多产。虽然他们以此尊崇乌拉尔达，但明显希望您以某种回报交换他们的仪式服务。

column1: Uralda cultists offered to perform a ritual to benefit our herds.

column1: They departed, to the cheers and good wishes of the carls.

column1: If they truly wish to honor Uralda, they should do it for nothing.

column2: 他们期待回报是合理的。

column2: 我们的氏族魔法薄弱；应该改赠牛只。

column2: 这些女魔头是想阉了我们所有人！

column2: 他们似乎在我们决定动手之前就知道我们要攻击他们。他们慌不择路地逃过山丘，我们一个也没抓住。就连他们的孩子也跑得像山羊一样快。

column1: The carls are very upset by this.
column2: 自由民对此非常不满。

column1: The carls are very upset by this, but if we tell them we will clear more land, everything will be fine.
column2: 自由民对此非常不满，但如果我们告诉他们我们会清理更多土地，一切都会好起来。

column1: It is always good to sacrifice to Ernalda.
column2: 向厄娜尔达献祭总是好的。

column1: Ernalda is not a goddess of malign earth, so she can do little to shield us from its effects.
column2: 厄娜尔达并非恶意大地的女神，因此她几乎无法保护我们免受其影响。

column1: Ernalda is not a goddess of malign earth, so she can do little to shield us from its effects; sacrifice to Maran Gor instead.
column2: 厄娜尔达并非恶意大地的女神，因此她几乎无法保护我们免受其影响；改向玛兰·戈尔献祭。

column1: We are not cursed by Maran Gor; this is just bad luck.
column2: 我们并未受玛兰·戈尔诅咒；这只是运气不好。

column1: Sacrifice to Humakt.
column2: 向胡马克特献祭。

column1: Sacrifice to Humakt; we have kept the warriors happy, so he will favor us with good luck.
column2: 向胡马克特献祭；我们一直让战士们满意，因此他会赐予我们好运。

column1: Sacrifice to Orlanth; we have won many victories, so he will favor us with good luck.
column2: 向奥兰斯献祭；我们赢了许多胜利，因此他会赐予我们好运。

column1: Sacrifice to Uralda; we have enlarged our herds, so she will favor us with good luck.
column2: 向乌拉尔达献祭；我们扩大了畜群，因此她会赐予我们好运。

column1: Do not sacrifice to Urox, for we have not stamped out the Chaos around our tula, and he thinks we are weak and foolish.
column2: 不要向乌洛克斯献祭，因为我们尚未扫清领地周围的混沌，他认为我们软弱而愚蠢。

column1: Sacrifice to Urox; we have kept Chaos away from our tula, so he will favor us with good luck.
column2: 向乌洛克斯献祭；我们已将混沌远离领地，因此他会赐予我们好运。

column1: Sacrifice to Chalana Arroy; we have many suffering people, and she will show us mercy.
column2: 向查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭；我们有许多受苦的人，她会向我们施以怜悯。

column1: Watch out for that first step, it’s a bit rough.
column2: 小心第一步，有点难走。

column1: Some earthquakes are sent by Maran Gor, one of the dangerous earth goddesses. Others are simply the result of bad luck.
column2: 有些地震是玛兰·戈尔——一位危险的 earth goddess——所降下的，另一些则纯粹是运气不好。

column1: Sacrifice to Lhankor Mhy; we love knowledge, so he will favor us with good luck.
column2: 向兰科·米献祭；我们热爱知识，因此他会赐予我们好运。

column1: Mother of earthshakers yearns for furrow-snack. Ring-breaking will send her embrace elsewhere.
column2: 地动者之母渴望犁沟点心。破戒将把她的拥抱送往别处。

column1: Devotees of the cult of Yinkin, the god of alynxes, appear before you soliciting your help.
column2: 银金——艾林克斯猫之神——的信徒出现在你们面前，请求你们的帮助。

column1: They remind you that you owe a favor to the cult of Yinkin, and that they expect you to honor it now.
column2: 他们提醒你们，你们欠银金教派一份恩惠，并期望你们现在履行承诺。

column1: What gifts do you offer them first?
column2: 你们首先献上什么礼物？

column1: They said that we were crazy, that dogs were better than alynxes, and that they were looking forward to gutting the stupid Yinkin people when they came.
column2: 他们说我们疯了，说狗比艾林克斯猫强，还说他们正期待着那些愚蠢的银金子民来时把他们开膛破肚。

column1: Give them gifts, so they can hire mercenaries.
column2: 给他们礼物，这样他们就能雇佣雇佣兵。

column1: We gave them gifts, so they could hire mercenaries.
column2: 我们给了他们礼物，这样他们就能雇佣雇佣兵。

column1: They seemed unhappy with what we gave them.
column2: 他们似乎对我们给的东西不满意。

column1: They thanked us and departed.
column2: 他们感谢我们后离开了。

column1: They thanked us for our help against the stinking dog-breeders.
column2: 他们感谢我们帮助他们对抗那些臭烘烘的养狗人。

column1: They said we would regret reneging on the favor we owed them.
column2: 他们说我们会后悔食言，辜负欠他们的那份恩惠。

column1: They departed, disappointed.
column2: 他们失望地离开了。

column1: Sacrifice to Yinkin on their behalf.
column2: 替他们向银金献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to Yinkin on their behalf.
column2: 我们替他们向银金献祭。

column1: The god-talkers said that Yinkin had received our sacrifice. The alynx god’s cultists were well pleased.
column2: 神言者说银金已接收了我们的献祭。艾林克斯猫之神的信徒们非常满意。

column1: The god-talkers could not say for sure that Yinkin had received our sacrifice. The alynx god’s cultists thanked us for trying.
column2: 神言者无法确定银金是否接收了我们的献祭。艾林克斯猫之神的信徒们感谢我们的尝试。

column1: warriors shared in the spoils.
column2: 战士们分享了战利品。

column1: Our warrior attacked the \x01@! dog breeders alongside the Yinkini, but they were driven off.
column2: 我们的战士与英金信徒一同攻击了 \x01@! 养狗人，但被击退了。

column1: Our fighter was slain, and many of the Yinkini were wounded.
column2: 我们的战士被杀，许多英金信徒受伤。

column1: We attacked the \x01@! dog breeders alongside the Yinkini, but were driven off.
column2: 我们与英金信徒一同攻击了 \x01@! 养狗人，但被击退了。

column1: One of our fighters was slain, and the other was wounded.
column2: 我们一名战士被杀，另一名受伤。

column1: One of our fighters was slain, and others were wounded.
column2: 我们一名战士被杀，其他人受伤。

column1: There are no dogs in Dragon Pass — or, at least, there shouldn’t be!
column2: 龙之隘口没有狗——或者说，至少不应该有！

column1: We can’t afford to give them cows.
column2: 我们给不起他们牛只。

column1: Dogs in Dragon Pass? It is an outrage! Give them cows!
column2: 龙之隘口有狗？真是岂有此理！给他们牛只！

column1: We don’t have goods to give them.
column2: 我们没有货物给他们。

column1: We have plenty of trade goods to give them.
column2: 我们有充足的贸易货物可以给他们。

column1: Our warriors are itching for a fight.
column2: 我们的战士们手痒想打架。

column1: Our warriors are not looking for a fight now.
column2: 我们的战士们现在不想打架。

column1: We can spare warriors for this mission.
column2: 我们可以派出战士执行这次任务。

column1: We can’t spare a single warrior for this mission.
column2: 我们连一名战士也派不出来执行这次任务。

column1: We owe them a favor, and so are obligated to help.
column2: 我们欠他们一份恩惠，因此有义务帮忙。

column1: We owe them no favors, and are not obligated to help.
column2: 我们不欠他们恩惠，也没有义务帮忙。

column1: Curs! They must pay!
column2: 恶犬！它们必须付出代价！

column1: A \x02\x03solid thumping/good thrashing/little stead-burning\x02 should teach those \x02\x03foul/stinking/fiendish\x02 rogues!
column2: 一场 \x02\x03结实的痛打/好好教训一顿/烧掉小牧场\x02 应该能教训那些 \x02\x03肮脏的/恶臭的/凶恶的\x02 恶棍！

column1: If we wished, we could try to talk with them. But our enemies are unlikely to listen.
column2: 若我们愿意，可以试着和他们谈谈。但我们的敌人不太可能听进去。

column1: Sacrifice to Yinkin.
column2: 向银金献祭。

column1: Our clan magic is strong. A sacrifice to Yinkin will help.
column2: 我们的氏族魔法很强大。向银金献祭会有所帮助。

column1: Our clan magic is weak. A sacrifice to Yinkin will do little good.
column2: 我们的氏族魔法很弱小。向银金献祭几乎没什么好处。

column1: Yinkin, one of Orlanth’s brothers, was hurt in the Gods War when the Bad Dogs attacked him and stole his fiery breath.
column2: 银金，奥兰斯的一个兄弟，在神战中被恶犬族攻击并偷走了他的火焰吐息而受伤。

column1: The enmity between alynxes and dogs is as old as the hatred between \x02\x03trolls and humans/elves and farmers/Orlanth and Yelm\x02.
column2: 山猫与犬之间的敌意，正如 \x02\x03巨魔与人类/精灵与农夫/奥兰斯与耶尔姆\x02之间的仇恨一样古老。

column1: We should have a shrine to Yinkin in our tula.
column2: 我们的领地应该有座银金的神殿。

column1: I once read a scroll which said that Yinkin represents the secret perceptions of Orlanth the King.
column2: 我曾读过一卷书卷，上面说银金代表着奥兰斯王的隐秘感知。

column1: I wonder where they got the dogs?
column2: 我好奇他们是从哪里弄来这些狗的？

column1: Do they \x02\x04hide the puppies under their cloaks/disguise the smaller dogs to look like their children/let a dog sit on the ring/harness the dogs to plow their fields\x02?
column2: 他们 \x02\x04把小狗藏在斗篷下/把体型小的狗伪装成自己的孩子/让一条狗坐在长老会里/给狗套上犁去耕田\x02吗？

column1: Devotees of the cult of Yinkin, the god of alynxes, have an offer to make to you. “We have noticed that the woods around your tula are infested with many types of rodents, including a type which is very susceptible to spirits of disease. If you want to give us something in return, we can perform a ritual which will improve the hunting abilities of your alynxes. They will kill these forest-dwelling rats, freeing you from the risk of disease.”
column2: 银金信徒——山猫之神——向您提出一个提议。“我们注意到你们领地周围的森林里充斥着多种啮齿动物，其中一种极易感染疾病之灵。如果你们愿意给予我们一些回报，我们可以举行一场仪式，提升你们山猫的狩猎能力。它们会杀死这些栖居林中的老鼠，让你们摆脱疾病的风险。”

column1: Yinkin cultists offered to perform a ritual which would make better hunters out of our alynxes. They would be better able to kill disease-bearing forest rats, or so the Yinkini said.
column2: 银金信徒提议举行一场仪式，使我们的山猫成为更出色的猎人。它们将能更好地杀死携带疾病的林鼠——至少银金信徒们是这么说的。

column1: They thanked us, in Yinkin’s name, and said their god’s children would have good hunting thanks to our gift.
column2: 他们以银金的名义感谢我们，并说，得益于我们的赠礼，他们神的子嗣将享有丰盛的猎获。

column1: They gathered our alynxes together in a stead. It was remarkable to see these willful creatures following the Yinkin cultists as if they had become sheep! We heard wails and howls coming from the stead, and could not tell which were made by people and which by cats. Finally the Yinkin people emerged, and said that the ritual was a success.
column2: 他们将我们的山猫聚集在一个牧场里。看到这些任性的生灵跟随银金信徒，仿佛变成了绵羊，真是不可思议！我们听到从牧场传来哀嚎和咆哮，分不清哪些是人发出的，哪些是猫发出的。最后银金信徒们走了出来，说仪式成功了。

column1: They gathered our alynxes together, and successfully performed their Yinkin ritual.
column2: 他们将我们的山猫聚集起来，并成功举行了他们的银金仪式。

column1: Offer them alynx kittens.
column2: 提供山猫幼崽给他们。

column1: We offered them alynx kittens.
column2: 我们提供了山猫幼崽给他们。

column1: They were honored, and inspected the kittens carefully. The leader’s brow furrowed, and sadness washed over his face. “I’m very sorry,” he said, “but these are descendants of \x02\x02Black Havoc/Doubleshadow the Worthless\x02. You’d be best to simply let them loose outside your tula. Yinkin would not honor such a gift.”
column2: 他们感到荣幸，并仔细检查了幼崽。领头的眉头紧锁，悲伤涌上脸庞。“非常抱歉，”他说，“但这些是 \x02\x02黑浩劫/无价双影\x02的后代。你们最好就是把它们放生在领地之外。银金不会认可这样的赠礼。”

column1: They were honored, and inspected the kittens carefully. A tear fell from the leader’s eye. “These creatures are too beautiful to take from you. We will perform the ritual, and will return the kittens to you as a token of our esteem.”
column2: 他们感到荣幸，并仔细检查了幼崽。一滴泪水从领头眼角滑落。“这些生灵太美了，我们不忍心从你们身边带走。我们会举行仪式，然后把这些幼崽归还给你们，作为我们敬意的象征。”

column1: They then gathered our alynxes together in a stead. It was remarkable to see these willful creatures following the Yinkin cultists as if they had become sheep! We heard wails and howls coming from the stead, and could not tell which were made by people and which by cats. Finally the Yinkin people emerged, and said that the ritual was a success.
column2: 然后他们将我们的山猫聚集在一个牧场里。看到这些任性的生灵跟随银金信徒，仿佛变成了绵羊，真是不可思议！我们听到从牧场传来哀嚎和咆哮，分不清哪些是人发出的，哪些是猫发出的。最后银金信徒们走了出来，说仪式成功了。

column1: Then they gathered our alynxes together, and successfully performed their Yinkin ritual.
column2: 然后他们将我们的山猫聚集起来，并成功举行了他们的银金仪式。

column1: Offer them goods or livestock.
column2: 提供货物或牲畜给他们。

column1: We asked what their price was.
column2: 我们询问了他们的要价。

column1: After talking to them for a while, it becomes apparent that they expect goods worth 10 cows in exchange for this service.
column2: 与他们交谈一阵后，情况明朗：他们期望得到价值10头牛的货物作为这项服务的交换。

column1: It was satisfactory, and we came to an agreement.
column2: 条件令人满意，我们达成了协议。

column1: The least they will accept is \x01@\x13 cows worth of goods. Do you accept?
column2: 他们最低能接受的是价值 \x01@\x13 头牛的货物。你接受吗？

column1: We reached a fairer price, and so they proceeded with the ritual.
column2: 我们谈成了一个更公平的价格，于是他们进行了仪式。

column1: They will not lower their price. Do you pay it anyway?
column2: 他们不愿降价。你还是支付吗？

column1: Refuse their offer.
column2: 拒绝他们的提议。

column1: They said we should not come crying to them when diseased rodents gave our people brain fever.
column2: 他们说，等病鼠让我们的子民得了脑热病时，我们别哭着去找他们。

column1: “We’ll owe you a favor.”
column2: “我们欠你一个人情。”

column1: We said we’d owe them a favor.
column2: 我们说我们欠他们一个人情。

column1: They agreed to this, and gathered our alynxes together in a stead. It was remarkable to see these willful creatures following the Yinkin cultists as if they had become sheep! We heard wails and howls coming from the stead, and could not tell which were made by people and which by cats. Finally the Yinkin people emerged, and said that the ritual was a success.
column2: 他们同意了这一点，然后将我们的山猫聚集在一个牧场里。看到这些任性的生灵跟随银金信徒，仿佛变成了绵羊，真是不可思议！我们听到从牧场传来哀嚎和咆哮，分不清哪些是人发出的，哪些是猫发出的。最后银金信徒们走了出来，说仪式成功了。

column1: Disease isn’t caused by rodents. It’s caused by evil spirits who inhabit our barley fields.
column2: 疾病不是由啮齿动物引起的。而是由栖息在我们大麦田里的邪灵引起的。

column1: The forest is full of terrible rats.
column2: 森林里到处都是可怕的老鼠。

column1: The forest is full of rats, and the dirty creatures are infested by disease spirits.
column2: 森林里到处都是老鼠，这些肮脏的生物染上了疾病精魂。

column1: The forest is full of rats, and the dirty creatures are infested by disease spirits. We have some fine kittens to trade.
column2: 森林里到处都是老鼠，这些肮脏的生物染上了疾病精魂。我们有些上好的小猫可以交易。

column1: The forest is full of rats, and the dirty creatures are infested by disease spirits. We have some fine kittens to trade, which the Yinkin people will greatly esteem.
column2: 森林里到处都是老鼠，这些肮脏的生物染上了疾病精魂。我们有些上好的小猫可以交易，银金子民会非常珍视。

column1: This trade is no different than any other.
column2: 这笔交易与任何其他交易没什么不同。

column1: It is not a good time to be trading things away.
column2: 现在不是做交易的好时机。

column1: We can well afford to pay for this service.
column2: 我们完全付得起这笔服务费用。

column1: Any asking price can be bargained down.
column2: 任何要价都可以讨价还价。

column1: The fewer fighters fall prey to disease, the better chance we’ll have of prevailing during raids.
column2: 染病的战士越少，我们在突袭中获胜的机会就越大。

column1: Dragon Pass is crawling with Yinkin worshippers. It is very foolish to offend them.
column2: 龙隘到处都是银金的崇拜者。冒犯他们非常不明智。

column1: The cult of Yinkin is very small, and has little influence.
column2: 银金教派规模很小，影响力也微乎其微。

column1: Yinkin magic will have us all chasing mice and climbing trees.
column2: 银金魔法会让我们全都去追老鼠、爬树。

column1: Their magic will last for many seasons.
column2: 他们的魔法会持续许多季节。

column1: Although he is a cat, Yinkin is Orlanth’s brother, and son of the mountain goddess Kero Fin.
column2: 银金虽然是猫，却是奥兰斯的兄弟，也是山女神凯罗·芬之子。

column1: Yinkin is one of Orlanth’s most loyal brothers, who provides insight when Orlanth most needs it.
column2: 银金是奥兰斯最忠诚的兄弟之一，在奥兰斯最需要时提供洞察。

column1: Anything that makes the healers’ job easier is good.
column2: 任何能让治疗者工作轻松些的事都是好事。

column1: Alynxes are disloyal; Eurmal was a better companion to Orlanth than Yinkin ever was.
column2: 艾林克斯猫不忠诚；尤尔马尔对奥兰斯而言是比银金更好的伙伴。

column1: We are giving too much of our food away!
column2: 我们把太多食物送出去了！

column1: They will be so honored by a gift of kittens that they will give the little creatures right back to us.
column2: 他们收到小猫礼物会深感荣幸，以至于会把小家伙们直接还给我们。

column1: I told you those rats were causing disease.
column2: 我告诉过你那些老鼠在引发疾病。

column1: We need Humakti to come and offer to perform a ritual to protect us from the undead.
column2: 我们需要呼马特信徒来举行仪式，保护我们免受亡灵侵害。

column1: I like these Yinkin people. They act smooth, but scratch them once and they’ll bite your head off.
column2: 我喜欢这些银金子民。他们看似圆滑，但只要刮他们一下，他们就会咬掉你的脑袋。

column1: The rats must have disease spirits as familiars!
column2: 那些老鼠一定把疾病精魂当作使魔！

column1: sceneR341
column2: sceneR341

column1: An ill-omen vexed us when a girl saw the shadow of a bird pass over her.
column2: 一个不祥之兆困扰着我们：一个女孩看见一只鸟的影子掠过她。

column1: The people waited to see what the omen meant.
column2: 人们等着看这征兆意味着什么。

column1: “This is not a bad omen.”
column2: “这不是个坏兆头。”

column1: The clan ring told the people, “This is not a bad omen.”
column2: 氏族议会告诉人们：“这不是个坏兆头。”

column1: The people were reassured.
column2: 人们放心了。

column1: The people said it was bad to be led by a foolish ring.
column2: 人们说被愚蠢的议会领导是不好的。

column1: “We are strong enough to face any misfortune.”
column2: “我们足够强大，能面对任何不幸。”

column1: The clan ring told the people, “We are strong enough to face any misfortune.”
column2: 氏族议会告诉人们：“我们足够强大，能面对任何不幸。”

column1: The people said that bold words were good, but that they were still afraid.
column2: 人们说豪言壮语很好，但他们仍然害怕。

column1: Send her to a distant clan, where her relatives can raise her.
column2: 把她送到一个遥远的氏族，让她的亲戚抚养她。

column1: Which clan do you send her to?
column2: 你把她送到哪个氏族？

column1: Send her on a pilgrimage to Kero Fin.
column2: 派她去凯罗·芬朝圣。

column1: How many guards do you send to escort her?
column2: 你派多少护卫护送她？

column1: The warriors refused to go with her, saying that ill-fortune doomed the expedition.
column2: 战士们拒绝跟她去，说不幸注定了这次远征会失败。

column1: Send her to live with priestesses in another clan.
column2: 送她去另一个氏族与女祭司同住。

column1: Uralda
column2: 乌拉尔达

column1: Chalana Arroy
column2: 查拉娜·阿罗伊

column1: Nevala
column2: 内瓦拉

column1: Babeester Gor
column2: 巴比斯特·戈尔

column1: Birds are bad because they were sacred to Orlanth’s enemy, Yelm the Emperor.
column2: 鸟类不好，因为它们对奥兰斯的敌人——皇帝耶尔姆来说是神圣的。

column1: If we send her off, we’ll avoid whatever misfortune awaits her.
column2: 如果我们把她送走，就能避免等待她的任何不幸。

column1: We can call on kin, even distant kin, in a case like this.
column2: 在这种情况下，我们可以求助亲属，即使是远亲。

column1: A pilgrimage would dispel any bad fortune this omen brings.
column2: 一次朝圣可以驱散这个征兆带来的任何厄运。

column1: Surround her with magic — send her to priestesses who will know how to disperse this ill luck.
column2: 用魔法环绕她——送她去知道如何驱散这厄运的女祭司那里。

column1: We should let a distant relative take her in. Her fate won’t affect us then, and they will likely escape it, too.
column2: 我们应该让一个远亲收养她。那样她的命运不会影响我们，她们也可能会逃过一劫。

column1: Circling the base of the Holy Mountain is believed to be a cure for all manner of evils.
column2: 绕圣山山脚行走被认为能治愈各种邪恶。

column1: Put her bad fortune in the midst of good magic, which will surround and undo it.
column2: 将她的厄运置于良好的魔法之中，魔法会环绕并消解它。

column1: We should tell the people not to worry.
column2: 我们应该告诉人们不要担心。

column1: It is better to inspire them than to argue what is a bad omen and what is not.
column2: 激励他们比争论什么是坏兆头、什么不是更好。

column1: Once everyone \x02\x03is talking about/is worried about/believes in\x02 an omen, they have a way of coming true. Reassurance is most needed here.
column2: 一旦每个人 \x02\x03都在谈论/担心/相信\x02 一个征兆，它们就有办法成真。这里最需要的是安抚。

column1: \x02\x02What is all this fuss over?/That’s no bad omen.\x02
column2: \x02\x02这大惊小怪是为了什么？/那不是坏兆头。\x02

column1: It is \x02\x03a dreadful/an awful/a very bad\x02 omen.
column2: 这是个 \x02\x03可怕的/糟糕的/非常坏的\x02 兆头。

column1: It is a very \x02\x03unlucky/nasty/bad\x02 omen, and our clan magic is weak. If we do not seek help from the gods, something \x02\x03disastrous/unfortunate/bad\x02 is bound to happen.
column2: 这是个非常 \x02\x03不吉利/恶劣/坏\x02 的兆头，而且我们的氏族魔法很弱。如果我们不向众神寻求帮助， \x02\x03灾难性的/不幸的/糟糕的\x02 事情一定会发生。

column1: We didn’t do anything the last time this happened, we could at least sacrifice for protection this time.
column2: 上次发生这种事我们什么都没做，这次至少可以献祭以求保护。

column1: Maybe something stronger than a sacrifice is called for this time.
column2: 也许这次需要比献祭更强大的手段。

column1: If we just go about our business as if nothing is wrong, we can confound this bad omen.
column2: 如果我们像没事一样继续我们的事务，就能挫败这个坏兆头。

column1: Just let me hunt down this bird, lest it cause consternation every time it flies across our tula.
column2: 就让我去追捕这只鸟吧，免得它每次飞过我们的领地都引起惊惶。

column1: We are doomed! There is nothing we can do!
column2: 我们注定完蛋！我们什么也做不了！

column1: We will be attacked by ghouls!
column2: 我们会遭到食尸鬼攻击！

column1: Elves wait to slaughter us!
column2: 精灵等着屠杀我们！

column1: Hang a horse shoe on the heavy beam above the door, or it might suddenly fall and crush your guests.
column2: 在门上的大梁挂一只马蹄铁，否则它可能会突然掉下来砸伤你的客人。

column1: \x02\x03Spit three times/Put a nail in your shoe/Wear your hat backwards\x02 when starting a trip, so you \x02\x03don’t get lost coming home/can find your way back/confuse the bad spirits, and amuse the good ones\x02.
column2: \x02\x03吐三次唾沫/往鞋里钉钉子/把帽子反着戴\x02 出发时这么做，你就 \x02\x03不会在回家时迷路/能找到回来的路/迷惑恶灵，并取悦善灵\x02。

column1: sceneR342
column2: sceneR342

column1: Our god-talkers were disappointed, as they already knew the myth.
column2: 我们的神言者很失望，因为他们已经知道这则神话。

column1: He told us the story called “\x01@\r.”
column2: 他给我们讲了一个名叫“\x01@\r”的故事。

column1: He told us the story called “\x01@\r,” but it was one we already knew.
column2: 他给我们讲了一个名叫“\x01@\r”的故事，但那个故事我们已经知道了。

column1: Marry her to the winner of a series of contests.
column2: 把她嫁给一系列竞赛的获胜者。

column1: We said that the winner of a series of contests could have her hand.
column2: 我们说，一系列竞赛的获胜者可以赢得她的手。

column1: The people were excited, and others came from miles around to witness the contests. We conducted favorable trade deals, and were given gifts by our neighbors.
column2: 人们兴奋不已，四面八方的人赶来观看竞赛。我们进行了有利的贸易，还收到了邻族的赠礼。

column1: The contests
column2: 竞赛

column1: Refuse them all.
column2: 全部拒绝。

column1: We refused them all.
column2: 我们全部拒绝了。

column1: If we hold contests, people from all around will come to watch. We will receive gifts from other clans.
column2: 如果我们举办竞赛，四面八方的人都会来观看。我们会收到其他氏族的赠礼。

column1: Make them pass tests.
column2: 让他们通过考验。

column1: It is the right of the clan ring to determine marriages.
column2: 氏族环有权决定婚姻。

column1: It is the right of the clan ring to determine marriages. The people will be scandalized if we let her choose.
column2: 氏族环有权决定婚姻。如果我们让她自己选择，人们会感到愤慨。

column1: All marriages are political; we must choose the clan we most want to strengthen ties with.
column2: 所有婚姻都是政治性的；我们必须选择最想加强联系的氏族。

column1: Orlanth had to pass the greatest test of all when wooing Ernalda. He had to overcome his own ignorance and fear.
column2: 奥兰斯在追求厄娜尔达时必须通过最伟大的考验。他必须克服自己的无知与恐惧。

column1: Take the horses!
column2: 收下马匹！

column1: Take the myth!
column2: 接受这则神话！

column1: Make sure one of the tests is an elf-killing test.
column2: 确保其中一项考验是杀精灵测试。

column1: There is no one right answer; each of the suitors has good qualities.
column2: 没有唯一正确的答案；每位求婚者都有优点。

column1: The suitors we turn away will urge their clans to make war on us!
column2: 我们拒绝的求婚者会怂恿他们的氏族向我们开战！

column1: sceneR343
column2: sceneR343

column1: Two handsome young men of the clan are captured by outlaw women! The women ride quickly onto your tula, grab the men, and ride off. Both men are married.
column2: 氏族两名英俊青年被流放女子掳走！女人们快速骑马冲入你的领地，抓住男人后疾驰而去。两名男子均已婚。

column1: Two handsome young men of our clan were kidnapped by outlaw women.
column2: 我们氏族的两个英俊青年被流放女子绑架了。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors said that the men were in no danger, unless we tried to rescue them. They said that this incident would one day result in an awkward gift.
column2: 我们祖先的灵说，除非我们试图救援，否则那些男子并无危险。他们说这件事终有一天会导致一件尴尬的礼物。

column1: Our god-talkers asked the spirits of our ancestors what to do, but the spirits only swirled sand around the temple floor and blew out our candles. No one knew what this meant.
column2: 我们的神言者询问祖先之灵该怎么办，但那些灵只是在神庙地板上卷起沙尘，吹灭了我们的蜡烛。没人知道这意味着什么。

column1: Sacrifice to Orlanth to strengthen your hand against outlaws.
column2: 向奥兰斯献祭，以增强你对抗流放者的力量。

column1: We sacrificed to Orlanth to strengthen our hand against outlaws.
column2: 我们向奥兰斯献祭，以增强我们对抗流放者的力量。

column1: The god-talkers said that the signs were good, and that Orlanth had heard our pleas.
column2: 神言者说征兆良好，奥兰斯已经听到了我们的祈求。

column1: The god-talkers said that the signs were not good, and that Orlanth had probably not heard our pleas.
column2: 神言者说征兆不好，奥兰斯可能没有听到我们的祈求。

column1: Send a war party to rescue the men and kill the outlaws.
column2: 派出战团救援那些男子并杀死流放者。

column1: We sent a war party to rescue the men and kill the outlaws.
column2: 我们派出战团救援那些男子并杀死流放者。

column1: We found the outlaw women and did battle with them and their fellows.
column2: 我们找到了那些流放女子，与她们及其同伙交战。

column1: We slew \x01@\x11 of the outlaws, men and women both. We freed the captured men of our clan, who thanked us for saving them before they were forced to commit acts that Ernalda would have disapproved of.
column2: 我们杀死了 \x01@\x11 个流放者，男女都有。我们解放了被俘的氏族男子，他们感谢我们及时解救，以免被迫做出厄娜尔达所不齿的行为。

column1: The outlaws ambushed our war party, killing some and wounding others. We failed to rescue our captured clansmen.
column2: 流放者伏击了我们的战团，杀死了一些人，打伤了其他人。我们未能解救被俘的同族。

column1: We did not find the outlaw women.
column2: 我们没有找到那些流放女子。

column1: Send a war party to rescue the men.
column2: 派出战团救援那些男子。

column1: We sent a war party to rescue the men.
column2: 我们派出战团救援那些男子。

column1: We found the outlaw women and their fellows, and fought to drive them off.
column2: 我们找到了流放女子及其同伙，并战斗以驱赶他们。

column1: When they saw how strong we were, they fled, leaving behind the captured men of our clan. Our fellows thanked us for saving them before they were forced to commit acts that Ernalda would have disapproved of.
column2: 当他们看到我们如此强大时，便逃跑了，留下了被俘的氏族男子。我们的同胞感谢我们及时解救，以免被迫做出厄娜尔达所不齿的行为。

column1: The outlaws were too strong for us, and we drew back. We failed to rescue our captured fellows.
column2: 流放者对我们来说太强大了，我们撤退了。我们未能解救被俘的同胞。

column1: It’s about time we killed the bandits in our midst!
column2: 是时候除掉我们中间的匪徒了！

column1: We have lost too many warriors of late. We dare not fight them.
column2: 我们最近损失了太多武士。我们不敢与他们交战。

column1: If we fight to drive them off, we risk less, but will get the same result when we succeed.
column2: 如果我们战斗以驱赶他们，风险较小，但成功时结果相同。

column1: The kidnapped men are married. If they dally with these outlaw women, they commit a grave offense!
column2: 被绑架的男子已婚。如果他们与这些流放女子厮混，就犯下了严重罪行！

column1: The outlaws mean to kill our fellows!
column2: 流放者想要杀死我们的同胞！

column1: Banditry in our area is making trade difficult.
column2: 我们地区的匪患使贸易变得困难。

column1: I have heard of these outlaw women. Every now and then they kidnap fine young men and have their way with them!
column2: 我听说过这些流放女子。她们时不时绑架优秀的年轻男子，然后为所欲为！

column1: We must learn the motives of the outlaws before we decide what to do.
column2: 在决定怎么做之前，我们必须了解流放者的动机。

column1: Although it would be good to learn the motives of the outlaws before deciding what to do, our magic is weak. A divination is unlikely to succeed.
column2: 虽然在决定怎么做之前了解流放者的动机是好的，但我们的魔法很弱。占卜不太可能成功。

column1: If we must think about raiding when it’s really time to work the fields, at least ask the gods first.
column2: 如果我们真的该干活时却要考虑突袭，至少先问问神明。

column1: Good King Oskul was born to an outlaw woman who once captured his father.
column2: 贤王奥斯库尔出生于一位曾俘获他父亲的流放女子。

column1: Every good cow has a right to choose a new bull.
column2: 每头好母牛都有权选择一头新公牛。

column1: If they’d taken me, I’d have shown them a trick or two.
column2: 要是他们抓了我，我会给他们露几手。

column1: Do nothing, and they will soon be home. They will be sheepish with their wives, and proud among the men.
column2: 什么都不做，他们很快就会回家。他们在妻子面前会羞怯，在男人中间会自豪。

column1: How dare these hags besmirch the virtue of our young men? They must be slain!
column2: 这些老巫婆怎敢玷污我们年轻人的清白？必须杀了她们！

column1: It is all some kind of trick. These rascals meant to be captured, so they would have an excuse for adultery!
column2: 这完全是某种诡计。这些无赖是故意被俘的，好为通奸找借口！

column1: A divination.
column2: 一次占卜。

column1: Sometimes the best action is no action at all.
column2: 有时最好的行动就是按兵不动。

column1: It is better to drive off a foe than to kill her, for mercy begets mercy.
column2: 击退敌人比杀死她更好，因为仁慈会换来仁慈。

column1: Nothing we can do will help them.
column2: 我们做什么都帮不了他们。

column1: sceneR344
column2: sceneR344

column1: \x02\x03Beresta/Hindanna/Orlena\x02
column2: \x02\x03贝雷斯塔/辛丹娜/奥琳娜\x02

column1: Ask \x01DT why she treats a horse skull like a valuable item.
column2: 询问 \x01DT 为何她把一个马头骨当作贵重物品。

column1: We asked \x01DT, the trader who brought the skull to our clan market, why she regarded it as a valuable item.
column2: 我们询问了 \x01DT——那个将头骨带到我们氏族市场的商人——为何她觉得这是件贵重物品。

column1: “Shamans traded it to me,” she said. “They claimed that it would grant a clan dominion over the ungodly Horse-Spawn.”
column2: “萨满把它卖给了我，”她说，“他们声称这东西能让一个氏族统治那些不敬神的马裔。”

column1: He was sick for a long time, but finally recovered. He rejoiced, considering himself free from the fate he had for so long feared. The people cheered.
column2: 他病了很久，但最终康复了。他欢欣鼓舞，以为自己终于摆脱了长久以来惧怕的命运。人们欢呼起来。

column1: Trade for the skull.
column2: 交易得到那头骨。

column1: We decided to trade for the skull that the trader \x01DT had brought to our clan market.
column2: 我们决定交易得到商人 \x01DT 带到我们氏族市场的那个头骨。

column1: “I will accept any other treasure in its stead,” said \x01DT.
column2: “我愿意用任何其他财宝代替它，” \x01DT说道。

column1: Hmmm…maybe the horse skull is a fetish that could keep our horses healthy.
column2: 嗯……也许这马头骨是个护符，能让我们的马保持健康。

column1: It will not be too hard to find shamans.
column2: 找到萨满应该不难。

column1: Prophecies are nothing but nonsense.
column2: 预言纯粹是胡说八道。

column1: It is pointless to try to prevent something ordained by prophecy.
column2: 试图阻止预言注定之事毫无意义。

column1: Shamans will not be able to help.
column2: 萨满帮不上忙。

column1: Bad King Urgrain would not heed the prophecies which foretold his doom, until he woke up one morning and found them tattooed on the lids of his eyes.
column2: 恶王乌格兰不肯理会预示他厄运的预言，直到有一天早上醒来，发现那些预言被纹在了自己的眼皮上。

column1: The skull may contain powerful magic.
column2: 那头骨可能蕴含强大的魔法。

column1: What strange magic is this? I see the motion rune before me! Do none of the rest of you see it?
column2: 这是什么奇怪的魔法？我看到了运动符文就在眼前！难道你们没人看见吗？

column1: Of course we must have this mysterious skull!
column2: 我们当然要得到这个神秘的头骨！

column1: Give her our best treasure, so that everyone will know our generosity.
column2: 把我们最好的财宝给她，让所有人都知道我们的慷慨。

column1: I have a pile of horse skulls much more frightening than that in the back of my stead!
column2: 我家后院有一堆比那个更吓人的马头骨！

column1: \x01DT is a dupe of the elves.
column2: \x01DT 是精灵的受骗者。

column1: Death comes for everyone.
column2: 死亡终将降临于每个人。

column1: Shamans.
column2: 萨满。

column1: She’s lucky we don’t flog her away from our tula, coming here and hurting one of our best weaponthanes.
column2: 她运气好，我们没把她鞭打出我们的领地——她跑来这里，还伤了我们最好的武器领主之一。

column1: Men are scared of the strangest things.
column2: 男人总对最奇怪的东西感到害怕。

column1: Never trust a female trader. Never.
column2: 永远别信女商人。永远。

column1: Thanes of the enemy people you know as the Horse-Spawn come looking for the warriors of their kind you took in a few seasons ago. In Tradetalk, they say, “Not blame you. They bad people, hurt our laws. We take them back, no blame to you.”
column2: 你称之为马裔的敌对氏族的领主们找上门来，索要几季前你们收留的那些他们族中的战士。他们用贸易语说：“不怪你们。他们是坏人，违反我们的法律。我们带回去，不怪你们。”

column1: Horse-Spawn thanes came seeking the Horse-Spawn warriors we took in a few seasons before.
column2: 马裔领主们前来索要我们几季前收留的那些马裔战士。

column1: Even those few Horse-Spawn proved to be ferocious enemies. They fought with fiery arrows and lances. Their peculiar horses leapt through our tula like giant grasshoppers, falling among us where we least expected them. Although they were mighty foes, we slew horses and riders alike. We measured the cost of this victory in blood; some were slain and many were wounded. We took jewels from the corpses of our enemies, and added them to our store of goods.
column2: 就连那几名马裔也证明是凶残的敌人。他们用火矢和长矛战斗。他们怪异的马匹像巨型蚱蜢一样跃过我们的领地，落在我们最意想不到的地方。尽管他们是强敌，我们仍人畜皆杀。我们用鲜血衡量这场胜利的代价：有人阵亡，多人受伤。我们从敌人的尸体上取下珠宝，添入我们的库存。

column1: Even those few horse-riders proved to be ferocious enemies. They fought with fiery arrows and lances. Their peculiar horses leapt through our tula like giant grasshoppers, falling among us where we least expected them. Many of our warriors were slain or wounded. The Horse-Spawn snatched up some of our leaders, taking \x01@\x01, \x01@\x02, and \x01@\x03 away with them.
column2: 就连那几名骑手也证明是凶残的敌人。他们用火矢和长矛战斗。他们怪异的马匹像巨型蚱蜢一样跃过我们的领地，落在我们最意想不到的地方。我们许多战士阵亡或受伤。马裔掳走了我们几位首领，把 \x01@\x01、 \x01@\x02和 \x01@\x03 带走了。

column1: Deny that the warriors are present.
column2: 否认那些战士在此。

column1: “They are not here,” we said.
column2: “他们不在这里，”我们说道。

column1: They believed us, and departed.
column2: 他们相信了我们，便离开了。

column1: “You lie!” they cried. “We know they are here.”
column2: “你们撒谎！”他们喊道，“我们知道他们在这里。”

column1: Hand over the warriors.
column2: 交出那些战士。

column1: We handed over the warriors. They struggled desperately, and we had to overpower them in order to deliver them to the Horse-Spawn thanes.
column2: 我们交出了那些战士。他们拼命挣扎，我们不得不制服他们，才能把他们交给马裔领主们。

column1: The warriors struggled desperately, and we had to overpower them in order to deliver them to the Horse-Spawn thanes.
column2: 那些战士拼命挣扎，我们不得不制服他们，才能把他们交给马裔领主们。

column1: The Horse-Spawn thanes took their prisoners away. Our weaponthanes were unhappy; they said that the warriors were our friends, and that we had betrayed them to ferocious enemies.
column2: 马裔领主们带走了俘虏。我们的武器领主们很不高兴；他们说那些战士是我们的朋友，而我们却把他们出卖给了凶残的敌人。

column1: Offer gifts to the Horse-Spawn thanes, so they will stop pursuing the warriors.
column2: 向马裔领主们送礼，好让他们停止追捕那些战士。

column1: We offered gifts to the Horse-Spawn thanes, so they would stop pursuing the warriors.
column2: 我们向马裔领主们送礼，好让他们停止追捕那些战士。

column1: They were offended by our offer. “Cattle is for thralls!” they snarled.
column2: 我们的提议触怒了他们。“牲口是给奴隶的！”他们咆哮道。

column1: They were offended by our offer. “You not know crimes they commit — much bigger crimes than amount you want to pay!”
column2: 我们的提议触怒了他们。“你们不知道他们犯下的罪行——比你们想付的数目大得多！”

column1: The Horse-Spawn thanes agreed to take the gifts and leave the warriors alone. They departed, satisfied. The warriors were so moved by our generosity and skillful bargaining that they asked to be initiated as Orlanthi. Soon, they were no longer strangers among us, but were full, proud members of our clan.
column2: 马裔领主们同意收下礼物，放过这些武士。他们满意地离开了。武士们被我们的慷慨和娴熟的议价深深打动，请求被接纳为奥兰斯人。很快，他们不再是我们中的陌生人，而是我们氏族正式而自豪的成员。

column1: Refuse to hand over the warriors.
column2: 拒绝交出武士。

column1: “We will not give them to you,” we said.
column2: “我们不会把他们交给你们，”我们说道。

column1: They said we would regret our choice, and departed. Our Horse-Spawn friends then stepped forward, and said they would be leaving, too. “Cannot endanger storm people, for storm people good to us.” They said they would make sure that others reported their movements, so that their people would not come here looking for them again.
column2: 他们说我们会后悔自己的选择，然后离开了。我们的马裔朋友们随后走上前来，说他们也要走了。“不能危及风暴之民，风暴之民对我们好。”他们说他们会确保其他人报告他们的行踪，这样他们的人就不会再来这里找他们了。

column1: Horse-Spawn steeds are known for their deadly, magical powers.
column2: 马裔战马以其致命的魔力而闻名。

column1: Offering gifts will just make things worse.
column2: 赠送礼物只会让事情更糟。

column1: Even weird foreigners like to receive gifts.
column2: 就连怪异的异乡人也喜欢收礼物。

column1: They do not value cows as we do; we should offer goods instead.
column2: 他们不像我们这样看重牛只；我们应该改用货物。

column1: They do not value cows as we do; we should offer goods instead. Give them at least ten cows’ worth.
column2: 他们不像我们这样看重牛只；我们应该改用货物。给他们至少相当于十头牛的价值。

column1: They do not value cows as we do; we should offer goods instead. Give them at least five cows’ worth.
column2: 他们不像我们这样看重牛只；我们应该改用货物。给他们至少相当于五头牛的价值。

column1: There are only a few of them. This will be an easy fight.
column2: 他们只有几个人。这将是一场轻松的战斗。

column1: We should attack them, of course.
column2: 我们当然应该攻击他们。

column1: The Horse-Spawn are among our deadliest foes. Even a few of them can be extremely dangerous.
column2: 马裔是我们最致命的敌人之一。即使只有几个也可能极其危险。

column1: We gave the warriors hospitality, and now owe them at least some degree of protection.
column2: 我们给予了武士们好客之礼，现在至少欠他们一定程度的保护。

column1: We gave the warriors hospitality, and now owe them at least some degree of protection. We don’t have to fight for them, but we shouldn’t betray them, either.
column2: 我们给予了武士们好客之礼，现在至少欠他们一定程度的保护。我们不必为他们而战，但我们也不该背叛他们。

column1: The Horse-Spawn warriors we took in are not entitled to the same privileges we would grant our own people. We are not obliged to protect them.
column2: 我们接纳的马裔武士无权享受我们给予自己人的同等特权。我们没有义务保护他们。

column1: Our weaponthanes have learned to respect the visiting Horse-Spawn warriors. They would be upset if we turned them over to their enemies.
column2: 我们的武器领主们已经学会尊重来访的马裔武士。如果我们把他们交给他们的敌人，他们会感到不安。

column1: If you can’t lie to Horse-Spawn, who can you lie to?
column2: 如果你不能对马裔撒谎，还能对谁撒谎？

column1: While we have sheltered them, the foreign warriors have proven themselves honorable.
column2: 尽管我们庇护了他们，这些异乡武士证明了自己是光荣的。

column1: The warriors are doomed, no matter what happens. We might as well avoid harm ourselves.
column2: 无论发生什么，这些武士都难逃一死。我们不如自己避免伤害。

column1: The thing — the thing is — there’s a solution here, that makes both — then again, I suppose there isn’t, really.
column2: 事情——问题是——这里有一个解决办法，能让双方——不过话说回来，我想其实并没有。

column1: The crime they have committed is surely nothing more serious than flouting the wishes of the Horse-Spawn tyrant. We must fight to protect their rights!
column2: 他们犯下的罪行肯定不过是藐视马裔暴君的意愿罢了。我们必须为保护他们的权利而战！

column1: It would be a shame to lose two good warriors, but it would be more of a shame to lose goods or cows.
column2: 损失两名优秀的武士固然可惜，但损失货物或牛只更可惜。

column1: We don’t know which of the many Horse-Spawn clans are involved here. We must be careful, and just.
column2: 我们不知道众多马裔部族中有哪一个牵涉其中。我们必须小心，公正行事。

column1: There must be a way to solve this without anyone getting hurt.
column2: 一定有不伤害任何人就能解决此事的办法。

column1: Humakti warriors come to warn you that you have earned their wrath. “Many times have you offended us. We who sever our ties to our kin in order to serve the Death Lord are honorable and patient. But you have exhausted that patience, and to suffer your insults any further would bring dishonor upon us. How do you intend to rectify this intolerable situation?”
column2: 胡马克特武士前来警告你们，你们已招致他们的愤怒。“你们多次冒犯我们。我们为了侍奉死亡领主而斩断与亲族的联系，我们光荣且有耐心。但你们已经耗尽了那份耐心，继续忍受你们的侮辱会给我们带来耻辱。你们打算如何纠正这不可容忍的局面？”

column1: Humakti warriors accused us of dishonoring them.
column2: 胡马克特武士指责我们侮辱了他们。

column1: Challenge their leader to a duel.
column2: 挑战他们的首领进行决斗。

column1: We said the dispute should be settled with a duel.
column2: 我们说争端应通过决斗解决。

column1: Who do you choose to fight for you?
column2: 你选择谁为你而战？

column1: \x01@\x05 and their leader, \x01@\x08 circled one another warily. They feinted at one another. Then \x01@\x05 lunged into \x01@\x08’s blind side, and blooded his arm. The duel was counted as a victory for our clan, and the Humakti withdrew their complaint against us.
column2: \x01@\x05 他们和他们的首领， \x01@\x08 警惕地互相盘旋。他们彼此佯攻。然后 \x01@\x05 猛扑向 \x01@\x08的盲侧，刺伤了他的手臂。这场决斗被视为我们氏族的胜利，胡马克特人撤回了对我们的指控。

column1: \x01@\x05 and their leader, \x01@\x08 circled one another warily. They feinted at one another. Then \x01@\x08 howled a war cry and charged \x01@\x05, smashing the weapon from \x04 grip. \x01@\x08’s sword carved a deep wound below \x01@\x05’s throat. Having exacted blood punishment, the Humakti said that we had paid our debt of honor, and departed.
column2: \x01@\x05 他们和他们的首领， \x01@\x08 警惕地互相盘旋。他们彼此佯攻。然后 \x01@\x08 发出战吼，冲向 \x01@\x05，打飞了 \x04 手中的武器。 \x01@\x08的剑在 \x01@\x05喉咙下方划出一道深深的伤口。以血偿血之后，胡马克特人说我们已经还清了荣誉债，然后离开了。

column1: Convince them that you have not dishonored them.
column2: 说服他们你没有侮辱他们。

column1: We said that we had not dishonored them.
column2: 我们说我们没有侮辱他们。

column1: They admitted that our actions could be seen in several ways, and that we had not meant to offend them. They withdrew their complaint against us, but said that they would be watching us carefully in the seasons to come.
column2: 他们承认我们的行为可以有几种解读，并且我们并非有意冒犯他们。他们撤回了对我们的投诉，但说在接下来的季节里会密切关注我们。

column1: Our efforts to persuade them only offended them further. “We demand satisfaction!” howled their leader, \x01@\x08.
column2: 我们说服他们的努力反而进一步冒犯了他们。“我们要你付出代价！”他们的首领 \x01@\x08吼道。

column1: They said they were satisfied with this token of respect, but would brook no further insults.
column2: 他们说他们对这个表示尊重的表示感到满意，但不会再容忍进一步侮辱。

column1: Offer them nothing.
column2: 什么都不给他们。

column1: We offered them nothing.
column2: 我们什么都不给他们。

column1: They said that we would regret this choice.
column2: 他们说我们会后悔这个选择。

column1: The signs attending our sacrifice were good; we showed the Humakti that their god held us in high esteem. They withdrew their complaint and departed.
column2: 我们献祭的征兆是吉兆；我们向胡马克特人展示了他们的神对我们高度尊崇。他们撤回了投诉并离开了。

column1: The signs attending our sacrifice were ambiguous; we could not prove to the Humakti that their god held us in high esteem.
column2: 我们献祭的征兆模棱两可；我们无法向胡马克提证明，他们的神对我们评价很高。

column1: We can afford to gift them, or to sacrifice to Humakt.
column2: 我们拿得出礼物送给他们，或者向胡马克特献祭。

column1: Tell them we can’t afford to gift them, or their god.
column2: 告诉他们，我们拿不出礼物送给他们或他们的神。

column1: They will be offended by an offer of gifts.
column2: 赠送礼物会冒犯他们。

column1: Any Orlanthi knows that to give someone a gift shows that you honor him.
column2: 任何奥兰提都知道，赠予他人礼物表示你尊敬他。

column1: They will accept even a token gift; the honor of the gesture is more important than the value of the goods.
column2: 即使象征性的礼物，他们也会接受；姿态的敬意比物品价值更重要。

column1: They will accept even a token gift, but the greater the gift, the longer it will be before the Humakti return with further complaints and veiled threats.
column2: 即使象征性的礼物他们也会接受，但礼物越大，胡马克提下次前来抱怨和暗含威胁的时间就越晚。

column1: It is not good to have the grim servants of the Death God angry at us.
column2: 让死亡之神那冷酷的仆从对我们发怒不是好事。

column1: If we offend them, they will one day ambush our explorers.
column2: 如果我们冒犯了他们，总有一天他们会伏击我们的探索者。

column1: Humakt severed his kin ties with Orlanth, so we owe his followers no respect.
column2: 胡马克特断绝了与奥兰斯的亲缘纽带，所以我们不必尊敬他的追随者。

column1: We have not always done what the Humakti wanted, but our offenses against them are not that great.
column2: 我们并非总顺着胡马克提的意思去做，但我们对他们的冒犯并不算严重。

column1: It will be hard to convince them that we never meant to offend them.
column2: 很难让他们相信我们从未有意冒犯他们。

column1: The Humakti prefer to settle disputes on the dueling ground.
column2: 胡马克提更喜欢在决斗场上解决争端。

column1: The Humakti prefer to settle disputes on the dueling ground; this fight need not be to the death.
column2: 胡马克提更喜欢在决斗场上解决争端；这场战斗不必至死方休。

column1: Show them that their god is not displeased with us.
column2: 向他们证明，他们的神对我们并无不满。

column1: Our magic is strong; we can show them that their god is not displeased with us.
column2: 我们的魔法很强；我们可以向他们证明，他们的神对我们并无不满。

column1: Our magic is weak; it will be hard to show that their god is pleased with us.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱；很难证明他们的神对我们满意。

column1: Because Humakt severed his kin ties and only later reconciled with Orlanth, Humakt and his followers are a part of our society, but they are also separate from it.
column2: 因为胡马克特断绝了亲缘纽带，后来又与奥兰斯和解，所以胡马克特及其追随者既是我们社会的一部分，又与之相分离。

column1: A duel will settle things.
column2: 一场决斗就能解决问题。

column1: Humakt is nothing but a sour-faced priss. It is mighty Urox that others should fear!
column2: 胡马克特不过是个苦脸怪人。别人该畏惧的是强大的乌罗克斯！

column1: \x02\x03I guess I shouldn’t have poured honey in their sword-sheaths last time they visited us./I can’t believe they are still upset over the way I…uh…never mind./Urk. Uh, I just remembered — really urgent — must go! Back later!\x02
column2: \x02\x03我想上次他们来访时我不该把蜂蜜倒进他们的剑鞘里。/我简直不敢相信他们还在为我……嗯……别管了的方式生气。/呃。啊，我刚想起来——真有急事——得走了！回头见！\x02

column1: There is no better way to honor a person than to sacrifice to his patron god.
column2: 没有什么比向其主神献祭更能表达对一个人的敬意了。

column1: Rock-faced, the urgers of the movement of points demand their pride-tokens.
column2: 他们厚着脸皮，那些计较荣誉点数的人要求得到他们的荣耀凭证。

column1: We must stop being rude to people. It only leads to trouble.
column2: 我们不能再对人无礼了。那只会招来麻烦。

column1: \x02\x03Tanevra/Dolkarla/Kolakar\x02
column2: \x02\x03塔内芙拉/多尔卡拉/科拉卡\x02

column1: Devotees of Odayla, the hunting god, seek your aid. “Game has been getting scarce of late, and we blame it on the depredations of Gagarth, god of the Wild Hunt, the left-blowing wind, who delights in fighting others of the storm tribe. \x01@\x08, the greatest among us, wishes to enter the realm of the gods to bring back the game that Gagarth has scared away. Our cult is small, and we need the support of others if \x01@\x08 is to succeed.”
column2: 狩猎神奥达拉的信徒向你们求助。“近来猎物日益稀少，我们将其归咎于加加斯——狂猎之神、左吹之风——的掠夺，他乐于与风暴部落的其他成员争斗。 \x01@\x08，我们中最伟大者，希望进入神域，带回被加加斯吓跑的猎物。我们教团很小，需要他人的支持， \x01@\x08 才能成功。”

column1: Devotees of Odayla, the hunting god, sought our support for a quest to the realm of the gods.
column2: 狩猎神奥达拉的信徒曾寻求我们的支持，以进行一趟进入神域的探索。

column1: Lend them a treasure.
column2: 借给他们一件宝物。

column1: We chose to lend them a treasure.
column2: 我们决定借给他们一件宝物。

column1: They were pleased to receive it, and said that \x01@\x08 would make use of it in the realm of the gods.
column2: 他们很高兴收到它，并表示 \x01@\x08 会在神域中善加利用。

column1: Not long after, we heard what had happened at the ritual.
column2: 不久之后，我们听说了仪式上发生的事情。

column1: \x01@\x08 entered the realm of the gods and did not come back; the treasure we lent her remained in the gods’ realm, too. Everyone at the ceremony knew that she had been swallowed up by Gagarth. Many of the worshippers at the ceremony fell over, dead. People throughout Dragon Pass were afraid of the terrible consequences of a heroquest gone wrong. And sure enough, our own hunters reported that all of the game around our tula had mysteriously vanished.
column2: \x01@\x08 进入了神域，再也没有回来；我们借给她的宝物也留在了神域。仪式上的所有人都知道，她被加加斯吞噬了。许多在场参拜的信众倒地而亡。整个龙之隘口的人都惧怕英雄探索失败带来的可怕后果。果不其然，我们自己的猎人报告说，我们图拉领地周围的所有猎物都神秘消失了。

column1: \x01@\x08 entered the realm of the gods and met Gagarth. She did not defeat him, but won from him an agreement not to vex us, at least for a while. \x01@\x08’s clan returned our treasure to us after the ceremony.
column2: \x01@\x08 进入了神域，遇见了加加斯。她没有击败他，但赢得了他的一份约定，至少暂时不来侵扰我们。 \x01@\x08的氏族在仪式后归还了我们的宝物。

column1: \x01@\x08 entered the realm of the gods and defeated Gagarth. Everyone knew that the hunting would now improve, and that those who had supported the Odaylans would be rewarded in kind. \x01@\x08’s clan returned our treasure to us after the ceremony.
column2: \x01@\x08 进入了神域，击败了加加斯。所有人都知道狩猎将会好转，而那些支持过奥达拉信徒的人将得到相应的回报。 \x01@\x08的氏族在仪式后归还了我们的宝物。

column1: Offer them a share of your clan magic.
column2: 将你们氏族魔法的一部分分给他们。

column1: They thanked us and departed, telling us that we had sacrificed greatly to strike a blow against Gagarth.
column2: 他们向我们致谢后离去，告诉我们说，我们为打击加加斯做出了巨大牺牲。

column1: They thanked us and departed, telling us that we had helped to strike a blow against Gagarth.
column2: 他们向我们致谢后离去，告诉我们说，我们帮助打击了加加斯。

column1: They thanked us briefly and left.
column2: 他们简短地致谢后便离开了。

column1: They accepted the gift silently and left. But we heard rude noises and disgusted words coming from their direction on the trail.
column2: 他们默默收下礼物后离开了。但我们从小路上他们离去的方向听到了粗鲁的噪音和厌恶的话语。

column1: \x01@\x08 entered the realm of the gods and did not come back. Everyone at the ceremony knew that she had been swallowed up by Gagarth. Many of the worshippers at the ceremony fell over, dead. People throughout Dragon Pass were afraid of the terrible consequences of a heroquest gone wrong. And sure enough, our own hunters reported that all of the game around our tula had mysteriously vanished.
column2: \x01@\x08 进入了神域，再未归来。仪式上所有人都知道她被加加斯吞噬了。仪式上许多朝拜者倒地死去。龙隘各处的人们都惧怕英雄任务失败的可怕后果。果然，我们自己的猎人报告说，领地周围的所有猎物都神秘消失了。

column1: \x01@\x08 entered the realm of the gods and met Gagarth. She did not defeat him, but won from him an agreement not to vex us, at least for a while.
column2: \x01@\x08 进入了神域，遇见了加加斯。她并未击败他，但赢得了他的承诺，至少在一段时间内不来侵扰我们。

column1: \x01@\x08 entered the realm of the gods and defeated Gagarth. Everyone knew that the hunting would now improve, and that those who had supported the Odaylans would be rewarded in kind.
column2: \x01@\x08 进入了神域，击败了加加斯。人人都知道狩猎即将好转，那些支持奥达拉信徒的人也将得到相应的回报。

column1: They said that they were disappointed in us. “We thought you were our friends, and wise folk also.”
column2: 他们说对我们很失望。“我们原以为你们是我们的朋友，也是明智之人。”

column1: Sacrifice to Odayla on their behalf.
column2: 代表他们向奥达拉献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to Odayla on their behalf.
column2: 我们代表他们向奥达拉献祭。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were good; Odayla had approved of our sacrifice, and would speed \x01@\x08’s hand in the realm of the gods.
column2: 神言者说征兆很好；奥达拉认可了我们的献祭，并将加快 \x01@\x08在神域的行动。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were hard to read. It could not be said that Odayla had approved of our sacrifice.
column2: 神言者说征兆难以解读。不能说奥达拉认可了我们的献祭。

column1: Send worshippers to the ceremony.
column2: 派遣朝拜者参加仪式。

column1: We chose to send worshippers to the ceremony.
column2: 我们决定派遣朝拜者参加仪式。

column1: How many?
column2: 多少人？

column1: The ritual was held not long after, on the ritual grounds of the \x01@! clan. \x01@\x10 of our people went there to lend their worship.
column2: 仪式不久后举行，在 \x01@! 氏族的仪式场地上。我们族中有 \x01@\x10 人前去献上他们的崇拜。

column1: \x01@\x08 entered the realm of the gods and did not come back. Everyone at the ceremony knew that she had been swallowed up by Gagarth. Many of the worshippers at the ceremony fell over, dead, including \x01@\x18 of our own people. People throughout Dragon Pass were afraid of the terrible consequences of a heroquest gone wrong. And sure enough, our own hunters reported that all of the game around our tula had mysteriously vanished.
column2: \x01@\x08 进入了神域，再未归来。仪式上所有人都知道她被加加斯吞噬了。仪式上许多朝拜者倒地死去，其中包括我们族中的 \x01@\x18 人。龙隘各处的人都惧怕英雄任务失败的可怕后果。果然，我们自己的猎人报告说，领地周围的所有猎物都神秘消失了。

column1: We can afford a sacrifice.

column2: 我们没有义务帮助他们。

column1: This matter has no political consequences.
column2: 此事没有政治后果。

column1: Most of the Odayla worshippers around here are of the \x01@! clan.
column2: 这里大多数奥达拉信徒来自 \x01@! 氏族。

column1: Most of the Odayla worshippers in Dragon Pass are of the \x01@! clan, who are our friends. They will understand if we do not involve ourselves in this dangerous enterprise.
column2: 龙隘大多数奥达拉信徒来自 \x01@! 氏族，他们是我们的朋友。如果我们不参与这项危险的事业，他们会理解的。

column1: There are many ways to help them; we should do so.
column2: 有许多方式可以帮助他们；我们应当这样做。

column1: Our magic is weak; a bungled ritual of sacrifice could lower \x01@\x08’s chances of success.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱；一场笨拙的献祭仪式可能会降低 \x01@\x08成功的几率。

column1: \x01@\x08 is a powerful quester. She deserves our support.
column2: \x01@\x08 是一位强大的探索者。她值得我们的支持。

column1: We must help them.
column2: 我们必须帮助他们。

column1: \x01@\x08 knows the Lady of the Wild but she does not understand Gagarth.
column2: \x01@\x08 认识荒野女士，但她不了解加加斯。

column1: The only thing Gagarth understands is force!
column2: 加加斯唯一理解的就是武力！

column1: Heroquests can be very dangerous for the participants.
column2: 英雄任务对参与者来说可能非常危险。

column1: We should attend the ceremony.
column2: 我们应该参加仪式。

column1: We don’t want to lose our treasure to Gagarth.
column2: 我们不想把宝物丢给加加斯。

column1: Most of these people are from our tribe. We should help them.
column2: 这些人大多来自我们部落。我们应该帮助他们。

column1: I do not know the myth this heroquest recreates. We should learn more of the ancient stories.
column2: 我不知道这个英雄任务重现的神话。我们应该多了解这些古老的故事。

column1: The uneasy peace between the tribes in Dragon Pass is broken again.
column2: 龙隘各部落之间脆弱的和平再次被打破。

column1: Unrest between the tribes has been growing for some time. Border disputes have erupted into fighting. Cattle raids have turned into full-pitched battles. Now it seems that war has broken out.
column2: 部落间的不安已经持续了一段时间。边界争端演变为战斗。偷牛事件变成了全面激战。现在似乎战争已经爆发。

column1: The result of this is that all the tribes are on edge, and even the smallest of disputes between long-time allies threatens to erupt into violence.
column2: 其结果是所有部落都处于紧张状态，就连长期盟友间最微小的争端也威胁会爆发暴力。

column1: The warring tribes are also \x02\x02putting pressure on their neighbors to align one way or the other/threatening their neighbors to join them, or fight them\x02.
column2: 交战的部落还在 \x02\x02向邻邦施压，迫使他们站队/威胁邻邦加入他们，否则就开战\x02。

column1: The result of this is that \x02\x02Dragon Pass is like dry wood, awaiting the spark to set everyone at war with each other/the slightest provocation could set all of Dragon Pass at war with itself\x02.
column2: 其结果是 \x02\x02龙隘如同干柴，只待火花点燃全面混战/最轻微的挑衅就可能使整个龙隘陷入内战\x02。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors say that we will have very little time to decide what we want to do, before we are caught in the crush of tribal war.
column2: 我们祖先之灵说，在陷入部落战争的漩涡之前，我们用来决定行动的时间将非常有限。

column1: Who heads the delegation?
column2: 谁率领使团？

column1: We decided to wait and see what happened.
column2: 我们决定观望事态发展。

column2: 提议在交战部落之间斡旋和平。

column2: 我们曾提议在交战的部落之间斡旋和平。

column2: 谁率领前往……的代表团 \x01Á?

column1: Together, we made plans for the warring monarchs to meet on our tula, atop our sacred hill, to forge a lasting peace.
column2: 我们共同计划，让交战的君主在我们的图拉领地的圣山上会面，以缔造持久的和平。

column1: Sacrifice to Issaries to protect trade.
column2: 向伊萨里斯献祭以保护贸易。

column1: We sacrificed to Issaries to protect trade.
column2: 我们向伊萨里斯献祭以保护贸易。

column1: The god-talkers at first thought that Issaries had not received our sacrifice. But that night \x01@N
column2: 神言者起初认为伊萨里斯没有接受我们的献祭。但当晚 \x01@N

column1: had the same dream as last time, with the Lord High Dragonewt presiding over a marriage between us and the Horse-Spawn, brought about because we made peace.
column2: 做了和上次同样的梦，高等龙新特领主主持了我们与马裔之间的联姻，这因为我们促成了和平而得以实现。

column1: When \x01@N woke up, \x06 saw something glowing. It was the motion rune on that mysterious, ragged banner the tricksters gave us.
column2: 当 \x01@N 醒来时， \x06 看到什么东西在发光。正是恶作剧者给我们的那面神秘破旧旗帜上的运动符文。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were bad. Issaries had not heard our plea, or was powerless to help us.
column2: 神言者说征兆不祥。伊萨里斯没有听到我们的祈求，或者无力帮助我们。

column1: This is not a serious problem.
column2: 这不是一个严重的问题。

column1: We have lost thirty cows worth of goods.
column2: 我们损失了价值三十头牛的货物。

column1: It is bad to lose thirty cows worth of goods, but worse to lose opportunities for future trade.
column2: 损失价值三十头牛的货物很糟糕，但更糟的是失去未来的贸易机会。

column1: It is bad enough to lose goods, but the worst harm is the loss of future trade. Only peace can rebuild those opportunities.
column2: 损失货物已经够糟糕，但最严重的危害是失去未来的贸易。唯有和平才能重建那些机会。

column1: It is bad to lose goods again, but worse is to think that this bickering will disrupt trade for a long time.
column2: 再次损失货物很糟糕，但更糟的是想到这场争吵将长期扰乱贸易。

column1: We must find a way to keep the peace, a way that will last long enough for trade to renew itself, or all our wealth will be lost!
column2: 我们必须找到维持和平的方法，一个足以让贸易自行恢复的持久方法，否则我们所有的财富都将丧失！

column1: It is bad to lose goods again, but worse is to think that Dragon Pass will become home to bandits and stickpickers! The only way to prevent this is to find a way to make a long peace.
column2: 再次损失货物很糟糕，但更糟的是想到龙隘将成为强盗和拾柴人的家园！防止这种情况的唯一办法是找到实现长期和平的方法。

column1: Find a way to make a long, long peace. Otherwise, we stare into the maw of war, which brings disease, hunger, and poverty.
column2: 找到实现长长久久和平的方法。否则，我们便凝视着战争的巨口，它将带来疾病、饥饿和贫困。

column1: Neither king can be blamed.
column2: 两位国王都无可指责。

column1: Each king is equally at fault.
column2: 两位国王同样有错。

column1: Each king is equally at fault, and you can bet that neither will admit it.
column2: 两位国王同样有错，而且你可以肯定谁都不会承认。

column1: Each king is at fault. Neither will admit it. There must be some other way to make them see reason.
column2: 两位国王都有错。谁都不会承认。一定还有其他办法让他们明白道理。

column1: It will not matter who was at fault if Dragon Pass is plunged into war. We must put ourselves right into the middle of this knot and untie it once and for all.
column2: 如果龙隘陷入战争，谁有错就无关紧要了。我们必须置身于这个结的正中央，一劳永逸地解开它。

column1: To make war is the right of kings.
column2: 发动战争是国王的权利。

column1: We should do something, I suppose.
column2: 我想，我们应该采取些行动。

column1: The \x01Á are likelier to give us a fair hearing.
column2: \x01Á 更有可能给我们一个公平的听证机会。

column1: If we can end this war, we will be renowned throughout Dragon Pass as able politicians.
column2: 如果我们能结束这场战争，我们将作为能干的政客名扬龙隘。

column1: If we can find a way out of this endless tribal warfare, we will be renowned throughout Dragon Pass as gifted politicians.
column2: 如果我们能找到摆脱这场无尽部落战争的方法，我们将作为天才的政治家名扬龙隘。

column1: Something tells me that this is more than just a petty trade fight. If we can end this war, we will be renowned throughout history.
column2: 我隐约觉得这不仅仅是一场琐碎的贸易冲突。如果我们能结束这场战争，我们将名垂青史。

column1: This is more than another petty trade disagreement. Ending this war could make us renowned for many generations to come.
column2: 这不仅仅是又一次琐碎的贸易分歧。结束这场战争可以让我们名扬后世数代。

column1: Oddly enough, I have not heard that the Horse-Spawn are taking advantage of these upheavals. Maybe their new ruler has a hand in that.
column2: 奇怪的是，我没有听说马裔在利用这些动乱。也许是他们的新统治者在这事上插了一手。

column1: Issaries may help us, better if we are willing to help him help us.
column2: 伊萨里斯可能会帮助我们，如果我们愿意帮他帮我们的话就更好了。

column1: Do not ask gods to do what men should undertake themselves.
column2: 不要请求神明去做人类自己应该承担的事。

column1: Asking the gods to bless and strengthen our cause will help us make peace.
column2: 祈求神明祝福并增强我们的事业，将有助于我们实现和平。

column1: King Heort said, “Make war when you must. Make peace when you can.”
column2: 赫奥特王说：“必须时征战，可行时媾和。”

column1: King Heort said, “Make peace when you can. Try to make peace as often as you can.”
column2: 赫奥特王说：“可行时媾和。尽可能经常地尝试媾和。”

column1: The last time something like this happened, there was a prophetic dream. We must follow the dream’s advice and make peace.
column2: 上次发生类似事件时，有一个预言之梦。我们必须遵循梦的指引，实现和平。

column1: I can’t say why, but my scalp tingles with some kind of strange anticipation.
column2: 我说不清为什么，但我的头皮因某种奇异的期待而刺痛。

column1: My \x02\x02heart aches/bones sing\x02 with certainty — this is truly a test the gods are giving us, to see if we are worthy of glory.
column2: 我的 \x02\x02心在痛/骨头在歌唱\x02 ——确凿无疑——这确实是神赐予我们的考验，看看我们是否配得上荣耀。

column1: We must broker a peace, and win renown for generations to come! And we must do it soon, or lose our very lives in the conflagration that is coming.
column2: 我们必须斡旋和平，为后世赢得声誉！而且我们必须尽快行动，否则将在即将到来的烈火中丧失生命。

column1: Kings are nothing but trouble.
column2: 国王们尽是麻烦。

column1: This will lead to greatness, if we make peace.
column2: 如果我们实现和平，这将带来伟大。

column1: This will lead to greatness, if we can but make peace.
column2: 如果我们能够实现和平，这将带来伟大。

column1: If war is the destiny of Dragon Pass, our clan won’t be remembered.
column2: 如果战争是龙隘的宿命，我们的氏族将不会被铭记。

column1: We should join one of them in making war on the other.
column2: 我们应该加入其中一方，对另一方作战。

column1: If we would just join one and crush the other, that would make peace.
column2: 如果我们加入一方并击垮另一方，那就会带来和平。

column1: Will this affect our beer supply?
column2: 这会影响我们的啤酒供应吗？

column1: We must fix this — I can’t imagine not having enough barley for beer, or wheat for my favorite cakes!
column2: 我们必须解决这个问题——我无法想象没有足够的大麦酿啤酒，或是没有小麦做我最爱的糕点！

column1: The Orlanthi don’t need dragons to kill the people of Dragon Pass this time — we’re ready to do it to ourselves.
column2: 奥兰提人这次不需要龙来杀死龙隘的人民——我们自己已经准备好自相残杀了。

column1: Warring tribes are like warring clans, only larger and more troublesome to more people.
column2: 交战中的部落就像交战中的氏族，只是规模更大，对更多人造成麻烦。

column1: Belonging to a tribe stops some of the clan fights. What is large enough to put an end to this tribal war?
column2: 归属一个部落能制止一些氏族争斗。什么东西大到足以终结这场部落战争？

column1: First, get them to agree on peace. Then, find something large enough to draw their time and energy away from warfare.
column2: 首先，让他们同意和谈。然后，找一件足够大的事，把他们的时间和精力从战争上引开。

column1: sceneR349
column2: sceneR349

column1: and maintain the respect of others.
column2: 并维护他人的尊重。

column1: and prevent the tribal warfare that threatens to engulf Dragon Pass.
column2: 并阻止威胁要吞没龙口的部落战争。

column1: Break off negotiations.
column2: 中断谈判。

column1: We broke off negotiations.
column2: 我们中断了谈判。

column1: Both kings blamed us for wasting their time, and went back to making war.
column2: 两位国王都指责我们浪费了他们的时间，然后回去继续开战了。

column1: “If one of you breaks the peace, our tribe will join your foe and fight you.”
column2: “如果你们中有一方破坏和平，我们的部落就会加入你们的敌人，与你们作战。”

column1: We said to them, “If one of you breaks the peace, our tribe will join your foe and fight you.”
column2: 我们对他们说：“如果你们中有一方破坏和平，我们的部落就会加入你们的敌人，与你们作战。”

column1: “Our lawspeakers will mediate future trade disputes.”
column2: “我们的律法师将为未来的贸易争端进行调解。”

column1: We told them, “Our lawspeakers will mediate future trade disputes.”
column2: 我们告诉他们：“我们的律法师将为未来的贸易争端进行调解。”

column1: “We should all build a town together, so all will prosper.”
column2: “我们应该一起建一座城镇，这样大家都会兴旺。”

column1: We told them, “We should all build a town together, so all will prosper.”
column2: 我们告诉他们：“我们应该一起建一座城镇，这样大家都会兴旺。”

column1: “We will pay to settle future disputes.”
column2: “我们会出钱来解决未来的争端。”

column1: We told them, “We will pay to settle future disputes.”
column2: 我们告诉他们：“我们会出钱来解决未来的争端。”

column1: Don’t go promising anything that costs us cows.
column2: 别随便许什么会让我们破费的承诺。

column1: Our generosity can end this war.
column2: 我们的慷慨可以结束这场战争。

column1: If we offer to pay to settle their disputes, they will both cheat us.
column2: 如果我们提出出钱解决他们的争端，他们俩都会欺骗我们。

column1: We should build a town. A town will make wealth, and there will be enough for all.
column2: 我们应该建一座城镇。城镇会创造财富，足够所有人享用。

column1: Towns and cities are enemies to Orlanth, who loves freedom.
column2: 城镇和城市是热爱自由的奥兰斯的敌人。

column1: Our lawspeakers are wise. We can mediate future disputes.
column2: 我们的律法师很睿智。我们可以调解未来的争端。

column1: We can volunteer to mediate disputes, but unless we have a way of forcing them to abide by our decisions, the peace will be a fragile one.
column2: 我们可以自愿调解争端，但除非我们有办法迫使他们遵守我们的裁决，否则和平将十分脆弱。

column1: Nobody wants to fight two other tribes at once.
column2: 没有谁想同时与另外两个部落交战。

column1: Neither king wishes to fight two other tribes at once, but do we wish to embroil ourselves in someone else’s war?
column2: 两位国王都不希望同时与另外两个部落交战，但我们愿意卷入别人的战争吗？

column1: Our relations with both tribes are good; we can persuade them.
column2: 我们与两个部落的关系都不错；我们可以说服他们。

column1: Our relations with both tribes are poor; we should work to improve our standing with them, and only then try to end the war.
column2: 我们与两个部落的关系都很糟；我们应该先提升在他们心中的地位，然后再尝试结束战争。

column1: It’s time for a new kind of ring. We should work to build a town.
column2: 是时候建立一种新的联席会议了。我们应该努力建一座城镇。

column1: King Heort said, “Without the sword, there can be no plows.”
column2: 赫奥特国王说：“没有剑，就不会有犁。”

column1: \x02\x03Orlanth dared to try something new./For there to be peace, there must be change./Since the Dragonkill, no one has dared build a true town. Let’s be the first!\x02
column2: \x02\x03奥兰斯敢于尝试新事物。/要有和平，就必须改变。/自从龙戮之后，没人敢建真正的城镇。让我们做第一个！\x02

column1: I know you never listen to me, but this time I mean it: we should make a town.
column2: 我知道你从不听我的，但这次我是认真的：我们应该建一座城镇。

column1: Towns are stupid, unless they have taverns. Then they are stupid, except for the taverns.
column2: 城镇很蠢，除非里面有酒馆。那样的话，除了酒馆，它们还是很蠢。

column1: Peace is overrated.
column2: 和平被高估了。

column1: Let us protect our own tribe, and forget the troubles of others.
column2: 让我们保护自己的部落，别管别人的麻烦。

column1: Some gods like war; others, peace. It is hard to know what to do.
column2: 有些神喜欢战争，有些喜欢和平。很难知道该怎么做。

column1: If we do things properly, this can be one small step towards becoming a tribe among tribes.
column2: 如果我们行事得当，这可以成为迈向众部落之中一个部落的一小步。
