column2: sceneR350

column1: The spirits of our ancestors told us that they had heard whisperings from the realm of the gods. Our little town was destined to grow into a great city, one that would always be remembered in history. The founders of that town were also destined for greatness, if they made the right decisions in the seasons to come. Our next challenge would be to settle a war between men and wolf-men.
column2: 祖先之灵告诉我们，他们听到了来自神域的耳语。我们的小镇注定要长成一座伟大的城市，一座永远载入史册的城市。这座城镇的奠基者们也注定走向伟大——只要他们在未来的季节里做出正确的决定。我们的下一个挑战将是调解人类与狼人之间的战争。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors told us that they had heard whisperings about this town from the realm of the gods, but had not heard enough to say whether the town was a good thing, or the beginning of a centuries-long curse. They said they hoped it was not a curse-bringer.
column2: 祖先之灵告诉我们，他们从神域听说了关于这座城镇的耳语，但还不足以判断这座城镇是好事，还是一段延续数个世纪的诅咒的开端。他们说，他们希望这不是带来诅咒之物。

column1: The other kings \x02\x02made their own observances to the gods/were happy to oversee the plans\x02.
column2: 其他国王 \x02\x02各自向神明献祭了礼仪/很高兴监督这些计划\x02。

column1: Sacrifice the motion rune banner to Issaries.
column2: 将运动符文旗献给伊萨瑞斯。

column1: We decided to sacrifice the motion rune banner to Issaries.
column2: 我们决定将运动符文旗献给伊萨瑞斯。

column1: When our god-talkers threw the banner in the fire, the flame would not eat it. The motion rune on the banner glowed in the color of fire, and everyone said that Issaries had returned the banner as a reciprocal gift. All agreed that this was a very good omen.
column2: 当我们的神言者将旗帜投入火焰时，火焰不肯吞噬它。旗帜上的运动符文闪耀着火焰般的颜色，所有人都说伊萨瑞斯把旗帜作为回礼送了回来。大家一致认为这是个非常吉利的征兆。

column1: Sacrifice to Issaries, god of markets.
column2: 向市场之神伊萨瑞斯献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to Issaries, god of markets.
column2: 我们向市场之神伊萨瑞斯献祭了。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were clear; Issaries smiled on our town.
column2: 神言者们说征兆很明确；伊萨瑞斯对我们的城镇露出了微笑。

column1: The god-talkers said the signs were hard to read. They could not say for sure that Issaries had received our sacrifice.
column2: 神言者们说征兆难以解读。他们无法肯定伊萨瑞斯是否接受了我们的献祭。

column1: See to it that members of your tribe profit from building efforts.
column2: 确保你的部落成员从建造努力中获益。

column1: We decided that members of our tribe should make the best trade arrangements.
column2: 我们决定让部落成员做出最好的贸易安排。

column1: We profited from the deals required to bring building supplies to the town, and gained part of each gift given to a carl who cut a stone or moved a pile of timber. Members of the other tribes complained that we were treating them unfairly; they said the city was meant to make peace for all, not wealth for a few.
column2: 我们从为城镇运送建材的交易中获利，并获得了每位自由民凿石或搬木时所赠礼物的一部分。其他部落的成员抱怨我们待他们不公；他们说这座城市是为了给大家带来和平，而不是给少数人带来财富。

column1: We failed to profit from deals required to bring building supplies to the town. The other tribes were cannier than us, and gained part of each gift given to a carl who cut a stone or moved a pile of timber. Moreover, they blamed us for greedily trying to interfere with the arrangements they had made.
column2: 我们未能从为镇子运送建材所需的交易中获利。其他部族比我们精明，他们从每个给砍石或搬木的卡尔的赠礼中分走了一份。不仅如此，他们还指责我们贪婪地试图干预他们早已安排好的交易。

column1: There will never be any profit in this town; it is folly to build such a thing.
column2: 这个镇子永远不会有任何利润；建造这种东西纯属愚蠢。

column1: The town is our idea. It is only fair that we should get the best share of the profits.
column2: 镇子是我们的主意。我们理应分得最大一份利润。

column1: Trade is about exchange, not about greed. Let us do something to make this new town last.
column2: 贸易在于交换，不在于贪婪。让我们做些事让这个新镇子长久存续。

column1: The other kings are trying to squeeze as much profit from this building enterprise as they can.
column2: 其他国王正试图从这项建设工程中榨取尽可能多的利润。

column1: Although the other kings are trying to squeeze as much profit from this building enterprise as they can, they will blame us if we try to do the same.
column2: 尽管其他国王正试图从这项建设工程中榨取尽可能多的利润，但若我们做同样的事，他们就会指责我们。

column1: We should sacrifice to Issaries, who blesses markets and protects towns.
column2: 我们应该向伊萨里斯献祭，祂祝福市场并保护城镇。

column1: Our magic is weak; divination will do no good, and an ordinary sacrifice will likely be ignored.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱；占卜无济于事，普通的献祭恐怕会被无视。

column1: Our magic is strong; an ordinary sacrifice will suffice.
column2: 我们的魔法很强；一次普通的献祭就足够了。

column1: We should sacrifice the motion rune banner.
column2: 我们应该献祭运动符文旗。

column1: I hope this town will not be a tempting target for the Horse-Spawn.
column2: 我希望这个镇子不会成为马裔的诱人目标。

column1: Knowledge is more important than luck. Ergo, divination is better than sacrifice.
column2: 知识比运气更重要。因此，占卜优于献祭。

column1: The spread of towns will weaken kin ties, which is not always a bad thing.
column2: 城镇的扩散会削弱亲缘纽带，但这不总是坏事。

column1: This land was once dotted with towns and cities, as a field is speckled with wildflowers. Then the dragons came and ate everyone.
column2: 这片土地曾如田野缀满野花般遍布村镇和城市。然后龙来了，吃掉了所有人。

column1: Sacrifice the motion rune banner? That’s mad! It is the magic of the banner that has brought us this far!
column2: 献祭运动符文旗？疯了！正是那面旗帜的魔力让我们走到了今天！

column1: We must fortify the town against the undead.
column2: 我们必须加固镇子以抵御亡灵。

column1: If we let the men run everything, every chance for profit will bleed away in a frenzy of drunken generosity.
column2: 如果我们让男人掌管一切，每一个获利机会都会在狂醉的慷慨中流失。

column1: The dragonewts will be happy to see towns in Dragon Pass again; it will remind them of their great, vanished Empire.
column2: 龙人会很高兴看到龙之隘口再次出现城镇；这会让他们想起伟大而消逝的帝国。

column1: Not long afterwards, the leaders of the three tribes met to choose a name for the new town.
column2: 不久之后，三个部族的首领聚集起来，为新镇子选一个名字。

column1: Pick a new name for the town.
column2: 为镇子选一个新名字。

column1: What do you call it?
column2: 你叫它什么？

column1: Newton
column2: 纽顿

column1: \x01@\x0Bton
column2: \x01@\x0B顿

column1: Everyone agreed to this.
column2: 所有人都同意了。

column1: \x01@\nton
column2: \x01@\nton

column1: \x01@\rton
Use divination to find the town name.
column2: 用占卜来寻找镇名。

column1: \x02\x05Quivinton/Esradan/Lhakton/Ironwall/Kallila\x02
column2: \x02\x05奎文顿/埃斯拉丹/拉克顿/铁壁/卡莉拉\x02

column1: The name should discourage attackers, it should make the town sound strong.
column2: 名字应能震慑攻击者，让镇子听起来很强大。

column1: Don’t ask for my help.
column2: 别找我帮忙。

column1: The name must reflect our leadership in forming the town.
column2: 名字必须体现我们在建镇中的领导地位。

column1: The name must show that this is a new thing, and that it is good.
column2: 名字必须表明这是一件新事物，并且是好事。

column1: We should listen to what all the tribes have to say, so that the name will have everyone’s support.
column2: 我们应该听听所有部族的意见，这样名字才能获得每个人的支持。

column1: The name should be strong, easy to say, and easy to remember.
column2: 名字应该有力、易说、易记。

column1: Towns. What a bore.
column2: 城镇。真无聊。

column1: Many towns are named after their founders — but we have several founders here.
column2: 许多城镇以创立者命名——但我们这里有好几位创立者。

column1: Many towns are named after their founders, but there are other ways of finding a name.
column2: 许多城镇以创立者命名，但也有其他找到名字的方法。

column1: Our magic is weak, a divination will not help us, and may even harm us.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱，占卜帮不了我们，甚至可能伤害我们。

column1: Our magic is strong, we can trust to the gods to find the right name for this town.
column2: 我们的魔法很强，我们可以信赖神明为这个镇子找到正确的名字。

column1: The gods will approve of our asking them what name to use.
column2: 神明会赞同我们询问他们该用何名。

column1: We can write our town name on the gates!
column2: 我们可以把镇名写在城门上！

column1: “A true name rings through the sagas like the clear call of a bell.”
column2: “真名在传说中回响，如同清亮的钟声。”

column1: Bad King Urgrain forced his name upon a town he built. No one remembers where it was, now.
column2: 恶王乌格兰曾强加他的名字给他建造的一个镇子。如今已无人记得它在何处。

column1: Call the town Best \x01@\x0Bton.
column2: 叫它最好 \x01@\x0B顿。

column1: Once again, I must insist that divination is the best way to decide.
column2: 我再次坚持，占卜是决定的最好方式。

column1: Call it Dragontown, and gain the dragonewts’s favor.
column2: 叫它龙镇，以赢得龙人的好感。

column1: I have to admit it, \x01@\x0Bton has a certain ring to it.
column2: 我得承认， \x01@\x0B顿听起来确实有那么点韵味。

column1: sceneR351
column2: sceneR351

column1: Progress on the new town is going well. It should be finished by next season.
column2: 新镇子的建设进展顺利。应该在下个季节前完工。

column1: Progress on the building of our new town continued.
column2: 新镇子的建设继续推进。

column1: The work went smoothly, and everyone admired their own and each other’s handiwork.
column2: 工作进展顺利，每个人都欣赏自己和彼此的手艺。

column1: Hire shamans to attract benign spirits to the town.
column2: 雇佣萨满来吸引善灵进入镇子。

column1: We decided to hire shamans to attract benign spirits to inhabit the town.
column2: 我们决定雇佣萨满来吸引善灵定居镇子。

column1: The shamans proved elusive; we found none to hire.
column2: 萨满们行踪不定；我们没有找到可雇佣的人。

column1: Shamans came and said they would attract benign spirits for the low price of fifteen cows.
column2: 萨满来了，说他们愿意以十五头牛的廉价吸引善灵。

column1: Shamans come and say they will attract benign spirits for the low price of \x01A$ cows.
column2: 萨满来了，说他们愿意以 \x01A$ 头牛的廉价吸引善灵。

column1: They performed many secret ceremonies at night in the heart of the unfinished town, obscured by darkness and smoke. After six days and six nights, they said that the town was now home to many good spirits.
column2: 他们在未完工的镇子中心，于夜色与烟雾的遮掩下举行了许多秘密仪式。六天六夜后，他们说镇子如今已是众多善灵的家园。

column1: The least they will accept is \x01@\x13 cows. Do you agree to pay?
column2: 他们最低接受 \x01@\x13 头牛。你同意支付吗？

column1: We reached a fairer price, and so they proceeded with their program of rituals.
column2: 我们谈到了更公平的价格，于是他们继续进行了他们的仪式计划。

column1: We couldn’t even pay the \x01@\x13 cows they asked, so had to send them on their way.
column2: 我们连他们要的 \x01@\x13 头牛都付不起，只好送他们上路。

column1: They will not lower their price. Do you agree to pay?
column2: 他们不会降价。你同意支付吗？

column1: They would not lower their price, and we could not meet it, so we sent them on their way.
column2: 他们不肯降价，我们也出不起，于是就把他们打发走了。

column1: We decided that members of our tribe should profit from building efforts.
column2: 我们决定让本族成员从建造劳作中获利。

column1: Now that there were many buildings planned, and labor to erect them was scarce, we controlled who did what work, and enriched ourselves thereby. Members of the other tribes complained that we were dishonest, but we said there was no law against the things we did. Such are the ways of cities, we told them.
column2: 如今有许多建筑计划，而建造的劳力稀缺，我们便掌控了谁做什么活，并以此自肥。其他部落的成员抱怨我们不诚实，但我们说，我们做的事情并不犯法。这就是城市的规矩，我们告诉他们。

column1: Now that there were many buildings planned, and labor to erect them was scarce, we found that the other tribes already controlled who did what work, and enriched themselves thereby. When we said we should share in this bounty, they said that the late-hatching chicken has no right to complain that his brothers have eaten the feed.
column2: 如今有许多建筑计划，而建造的劳力稀缺，我们发现其他部落已经掌控了谁做什么活，并以此自肥。当我们说应当分享这笔财富时，他们说，晚出壳的小鸡没有权利抱怨兄弟吃掉了饲料。

column1: Send delegations to Heortland to find craftsmen and artisans to live in the new town.
column2: 派遣使团前往赫奥特兰寻找工匠和手艺人，让他们定居新城。

column1: We sent delegations to Heortland to find craftsmen and artisans to live in the new town.
column2: 我们派遣了使团前往赫奥特兰寻找工匠和手艺人，让他们定居新城。

column1: Our missions found many people eager to come to our new town and help bring about its prosperity. The clans of Dragon Pass celebrated us for finding these people, and for creating opportunity by bringing them here. The artisans themselves gave us fine gifts, so that everyone would know of their skills.
column2: 我们的任务发现许多人渴望来到我们的新城，帮助它繁荣。龙之隘口的氏族称赞我们找到了这些人，并通过带他们前来创造了机会。工匠们自己赠予我们精美的礼物，以便让所有人都知道他们的技艺。

column1: Our missions found that everyone in Heortland was afraid to come to Dragon Pass. The Orlanthi who remained there portrayed us as ignorant savages living in a barren land. When we came back and told this to our fellow settlers in Dragon Pass, they vowed to make the city grander than any in the Holy Country, and show those old Heortlanders who was grand and who was small.
column2: 我们的任务发现赫奥特兰的所有人都害怕前来龙之隘口。留在那里的奥兰斯人将我们描绘成生活在贫瘠土地上的无知野蛮人。当我们回来将此告知龙之隘口的同胞定居者时，他们发誓要让这座城市比圣国的任何一座都更加宏伟，让那些老赫奥特兰人看看谁伟大谁渺小。

column1: Send war parties to clear the area of bandits.
column2: 派遣战团清除该地区的土匪。

column1: We sent war parties to clear the area of bandits.
column2: 我们派遣了战团清除该地区的土匪。

column1: They found no bandits. Some people from the other tribes laughed at us; they said that the area had been free of bandits for a while, and that we were just showing off.
column2: 他们没有找到土匪。其他部落的一些人嘲笑我们；他们说该地区已经有一段时间没有土匪了，我们只是在炫耀。

column1: They found no bandits. Some people from the other tribes laughed at us; they said that the hills around the town were full of bandits, and that anyone who was not a half-wit could have found them.
column2: 他们没有找到土匪。其他部落的一些人嘲笑我们；他们说城镇周围的山丘上满是土匪，任何一个不是半傻子的人都能找到他们。

column1: They found bandits and fought with them.
column2: 他们找到了土匪并与他们交战。

column1: The bandits bested our war parties; some were killed and many were wounded. Our warriors were humiliated by this defeat, and we lost the respect of other clans.
column2: 土匪击败了我们的战团；一些人被杀，许多人受伤。我们的战士因这次失败而蒙羞，我们失去了其他氏族的尊重。

column1: We cut like a scythe through the bandit lairs, killing many and sending the rest fleeing into Horse-Spawn territory. Our warriors were cheered by this victory. Other clans gifted us for our service on behalf of all, and our people were toasted wherever they supped.
column2: 我们如镰刀般扫过土匪巢穴，杀死了许多，余者逃入马裔领地。我们的战士因这场胜利而欢呼。其他氏族为我们的公益之举馈赠厚礼，我们的人民无论在哪里用餐都受到敬酒。

column1: We can’t afford to hire shamans. Those crazy people are always gouging us.
column2: 我们雇不起萨满。那些疯子总是敲诈我们。

column1: We can afford to hire shamans, if need be.
column2: 如果有必要，我们雇得起萨满。

column1: If we bring in a bunch of outsiders, the locals will get angry.
column2: 如果我们招来一群外人，当地人就会生气。

column1: A town is not a town without artisans and craftsmen.
column2: 没有工匠和手艺人的城镇不能算城镇。

column1: The Orlanthi who still live in Heortland have been fed many false rumors about us. It will be hard to recruit artisans.
column2: 仍然生活在赫奥特兰的奥兰斯人听信了许多关于我们的虚假谣言。招募工匠会很困难。

column1: It will be hard to recruit artisans, because Heortlanders have been fed many false rumors about us. People here know this, and will not blame us if we try and fail.
column2: 招募工匠会很困难，因为赫奥特兰人听信了许多关于我们的虚假谣言。这里的人知道这一点，如果我们尝试却失败，他们不会责怪我们。

column1: We must let bandits know they are not welcome here.
column2: 我们必须让土匪知道这里不欢迎他们。

column1: Since there are no bandits hereabouts, it would be foolish to go chasing them.
column2: 既然附近没有土匪，去追捕他们是愚蠢的。

column1: We can easily defeat the bandits around here.
column2: 我们可以轻松击败这一带的土匪。

column1: There are a great many bandits in the area; they will be hard to defeat.
column2: 该地区有大量土匪；他们很难被击败。

column1: The other kings are using this as an opportunity to profit.
column2: 其他国王正在借此机会牟利。

column1: The other kings are already extorting gifts from the laborers, and the thanes who wish to use them. If we try to get our fair share, they will only resent us.
column2: 其他国王已经在向劳工和想雇佣他们的领主勒索礼物。如果我们试图得到应得的一份，他们只会怨恨我们。

column1: Hire shamans to bring good spirits to this town. They will drive out any bad spirits who wish to live here, and bring us luck.
column2: 雇佣萨满为好神灵引路来到此镇。他们将驱走任何想定居此地的恶灵，并为我们带来好运。

column1: I have found certain prophecies which predict great good fortune should our town-building efforts succeed. This is what Saraska should have done.
column2: 我发现了一些预言，预言说如果我们建城努力成功，将带来巨大的好运。这正是萨拉斯卡本该做的。

column1: This town will bring peace, if we let it.
column2: 如果我们允许，这座城镇将带来和平。

column1: If people start to live in towns, it will reduce the control that clans have over marriage.
column2: 如果人们开始居住在城镇中，就会削弱氏族对婚姻的控制。

column1: We must build a great temple to the gods in the middle of the town.
column2: 我们必须在城镇中央建造一座大神殿献给众神。

column1: Are we sure that this town was a good idea?
column2: 我们确定建镇是个好主意吗？

column1: I feel a great poem coming to my lips… well, not so much a poem as a little saying… a trifle, really… Oh, it’s not worth saying.
column2: 我感觉一首伟大的诗即将脱口而出……嗯，倒不如说是一句小谚语……其实只是雕虫小技……哦，不值得一说。

column1: sceneR352
column2: sceneR352

column1: Word reaches you that the \x01@B and \x01@C tribes are fighting a war with the Telmori, the strange and savage folk who are part man, part wolf. Orlanthi losses have been heavy, because the Telmori know the land well, and have magics unfamiliar to the Orlanthi god-talkers.
column2: 消息传到你的耳中： \x01@B 部落和 \x01@C 部落正在与特尔莫里人——那些半人半狼、奇异而野蛮的族群——交战。奥兰斯人损失惨重，因为特尔莫里人熟悉这片土地，还拥有奥兰斯神言者不熟悉的魔法。

column1: Although once hostile to one another, the tribes have united behind a war leader called Hauberk Jon. Under his leadership, the Orlanthi have rallied somewhat, but their cause still seems desperate.
column2: 尽管彼此曾经敌对，但各部族如今已团结在一位名为霍伯克·乔恩的战争领袖身后。在他的领导下，奥兰斯提人虽有所振作，但前路仍显绝望。

column1: We learned that the \x01@B and \x01@C tribes were fighting a losing war with the Telmori.
column2: 我们得知 \x01@B 和 \x01@C 部族正与特尔莫里人进行一场必败之战。

column1: We raided their weakened tulas, which were full of mourners and wounded warriors.
column2: 我们突袭了他们衰弱的图拉领地，那里满是哀悼者和受伤的战士。

column1: They gave us little resistance, and only a few of us were wounded. Fewer still were slain. We drove away large herds, and celebrated our newfound wealth. Others thought us cruel, but our warriors did not care. A victory was a victory.
column2: 他们几乎没有抵抗，我们仅有少数人受伤。阵亡者更少。我们驱走了大群牲畜，庆贺新得的财富。有人指责我们残忍，但我们的战士并不在乎。胜利就是胜利。

column1: Convince your town-making allies to help you fight the Telmori.
column2: 说服你建城的盟友协助你对抗特尔莫里人。

column1: We told the \x01@@ and \x01@A kings that they should help us fight the Telmori.
column2: 我们告诉 \x01@@ 和 \x01@A 国王，他们应该帮助我们对抗特尔莫里人。

column1: “You convinced us to do this before, and we accomplished nothing, unless you count sending our young warriors to early graves,” our partner kings said. “The other tribes must fight their own fight.”
column2: “你们之前就说服我们这么做，结果一无所获，除非把送年轻战士早赴坟墓也算作成就，”我们的盟王说道，“其他部族必须自己打自己的仗。”

column1: We heard later that the \x01@C and \x01@B fought on against the Telmori for some time, with great losses on both sides, until the \x01@A tribe managed to broker a peace between them. Great songs of praise for the \x01@A now fill all the clan halls throughout Dragon Pass.
column2: 后来我们听闻， \x01@C 和 \x01@B 继续与特尔莫里人战斗了一段时间，双方均损失惨重，直到 \x01@A 部族设法促成了和平。如今，龙之隘口所有部族大厅里都传唱着颂扬 \x01@A 的赞美歌。

column1: Tell Hauberk Jon you will make peace with the Telmori if he agrees to build a town.
column2: 告诉霍伯克·乔恩，若他同意建城，你就与特尔莫里人议和。

column2: \x01@\x05 和一群战士前往霍伯克·乔恩已知的最后一处营地。

column1: They hid behind rocks as Telmori warriors passed by.
column2: 他们躲在岩石后，看着特尔莫里战士经过。

column2: 途中，他们遭到了特尔莫里战士的攻击。

column1: Our warriors successfully fought them off.
column2: 我们的战士成功击退了他们。

column2: 特尔莫里人不知从何处出现，杀死了 \x01@\x1A 名 \x01@\x05的战士。无人受伤：每位被特尔莫里武器击中的战士都受了致命伤。

column1: Sometimes the Telmori are wolves; sometimes they are men.
column2: 有时特尔莫里人是狼；有时他们是人。

column1: Our own herds are dwindling, and kings cannot hold power without many cattle. If an enemy is weak, that is all the more reason to raid them.
column2: 我们自己的牲畜正在减少，没有大量牛群，国王就无法维持权力。若敌人虚弱，那更是袭击他们的理由。

column1: It is hard to make peace with foreigners like the Telmori. But Issaries made conciliation between peoples whose differences were even greater than our differences with the wolf-folk.
column2: 与特尔莫里这样的异族议和很难。但伊萨里斯曾调解过比我们与狼人之间分歧更大的民族。

column1: If Issaries found a way to settle the differences between the Long-Noses and Big-Tooths, then we must try to reconcile Orlanthi and Telmori.
column2: 如果伊萨里斯能找到办法解决长鼻族与大牙族之间的分歧，那么我们必须尝试调和奥兰斯提人与特尔莫里人。

column1: Making peace with the Telmori will be hard. Make sure we send someone equipped to survive.
column2: 与特尔莫里人议和会很困难。务必派一个有能力幸存的人去。

column1: Making peace with the Telmori will be harder now, but if we achieve it, we will be remembered forever.
column2: 现在与特尔莫里人议和会更加困难，但若成功，我们将永被铭记。

column1: Making peace with the Telmori will be very difficult, but if we achieve it, we can ask whatever we want.
column2: 与特尔莫里人议和将极其困难，但若成功，我们可以索要任何想要之物。

column1: If we want peace with the Telmori, send an emissary as strong as he or she is clever.
column2: 若想与特尔莫里人议和，就派一位既强壮又聪明的使者。

column1: Somewhere in this situation there is a good fight to be had.
column2: 在目前局势中，总有一场好仗可打。

column2: 攻击一个衰弱的邻邦比对抗特尔莫里人更容易。

column1: It must be easier to attack a weakened neighbor than to fight the Telmori, who are emboldened by their recent victories.
column2: 攻击一个衰弱的邻邦必定比对抗特尔莫里人更容易，后者近来大胜而胆气更壮。

column1: If we beat a weakened neighbor, the spoils could be great. If we lose, we can expect savage reprisals.
column2: 若击败一个衰弱的邻邦，战利品可能非常丰厚。若失败，则可能招致残忍报复。

column1: There is little glory in thumping an already-weakened foe, unless you’re the one who weakened them.
column2: 痛击一个本已衰弱的敌人没什么荣耀可言，除非衰弱就是你所为。

column1: Sometimes it is better to talk than to fight, but only if the talker is also a fighter.
column2: 有时谈谈比打仗好，但前提是谈话者同时也是战士。

column1: Talk is useful when fighting proves impossible. Talk backed up with strength of arms.
column2: 当战斗无望时，谈判就有用了——以武力为后盾的谈判。

column1: The Telmori may look like our hated ancestral enemies, the Beastfolk, but they are really humans suffering under a vile curse. Even if we don’t like them, we won’t hurt our magic by dealing with them.
column2: 特尔莫里人或许看起来像我们憎恨的祖先宿敌——兽人，但他们其实是遭受恶毒诅咒的人类。即使我们不喜欢他们，与他们打交道也不会损害我们的魔力。

column1: What we do here will affect how others see us.
column2: 我们在此处的作为将影响他人如何看待我们。

column1: The \x01@B have treated us with less respect than the \x01@C; we should attack them.

column1: The true leader does not do what is expedient; he does what others think impossible.
column2: 真正的领袖不做权宜之事；他做他人认为不可能之事。

column1: The true leader does not see what everyone else sees. The true leader sees the real problem, and finds the best way for all.
column2: 真正的领袖不只见众人所见。真正的领袖看到真正的问题，找到对所有人最好的路。

column1: How can we even think of making such a dishonorable war during Sea season? Find a different way.
column2: 我们怎能考虑在海季发动如此不名誉的战争？另寻他法。

column1: A town could have a special stead devoted to keeping the scrolls!

column1: Warfare makes literacy difficult. Towns make reading easier to teach. Build a town.
column2: 战争使读写难以传授。城镇使阅读更易教授。建一座城镇吧。

column2: 泰尔莫利人曾崇拜混沌神祇格巴吉，如今在大地上流浪，不得安宁。

column1: Do not make needless war.
column2: 不要发动无谓的战争。

column1: Don’t send just any trader into that fray — send a someone who is a tough fighter, too.
column2: 别随便派个商人进入那场争斗——派一个也是强悍战士的人去。

column2: 派一个能言善辩且利刃锋利的人去与霍伯克·乔恩谈判。

column1: What are we worried about? Werewolves are not undead.
column2: 我们在担心什么？狼人并非亡灵。

column2: 攻击一个虚弱的对手是粗鲁的。

column2: 国王们拒绝考虑这一点；每一方都拒绝承认对方在城镇中收取礼物的任何权利。

column1: “Share gifts equally between the three founding tribes.”

column1: We told the kings that any gifts gained should be distributed equally between the three founding tribes.
column2: 我们告诉国王们，任何获得的礼物都应在三个创始部落间平均分配。

column1: The kings agreed that this was fair; all who had made the town should benefit from it equally. They redistributed the gifts they had been given, and we got our proper share.
column2: 国王们同意这是公平的；所有创建城镇的人都应平等受益。他们重新分配了收到的礼物，我们得到了应有的份额。

column1: The kings were too blinded by greed to consider sharing, even though it was the fairest choice. They insulted one another, but then joined together in insulting our bargainers.
column2: 国王们被贪婪蒙蔽，不愿考虑分享，尽管这是最公平的选择。他们互相侮辱，然后又联合起来侮辱我们的谈判者。

column1: “If we quarrel, a great destiny will pass us by.”
column2: “如果我们争吵，伟大命运就会与我们擦肩而过。”

column1: We said to the kings, “If we quarrel, a great destiny will pass us by.”
column2: 我们对国王们说：“如果我们争吵，伟大命运就会与我们擦肩而过。”

column1: The kings then realized that their real opportunity had not yet arrived. “Our divinations have for a long time predicted a great destiny, one that we will take a part in. However, the newness of the town, and the wealth it has brought, temporarily blinded us to this higher purpose. We will end our quarrel, and do what we can to serve the greater destiny.”
column2: 国王们随后意识到他们真正的机会尚未到来。“我们的占卜长期以来一直预言着一个伟大命运，一个我们将参与其中的命运。然而，城镇的新颖以及它带来的财富，暂时蒙蔽了我们，使我们看不到这个更高目的。我们将结束争吵，尽我们所能服务这更伟大的命运。”

column1: The kings laughed and spit. “This destiny is only in your head. You are foolish dreamers. By creating this town, your foolishness has helped us. Now it is time you got out of the way, so the sensible people who care about real things, like cows and silver, can run things.”
column2: 国王们嘲笑并吐唾沫。“这个命运只存在于你的脑袋里。你们是愚蠢的梦想家。创建这个城镇，你们的愚蠢帮了我们。现在该你们让路了，让那些关心实在东西（比如牛和白银）的明智之人来掌管事务。”

column1: “We have no right to demand gifts from the townsfolk.”
column2: “我们没有权利向镇民索要礼物。”

column1: We said to the kings, “None of us have the right to demand gifts from the townsfolk.”
column2: 我们对国王们说：“我们谁都没有权利向镇民索要礼物。”

column1: “This is a strange new law you propose,” they said. “For it is the king’s right to give gifts to his people. In order to exercise this right, he must be wealthy. What good is this town thing of yours if it does not make us wealthy?”
column2: “这是你们提出的一条奇怪的新法律，”他们说。“因为国王有权赐予他的子民礼物。为了行使这个权利，他必须富有。如果这个所谓的城镇不能让我们富有，那它有什么用？”

column1: They thought for a while more and then said, “The town is a new thing, so perhaps it does require new laws. You have done good things for us so far, so we will let you enact this law, and see if we are better off for it.”
column2: 他们又思考了一会儿，然后说：“城镇是新事物，所以或许它确实需要新法律。到目前为止你们为我们做了好事，所以我们会让你们制定这条法律，看看我们是否会因此过得更好。”

column1: The motion rune on our magic banner glowed, so we knew we had done the right thing.
column2: 我们魔法旗帜上的动向符文发光了，所以我们知道我们做了正确的事。

column1: They thought for a while more and said, “No, you are wrong. Under Heort’s laws, we have the right to demand gifts.”
column2: 他们又思考了一会儿，说：“不，你们错了。根据赫尔特法令，我们有权索要礼物。”

column1: “We must create a town ring to settle such disputes.”
column2: “我们必须创建一个镇议会来解决此类争端。”

column1: We said to the kings, “We must create a town ring to settle such disputes.”
column2: 我们对国王们说：“我们必须创建一个镇议会来解决此类争端。”

column1: They thought on this for a while and then said, “We are fighting because there is no one to make final decisions in this new town. You are right; the only way to preserve this town, which makes wealth for us, is to create a town ring.” And so the three tribes made a town ring, each of them seating some of its own members on the ring.
column2: 他们对此思考了一会儿，然后说：“我们争斗是因为在这个新城镇中没有人做最终决定。你们是对的；保护这个为我们创造财富的城镇的唯一方法就是创建一个镇议会。”于是三个部落创建了一个镇议会，每个部落都在议会中安插了自己的一些成员。

column1: They thought for a while more and said, “No, making the town was a good idea, but this idea is very stupid. We will not agree.”
column2: 他们又思考了一会儿，说：“不，创建城镇是个好主意，但这个想法非常愚蠢。我们不同意。”

column1: We have done great works, but our herds are dwindling. We must share in the proceeds from this new town.
column2: 我们完成了伟大的事业，但我们的畜群正在减少。我们必须分享这个新城镇的收益。

column1: Even without the proceeds from this new town, we are prosperous. We can afford to be generous with the other kings.
column2: 即使没有这个新城镇的收益，我们也很繁荣。我们可以对其他国王慷慨一些。

column1: This town will never amount to anything. Let’s abandon it.
column2: 这个城镇永远不会有什么成就。我们放弃它吧。

column1: We took more than our share earlier, so it will be hard to argue for a fair share now.
column2: 我们之前拿走了超出我们份额的部分，所以现在很难争取公平份额。

column1: If everyone demands gifts from the townsfolk, they will stop coming here. Then everyone will lose out.
column2: 如果每个人都向镇民索要礼物，他们就不会再来了。那样每个人都会受损。

column1: If the townsfolk do not want to belong to clans, we can do whatever we want with them.
column2: 如果镇民不想属于氏族，我们可以对他们为所欲为。

column1: The laws governing towns can be different from the rules governing clans.
column2: 管理城镇的法律可以与管理氏族的规则不同。

column1: These disputes will continue so long as there is no proper authority to govern the town.
column2: 只要没有适当的权威来治理城镇，这些争端就会继续。

column1: If we act generously, people all around Dragon Pass will respect our leadership.
column2: 如果我们慷慨行事，整个龙之隘口的人们都会尊重我们的领导力。

column1: If we claim a great destiny, but fail to convince them, people all around Dragon Pass will laugh at us.
column2: 如果我们声称拥有伟大命运，却未能说服他们，整个龙之隘口的人们都会嘲笑我们。

column1: A swift, fair solution is best. We waste time with this petty bickering.
column2: 迅速、公正的解决方案是最好的。我们浪费时间在这些琐碎的争吵上。

column1: If the founding tribes quarrel, a great destiny will pass us by.
column2: 如果创始部落争吵不休，伟大命运就会从我们身边溜走。

column1: By making new and righteous laws for this new town, we bring ourselves closer to our great destiny.
column2: 为这座新城制定新而公正的法律，我们就能更接近我们的伟大命运。

column1: By making new and righteous laws for this new town, we bring ourselves closer to our great destiny, and, in so doing, strengthen our clan magic.
column2: 为这座新城制定新而公正的法律，我们就能更接近我们的伟大命运，并且，借此强化我们的氏族魔法。

column1: Greed will attract greed. We are a ripe fruit in danger from these worms within, and ripe for plucking by those outside.
column2: 贪婪会引来贪婪。我们就像一颗成熟的果实，既面临内部这些蛀虫的危险，又容易被外部的人摘取。

column1: When Tragic King Errarth was felled, the Boar of Pestilence strode the streets of Errat Town, and drove the people from the city.

column1: If a great destiny awaits us, we can’t allow greed and foolishness to stand in its way.
column2: 如果伟大命运在等待着我们，我们就不能让贪婪和愚蠢挡住它的道路。

column1: Bulls butt heads; cows join herds.

column1: A young town is like an expectant mother; it must be left in peace.

column1: Our tribe deserves its share.

column1: If we make new and proper laws, people all around Dragon Pass will respect our leadership.

Their parley lasted for a long time.
column2: 起初，马裔很愤怒。接着他们大笑起来。然后奇怪的事情发生了。他们那些灰白色胡须的长老策马冲到阵型中央，那里是他们的战争领袖所在之处。他们与战争领袖商议，战争领袖看上去既惊讶又困惑。他们的商谈持续了很长时间。

column1: Then their war leader spoke up, “It may be that there are certain prophecies. They make your strange offer acceptable, so we will not kill you now. In one season, send \x01@\x0B and delegation to seek audience with our great queen.” Then they rode off, their plans for war interrupted.

column1: Tell them that the town is part of a great destiny.

column1: They whinnied like excited horses. “Its destiny is to anger us,” said the Horse-Spawn war leader, “for it is an affront to all that is free under the sun. The destiny of things which anger the Grazers is to be destroyed!”
column2: 他们像兴奋的马一样嘶鸣。“它的命运就是激怒我们，”马裔战争领袖说，“因为它冒犯了阳光下一切自由之物。激怒放牧者的事物，其命运就是被摧毁！”

column2: 我们告诉他们，如果他们攻击城镇，就会被打败。

column1: Their horses capered about, and they consulted amongst themselves. “Very well, then we shall be back later, with a larger force. Then we shall destroy you.”
column2: 他们的战马蹦跳着，他们内部商量了一番。“很好，那我们晚点再来，带上更庞大的军队。那时我们就会摧毁你们。”

column1: They rattled their swords and chanted a chant of war. “It is you who shall be destroyed, if you do not flee,” said their war leader, baring his squarish teeth.
column2: 他们敲击着长剑，唱起了战歌。“如果你们不逃走，被摧毁的将是你们，”他们的战争领袖龇着方牙说道。

column1: We cannot afford to give them tribute.
column2: 我们付不起贡品。

column1: We can afford tribute, so let’s pay it and get this over with.
column2: 我们付得起贡品，就付了吧，赶紧了结此事。

column1: I suppose we can afford to pay tribute again, so let’s get it over with.
column2: 我想我们还能再付一次贡品，那就赶紧了结吧。

column1: I’m sick of building our herds up, just to watch them walk off with those — those — horse-lovers!
column2: 我受够了辛辛苦苦壮大我们的畜群，结果眼睁睁看着它们被那些——那些——爱马的家伙牵走！

column1: We cannot let the town be destroyed; it is too important to trade!
column2: 我们不能让城镇被摧毁；它对贸易太重要了！

column1: Bring them on! This will be an easy victory!
column2: 放马过来吧！这会是一场轻松的胜利！

column1: The Horse-Spawn are among our most fearsome foes.
column2: 马裔是我们最可怕的敌人之一。

column1: Even if we defeat the Horse-Spawn, we will lose many warriors, and so will our allies.
column2: 即使我们击败了马裔，我们和我们的盟友也会损失许多勇士。

column1: Sooner or later they will tire of our delaying tactics. Let’s make it later, so we can strengthen our forces.
column2: 他们迟早会厌倦我们的拖延战术。那就让它晚些到来，好让我们能增强兵力。

column1: Although the Horse-Spawn are among our most fearsome foes, I may be able to bluff them into withdrawing.
column2: 尽管马裔是我们最可怕的敌人之一，但我或许能虚张声势逼他们撤退。

column1: I don’t think the Horse-Spawn will believe two bluffs in a row.
column2: 我不认为马裔会连续两次相信虚张声势。

column1: I can try to bluff them into withdrawing, but the next time they come, we had better prepare for battle.
column2: 我可以尝试虚张声势逼他们撤退，但他们下次再来时，我们最好做好战斗准备。

column1: Making peace with our long-standing enemies would seal our place in the sagas.
column2: 与我们长期的敌人媾和，将确保我们在传说中留名。

column1: The Horse-Spawn have a new leader. I wonder if this Feathered Horse Queen is the same as the queen of feathers mentioned in the prophecies?
column2: 马裔有了新领袖。我想知道这位羽马女王是否就是预言中提到的羽翼女王？

column1: If we give tribute to the cruel Horse-Spawn, our allies will lose respect for us.
column2: 如果我们向残暴的马裔进贡，盟友会失去对我们的尊重。

column1: Our allies will abandon us if we keep paying tribute to the Horse-Spawn.
column2: 如果我们继续向马裔进贡，盟友就会抛弃我们。

column1: If we retreat or give tribute to the cruel Horse-Spawn, our allies will lose respect for us.
column2: 如果我们撤退或向残暴的马裔进贡，盟友会失去对我们的尊重。

column1: There seems to be no end to this Horse-Spawn tribe — we cannot win against an unlimited foe!
column2: 这个马裔部落似乎永无止境——我们无法战胜无穷无尽的敌人！

column1: We must find a way out of this that escapes fighting and avoids paying more tribute.
column2: 我们必须找到一条出路，既能避免战斗，又不必再进贡。

column1: Even suggesting union with the hated Horse-Spawn will wither our clan magic forever.
column2: 即便只是提议与可憎的马裔联合，也会永远削弱我们的氏族魔法。

column1: The town is part of a great destiny.
column2: 这座城镇是伟大命运的一部分。

column1: The town is part of a great destiny. We have united warring tribes and sought peace with the Telmori. The next stage is union with our worst enemies, the Horse-Spawn.
column2: 这座城镇是伟大命运的一部分。我们联合了交战的部落，与泰尔莫里寻求和平。下一阶段是与我们最大的敌人——马裔的联合。

column1: These Horse-Spawn seem to speak our language much better than they used to. Either they learn quickly, or we are dealing with higher-ranking folk than we ever have before.
column2: 这些马裔说我们语言的能力似乎比以前好多了。要么是他们学得很快，要么是我们面对的是前所未见的高阶人物。

column1: Horse-folk always ruin everything.
column2: 马裔总是毁掉一切。

column1: King Heort said, “It is better to make an ally of a foe than to destroy him, for an ally can help you, and a dead foe cannot.”
column2: 赫尔特王说过：“与其毁灭敌人，不如与之结盟，因为盟友能帮助你，而死的敌人不能。”

column1: Bad King Urgrain never lost a chance to turn friends into foes. And he never took a chance on making an ally out of an enemy, either.
column2: 恶王乌格兰从不放过把朋友变成敌人的机会。他也从未尝试过把敌人变成盟友。

column1: One of King Heort’s favorite proverbs was: “Former enemies make the tightest allies.”
column2: 赫尔特王最喜欢的谚语之一是：“曾经的敌人能成为最紧密的盟友。”

column1: We must appease these minor foes, so that we will be strong when the inevitable elf attack comes.
column2: 我们必须安抚这些小敌，这样当不可避免的精灵进攻到来时，我们才能足够强大。

column1: Unless we abandon the town right away, their fiery, hopping-horse magics will destroy us all!
column2: 除非我们立刻放弃这座城镇，否则他们那跳跃火焰般的马匹魔法会把我们都毁灭！

column1: There is no reasoning with rude foreigners.
column2: 与粗鲁的外来人没什么道理可讲。

column1: Better to die than to pay a wretched foe.
column2: 宁死不向卑鄙的敌人进贡。

column1: I have \x02\x03lived for/yearned for/dreamed of\x02 this day, this final day of blood.
column2: 我 \x02\x03活过/渴望过/梦想过\x02 这一天，这流血终结之日。

column1: We cannot let them take the town square temple.
column2: 我们不能让他们占领城镇广场的神殿。

column1: Saraska was a fool who tried to make a kingdom by threatening war. We have found another way.
column2: 萨拉斯卡是个傻瓜，妄想用战争威胁来建立王国。我们找到了另一条路。

column1: We must forget our old grudges and make something new.
column2: 我们必须忘记旧怨，开创未来。

column1: This stand-off is absurd. If we wish to carve our names into the sagas, we must act like heroes!
column2: 这种对峙简直荒谬。如果要在传说中刻下我们的名字，就必须像英雄一样行动！

column1: We lost good warriors, but one by one we slew the Horse-Spawn and their terrible mounts. We took a generous share of the spoils, and no one disputed our right to it.
column2: 我们损失了优秀的战士，但一个接一个地杀死了马裔和他们可怕的坐骑。我们分得了丰厚的战利品，无人质疑我们的权利。

column1: sceneR357
column2: sceneR357

column1: A group of tricksters from various local clans assembles to offer you a gift, which they refer to as a treasure. It is a ragged banner with the motion rune crudely painted on it. The appearance of so many tricksters at once makes your people nervous. Some say you should accept the gift, because it is unwise to give tricksters cause to play pranks on you. Others say that the gift itself is probably a prank, and possibly a dangerous one.
column2: 一群来自各地方氏族的恶作剧者聚集起来，向你献上一份礼物，他们称之为宝藏。那是一面破旧的旗帜，上面粗糙地画着运动符文。同时出现这么多恶作剧者让你的人民紧张不安。有人说你应该接受礼物，因为招惹恶作剧者让他们对你恶作剧是不明智的。也有人说这份礼物本身可能就是个恶作剧，而且很可能是危险的恶作剧。

column1: A group of tricksters offered us a gift; it was a banner with the motion rune painted on it.
column2: 一群恶作剧者送了我们一份礼物；那是一面画着运动符文的旗帜。

column1: The tricksters capered away, singing a vulgar song about cheese and wine.
column2: 恶作剧者们蹦蹦跳跳地离去，唱着关于奶酪和葡萄酒的粗俗歌曲。

column1: Accept the gift; get the tricksters drunk.
column2: 接受礼物；把恶作剧者灌醉。

column1: We accepted the gift and tried to get the tricksters drunk.
column2: 我们接受了礼物，试图把恶作剧者灌醉。

column1: This was not at all hard to do. They drank more beer and wine than we would have thought possible.
column2: 这根本不费吹灰之力。他们喝的啤酒和葡萄酒比我们想象的还多。

column1: Just before they fell over, they said, “Keep this banner always. You will need it especially in \x01@\x1A years. To use it properly, make sure one of you is king of a tribe; otherwise, destiny will pass you by. When the time comes, you must stop a war by turning it into stone and mortar. You must make a peace by conjuring a wolf. Then you must marry a horse. There is more to it, but it is for someone else to say.”
column2: 就在他们醉倒之前，他们说：“永远留着这面旗帜。你们在 \x01@\x1A 年会特别需要它。要正确使用它，你们中必须有一人是部落的王；否则命运就会与你们擦肩而过。时机到来时，你们必须通过把战争化为砖石来阻止战争。你们必须通过召唤狼来缔造和平。然后你们必须与马联姻。还有更多，但那是留给别人说的事。”

column1: Then they slept, drenched in their own vomit.
column2: 然后他们睡着了，浑身浸满自己的呕吐物。

column1: Accept the gift; gift them in return.
column2: 接受礼物；回赠他们礼物。

column1: We accepted the banner and gave them a gift in return.
column2: 我们接受了旗帜，并回赠了他们礼物。

column1: “Curses!” they shouted. “You have obligated us to tell you what this is about, although it would be much funnier not to, and to just let this thing rot in someone’s stead, unused. Keep this banner always. You will need it especially around \x01@\x1A years from now. To use it properly, you must make sure that one of you is king of a tribe; otherwise, destiny will pass you by. When the time comes, you must stop a war by turning it into stone and mortar. You must make a peace by conjuring a wolf. Then you must marry a horse. There is more to it, but it is for someone else to say.”
column2: “诅咒！”他们喊道，“你已经逼得我们必须告诉你这是怎么回事，尽管不告诉你会更有趣，就让这东西在某个人的角落里烂掉、无人使用。永远保存这面旗帜。大约从 \x01@\x1A 年后起你会特别需要它。要正确使用它，你必须确保你们中有一人是部落之王；否则命运将与你擦肩而过。当时机到来，你必须通过将它化为石头和砂浆来阻止一场战争。你必须通过召唤一匹狼来实现和平。然后你必须与一匹马成婚。还有更多，但那是别人要说的。”

column1: They thanked us for honoring them, and departed.
column2: 他们感谢我们的敬意，然后离去了。

column1: Ask the tricksters what its significance is.
column2: 问问恶作剧者们这东西有什么意义。

column1: We asked the tricksters what its significance is.
column2: 我们问了恶作剧者们这东西有什么意义。

column1: Reject the gift.
column2: 拒绝礼物。

column1: We rejected the gift.
column2: 我们拒绝了礼物。

column1: They skipped away, laughing. “This is the funniest joke of all,” they said.
column2: 他们蹦跳着走开了，笑着说：“这是所有玩笑中最好笑的一个。”

column1: Drink! Drink! We must all drink with them!
column2: 喝！喝！我们一定要和他们一起喝！

column1: We might be able to trade it for something useful.
column2: 我们也许可以用它换些有用的东西。

column1: We must know more about it before we accept it.
column2: 我们在接受之前必须先了解更多。

column1: Tricksters are lawless and lack discipline; to accept their gift would set a bad example.
column2: 恶作剧者无法无天、缺乏纪律；接受他们的礼物会树立坏榜样。

column1: Tricksters often betray you, but sometimes the way you overcome the betrayal brings a new kind of victory.
column2: 恶作剧者经常背叛你，但有时你克服背叛的方式会带来一种新的胜利。

column1: Tricksters are earthy, but they are not of the earth.
column2: 恶作剧者很粗俗，但他们不属于大地。

column1: They are funny, so long as they are not making fun of me.
column2: 他们很有趣，只要他们不是在取笑我。

column1: Do not ask them serious questions, or they will release a bowel-stink that will dry up our milk cows.
column2: 不要问他们严肃的问题，否则他们会放出一种让我们的奶牛干涸的肠臭。

column1: Take pity on the poor souls, and treat them with dignity.
column2: 可怜可怜这些穷魂，用尊严对待他们。

column1: Tricksters disrupt the safety of the clan. We must not trust them.
column2: 恶作剧者破坏氏族的安宁。我们不能信任他们。

column1: Hah! Tricksters giving gifts. Why not?
column2: 哈！恶作剧者送礼物。有何不可？

column1: I came back to the clan hall for this?
column2: 我就是为了这个跑回部族大厅的？

column1: sceneR358
column2: sceneR358

column1: Apologize for past transgressions against her people.
column2: 为她的人民过去所受的冒犯道歉。

column1: Many of the warriors in the delegation were disquieted by this apology, for the Horse-Spawn had been our worst enemies for a long time.
column2: 使团中的许多战士对这番道歉感到不安，因为马裔长久以来一直是我们最凶恶的敌人。

column1: In response to the king’s words of atonement, the Feathered Horse Queen said nothing.
column2: 对于国王的赎罪之言，羽马女王一言不发。

column1: Offer her gifts.
column2: 向她献上礼物。

column1: Promise to stop calling her people “Horse-Spawn.”
column2: 承诺不再称她的人民为“马裔”。

column1: The king promised to stop calling her people “Horse-Spawn.”
column2: 国王承诺不再称她的人民为“马裔”。

column1: “From now on,” the Feathered Horse Queen said, “you must call us what we call ourselves — Grazers.”
column2: “从现在起，”羽马女王说，“你们必须用我们自称的称呼——放牧者。”

column1: Propose marriage.
column2: 求婚。

column1: Accept these terms.
column2: 接受这些条件。

column1: We drank a ritual toast with the Grazers to ask for blessings on all of us.
column2: 我们与放牧者共饮了仪式祝酒，祈求为我们所有人赐福。

column1: Reject these terms.
column2: 拒绝这些条件。

column1: The Feathered Horse Queen refused his entreaty. “There will be a contest for my hand, and for the title of King of Dragon Pass. But you shall not be invited to participate in this contest.”
column2: 羽马女王拒绝了他的恳求。“我的婚约，以及龙隘之王的头衔，将有一场竞争。但你们不会被邀请参加这场竞争。”

column1: Remind her of the good things you have done for her people.
column2: 提醒她你为她的人民做过的好事。

column1: In response to the king’s litany of favors, the Feathered Horse Queen said nothing.
column2: 对于国王列举的恩惠，羽马女王一言不发。

column1: We can’t afford to give her very much.
column2: 我们给不了她太多东西。

column1: We can afford to gift her generously.
column2: 我们还能慷慨地赠她礼物。

column1: She will be offended by an offer of gifts.
column2: 献上礼物的提议会冒犯她。

column1: Before you do anything else, offer her gifts.
column2: 在做任何其他事之前，先献上礼物。

column1: Before you do anything else, offer her at least ten cows worth of goods.
column2: 在做任何其他事之前，先献上至少价值十头牛的货物。

column1: Before you do anything else, offer her gifts, as much as we can afford. Anything less than twenty cows will seem like less than a trifle to her.
column2: 在做任何其他事之前，先献上礼物，尽我们所能。任何少于二十头牛的东西在她看来都微不足道。

column1: The Horse-Spawn have always been our foes; the warriors will be offended if our king grovels before their whorish queen.
column2: 马裔一直是我们的敌人；如果我们的国王在他们那淫妇女王面前卑躬屈膝，战士们会感到被冒犯。

column1: They don’t speak our language, so why would they care if we call them “Horse-Spawn”?
column2: 他们不说我们的语言，所以我们在意他们叫我们“马裔”吗？

column1: They are foreigners, with foreign ways. It is hard to know how they expect us to behave.
column2: 他们是外国人，有外国习俗。很难知道他们期望我们如何行事。

column1: They don’t like us calling them “Horse-Spawn,” but could be offended if we even mention this term.
column2: 他们不喜欢我们叫他们“马裔”，但如果我们提及这个称呼，他们可能会被冒犯。

column1: Before you do anything else, promise not to call them “Horse-Spawn” any more.
column2: 在做任何其他事之前，先承诺不再叫他们“马裔”。

column1: The Feathered Horse Queen hates delays and flattery; start right with the marriage proposal.
column2: 羽马女王讨厌拖延和奉承；直接以求婚开始。

column1: We must soften them up before proposing marriage.
column2: 我们必须先软化他们再求婚。

column1: We must do everything we can to curry favor before proposing marriage. It is always good to start with gifts.
column2: 在求婚之前我们必须尽一切可能讨好他们。总以礼物开始是好的。

column1: Although the Horse-Spawn have good reason to hate us, the magic of the motion rune will bring about a union of opposites.
column2: 尽管马裔有充分的理由恨我们，但运动符文的力量将促成对立之物的结合。

column1: This marriage will be unprecedented. But the prophets have been hinting at it. And Orlanth didn’t change the world by doing what everyone had done before him.
column2: 这场婚姻将史无前例。但先知们一直在暗示它。而奥兰斯并非靠做每个人都做过的事来改变世界。

column1: The marriage of Leibarth and Olfreda brought only misfortune to the tribe of Errarth, the Tragic King.
column2: 莱巴思与奥尔弗雷达的婚姻只给悲剧之王埃拉思的部落带来了不幸。

column1: This marriage will be the talk of all Dragon Pass!
column2: 这场婚姻将成为整个龙隘的话题！

column1: She’s ugly. The most wrinkled Orlanthi crone is more of a queen than her.
column2: 她真丑。最皱巴巴的奥兰西老妇都比她更像女王。

column1: This day shall be remembered forever!
column2: 这一天将被永远铭记！

column1: She will not necessarily agree to this match — first I must prove my goodwill, my sincerity, and my worth.
column2: 她不一定同意这门亲事——首先我必须证明我的善意、真诚和我的价值。

column2: sceneR359

column1: Apologize for past transgressions against his people.
column2: 为他的人民过去所受的冒犯道歉。

column1: In response to the queen’s words of atonement, the Luminous Stallion King said nothing.
column2: 针对女王的赎罪之言，光辉雄马王一言不发。

column1: Offer him gifts.
column2: 向他奉上礼物。

column1: Promise to stop calling his people “Horse-Spawn.”
column2: 承诺不再称呼其族人为"马裔"。

column2: 女王承诺不再称呼其族人为"马裔"。

column1: “From now on,” the Luminous Stallion King said, “you must call us what we call ourselves — Grazers.”
column2: 从今往后，光辉雄马王说道，"你们必须按我们的自称来称呼我们——放牧者。"

column1: The Luminous Stallion King refused her entreaty. “There will be a contest for to see who will be my bride, and who will become Queen of Dragon Pass. But you shall not be invited to participate in this contest.”
column2: 光辉雄马王拒绝了她的恳求。"将有一场比试来决定谁将成为我的新娘，谁将成为龙之隘口女王。但你将不会被邀请参加这场比试。"

column1: Remind him of the good things you have done for his people.
column2: 提醒他你曾为其部族做过的善事。

column1: In response to the queen’s litany of favors, the Luminous Stallion King said nothing.
column2: 面对女王历数恩惠的长篇大论，光辉雄马王一言不发。

column1: We can’t afford to give him very much.
column2: 我们拿不出太多东西给他。

column1: We can afford to gift him generously.
column2: 我们可以慷慨地赠予他礼物。

column1: The Luminous Stallion King will be offended if a woman offers him gifts.
column2: 若由女子赠礼，光辉雄马王会感到受辱。

column1: Before you do anything else, offer him gifts.
column2: 在采取任何其他行动之前，先向他奉上礼物。

column2: 没有什么问题是慷慨馈赠牛只解决不了的。

column1: It will cost us a mere ten cows to buy each thrall.
column2: 只需花费十头牛，就能买下每个奴隶。

column1: It will cost us a mere five cows to buy each thrall.
column2: 只需花费五头牛，就能买下每个奴隶。

column1: Normally, it would cost us a mere five cows to buy each thrall, but since they need to be captured to be of any use, we can get them for far less.
column2: 通常每个奴隶只需五头牛就能买下，但既然他们需要先被捕获才派得上用场，我们就能以低得多的价格弄到手。

column1: Normally, it would cost us a mere five cows to buy each thrall, but since they need to be captured to be of any use, we can get them for far less. I’ll go; you need send only a few warriors with me.
column2: 通常每个奴隶只需五头牛就能买下，但既然他们需要先被捕获才派得上用场，我们就能以低得多的价格弄到手。我去办吧，你只需派几个战士跟我同行就行。

column1: Our people have always supported the taking of thralls.
column2: 我们的人民一向支持收容奴隶。

column1: Our people have always opposed the taking of thralls.
column2: 我们的人民一向反对收容奴隶。

column1: Our people have always opposed the taking of thralls. We should convince the \x01@! thanes to abandon their pursuit.
column2: 我们的人民一向反对收容奴隶。我们应该说服 \x01@! 领主们放弃追捕。

column1: Our people have always opposed the taking of thralls. We should send a war party to intercept the \x01@! thanes.
column2: 我们的人民一向反对收容奴隶。我们应该派出战团去拦截 \x01@! 领主们。

column1: If we act in accordance with the traditions of our ancestors, our clan magic will be strengthened.
column2: 如果我们遵照祖先的传统行事，氏族魔法就会得到增强。

column1: We could use a few more thralls to help us work the fields.
column2: 我们确实需要再多几个奴隶来帮忙耕种田地。

column1: We could use a few more thralls to help us work the fields. But buy them, don’t go sending farmers off to raid during Sea season.
column2: 我们确实需要再多几个奴隶来帮忙耕种田地。但要去买，别在海季把农夫派出去劫掠。

column1: We could use a few more thralls to help us work the fields. But buy them, don’t go sending farmers off to raid during Earth season.
column2: 我们确实需要再多几个奴隶来帮忙耕种田地。但要去买，别在地季把农夫派出去劫掠。

column1: We can’t afford to get embroiled in all this now — our fields need work, our crops need care.
column2: 我们现在可禁不起卷入这种事——我们的田地需要耕作，庄稼需要照料。

column1: I wonder how dragonewts feel about the keeping of thralls…
column2: 我很好奇龙人对豢养奴隶是怎么看的……

column1: The \x01@! clan are not as merciful as we are; they will surely do terrible things to the thralls, if they catch them.
column2: \x01@! 氏族可不像我们这么仁慈；他们要是抓住了那些奴隶，肯定会做出可怕的事来。

column1: Let us not the words of vengeful women get us into trouble. You know who I’m talking about.
column2: 别让那些复仇女人的话给我们惹麻烦。你知道我说的是谁。

column1: Some say the gods oppose the taking of thralls; others say the gods take thralls themselves. It is hard to know what to do.
column2: 有人说众神反对收容奴隶，也有人说众神自己就收容奴隶。真难决定该怎么做。

column2: sceneR365

column1: How many warriors do you send with \x01@\x10?
column2: 你派了多少战士跟着 \x01@\x10一起去？

column1: The clan ring did nothing about this.
column2: 氏族议会对此什么也没做。

column1: The people grumbled about this incident, but soon forgot that it had happened.
column2: 人们对这件事嘟囔了几句，但很快就忘了曾经发生过。

column1: We launched a legal claim against her.
column2: 我们对她提起了法律诉讼。

column1: Her clan is in your tribe.
column2: 她的氏族隶属你的部落。

column1: Take your claim to her clan ring.
column2: 向她的氏族议会提出你的诉讼。

column1: We took our claim to her clan ring.
column2: 我们向她的氏族议会提出了诉讼。

column1: Who argues the case?
column2: 谁来陈述案情？

column1: The other clans said that everyone knows that ducks are bad, and that we were bad for being friends to ducks. They would not uphold our claim, and the people were sorely disappointed.
column2: 其他部族说，大家都知道鸭人是坏的，我们与鸭人为友也是坏的。他们不会支持我们的主张，人们深感失望。

column1: The people celebrated the erasure of this humiliating insult.
column2: 人们庆祝这一屈辱的侮辱被抹去。

column1: Neither \x01@\x05 nor \x04 party ever returned.
column2: 既没有 \x01@\x05 也没有 \x04 一方回来过。

column1: We could only assume that they were ambushed by the ducks.
column2: 我们只能假设他们遭到了鸭人的伏击。

column1: We scoured the marshes, but did not find any ducks.
column2: 我们搜遍了沼泽，但没有找到任何鸭人。

column1: We found a group of ducks and did battle with them.
column2: 我们发现了一群鸭人并与之交战。

column1: We slew \x01@\x18 of them, proving to all that the friendship of ducks meant nothing to us. We took the goods they were carrying, and celebrated our victory.
column2: 我们杀了 \x01@\x18 个他们的人，向所有人证明鸭人的友谊对我们毫无意义。我们拿走了他们携带的货物，庆祝了胜利。

column1: The small creatures fought back with surprising ferocity, and felled many of our warriors. Some survived the battle with serious wounds. Others were hamstrung, and then had their throats slit.
column2: 这些小生物以惊人的凶猛反击，击倒了许多我们的战士。有些人幸存下来，但受了重伤。另一些人被挑断脚筋，然后被割喉。

column1: I have dealt with the ducks, and they are no friends of the undead.
column2: 我和鸭人打过交道，他们不是亡灵的朋友。

column1: Ducks are no threat; let’s attack them.
column2: 鸭人不足为惧；我们进攻吧。

column1: Ducks seem funny, but they’ll hamstring you and slit your throat faster than you can cry for help.
column2: 鸭人看起来滑稽，但他们会比你呼救还快地挑断你的脚筋并割开你的喉咙。

column1: Relations with the other clans of the tribe are not good; we will have to bring many warriors and gift the other chieftains lavishly if we want to win at the moot.
column2: 与部落中其他氏族的关系并不好；如果我们想赢得议会，就必须带上许多勇士，并向其他酋长慷慨赠送礼物。

column1: This is what I’ve been trying to say all along, we can’t afford to be allied with these little monsters.
column2: 我一直想说的就是这点，我们承受不起与这些小怪物结盟。

column1: It is high time we did something to prove our valor.
column2: 是时候做些什么来证明我们的英勇了。

column1: I read a scroll that said that the ducks serve Delecti the Necromancer. If someone bothered to write it down, it must be true.
column2: 我读到一卷卷轴，上面说鸭人服务于死灵法师德莱克提。如果有人费心写下来，那一定是真的。

column1: In pine-blood he was ducked.
column2: 他在松血中被鸭了。

column1: If we were the royal clan, we would not be humiliated like this.
column2: 如果我们王族，就不会这样受辱。

column2: sceneR366

column1: Warriors of the \x01@! clan make a daring raid into your tula, driving off a small herd of \x01@\x1A cattle before your own defenders can react.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的勇士大胆侵入我们的领地，在我们的守卫反应过来之前赶走了一小群 \x01@\x1A 牛。

column1: \x01@! warriors raided us, driving off a small herd of cattle before we could even react.
column2: \x01@! 勇士们袭击了我们，在我们甚至来不及反应之前就赶走了一小群牛。

column1: The people were angry that the ring refused to protect their cattle.
column2: 人们因长老会拒绝保护他们的牛而愤怒。

column1: Launch a punitive raid against the \x01@! clan.
column2: 对 \x01@! 氏族发动惩罚性袭击。

column1: We raided them in return.
column2: 我们袭击了他们作为报复。

column1: The people were glad that we had struck a blow against the dirty cattle thieves.
column2: 人们很高兴我们对那些肮脏的偷牛贼给予了打击。

column1: Our raid was less successful than theirs, and the people lamented our bad luck.
column2: 我们的袭击没有他们成功，人们哀叹我们的厄运。

column1: Send a delegation to threaten them.
column2: 派一个代表团去威胁他们。

column1: We sent a delegation to threaten them.
column2: 我们派了一个代表团去威胁他们。

column1: They were afraid of our might, and returned the stolen cattle.
column2: 他们害怕我们的力量，归还了偷走的牛。

column1: They responded to our threats with bold defiance.
column2: 他们对我们的威胁报以大胆的蔑视。

column1: Our warriors were chagrined.
column2: 我们的勇士们感到懊恼。

column1: Send a delegation to urge them to cease their raiding.
column2: 派一个代表团去敦促他们停止袭击。

column1: We sent a delegation to urge them to cease their raiding.
column2: 我们派了一个代表团去敦促他们停止袭击。

column1: They said that they wanted to get along with us, and would not raid us again. They returned the cows they had stolen.
column2: 他们说他们想与我们和睦相处，不会再袭击我们。他们归还了偷走的牛。

column1: They responded to our entreaties with jibes and insults.
column2: 他们对我们的恳求报以嘲讽和侮辱。

column1: We reached a fairer price, and so they proceeded with the curse ceremony.
column2: 我们谈到了更公平的价格，于是他们进行了诅咒仪式。

column1: They offered a lower price of \x01@\x13 cows, but that was still too rich for us.
column2: 他们提供了更低的 \x01@\x13 头牛的价格，但对我们来说仍然太高。

column1: We couldn’t meet their price and had to send them on their way.
column2: 我们无法满足他们的要价，只好送他们离开。

column1: They would not lower their price, which was too rich for us, and we had to send them on their way.
column2: 他们不愿降低价格，这对我们来说太高了，我们只好送他们离开。

column1: We can’t afford to lose cows like this. We certainly can’t give away more cows to unreliable shamans.
column2: 我们承受不起这样损失牛。我们当然不能把更多的牛送给不可靠的萨满。

column1: Although we have many cows, we can’t permit this sort of thing to go unpunished. We must curse them, and let them know we did it.
column2: 虽然我们有很多牛，但不能容许这种事不受惩罚。我们必须诅咒他们，并让他们知道是我们干的。

column1: They stole our cattle so easily! They’re bound to be tempted to try it again, unless we do something about it.
column2: 他们如此轻易地偷了我们的牛！除非我们采取行动，否则他们肯定会被诱惑再次尝试。

column1: And why do we support weaponthanes, giving them extra food and gifts, when they let the \x01@! steal our cows from beneath their noses?
column2: 而且我们为什么还要支持武器领主，给他们额外的食物和礼物，当他们让 \x01@! 在他们眼皮底下偷走我们的牛时？

column1: We must put an end to this — we might just as well slaughter these cows ourselves, and save the \x01@! clan the trouble of stealing them.
column2: 我们必须终结这一切——我们还不如自己宰了这些牛，省得 \x01@! 氏族费心偷它们。

column1: There are shamans in the hills who will lay curses in exchange for cattle.
column2: 山里有萨满，愿意以牛为交换施咒。

column1: I’d rather spend ten cows to harass the \x01@!, than lose one calf to those ruffians.
column2: 我宁愿花十头牛去骚扰 \x01@!，也不愿让那些恶棍偷走一头小牛。

column1: Ancient law permits their clan to steal from others.
column2: 古老的法律允许他们的氏族偷窃他人。

column1: Everyone steals cattle, when they can get away with it.
column2: 每个人都偷牛，只要他们能得逞。

column1: If we attack them, they’ll wet the fields with our blood.
column2: 如果我们攻击他们，他们会用我们的血浸湿田野。

column1: They are scum — let’s raid them!
column2: 他们是渣滓——我们去袭击他们！

column1: Threats are only good if we’re prepared to back them up.
column2: 威胁只有在我们准备付诸行动时才有用。

column1: They’re weaker than we are, so we should just raid them, and be done with it.
column2: 他们比我们弱，所以我们直接袭击他们，一了百了。

column1: We will be the laughingstock of Dragon Pass if we don’t teach them a lesson.
column2: 如果我们不教训他们，就会成为龙之隘口的笑柄。

column1: They’re stronger than we are, so there’s no point raiding them, or threatening to raid them.
column2: 他们比我们强，所以袭击他们或威胁袭击都没有意义。

column1: We’re weaker than they are, so if we raid, be prepared to get beaten and suffer big losses.
column2: 我们比他们弱，所以如果袭击，就要做好挨打并遭受重大损失的准备。

column1: If we want to avoid this in the future, we must increase our patrols.
column2: 如果我们想在未来避免这种情况，就必须加强巡逻。

column1: We must hire more weaponthanes, and put all of them to work on patrol, guarding the herds.
column2: 我们必须雇佣更多武器领主，并让他们全部巡逻，守卫畜群。

column1: People would rather be cajoled than threatened.
column2: 人们宁愿被哄骗，也不愿被威胁。

column1: They dislike us; we’ll get farther with threats than with entreaties.
column2: 他们不喜欢我们；用威胁比用恳求更能让我们走得更远。

column1: Except for this small matter, they have always treated us with respect. Diplomacy will get us farther than threats.
column2: 除了这件小事，他们一直对我们尊敬有加。外交比威胁更能让我们走得更远。

column1: There is no point in cursing them if we don’t tell them we did it.
column2: 如果不告诉他们是我们下的诅咒，诅咒他们就毫无意义。

column1: There is no point in cursing them if we don’t tell them we did it; if we do tell them, they might well curse us in return.
column2: 如果不告诉他们是我们下的诅咒，诅咒他们就毫无意义；如果我们告诉他们，他们很可能会回诅咒我们。

column1: We must do something — something that doesn’t meddle in our planting.
column2: 我们必须做点什么——不影响播种的事情。

column1: We must do something — something that doesn’t meddle in our harvest.
column2: 我们必须做点什么——不影响收获的事情。

column1: Orlanth stole cattle from the Emperor, who said, “Those beasts are mine.” Orlanth said, “They used to be yours. Soon the same will be said of the world — that it used to be yours.”
column2: 奥兰斯从皇帝那里偷了牛，皇帝说：“那些牲畜是我的。”奥兰斯说：“它们曾经是你的。很快世人就会同样说这个世界——它曾经是你的。”

column1: Bad King Urgrain stole cattle wherever he could. Then all the clans he stole from sent a curse on his herds and all the stolen cows died hideous deaths.
column2: 恶王乌格兰无论到哪里都偷牛。于是所有被他偷过牛的氏族都对牛群下了诅咒，所有被偷的牛都死得极其凄惨。

column1: “Eat early before you visit friends, or you might go hungry, afraid to ask for a meal.”
column2: “拜访朋友前先吃饱，否则你可能因不好意思讨饭而挨饿。”

column1: “Put one hand in one pocket, and the other in a different pocket. Then switch pockets.”
column2: “一只手放一个口袋，另一只手放另一个口袋。然后互换口袋。”

column1: “Pretty talk precedes ugly faces, ugly faces precede smashing fists.”
column2: “甜言蜜语之后是恶脸相向，恶脸相向之后是拳拳到肉。”

column1: It is a simple matter. They stole from us, so we should steal from them.
column2: 事情很简单。他们偷了我们的，所以我们应该偷他们的。

column1: \x02\x03Tit for tat/Hit them back/Punish them\x02.
column2: \x02\x03以牙还牙/回击他们/惩罚他们\x02。

column1: They have Orlanth’s Bull-Roarer, which will deafen our warriors if we attack them.
column2: 他们有奥兰斯的牛吼器，如果我们进攻，它会震聋我们的战士。

column1: If we threaten them, they will be angry and attack us, and take even more cattle.
column2: 如果我们威胁他们，他们会生气并攻击我们，抢走更多牲口。

column1: I just know they will wind up with most of our cows, and we shall go clanless and poor.
column2: 我就知道他们最终会夺走我们多数牛只，我们就会失去氏族，变得一贫如洗。

column1: \x02\x03Talking is better than fighting./Peace is better than battle./Getting along with our neighbors is more important than beating them.\x02
column2: \x02\x03交谈胜过争斗。/和平胜过战争。/与邻族和睦相处比击败他们更重要。\x02

column1: sceneR367
column2: sceneR367

column1: \x01@! warriors severely beat one of our carls, and hurt his wife.
column2: \x01@! 武士们毒打了一名我们的自由民，还伤了他的妻子。

column1: “Mere words won’t heal my wounds, nor poetry soften my poor wife’s bruises!”
column2: “只言片语治不好我的伤口，诗歌也舒缓不了我可怜妻子的淤伤！”

column1: Soon, the poem was on everyone’s lips, and even the vengeance-takers’ kinfolk were laughing at them.
column2: 很快，这首诗传遍众人之口，连复仇者的族人也嘲笑他们。

column1: Soon, the poem was on everyone’s lips, hardening the attitude of the vengeance-takers’ clan towards us.
column2: 很快，这首诗传遍众人之口，使得复仇者的氏族对我们的态度更加强硬。

column1: Launch a legal claim against the attackers.
column2: 对攻击者提出法律诉讼。

column1: We launched a legal claim against the vengeance-takers.
column2: 我们对复仇者提出了法律诉讼。

column1: Their clan is in your tribe.
column2: 他们的氏族在你们的部落里。

column1: Take your claim to their clan ring.
column2: 将你的诉讼提交到他们的氏族议会。

column1: We took our claim to their clan ring.
column2: 我们将诉讼提交到了他们的氏族议会。

column1: \x01@\x01 successfully argued the case, and their clan ring ordered them to pay us reparations for taking revenge too far.
column2: \x01@\x01 成功辩护，他们的氏族议会命令他们向我们支付赔偿，因为他们复仇过度。

column1: \x01@\x01 argued well, but their clan ring sided with their kin, instead of listening to the precedents.
column2: \x01@\x01 辩护得当，但他们的氏族议会偏袒自己的族人，而不听从前例。

column1: \x01@\x01 argued well, but the vengeance-takers’ clan ring refused to consider the merits of our case, and sided with their kin.
column2: \x01@\x01 辩护得当，但复仇者的氏族议会拒绝考虑我们案情的实质，偏袒了自己的族人。

column1: We launched a raid against the attackers’ clan.
column2: 我们对攻击者的氏族发动了一场突袭。

column1: The people celebrated the righteous blow we struck that day.
column2: 人民庆祝我们当日施行的正义打击。

column1: The people lamented the feeble blow we struck against the \x01@! swine.
column2: 人民哀叹我们对那群 \x01@! 猪猡施行的软弱打击。

column1: He would not hear the ring’s entreaties.
column2: 他不肯听长老会的恳求。

column1: If we attack them, we are sure to win.
column2: 如果我们进攻他们，我们必胜。

column1: We don’t dare attack them; they are too strong.
column2: 我们不敢进攻他们；他们太强了。

column1: They must pay for this!
column2: 他们必须为此付出代价！

column1: They are weak; if we attack them, we are likely to win.
column2: 他们很弱；如果我们进攻他们，很可能赢。

column1: We can still beat them, and beat them soundly.
column2: 我们仍然可以打败他们，而且狠狠打败。

column1: They are strong; if we attack them, we are likely to lose.
column2: 他们很强；如果我们进攻他们，很可能输。

column1: We aren’t ready to smash them yet.
column2: 我们还没准备好粉碎他们。

column1: Private vengeance is perfectly acceptable; we have no claim against them.
column2: 私下复仇完全可以接受；我们对他们没有诉讼理由。

column1: Heort made the laws so we would not have to rely on vengeance alone.
column2: 赫奥特制定了法律，这样我们就不必只依赖复仇。

column1: They belong to our tribe; we can expect a fair hearing at the tribal moot.
column2: 他们属于我们的部落；我们可以期待在部落大会上得到公正的审理。

column1: The rest of our tribe is getting tired of this fighting, and will judge fairly to end it.
column2: 我们部落的其他成员已厌倦这场争斗，会公正裁决以终止它。

column1: The nastiest revenge is not always the bloodiest.
column2: 最恶毒的复仇并不总是最血腥的。

column1: The people will be happy if we do nothing.
column2: 如果我们什么都不做，人民会高兴。

column1: Do something that doesn’t delay the planting.
column2: 做点不会耽误播种的事。

column1: Do something that doesn’t delay the harvest.
column2: 做点不会耽误收获的事。

column1: This situation calls for a dirty poem.
column2: 这种情况需要一首下流的诗歌。

column1: This situation calls for the grey-beards. And the brown- and blond- and red-beards, too.
column2: 这种情况需要长者们。还有棕须、金须和红须的长者们。

column1: This situation calls for impassioned pleas, breast-beating, and chest-thumping.
column2: 这种情况需要激昂的恳求、捶胸顿足、拍胸脯表态。

column1: Before he wounded him with his sword, Oskul wounded Bad King Urgrain with a clever satire.
column2: 在奥库尔用剑砍伤他之前，他用一首巧妙的讽刺诗先伤了恶王乌格兰。

column1: Orlanth undermined the Bad Emperor with scathing kennings. The Emperor heard Orlanth’s verses sung by his birds and mooed by his cattle. This is why all the Emperor’s minions helped Orlanth when he came to rescue Ernalda.
column2: 奥兰斯用尖刻的复合譬喻削弱了恶皇帝。皇帝听到他的鸟儿吟唱奥兰斯的诗句，他的牛群哞叫奥兰斯的诗行。这就是为什么当奥兰斯前来拯救厄纳尔达时，皇帝的所有仆从都帮助了他。

column1: We speak before we fight, we sing before we hit.
column2: 我们在战斗前说话，在出手前歌唱。

column1: Find a peaceful solution.
column2: 寻找一个和平的解决方案。

column1: Unlike most of the problems we face, this will one not drain our treasury.
column2: 与我们面对的大多数问题不同，这一个不会耗尽我们的国库。

column1: This problem could even gain us cows.
column2: 这个问题甚至能为我们赢得牛只。

column1: Words are cheap.
column2: 空话不值钱。

column1: Hire a poet.
column2: 雇佣一位诗人。

column1: No matter what we say, this will not end until more blood is shed.
column2: 无论我们说什么，除非再流更多血，这事不会了结。

column1: The civilized thing to do is to launch a legal claim.
column2: 文明的做法是发起法律诉讼。

column1: Another of our carls was found dead, a victim of secret murder.
column2: 我们又一名自由民被发现死亡，是秘密谋杀的受害者。

column1: One of our carls was found dead, a victim of secret murder.
column2: 我们的一名自由民被发现死亡，是秘密谋杀的受害者。

column1: What do you do now?
column2: 你现在怎么做？

column1: Send a war party to punish outlaws.
column2: 派出战团惩罚不法之徒。

column1: We knew they were right to wonder, because the god-talkers said our ancestors were angry with us.
column2: 我们知道他们怀疑得有道理，因为神言者说我们的祖先对我们发怒。

column1: Blame Chaos cultists within your own clan.
column2: 怪罪自己氏族内的混沌邪教徒。

column1: \x01@N interrogated the people, but discovered no one who was worshipping Chaos. The people were afraid, and everyone wondered if his neighbor was not harboring murderous thoughts.
column2: \x01@N 审问了民众，但没有发现任何崇拜混沌的人。民众很害怕，每个人都怀疑自己的邻居是否心怀杀意。

column1: Blame no one; console the people.
column2: 谁也不怪；安抚民众。

column1: The clan ring tried to console the people.
column2: 氏族议会试图安抚民众。

column1: The people would not be consoled. “How can you say pretty words,” they asked, “when a murderer roams free?”
column2: 民众不接受安抚。“你们怎能说漂亮话，”他们问道，“当凶手逍遥法外时？”

column1: The people roared for vengeance.
column2: 民众怒吼着要求复仇。

column1: You could take the matter to the moot, or bide your time. Do you bring this up before the moot?
column2: 你可以将此事提交议会，或等待时机。你要在议会前提出此事吗？

column1: With some difficulty, the ring made the people understand the need for patience before vengeance.
column2: 长老会费了些力气，让民众明白复仇前需要耐心。

column1: Blame the \x01@! clan.
column2: 怪罪 \x01@! 氏族。

column1: We blamed the \x01@! clan.
column2: 我们怪罪 \x01@! 氏族。

column1: This is the work of the cowardly \x01@a clan; they cannot beat us on the battlefield, so they resort to secret murder!
column2: 这是懦弱的 \x01@a 氏族干的；他们在战场上打不过我们，所以诉诸秘密谋杀！

column1: This is the work of bandits!
column2: 这是匪徒干的！

column1: This is the work of bandits; the hills are full of them.
column2: 这是匪徒干的；山里到处都是他们。

column1: This is the work of bandits. There is a gang of them in the hills nearby, and they drink bad wine that makes them crazy enough to kill for no reason.
column2: 这是匪徒干的。附近山里有一帮匪徒，他们喝劣酒，喝到疯狂，无缘无故杀人。

column1: The \x01@a clan have run out of ways to insult us, so now they stoop to secret murder.
column2: \x01@a 氏族已经用尽侮辱我们的方式，现在他们沦落到秘密谋杀。

column1: It is either the \x01@a or \x01@! clan that is responsible for this terrible act.
column2: 要么是 \x01@a 氏族，要么是 \x01@! 氏族对这件可怕的事负责。

column1: We can’t rule out a member of our own clan.
column2: 我们不能排除我们自己氏族的成员。

column1: We still can’t rule out a member of our own clan, though it’s unlikely.
column2: 我们仍然不能排除我们自己氏族的成员，尽管不太可能。

column1: We can’t rule out a member of our own clan. And one of our own would do this only if trapped under the stinking yoke of Chaos.
column2: 我们不能排除我们自己氏族的成员。而我们自己人会这样做，只有当陷入混沌的恶臭枷锁之下时。

column1: We must check ourselves again, to sniff out if the stink of Chaos is coming from us.
column2: 我们必须再次自省，嗅出混沌的恶臭是否来自我们自身。

column1: This stinks of Chaos. Let me interrogate the people, and I will find the betrayer.
column2: 这有混沌的臭味。让我审问民众，我会找到背叛者。

column1: This reeks of Chaos. Once more, I will interrogate the people. This time I will find the betrayer.
column2: 这散发着混沌的恶臭。我会再次审问民众。这次我会找到背叛者。

column1: None of us saw what happened, but the spirits of our ancestors surely did.
column2: 我们谁也没看到发生了什么，但我们祖先之灵肯定看到了。

column1: None of us saw what happened, but the spirits of our ancestors surely did. Our magic is strong, so we are certain to reach them.
column2: 我们谁也没看到发生了什么，但我们祖先之灵肯定看到了。我们的魔法强大，所以我们一定能接触到他们。

column1: Call upon the spirits of our ancestors, who see all that happens. Surely they will lead us to the answer.
column2: 呼唤我们祖先之灵，他们目睹一切。他们一定会引导我们找到答案。

column1: If only our magic were stronger; the spirits of our ancestors could tell us who did this.
column2: 要是我们的魔法更强就好了；祖先之灵就能告诉我们是谁干的。

column1: Why does something this awful have to happen during planting season?
column2: 为什么这么可怕的事偏偏发生在播种季节？

column1: Why does something this awful have to happen during the harvest?
column2: 为什么这么可怕的事偏偏发生在收获时节？

column1: If people know you did it, killing a person is sometimes bad, but never unforgivable. Secret murder, on the other hand…
column2: 如果人们知道是你做的，杀人有时是坏事，但从不不可原谅。但秘密谋杀……

column1: Secret murder is one of the worst things an Orlanthi can do. And no true Orlanthi would do it.
column2: 秘密谋杀是奥兰斯人能做的最坏的事之一。而真正的奥兰斯人不会这么做。

column1: By Urox’s stones of manhood, this has to be the work of Chaos!
column2: 以乌洛克斯的男子气概之石起誓，这一定是混沌的勾当！

column1: I still \x02\x02smell/sniff\x02 the \x02\x03reek/putrid stench/stink\x02 of Chaos in this!
column2: 我仍然 \x02\x02闻到/嗅到\x02  \x02\x03恶臭/腐臭/臭味\x02 混沌在其中！

column1: We must be ever-vigilant against the scourge of banditry.
column2: 我们必须时刻警惕匪患的祸害。

column1: The \x01@! clan did this, and only our fiercest attack can make things right.
column2: \x01@! 氏族干了这事，唯有我们最猛烈的攻击才能纠正。

column1: The \x01@a clan did this, and only our fiercest attack can make things right.
column2: \x01@a 氏族干了这事，唯有我们最猛烈的攻击才能纠正。

column1: This is the price we pay for greatness; the jealousy of others leads to murder.
column2: 这是我们为伟大付出的代价；他人的嫉妒导致谋杀。

column1: If we were more generous towards others, this sort of thing wouldn’t happen.
column2: 如果我们对他人更慷慨，这种事就不会发生。

column1: We will have to find a new bride for her husband, after a suitable time has passed.
column2: 过一段合适的时间后，我们必须为她丈夫找一位新新娘。

column1: We slew \x01A_ of them, and either captured the others or drove them off.
column2: 我们杀了他们 \x01A_ 人，要么俘虏了其他人，要么赶走了他们。

column1: \x02\x04an old man who was thought of as kindly and learned/a crafter well-skilled in pottery/one of our laziest farmers/a cottar who had taken to mumbling to himself all the time\x02, had gone mad, and
column2: \x02\x04一位被认为仁慈博学的老人/一位精通陶器的工匠/我们最懒惰的农夫之一/一个整天自言自语的小佃农\x02，发疯了，而且

column1: \x02\x04followed the bidding of a red monster that appeared to him in dreams/listened to voices he heard in the ground/was under the spell of evil whispers he heard from the rocks/obeyed an eyeless spirit that only he could see\x02.
column2: \x02\x04听从了梦中出现的红色怪物的命令/听从了在地底听到的声音/被从岩石听到的邪恶低语施了咒/服从了只有他能看见的无眼之灵\x02。

column1: We outlawed him and slew him, and the people were both happy and sad. They were \x02\x03glad/relieved/happy\x02 that the source of Chaos had been found and expunged, but
column2: 我们将他逐出氏族并斩杀，民众既欣喜又悲伤。他们 \x02\x03高兴/如释重负/欣慰\x02 于混沌之源已被发现并清除，但

column1: \x02\x03dismayed/sorry/sad\x02 that it had claimed two good clan members — one through murder, and the other through madness.
column2: \x02\x03沮丧/遗憾/悲伤\x02 于它夺走了两位优秀的氏族成员——一人死于谋杀，另一人则因疯狂而亡。

column1: \x01@N interrogated the people, and realized that our suspicions were wrong. There were no Chaos cultists in our clan. The people were relieved to hear this conclusion.
column2: \x01@N 审问了民众，意识到我们的怀疑错了。氏族中并无混沌邪教徒。民众听到这一结论后如释重负。

column1: \x01@N spoke noble and soothing words, and the people were consoled.
column2: \x01@N 说了一些高尚而安抚的话语，民众得到了慰藉。

column1: The people cheered loudly when they knew we had taken our revenge.
column2: 当民众得知我们已复仇时，他们高声欢呼。

column2: sceneR369

column1: Carls of your clan are excited to see a rainbow touch down in one of your fields. As Orlanthi, you are Storm People, and there are few omens as positive as a rainbow, the beautiful gift left by the gods in the wake of a storm. It meant we were due for a time of good luck.
column2: 你氏族的自由民看到一道彩虹降落在你们的某片田地里，兴奋不已。作为奥兰斯信徒，你们是风暴之民，几乎没有比彩虹更吉利的征兆了——那是神祇在暴风雨后留下的美丽馈赠。它意味着我们即将迎来一段好运时光。

column1: We saw a rainbow; the people were cheered by this good omen.
column2: 我们看到了彩虹；民众因这吉兆而振奋。

column1: We were content with knowledge that the gods had smiled upon us.
column2: 得知神祇曾向我们微笑，我们心满意足。

column1: Embark on a raid.
column2: 发起一次袭击。

column1: Because we were lucky, we embarked on a raid.
column2: 因为我们幸运，我们发起了一次袭击。

column1: We thanked Orlanth that the rainbow landed in our tula instead of in the \x01@! fields.
column2: 我们感谢奥兰斯，彩虹落在我们的图拉领地而非 \x01@! 田地。

column1: We wondered if we were mistaken by interpreting the sign of the gods’ blessing as a signal to attack our neighbors.
column2: 我们怀疑自己是否误解了神祇赐福的征兆，将其当作攻击邻族的信号。

column1: Pursue trade opportunities.
column2: 寻求贸易机会。

column1: Because we were lucky, we decided to pursue trade opportunities.
column2: 因为我们幸运，我们决定寻求贸易机会。

column1: Our traders said that our good luck would turn into silver for years to come.
column2: 我们的商人说，我们的好运将在未来数年里化为银钱。

column1: Make friends with another clan.
column2: 与另一个氏族结为友邦。

column1: With this blessing, we sought to build friendships.
column2: 承此赐福，我们努力建立友谊。

column1: Which clan do you wish to improve your relations with?
column2: 你希望与哪个氏族改善关系？

column1: We went to our enemies, the \x01@! clan, to make a speech about friendship between our two clans. Though they glowered, they did not throw us off their tula and even appeared to listen to us.
column2: 我们前往我们的敌人—— \x01@! 氏族，发表了一场关于两族友谊的演说。尽管他们怒目而视，却没有将我们赶出他们的图拉领地，甚至似乎听我们说了话。

column1: The chief and thanes of the \x01@! clan pledged their friendship to us.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的酋长与领主们向我们宣誓了友谊。

column1: Thank the gods with a sacrifice.
column2: 用献祭感谢神祇。

column1: How much do you want to sacrifice?
column2: 你打算献祭多少？

column1: We thanked the gods with a sacrifice.
column2: 我们用献祭感谢了神祇。

column1: The gods returned our gift.
column2: 神祇回报了我们的祭品。

column1: The gods will dislike us if we waste their gift of luck on a raid.
column2: 若我们将他们赐予的好运用在一次袭击上，神祇会厌恶我们。

column1: Now that we are lucky, it is time to strike!
column2: 现在我们交了好运，正是出击之时！

column1: Now that we are lucky, it is time to strike! The \x01@a clan is fat and complacent, and deserves to taste the fury of our blades.
column2: 现在我们交了好运，正是出击之时！ \x01@a 氏族肥硕而自满，该尝尝我们刀刃的怒火了。

column1: Now that we are lucky, it is time to strike! The \x01@u clan is weak, and we can easily beat them.
column2: 现在我们交了好运，正是出击之时！ \x01@u 氏族弱小，我们可以轻易击败他们。

column1: Luck has nothing to do with trade. The clever trader makes his own luck.
column2: 运气与贸易无关。聪明的商人自己创造运气。

column1: The clever trader knows when to seize on good luck, and turn it into silver and cows.
column2: 聪明的商人知道何时抓住好运，将其化为银钱和牛只。

column1: No one else will care about this rainbow.
column2: 其他任何人不会在意这道彩虹。

column1: Others who hear about this rainbow will want to be our friends.
column2: 其他听到这道彩虹的人会想成为我们的朋友。

column1: Others who hear about this rainbow will want to be our friends. We should court the favor of the \x01@r clan, who are on the verge of a feud with us.
column2: 其他听到这道彩虹的人会想成为我们的朋友。我们应该争取 \x01@r 氏族的恩惠，他们正濒临与我们的世仇。

column1: The rainbow is good, but it will not strengthen our clan magic.
column2: 彩虹虽好，但不会增强我们的氏族魔法。

column1: The appearance of the rainbow strengthens our clan magic. If we do nothing, we will keep its blessing for a time when we really need it.
column2: 彩虹的出现增强了我们的氏族魔法。若我们什么都不做，就能保留其赐福，留到真正需要之时。

column1: If we sacrifice to the gods now that the gods are already smiling upon us, it will cost us less to get their attention.
column2: 既然神祇已向我们微笑，此时向他们献祭，获取他们关注的代价会更小。

column1: Our clan magic has been weak for a long time. We should not squander the rainbow’s blessing.
column2: 我们的氏族魔法已经衰弱很久了。我们不应浪费彩虹的赐福。

column1: The gods might take great offense if we use this blessing to raid when we are supposed to be planting.
column2: 若我们在本该播种之时利用这个赐福去袭击，神祇可能会大为恼怒。

column1: The gods might take great offense if we use this blessing to raid when we are supposed to be harvesting.
column2: 若我们在本该收割之时利用这个赐福去袭击，神祇可能会大为恼怒。

column1: The year after the death of Errarth, the tragic king, a rainbow kissed the spot where he breathed his last.
column2: 在悲剧国王埃拉斯去世后的那一年，一道彩虹亲吻了他咽气的地点。

column1: Why, the colors, the shining-ness of… I’m sorry. “Shining-ness” is not a proper word, is it?
column2: 哎呀，那色彩，那闪亮……抱歉。“闪亮性”不是一个恰当的用词，对吧？

column1: We have been blessed. It would be rude to turn our blessing into someone else’s defeat.
column2: 我们受到了赐福。将我们的赐福变成他人的败绩，那将是无礼之举。

column1: Dragonewts love rainbows.
column2: 龙人喜爱彩虹。

column1: Good luck is always followed by bad.
column2: 好运之后总是跟着厄运。

column1: I told you good luck was just around the bend.
column2: 我告诉过你好运就在不远处。

column1: If we make an alliance with another clan, they will be more likely to gift us with a treasure.
column2: 如果我们与另一个氏族结成联盟，他们更有可能馈赠我们一件宝物。

column1: We must do something manly with this gift of luck.
column2: 我们必须用这运气之礼做些男人气概的事。

column2: sceneR370

column1: The two captured fellows came back. Although they told a different story, some of the clan women thought they had engaged in adultery with the outlaw women.
column2: 那两个被俘的家伙回来了。尽管他们讲的故事不同，一些氏族女人认为他们与被放逐的女人通奸了。

column1: Convince the women that nothing untoward happened.
column2: 说服女人们，没有发生任何不轨之事。

column1: \x01@N told the women that they should not think that something untoward had happened.
column2: \x01@N 告诉女人们，她们不应认为发生了不轨之事。

column1: The women agreed that it was not right to treat suspicion as fact, and there the matter rested.
column2: 女人们同意，将怀疑当作事实是不对的，事情就此了结。

column1: The clan ring did not pursue the matter further.
column2: 氏族议会没有进一步追究此事。

column1: Send a war party to drive off the outlaws.
column2: 派遣一支战团驱赶那些被放逐者。

column1: We sent a war party to drive off the outlaws.
column2: 我们派出了一支战团去驱逐那些法外人。

column1: We did not find the women outlaws. They must have known that we would be outraged, and had already left the area.
column2: 我们没有找到那些女法外人。她们必定知道我们会震怒，早已离开了这片区域。

column1: We found the women outlaws and did battle with them. They were clearly in no mood for a fight, and were easily driven off.
column2: 我们找到了那些女法外人并与之交战。她们显然毫无战意，轻易就被驱散了。

column1: Send a war party to slay the outlaws.
column2: 派出战团去斩杀法外人。

column1: We sent a war party to slay the outlaws.
column2: 我们派出了一支战团去斩杀法外人。

column1: We found the women outlaws and did battle with them.
column2: 我们找到了那些女法外人并与之交战。

column1: We slew \x01@\x11 of them, and the others fled. Everyone celebrated our victory over these women, who flouted all Orlanthi standards of decency.
column2: 我们斩杀了 \x01@\x11 个，其余的都逃了。所有人都为战胜这些无视一切奥兰提斯体面准则的女人而欢庆。

column1: They struck at us fiercely, using many powerful magics. One threw shining bolts at our warriors, which hurt them and caused them to draw back in pain. Another had a blade that blazed blue flame. Some of our warriors were slain, and others were injured.
column2: 她们猛烈地攻击我们，使用了众多强大的法术。其中一人向我们的战士投掷灼烧的射线，击伤他们，使他们痛苦地后退。另一人握着一柄燃着蓝焰的利刃。我们的一些战士阵亡，另一些受了伤。

column1: \x01@\r, who led the party, was among the slain, \x04 head sliced clean off by the outlaw’s blue-flame blade.
column2: \x01@\r是这支队伍的领袖，也战死在那场厮杀中， \x04 的头颅被法外人的蓝焰之刃齐颈斩下。

column1: Do you outlaw them?
column2: 你们要流放他们吗？

column1: We outlawed both adulterers; the people said we had behaved in a just manner.
column2: 我们流放了那对通奸者；民众说我们行事公正。

column1: We pardoned them, because what they had done, they did under duress.
column2: 我们宽恕了他们，因为他们所为是出于胁迫。

column1: These fellows are telling the truth.

column1: The truth has many virtues, but it does not help you sleep at night.
column2: 真相有许多好处，但它并不能让你安眠。

column1: We must not shirk from our duty, even if it is unpleasant.
column2: 我们绝不能推卸责任，即使这令人不快。

column2: 睡着的林猫最好别去惊扰。

column1: Do not listen to the constant complaints of the women; they are too vengeful, and do not know when to let a matter rest.
column2: 别听女人们没完没了的抱怨；她们太记仇了，不知何时该放下。

column1: You cannot blame the young fellows; what they did, they did while captured.

column1: This is not the usual case of shilly-shallying in the bushes. We must determine the truth.
column2: 这不是那种在灌木丛里偷偷摸摸的寻常勾当。我们必须查明真相。

column2: 我们已经宽恕了父亲们，现在又收养了孩子们。没有人抱怨，事实上婴儿们健壮的四肢和欢快的咿呀声软化了氏族里仅存的铁石心肠。

column1: They departed, laughing. “Do you not think we would know better than you who sired our children?”

Some of our warriors were killed in the attempt, and others were wounded. We hoped that we could use the blue blade as a treasure, but could not figure out how to use it.
column2: 那些女法外人看到我们的意图时像可怕的野兽般嚎叫，并用强大的法术反击，包括痛苦射线和一柄蓝焰之刃。我们的一些战士在行动中阵亡，另一些受了伤。我们希望那柄蓝刃能用作宝物，但不知如何使用。

column1: Kill the women; take the children.

column2: 那些女法外人用强大的法术反击，包括痛苦射线和一柄蓝焰之刃。许多战士在战斗中受伤。我们希望那柄蓝刃能用作宝物，但不知如何使用。

column1: Tell them to keep the children.

column1: We outlawed both adulterers; the women were satisfied, and said that good laws must sometimes be enforced without mercy.
column2: 我们将两名通奸者放逐；女人们表示满意，并说道，好的法律有时必须毫不留情地执行。

column1: We pardoned them, because, even though they had lied, they had committed their original crimes under duress.
