column1: \x01@N explained this to the women, who protested. “Good laws must sometimes be enforced without mercy,” they said.
column2: \x01@N 向女人们解释了这一点，她们表示抗议。“好的法律有时必须毫不留情地执行，”她们说。

column1: We outlawed both adulterers; the people said we behaved justly in this.
column2: 我们将两名通奸者放逐；人们说我们在这件事上行事公正。

column1: They are the children of adultery, and so must die.
column2: 他们是通奸所生的孩子，因此必须死。

column1: There are precedents for killing the outlaws, outlawing the men, and slaying the children. But these are cruel precedents, not often cited.
column2: 有处死被放逐者、放逐男人、斩杀孩子的先例。但这些都是残酷的先例，不常被引用。

column1: Outlaws must die!
column2: 被放逐者必须死！

column1: If we kill these two, we will eliminate the threat of bandits in the area.
column2: 如果我们杀了这两个人，就能消除该地区的匪患威胁。

column1: If we kill these two, their fellows will come seeking vengeance.
column2: 如果我们杀了这两个人，他们的同伙会来寻仇。

column1: Our women will be angry if we do nothing about admitted adultery. We must deny this.
column2: 如果我们对承认的通奸行为无所作为，我们的女人会愤怒。我们必须否认此事。

column1: We have already pardoned the men for their adultery, so the people have no reason to be perturbed.
column2: 我们已经赦免了那些男人的通奸罪，所以人们没有理由感到不安。

column1: I have heard that these women wield powerful magics; it might not be wise to attack them.
column2: 我听说这些女人掌握强大的魔法；攻击她们可能不是明智之举。

column1: We need young ones to grow up and work the fields.
column2: 我们需要年轻人长大并耕种田地。

column1: Our clan lacks children. We need these babes, whether they are half ours or not.
column2: 我们氏族缺少孩子。我们需要这些婴儿，无论他们是否一半是我们的血脉。

column1: Children can be born as criminals. Bad King Urgrain was born when he tore through his mother’s womb four weeks early. Some said he was like a broo; others, that his birth was his mother’s murder.
column2: 孩子也可能生而为罪犯。恶王乌格兰出生时，提前四周撕裂了母亲的子宫。有人说他像布洛；也有人说，他的出生就是谋杀母亲。

column1: A law that cannot be enforced harshly is no law at all.
column2: 无法严厉执行的法律根本不算法律。

column1: I once knew a story about this. If only we had it written down…
column2: 我曾经知道一个关于这个的故事。要是我们把它写下来就好了……

column1: Ask them if they know where to find the legendary sword, Chaos Striker.
column2: 问问他们是否知道去哪里寻找传说中的剑，混沌打击者。

column1: There is no escaping a bad act.
column2: 恶行无法逃避。

column1: Do not blame the calves for the bad behavior of the bulls.
column2: 不要因公牛的不良行为而责怪小牛。

column1: Let us accept these new lives, and let this be a new beginning.
column2: 让我们接纳这些新生命，让这成为一个新的开始。

column1: This is not the usual case of an unlawful roll in the hay-pile. A unique circumstance calls for a unique solution.
column2: 这不是普通的在干草堆里非法翻滚的案子。独特的情况需要独特的解决方案。

column1: Your explorers are attacked by Humakti warriors, who mean to avenge what they see as insults against their cult and their god. Their attack is swift and efficient; they leave but one explorer alive. They spare \x01@\x01 for one reason only — to tell the tale to the rest of the clan.
column2: 你们的探险队遭到胡马克提战士的攻击，他们意图报复那些他们认为对其教派和神祇的侮辱。他们的攻击迅速而高效；只留一名探险者活口。他们饶恕 \x01@\x01 只有一个原因——将此事禀告氏族人。

column1: Humakti warriors slew almost every member of one of our exploration parties. They told \x01@\x01, who was the only one left alive, that we had insulted them and their god, and thus deserved their attack.
column2: 胡马克提战士杀死了我们一支探险队几乎全体成员。他们告诉 \x01@\x01——唯一的幸存者——说我们侮辱了他们的教派和神祇，因此理应受到攻击。

column1: The people complained that we were courting disaster.
column2: 人们抱怨说我们是在自招灾祸。

column1: Sacrifice to Humakt, to show you have not meant to offend him.
column2: 向胡马克特献祭，以表明你无意冒犯他。

column1: How much do you sacrifice to Humakt?
column2: 你向胡马克特献祭多少？

column1: We sacrificed to Humakt, to show we did not mean to offend him.
column2: 我们向胡马克特献祭，以表明我们无意冒犯他。

column1: The god-talkers said that Humakt gladly received our sacrifice and granted us his blessing. The hatred of the Humakti was another matter.
column2: 神言者说胡马克特欣然接受了我们的献祭，并赐予我们他的祝福。而胡马克提战士的仇恨则是另一回事。

column1: Send a delegation to gift the Humakti.
column2: 派遣使团向胡马克提战士赠送礼物。

column1: We sent a delegation to gift the Humakti.
column2: 我们派遣使团向胡马克提战士赠送了礼物。

column1: The grim Humakti accepted our gifts, and said that they would no longer see us as their enemies.
column2: 冷酷的胡马克提战士接受了我们的礼物，并说他们将不再视我们为敌人。

column1: The grim Humakti said that our paltry offer was merely evidence of further insult, and that we should not think about sending out explorers until we had seen the error of our ways.
column2: 冷酷的胡马克提战士说，我们微薄的奉献只是进一步侮辱的证据，在我们认识到自己的错误之前，不应再考虑派出探险队。

column1: Send a war party to attack the Humakti.
column2: 派遣一支战队攻击胡马克提战士。

column1: We sent a war party to attack the Humakti.
column2: 我们派遣了一支战队攻击胡马克提战士。

column1: We did not find the Humakt cultists we were looking for.
column2: 我们没有找到我们要找的胡马克特信徒。

column1: We found the Humakt cultists we were looking for and did battle with them.
column2: 我们找到了我们要找的胡马克特信徒，并与他们交战。

column1: The Humakti are too proud and honorable to accept any gifts from those they deem to have insulted them.
column2: 胡马克提战士过于骄傲和尊贵，不会接受那些他们认为侮辱过他们的人的礼物。

column1: Humakti are grim, but not so grim that they’ll refuse gifts.
column2: 胡马克提战士冷酷，但不至于冷酷到拒绝礼物。

column1: We must give them goods worth at least \x01@\x16 cows.
column2: 我们必须给他们价值至少 \x01@\x16 头牛的货物。

column1: We must give them goods worth at least \x01@\x17 cows.
column2: 我们必须给他们价值至少 \x01@\x17 头牛的货物。

column1: We must give them goods worth at least \x01@\x18 cows.
column2: 我们必须给他们价值至少 \x01@\x18 头牛的货物。

column1: Humakti are above the law.
column2: 胡马克提战士凌驾于法律之上。

column1: Humakti think they are above the law.
column2: 胡马克提战士认为他们凌驾于法律之上。

column1: Humakti sometimes think they are above the law. Even if they were, they may not be above the persuasive powers of gifts.
column2: 胡马克提战士有时认为他们凌驾于法律之上。即便他们真的如此，也许也无法抗拒礼物的说服力。

column1: Blood vengeance is our only recourse.
column2: 血亲复仇是我们唯一的办法。

column1: We could fight the Humakti, but in the arts of war, they are second to none.
column2: 我们可以与胡马克提战士战斗，但在战争技艺上，他们无与伦比。

column1: To attack the Humakti would be sheer folly.
column2: 攻击胡马克提战士纯粹是愚蠢之举。

column1: We must improve our relations with these dangerous warriors.
column2: 我们必须改善与这些危险战士的关系。

column1: What rashness is this? Let alone making war during Sea season, we’d be stupendously foolish to attack these warriors.
column2: 这是何等鲁莽？且不说在海季发动战争，攻击这些战士简直是愚蠢至极。

column1: What rashness is this? Let alone making war during Earth season, we’d be stupendously foolish to attack these warriors.
column2: 这是何等鲁莽？且不说在地季发动战争，攻击这些战士简直是愚蠢至极。

column1: If we sacrifice to Humakt now, we will get nothing but bad luck.
column2: 如果我们现在向胡马克特献祭，只会招来厄运。

column1: It is one thing to have Humakti angry at us, but another to have Humakt himself angry!
column2: 胡马克特信徒对我们发怒是一回事，但胡马克特本神发怒是另一回事！

column1: Humakt is not angry at us; the Humakti are.
column2: 对我们发怒的不是胡马克特，而是那些胡马克特信徒。

column1: After Humakt made himself a stranger, he and Orlanth fought, and found a new position for Humakt in society.
column2: 胡马克特使自己成为陌客之后，他与奥兰斯战斗，并为胡马克特在社会中找到了新的位置。

column1: Gift them, or leave them alone.
column2: 要么送礼给他们，要么别管他们。

column1: I am glad that the warriors of Vinga are not so lawless.
column2: 我很高兴维加的女战士们并非如此无法无天。

column1: It is sometimes good to feud, but it is also sometimes good to make peace.
column2: 有时结仇有利，但有时和解也是好事。

column1: We must not risk Humakt’s wrath.
column2: 我们绝不能冒犯胡马克特的怒火。

column1: Why would they — the explorers did nothing to — just a big gang of — !
column2: 他们为什么要——那些探险者什么都没做——就是一大帮——！

column1: If we had a temple to Humakt, they wouldn’t treat us like this.
column2: 如果我们有一座胡马克特的神庙，他们就不会这样对待我们了。

column1: If we were on better terms with the dragonewts, they would protect us from the death-loving Humakti.
column2: 如果我们与龙人的关系更好，他们会保护我们不受那些热爱死亡的胡马克特信徒侵扰。

column2: 我们寻找了公正的证人。

column1: Try to broker a different kind of peace between them.
column2: 尝试在他们之间斡旋另一种和平。

column1: We can gang up and beat whoever we choose, but I’m not sure that’s the point.
column2: 我们可以联合起来打败任何我们选中的对手，但我不确定那是重点。

column1: Much as I would relish another victory, another tribal war won’t solve anything. Try something else.
column2: 尽管我很想再赢一场，但另一场部落战争解决不了任何问题。试试别的办法。

column1: Impartial witnesses will not step forward.

column2: 我们应该寻找公正的证人。

column2: 我们应该寻找公正的证人；在他们的帮助下，我可以筛选出真相。

column1: They are both in the wrong. But we may have been mistaken to threaten them in the first place.

column1: No one will blame us if we wash our hands of this matter.

column1: Lawspeakers from the formerly warring tribes came to demand that we pay the difference in a trade dispute between them, which we had promised to do during the peace negotiations.

column1: Our people were glad that we had freed ourselves from a fool’s obligation. But both delegations swore that we had broken our word, and that everyone would know that we were not to be listened to when important matters were at stake.

column1: If we dedicate the town to Issaries, he will grant us luck, and the esteem of others.
column2: 如果我们把城镇奉献给伊萨里斯，他会赐予我们好运，以及他人的敬重。

column1: Issaries is pleased by towns; if we embark on his heroquest now, we will have a greater than normal chance of success.
column2: 伊萨里斯喜爱城镇；如果我们现在踏上他的英雄探索之路，成功的几率会比平常更大。

column1: Issaries is pleased by towns. He will favor us if we dedicate it to him.
column2: 伊萨里斯喜爱城镇。如果我们把它奉献给他，他会眷顾我们。

column1: Our most famous ancestors all went on heroquests.
column2: 我们最著名的先祖都曾踏上英雄任务。

column1: Let us be generous, so that tongues will repeat the tale of our name and our town.
column2: 让我们慷慨一些，这样人们就会传颂我们的名字和城镇的故事。

column1: The Talk-Too-Much God can be useful, but do not raise him up above Orlanth, who made the laws.

column1: I am glad there are no violent choices before us, for once.
column2: 我很高兴这一次我们面前没有暴力的选项。

column2: 我们必须保持警惕，否则城镇会被不死街头艺人 infestation。

column2: 我们必须确保女人们不会用她们冒犯的行为和古怪的方式毁掉这座美丽的城镇。

column1: We must make sure that the men behave properly in this new town, and do not bring it to ruin.
column2: 我们必须确保男人们在这座新城里行为得体，不让它走向毁灭。

column1: The learned man, no matter how great his knowledge, is rarely happy.
column2: 有学识的人，无论知识多么渊博，很少真正快乐。

column1: This town will be the ruin of us all.
column2: 这座城镇会是我们所有人的葬身之地。

column1: We must honor Issaries, patron of markets.
column2: 我们必须尊崇市场之神伊萨里斯。

column2: 泰尔莫里人领着 \x01@\x05 来到一具尸架前，上面躺着他们被杀的首领弗拉林·溪跃者。“如果你们能让他复活，”他们说，“我们就与你们讲和。如果失败，我们就会杀了你们，正如我们承诺的那样。”

column1: The Telmori took \x01@\x05 to the bier of their slain chieftain.
column2: 泰尔莫里人带着 \x01@\x05 走向他们被杀首领的尸架。

column1: Convince them that you can lift their curse.

column1: \x01@\x05 told them that they would no longer be doomed to wander the earth, for
column2: \x01@\x05 告诉他们，他们不再注定要永世流浪，因为

column1: was creating a new kingdom here in Dragon Pass, and they could be part of it. “It will not be magic that lifts this curse,” \x01@\x05 said, “but talk of peace, which is its own kind of magic.”
column2: 正在龙之隘口建立一个新王国，而他们可以成为其中一部分。“解除这个诅咒的不会是魔法，” \x01@\x05 说，“而是和平的对话——那本身就是一种魔法。”

column1: The Telmori were swayed by this prophecy, and agreed that they would come and talk peace, once they had chosen a new chieftain to replace Vraling Creekleaper.
column2: 泰尔莫里人被这个预言打动，同意一旦他们选出一位新首领接替弗拉林·溪跃者，就会前来谈和。

column1: Kostajor Many-Whelps
column2: 科斯塔乔·多崽者

column1: The Telmori circled around \x01@\x05, growling to one another. It seemed at first that they liked \x01@\x05’s prophecy, but then the entire encampment of wolf-warriors swarmed down upon \x01@\x05 and \x04 guardians, slaying them all.
column2: 泰尔莫里人围着 \x01@\x05打转，彼此低吼着。起初他们似乎喜欢 \x01@\x05的预言，但随后整个狼战士营地蜂拥扑向 \x01@\x05 和 \x04 的护卫，将他们全部杀死。

column1: Magically create a new chieftain.
column2: 用魔法创造一位新首领。

column1: \x01@\x05 tried to magically create a new chieftain.
column2: \x01@\x05 试图用魔法创造一位新首领。

column1: \x01@\x05 set up a tent and went inside, and began to create a ritual to make a new Telmori chieftain. \x05 stayed there for many hours.
column2: \x01@\x05 支起帐篷走了进去，开始举行仪式，创造一位新的泰尔莫里首领。 \x05 在那里待了好几个小时。

column1: At daybreak, \x06 emerged with a young Telmori no one had ever seen before. Four wolf-brothers bounded from the woods to join this man, who \x01@\x05 introduced as Ostling Four-Wolf. The other Telmori considered this a miracle, for until that day, no one ever had more than one beast brother at a time. Ostling said he would undergo the tests of the Telmori and become their chieftain, and would then come to our tula to talk peace.
column2: 破晓时， \x06 带着一个从没人见过的年轻泰尔莫里人走了出来。四只狼兄弟从树林里跃出，加入这个男子—— \x01@\x05 将他介绍为奥斯特林·四狼。其他泰尔莫里人认为这是奇迹，因为在那之前，从未有人同时拥有超过一只兽兄弟。奥斯特林说他将接受泰尔莫里的考验成为首领，然后会到我们的图拉领地来谈和。

column1: Ostling Four-Wolf
column2: 奥斯特林·四狼

column1: At daybreak, \x06 snuck out of the tent and whispered to \x04 companions: “I have failed. We must flee.” And they did.
column2: 破晓时， \x06 溜出帐篷，低声对 \x04 同伴说：“我失败了。我们得逃。”于是他们逃走了。

column1: Magically revive Vraling.
column2: 用魔法复活弗拉林。

column1: \x01@\x05 tried to magically revive Vraling.
column2: \x01@\x05 试图用魔法复活弗拉林。

column1: Vraling, whose neck was broken, whose body was white from loss of blood, whose chest was torn open, writhed and stirred upon his bier. His broken bones cracked back together again. His body filled with new blood. His wounds sealed up. He sat up on his death pallet and said, “Who has rescued me from the Howling Place?” \x01@\x05 stepped forward and claimed credit for the deed, and also claimed the right to make peace. Vraling promised to meet us in our clan hall in a season’s time.
column2: 弗拉林——他的脖子断了，身体因失血而苍白，胸口被撕开——在尸架上扭动起来。他断裂的骨头咔嚓一声重新接合。他的身体注满新血。伤口愈合了。他在死亡垫上坐起来说：“是谁把我从嚎叫之地救回来的？” \x01@\x05 上前一步，宣称是自己做的，并声称有权缔结和约。弗拉林答应在一个季节后到我们的部族大厅与我们会面。

column1: \x05 tried, but could not find the right magic. \x01@\x05 and \x04 bodyguard ran away from the Telmori encampment.
column2: \x05 尝试了，但找不到正确的魔法。 \x01@\x05 和 \x04 的保镖逃离了泰尔莫里营地。

column1: Magically turn one of your warriors into a Telmori chieftain.
column2: 用魔法将你的一名战士变成泰尔莫里首领。

column1: \x01@\x05 tried to magically turn one of our warriors into a Telmori chieftain.
column2: \x01@\x05 试图用魔法将我们的一名战士变成泰尔莫里首领。

column1: \x01@\x05 set up a tent and went inside. Later, as planned, one of the warriors, whose name was Odgarl, snuck into the tent, too.
column2: \x01@\x05 支起帐篷走了进去。后来，按照计划，一个名叫奥德加尔的战士也溜进了帐篷。

column1: At daybreak, \x06 snuck out of the tent and whispered to \x04 companions: “I have failed; Odgarl is still no Telmori. We must flee.” And they did.
column2: 破晓时， \x06 溜出帐篷，低声对 \x04 同伴说：“我失败了；奥德加尔还不是泰尔莫里人。我们得逃。”于是他们逃走了。

column1: \x01@\x05 and his companions ran away.
column2: \x01@\x05和他的同伴逃跑了。

column1: Although the Telmori hordes pursued them remorselessly, they were able to escape, and returned to our tula unharmed.
column2: 尽管泰尔莫里大军无情地追击，他们还是成功逃脱，毫发无损地回到了我们的图拉领地。

column1: The Telmori hordes were too fast for them, and brought them down. All were slain.
column2: 特摩尔人部族对他们来说太快了，把他们击倒了。所有人都被杀死了。

column1: They want to see us try the impossible, and fail. Instead, let’s give them what they really want.
column2: 他们想看到我们尝试不可能之事，然后失败。不如，我们给他们真正想要的东西。

column1: I can create a new chieftain out of thin air!
column2: 我能凭空创造一个新酋长！

column1: I am neither magician nor prophet. We must flee.
column2: 我既不是法师也不是先知。我们必须逃跑。

column1: I am no magician, but maybe I can convince them that we can lift their curse, which is to wander forever without peace. Or we could just run.
column2: 我不是法师，但也许我能说服他们我们可以解除他们的诅咒——即永无休止地漂泊。或者我们干脆逃跑。

column1: It will be hard, but I know the rituals needed to revive the slain.
column2: 这会很难，但我知道复活死者所需的仪式。

column1: It will be easier to turn one of our people into an Orlanthi than to make a new person out of nothing.
column2: 把我们的人变成一个奥兰提人比凭空创造一个新的人更容易。

column1: They are only looking as far as their noses. What they truly want is a home, not the return of a failed king.
column2: 他们的目光只看到鼻子尖。他们真正想要的是一个家园，而不是一个失败的国王回归。

column1: Maybe, instead, I can convince them that we can lift their curse, which is to wander forever without peace.
column2: 也许，我可以转而说服他们我们能解除他们的诅咒——即永无休止地漂泊。

column1: They have forgotten their true problem. What they need is a home, and an end to their cursed wandering.
column2: 他们忘记了自己真正的问题。他们需要一个家园，以及被诅咒的流浪的终结。

column1: At daybreak, they emerged. Odgarl now looked like a young Telmori. Four wolf-brothers bounded from the woods to join him, and \x01@\x05 introduced him as Ostling Four-Wolf. The other Telmori sniffed him and said that he was one of them. They considered his appearance a miracle — until that day, no one ever had more than one beast brother at a time.
column2: 黎明时分，他们出现了。奥德加尔现在看起来像一个年轻的特摩尔人。四只狼兄弟从树林中跃出加入了他， \x01@\x05 介绍他是奥斯特林·四狼。其他特摩尔人嗅了嗅他，说他是他们的一员。他们认为他的出现是个奇迹——在那天之前，从没有人一次拥有超过一个野兽兄弟。

column1: Ostling said he would undergo the tests of the Telmori and become their chieftain, and would then come to us to talk peace.
column2: 奥斯特林说他将接受特摩尔人的考验，成为他们的酋长，然后来与我们谈和。

column1: \x01@\x0B traveled to the Hidden Temple, where the crone priestess of Maran Gor demanded that \x06 prove that \x06 was worthy enough to learn of the three tests.
column2: \x01@\x0B 前往隐殿，玛兰·戈尔的老女祭司要求 \x06 证明 \x06 有足够的价值了解那三项考验。

column1: Gift her.
column2: 赠予她礼物。

column1: \x01@\x0B chose to give her gifts.
column2: \x01@\x0B 选择赠予她礼物。

column1: What do you offer her?
column2: 你献给她什么？

column1: The crone seemed pleased with the gifts, and said she would tell \x01@\x0B what the tests were.
column2: 老女祭司似乎对礼物很满意，并说她将告诉 \x01@\x0B 考验是什么。

column1: The crone said that she was pleased by the gifts, but not yet pleased enough that she could tell \x01@\x0B from a cottar.
column2: 老女祭司说她对这些礼物很满意，但尚未满意到能告诉 \x01@\x0B 与一个贫农的区别。

column1: Give her a treasure.
column2: 给她一件宝物。

column1: \x01@\x0B gave her a treasure.
column2: \x01@\x0B 给了她一件宝物。

column1: What treasure do you give her?
column2: 你给她什么宝物？

column1: The crone thanked us for this gift, but said she could not accept it. “You have proven that you have the right to learn of the tests,” she said.
column2: 老女祭司感谢我们这份礼物，但说她不能接受。“你们已经证明自己有资格了解考验，”她说。

column1: The crone thanked us for our gift, which she deemed especially appropriate. “You have earned the favor of Maran Gor, and the right to know of the tests,” she said.
column2: 老女祭司感谢我们的礼物，她认为这特别合适。“你们赢得了玛兰·戈尔的恩惠，以及了解考验的权利，”她说。

column1: The crone was pleased with this generous gift, and said she would tell \x01@\x0B what the tests were.
column2: 老女祭司对这份慷慨的礼物很满意，并说她将告诉 \x01@\x0B 考验是什么。

column1: The crone said it was good to have a treasure, but that \x01@\x0B had still not earned the full favor of the Earth-Shaking Goddess.
column2: 老女祭司说有一件宝物是好事，但 \x01@\x0B 仍然没有赢得震地女神的完全恩惠。

column1: Give her thralls to sacrifice.
column2: 给她奴隶作为献祭。

column1: \x01@\x0B chose to give her thralls for sacrifice.
column2: \x01@\x0B 选择给她奴隶用于献祭。

column1: How many thralls?
column2: 多少个奴隶？

column1: The crone’s eyes flashed with greedy delight as she accepted the thralls. “You know the price to open this gate,” she said.
column2: 老女祭司接受奴隶时，眼中闪过贪婪的喜悦。“你知道打开这扇门的代价，”她说。

column1: The crone said that we knew something of the demands of the earth, but she was unsure if we knew enough.
column2: 老女祭司说我们知道一些大地的要求，但她不确定我们是否知道得足够。

column1: Give up on the quest.
column2: 放弃这个任务。

column1: \x01@\x0B abandoned the quest.
column2: \x01@\x0B 放弃了任务。

column1: Remind her of your good relations with the Hidden Temple.
column2: 提醒她你与隐殿的良好关系。

column1: \x01@\x0B reminded the crone of our good relations with the Hidden Temple.
column2: \x01@\x0B 提醒了老女祭司我们与隐殿的良好关系。

column1: “You are a liar and a fool!” she cackled.
column2: “你是个骗子和傻瓜！”她咯咯笑道。

column1: “Your words ring true, and so I shall open the gate to awareness,” the crone said.
column2: “你的话听起来是真的，所以我会打开通往认知的门，”老女祭司说。

column1: The crone muttered something unintelligible, and then said she would share with us the secret of the tests.
column2: 老女祭司喃喃自语一些听不懂的话，然后说她会与我们分享考验的秘密。

column1: “You do not know who you scold, foolish one,” the crone muttered.
column2: “你不知道你在责骂谁，蠢货，”老女祭司咕哝道。

column1: “First,” said the crone, “you must tame a dragon. Then, you must win the favor of the Brass Man.
column2: “首先，”老女祭司说，“你必须驯服一条龙。然后，你必须赢得黄铜人的恩惠。

column1: Finally, you must mate with the mountain, and thereby win the blessing of the goddess Kero Fin.”
column2: 最后，你必须与山脉交配，从而赢得女神凯罗·芬的祝福。”

column1: Finally, you must be reborn as daughter of the mountain, and thereby win the blessing of the goddess Kero Fin.”
column2: 最后，你必须作为山脉的女儿重生，从而赢得女神凯罗·芬的祝福。”

column1: Don’t go giving her cows we can’t afford.
column2: 别把我们负担不起的牛给她。

column1: We can afford to give her cows.
column2: 我们负担得起给她牛。

column1: Any offer of material goods will simply offend her.
column2: 任何物质货物的赠予都只会冒犯她。

column1: The more generous our gift, the greater chance of success we have.
column2: 我们的礼物越慷慨，成功的机会就越大。

column1: Although she will settle for ordinary gifts, she most wants a treasure with an affinity for her temple.
column2: 虽然她会接受普通礼物，但她最想要一件与她的神庙有亲和力的宝物。

column1: Although she will settle for ordinary gifts, and would be pleased by a treasure with an affinity for her temple, she most wants thralls for sacrifice.
column2: 虽然她会接受普通礼物，也会对与神庙有亲和力的宝物感到满意，但她最想要的是用于献祭的奴隶。

column1: It is unlawful to deal with the malign priestesses of the Hidden Temple.
column2: 与隐殿的邪恶女祭司打交道是非法的。

column1: Maran Gor is a frightening goddess, one that wise folk steer clear of.
column2: 玛兰·戈尔是一位可怕的女神，明智之人都会避开。

column1: Although Maran Gor is a frightening goddess, she is Ernalda’s sister, and is not considered an enemy of our people.
column2: 尽管玛兰·戈尔是位可怖的女神，但她也是厄纳尔达的姐妹，不被视作我族的仇敌。

column1: How dare she insult a king?
column2: 她怎敢冒犯一位王者？

column1: It would be unwise to scold her, to say the least.
column2: 至少可以说，责骂她是不明智的。

column1: The Hidden Temple has reason to respect us; it will not hurt to remind them of this.
column2: 隐殿有理由敬重我们；提醒他们这一点并无害处。

column1: The Hidden Temple has reason to dislike us, so it would be folly to claim some right of friendship with them.
column2: 隐殿有理由厌恶我们，因此声称与他们有某种友谊是愚蠢的。

column1: The Hidden Temple has reason to respect us, but its priestesses are truculent, and might not like it if we directly remind them of the favors they owe us.
column2: 隐殿有理由敬重我们，但它的女祭司们好斗，若是我们直接提醒它们欠我们恩惠，她们恐怕会不快。

column1: Although she is a terrifying goddess, Maran Gor fought Chaos with the help of her patron animals, the enormous Earthshakers.
column2: 尽管她是位可怖的女神，玛兰·戈尔仍以其护佑巨兽——巨大的地动者——为助，大战混沌。

column1: Although she serves the earth’s dark side, she serves the earth nonetheless.
column2: 她虽侍奉大地阴暗面，却终究还是侍奉着大地。

column1: Eurmal once looked at Maran Gor’s secret parts, and his eyes rolled out upon the ground, which swallowed them up.
column2: 尤尔马尔曾窥视玛兰·戈尔私密之处，结果他的眼珠滚落在地，被大地吞噬。

column1: She makes me nervous.
column2: 她让我紧张不安。

column1: There is nothing so courteous as a generous gift.
column2: 慷慨赠礼莫过于最礼貌之举。

column1: We helped her!
column2: 我们帮过她！

column1: She’s right. We aren’t worthy.
column2: 她说的对。我们不配。

column1: I told you she wouldn’t just tell us what the tests are.
column2: 我早跟你说过，她不会直接告诉我们考验是什么。

column1: Maran Gor may be bloodthirsty, but at least she is no elf-friend.

column1: Without husbands, there can be no mothers.
column2: 没有丈夫，便没有母亲。

column1: A good king shows mercy to the people.
column2: 好王对子民仁慈。

column1: It can be risky to pursue the favors of a great mother goddess like Kero Fin; if she deems \x01@\x0B unworthy, she will slay him. And this is how it should be.
column2: 追求像凯罗·芬这样伟大的母神之青睐可能有风险；若她认为 \x01@\x0B 不配，便会杀了他。这正是应得的下场。

column1: Tell Kero Fin that we have been stalwart in pursuit of the undead.
column2: 告诉凯罗·芬，我们一直坚定地追杀亡灵。

column1: Tell Kero Fin that we have always been good friends to the dragonewts.
column2: 告诉凯罗·芬，我们一直是龙人的好友。

column1: I can only pray the goddess finds me worthy.
column2: 我只能祈祷女神认为我配得上。

column1: Now that \x01@\x0B has tamed the dragon and won the brass man’s favor, it is time for her to become the daughter of the mountain. Your god-talkers say that the mountain must be Kero Fin, mother of Orlanth and guardian of Dragon Pass. What does \x01@\x0B do in preparation for this mystical transformation?
column2: 既然 \x01@\x0B 已驯服了龙并赢得了黄铜人的欢心，现在是她成为山之女的时候了。你们的神言者说，这座山必定是奥兰斯之母、龙之隘口的守护者凯罗·芬。 \x01@\x0B 要做什么来准备这场神秘的转变？

column1: The god-talkers said that it was time to become the daughter of Kero Fin.
column2: 神言者说，是时候成为凯罗·芬的女儿了。

column1: End your attempt to become Queen of Dragon Pass.
column2: 终止你成为龙之隘口女王的尝试。

column1: \x01@\x0B gave up on becoming Queen of Dragon Pass.
column2: \x01@\x0B 放弃了成为龙之隘口女王。

column1: The queen went into seclusion for three days and three nights.
column2: 女王避世斋戒了三天三夜。

column1: The god-talkers said that the omens were good. They said that \x01@\x0B should enter Kero Fin’s cave clothed, and then leave it naked, taking a new name, so it would be as if she had been born anew.
column2: 神言者说征兆吉利。他们说 \x01@\x0B 应当穿着衣服进入Kero Fin的洞穴，然后裸身离开，取一个新名字，这样她就好比是重生了一般。

column1: The god-talkers said that the omens were bad, and that \x01@\x0B should court Kero Fin’s favor by improving his relations with the carls, who are the people of the earth. When this was done, they said, \x01@\x0B should enter Kero Fin’s cave clothed, and then leave it naked, taking a new name, so it would be as if she had been born anew.
column2: 神言者说征兆不吉， \x01@\x0B 应当改善与大地之民——自由民——的关系，以博取Kero Fin的欢心。待此事完成后，他们说 \x01@\x0B 应当穿着衣服进入Kero Fin的洞穴，然后裸身离开，取一个新名字，这样她就好比是重生了一般。

column1: The god-talkers said that the omens were bad, and that \x01@\x0B should court Kero Fin’s favor by sacrificing to her, or by going into seclusion for three days and three nights.
column2: 神言者说征兆不吉， \x01@\x0B 应当通过献祭给Kero Fin，或者隐居三天三夜，来博取她的欢心。

column1: How many warriors does \x01@\x0B take with her to the mountain?
column2: \x01@\x0B 带多少战士上山？

column1: \x01@\x0B travels to the mountain and finds a cave there. What does she do?
column2: \x01@\x0B 她来到山上，发现一个洞穴。然后她做什么？

column1: Earnestly petitions Kero Fin for permission to marry the Luminous Stallion King.
column2: 恳切请求Kero Fin准许与光辉雄马王成婚。

column1: \x01@\x0B earnestly petitioned Kero Fin for permission to marry the Luminous Stallion King.
column2: \x01@\x0B 恳切请求了Kero Fin准许与光辉雄马王成婚。

column1: Enters the cave clothed and exits it naked, adopting a new name afterwards.
column2: 穿着衣服进入洞穴，裸身离开，之后取了一个新名字。

column1: \x01@\x0B entered the cave clothed and came out again naked. She said her name was now \x01@\x0E.
column2: \x01@\x0B 穿着衣服进入洞穴，又裸身出来。她说她现在名叫 \x01@\x0E。

column1: \x01@\x0B realized that her name was now \x01@\x0E.
column2: \x01@\x0B 意识到她现在名叫 \x01@\x0E。

column1: Recites the lineage of her people, mentioning the things they have done to strengthen the earth.
column2: 吟诵她族人的谱系，提到他们为强化大地所做之事。

column1: \x01@\x0B recited the lineage of her people, mentioning the things they had done to strengthen the earth.
column2: \x01@\x0B 吟诵了她族人的谱系，提到他们为强化大地所做之事。

column1: Removes her clothes and enters the cave, enacting a mating ritual.
column2: 脱去衣服进入洞穴，进行交配仪式。

column1: \x01@\x0B removed her clothes and entered the cave, where she enacted a mating ritual.
column2: \x01@\x0B 脱去衣服进入洞穴，并在其中进行了交配仪式。

column1: \x01@\x0B unfurled the Motion Rune banner and wore it as a cape.
column2: \x01@\x0B 展开了运动符文旗，将它当作披风披上。

column1: The mountain shook, and \x01@\x0B knew that she had become the daughter of Kero Fin, granting her sovereignty over Dragon Pass. As she exited the caves, she saw the ghosts of all of her clan’s dead carls gathered below. The ghosts cheered for her, heralding this great turning point in the history of Dragon Pass.
column2: 山峦震动， \x01@\x0B 明白自己已成为Kero Fin之女，获得了对龙之隘口的统治权。当她走出洞穴，她看到所有她氏族死去自由民的幽灵聚集在下方。幽灵们为她欢呼，宣告着龙之隘口历史上的这个伟大转折点。

column1: Nothing happened. \x01@\x0B knew that her magic had failed, and that she would not be Queen of Dragon Pass.
column2: 什么都没有发生。 \x01@\x0B 知道她的魔法失败了，她不会成为龙之隘口女王。

column1: Why should you gift the carls? It is force of arms that makes a queen!
column2: 为什么要馈赠自由民？武力才能成就女王！

column1: This is too risky. Let someone else become Queen of Dragon Pass.
column2: 这太冒险了。让别人去当龙之隘口女王吧。

column1: The carls are great supporters of our queen.
column2: 自由民是我们女王的有力支持者。

column1: This is all about life, and so I have nothing to say.
column2: 这关乎生命，所以我没什么好说的。

column1: The good queen is a generous queen.
column2: 好女王是慷慨的女王。

column1: \x01@\x0B, don’t do anything that might give offense to prim Kero Fin.
column2: \x01@\x0B别做任何可能冒犯拘谨的Kero Fin的事。

column1: The good queen is a cautious queen.
column2: 好女王是谨慎的女王。

column1: How do we know that this wretched little backwater deserves us?
column2: 我们怎么知道这个可怜的小穷乡僻壤配得上我们？

column1: This is all bound up in ancient women’s magic, and is bound to come to no good.
column2: 这全都与古老的女巫术纠缠不清，注定不会有好下场。

column1: The queen’s life is at risk; we must give up on this foolish quest!
column2: 女王性命堪忧；我们必须放弃这愚蠢的追求！

column1: “I am now King of Dragon Pass.”
column2: “我现在是龙隘之王。”

column1: “You mean that you will soon be King of Dragon Pass,” she said. “The wedding will commence when Earth season next begins.”
column2: “你的意思是你很快就会成为龙隘之王，”她说。“婚礼将在下一个地季开始时举行。”

column1: “I have passed the tests you set for me, and more.”
column2: “我通过了你为我设下的考验，甚至更多。”

column1: “We know that you have passed the tests,” she said. “The wedding will commence when Earth season next begins.”
column2: “我们知道你通过了考验，”她说。“婚礼将在下一个地季开始时举行。”

column1: “I have passed the tests you set for me.”
column2: “我通过了你为我设下的考验。”

column1: “I know,” she said. “The wedding will commence when Earth season next begins.”
column2: “我知道，”她说。“婚礼将在下一个地季开始时举行。”

column1: “I have tamed the dragon, won the favor of the Brass Man, and was reborn within the earth.”
column2: “我驯服了龙，赢得了黄铜人的恩惠，并在大地中重生。”

column1: “You do not need to tell us this,” the Feathered Horse Queen said. “We already know.” She said that the wedding would occur when Earth season next began.
column2: “你不必告诉我们这些，”羽马女王说。“我们早已知道。”她说婚礼将在下一个地季开始时举行。

column1: “Woman, you are mine, and soon I will ride you.”
column2: “女人，你是我的，很快我就要骑你。”

column1: The Feathered Horse Queen sighed. “It is true that you have passed the tests; this we know. And we should have expected some sort of barbaric utterance from you. You will be King of Dragon Pass, but there is much to teach you.” She said that the wedding would occur when Earth season next began.
column2: 羽马女王叹了口气。“你确实通过了考验；这我们知道。而且我们本该料到你会说出某种野蛮言语。你将成龙隘之王，但还有很多东西要教你。”她说婚礼将在下一个地季开始时举行。

column1: She must know that we are bold enough to put down the elves whenever they rise up.
column2: 她必须知道我们足够勇敢，能在精灵一旦作乱时镇压他们。

column1: Tell her she’s in for the rutting of her life.
column2: 告诉她，她这辈子要好好被干一场。

column1: The legend of these tests will be remembered forever!
column2: 这些考验的传说将永世铭记！

column1: It doesn’t matter what we say; she already knows.
column2: 我们说什么都没关系；她早就知道了。

column1: Don’t offend her!
column2: 别惹她生气！

column1: Don’t, don’t try to say too much, or you’ll trip over — I don’t mean literally trip over, I mean of the tongue… a trip of the — or is that slip of the…?
column2: 别，别想说太多，你会绊倒——我不是说真的绊倒，我是说舌头……打个结——还是说口误……？

column1: It never hurts to brag a little.
column2: 稍微吹嘘一下也无妨。

column1: There’s some mistake we made, something that will invalidate our claim…
column2: 我们犯了个错误，会让我们的宣称失效……

column1: A lengthy speech is an eloquent speech.
column2: 长篇大论才显得雄辩。

column1: Oh, what a glorious day!
column2: 哦，多么荣耀的日子！

column1: The wise king is as parsimonious with his words as he is with his cows.
column2: 睿智的国王吝于言辞，如同他吝于牛只。

column1: I will be ready when the wedding day arrives.
column2: 婚礼之日到来时，我会准备好。

column1: Begin this alliance with courteous words.
column2: 用礼貌的言辞开始这段联盟。

column1: Finally there will be peace.
column2: 终于将有和平。

column1: Tell her.
column2: 告诉她。

column1: I always knew we would rule Dragon Pass.
column2: 我一直知道我们会统治龙之隘口。

column1: There has been too much peace. After the marriage, perhaps we can join with the Horse-Spawn for a war against the Pharaoh.
column2: 和平太久了。婚礼之后，也许我们可以和马裔联手，对法老开战。

column1: “I am now Queen of Dragon Pass.”
column2: “我现在是龙之隘口女王了。”

column1: “You mean that you will soon be Queen of Dragon Pass,” he said. “The wedding will commence when Earth season next begins.”
column2: “你的意思是你很快就会成为龙之隘口女王，”他说，“婚礼将在下一个地季开始时举行。”

column1: “We know that you have passed the tests,” he said. “The wedding will commence when Earth season next begins.”
column2: “我们知道你通过了试炼，”他说，“婚礼将在下一个地季开始时举行。”

column1: “I know,” he said. “The wedding will commence when Earth season next begins.”
column2: “我知道，”他说，“婚礼将在下一个地季开始时举行。”

column1: “You do not need to tell us this,” the Luminous Stallion King said. “We already know.” He said that the wedding would occur when Earth season next began.
column2: “你不必告诉我们这些，”光辉雄马王说，“我们早已知道。”他说婚礼将在下一个地季开始时举行。

column1: “You are mine, Horse-Man, and soon I will ride you.”
column2: “你是我的，马人，很快我就会骑你。”

column1: The Luminous Stallion King rolled his eyes. “It is true that you have passed the tests; this we know. And we should have expected some sort of barbaric utterance from you. You will be Queen of Dragon Pass, but there is much to teach you.” He said that the wedding would occur when Earth season next began.
column2: 光辉雄马王翻了个白眼。“你的确通过了试炼，这我们知道。我们也该料到你会说出些粗野之言。你会成为龙之隘口女王，但还有很多要教你。”他说婚礼将在下一个地季开始时举行。

column1: Submit humbly to this man, who will rule you, as husbands should.
column2: 谦卑地顺从这个男人，他将统治你，正如丈夫应有的那样。

column1: Say nothing provocative; we could still fall into war, even at this late hour.
column2: 别说挑衅的话；我们仍可能陷入战争，即使到了这个节骨眼上。

column1: First the snake-cow, then the brass-clam, then the snow-skirted goddess.
column2: 先是蛇牛，再是铜蛤，然后是雪裙女神。

column1: Don’t brag; avoid presumption.
column2: 别吹嘘；避免自以为是。

column1: Never trust a half-burned stead, or a horse with a broken leg.
column2: 绝不要相信半烧过的庄园，或断腿的马。

column1: He must know that we have the dragon’s blessing!
column2: 他必须知道我们得到了龙的祝福！

column1: Pride is a royal virtue.
column2: 骄傲是王者的美德。

column1: A queen must be generous in her words, as she is generous with her cows and goods.
column2: 女王必须言辞慷慨，正如她对牛只和财物慷慨一样。

column1: Keep it simple.
column2: 简单点。

column1: Demand that he build a temple to our gods.
column2: 要求他为我们众神建造一座神庙。

column1: Ask if he has a treasure to give us.
column2: 问他是否有宝藏赠与我们。

column1: It’s not too late — we can still have a war with them, if we say something insulting!
column2: 还不晚——我们仍可和他们开战，只要说些侮辱的话！

column1: I told you this would all have a happy ending.
column2: 我告诉过你这一切会有个美满结局。

column1: Fate has finally revealed itself. Who would have thought that we would come out on top?
column2: 命运终于显现。谁能想到我们会胜出呢？

column1: This is a great day!
column2: 这是伟大的一天！

column1: Good, I think.
column2: 好吧，我想。

column1: Talk to her now, make sure that the elves are not allowed into the new kingdom.
column2: 现在和她谈谈，确保精灵不被允许进入新王国。

column2: \x01@\x0B 呼唤凯罗·芬保护 \x08。

column2: 凯罗·芬动了起来，作为她裙摆的积雪如雨般落下。没有一片雪触碰到 \x01@\x0B，但每一个伏击者都被雪崩压碎。

column1: Kero Fin did not aid \x08, and the ambushers cut \x08 down.
column2: 凯罗·芬没有帮助 \x08，伏击者将 \x08 砍倒。

column1: “Do not harm me, for I have been granted sovereignty over Dragon Pass!”
column2: “不要伤害我，因为我已经被授予龙之隘口的统治权！”

column1: \x01@\x0B cried out: “Do not harm me, for I have been granted sovereignty over Dragon Pass!”
column2: \x01@\x0B 喊道：“不要伤害我，因为我已经被授予龙之隘口的统治权！”

column1: The ambushers lay down their weapons and ask to be adopted into your clan.
column2: 伏击者放下武器，请求被你的氏族接纳。

column1: Adopt them.
column2: 接纳他们。

column1: \x01@\x0B graciously adopted them into our clan.
column2: \x01@\x0B 慷慨地将他们接纳进我们的氏族。

column1: \x01@\x0B refused them.
column2: \x01@\x0B 拒绝了他们。

column1: They laughed at \x01@\x0B’s words, and cut \x08 down.
column2: 他们嘲笑 \x01@\x0B的话，砍倒了 \x08 。

column1: Fights them single-handedly.
column2: 独自与他们战斗。

column1: \x01@\x0B fought them single-handedly.
column2: \x01@\x0B 独自与他们战斗。

column1: \x01@\x0B became a whirlwind of furious motion. \x05 killed the first ambusher with \x04 bare hands, and seized that man’s sword. With that sword, \x06 quickly dispatched the other fifteen attackers.
column2: \x01@\x0B 化作狂暴的旋风。 \x05 用 \x04 双手杀死了第一个伏击者，夺过那人的剑。用那把剑， \x06 迅速解决了其他十五个攻击者。

column1: \x01@\x0B struggled valiantly against the foes that so outnumbered \x08, but they eventually cut \x08 down.
column2: \x01@\x0B 英勇地对抗那些数量远超 \x08的敌人，但最终他们将 \x08 砍倒。

column1: \x01@\x0B said \x06 would give them gifts if they would spare \x04 life.
column2: \x01@\x0B 说 \x06 会给予他们礼物，如果他们饶恕 \x04 性命。

column1: Contemptuously, their leader said, “Through your cowardice, you show that you are not fit to rule us. Before, I thought what we were doing was wrong. Now I see that it is ordained by Humakt, guardian of honor.” And with that, he cut our glorious ruler down.
column2: 他们的首领轻蔑地说：“通过你的懦弱，你证明你不配统治我们。之前，我以为我们做错了。现在我明白这是由荣誉守护者胡马克特所命定的。”说完，他砍倒了我们光荣的统治者。

column1: Kero Fin has granted me sovereignty; they will not attack if they know this fact.
column2: 凯罗·芬授予我统治权；如果他们知道这一事实，就不会攻击。

column1: Kero Fin will protect me.
column2: 凯罗·芬会保护我。

column1: Kero Fin will grant me the strength to slay them all.
column2: 凯罗·芬会赐予我杀死他们所有人的力量。

column1: Even though your contestant failed to win her hand, your people have been invited to the ceremony. You are far from the center of the action, though; in fact, you are so far back that you can hardly see what is going on.
column2: 尽管你的竞争者未能赢得她的手，但你的人民已被邀请参加典礼。不过，你离活动中心很远；事实上，你靠后得几乎看不见发生了什么。

column1: Even though your tribe was never in the running for this honor, your people have been invited to the wedding. The ceremony is a long way away from you, though.
column2: 尽管你们的部落从未有望获此殊荣，但你们的人民还是受邀参加了婚礼。不过，典礼离你们十分遥远。

column1: Even though your king died trying to win her hand, your people have been invited to the ceremony. You are far from the center of the action, though; in fact, you are so far back that you can hardly see what is going on.
column2: 尽管你们的国王为赢得她的芳心而死，但你们的人民还是受邀参加了典礼。不过，你们远离事件中心；事实上，你们站得太靠后，几乎看不清发生了什么。

column1: They lament the fact that, if the clan is to be remembered at all, it will be remembered as a foolish clan. “We made many terrible mistakes over the years,” the people say.
column2: 他们哀叹道，如果这个氏族会被人们记住，那也将是作为一个愚蠢的氏族被记住。“这些年来我们犯了许多可怕的错误，”人们说。

column1: We realized that we would be remembered as a foolish clan.
column2: 我们意识到，我们将被记住为一个愚蠢的氏族。

column1: They lament the fact that the clan will probably not be remembered at all. “We didn’t make terrible mistakes,” the people say, “but we didn’t do enough bold things, either.”
column2: 他们哀叹道，这个氏族很可能根本不会被人们记住。“我们没有犯可怕的错误，”人们说，“但我们也没有做足够多的大胆之事。”

column1: We realized that we would never be remembered in the great sagas of our time.
column2: 我们意识到，我们永远不会被这个时代的伟大传说所铭记。

column1: We thought about the many great deeds we had done, deeds which would be remembered in the sagas of our time.
column2: 我们思考了我们做过的许多伟大事迹，这些事迹将被我们这个时代的传说所铭记。

column1: We lamented the poor state of our herds.

column1: Even though your queen died trying to win his hand, your people have been invited to the ceremony. You are far from the center of the action, though; in fact, you are so far back that you can hardly see what is going on.
column2: 尽管你们的女王为赢得他的心而死，但你们的人民还是受邀参加了典礼。不过，你们远离事件中心；事实上，你们站得太靠后，几乎看不清发生了什么。

column1: Women from the enemy people you know as the Horse-Spawn come to speak to your priestesses. They come not to make threats but to inform you of a change of leadership within the Horse-Spawn ranks. Their new leader is not a king, but the Feathered Horse Queen, who derives her power from the goddesses of the earth, not from the god of the sun. “We offer your people an opportunity to make a new relationship with our new queen,” they say.
column2: 敌人——你们称之为“马裔”一族的女性——前来与你们的女祭司交谈。她们并非来威胁，而是来告知你们马裔内部领导层的变动。她们的新领袖不是一位国王，而是羽马女王，她的权力源自大地女神，而非太阳神。“我们为你们的人民提供一个与我们的新女王建立新关系的机会，”她们说道。

column1: Horse-spawn women came to tell our priestesses that they had a new leader, a woman with earth powers who was called the Feathered Horse Queen.
column2: 马裔女性前来告诉我们的女祭司，她们有了一位新领袖，一位拥有大地力量的女性，被称为羽马女王。

column1: We gave them a treasure.
column2: 我们给了她们一件宝物。

column1: They said that the Feathered Horse Queen would be most pleased by our generous gift. After they were gone, the warriors said we should not have given such a valuable thing to an enemy.
column2: 她们说羽马女王会对我们的慷慨礼物极为满意。她们走后，战士们说我们不该把如此珍贵的东西给敌人。

column1: They said we would be glad we had gifted them. After they were gone, the warriors said we should not have paid such tribute to an enemy.
column2: 她们说我们会为自己赠予了礼物而高兴。她们走后，战士们说我们不该给敌人进贡这样的东西。

column1: Offer them hospitality.
column2: 向她们提供款待。

column1: They thanked us for the offer, but declined it. “We do not know your customs, and do not wish to give offense,” they said. “Still, we will tell the Feathered Horse Queen that you offered us a place at your table.”
column2: 她们感谢我们的提议，但婉拒了。“我们不熟悉你们的习俗，也不愿冒犯，”她们说。“不过，我们会告诉羽马女王，你们曾为我们在桌边留了一席之地。”

column1: They declined our offer. “We will tell the Feathered Horse Queen that you do not know an opportunity when you see it.”
column2: 她们拒绝了我们的提议。“我们会告诉羽马女王，你们面对机会却认不出来。”

column1: Send them packing.
column2: 打发她们走。

column1: We sent them packing.
column2: 我们把她们打发走了。

column1: The people cheered, pleased that we had boldly rebuffed their false offer of peace.
column2: 人们欢呼雀跃，满意于我们大胆回绝了她们虚假的和平提议。

column1: Thank them for the news, but offer them nothing.
column2: 感谢她们带来的消息，但什么也不给。

column1: We thanked them for the news, but offered them nothing.
column2: 我们感谢了她们带来的消息，但什么也没给。

column1: They departed, saying, “We will tell the Feathered Horse Queen that you do not know an opportunity when you see it.”
column2: 她们离开了，说道：“我们会告诉羽马女王，你们面对机会却认不出来。”

column1: We can’t afford to give them anything.
column2: 我们给不起她们任何东西。

column1: It couldn’t hurt to be generous with them.
column2: 对她们慷慨些不会有坏处。

column1: It is all some kind of trick. Don’t trust them.
column2: 这全然是个诡计。不要信任她们。

column1: If we make peace with them, then maybe we can trade with them.
column2: 如果我们与她们讲和，也许就能与她们交易。

column1: The Horse-Spawn hold us in low esteem. We should gift them generously, and turn a foe into a friend.
column2: 马裔对我们评价很低。我们应该慷慨赠礼，将敌人变成朋友。

column1: Although Horse-Spawn and Orlanthi have never been friends, they respect our clan. A token gift will suffice.
column2: 尽管马裔和奥兰斯人从未交好，但他们尊重我们的氏族。一份象征性的礼物就足够了。

column1: The warriors will not be pleased if we cower before an enemy.
column2: 如果我们向敌人畏缩，战士们会不高兴。

column1: The warriors will not be pleased if we pay tribute to an enemy; the more we give, the more unhappy they will be.
column2: 如果我们向敌人纳贡，战士们会不高兴；我们给得越多，他们就越不快。

column1: The warriors will be pleased if we boldly rebuff them.
column2: 如果我们大胆回绝她们，战士们会高兴。

column1: We are obligated to treat them as friends, because they worship the earth.
column2: 我们有义务视他们为友，因为他们崇拜大地。

column1: Foreigners cannot be trusted to follow our laws.
column2: 外人不可信，他们不会遵守我们的律法。

column1: We are not obligated to scorn them, nor are we obligated to befriend them.
column2: 我们没有义务蔑视她们，也没有义务与她们结交。

column1: An offer of hospitality will neither offend the Horse-Spawn, or arouse the anger of our warriors.
column2: 提供款待既不会冒犯马裔，也不会激起我们战士的怒火。

column1: They will be offended by a mere offer of hospitality.
column2: 仅仅提供款待便会冒犯她们。

column1: Everyone likes to get magical treasures, but can we afford to spare ours?
column2: 人人都喜欢得到魔法宝物，但我们能匀出自己的吗？

column1: Many times have they raided Orlanthi clans, aided by their fiery, leaping steeds.
column2: 她们曾多次借助喷火跳跃的坐骑劫掠奥兰斯氏族。

column1: Elmal is the only trustworthy sun god; it is good that earth women have overthrown their old leaders.
column2: 埃尔马尔是唯一可信的太阳神；大地女性推翻了她们的旧领袖，这很好。

column1: If we gift them now, we will be glad later.
column2: 如果现在赠礼，日后我们会感到欣慰。

column1: Feathers? Queen? Let me check my scrolls — this sounds familiar.
column2: 羽毛？女王？让我查查卷轴——这听起来很耳熟。

column1: The only gift we should give them is a fist in the face!
column2: 我们该给她们的唯一礼物，就是一拳打在脸上！

column1: We should be cautious, until we know what the rest of the tribe thinks of this development.
column2: 我们应当谨慎，直到知道部落其他人对此动向的看法。

column1: If we gift them today, they’ll want to marry our men tomorrow.
column2: 如果我们今天送礼，他们明天就会想娶我们的男人。

column1: I told you the Horse-Spawn would be overthrown from within.
column2: 我告诉过你，马裔会从内部被推翻。

column1: Make peace with the Horse-Spawn, so we can better make war on the elves.
column2: 与马裔讲和，这样我们就能更好地对精灵开战。

column1: Peace with the Horse-Spawn? I’d sooner choke on my own tongue!
column2: 与马裔讲和？我宁愿咬舌自尽！

column1: The moon… something will happen to the Red Moon soon.
column2: 月亮……红月很快会发生什么事。

column1: This is a rare chance to improve our antagonistic relations with these people.
column2: 这是改善我们与这些人敌对关系的难得机会。

column1: We should show them hospitality, at least.
column2: 至少我们应该向他们展示好客之道。

column1: Boast of your military strength.
column2: 夸耀你的军事实力。

column2: 我们夸耀了我们的军事实力。

column1: They did not admit that we were stronger than they were, but we saw the color drain from their faces. They left, and we knew they would not attack us.
column2: 他们没有承认我们比他们强大，但我们看到他们脸色发白。他们离开了，我们知道他们不会攻击我们。

column1: They departed, unfazed by our boasts.
column2: 他们离开了，对我们的夸耀无动于衷。

column2: 我们给了他们 \x01@\x01\x01@\x07。

column1: They accepted the treasure, and said that it would cool their warriors’ martial ardor — at least for a while.
column2: 他们接受了宝物，并说这会冷却他们战士的战斗热情——至少暂时如此。

column1: Give them tribute.
column2: 向他们进贡。

column1: They said we were wise to pay tribute, and that this would quench their warrior’s thirst for battle — for a time.
column2: 他们说我们进贡是明智的，这能暂时平息他们战士对战斗的渴望。

column1: They said that our pathetic attempt at tribute was an obvious insult. They vowed that we would pay in blood what we would not pay in wealth.
column2: 他们说我们可怜的进贡企图是明显的侮辱。他们发誓，我们不愿用财富偿还的，必用鲜血偿还。

column1: Persuade them that you have not offended them.
column2: 说服他们你没有冒犯他们。

column1: We told them we had not offended them.
column2: 我们告诉他们我们没有冒犯他们。

column1: Their laughter was so loud that it hurt the ears of sleeping babes.
column2: 他们的笑声如此响亮，刺痛了睡梦中婴儿的耳朵。

column1: They promised that the next time we saw them, we would be staring down at the swords they had plunged into our flesh.
column2: 他们承诺，下次我们见到他们时，我们将会低头看着他们刺入我们血肉的剑。

column1: We have so few cows that we must fight to protect each and every one of them.
column2: 我们的牛只如此之少，必须为保护每一头而战。

column1: Better to lose a few cows now than many cows later.
column2: 现在损失几头牛好过以后损失许多头。

column1: It is an empty threat. Pay them no mind.
column2: 这是空洞的威胁。不必理会。

column1: They truly despise us. Even a gift may not be enough to keep them from making war.
column2: 他们确实鄙视我们。即使一份礼物也可能不足以阻止他们开战。

column1: They utterly despise us. Only a truly generous a gift will keep them from making war.
column2: 他们彻底鄙视我们。只有一份真正慷慨的礼物才能阻止他们开战。

column1: We’re doomed! Doomed, I tell you!
column2: 我们完了！我告诉你，完了！

column1: They’re insane to challenge us. We’ll crush them like so many rotten turnips.
column2: 他们挑战我们是疯了。我们会像碾碎许多腐烂的萝卜一样碾碎他们。

column1: They are right; if we go to war with them, we will probably lose.
column2: 他们是对的；如果我们与他们开战，我们很可能会输。

column1: We have done nothing to offend them.
column2: 我们从未做过冒犯他们的事。

column1: It will be hard to convince them that we have not offended them.
column2: 要让他们相信我们没有冒犯他们，这很难。

column1: We have nothing to lose by trying to convince them of our good intentions. The worst they will do is laugh at us.
column2: 尝试说服他们我们的善意，我们没什么可损失的。最坏不过是被他们嘲笑。

column1: They will be glad to get a magical treasure.
column2: 他们会很高兴得到一件魔法宝物。

column1: If we give them a magical treasure, they will act as if we had given them twenty-five cows.
column2: 如果我们给他们一件魔法宝物，他们的反应会如同我们给了他们二十五头牛。

column1: Tragic King Errarth thought he could make peace with the Surprising Tribe, not knowing that the tribe was made to destroy him.
column2: 悲剧王埃拉思以为他能与惊奇部落讲和，却不知这个部落生来就是要毁灭他的。

column1: If we give in to them, we will be dishonored.
column2: 如果我们向他们让步，我们将蒙受耻辱。

column1: It was the men who offended them, but it is the women who will have to pay for it.
column2: 冒犯他们的是男人，但为此付出代价的却是女人。

column1: The mood of our own tribe is already bad. We can’t risk a war.
column2: 我们本部落的士气已经很差了。我们不能冒险开战。

column1: There must be a peaceful solution.
column2: 一定有和平的解决办法。

column1: “A coward’s longevity is nothing if, in old age, remorse wracks his spear-spared limbs.”
column2: “懦夫的长寿毫无意义，若在暮年，悔恨折磨他那未被长矛刺伤的四肢。”

column1: We must stand up to these greedy thieves right away.
column2: 我们必须立刻反抗这些贪婪的窃贼。

column1: We will lose the kingship if we give in to these bullies. But first we must buy a little time to prepare for war.
column2: 如果我们向这些恶霸让步，就会失去王位。但首先我们必须争取一点时间来备战。

column1: What strange tales and false rumors are they believing of us? I will set them straight.
column2: 他们相信了关于我们的什么奇谈怪论和虚假谣言？我会纠正他们。

column1: They could easily best us in battle. If we buy them off now, we’ll have time to improve our forces.
column2: 他们能在战斗中轻易击败我们。如果我们现在收买他们，就有时间增强我们的兵力。

column1: A promise to stop attacking them.

column1: We promised to stop attacking them.
column2: 我们承诺停止攻击他们。

column1: “But it is we who are attacking you — and winning!” the werewolves scoffed.
column2: “但攻击你们的是我们——而且我们正在取胜！”狼人嘲笑道。

column1: We offered them a treasure.
column2: 我们向他们提供了一件宝物。

column1: Cattle.
column2: 牛只。

column1: We offered them cattle.
column2: 我们向他们提供了牛只。

column1: What type of gift is this?
column2: 这是什么类型的礼物？

column1: One time only.
column2: 仅一次。

column1: An amount to be given annually.
column2: 每年给予的数量。

column1: How much do you offer them?
column2: 你提供多少给他们？

column1: Territory.
column2: 领土。

column1: We offered them territory.
column2: 我们向他们提供了领土。

column1: The chance to build a town.
column2: 建镇的机会。

column1: We offered them the chance to build a town.
column2: 我们向他们提供了建镇的机会。

column1: Werewolves are afraid of cows, and so will be insulted if we offer them cattle.
column2: 狼人害怕牛，所以如果我们向他们提供牛只，他们会感到被侮辱。

column1: We can’t give them cattle; we can’t afford it.
column2: 我们不能给他们牛只；我们负担不起。

column1: Our herds are large, and we can afford to be generous.
column2: 我们的畜群很大，我们负担得起慷慨。

column1: Give them twenty cows.
column2: 给他们二十头牛。

column1: Offer them thirty cows every year.
column2: 每年给他们三十头牛。

column1: Offer them forty cows every year.
column2: 每年给他们四十头牛。

column1: They want to end the fighting just as much as we do.
column2: 他们和我们一样想结束战斗。

column1: They might want to end the fighting, too.
column2: 他们可能也想结束战斗。

column1: They started the war, and they are winning it. It would be foolish to promise them nothing more than an end to the fighting.
column2: 他们发动了战争，而且正在取胜。只承诺结束战斗而不给其他，那是愚蠢的。

column1: The chance to build a town is the chance to become civilized.
column2: 建镇的机会就是变得文明的机会。

column1: The Telmori are not interested in becoming civilized.
column2: 特尔莫里人对变得文明不感兴趣。

column1: If we succeed, we will win the esteem of our tribe.
column2: 如果我们成功，我们将赢得我们部落的尊敬。

column1: If we succeed, we will win the esteem of all Dragon Pass.
column2: 如果我们成功，我们将赢得整个龙之隘口的尊敬。

column1: The Telmori were cursed by the Chaos god, Gbaji.
column2: 特尔莫里人受到了混沌神格巴吉的诅咒。

column1: The Telmori were cursed by the Chaos god, Gbaji, and condemned to a wandering life.
column2: 特尔莫里人受到了混沌神格巴吉的诅咒，被迫过着流浪生活。

column1: The Telmori were cursed by the Chaos god, Gbaji, and condemned to a wandering life. What they most want is a territory — a home to end their wandering.
column2: 特尔莫里人被混沌之神格巴吉诅咒，注定要过漂泊的生活。他们最渴望的是一片领地——一个能结束他们流浪的家园。

column1: There is no gift more impressive than a treasure.
column2: 没有比财宝更令人印象深刻的礼物了。

column1: A single treasure is not enough to end a war.
column2: 单单一件财宝不足以结束战争。

column1: We can trust them, for they are ruled by men, not women.
column2: 我们可以信任他们，因为他们由男人统治，而非女人。

column1: To suckle at the peace-teat, the form-changers did come.
column2: 为了啜饮和平的乳头，那些变形者确实来了。

column1: It is territory they want.
column2: 他们想要的是领地。

column1: The dragonewts will be pleased to see us making peace like this.
column2: 龙人会很高兴看到我们这样缔造和平。

column1: I smelled the forge of Gustbran the Smith, making something to herald this day. When I awoke, I found this golden armband at my feet, and I knew that it was your ten-year ring. Hang it high in your hall, among the spirits of your tribe, safe from thieves and bad spirits.”
column2: 我闻到了铁匠古斯特布兰的熔炉气息，他在打造某物以宣告今天。当我醒来时，发现这只金臂环在我脚边，我便知道这就是你们的十年之环。把它高高挂在大厅里，置于你们部落的灵体之中，远离盗贼与恶灵。”

column1: “Use the ring’s magic to strengthen you, and prove your worth to Elmal by his heroquest.

column1: The prophet Einarth Milk-Eyes came to us with a great golden armband, which he said would be our ten-year ring.
column2: 先知艾纳斯·奶眼带着一只巨大的金臂环来到我们这里，他说这将是我们氏族的十年之环。

column1: He told us to perform heroquests, stay in command, and prosper.
column2: 他指示我们进行英雄任务，保持统领，并繁荣昌盛。

column1: Compose a poem about the ten-year ring.

column2: 那是一首宏伟的诗，人们备受鼓舞。很快，这首诗在他人之间传诵，龙之谷的所有人都知道了我们的伟大。

column1: The poem was not a memorable one.

column1: Express your gratitude to Orlanth with a sacrifice.
column2: 用献祭向奥兰斯表达感激。

column1: What do you express you gratitude with?
column2: 你用什么来表达感激？

column1: As we sacrificed, Orlanth’s blessing charged the air near the altar. Those closest to the magic felt their hair stand on end, as if Orlanth himself were about to appear in a burst of lightning.
column2: 当我们献祭时，奥兰斯的祝福充盈了祭坛附近的空气。离魔法最近的人感到头发竖立，仿佛奥兰斯本人即将在一道闪电中现身。

column1: Give gifts to Einarth.
column2: 给艾纳斯礼物。

column1: He said he would tell his clan of our generosity, and would praise us to others.
column2: 他说他会将我们的慷慨告知他的氏族，并会向其他人称赞我们。

column1: Hold a feast to consecrate the ten-year ring.
column2: 举办一场宴会来祝圣十年之环。

column1: We held a feast to consecrate the ten-year ring.
column2: 我们举办了一场宴会来祝圣十年之环。

column1: The people were happy, and the god-talkers said that our clan magic had been strengthened.
column2: 人们很高兴，神言者说我们的氏族魔法得到了加强。

column1: Thank Einarth and send him on his way.
column2: 感谢艾纳斯并送他上路。

column1: We thanked Einarth and sent him on his way.
column2: 我们感谢了艾纳斯并送他上路。

column1: He gave us much to think about and prepare for in the seasons to come.
column2: 他给了我们很多在今后季节里需要考虑和准备的东西。

column1: Einarth does our clan, and me, a great honor.
column2: 艾纳斯为我们氏族，也为我，带来了极大的荣耀。

column1: Sometimes the blind see the farthest.
column2: 有时盲人望得最远。

column1: His dreams are powerful things. Let it be so.
column2: 他的梦境是强大的东西。就这样吧。

column1: If we must gift Einarth, do it with trade goods.
column2: 如果我们必须赠予艾纳斯礼物，就用贸易货物吧。

column1: We have many cows, and can afford to give some to blessed Einarth.
column2: 我们有许多牛，可以负担得起赠予一些给蒙福的艾纳斯。

column1: A god-talker as famous as Einarth would be offended by a gift of smelly old cows.
column2: 像艾纳斯这样著名的神言者，会被发臭的牛礼物冒犯。

column1: A god-talker as holy as Einarth is indifferent to worldly goods.
column2: 像艾纳斯这样圣洁的神言者，对世俗财物毫不在意。

column1: We can’t afford to give Einarth any of our trade goods.
column2: 我们负担不起赠予艾纳斯任何贸易货物。

column1: Our stores of trade goods are plentiful; we can well afford to gift this revered god-talker.
column2: 我们的贸易货物储备充足；我们完全可以赠予这位受尊敬的神言者。

column1: A well-spoken poem will bring cheer to our people.
column2: 一首动听的诗会给人民带来欢欣。

column1: A well-spoken poem will bring cheer to our people, and make other clans respect us.
column2: 一首动听的诗会给人民带来欢欣，并让其他氏族尊敬我们。

column1: We should thank Orlanth for this boon.
column2: 我们应该为这份恩赐感谢奥兰斯。

column1: If we hold a feast to consecrate the ring, it should strengthen our clan magic.
column2: 如果我们举办宴会祝圣这枚环，它应该会加强我们的氏族魔法。

column1: Orlanth knows us, so he will give us generous reciprocal gifts in return for sacrifice.
column2: 奥兰斯了解我们，所以他会以慷慨的回礼来回报我们的献祭。

column1: Bad King Urgrain had a prophet dipped in lime, but it was his own skin that peeled off.
column2: 恶王乌格兰有个浸泡在石灰中的先知，但最后剥落的是他自己的皮。

column1: Einarth is a worthy messenger, but it is Orlanth the King we must thank for this show of favor.
column2: 艾纳斯是值得信赖的信使，但我们必须感谢的是王奥兰斯，他展示了这份恩宠。

column1: The presence of the ten-year ring is all the more reason to be vigilant in guarding our sacred hall.
column2: 十年之环的存在，更让我们有理由警惕守护我们神圣的大厅。

column1: Old Einarth has come a long way; the least we can do is compensate him for his trouble.
column2: 老艾纳斯远道而来；我们至少应该补偿他的辛劳。

column1: With the power of the ten-year ring, we can boldly raid our neighbors!
column2: 有了十年之环的力量，我们可以大胆袭击我们的邻居了！

column1: Einarth is so holy that he probably has more gifts than he knows what to do with. No need to burden him further.
column2: 艾纳斯如此圣洁，他可能已经拥有多得不知如何处理的礼物了。不必再给他添加负担。

column1: If this were a gift from Ernalda, it would be worth taking seriously.
column2: 如果这是来自埃尔娜达的礼物，那才值得认真对待。

column1: Will the accursed elves fear us, now that we have the ten-year ring?
column2: 那些被诅咒的精灵现在会惧怕我们吗，既然我们有了十年之环？

The other kings of Dragon Pass envy you, and wish to emulate your wisdom. The gods smiled upon your quests. The many great deeds of your clan will be celebrated in verse; when you are gone to the Halls of the Dead, your descendants will gain strong magic from these memories.
column2: 先知艾纳斯·奶眼归来，祝贺你们成功实现了十年之环的承诺。“ \x01@\x0B 和 \x04 \x01@" 氏族的名字将被永远铭记，因为你们对 \x01@< 部落的统治是成功的。龙之隘口的其他国王都嫉妒你们，希望效仿你们的智慧。众神在你们的任务上微笑。你们氏族的诸多伟大事迹将被诗歌传颂；当你们前往死者之厅时，你们的后代将从这些记忆中获得强大的魔法。

column1: Einarth Milk-Eyes returned to congratulate us on successfully living up to the promise of the ten-year ring. He said that the great deeds of our clan would be celebrated in verse, and that our descendants would gain strong magic from us after we have gone to the Halls of the Dead.
column2: 艾纳斯·奶眼归来，祝贺我们成功实现了十年之环的承诺。他说我们氏族的伟大事迹将被诗歌传颂，我们前往死者之厅后，后代将从中获得强大魔法。

column1: There have been other kings in our history who have made great ten-year rings,” Einarth continued, “but few can outshine your clan’s record of generous and heroic deeds.
column2: “我们历史上还有其他国王做出过伟大的十年之环，”艾纳斯继续说道，“但很少有人能超越你们氏族慷慨而英勇的事迹纪录。”

column1: He said that our generous and heroic deeds outshone those of other clans who presided over the ten-year rings of the past.
column2: 他说我们慷慨英勇的事迹超越了其他主持过过去十年之环的氏族。

column1: The poets will praise your large and healthy herds.
column2: 诗人们将赞美你们庞大而健康的畜群。

column1: He praised the fine state of our herds.
column2: 他称赞我们畜群的良好状态。

column1: Considered beside these great deeds, the relatively small size of your herds will soon be forgotten.
column2: 与这些伟大事迹相比，你们畜群相对较小的规模很快将被遗忘。

column1: Einarth said that our herds were small, but that no one would include this fact in the sagas.
column2: 艾纳斯说我们的畜群很小，但没有人会把这一事实写入传说。

column1: In thundering martial verse, people will recall the might of your warriors.
column2: 在雷鸣般的战诗中，人们会回忆起你们战士的勇武。

column1: Einarth said that the might of our warriors would be remembered.
column2: 艾纳斯说我们战士的勇武将被铭记。

column1: The small size of your martial forces will be of little interest to those who make the sagas of this time.
column2: 你们军队规模较小，对那些创作这个时代传说的人而言无关紧要。

column1: Einarth said that the small size of our martial forces would not be thought important by later generations.
column2: 艾纳斯说我们军队规模较小，后代不会认为重要。

column1: Your comparative lack of success in trade means little.
column2: 你们在贸易上相对缺乏成功关系不大。

column1: He remarked upon our lack of success at trade, but said it meant little.
column2: 他提到我们在贸易上缺乏成功，但说关系不大。

column1: Your success in trade is the envy of all.
column2: 你们在贸易上的成功令所有人嫉妒。

column1: Einarth said that our success in trade was fit cause for boasting.
column2: 艾纳斯说我们在贸易上的成功值得夸耀。

column1: Perhaps you could have done more to strengthen your magic, but you have prospered nonetheless.
column2: 也许你们本可以做得更多来强化魔法，但你们仍然兴旺了。

column1: He told us that we had prospered even though we could have done more to strengthen our magic.
column2: 他告诉我们，即使我们本可以在强化魔法上做得更多，我们仍然兴旺了。

column1: Your success in keeping your clan magic strong shall serve as a positive lesson for others.
column2: 你们在保持氏族魔法强大方面的成功将为他人提供正面榜样。

column1: He praised us for keeping our clan magic strong.
column2: 他称赞我们保持了氏族魔法强大。

column1: If you have not gained the universal esteem of your neighbors, that is to be expected,” Einarth concluded. “For the strong often arouse the envy of the weak.
column2: “如果你们没有获得邻居们的普遍尊重，那也是意料之中的，”艾纳斯总结道。“因为强者常激起弱者的嫉妒。”

column1: In conclusion, Einarth said it was acceptable to have aroused the envy of the weak, for we were great, and should celebrate that greatness.
column2: 最后，艾纳斯说激起弱者的嫉妒是可以接受的，因为我们伟大，应当庆祝这份伟大。

column1: You have done all these things while still maintaining the esteem of your neighbors, and that is good,” Einarth concluded. “It is not easy to be strong without arousing the envy of the weak.
column2: “你们在所有这些事情上仍保持了邻居的尊重，这很好，”艾纳斯总结道。“强大而不激起弱者嫉妒是不容易的。”

column1: In conclusion, Einarth praised us for maintaining the esteem of our neighbors.
column2: 最后，艾纳斯称赞我们保持了邻居的尊重。

column1: \x01@\x0B must be praised, and so should every one of you. Feast now, my friends. Feast the feast of the victorious.”
column2: \x01@\x0B ……必须被赞扬，你们每个人都应被赞扬。现在宴饮吧，我的朋友们。宴饮胜利之宴。”

column1: “Your deeds will be remembered, but not as great deeds. Instead, the sagas will recall your clan as one that made terrible mistakes. You were cautious when you should have been bold, foolish when you should have been wise, and greedy when you should have been generous.
column2: “你的功绩将被铭记，但并非作为伟业。相反，传说将把你的氏族记作犯下可怕错误的一个。你在该勇敢时谨慎，在该明智时愚蠢，在该慷慨时贪婪。

column1: Einarth said that our deeds were memorable, but not in a good way.
column2: 艾纳斯说我们的功绩令人难忘，但并非以好的方式。

column1: “Unfortunately, you have few great accomplishments to boast of. Your deeds have been neither foolish nor wise, neither cruel or generous. No poet will make a saga about your clan, for fear of putting his audience to sleep.
column2: “不幸的是，你几乎没有伟大成就可夸耀。你的行为既不愚蠢也不明智，既不残酷也不慷慨。没有诗人会为你的氏族创作传说，唯恐让听众睡着。

column1: Einarth said that our deeds were unmemorable.
column2: 艾纳斯说我们的功绩不值得铭记。

column1: “Your failure comes despite a record of generous and heroic deeds. For it is not great deeds alone that make a clan, but also the judicious husbanding of your resources.
column2: “尽管有慷慨与英雄事迹的记录，你的失败依然到来。因为造就一个氏族的不仅伟大功绩，还有对资源的明智管理。

column1: It is in those small things that the outline of your failure can be read.
column2: 正是在那些小事中，可以读出你失败的轮廓。

column1: He said that our record of generous and heroic deeds was not enough to compensate for our other failures.
column2: 他说我们慷慨与英雄事迹的记录不足以弥补我们的其他失败。

column1: Although you have not been successful, you can take consolation in the health and size of your herds.
column2: 尽管你未成功，你可以在畜群的健康和规模中得到安慰。

column1: Despite this, he praised the fine state of our herds.
column2: 尽管如此，他称赞了我们畜群的优良状况。

column1: Among your greatest follies was your failure to maintain a large and healthy herd of cattle.
column2: 你最大的愚蠢之一就是未能维持庞大健康的牛群。

column1: Einarth told us that we had failed to maintain a large and healthy herd of cattle.
column2: 艾纳斯告诉我们，我们未能维持庞大健康的牛群。

column1: Your failure is mitigated by your large force of brave warriors.
column2: 你的失败因你拥有众多勇敢战士而有所减轻。

column1: The small size of your martial forces has not won you any honor.
column2: 你军事力量的弱小并未为你赢得任何荣誉。

column1: Einarth said that the small size of our martial forces had won us no honor.
column2: 艾纳斯说我们军事力量的弱小未为我们赢得荣誉。

column1: Your lack of success in trade is shameful.
column2: 你在贸易上的缺乏成功是可耻的。

column1: He remarked upon our lack of success at trade, and said it was shameful.
column2: 他评论了我们在贸易上的缺乏成功，并说这是可耻的。

column1: Your success in trade should provide some relief in these dark days.
column2: 你在贸易上的成功应为这些黑暗日子提供一些慰藉。

column1: He said that our success in trade should provide some consolation.
column2: 他说我们在贸易上的成功应提供一些安慰。

column1: Perhaps if you had done more to strengthen your magic, you would not be in this strait today.
column2: 或许若你更努力加强你的魔法，你今天就不会陷入此等困境。

column1: He told us we should have done more to strengthen our magic.
column2: 他告诉我们，我们本应更努力加强魔法。

column1: You can at least point to your magic, and say that it is strong.
column2: 你至少可以指着你的魔法，说它很强大。

column1: This disaster is to be expected,” Einarth concluded, “for you have failed to build strong friendships with your neighbors.”
column2: “这场灾难在所难免，”艾纳斯总结道，“因为你未能与邻族建立牢固的友谊。”

column1: In conclusion, Einarth said that our failure to build friendships with our neighbors had ruined our chances of success.
column2: 总之，艾纳斯说我们未能与邻族建立友谊毁掉了成功的机会。

column1: At least you still maintain the esteem of your neighbors, and that is good,” Einarth concluded. “Otherwise, the other clans might have descended upon you like wolves, sensing your weakness.”
column2: “至少你仍保持着邻族的尊重，这很好，”艾纳斯总结道。“否则其他氏族可能像狼一样扑向你们，察觉到你们的软弱。”

column1: In conclusion, Einarth praised us for at least maintaining the esteem of our neighbors.
column2: 总之，艾纳斯称赞我们至少保持了邻族的尊重。

column1: Einarth leaves with the ten-year ring, and disappointment reigns.
column2: 艾纳斯带着十年之环离去，失望笼罩一切。

column1: Beat the most troublesome of the thralls.
column2: 鞭打最捣乱的奴隶。

column1: We beat the most troublesome of the thralls.
column2: 我们鞭打了最捣乱的奴隶。

column1: The thralls were, of course, unhappy to face our rough justice, but the carls said that they were satisfied with the actions of the clan ring.
column2: 奴隶们自然不满于我们粗暴的裁决，但自由民们表示他们对氏族议会的行动感到满意。

column1: Convince the carls that their concerns are unwarranted.
column2: 说服自由民，他们的担忧毫无根据。

column1: \x01@N told the carls that their concerns were unwarranted.
column2: \x01@N 告诉自由民他们的担忧毫无根据。

column1: After much discussion, the carls agreed that their accusations against the thralls lacked merit, and withdrew them. The thralls were heartened to learn that even they were treated fairly by our clan ring.
column2: 经过大量讨论，自由民同意他们对奴隶的指控缺乏依据，并撤回了指控。奴隶们得知即便他们也能得到我们氏族议会的公平对待，感到振奋。

column1: The carls were most affronted, accusing \x01@N of caring more for wretched thralls than for \x04 own people.
column2: 自由民感到极大冒犯，指责 \x01@N 更关心可怜的奴隶而非 \x04 自己人。

column1: Raise a few of the most obedient thralls to cottar status.
column2: 将几个最顺从的奴隶提升为佃农。

column1: We raised a few of the most obedient thralls to cottar status.
column2: 我们将几个最顺从的奴隶提升为佃农。

column1: The freed thralls were extravagant in their praise of the ring. They said that the behavior of the others would improve, now that they saw that there was a reward for obedience. The carls, however, were most displeased, and said that we would soon be rewarding Chaos creatures for impregnating our cattle.
column2: 被释放的奴隶对议会赞不绝口。他们说，既然看到服从有奖励，其他奴隶的行为也会改善。然而，自由民们极为不满，说我们很快就要奖赏混沌生物，因为它们让我们的牲畜怀孕了。

column1: Threaten the thralls with beatings if their wickedness continues.
column2: 威胁奴隶，如果他们的恶行继续，就鞭打他们。

column1: We threatened the thralls with beatings.
column2: 我们威胁要鞭打奴隶。

column1: The carls said that they would wait and see if the behavior of the thralls improved. They said we should do more than threaten the thralls next time they caused trouble.
column2: 自由民们说他们会等着看奴隶的行为是否改善。他们说下次奴隶惹麻烦时，我们做的应该不止是威胁。

column1: Free the thralls.
column2: 释放奴隶。

column1: We freed the thralls.
column2: 我们释放了奴隶。

column1: Adopt them as cottars.
column2: 接纳他们为佃农。

column1: Then we adopted them as cottars.
column2: 然后我们接纳他们为佃农。

column1: The carls were not happy with this arrangement. They said that the thralls were laggards and half-wits, and that slavery was their deserved lot in life.
column2: 自由民对这个安排不满意。他们说奴隶是懒汉和弱智，奴役是他们应得的命运。

column1: Encourage them to leave your tula.
column2: 鼓励他们离开你们的领地。

column1: They quickly left our tula, which is what we wished of them.
column2: 他们迅速离开了我们的领地，这正是我们所希望的。

column1: The carls were not happy with this arrangement; they said they liked having thralls to do those jobs which were unworthy of free Orlanthi.
column2: 自由民对这个安排不满意；他们说他们喜欢让奴隶做那些不适合自由奥兰提人的工作。

column1: Let them choose whether to leave, or to stay as cottars.
column2: 让他们选择是离开，还是作为佃农留下。

column1: We said they could leave us, or join us as cottars.
column2: 我们说他们可以离开我们，或者作为佃农加入我们。

column1: They chose to stay.
column2: 他们选择留下。

column1: The carls were not happy with this choice. They said that the thralls were laggards and half-wits, and that slavery was their deserved lot in life.
column2: 自由民对这个选择不满意。他们说奴隶是懒汉和弱智，奴役是他们应得的命运。

column1: They chose to leave.
column2: 他们选择离开。

column1: The carls were not happy with this choice; they said they liked having thralls to do those jobs which were unworthy of free Orlanthi.
column2: 自由民对这个选择不满意；他们说他们喜欢让奴隶做那些不适合自由奥兰提人的工作。

column1: We must respect the wishes of the carls in this matter.
column2: 在这件事上我们必须尊重自由民的意愿。

column1: We have heeded the wishes of the carls in many things, and can afford to disappoint them now, if need be.
column2: 我们在许多事情上听从了自由民的意愿，如果需要，现在可以承担让他们失望的后果。

column1: The carls would not bring a complaint against the thralls without good reason.
column2: 自由民不会无缘无故投诉奴隶。

column1: The carls have learned to enjoy their power over the thralls. Their complaints must be seen in that light.
column2: 自由民已经学会享受他们对奴隶的权力。必须从这个角度看待他们的投诉。

column1: We have no choice but to punish them severely.
column2: 我们别无选择，只能严厉惩罚他们。

column1: They are thralls. We can do what we want with them.
column2: 他们是奴隶。我们可以随意处置他们。

column1: Even thralls will fight back if you mistreat them badly enough.
column2: 如果你虐待得太过分，连奴隶也会反抗。

column1: If we are generous to the thralls, we displease the carls.
column2: 如果我们对奴隶仁慈，就会让自由民不快。

column1: If we are generous to the thralls, we displease the carls. If we do as the carls wish, we increase the chances of a thrall rebellion.
column2: 如果我们对奴隶仁慈，就会让自由民不快。如果我们按自由民的意思做，就会增加奴隶叛乱的机会。

column1: A truly confident leader knows when to be generous.
column2: 真正自信的领导者知道何时该慷慨。

column1: Our people have always kept thralls; doing so strengthens our clan magic.
column2: 我们的人民一直蓄养奴隶；这样做能增强我们的氏族魔法。

column1: Our ancestors said it was wrong to keep thralls. If we mistreat them, we will weaken our clan magic.
column2: 我们的祖先说蓄养奴隶是错误的。如果我们虐待他们，就会削弱我们的氏族魔法。

column1: There’s nothing wrong with the thralls a good thrashing won’t cure.
column2: 奴隶们没什么问题是一顿好揍解决不了的。

column1: Why strike one foe, when you can strike them all?
column2: 既然能打倒所有敌人，为何只打一个？

column1: We must temper justice with mercy.
column2: 我们必须以仁慈调和正义。

column1: Bad King Urgrain was once a thrall. The mistreatment he faced at the hands of the Red Tongue Clan made him hateful and cruel.
column2: 恶王乌格兰曾经是个奴隶。他在红舌氏族手中遭受的虐待使他充满憎恨与残忍。

column1: Bad King Urgrain was once a thrall. If his captors had broken his cruel and hateful spirit, the world would have been spared all the trouble he caused.
column2: 恶王乌格兰曾经是个奴隶。如果俘获他的人打碎了他那残忍而充满恨意的灵魂，世界就能免去他制造的种种麻烦。

column1: We can count on the duplicitous elves to exploit any problems we have with disobedient thralls.
column2: 我们可以指望狡诈的精灵利用我们与不服从的奴隶之间的任何问题。

column1: The dragonewts would want us to talk sense into our carls.
column2: 龙人会希望我们去劝说自由民通情达理。

column1: I could never beat the thralls, even though they deserve it. I am too weak-hearted to serve on the ring, and should be replaced.
column2: 我永远无法鞭打奴隶，即使他们活该。我心地太软，不适合在议会任职，应该被替换。

column1: As Oskul once said, “Wise words stave off sorrow.”
column2: 正如奥斯库尔所言：“聪明的话能避免悲伤。”

column1: sceneR395
column2: sceneR395

column1: We killed the thrall.
column2: 我们杀死了那个奴隶。

column1: The carls were satisfied with our justice, and said it would be an example to the other thralls.
column2: 自由民对我们的裁决感到满意，说这将对其他奴隶起到警示作用。

column1: How many thralls do you trade?
column2: 你要交易多少奴隶？

column1: To which clan do you try to trade them?
column2: 你试图将他们交易给哪个氏族？

column1: The usual price for a healthy thrall is 5 cows. What do you ask for each thrall?
column2: 一个健康奴隶的通常价格是5头牛。你每个奴隶要价多少？

column1: The \x01Ý accepted our offer, and took the thralls off our hands.
column2: \x01Ý 接受了我们的提议，接手了这些奴隶。

column1: They are only willing to give you \x01@\x18 cows for the thralls. Do you accept the deal?
column2: 他们只愿意为这些奴隶付给你 \x01@\x18 头牛。你接受这笔交易吗？

column1: The \x01Ý bargained shrewdly, and paid less for the thralls than we had hoped.
column2: \x01Ý 精于讨价还价，为奴隶付的价钱比我们希望的少。

column1: The \x01Ý offered us less than we wanted. We returned home without trading the thralls away.
column2: \x01Ý 出的价低于我们的期望。我们没能卖掉奴隶，空手而归。

column1: The carls are furious about this.
column2: 自由民对此极为愤怒。

column1: We will get the best price for our thralls if we approach the \x01@a clan.
column2: 如果我们去找 \x01@a 氏族，就能给奴隶卖个好价钱。

column1: We will get the best price for our thralls if we approach the \x01@! clan.
column2: 如果我们去找 \x01@! 氏族，就能给奴隶卖个好价钱。

column1: The carls are sure this will happen again if we do not mete harsh justice.
column2: 自由民确信，若我们不施以严苛的正义，这种事还会发生。

column1: We have too many thralls, and are likely to face an uprising if we do not get rid of at least \x01@\r of them.
column2: 我们的奴隶太多了，若不放走至少 \x01@\r个，很可能会面临暴动。

column1: Our people have always kept thralls; by doing as our ancestors did, we strengthen our clan magic.
column2: 我们的人民向来蓄养奴隶；效仿祖先所为，能增强我们的氏族魔法。

column1: Our ancestors said it was wrong to keep thralls. We should either trade our thralls away or wait until tempers cool and set them all free.
column2: 我们的祖先说过，蓄养奴隶是不对的。我们应当把奴隶卖掉，或者等人们火气消了，把他们都释放。

column1: We must make a death today.
column2: 今天必须有人死。

column1: Surely this can be resolved without further violence.
column2: 此事定能无需更多暴力就解决。

column1: While a thrall of the Red Tongue clan, many years before he became a bad king, Urgrain assaulted the chieftain’s wife. In due course, she gave birth to a litter of blue-skinned foemen.
column2: 厄格瑞因还是红舌氏族的奴隶时——远在他成为昏君多年之前——就袭击了酋长的妻子。后来，她产下了一窝蓝皮肤的敌人。

column1: When next we sacrifice, we should sacrifice a thrall.
column2: 下次献祭时，我们应当献祭一个奴隶。

column1: What this reminds me of is … is … I forget what it reminds me of, exactly, but I’m sure there was something I…
column2: 这让我想起的是……是……我忘了具体是什么，但我肯定有什么事我……

column1: Oskul said, “Had our foe been killed while he was a rebellious thrall, our families would be alive today.”
column2: 奥斯库尔说：“要是我们的敌人在他还只是个反叛的奴隶时就杀掉，我们的家人今天还会活着。”

column1: sceneR396
column2: sceneR396

column1: Your thralls have risen up against you. They have captured several of your carls, and are now advancing on your clan hall, torches at the ready.
column2: 你的奴隶起兵反你。他们抓住了你的一些自由民，现在正手持火把，向你的部族大厅逼近。

column1: Our thralls rose up against us. They captured some of our carls, and made ready to burn our clan hall.
column2: 我们的奴隶起兵反我们。他们抓住了我们的一些自由民，准备烧毁我们的部族大厅。

column1: Attack them without mercy.
column2: 毫不留情地攻击他们。

column1: We attacked them without mercy.
column2: 我们毫不留情地攻击了他们。

column1: \x01@\x19 of our warriors were slain.
column2: \x01@\x19 我们的战士中有数人阵亡。

column1: We hewed our way through the ranks of the thralls, until the tula was heaped with the corpses of rebellious slaves.
column2: 我们在奴隶的队列中杀出一条血路，直到图拉上堆满反叛奴隶的尸体。

column1: There were no survivors.
column2: 没有幸存者。

column1: The survivors begged abjectly for their lives.
column2: 幸存者们卑躬屈膝地求饶。

column1: They fought with surprising ferocity, killing many of us. They looted and burnt the clan hall before finally breaking ranks and fleeing for the hills.
column2: 他们以惊人的凶残战斗，杀死了我们许多人。他们劫掠并烧毁了部族大厅，最后才溃散，逃向山中。

column1: Convince them to surrender.
column2: 说服他们投降。

column1: We told them to surrender.
column2: 我们叫他们投降。

column1: Confronted by the formidable \x01@N, the crazed thralls became meek, and surrendered, agreeing never again to break the law in this way.
column2: 面对令人生畏的 \x01@N，狂乱的奴隶变得温顺，投降了，并承诺再不会这样触犯律法。

column1: The thralls scoffed at \x01@N’s words, and said that we had so mistreated them that they would never listen to us again.
column2: 奴隶们嘲笑 \x01@N的话，说我们虐待他们太甚，他们再也不会听我们的话了。

column1: Evacuate the clan hall.
column2: 撤离部族大厅。

column1: We evacuated the clan hall.
column2: 我们撤离了部族大厅。

column1: The thralls fell upon it in a wild-eyed frenzy, looting it and burning it to the ground. They would have destroyed our clan regalia, too, if we had not taken it from the hall. When their fury was spent, they split up and fled for the hills.
column2: 奴隶们以狂乱的眼神扑向它，洗劫一空，将其烧为平地。要不是我们把氏族圣物从大厅中取出，他们连那个也会毁掉。等他们的怒火发泄完毕，便四散逃往山中。

column1: Offer them gifts if they agree to leave your lands peacefully.
column2: 如果他们同意和平离开你的土地，就送他们礼物。

column1: We offered them gifts if they would leave our lands peacefully.
column2: 我们提议送他们礼物，只要他们和平离开我们的土地。

column1: \x01@N persuaded the thralls to accept our offer. They took the goods and honored their side of the bargain by quickly departing.
column2: \x01@N 说服了奴隶们接受我们的提议。他们拿走了货物，并履行承诺迅速离去。

column1: They scorned \x01@N’s offer. “You have treated us like we are worse than animals,” they said. “We do not trust your promise of safety.”
column2: 他们鄙视了 \x01@N的提议。“你们待我们连畜生都不如，”他们说，“我们不信任你们所谓的安全承诺。”

column1: Their courage soon flagged in the face of our righteous determination, and they fled for the hills.
column2: 面对我们正义的决心，他们的勇气很快消退，逃往山中。

column1: They fought with surprising ferocity, forcing our warriors back. They looted and burnt the clan hall before finally breaking ranks and fleeing for the hills.
column2: 他们以惊人的凶残战斗，逼退我们的武士。他们劫掠并烧毁了部族大厅，最后才溃散，逃往山中。

column1: We shouldn’t have treated them so harshly.
column2: 我们本不该那样虐待他们。

column1: They are no threat to us.
column2: 他们对构不成威胁。

column1: If we fight without quarter, so will they.
column2: 如果我们不留活口地打，他们也会这样。

column1: Although it is riskier to fight without quarter, it is the only way to recapture them.
column2: 虽然不留活口地打风险更大，但这是重新抓住他们的唯一办法。

column1: Offer them goods, and they will leave.
column2: 给他们些财物，他们就会离开。

column1: It is less humiliating to give them something than it is to have something taken from us.
column2: 主动给他们点什么，总比让他们从我们这里抢走什么要少些耻辱。

column1: The people will understand that we must abandon the clan hall.
column2: 人民会理解我们不得不放弃部族大厅。

column1: It will be very hard to convince them to submit to us once more.
column2: 要再次说服他们臣服于我们，会非常困难。

column1: We will be humiliated if mere thralls burn our clan hall.
column2: 如果被区区奴隶烧了部族大厅，我们会颜面扫地。

column1: They are breaking the law. We must order them to obey!
column2: 他们在犯法。我们必须命令他们服从！

column1: They do not care that they break the law, for the law does not favor them.
column2: 他们不在乎自己是否违法，因为法律并不偏向他们。

column1: Better to lose the clan hall than to lose lives.
column2: 宁可失去部族大厅，也不能失去人命。

column1: Vinga said, “Because my hair is the color of blood, I will not bleed tonight. It is my foe who shall be reddened.”
column2: 文加说：“因为我头发是血色，今夜流血不会是我。该被染红的是我的敌人。”

column1: Better to give away a cow than to have five stolen.
column2: 宁愿送出一头牛，也好过被偷走五头。

column1: We are in danger — in danger of laughing ourselves to death! Let us make crow food of them!
column2: 我们有危险——有笑死的危险！让他们变成乌鸦的食物！

column1: The vampires put them up to this!
column2: 是吸血鬼怂恿他们这么做的！

column1: “Never trust a witch’s welcome, your brother’s killer, the play of a bear, or the wit of a thrall.”
column2: “永远别信巫女的欢迎、你兄长的杀手、熊的把戏、奴隶的机灵。”
