column2: sceneR397

column1: The spirits of our ancestors said that \x01@\x07 had in fact used a Listening Wind against \x01@\x01.
column2: 我们的祖先之灵称， \x01@\x07 实际上对 \x01@\x01使用了聆听之风。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors said that \x01@\x07 had not used his Listening Wind against \x01@\x01.
column2: 我们的祖先之灵称， \x01@\x07 并未对 \x01@\x01使用他的聆听之风。

column1: Penalize both parties.
column2: 惩罚双方。

column1: \x01@\x0B chose to penalize both parties.
column2: \x01@\x0B 选择惩罚双方。

column1: Rule in favor of \x01@\x07.
column2: 裁定支持 \x01@\x07。

column1: \x01@\x0B ruled in favor of \x01@\x07.
\x01@\x07 thanked us for our wisdom. \x01@\x01 said nothing, but was clearly angry.
column2: \x01@\x07 感谢我们的智慧。 \x01@\x01 一言不发，但显然很愤怒。

column1: Rule in favor of \x01@\x01.
column2: 裁定支持 \x01@\x01。

column1: \x01@\x0B ruled in favor of \x01@\x01.

\x01@\x01 praised us for seeing with an unclouded eye, and gifted us with half of the horses we had ordered \x01@\x07 to turn over to her. \x01@\x07’s face lost its usual smile, but he said nothing about our verdict.
column2: \x01@\x01 赞赏我们用不受蒙蔽的眼睛看问题，并将我们命令 \x01@\x07 移交给她的一半马匹赠予我们。 \x01@\x07脸上失去了惯常的笑容，但对我们的裁决一言不发。

column1: Tell them to take the matter to a full moot.
column2: 告诉他们将此事提交全体议会。

column1: \x01@\x0B told them to take the matter to a full moot.
column2: \x01@\x0B 告诉他们将此事提交全体议会。

column1: Both seemed displeased, for this would require them to compete in gift-giving to the other clans. At the moot, we received cows from both clans.
column2: 双方都不悦，因为这将迫使他们在其他氏族面前竞相赠礼。在议会上，我们收到了来自两个氏族的牛只。

column1: The moot found that \x01@\x07 had indeed used a Listening Wind to eavesdrop on the private conversations of the \x01@! traders.
column2: 议会裁定， \x01@\x07 确实使用了聆听之风窃听 \x01@! 商人们的私下谈话。

column1: It therefore ruled in favor of \x01@\x01, and condemned \x01@\x07 for using sacred war magic to gain petty advantage over a member of his own tribe.
column2: 因此裁定支持 \x01@\x01，并谴责 \x01@\x07 使用神圣战争魔法在同族成员身上谋取微小利益。

column1: Despite this finding of fact, the moot decided in favor of \x01@\x07. It ruled that the Listening Wind was a gift from Orlanth, and that one favored by the gods should be able to use the tokens of that favor in the manner of his choosing.
column2: 尽管有此事实认定，议会仍决定支持 \x01@\x07。它裁定聆听之风是奥兰斯的恩赐，受神明眷顾者理应按自己选择的方式使用这份恩赐的象征。

column1: The moot found that \x01@\x01’s accusations were groundless, and that \x01@\x07 had not used a Listening Wind against her. \x01@\x01 blamed this ruling on the divination we had performed, pronouncing it faulty.
column2: 议会裁定 \x01@\x01的指控毫无根据， \x01@\x07 并未对她使用聆听之风。 \x01@\x01 将此裁决归咎于我们进行的占卜，称其有误。

column1: We can enrich ourselves by fining both parties.
column2: 我们可以通过罚款双方来充实自己。

column1: We can enrich ourselves by fining both parties, but doing so would make us unpopular.
column2: 我们可以通过罚款双方来充实自己，但那样会令我们不得人心。

column1: If the case goes to a full moot, we will get gifts from both clans.
column2: 如果案件进入全体议会，我们将收到两个氏族的赠礼。

column1: If we rule in \x01@\x01’s favor, she will give us a share of the fine.
column2: 如果我们裁定支持 \x01@\x01，她将分给我们一部分罚款。

column1: \x01@\x01’s clan is a stouter wartime ally than \x01@\x07’s.
column2: \x01@\x01的氏族是比 \x01@\x07的氏族更坚毅的战时盟友。

column1: \x01@\x07’s clan is a stouter wartime ally than \x01@\x01’s.
column2: \x01@\x07的氏族是比 \x01@\x01的氏族更坚毅的战时盟友。

column1: \x01@\x07 is blameless here.
column2: \x01@\x07 在此处无可指摘。

column1: This is a difficult case.
column2: 这是个棘手的案件。

column1: If \x01@\x07 did send a Listening Wind against \x01@\x01, he should be penalized.
column2: 如果 \x01@\x07 确实对 \x01@\x01释放了聆听之风，他应受到惩罚。

column1: Even if \x01@\x07 did send a Listening Wind against \x01@\x01, he may not be guilty of any offense under the law.
column2: 即使 \x01@\x07 确实对 \x01@\x01释放了聆听之风，根据法律他也可能不构成任何罪行。

column1: The loser of this dispute will blame us, if it is we who rule.
column2: 如果我们来裁决，这场纠纷的输家会怪罪我们。

column1: This is a question of spirit magic. Let us consult the spirits of our ancestors.
column2: 这是灵魂魔法的问题。让我们咨询祖先之灵。

column1: Our magic is weak, and the spirits of our ancestors may be deceived if we attempt a divination.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱，若尝试占卜，祖先之灵可能会被欺骗。

column1: Our magic is strong enough to guide the spirits of our ancestors to find the truth of this matter.
column2: 我们的魔法足够强大，能够引导祖先之灵找出此事的真相。

column1: A Listening Wind is a type of spirit sent by Orlanth to help his great heroes to hear the plans of their foes.
column2: 聆听之风是奥兰斯派遣的一种灵体，帮助他的伟大英雄窃听敌人的计划。

column1: They should both be punished for bothering us with such a trivial matter. If this were about cows, instead of horses, it would be different.
column2: 他们二人都该因拿这种小事烦扰我们而受罚。如果事关牛只而非马匹，那就另当别论。

column1: The word-thief gave advantage to the Wind-Sword.
column2: 窃语者给了风剑以优势。

column1: I told you we’d be swamped in foolish disputes if we won the crown.
column2: 我跟你说过，如果我们赢得王冠，就会被愚蠢的纠纷淹没。

column1: Even regular eavesdropping is rude, and should be forbidden. To do so magically … it is shocking!
column2: 即便普通的窥听也是无礼的，应当禁止。用魔法做这种事……真是骇人听闻！

column1: Closely question the priests and tricksters.
column2: 仔细盘问祭司和恶作剧者。

column1: We closely questioned the priests and tricksters.
column2: 我们仔细盘问了祭司和恶作剧者。

column1: \x01@N said that the tricksters were lying.
column2: \x01@N 称恶作剧者在撒谎。

column1: \x01@N said that the tricksters were telling the truth.
column2: \x01@N 称恶作剧者说的是实话。

column1: \x01@N said that the priests were clearly mistaken, and had wrongly identified the tricksters as the cause of their misfortune.
column2: \x01@N 称祭司们显然弄错了，错误地将恶作剧者指为他们不幸的根源。

column1: \x01@N said that the priests were correct, and that the tricksters were clearly the cause of their misfortune.
column2: \x01@N 称祭司们是正确的，恶作剧者显然是他们不幸的根源。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors said that the tricksters were guilty.
column2: 我们的祖先之灵称恶作剧者有罪。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors said that the \x01@a tricksters were blameless.
column2: 我们的祖先之灵称 \x01@a 的恶作剧者无可指摘。

column1: Find in favor of the \x01@a tricksters.
column2: 裁定支持 \x01@a 的恶作剧者。

column1: \x01@\x0B ruled in favor of the \x01@a tricksters.
column2: \x01@\x0B 裁定支持 \x01@a 的恶作剧者。

column1: The tricksters thanked us for our mercy, and gifted us with a broken flagon, which they said would bring us good luck.
column2: 恶作剧者们感谢我们的仁慈，并赠予我们一只破损的酒壶，据说能带来好运。

column1: Find in favor of the \x01@! priests.
column2: 裁决支持 \x01@! 祭司。

column1: \x01@\x0B found in favor of the \x01@! priests.
column2: \x01@\x0B 已裁决支持 \x01@! 祭司。

column1: The moot found in favor of the \x01@! priests. They proclaimed the righteousness of the verdict, and the tricksters quailed in fear.
column2: 议会裁决支持 \x01@! 祭司。他们宣称裁决公正，恶作剧者们吓得畏缩不前。

column1: \x01@a magicians said that we had performed a faulty divination, and that the moot had used this to reach an unfair verdict.
column2: \x01@a 法师们说我们进行了一次错误的占卜，议会利用这一点做出了不公正的裁决。

column1: The moot judged the \x01@a tricksters innocent of the charges made against them by the \x01@! priests. The tricksters cartwheeled for joy, but the priests muttered darkly.
column2: 议会裁定 \x01@a 恶作剧者无罪，未犯下 \x01@! 祭司指控的罪行。恶作剧者高兴地翻着筋斗，而祭司们阴沉地低语。

column1: They said that we had performed a faulty divination, and that the moot had used this to reach an unfair verdict.
column2: 他们说我们进行了一次错误的占卜，议会利用这一点做出了不公正的裁决。

column1: If we rule in favor of the tricksters, they will give us a gift of magic.
column2: 如果我们裁决支持恶作剧者，他们会赠予我们一件魔法礼物。

column1: The priests’ clan is a stouter wartime ally than the tricksters’.
column2: 祭司的氏族比恶作剧者的氏族是更可靠的战时盟友。

column1: The tricksters’ clan is a stouter wartime ally than the priests’.
column2: 恶作剧者的氏族比祭司的氏族是更可靠的战时盟友。

column1: This case boils down to a dispute of fact: did the tricksters redirect a plague meant for them, or not?
column2: 此案归结于事实争议：恶作剧者是否将本应指向他们的瘟疫转移了？

column1: Allow me to cross-examine each party to the dispute. I can ferret out the truth of the matter.
column2: 请允许我盘问争议的每一方。我能查明事实真相。

column1: We needn’t resort to divination to find the truth; I am wise enough in the ways of magic to tell if the priests are correct.
column2: 我们不必借助占卜来查明真相；我对魔法之道足够睿智，能判断祭司是否正确。

column1: Eurmal’s magic is sometimes useful, but often has unintended consequences.
column2: 尤尔马尔的魔法有时有用，但往往带来意想不到的后果。

column1: Do not trust those mingy priests.
column2: 不要相信那些吝啬的祭司。

column1: One must always take a firm hand with tricksters.
column2: 对付恶作剧者必须始终采取强硬手段。

column1: It would be rude to disappoint either clan.
column2: 让任何一个氏族失望都是不礼貌的。

column1: Running a tribe is costly. We must fine both sides, to help recoup what we have lost.
column2: 管理部落花费很大。我们必须对双方处以罚款，以弥补我们的损失。

column1: Dragonewts love tricksters.
column2: 龙人喜爱恶作剧者。

column1: They should settle these matters on their own. Let’s penalize their stupidity.
column2: 他们应该自己解决这些事情。让我们惩罚他们的愚蠢。

column1: I love hearing the one side, then the other, then hearing what the gods have to say.
column2: 我喜欢先听一方，再听另一方，然后听听神祇怎么说。

column2: sceneR399

column1: Closely question both chieftains.
column2: 严密盘问两位酋长。

column1: We closely questioned both chieftains.
column2: 我们严密盘问了两位酋长。

column1: \x01@\x01 said that \x01@\x0F’s weaponthanes had left him because he treated them with disrespect, but \x01@N found her account unconvincing.
column2: \x01@\x01 说 \x01@\x0F的武器领主们离开了他，因为他待他们不敬，但 \x01@N 认为她的说法不可信。

column1: \x01@\x01 said that \x01@\x0F’s weaponthanes had left him because he treated them with disrespect, and \x01@N said that her account seemed convincing.
column2: \x01@\x01 说 \x01@\x0F的武器领主们离开了他，因为他待他们不敬，而 \x01@N 说她的说法似乎可信。

column1: \x01@\x0F denied his rival’s claim that his weaponthanes had left him because he treated them with disrespect, but \x01@N found his denials simply served to bolster \x01@\x01’s version of events.
column2: \x01@\x0F 否认了对手的指控，即他的武器领主们离开他是因为他待他们不敬，但 \x01@N 发现他的否认反而加强了 \x01@\x01对事件的描述。

column1: \x01@\x0F denied his rival’s claim that his weaponthanes had left him because he treated them with disrespect, and \x01@N found no reason to doubt his words.
column2: \x01@\x0F 否认了对手的指控，即他的武器领主们离开他是因为他待他们不敬，而 \x01@N 认为没有理由怀疑他的话。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors said that \x01@\x01 had wrongly induced the weaponthanes to leave the \x01@! clan.
column2: 祖先之灵说 \x01@\x01 错误地引诱武器领主们离开了 \x01@! 氏族。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors said that the weaponthanes had left \x01@\x0F’s household on their own accord, because he had ridiculed their telling of the sacred myths.
column2: 祖先之灵说武器领主们是自愿离开 \x01@\x0F家族的，因为他嘲笑了他们对神圣神话的讲述。

column1: Find in favor of \x01@\x01.
column2: 裁决支持 \x01@\x01。

column1: Find in favor of \x01@\x0F.
column2: 裁决支持 \x01@\x0F。

column1: \x01@\x0B found in favor of \x01@\x0F.
column2: \x01@\x0B 已裁决支持 \x01@\x0F。

column1: Both chieftains were angered, and promised that we would regret the day that greed overcame justice.
column2: 两位酋长都愤怒了，并承诺我们将为贪欲压倒正义的那一天后悔。

column1: The moot judged the \x01@a chieftain blameless in the incident, and said that \x01@\x0F had driven the weaponthanes away through his own foolishness.
column2: 议会裁定 \x01@a 酋长在此事件中无可指责，并说 \x01@\x0F 因自己的愚蠢赶走了武器领主们。

column1: The winner of this dispute will give us a gift.
column2: 这场争议的赢家将赠予我们一件礼物。

column1: \x01@\x0F’s clan is a stouter wartime ally than \x01@\x01.
column2: \x01@\x0F's clan is a stouter wartime ally than \x01@\x01.

column1: \x01@\x01’s clan is a stouter wartime ally than \x01@\x0F’s.
column2: \x01@\x01's clan is a stouter wartime ally than \x01@\x0F's.

column1: If \x01@\x01 induced the weaponthanes to leave, she is in the wrong. But if they left of their own accord, she is blameless.
column2: 如果 \x01@\x01 引诱武器领主们离开，那么她错了。但如果他们是自愿离开，她就无可指责。

column1: Clan chiefs may be either men or women.
column2: 氏族酋长可以是男性也可以是女性。

column1: If a chief does not respect his weaponthanes, as Orlanth paid respect to Humakt, they have every right to find a wiser leader.
column2: 如果酋长不像奥兰斯尊重胡马克特那样尊重他的武器领主们，他们完全有权寻找一位更明智的领袖。

column1: No one should interfere with the bonds of loyalty between a chief and his weaponthanes.
column2: 任何人都不应干涉酋长与其武器领主之间的忠诚纽带。

column1: Both chiefs treat the weaponthanes as a mere possession to fight over. Both should be punished for their folly.
column2: 两位酋长都把武器领主当作争夺的财产。他们的愚蠢都应受到惩罚。

column1: We should not disappoint either of them.
column2: 我们不应让他们中的任何一个失望。

column1: If we do not consult the spirits of our ancestors, they will be angry with us, and cause our limbs and noses to fall off.
column2: 如果我们不咨询祖先之灵，他们会生我们的气，让我们的四肢和鼻子脱落。

column1: I do not trust her.
column2: 我不信任她。

column1: She is a more reliable foe of the undead.
column2: 她是亡灵更可靠的敌人。

column1: sceneR400
column2: sceneR400

column1: Another delegation came from the Colymar tribe, demanding tribute again.
column2: 科利马尔部落又派来一支代表团，再次索要贡品。

column1: A delegation came from the Colymar tribe, demanding a large tribute from us.
column2: 科利马尔部落派来一支代表团，向我们索要大笔贡品。

column1: They fought ferociously, and we drove them back, but at great cost. Some were killed, and many others were wounded.
column2: 他们凶猛作战，我们击退了他们，但代价惨重。有人阵亡，还有许多负伤。

column1: They overran us and looted at their leisure, killing many. They took cattle and goods worth about as much as the tribute they had demanded of us.
column2: 他们冲垮了我们，从容劫掠，杀死许多人。他们带走的牲畜和货物价值大约相当于向我们索要的贡品。

column1: Offer them a different amount.
column2: 给他们一个不同的数额。

column1: We offered them a different amount.
column2: 我们给了他们一个不同的数额。

column1: They accepted what we offered them, and departed.
column2: 他们接受了我们的献纳，然后离开了。

column1: We paid them what they asked without a fuss, though the carls protested bitterly for weeks.
column2: 我们干脆地付清了他们索要的数目，尽管自由民们痛苦地抗议了数周。

column1: Petition them for membership in their tribe.
column2: 向他们请求加入部落。

column1: We said that we would like to join their tribe.
column2: 我们说我们想加入他们的部落。

column1: They said we could come before their moot and petition them to join the great Colymar tribe.
column2: 他们说我们可以到他们的集会上去，请求加入伟大的科利马尔部落。

column1: What do you give their king?
column2: 你给他们国王什么？

column1: They accepted us, and from that day onward we were part of the Colymar tribe.
column2: 他们接纳了我们，从那天起我们便成了科利马尔部落的一部分。

column1: They rejected us.
column2: 他们拒绝了我们。

column1: Their traders said that we were rich enough to rob, but not rich enough to join them.
column2: 他们的商人说我们富到可以抢劫，却穷到不足以加入他们。

column1: Their war leaders said that we were too weak to bother with.
column2: 他们的战争领袖说我们太弱，不值得理会。

column1: Their priests said that our magic was weak.
column2: 他们的祭司说我们的魔法太弱。

column1: Their poets said that we had done no great deeds, and would bring no glory to the Colymar name.
column2: 他们的诗人说我们从未建立伟大功业，不会给科利马尔之名带来荣耀。

column1: Their chieftains said that our ring was unwise, and blind to Orlanthi virtues.
column2: 他们的酋长说我们的议政会不明智，对奥兰斯美德视而不见。

column1: They said that they would be back, but that next time they would not stop to parley.
column2: 他们说他们会回来，但下一次不会停下来谈判。

column1: We can’t afford to pay tribute to them.
column2: 我们无法负担向他们进贡。

column1: We can’t afford to keep paying tribute like this.
column2: 我们无法继续这样进贡。

column1: We can afford to pay.
column2: 我们付得起。

column1: We can part with some of our cattle, but I fear they mean to take all of it.
column2: 我们可以放弃一些牲畜，但我怕他们想全部拿走。

column1: They will not want us to join them, because our herds are small.
column2: 他们不会希望我们加入，因为我们的牧群很小。

column1: If we agree to this, our herds will dwindle rapidly.
column2: 如果我们答应这个，我们的牧群会迅速减少。

column1: If we pay tribute to them now, they will come back again to ask for more.
column2: 如果我们现在向他们进贡，他们会再回来索取更多。

column1: If we pay tribute to them now, they will come back again and again. Each time they will increase the amount they demand.
column2: 如果我们现在向他们进贡，他们会一次又一次地回来。每次都会提高索要的数额。

column1: Here they are, back again. At this rate, we shall grow poor and become stickpickers in the blink of an eye!
column2: 他们又来了。照这样下去，我们很快就会变穷，眨眼间变成拾柴人！

column1: We are poor traders, and they will reject us if we petition to join them.
column2: 我们是蹩脚的交易者，如果请求加入他们，他们会拒绝我们。

column1: They do not look like they will agree to any negotiation about the tribute amount.
column2: 他们看起来不会同意任何关于贡品数额的谈判。

column1: We have nothing to fear from the puny Colymar!
column2: 没什么好怕那弱小的科利马尔人的！

column1: We’d be lucky to drive off this delegation, let alone defeat a full Colymar raiding party.
column2: 我们能赶走这支代表团就算走运了，更别提击败一整支科利马尔袭击队。

column1: We would likely lose, but we could try making their tribute collection as painful for them as possible.
column2: 我们很可能会输，但我们可以试着让他们的征贡过程变得尽可能痛苦。

column1: We have yet to make a reputation for great deeds and wise leadership; they will reject us if we ask to join them.
column2: 我们尚未凭伟大功业和英明领导赢得名声；如果我们请求加入，他们会拒绝我们。

column1: We have yet to grow strong enough to prevent this sort of thing from happening to us.
column2: 我们尚未强大到足以阻止这种事情发生在我们身上。

column1: If you can’t beat them, join them.
column2: 如果你无法击败他们，就加入他们。

column1: We must figure out a way to form a tribe of our own, so that we can compete with the Colymar on an even footing.
column2: 我们必须想办法建立自己的部落，这样才能与科利马尔人平等竞争。

column1: In order to successfully petition for membership, we must gift them with an amount even greater than the tribute they ask.
column2: 为了成功请求入部，我们必须赠予他们比他们索要的贡品还要多的财物。

column1: They will bleed us to death, we must try some other way to get around this.
column2: 他们会把我们榨干，我们必须另想办法避开这个局面。

column1: The Colymar priests will try to bar our entry into their tribe, because our magic is weak.
column2: 科利马尔的祭司会试图阻止我们加入他们的部落，因为我们的魔法很弱。

column1: Do whatever it takes to get them out of our hair right now, so we can take of our fields. Then, hit them during the next Fire season.
column2: 不惜一切代价先把他们打发走，这样我们就能照料田地。然后，在下一个火之季袭击他们。

column1: The Colymar were a tribe in Dragon Pass before we even left the Holy Country.
column2: 科利马尔部落早在我们离开圣国之前就已是龙隘的一个部落。

column1: I’d spit on them, but the Colymar aren’t good enough for our glorious sputum!
column2: 我恨不得啐他们一口，但科利马尔人还不配享用我们光荣的唾沫！

column1: The Colymar is not worth joining, for they are ruled by foolish men.
column2: 科利马尔部落不值得加入，因为他们由愚蠢的人统治。

column1: They will kill us if we don’t give them what they want.
column2: 如果不给他们想要的，他们会杀了我们。

column1: \x02\x03They’re/It’s/He’s\x02 — \x02\x03they’re/he’s/it’s\x02 — \x02\x03they’re/he’s/it’s\x02 —
column2: \x02\x03他们是/它是/他是\x02 —— \x02\x03他们是/他是/它是\x02 —— \x02\x03他们是/他是/它是\x02 ——

column1: At first, they were surprised to be attacked, and so we pressed an early advantage against them. But then they rallied.
column2: 起初，他们被攻击时很惊讶，于是我们利用了早期优势。但随后他们重新集结。

column1: We overcame this rally, and managed to drive them off, but some of our fighters were slain, and many others injured.
column2: 我们击退了这次反攻，成功驱赶了他们，但我们的一些战士阵亡，许多人受伤。

column1: They smashed through our line and looted us without mercy, killing many in their fury. They took cattle and goods worth much more than the tribute they had demanded.
column2: 他们冲破我们的防线，无情地劫掠我们，狂怒中杀死了许多人。他们带走的牲畜和货物价值远远超过了他们索要的贡品。

column1: We paid. But many in the clan thought that we would have been better off fighting.
column2: 我们付了。但氏族中许多人认为我们当初战斗会更好。

column1: They said we could come before their moot and sue to join the great Colymar tribe.
column2: 他们说我们可以到他们的集会上去，恳求加入伟大的科利马尔部落。

column1: They rejected us again. Some of our people said that they would always reject us, and that they let us petition only so they could take our gifts, and then humiliate us.
column2: 他们再次拒绝了我们。我们的一些人说他们会永远拒绝我们，他们让我们请求入部只是为了收下我们的礼物，然后羞辱我们。

column1: We can’t afford to keep paying this damnable tribute!
column2: 我们无法继续支付这可恶的贡品了！

column1: How long will we have these fine herds, if we must give them over to the Colymar whenever they ask?
column2: 如果每次科利马人要，我们就得交出去，那这些好牛群我们还能拥有多久？

column1: We’ll have to continue to pay tribute to them, until we are strong enough to stand against an entire tribe.
column2: 我们必须继续向他们进贡，直到我们强大到足以对抗整个部落。

column1: They will continue to increase their demands, unless we make it clear than we cannot afford to give them more each time.
column2: 他们会不断加码，除非我们明确表示再也给不起了。

column1: Let me bargain with them. At the very least, I can stop them from increasing their demand each time they come.
column2: 让我去和他们讲价。至少，我能阻止他们每次来都提高要求。

column1: Let me try to bargain with them. Surely they will see that by asking for more each time, there will come a time when we have nothing to give.
column2: 让我试着去和他们谈谈。他们总该明白，每次要得更多，总有一次我们会一无所有。

column1: Carl and weaponthane alike despises the cursed Colymar! We must make them pay for their crimes against us!
column2: 卡尔和武器领主们都憎恨这该死的科利马！我们必须让他们为对我们的罪行付出代价！

column1: It is no different from the last time. A tribe is always stronger than a single clan.
column2: 和上次没什么不同。一个部落总是比单个氏族强大。

column1: They aren’t as alert as they were the last time. They expect us to meekly submit, and aren’t ready for a fight.
column2: 他们没有上次那么警惕了。他们以为我们会乖乖屈服，根本没准备好战斗。

column1: They aren’t as alert as they were the last time. But even if we win against the delegation, we will face a raid from the entire tribe. Then it’s we who will lose.
column2: 他们没有上次那么警惕了。但就算我们打败了这支使团，也会招来整个部落的袭击。到时候输的还是我们。

column1: A bully beats up those weaker than him, knowing he can’t lose. But poke or slap him, and watch him run away.
column2: 恶霸只会欺负比自己弱的人，因为他知道自己不会输。但你要是戳他一下或扇他一巴掌，看他逃得多快。

column1: The more we roll over like puppies, the more they will kick us.
column2: 我们越像小狗一样打滚求饶，他们就越会踢我们。

column1: We are squeezed like a minnow in a crayfish’s claw! We must find some way out of this intolerable situation!
column2: 我们被夹得像小龙虾钳子里的小鱼！必须想办法摆脱这无法忍受的处境！

column1: They refused our petition to join them once, which increases the chance that they will refuse us again.
column2: 他们曾经拒绝过我们加入的请求，这增加了再次拒绝我们的可能性。

column1: They refuse to let us join them, so there is no point in shaming ourselves by asking over and over like whining children.
column2: 他们拒绝让我们加入，所以像哭闹的孩子一样反复请求，只会自取其辱，毫无意义。

column1: We should at least try to join them.
column2: 我们至少该试试加入他们。

column1: We should try to join them before we are so weak it would it be laughable.
column2: 我们应该在变得弱小到可笑之前就去请求加入。

column1: Every time they reject our petition to join them, our humiliation grows.
column2: 每次他们拒绝我们加入的请求，我们的屈辱就增加一分。

column1: Do not bother to petition to join them. Do not act the \x02\x03simpleton/fool/buffoon\x02.
column2: 别去扮演 \x02\x03蠢货/傻瓜/小丑\x02的角色。

column1: They take from us because we are weak. If we were strong and they were weak, it would be right for us to take from them.
column2: 他们掠夺我们是因为我们弱小。如果我们强大而他们弱小，那我们去掠夺他们也是天经地义。

column1: If we were strong and they were weak, we would take from them. Unless they hurt us badly when we tried.
column2: 如果我们强大而他们弱小，我们会去掠夺他们。除非我们在尝试时被他们重创。

column1: We can’t afford to keep paying them!
column2: 我们再也付不起了！

column1: I cannot sleep at night for thinking of our lost wealth.
column2: 我夜不能寐，想着我们失去的财富。

column1: Not one more \x02\x03cow/barleycorn/thing\x02. Not a one.
column2: 再一个 \x02\x03牛/谷粒/东西\x02也不给。一个也不给。

column1: If we hadn’t followed the stupid advice of the women, we’d be strong enough to withstand even the Colymar.
column2: 如果我们当初没有听那些女人的蠢建议，我们现在应该强大到连科利马都能抵挡。

column1: If we hadn’t let the foolish men handle this, we’d have found a way around the Colymar by now.
column2: 如果我们当初没让那些蠢男人处理这事，早就找到对付科利马的办法了。

column1: Perhaps we could find some ancient texts which tell how to win against an entire tribe.
column2: 也许我们可以找到一些古代典籍，记载着如何战胜整个部落。

column1: This mustn’t distract us from the war on the walking dead.
column2: 这绝不能分散我们对行尸战争的注意。

column1: They will let us pay less tribute if we explain that we need our cows to pay to build a temple.
column2: 如果我们解释需要牛来支付建造神庙的费用，他们会让我们少交贡品。

column1: sceneR402
column2: sceneR402

column1: Convince them to abandon their plan.
column2: 说服他们放弃计划。

column1: Hear them out, then warn \x01@\x0B.
column2: 先听他们说完，然后警告 \x01@\x0B。

column1: We heard them out, then warned \x01@\x0B of the plot against \x08.
column2: 我们听他们说完，然后警告 \x01@\x0B 关于针对 \x08的阴谋。

column1: Instruct your weaponthanes to participate.
column2: 命令你的武器领主们参与。

column1: With our help, she said she would act without further delay. Alas, the protective spirits of the Colymar revealed the ambushers’ intentions, and \x01@\x0B was well prepared for battle. Two of our weaponthanes were slain, the others injured. The Colymar swore that we would pay for our part in the assault.
column2: 在我们的帮助下，她说她会不再拖延立即行动。唉，科利马的保护之灵暴露了伏击者的意图， \x01@\x0B 做好了充分战斗准备。我们的两位武器领主战死，其余受伤。科利马人发誓要让我们为参与袭击付出代价。

column1: Let your weaponthanes decide for themselves.
column2: 让你的武器领主们自己决定。

column1: We allowed our weaponthanes to decide for themselves.
column2: 我们让武器领主们自己决定。

column1: It’s not as if the Colymar have taken tribute from us.
column2: 又不是科利马人向我们索取过贡品。

column1: The Colymar are rich; we should not antagonize them.
column2: 科利马人很富有；我们不该与他们为敌。

column1: If we take this news to \x01@\x0B, \x06 will reward us with silver.
column2: 如果我们把这个消息带给 \x01@\x0B， \x06 会用银子奖赏我们。

column1: The Colymar must die!
column2: 科利马人必须死！

column1: The Colymar are strong because they are a tribe, while the rest of us are mere clans.
column2: 科利马强大是因为他们是一个部落，而我们都只是单个氏族。

column1: The weaponthanes are dispirited, and scarcely eager for a fight with an opponent as formidable as \x01@\x0B.
column2: 武器领主们士气低落，几乎不愿与像 \x01@\x0B这样强大的对手作战。

column1: The ambush will fail.
column2: 伏击会失败。

column1: If we let the weaponthanes decide what to do, they will not blame us for the outcome.
column2: 如果我们让武器领主们决定怎么做，他们就不会因结果而责怪我们。

column1: The \x01@! and \x01@a clans regard us highly. They will not like it if we disappoint them, but we can afford to do so.
column2: \x01@! 氏族和 \x01@a 氏族对我们评价很高。如果我们让他们失望，他们会不高兴，但我们承受得起。

column1: The \x01@! and \x01@a clans regard us highly. They will be thankful if I can dissuade them from this dangerous course.
column2: \x01@! 氏族和 \x01@a 氏族对我们评价很高。如果我能劝他们放弃这条危险的道路，他们会感激的。

column1: The Colymar got here before anyone else, and formed a tribe before anyone else. They are the ones who countered the powers of the dragonewt barrier called the Crossline.
column2: 科利马人比任何人都先到达这里，比任何人都先组成部落。正是他们抵御了被称为“交叉线”的龙蜥人屏障的力量。

column1: \x01@\x0B is due for a humbling.
column2: \x01@\x0B 该被教训一下了。

column1: Let the weaponthanes decide for themselves.
column2: 让武器领主们自己决定。

column1: I have kept a long list of Colymar slights against us; I say it is time to make them pay.
column2: 我记着柯利玛人对我们的种种轻慢；我说，是时候让他们付出代价了。

column1: The only way to beat the Colymar is by forming a tribe to rival theirs. We must do wise things, and eventually a tribe will form around us.
column2: 打败柯利玛的唯一方法是组建一个与他们匹敌的部落。我们必须做明智之事，最终一个部落会围绕我们形成。

column1: Let us give away some cows, to show that we are generous.
column2: 让我们送掉一些牛，以展示我们的慷慨。

column1: \x02\x03Minorya/Nalrada/Uraldesta\x02
column2: \x02\x03米诺利亚/纳尔拉达/乌拉尔德斯塔\x02

column1: \x01@\x01, Ernalda priestess of the \x01@! clan, told us that they had freed their thralls, and that we should do the same.
column2: \x01@\x01 \x01@! 氏族的厄纳尔达女祭司告诉我们，他们已经释放了他们的奴隶，我们也应该这么做。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors told us that we were foolish for listening to this stupid priestess; they had always kept thralls, and we should do the same. They said that they would reward us for insulting this meddlesome woman, who had offended them.
column2: 我们的祖先之灵告诉我们，听信这个愚蠢的女祭司是愚蠢的；他们一直蓄养奴隶，我们也应该这么做。他们说，如果我们侮辱这个多管闲事的女人，就会奖赏我们，因为她冒犯了他们。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors told us that \x01@\x01 was right; they had not taken thralls in their day, and we should not, either. They said they would reward us if we freed our thralls.
column2: 我们的祖先之灵告诉我们， \x01@\x01 是对的；他们那个时代没有蓄养奴隶，我们也不应该蓄养。他们说，如果我们释放奴隶，就会奖赏我们。

column1: Free your thralls.
column2: 释放你们的奴隶。

column1: “We will consider what you have said.”
column2: “我们会考虑你说的话。”

column1: We told \x01@\x01 that we would consider her words.
column2: 我们告诉 \x01@\x01 ，我们会考虑她的话。

column1: She left us, saying that she would talk to our thralls and advise them to press us on this issue. The carls were most perturbed; they said that the thralls were difficult enough to handle as it was, without her meddling.
column2: 她离开了我们，说她会去找我们的奴隶谈话，并建议他们向我们施压。自由民们非常不安；他们说奴隶本来就已经够难对付的了，她还要来多管闲事。

column1: “You should not meddle in our business, priestess.”
column2: “你不该插手我们的事，女祭司。”

column1: She was affronted, and said that she would tell her fellows of the disrespect we had shown her.
column2: 她感到受辱，说她会告诉她的同伴们我们对她表现出的不敬。

column1: Politely refuse her.
column2: 礼貌地拒绝她。

column1: We politely refused her.
column2: 我们礼貌地拒绝了她。

column1: She said that we would eventually come around to the right way of thinking. She departed, saying that she would talk to our thralls and advise them to press us on this issue. The carls were most perturbed; they said that the thralls were difficult enough to handle as it was, without her meddling.
column2: 她说我们最终会转变到正确的思维方式上来。她离开了，说她会去找我们的奴隶谈话，并建议他们向我们施压。自由民们非常不安；他们说奴隶本来就已经够难对付的了，她还要来多管闲事。

column1: Appease ancestral spirits, then free the thralls.
column2: 安抚祖先之灵，然后释放奴隶。

column1: In preparation for freeing the thralls, we appeased our ancestral spirits.
column2: 为释放奴隶做准备，我们安抚了我们的祖先之灵。

column1: The spirit-talkers said that the signs were good; our ancestors would not punish us for turning our back on the traditions they had established.
column2: 灵语者说征兆良好；我们的祖先不会因为我们背弃他们确立的传统而惩罚我们。

column1: The spirit-talkers said that our ancestors were angry, and would not receive our sacrifice.
column2: 灵语者说我们的祖先很愤怒，不会接受我们的献祭。

column1: We adopted our freed thralls as cottars.
column2: 我们将被释放的奴隶接纳为佃农。

column1: At first the carls grumbled, but when the freed thralls worked even harder as full members of our clan, everyone came around to accepting them fully.
column2: 起初自由民们抱怨，但当被释放的奴隶作为氏族的正式成员更加努力工作时，每个人都完全接受了他们。

column1: We told the thralls to go; they were free.
column2: 我们告诉奴隶们走吧；他们自由了。

column1: The carls wondered aloud why we bothered to take thralls if we were just going to let them go again.
column2: 自由民们大声质疑，既然我们打算放他们走，为什么还要费心去抓奴隶。

column1: The carls won’t like it if we free the thralls.
column2: 如果我们释放奴隶，自由民们不会高兴。

column1: The carls will complain for a while if we free the thralls, but it will not be serious.
column2: 如果我们释放奴隶，自由民们会抱怨一阵子，但不会严重。

column1: The carls are already unhappy. They will complain bitterly if we free the thralls.
column2: 自由民们已经不高兴了。如果我们释放奴隶，他们会痛苦地抱怨。

column1: The carls are already unhappy. Insulting this meddler will cheer them up.
column2: 自由民们已经不高兴了。侮辱这个多管闲事的人会让他们高兴起来。

column1: It seems odd that freeing the thralls would make us better off, but she is right — provided we adopt the thralls as cottars.
column2: 释放奴隶会让我们过得更好，这似乎很奇怪，但她是对的——前提是我们把奴隶接纳为佃农。

column1: Thralls are valuable. We wouldn’t simply free our cows. Why would we do so for thralls?
column2: 奴隶是宝贵的。我们不会随便放走牛。为什么要对奴隶这么做？

column1: Her eyes burn with the zeal of the converted. She will make trouble for us if we refuse her outright.
column2: 她的眼中燃烧着皈依者的狂热。如果我们直接拒绝她，她会给我们找麻烦。

column1: Her eyes burn with the zeal of the converted. She will make trouble for us unless we immediately heed her request.
column2: 她的眼中燃烧着皈依者的狂热。除非我们立即听从她的请求，否则她会给我们找麻烦。

column1: Our relations with her clan are strong, and can withstand her displeasure.
column2: 我们与她氏族的关系牢固，能承受她的不快。

column1: Our relations with her clan are poor; we should not make matters worse by insulting her.
column2: 我们与她氏族的关系很差；我们不应该侮辱她，使事情变得更糟。

column1: Freeing the thralls would be a big step. We should ask the spirits of our ancestors what to do.
column2: 释放奴隶将是一大步。我们应该问问我们的祖先之灵该怎么办。

column1: Our ancestors believed that it was right and good to keep thralls. Their spirits will be affronted if we repudiate the traditions they set out for us.
column2: 我们的祖先认为蓄养奴隶是正确且好的。如果我们否定他们为我们制定的传统，他们的灵魂会感到受辱。

column1: Our ancestors believed that it was wrong to keep thralls. Perhaps, if we return to this tradition, our luck will improve.
column2: 我们的祖先认为蓄养奴隶是错误的。也许，如果我们恢复这个传统，我们的运气会变好。

column1: If we really want to free the thralls, we must sacrifice to our ancestors, who believed that it was right and good to keep thralls, and would otherwise be offended.
column2: 如果我们真的想释放奴隶，我们必须向祖先献祭，他们相信蓄养奴隶是正确且好的，否则他们会生气。

column1: Some Orlanthi clans keep thralls, while others shun the practice.
column2: 有些奥兰斯氏族蓄养奴隶，而另一些则回避这种做法。

column1: The keeping of thralls spreads Chaos.
column2: 蓄养奴隶会传播混沌。

column1: The freeing of thralls spreads Chaos.
column2: 释放奴隶会传播混沌。

column1: Freeing them would show great generosity.
column2: 释放他们会显示出极大的慷慨。

column1: \x01@\x01 is right.
If we free the thralls, the elves will not be able to use their discontent against us.
column2: 如果我们释放奴隶，精灵们就无法利用他们的不满来对付我们。

column1: The dragonewts would want us to free the thralls.
column2: 龙人会希望我们释放奴隶。

column2: sceneR404

column1: \x01@\x01, the ranking Uralda priestess of the \x01@! clan, wants to marry one of your young men, the melancholy weaponthane \x01@\x10. She offers the clan chief a gift of fifty cows in addition to the dowry paid to his family, so that he will come to live with her clan. But \x01@\x10 has made his unwillingness to marry her clear.
column2: \x01@\x01氏族首席乌拉尔达祭司 \x01@! ，想要嫁给你的一名年轻男子——忧郁的武器领主 \x01@\x10。除了支付给他家族的嫁妆之外，她还向氏族酋长赠送了五十头牛的礼物，这样他就会来与她同族居住。但 \x01@\x10 已明确表示不愿娶她。

column1: He says that he loves another: the beautiful young \x01@\x07 of the \x01@a clan.
column2: 他说他爱着另一个人： \x01@a 氏族那美丽年轻的 \x01@\x07 。

column1: He won’t come out and say it, but it is clear that he thinks \x01@\x01 too old for him.
column2: 他没有明说，但显然他认为 \x01@\x01 对他来说太老了。

column1: He claims that he made a pledge to a muse spirit that he would remain celibate, so that his poetry would be remembered forever.
column2: 他声称曾向一位缪斯之灵立下誓言，要保持独身，这样他的诗歌才会被永远铭记。

column1: \x01@\x01, the ranking Uralda priestess of the \x01@! clan, wanted to marry our melancholy young weaponthane \x01@\x10, but he was reluctant.
column2: \x01@\x01 \x01@! 氏族的首席乌拉尔达祭司，曾想嫁给我们忧郁的年轻武器领主 \x01@\x10，但他不情愿。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors said that we had unnecessarily disturbed them from their revels in the Halls of the Dead. Any fool could see that the clan ring had the right to make matches for its young people.
column2: 我们祖先之灵说，我们平白无故打扰了他们在死者之厅的欢宴。任何傻瓜都能看出，氏族议会有权为其年轻人安排婚事。

column1: They said they would take some of our luck from us, so as to encourage us to contact them only to ask questions we did not already know the answer to.
column2: 他们说要从我们这里取走一些运气，以此鼓励我们只在询问那些我们已经不知道答案的问题时才去联系他们。

column1: Convince him to marry her.
column2: 说服他娶她。

column1: \x01@N spoke to \x01@\x10, disputing his objections to the match.
column2: \x01@N 对 \x01@\x10说了话，反驳他对这门亲事的反对。

column1: \x01@\x10 would not be persuaded.
column2: \x01@\x10 没有被说服。

column1: “Our love is too powerful a thing to be swept away by mere words,” he said.
column2: “我们的爱太过强大，不能仅仅被几句话就冲走，”他说。

column1: \x01@\x10 was forced to concede that his love for \x01@\x07 was unrequited.
column2: \x01@\x10 被迫承认他对 \x01@\x07 的爱是单相思。

column1: \x01@\x10 admitted that other marriages prospered despite great age differences.
column2: \x01@\x10 承认尽管年龄相差悬殊，其他婚姻依然美满。

column1: \x01@\x10 admitted that his muse spirit had helped him to create no truly memorable poems.
column2: \x01@\x10 承认他的缪斯之灵并未帮他创作出任何真正值得铭记的诗歌。

column1: The match was made, sealing an alliance between our two clans. The people of both clans rejoiced.
column2: 婚事已定，为我们两个氏族之间的联盟加了封印。两个氏族的百姓都欢欣鼓舞。

column1: “My love for \x01@\x07 is too powerful a thing to be swept away by mere words,” he said.
column2: “我对 \x01@\x07 的爱太过强大，不能仅仅被几句话就冲走，”他说。

column1: “It may be wrong, but I cannot love a woman who is not beautiful to me,” he said.
column2: “也许这是不对的，但我无法爱上一个在我看来不美丽的女人，”他说。

column1: “I will not break a promise, even a promise made to an insubstantial spirit,” he said.
column2: “我不会违背诺言，即使是向一个虚幻的灵体许下的诺言，”他说。

column1: Order him to marry her.
column2: 命令他娶她。

column1: The clan ring ordered him to submit to the match.
column2: 氏族议会命令他服从这门亲事。

column1: The match was made, sealing an alliance between our two clans. The carls were pleased by his bride’s gift to the clan, but the weaponthanes felt sorry for him.
column2: 婚事已定，为我们两个氏族之间的联盟加了封印。自由民对他的新娘赠予氏族的礼物感到满意，但武器领主们为他感到难过。

column1: Refuse the match.
column2: 拒绝这门亲事。

column1: We refused the match.
column2: 我们拒绝了这门亲事。

column1: The carls were displeased that we would not get the gift she had promised to the clan, but the warriors were pleased that the clan ring would not force their fellow into an unhappy marriage. We could see that \x01@\x01 and her entourage were disappointed by our refusal.
column2: 自由民对我们得不到她许诺给氏族的礼物感到不悦，但武士们很高兴氏族议会没有强迫他们的同胞进入一段不幸的婚姻。我们能看到 \x01@\x01 和她的随从对我们的拒绝感到失望。

column1: Convince \x01@\x07 to renounce him.
column2: 说服 \x01@\x07 放弃他。

column1: \x01@N went to \x01@\x07, to convince her to renounce any love for \x01@\x10.
column2: \x01@N 去找 \x01@\x07，说服她放弃对 \x01@\x10的爱。

column1: She said that her affections lay elsewhere, and that she would inform him of this. She did so, and \x01@\x10 disappeared soon thereafter. The people feared that he had done some great harm to himself.
column2: 她说她的情意另有所属，并会告知他这一点。她这么做了，而 \x01@\x10 此后不久便消失了。人们担心他对自己做了什么严重的伤害。

column1: \x01@\x01 had little to say about the disappearance of her intended.
column2: \x01@\x01 对她心上人的失踪几乎没说什么。

column1: She said she would rather leap onto a flaming pyre than to break the heart of silver-tongued \x01@\x10. Her clan mates reproached \x01@N for asking her to do such a cruel thing, and said that we were greedy for the old hag’s cows.
column2: 她说她宁愿跳入熊熊火堆，也不愿伤透那银舌诗人 \x01@\x10的心。她的氏族同伴责备 \x01@N 要求她做出如此残忍之事，并说我们是贪图老巫婆的那些牛。

column1: The carls will understand if we don’t get \x01@\x01’s cows.
column2: 如果我们得不到 \x01@\x01的牛，自由民会理解的。

column1: The carls want those fifty cows.
column2: 自由民想要那五十头牛。

column1: Fifty cows is worth more than a young man’s feelings.
column2: 五十头牛比一个年轻人的感情更有价值。

column1: Persuasion is better than coercion.
column2: 劝说比强迫更好。

column1: You can’t be a good trader without a thorough understanding of the human heart. I’ll talk to \x01@\x07, and clear the way for a prosperous marriage.
column2: 不彻底了解人心，就当不好商人。我会去和 \x01@\x07谈谈，为一段美满的婚姻扫清道路。

column1: The weaponthanes feel sorry for \x01@\x10. They don’t want us to force him to marry the old cow woman.
column2: 武器领主们为 \x01@\x10感到难过。他们不希望我们强迫他娶那个养牛的老太婆。

column1: We may take \x01@\x10’s desires into account, but this is our decision to make.
column2: 我们可以考虑 \x01@\x10的愿望，但这是由我们来做决定。

column1: \x01@\x01’s child needs a father.
column2: \x01@\x01. 的孩子需要一个父亲。

column1: Every man is fearful of marriage at first. \x01@\x10 will come to love \x01@\x01 in time.
column2: 每个男人起初都害怕婚姻。 \x01@\x10 迟早会爱上 \x01@\x01 的。

column1: She is a very holy woman. It is not right for a fertility priestess to be without a stud.
column2: 她是一位非常神圣的女人。一位丰饶祭司没有种马可不行。

column1: \x01@\x01’s clan is in our tribe. If we please them, we will have an advantage at tribal moots.
column2: \x01@\x01. 的氏族与我们在同一个部落。如果我们让他们高兴，在部落大会上我们就会有优势。

column1: If we get those cows from \x01@\x01, we can give them to other clans, and increase our standing in Dragon Pass.
column2: 如果我们从 \x01@\x01得到那些牛，就可以分给其他氏族，提高我们在龙之隘口的地位。

column1: It would be wrong to force him to marry if he does not want to.
column2: 如果他不想结婚，强迫他是不对的。

column1: I told you that the widows would come out of the woodwork once they got a look at \x01@\x10’s warm and melting eyes.
column2: 我告诉过你，那些寡妇一见到 \x01@\x10那温暖融化的眼神，就会纷纷冒出来。

column1: Marriages make peace.
column2: 联姻带来和平。

column2: sceneR405

column1: A large group of people are moving towards your tula. Your warriors ride to meet them, and learn that they are the \x01@! clan. They have come from Heortland, just as you once did, and they seek permission to move through your territory on their trek northwards.
column2: 一大群人正朝你的领地移动。你的武士骑马前去迎接，得知他们是 \x01@! 氏族。他们来自赫奥特兰，就像你们当年一样，请求允许经过你的领土向北迁徙。

column1: How many warriors do you attack with?
column2: 你派多少武士进攻？

column1: We attacked the \x01@! clan.
column2: 我们袭击了 \x01@! 氏族。

column1: They thanked us, and said they would remember the good turn we had done them.
column2: 他们向我们道谢，说会记住我们的善意。

column1: Hint that it would be good if they gave you a gift.
column2: 暗示他们最好送份礼物。

column1: Our emissaries indicated that a gift might be appropriate in this situation.
column2: 我们的使者表示，这种情况送份礼物或许合适。

column1: They gave us jewelry of silver, with fine stones. We allowed them to pass.
column2: 他们给了我们银制珠宝，镶有精美的宝石。我们允许他们通过。

column1: They seemed affronted by this suggestion, saying that where they came from, there was a difference between a gift given willingly, and tribute demanded by a greedy clan.
column2: 他们似乎被这个提议冒犯了，说在他们家乡，自愿赠予的礼物与贪婪氏族索要的贡品是有区别的。

column1: Propose an alliance.
column2: 提议结盟。

column1: We proposed an alliance with them.
column2: 我们提议与他们结盟。

column1: Their clan ring agreed that it would be good to have friends in a new land. To seal the arrangement, we exchanged gifts of equal value. Then we let them pass through our tula.
column2: 他们的氏族议会同意，在新土地上有朋友是好事。为缔结盟约，我们交换了等值礼物。然后让他们通过了我们的领地。

column1: Their chief did not rule out a future alliance, but said that it would be unwise to make commitments until they had settled themselves in this unfamiliar land.
column2: 他们的首领没有排除未来结盟的可能，但说在这片陌生土地安顿下来之前就做出承诺是不明智的。

column1: They said they would seek a more gracious clan.
column2: 他们说会去找更友善的氏族。

column1: What do you demand of them?
column2: 你向他们要求什么？

column1: They gave us what we demanded, so we let them pass.
column2: 他们给了我们所要求的，于是我们放他们通过。

column1: They were angered by our demand, and said they would seek another route, finding a way to their destination that did not take them through the lands of a greedy clan.
column2: 我们的要求激怒了他们，他们说会另寻路线，找一条不经过贪婪氏族领地的路前往目的地。

column1: Their cows are sick. Do we really want them tramping through our tula, and possibly passing the disease spirits along to our own herds?
column2: 他们的牛生病了。我们真想让它们踩过我们的领地，可能把疾病之灵传给我们的牲畜吗？

column1: They have many cows. They should give us some.
column2: 他们有很多牛。应该给我们一些。

column1: They have many cows. We should raid them.
column2: 他们有很多牛。我们应该去抢。

column1: What do you think we can get out of them?
column2: 你觉得我们能从他们那里得到什么？

column1: If our request for a reward is clumsily worded, they may be insulted.
column2: 如果我们索要报酬的话说得不妥，他们可能会觉得受辱。

column1: I’m not saying we should demand tribute. But if we do, we should ask for no more than twenty cows.
column2: 我不是说我们应该索要贡品。但如果真要，最多不超过二十头牛。

column1: Do not try to fight them; they have grown strong from many seasons of hard survival in the wilderness.
column2: 别试图与他们战斗；他们在荒野中历经多季艰苦求生，已经变得强大。

column1: Their long trek has weakened them, and we know this terrain better than they. They will be easy prey for our fighters.
column2: 他们的长途跋涉削弱了他们，而我们比他们更熟悉这片地形。对我们的战士来说，他们是容易得手的猎物。

column1: Their warriors are many, and they have been hardened by the long trek north. We should not fight with them, but ally with them.
column2: 他们的武士很多，而且漫长的北行之旅使他们变得坚韧。我们不应与他们交战，而应结盟。

column1: They may or may not be willing to forge an alliance when they do not know the clans hereabouts.
column2: 他们不熟悉此地的氏族，可能愿意也可能不愿意缔结联盟。

column1: They may or may not be willing to forge an alliance when they do not know the clans hereabouts, but there is no harm in asking.
column2: 他们不熟悉此地的氏族，可能愿意也可能不愿意缔结联盟，但问一问也无妨。

column1: We don’t need to make more enemies now, when we belong in the fields, planting.
column2: 我们现在不需要树敌更多，这时候我们应该在田里播种。

column1: We don’t need to make more enemies now, when we belong in the fields, harvesting.
column2: 我们现在不需要树敌更多，这时候我们应该在田里收割。

column1: For years, brave Orlanthi from Heortland have left their home for this new place, fleeing the rule of the usurper called the Pharaoh.
column2: 多年来，勇敢的赫奥特兰奥兰斯人逃离自称为法老的篡位者的统治，离开家园来到这片新地方。

column1: Excessive kindness should not blind us to opportunities for plunder and glory.
column2: 过度的仁慈不应让我们对劫掠与荣耀的机会视而不见。

column1: An alliance is only good if it brings peace.
column2: 联盟只有在带来和平时才有意义。

column1: Of course we must let them pass! Think of how we would feel if we wore their boots!
column2: 当然要让他们通过！想想如果我们穿上他们的靴子会作何感受！

column1: Let them through.
column2: 放他们过去。

column1: These wriggling maggots would pollute our tula by their very presence!
column2: 这些蠕动的蛆虫，光是存在就会玷污我们的领地！

column1: Those who can no longer embrace a new friend will one day be embraced by Wakboth the Devil.
column2: 那些无法接纳新朋友的人，终有一天会被恶魔瓦克博斯所接纳。

column1: Mosgrain, one of the weaponthanes you sent on the exploration party to the \x01@O, returns from the expedition without a hand. He tells a terrifying story. “We found a land still impregnated by Chaos, especially in the many tunnels and caves that underlie it. \x01@I and I chose to explore one of the larger groups of tunnels, for we saw broo within and thought it would be holy to slay them. Instead, we fought a Chaotic magician with a hand for a head, and hands for feet. He captured me and chopped off my hand. Then \x01@I and others came and rescued me from his clutches. I know he means to make my hand a part of him, and fear that I will be forever cursed by Chaos unless it is destroyed. Please, let us assemble another expedition quickly, before we are all tainted by this awful magic.”
column2: 莫斯格兰，你派往 \x01@O的探险队中的一位武器领主，少了一只手回到了远征队。他讲述了一个可怕的故事：“我们发现了一片仍被混沌浸染的土地，尤其是底下众多隧道和洞穴。 \x01@I 和我选择了探索一个较大的隧道群，因为我们看到里面有兽人，认为杀死他们会是神圣之举。然而，我们与一个奇异的混沌法师战斗，他长着像手一样的头和手脚。他抓住了我，砍掉了我的手。然后 \x01@I 和其他人赶来，把我从他手中救出。我知道他想把我的手变成他的一部分，我担心除非毁掉它，否则我将永远被混沌诅咒。请让我们尽快再组一支远征队，免得我们全被这可怕的魔法玷污。”

column1: We went exploring and found a land still impregnated by Chaos. A weird magician stole Mosgrain’s hand and made it a part of him. Mosgrain wanted to go back and destroy his stolen hand.
column2: 我们去探险，发现了一片仍被混沌浸染的土地。一个奇怪的法师偷走了莫斯格兰的手，并把它变成了他的一部分。莫斯格兰想回去毁掉他被偷走的手。

column1: Enact a ritual to remove the taint of Chaos from him.
column2: 举行仪式来祛除他身上混沌的污染。

column1: We enacted a ritual, which we hoped would remove the taint of Chaos from him.
column2: 我们举行了一场仪式，希望能祛除他身上混沌的污染。

column1: Our clan magicians said the signs were good.
column2: 我们的氏族法师说，征兆是吉的。

column1: “Mosgrain need not worry about Chaos taint, nor should any of the rest of us.”
column2: “莫斯格兰不必担心混沌污染，我们其他人也一样。”

column1: “We have reduced the threat of Chaos, but cannot say that Mosgrain is fully free from its taint.
column2: “我们削弱了混沌的威胁，但不能说莫斯格兰已完全摆脱其污染。”

column1: Our clan magicians shook their heads, and said that our ritual had not prevailed against Chaos.
column2: 我们的氏族法师摇了摇头，说我们的仪式没能战胜混沌。

column1: Hire mercenaries to destroy Mosgrain’s hand.
column2: 雇佣佣兵摧毁莫斯格兰的手。

column1: We decided to hire mercenaries to destroy Mosgrain’s hand.
column2: 我们决定雇佣佣兵摧毁莫斯格兰的手。

column1: We found no one willing to fight a Chaos magician on our behalf.
column2: 我们找不到愿意为我们对抗混沌法师的人。

column1: Warriors of the \x01@! clan will do it if you gift each of them with ten milk cows.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的武士会去做，只要你赠予他们每人十头奶牛。

column1: They brought back Mosgrain’s hand, and said that we had bargained well with them. “We would never go to that place again, even if you gave us twenty cows each.”
column2: 他们带回了莫斯格兰的手，说我们与他们谈了一笔好买卖。“就算你给我们每人二十头牛，我们也不会再去那个地方了。”

column1: They never came back. Their families came to our tula to accuse us of hiring them for a mission we knew meant certain death.
column2: 他们再也没有回来。他们的家人来到我们的图拉领地，指控我们雇佣他们执行一项我们明知必死的任务。

column1: Do you compensate their families for their deaths, as if wergild were due to them?
column2: 你是否要像支付血偿金一样，补偿他们家人的死亡？

column1: We compensated the families for their deaths, as if wergild were to due them.
column2: 我们补偿了他们家人的死亡，就像血偿金应得的那样。

column1: They pronounced themselves more than satisfied with this result.
column2: 他们宣称对这个结果非常满意。

column1: We did nothing to remedy their grief.
column2: 我们没有采取任何行动来抚慰他们的悲痛。

column1: They said that they would tell people never to trust us.
column2: 他们说会告诉世人永远不要信任我们。

column1: Outlaw Mosgrain, then kill him.
column2: 将莫斯格兰逐出氏族，然后杀了他。

column1: We outlawed Mosgrain, and then killed him.
column2: 我们将莫斯格兰逐出氏族，然后杀了他。

column1: The other weaponthanes were most perturbed, but the other people said that this harsh measure was necessary to ward off Chaos.
column2: 其他武器领主极为不安，但其他人说，这种严厉措施是抵御混沌所必需的。

column1: The weaponthanes were displeased by this decision; they felt we should have granted Mosgrain’s request. The devotees of Urox said that the clan ring was courting Chaos.
column2: 武器领主们对此决定感到不满；他们认为我们本该同意莫斯格兰的请求。尤洛克斯的信徒说氏族议会正在招惹混沌。

column1: Send a party to recover Mosgrain’s hand.
column2: 派遣一支队伍去取回莫斯格兰的手。

column1: We sent a party to recover Mosgrain’s hand.
column2: 我们派遣了一支队伍去取回莫斯格兰的手。

column1: Who leads the party to the Chaos lands?
column2: 谁率领这支队伍前往混沌之地？

column1: \x01@\x05 could not find the sorcerer, although \x06 witnessed many other horrors in the Chaos-soaked tunnels of this place. \x01@\x05 took several wounds doing battle with them.
column2: \x01@\x05 未能找到那巫师，尽管 \x06 目睹了这个地方被混沌浸透的隧道中的许多其他恐怖景象。 \x01@\x05 在与它们战斗时受了几处伤。

column1: \x01@\x05 could not find the sorcerer, although the party witnessed many other horrors in the Chaos-soaked tunnels of this place. Several of our warriors were wounded in battle with them.
column2: \x01@\x05 未能找到那巫师，尽管队伍目睹了这个地方被混沌浸透的隧道中的许多其他恐怖景象。我们有几名武士在与它们战斗时受了伤。

column1: \x01@\x05 found the magician’s lair, and our party did battle with him. He turned the air green, and monsters came forth from it and sliced at us.
column2: \x01@\x05 找到了那法师的巢穴，我们的队伍与他交战。他将空气变成绿色，怪物从中涌出，向我们砍杀。

column1: \x01@\x05 found the magician’s lair, and did battle with him. He turned the air green, and monsters came forth from it and sliced at \x01@\x05.
column2: \x01@\x05 找到了那法师的巢穴，并与他交战。他将空气变成绿色，怪物从中涌出，向 \x01@\x05砍杀。

column1: It was hard to fight in the tunnels, for there wasn’t room for all of our warriors to fight at once. Some looked on helplessly as their forward fellows were wounded.
column2: 在隧道中战斗很艰难，因为空间不足以让所有武士同时作战。一些人只能无助地看着前方的同伴受伤。

column1: Finally, \x01@\x05 got close enough to the magician to lop his right hand off. \x05 lopped off the left for good measure. The magician folded himself up into a square and vanished, but
column2: 终于， \x01@\x05 靠近到足以砍掉那法师右手的距离。 \x05 又砍掉了左手以绝后患。那法师将自己折叠成一个方块消失了，但

column1: the objective had been achieved. \x01@\x05 found silver combs and a bejeweled sword hilt in the magician’s lair.
column2: 目标已经达成。 \x01@\x05 在法师的巢穴中发现了银梳子和一把镶宝石的剑柄。

column1: our objective had been achieved. We found silver combs and a bejeweled sword hilt in the magician’s lair.
column2: 我们的目标已经达成。我们在法师的巢穴中发现了银梳子和一把镶宝石的剑柄。

column1: Do you take the treasure?
column2: 你拿不拿这些宝物？

column1: \x01@\x05 claimed these spoils.
column2: \x01@\x05 声称占有了这些战利品。

column1: We claimed these spoils.
column2: 我们声称占有了这些战利品。

column1: \x01@\x05 did not take it.
column2: \x01@\x05 没有拿走它。

column1: We did not take it.
column2: 我们没有拿走它。

column1: The magician’s spectral minions painted the walls of his cave with our blood.
column2: 法师的幽魂仆从用我们的血涂满了他的洞穴墙壁。

column1: Finally \x01@\x05 was forced to withdraw, having failed to achieve \x04 objective.
column2: 终于， \x01@\x05 被迫撤退，未能达成 \x04 目标。

column1: Finally we were forced to withdraw, having failed to achieve our objective.
column2: 终于，我们被迫撤退，未能达成我们的目标。

column1: \x01@\x05, who led the party, seemed unharmed after we left the tunnels. But soon after \x06 regurgitated something which was green and writhed, and died shortly thereafter.
column2: \x01@\x05，他率领队伍，离开隧道后似乎毫发无伤。但不久之后， \x06 吐出了一团绿色扭动的东西，随即死去。

column1: We can’t afford to hire mercenaries.
column2: 我们雇不起佣兵。

column1: We can afford to hire mercenaries; better to lose cows than the lives of our own warriors.
column2: 我们雇得起佣兵；损失奶牛总好过牺牲我们自己武士的生命。

column1: Mercenaries will ask for many cows when they learn that their foe is Chaos.
column2: 当佣兵得知他们的敌人是混沌时，他们会索要许多奶牛。

column1: We will have to pay ten cows apiece to convince mercenaries to fight Chaos for us.
column2: 我们必须为每个佣兵支付十头奶牛，才能说服他们为我们对抗混沌。

column1: We will have to pay ten cows apiece to convince mercenaries to fight Chaos for us. If they are slain, their families may expect further compensation.
column2: 我们必须为每个佣兵支付十头奶牛，才能说服他们为我们对抗混沌。如果他们被杀，他们的家人可能期望进一步的补偿。

column1: Mosgrain has done nothing wrong. We can’t outlaw him, much less kill him.
column2: 莫斯格兰没有做错任何事。我们不能将他逐出氏族，更不用说杀了他。

column1: We have the legal right to outlaw Mosgrain. He wouldn’t be the first Orlanthi who was ever unfairly outlawed.
column2: 我们有合法权利将莫斯格兰逐出氏族。他不会是被不公正地逐出氏族的第一个奥兰提人。

column1: Although it would be very harsh and perhaps unjust, ending the Chaos taint by killing Mosgrain would not be unprecedented.
column2: 尽管这样做会非常严厉甚至可能不公，但通过杀死莫斯格兰来终结混沌污染并非没有先例。

column1: We needn’t fear Chaos.
column2: 我们无需畏惧混沌。

column1: Chaos is always a dangerous enemy.
column2: 混沌始终是危险的敌人。

column1: If the warriors are to fight in an underground lair, there is no point in sending too many of them. Only so many will be able to join such a battle.
column2: 若战士要在地下巢穴作战，派去太多人也无意义。能参与此战的只有那么多人。

column1: If the warriors are to fight in an underground lair, there is no point in sending more than ten of them. The others would be able to do nothing more than look on as the others battle.
column2: 若战士要在地下巢穴作战，派去超过十人也无意义。其他人除了旁观作战，别无他事可做。

column1: Mosgrain’s fellows will understand if we outlaw him.
column2: 莫斯格兰的同袍们会理解我们将他放逐。

column1: Mosgrain’s fellows will be demoralized if we outlaw and slay him.
column2: 若我们放逐并处死莫斯格兰，他的同袍们会士气低落。

column1: Mosgrain’s fellows will be demoralized if we outlaw and slay him, but the carls will be glad to know that his presence will not taint us with Chaos.
column2: 若我们放逐并处死莫斯格兰，他的同袍们会士气低落，但自由民们会很高兴，知道他的存在不会让混沌玷污我们。

column1: The theft of Mosgrain’s hand will not taint us.
column2: 莫斯格兰的手被夺，不会玷污我们。

column1: If Mosgrain’s hand lives at the end of a magician’s arm, he will be haunted by Chaos — and so will those who harbor him.
column2: 若莫斯格兰的手存活在法师的臂膀末端，他将被混沌纠缠——收留他的人亦然。

column1: Our magic is strong; we should enact a ritual to purify Mosgrain.
column2: 我们的魔法强大；应当举行仪式净化莫斯格兰。

column1: Our magic is weak; a ritual to purify Mosgrain is likely to fail.
column2: 我们的魔法弱小；净化莫斯格兰的仪式很可能会失败。

column1: Let me lead the party; only I can find the magician’s cave again.
column2: 让我带领队伍；只有我能再次找到法师的洞穴。

column1: Let me lead the party; only I can properly smite Chaos!
column2: 让我带领队伍；只有我能正确击溃混沌！

column1: Let me lead the party; only I can steal the hand off a person’s wrist.
column2: 让我带领队伍；只有我能从人的手腕上偷走那只手。

column1: There are so many… I just don’t…
column2: 太多了……我只是不……

column1: No one will marry into our clan if Mosgrain stays here.
column2: 若莫斯格兰留在这里，没人会嫁入我们的氏族。

column1: Let someone else fight Chaos for us!
column2: 让其他人替我们对抗混沌吧！

column1: The exploration mission to the \x01@O has returned. Alirene, one of the weaponthanes you sent on that mission, reports that the area is full of dragonewts. “We found one interesting place there. A temple of sorts. Had a silver statue of a dragon, with gems for eyes. It must be very valuable. Let’s send a group there to steal it and bring it back.”
column2: 前往 \x01@O 的探索任务已返回。你派去的武器领主之一阿莉蕾妮报告说，该地遍布龙人。“我们在那里发现了一个有趣的地方。某种神殿。有座银龙雕像，眼睛镶着宝石。一定非常值钱。我们派一队人去偷走它，带回来吧。”

column1: The exploration mission to the \x01@O returned, having sighted many dragonewts there. Alirene, one of our weaponthanes, said we should go back to steal a silver statue of a dragon from them.
column2: 前往 \x01@O 的探索任务返回了，他们在那里见到了许多龙人。我们的武器领主之一阿莉蕾妮说，我们应当回去从它们手中偷走一座银龙雕像。

column1: Compose a poem to commemorate Alirene’s adventure.
column2: 创作一首诗来纪念阿莉蕾妮的冒险。

column1: We composed a poem to commemorate Alirene’s adventure.
column2: 我们创作了一首诗来纪念阿莉蕾妮的冒险。

column1: Everyone said it was an excellent poem, and would increase our fame.
column2: 人人都说这是首卓越的诗，能提高我们的声望。

column1: It was not one of \x01@N’s better efforts.
column2: 这算不上 \x01@N的佳作之一。

column1: Alirene
column2: 阿莉蕾妮

column1: Forget the incident.
column2: 忘了这件事。

column1: We chose not to pursue the matter.
column2: 我们选择不再追究此事。

column1: Hire mercenaries to get the treasure for you.
column2: 雇佣佣兵替你去取宝物。

column1: We decided to hire mercenaries to get the treasure.
column2: 我们决定雇佣佣兵去取宝物。

column1: Warriors of the \x01@! clan will do it if you gift each of them with five cows worth of goods.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的战士愿意做这件事，只要赠予每人价值五头牛的财物。

column1: We seized the statue from them.
column2: 我们从他们手中夺走了雕像。

column1: We failed to find the silver dragon statue.
column2: 我们未能找到银龙雕像。

column1: Launch a legal claim.
column2: 提起法律诉讼。

column1: They denied that they had the statue, and we had no proof to the contrary.
column2: 他们否认拥有雕像，我们也没有反证。

column1: Forget the matter.
column2: 忘了这事。

column1: The people said it was our fault for trying to get a great treasure at a bargain price.
column2: 人们说，我们试图以低价获取重宝，是我们的过错。

column1: They never came back. Instead their families came to our tula to accuse us of hiring them for a mission we knew meant certain death.
column2: 他们再未归来。反而他们的家人来到我们的图拉领地，指控我们雇佣他们执行明知必死的任务。

column1: We compensated these families for the deaths, as if wergild were due to the relatives of the \x01@! warriors.
column2: 我们补偿了这些死者家属，如同向 \x01@! 族战士的亲属支付了血偿金。

column1: We did nothing to remedy the grief of the relatives of the \x01@! warriors.
column2: 我们未采取任何措施安抚 \x01@! 族战士亲属的悲痛。

column1: Send a party to steal the statue.
column2: 派一队人去偷雕像。

column1: We sent a party to steal the statue.
column2: 我们派了一队人去偷雕像。

column1: They found the statue and spirited it away, without attracting the attention of the dragonewts.
column2: 他们找到了雕像并悄悄带走，未引起龙人的注意。

column1: They found the statue, but also attracted the attention of the dragonewts, who attacked furiously. There were many more dragonewts than we had expected.
column2: 他们找到了雕像，但也引起了龙人的注意，龙人愤怒地发动攻击。龙人的数量远超我们的预期。

column1: They held them off until a good opportunity to escape presented itself. In so doing, they slew \x01@\x1A dragonewts.
column2: 他们抵挡龙人，直到找到逃脱良机。在此过程中，他们杀死了 \x01@\x1A 只龙人。

column1: Alirene fought like a woman possessed; the entire party would have perished without her.
column2: 阿莉蕾妮战斗如同被附身的女战士；若没有她，整队人都会丧命。

column1: Their numbers were too much for us, and they fell upon us, killing some and wounding others. The warrior holding the silver statue was the first to die.
column2: 敌人数量太多，我们无法抵挡，他们扑上来，杀死了一些人，伤及另一些。手持银龙雕像的战士最先死去。

column1: Alirene, who’d found the statue, and \x01@\x05, who led the party, were among the slain.
column2: 发现雕像的阿莉蕾妮和率领队伍的 \x01@\x05都在阵亡之列。

column1: Alirene, who’d found the statue, was among the slain.
column2: 发现雕像的阿莉蕾妮在阵亡之列。

column1: Tell another clan about this opportunity.
column2: 把这次机会告诉另一个氏族。

column1: We told the \x01Ý about this opportunity.
column2: 我们把这次机会告诉了 \x01Ý 。

column1: A few weeks later, they came to thank us. They said that their warriors had captured the silver dragon. They gave us some horses as a token of gratitude.
column2: 数周后，他们前来道谢。他们说自己的战士已夺取银龙。他们赠予我们一些马匹作为谢礼。

column1: A few weeks later, we heard that many of their warriors had been slain by dragonewts while attempting to take the statue. Our people were glad that we had not risked doing so.
column2: 数周后，我们听说他们许多战士在试图夺取雕像时被龙人杀死。我们的人庆幸没有冒险这么做。

column1: We could trade such a statue for many cows.
column2: 我们可以用这样一尊雕像换取许多牛只。

column1: We should hire others to do it; although it will cost us a few cows for each warrior we hire, the value of the statue is much greater.
column2: 我们应当雇佣他人去做；虽然雇佣每个战士会花费我们几头牛，但雕像的价值大得多。

column1: People fear the dragonewts. We might have trouble finding mercenaries to steal the treasure for us.
column2: 人们害怕龙人。我们可能很难找到佣兵来为我们偷取宝物。

column1: Even if mercenaries manage to outwit and outfight the dragonewts, they’ll simply take the treasure for themselves.
column2: 即便佣兵们设法智取和战胜了龙人，他们也会将宝物据为己有。

column1: Dragonewts aren’t as fearsome as they’re made out to be.
column2: 龙人并不像传闻中那样可怕。

column1: Dragonewts are fearsome opponents, but I think this is worth the risk.
column2: 龙人是可怕的对手，但我认为这值得冒险。

column1: It is a tricky situation. The more men we send, the more likely the dragonewts are to discover them. But if the party is discovered, they will need many men to successfully fight the dragonewts.
column2: 这是一个棘手的局面。我们派出的人越多，就越容易被龙人发现。但如果小队被发现，他们又需要足够的人手才能成功与龙人作战。

column1: A well-made poem will give cheer to the warriors.
column2: 一首好诗能振奋战士们的士气。

column1: A well-made poem will give cheer to the warriors and increase our fame.
column2: 一首好诗能振奋战士们的士气，并增加我们的声望。

column1: Another clan will be suspicious if we tell them of this, and will throw rotten apples at our emissaries.
column2: 如果我们把这事告诉另一个氏族，他们会起疑心，并向我们的使者扔烂苹果。

column1: This is a chance to improve our relations with another clan.
column2: 这是一个改善我们与其他氏族关系的机会。

column1: This is a chance to improve our relations with the \x01@a clan.
column2: 这是一个改善我们与 \x01@a 氏族关系的机会。

column1: This is a chance to improve our relations with the \x01@u clan.
column2: 这是一个改善我们与 \x01@u 氏族关系的机会。

column1: This sounds like another way to pull farmers away from planting and lose them forever in some foreign place.
column2: 这听起来像是另一种把农夫从播种中拉走，让他们永远迷失在某个异乡的办法。

column1: This sounds like another way to pull farmers away from the harvest and lose them forever in some foreign place.
column2: 这听起来像是另一种把农夫从收割中拉走，让他们永远迷失在某个异乡的办法。

column1: Some say that the dragonewts worship dragons. Others say that they worship in order to become dragons themselves.
column2: 有人说龙人崇拜龙。也有人说他们崇拜是为了让自己变成龙。

column1: Only I can lead the party, for I am tricky enough to succeed.
column2: 只有我能带领这支队伍，因为我有足够的机巧确保成功。

column1: Only I am cool-headed enough to lead this party.
column2: 只有我足够冷静，能带领这支队伍。

column1: I must lead the party, for it is my turn for glory!
column2: 我必须带领这支队伍，因为轮到我获取荣耀了！

column1: It would be insane to insult our friends, the dragonewts.
column2: 侮辱我们的朋友龙人，简直是疯了。

column1: If we anger them too greatly, the dragonewts will destroy us all!
column2: 如果我们太过激怒他们，龙人会摧毁我们所有人！

column1: It is rude to steal.
column2: 偷窃是不礼貌的。

column1: After examining the statue of the Silver Dragon, I am ready to say this: I don’t quite know what it is, but I do know that it is powerful magic. Don’t let anyone talk us into selling it or giving it away. I think it will help us more than we realize.
column2: 在检查了银龙雕像之后，我可以这样说：我不太清楚它究竟是什么，但我知道它蕴藏着强大的魔力。别让任何人说服我们卖掉它或把它送人。我认为它的帮助会超乎我们的想象。

column1: Lesarli, a trader of your clan, reports back on the recent exploratory mission to the wastelands of Prax. There the party met a group of nomads who rode fabulous birds, and claimed to be doughty warriors. They offered to help us raid another clan in Dragon Pass, in exchange for twenty cows worth of silver, and a quarter of the spoils.
column2: 你族中的一位商人莱萨莉，汇报了最近对普拉克斯荒地的探险任务。在那里，小队遇到了一群骑着神骏大鸟的游牧民，他们自称是勇猛的战士。他们提出帮助我们袭击龙隘地区的另一个氏族，以换取价值二十头牛的银币，外加战利品的四分之一。

column1: While exploring in Prax, we found a group of bird-riding nomads willing to help us raid a neighboring clan.
column2: 在普拉克斯探险时，我们发现了一群骑鸟游牧民，愿意帮我们袭击一个邻近氏族。

column1: Accept their offer; delay raid until later.
column2: 接受他们的提议；暂缓袭击。

column1: We gave them their silver, and told them we would call on them later.
column2: 我们给了他们银币，并告诉他们我们日后会召唤他们。

column1: The god-talkers said that our ancestors were unhappy that we’d made deals with the hated Praxians.
column2: 神言者们说，我们的祖先对我们与可憎的普拉克斯人做交易感到不悦。

column1: Accept their offer; stage an immediate raid.
column2: 接受他们的提议；立即发动袭击。

column1: We took them up on their offer.
column2: 我们接受了他们的提议。

column1: With Praxian help, our raid was a success.
column2: 在普拉克斯人的帮助下，我们的袭击成功了。

column1: But the god-talkers said that our ancestors were unhappy that we’d allied with the hated Praxians.
column2: 但神言者们说，我们的祖先对我们与可憎的普拉克斯人结盟感到不悦。

column1: The help of the Praxians was not enough to allow us to overcome our foes.
column2: 普拉克斯人的帮助不足以让我们战胜敌人。

column1: The god-talkers said that our ancestors thought it served us right, and that they hoped we never again allied with the hated Praxians.
column2: 神言者们说，我们的祖先认为我们活该如此，并希望我们再也不要与可憎的普拉克斯人结盟。

column1: Forget their offer.
column2: 忘了他们的提议。

column1: We did not pursue their offer.
column2: 我们没有理会他们的提议。

column1: We couldn’t be bothered with mere Praxians.
column2: 我们无暇理会区区普拉克斯人。

column1: Send a party to raid them.
column2: 派一支队伍去袭击他们。

column1: We sent a war party to raid them.
column2: 我们派了一支战团去袭击他们。

column1: The nomads must have sensed our hostile intent. We did not find them again.
column2: 那些游牧民一定察觉到了我们的敌意。我们没能再找到他们。

column1: We found the nomads and did battle with them.
column2: 我们找到了那些游牧民并与他们交战。

column1: We slew \x01@\x18 of them, sending the rest to rout. The ardor of our victorious warriors was cooled by the lack of treasure to be had.
column2: 我们杀了他们 \x01@\x18 人，将其余的击溃。然而因缴获甚少，获胜战士们的热情也随之冷却。

column1: They were accustomed to fighting on the flat, hot plains of Prax, and our warriors could not counter the speed they reached on top of those great running birds of theirs.
column2: 他们习惯了在普拉克斯平坦炎热的平原上战斗，我们的战士无法应对他们骑乘那些巨大奔跑鸟时达到的速度。

column1: None of us died in the melee.
column2: 我们在混战中无人阵亡。

column1: One of our warriors died in the melee.
column2: 我们的一名战士在混战中阵亡。

column1: \x01@\x1A of our warriors died in the melee.
column2: \x01@\x1A 我们的一名战士在混战中阵亡。

column1: We were lucky and only took minor scratches.
column2: 我们很幸运，只受了些轻伤。

column1: We limped home with
column2: 我们一瘸一拐地回到家中，带着

column1: We limped home with \x01@} bleeding weaponthanes and
column2: 我们一瘸一拐地回到家中，带着 \x01@} 名流血的武器领主和

column1: the footmen sporting only minor cuts and bruises.
column2: 步兵们只受了些轻微擦伤和瘀伤。

column1: one badly hurt footman.
column2: 一名重伤的步兵。

column1: \x01@y badly hurt footmen.
column2: \x01@y 数名重伤的步兵。

column1: Send them gifts.
column2: 送他们礼物。

column1: The nomads were very appreciative of the gifts we sent them.
column2: 那些游牧民非常感激我们送去的礼物。

column1: Our ancestors, however, were displeased, since they had warred against the Praxians.
column2: 然而，我们的祖先对此很不满，因为他们曾与普拉克斯人交战。

column1: This is a good chance to steal cows.
column2: 这是一个偷牛的好机会。

column1: We should raid the \x01@a clan; they have the most cows.
column2: 我们应该袭击 \x01@a 氏族；他们的牛最多。

column1: We have many cows, so there is no point in raiding.
column2: 我们有很多牛，所以没有袭击的必要。

column1: We have many cows now, but we might not later. Let’s pay them now, so we’ll have their help when we need it.
column2: 我们现在有很多牛，但日后未必。现在就付给他们，这样我们以后需要帮助时就能得到他们的支援。

column1: We can’t trust these thieving nomads.
column2: 我们不能信任这些偷窃成性的游牧民。

column1: I’m not sure if we can trust these nomads.
column2: 我们不确定能否信任这些游牧民。

column1: There is nothing to be gained in giving them gifts.
column2: 送他们礼物毫无益处。

column1: It is customary to give generously to foreigners who offer to raid your enemies.
column2: 按习俗，应当慷慨款待那些提议劫掠你敌人的异乡人。

column1: Let’s raid these puny nomads instead!
column2: 不如我们去劫掠这些弱小的游牧民！

column1: Let’s raid the \x01@r clan.
column2: 我们去劫掠 \x01@r 部族。

column1: These are our ancient enemies!
column2: 这些是我们的宿敌！

column1: If we raid the nomads, we can plunder without angering our neighbors.
column2: 如果我们劫掠游牧民，就能掠夺财物而不会激怒邻族。

column1: The nomads of Prax are our ancient enemies. If we ally with them, we weaken our clan magic. If we raid them, we strengthen it.
column2: 普拉克斯的游牧民是我们的宿敌。若与他们结盟，会削弱我们的氏族魔法。若劫掠他们，则会增强它。

column1: Take them up on their offer after the seeds are sown in the fields.
column2: 等到田野里的种子播下后再接受他们的提议。

column1: Take them up on their offer after the grain is cut and the harvest is counted.
column2: 等到谷物收割、收成清点后再接受他们的提议。

column1: Prax is populated by warring nomad tribes, each of which rides a different kind of animal.
column2: 普拉克斯居住着好战的游牧部落，每个部落骑乘不同种类的动物。

column1: We have warred against the Praxians since before the days of Tada. Better to fight against them, or leave them alone.
column2: 早在塔达时代之前，我们就与普拉克斯人交战。要么与他们作战，要么别去招惹。

column1: Some of you are wasting your breath, we can’t afford to hire them for anything.
column2: 你们有些人是在白费口舌，我们雇不起他们做任何事。

column1: We should gift them, so they will tell us their stories.
column2: 我们应该送他们礼物，这样他们就会给我们讲述他们的故事。

column1: They do not worship Humakt, but they will help him by bringing about the deaths of our foes.
column2: 他们不崇拜胡马克特，但会通过杀死我们的敌人来帮助他。

column1: It is time to hear the ring of sword against sword!
column2: 是时候听剑刃相击的铿锵之声了！

column1: We must respond to their generous offer with generosity of our own, lest we be shamed.
column2: 我们必须以我们自己的慷慨回应他们的慷慨提议，以免蒙羞。

column1: The nomads are elf-friends, and we should punish them for it.
column2: 这些游牧民是精灵之友，我们应该为此惩罚他们。

column1: The Praxians are fiercely tribal. We should not trust them.
column2: 普拉克斯人部落意识极强。我们不应该信任他们。

column2: sceneR409

column1: Helganna the Knowing, a Lhankor Mhy devotee of your clan, describes to you a curious event that took place while your exploratory party visited Mount Kero Fin. There they encountered a number of wind spirits, who claim kinship with Orlanth, and with Orlanth’s mother, the goddess Kero Fin. Some of them are called the Listening Winds; others are called the Seeing Winds. Helganna has now visited with these spirits, and suggests that the clan sacrifice to them and gain their favor.
column2: 智者赫尔甘娜，你们氏族的一位兰科尔·米信徒，向你们讲述了一件奇事，发生在你们的探险队造访凯罗芬山时。在那里，他们遇到了一些风灵，这些风灵声称与奥兰斯以及奥兰斯的母亲——女神凯罗芬有亲缘关系。其中一些被称为“听风”，另一些被称为“看风”。赫尔甘娜已拜访过这些风灵，并建议氏族向它们献祭，以获取它们的恩惠。

column1: Our explorers found spirits at Mount Kero Fin, who claimed kinship with Orlanth. Helganna the Knowing said we should sacrifice to them.
column2: 我们的探险者在凯罗芬山发现了风灵，它们声称与奥兰斯有亲缘关系。智者赫尔甘娜说我们应该向它们献祭。

column1: We did not pursue the matter.
column2: 我们没有继续追究此事。

column1: Helganna said that even if we weren’t interested in the spirits, there were many more wonders to be discovered at Mount Kero Fin.
column2: 赫尔甘娜说，即使我们对那些风灵不感兴趣，凯罗芬山还有许多奇观等待发现。

column1: Invite the spirits to inhabit a shrine at your temple.
column2: 邀请这些风灵入住你们神庙中的神龛。

column1: We built a shrine at our temple and encouraged the spirits to inhabit it.
column2: 我们在神庙中建造了一座神龛，并鼓励风灵入住其中。

column1: How much do you barter away in order to furnish this shrine?
column2: 为了装饰这座神龛，你们要交易掉多少物资？

column1: We performed a ceremony of dedication, and the spirits manifested themselves at our shrine.
column2: 我们举行了奉献仪式，风灵在我们的神龛中显灵了。

column1: Helganna was happy, and said that we’d probably find more wonders on Mount Kero Fin.
column2: 赫尔甘娜很高兴，并说我们或许会在凯罗芬山发现更多奇观。

column1: We performed a ceremony of dedication, but the spirits did not manifest themselves.
column2: 我们举行了奉献仪式，但风灵没有显灵。

column1: Helganna was disappointed, but said that we’d probably find more wonders on Mount Kero Fin.
column2: 赫尔甘娜很失望，但说我们或许会在凯罗芬山发现更多奇观。

column1: Recite to the spirits a poem you have composed in their honor.
column2: 向风灵吟诵一首你为赞美它们而创作的诗。

column1: \x01@N composed a poem in their honor and recited it to them.
column2: \x01@N 创作了一首赞美它们的诗并向它们吟诵。

column1: The spirits were pleased by the poem. A spirit which called itself an Understanding Wind said that it would bring wisdom to \x01@N.
column2: 风灵对这首诗很满意。一个自称“理解之风”的风灵说，它将为 \x01@N带来智慧。

column1: Helganna was also pleased, and said that we’d probably find more wonders on Mount Kero Fin.
column2: 赫尔甘娜也很满意，并说我们或许会在凯罗芬山发现更多奇观。

column1: The only response to \x01@N’s declamation were the howling sounds of an approaching mountain storm.
column2: 对 \x01@N的朗诵，唯一的回应是逼近的山中风暴的呼啸声。

column1: Helganna said that the signs were good, and that the spirits would favor us.
column2: 赫尔甘娜说征兆很好，风灵会眷顾我们。

column1: She said there were probably more wonders to be found on Mount Kero Fin.
column2: 她说凯罗芬山可能还有更多奇观等待发现。

column1: Helganna said that the signs were not good; the spirits had not chosen to favor us.
column2: 赫尔甘娜说征兆不妙；风灵没有选择眷顾我们。

column1: She was disappointed, but said that we’d probably find more wonders on Mount Kero Fin.
column2: 她很失望，但说我们或许会在凯罗芬山发现更多奇观。

column1: They came back a few weeks later to thank us. They said they had sacrificed to the spirits, gaining several magical powers from them. In return for our help, they performed a ritual meant to bring us luck.
column2: 几周后他们回来感谢我们。他们说已向风灵献祭，从中获得了数种魔法力量。为了回报我们的帮助，他们举行了一场旨在为我们带来好运的仪式。

column1: Helganna said that we’d probably find more wonders on Mount Kero Fin.
column2: 赫尔甘娜说我们或许会在凯罗芬山发现更多奇观。

column1: We can’t afford to sacrifice any cows to these spirits.
column2: 我们献祭不起任何牛只给这些风灵。

column1: We can well afford a sacrifice.
column2: 我们完全承担得起一次献祭。

column1: Building a shrine might be costly; so would a sacrifice.
column2: 建造神龛可能花费不菲；献祭也是如此。

column1: Building a shrine might be costly, but then again the spirits may have valuable gifts to give us in return.
column2: 建造神龛可能花费不菲，但话说回来，风灵也许会赐予我们宝贵的回礼。

column1: There is no more lasting gift than a great poem, which is remembered forever.
column2: 没有比一首伟大的诗更持久的礼物了，它会永远被铭记。

column1: Another clan will be suspicious if we tell them of this, and will make quacking noises at us, as if to say that we are as foolish as ducks.
column2: 如果我们把这件事告诉另一个氏族，他们会起疑心，并朝我们发出嘎嘎声，仿佛在说我们像鸭人一样愚蠢。

column1: This could even be a chance to improve our relations with the \x01@u clan.
column2: 这甚至可能是一个改善我们与 \x01@u 部族关系的机会。

column1: Spirits cannot be kin to gods. It makes no sense.
column2: 风灵不可能是神祇的亲戚。这说不通。

column1: The spirits may be less willing to leave their home than to accept a sacrifice.
column2: 风灵可能更不愿离开家园，而不是接受献祭。

column1: If we sacrifice to them, we will get one gift. If we build a shrine, we will get the chance to sacrifice to them repeatedly, getting a boon each time.
column2: 如果我们向他们献祭，会得到一件赐礼。如果我们修建一座神龛，就能反复向他们献祭，每次获得一份恩惠。

column1: These spirits can help us hear what our enemies are saying. They can watch our foes’ movements from the air. They can give us wisdom.
column2: 这些精魂能帮我们窃听敌人的谈话。它们能从空中监视敌人的动向。它们能赐予我们智慧。

column1: The goddess Kero Fin, of the snowy skirts, is mother to Orlanth and to Yinkin.
column2: 雪裙女神凯罗·芬，是奥兰斯与因金之母。

column1: We must build that shrine! We will have something no other clan has!
column2: 我们必须修建那座神龛！我们将拥有其他氏族没有的东西！

column1: We must be generous to these great spirits.
column2: 我们必须对这些伟大的精魂慷慨大方。

column1: Everyone will want to marry into our clan if we have a special shrine.
column2: 如果我们有一座特殊的神龛，人人都想嫁入我们氏族。

column1: These spirits are only useful if they will help us in war.
column2: 这些精魂只有在战争中帮助我们时才有用。

column1: The amount we sacrifice makes no difference; these spirits have already made up their minds about us.
column2: 我们献祭多少都无关紧要；这些精魂早已对我们有了定见。

column1: We should not encourage these winds, for we do not know what the dragonewts think about them.
column2: 我们不应鼓励这些风灵，因为我们不知道龙人对它们作何感想。
