column2: sceneR410

column1: land
column2: 土地

column1: kingdom
column2: 王国

column1: Sadratha, one of the explorers you sent to the far northwest, reports back. “We found a \x01@\x10 called Tarsh. They are a little different from us, but still know the laws and stories of the gods. While there, we were approached by an odd and dandyish fellow who called himself The Prince of Masks. He said that if we gave him silver and gems worth fifty cows, that he would visit a magical catastrophe upon any clan in Dragon Pass we chose.”
column2: 你派往远西北的探险者之一萨德拉莎回报：“我们发现了一个叫塔什的 \x01@\x10 。他们和我们有些不同，但依然懂得诸神的律法与故事。在那里，一个古怪又浮夸的家伙找上了我们，他自称面具王子。他说如果我们给他价值五十头牛的银子和宝石，他就会为我们所选的龙之隘口任意一个氏族降下魔法灾祸。”

column1: Our explorers went to the Orlanthi \x01@\x10 of Tarsh. There they met an odd fellow who called himself the Prince of Masks, and said he would visit a magical catastrophe upon any clan in Dragon Pass we chose, in exchange for a gift of silver.
column2: 我们的探险者前往塔什的奥兰西 \x01@\x10 。在那里他们遇见了一个古怪的家伙，他自称面具王子，并说只要给他一份银礼，他就会为我们所选的龙之隘口任意一个氏族降下魔法灾祸。

column1: Agree to his proposal.
column2: 同意他的提议。

column1: We agreed to his proposal.
column2: 我们同意了他的提议。

column1: Bargain with him.
column2: 与他讨价还价。

column1: We bargained with him.
column2: 我们与他讨价还价。

column1: What is the most you will give him for this service?
column2: 你最多愿为他这项服务支付多少？

column1: We could not reach an acceptable price, and left Tarsh without making an arrangement with the magician.
column2: 我们未能达成可接受的价格，于是离开了塔什，没有与那位法师达成协议。

column1: We agreed upon a price of \x01@\x15 cows worth of silver, and so he proceeded to work his magics.
column2: 我们商定了一个价格为 \x01@\x15 头牛等值的银两，于是他开始施展他的魔法。

column1: He was much affronted by our desire to bargain with him, and withdrew his offer.
column2: 我们想要讨价还价的愿望大大触怒了他，于是他收回了提议。

column1: “I should have known better than to deal with folk in Dragon Pass, who are known to be much ruder and thicker of skull than the Orlanthi of Tarsh.”
column2: “我早该知道不该与龙之隘口的人打交道，他们比塔什的奥兰西人粗鲁得多、头脑也迟钝得多。”

column1: Our warleader \x01@\x17 said that \x06 would not forget that we passed up an opportunity to settle an enemy once and for all.
column2: 我们的战争领袖 \x01@\x17 说 \x06 不会忘记我们错过了一个一劳永逸解决敌人的机会。

column1: Send a party to attack him.
column2: 派出一队人马攻击他。

column1: We sent a war party to attack him.
column2: 我们派出一支战团攻击他。

column1: Our hostile intent must have been all too clear, for the Prince of Masks did not meet our next rendezvous. Our party went all the way to Tarsh for no good reason, or so the weaponthanes grumbled.
column2: 我们的敌意一定太过明显，因为面具王子没有赴我们下一次的会面。我们的人马白跑了一趟塔什，武器领主们如此抱怨道。

column1: We found the Prince of Masks and did battle with him, much to the displeasure of the Tarshite authorities. They joined in the fight, to support their countryman.
column2: 我们找到了面具王子并与他交战，这大大激怒了塔什当局。他们加入了战斗，以支持他们的同胞。

column1: We slew \x01@\x18 Tarshite defenders, but the Prince of Masks vanished in the melee. We withdrew from Tarsh, a legion of howling warriors at our backs.
column2: 我们杀死了 \x01@\x18 名塔什守卫，但面具王子在混战中消失了。我们撤出塔什，身后是一群嚎叫的战士。

column1: Soon after, our weaponthanes began to bleed from their pores. Some recovered, but one died.
column2: 不久之后，我们的武器领主开始从毛孔中渗血。有些人康复了，但有一人死去。

column1: Soon after, our weaponthanes began to bleed from their pores. Some recovered, but others died.
column2: 不久之后，我们的武器领主开始从毛孔中渗血。有些人康复了，但另一些人死去。

column1: Soon after, many of our children died in their sleep, and our tula shook with the sounds of heartsick mourning.
column2: 不久之后，我们的许多孩子在睡梦中死去，我们的领地因心碎的哀悼之声而震颤。

column1: Soon after, many herds of our cattle were stricken with a mysterious ailment, and fell dead.
column2: 不久之后，我们的许多牛群染上怪病，倒地而死。

column1: Soon after, rodents swarmed our grain bins, and devoured large amounts of food.
column2: 不久之后，啮齿动物涌入我们的粮仓，吞食了大量食物。

column1: Soon after, the silver rings owned by our chieftain turned to horse dung. Our neighbors made many japes at our expense.
column2: 不久之后，我们首领的银环变成了马粪。我们的邻居拿我们当笑柄，开了很多玩笑。

column1: Our god-talkers said that this curse must have been visited upon us by the vengeful Prince of Masks.
column2: 我们的神言者说，这诅咒一定是复仇的面具王子降在我们身上的。

column1: With confusing magics that made the world swirl before us, the Prince of Masks made us easy prey for his defenders.
column2: 用令我们眼前世界旋转的混乱魔法，面具王子让我们成了他守卫的易捕猎物。

column1: Tell another clan about him.
column2: 将他的事告知另一个氏族。

column1: We told the \x01Ý about him.
column2: 我们告诉了 \x01Ý 关于他的事。

column1: Soon we heard that many herds of \x01@! cattle were stricken with a mysterious ailment, and fell dead.
column2: 很快我们听说， \x01@! 的许多牛群染上怪病，倒地而死。

column1: Soon we heard that many of the \x01@! weaponthanes began to bleed from their pores. Some recovered, but many others died.
column2: 很快我们听说， \x01@! 的许多武器领主开始从毛孔渗血。有些人康复了，但许多其他人死了。

column1: Soon we heard that many \x01@! children died in their sleep, and that their tula echoed with the sounds of heartsick mourning.
column2: 很快我们听说，许多 \x01@! 的孩子在睡梦中死去，他们的领地回荡着心碎的哀悼之声。

column1: They were sorely affronted. Their chieftain said, “Do you think we are a godless clan, one that consorts with weird foreign magicians?”
column2: 他们被深深冒犯了。他们的首领说：“你以为我们是一个没有神的氏族，一个与古怪的外地法师勾结的氏族吗？”

column1: Which clan do you ask him to curse?
column2: 你请他诅咒哪个氏族？

column1: The Prince of Masks said he would work his magics, but we didn’t hear about any catastrophes striking the \x01Ý.
column2: 面具王子说他将施展魔法，但我们没有听说任何灾祸降临在 \x01Ý.

column1: We should bargain that price down.
column2: 我们应该把那个价格压低。

column1: He is a haughty fellow, and will be offended if we try to bargain with him.
column2: 他是个傲慢的家伙，我们若想与他讨价还价，他会觉得被冒犯。

column1: He is a haughty fellow, and will be offended if we try to bargain with him — so offended that he will refuse to deal with us at all.
column2: 他是个傲慢的家伙，我们若想与他讨价还价，他会觉得被冒犯——冒犯到根本不愿与我们打交道。

column1: Hire him to curse one of our enemies!
column2: 雇他去诅咒我们的某个敌人！

column1: King Heort, who made the laws, decreed that we must kill strange magicians wherever we find them.
column2: 制定律法的赫奥特王曾下令，凡遇异乡法师，必杀之。

column1: Hiring foreign magicians to vex one’s foes is not illegal.
column2: 雇佣异乡法师去搅扰仇敌并不违法。

column1: Hiring foreign magicians to vex one’s foes is not illegal, but I can’t think of any great kings or heroes who would have done such a thing.
column2: 雇佣异乡法师去搅扰仇敌并不违法，但我想不出哪位伟大的国王或英雄会做这种事。

column1: We should curry favor with another clan by telling them of this opportunity to harass their foes.
column2: 我们应将这个骚扰仇敌的机会告知另一个氏族，以博取他们的好感。

column1: We should curry favor with another clan by telling them of this opportunity to harass their foes. But we must choose a clan which regards us favorably, or they will take it wrongly.
column2: 我们应将这个骚扰仇敌的机会告知另一个氏族，以博取他们的好感。但我们必须选择一个对我们有好感的氏族，否则他们会误解我们的意图。

column1: He hasn’t told us exactly what he would do to our enemies. His offer is too vague.
column2: 他没说清楚究竟会对我们的敌人做什么。他的提议太模糊了。

column1: He hasn’t told us exactly what he would do to our enemies. His offer is too vague, and we have no assurances that his magic even works.
column2: 他没说清楚究竟会对我们的敌人做什么。他的提议太模糊了，而且我们无法确认他的魔法是否真的有效。

column1: If the rest of you want to fiddle with foreign magicians, so be it. Just don’t go raiding now, when the farmers are working hard in their fields to provide the clan with food.
column2: 如果你们其他人想与异乡法师纠缠，那就随你们去吧。只是现在别去劫掠，农夫们正在田里辛勤劳作，为氏族提供食物。

column1: We have been cut off from the lands to the north for centuries. There is no telling what strange magic might be known up there.
column2: 我们与北方的土地隔绝已有数百年。谁知道那里有什么样的奇异魔法。

column1: Slay the magician! He is obviously Chaotic.
column2: 杀死那个法师！他显然是个混沌之物。

column1: There is much to admire in this fellow.
column2: 这家伙有不少值得钦佩之处。

column1: It is good to take vengeance.
column2: 报仇是件好事。

column1: Is this curse really worth the silver?
column2: 这个诅咒真值那些银子吗？

column1: It is rude to anonymously curse another clan.
column2: 匿名诅咒另一个氏族是粗鲁的行为。

column1: The silver he wants would be better spent on a new shrine or temple.
column2: 他索要的银子不如用来建座新的圣所或神庙。

column1: We don’t know what sort of curse he would make. Are we sure we could live with ourselves if he did something truly terrible to our rivals?
column2: 我们不知道他会施什么样的诅咒。如果他真的对我们的对手做了什么可怕的事，我们确信自己能心安理得吗？

column1: His magics are nothing compared to ours.
column2: 他的魔法与我们的相比不值一提。

column1: We should keep exploring, until we find a Tarshite sorcerer willing to teach us magic to use against the undead.
column2: 我们应该继续探索，直到找到一个愿意教我们对付亡灵的魔法的塔什巫师。

column1: sceneR411
column2: sceneR411

column1: While exploring, you find evidence that a great battle was fought on your tula on some long-forgotten day.
column2: 在探索中，你发现证据表明，在某个早已被遗忘的日子，你的领地上曾发生过一场大战。

column1: While exploring our tula, we found traces of an ancient battle.
column2: 在探索我们的领地时，我们发现了古战场的痕迹。

column1: Add the most interesting old weapon to your tribal regalia.
column2: 将最有趣的古武器加入部落圣物。

column1: We added an interesting old weapon to our tribal regalia.
column2: 我们将一件有趣的古武器加入了部落圣物。

column1: Our weaponthanes all thought that the axe whose blade reminded them of a bull’s horn was a fine addition to the tribal regalia. The other clans in the tribe agreed.
column2: 我们的武器领主们都认为，那柄刃口让人联想到牛角的斧头，是部落圣物的绝佳补充。部落中的其他氏族也赞同。

column1: Brag to other clans about this find.
column2: 向其他氏族吹嘘这一发现。

column1: We went to other clans and bragged about this find.
column2: 我们去其他氏族那里吹嘘了这一发现。

column1: Our neighbors were much impressed.
column2: 我们的邻居们印象深刻。

column1: Our neighbors thought we were fools for bragging about a pile of old junk.
column2: 我们的邻居认为我们为一堆破烂货吹嘘是傻瓜。

column1: Unfamiliar spirits appeared to our god-talkers. They said that they were the shield-bearers of Fynin, the Legless King, who battled the Ore Digging Tribe on this very spot, more than a thousand years ago. The great Fynin died here on that day, but killed a score and ten of his foes. The spirits recited the details of this battle, and said we should reenact it, so that Fynin’s spirit would give us a gift.
column2: 陌生的灵体出现在我们的神言者面前。他们说自己是无腿之王菲宁的盾卫者，一千多年前菲宁在此地与挖矿部落交战。伟大的菲宁在那天战死于此，但他也杀死了三十个敌人。灵体们详述了这场战斗的细节，并说我们应该重演这场战斗，这样菲宁的灵就会赐予我们礼物。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors could not tell us of this old battlefield; it was part of someone else’s history.
column2: 我们的祖先之灵无法告诉我们这片古战场的故事；它属于别人的历史。

column1: Ritually reenact the battle on this spot.
column2: 在这片土地上按仪式重演战斗。

column1: We ritually reenacted the battle.
column2: 我们按仪式重演了战斗。

column1: At the height of our ritual, we heard the clash of sword on shield, and saw the Legless King fighting his last, valiant fight. Soon afterwards, \x01@\x19 weaponthanes from far-off Tarsh came to our tula. They said that they had dreamt about King Fynin, who told them to come here and offer their services to us.
column2: 在我们仪式的高潮时，我们听到了剑盾交击之声，看到了无腿之王进行他最后的英勇战斗。不久之后， \x01@\x19 来自遥远塔什的武器领主们来到我们的领地。他们说他们梦见了菲宁王，是菲宁让他们来到这里，为我们效劳。

column1: Adopt the weaponthanes.
column2: 接纳这些武器领主。

column1: We adopted the weaponthanes.
column2: 我们接纳了这些武器领主。

column1: They told us their version of the story called “Humakt the Champion,” which was well-known up in Tarsh.
column2: 他们讲述了他们版本的“捍卫者胡玛克特”故事，这个故事在塔什那边广为人知。

column1: Our weaponthanes welcomed them warmly.
column2: 我们的武器领主热情地欢迎了他们。

column1: Everyone was glad that we now had weaponthanes to defend the clan, and gave a warm welcome to the Tarshite warriors.
column2: 所有人都很高兴我们如今有了武器领主来保卫氏族，并热烈欢迎了塔什战士。

column1: They did not voice their disappointment, but our own weaponthanes did, at great length.
column2: 他们没有表露失望，但我们自己的武器领主却大大地表达了不满。

column1: Nothing of note happened.
column2: 没有发生值得注意的事。

column1: Shrug and go about your business.
column2: 耸耸肩，继续做自己的事。

column1: I wonder if we can use this to bring cheer to the weaponthanes.
column2: 我想知道我们是否能借此给武器领主们带来些鼓舞。

column1: I do not know my history well enough to identify the banners.
column2: 我对自己的历史了解不够，认不出那些旗帜。

column1: Those weapons are very ancient. Maybe they were made before the Dawn.
column2: 那些武器非常古老。也许是在黎明时代之前打造的呢。

column1: Those weapons are about a thousand years old.
column2: 那些武器大约有一千年历史了。

column1: One of those battle standards belongs to the famous king, Fynin the Legless, who fought as well as any ten of his two-legged foes.
column2: 那面战旗属于著名的无腿之王菲宁，他一人能敌十名双腿健全的敌人。

column1: We must boast of this.
column2: 我们一定要吹嘘此事。

column1: If we boast well, we will gain the respect of our neighbors. If we boast poorly, they will ridicule us.
column2: 如果吹得好，我们会赢得邻族的尊重。如果吹得差，他们就会嘲笑我们。

column1: I am an accomplished boaster. Let me go to our neighbors, and brag of this find.
column2: 我是吹嘘的老手。让我去我们的邻居那里，夸耀这次发现。

column1: If we add to the tribal regalia, we will gain the respect of others, and strengthen our clan magic.
column2: 如果我们增添部落圣物，就会赢得他人的尊敬，并强化我们的氏族魔法。

column1: Our magic is strong; a divination will tell us more about these mysterious artifacts.
column2: 我们的魔法强大；一次占卜能告诉我们更多关于这些神秘器物的信息。

column1: Our magic is weak; there is no point in performing a divination.
column2: 我们的魔法弱小；进行占卜毫无意义。

column1: If a divination provides us with the details of this battle, we should ritually reenact it, to bring us good magic.
column2: 如果占卜提供这场战斗的详情，我们应该以仪式重演它，以带来好魔法。

column1: Who cares? Let’s get that junk out of the field, so we can plant.
column2: 谁在乎？把那堆破烂从田里清走，好让我们耕种。

column1: Although this land has been empty of humans for hundreds of years, we are not the first Orlanthi to live here.
column2: 虽然这片土地数百年来空无人烟，但我们并非最早居住于此的奥兰斯人。

column1: What brave defenders died on that ancient day?
column2: 那个古老的日子里，有怎样的英勇守卫者倒下？

column1: That field will be fertile, for it is seeded by death.
column2: 那片田地将会肥沃，因为它以死亡为种子。

column1: Although it leaves no such relics, peace is to be celebrated over war.
column2: 虽然和平不留下这样的遗物，但它比战争更值得庆祝。

column1: I told you we’d find interesting things if we studied our own tula more carefully.
column2: 我告诉过你，如果我们更仔细地研究自己的图拉领地，就会发现有趣的东西。

column1: Some day we will be nothing more than a pile of relics cluttering up someone else’s field. All crumbles to dust.
column2: 终有一天，我们也会变成一堆遗物，塞满别人的田地。一切都化为尘土。

column1: Things to thank Orlanth for, when night falls: a spent day, a guttered torch, a tested sword, the entrapment of the Devil, good ale.
column2: 夜幕降临时，要感谢奥兰斯的事：用尽的一天，燃尽的火炬，经过考验的剑，魔鬼的囚禁，好麦酒。

column1: sceneR412
column2: sceneR412

column1: Your explorers find an old series of sacred stones in a forest clearing while exploring your tula. Your magicians say that the stones are probably inhabited by sleeping spirits.
column2: 你的探索者在勘察你的图拉领地时，在林间空地发现了一排古老的圣石。你的法师说，这些石头很可能寄居着沉睡的灵体。

column1: We found an old series of sacred stones in a forest clearing on our tula.
column2: 我们在自己的图拉领地上一片林间空地发现了一排古老的圣石。

column1: Our neighbors thought we were fools for bragging about a bunch of old rocks with no magic left in them.
column2: 我们的邻居觉得我们是傻瓜，竟夸耀一堆毫无魔力的旧石头。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors said that the slumbering stone spirits were malign, and had once served the dragon empire. They said we should leave them alone.
column2: 祖先之灵说，沉睡的石头灵体是恶意的，曾效忠于龙帝国。他们说我们不该打扰它们。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors said that we should awaken the spirits, who would teach us ancient secrets of craftsmanship.
column2: 祖先之灵说，我们应该唤醒那些灵体，它们会教我们古老的手艺秘诀。

column1: The spirits of our ancestors said that the slumbering stone spirits were malign, and had once served the dragon empire. They said we should get rid of them by digging up the stones.
column2: 祖先之灵说，沉睡的石头灵体是恶意的，曾效忠于龙帝国。他们说我们应该挖出石头来除掉它们。

column1: Dig up the stones.
column2: 挖出石头。

column1: We dug up the stones.
column2: 我们挖出了石头。

column1: That night, the carls who worked to remove the stones had terrible dreams. Our god-talkers said that the spirits were angry at us, and would bring us misfortune for many seasons to come.
column2: 当晚，劳作移除石头的自由民做了可怕的梦。我们的神言者说灵体对我们很愤怒，并将给未来多个季节带来厄运。

column1: Find shamans to awaken the spirits of the stones.
column2: 找萨满来唤醒石头灵体。

column1: We decided to find shamans to awaken the stone spirits.
column2: 我们决定找萨满来唤醒石头灵体。

column1: \x01@N finds shamans willing to help us, if you offer them \x01A$ cows.
column2: \x01@N 找到愿意帮助我们的萨满，如果你献给他们 \x01A$ 头牛。

column1: \x01@N found shamans willing to help us, if we gave them \x01A$ cows.
column2: \x01@N 找到愿意帮助我们的萨满，如果我们给他们 \x01A$ 头牛。

column1: Forget it.
column2: 算了吧。

column1: We thought their price too steep, and did not pursue the matter further.
column2: 我们认为要价太高，便没有再追究。

column1: We could not meet their price of \x01A$ cows, and so did not pursue the matter further.
column2: 我们无法满足他们 \x01A$ 头牛的代价，便没有继续下去。

column1: No shamans were willing to help us.
column2: 没有萨满愿意帮助我们。

column1: None were willing to help us.
column2: 谁都不愿帮助我们。

column1: To be safe, we let the stones alone, and told our hunters to stay away from them.
column2: 为安全起见，我们不去碰那些石头，并让猎人远离它们。

column1: They awakened the spirits, but then realized that they meant us no good. They predicted ill fortune for many seasons to come.
column2: 他们唤醒了灵体，但随后发现它们对我们不怀好意。他们预言未来多个季节会有厄运。

column1: They awakened the spirits, who said that they would teach us many forgotten secrets of crafting, which would increase our success in trade.
column2: 他们唤醒了灵体，灵体说它们会教我们许多被遗忘的工艺秘诀，这将增加我们在贸易中的成功。

column1: I can find us some shamans.
column2: 我能为我们找到一些萨满。

column1: There are shamans among the \x01@! clan, which is part of our tribe. They will help us.
column2: 在 \x01@! 氏族中有萨满，那是我部落的一部分。他们会帮助我们。

column1: The shamans will want a gift of ten cows to awaken the stone spirits.
column2: 萨满们会想要十头牛作为礼物，来唤醒石头灵体。

column1: We don’t know who left these stones here.
column2: 我们不知道是谁把这些石头留在这里的。

column1: This area was last inhabited by dragonfriends. If they left these stones, the spirits might be malign.
column2: 这片区域最后居住的是龙友。如果这些石头是他们留下的，灵体可能是恶意的。

column1: This area was last inhabited by other dragonfriends. Spirits in the stones might be friendly.
column2: 这片区域最后居住的是其他龙友。石头里的灵体可能是友善的。

column1: The other clans must hear of this.
column2: 其他氏族必须知晓此事。

column1: If we can boast as well as Orlanth, the other clans will be impressed by our find. If we boast like Eurmal, they will think less of us.
column2: 如果我们能像奥兰斯那样吹嘘，其他氏族会对我们的发现印象深刻。如果我们像欧尔马那样吹嘘，他们就会看轻我们。

column1: I have heard Orlanth speak in the Sacred Time and understand how to impress our neighbors with glorious words.
column2: 我在神圣时间听过奥兰斯的讲话，懂得如何用荣耀的言辞打动邻族。

column1: The way to protect ourselves from these malign spirits is to dig up the stones.
column2: 保护我们免受这些恶意灵体侵害的方法就是挖出石头。

column1: We should not do anything without knowing more about the spirits sleeping in the stones.
column2: 在不了解更多关于石头中沉睡的灵体之前，我们不应轻举妄动。

column1: If we dig up the stones, the spirits inside could curse us.
column2: 如果我们挖出石头，里面的灵体可能会诅咒我们。

column1: The spirits will be unfriendly towards us. Best to let them slumber.
column2: 灵体会对我们不友好。最好让它们沉睡。

column1: The spirits will grant us a great boon if we awaken them.
column2: 如果我们唤醒灵体，它们会赐予我们巨大的恩惠。

column1: Almost anything that is holy has its own spirit. Not all spirits are friendly.
column2: 几乎任何神圣之物都有其自己的灵体。并非所有灵体都是友善的。

column1: Dig those rocks!
column2: 挖那些石头！

column1: The spirits won’t like us.
column2: 灵体不会喜欢我们。

column1: If one of us is to become king one day, we must tell others of this blessing.
column2: 如果我们中的一人有朝一日要成为王，我们必须把这份祝福告知他人。

column1: Whatever the women think we should do is wrong.
column2: 无论女人们认为我们该做什么，都是错的。

column1: sceneR413
column2: sceneR413

column1: As your people explore your tula, you find many unusual features. One of these is a cave. The cave is inhabited by large, armored rodents with huge mouths filled with teeth, each as sharp as a needle. The creatures swarm out of the cave and attack the carls who found the cave, injuring several of them. The people are worried that these creatures will cause more harm.
column2: 当你们的人民在领地中探索时，发现了许多不寻常的地貌。其中一处是一个洞穴。洞穴里居住着大型、身披甲壳的啮齿动物，它们的巨口里长满锋如尖针的利齿。这些生物蜂拥而出，袭击了发现洞穴的自由民，咬伤了好几个人。大家担心这些家伙会造成更多伤害。

column1: We found a cave full of dangerous, armored rodents on our tula.
column2: 我们在领地上发现了一个洞穴，里面满是危险的、身披甲壳的啮齿动物。

column1: The dangerous rodents are back.
column2: 那些危险的啮齿动物又回来了。

column1: They found ways out of their cave, even though you blocked it up.
column2: 尽管你堵住了洞口，它们还是找到了出路。

column1: The trickster magic you used against them lured them away, but did not prevent them from returning.
column2: 你用来对付它们的恶作剧魔法将它们引开了，但并未阻止它们返回。

column1: The outsiders you hired to exterminate them didn’t do a very thorough job.
column2: 你雇来消灭它们的外乡人干得不太彻底。

column1: Your weaponthanes thought that they’d killed them all, but here they are again. A few of them must have survived and multiplied.
column2: 你的武器领主们以为已经将它们赶尽杀绝了，但它们又出现了。肯定有几只幸存下来并繁衍开了。

column1: They swarm to attack several of your horses, mauling one so badly that it must be destroyed. They also bite some of the old women and children. The people say that it is about time the clan ring did something about these loathsome creatures.
column2: 它们蜂拥而至，攻击了你们的几匹马，其中一匹伤重不得不处理掉。它们还咬伤了一些老妇和孩子。人们说，氏族议会是时候该对这些可恶的家伙做点什么了。

column1: The dangerous rodents came back and bit children and horses.
column2: 危险的啮齿动物回来了，咬伤了孩子和马匹。

column1: Block the cave entrance.
column2: 堵住洞口。

column1: We blocked up the cave entrance.
column2: 我们堵住了洞口。

column1: Many of the carls were bitten as they piled rocks inside it. They said the warriors should have been ordered to exterminate the creatures.
column2: 许多自由民在往里面堆石头时被咬伤了。他们说本该命令武士们去消灭这些家伙。

column1: Have \x01@t lure them away with trickster magic.
column2: 让 \x01@t 用恶作剧魔法把它们引开。

column1: \x01@t said \x06 would lure them away with trickster magic.
column2: \x01@t 说 \x06 要用恶作剧魔法把它们引开。

column1: \x05 pranced about the cave mouth, singing a song which \x06 said was an irresistibly salacious tune in the language of the killer rodents. It seemed absurd, but the rodents formed a line and followed \x01@t as \x06 danced away from the borders of our tula and towards those of the \x01@a clan.
column2: \x05 在洞口蹦蹦跳跳，唱了一首歌， \x06 说那是一首用杀手啮齿动物的语言唱出的、令人无法抗拒的淫秽曲子。这看起来有些荒谬，但那些啮齿动物排成一列，跟随 \x01@t 一起， \x06 跳着舞离开了我们领地的边界，朝着 \x01@a 氏族的领地而去。

column1: Find outsiders to exterminate the creatures.
column2: 找外乡人来消灭这些家伙。

column1: We decided to seek outsiders to exterminate the creatures.
column2: 我们决定找外乡人来消灭这些家伙。

column1: We found weaponthanes of the \x01@! clan willing to do it, for half a cow worth of silver each. Many of them were wounded, and they blamed us for not warning them how dangerous these rodents were. They said that all of the creatures were dead.
column2: 我们找到了 \x01@! 氏族里愿意接这活的武器领主，每人要价半头牛的银子。他们中很多人受了伤，还责怪我们没有事先警告他们这些啮齿动物有多危险。他们说所有家伙都死了。

column1: Order your weaponthanes to exterminate the creatures.
column2: 命令你的武器领主们去消灭这些家伙。

column1: We ordered our weaponthanes to exterminate them.
column2: 我们命令我们的武器领主去消灭它们。

column1: They said the carls should have been ordered to block the cave entrance.
column2: 他们说本该命令自由民去堵住洞口的。

column1: Many of them were wounded, but they said that they killed them all.
column2: 他们中很多人受了伤，但他们说把所有家伙都杀光了。

column1: The clan ring did not concern itself with this problem.
column2: 氏族议会没有理会这个问题。

column1: The rodents departed.
column2: 那些啮齿动物离开了。

column1: Don’t worry. They’ll go away of their own accord.
column2: 别担心。它们会自行离开的。

column1: They won’t be easily dealt with.
column2: 它们可不好对付。

column1: These things are called Rubble Runners. They multiply like mad, are very dangerous, and nearly impossible to get rid of.
column2: 这些家伙叫做碎石鼠。它们疯狂繁殖，非常危险，而且几乎不可能彻底消灭。

column1: See how quickly the Rubble Runners breed, and how \x02\x03tough/resilient/scrappy\x02 they are?
column2: 看看这些碎石鼠繁殖得多快，以及它们有多么 \x02\x03顽强/坚韧/好斗\x02 ？

column1: These things are called Rubble Runners. They multiply like mad and are very dangerous. The only way to get rid of them is to kill each and every one of them.
column2: 这些家伙叫做碎石鼠。它们疯狂繁殖，非常危险。消灭它们的唯一方法就是杀光每一个。

column1: The carls do not want to go near those things again. They say it time for the weaponthanes to kill them.
column2: 自由民们不想再靠近那些家伙了。他们说，是时候让武器领主们去杀死它们了。

column1: The carls do not want to go near those things, but since the weaponthanes have tried their best, the carls feel they must make an effort, too.
column2: 自由民们不想靠近那些家伙，但既然武器领主们已经尽力了，他们觉得自己也该出一份力。

column1: The carls do not want to go near those things. Some of them were hoping that trickster magic could lure the beasties away.
column2: 自由民们不想靠近那些家伙。其中一些人曾希望恶作剧魔法能把那些小畜生引走。

column1: These things are called Rubble Runners. They multiply like mad and are very dangerous. Only our own weaponthanes can be trusted to kill each and every one of them.
column2: 这些家伙叫做碎石鼠。它们疯狂繁殖，非常危险。只有我们自己的武器领主才值得信赖，能够杀光它们每一个。

column1: We can play with magic, or stones, while these Rubble Runners breed and breed and breed. Or we can do what we know we must do: kill them all.
column2: 我们可以玩弄魔法，或者石头，任由这些碎石鼠不断繁殖、繁殖、再繁殖。或者，我们可以做我们知道必须做的事：杀光它们。

column1: The weaponthanes say that this is a matter for the carls to deal with. They are not rat-catchers.
column2: 武器领主们说，这是自由民该处理的事。他们不是捕鼠人。

column1: The weaponthanes don’t want to do this work. But they will, if ordered to.
column2: 武器领主们不想干这活。但如果命令他们，他们还是会干的。

column1: The weaponthanes say that the Rubble Runners are far nastier than they envisioned. They are almost a worthy foe.
column2: 武器领主们说，碎石鼠比他们想象的麻烦得多。它们几乎算得上是个值得一战的对手。

column1: Why risk getting bitten ourselves, when we can find someone to do it for us?
column2: 既然我们能找到别人替我们干，何必冒着自己被咬的风险呢？

column1: Our neighbors are already angry at us for our reckless use of trickster magic. Let us find another way.
column2: 我们的邻居已经因为我们鲁莽使用恶作剧魔法而很生气了。我们另想办法吧。

column1: These lowly animals will afflict everyone if we don’t get rid of them.
column2: 如果我们不除掉这些低等动物，它们会祸害所有人的。

column1: We must do whatever it takes to get rid of these pests before they overrun our steads, regardless of who thinks what.
column2: 不管谁怎么想，我们都必须不惜一切代价除掉这些害虫，免得它们泛滥到我们的农庄里来。

column1: These lowly animals are extremely dangerous. This isn’t a matter of who likes to do what, or whose job they think it is. It is a matter of our survival.
column2: 这些低等动物极其危险。这不是谁喜欢干什么，或者谁认为这该是谁的活的问题。这是关乎我们生存的问题。

column1: We need some kind of magic solution to this infestation.
column2: 我们需要某种魔法手段来解决这场虫害。

column1: Only trickster magic can end this infestation.
column2: 只有恶作剧魔法才能终结这场虫害。

column1: If we had an Eurmal devotee on the ring, we could make use of trickster magic, which can be useful in odd situations like this.
column2: 如果我们长老会里有一位尤尔马尔信徒，就能利用诡术魔法，在这种异常情况下会很有用。

column1: The carls say that this is a killing matter, and thus the responsibility of the weaponthanes.
column2: 自由民们说这是杀人事件，因此应由武器领主们负责。

column1: The carls say that they will do what they can to get rid of these abominations.
column2: 自由民们说他们会尽力清除这些孽物。

column1: The carls don’t care who gets rid of them, as long as they are gone for good.
column2: 自由民们不在乎谁去清除它们，只要它们永远消失就行。

column1: During the Storm Age, Orlanth the King was never bedevilled by petty problems such as this!
column2: 在风暴时代，奥兰斯王从未被这等琐碎问题困扰过！

column1: Creatures like this are often companions to spirits of disease.
column2: 这种生物常与疫病精魂为伴。

column1: This matter is beneath the dignity of proud weaponthanes.
column2: 此事有损骄傲武器领主们的尊严。

column1: No one will want to marry into our clan if we show ourselves incapable of dealing with a few rodents.
column2: 若我们连几只啮齿兽都对付不了，就没人愿与我们氏族联姻。

column1: “Better to be killed by an axe than by the nibble of a rat.”
column2: “宁被斧砍，不被鼠啮。”

column1: “A scythe in one hand, a sword in the other, and arrows in your teeth.”
column2: “一手镰刀，一手剑，嘴里衔着箭。”

column1: This is a problem for the men to deal with — lazy sods!
column2: 这是男人们该管的事——懒骨头们！

column1: Animals that travel in packs are no better than men who do the same.
column2: 成群结队的野兽与结党营私的人类一样恶劣。

column1: Let us show our neighbors that we are rich enough to have others dispose of our dangerous rodents.
column2: 让邻居们看看，我们富到能雇人来处理危险啮齿兽。

column1: Just let me play my little pipe for them! Please! Please!
column2: 让我为它们吹吹我的小笛子吧！求求啦！求求啦！

column1: Want me to charm them right into the cooking pit?
column2: 要我直接把它们迷进烹饪坑吗？

column1: sceneR414
column2: sceneR414

column1: Glendara, a prosperous carl of your clan, comes before you to complain that her prize stallion, Tempest, has been stolen. Although no one saw the theft, Glendara is certain that it was committed by the sons of Rangarda Dark-Eyes, a well-off carl of the \x01@! clan. “Many times has she offered to buy that horse, and many times did I refuse her. It is the most beautiful stallion in all of Dragon Pass, and I would not let her have it. So she has ordered her sons to steal it.”
column2: 格伦达拉，你们氏族一位富裕的自由民，前来控诉说她的获奖种马“风暴”被偷了。虽然没人目睹盗窃，但格伦达拉确信是 \x01@! 氏族一位富裕自由民黑眼朗加尔达的儿子们所为。“她多次想买那匹马，我多次拒绝。那是龙之隘口最漂亮的种马，我不愿给她。于是她指使儿子们偷走了它。”

column1: Glendara, a carl of our clan, said that her prize stallion, Tempest, had been stolen by Rangarda Dark-Eyes of the \x01@! clan.
column2: 格伦达拉，我们氏族的一位自由民，说她的获奖种马“风暴”被 \x01@! 氏族的黑眼朗加尔达偷走了。

column1: Launch a legal claim against Rangarda Dark-Eyes.
column2: 对黑眼朗加尔达提起法律诉讼。

column1: We launched a legal claim against Rangarda Dark-Eyes.
column2: 我们对黑眼朗加尔达提起了法律诉讼。

column1: Rangarda denied that she had anything to do with the disappearance of Glendara’s horse. Her clan leaders seemed to make an honest effort to determine the truth, but ultimately ruled that there was no evidence of wrongdoing on Rangarda’s part.
column2: 朗加尔达否认自己与格伦达拉的马失踪有任何关系。她氏族的首领们似乎确实努力查明真相，但最终裁定没有证据表明朗加尔达有过错。

column1: Glendara was most displeased by this result.
column2: 格伦达拉对此结果极为不满。

column1: “By Elmal’s balls,” she swore, “I will recover that horse, if it costs me my last breath.”
column2: “以埃尔马尔的卵蛋发誓，”她赌咒道，“就算搭上最后一口气，我也要找回那匹马。”

column1: We took her claim to the moot.
column2: 我们将她的诉求提交到了议会。

column1: How much wealth do you give to the other clans before the case is judged?
column2: 在案件裁决前，你向其他氏族支付多少财富？

column1: Although she continued to deny it, the other clans ruled that Rangarda Dark-Eyes was responsible for the disappearance of Tempest. They demanded that she produce the stallion, but she said that she could not. So the \x01@! clan was instead ordered to pay compensation to Glendara.
column2: 尽管她继续否认，但其他氏族裁定黑眼朗加尔达对“风暴”失踪负有责任。他们要求她交出种马，但她说交不出来。于是 \x01@! 氏族被责令向格伦达拉支付补偿。

column1: Despite our victory, Glendara later pronounced herself unsatisfied with the conclusion of the case.
column2: 尽管我们获胜，格伦达拉后来仍表示对案件结论不满意。

column1: The other clans ruled that there was no evidence to link Rangarda Dark-Eyes to Tempest’s disappearance. They ruled against us, and the people were discouraged.
column2: 其他氏族裁定没有证据将黑眼朗加尔达与“风暴”失踪联系起来。他们判我们败诉，族人们灰心丧气。

column1: Glendara said that this would not be the end of the matter.
column2: 格伦达拉说此事不会就此了结。

column1: How many warriors do you send to support your case?
column2: 你派出多少战士来支持你的诉求？

column1: Launch a raid against the \x01@! clan.
column2: 对 \x01@! 氏族发起突袭。

column1: We raided the \x01@! clan.
column2: 我们突袭了 \x01@! 氏族。

column1: Although we bested the \x01@! warriors, we found no trace of the stallion called Tempest. Glendara swore that Rangarda Dark-Eyes had hidden the horse somewhere, and that she would not rest until she recovered it.
column2: 尽管我们击败了 \x01@! 战士，但没有发现名叫“风暴”的种马踪迹。格伦达拉发誓说黑眼朗加尔达把马藏到了某处，她不找回马绝不罢休。

column1: Not only did the \x01@! clan defeat us, but we found no trace of the stallion called Tempest. Glendara swore that Rangarda Dark-Eyes had hidden the horse somewhere, and that she would not rest until she recovered it. The weaponthanes complained that they had been led into a losing battle over a single horse, and blamed the clan ring for making Glendara’s business the clan’s business.
column2: 不仅 \x01@! 氏族击败了我们，而且我们没有发现名叫“风暴”的种马踪迹。格伦达拉发誓说黑眼朗加尔达把马藏到了某处，她不找回马绝不罢休。武器领主们抱怨说他们因为一匹马而被带入一场败仗，并指责氏族议会将格伦达拉的私事变成了氏族事务。

column1: Offer her compensation.
column2: 向她提供补偿。

column1: The clan ring offered her compensation.
column2: 氏族议会向她提供了补偿。

column1: Glendara said, “It is not the trade value of Tempest that concerns me. It is the principle of the thing. By stealing my prize stallion, she has stolen my honor.”
column2: 格伦达拉说：“我在意的不是‘风暴’的交易价值，而是原则。她偷走我的获奖种马，就是偷走了我的荣誉。”

column1: Persuade her to forget the matter.
column2: 劝她忘记此事。

column1: Members of the clan ring tried to persuade her to forget the matter.
column2: 氏族议会的成员们试图劝她忘记此事。

column1: She would not hear of it. “No argument can sway me, while that mangy, dug-dragging she-dog has my Tempest.”
column2: 她根本听不进去。“那只长疥疮、拖乳房的母狗还占着我的‘风暴’，任何说辞都动摇不了我。”

column1: “This is not a matter for the clan.”
column2: “这不是氏族该管的事。”

column1: Our leaders said, “This is not a matter for the clan.”
column2: 我们的首领们说：“这不是氏族该管的事。”

column1: Glendara said that she understood their ruling, and would rely on her own family to make things right.
column2: 格伦达拉说她理解他们的裁决，并会依靠自己的家族来解决问题。

column1: The carls, however, thought that we should have done more to help her.
column2: 不过，自由民认为我们本该做得更多来帮她。

column1: That bony old nag probably went off and died somewhere.
column2: 那匹瘦骨嶙峋的老马大概跑哪儿去死了。

column1: Tempest was a fine horse indeed, one worth starting a war over.
column2: 暴风确实是匹好马，值得为它开战。

column1: Tempest was a fine stallion, but he is not worth fighting over.
column2: 暴风是匹好公马，但不值得为此争斗。

column1: It is foolish to make war over a single horse. If we lose, the weaponthanes will be resentful.
column2: 为一匹马开战太蠢了。要是我们输了，武器领主们会心怀怨恨。

column1: It would not be smart to fight them now.
column2: 现在跟他们打可不明智。

column1: We have a strong case.
column2: 我们很有道理。

column1: Without proof, our case is weak.
column2: 没有证据，我们就站不住脚。

column1: Without proof, our case is weak. We are not obligated to make this a clan matter.
column2: 没有证据，我们就站不住脚。我们没有义务把这事变成氏族事务。

column1: Although our case is weak, and we are not obligated to make this a clan matter, we could win by outspending them at the tribal moot.
column2: 尽管道理不足，我们也没义务把这事变成氏族事务，但可以在部落大会上用钱砸赢他们。

column1: Rangarda Dark-Eyes did want that stallion, but we have no reason to believe that she ordered it stolen.
column2: 黑眼朗加尔达确实想要那匹公马，但我们没理由相信是她指使人偷的。

column1: Rangarda Dark-Eyes did come here many times to offer to buy the stallion; she may well have ordered her boys to steal it.
column2: 黑眼朗加尔达确实多次来出价买那匹公马；她很可能是她让手下偷的。

column1: Rangarda Dark-Eyes did come here many times to offer to buy the stallion, and I am sure she ordered her boys to steal it.
column2: 黑眼朗加尔达确实多次来出价买那匹公马，我敢肯定是她让手下偷的。

column1: This could cause trouble between our clans.
column2: 这会在我们氏族之间惹麻烦。

column1: Let’s not pull farmers away from the critical task of planting to avenge a deed we have no real proof of!
column2: 别把农夫从关键的播种活计上拉下来去报复一件我们根本没证据的事！

column1: Let’s not pull farmers away from the critical task of bringing in the harvest to avenge a deed we have no real proof of!
column2: 别把农夫从关键的收获活计上拉下来去报复一件我们根本没证据的事！

column1: Although the other carls admire her wealth and success, Glendara’s family has always held itself at a remove from the rest of our clan.
column2: 尽管其他自由民羡慕她的财富和成功，格伦达拉的家族一直与我们氏族其他人保持距离。

column1: Glendara is an eccentric. She has always valued horses more than cows.
column2: 格伦达拉是个怪人。她向来把马看得比牛重。

column1: Let her pursue this affront to honor on her own terms.
column2: 让她按自己的方式去讨回这桩荣誉的冒犯吧。

column1: Mark my words — a feud between women always results in the death of men.
column2: 记住我的话——女人之间的仇怨总会导致男人丧命。

column1: Glendara has prospered because of her thrift. We would do well to emulate her — and avoid costly raids and lawsuits.
column2: 格伦达拉因节俭而兴旺。我们最好学她——避免代价高昂的劫掠和诉讼。

column1: I have never liked Glendara. She is scornful of me when I can’t come up with the right…you know…it’s on the tip of my…
column2: 我从不喜欢格伦达拉。每当我想不出合适的……你知道……就在嘴边时，她就嘲笑我……

column1: It is good to have a stormy temperament, but Glendara abuses the privilege.
column2: 脾气暴躁是好事，但格伦达拉滥用这种特权。

column1: Glendara is not the most polite woman of our clan.
column2: 格伦达拉不是氏族里最有礼数的女人。

column1: sceneR415
column2: sceneR415

column1: Glendara’s sons and daughter have done what the clan could not do; they have recovered Tempest.
column2: 格伦达拉的儿子和女儿做到了氏族做不到的事；他们找回了暴风。

column1: Glendara’s sons and daughter recovered the stolen stallion Tempest.
column2: 格伦达拉的儿子和女儿找回了被盗的公马暴风。

column1: They found him in a hidden cave on the \x01@! tula, where they fought off the sons of Rangarda Dark-Eyes. One of the defenders, named Norpent Rangardasson, was slain, and another badly hurt. But justice has been served, for Glendara’s prize horse is hers again, and her honor is restored.
column2: 他们在一处隐藏在 \x01@! 图拉上的洞穴里找到了它，在那里击退了黑眼朗加尔达的儿子们。一名守卫，叫诺彭特·兰加达森，被杀，另一人重伤。但正义已得伸张，因为格伦达拉的珍贵马匹又归她了，她的荣誉也恢复了。

column1: The sons and daughter of Glendara recovered the stallion called Tempest, which they found secreted away on the tula of the \x01@! clan. They slew one of Rangarda Dark-Eye’s sons, and wounded another.
column2: 格伦达拉的儿子和女儿找回了名叫暴风的公马，他们发现它被藏在 \x01@! 氏族的图拉上。他们杀了黑眼朗加尔达的一个儿子，还伤了另一个。

column1: Praise Glendara.
column2: 赞扬格伦达拉。

column1: Clan leaders praised Glendara.
column2: 氏族首领赞扬了格伦达拉。

column1: The people were cheered by their words.
column2: 人们因他们的话而振奋。

column1: The people were displeased, for they worried that her actions would embroil the clan in a costly feud.
column2: 人们不高兴，因为他们担心她的行动会让氏族卷入代价高昂的宿怨。

column1: Scold Glendara.
column2: 斥责格伦达拉。

column1: Clan leaders scolded Glendara.
column2: 氏族首领斥责了格伦达拉。

column1: She was unrepentant.
column2: 她毫无悔意。

column1: The people were glad to see her chastised, for they worried that her actions would embroil the clan in a costly feud.
column2: 人们看到她被训诫很高兴，因为他们担心她的行动会让氏族卷入代价高昂的宿怨。

column1: The people were offended; they said that Glendara had taken action to protect her honor, as any true Orlanthi should.
column2: 人们被冒犯了；他们说格伦达拉采取行动保护自己的荣誉，正如任何真正的奥兰塞人应该做的那样。

column1: The \x01@! ring claims to have had no knowledge of Rangarda’s crime. They offer you ten cows as a token of apology.
column2: \x01@! 之环声称对朗加尔达的罪行一无所知。他们向您提供十头牛作为道歉的象征。

column1: Accept their gift, pronounce the matter settled.
column2: 接受他们的礼物，宣布此事已了结。

column1: We accepted the gift and pronounced the matter settled.
column2: 我们接受了礼物，并宣布此事已了结。

column1: Reject their gift.
column2: 拒绝他们的礼物。

column1: We rejected their gift.
column2: 我们拒绝了他们的礼物。

column1: They were most affronted, and said that our alliance with them was ended.
column2: 他们深感侮辱，说我们之间的联盟就此终结。

column1: They were most affronted, and said that our intentions were to smear their name regardless of truth.
column2: 他们深感侮辱，说我们无论真相如何只想抹黑他们的名声。

column1: What do you offer them? (The standard wergild for a slain carl is \x01A .)
column2: 你给他们什么？（被杀自由民的标准血偿金是 \x01A 。）

column1: They accepted the gifts, though they were still feuding with us over other matters.
column2: 他们接受了礼物，尽管仍因其他事情与我们敌对。

column1: Still, their chief agreed that the dispute between Glendara and Rangarda Dark-Eyes is not a part of our current feud with them.
column2: 不过，他们的首领同意，格伦达拉与黑眼朗加尔达之间的争端不属于我们当前与他们宿怨的一部分。

column1: They refused to accept them, and angrily escorted us off their tula.
column2: 他们拒绝接受，并愤怒地将我们护送离了他们的图拉。

column1: We were hurried off the tula, gifts and all.
column2: 我们匆忙被赶下图拉，礼物也带回来了。

column1: They praised us for our generous gesture, and gave us a reciprocal gift equal in value to our own. They said that we should consider the fighting between the families of Glendara and Rangarda as a personal matter, and one which would not interfere with the strong relations between our two clans.
column2: 他们称赞我们的慷慨姿态，并回赠了价值相等的礼物。他们说我们应该把格伦达拉和朗加尔达两家之间的争斗视为私人事务，不会干扰我们两氏族之间的牢固关系。

column1: Glendara and her oldest son made a point of parading Tempest around to all the god-talkers’ steads to celebrate their victory.
column2: 格伦达拉和她的长子特意牵着“风暴”巡游所有神言者的农庄，以庆祝他们的胜利。

column1: If Rangarda’s family is proud, they will seek vengeance against Glendara’s family.
column2: 如果朗加尔达家族心高气傲，他们就会寻求向格伦达拉家族复仇。

column1: They lied to us! We must seek redress!
column2: 他们骗了我们！我们必须讨个公道！

column1: Glendara was within her rights to do what she did. There is no cause to scold her.
column2: 格伦达拉做她所做的事是她的权利。没有理由责备她。

column1: If this continues, we could see our \x01@! friends quickly turn to foes.
column2: 若继续下去，我们可能会眼见我们的 \x01@! 朋友转眼变成敌人。

column1: We must stop this from turning into a feud. It will be easier to placate our \x01@! friends than to convince strong-willed Glendara she was wrong to do this.
column2: 我们必须阻止此事演变成世仇。安抚我们的 \x01@! 朋友，比说服固执的格伦达拉承认自己做错了要容易。

column1: Some of the carls are worried that this will lead to a costly series of reprisals. Others admire her and support what she did.
column2: 一些自由民担心这会导致一系列代价高昂的报复。另一些人则钦佩她，支持她的所作所为。

column1: When the Rain Cauldron was stolen, King Oskul’s carls came to him for aid. He said, “Do what you must, but I have shed enough blood for seven kings, and will kill no more.”
column2: 当雨之釜被盗时，奥斯库尔王的自由民前来向他求助。他说：“去做你们必须做的事吧，但我的血已为七位国王流得够多，不会再杀人了。”

column1: It is good to have Tempest back in the clan again.
column2: 能让“风暴”重回氏族，真好。

column1: This is still not a matter for clan leaders.
column2: 这仍然不是氏族首领该管的事。

column1: It is wrong to kill a man to gain a horse.
column2: 为得一匹马而杀人是不对的。

column1: Glendara is an example to us all.
column2: 格伦达拉是我们所有人的榜样。

column1: We should be worrying about ghosts and zombies, not about trivial matters such as this.
column2: 我们应该操心的是幽灵和僵尸，而不是这种小事。

column1: Glendara is going to get us in trouble!
column2: 格伦达拉会给我们惹麻烦的！

column1: Good for Glendara!
column2: 格伦达拉干得好！

column1: Glendara has often mocked the need to be vigilant against the elves. Now she has gone too far!
column2: 格伦达拉经常嘲笑需要警惕精灵这件事。现在她太过分了！

column1: This is no occasion for gift-giving.
column2: 这不是送礼的场合。

column1: Glendara’s honor belongs not to the clan, but to her. She has taken action to protect it, and is worthy of praise.
column2: 格伦达拉的荣誉不属于氏族，只属于她自己。她采取了行动来捍卫它，值得赞扬。

column1: sceneR416
column2: sceneR416

column1: Brodasart, son of the prosperous carl Glendara, has been slain in an ambush. Friends, who were with him when he was attacked, report that the assailants were relatives of Rangarda Dark-Eyes of the \x01@! clan. According to his friends, the killers said to them, “Stand aside, for our quarrel is only with the family that killed our kinsman, not with others of the \x01@" clan.” Everyone remembers the incident in which Rangarda stole Glendara’s prize stallion, and Glendara’s children slew one of Rangarda’s sons while retrieving it.
column2: 富庶自由民格伦达拉之子布罗达萨特，在伏击中身亡。遇袭时与他同在的朋友们报告说，袭击者是 \x01@! 氏族中黑眼朗加尔达的亲戚。据他的朋友们说，凶手对他们讲：“闪开，我们只与杀死我们亲人的家族有仇，与其他 \x01@" 氏族的人无关。”人人都记得朗加尔达偷走格伦达拉的获奖种马，而格伦达拉的孩子们在夺回种马时杀死了朗加尔达的一个儿子那件事。

column1: Brodasart, son of Glendara, was slain by relatives of Rangarda Dark-Eyes of the \x01@! clan.
column2: 格伦达拉之子布罗达萨特，被 \x01@! 氏族中黑眼朗加尔达的亲戚杀害。

column1: Compose a poem in honor of Brodasart.
column2: 作一首诗纪念布罗达萨特。

column1: \x01@N composed a poem in honor of Brodasart.
column2: \x01@N 作了一首诗纪念布罗达萨特。

column1: The poem was a beautiful tribute to a brave fighting carl, and everyone said they would remember it always.
column2: 这首诗是对一位勇敢善战的自由民的美好致敬，人人都说会永远铭记。

column1: It was a good effort, but no one thought that the poem would be remembered past the time of mourning.
column2: 这是一番努力，但没人认为这首诗能在悼念期结束后仍被记住。

column1: Encourage Glendara to swear off vengeance.
column2: 鼓励格伦达拉发誓放弃复仇。

column1: Clan leaders encouraged Glendara to swear off vengeance.
column2: 氏族首领鼓励格伦达拉发誓放弃复仇。

column1: She said that she was sick of heart, and would think only of her son until his funerary rites had been completed. Some of the people said that the clan leaders were wrong to discourage Glendara from pursuing her natural rights of vengeance.
column2: 她说她心已伤透，在葬礼完成之前只愿思念儿子。有些人说氏族首领不该劝阻格伦达拉追求她天生的复仇权利。

column1: The people cheered this victory, and said that a blow had been struck in Brodasart’s memory.
column2: 人们为这次胜利欢呼，说是为布罗达萨特打出了一记重拳。

column1: The people regretted this loss, but said that it was good to have struck a blow in Brodasart’s memory.
column2: 人们对这次损失感到遗憾，但说能为布罗达萨特打出一记重拳也是好事。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods in honor of Brodasart.
column2: 向诸神献祭以纪念布罗达萨特。

column1: We sacrificed in honor of Brodasart.
column2: 我们献祭以纪念布罗达萨特。

column1: The people were pleased when the god-talkers reported that the sacrifices had been accepted.
column2: 当神言者报告说献祭已被接纳时，人们感到高兴。

column1: The people sympathized with Glendara’s loss, and some wished we had taken up arms for the sake of Brodasart’s memory.
column2: 人们对格伦达拉的损失表示同情，有些人希望我们曾为纪念布罗达萨特拿起武器。

column1: Warn \x01@! leaders that more killing may follow.
column2: 警告 \x01@! 首领们，杀戮可能还会继续。

column1: We warned \x01@! leaders that more killing might follow.
column2: 我们警告了 \x01@! 首领们，杀戮可能还会继续。

column1: The carls were once worried that Glendara would start a feud, but Brodasart was a popular fellow, and now they are hungry for vengeance.
column2: 自由民曾担心格伦达拉会挑起世仇，但布罗达萨特是个受欢迎的人，如今他们渴望复仇。

column1: By Orlanth’s thundering song, we must raid them!
column2: 以奥兰斯的雷鸣之歌起誓，我们必须突袭他们！

column1: There is no occasion for which a poem is unsuitable.
column2: 没有哪首诗是不合时宜的。

column1: Glendara is within her rights to pursue vengeance.
column2: 格伦达拉有权追求复仇。

column1: Glendara is within her rights to pursue vengeance. The people will be unhappy if we try to convince her to forswear these rights.
column2: 格伦达拉有权追求复仇。如果我们试图说服她放弃这些权利，人们会不高兴。

column1: Our formerly good relations with the \x01@! clan are now in danger.
column2: 我们与 \x01@! 氏族原本良好的关系现在处于危险之中。

column1: It is at times like this that our thoughts must turn to the gods, who were the first to experience the pangs of loss, and thus laid the way for the rest of us.
column2: 正是在这样的时刻，我们的思绪必须转向诸神——他们是第一批经历丧亲之痛的存在，因此为我们其余人铺平了道路。

column1: The carls want vengeance, but the clan needs its crops planted.
column2: 自由民想要复仇，但氏族需要播种谷物。

column1: The carls want vengeance, but the clan needs the crops harvested.
column2: 自由民想要复仇，但氏族需要收割庄稼。

column1: The theft of the Rain Cauldron brought great misery to King Oskul’s people. They begged him to pick up his sword again, the one he had used to slay Bad King Urgrain.
column2: 雨之釜被盗给奥斯库尔王的人民带来了巨大的苦难。他们恳求他再次拿起那把曾用来斩杀恶王乌格兰的剑。

column1: It is good when bulls fight, for it makes strong bulls stronger. But it is bad when this fighting endangers the cows.
column2: 公牛相斗是好事，因为能让强壮的公牛更强。但若这种争斗危及母牛，便是坏事。

column1: It is as I said. Womanish pride has led to the spilling of manly blood.
column2: 正如我所说。妇人之傲导致了男儿之血的流淌。

column1: Does this fruitless bloodshed win us any treasure? We should be exploring, instead.
column2: 这无果的流血能为我们赢得任何财富吗？我们本该去探索才对。

column1: We must attend to our own clan, peacefully if possible, but if that is not enough, then by warlike means.
column2: 我们必须照管好自己的氏族，能和平解决就和平解决，但若不足，则用战争手段。

column1: Glendara’s family has again struck at the \x01@! family headed by Rangarda Dark-Eyes. This time they set a stead on fire, and Rangarda herself was badly burned. She is not expected to live.
column2: 格伦达拉的家族再次袭击了 \x01@! 黑眼朗加尔达领导的家族。这次他们放火烧了一座农庄，朗加尔达本人被严重烧伤。预料她活不成了。

column1: Glendara, the prosperous carl of our clan whose horse was once stolen by Rangarda Dark-Eyes of the \x01@! clan, now lies dead. She succumbed to apoplexy earlier today. Perhaps this will end the feud between the two families.
column2: 格伦达拉，我们氏族中那位曾被盗走马匹的富裕自由民——盗马者是 \x01@! 氏族的黑眼朗加尔达——如今死了。她今天早些时候死于中风。也许这能终结两家的世仇。

column1: Remember Rangarda Dark-Eyes of the \x01@! clan, who feuded with Glendara over a stolen horse? She survived when Glendara’s family burned her stead, but now she is as dead as Glendara, felled not by fighting but by a coughing disease. The last words on her lips were of Glendara, exulting in the fact that she outlived her rival.
column2: 还记得 \x01@! 氏族的黑眼朗加尔达吗？她曾因一匹被盗的马与格伦达拉结仇。格伦达拉家族烧她农庄时她活了下来，但现在她和格伦达拉一样死了——并非死于争斗，而是咳嗽病。她临终最后的话语提到格伦达拉，为自己比对手活得更久而得意。

column1: sceneR417
column2: sceneR417

column1: Young boys of the \x01@! clan, not even men yet, come to your tula and attack another young boy with a sword. Fortunately, the victim’s mother, Domasa Glendarasdaughter, is able to separate the boys before any real harm can be done. It turns out that the \x01@! boys are sons of Norpent Rangardasson, who was slain by Domasa and her late brother Brodasart when they recovered the stolen stallion Tempest from Rangarda Dark-Eyes. The boys seek vengeance in their father’s name, even though they are too young to have a right to it.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的年轻男孩们，甚至还算不上男人，来到你们的领地，用剑攻击另一个年轻男孩。幸运的是，受害者母亲多玛萨·格伦达拉之女在真正伤害造成前分开了他们。原来这些 \x01@! 男孩是诺彭特·兰加达森的儿子——诺彭特曾被多玛萨和她已故的兄弟布罗达萨特杀死，当时他们正从黑眼朗加尔达那里夺回被盗的种马“风暴”。男孩们以父亲的名义寻求复仇，尽管他们还太年轻，没有权利这么做。

column1: Furthering a long-festering feud, young boys of the \x01@! clan came here to attack a boy of our clan.
column2: 一场长期酝酿的世仇加剧了， \x01@! 氏族的年轻男孩们来到这里攻击我们氏族的一个男孩。

column1: Convince the boys to renounce vengeance.
column2: 说服男孩们放弃复仇。

column1: We told the boys that they should renounce vengeance.
column2: 我们告诉那些男孩，他们应该放弃复仇。

column1: They said they would do so.
column2: 他们说他们会照做。

column1: Kill the boys.
column2: 杀死男孩们。

column1: We killed the boys.
column2: 我们杀死了男孩们。

column1: We let them return to their home tula.
column2: 我们让他们返回自己家的领地。

column1: People said that the clan leaders should have done something to end the fight between the families of Glendara and Rangarda, now that both women were long dead.
column2: 人们说氏族首领早该做点什么来终结格伦达拉和朗加尔达两家之间的争斗，既然两个女人都已死去多年。

column1: Ransom the boys to the \x01@! clan.
column2: 向 \x01@! 氏族索取赎金赎回男孩们。

column1: We ransomed the boys back to their clan.
column2: 我们把男孩们赎回他们的氏族。

column1: They fetched a handsome price.
column2: 他们卖了个好价钱。

column1: We did not get as much for them as \x01@N had hoped.
column2: 我们从他们身上没得到像 \x01@N 所希望的那么多。

column1: Take them back to their clan.
column2: 把他们带回他们的氏族。

column1: We took them back to their clan.
column2: 我们把它们带回了他们的氏族。

column1: \x01@! leaders said that we had acted honorably, and said that they hoped this would be the end of the fight between the families of Glendara and Rangarda.
column2: \x01@! 首领们说我们行事光明磊落，并说希望这能结束格伦达拉与朗加尔达两家之间的争斗。

column1: They are boys, yet behave as men. We must kill them.
column2: 他们是男孩，却行事如男子汉。我们必须杀了他们。

column1: Until they are men, they have no rights of vengeance.
column2: 他们成年之前没有复仇的权利。

column1: They are not men, and are not yet accountable for their actions.
column2: 他们不是男人，也不必为自己的行为负责。

column1: I could maybe get three cows each for them.
column2: 我大概每个能换三头牛。

column1: The proper ransom for these boys would be five cows each.
column2: 这些男孩的合适赎金是每人五头牛。

column1: The proper ransom for these boys would be five cows each, but I think I can get more.
column2: 这些男孩的合适赎金是每人五头牛，但我觉得我能要到更多。

column1: This is not the first time this old feud has caused tensions between our clans.
column2: 这已经不是这场旧世仇第一次在我们氏族间制造紧张了。

column1: If another generation takes it up, this feud will never end, or so say the carls.
column2: 如果下一代也接过去，这场世仇将永无止境——自由民们是这么说的。

column1: If another generation takes it up, this feud will never end, or so say the carls. They will be unhappy if we do nothing to stop it.
column2: 如果下一代也接过去，这场世仇将永无止境——自由民们是这么说的。如果我们不采取任何措施阻止，他们会不高兴。

column1: King Oskul was slain not in a glorious battle, like the ones he fought against Bad King Urgrain, but was killed by a rock-throwing boy, in a feud he swore to end.
column2: 奥斯库尔王并非死于辉煌战役——就像他对抗恶王乌格兰时打过的那些——而是被一个扔石头的男孩杀死，就在他发誓要终结的一场世仇中。

column1: Vengeance is like a snake swallowing its tail — its end is never in sight.
column2: 复仇就像蛇吞尾——永无尽头。

column1: Orlanth made justice so that disputes could be ended by words as well as swords.
column2: 奥兰斯创立了正义，这样争端既可用剑也可用言语解决。

column1: We must squeeze some benefit out of this annoying dispute.
column2: 我们必须从这场烦人的争端中榨出些好处来。

column1: There is nothing we can do, short of killing them — they will grow older and return to fight again.
column2: 除非杀了他们，否则我们无能为力——他们会长大，然后回来再战。

column1: These boys will be fine warriors some day; perhaps great poems will be written about them.
column2: 这些男孩有朝一日会成为好战士；也许会有伟大的诗歌歌颂他们。

column1: sceneR418
column2: sceneR418

column1: Robarth, a member of one of your most prosperous families of carls, is attacked by two brothers from the \x01@! clan. His mother, Domasa Glendarasdaughter, looks on helplessly as they skirmish. Robarth is wounded, but manages to slay one of the brothers, Burthalor. This fight is a deadly reiteration of one that occurred about ten years ago, when all three combatants were children. It grows from a long-running feud between the two families, which started when Burthalor’s grandmother stole a fine stallion from Robarth’s.
column2: 罗巴特——你最富裕的自由民家庭之一中的一员——遭到 \x01@! 氏族两兄弟的攻击。他的母亲多玛萨·格伦达拉之女无助地看着他们缠斗。罗巴特受了伤，但设法杀死了其中一兄弟布罗达萨特。这场打斗是大约十年前一场争斗的致命重演——当时三个参与者都还是孩子。它源于两家长年世仇，始于布罗达萨特的祖母从罗巴特家偷了一匹好种马。

column1: Convince Burthalor’s family to renounce further vengeance.
column2: 说服伯萨洛尔的家族放弃继续复仇。

column1: Our clan leaders sought to convince Burthalor’s relatives to renounce further vengeance.
column2: 我们的氏族首领试图说服伯萨洛尔的亲属放弃继续复仇。

column1: What do you offer them in gifts?
column2: 你赠予他们什么礼物？

column1: When our people heard of this, they complained that we paid more than the proper wergild for Burthalor’s death. They were affronted by this, because they said that Burthalor had attacked Robarth, and brought his doom upon himself.
column2: 我们的人民听闻此事后抱怨道，我们为伯萨洛尔之死支付的赔偿超出了应有的血偿金。他们对此感到愤慨，因为伯萨洛尔先攻击了罗巴特，是自己招致了厄运。

column1: Burthalor’s brother, Jakolorth, swore that the dispute would now end. “When you first arrived, such a promise was the last thing on my mind, but your eloquent words have convinced me otherwise.”
column2: 伯萨洛尔的兄弟贾科洛尔发誓争端就此了结。“你们初到时，我根本没想过会做出这样的承诺，但你们雄辩的说辞说服了我改变主意。”

column1: Burthalor’s brother, Jakolorth, castigated our emissaries as fools, and said that, if we wanted to end the dispute, that we ought to muzzle our own villainous families. He said he would tell his clanmates of our dishonorable approach to him in his moment of grief.
column2: 伯萨洛尔的兄弟贾科洛尔斥责我们的使者愚蠢，并说如果我们想结束争端，就该先管住自己那些恶棍家族。他说他会告诉族人们，我们在他悲痛之际用不光彩的手段逼迫他。

column1: Convince Robarth and his family to renounce further vengeance.
column2: 说服罗巴特及其家族放弃继续复仇。

column1: Our clan leaders sought to convince Robarth and his family to renounce further vengeance.
column2: 我们的氏族首领试图说服罗巴特及其家族放弃继续复仇。

column1: Does the chief offer them gifts?
column2: 首领是否赠予他们礼物？

column1: The people complained that Robarth’s family were being too well-rewarded for making trouble with our neighbors.
column2: 人民抱怨罗巴特家族因与我们邻居生事而获得了过高的奖赏。

column1: Robarth swore he would not take vengeance, so long as there were no further provocations from Burthalor’s family.
column2: 罗巴特发誓，只要伯萨洛尔家族不再挑衅，他就不会复仇。

column1: Robarth hotly replied that the clan sought to strip him of his rights of vengeance, which was an unjust theft of his freedom. He rallied many hotheads of the clan to support his position, and there was much unrest in the clan hall that night.
column2: 罗巴特激烈反驳说，氏族试图剥夺他的复仇权，这是对他自由的不公正掠夺。他召集了族中许多冲动之徒支持他的立场，当晚部族大厅里骚动不已。

column1: Outlaw Robarth, Domasa, and all of their family members.
column2: 将罗巴特、多玛萨及其所有家族成员放逐。

column1: We outlawed Robarth and his entire family.
column2: 我们将罗巴特及其整个家族放逐了。

column1: The carls were outraged by this decision, and there was great unrest among them for many weeks afterwards. Eight weeks later, we heard from a trader that Robarth and his relatives were heading back to Heortland. We never learned if they returned in safety to the land of the Pharaoh.
column2: 自由民对此决定极为愤怒，随后数周内他们中动荡不安。八周后，我们从一个商人那里听说罗巴特及其亲属正返回赫欧特兰。我们始终未得知他们是否平安回到了法老之地。

column1: Seek aid of \x01@! leaders in ending the feud.
column2: 寻求 \x01@! 首领的帮助以结束世仇。

column1: Our clan leaders sought the aid of their \x01@! counterparts in ending the feud.
column2: 我们的氏族首领寻求了他们 \x01@! 对应首领的帮助以结束世仇。

column1: They said that they would attempt to restrain Burthalor’s relatives, but could make no promises that they would succeed.
column2: 他们表示会尽力约束伯萨洛尔的亲属，但无法保证成功。

column1: They refused to intervene in what they said was a private matter between families.
column2: 他们拒绝干预，称这是家族间的私事。

column1: The carls rolled their eyes. They knew that this matter was far from settled, ring or no ring.
column2: 自由民翻了个白眼。他们知道此事远未了结，无论有没有指环。

column1: Our clan leaders refrained from involving themselves in this private matter.
column2: 我们的氏族首领避免介入这件私事。

column1: Private feuds have a way of becoming clan feuds, just as water has a way of bubbling when placed over a fire.
column2: 私仇往往会变成氏族世仇，正如水放在火上就会沸腾一样。

column1: It will be very hard to convince Burthalor’s relatives to give up now that he is fresh-killed.
column2: 如今伯萨洛尔刚死，要说服其亲属放弃复仇将非常困难。

column1: Promises made now will not be considered binding later.
column2: 现在做出的承诺将来未必会被视为有约束力。

column1: We are obligated to do something about this.
column2: 我们有义务对此采取行动。

column1: This is not a fight between clans, unless we choose to make it so.
column2: 这不是氏族间的争斗，除非我们选择将其变成这样。

column1: If we wish to give gifts to Burthalor’s family, these should not exceed a fair wergild for his death — that is, ten cows.
column2: 如果我们想赠予伯萨洛尔家族礼物，这些不应超过他一命应得的血偿金——即十头牛。

column1: Outlaw the family.
column2: 放逐这个家族。

column1: We should make certain that this does not damage our relations with the \x01@! clan.
column2: 我们必须确保这不会损害我们与 \x01@! 氏族的关系。

column1: This episode of feuding won’t cause a feud with the entire \x01@! clan, but what about the next?
column2: 这次世仇事件不会引发与整个 \x01@! 氏族的仇恨，但下一次呢？

column1: The only way to guarantee a permanent end to the feud is to outlaw Robarth, Domasa, and the entire family. However, the carls would not stand for it.
column2: 确保世仇永久终结的唯一方法是放逐罗巴特、多玛萨及整个家族。然而，自由民不会容忍这种做法。

column1: Vamar Oskulsson waited until the boy who had killed his father was a man. Then he killed the killer with the same stone that felled great Oskul.
column2: 瓦马尔·奥斯库尔森一直等到杀父仇人长大成人，然后用当年击杀伟大奥斯库尔的同一块石头杀死了那个凶手。

column1: It is proper to pursue vengeance. We should interfere with neither family’s right to do so.
column2: 追求复仇是正当的。我们不应干涉任何一个家族的这项权利。

column1: Robarth is not at fault here; he merely defended himself from attack. It is Burthalor’s kin who must promise peace, if peace is to be promised.
column2: 罗巴特在此并无过错；他只是自卫还击。若要承诺和平，必须是伯萨洛尔的亲属来承诺。

column1: Orlanth made justice so that talking would come before fighting.
column2: 奥兰斯制定公正，为的是谈判先于战斗。

column1: With his Humakt-cross did Robarth become Burthalor’s meat-maker.
column2: 罗巴特凭借他的胡马特十字，成了伯萨洛尔的屠戮者。

column1: There is always another option.
column2: 总还有别的选择。

column1: This is my fault. I should have done something to prevent it.
column2: 这是我的错。我本该采取行动阻止此事。

column1: “Do not speak to oafs or sit with apes.”
column2: “勿与蠢人交谈，勿与猿猴同坐。”

column1: Domasa Glendarasdaughter, who took part in the feud with Rangarda Dark-Eyes of the \x01@! clan, died in her sleep last night. Perhaps this will finally end the private feud between the two families.
column2: 曾参与与 \x01@! 氏族黑眼朗加尔达世仇的多玛萨·格伦达拉之女，昨夜在睡梦中去世。或许这终将结束两族间的私仇。

column1: Outlaw Robarth.
column2: 放逐罗巴特。

column1: We outlawed Robarth.
column2: 我们放逐了罗巴特。

column1: The carls were unhappy about this decision, but understood why the clan leaders had taken it.
column2: 自由民对这个决定感到不满，但理解氏族首领为何做出此决定。

column1: The people judged this necessary, for they feared being drawn into a full-fledged feud with a stronger clan.
column2: 人民认为此举必要，因为他们害怕被卷入与更强氏族的全面世仇。

column1: No one ever saw the goods again.
column2: 再也没有人见过那些财物。

column1: Outlaw Robarth and all of his relatives.
column2: 放逐罗巴特及其所有亲属。

column1: The carls were outraged by this decision, which they said was far out of proportion with Robarth’s offense.
column2: 自由民对这个决定极为愤怒，称这与罗巴特的过错完全不成比例。

column1: The people judged this a harsh but necessary course of action, for they feared being drawn into a full-fledged feud with a stronger clan.
column2: 人们认为此举严苛却必要，唯恐被卷入与更强氏族的全面世仇。

column1: Return the goods.
column2: 归还货物。

column1: We returned the goods.
column2: 我们归还了货物。

column1: It turned out that Robarth had stolen goods worth eighty cows.
column2: 结果发现罗巴特偷窃了价值八十头牛的货物。

column1: The \x01@! leaders said that we should do more to contain our errant carls.
column2: \x01@! 首领们说，我们应更尽力约束那些越轨的自由民。

column1: The \x01@! leaders were so impressed by our action that they declared our feud over, and said that there would now be peace between our clans — so long as we contained our errant carls.
column2: \x01@! 首领们对我们的行动印象深刻，宣布世仇已了，并称只要我们能约束越轨的自由民，两族之间便可和平。

column1: Return the goods and pay additional compensation.
column2: 归还货物并额外支付补偿。

column1: We returned the goods, and paid more besides.
column2: 我们归还了货物，还额外支付了赔偿。

column1: The \x01@! leaders said that we had shown good faith, and that the actions of our errant carl would not be held against us.
column2: \x01@! 首领们说，我们展现了诚意，不会因越轨自由民的行为而追究我们。

column1: Scold Robarth.
column2: 斥责罗巴特。

column1: Clan leaders scolded Robarth.
column2: 氏族首领们斥责了罗巴特。

column1: Robarth seemed repentant, and the people felt that the clan leaders had acted wisely in chastising him.
column2: 罗巴特似乎有悔意，人们认为首领们惩戒他是明智之举。

column1: Robarth was unrepentant, and said
column2: 罗巴特毫无悔意，说

column1: he did not care if we ended up feuding with the entire \x01@! clan.
column2: 他不在乎我们是否最终与整个 \x01@! 氏族结下世仇。

column1: The people were most distressed by his words, for a feud with the \x01@! was precisely what they feared.
column2: 人们对他的话极为不安，因为他们最怕的就是与 \x01@! 部族结仇。

column1: The people were disturbed by his lack of respect for our chosen leaders.
column2: 人们因他对我们选出的首领缺乏尊重而感到不安。

column1: he did not care if he added fuel to our feud with the \x01@! clan.
column2: 他不在乎是否加剧我们与 \x01@! 氏族的世仇。

column1: For a time, Robarth and his kin became famous for their generosity.
column2: 一时间，罗巴特及其亲族因慷慨而名声大噪。

column1: That caravan contained nothing of value.
column2: 那支商队毫无值钱之物。

column1: That caravan contained perhaps fifty cows worth of goods.
column2: 那支商队货物约值五十头牛。

column1: That caravan contained perhaps a sixty cows worth of goods.
column2: 那支商队货物约值六十头牛。

column1: That caravan contained perhaps seventy worth of goods.
column2: 那支商队货物约值七十头牛。

column1: That caravan contained perhaps eighty cows worth of goods.
column2: 那支商队货物约值八十头牛。

column1: Those goods rightly belong to Robarth, who risked his life for them.
column2: 那些货物理应归罗巴特所有，是他冒死得来的。

column1: Robarth did not seek our permission before doing this thing, so we can rightly confiscate the spoils of his errant act.
column2: 罗巴特做此事前未征得我们同意，因此我们完全有权没收他越轨行为的战利品。

column1: Vamar Oskulson slew the man who killed his father, and was in turn laid low by that man’s son.
column2: 瓦玛·奥斯库尔松杀死了杀父仇人，随即又被那人的儿子所杀。

column1: This is a stupid dispute. No one even remembers how it started.
column2: 这是愚蠢的争端。甚至没人记得争端如何而起。

column1: If only we could all read! Then we might learn, from the chronicles, that vengeance is a sword whose hilt cuts as deep as its blade.
column2: 要是我们人人都能识字该多好！那样我们便可以从编年史中得知，复仇是一柄剑，其剑柄伤人如剑刃。

column1: They are our tribemates. Snow-haired Robarth must pay for abusing them so!
column2: 他们是我们的族胞。雪发的罗巴特必须为如此虐待他们而付出代价！

column1: With the proceeds from Robarth’s robbery, we could build quite a temple.
column2: 用罗巴特抢劫来的收益，我们能建一座不错的圣殿。

column1: No one will marry into Robarth’s family, for they know their sons and daughters might be killed in some pointless squabble.
column2: 没人愿意与罗巴特家族联姻，因为他们知道自家儿女可能死于某场无谓的争吵。

column1: sceneR420
column2: sceneR420

column1: One of our steads was attacked and looted by a party from the \x01@! clan, who were led by a woman named Iristha.
column2: 我们的一处农庄遭到 \x01@! 氏族一伙人的袭击和劫掠，为首的女子名叫伊里斯塔。

column1: Convince Iristha to end the family dispute.
column2: 说服伊里斯塔结束家族争端。

column1: We tried to convince Iristha to end the family dispute.
column2: 我们试图说服伊里斯塔结束家族争端。

column1: She said that, as far as she was concerned, all accounts were fully paid. She would make no more trouble as long as Janara’s family did the same.
column2: 她说，在她看来，所有账目已两清。只要贾娜拉的家族不再生事，她也不会再找麻烦。

column1: Convince Janara to let the matter lie.
column2: 劝说贾娜拉放下此事。

column1: Clan leaders told Janara to let the matter lie.
column2: 氏族首领们让贾娜拉放下此事。

column1: She agreed to do so, although she said she hoped the spirit of her great-grandmother was not watching, for Glendara would never have approved.
column2: 她同意了，不过她说希望曾祖母的在天之灵没有看到，因为格伦达拉绝不会赞同。

column1: She refused to obey the wishes of the ring, and spread many insults and lies about its members. The people were perturbed by her actions.
column2: 她拒绝服从长老会的意愿，并散布了许多关于其成员的辱骂和谎言。人们被她的行为激怒了。

column1: Ignore the matter.
column2: 不予理会。

column1: Clan leaders chose to ignore the matter. The people were unhappy with their decision.
column2: 氏族首领们选择不予理会。人们对此决定不满。

column1: The people were unhappy with the ring’s decision.
column2: 人们不满长老会的决定。

column1: Launch a legal claim against the robbers.
column2: 对抢匪提起法律诉讼。

column1: We launched a legal claim against the robbers.
column2: 我们对抢匪提起了法律诉讼。

column1: Iristha’s clan is in your tribe.
column2: 伊里斯塔所在氏族隶属本部落。

column1: The \x01@! leaders agreed to return the stolen goods, and also to compensate those wounded in the attack.
column2: \x01@! 首领们同意归还赃物，并赔偿袭击中的伤者。

column1: The \x01@! leaders agreed to return the stolen goods, but would not compensate those wounded in the attack.
column2: \x01@! 首领们同意归还赃物，但拒绝赔偿袭击中的伤者。

column1: They laughed at us and threw stones at our emissaries, wounding several of them. “We are feuding, yet you try to make a legal claim against us?”
column2: 他们嘲笑我们，并向我们的使者投掷石块，伤了好几人。“我们正在结仇，你们还想对我们提起法律诉讼？”

column1: We launched a raid against the \x01@! clan.
column2: 我们对 \x01@! 氏族发动了一次突袭。

column1: We recovered most of the goods that had been stolen from us, and a few more besides.
column2: 我们追回了大部分被劫货物，还额外多得了些。

column1: The weaponthanes were discouraged by our defeat at \x01@! hands.
column2: 武器领主们因败于 \x01@! 之手而士气受挫。

column1: The goods they took belonged to Janara’s family, not to the clan. But we would do well to ask for compensation for the burned steads.
column2: 他们夺走的货物属于贾娜拉家族，而非氏族。不过我们最好还是就焚毁的农庄要求赔偿。

column1: We must raid them.
column2: 我们必须突袭他们。

column1: It would not be smart to raid them now.
column2: 现在突袭他们不是明智之举。

column1: We have a good basis for a legal claim against Iristha.
column2: 我们对伊里斯塔有充分的法律诉讼依据。

column1: The \x01@! leaders will not want to jeopardize the good relations between our clans by ruling against us.
column2: \x01@! 首领们不愿因不利判决而危及两族间的良好关系。

column1: Our relations with our tribe mates leave much to be desired. They will rule against us if we take this to a moot.
column2: 我们与部落同胞的关系不尽如人意。若将此案提交公裁，他们会对我们不利。

column1: Our relations with our tribe mates are strong. They would rule in our favor, even if we were not so clearly in the right.
column2: 我们与部落同胞的关系十分牢固。即使我们并非如此明显地占理，他们也会做出有利判罚。

column1: Don’t let these family quarrels interfere with getting our crops planted.
column2: 别让这些家族纷争耽误我们把庄稼种下去。

column1: Don’t let these family quarrels interfere with getting our crops harvested.
column2: 别让这些家族纷争耽误我们把庄稼收回来。

column1: I believe that this dispute began four generations ago, when Iristha’s great-grandmother stole a horse belonging to Janara’s great-grandmother.
column2: 我相信这场争端始于四代前，当时伊里斯塔的曾祖母偷走了属于贾娜拉曾祖母的一匹马。

column1: I think I remember my grandmother telling me something about … now what was it?
column2: 我好像记得我祖母跟我讲过一些事……是什么呢来着？

column1: This dispute will continue until one of the families is extinct. There is nothing we can do.
column2: 这场争端会一直持续到其中一族灭绝。我们无能为力。

column1: I am sure that Janara will listen to reason, if we approach her properly.
column2: 我确信贾娜拉会听从道理，只要我们用恰当的方式去接近她。

column1: We must respect Janara’s rights, and raid them.
column2: 我们必须尊重贾娜拉的权利，然后袭击他们。

column2: sceneR421

column2: 惊愕的自由民看见两个幽灵在你的图拉领地上相互搏斗。人们深感忧虑——这是个可怕的预兆。

column1: Our carls saw two ghosts fighting one another.
column2: 我们的自由民看见两个幽灵在相互搏斗。

column1: concerned — this is a bad omen.
column2: 感到担忧——这是个不祥的预兆。

column1: annoyed — they are sick of coming upon these two old wraiths whacking at each other.
column2: 感到恼火——他们厌倦了撞见这两个老鬼魂互相殴打。

column1: Find shamans to chase the ghosts away.
column2: 找萨满来驱赶幽灵。

column1: We looked for shamans to chase the ghosts away.
column2: 我们找了萨满来驱赶幽灵。

column1: Shamans from the \x01@a clan volunteered to help us. They performed a lengthy ritual. At its end, they said that the ghosts were those of Robarth, of our clan, and Burthalor, of the \x01@! clan. Their families fought while they were alive, and they had been unable to release themselves from this feud in death. The shamans said they sent the spirits on their way, although they are probably doomed to walk the earth forever, locked in furious embrace.
column2: \x01@a 氏族的萨满自愿帮助我们。他们进行了一次冗长的仪式。仪式结束时，他们说这两个幽灵是我们的氏族罗巴特和 \x01@! 氏族的伯萨洛尔。他们活着时家族就在争斗，死后也无法从世仇中解脱。萨满们说他们已送走亡灵，尽管它们可能注定永远在地上游荡，在愤怒的纠缠中无法分开。

column1: \x01@N found shamans willing to undertake the task, in exchange for \x01A$ cows. They performed a lengthy ritual. At its end, they said that the ghosts were those of Robarth, of our clan, and Burthalor, of the \x01@! clan. column2: \x01@N 找到了愿意承担此任务的萨满，换取 \x01A$ 头牛。他们进行了一次冗长的仪式。仪式结束时，他们说这两个幽灵是我们的氏族罗巴特和 \x01@! 氏族的伯萨洛尔。他们活着时家族就在争斗，死后也无法从世仇中解脱。萨满们说他们已送走亡灵，尽管它们可能注定永远在地上游荡，在愤怒的纠缠中无法分开。

column1: \x01@N found no shamans willing to help.
