column1: Launch a legal claim against the ghosts.
column2: 对幽灵提起法律诉讼。

column1: We launched a legal claim against the ghosts.
column2: 我们对幽灵提起了法律诉讼。

column1: \x01@N found that they were the ghosts of Robarth, of our clan, and Burthalor, of the \x01@! clan. Their families fought while they were alive, and they had been unable to release themselves from this feud in death.
column2: \x01@N 发现他们是我们的氏族罗巴特和 \x01@! 氏族的伯萨洛尔的幽灵。他们活着时家族就在争斗，死后也无法从世仇中解脱。

column1: \x01@N found that they were the same old ghosts we’d seen before, spirits caught up in fighting, even in death.
column2: \x01@N 发现他们是我们以前见过的那些老幽灵，即便死后也纠缠在争斗中的亡灵。

column1: The ghosts agreed that they had been unlawfully occupying lands meant for the living, and promised to continue their fight somewhere else.
column2: 幽灵们同意他们非法占用了属于活人的土地，并承诺会换个地方继续打斗。

column1: The spirits contended that they had every right to occupy themselves in death as they had in life, and refused to leave. The people were alarmed, for they did not know when the hauntings would end.
column2: 亡灵们争辩说他们完全有权在死后像生前一样忙自己的事，并拒绝离开。人们惊慌起来，因为他们不知骚扰何时才结束。

column1: Ignore the apparitions.
column2: 无视这些幻影。

column1: We ignored the apparitions, but the people were uneasy about this.
column2: 我们无视了这些幻影，但人们对此感到不安。

column1: We ignored the apparitions, but the people were unsettled because of this.
column2: 我们无视了这些幻影，但人们因此心神不宁。

column1: We ignored the apparitions, and the people weren’t happy, but they had seen these particular ghosts often enough that they no longer feared them.
column2: 我们无视了这些幻影，人们虽不悦，但他们已多次见过这些特定幽灵，不再害怕了。

column1: Leave an offering to the ghosts.
column2: 向幽灵献上祭品。

column1: We left an offering to the ghosts.
column2: 我们向幽灵献上了祭品。

column1: They took our offering, and vanished. We never learned who they were.
column2: 他们收下了我们的祭品，消失了。我们始终不知他们是谁。

column1: They took our offering, and vanished.
column2: 他们收下了我们的祭品，消失了。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods for protection from ghosts.
column2: 向诸神献祭以求免受幽灵侵扰。

column1: We made an offering to the gods, so that they might protect us from ghosts.
column2: 我们向诸神献祭，求他们保护我们免受幽灵侵扰。

column1: Our prayers were answered, for the ghosts vanished. We never did learn who they were.
column2: 我们的祈祷应验了，因为幽灵消失了。我们始终没弄清他们是谁。

column1: Our prayers were answered, for the ghosts vanished.
column2: 我们的祈祷应验了，因为幽灵消失了。

column1: The ghosts continued to fight on our lands, and the people were discouraged, thinking that we had lost the favor of the gods.
column2: 幽灵继续在我们的土地上争斗，人们感到沮丧，认为我们失去了诸神的眷顾。

column1: Scold them for frightening their descendants and relatives.
column2: 责骂他们惊吓自己的后代和亲戚。

column1: God-talkers from both clans performed a ritual at the gravesite.
column2: 两个氏族的神言者在其墓地举行了一场仪式。

column1: They reminded the ghosts that feuds were for the living, and that both clans would fight better without their interference.
column2: 他们提醒幽灵，世仇是活人的事，两个氏族没有它们的干预会打得更好。

column1: They told the ghosts that the fight was over, and said that since our two clan were not feuding, why should they?
column2: 他们告诉幽灵，争斗已经结束，既然我们两个氏族并未结仇，它们又何必呢？

column1: Finally, they chided the spirits for scaring the living and for seeking more than their fair share of attention. “We will honor you properly in the Sacred Time, as befits our ancestors,” they said. “Do not be so greedy as to seek our attention with this unseemly show!”
column2: 最后，他们斥责亡灵吓唬活人，并寻求超出应有关注。“我们会在神圣时间恰当地尊崇你们，如同对待我们的祖先，”他们说，“不要如此贪婪，用这不体面的表演来吸引我们的注意！”

column1: The ritual seemed to calm the ghosts; they were not seen fighting again by us or by the \x01@! clan.
column2: 仪式似乎安抚了幽灵；我们和 \x01@! 氏族都再没看到它们争斗。

column1: Let me gather the \x01@! clan god-talkers with ours, and put these spirits to rest.
column2: 让我召集 \x01@! 氏族的神言者与我们的会合，让这些亡灵安息。

column1: Orlanth’s brother, Kolat, is master of spirits. He is worshipped only by shamans, so it is shamans we should seek.
column2: 奥兰斯的兄弟科拉特是灵魂之主。只有萨满才崇拜他，所以我们应当寻找萨满。

column1: It is not unheard of to dispose of ghosts by launching legal claims against them.
column2: 对幽灵提起法律诉讼来驱散它们，这并非闻所未闻。

column1: From the look of the clan insignia those ghosts are wearing, one of them is from our clan, and the other from the \x01@! clan.
column2: 从那些幽灵佩戴的氏族徽记来看，其中一个是我们的族人，另一个来自 \x01@! 氏族。

column1: Humakt hates the undead, and ghosts are undead. Sacrifice to Humakt, and he will sweep them away with the flat of his sword.
column2: 胡马克特憎恨亡灵，而幽灵正是亡灵。向胡马克特献祭，他会用剑脊将它们扫除。

column1: Sacrifice to Eurmal. He will trick the ghosts into going away.
column2: 向尤尔马尔献祭。他会欺骗幽灵离开。

column1: The gods do not want to be bothered with mere ghosts. Leave an offering directly to the spirits, and bribe them into leaving.
column2: 神祇们不想被区区幽灵打扰。直接向灵魂留下祭品，贿赂它们离开。

column1: Elmal will defend our hearth against bad spirits.
column2: 埃尔马尔会守护我们的炉膛，抵御恶灵。

column1: Sacrifice to Urox; he will scour our tula of Chaos.
column2: 向乌洛克斯献祭；他会将混沌从我们的图拉领地涤荡干净。

column1: No one will want to marry into a ghost-haunted clan.
column2: 没人愿意与闹鬼的氏族通婚。

column1: The elves are responsible for this.
column2: 精灵们对此负有责任。

column1: Our tula is the most lovely and bountiful in all of Dragon Pass, so it is no wonder that even the dead want to live here.
column2: 我们的图拉领地是整个龙隘中最美丽富饶的，难怪连死者都想住在这里。

column1: They are acting like children. Scold them like children.
column2: 它们像孩子一样行事。就像教训孩子那样训斥它们。

column1: We have no right to interfere with their freedoms. Even though they are dead, they are still Orlanthi.
column2: 我们无权干涉它们的自由。哪怕它们已死，也仍然是奥兰斯人。

column1: I think that it is old Robarth, and the enemy he slew, Burthalor!
column2: 我想那是老罗巴特和他杀死的敌人伯萨洛尔！

column1: Maybe they need to be reminded that they’re dead.
column2: 也许需要提醒它们已经死了。

column1: It’s the moment I’ve been warning you about for ages!
column2: 这正是我长久以来警告你们的时刻！

column1: sceneR422
column2: sceneR422

column1: Wilkossi, one of the warriors you sent on your exploratory mission, reports on its unfortunate and premature end.
column2: 威尔科西，你派去执行探险任务的一名战士，报告了这次不幸而过早结束的任务。

column1: “One of our fellows, Thadart, was taken by the cruel enemies known as Tusk Riders. We fought valiantly to rescue him, but they were fierce, their boarish steeds were fresh, and they knew the terrain better than we. We have heard from our neighbors about the bloodthirsty gods they worship, and know of their murderous habits. Unlucky Thadart is surely dead by now.”
column2: “我们的一位同伴萨达特，被名为獠牙骑手的残酷敌人抓走了。我们英勇作战想救回他，但他们凶残，他们的野猪坐骑精力充沛，而且比我们更熟悉地形。我们从邻居那里听说过他们崇拜的嗜血神祇，也了解他们杀人的习性。不幸的萨达特此时肯定已经死了。”

column1: An exploratory mission came home early to report that one of them had been taken by Tusk Riders, and could now be presumed dead.
column2: 一支探险队提前返回，报告说其中一人被獠牙骑手抓走，如今可能已经遇害。

column1: Compose a funeral poem.
column2: 创作一首葬礼诗。

column1: \x01@N composed a poem to celebrate Thadart’s life and mourn his death.
column2: \x01@N 创作了一首诗来颂扬萨达特的一生，哀悼他的死亡。

column1: The people were much cheered by it. They said that other clans would now remember Thadart and his deeds.
column2: 族人们因此备受鼓舞。他们说其他氏族现在会记住萨达特和他的事迹。

column1: All agreed that the poem had not captured Thadart’s heroic qualities. They said that its quality made our commemoration of the man’s death seem shabby.
column2: 所有人都认为这首诗未能捕捉萨达特的英雄品质。他们说诗作的质量使得我们对这位勇士亡故的纪念显得寒酸。

column1: Give gifts to Thadart’s relatives.
column2: 向萨达特的亲属赠送礼物。

column1: The people were cheered by this display of generosity.
column2: 族人们因这一慷慨之举而振奋。

column1: Remind the people that danger is a part of life.
column2: 提醒族人危险是生活的一部分。

column1: \x01@N reminded the people that danger is a part of life.
column2: \x01@N 提醒族人危险是生活的一部分。

column1: The people were moved by the wisdom of \x01@N’s oration.
column2: 族人们被 \x01@N的演说中的智慧所打动。

column1: Although they did not say as much, the people found a hollow ring in \x01@N’s words.
column2: 尽管没有明说，族人们觉得 \x01@N的话语空洞无物。

column1: Sacrifice to the gods in Thadart’s honor.
column2: 以萨达特的名义向神祇献祭。

column1: We sacrificed in Thadart’s honor.
column2: 我们以萨达特的名义献了祭。

column1: The god-talkers said that the sacrifice was accepted, but other signs indicated that the ritual was going to fail. No one could say what this meant.
column2: 神言者们说献祭被接受了，但其他迹象表明仪式将要失败。没人能说出这意味着什么。

column1: “There will be no funeral until Thadart is proven dead.”
column2: “除非证明萨达特已死，否则不发葬礼。”

column1: Clan leaders said, “There will be no funeral until Thadart is proven dead.”
column2: 氏族首领们说：“除非证明萨达特已死，否则不发葬礼。”

column1: The people were heartened, and remembered the words of King Vingkot: “Six times have my enemies thought me dead, and six times have I returned to harry them. Six times have I vanished, and six times have my friends kept my place at table, knowing that I would be back.”
column2: 族人们感到振奋，记起了文科特王的话：“我的敌人有六次以为我死了，又有六次我回来袭击他们。我有六次消失不见，又有六次朋友们为我保留着席位，知道我会回来。”

column1: The people shook their heads. It was clear from the grim expression on their faces that they thought the ring members were fooling themselves.
column2: 族人们摇了摇头。从他们脸上阴郁的表情可以清楚看出，他们认为长老会成员是在自欺欺人。

column1: Send a war party to hunt for Thadart.
column2: 派出战团搜寻萨达特。

column1: We sent a war party to hunt for Thadart.
column2: 我们派出战团搜寻萨达特。

column1: \x01@\x05, who led the party, searched valiantly for him, but there was no trace of Thadart to be found.
column2: \x01@\x05率领战团的[某人]英勇地搜寻他，但没能找到萨达特的任何踪迹。

column1: Although many Tusk Riders live in the Stinking Forest, others roam Dragon Pass, causing trouble.
column2: 尽管许多獠牙骑手住在恶臭森林，另一些则游荡在龙隘各处，制造麻烦。

column1: Danger is a part of life.
column2: 危险是生活的一部分。

column1: Thadart was one of our most warlike carls. But he knew that exploration was dangerous when he agreed to go.
column2: 萨达特是我们最好战的自由民之一。但他答应出发时就知道探索是危险的。

column1: Thadart was very skilled with weapons. Even though he was not a weaponthane, we should honor him as one.
column2: 萨达特非常擅长武器。即便他不是武器侍卫，我们也应当像对待武器侍卫一样尊崇他。

column1: We should give gifts to Thadart’s relatives.
column2: 我们应当向萨达特的亲属赠送礼物。

column1: A poem has more power to stir the heart than an ordinary speech, or even a generous gift.
column2: 一首诗比普通的演说，甚至比慷慨的礼物更能撼动人心。

column1: We should sacrifice in Thadart’s honor.
column2: 我们应当以萨达特的名义献祭。

column1: We should sacrifice in Thadart’s honor, to speed his spirit to the Halls of the Dead.
column2: 我们应当以萨达特的名义献祭，以加速他的灵魂前往死者之厅。

column1: King Vingkot disappeared many times, and those of weak confidence thought him slain. But each time he came back, hungry and wanting his dinner, having miraculously escaped death.
column2: 文科特王多次消失，那些信心不足的人都以为他遇害了。但每次他都回来了，饥肠辘辘想要吃饭，奇迹般地从死亡中逃脱。

column1: If only we knew the location of the Tusk Rider lair — then we could courageously risk our lives to recover Thadart’s bones!
column2: 要是我们知道獠牙骑手巢穴的位置就好了——那样我们就能勇敢地冒生命危险去取回萨达特的遗骨！

column1: We must think of the family.
column2: 我们必须为家族着想。

column1: It would be cruel to give the people false hope.
column2: 给人们虚假的希望是残忍的。

column1: If more of us knew how to write, we could not only compose poems, but preserve them for the ages.
column2: 如果我们中更多人会写字，我们不仅能创作诗歌，还能把它们流传千古。

column1: “Smile while alive, lest your only grin be that of your skull.”
column2: “活着时微笑，免得你唯一的咧嘴笑只剩下骷髅。”

column1: And to think, we were seeking a bride for Thadart. At least there is no fresh widow to choke on her tears.
column2: 想想看，我们还在为萨达特寻找新娘。至少没有新寡妇被泪水噎住。

column1: Generosity is a holy thing; never more so than at times like these.
column2: 慷慨是神圣的；在这样的时候尤其如此。

column1: There is no point in hunting for Thadart; we will try and fail, and further lower the spirits of our warriors.
column2: 寻找萨达特毫无意义；我们会尝试然后失败，进一步打击战士们的士气。

column1: By Elmal’s fiery locks, we must find him!
column2: 以埃尔马尔火焰般的发绺起誓，我们必须找到他！

column1: sceneR423
column2: sceneR423

column1: A man who looks like a Tusk Rider comes to your tula, as if expecting a welcome. The man claims to be Thadart, the explorer of your clan, who was taken by Tusk Riders and presumed dead. He says that he was tortured by the Tusk Riders, and left to die of exposure on an altar to their terrible god. But the god spared his life, changing his face so that he looked like a Tusk Rider. “Their god meant it as a grim joke, but you are my clan-mates, and I know that you will accept me, even though I am disfigured.”
column2: 一个看起来像獠牙骑手的人来到你的图拉领地，似乎期待受到欢迎。此人自称是你们氏族的探险者萨达特，他被獠牙骑手掳走，人们以为他已经死了。他说他被獠牙骑手折磨，被丢在他们可怕之神的祭坛上等死。但神饶了他一命，改变了他的面容，使他看起来像个獠牙骑手。“他们的神把这当作一个残酷的玩笑，但你们是我的氏族同胞，我知道你们会接受我，尽管我已毁容。”

column1: A man with the face of a Tusk Rider came to our tula and claimed to be Thadart. He said his disfigurement was a grim joke of the Tusk Riders’ god.
column2: 一个长着獠牙骑手面容的人来到我们的图拉领地，声称自己是萨达特。他说他的毁容是獠牙骑手之神的一个残酷玩笑。

column1: Allow him to return.
column2: 允许他回来。

column1: We allowed him to return.
column2: 我们允许他回来了。

column1: He was pleased to be welcomed back. “It is shameful to admit, but part of me was afraid that you would reject me, now that I am disfigured.” Some of the people whispered in fear, for they were certain that Thadart was dead, and this was a monstrous impostor.
column2: 他很高兴受到欢迎归来。“承认这一点很丢人，但我一部分内心曾害怕你们会拒绝我，现在我已毁容。”有些人恐惧地窃窃私语，因为他们确信萨达特已经死了，而这是一个可怕的冒牌货。

column1: He defended himself fiercely, wounding several of our weaponthanes before he was finally driven to his knees. It was Wilkossi, who was with Thadart when he was captured, who finally slit the intruder’s throat. “This is for tainting the memory of our brave, dead comrade,” Wilkossi said. The people were dismayed and upset by this bloody scene.
column2: 他激烈自卫，伤了我们好几位武器领主，最终才被按跪在地。是威尔科西——萨达特被俘时和他在一起的人——最终割断了入侵者的喉咙。“这是为了玷污我们勇敢的已故战友的名声，”威尔科西说。人们被这血腥场面弄得沮丧不安。

column1: Convince the people that he should be allowed to return.
column2: 说服人们应该允许他回来。

column1: Our clan leaders sought to convince the people that he should be allowed to return.
column2: 我们的氏族领袖试图说服人们应该允许他回来。

column1: \x01@N’s eloquent words persuaded them that this was indeed Thadart returned, and not some terrible monster.
column2: \x01@N他雄辩的言辞说服了他们，这确实是萨达特归来，而不是某个可怕的怪物。

column1: After all, the clan ring had predicted his eventual return.
column2: 毕竟，氏族议会曾预言他最终会回来。

column1: The people welcomed him back, and there was much rejoicing.
column2: 人们欢迎他归来，一片欢腾。

column1: \x01@N’s words did not quell the fears of the people. They would not look beyond the ugliness of his new visage.
column2: \x01@N他的话没有平息人们的恐惧。他们无法忽视他新面容的丑陋。

column1: Send him away.
column2: 把他赶走。

column1: He protested, but when it finally became obvious that we would not relent, he hung his head and left. The people said we had done the right thing, for surely he was a monster.
column2: 他抗议了，但当最终我们显然不会让步时，他低下头离开了。人们说我们做得对，因为他肯定是个怪物。

column1: “You may return, but we will be watching you.”
column2: “你可以回来，但我们会盯着你。”

column1: Our clan leaders said, “You may return, but we will be watching you.”
column2: 我们的氏族领袖说：“你可以回来，但我们会盯着你。”

column1: He said, “I expected a better welcome than this, but I will prove to you that I am the same Thadart I was before.” His words did not quell the worries of the people, who were afraid that he would turn out to be a monster.
column2: 他说：“我期待过比这更好的欢迎，但我会向你们证明我还是从前的那个萨达特。”他的话没有平息人们的担忧，他们害怕他结果会是一个怪物。

column1: It’s not Thadart.
column2: 这不是萨达特。

column1: I think he is really Thadart.
column2: 我认为他真的是萨达特。

column1: I am certain that this is Thadart.
column2: 我确信这就是萨达特。

column1: I am certain that this is Thadart, and he remains a good Orlanthi. He will not harm us.
column2: 我确信这就是萨达特，而且他仍然是一个好奥兰特人。他不会伤害我们。

column1: If this is really Thadart, we are obligated to allow him to return.
column2: 如果这真的是萨达特，我们有义务允许他回来。

column1: If this is Thadart, we are still permitted to outlaw him. We would not be the first clan to outlaw a person without just cause.
column2: 如果这是萨达特，我们仍然可以剥夺他的氏族身份。我们不会是第一个无正当理由就剥夺某人氏族身份的氏族。

column1: The people are worried that it is not Thadart, but some kind of monster.
column2: 人们担心这不是萨达特，而是某种怪物。

column1: The people are worried that it is not Thadart, but some kind of monster. We must either reject him, or allay their fears.
column2: 人们担心这不是萨达特，而是某种怪物。我们必须要么拒绝他，要么消除他们的恐惧。

column1: Who knows what terrible magics the Tusk Rider god is capable of?
column2: 谁知道獠牙骑手之神能施展什么可怕的魔法？

column1: A Chaos creature slew King Heort’s holder of regalia and thus gained entry to Heort’s encampment, almost killing our great lord.
column2: 一个混沌生物杀死了赫尔特王持有王权象征物的人，从而得以进入赫尔特营地，差点杀了我们伟大的领主。

column1: We cannot risk letting a monster into our tula.
column2: 我们不能冒险让一个怪物进入我们的图拉领地。

column1: We must be thoughtful, and not act on our feelings alone.
column2: 我们必须深思熟虑，不能只凭感情行事。

column1: There is no chance of finding a bride for him now.
column2: 现在没机会为他找新娘了。

column1: The Tusk Rider deity is a destructive boar god. We cannot trust that this is really Thadart.
column2: 獠牙骑手神祇是一位破坏性的野猪神。我们不能相信这真的是萨达特。

column1: Kill him before he kills us!
column2: 趁他杀我们之前杀了他！

column1: We must give him the benefit of the doubt.
column2: 我们必须假定他是无辜的。

column1: “Laugh when your friends laugh, but return a liar’s words with lies of your own.”
column2: “朋友笑时你便笑，但要对说谎者以谎还谎。”

column1: If we do not give himself a chance to prove himself, this is not a clan of free men, but a prison.
column2: 如果我们不给他一个证明自己的机会，那这就不算自由人的氏族，而是一座监狱。

column1: Kill him, and then kill the other tusk riders!
column2: 杀掉他，然后再杀掉其他獠牙骑手！

column1: I think that this is Thadart, but we should send him away anyway, lest his gruesome features distract us from our battle against the undead.
column2: 我想这就是萨达特，但我们还是应该把他送走，免得他那可怕的模样让我们在与亡灵的战斗中分心。

column1: sceneR424
column2: sceneR424

column1: Thadart, the warrior of your clan whose visage was made monstrous by the alien god of the Tusk Riders, comes before the clan ring, demanding redress of a grievance. “I am dishonored in my own clan. I am continually insulted, whispered about, and treated as some kind of outlaw or foreigner. No one will look me in the eye.
column2: 萨达特，你们氏族的那位战士，其面容被獠牙骑手的外来神祇变得狰狞可怖，来到氏族议会面前，要求为他所受的委屈讨回公道。“我在自己的氏族中蒙受耻辱。我不断被侮辱、被窃窃私语、被当作某种亡命徒或外人对待。没有人敢直视我的眼睛。

column1: On our last raid, no one would turn their backs to me. When I was cut off by the \x01@! weaponthanes, no one came to my aid.
column2: 在我们上次突袭中，没有人敢把后背对着我。当我被 \x01@! 武器领主截断时，没有人来支援我。

column1: You welcomed me here, but the others have done everything they can to drive me from the home of my birth.
column2: 你们欢迎我来到这里，但其他人却竭尽全力要把我从生我养我的家园赶走。

column1: I do not wish to fight those of my own clan, although they dishonor me. I instead demand that you reproach them for their misbehavior, so that they will correct it.”
column2: 我不想与同族之人兵戈相向，尽管他们羞辱我。我反而要求你们斥责他们的不当行为，好让他们改正。”

column1: Thadart, the warrior whose visage was made monstrous by the alien god of the Tusk Riders, said that other members of the clan had dishonored him, and demanded that the clan ring reproach them.
column2: 萨达特，那位面容被獠牙骑手的外来神祇变得狰狞可怖的战士，声称其他氏族成员羞辱了他，并要求氏族议会斥责他们。

column1: Give him gifts.
column2: 给他礼物。

column1: The chief gave him gifts.
column2: 酋长给了他礼物。

column1: What do you offer him?
column2: 你给他什么？

column1: Thadart accepted the gifts, but was clearly unsatisfied. The people in turn complained that we had encouraged a troublemaker.
column2: 萨达特接受了礼物，但显然并不满意。人们转而抱怨我们鼓励了一个惹是生非的家伙。

column1: Persuade him to be more understanding of the others’ fears.
column2: 说服他对其他人的恐惧多些理解。

column1: \x01@N said he should be more tolerant of the others’ fears.
column2: \x01@N 说他应该对其他人的恐惧更加宽容。

column1: Thadart agreed that it was natural for the others to fear him, and said that he would work to disregard their ignorant slights.
column2: 萨达特同意别人害怕他是自然的，并表示他会努力无视他们那些无知的轻慢。

column1: Thadart replied, “If I get killed on a raid, because the others are too fearful to support me, my understanding of their fears will be little consolation.” He repeated his demand.
column2: 萨达特回答说：“如果我在一次突袭中因为其他人太害怕而无法支援我而被杀，那我对他们恐惧的理解将毫无安慰。”他重复了他的要求。

column1: Persuade the people to treat him with greater respect.
column2: 说服人们对他更加尊重。

column1: \x01@N sought to persuade the people to treat him with greater respect.
column2: \x01@N 试图说服人们对他更加尊重。

column1: They agreed that they had not behaved properly towards Thadart, and promised to mend their ways. Thadart said he had much ale for them to drink, if they would do him the honor of accepting his hospitality. The people drank long into the night, and the matter was settled.
column2: 他们同意自己对待萨达特的方式不妥，并承诺改正。萨达特说他有很多麦酒给他们喝，只要他们赏脸接受他的款待。人们痛饮至深夜，事情就此解决。

column1: They protested that Thadart had not proven himself; he could still be a monster, waiting for the time to strike. Thadart was angered by their response and departed, never to return.
column2: 他们抗议说萨达特还没有证明自己；他可能还是个怪物，在等待时机出手。萨达特被他们的回应激怒，离开了，再也没有回来。

column1: Reproach the people for dishonoring him.
column2: 斥责那些羞辱了他的人。

column1: \x01@N reproached the people for dishonoring him.
column2: \x01@N 斥责了那些羞辱了他的人。

column1: They hung their heads in contrition, and said that they had not acted properly. They promised to mend their ways, and Thadart said he had much ale for them to drink, if they would do him the honor of accepting his hospitality. The people drank long into the night, and the matter was settled.
column2: 他们懊悔地低下头，说自己做得不对。他们承诺改正，萨达特说他有很多麦酒给他们喝，只要他们赏脸接受他的款待。人们痛饮至深夜，事情就此解决。

column1: They were most affronted, and said that the ring had overstepped the bounds of their authority by telling free Orlanthi how to act. Thadart, however, said that his honor had been satisfied by this reproach, and would consider the matter settled.
column2: 他们非常愤怒，说氏族议会越权了，居然指导自由奥兰提人该如何行事。然而萨达特说这次斥责已经满足了他的荣誉，他会认为此事已经解决。

column1: “You are lucky we let you live here at all.”
column2: “你能在这儿活着就算走运了。”

column1: Clan leaders said to him, “You are lucky we let you live here at all.”
column2: 氏族首领对他说：“你能在这儿活着就算走运了。”

column1: “It is not lucky to live among dishonorable companions,” Thadart retorted. He packed up his goods and departed, never to be seen again.
column2: “与不光彩的同伴为伍并非幸运，”萨达特反驳道。他收拾行装离开了，从此再未现身。

column1: Gifts will make him happy.
column2: 礼物会让他高兴。

column1: He doesn’t want gifts. He wants a promise of better treatment.
column2: 他不想要礼物。他想要得到更好对待的承诺。

column1: He must be made to understand that the others treat him badly out of fear.
column2: 必须让他明白，其他人对他不好是出于恐惧。

column1: We have the right to reproach our own people.
column2: 我们有权斥责自己人。

column1: We can’t make anyone do anything.
column2: 我们不能强迫任何人做任何事。

column1: If we reproach the others, he will consider his honor satisfied, even if their response is bad.
column2: 如果我们斥责其他人，他会认为自己的荣誉得到满足，即使他们的反应不好。

column1: What this upstart needs is a good scolding!
column2: 这个暴发户需要的是一顿痛骂！

column1: If we give him gifts, the others will be jealous.
column2: 如果我们给他礼物，其他人会嫉妒。

column1: If we can solve this matter while displeasing neither Thadart or the others, we will gain a reputation for wisdom.
column2: 如果我们能解决这件事，既不惹恼萨达特也不惹恼其他人，我们就能赢得智慧的名声。

column1: He is lucky we let him live here at all.
column2: 他能在这儿活着就算走运了。

column1: The people cannot be blamed. They are simply concerned with the security of the clan.
column2: 人们无可指责。他们只是关心氏族的安危。

column1: He will leave our clan eventually, no matter what we do. The fear of the others is too strong to permit him to live here in harmony.
column2: 无论我们做什么，他最终都会离开我们的氏族。其他人的恐惧太强烈，无法让他和谐地住在这里。

column1: He has been touched by a foreign god. His presence contaminates our shrines and temples.
column2: 他被异神触碰过。他的存在污染了我们的圣祠和神庙。

column1: If our warriors are afraid of one another, our next raid is doomed to fail. We must solve this problem.
column2: 如果我们战士之间互相害怕，我们的下一次突袭注定失败。我们必须解决这个问题。

column1: I told you taking him in would cause problems.
column2: 我告诉过你收留他会带来麻烦。

column1: After reconciling Thadart with the weaponthanes, we should launch a raid, to prove their renewed bonds of friendship.
column2: 在让萨达特和武器领主和解之后，我们应该发动一次突袭，以证明他们重续的友谊纽带。

column1: Thadart, the warrior of your clan whose visage was made monstrous by the alien god of the Tusk Riders, comes before the clan ring with a request. “My parents have tried to find a bride for me, but have been rebuffed at every turn, even by our closest allies. I understand that it is difficult to find a woman to marry a man with a face like mine. I do not expect a beautiful bride, or a clever one, or even a kindly one. But I do need a bride, so that I may carry on the sacred line of my ancestors. I implore you to intervene in this matter, and find me a mate.”
column2: 萨达特，你们氏族的战士，其面容被獠牙骑手的异神变得可怖，来到氏族议会前提出一个请求。“我的父母曾试图为我找一位新娘，但每次都被拒绝，甚至我们最亲密的盟友也如此。我理解，要找到一个女人嫁给像我这样一张脸的男人很难。我并不期待美丽的新娘，或聪慧的，甚至善良的。但我确实需要一个新娘，这样我才能延续祖先的神圣血脉。我恳请你们介入此事，为我找一个伴侣。”

column1: Thadart, the warrior with the Tusk Rider face, implored us to find him a bride.
column2: 萨达特，那位有着獠牙骑手面孔的战士，恳求我们为他找一位新娘。

column1: “If you keep bothering us, we will outlaw you.”
column2: “如果你继续打扰我们，我们就会宣布你为法外之徒。”

column1: The clan ring said, “If you keep bothering us, we will outlaw you.”
column2: 氏族议会说：“如果你继续打扰我们，我们就会宣布你为法外之徒。”

column1: Thadart said that he could tell when he was not wanted, and departed from our tula, never to be seen again.
column2: 萨达特说他能看出自己不受欢迎，便离开了我们的领地，从此再也未曾露面。

column1: The people, who had cast aside their earlier fear of him, excoriated the ring members for their cruelty and indifference. They said that the ring was not fit to rule them.
column2: 人们早已放下先前对他的恐惧，严厉谴责议会成员的残忍和冷漠。他们说议会不配统治他们。

column1: The people were glad to see him go. They said his monstrousness was like a cloud hanging over the entire clan.
column2: 人们很高兴看到他离开。他们说他的可怖如同笼罩整个氏族的阴云。

column1: “If your parents will not perform this duty, it is not a matter for the ring.”
column2: “如果你的父母不愿履行这项职责，那就不是议会该管的事。”

column1: Our clan leaders said, “If your parents will not perform this duty, it is not a matter for the ring.”
column2: 我们氏族的首领说：“如果你的父母不愿履行这项职责，那就不是议会该管的事。”

column1: Thadart was clearly disappointed, but said nothing.
column2: 萨达特显然很失望，但什么也没说。

column1: The people, who had embraced Thadart and his cause, were dissatisfied with this decision.
column2: 那些支持萨达特及其诉求的人们对这个决定感到不满。

column1: Promise to find him a bride.
column2: 承诺为他找到新娘。

column1: Clan leaders promised to find him a bride.
column2: 氏族首领承诺为他找到新娘。

column1: After long discussions with a number of friendly clans, we found a prospect for him: Kistrald of the \x01@! clan. She was neither lovely nor clever, but when Thadart’s set eyes upon her, both were filled with love.
column2: 经过与多个友好氏族的漫长商议，我们为他找到一个合适人选： \x01@! 氏族的基斯特拉尔德。她既不美丽也不聪慧，但萨达特的目光落在她身上时，两人心中都充满了爱意。

column1: The people, who had embraced Thadart and his cause, rejoiced. They set about making a wedding celebration that would be remembered in Dragon Pass for generations to come.
column2: 那些支持萨达特及其诉求的人们欢欣鼓舞。他们着手准备一场婚礼庆典，将让龙隘在未来数代间铭记。

column1: Despite long discussions with a number of friendly clans, we found no prospects for him. In approaching them repeatedly, we strained our relations with them. Thadart could not conceal his disappointment.
column2: 尽管与多个友好氏族进行了漫长的商议，我们仍未能为他找到合适人选。反复交涉中，我们与它们的关系变得紧张。萨达特无法掩饰自己的失望。

column1: The people, who had embraced Thadart and his cause, were also despondent.
column2: 那些支持萨达特及其诉求的人们也同样沮丧。

column1: Try to find him a bride, but promise nothing.
column2: 试着为他找新娘，但不做任何承诺。

column1: Without making any promises, clan leaders said they would try to find him a bride.
column2: 氏族首领没有做出任何承诺，只说会尽力为他找到新娘。

column1: Despite long discussions with a number of friendly clans, we found no prospects for him. In approaching them repeatedly, we strained our relations with them. Thadart said he was disappointed, but not entirely surprised.
column2: 尽管与多个友好氏族进行了漫长的商议，我们仍未能为他找到合适人选。反复交涉中，我们与它们的关系变得紧张。萨达特说他很失望，但并不完全意外。

column1: “You cannot expect to marry, looking as you do.”
column2: “看你这副模样，别指望能结婚。”

column1: Clan leaders told him, “You cannot expect to marry, looking as you do.”
column2: 氏族首领告诉他：“看你这副模样，别指望能结婚。”

column1: Thadart said it was the right of any red-blooded Orlanthi male to seek marriage, no matter what he looked like.
column2: 萨达特说，任何热血奥兰斯男性都有权追寻婚姻，不论他长什么样。

column1: The people said that the ring members were cruel to remind poor Thadart of his deformity, which he had suffered while undertaking the clan’s business.
column2: 人们说议会成员残忍地提醒可怜的萨达特他的残疾，而他正是在执行氏族事务时遭受此难的。

column1: We can easily find some homely, desperate widow or spinster for him.
column2: 我们很容易就能为他找个样貌平平、走投无路的寡妇或老处女。

column1: We have become used to Thadart’s visage, but it is new to our neighbors. It will be hard to find even a homely widow or spinster for him.
column2: 我们已经习惯了萨达特的面容，但对我们邻居来说是陌生的。即使找个样貌平平的寡妇或老处女也会很难。

column1: It will be hard to find a bride for him, but I think I can do it.
column2: 为他找到新娘会很难，但我觉得我能做到。

column1: It will be hard to find a bride for him, but I am nonetheless certain that I can do it.
column2: 为他找到新娘会很难，但我仍然确信我能做到。

column1: Thadart is still the object of considerable fear and mistrust among our own clan members. There is no need to exert ourselves on his behalf.
column2: 萨达特在我们氏族成员中仍然引起相当大的恐惧和不信任。没必要为他出力。

column1: Though once feared and mistrusted, Thadart is now popular with the people. They will be unhappy if we do not help him.
column2: 尽管曾经被恐惧和不信任，萨达特现在深受人们喜爱。如果我们不帮他，他们会不高兴。

column1: Thadart is still the object of considerable fear and mistrust among our own clan members. The people would be glad to see him go.
column2: 萨达特在我们氏族成员中仍然引起相当大的恐惧和不信任。人们会很高兴看到他离开。

column1: We are legally obligated to do as he asks.
column2: 我们在法理上有义务按他要求的去做。

column1: It is his parents’ job to find a bride; our duty is only to approve the match once it is made.
column2: 找新娘是他父母的事；我们的职责只是在婚事定下后予以批准。

column1: Although it is up to his parents to pick a bride, clan leaders may step in when a deserving person finds it difficult to find a mate.
column2: 虽然应由他父母选新娘，但当一位值得的人难以找到伴侣时，氏族首领可以介入。

column1: The people will be heartened if we promise to find him a bride, no matter what.
column2: 如果我们无论如何都承诺为他找到新娘，人们会感到振奋。

column1: Better not to promise, unless we are sure of success.
column2: 最好不要承诺，除非我们确信能成功。

column1: It is possible that we will offend our allies by asking them for a bride for a fellow so hideous.
column2: 我们可能会因为为如此丑陋的家伙向他们要新娘而冒犯盟友。

column1: Other clans might think him tainted by Chaos.
column2: 其他氏族可能会认为他被混沌污染了。

column1: Orlanth found it difficult to court Ernalda, but not because he was ugly as a pig.
column2: 奥兰斯追求厄娜尔达时也觉得困难，但不是因为他丑得像头猪。

column1: If we disappoint Thadart, he will find a way to die.
column2: 如果我们让萨达特失望，他会想办法寻死。

column1: Marriage negotiations are also a good time to extract pledges from our allies to launch a sustained campaign against the undead.
column2: 联姻谈判也是向盟友索取承诺，发动对亡灵持续征讨的好时机。

column1: Before his face was changed, I thought it would be easy to find a bride for him. But now…
column2: 在他面容变样之前，我以为给他找个新娘很容易。但现在……

column1: Thadart, the warrior with the Tusk Rider face, died in the last raid. He attacked recklessly, as if trying to get himself killed. Those who knew him said that he was despondent over the ring’s failure to find a bride for him.
column2: 长着獠牙骑士面孔的战士萨达特，在最后一次突袭中阵亡。他鲁莽地进攻，仿佛一心求死。认识他的人都说，他因长老会未能为他找到新娘而沮丧。

column1: The clan mourned the death of Thadart, the warrior with the Tusk Rider face, who fought recklessly in our last battle.
column2: 氏族哀悼了长着獠牙骑士面孔的战士萨达特的死，他在我们上一场战斗中作战鲁莽。

column1: Although the people did not honor him in life, they are now remorseful, for they can see that Thadart never did anything monstrous, and was in fact as good a person as before his face was changed.
column2: 尽管人们生前并不敬重他，如今却感到悔恨，因为他们看得出萨达特从未做过任何可怕之事，实际上他和面容被改变前一样善良。

column1: The people mourn his death extravagantly. Although they were unkind to him at first, he had long since won them over. They say the ring should have done more to help him.
column2: 人们隆重地哀悼他的死。尽管起初他们对他不友善，但他早已赢得了他们的心。他们说长老会本应做更多来帮助他。

column1: sceneR426
column2: sceneR426

column1: Thadart and his bride, Kistrald, have had a son. They have named him Palagor. Although Thadart’s pride in his child is great, some of his relatives, and other members of the clan, are gravely concerned. The boy shares Thadart’s Tusk Rider features. It was hoped that Thadart’s curse would not be hereditary, but indeed it is.
column2: 萨达特与他的新娘基斯特拉尔德有了一个儿子。他们给他取名帕拉戈尔。尽管萨达特对孩子深感自豪，但他的一些亲属和氏族的其他成员却深感忧虑。这孩子继承了萨达特的獠牙骑士特征。人们曾希望萨达特的诅咒不会遗传，但确实遗传了。

column1: A son, Palagor, was born to Thadart and Kistrald. The people were concerned, because Palagor shared his father’s facial deformity.
column2: 萨达特和基斯特拉尔德生了一个儿子，帕拉戈尔。人们感到担忧，因为帕拉戈尔遗传了他父亲的面部畸形。

column1: Outlaw Thadart, Kistrald, and their son.
column2: 将萨达特、基斯特拉尔德和他们的儿子逐出氏族。

column1: We outlawed the three of them.
column2: 我们将他们三人逐出了氏族。

column1: Some people said that this was the only safe thing to do. Others said that it was harsh and unnecessary, and would reflect badly upon us. The three of them were adopted by Kistrald’s birth clan; their new clan leaders said that they would no longer trust us.
column2: 有些人说这是唯一稳妥之举。另一些人则说这过于严苛且不必要，会给我们带来坏名声。他们三人被基斯特拉尔德的生氏族收养；他们的新氏族首领说他们将不再信任我们。

column1: We chose to ignore the event, and the people’s muttering subsided, even if their qualms did not.
column2: 我们选择忽略此事，人们的嘀咕平息了，尽管他们的疑虑并未消失。

column1: Forbid Thadart to father any more children.
column2: 禁止萨达特再生养孩子。

column1: We forbade Thadart to father any more children.
column2: 我们禁止萨达特再生养孩子。

column1: Although at first disturbed by this order, he eventually agreed that it was unfair to bring more children in the world to face a life of insults and mistrust. “I will pin all of my hopes on Palagor,” he said.
column2: 尽管起初被这道命令困扰，但他最终同意，让更多孩子来到这个世界面对侮辱和猜疑是不公平的。“我将把所有希望寄托在帕拉戈尔身上，”他说。

column1: Thadart’s friends, however, were less accepting of the edict of the clan leaders than he was. They loudly suggested that the ring members should be replaced.
column2: 然而，萨达特的朋友们对他的族老命令不如他那样接受。他们大声建议更换环成员。

column1: Quell the peoples’ fears.
column2: 平息人们的恐惧。

column1: Clan leaders sought to quell the peoples’ fears.
column2: 族老们试图平息人们的恐惧。

column1: \x01@N’s soothing words made them less apprehensive, and they gave many generous birth gifts to Thadart and Kistrald.
column2: \x01@N[发言人]的安抚之词减轻了他们的忧虑，他们给萨达特和基斯特拉尔德送了许多丰厚的生育礼。

column1: \x01@N’s words were less soothing than \x06 intended them to be. They served only to heighten the apprehensions of the people, who soon convinced themselves that Thadart’s curse would spread to all children born on our tula.
column2: \x01@N[发言人]的话未能像 \x06 所期望的那样安抚人心。它们反而加剧了人们的忧虑，他们很快说服自己，萨达特的诅咒将蔓延到所有出生在我们领地内的孩子身上。

column1: Conduct a ritual to protect Thadart’s future children from this curse.
column2: 举行一场仪式，保护萨达特未来的孩子免受此诅咒。

column1: We conducted a ritual to protect Thadart’s future children from this curse.
column2: 我们举行了一场仪式，保护萨达特未来的孩子免受此诅咒。

column1: Our god-talkers said that they could not be sure, but that they thought the signs were good.
column2: 我们的神言者说他们不能确定，但他们认为征兆是吉利的。

column1: Our god-talkers said that they could not tell whether the curse had been lifted or not. The only way to know for sure was for Thadart and Kistrald to have another baby.
column2: 我们的神言者说他们无法判断诅咒是否已被解除。唯一确知的办法就是让萨达特和基斯特拉尔德再生一个孩子。

column1: Demand that the people treat them with respect.
column2: 要求人们以尊重对待他们。

column1: Clan leaders demanded that they be treated with respect.
column2: 族老们要求以尊重对待他们。

column1: The people promised to do so, no matter what their fears. To show their good intentions, they gave many generous birth gifts to Thadart and Kistrald.
column2: 人们承诺会照做，无论他们有多恐惧。为表善意，他们给萨达特和基斯特拉尔德送了许多丰厚的生育礼。

column1: People said that the gods did not regard Thadart highly, or they would not have cursed him so. They said we were foolish to try to change their minds about this terrible omen.
column2: 人们说神明并不看重萨达特，否则就不会这样诅咒他。他们说我们试图改变神明对这个凶兆的态度，实属愚蠢。

column1: I would hate to lose a carl who fights as well as Thadart.
column2: 我不愿失去像萨达特这样能征善战的自由民。

column1: A ritual has no chance of succeeding.
column2: 仪式绝无成功的可能。

column1: I find it hard to think of a mythic event which we could ritually reenact in order to lift this curse.
column2: 我觉得很难想出一个我们可以通过仪式重演来解除此诅咒的神话事件。

column1: Not only do I find it hard to think of a mythic event which we could ritually reenact in order to lift this curse, but our magic is weak, as well.
column2: 我不仅觉得很难想出一个我们可以通过仪式重演来解除此诅咒的神话事件，而且我们的魔法也很弱小。

column1: Although I find it hard to think of a mythic event which we could ritually reenact in order to lift this curse, our magic is strong.
column2: 虽然我觉得很难想出一个我们可以通过仪式重演来解除此诅咒的神话事件，但我们的魔法很强大。

column1: We should convince the people that there is nothing to fear.
column2: 我们应该说服人们，没有什么好怕的。

column1: We could outlaw them.
column2: 我们可以将他们逐出氏族。

column1: We could outlaw them, but it would be a very harsh measure.
column2: 我们可以将他们逐出氏族，但那会是非常严厉的措施。

column1: It is somewhat beyond our legal powers, but we could try to forbid him to father any more children.
column2: 这有点超出我们的法定权限，但我们可以尝试禁止他再生养孩子。

column1: The people are afraid. We should quell their fears.
column2: 人们在害怕。我们应该平息他们的恐惧。

column1: We can enhance our reputation for good leadership by acting magnanimously.
column2: 我们可以通过宽宏大量的举动来提升我们善于领导的名声。

column1: Some peoples of Glorantha have suffered curses that have lasted hundreds of years. The trolls, who are cursed to bear only stunted children, come to mind.
column2: 格洛兰萨的一些民族遭受了持续数百年的诅咒。巨魔就是其中之一，他们被诅咒只能生下发育不良的孩子。

column1: If we act like kings, perhaps one day one of us will become a king.
column2: 如果我们像国王一样行事，或许有一天我们中的某人会成为国王。

column1: None of the choices are costly, so I have no objection to any of them.
column2: 这些选择都不昂贵，所以我都不反对。

column1: This is a matter for Thadart and his family, not for the clan ring.
column2: 这是萨达特和他的家人的事，不是氏族议会的事。

column1: “Make boots for none but yourself, or you’ll be kicked when you make a bad one.”
column2: “只给自己做靴子，否则做坏了会被踢。”

column1: Rely on the mercy of the gods.
column2: 信赖众神的仁慈。

column1: I told you the curse would reach down through the generations.
column2: 我告诉过你，诅咒会代代相传。

column1: Thadart and Kistrald have had another child. Like the first child, this one has Thadart’s monstrous visage. The people are most distressed.
column2: 萨达特和基斯特拉尔德又生了一个孩子。和第一个孩子一样，这个孩子也长着萨达特那怪物般的面容。人们非常沮丧。

column1: Thadart and Kistrald have had another child. This one is free of the curse; it does not look like a Tusk Rider. The people are overjoyed that the curse has been lifted.
column2: 萨达特和基斯特拉尔德又生了一个孩子。这个孩子没有受到诅咒，看起来不像獠牙骑手。人们对诅咒解除欣喜若狂。

column1: Patrols spot a massive group of Tusk Riders galloping towards your tula on their giant boar mounts. The people are frightened. Some of them accuse Thadart, the warrior cursed to wear a Tusk Rider’s face, of alerting them to your tula’s location. He scoffs at this accusation. Then he offers to ride out to the Tusk Riders and negotiate with them. “Perhaps I can make some use of this cursed face, and somehow convince them to turn back their assault.”
column2: 巡逻队发现一大群獠牙骑手骑着巨大的野猪坐骑向你们的图拉领地疾驰而来。人们惊恐万分。有些人指责萨达特——那个被诅咒长着獠牙骑手面孔的战士——是他们向獠牙骑手暴露了你们的图拉领地的位置。他对这一指控嗤之以鼻。然后他主动提出骑马去找獠牙骑手谈判。“也许我这张被诅咒的脸能派上用场，说服他们退兵。”

column1: We were raided by an enormous force of Tusk Riders. Some people blamed Thadart, the warrior with the Tusk Rider face, for betraying us to them. Thadart denied this accusation, and offered to ride out to negotiate with the Tusk Riders.
column2: 我们遭到一支庞大的獠牙骑手部队袭击。一些人指责萨达特，那个长着獠牙骑手面孔的战士，说他把我们出卖给了他们。萨达特否认了这一指控，并主动提出骑马去与獠牙骑手谈判。

column1: Immediately charge the incoming raiders.
column2: 立即冲向来袭的袭击者。

column1: We immediately charged the incoming raiders.
column2: 我们立即冲向来袭的袭击者。

column1: Thadart fought as gloriously and courageously as any hero in our legends.
column2: 萨达特战斗得如同我们传说中任何一位英雄般光荣而勇敢。

column1: His courage on the battlefield shamed those who had mistrusted him. Afterwards, Thadart
column2: 他在战场上的勇气让那些曾不信任他的人感到羞耻。此后，萨达特

column1: and his family
column2: 和他的家人

column1: lived with honor and acceptance in our tula.
column2: 在我们的图拉领地上受人尊敬与接纳地生活。

column1: His inspired death shamed those who had mistrusted him and vindicated his
column2: 他那鼓舞人心的死亡让那些不信任他的人感到羞耻，并证明了他的

column1: friends.

column1: Kill Thadart for betraying you to the Tusk Riders.
column2: 杀死萨达特，因为他把你出卖给了獠牙骑手。

column1: We killed Thadart for betraying us to the Tusk Riders.
column2: 我们杀死了萨达特，因为他把我们出卖给了獠牙骑手。

column1: His wife, Kistrald, bitterly denounced us, and said that we had let ourselves be ruled by fear. She was shouted down as we prepared to face the Tusk Rider attack.
column2: 他的妻子基斯特拉尔德痛斥我们，说我们让自己被恐惧支配。在我们准备应对獠牙骑手进攻时，她的声音被压制下去。

column1: After the battle, Thadart’s family went missing. The people were deeply ashamed and saddened, too, when we found that Kistrald had deliberately poisoned herself and her children rather than live among hostile people.
column2: 战斗结束后，萨达特一家失踪了。当我们发现基斯特拉尔德是故意毒死自己和孩子们，宁死也不愿生活在充满敌意的人群中时，人们深感羞愧和悲伤。

column1: After the battle, we realized that we had unfairly blamed Thadart. His friends said the ring had repaid Thadart’s loyalty with death.
column2: 战斗结束后，我们意识到我们冤枉了萨达特。他的朋友们说长老会用死亡回报了萨达特的忠诚。

column1: Let Thadart negotiate with the Tusk Riders.
column2: 让萨达特与獠牙骑手谈判。

column1: We let him do this.
column2: 我们让他这么做了。

column1: Our patrollers watched nervously as Thadart rode out. For a moment, it looked as if the tuskers would ride right over him, but then they stopped, and parleyed. We anxiously looked on as Thadart gestured and snorted at the Tusk Rider leaders, and they gestured and snorted in return.
column2: 我们的巡逻员紧张地看着萨达特骑马而去。有那么一会儿，看起来獠牙骑手们会直接从他身上践踏过去，但随后他们停了下来，开始谈判。我们焦急地旁观，萨达特对獠牙骑手首领打手势、哼叫，他们也用同样方式回应。

column1: Finally they turned away, and the assault was averted. Thadart returned to us, and everyone asked him how he had convinced them to leave.
column2: 最后他们转身离去，进攻被化解了。萨达特回到我们身边，大家都问他如何说服他们离开的。

column1: Abruptly, one of them took his spear and impaled poor Thadart upon it. They laughed as Thadart died, and then rode on towards us.
column2: 突然，其中一个獠牙骑手拿起长矛，刺穿了可怜的萨达特。他们笑着看萨达特死去，然后继续朝我们冲来。

column1: Steel yourselves for the attack.
column2: 做好战斗准备。

column1: We steeled ourselves for the attack.
column2: 我们做好了战斗准备。

column1: Tell Thadart to direct the Tusk Riders to another clan.
column2: 告诉萨达特，让他把獠牙骑手引向另一个氏族。

column1: We told Thadart to direct the Tusk Riders to another clan.
column2: 我们告诉萨达特，让他把獠牙骑手引向另一个氏族。

column1: Kill Thadart! He has betrayed us!
column2: 杀了萨达特！他背叛了我们！

column1: The people are understandably concerned about Thadart’s loyalty.
column2: 人们担心萨达特的忠诚，这可以理解。

column1: Thadart would not betray us.
column2: 萨达特不会背叛我们。

column1: Tusk Riders are cruel and stupid, but if anyone can stay their hand, it would be Thadart.
column2: 獠牙骑手残忍又愚蠢，但如果有人能阻止他们，那一定是萨达特。

column1: This is no time for talking.
column2: 现在不是谈判的时候。

column1: The tuskers are fierce but stupid. If we immediately counterattack, we stand a chance of breaking them into a rout.
column2: 獠牙骑手凶猛但愚蠢。如果我们立即反击，有机会将他们击溃。

column1: We should send them against our enemies in the \x01@u clan.
column2: 我们应该把他们引向 \x01@u 氏族的敌人。

column1: Tusk Riders do not normally gather in such large groups; they hate each other nearly as much as they hate all other peoples.
column2: 獠牙骑手通常不会聚集得如此庞大；他们彼此间的仇恨几乎和仇恨其他所有民族一样深。

column1: Even if Thadart has betrayed us, we must take mercy on his bride and child.
column2: 即使萨达特背叛了我们，我们也必须怜悯他的新娘和孩子。

column1: To think, we all gave generous gifts to this traitor when his son, Palagor, was born!
column2: 想想看，我们都在他的儿子帕拉戈尔出生时送给这个叛徒丰厚的礼物！

column1: I knew Thadart was a traitor when he said that the elves were not our worst enemies.
column2: 当萨达特说精灵不是我们最坏的敌人时，我就知道他是叛徒。

column1: We have been suckling a viper all this time!
column2: 我们一直以来都在喂养一条毒蛇！

column1: One person can make a difference.
column2: 一个人可以带来改变。

column1: The Tusk Riders are somehow bothered by the fact that we formed a tribe.
column2: 獠牙骑手对我们组建了一个部落这件事感到不安。

column1: Thadart cannot be a traitor, for he hates the undead as much as I do!
column2: 萨达特不可能是叛徒，因为他和我一样憎恨亡灵！

column1: If Thadart has betrayed us, that homely bride of his put him up to it.
column2: 如果萨达特背叛了我们，那一定是他那相貌平平的妻子唆使的。

column1: Thadart’s sudden death shamed those who had mistrusted him and saddened his friends.
column2: 萨达特的猝死让那些曾怀疑他的人感到羞愧，也让他的朋友们悲伤。

column1: “I tricked them,” he said.
column2: “我骗了他们，”他说。

column1: “I claimed to be a favored son of their terrible god, and said that my presence here was part of his plan. I told them that he would curse them if they raided us — he would give them the ugly, monstrous faces of humans!”
column2: “我自称是他们可怕的神的宠儿，说我的出现是他的计划的一部分。我告诉他们，如果他们袭击我们，神就会诅咒他们——让他们长出人类丑陋狰狞的面孔！”

column1: Many toasts were made to Thadart that night, as the people rejoiced in their good fortune.
column2: 那天晚上，人们为自己的好运而欢庆，向萨达特敬了许多杯酒。

column2: 哭泣的 \x01@! 氏族家臣将他们的酋长带到你面前，他已死去。

column1: “You have a temple to Chalana Arroy, and thus your priestesses
column2: “你们有查拉娜·阿罗伊的神庙，因此你们的祭司女

column2: “你们的祭司女习得了许多查拉娜·阿罗伊的奥秘，

column1: can on occasion bring the dead back to life. We implore you to do so for our beloved chieftain, laid low by \x02\x08a traitor’s blow/raiders/vengeful minotaurs/sneaky Ducks/a disease sent by the cruel goddess Malia/the trickery of spirits/bad meat/the evil eye\x02.” They offer you fifty cows in exchange for performing this great magic.
column2: “并且有时能让死者复活。我们恳求你们为我们心爱的酋长这样做，他被 \x02\x08叛徒的袭击/劫掠者/复仇的牛头人/鬼祟的鸭人/残酷女神玛利亚降下的疾病/精魂的诡计/变质的肉/邪眼\x02所害。”他们向你们献上五十头牛以换取施展这一伟大魔法。

column1: Ask for higher compensation.
column2: 要求更高的补偿。

column1: We told them that their offer of fifty cows was insufficient.
column2: 我们告诉他们，他们提出的五十头牛不够。

column1: The most they are prepared to offer you is \x01@\x18 cows. Do you accept?
column2: 他们最多愿意提供 \x01@\x18 头牛。你接受吗？

column1: They said they expected more from their allies.
column2: 他们说他们原本期望从盟友那里得到更多。

column1: They said that they had expected nothing from us, as we were foes, and would remain foes until the end of time.
column2: 他们说他们本来就没指望我们，因为我们是敌人，而且直到时间尽头都将是敌人。

column1: They wondered why they were in a tribe, if their tribemates would not help when most needed.
column2: 他们想知道，如果氏族同伴在最需要的时候都不帮忙，那他们为什么还要待在氏族里。

column1: They said that the goddess of mercy might not like to see her services bartered, as if she were a painted lady from a dirty poem. The people were offended by their words.
column2: 他们说仁慈女神不会乐意看到自己的服务被讨价还价，仿佛她是下流诗里涂脂抹粉的荡妇一般。人们被他们的话冒犯了。

column1: Perform the ritual, asking nothing in return.
column2: 举行仪式，不求任何回报。

column1: We said we would perform the resurrection, and would ask nothing in return.
column2: 我们说我们会举行复活仪式，并且不求任何回报。

column1: Perform the ritual in exchange for an alliance between your clans.
column2: 以两个氏族结盟为交换举行仪式。

column1: We said we would perform the ritual in exchange for an alliance between our clans.
column2: 我们说我们会以我们两个氏族结盟为交换举行仪式。

column1: Perform the ritual in exchange for an end to the feud between you.
column2: 以结束你们之间的世仇为交换举行仪式。

column1: We told them we would perform the ritual in exchange for an end to the feud between us.
column2: 我们告诉他们，我们会以结束我们之间的世仇为交换举行仪式。

column1: Finally, they said that they understood. Resurrection is a rare and powerful magic, and is not always available.
column2: 最后，他们表示理解。复活是一种稀有而强大的魔法，并非总能实现。

column1: Cows are better than intangible favors. Take the cows.
column2: 牛比无形的恩惠更好。收下牛吧。

column1: They will pay no more than fifty cows.
column2: 他们最多只会支付五十头牛。

column1: They are in no position to bargain. We can get more from them.
column2: 他们没有讨价还价的余地。我们可以从他们那里得到更多。

column1: They will think highly of the entire clan if we ask nothing in return for the performance of the ritual.
column2: 如果我们不求回报地举行仪式，他们就会高度评价整个氏族。

column1: As our allies, they expect our aid.
column2: 作为我们的盟友，他们期待我们的帮助。

column1: They are our foes, and expect nothing from us.
column2: 他们是我们的敌人，对我们不抱任何期望。

column1: They belong to our tribe. If we disappoint them, they will question the usefulness of tribes.
column2: 他们属于我们的部落。如果我们让他们失望，他们就会质疑部落的作用。

column1: We have no special relationship with them, but their attitude towards us could stand improvement.
column2: 我们与他们没有特殊关系，但他们对我们的态度有待改善。

column1: We have no special relationship with them, but their attitude towards us is already positive. We needn’t make undue sacrifices for them.
column2: 我们与他们没有特殊关系，但他们对我们的态度已经积极。我们不必为他们做出不必要的牺牲。

column1: They are our foes, and expect nothing from us. We could end our feud through a show of generosity.
column2: 他们是我们的敌人，对我们不抱任何期望。我们可以通过展现慷慨来结束世仇。

column1: A ritual of resurrection is rare and expends much mystic energy. If we perform it, our clan magic will take a while to recover.
column2: 复活仪式很稀有，会消耗大量神秘能量。如果我们举行它，氏族魔法将需要一段时间才能恢复。

column1: Our magic is weak, and will remain so for a long time if we perform this ritual, even if it fails — which is more than likely.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱，如果我们举行这个仪式，它将在很长一段时间内保持虚弱，即使它失败了——这很可能会发生。

column1: Our magic is strong now, but if we perform this potent ritual, it will take a while to recover.
column2: 我们的魔法现在很强，但如果我们举行这个强大的仪式，就需要一段时间才能恢复。

column1: Our magic is strong now, but if we perform this potent ritual, it will take a while to recover. Even with strong magic, this difficult ritual is not guaranteed to succeed.
column2: 我们的魔法现在很强，但如果我们举行这个强大的仪式，就需要一段时间才能恢复。即使有强大的魔法，这个艰难的仪式也不能保证成功。

column1: Chalana Arroy went with Orlanth and his companions on the Lightbringers Quest, and helped bring many dead gods back to life.
column2: 查拉娜·阿罗伊与奥兰斯及其同伴一同踏上了光明使者追寻，并帮助让许多死去的神复活。

column1: Our Chalana Arroy temple makes it much more likely that we can succeed with a resurrection.
column2: 我们的查拉娜·阿罗伊神庙大大增加了我们成功复活的可能性。

column1: There is a sharp sword-line between life and death, and it is wrong to violate its sanctity.
column2: 生与死之间有一道锋利的刀锋之线，侵犯它的神圣是不对的。

column1: It is holy to bring the dead back to life, but we must be sure that this chieftain is a deserving candidate.
column2: 让死者复活是神圣的，但我们必须确保这位酋长是值得的人选。

column1: If Ty Kora Tek, goddess of the dead, decides to hang her dusty arms around their chief, there is nothing we can do.
column2: 如果死亡女神泰·科拉·特克决定将她布满灰尘的双臂环绕他们的酋长，那我们便无能为力。

column1: We must agree.
column2: 我们必须同意。

We will give you ten cows if your priests can perform magic which will tell us what the scroll means.”
column2: 满怀期待的领主们从 \x01@! 氏族前来，请求我们兰科·米祭司的帮助。“我们在探索 \x02\x06被混沌生物侵蚀的地下隧道/龙人之地/獠牙骑手的神庙/普拉克斯的干旱平原/塔尔什的奥兰斯王国/巨魔女巫克拉格斯派德的领地\x02时发现了这卷奇怪的卷轴。如果你们的祭司能施展魔法告诉我们卷轴的含义，我们将给你们十头牛。”

column1: Thanes from the \x01@! clan came to ask our Lhankor Mhy priests to magically translate an old scroll they had found.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的领主们前来请求我们兰科·米祭司用魔法翻译他们发现的一卷古卷轴。

column1: We told them that their offer of ten cows was insufficient.
column2: 我们告诉他们，他们提供的十头牛不够。

column1: They increased their offer, and we agreed to perform the necessary rituals.
column2: 他们提高了报酬，我们同意举行必要的仪式。

column1: They would not pay what we wanted, and so we refused them.
column2: 他们不愿支付我们索要的价钱，于是我们拒绝了他们。

column1: They said that the scroll probably contained no useful information anyway, and departed.
column2: 他们说那卷轴反正可能也没什么有用信息，然后就离开了。

column1: They said that the magic was important, but not that important. They departed, looking at us as if we were crazy.
column2: 他们说这魔法很重要，但没那么重要。他们离开了，看我们的眼神像在看疯子。

column1: We told them we would perform the ritual in exchange for an end to the feud between us. They said they might end the feud, if we gave them cows, too.
column2: 我们告诉他们，我们可以举行仪式，但要以结束我们之间的世仇为交换。他们说，如果我们再给他们一些牛，他们可能会考虑结束世仇。

column1: They respond as follows: “This ritual is worth something, but not so much. Perhaps if you give us cows, also, we will end the feud.”
column2: 他们回应如下：“这仪式值点东西，但没那么值。也许你们再给我们一些牛，我们就结束世仇。”

column1: They said they would end the feud.
column2: 他们说他们会结束世仇。

column1: They said that we had not offered enough cows to compensate them for what they would lose if they ended the feud. We asked them what they would lose, and they said, “The pleasure of killing you.” Then they departed, which was good, for by then we were sorely tempted to break the laws of hospitality.
column2: 他们说我们给的牛不够补偿他们结束世仇的损失。我们问他们损失了什么，他们回答：“杀死你们的乐趣。”然后他们离开了，这倒好，因为那时我们正极度想打破好客之道。

column1: We refused them, and they said they would rather feud with us than make peace, anyway. They departed, and we were glad to see them go.
column2: 我们拒绝了他们，他们说反正他们宁愿和我们世仇也不愿和解。他们离开了，我们很高兴看到他们走。

column1: They wondered why they were in a tribe, if their tribemates would not help them even in a trivial matter such as this.
column2: 他们想知道，如果部落同胞连这种小事都不帮忙，他们为什么还要待在这个部落里。

column1: They departed, clearly disappointed.
column2: 他们离开了，显然很失望。

column1: Our priests performed the necessary ritual, and discovered that the scroll contained \x02\tsecrets of the dragonewts/a genealogy of a long-dead family of ducks/instructions for the making of wine/erotic poems/accounting records from an ancient trading concern/a discourse on trollish etiquette/a dwarven work schedule/musical notation for long-forgotten instruments/directions to the location of a great treasure\x02.
column2: 我们的祭司举行了必要的仪式，发现卷轴中记载着 \x02\t龙人的秘密/早已灭绝的鸭人家族的族谱/酿酒指南/情色诗歌/古代商会的账目记录/巨魔礼仪论述/矮人工作排班表/早已失传的乐器的乐谱/通往巨大宝藏所在地的指引\x02。

column1: Our priests performed the necessary ritual, but still could not decipher the contents of the scroll. The \x01@! thanes were displeased.
column2: 我们的祭司举行了必要的仪式，但仍然无法破译卷轴的内容。 \x01@! 领主们很不高兴。

column1: They said that they had wasted the cows they gave us.
column2: 他们说我们浪费了他们给我们的牛。

column1: They said that they would not resume their feud, but that this was not an auspicious beginning to a time of improved relations.
column2: 他们说他们不会重启世仇，但这并不是关系改善的良好开端。

column1: They said that we had great gall, to negotiate a higher price and then fail to translate the document.
column2: 他们说我们胆子不小，谈了个高价却没能翻译出文件。

column1: They will pay no more than they offer.
column2: 他们最多只愿意付这个数。

column1: We can get more from them.
column2: 我们可以从他们那里得到更多。

column1: The service they ask of us is not worth much more than ten cows, but I can get a little more from them.
column2: 他们要求的服务不值十头牛以上，但我可以再从他们那里多榨一点。

column1: They would be indebted to us if we did it as a favor.
column2: 如果我们当作人情去做，他们会欠我们人情。

column1: The ritual they request will reduce the strength of our clan magic.
column2: 他们要求的仪式会削弱我们氏族魔法的力量。

column1: Our magic is weak, and will remain so for some time if we perform this task. In addition, the ritual is likely to fail.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱，如果完成这个任务，它会在一段时间内保持虚弱。此外，仪式很可能会失败。

column1: Our magic is strong now, and we are likely to succeed. Performing the ritual will reduce the strength of our clan magic, however.
column2: 我们的魔法现在很强，我们很可能会成功。然而，举行仪式会削弱我们氏族魔法的力量。

column1: During the Lightbringers Quest, the Knowing God was often called upon to translate cryptic messages for Orlanth and the other companions.
column2: 在光明使者追寻中，全知之神常被召唤来为奥兰斯和其他同伴翻译 cryptic 信息。

column1: If the scroll contains directions to a lost cache of silver, we should tell them it says something different, and then go get the loot ourselves.
column2: 如果卷轴里藏着通往失落白银藏匿处的指引，我们应该告诉他们里面写的是别的东西，然后自己去取那批货。

column1: We must help them, for the scroll surely contains new techniques for fighting the undead.
column2: 我们必须帮助他们，因为卷轴里肯定有对抗亡灵的新技巧。

column1: I told you they’d come to us for help.
column2: 我跟你说过他们会来找我们帮忙。

column1: They are in our tribe; if we make them happy, we strengthen our hold on the throne.
column2: 他们在我们部落里；如果我们让他们满意，就能巩固我们对王座的掌控。

column1: Ask if they have any brides for our eligible males.
column2: 问问他们有没有适婚女性可以配给我们中符合条件的男性。

column1: sceneR430
column2: sceneR430

column1: We told them that their offer of twenty-five cows was insufficient.
column2: 我们告诉他们，他们提供的二十五头牛不够。

column1: He increased his offer, and we agreed to perform a blessing against Chaos.
column2: 他提高了报酬，我们同意举行一次对抗混沌的赐福仪式。

column1: He would not pay what we wanted, and so we refused them.
column2: 他不愿支付我们索要的价钱，于是我们拒绝了他。

column1: Chaos was a threat to all, he protested. He said that others would hear of our selfish behavior.
column2: 他抗议说混沌威胁着所有人。他说其他人会知道我们的自私行为。

column1: We said we would perform the ritual, and would ask nothing in return.
column2: 我们说我们会举行仪式，不要求任何回报。

column1: They praised our dedication in the fight against Chaos.
column2: 他们赞扬了我们在对抗混沌中的奉献精神。

column1: He agreed to this. “When Chaos threatens, people must band together,” he said.
column2: 他同意了这一点。“当混沌威胁时，人们必须团结在一起，”他说。

column1: He agreed to this. “When Chaos threatens, Orlanthi realize who their true enemies are,” he said.
column2: 他同意了这一点。“当混沌威胁时，奥兰斯人会认识到谁才是他们真正的敌人，”他说。

column1: The Storm Bull priests performed the cleansing ritual, and said that Urox had heard their pleas. The Cleansing Wind would scour the \x01@! tula of Chaotic influence.
column2: 风暴之牛祭司举行了净化仪式，并说乌洛克斯听到了他们的祈求。净化之风将扫除 \x01@! 图拉上的混沌影响。

column1: He said that his clan had wasted the cows they gave us.
column2: 他说他的氏族已经浪费了我们给他们的牛只。

column1: He said that his clan would not resume the feud against us, but that this was not an auspicious beginning to a time of improved relations.
column2: 他说他的氏族不会重启对我们的世仇，但这并非改善关系时期的好开端。

column1: He said that Urox was perhaps offended that we had negotiated a higher price than he wanted to pay. But the priests laughed at him, saying that bullying behavior is simply a holy expression of their god’s essence.
column2: 他说乌洛克斯或许因我们谈成了比他愿意支付更高的价钱而恼怒。但祭司们嘲笑他，称欺凌行为不过是对他们神祇本质的神圣表达。

column1: It is fitting that Storm Bull be given cows in exchange for his magic.
column2: 以牛只换取风暴公牛的法术，是合宜的。

column1: If it is fitting that Storm Bull be given cows in exchange for his magic, it is even more fitting that he be given even more cows.
column2: 若以牛只换取风暴公牛的法术是合宜的，那么给他更多的牛只就更合宜了。

column1: We can get more from him.
column2: 我们能从他那里得到更多。

column1: He is in no position to bargain. We can get more.
column2: 他没有讨价还价的余地。我们能得到更多。

column1: Just because our magic fights Chaos does not mean that we are obligated to perform for anyone who sees a broo on his tula.
column2: 仅仅因为我们的法术对抗混沌，并不意味着我们有义务为每一个在图拉领地上看到兽人的人表演。

column1: By building a temple to Urox, we proclaimed to our neighbors that we aimed to fight Chaos. It would be unseemly to withhold our magic now.
column2: 通过建造一座献给乌洛克斯的神庙，我们向邻居宣告了我们旨在对抗混沌。如今若吝啬我们的法术，便不合时宜了。

column1: Our magic is strong now, and we are likely to succeed. Performing the ritual will reduce its strength, however.
column2: 我们的法术如今很强，我们很可能会成功。然而，执行仪式会削弱它的力量。

column1: Urox became the special foe of Chaos, as he was the most affronted by the betrayal of the Brother We Do Not Name.
column2: 乌洛克斯成了混沌的特殊克星，因为他最受无名兄弟背叛的冒犯。

column1: Orlanth fought Chaos, as did all of his tribe. But the most determined foe of Chaos was Urox, also called the Cleansing Wind, also called the Storm Bull.
column2: 奥兰斯曾对抗混沌，他部落的所有成员也是如此。但最坚决对抗混沌的敌人是乌洛克斯，也被称为净化之风，也被称为风暴公牛。

column1: All of these petitions to fight Chaos are distracting us from exploration, and the seeking of magical treasures.
column2: 所有这些请求对抗混沌的请愿，都在分散我们探索与寻求魔法宝物的精力。

column1: They are hostile to the dragonewts. We should refuse them.
column2: 他们对龙人怀有敌意。我们应当拒绝他们。

column1: If we are good to them now, maybe they will make a tribe with us later.
column2: 若我们现在善待他们，也许日后他们会与我们结盟。

column1: The Bull is strong! Chaos bad! Kill Chaos!
column2: 公牛强大！混沌邪恶！杀死混沌！

column1: Weaklings! First we kill their Chaos creatures, then we must raid and take their cows!
column2: 弱者们！先杀掉他们的混沌生物，然后我们必须劫掠并抢走他们的牛只！

column1: They’re feeble, but at least they know who to run to when they’re in trouble.
column2: 他们弱小，但至少他们知道遇到麻烦时该向谁求助。

column1: Chaos creatures must die!
column2: 混沌生物必须死！

column1: Ducks from the Upland Marsh, accompanied by warriors of the \x01@! clan, petition you for aid in their fight against the undead creatures of the marsh. “The ghouls and zombies have grown very strong of late, and it is time something was done about them. We are ready to mount a serious assault on them. We want your devotees of Humakt to enact a ritual at your temple, one which will strengthen our sword-arms and weaken our unliving foes.” They offer you twenty-five cows in exchange for this service.
column2: 来自高地沼泽的鸭人，在 \x01@! 氏族战士的陪同下，向你请愿，请求协助他们对抗沼泽中的亡灵生物。“食尸鬼和僵尸近来变得非常强大，是时候做点事了。我们准备对他们发动一次认真突击。我们希望你们中呼玛克特的虔诚信徒在你们的神庙中举行一个仪式，一个会强化我们剑臂、削弱我们不死敌人的仪式。”他们为此服务提供二十五头牛。

column1: Ducks from the Upland Marsh, accompanied by warriors of the \x01@! clan, petitioned our Humakti devotees for ritual aid in the fight against the undead creatures of the marsh.
column2: 来自高地沼泽的鸭人，在 \x01@! 氏族战士的陪同下，曾向我们呼玛克特的虔诚信徒请愿，请求仪式协助以对抗沼泽中的亡灵生物。

We are ready to mount a serious assault on them. column2: 来自一个他们称为高地沼泽的地方的鸭人，在 \x01@! 氏族战士的陪同下，向你请愿，请求协助他们对抗沼泽中的亡灵生物。“食尸鬼和僵尸近来变得非常强大，是时候做点事了。我们准备对他们发动一次认真突击。我们希望你们中呼玛克特的虔诚信徒在你们的神庙中举行一个仪式，一个会强化我们剑臂、削弱我们不死敌人的仪式。”他们为此服务提供二十五头牛。

column2: 来自一个他们称为高地沼泽的地方的鸭人，在 \x01@! 氏族战士的陪同下，曾向我们呼玛克特的虔诚信徒请愿，请求仪式协助以对抗沼泽中的亡灵生物。

column1: The most they are prepared to offer is \x01@\x18 cows. Do you accept?
column2: 他们准备提供的最高数量是 \x01@\x18 头牛。你接受吗？

column1: They increased their offer, and we agreed to perform the ritual they sought.
column2: 他们提高了出价，我们同意执行他们所需的仪式。

column1: The \x01@! warriors said their people expected more from their allies — especially against such an obvious threat to the welfare of all. Others would hear of our selfish behavior, they said. The ducks told us that we would be known among their kind as short-sighted fools who did not understand the true worship of Humakt. This last remark offended our warriors.
column2: \x01@! 的战士们说，他们的人民对盟友期望更多——尤其是在面对这种对所有生灵福祉的明显威胁时。他们说，其他人会听闻我们自私的行为。鸭人告诉我们，在他们一族中，我们会被称为目光短浅的愚者，不懂得真正的呼玛克特崇拜。最后那句话触怒了我们的战士。

column1: The \x01@! warriors said that even foes should band together when the dead walk the earth. Others would hear of our selfish behavior, they said. The ducks told us that they had not known there was a feud between our clans, but said we should put petty human grudges behind us.
column2: \x01@! 的战士们说，当亡者在世间行走时，即使是仇敌也应联手。他们说，其他人会听闻我们自私的行为。鸭人告诉我们，他们不知道我们氏族间有世仇，但说我们应将人类的小小恩怨抛诸脑后。

column1: The \x01@! warriors said that their people would wonder why they were in a tribe, if their tribemates would not help when most needed. The walking dead were a threat to all, they argued. They said that others would hear of our selfish behavior. The ducks told us that we would be known among their kind as short-sighted fools who did not understand the true worship of Humakt. This last remark offended our warriors.
column2: \x01@! 的战士们说，如果他们部族中的成员在最需要帮助时不愿出手，他们的人民会质疑为何身处这个部族。他们辩称，行尸是对所有人的威胁。他们说，其他人会听闻我们自私的行为。鸭人告诉我们，在我们一族中，我们会被称为目光短浅的愚者，不懂得真正的呼玛克特崇拜。最后那句话触怒了我们的战士。

column1: The undead were a threat to all, protested the warriors of clan \x01@!. They said that others would hear of our selfish behavior. The ducks told us that we would be known among their kind as short-sighted fools who did not understand the true worship of Humakt. This last remark offended our warriors.
column2: 亡灵对所有人都是威胁， \x01@!氏族的战士们抗议道。他们说，其他人会听说我们自私的行为。鸭人告诉我们，在他们的族群中，我们会被视为短视的傻瓜，根本不懂何为对胡马克特的真正崇拜。最后这句话激怒了我们的战士。

column1: The \x01@! thanes agreed to this. “When danger threatens, people must band together,” they said.
column2: 第 \x01@! 位领主同意了此事。“当危险逼近时，人们必须团结起来，”他们说。

column1: They agreed to this. “When the dead walk the earth, Orlanthi realize who their true enemies are,” he said.
column2: 他们同意了此事。“当死者行走于大地时，奥兰西人就会明白谁才是他们真正的敌人，”他说。

column1: Our devotees of Humakt performed the necessary ritual at the appointed time.
column2: 我们供奉胡马克特的信徒在指定时间举行了必要的仪式。

column1: Twenty-five is a goodly number of cows.
column2: 二十五头牛是个不错的数目。

column1: We are lucky they are offering us twenty-five cows; they will pay no more than that.
column2: 我们很幸运他们愿意出二十五头牛；他们不会付更多了。

column1: Our relations with the ducks are good. If we disappointed them in this matter, it wouldn’t be the end of the world.
column2: 我们与鸭人的关系不错。如果在这件事上让他们失望，也不至于天塌下来。

column1: The ducks already have reason to dislike us. And if they say bad things about us to their Beastman allies, we could be in big trouble…
column2: 鸭人已经有理由不喜欢我们了。如果他们向自己的兽人盟友说我们的坏话，我们可能会遇到大麻烦……

column1: Humakt is the foe of the undead, but that does not obligate us to help everyone who sees a ghost on his tula.
column2: 胡马克特是亡灵的敌人，但这并不等于我们必须帮助每个在自己的领地上见到鬼魂的人。

column1: By building a temple to Humakt, we created the expectation that we would willingly fight the undead.
column2: 通过建造胡马克特神庙，我们制造了一种期待：我们会愿意与亡灵作战。

column1: Our magic is strong now, and we are likely to succeed. Performing the ritual will reduce the strength of our magic, however.
column2: 我们的魔法现在很强，成功的可能性很大。然而，举行仪式会削弱我们的魔法力量。

column1: Humakt, the Death God, despises those creatures who blur the line between life and death.
column2: 死亡之神胡马克特鄙视那些模糊生与死界限的造物。

column1: I can see why we should help, but I don’t think the zombies will threaten our clan.
column2: 我能理解为什么我们应该帮忙，但我不觉得那些僵尸会威胁到我们的氏族。

column1: “He who hovers over the feast is feathered.”
column2: “徘徊于盛宴之上者，羽毛加身。”

column1: We should ask for fifty cows, for our participation in this action means that success is certain.
column2: 我们应该要五十头牛，因为我们参与这次行动就意味着成功必然到手。

column1: We should do this for nothing! By Humakt’s blade, we should have thought of it before they did!
column2: 我们应该分文不取地做这件事！以胡马克特之剑起誓，我们本该在他们想到之前就想到！

column1: Mere shades and will-o-wisps are no threat to us. It is the elves we should be worried about.
column2: 区区幽影和鬼火对我们构不成威胁。我们该担心的是精灵。

column1: This is a manly plan, and we should assist them.
column2: 这是个充满男子气概的计划，我们应该协助他们。

column1: Determined were the hilt-thanes to slay the corpse-men.
column2: 剑柄领主们决心击杀那些尸人。

column1: The ducks do us a great favor by fighting the undead. We must support them.
column2: 鸭人与亡灵作战是帮了我们大忙。我们必须支持他们。

column1: We do not have to be paid to perform a holy act.
column2: 行神圣之事不一定要收报酬。

column1: This time the zombies are strong. I can feel it.
column2: 这次僵尸很强。我能感觉到。

column1: give you ten cows for this service.”
