column1: Despite the beating we gave him,
column2: 尽管我们揍了他一顿，

column1: We told him that his offer of ten cows was insufficient.
column2: 我们告诉他，他出的十头牛不够。

column1: He would not pay what we wanted, and so we refused him.
column2: 他不肯付我们想要的价格，于是我们拒绝了他。

column1: “The people of my clan will know how you hoard your trickster powers to yourselves!” he promised.
column2: “我氏族的人民会知道你们是如何把诡术力量藏起来独享的！”他保证道。

column1: Ten cows is not a number to get excited over.
column2: 十头牛不是什么值得激动的数目。

column1: We need all the cows we can get. We should dicker with him, but do not refuse him, even if his offer does not increase much.
column2: 我们需要搞到所有能搞到的牛。我们应该跟他讨价还价，但不要拒绝他，哪怕他的出价提高不了多少。

column1: It is unlawful to engage in such trickery.
column2: 参与这种诡诈之事是不合法的。

column1: By putting an Eurmali on the ring, we created the expectation that we would spread trickery and confusion throughout Dragon Pass.
column2: 通过在氏族议会中安排一位尤尔马尔教徒，我们制造了一种期待：我们会在整个龙之隘口散播诡诈与混乱。

column1: By putting an Eurmali on the ring, we created the expectation that we would spread trickery and confusion throughout Dragon Pass. But we can trick people by confounding this expectation.
column2: 通过在氏族议会中安排一位尤尔马尔教徒，我们制造了一种期待：我们会在整个龙之隘口散播诡诈与混乱。但我们也可以通过违逆这种期待来欺骗别人。

column1: Our magic is weak, and the ritual is likely to fail.
column2: 我们的魔法很弱，仪式很可能会失败。

column1: Our magic is strong now, and we are likely to succeed.
column2: 我们的魔法现在很强，成功的可能性很大。

column1: Our magic is strong now, and we are likely to succeed. But the \x01@a priests will know what we have done.
column2: 我们的魔法现在很强，成功的可能性很大。但第 \x01@a 位祭司会知道我们做了什么。

column1: Eurmal is the god of trickery and confusion. He often betrayed Orlanth and his companions, but sometimes this worked to their benefit, when all was said and done.
column2: 尤尔马尔是诡诈与混乱之神。他经常背叛奥兰斯及其同伴，但有时候，到头来这对他们反而有益。

column1: Let me beat him again with my magic Eurmal stick!
column2: 让我再用我的魔法尤尔马尔棍子揍他一顿！

column1: Of course we should aid this admirable fellow.
column2: 我们当然应该帮助这位可敬的伙计。

column1: Get more from him.
column2: 从他那里多要点。

column1: Our devotees of Eurmal performed the ritual of trickery.
column2: 我们供奉尤尔马尔的信徒举行了诡诈仪式。

column1: \x01Bs, who had made trouble in the past, was there to complain again. She said that the ring was very foolish, and that its members should step down.
column2: \x01Bs那位过去就惹过麻烦的人又来了，再次抱怨。她说长老会非常愚蠢，成员们应该下台。

column1: The carls warned the clan ring again that there were too many people, and they still could not produce enough food for everyone.
column2: 自由民再次提醒氏族议会，人太多了，他们仍然无法为所有人生产足够的食物。

column1: Your carls come together to warn the clan ring that your tula cannot support its population. “There are too many people now.
column2: 你们的自由民聚集起来，警告氏族议会说你们的领地供养不了那么多人口。“现在人太多了。

column1: We can’t produce enough food for everyone. We could trade for more food, but soon we would be in the same fix again.
column2: 我们无法为所有人生产足够的食物。我们可以贸易换取更多食物，但很快又会陷入同样的困境。

column1: Right now, we have enough food, but we can’t keep producing enough.
column2: 眼下我们有足够的食物，但无法持续生产足够的分量。

column1: People will starve if we don’t do something.” Some of them suggest that about a quarter of the clan should split off, and go off to seek a new tula of their own. Others say you should seize land from a neighbor.
column2: 如果不想办法，就会有人饿死。”其中一些人建议大约四分之一的氏族分出去，去寻找属于自己的新领地。另一些人说你们应该从邻居那里夺取土地。

column1: The carls warned the clan ring that there were too many people, and they could not produce enough food for everyone.
column2: 自由民警告氏族议会说，人太多了，他们无法为所有人生产足够的食物。

column1: Seek volunteers to split off.
column2: 寻找志愿者分出去。

column1: We sought volunteers to split off.
column2: 我们找了志愿者分出去。

column1: Most were reluctant to step forward, but everyone knew that a split in the clan was necessary for survival. Eventually a quarter of our families stepped forward. They left for an unsettled part of Dragon Pass, taking food, livestock and goods with them.
column2: 多数人不愿站出来，但人人都知道氏族分裂是生存所必需。最终，四分之一的家庭站了出来。他们带着食物、牲畜和货物，前往龙隘荒野之地。

column1: Split from us
column2: 与我们分裂

column1: We heard later that they were calling themselves the \x01@! clan.
column2: 我们后来听说，他们自称为 \x01@! 氏族。

column1: Choose the worst troublemakers to split off.
column2: 选出最恶劣的捣乱者，让他们分裂出去。

column1: Our clan leaders picked those families who made the most trouble for them, and told them to leave.
column2: 氏族首领挑选了给他们制造最多麻烦的家庭，命令他们离开。

column1: They were angry and complained a lot, but those who were staying were glad to be rid of them. They left for an unsettled part of Dragon Pass, taking their share of food, livestock and goods with them. As they were the laziest of us, their share was not as great as it might otherwise have been. People said that they would have a hard time of it, now that they had to shift for themselves.
column2: 他们怒气冲冲，抱怨不已，但留下的人很高兴摆脱了他们。他们带着自己那份食物、牲畜和货物，前往龙隘的荒野。由于他们是族中最懒惰之流，所得份额并不丰厚。人们说，如今他们得自谋生路，日子怕不好过。

column1: \x01Bs was among those who left, and those who stayed behind were glad to see the back of her.
column2: \x01Bs 是离开者之一，留下的人乐得见她背影。

column1: Choose those best equipped to survive if they split off.
column2: 选出那些生存能力最强的家庭，让他们分裂出去。

column1: Our clan leaders picked those families best equipped to survive.
column2: 氏族首领挑选了那些最具备生存能力的家庭。

column1: They were the wealthiest families, on the whole, and those who remained worried that it would be harder to get along without them. They left for an unsettled part of Dragon Pass, taking their share of clan wealth with them. Although one in four of us left, they took more than one in four of our cattle, and more than a quarter of our goods, because they had worked hard for it. People said that they would prosper wherever they settled.
column2: 总体而言，他们是族中最富裕的家庭，留下的人担心少了他们会更难过。他们带着氏族财富中自己的那份，前往龙隘的荒野。虽然我们四中去一，他们却带走了超过四分之一的牛和超过四分之一的货物，因为那是他们辛苦挣来的。人们说，他们无论在何处扎根都会兴旺。

column1: Delay action by trading for more food.
column2: 通过交易更多食物来拖延行动。

column1: Clan leaders decided to delay action by trading for more food.
column2: 氏族首领决定通过交易更多食物来拖延行动。

column1: The carls complained that delay would accomplish nothing, but that we had better hurry and send the trading missions.
column2: 自由民抱怨拖延无济于事，但我们最好尽快派出贸易队伍。

column1: Seize land from a neighbor.
column2: 从邻族夺取土地。

column1: Which neighbor?
column2: 哪个邻族？

column1: We chose to seize land from the neighboring \x01@! clan.
column2: 我们选择从邻族 \x01@! 氏族手中夺取土地。

column1: The carls muttered darkly that this had not worked before.
column2: 自由民阴沉地嘀咕，说这招以前就不奏效。

column1: The people were glad, and spread out to occupy this land, ours by right of conquest.
column2: 人们欢欣鼓舞，四散占领这片征服得来的土地。

column1: We beat them, but they were determined foes and refused to leave their land.
column2: 我们击败了他们，但他们是顽敌，拒绝离开自己的土地。

column1: The people were dispirited, for we were no closer to solving our problem.
column2: 人们士气低落，因为问题依然毫无解决迹象。

column1: The people were displeased that we had the opportunity to seize land, but chose not to.
column2: 人们不满，因为我们有机会夺取土地却放弃了。

column1: The people were displeased, for we had lost, and were no closer to solving our problem.
column2: 人们心怀不满，因为我们战败，且问题毫无进展。

column1: Anyone could see this coming. There are too many farmers, and we will have to split the clan.
column2: 谁都料到了。农夫太多，我们不得不分裂氏族。

column1: This should not be a surprise. There are too many farmers, and we will have to split the clan. If not today, soon.
column2: 这不足为奇。农夫太多，我们不得不分裂氏族。不是今天，就是不久。

column1: If a quarter of our people go, they will take a quarter of our cows with them.
column2: 如果四分之一的人口离开，他们会带走四分之一的牛只。

column1: The worst troublemakers have the fewest cows, so sending them away will impoverish us the least.
column2: 最恶劣的捣乱者牛最少，所以送走他们对我们的损失最小。

column1: If we trade for more food, maybe something will happen in the interim, so that our clan does not have to split.
column2: 如果我们交易更多食物，或许期间会发生什么，让氏族不必分裂。

column1: Those best equipped to survive are the wealthiest families. They will take more than a quarter of the livestock, food and goods if they go.
column2: 最具备生存能力的是最富裕的家庭。他们若离开，会带走超过四分之一的牲畜、食物和货物。

column1: If we send the wealthiest families, they will take more than a quarter of our livestock, food and goods. If we send the troublemakers, they may not have enough to survive with and their kin will fear for them.
column2: 如果送走最富裕的家庭，他们会带走超过四分之一的牲畜、食物和货物。如果送走捣乱者，他们可能不足以维生，亲属会为他们担忧。

column1: If we ask for volunteers then there will be no ill-will about who goes and who stays.
column2: 如果我们征求志愿者，就不会因谁走谁留而结怨。

column1: We should raid the \x01@! clan.
column2: 我们应该突袭 \x01@! 氏族。

column1: We should raid the \x01@a clan.
column2: 我们应该突袭 \x01@a 氏族。

column1: We should raid the \x01@u clan.
column2: 我们应该突袭 \x01@u 氏族。

column1: If we keep raiding and failing to gain land, we could lose enough people that we don’t have to split up after all.
column2: 如果我们持续突袭却未能夺取土地，可能会损失足够多的人口，最终反而不必分裂。

column1: Orlanthi clans split up every few generations. We split off from our old clan in Heortland.
column2: 奥兰色氏族每隔几代人就会分裂。我们就是从赫奥特兰的旧氏族分裂出来的。

column1: This is not at all unusual. Orlanthi clans split up every few generations. We split off from our old clan in Heortland.
column2: 这毫不稀奇。奥兰色氏族每隔几代人就会分裂。我们就是从赫奥特兰的旧氏族分裂出来的。

column1: If we seek volunteers, our reputation for leadership will be undimmed.
column2: 如果我们寻求志愿者，我们领导力的声誉将不受影响。

column1: If we get rid of the worst troublemakers, the mood of those who remain will improve, but our reputation for generosity will be diminished.
column2: 如果我们除掉最恶劣的捣乱者，留下的人情绪会好转，但我们慷慨的名声会受损。

column1: If we make the new clan from those best equipped to survive, the people who remain will be nervous, but our reputation for good leadership will increase.
column2: 如果我们用最具备生存能力的人组建新氏族，留下的人会紧张不安，但我们领导有方的名声会提升。

column1: We must split up. If we send the discontented families off, the ones who stay behind will be free from their griping.
column2: 我们必须分裂。如果送走心怀不满的家庭，留下的人将免受他们的怨言。

column1: Trading for food is just delaying a decision. Trying to seize land is just making our problem someone else’s. A clan split is the best way.
column2: 交易食物只是拖延决定。夺取土地不过是将我们的问题转嫁他人。氏族分裂才是上策。

column1: Spirits would be higher if we sent off those who are unhappiest here.
column2: 如果送走那些在此最不快乐的人，士气会更高。

column1: Raiding for land is very risky, and will ruin our chances at planting enough food to see us through another year.
column2: 为土地突袭风险极大，会毁掉我们播种足够食物以度来年的机会。

column1: Raiding for land is very risky, and will ruin our work of harvesting the crops we need to see us through another year.
column2: 为土地突袭风险极大，会毁掉我们收割所需作物以度来年的劳作。

column1: If the new clan is less than a quarter of the size of ours, it has no chance of survival.
column2: 如果新氏族规模不足我们四分之一，它便没有生存机会。

column1: If the new clan takes too much of our wealth, our own survival will be difficult.
column2: 如果新氏族带走我们太多财富，我们自己的生存将变得困难。

column1: When Bad King Urgrain had to split up his clan, he sundered families and picked people at random. His people were so enraged that they all left him at once.
column2: 当恶王乌格兰不得不分裂他的氏族时，他拆散家庭，随意挑选人手。他的子民极为愤怒，立刻全部离他而去。

column1: We must send those most capable of defending their new steads.
column2: 我们必须派遣那些最能保卫新农庄的人。

column1: I told you we had too many people.
column2: 我告诉过你我们人太多了。

column1: I told you that attacking our neighbors was a foolish idea.
column2: 我告诉过你攻击邻族是个愚蠢的主意。

column1: We should get rid of those least likely to learn to read.
column2: 我们应该摆脱那些最不可能学会读写的人。

column1: “If you visit a home too late, the ale will be drunk. If you go too early, it will still be unbrewed.”
column2: “若你拜访得太晚，麦酒已被人喝尽。若你到得太早，酒还未酿成。”

column1: “The mouse hides its head when a shadow passes, but the hawk sees the mouse anyway.”
column2: “阴影掠过时老鼠藏起脑袋，但鹰隼终究还是看见了它。”

column1: Our neighbors will band together to fight us if we try to seize land from one of them.
column2: 如果我们试图从某个邻族夺取土地，他们就会联合起来对抗我们。

column1: I should have seen this coming. I’m \x02\x03stupid — stupid — stupid/dumb — dumb — dumb/an idiot — a pure idiot\x02!
column2: 我早该料到会这样。我 \x02\x03愚蠢——愚蠢——愚蠢/迟钝——迟钝——迟钝/一个白痴——一个彻头彻尾的白痴\x02！

column1: The farmers want more land, but the problem goes beyond that.
column2: 农夫们想要更多土地，但问题不止于此。

column1: \x01Bs, who had made trouble in the past, adds to the chorus of complaints. She says that the ring is very foolish, and that its members should step down.
column2: \x01Bs此人过去曾制造麻烦，如今又加入了抱怨的合唱。她说长老会非常愚蠢，其成员应当下台。

column1: The warriors again warned the clan ring that many of the great and ancient families of the clan were not getting their due representation in the clan hall.
column2: 战士们再次警告氏族议会，氏族中许多古老而伟大的家族在部族大厅中未获得应有的代表权。

column1: Your warriors come together to complain that not all of the great and ancient families of the clan are getting their due in the clan hall. They say that many bloodlines are unrepresented on the clan ring. “Why should we obey the ring, when our kin are not on it. No one can make us do anything, and unless our families are properly respected, we do not wish to do what you say.” Other people, whose families are represented on the ring, say that the clan is ungovernable because it has grown too large. They suggest that about a quarter of the clan should split off, and seek a new tula of their own.
column2: 你的战士们聚在一起抱怨，并非所有古老伟大的氏族家族都在部族大厅得到应有的待遇。他们说许多血脉在氏族议会中没有代表。“既然我们的亲族不在议会中，我们为何要服从议会？没有人能强迫我们做任何事，除非我们的家族得到应有的尊重，否则我们不愿听从你们的话。”另一些家族在议会有代表的人则表示，氏族已变得过于庞大，难以治理。他们建议大约四分之一的氏族应分裂出去，寻找属于他们自己的新图拉领地。

column1: \x01Bs, who had made trouble in the past, added to the chorus of complaints. She said that the ring was very foolish, and that its members should step down.
column2: \x01Bs此人过去曾制造麻烦，又加入了抱怨的合唱。她说长老会非常愚蠢，其成员应当下台。

column1: The warriors warned the clan ring that many of the great and ancient families of the clan were not getting their due representation in the clan hall.
column2: 战士们警告氏族议会，氏族中许多古老而伟大的家族在部族大厅中未获得应有的代表权。

column1: Most were reluctant to step forward, but everyone knew that a split in the clan was necessary for survival. Eventually a quarter of our families stepped forward.
column2: 大多数人犹豫不前，但人人都知道，为了生存，氏族分裂是必要的。最终，我们四分之一的家族站了出来。

column1: Do you split off your own tula, and give the new clan some of your land?
column2: 你是否分裂出自己的图拉领地，并给予新氏族一些你的土地？

column1: We split off our own tula, giving them some of our land.
column2: 我们分裂出自己的图拉领地，给了他们一些我们的土地。

column1: We would not split off our tula, so they had to find a new place to live.
column2: 我们不愿分裂图拉领地，所以他们不得不另寻居处。

column1: They said that we were wanting in generosity. They left to look for empty land, where they could make a new home.
column2: 他们说我们缺乏慷慨。他们离去寻找无主的土地，在那里建立新家园。

column1: They left for the north, where they would seek out a home. We heard later that they were calling themselves the \x01@! clan.
column2: 他们向北而去，寻找安身之所。我们后来听说，他们自称为 \x01@! 氏族。

column1: They were angry and complained a lot, but those who were staying were glad to be rid of them. They prepared to leave, assembling their share of food, livestock and goods for the journey. As they were the laziest of us, their share was not as great as it might otherwise have been. People said that they would have a hard time of it, now that they had to shift for themselves.
column2: 他们愤怒不已，抱怨连连，但留下的人庆幸能摆脱他们。他们准备离开，汇集他们那份食物、牲畜和物品以供旅途之需。由于他们是我们中最懒惰的人，他们所分得的不如本该有的那么多。人们说，现在他们不得不自谋生路，日子会很难熬。

column1: They said that we were wanting in generosity. They left for the north, where they would seek out a home.
column2: 他们说我们缺乏慷慨。他们向北而去，寻找安身之所。

column1: They were the wealthiest families, on the whole, and those who remained worried that it would be harder to get along without them. Although one in four of us prepared to go, they were entitled to more than one in four of our cattle, and more than a quarter of our goods, because they had worked hard for it. People said that they would prosper wherever they settled.
column2: 总体而言，他们是最富有的家族，留下的人担心没有他们会更难维持。尽管我们中四分之一的人准备离开，但他们有权获得超过四分之一的牛群和超过四分之一的货物，因为他们为此辛苦劳作。人们说，无论他们在哪里定居，都会兴旺发达。

column1: Give gifts to the complainants.
column2: 向抱怨者赠送礼物。

column1: Our clan leaders decided to delay action by giving gifts to the complainants.
column2: 我们的氏族领袖决定通过向抱怨者赠送礼物来拖延行动。

column1: But new complainers took their place.
column2: 但新的抱怨者取代了他们。

column1: People who were not complaining suddenly felt slighted, and loudly voiced their discontent with the clan ring. They agreed with the warriors: splitting the clan was inevitable.
column2: 原本没有抱怨的人突然感到受怠慢，大声表达对氏族议会的不满。他们赞同战士们：分裂氏族已是不可避免。

column1: The people who were not complaining suddenly felt slighted, and loudly voiced their discontent.
column2: 原本没有抱怨的人突然感到受怠慢，大声表达他们的不满。

column1: Reorganize the ring.
column2: 重组长老会。

column1: Ring members stepped down, and allowed others to take their places.
column2: 长老会成员退位，让其他人接替他们的位置。

column1: The complainants were mollified, although some worried that the underlying problem had not been solved; the clan was still too big. Soon, they fretted, people whose bloodlines were now unrepresented on the ring would be making the same kind of trouble.
column2: 抱怨者被安抚了，尽管有些人担心根本问题并未解决；氏族仍然太大了。他们担心，很快那些血脉如今在长老会上没有代表的人会制造同样的麻烦。

column1: The complainants were mollified, but the people whose bloodlines were now unrepresented on the ring were angry, and said that we had not removed the insult, but merely moved it around.
column2: 抱怨者被安抚了，但那些血脉如今在长老会上没有代表的人却很愤怒，说我们并未消除侮辱，只是把侮辱挪了地方。

column1: No sensible person scorns a gift.
column2: 明智之人不会轻视礼物。

column1: No sensible person scorns a gift. But gifts won’t settle all our woes here, either.
column2: 没有理智之人会轻蔑礼物。但礼物也无法解决我们这里的所有苦难。

column1: A great rule of our society, one laid down by Orlanth’s father, says that no one can make you do anything.
column2: 我们社会的一条伟大准则——由奥兰斯之父所立——规定，无人能强迫你做任何事。

column1: They are right. Our clan has grown too large, and will be impossible to govern unless we split off some of the bloodlines.
column2: 他们说得对。我们氏族已经变得过于庞大，除非分出部分血脉，否则将无法治理。

column1: Reorganizing the ring will afford only temporary relief. Giving gifts to some will only provoke resentment in others.
column2: 重组长老会只能带来短暂缓解。给某些人送礼只会激起其他人的怨恨。

column1: If our clan were a failure, we would not have this problem! But this is what happens when your clan grows.
column2: 如果我们氏族是个失败者，就不会有这个问题！但这就是你的氏族壮大时会发生的事。

column1: We must stop stalling, and gather heart to do what must be done.
column2: 我们必须停止拖延，鼓起勇气去做该做的事。

column1: If we send the troublemakers away, soon they will be our enemies.
column2: 如果我们把惹事者送走，他们很快就会成为我们的敌人。

column1: Reorganizing the ring is just delaying a decision. Gifts won’t solve the problem. A clan split is the best way.
column2: 重组长老会只是在拖延决定。礼物解决不了问题。分族是最好的办法。

column1: We have more land than we need. We could split our tula, and let the new clan settle on the remainder.
column2: 我们的土地比所需多得多。我们可以分割我们的图拉领地，让新氏族定居在剩余土地上。

column1: With so much land, we could split our tula, and the new clan could settle somewhat near to their kin and their friends.
column2: 拥有这么多土地，我们可以分割我们的领地，而新氏族可以定居在距离其亲族和朋友不远的地方。

column1: The more ring members who step down, the greater chance we have of satisfying the complainants.
column2: 辞职的长老会成员越多，我们满足抱怨者的机会就越大。

column1: We can’t just rearrange the ring all the time.
column2: 我们不能一直重新安排长老会。

column1: Those who were unhappy to begin with are even more surly now. Let them go.
column2: 那些从一开始就不满的人现在更加乖戾了。让他们走吧。

column1: Send troublemakers.
column2: 送走惹事者。

column1: Send the most godly of our people, for they will have the strong magic necessary to survive.
column2: 送走我们中最虔诚的人，因为他们拥有生存所需的强大魔法。

column1: Send those best equipped to defend themselves.
column2: 送走那些最能自卫的人。

column1: Send the troublemakers. They are mostly quarrelsome women and hen-pecked men, anyway. Good riddance, I say!
column2: 送走惹事者。反正他们大多是爱争吵的女人和被妻子管束的男人。我说，摆脱得好！

column1: Quiet them with gifts. We need every last person to help fight the undead.
column2: 用礼物安抚他们。我们需要每个人来对抗亡灵。

column1: A thane of the \x01@! clan sought to hire our Humakti warriors as mercenaries; they wanted us to hurt the elders of the \x01@a clan.
column2: \x01@! 氏族的一位领主试图雇佣我们的胡马克特战士作为雇佣兵；他们想让我们伤害 \x01@a 氏族的首领们。

column1: Agree to their terms.
column2: 同意他们的条件。

column1: We agreed to their terms.
column2: 我们同意了他们的条件。

column1: We told them that their offer of five cows for each \x01@a leader wounded was insufficient.
column2: 我们告诉他们，对于每名受伤的 \x01@a 首领，五头牛的出价不够。

column1: They increased their offer, and we agreed to strike at their \x01@a foes.
column2: 他们提高了出价，我们同意攻击他们的 \x01@a 敌人。

column1: We decided not to send our warriors to do another clan’s dirty work.
column2: 我们决定不派出我们的战士去干其他氏族的脏活。

column1: They said that they expected more from their allies.
column2: 他们说，他们对盟友的期望不止于此。

column1: Do as they ask, seeking nothing in return.
column2: 按照他们的要求去做，不求回报。

column1: We said we would strike at their \x01@a foes, and would ask nothing in return.
column2: 我们说我们会攻击他们的 \x01@a 敌人，且不要求任何回报。

column1: Their praise for this display of friendship was effusive.
column2: 他们对这种友谊的展示赞不绝口。

column1: They were disappointed, but said that we were within our rights to refuse them.
column2: 他们很失望，但说我们有权拒绝他们。

column1: \x01@\x05 led our mercenaries to triumph; we wounded \x01@\x11 of the \x01@a leaders.
column2: \x01@\x05 带领我们的雇佣兵取得胜利；我们击伤了 \x01@a 首领中的 \x01@\x11 人。

column1: The \x01@a clan blamed the \x01@! clan for seeking our mercenary services, and raided them in reprisal.
column2: \x01@a 氏族指责 \x01@! 氏族寻求我们的雇佣兵服务，并为此袭击了他们作为报复。

column1: Some of them were wounded.
column2: 他们中的一些人受了伤。

column1: All of them were wounded.
column2: 他们中的所有人都受了伤。

column1: As Ernalda said when Uralda led the four-legged people into the steads of the two-legged people, “Cows will never be unwelcome here.”
column2: 正如厄纳尔达在乌拉尔达带领四足生灵进入两足生灵的农庄时所说：“牛群在这里永远不会不受欢迎。”

column1: We have many cows, but more are always welcome.
column2: 我们有很多牛，但更多的牛总是受欢迎的。

column1: Let me bargain with them; I can drive their price up.
column2: 让我与他们讨价还价；我能把他们的价码抬上去。

column1: We cannot shirk our holy responsibility to make death throughout Dragon Pass.
column2: 我们不能逃避在龙之隘口制造死亡的圣洁职责。

column1: We can easily beat them, bringing cheer to our warriors.
column2: 我们可以轻易击败他们，让我们的战士欢欣鼓舞。

column1: The \x01@a clan are stronger than we are. We should not attack now, but rather build up our strength, to be worthy of our affiliation with Humakt.
column2: \x01@a 氏族比我们强大。我们现在不应该进攻，而应该积攒力量，配得上与胡马克特的联系。

column1: Humakt is the Maker of Death, but that does not obligate us to help kill everyone in sight.
column2: 胡马克特是死亡制造者，但这并不迫使我们帮助杀死见到的每个人。

column1: They ask us to attack our allies. It is out of the question; in fact, we must warn our friends.
column2: 他们要求我们攻击我们的盟友。这绝不可能；事实上，我们必须警告我们的朋友。

column1: They are our foes, yet expect us to attack their other foes? We should help their enemies, instead!
column2: 他们是我们的敌人，却期望我们去攻击他们的其他敌人？我们应该去帮助他们的敌人！

column1: Neither clan is especially friendly or especially hostile to us. It matters not to me what we do.
column2: 两个氏族都既不特别友好也不特别敌对。我不在乎我们怎么做。

column1: We should support our tribemates, and do this for nothing.
column2: 我们应该支持我们的部落同胞，无偿做这件事。

column1: We should support our tribemates, and warn them of their enemy’s hostile intent.
column2: 我们应该支持我们的部落同胞，并警告他们敌人有敌对意图。

column1: Why couldn’t they ask us during Fire season? Or Storm season? Why must their request interfere with our planting?
column2: 为什么他们不能在火之季问我们？或者风暴季？为什么他们的请求必须干扰我们的播种？

column1: Why couldn’t they ask us during Fire season? Or Storm season? Why must their request interfere with our harvest?
column2: 为什么他们不能在火之季问我们？或者风暴季？为什么他们的请求必须干扰我们的收割？

column1: It’s all very well to fight for Humakt, but not against our own allies!
column2: 为胡马克特而战很好，但不能反对我们自己的盟友！

column1: Every clan has, in addition to its formal ring, an informal Outer Ring made up of twenty or so wise folk. It is these people our Humakti warriors are meant to wound.
column2: 每个氏族除了正式的长老会之外，还有一个由大约二十位智者组成的非正式外环议会。我们的胡马克特战士要伤害的就是这些人。

column1: They honor Humakt with their request; we must do as they ask, and accept nothing in return.
column2: 他们以这个请求来尊崇胡马克特；我们必须按他们说的做，不接受任何回报。

column1: It is not only Humakt who can strike against the foes of our friends. Proud, red Vinga can do so, also!
column2: 并非只有胡马克特能攻击我们朋友的敌人。骄傲的红文加也能做到！

column1: A king employs mercenaries, but is not mercenary himself.
column2: 国王雇佣雇佣兵，但他本人并非雇佣兵。

column1: Many elders of the \x01@! can read, so we should support them.
column2: \x01@! 的许多首领能识字，所以我们应当支持他们。

column1: Just because we have a temple to Humakt doesn’t mean we should always be risking our hides, does it?
column2: 虽然我们有座胡马克特神庙，但也不代表我们总得拿命去冒险，对吧？

column1: What joke is this, that a clan outside our tribe asks us for aid to harm a tribe-mate?
column2: 这是什么笑话？族外一个氏族竟来求我们帮忙伤害同族之人？

column1: Neither clan is under our wing, we can make what profit we want.
column2: 两个氏族都不受我们庇护，我们想赚多少就赚多少。

column1: I cannot encourage the clans in the tribe to have-at each other. We have enough enemies outside, we don’t need to hurt ourselves, too.
column2: 我不能纵容族内氏族互相攻击。外面的敌人已经够多了，我们不能再自相残杀。

column1: Compensate him, but give less than he asks.
column2: 赔偿他，但给得比他要求的少。

column1: We gave him less than he asked.
column2: 我们给了他少于他要求的。

column1: But our own Humakti warriors were most dissatisfied with this outcome. They said that it was wrong to give him anything; we had dishonored them by falsely admitting that what they had done was wrong.
column2: 但我们自己的胡马克特战士对这个结果极为不满。他们说给他任何东西都不对；我们错误地承认他们做错了，从而羞辱了他们。

column1: Give him what he asks.
column2: 给他他要求的。

column1: We gave him what he asked.
column2: 我们给了他他所要求的。

column1: The warriors of Humakt were most dissatisfied with this outcome; they said that we dishonored them by falsely admitting that what they had done was wrong.
column2: 胡马克特的战士们对这个结果极为不满；他们说我们错误地承认他们做错了，从而羞辱了他们。

column1: Propose that the matter be adjudicated by a neutral juror.
column2: 提议由中立的裁决者来裁定此事。

column1: We said that the matter should be adjudicated by a neutral juror.
column2: 我们说此事应由中立的裁决者来裁定。

column1: Propose to take the matter before a tribal moot.
column2: 提议将此事提交部落大会。

column1: We said he should take the matter before a tribal moot.
column2: 我们说应将此事提交部落大会。

column1: He was angry, and promised to take the matter before a tribal moot. Before long, moot day was upon us.
column2: 他愤怒了，并承诺要将此事提交部落大会。不久，大会之日来临。

column1: Our people were jubilant that we had been vindicated.
column2: 我们的人民因我们被证明清白而欢欣鼓舞。

column1: This is a warrior problem; it should not cost us cows.
column2: 这是战士的问题，不该让我们损失牛只。

column1: We can’t afford to give him what he wants.
column2: 我们给不起他想要的东西。

column1: We have many cows; let us get rid of this nuisance.
column2: 我们牛多，干脆打发走这个麻烦吧。

column1: He will not be satisfied by any lesser amount.
column2: 给少了他是不会满意的。

column1: He will be displeased if we offer him less, but he will take it.
column2: 如果我们给少了，他会不高兴，但他会接受。

column1: He knows he is on shaky ground. Let us call his bluff.
column2: 他知道自己站不住脚。我们来戳穿他的虚张声势。

column1: His case against us is clad in iron.
column2: 他对我们的指控铁证如山。

column1: His case is without merit; the precedents all say that mercenaries are not to be held accountable for the decisions of those who employ them.
column2: 他的指控毫无根据；过往判例都表明，佣兵不必为其雇主们的决定负责。

column1: His case is without merit; the precedents all say that mercenaries are not to be held accountable for the decisions of those who employ them. Still, no legal result is ever guaranteed.
column2: 他的指控毫无根据；过往判例都表明，佣兵不必为其雇主们的决定负责。不过，判决结果向来难以预料。

column1: If we do not give him what he asks, we will earn the enmity of his clan.
column2: 如果我们不给他所要求的，就会招来他氏族的敌意。

column1: We should not have attacked our ally in the first place.
column2: 我们一开始就不该攻击我们的盟友。

column1: His people already dislike us; a refusal will offend them further.
column2: 他的人民已经不喜欢我们了；拒绝会进一步激怒他们。

column1: Our relations with his clan are generally good; even if we offend them in this instance, the results will not be serious.
column2: 我们与他氏族的总体关系良好；即便这次冒犯了他们，后果也不会太严重。

column1: Although the Orlanthi have many laws, the first law is “No one can make you do anything.”
column2: 尽管奥兰提人有众多律法，但首要一条是“没人能强迫你做任何事。”

column1: I’m thinking it was probably a mistake to send our warriors against our ally.
column2: 我觉得派我们的战士去攻击盟友可能是个错误。

column1: Last time I had nothing to say, and I made a fool of myself by going on and on about it. Well, this time you can bet that I’m going to keep my mouth firmly shut. No more running off at the mouth for me.
column2: 上次我无话可说，却喋喋不休地出丑。好吧，这次你尽管放心，我会把嘴闭得严严实实。再也不乱说话了。

column1: If this fool wants wealth, he should go exploring for treasures, instead of exploring the limits of our patience.
column2: 如果这个蠢货想要财富，他该去寻宝，而不是试探我们的耐心底线。

column1: Take pity on him. He will be humiliated if he returns to his people with nothing.
column2: 可怜可怜他吧。要是什么都没带就回去，他会蒙羞的。

column1: We should resort to trial by combat!
column2: 我们应该诉诸战斗审判！

column1: is clearly more interested in profit than vengeance, and comes to engage in routine trading despite the feud between your clans.
column2: 显然更在意利益而非复仇，尽管你们两族之间有着世仇，他还是来做日常交易。

column1: “Surely you are good Orlanthi, and will not deny me hospitality here,” he says, “even though outside this tula you have treated me badly.”
column2: “想必你们是善良的奥兰提人，不会在此地拒绝我的好客之请，”他说，“尽管在这图拉领地之外你们曾对我很坏。”

column1: comes to engage in routine trading.
column2: 来做日常交易。

column1: As he is concluding his business, he again issues his warning.
column2: 在他结束交易时，他再次发出警告。

column1: As he is concluding his business, he issues a warning.
column2: 在他结束交易时，他发出警告。

column1: “You will rue your cruelty to me when the truth is known,” he says.
column2: “等真相大白，你们会后悔对我如此残忍，”他说。

column1: Avoid entanglement in this dispute.
column2: 避免卷入这场争议。

column1: We avoided becoming entangled in this dispute.
column2: 我们避免了卷入这场争议。

column1: The people were glad the ring refused to get caught up in gossip outside the clan, though our traders reported that the \x01@! clan was now even more hostile towards us than before.
column2: 人民很高兴长老会拒绝卷入族外流言，不过我们的商人报告说 \x01@! 氏族现在对我们比以往更敌视了。

column1: The people were glad the ring refused to get caught up in gossip outside the clan.
column2: 人民很高兴长老会拒绝卷入族外流言。

column1: Who do you send to confront her?
column2: 你派谁去面对她？

column1: How many guards do you send with \x01@\x05?
column2: 你派多少护卫随 \x01@\x05同去？

column1: \x01@\x05 felt that she was telling the truth.
column2: \x01@\x05 认为她说了实话。

column1: \x01@\x05 felt that she was lying.
column2: \x01@\x05 认为她在撒谎。

column1: Who do you send to tell her?
column2: 你派谁去告诉她？

column1: She thanked us for the warning, and gave us gifts.
column2: 她感谢我们的警告，并赠予我们礼物。

column1: \x01@\x05 was struck by her honesty and proper manners.
column2: \x01@\x05 被她的诚实和得体举止所打动。

column1: We must somehow resolve this dispute.
column2: 我们必须设法解决这场争议。

column1: This is none of our business.
column2: 这不关我们的事。

column1: Send me to the \x01@a tula; I will determine the veracity of these rumors.
column2: 派我去 \x01@a 图拉领地吧；我会查明这些传闻的真假。

column1: There is nothing to be gained by getting entangled in a dispute between traders.
column2: 卷入商人们的纠纷毫无益处。

column1: Each clan sanctions its traders to do business on behalf of the clan ring; each trader serves as an emissary for his clan.
column2: 每个氏族都授权其商人代表氏族议会交易；每位商人都是他氏族的使者。

column1: This is all going to end badly.
column2: 这一切都不会有好结果。

column1: The two of them should settle this dispute without involving others.
column2: 他们俩应该在不牵连他人的情况下解决这场纠纷。

column1: The treachery of Woman is constant. Remember Molanni, goddess of still air, who dallied with the Fire Tribe? Remember Thed and Malia, who founded the Unholy Trio?
column2: 女性的背叛亘古不变。还记得静止空气女神莫兰尼与火族调情的事吗？还记得创立邪恶三神的塞德和玛利亚吗？

column1: We decided that she was.
column2: 我们断定她就是。

column1: We decided that she was not. She sensed this, and seemed sorely affronted.
column2: 我们断定她不是。她察觉到了，似乎深感被冒犯。

column1: Listen to her, but promise nothing.
column2: 听她说，但别做任何承诺。

column1: We listened to her, but promised nothing.
column2: 我们听了她的话，但没有承诺任何事。

column1: She said that time would prove the truth of her words.
column2: 她说时间会证明她的话属实。

column1: We cried thus: “Skel speaks true! You are a villainess!”
column2: 我们如此高呼：“斯凯尔所言不虚！你是个恶妇！”

column1: The people were pleased that we had scolded her.
column2: 民众对我们斥责了她感到满意。

column1: This is not a matter of concern to warriors.
column2: 这不是武士该操心的事。

column1: We must make justice here.
column2: 我们必须在此主持公道。

column1: Let me question her; I will determine the truth.
column2: 让我来审问她；我会查明真相。

column1: Kings do not get involved in stupid disputes.
column2: 王者不卷入愚蠢的争端。

column1: This isn’t going to cost us anything, is it?
column2: 这不会让我们付出任何代价，对吧？

column1: We don’t necessarily need to believe either of these traders. We can try to determine the truth ourselves.
column2: 我们不一定非得相信这两个商人中的任何一个。我们可以自己设法查明真相。

column1: We must know more, and not jump to conclusions that could disturb tribal harmony.
column2: 我们必须了解更多，不能草率下结论，以免扰乱部族的和谐。

column1: A group of Telmori wolfmen evade your patrols and kill several more of your cattle, boldly butchering them under your very noses. They escape before your warriors rally. Once again they have ignored the alliance your clan once made with them.
column2: 一群泰尔莫里狼人避开了你们的巡逻队，又杀了几头你们的牛，公然在你们眼皮底下屠宰。你们战士集结之前他们就逃走了。他们再次无视了你们部族曾与他们缔结的盟约。

column1: Telmori wolfmen again broke the terms of our alliance with their people. They killed several of our cattle, boldly slaughtering them under our very noses.
column2: 泰尔莫里狼人再次破坏了我们的部族与他们族人之间的盟约。他们杀了我们好几头牛，公然在我们眼皮底下屠宰。

column1: A group of Telmori wolfmen break the terms of the alliance your clan once made with their people. Eluding your patrols, they kill several of your cattle, boldly butchering them under your very noses. They escape before your warriors can equip themselves for battle.
column2: 一群泰尔莫里狼人破坏了你们部族曾与他们族人缔结的盟约。他们避开你们的巡逻队，杀了你们几头牛，公然在你们眼皮底下屠宰。在你们的战士准备好战斗之前他们就逃走了。

column1: Telmori wolfmen broke the terms of our alliance with their people. Eluding our patrols, they killed several of our cattle, boldly butchering them under our very noses.
column2: 泰尔莫里狼人破坏了我们的部族与他们族人之间的盟约。他们避开我们的巡逻队，杀了我们好几头牛，公然在我们眼皮底下屠宰。

column1: Attack the Telmori encampment.
column2: 进攻泰尔莫里营地。

column1: We attacked the Telmori encampment.
column2: 我们进攻了泰尔莫里营地。

column1: We searched for them but found only an abandoned encampment.
column2: 我们搜寻了他们，但只发现一个被遗弃的营地。

column1: They did not expect our war party, and shouted in surprise and dismay at our appearance. They cursed us as oath-breakers, but could not back their words with action. We cut many of them down, and drove others from their camp.
column2: 他们没有料到我们的战团，对我们的出现发出惊讶和沮丧的喊叫。他们咒骂我们是背誓者，但无法用行动支持自己的言语。我们砍倒了许多人，把其他人都赶出了营地。

column1: They did not expect our war party, and shouted in surprise and dismay at our appearance. They cursed us as oath-breakers, and rallied against us, growling in fury. They drove us back, killing some and wounding others.
column2: 他们没有料到我们的战团，对我们的出现发出惊讶和沮丧的喊叫。他们咒骂我们是背誓者，并集结起来对抗我们，愤怒地咆哮着。他们击退了我们，杀了一些人，伤了一些人。

column1: Convince your people that this matter is best ignored.
column2: 说服你的民众，此事最好不予理会。

column1: \x01@\x03 told the people that this matter was best ignored.
column2: \x01@\x03 告诉民众此事最好不予理会。

column1: The herders were angry, and said that our inaction merely encouraged the Telmori to strike again.
column2: 牧人们很愤怒，说我们的不作为只会鼓励泰尔莫里人再次袭击。

column1: The Telmori chieftain said that he had not given his blessing to the raid against us. He snapped and snarled at the wolfmen who killed our cows, and forced them to offer plundered silver in reparation for their offense against us.
column2: 泰尔莫里酋长说他并未准许袭击我们。他对那些杀了我们牛的狼人厉声呵斥、咆哮，并强迫他们献出劫掠来的白银，作为冒犯我们的赔偿。

column1: The Telmori chieftain said that he had not given his blessing to the raid against us, and so could not be held responsible for it. He offered us no satisfaction.
column2: 泰尔莫里酋长说他并未准许袭击我们，因此不能为此负责。他没有给我们任何补偿。

column1: Tell other clans that the Telmori cannot be trusted.
column2: 告诉其他部族，泰尔莫里人不可信任。

column1: We told other clans that the Telmori could not be trusted.
column2: 我们告诉其他部族，泰尔莫里人不可信任。

column1: The Telmori got the better of them, capturing and ransoming some of their weaponthanes. While captive, these weaponthanes told the wolfmen that it was we who had inspired their attack.
column2: 泰尔莫里人占了上风，俘虏了他们的一些武器领主并索要赎金。被俘期间，这些武器领主告诉狼人，是我们在背后鼓动他们发起袭击。

column1: They struck hard against the wolf-folk, driving them away from the pastureland of Dragon Pass.
column2: 他们重击了狼族，将他们赶出了龙之隘口的牧地。

column1: We decided to track and kill the Telmori who took our cattle.
column2: 我们决定追踪并杀死那些抢走我们牛只的泰尔莫里人。

column1: Who leads the hunt?
column2: 由谁带领狩猎队？

column1: \x01@\x05 found them, and our warriors slew them.
column2: \x01@\x05 找到了他们，我们的战士杀死了他们。

column1: \x01@\x05 did not find them, and so our aims were thwarted.
column2: \x01@\x05 没有找到他们，因此我们的目标受挫。

column1: The carls don’t mind if a few cattle disappear every now and then.
column2: 自由民并不介意偶尔丢失几头牛。

column1: The carls hate these cattle killers. They will be affronted if we do nothing.
column2: 自由民痛恨这些杀牛者。如果我们无所作为，他们会感到被冒犯。

column1: The carls want us to act, but we can convince them that this matter can be safely ignored.
column2: 自由民希望我们采取行动，但我们可以说服他们，此事可以放心地不予理会。

column1: If we do nothing, the raiders will return.
column2: 如果我们无所作为，袭击者还会再来。

column1: They cannot be allowed to continue killing our cattle!
column2: 绝不能让他们继续杀害我们的牛！

column1: If we can’t stop them by ourselves, maybe other clans can help.
column2: 如果我们自己阻止不了他们，也许其他部族能帮忙。

column1: If we do nothing, there is a good chance that the raiders will return.
column2: 如果我们无所作为，袭击者很可能还会再来。

column1: The more we ignore them, the bolder they will grow.
column2: 我们越是不理会他们，他们就会越大胆。

column1: If we continue to ignore them, the odds are better than even that they will raid again.
column2: 如果我们继续无视他们，他们再次袭击的几率会超过一半。

column1: The other clans will want to know of Telmori treachery.
column2: 其他部族会想知道泰尔莫里人的背信弃义。

column1: The other clans are panting for a reason to attack the wolfmen. If we spread word of this raid, you can bet that someone will go after them.
column2: 其他部族正亟需一个攻击狼人的理由。如果我们散布这次袭击的消息，保准会有人去找他们算账。

column1: The Telmori are tough to find. Once found, they are tough to kill.
column2: 泰尔莫里人很难找到。一旦找到，又很难杀死。

column1: They think of us as allies. If we attack, we will have the advantage of surprise.
column2: 他们认为我们是盟友。如果我们发动攻击，将拥有出其不意的优势。

column1: They don’t seem to care if we are allies or not. We can spring an attack on them and scatter their fur on the wind.
column2: 他们似乎不在乎我们是不是盟友。我们可以突袭他们，把他们的皮毛撒向风中。

column1: It would be better to punish the ones who are raiding us, than to try to find and fight all the Telmori.
column2: 与其试图找到并对抗所有泰尔莫里人，不如惩罚那些正在袭击我们的人。

column1: Send \x01@\x07; \x06 is best suited to track down the raiders we seek.
column2: 派遣 \x01@\x07； \x06 最适合追踪我们要找的袭击者。

column1: An alliance made with wolfmen is worthless; we can’t expect them to give us satisfaction.
column2: 与狼人结盟毫无价值；我们不能指望他们给我们一个交代。

column1: They do not follow our laws, but I can convince them to make good on their alliance with us.
column2: 他们不遵从我们的法律，但我可以说服他们履行与我们结盟的承诺。

column1: They do not follow our laws, but we should follow them. We must give them a chance to make good before making war on them.
column2: 他们不遵从我们的法律，但我们应该遵守法律。在向他们开战之前，我们必须给他们一个履行承诺的机会。

column1: The carls are restive. They won’t want to hear any excuses from us.
column2: 自由民焦躁不安。他们不想听我们任何借口。

column1: The carls are busy planting, and want us to settle this without fighting.
column2: 自由民正忙于播种，希望我们不动刀兵解决此事。

column1: The carls are busy harvesting, and want us to settle this without fighting.
column2: 自由民正忙于收割，希望我们不动刀兵解决此事。

column1: The carls are anxious. They want us to act, and act now.
column2: 自由民忧心忡忡。他们要我们行动，马上行动。

column1: The carls are impatient. They don’t care about much except this loss of cattle to the wolf-men.
column2: 自由民不耐烦了。除了这些被狼人偷走的牛，他们别无所求。

column1: The carls are in a good enough mood, but they will grow angry if we lose too many more cattle.
column2: 自由民心情还算不错，但如果我们再损失太多牛只，他们会恼怒起来。

column1: Despite these incidents, the carls are still in a good mood. But that doesn’t mean we can ignore the Telmori threat to our cattle.
column2: 尽管发生了这些事，自由民心情依然不错。但这并不意味着我们可以忽视泰尔莫里人对我们牛群的威胁。

column1: We can blacken the Telmori name all we want, so long as our words do not get back to them.
column2: 我们可以尽情抹黑泰尔莫里人的名声，只要这话不传到他们耳中。

column1: Let me dress up in a wolf-skin and infiltrate their camp!
column2: 让我披上狼皮，潜入他们的营地！

column1: I know! Paint the cows, and when the wolf-men handle one, we’ll know which of them are raiding us.
column2: 我知道了！给牛涂上颜料，等狼人碰到牛，我们就知道哪些人在袭击我们。

column1: None of these options are worth considering until we improve our patrols.
column2: 在我们加强巡逻之前，这些选项都不值得考虑。

column1: These wolf-people are like the cruel biting things who tormented Uralda during the God’s War. If they are not punished, the Cow Goddess will withhold her bounty from us.
column2: 这些狼人就像神战期间折磨乌拉尔达的残忍噬咬之物。若他们不受惩罚，母牛女神将不会赐予我们恩泽。

column1: The wolf-people are the natural foes of cattle, and the natural foes of Uralda. If \x02\x03we cannot stop this slaughter/we don’t find and fight them/they are not punished\x02, the Cow Goddess will withhold her bounty from us.
column2: 狼人是牛的天敌，也是乌拉尔达的天敌。如果 \x02\x03我们不能阻止这场屠杀/我们找不到并与之战斗/他们没有受到惩罚\x02，母牛女神将不会赐予我们恩泽。

column1: If we spread word of Telmori treachery, it will not be long before another clan invites us to hunt them.
column2: 如果我们散布泰尔莫里人背信弃义的消息，不久就会有其他氏族邀请我们一同猎杀他们。

column1: There’s one important thing that you must remember when dealing with Telmori. Um, and as soon as I remember it, I’ll let you know what it is.
column2: 在对付泰尔莫里人时，有一件重要的事你必须记住。呃，等我想起来，就告诉你是什么。

column1: \x02\x03Ah/Oh/Heh\x02! The Telmori \x02\x03are/must/will\x02 — I mean they \x02\x03aren’t like other/don’t do the same/have very different\x02 — it’s not like \x02\x03they can/they see/they worship\x02 — ah — ahem. I forget.
column2: \x02\x03啊/哦/嘿\x02！泰尔莫里人 \x02\x03是/必须/将会\x02 ——我是说他们 \x02\x03不像其他人/不做同样的事/有非常不同的\x02 ——不像 \x02\x03他们能/他们看到/他们崇拜\x02 ——啊——嗯哼。我忘了。

column1: I told you they wouldn’t honor their alliance.
column2: 我告诉过你，他们不会履行盟约。

column1: These raiders may not know of our alliance with their people. Should we excuse their ignorance?
column2: 这些袭击者可能不知道我们与他们的族人有盟约。我们该原谅他们的无知吗？

column1: “Maybe you don’t know much about these wolf-people, but here is your chance to learn,” he says.
column2: “也许你对这些狼人不太了解，但现在你有个学习的机会，”他说。

column1: Accept his invitation.
column2: 接受他的邀请。

column1: We accepted his invitation.
column2: 我们接受了他的邀请。

column1: He said this would end our feud, and that our clans could now draw the blood of outsiders, instead of fighting each other.
column2: 他说这能终结我们的世仇，现在两个氏族可以共同向外族人索血，而不是自相残杀。

column1: He was pleased by this response, and said that his clan would not forget the aid we gave them this day.
column2: 他对这个答复很满意，并说他的氏族不会忘记我们今日的援助。

column1: Decline his invitation.
column2: 拒绝他的邀请。

column1: We declined his invitation.
column2: 我们拒绝了他的邀请。

column1: He said we were no use to him.
column2: 他说我们对他毫无用处。

column1: He said we were entitled to refuse, but the smirk of contempt on his face showed that he thought worse of us.
column2: 他说我们有权拒绝，但他脸上轻蔑的假笑表明他对我们评价更低了。

column1: He said that we were under no obligation to help, and that he hoped we would think of unity among the people of Dragon Pass.
column2: 他说我们没有义务帮忙，但他希望我们考虑一下龙之隘口人民的团结。

column1: He said that the gods would look upon us with disfavor for our cowardly refusal.
column2: 他说诸神会因为我们的怯懦拒绝而不悦。

column1: Decline his invitation; make peace with the Telmori.
column2: 拒绝他的邀请；与泰尔莫里人讲和。

column1: We sought peace with the Telmori.
column2: 我们寻求与泰尔莫里人讲和。

column1: “We allied with you once, and you turned out to be liars,” said their king. “You were liars then, and you are liars now.”
column2: “我们曾与你们结盟，结果你们是骗子，”他们的国王说。“你们那时是骗子，现在还是骗子。”

column1: leaders were reluctant at first, but before long we were teaching them great poems, and they were teaching us how to howl.
column2: 首领们起初不愿，但不久我们就教他们伟大的诗篇，而他们教我们如何嚎叫。

column1: He laughed at the suggestion and repeated his invitation. “Peace does not win plunder!” he exclaimed.
column2: 他对这个建议报以大笑，并再次发出邀请。“和平换不来战利品！”他喊道。

column1: His face hardened. “Peace is for ponds and stalks of wheat. We are men, and live for war.”
column2: 他脸色一沉。“和平是给池塘和麦秆的。我们是男人，为战斗而生。”

column1: He smiled. “Your intentions are honorable; it is good to make peace. But let us bring peace to our own people by making war upon a common enemy — the drooling, Chaos-tainted Telmori horde!”
column2: 他微笑道：“你的意图可敬；讲和是好事。但让我们通过对共同的敌人——那流着口水、受混沌污染的泰尔莫里兽群——开战，来为我们自己的人民带来和平！”

column1: He seemed shocked by this response. “Make peace with the spawn of Chaos? Next you’ll be telling me that you’ve chosen a broo as your chieftain!”
column2: 他似乎被这个答复震惊了。“与混沌的孽种讲和？接下来你是不是要告诉我，你选了一个布鲁兽做酋长！”

column1: It was far from easy to persuade him, but we turned his own arguments against him, and he was left with no choice but to let us try.
column2: 说服他绝非易事，但我们用他自己的论点反将他了一军，他别无选择，只能让我们试试。

column1: Who do you send to the Telmori encampment?
column2: 你派谁去泰尔莫里营地？

column1: The other clans of Dragon Pass were amazed by what we had accomplished, and said that our clan might be destined for great things.
column2: 巨龙隘口的其他氏族对我们的成就感到惊讶，并说我们的氏族也许注定要成就伟业。

column1: “We are beginning to regret the peace we made with you,” he said.
column2: “我们开始后悔与你们达成的和平了，”他说。

column1: “This peace mission is but a trick to set us off our guard.”
column2: “这次和平使命不过是一个让我们放松警惕的诡计。”

column1: “We will go with you, but your clan will owe us a favor.”
column2: “我们会与你们同去，但你们氏族将欠我们一个人情。”

column1: We said to him, “We will go with you, but your clan will owe us a favor.”
column2: 我们对他说：“我们会与你同去，但你们氏族将欠我们一个人情。”

column1: “A share of the plunder is all I offer,” he said.
column2: “我只提供一份战利品，”他说。

column1: “Increased skill at arms is its own reward,” he said.
column2: “武艺精进本身就是奖赏，”他说。

column1: He smiled ruefully. “I wish I could offer you more than unity, but I have little else to give.”
column2: 他苦笑了一下。“我希望我能给你比团结更多的东西，但我几乎别无他物可给。”

column1: His mouth gaped open in affronted surprise. “It is I who do you a favor, by giving you this chance to win the blessings of the gods!”
column2: 他震惊得张大了嘴。“是我在帮你一个忙，给了你这个赢得诸神祝福的机会！”

column1: We sent \x01@\x05 to lead our war party against the Telmori.
column2: 我们派遣 \x01@\x05 率领我们的战团去攻打泰尔莫里人。

column1: Together our clans laid waste to the Telmori encampment, slaying their warriors and driving their women and children deep into the woods.
column2: 我们两个氏族联手摧毁了泰尔莫里营地，杀死了他们的战士，并将他们的妇女和儿童驱赶入森林深处。

column1: \x01@\x05 \x02\x03was bitten deeply in many places and quickly bled to death/was killed by a fiery arrow/was found under other dead bodies, stabbed, bitten and mauled\x02. The people mourned \x04 loss.
column2: \x01@\x05 \x02\x03被多处深咬伤后迅速失血而死/被一支火箭射死/被发现压在别的尸体下，被刺、被咬、被撕成重伤\x02。族人为 \x04 的死哀悼。

column1: The Telmori are notorious for stealing livestock. They are a threat to our way of life.
column2: 泰尔莫里人以偷牲畜而臭名昭著。他们威胁着我们的生活方式。

column1: A fight with the Telmori is not something we should undertake lightly.
column2: 与泰尔莫里人开战不是我们应该轻率决定的事。

column1: The warriors are spoiling for a fight.
column2: 勇士们渴望一战。

column1: The warriors are in no mood for a fight.
column2: 勇士们无心战斗。

column1: If we accept his invitation, it will improve our relations with the \x01@! clan.
column2: 如果我们接受他的邀请，将改善我们与 \x01@! 氏族的关系。

column1: Maybe we should make peace with the Telmori. There will never be a shortage of foes in Dragon Pass.
column2: 也许我们应该与泰尔莫里人讲和。巨龙隘口从不缺敌人。

column1: Our most ancient enemies were half beast and half man. Every time we strike at the Telmori, we strengthen our magic.
column2: 我们最古老的宿敌半人半兽。每当我们打击泰尔莫里人，我们的魔法就会增强。

column1: I am no friend of the wolf people, but this is the time to sow our crops.
column2: 我不是狼人的朋友，但现在是播种的时候。

column1: I’m all in favor of attacking the wolf-folk, but later. Not during the harvest.
column2: 我完全赞成攻击那些狼人，但要等以后。不能赶在收获期间。

column1: If we could learn to get along with the Telmori, instead of slaughtering them, would that not be a kingly act?
column2: 如果我们能学会与泰尔莫里人和平共处，而不是屠杀他们，这难道不是王者之举吗？

column1: The Telmori are a cursed and savage people, who turn into wolves one day a week, whether they want to or not. They live like nomads and steal sheep and cattle from honest herdsmen.
column2: 泰尔莫里人是一个受诅咒的野蛮民族，每周有一天会变成狼，无论他们是否愿意。他们像游牧民一样生活，从诚实的牧民那里偷羊偷牛。

column1: We made a peace pact with the Telmori; it is still in force.
column2: 我们与泰尔莫里人订立了和平条约；目前仍然有效。

column1: We used to have a peace pact with the Telmori, but it was broken.
column2: 我们曾与泰尔莫里人有过和平条约，但被打破了。

column1: Tell him what he least expects to hear.
column2: 告诉他他最不想听到的话。

column1: It feels like forever since I last crushed a foeman’s skull.
column2: 感觉自上次砸碎敌人的头骨以来已经过了很久。

column1: Breaking our pact with the Telmori would be dishonorable.
column2: 违背我们与泰尔莫里人的条约是不光彩的。

column1: The Telmori can’t help it if they have to steal our cattle to live.
column2: 泰尔莫里人也是迫不得已，为了生存才偷我们的牛。

column1: The Telmori are but a distraction from our real foe — zombies!
column2: 泰尔莫里人只是转移我们注意力的东西，我们真正的敌人是——僵尸！

column1: If we enrage the Telmori, they will sweep down upon us and exterminate our entire clan!
column2: 如果我们激怒泰尔莫里人，他们会横扫而来，灭绝我们整个氏族！

column1: We can’t afford to offend the Telmori any further.
column2: 我们不能再进一步得罪泰尔莫里人了。

column1: Kill them! Kill them all!
column2: 杀了他们！全部杀光！

column1: sceneR441
column2: sceneR441

column1: A delegation of Telmori wolf-men come to your tula to deliver a warning. “Many times have you offended us,” they say. “You do not permit us to live as our ancestors say we must. We will visit terrible vengeance upon you if you oppress us any further. Do you understand us? This is your last warning.”
column2: 一队泰尔莫里狼人来到你们的图拉领地发出警告。“你们多次冒犯我们，”他们说。“你们不允许我们按照祖先规定的方式生活。如果你们继续压迫我们，我们将对你们施以可怕的复仇。你们明白吗？这是最后一次警告。”

column1: A delegation of Telmori warned us that they would attack us if we did not mend our ways toward them.
column2: 一队泰尔莫里人警告我们，如果我们不改变对待他们的方式，他们将攻击我们。

column1: Demand that they leave.
column2: 要求他们离开。

column1: We demanded that they leave, and they did.
column2: 我们要求他们离开，他们照做了。

column1: They snarled at us, and left.
column2: 他们对我们咆哮了一番，然后离开了。

column1: We listened to them, but made no promises.
column2: 我们听了他们的话，但没有做出任何承诺。

column1: They growled and bared their teeth at us, and left.
column2: 他们咆哮着，对我们龇牙咧嘴，然后离开了。

column1: They accepted it, and said that it would go some way towards addressing their grievance against us.
column2: 他们接受了，并说这能在一定程度上解决他们对我们的不满。

column1: They departed, taking what we offered them, but saying little.
column2: 他们带走了我们给的东西，但没说几句话就离开了。

column1: An enormous force of Telmori raiders descends on your tula, attacking with shocking ferocity. They kill most of your warriors and leaders. They kill most of your livestock; when the battle is done, they butcher it on the spot, for easy division of spoils. They take your stored food. They take some of your trade goods, destroying the rest. As the fighting dies down, the more adventurous of them burn your steads, even though they seem afraid of fire. Some, still possessed by animalistic fury, fall upon the noncombatants and tear them limb from limb. They vanish into the woods, leaving only a swollen full moon to look balefully down on the few survivors.
