column1: If we teach them secrets, they will prosper in the realm of the gods, and may bring back powerful weapons. They are our enemies, and will use these weapons against us.
column2: 如果我们教给他们秘密，他们将在神域繁荣，并可能带回强大的武器。他们是我们的敌人，会将这些武器用于对付我们。

column1: We owe them a favor, and are obligated to assist them as they ask.
column2: 我们欠他们一份恩惠，有义务按他们的请求提供帮助。

column1: We owe them a favor, but need not grant them exactly the favor they request.
column2: 我们欠他们一份恩惠，但不必完全满足他们所求的恩惠。

column1: I don’t know what happens when you tell lies about the gods, but \x02\x02I’m sure/I bet\x02 it isn’t good.
column2: 我不知道对诸神撒谎会有什么后果，但 \x02\x02我肯定/我打赌\x02 那不会是什么好事。

column1: \x02\x03Mythic secrets/Hidden wisdom/Secret stories\x02 of the gods bring \x02\x03blessings/great rewards/power\x02 to those who know them.
column2: \x02\x03诸神的\x02 神话秘密/隐藏智慧/秘闻给知晓者带来 \x02\x03祝福/丰厚回报/力量\x02 。

column1: Let me tell, let me tell! I can spin a yarn with made-up details and they’ll never know the difference.
column2: 让我来讲，让我来讲！我能编造细节，他们永远不会察觉有异。

column1: Let me tell them my “Eurmal In the Cow Barn” secrets!
column2: 让我告诉他们我的“牛棚里的尤马尔”秘闻！

column1: First, tell them that they must roll in cow-dung before we can let them in on the secret. Then, when they do this, refuse them.
column2: 首先，告诉他们必须先在牛粪里打滚，我们才能透露秘密。然后，等他们照做，就拒绝他们。

column1: The gods don’t mind when you tell lies about them, if you do it for a good reason.
column2: 若出于正当理由，诸神并不在意你对他们撒谎。

column1: The fewer favors we owe them, the more likely they will be to support us when we want to make a king.
column2: 我们欠他们的恩惠越少，当我们想推选王时，他们就越可能支持我们。

column1: The fewer favors we owe them, the more likely they are to support us.
column2: 我们欠他们的恩惠越少，他们就越可能支持我们。

column1: They are not in our tribe, and no use in kingmaking. Brush them off.
column2: 他们不属于我们的部落，对推选王也无助益。打发他们走。

column1: Helping them could be the first step towards making a tribe together.
column2: 帮助他们可能是共同组建部落的第一步。

column1: Clans form tribes for mutual support. We must see that our tribe has wisdom enough to stay loyal.
column2: 氏族组成部落是为了互相扶持。我们必须确保我们的部落有足够的智慧保持忠诚。

column1: They don’t belong to our tribe, but their chief is known to be quite pious. It would do us good to share.
column2: 他们不属于我们的部落，但他们的酋长以非常虔诚著称。分享对我们有好处。

column1: They don’t belong to our tribe, and their chief is not known to be especially pious. It would do us no harm to refuse them.
column2: 他们不属于我们的部落，他们的酋长也并非以特别虔诚著称。拒绝他们对我们没有坏处。

column1: They don’t belong to our tribe, their chief is not known to be especially pious, and we don’t know what they ask anyway. Just refuse them.
column2: 他们不属于我们的部落，他们的酋长并非以特别虔诚著称，而且我们也不知道他们究竟要什么。直接拒绝他们。

column1: \x01@\x01, a thane of the \x01@! clan, asks you for a gift of luck and divine favor on behalf of his people. He reminds you that you owe them a favor.
column2: \x01@\x01 \x01@! 氏族的一位乡绅，代表其族人向您请求一份好运和神圣恩惠的礼物。他提醒您，您欠他们一份恩惠。

column1: \x01@\x01 spat. “I will see to it that all of the clans in Dragon Pass know just how worthless your word is.”
column2: \x01@\x01 啐了一口。“我会让龙之隘口的所有氏族都知道，你的话一文不值。”

column1: \x01@\x01 said it was good that we honored our obligations.
column2: \x01@\x01 说我们履行义务是件好事。

column1: “I would prefer a gift of magic,” \x01@\x01 said. “But I suppose that I could find shamans, trade these gifts to them, and receive spiritual power in return.”
column2: “我更希望得到一件魔法礼物，” \x01@\x01 说。“但我想我可以找到萨满，把这些礼物与他们交易，换取灵力。”

column1: \x01@\x01 said, “I suppose that I could find shamans, trade these gifts to them, and receive spiritual power in return.”
column2: \x01@\x01 说：“我想我可以找到萨满，把这些礼物与他们交易，换取灵力。”

column1: \x01@\x01 refused our offer, insisting on receiving magic for the favor we owed his clan.
column2: \x01@\x01 拒绝了我们的提议，坚持要获得魔法作为我们欠他氏族的恩惠的回报。

column1: “I’ve come for luck, not for gifts,” said \x01@\x01. “Surely you will be willing to help us, as we helped you in the past.”
column2: “我是来求好运的，不是来要礼物的，” \x01@\x01说。“你们一定会愿意帮助我们，就像我们过去帮助你们那样。”

column1: \x01@\x01 said that while he appreciated our gifts, he would not be able to take them, for his clan needed magic, not cattle or silver.
column2: \x01@\x01 说虽然他感谢我们的礼物，但他不能收下，因为他的氏族需要的是魔法，而不是牲畜或白银。

column1: He said that he was sorry to trouble us, and would seek to collect the favor on some other occasion.
column2: 他说很抱歉打扰我们，并会另找机会来索取这份恩惠。

column1: \x01@\x01 accused us of lying, and of refusing to honor an obligation.
column2: \x01@\x01 指责我们撒谎，拒绝履行义务。

column1: Our herds are large. We should give cows instead of magic.
column2: 我们的牧群很大。我们应该给牛而不是法术。

column1: They’ve helped us. We should help them.
column2: 他们帮过我们，我们该帮他们。

column1: We owe them a favor, and must make at least some effort to make good on it.
column2: 我们欠他们一份恩惠，必须至少做些努力来偿还。

column1: We owe them a favor, but don’t necessarily have to give them exactly what they want, exactly when they want it.
column2: 我们欠他们一份恩惠，但不一定要在他们想要的时候，给他们恰好想要的东西。

column1: Help them; \x02\x02maybe/perhaps\x02 they need the magic \x02\x04for curing sick infants/for healing their herdsmen/to perform beneficial rites/to perform rituals of healing\x02.
column2: 帮助他们； \x02\x02也许/或许\x02 他们需要魔法 \x02\x04来治愈生病的婴儿/来医治他们的牧民/来执行有益的仪式/来施行治疗仪式\x02。

column1: I finally \x02\x03know/can tell/figured out\x02 what \x02\x03I wanted to say back then/I meant — I mean/to tell, uh,\x02 — \x02\x03about that other thing/to say now/that — never mind\x02.
column2: 我终于 \x02\x03知道/能说出/弄明白\x02 我 \x02\x03当时想说的话/我的意思——我是说/想说的是，呃，\x02 —— \x02\x03关于那另一件事/现在想说的/那个——算了\x02。

column1: Bad King Urgrain owed many favors. When thanes of other kingdoms came to collect these favors, he said, “I am doing you a favor by leaving your heads on your shoulders.”
column2: 恶王乌格兰欠下许多恩惠。当其他王国的领主们来索取这些恩惠时，他说：“我把你们的脑袋留在脖子上，这就算帮你们一个忙了。”

column1: Chalana Arroy healed the angry Wasp Queen when her nest fell, and healed all her children. And to this day, wasps will not bother a healer.
column2: 查拉娜·阿罗伊治好了愤怒的黄蜂女王，当时她的巢穴塌了，还治好了她所有的孩子。直到今天，黄蜂都不会打扰治疗者。

column1: Sofala the Turtle owed Orlanth a favor, because Orlanth had once saved her from pecking birds. Without this debt, she would not have ferried Orlanth and his companions across the sea to the Kingdom of the Dead.
column2: 乌龟索法拉欠奥兰斯一份恩情，因为奥兰斯曾从啄食的鸟群中救过她。没有这份欠债，她就不会载着奥兰斯和他的同伴渡海前往死者之国。

column1: \x01B}, a prosperous herdsman of the \x01@! clan, has come as an emissary from his clan leaders. He has gifts for you; he says they are worth \x01@\x1A cows altogether.
column2: \x01B} \x01@! 氏族的一位富有的牧民，作为氏族领袖的使者前来。他带来了礼物；他说这些总共值 \x01@\x1A 头牛。

column1: \x01B} of the \x01@! clan offered us gifts.
column2: \x01B}  \x01@! 氏族的人赠予我们礼物。

column1: Accept the gifts.
column2: 接受礼物。

column1: We accepted the gifts.
column2: 我们接受了礼物。

column1: Accept the gifts; throw a feast for \x01@! thanes.
column2: 接受礼物；为 \x01@! 领主们举办宴会。

column1: We threw a feast for thanes of \x01B}’s clan.
column2: 我们为 \x01B}氏族的领主们举办了宴会。

column1: They toasted our generosity, and said they would speak of it to others. Our people made merry, and also toasted the clan ring.
column2: 他们为我们的慷慨举杯，并说会向其他人传扬。我们的人民尽情欢乐，也向氏族议会举杯。

column1: Give \x01B} a reciprocal gift.
column2: 给 \x01B} 一份回礼。

column1: We gave \x01B} a reciprocal gift.
column2: 我们赠予了 \x01B} 一份回礼。

column1: He said we were very generous, and that he would say so to others.
column2: 他说我们非常慷慨，并会向他人如此传扬。

column1: Refuse to accept the gifts.
column2: 拒绝接受这些礼物。

column1: We refused to accept his gifts.
column2: 我们拒绝接受他的礼物。

column1: We made \x01B} fear us, and he gave us a total of \x01@\x15 cows worth of trade goods.
column2: 我们让 \x01B} 畏惧我们，于是他给了我们价值共 \x01@\x15 头牛的贸易货物。

column1: Take the gifts, and trade for more cattle.
column2: 收下礼物，再换取更多牛只。

column1: It would be generous to give them a reciprocal gift.
column2: 赠予他们一份回礼将是慷慨之举。

column1: The thought of this gift pleases the people.
column2: 这份礼物的念想令民众欣喜。

column1: If we feasted them, we would bring cheer to our own people.
column2: 若我们宴请他们，将为我们的族人带来欢愉。

column1: If we feasted them, we would bring cheer to our own people and theirs.
column2: 若我们宴请他们，将为我们的族人与他们的族人都带来欢愉。

column1: The \x01@! clan seeks to make amends for past damages. Shall we feast with them? Or push our claims?
column2: \x01@! 氏族寻求弥补往日的损失。我们应当与他们共宴吗？还是坚持我们的索求？

column1: Are these gifts enough for us to forget our feud? The rest of you will have to decide.
column2: 这些礼物足以让我们忘却世仇吗？其余诸君须自行决断。

column1: After Oskul the Just slew Bad King Urgrain and took his throne, he gave gifts to all who had helped him. The Angry Clan spat upon his gifts, which led to war when there should have been peace.
column2: 公正者奥斯库尔斩杀恶王乌格兰并夺取王座后，向所有助他之人赠予礼物。愤怒氏族唾弃他的礼物，从而引发了本应和平之时的战争。

column1: When thanes arrived to gift Bad King Urgrain, he took their wares and their wagons and horses, too. He then enslaved the thanes. Their clan came and made war on him, laying waste to his fields.
column2: 当领主们前来向恶王乌格兰进献礼物时，他夺走了他们的货物、马车与马匹，随后又将领主们奴役。他们的氏族前来向他宣战，摧毁了他的田地。

column1: After Bad King Urgrain lost many battles, he tried making peace by giving gifts. He gave musty cloth full of holes, flat beer, and rotten grain. And this caused the other clans to rise up and smash him.
column2: 恶王乌格兰屡战屡败后，试图通过赠礼求和。他赠予了满是破洞的发霉织物、走气的啤酒和腐坏的谷物。这反倒使其他氏族奋起将他击溃。

column1: When Orlanth armed himself, all of the thanes of the Storm Tribe gathered to give him gifts of martial splendor. In return, he feasted them.
column2: 当奥兰斯武装自身时，风暴部落的所有领主齐聚，向他进献战争荣光的礼物。作为回报，他宴请了他们。

column1: He seeks to tie our clan to his. But some ties were meant to be severed.
column2: 他试图将我们的氏族与他的捆绑。但有些纽带注定要被斩断。

column1: A surprise gift is a \x02\x03sign of the favor of/blessing from/gift of\x02 the gods; we risk bad luck if we refuse them.
column2: 一份意外之礼是 \x02\x03神祇\x02 的恩宠/祝福/礼物的征兆；若我们拒绝，将招致厄运。

column1: It would be very \x02\x03impolite/rude/embarrassing for us\x02 to turn them away.
column2: 拒绝他们会让我们非常 \x02\x03失礼/粗鲁/尴尬\x02 。

column1: There’s something — this \x01B} bothers — I just can’t — refuse him. I think.
column2: 有些事——这 \x01B} 困扰——我实在无法——拒绝他。我想。

column1: We can use this gift to \x02\x04expand our scroll collection/expand our Lhankor Mhy magic/hire tutors to teach our children to read/sacrifice for Lhankor Mhy’s blessings\x02.
column2: 我们可以用这份礼物来 \x02\x04扩充我们的卷轴收藏/增强我们兰科尔·莫的魔法/雇佣导师教我们的孩子识字/献祭以获得兰科尔·莫的祝福\x02。

column1: Their gift will help us \x02\x03add to our shrines/learn more blessings/improve our temples\x02.
column2: 他们的礼物将帮助我们 \x02\x03增建神龛/学习更多祝福/改进神庙\x02。

column1: We can use their gift to equip an expedition to hunt down elves. Then we can kill the elves. Yes. Take the gift.
column2: 我们可以用他们的礼物装备一支远征队去猎杀精灵。然后我们就能杀死精灵。是的。接受礼物。

column1: We can use their gift to arm ourselves well. Then we can provoke a fight with the elves, and slay them.
column2: 我们可以用他们的礼物好好武装自己。然后挑衅精灵，斩杀他们。

column1: The goods they offer us should be used to trade for a treasure.
column2: 他们提供的货物应该用来交换一件宝物。

column1: This gift could be turned into a bride-price or dowry.
column2: 这份礼物可以当作聘礼或嫁妆。

column1: With the goods they offer, I could buy a new book of proverbs.
column2: 用他们提供的货物，我可以买一本新的谚语书。

column1: Mordrim
column2: 莫德里姆

column1: Agree to an alliance.
column2: 同意结盟。

column1: He seemed disappointed, but left without saying so.
column2: 他似乎很失望，但没有明说就离开了。

column1: “If we agreed, we would have too many allies to please.”
column2: “如果我们同意，就有太多盟友要讨好。”

column1: We said to him, “If we agreed, we would have too many allies to please.”
column2: 我们对他说：“如果我们同意，就有太多盟友要讨好。”

column1: “We will not hold this rejection against you, although we wish things could be different,” he said.
column2: “我们不会因这次拒绝而记恨你，尽管我们希望事情能有所不同，”他说。

column1: “You are just saying that because you will not ally with us,” he complained.
column2: “你这么说只是因为你不想与我们结盟，”他抱怨道。

column1: See if you can get more gifts out of him.
column2: 看看你能不能从他那里得到更多礼物。

column1: We tried to get him to give us more gifts.
column2: 我们试图让他给我们更多礼物。

column1: He gave us goods worth an additional \x01@\x1A cows.
column2: 他给了我们价值额外 \x01@\x1A 头牛的货物。

column1: We did not succeed.
column2: 我们没有成功。

column1: It is good to have someone to give you cows when you need them.
column2: 在需要的时候有人给你牛是件好事。

column1: We have more cows than they do. It is us who will be helping them.
column2: 我们的牛比他们多。是我们需要帮助他们。

column1: We have about the same size herds, which means we help each other out fairly.
column2: 我们的畜群规模大致相当，意味着我们公平互助。

column1: They have large herds, and will be able to help us when our herds get thin.
column2: 他们有大畜群，当我们的畜群减少时能帮助我们。

column1: They have more silver in that chest of theirs.
column2: 他们那个箱子里有更多银子。

column1: We are more prosperous than they; they’re just looking for a handout.
column2: 我们比他们富足；他们只是来讨要施舍。

column1: They are about as prosperous as we are, so we are well-matched to be allies.
column2: 他们的富足程度与我们相当，因此很适合结盟。

column1: They are prosperous, and worth allying ourselves with.
column2: 他们很富足，值得我们与之结盟。

column1: Their fyrd is not as big as ours. It is we who would help them on the field of battle, not the other way around.
column2: 他们的民兵不如我们规模大。战场上是我们帮助他们，而不是相反。

column1: They have many more warriors than we do. We should ally with them, and gain their aid on the field of battle.
column2: 他们的战士比我们多得多。我们应该与他们结盟，在战场上获得他们的援助。

column1: We are fairly matched in warriors. We are better as allies than as rivals.
column2: 我们在战士数量上旗鼓相当。我们结盟比敌对更好。

column1: It is \x02\x03excellent/good/auspicious\x02 to have allies, and \x02\x04harmful/unlucky/bad/annoying\x02 to have feuds.
column2: 有盟友是 \x02\x03卓越的/好的/吉利的\x02 ，而有世仇则是 \x02\x04有害的/不幸的/坏的/恼人的\x02 。

column1: If we ally with them, we will have so many allies that it will be hard to meet our commitments to all of them.
column2: 如果我们与他们结盟，我们将有太多盟友，以至于难以履行对所有人的承诺。

column1: A little white lie will soothe any injured feelings.
column2: 一个小小的善意谎言可以抚慰任何受伤的情感。

column1: The more the merrier!
column2: 多多益善！

column1: An alliance will improve relations. “Fighting together forges the best friendship.”
column2: 结盟将改善关系。“并肩作战铸就最深厚的友谊。”

column1: Our mutual respect and admiration is so great that we are practically one clan already.
column2: 我们相互的尊重和钦佩如此深厚，实际上我们已经如同一族。

column1: If we ally with them, it will cause trouble, because our people will see how much smarter the \x01@! clan leaders are.
column2: 如果我们与他们结盟，会惹来麻烦，因为我们的人民会看到 \x01@! 氏族首领们有多么聪明。

column1: I told you they’d \x02\x03seek/come sniffing around for/want to make\x02 an alliance with us.
column2: 我告诉过你他们会 \x02\x03寻求/来打探/想要与\x02 我们结盟。

column1: Allies might help us to \x02\x03build more/expand/improve\x02 our temples.
column2: 盟友可能帮助我们 \x02\x03建造更多/扩建/改善\x02 我们的神庙。

column1: “You remain allied with too many clans, and the value of a pact with you is steadily waning. \x02\x05You no longer have enough wives for our bachelors./Some of your friends are our foes, and we cannot accept that./How can we count on you for help in raids, when we know you might have committed those warriors to help someone else?/When we come to you for food, will you have already given it away to another clan?/If we give you important information, how do we know that you will not pass it along to our rivals?\x02”
column2: “你与太多部族结盟，与你缔约的价值正在稳步下降。 \x02\x05你们没有足够的女子配给我们的单身汉。/你们的一些朋友是我们的敌人，我们不能接受。/当我们知道你可能已经派那些战士去帮助别人时，我们如何能指望你在袭击中提供帮助？/当我们向你索要食物时，你是否已经把它给了别的部族？/如果我们给你重要情报，我们怎么知道你不会把它泄露给我们的对手？\x02”

column1: End your alliance with another clan.
column2: 结束与其他部族的联盟。

column1: We chose to end our alliance with one of the other clans.
column2: 我们选择结束与另一个部族的联盟。

column1: We gave him gifts, as a token of our commitment to his clan.
column2: 我们给了他礼物，作为对他部族承诺的象征。

column1: Once he had gone, the carls complained that we had given him too much.
column2: 他走后，自由民抱怨我们给他太多了。

column1: Once he had gone, the weaponthanes complained that we had given him too much.
column2: 他走后，武器领主抱怨我们给他太多了。

column1: Don’t go giving him any cows; we can’t afford it.
column2: 别给他任何牛；我们负担不起。

column1: Our herds are large. Give him some cattle, and send him on his way.
column2: 我们的畜群很大。给他一些牛，打发他上路。

column1: Our herds are still large. Give him some more cattle, and send him along.
column2: 我们的畜群仍然很大。再给他一些牛，打发他走。

column1: If one alliance is good, many are great. But too many are bad.
column2: 一个联盟若好，多个则更好。但太多就不好了。

column1: We should give him twenty head of cattle, or goods worth twenty head of cattle.
column2: 我们应该给他二十头牛，或价值二十头牛的货物。

column1: Give him twenty head of cattle, or goods worth twenty head of cattle, to show \x02\x03that we are still wealthy/that we remain strong/that we are secure enough to honor our alliance\x02.
column2: 给他二十头牛，或价值二十头牛的货物，以展示 \x02\x03我们仍然富足/我们保持强大/我们足够稳固能够履行联盟\x02。

column1: Tell these pipsqueaks that we can crush them any day of the week!
column2: 告诉这些无名小卒，我们随时都能碾碎他们！

column1: We are stronger than they are. Remind them of this.
column2: 我们比他们强大。提醒他们这一点。

column1: They are stronger than we are, so threats will get us nowhere.
column2: 他们比我们强大，所以威胁无济于事。

column1: There is no law against having large numbers of allies.
column2: 没有法律禁止拥有大量盟友。

column1: We have taken on so many allies that we cannot meet our obligations to all of them. But if we drop one, we will offend its people.
column2: 我们接纳了太多盟友，以至于无法履行对所有人的义务。但如果我们放弃一个，就会得罪其人民。

column1: We have taken on so many allies that we cannot meet our obligations to all of them. We may have no choice but to drop one.
column2: 我们接纳了太多盟友，以至于无法履行对所有人的义务。我们可能别无选择，只能放弃一个。

column1: Alliances between Heortling clans \x02\x03are always changing/go this way, then that way, then the other way/are constantly shifting\x02.
column2: 希欧林氏族之间的联盟 \x02\x03总是变化无常/时而这样，时而那样，又时而另一副模样/不断转变\x02。

column1: We can’t drop anyone, for \x02\x03they will attack us/they will spread false rumors about us/they will raid us\x02 if we \x02\x03offend/insult/slight\x02 them so!
column2: 我们不能放弃任何人，因为 \x02\x03他们会攻击我们/他们会散播关于我们的谣言/他们会袭击我们\x02 ，如果我们 \x02\x03冒犯/侮辱/轻视\x02 他们！

column1: Better to lose an ally than to lose a herd.
column2: 失去盟友也好过失去牛群。

column1: Allies come, allies go. Cattle are the best security.
column2: 盟友来来去去。牛群才是最可靠的保障。

column1: “\x02\x03Threads are woven tight in the best cloth, and fall loose in the worst rags./The eagle wants a sturdy branch to perch on./Kind words can win friends, even when your loaf is half-eaten, and your flagon full of foam.\x02”
column2: “\x02\x03在最精良的布料中丝线织得紧密，在最破旧的衣衫里丝线松散脱落。/雄鹰需要坚固的枝头栖息。/亲切的话语能赢得朋友，即使你的面包已吃一半，酒壶里满是泡沫。\x02”

column1: Alliances were made to be broken.
column2: 结盟就是为了被打破。

column1: A delegation from the \x01@! came to our tula to suggest a peace settlement.
column2: \x01@! 派来了一支代表团，来到我们的领地提出和平解决。

column1: A delegation from the \x01@! clan comes to your tula to propose a peace settlement.
column2: \x01@! 氏族派来了一支代表团，来到你们的领地提出和平解决。

column1: “Our clans tried before to make our lives less difficult by ending our feud. We could not agree that day, but we would like to talk peace again. Do you wish to come to an honorable settlement of our pointless fight, or shall we keep on spilling each others’ blood?”
column2: “我们的氏族之前曾试图结束世仇让日子好过一些。那时我们未能达成一致，但现在我们愿意再次和谈。你们是希望以光荣的方式解决我们这场无谓的争斗，还是继续让彼此流血？”

column1: We said to them, “We accept your offer of peace! Let us feast!”
column2: 我们对他们说：“我们接受你的和平提议！让我们宴饮吧！”

column1: The atmosphere at the feast was tense at first, but eventually weaponthanes from both clans drank together, and a spirit of goodwill overcame the revelers. A few days later, our clan leaders met with theirs to attempt to negotiate a settlement of our grievances.
column2: 宴会的气氛起初很紧张，但最终两个氏族的武器领主开始共饮，善意之精神战胜了狂欢者。几天后，我们氏族的首领与他们的首领会面，试图谈判解决我们的积怨。

column1: When they got to drinking, weaponthanes of both clans began to insult one another, and each group had a long list of grievances to hurl against the other. Fighting broke out, and weaponthanes were wounded on both sides of the brawl. The \x01@! peace overture was soon forgotten.
column2: 喝起酒来后，双方氏族的武器领主开始互相辱骂，每一方都有长长的怨言清单要往对方头上扣。打斗爆发了，斗殴中双方武器领主均有人受伤。 \x01@! 和平倡议很快被遗忘。

column1: We said to them, “We are always ready to talk.”
column2: 我们对他们说：“我们随时愿意谈判。”

column1: They said that if we did not understand peace, they would make us understand war.
column2: 他们说如果我们不懂得和平，他们就会让我们懂得战争。

column1: They proposed to leave six of their young men with us for a year, provided that we left six of our young men as their hostages during the same period.
column2: 他们提议留下六名年轻男子在我们这里一年，条件是我们也在同期留下六名年轻男子作为他们的人质。

column1: They agree to leave six of their young men with us for a year, provided that we leave six of our young men as their hostages their hostages for the same period. Do you agree?
column2: 他们同意留下六名年轻男子在我们这里一年，条件是我们也在同期留下六名年轻男子作为他们的人质他们的人质。你同意吗？

column1: We agreed to do so.
column2: 我们同意这样做。

column1: We refused to go along with this.
column2: 我们拒绝接受。

column1: They refused to go along with this, and departed.
column2: 他们拒绝接受，然后离开了。

column1: “If you need so much proof of our trustworthiness, then it means you yourselves are not to be trusted!” They said they remembered all the good reasons they had to feud with us and departed. No peace was made that day.
column2: “如果你们需要这么多证明我们可信，那就说明你们自己不值得信任！”他们说他们记得所有与我们结仇的充分理由，然后离开了。那一天没有达成和平。

column1: They agreed to our demand. Together, we entered into a peace parley on neutral ground.
column2: 他们同意了我们的要求。我们一起在中立地带进行了和平谈判。

column1: They said that they would be happy to comply, for the gods knew they had honorable intentions.
column2: 他们说他们很乐意服从，因为众神知道他们心怀真诚。

column1: “Then you are unaware of the dangers confronting you, and should take a second look at your situation,” they said.
column2: “那么你们并未意识到面临的危险，应该重新审视自己的处境，”他们说。

column1: “Then you should make peace with us, so you can enjoy the fruits of your good fortune,” they said.
column2: “那么你们应当与我们讲和，这样就能享受好运带来的果实，”他们说。

column1: They give you gifts worth \x01@\x1A cows. What do you offer them in return?
column2: 他们赠送你价值 \x01@\x1A 头牛的礼物。你回赠他们什么？

column1: But several of our nobles thought that resentment still simmered under the surface, and that the \x01@! carls might not be as quick to forgive as their leaders.
column2: 但我们几位贵族认为，怨恨仍在表面之下暗流涌动， \x01@! 自由民可能不会像他们的首领那样轻易原谅。

column1: The leaders of the two clans could not resolve the long-simmering disputes between us, and no peace was made.
column2: 两个氏族的首领无法解决我们之间长期积压的争端，未能达成和平。

column1: If anything, the talks made bad feelings between our clans even worse than they were before.
column2: 反而，谈判让两个氏族之间的敌意比之前更甚。

column1: They are coming to us. We don’t need to worry about making a good impression on them.
column2: 是他们来我们这里。我们不必担心给他们留下好印象。

column1: We need not be too generous with the gifting this time.
column2: 这次我们没必要太慷慨地送礼。

column1: They have seen what our stronger force can do; it is no wonder that they sue for peace.
column2: 他们见识了我们更强武力的厉害；难怪他们要乞求和平。

column1: We have the tougher force; no wonder they keep trying to make peace.
column2: 我们拥有更强的武力；难怪他们不断试图求和。

column1: We still have the weaker force; I wonder why they continue to sue for peace.
column2: 我们仍然处于武力劣势；我不明白他们为何继续乞求和平。

column1: Our force is smaller than theirs. What is their real reason for repeatedly trying to make peace?
column2: 我们的兵力比他们少。他们反复试图讲和的真正原因是什么？

column1: Asking for proof of their intentions is not meant as an insult. It’s meant as insurance in case negotiations break down.
column2: 要求他们证明意图并非侮辱之意，而是为了在谈判破裂时有所保障。

column1: They are approaching us again, and we can ask for proof of their intentions. Though their repeated attempts to make peace may be proof enough.
column2: 他们再次接近我们，我们可以要求他们证明意图。不过，他们反复求和或许已经是足够的证明了。

column1: Everyone is surprised at their persistence.
column2: 所有人都对他们的执着感到惊讶。

column1: A feast creates goodwill between clans, or at least that is what it is meant to do.
column2: 宴席能在氏族之间营造善意——至少本意如此。

column1: Have they atoned for the wrongs they have done us? I don’t think so!
column2: 他们是否已为我们所受的冤屈赎罪？我看没有！

column1: Why do they persist in seeking peace before we have taken our vengeance on them? All their talk does not begin to make up for their crimes against us.
column2: 为什么他们在我们尚未复仇之前就执意求和？他们所有的说辞根本无法弥补对我们犯下的罪行。

column1: Surely such perseverance merits our attention.
column2: 如此执着必然值得我们关注。

column1: They are so eager for peace, let them pay us!
column2: 他们如此渴望和平，那就让他们付出代价！

column1: Their insistence on peace makes me wonder if they are good candidates to make a tribe with.
column2: 他们对和平的坚持让我怀疑他们是否适合结盟。

column1: Look at how they come back to us. We must find a way to make peace with them.
column2: 看看他们如何回到我们身边。我们必须设法与他们和解。

column1: Again, they come to us, looking for a way to end the bloodshed. We must find a way to make peace with them.
column2: 他们再次来到我们这里，寻求终结流血的方式。我们必须设法与他们和解。

column1: Refuse them, then raid them. How dare they come here like that?
column2: 拒绝他们，然后突袭他们。他们怎敢就这样来？

column1: I still say we should refuse their offer, then raid them. We’ll get more that way.
column2: 我仍说我们应该拒绝他们的提议，然后突袭他们。那样我们能得到更多。

column1: sceneR460
column2: sceneR460

column1: A plague has broken out again. About \x01@\x1A have the disease so far. As before, they are weak and fevered; some are barely conscious. Those with more advanced cases show have painful pox erupting on their skins. Several children have died.
column2: 瘟疫再次爆发。目前约有 \x01@\x1A 人染病。和之前一样，他们虚弱且发烧；有些人几乎失去意识。那些病情更严重的，皮肤上冒出疼痛的痘疮。好几个孩子已经死了。

column1: The god-talkers say that this plague has come because you stopped sacrificing to Malia.
column2: 神言者说这场瘟疫降临是因为你停止了向玛利亚献祭。

column1: A terrible plague struck our tula.
column2: 一场可怕的瘟疫袭击了我们的领地。

column1: The god-talkers said this was because we had stopped sacrificing to Malia.
column2: 神言者说这是因为我们停止了向玛利亚献祭。

column1: A plague has stricken your tula. About \x01@\x1A have caught the disease so far. They are weak and unable to exert themselves; some of them are barely able to remain conscious. They are feverish; those with more advanced cases also suffer from a painful pox which erupts on their skins. Several children have died.
column2: 一场瘟疫袭击了你的领地。目前约有 \x01@\x1A 人染病。他们虚弱无力，无法劳作；有些人几乎无法保持清醒。他们发烧；病情更严重的还出现皮肤上冒出疼痛的痘疮。好几个孩子已经死了。

column1: Go to the \x01@! temple to sacrifice to Chalana Arroy.
column2: 前往 \x01@! 神庙向查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭。

column1: We went to the temple of the \x01@! clan to sacrifice to Chalana Arroy, goddess of healing.
column2: 我们前往 \x01@! 氏族的神庙向治愈女神查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭。

column1: The \x01@! elders say that you are no friends to them, and ask why you should be allowed to sacrifice at their temple.
column2: \x01@! 长老们说你们不是他们的朋友，并质问为何允许你们在他们的神庙献祭。

column1: The \x01@! elders said that we were no friends to them, and asked why we should be allowed to sacrifice at their temple.
column2: \x01@! 长老们说我们不是他们的朋友，并质问为何允许我们在他们的神庙献祭。

column1: They accepted these gifts, and allowed us to proceed.
column2: 他们接受了这些礼物，并允许我们继续。

column1: Beg their forgiveness.
column2: 乞求他们的宽恕。

column1: We begged their forgiveness for our transgressions against them.
column2: 我们为自己对他们的冒犯乞求宽恕。

column1: They pronounced themselves satisfied by our show of contrition. But many people in our own clan said they hated to see our emissaries prostrate themselves in this way.
column2: 他们表示对我们的忏悔表示满意。但我们自己氏族中有许多人说讨厌看到我们的使者这样匍匐在地。

column1: They seemed offended even by our apology, but allowed us to proceed with our intended sacrifice.
column2: 他们似乎连我们的道歉都感到冒犯，但还是允许我们继续打算进行的献祭。

column1: Remind them that it is their religious duty to help the sick.
column2: 提醒他们，帮助病患是他们宗教上的职责。

column1: We reminded them that it was their religious duty to help the sick.
column2: 我们提醒他们，帮助病患是他们宗教上的职责。

column1: They admitted that this was so, but seemed to dislike hearing it from us.
column2: 他们承认确实如此，但似乎不喜欢听我们这么说。

column1: Our god-talkers were disheartened, for the signs were bad; it was unlikely that Chalana Arroy had taken notice of our sacrifices. And indeed, the sick got sicker, and the healthy became ill.
column2: 我们的神言者感到沮丧，因为征兆不好；查拉娜·阿罗伊很可能并未注意到我们的献祭。果然，病人病得更重，健康的人也病倒了。

column1: Propitiate Malia, goddess of disease.
column2: 安抚疾病女神玛利亚。

column1: We propitiated Malia, goddess of disease.
column2: 我们安抚了疾病女神玛利亚。

column1: The god-talkers said that we had not sacrificed enough to the dread goddess. If we wanted to succeed, we would have to do it again.
column2: 神言者说我们对可怕女神的献祭还不够。要想成功，我们必须再做一次。

column1: Sacrifice to Chalana Arroy at your temple.
column2: 在你的神庙向查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to Chalana Arroy, goddess of healing.
column2: 我们向治愈女神查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭。

column1: Send for shamans to chase away the disease spirits.
column2: 派人去请萨满驱除疾病之灵。

column1: We sent for shamans to chase away the disease spirits.
column2: 我们派人去请萨满驱除疾病之灵。

column1: Shamans came and said that it was very risky to chase disease spirits away. “We will try, but we insist on 25 cows, no bargaining. This is because they might infect us. And we tell you that you would be more certain of success if you sacrificed to Malia.”
column2: 萨满来了，他们说驱除疾病之灵非常危险。“我们会尝试，但我们坚持要25头牛，不议价。因为它们可能会感染我们。而且我们告诉你，如果你向玛利亚献祭，成功会更确定。”

column1: Shamans come and say that it is very risky to chase disease spirits away. “We will try, but we insist on 25 cows, no bargaining. This is because they might infect us. And we tell you that you would be more certain of success if you sacrificed to Malia.”
column2: 萨满来了，他们说驱除疾病之灵非常危险。“我们会尝试，但我们坚持要25头牛，不议价。因为它们可能会感染我们。而且我们告诉你，如果你向玛利亚献祭，成功会更确定。”

column1: The shamans had their boy assistants take the cows away. Then they danced and shook and rattled their rattles.
column2: 萨满让他们的少年助手把牛带走。然后他们跳舞、颤抖、摇响板。

column1: One of them got sick and another became even crazier than usual. They left, and told us again to propitiate Malia.
column2: 其中一个病倒了，另一个变得比平时更疯癫。他们离开了，并再次告诉我们要安抚玛利亚。

column1: We decided that their price was too high.
column2: 我们认定他们的要价太高了。

column1: They shrugged and left us to deal with the plague in some other way.
column2: 他们耸耸肩，留下我们用其他方式处理瘟疫。

column1: Our lack of cattle forced us to refuse, since their price was too high.
column2: 由于我们缺乏牛只，不得不拒绝，因为他们的要价太高了。

column1: We couldn’t pay the 25 cows.
column2: 我们付不起那25头牛。

column1: Tend to the suffering as well as you can.
column2: 尽力照料受苦的人。

column1: We did our best to tend to the suffering people.
column2: 我们尽力照料受苦的人们。

column1: Some fully recovered; others died. Others lingered in their diseased state, although the worst of the illness passed. The children were hard hit, and their kin who survived filled the tula with the sound of weeping.
column2: 有些人完全康复了；其他人死了。还有些人虽然最严重的病程已经过去，但依然处于患病状态。孩子们受创严重，他们幸存的亲属的哭声充满了整个领地。

column1: Sacrifice goods, not cows.
column2: 献祭货物，不要献祭牛只。

column1: We can’t afford to sacrifice any cows. Sacrifice goods instead.
column2: 我们献祭不起任何牛。改献货物吧。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice a few cows.
column2: 我们还能献祭几头牛。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice a few cows, if we sacrifice to Chalana Arroy. I’d sooner kill them myself than sacrifice to Malia again.
column2: 我们可以牺牲几头牛，如果我们是向查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭。我宁愿亲手宰了他们，也不愿再向玛利亚献祭。

column1: Sacrifice cows, not much-needed trade goods.
column2: 献祭牛，而非急需的贸易商品。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice some valuable trade items.
column2: 我们可以牺牲一些有价值的贸易品。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice valuable trade items — to Chalana Arroy, not to Malia again!
column2: 我们可以牺牲有价值的贸易品——献给查拉娜·阿罗伊，而不是再给玛利亚！

column1: We can’t afford to sacrifice any trade items.
column2: 我们牺牲不起任何贸易品。

column1: I don’t know of any other clans with a Chalana Arroy shrine.
column2: 我不知道还有其他氏族拥有查拉娜·阿罗伊的神殿。

column1: A sacrifice to Malia guarantees success.
column2: 向玛利亚献祭保证成功。

column1: A sacrifice to Malia guarantees success, if you sacrifice enough.
column2: 向玛利亚献祭保证成功——只要你献祭足够多。

column1: A sacrifice to Malia guarantees success, if you sacrifice enough. But if you start propitiating her, you must keep doing it forever. Better to sacrifice to Chalana Arroy.
column2: 向玛利亚献祭保证成功，只要你献祭足够多。但一旦开始安抚她，就必须永远持续下去。不如献祭给查拉娜·阿罗伊。

column1: Every time we sacrifice to Malia, it makes things worse. If only we had never started!
column2: 每次我们向玛利亚献祭，情况都会变得更糟。要是我们从未开始就好了！

column1: Malia is the dreaded goddess of disease, one of the Unholy Trio of deities who brought about the Great Darkness and destroyed Orlanth’s time of justice.
column2: 玛利亚是可怕的疾病女神，是带来大黑暗、摧毁欧兰斯正义时代的不洁三神组之一。

column1: Malia is a Chaos goddess! We must never sacrifice to her!
column2: 玛利亚是混沌女神！我们绝不能向她献祭！

column1: Malia is expensive, but gets results. Give her \x01@\x18 cows.
column2: 玛利亚代价高昂，但有效果。给她 \x01@\x18 牛。

column1: A bargain with Malia \x02\x03is a deal with Chaos/will be worse than this plague/is no bargain at all\x02!
column2: 与玛利亚的交易 \x02\x03是与混沌的交易/会比这场瘟疫更糟糕/根本不是什么交易\x02！

column1: If we sacrifice to the disease goddess, we will make things harder for our neighbors; they will send priests to scold us.
column2: 如果我们向疾病女神献祭，就会让邻居的日子更难过；他们会派祭司来责骂我们。

column1: Sacrificing to Malia will save us cows in the long run.
column2: 从长远来看，向玛利亚献祭会为我们节省牛只。

column1: I told you this would happen if we stopped propitiating Malia!
column2: 我告诉过你们，如果我们停止安抚玛利亚就会这样！

column1: Did I bring this?
column2: 这是我带来的吗？

column1: Our god-talkers said that the signs were good; the merciful goddess looked upon our sacrifice with favor. And indeed, the sick recovered over the next few weeks. The people rejoiced in our good fortune.
column2: 我们的神言者说，征兆是好的；慈悲女神眷顾了我们的献祭。果然，病人在接下来的几周内痊愈了。人们为我们的好运而欢欣。

column1: The god-talkers said that the sacrifice was a success; the dread goddess had received our gifts. Now that we had given to her once, she would expect us to keep doing it, they added. However costly our choice, it worked; soon the people were recovering from the plague.
column2: 神言者说献祭成功了；可怕女神收下了我们的礼物。他们补充说，既然我们已经给过一次，她就会期望我们继续下去。无论我们的选择代价多大，它确实有效；很快人们就开始从瘟疫中康复。

column1: Our god-talkers said that the signs were good; the merciful goddess looked upon our sacrifice with favor. And indeed, the sick recovered over the next day or so. The people rejoiced in our good fortune.
column2: 我们的神言者说，征兆是好的；慈悲女神眷顾了我们的献祭。果然，病人在接下来的一天左右康复了。人们为我们的好运而欢欣。

column1: Eventually, they said that the spirits of disease had been driven from our tula. And indeed, the people slowly got better over the next day or so.
column2: 最终，他们说疾病的灵体已被逐出我们的领地。果然，人们在接下来的一天左右慢慢好转。

column1: It has been about a year since we last sacrificed to Malia, goddess of disease. Do we wish to do so again, or do we risk angering her by ending the sacrifices?
column2: 距离我们上次向疾病女神玛利亚献祭大约一年了。我们是愿意再次献祭，还是冒险因终止献祭而激怒她？

column1: End the sacrifices.
column2: 终止献祭。

column1: We chose to cease our sacrifices to Malia, goddess of disease.
column2: 我们选择停止向疾病女神玛利亚献祭。

column1: Sacrifice again.
column2: 再次献祭。

column1: Resign yourself to annual propitiation.
column2: 接受每年安抚的宿命。

column1: We can’t afford to sacrifice any cows. Sacrifice nothing.
column2: 我们牺牲不起任何牛。什么都不献祭。

column1: We can afford to sacrifice a few more cows, but when do we stop?.
column2: 我们可以再牺牲几头牛，但何时停止呢？.

column1: We can afford to sacrifice some valuable trade items, but then what happens next year?
column2: 我们可以牺牲一些有价值的贸易品，但明年怎么办？

column1: We can’t afford to sacrifice any trade items now.
column2: 我们现在牺牲不起任何贸易品。

column1: Word will get out that we are propitiating the disease goddess. \x02\x03Our neighbors will shrink from contact with us./The respect and goodwill of our neighbors will flee from us./We will be reviled throughout Dragon Pass.\x02
column2: 消息会传出去，说我们在安抚疾病女神。 \x02\x03我们的邻居会避免与我们接触。/邻居们的尊重和善意会离我们而去。/我们将在整个龙之隘口被唾骂。\x02

column1: A sacrifice to Malia guarantees success, if you can keep on sacrificing enough.
column2: 向玛利亚献祭保证成功——只要你能持续献祭足够多。

column1: Every time we sacrifice to Malia, it makes things worse. But stopping the sacrifices is risky and requires reserves and fortitude.
column2: 每次我们向玛利亚献祭，情况都会变得更糟。但停止献祭也很危险，需要储备和毅力。

column1: Each time we sacrifice to Malia, she wants more. We must be brave, and stop while we still have some reserves left.
column2: 每次我们向玛利亚献祭，她要得就更多。我们必须勇敢，在还有储备时停下来。

column1: Malia is a Chaos goddess! I am appalled that we ever started sacrificing to her — and we must cease NOW!
column2: 玛利亚是混沌女神！我对我们竟然开始向她献祭感到震惊——我们必须现在停止！

column1: I must \x02\x03restrain myself from beating up the rest of the clan ring/find a priest and bash his head against a tree/smash the goods meant for Malia\x02 now.
column2: 我必须 \x02\x03克制自己不揍氏族议会的其他人/找个祭司，把他的头撞在树上/砸碎准备献给玛利亚的货物\x02 现在。

column1: We could avoid yearly arguments by just committing ourselves to an annual sacrifice.
column2: 我们可以通过承诺每年献祭来避免每年的争论。

column1: Sacrifice to Eurmal instead. At least he’d just \x02\x03send a pox of pillbugs on us/give us rashes in embarrassing places/make us all pass volumes of putrid gas\x02 before making us well again.
column2: 不如向尤尔马尔献祭。至少他只会 \x02\x03给我们送来一场潮虫瘟疫/让我们在尴尬的地方长皮疹/让我们都放出大量恶臭气体\x02 然后让我们康复。

column1: Bargains with Malia have a way of \x02\x03costing more than the sickness ever would/trapping those who make the sacrifice/spreading like an illness\x02.
column2: 与玛利亚的交易往往会 \x02\x03比疾病本身代价更高/困住献祭者/像疾病一样蔓延\x02。

column1: If we sacrifice to the disease goddess again, we will make things even harder for our neighbors; they will send priests to scold us.
column2: 如果我们再次向疾病女神献祭，会让邻居的日子更加难过；他们会派祭司来责怪我们。

column1: Maybe sacrificing to Malia will actually cost us cows in the long run.
column2: 也许向玛利亚献祭从长远来看反而会让我们损失牛只。

column1: Save the cows for Chalana Arroy. Then — then — aaaah — sacrifice them at her temple.
column2: 把牛留给查拉娜·阿罗伊。然后——然后——啊啊啊——在她的神殿献祭它们。

column1: I told you we’d be in trouble if we sacrificed to Malia!
column2: 我告诉过你们，如果我们向玛利亚献祭会有麻烦！

column1: Sacrifice to Malia is effective, but dangerous.
column2: 向玛利亚献祭有效，但危险。

column1: Sacrifice to Malia is a slippery slope indeed.
column2: 向玛利亚献祭确实是一条危险的滑坡。

column1: Sacrifice to Malia is a fools’s bargain — sometimes we should just suffer our fate as best we can, without calling on odd gods or spells.
column2: 向玛利亚献祭是傻瓜的交易——有时候我们只需尽力承受命运，而不必求助于怪异的神祇或法术。

column1: We were desperate, to sacrifice to Malia. Now we are made desperate by that sacrifice. We must suffer our fate as best we can, without recourse to this unholy goddess.
column2: 我们走投无路，才向玛利亚献祭。如今那场献祭却让我们陷入绝境。我们只能尽力承受命运，不再求助于这位不洁的女神。

column1: The carls, represented by \x01BI, are angry and dejected. “These sacrifices to Malia are \x02\x03exorbitant/extreme/outlandish\x02! More and more of our herds and crafts go to her every year. Sooner or later — and probably sooner — we will have no herds and no goods and die of disease or starvation anyway. What are you going to about this?”
column2: 以 \x01BI为代表的自由民们既愤怒又沮丧。“这些向玛利亚的献祭实在是 \x02\x03过分/极端/离谱\x02！每年我们越来越多的牲畜和手工品都给了她。迟早——而且很可能是很快——我们就会既无牲畜也无货物，终归死于疾病或饥饿。你打算怎么办？”

column1: \x01BI led a delegation of carls to renew their protest against the ever-increasing sacrifices to Malia.
column2: \x01BI 带领一队自由民再次抗议不断增加的向玛利亚的献祭。

column1: The carls, represented by \x01BI, are angry and disheartened. “The sacrifices to Malia are getting out of hand! An ever increasing portion of our herds and crafts go to her every year, and all we can see is that we will eventually have no herds and no goods and die of either disease or starvation anyway. What are you going to about this?”
column2: 以 \x01BI为代表的自由民们既愤怒又灰心。“向玛利亚的献祭已经失控了！每年我们越来越多的牲畜和手工品都给了她，而我们看到的只是最终我们会既无牲畜也无货物，终归死于疾病或饥饿。你打算怎么办？”

column1: \x01BI led a delegation of carls to protest the ever-increasing sacrifices to Malia.
column2: \x01BI 带领一队自由民抗议不断增加的向玛利亚的献祭。

column1: Love of our own wealth overcame the fear of plague. Though we trembled a bit, we chose to cease our sacrifices to Malia, goddess of disease.
column2: 对自身财富的眷恋战胜了对瘟疫的恐惧。尽管我们有些颤抖，但还是选择停止向疾病女神玛利亚献祭。

column1: Promise to increase raids and trade to enlarge our supply of wealth.
column2: 承诺增加劫掠和贸易以扩大我们的财富储备。

column1: The carls said that now we were adding the lives of clan members to the sacrifices. \x01BI said, “Malia gets our cattle, then our goods, then our lives — then what?” and stormed out, muttering disgustedly about Bad King Urgrain.
column2: 自由民们说现在我们是在把氏族成员的生命也加入献祭。 \x01BI 说：“玛利亚先要我们的牛，然后是我们的货物，然后是我们的命——然后呢？”然后愤然离去，厌恶地嘟囔着恶王乌格兰。

column1: Convince the carls to continue our sacrifices to Malia.
column2: 说服自由民们继续向玛利亚献祭。

column1: Sacrifice to Chalana Arroy to break Malia’s hold.
column2: 向查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭，以打破玛利亚的掌控。

column1: We sacrificed to Chalana Arroy, goddess of healing, hoping to break Malia’s grip on us.
column2: 我们向治愈女神查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭，希望能打破玛利亚对我们的钳制。

column1: Our god-talkers said that the signs were good; the merciful goddess took pity upon us and broke Malia’s hold on the clan.
column2: 我们的神言者们说，征兆是好的；慈悲女神怜悯了我们，打破了玛利亚对氏族的掌控。

column1: The people hoped that we had escaped from Malia’s greedy clutches. They sang praise songs for Chalana Arroy, who is kind enough to heal even people like us.
column2: 人们希望我们已经逃脱了玛利亚贪婪的魔爪。他们唱起赞美查拉娜·阿罗伊的颂歌，她如此仁慈，甚至愿意治愈像我们这样的人。

column1: Our god-talkers were disheartened, for the signs were bad; it was unlikely that Chalana Arroy had taken notice of our sacrifices. Or perhaps even the merciful goddess was too angry at our foolishness to help us now.
column2: 我们的神言者们灰心丧气，因为征兆不妙；查拉娜·阿罗伊似乎没有注意到我们的献祭。或者，就连慈悲女神也对我们曾经的愚蠢太过愤怒，不愿此时出手相助。

column1: The carls could afford to lose a few cows.
column2: 自由民们承受得起损失几头牛。

column1: We will need some more cows to keep up these sacrifices.
column2: 我们需要更多的牛来维持这些献祭。

column1: We will need more cows than we know to keep up these sacrifices.
column2: 我们需要多得超乎想象的牛来维持这些献祭。

column1: I would gladly sacrifice twice or thrice as many cattle to Chalana Arroy, if she could break Malia’s clutch on us.
column2: 如果查拉娜·阿罗伊能打破玛利亚对我们的钳制，我很乐意献上双倍甚至三倍的牛。

column1: I would happily part with all our trade goods to build a temple to Chalana Arroy, so we could beseech her to rescue us from our own folly.
column2: 我很乐意拿出所有贸易货物为查拉娜·阿罗伊建一座神殿，这样我们就能恳求她把我们从自身的愚蠢中拯救出来。

column1: Why not sacrifice to Chalana Arroy? Surely she could heal us of this foolishness.
column2: 为什么不向查拉娜·阿罗伊献祭？她一定能比我们这种愚蠢。

column1: Sacrifice to Malia is a fools’s bargain — we should suffer our fate as best we can, without recourse to odd gods or spells.
column2: 向玛利亚献祭是傻瓜的交易——我们应该尽力承受命运，不求助于怪异的神祇或法术。

column1: Sacrificing to Malia keeps plague away.
column2: 向玛利亚献祭能驱散瘟疫。

column1: Sacrificing to Malia keeps plague away — but what price success?
column2: 向玛利亚献祭能驱散瘟疫——但成功的代价是什么？

column1: If we would show Chalana Arroy more respect than we show Malia, she would help us out.
column2: 如果我们对查拉娜·阿罗伊比对玛利亚更加尊敬，她就会帮助我们。

column1: Bad King Urgrain offended good Orlanthi deities and befriended others who contributed to his clan’s destruction.
column2: 恶王乌格兰得罪了善良的奥兰斯诸神，却结交了那些最终导致他氏族毁灭的其他神祇。

column1: Bad King Urgrain talked an ally into sacrificing to Malia. They eventually had to sacrifice everything they owned and were forced to disband.
column2: 恶王乌格兰说服一位盟友向玛利亚献祭。他们最终不得不献出所有的一切，被迫解散。

column1: No one is listening. No one understands what I’ve been trying to tell them.
column2: 没人肯听。没人理解我一直想告诉他们的话。

column1: Malia is a Chaos goddess! I am disgusted that we ever sacrificed anything — but we must stop NOW!
column2: 玛利亚是混沌女神！我为我们竟然献祭过东西而深感厌恶——但我们必须现在停止！

column1: I told you propitiating Malia would bring trouble.
column2: 我告诉过你安抚玛利亚会招来麻烦。

column1: I told you we should stop sacrificing to Malia.
column2: 我告诉过我们应该停止向玛利亚献祭。

column1: Maybe a nice sacrifice to Eurmal would make him trick her into thinking some other clan is us. Then she could send the plague over there.
column2: 也许向尤尔玛尔献上一份好祭品，就能让他骗过她，让她以为另一个氏族是我们。这样她就会把瘟疫送到那边去。

column1: If we honored Chalana Arroy by, say, building a temple, we could ask her to stop this madness.
column2: 如果我们通过建造神殿等方式来尊崇查拉娜·阿罗伊，就能请求她终止这场疯狂。

column1: We have a beautiful temple to the healing goddess, Chalana Arroy. We must ask her to stop this madness.
column2: 我们有一座献给治愈女神查拉娜·阿罗伊的美丽神殿。我们必须请求她终止这场疯狂。

column1: \x02\x02A bargain with Malia is worse than the disease the bargain cures!/Chalana Arroy could and would cure this madness.\x02
column2: \x02\x02与玛利亚的交易比它治愈的疾病更糟！/查拉娜·阿罗伊能够也愿意治愈这种疯狂。\x02

column1: Our neighbors do not approve of our sacrifices to Malia — with each propitiation, their opinion worsens.
column2: 我们的邻居不赞同我们向玛利亚献祭——每一次安抚，他们对我们的看法就更糟一分。

column1: Save the cows for Chalana Arroy. Then — then — sacrifice them at her temple.
column2: 把牛留给查拉娜·阿罗伊。然后——然后——在她的神殿里献祭它们。

column1: I never thought I’d say this! Spend for a temple to Chalana Arroy. Then — ahem — sacrifice to her. Sacrifice — er, as mu — much as we need to stop this Malia thing.
column2: 我从没想过我会说这话！为查拉娜·阿罗伊建一座神庙。然后——咳咳——向她献祭。献祭——呃，尽我们所——需要多少就多少，来阻止这个玛利亚的破事。

Your nephew is the cause of our woe. He is drying my yields and starving the world. His name is Daga, the son of Molanni, your niece.”
column2: 厄纳尔达女祭司说出了厄纳尔达曾对奥兰斯说的话。“只有一个人在做这事，但我一直没告诉你，亲爱的丈夫，因为我知道你如此看重亲族情谊。” \x01@K 说着奥兰斯的话，并示意她继续。“遵从你的命令，哦，丈夫，我将挑起亲族争斗。你的侄子是我们苦难的根源。他正使我的收成干枯，让世界饥荒。他的名字是达加，莫兰尼之子，你的侄女。”

column1: \x01@\x12 summons the rest of the clan ring to discuss \x04 dream. “For the past week I’ve dreamed of strange warriors who dropped from the sky and defended Horseback Hill, at the edge of our tula, from invaders. They wore good armor and fought with gold-tipped spears. Each night they win, but each night there are more invaders. And tonight will be the seventh night.”
column2: \x01@\x12 召来氏族议会的其他成员，讨论 \x04 的梦。“过去一周，我不断梦见奇异武士从天而降，守护我们领地边界的马背山，抵御入侵者。他们身着精良铠甲，手持金尖长矛。每夜他们都获胜，但每夜入侵者都越来越多。而今晚将是第七夜。”

column1: \x01@\x12 had a recurring dream of warriors from the sky who defended a hill on our tula.
column2: \x01@\x12 做了一个反复出现的梦，梦见从天而降的武士守护着我们领地的一座山丘。

column1: “It’s just a dream.”
column2: “只是个梦罢了。”

column2: 人们并不完全确定，但多数人同意 \x01@N 的说法：有时梦并非神明所赐。

column2: \x01@N 当 \x06 说并非所有梦都来自神明时，遭到了嘲笑。

column1: Conduct a ritual to defeat the strange warriors.
column2: 举行仪式以击败那些奇异武士。

column1: The god-talkers hastily prepared a ritual to summon a great wind from Orlanth, to drive off the warriors.
column2: 神言者匆忙准备了一场仪式，从奥兰斯那里召唤一股强风，以驱散那些战士。

column1: \x01@\x12 dreamed that the warriors were blown far away, and landed on another tula. \x05 was not troubled by those dreams again.
column2: \x01@\x12 梦见那些战士被吹得很远，降落在另一个图拉领地上。 \x05 再也没有被那些梦境困扰。

column1: \x01@\x12 dreamed that the warriors drove off our wind with great gouts of flame from their spears, but then leaped back into the night sky. \x05 was not troubled by those dreams again.
column2: \x01@\x12 梦见那些战士用他们矛尖喷出的巨大火焰驱散了我们的风，但随后跳回夜空。 \x05 再也没有被那些梦境困扰。

column1: Conduct a ritual to help the strange warriors.
column2: 举行仪式帮助那些陌生的战士。

column1: The god-talkers hastily prepared a ritual to summon a great wind from Orlanth to aid the warriors.
column2: 神言者匆忙准备了一场仪式，从奥兰斯那里召唤一股强风以援助那些战士。

column1: That night \x01@\x12 dreamed that a vast horde of creatures swarmed up the hill.
column2: 那天晚上， \x01@\x12 梦见一大群生物涌上山丘。

column1: It was a close thing, but thanks to the mighty storm, the warriors drove off the attack.
column2: 真是险象环生，但多亏了强大的风暴，那些战士击退了进攻。

column1: The next morning, the god-talkers had new insights into the myth “\x01@\r.”
column2: 第二天早晨，神言者对神话“\x01@\r”有了新的领悟。

column1: The god-talkers dreamed of Elmal’s myths, but did not learn anything new.
column2: 神言者梦见了埃尔玛的神话，但没有学到任何新东西。

column1: Our wind helped, but the warriors from the stars drove off the attack only at the cost of their own lives.
column2: 我们的风起了作用，但来自星辰的战士只有牺牲自己的生命才击退了进攻。

column1: The people were pleased that we had given aid to warriors sent by Elmal.
column2: 人们很高兴我们援助了埃尔玛派来的战士。

column1: Send warriors to the ridge.
column2: 派遣战士到山脊。

column1: How many warriors do you send with \x01@\x12?
column2: 你派多少战士与 \x01@\x12同行？

column1: \x01@\x12 led a small war band to Horseback Hill, but found nothing unusual. \x05 decided to stay until the next morning. About the middle of the night, the warriors came streaming down from the stars, trailing bright sparks. No sooner had they landed than a howling mob of warriors charged up the other side of the hill at them.
column2: \x01@\x12 带领一支小型战帮前往马背山，但没有发现任何异常。 \x05 决定留到第二天早晨。大约在午夜时分，那些战士从星辰上倾泻而下，身后拖着明亮的火花。他们刚一落地，一群嚎叫的战士就从山的另一侧向他们发起冲锋。

column1: Help the star warriors.
column2: 帮助星辰战士。

column1: Our warriors helped defend Horseback Hill, and were blessed by Elmal.
column2: 我们的战士帮助保卫了马背山，并得到了埃尔玛的祝福。

column1: It was a desperate fight, but our warriors helped \x02\x03defend the hill/drive off the attack/repel the invaders\x02.
column2: 这是一场殊死搏斗，但我们的战士协助 \x02\x03守住了山丘/击退了进攻/驱逐了入侵者\x02。

column1: \x01@\x12 fought \x02\x02like a hero/tirelessly\x02.
column2: \x01@\x12 战斗 \x02\x02如英雄般/不知疲倦地\x02。

column1: \x01@\x11 of our warriors were wounded.
column2: \x01@\x11 我们的战士负伤。

column1: In the end, the invaders \x02\x02were slain/turned and fled\x02.
column2: 最终，入侵者 \x02\x02被杀死/转身逃窜\x02。

column1: Although none of the warriors from the sky spoke, it was clear to everyone present that their master, Elmal, would smile on us.
column2: 尽管天降战士无人开口，但在场所有人都明白，他们的主人埃尔马尔会向我们微笑。

column1: Join the attack on the star warriors.
column2: 加入对星之战士的攻击。

column1: \x01@\x12 led the charge up the hill, which drove the sky warriors back to where they came. However, \x06 was seriously burned by their flaming spears.
column2: \x01@\x12 率队冲上山丘，将天降战士赶回了他们来的地方。然而， \x06 被他们的火焰长矛严重烧伤。

column1: Our warriors helped drive the sky warriors off our tula. \x01@\x12 took a wound in the process.
column2: 我们的战士协助将天降战士赶出了我们的领地。 \x01@\x12 在此过程中负伤。

column1: Outnumbered, the sky warriors redoubled their efforts. They suffered losses of their own, but killed \x01@\x11 of our force, and seriously wounded \x01@\x12. At the end of the night, they still held the hilltop.
column2: 尽管寡不敌众，天降战士却加倍努力。他们自身也有损失，但杀死了我军的 \x01@\x11 人，并重伤了 \x01@\x12。到夜晚结束时，他们仍守住山顶。

column1: We were unable to drive the sky warriors back to the stars, though the dreams stopped.
column2: 我们未能将天降战士驱逐回星辰，尽管梦境停止了。

column1: Watch the fight.
column2: 观战。

column1: We sent warriors to the ridge, but they didn’t get involved.
column2: 我们派遣战士前往山脊，但他们没有介入。

column1: The sky warriors waited for us to join them, but when it was clear we were only there to watch,
column2: 天降战士等待我们加入他们，但当他们清楚我们只是在那里观望时，

column1: they charged into the massed foes, scattering them. Then they leaped back to the stars without a word.
column2: 他们冲入密集的敌人中，将其驱散。然后一言不发跃回星辰。

column1: We watched them defeat the invader, then leap back to the stars.
column2: 我们看着他们击败入侵者，然后跃回星辰。

column1: We watched them drive away the invaders, at the cost of their own lives.
column2: 我们看着他们驱逐入侵者，付出了生命的代价。

column1: In the morning there were only burnt patches on the grass.
column2: 清晨，草地上只剩下烧焦的斑块。

column1: Of course we must help warriors from the stars however we can!
column2: 当然，我们必须尽一切可能帮助来自星辰的战士！

column1: There is probably no way we can help each other.
column2: 我们可能无法互相帮助。

column1: If we help them, they may help us.
column2: 如果我们帮助他们，他们可能会帮助我们。

column1: These warriors are probably on Horseback Hill every night.
column2: 这些战士可能每晚都在马背山。

column1: I can take a small party to Horseback Hill. These warriors will be there again.
column2: 我可以带一小队人去马背山。这些战士还会在那里。

column1: We need to take some action, or the people will wonder why we ignore a message from the gods.
column2: 我们必须采取行动，否则人们会奇怪我们为何无视神明的讯息。

column1: These warriors were probably sent by our patron god, Elmal. We should help.
column2: 这些战士大概是我们守护神埃尔马尔派来的。我们应该帮助。

column1: Not all warriors are friends.
column2: 并非所有战士都是朋友。

column1: These warriors were sent by our patron god, Elmal. We need to help.
column2: 这些战士是我们守护神埃尔马尔派来的。我们必须帮助。

column1: Not all warriors are friends. But these are probably sent by Elmal.
column2: 并非所有战士都是朋友。但这些大概是埃尔马尔派来的。

column1: We don’t need help defending Horseback Hill!
column2: 我们不需要帮助防守马背山！

column1: To the hilltop!
column2: 上山丘顶！

column1: Even if this is a true dream, there is little we can do to change a dream.
column2: 即使这是一个真实的梦，我们也几乎无法改变一个梦。

column1: We cannot have strange warriors on our hilltops, which are sacred to Orlanth!
column2: 我们的山丘上不能有陌生战士，这些山丘是献给奥兰特的圣地！

column1: Just because they drive off dangerous foes does not mean they are our friends.
column2: 仅仅因为他们驱走了危险的敌人，并不意味着他们是我们的朋友。

column1: They are sent by Elmal to help us.
column2: 他们是埃尔马尔派来帮助我们的。

column1: If we have to help, we should come up with a plan that doesn’t involve sacrificing our wealth.
column2: 如果我们必须帮忙，应该想出一个不涉及牺牲我们财富的计划。

column1: This is surely a message from the gods.
column2: 这肯定是众神传来的讯息。

column1: Warriors fighting with Elmal’s gift, they are Elmal’s gift.
column2: 战士们带着埃尔马尔的赠礼作战，他们本身就是埃尔马尔的赠礼。

column1: If their spears are tipped with gold, we must sacrifice gold to help.
column2: 如果他们的矛尖镶金，我们就必须献祭黄金来帮忙。

column1: Help them.
column2: 帮助他们。

column1: If we help them, perhaps we can call them back later.
column2: 如果我们帮助他们，或许以后还能再召唤他们回来。

column1: Didn’t I say that Horseback Ridge was somehow special?
column2: 我不是说过马背岭有些特别吗？

column1: Sometimes dreams are just dreams. Sometimes if I drink enough, I don’t dream at all.
column2: 有时候梦只是梦。有时候我喝够了，就根本不做梦。

column1: If we help them, we will gain a powerful ally. With sky warriors at our side, we could even attack the forces of water.
column2: 如果我们帮助他们，就能得到一个强大的盟友。有天空武士相助，我们甚至可以攻击水的势力。

column1: Oskul dreamed that a fox was trapped by a fallen tree. In the dream he rescued it, and the next day an army of beast-folk offered to fight Bad King Urgrain at his side.
column2: 奥斯库尔梦见一只狐狸被倒下的树困住。在梦里他救了它，第二天一支兽人军队便主动提出要与他并肩作战，对抗恶王乌格兰。

column1: That troll attack a few days ago came from Horseback Hill. People are saying that the sky warriors were defending the tula, and we should have helped them.
column2: 几天前那次巨魔袭击是从马背山来的。人们都说那些天空武士是在保卫领地，我们本该帮他们的。

column1: \x01@\x12 calls the rest of the clan ring to discuss \x04 dream. “For the past week I’ve dreamed of a god-talker driving an ox cart with a statue of Orlanth. His companions wore no shirts and played horns and drums. But the oxen were from some foreign land, and the god-talker \x02\x04never took a breath/had volcanic blue eyes/sang in a strange language/looked like a man outlawed when I was a child\x02. When the cart gets to our boundary stones, I wake up. Tonight will be the seventh dream — we should do something.”
column2: \x01@\x12 召集氏族议会的其他成员讨论 \x04 的梦。“过去一周我梦见一个神言者赶着一辆牛车，车上载着一尊奥兰斯雕像。他的同伴们赤膊上阵，吹着号角，敲着鼓。但那些牛来自异乡，而那个神言者 \x02\x04从未换气/有火山般的蓝眼/用奇怪的语言歌唱/长得像我小时候被放逐的那个男人\x02。当牛车到达我们界石时，我就醒了。今晚将是第七次梦——我们该做点什么。”

column1: \x01@\x12 had a recurring dream of a strange god-talker driving an ox cart with a statue of Orlanth.
column2: \x01@\x12 反复梦见一个奇怪的神言者赶着牛车，车上载着一尊奥兰斯雕像。

column1: People weren’t entirely certain, but most agreed with \x01@N that sometimes dreams were not sent from the gods.
column2: 人们并不完全确定，但多数人赞同 \x01@N ，认为有时梦并非神所赐予。

column1: And indeed, \x06 did not have that dream again.
column2: 而确实， \x06 再也没有做过那个梦。

column1: Conduct a ritual to drive off the procession.

column2: 神言者们匆忙准备了一场仪式，召唤凶猛的 \x02\x02大地/岩石\x02 之灵来守卫我们的边界。

column1: \x01@\x12 dreamed that the oxen were terrified, and the god-talker abandoned the statue of Orlanth, showing that he was false. \x05 was not troubled by those dreams again.

column2: \x01@\x12 梦见那个奇怪的神言者发出一声号令，那些精灵便跪在奥兰斯雕像前。那队人马随即转身离去。 \x05 从此不再受这些梦困扰。

column1: next day, our temple to Orlanth was hit by lightning and burned to the ground.
column2: 二天，我们的奥兰斯神庙被闪电击中，烧为平地。

column1: People were angry that the ring had turned away Orlanth’s messengers.
column2: 人们因为长老会赶走了奥兰斯的信使而愤怒。

column1: Conduct a ritual to welcome the procession.
column2: 举行仪式迎接那队人马。

column1: The god-talkers hastily prepared a ritual, sacrificing an oxcart and all the accoutrements from the dream.
column2: 神言者们匆忙准备了一场仪式，献祭了一辆牛车和梦中所有的配备。

column1: That night, \x01@\x12 dreamed that \x06 drove our cart to meet them.
column2: 那夜， \x01@\x12 梦见 \x06 赶着我们的车去迎接他们。

column1: The strange god-talker gave the Greeting, and \x01@\x12 replied. The two then exchanged gifts.
column2: 那个奇怪的神言者行了问候礼， \x01@\x12 也回了礼。然后两人交换了礼物。

column1: \x01@\x12 can’t recall all of the dream, but the travellers headed on towards Stormwalk Mountain.
column2: \x01@\x12 记不清全部梦境，但那些旅人继续朝风暴行山进发。

column1: The next morning, our god-talkers had new insights into the myth “\x01@\r.”
column2: 第二天早晨，我们的神言者们对神话“\x01@\r”有了新的领悟。

column1: Our god-talkers dreamed of Orlanth’s myths. Although they did not learn new secrets, they said Orlanth had blessed the clan.
column2: 我们的神言者们梦见了奥兰斯的神话。虽然没有学到新的秘密，但他们说奥兰斯赐福了氏族。

column1: The strange procession veered off to the left. \x01@\x12 dreamed that they marched all the way around the tula, then departed. \x05 felt that we had been found wanting.
column2: 那队奇怪的人马向左转去。 \x01@\x12 梦见他们绕领地走了一圈，然后离开了。 \x05 觉得我们被发现有不足。

column1: Meet them at the boundary stones.
column2: 在界石处迎接他们。

column1: Who do you send to the edge of the tula?
column2: 你派谁去领地的边界？

column1: \x01@\x07 led a \x02\x02small group/few musically inclined clan members\x02 to the boundary stones, but found nothing unusual. \x05 decided to stay until the next morning.
column2: \x01@\x07 率领一队 \x02\x02少数几人/几个喜好音乐的族人\x02 来到界石处，但没有发现异常。 \x05 决定待到次日早晨。

column1: We sent \x01@\x07 to meet the ox cart at the edge of our tula.
column2: 我们派 \x01@\x07 去领地的边界迎接牛车。

column1: They exchanged the Greeting, and then gifts.
column2: 他们行了问候礼，然后交换了礼物。

column1: The two then ate and drank together.
column2: 然后两人一起吃喝。

column1: Afterwards, \x01@\x07 was stronger and tougher. \x05 seemed to move quicker, too.
column2: 之后， \x01@\x07 变得更强壮坚韧。 \x05 似乎也移动得更快了。

column1: The two then discussed various rituals.
column2: 然后两人讨论了各种仪式。

column1: Afterwards, \x01@\x07 was closer to the ways of the gods, and more sure casting magic.
column2: 之后， \x01@\x07 更接近神灵之道，施展魔法也更确信。

column1: Each of them then recited a poem they had composed.
column2: 然后他们各自朗诵了自己创作的诗。

column1: People listened more intently to \x01@\x07 afterwards, saying \x06 had been blessed by Orlanth.
column2: 之后人们更专心地听 \x01@\x07 讲话，说 \x06 得到了奥兰斯的祝福。

column1: But apart from that, \x01@\x07 found it hard to understand the outlandish language of the travellers. After much smiling and hand-waving, the procession left us, heading for Stormwalk Mountain.
column2: 但除此之外， \x01@\x07 很难理解那些旅人的异域语言。经过许多微笑和挥手示意后，那队人马离开了我们，朝风暴行山进发。

column1: I wonder where they are from? Those oxen don’t look like ours.
column2: 我好奇他们是从哪里来的？那些牛看起来不像我们的。

column1: They don’t seem on their way to raid us.
column2: 他们看起来不像是来袭击我们的。

column1: It doesn’t seem like they are a strong fighting force. But their magic surely makes up for that.
column2: 他们似乎不是一支强大的战斗力量。但他们的魔法肯定弥补了这一点。

column1: If they are Orlanthi, they will know the Greeting.
column2: 如果他们是奥兰斯信徒，他们应该知道问候礼。

column1: People aren’t going to worry about the dreams of ring members.
column2: 人们不会去担心长老会成员的梦境。

column1: If we do nothing, people will wonder why we ignore a message from the gods.
column2: 如果我们什么都不做，人们会疑惑我们为何忽视来自神明的讯息。

column1: Not all strange god-talkers are friends.
column2: 并非所有陌生的神言者都是朋友。

column1: These travellers were sent by our patron god, Orlanth. We need to help.
column2: 这些旅者是由我们的守护神奥兰斯派来的。我们必须提供帮助。

column1: These may be heroquesters, or spirits Orlanth is sending to test us. We should help.
column2: 这些可能是英雄探索者，或是奥兰斯派来考验我们的灵体。我们应当帮助。

column1: This one is obvious, I mean clear. Yes, we must… Orlanth says… A dream.
column2: 这个很明显，我是说清楚。是的，我们必须……奥兰斯说……一个梦。

column1: I don’t believe they mean us harm. I don’t know if they can help us.
column2: 我不认为他们有意伤害我们。我也不知道他们能否帮助我们。

column1: Maybe they are some sort of God Learner, trying to steal our secret knowledge!
column2: 也许他们是某种神明学者，想要窃取我们的秘密知识！

column1: At the very least, we should give these travellers hospitality.
column2: 至少，我们应当给予这些旅者好客之礼。

column1: If we have to help, we should think of a way that doesn’t involve sacrificing our wealth.
column2: 如果我们必须帮助，就该想个不用牺牲我们财富的办法。

column1: This is clearly a message from the gods.
column2: 这显然是一条来自神明的讯息。

column1: Let’s help.
column2: 我们去帮忙吧。

column1: This isn’t a very exciting dream. Not like some of the mushroom dreams I have.
column2: 这个梦不算很有看头。不像我那些蘑菇梦。

column1: We must fight them, either with magic or on our tula.
column2: 我们必须与他们战斗，要么用魔法，要么在我们的图拉领地上。

column1: The procession may be foreigners, but they are clearly worshippers of Orlanth. At the least, we can give the Greeting.
column2: 这支队伍可能是外国人，但他们显然是奥兰斯的信徒。至少我们可以行问候礼。

column1: I will go meet them.
column2: 我去见他们。

column1: Usually I have visions, not dreams. It still has meaning.
column2: 我通常看到的是幻象，不是梦。但它仍有意义。

column1: I will not be Bad King Urgrain, to turn away powerful guests.
column2: 我不会像恶王乌格兰那样，拒绝强大的客人。

column1: Dreams are almost always sent by the gods. The hard part is figuring out what they are trying to tell us.
column2: 梦几乎总是由神明送来的。难的是弄明白他们想告诉我们什么。

column1: has no horses.
column2: 没有马匹。

column2: 只有一匹马。

column1: Accept her offer.
column2: 接受她的出价。

column2: 我们争取了更好的交易。

column2: 少买几匹马。

column1: How many horses do you buy?
column2: 你买多少匹马？

column2: 我们决定只买她一部分昂贵的马匹。

column1: We declined her offer as too expensive.
column2: 我们因出价太高而拒绝了。

column1: \x01B} looked disappointed. “I’m sorry we couldn’t \x02\x02come to an agreement/make a deal\x02. I will keep looking for the cows I need.”
column2: \x01B} 显得很失望。“很抱歉我们未能 \x02\x02达成协议/达成交易\x02。我会继续寻找我需要的牛只。”

column1: People agreed that the deal would have harmed our herds, but pointed out that the clan needed the horses.
column2: 人们同意这笔交易本会损害我们的畜群，但也指出氏族需要马匹。

column1: People complained that the ring had lost an opportunity to replenish our stock of horses.
column2: 人们抱怨长老会错失了补充马匹储备的机会。

column1: \x01B} thought long and hard. “I suppose this is the only way I can get the cows I need. Very well.”
column2: \x01B} 深思熟虑。“我想这是我得到所需牛匹的唯一办法。好吧。”

column1: People realized that the clan needed the horses, but hoped that we would not be asked to repay the favor soon.
column2: 人们意识到氏族需要马匹，但希望我们不会很快被要求偿还这笔恩惠。

column1: People complained that the ring was only delaying the day of reckoning, and that \x01B} would soon return to collect on the favor.
column2: 人们抱怨长老会只是在拖延结算之日，而且 \x01B} 很快会回来收取恩惠。

column1: We suggested owing a favor, but \x01B} would not accept this.
column2: 我们提议欠一个人情，但 \x01B} 不愿接受。

column1: \x01B} said that she herself needed the cows, and was not acting on behalf of the \x01@! clan.
column2: \x01B} 说她本人需要这些牛，并非代表 \x01@! 氏族行事。

column1: People were \x02\x02pleased/glad\x02 that we had not had to pay more than the customary amount.
column2: 人们 \x02\x02高兴/开心\x02 我们没有支付超出惯例的数量。

column1: People weren’t happy that we had to pay so much, but agreed that the clan needed the horses.
column2: 人们对我们不得不付这么多钱而不满，但同意氏族需要马匹。

column1: People complained that the ring had given away too many cows \x02\x02so that they would be able to ride/rather than organizing trade caravans\x02.
column2: 人们抱怨长老会给出了太多牛只 \x02\x02好让他们能够骑马/而非组织商队\x02。

column1: We need cows more than we need horses.
column2: 我们更需要牛，而不是马。

column1: We don’t have enough horses to mount all our nobles and weaponthanes.
column2: 我们没有足够的马匹来配备所有贵族和武器领主。

column1: We are indeed desperate, and should take her deal.
column2: 我们确实很迫切，应当接受她的交易。

column1: We are in need of horses, but I think her price is excessive.
column2: 我们需要马匹，但我认为她的价格过高。

column1: I think I can get her to offer a more fair deal.
column2: 我想我能让她给出更公平的交易。

column1: We have enough warriors, so we don’t need to buy her horses.
column2: 我们有足够的战士，所以不需要买她的马。

column1: We need the horses so we can outfit more weaponthanes.
column2: 我们需要马匹，以便装备更多的武器领主。

column1: The people won’t be happy at the terms of this deal.
column2: 人们不会对这个交易条款感到满意。

column1: The people won’t like the terms of the deal, but our thanes need to ride.
column2: 人们不会喜欢交易条款，但我们的领主需要坐骑。

column1: This is not cheap, but at least it gets us the horses we need.
column2: 这不便宜，但至少让我们得到了需要的马匹。

column1: If we bargain with her, she will refuse to deal.
column2: 如果我们跟她讨价还价，她会拒绝交易。

column1: We should never have let ourselves get into this strait!
column2: 我们就不该让自己陷入这种困境！

column1: I trust our own traders more than this woman.
column2: 我更信任我们自己的商人，而不是这个女人。

column1: This is preposterous! If she needs the cows so much, she should be offering us a good deal, not a bad one.
column2: 这太荒谬了！如果她那么需要牛，她应该给我们一个好交易，而不是一个糟糕的。

column1: She has come all this way. We should buy something from her, no matter how dear.
column2: 她大老远来了。我们应该从她那里买点什么，不管多贵。

column1: Far better to take this offer than spend time and trouble getting a better deal.
column2: 接受这个提议，远好过花时间和麻烦去争取更好的条件。

column1: This sort of thing would never happen if we were in a tribe, and could ask tribe-mates for help.
column2: 如果我们在部落里，可以向族人求助，这种事就永远不会发生。

column1: Bad King Urgrain once sold his daughter-in-law for a war horse. The horse was struck by an arrow in the first battle, and threw Bad King Urgrain.
column2: 恶王乌格兰曾为了一匹战马卖掉自己的儿媳。那匹马在第一场战斗中被箭射中，把恶王乌格兰摔了下来。

column1: Traders from the \x01@! clan arrive with a huge book bound in exotic leather.
column2: 来自 \x01@! 氏族的商人到了，带着一本用异国皮革装订的巨大书籍。

column1: They say that it is called “Belintar’s Book,” and is a compilation of myths and legends written by the Pharaoh himself.
column2: 他们说这本书叫“贝林塔之书”，是法老亲手编写的神话传说合集。

column1: They offer to sell it for 80 cows worth of goods. When asked how they obtained it, they said it had been stolen from the Pharaoh, but would not offer details.
column2: 他们开价80头牛的货物出售。问他们如何得到这本书时，他们说是从法老那里偷来的，但不愿透露细节。

column1: \x01@! traders offered us the massive “Belintar’s Book,” which they claimed had been stolen from the Pharaoh.
column2: \x01@! 商人们向我们兜售巨大的“贝林塔之书”，声称是从法老那儿偷来的。

column1: We could not agree on a price we could afford.
column2: 我们无法就我们出得起的价格达成一致。

column1: We ended up being convinced it was worth more than their original offer.
column2: 我们最终被说服，认为它比最初的要价更值钱。

column1: \x01@\x12 said it was still a bargain.
column2: \x01@\x12 说这仍然很划算。

column1: The weaponthanes stare at \x01@\x03 in shock. Finally \x01@\r says, “Stealing from a guest would be a breach of hospitality. I will not be a party to violating Orlanth’s laws over a mere book.”
column2: 武器领主们震惊地盯着 \x01@\x03 。最后 \x01@\r说道：“从客人那里偷窃会有违好客之道。我不会为了一本书而参与违反奥兰斯律法的事。”

column1: The weaponthanes refused to take the book from guests when the ring asked them to.
column2: 当长老会要求武器领主们从客人手中夺取那本书时，他们拒绝了。

column1: Let the matter drop.
column2: 就此作罢。

column1: The other weaponthanes praised \x01@\r for staying true to Orlanth’s virtues.
column2: 其他武器领主称赞 \x01@\r 坚守了奥兰斯的德行。

column1: Repeat the order.
column2: 重复命令。

column1: \x01@\r refused again, and led the weaponthanes from the hall.
column2: \x01@\r再次拒绝，并带领武器领主们离开大厅。

column1: “Even so far from Heortland, the Pharaoh stirs up trouble,” said the \x01@! leader.
column2: “即使离赫特兰如此遥远，法老仍能惹出麻烦，” \x01@! 首领说。

column1: With that, they left.
column2: 说完，他们便离开了。

column1: Although some people thought we could have used the book against the Pharaoh somehow, people were content not to pay for it.
column2: 虽然有些人认为我们本可以用这本书以某种方式对付法老，但人们对于没花钱买它感到满意。

column1: We declined.
column2: 我们婉拒了。

column1: “We want nothing of the Pharaoh’s!”
column2: “我们不要法老的任何东西！”

column1: We told them, “We want nothing of the Pharaoh’s!”
column2: 我们告诉他们：“我们不要法老的任何东西！”

column1: They said, “We understand, though there is much to be said for knowing your enemy.” Some of our people thought we should have traded for the book to use against the Pharaoh somehow.
column2: 他们说：“我们理解，不过了解敌人总归有好处。”我们的一些人认为本应交易这本书，用来以某种方式对付法老。

column1: \x01@\x12 took charge of the book.
column2: \x01@\x12 接手了这本书。

column1: \x01@\x12 read the book carefully.
column2: \x01@\x12 仔细阅读了这本书。

column1: \x05 diligently read the volume. Between boasts of the Pharaoh’s knowledge and power were a large body of myths, most widely known to any boy or girl.
column2: \x05 勤奋地阅读了这部巨著。在法老知识与力量的吹嘘之间，有大量神话，大多数是任何一个男孩女孩都熟知的。

column1: The variant of “\x01@\r” was new to us.
column2: “\x01@\r”的变体版本对我们来说是新的。

column1: The version of “\x01@\r” was new to us.
column2: “\x01@\r”的版本对我们来说是新的。

column1: So was the retelling of “\x01@\r.”
column2: 也是“\x01@\r.”的复述。

column1: It was simply a collection of well-known stories.
column2: 这不过是知名故事的合集。

column1: None of the contents were very useful to us, though we kept the book with the clan treasures.
column2: 其中的内容对我们都没什么大用，不过我们还是把这本书收入了氏族宝库。

column1: \x05 found it confusing and useless.
column2: \x05 发现它令人困惑且毫无用处。

column1: \x05 found it a confusing collection of contradictory story fragments, in no particular order. If there was anything of value here, it would take another clan to decipher it.
column2: \x05 发现这是一本混乱的、自相矛盾的故事片段合集，毫无顺序可言。就算里面有什么有价值的东西，也得由另一个氏族来破译。

column1: \x05 found that it contradicted our myths, and was no longer sure of the right version.
column2: \x05 发现它与我们的神话相矛盾，不再确定哪个版本才是正确的。

column1: \x05 plunged into the work, reveling in the carefully annotated variants of a number of well-known myths. Unfortunately, these contradicted several we thought we had known, but could no longer be certain we knew the correct version of.
column2: \x05 一头扎进这本书，沉醉于许多知名神话中被精心注释的变体。不幸的是，这些变体与我们原本认为知道的几个神话相矛盾，我们不再能确定自己是否掌握正确的版本了。

column1: What an opportunity! At best, we will gain a weapon against the Pharaoh. At worst, it is a great treasure.
column2: 多么好的机会！往好处想，我们将获得一件对抗法老的武器。往坏处想，这也是一件了不起的宝物。

column1: The only question is whether we can save something on the exchange.
column2: 唯一的问题是我们能否在交易中省下点什么。

column1: This book is unique, so it is hard to put a value on it. But most treasures are worth at least 40 cows.
column2: 这本书独一无二，所以很难估价。但大多数宝物至少值40头牛。

column1: This book is unique, so it is hard to put a value on it. But most treasures are worth at least 50 cows.
column2: 这本书独一无二，所以很难估价。但大多数宝物至少值50头牛。

column1: We might learn new myths from a book that large.
column2: 这么大一本书，我们或许能学到新的神话。

column1: There are certainly new myths in this book. But if they were collected by the Pharaoh, are they good myths?
column2: 这本书里肯定有新神话。但如果是法老搜集的，那会是好神话吗？

column1: Ask if the book has any myths of how to kill elves.
column2: 问问这本书里有没有关于如何杀死精灵的神话。

column1: Does this book contain secrets of undead-slaying?
column2: 这本书是否包含杀死不死生物的秘密？

column1: We left our ancestral home because the Pharaoh ruined it. And so far, we have done quite well without his book.
column2: 我们离开祖地就是因为法老毁了它。到目前为止，没有他的书我们也过得不错。

column1: Orlanth is a thief in many stories. His thefts almost always benefit his people.
column2: 在许多故事里，奥兰斯是个盗贼。他的偷窃几乎总是造福于他的人民。

column1: What has reading ever done for us? But maybe we could drop it on our foes.
column2: 读书对我们有什么用？不过也许我们可以拿它砸向敌人。

column1: If the Pharaoh thinks it is important, then to us it is nothing.
column2: 如果法老觉得它重要，那对我们来说就一文不值。

column1: The Pharaoh is no better than any of us. If we needed a book like this, we would write it.
column2: 法老并不比我们任何人高明。如果我们需要这样一本书，我们自己就会写。

column1: How do we really know this was written by the Pharaoh?
column2: 我们怎么知道这真是法老写的呢？

column1: If this book was stolen, then they cannot complain if we take it from them.
column2: 如果这本书是偷来的，那我们把它从他们手里拿走，他们也没法抱怨。

column1: One man’s garbage is another man’s gold.
column2: 一个人的垃圾是另一个人的黄金。

column1: If only this were “The Book of Kings…”
column2: 要是这是《王者之书》就好了……

column1: We should pay whatever it takes to own a one-of-a-kind item like this!
column2: 我们应该不惜代价拥有这样一件独一无二之物！

column1: Nobody in the clan likes the Pharaoh. So they won’t want to have anything he made. On the other hand, if it’s stolen he probably wants it back. And if we had it, the Pharaoh wouldn’t. So that would be a good thing.
column2: 族中没人喜欢法老。所以他们不会想要他做的任何东西。另一方面，如果是偷来的，他大概会想找回去。而如果我们有了它，法老就没有了。所以那是件好事。

column1: I wonder if there any tales of dragonewts in that thing? You don’t think it’s bound in dragonhide, do you?
column2: 我在想那东西里有没有龙人的故事？你不会觉得它是用龙皮装订的吧？

column1: “Not all knowledge can be bound in leather.”
column2: “并非所有知识都能被皮革装订。”

column1: I’m sure there are myths in there that would make us lose sleep if we read them.
column2: 我敢肯定里面有神话，读了会让我们失眠。

column1: Now we’re going to get blamed for stealing the book, no matter what we do.
column2: 现在我们会被指责偷了书，不管我们做什么。

column1: Think of this book as part of our tribal regalia! Other clans will want to join.
column2: 把这本书看作我们部落的徽记！其他氏族会想加入的。

column1: Think of this book as part of our tribal regalia some day!
column2: 总有一天这本书会成为我们部落的徽记！

column1: Southerners come to your tula, claiming to be agents of the Pharaoh, the tyrannical ruler your people fled when you came to this land. They appear to be sorcerers; at the very least, those strange implements they carry are probably magical weapons.
column2: 南方人来到你们的领地，自称是法老的代理人——那位你们族人逃到这片土地时所逃离的暴虐统治者。他们看起来像是巫师；至少，他们携带的那些奇怪器具很可能是魔法武器。

column1: The Pharaoh’s sorcerers came to us looking for “Belintar’s Book,” a large tome which they say was stolen from the Pharaoh.
column2: 法老的巫师来找我们，寻找“贝林塔之书”，一本他们说法老被盗走的巨著。

column1: They are looking for “Belintar’s Book,” a large tome which they say was stolen from the Pharaoh.
column2: 他们在寻找“贝林塔之书”，一本他们说法老被盗走的巨著。

column2: ……把这本书给了你

column2: “我们见过那本书，但没拿到。”

column1: “Hah! Your shallow minds are open to us.”

column2: “是 \x01E) 氏族。”

column2: 你告诉他们哪个氏族拿了书？

column2: 我们撒了谎，告诉他们 \x01@! 把书给了我们。

column2: 我们告诉他们 \x01@! 把书给了我们，虽然我们从未见过。

column2: “我们买了它，但可以卖给你。”

column2: “我们大老远来不是跟野蛮人讨价还价的。把书给我们。”

column2: 我们提出出售，但他们坚持要拿走。

column1: “I know you have two eggs. I want them back. Now.”
column2: “我知道你们有两颗蛋。我要拿回来。现在。”

column1: A duck named \x01B~ who claimed to be a Humakti Deathlord stalked into the tula, demanding the duck eggs we had traded for.
column2: 一只名叫 \x01B~ 的鸭子，自称是胡马克特的死亡领主，大步走进图拉领地，索要我们交易得来的鸭蛋。

column1: “We don’t have them.”
column2: “我们没有。”

column1: “Don’t think you can lie to a Humakti. Or maybe you’re just \x02\x02idiots/muttonheads\x02. Hurry it up and give back the eggs.”
column2: “别以为你能对胡马克提说谎。也许你只是 \x02\x02蠢货/木头脑袋\x02。快点把蛋还回来。”

column1: We told \x01B~ we didn’t have the eggs, but he called us names and repeated his demand.
column2: 我们告诉 \x01B~ 我们没有蛋，但他辱骂我们并重复了他的要求。

column1: Give them back.
column2: 把它们还回去。

column1: We gave them back.
column2: 我们把它们还回去了。

column1: Without a word of thanks, \x01B~ and his companions tenderly took the eggs, and left.
column2: 没有一句感谢， \x01B~ 和他的同伴们小心翼翼地拿起蛋，离开了。

column1: Sell them back.
column2: 把它们卖回去。

column1: “You featherless types are as stupid as you look. I didn’t come here to haggle like a pig farmer at the slop market. Let me use short words: give back the eggs.”
column2: “你们这些没毛的家伙跟外表一样蠢。我不是来这儿像猪农在泔水市场讨价还价的。用简短的话说：把蛋还回来。”

column1: When we offered to trade the eggs, \x01B~ insulted us.
column2: 当我们提出交易这些蛋时， \x01B~ 侮辱了我们。

column1: A shame we never got to see them hatch into duckling-folk.
column2: 可惜我们没能看到它们孵出鸭人。

column1: We paid \x01E+ cows for those eggs.
column2: 我们付了 \x01E+ 牛只买下这些蛋。

column1: He has no legal claim against us.
column2: 他对我们没有法律诉讼权。

column1: \x01B~ may be a duck, but he is still a Deathlord.
column2: \x01B~ 也许是个鸭子，但他仍是一位死亡领主。

column1: We paid \x01E+ cows for those eggs. We’re certainly not giving them back because some sword-waving duck asks us to.
column2: 我们付了 \x01E+ 牛只买下这些蛋。我们当然不会因为某个舞剑的鸭子开口要就还回去。

column1: Some duck-lady must be wishing she had her brood back.
column2: 某位鸭女士一定在希望她找回自己的那一窝。

column1: This is not a very funny duck. Let’s see if we can make him laugh.
column2: 这只鸭子真不好笑。看看我们能不能让他笑一笑。

column1: I have heard of this \x01B~. He is a tireless fighter against the unquiet dead.
column2: 我听说过这位 \x01B~。他是对抗不安死者的不懈斗士。

column1: He may call himself a Humakti, but he is still just a duck.
column2: 他可以自称胡马克提，但他仍不过是一只鸭子。

column1: We should not lie to him.
column2: 我们不应该对他说谎。

column1: “A duck may be somebody’s mother.”
column2: “一只鸭子也许是谁的母亲。”

column1: Give him the eggs as a gift.
column2: 把蛋当作礼物送给他。

column1: A duck of few words.
column2: 一只寡言的鸭子。

column1: I told you we should not have bought the eggs.
column2: 我告诉过我们不该买这些蛋。

column1: If they are not to be clan treasures, we should get wealth we can trade for another treasure.
column2: 如果它们不能成为氏族宝藏，我们应该换取可以交易另一件宝藏的财富。

column1: Clearly it is time to attack the ducks, if they think they can just waddle in and make demands of us.
column2: 显然现在是进攻鸭子的时候了，如果他们以为可以摇摇摆摆走进来对我们提要求。

column1: Our ancestors fought long and hard against King of the Beastmen. And the ducks are counted among the beastmen.
column2: 我们的祖先曾与兽人之王长期苦战。而鸭子被算在兽人之中。

column1: The ducks are beast-folk. They were not the foe of our ancestors.
column2: 鸭子是兽人。他们并非我们祖先的敌人。

column1: \x01B~ closed his eyes, then drew one of his swords and held it above his head with both hands. He began a croaking song that somehow reverberated from the rafters.
column2: \x01B~ 闭上了眼睛，然后拔出一把剑，双手高举过头。他开始唱起一首嘎嘎作响的歌，那歌声竟从椽木间回荡开来。

column1: \x01B~ began singing a ritual song.
column2: \x01B~ 开始唱一首仪式歌。

column1: When \x01B~ opened his eyes, there was a hero light in them.
column2: 当 \x01B~ 睁开眼睛时，眼中闪烁着英雄之光。

column1: When \x01B~ began singing a ritual song, we attacked.
column2: 当 \x01B~ 开始唱仪式歌时，我们发起了攻击。

column1: Without opening his eyes, \x01B~ opened the belly of the first warrior who rushed him.
column2: 没有睁开眼睛， \x01B~ 劈开了第一个冲向他战士的肚子。

column1: Give back the eggs.
column2: 把蛋还回来。

column1: When \x01B~ began singing, we gave back the eggs.
column2: 当 \x01B~ 开始唱歌时，我们把蛋还了回去。

column2: \x01B~ 停止了唱歌，但没有收剑入鞘。

column1: Without a word of thanks, his companions tenderly took the eggs, and left. \x01B~ did not put away his sword until he had killed one of our cows as they crossed a meadow on their way towards the marsh.
column2: 没有一句感谢，他的同伴们小心翼翼地拿起蛋，离开了。 \x01B~ 直到他们穿过一片草地走向沼泽时杀死我们的一头牛，才收起剑。

column1: After that, it was hard to keep track of just what happened. \x01B~ seemed to be surrounded by a fog of blood, slashing and stabbing everywhere with two swords. His two companions were no match for us, but nobody could even wound \x01B~ until \x01@\x17 took him out with a blow to the head.
column2: 之后，很难弄清楚到底发生了什么。 \x01B~ 似乎被一片血雾笼罩，双剑四处劈刺。他的两个同伴不是我们的对手，但没有人能伤到 \x01B~ 分毫，直到 \x01@\x17 一击命中头部将他击倒。

column1: \x01B~ killed and wounded many of our warriors.
column2: \x01B~ 杀死并打伤了我们许多战士。

column1: Then \x01@\x17 looked down in surprise at a gaping wound to \x04 side and collapsed.
column2: 然后 \x01@\x17 惊讶地低头看着 \x04 身侧一道裂开的伤口，倒了下去。

column1: Finally, \x01@\x17 killed him, but was seriously wounded in turn.
column2: 最终， \x01@\x17 杀死了他，但自己也受了重伤。

column1: Finally, \x01@\x17 killed him, but was seriously injured and died of \x04 wound.
column2: 最终， \x01@\x17 杀死了他，但受了重伤并因 \x04 伤口而死。

column1: Hospitality is one of our oldest virtues. We cannot attack a guest.
column2: 好客是我们最古老的美德之一。我们不能攻击客人。

column1: That is not just a song, it is part of a ritual.
column2: 那不仅仅是首歌，而是仪式的一部分。

column1: That is not just a song, it is part of a Humakti ritual.

column1: Think of the ducklings!
column2: 想想小鸭子们！

column2: 他正在开始他的死亡之歌。死亡将行于这座厅堂。

column1: Death will stalk the hall.
column2: 死亡将潜行在厅堂中。

column1: That is the worst singing I have ever heard!
column2: 这是我听过最糟的歌声！

column1: We must kill him before he kills.
column2: 我们必须在他杀人之前杀了他。

column1: We have already made our decision.
column2: 我们已经做了决定。

column1: Oh no!
column2: 哦不！

column1: We have to! Right now!
column2: 我们必须！立刻！

column1: What he really wants are the eggs.
column2: 他真正想要的是这些蛋。

column1: This is all my fault.
column2: 这都是我的错。

column1: I hope someone is writing down that song.
column2: 我希望有人在记下那首歌。

column1: Ask him to put away the sword first.
column2: 先让他收起剑。

column1: Hospitality is sacred. The gods would not forgive us if we harm a guest.
column2: 好客是神圣的。如果我们伤害客人，众神不会原谅我们。

column1: Just give him what he came for.
column2: 就把他要的东西给他吧。

column1: I told you to give him the eggs.
column2: 我告诉过你把蛋给他。

column1: No sense of humor at all. And why is he holding Death like that?
column2: 完全没有幽默感。再说他为什么那样握着死亡？

column1: What is he squawking? “I am the one called Humakt’s Wrath. I brought strife and clamor to my enemy.” That sounds familiar…
column2: 他在嘎嘎叫什么？“我名为‘胡马克特之怒’。我给我的敌人带来纷争与喧嚣。”这听起来有点耳熟……

column1: People were unhappy that the clan ring had decided to trade for the duck eggs in the first place.

column1: “Refund the \x01E+ cows worth of goods we paid.”
column2: “退还我们支付的价值 \x01E+ 头牛的货物。”

column1: Issaries.
column2: 伊萨里斯。

column1: Nor had we asked.
column2: 我们也没有要求过。

column2: “退还我们支付的一半。”

column2: “我们要回我们的宝物。”

column1: Finally, \x01@\x08 denied our claim.

column1: Normally a deal is a deal.

column1: Not bad.
