column2: 一场猎熊大行动开始了。它带着我们东奔西跑，但最终还是被逼入绝境。它咬伤了我们三名战士后才死去。我们将它的毛皮挂在部族大厅里展示。

column1: After it died, the bear turned into a man.
column2: 那头熊死后，变成了一个人。

column1: We could not identify what clan he was from, so we buried him with due honor. People worried that we might be cursed for killing a bearwalker.
column2: 我们无法辨认他来自哪个氏族，于是以应有的荣誉安葬了他。人们担心我们可能因杀死熊行者而遭受诅咒。

column1: \x01@\x0F said that Odayla was pleased that we had hunted the bear in his honor.
column2: \x01@\x0F 据说奥达亚很高兴我们以他的名义猎杀了那头熊。

column1: Our hunters tracked the bear for days, but it seemed to realize it was being stalked, and would not allow them to close, even when they worked Odayla’s magics.
column2: 我们的猎人追踪那头熊数日，但它似乎意识到自己被跟踪，即便他们施展了奥达亚的魔法，也不让他们靠近。

column1: Purify the shed.
column2: 净化棚屋。

column1: The women of the clan held a ritual that lasted for three days. The men back home heard drumming and singing, and at one point could make out green smoke.
column2: 氏族的女人们举行了一场持续三天的仪式。在家的男人们听到了鼓声和歌声，一度还看到了绿色的烟雾。

column1: Finally the women returned to their husbands.
column2: 最终女人们回到了她们的丈夫身边。

column1: The women purified their shed in a three-day ritual.
column2: 女人们通过三天仪式净化了她们的棚屋。

column1: The women returned in foul moods. It was clear that the goddesses were not pleased.
column2: 女人们回来时心情恶劣。显然女神们并不高兴。

column1: The women attempted to purify their shed, but the ritual was not a great success.
column2: 女人们试图净化她们的棚屋，但仪式并不很成功。

column1: Find suitable ritual items to replace those destroyed.
column2: 寻找合适的仪式物品来替代那些被毁的。

column1: First, the clan traders obtained rare and unusual goods. Then
column2: 首先，氏族的商人们获得了稀有罕见的货物。然后

column1: our crafters made some \x02\x02lovely/gorgeous\x02 items that captured the spirit of those that had been destroyed. People were pleased.
column2: 我们的工匠制作了一些 \x02\x02精美的/华丽的\x02 物品，它们捕捉到了被毁物品的神韵。人们很满意。

column1: We made new ritual items to replace those the bear had destroyed.
column2: 我们制作了新的仪式物品来替代那些被熊毁掉的。

column1: our crafters spent days trying to recreate some of the destroyed items. They felt they had not captured the inspiration of the originals.
column2: 我们的工匠花了数日尝试重现一些被毁的物品。他们觉得没有捕捉到原件的灵感。

column1: We made new ritual items, but they couldn’t replace those the bear had destroyed.
column2: 我们制作了新的仪式物品，但它们无法替代那些被熊毁掉的。

column1: Sacrifice to Odayla, god of hunting and bears.
column2: 向狩猎与熊之神奥达亚献祭。

column1: We sacrificed to Odayla.
column2: 我们向奥达亚献祭了。

column1: The god of bears ensured that the bear troubled us no more.
column2: 熊之神确保那熊不再骚扰我们。

column1: Although we sacrificed to the god of bears, the bear continued to prowl our tula for several weeks, causing more mischief and making off with some stored food.
column2: 尽管我们向熊之神献祭了，那头熊仍在我们的图拉领地游荡了数周，造成了更多麻烦，还偷走了一些储存的食物。

column1: Leave offerings to the bear.
column2: 向熊献上祭品。

column1: \x01@N carefully placed several caches of food, getting larger towards the edges of our tula. The bear seemed satisfied with devouring them, and caused no more trouble.
column2: \x01@N 我们精心放置了几处食物储藏点，越靠近领地边缘规模越大。熊似乎很享受狼吞虎咽这些食物，没再制造更多麻烦。

column1: We lured the bear away from our settlement by leaving food for it.
column2: 我们留下食物将熊引离定居点。

column1: Although we left caches of food far from our settlements, eating them only seemed to encourage the bear. It continued to prowl our tula for several weeks, causing more mischief and making off with some stored food.
column2: 尽管我们在远离定居点的地方放置了食物储藏点，熊吃掉它们后反而变本加厉。它继续在我们领地上徘徊数周，制造更多祸端，还偷走了一些储备粮。

column1: The carls complained that the ring was not concerned with their problems. The bear was spotted a few more times, but then didn’t return.
column2: 自由民抱怨长老会不关心他们的疾苦。那熊又被目击了几次，但随后便未再返回。

column1: The bear continued to prowl our tula for several weeks, causing more mischief and making off with some stored food.
column2: 熊继续在我们领地上徘徊数周，制造更多祸端，还偷走了一些储备粮。

column1: The carls complained that the ring should have listened to clear warnings.
column2: 自由民抱怨长老会本该听取明确的警示。

column1: Bears are sacred to Odayla. We should hunt it to honor him.
column2: 熊是欧达伊拉的圣兽。我们该猎杀它来荣耀他。

column1: The magic of all our women could be endangered.
column2: 我们所有女性的魔法都可能陷入危险。

column1: This mighty creature won’t be easy to track down.
column2: 这头强大的生灵可不好追踪。

column1: If we sacrifice to Odayla, he will protect us from his creatures.
column2: 如果我们向欧达伊拉献祭，他将庇佑我们免受他的造物所害。

column1: It’s hard to know if this will affect our fertility magic if we ignore it.
column2: 若我们置之不理，很难说这是否会影响我们的丰收魔法。

column1: It’s hard to know for sure, but this probably won’t affect our fertility magic.
column2: 确切结论尚难知晓，但这大概不会影响我们的丰收魔法。

column1: A bear can be a threat to more than just the sacred shed. It’s clearly after food.
column2: 熊的威胁可不止于圣棚。它明摆着是冲着食物来的。

column1: There are many stories of bearwalkers, who live in the wilderness and transform into bears, prowling the woods and hills.
column2: 关于熊行者的传说很多——他们栖身荒野，化作熊形，在树林与山丘间游荡。

column1: Honey-thief plunders Esra’s gold-store. Winter-sleeper should gift us.
column2: 偷蜜贼劫掠艾斯拉的金库。冬眠者理当馈赠我们。

column1: “The farmer grows the barley, but the bear eats it.”
column2: “农夫种大麦，熊却来吃它。”

column1: If that is a male bear, it has no business anywhere near that shed.
column2: 如果那是头公熊，它根本不该靠近那个棚子。

column1: If the women took better care of their ritual items, this sort of thing wouldn’t happen.
column2: 要是女人们把仪式用品保管得更好些，这种事就不会发生。

column1: I knew stockpiling food out away from the settlement was a bad idea.
column2: 我就知道在定居点外囤积食物是个馊主意。

column1: The poor thing is just hungry.
column2: 那可怜的家伙只是饿了。

column1: \x01@\x07 reports that while she was gathering food in the woods, a tree snatched up her daughter, and she was barely able to rescue her in time. When she led a group of warriors and god-talkers back, they conducted a ritual and learned that the tree spirit demanded a human sacrifice, but in turn would gift us with either magic or food. It insisted that only a human life would do.
column2: \x01@\x07 报告称，她在林间采集食物时，一棵树掳走了她的女儿，她险些没能及时救回。当她带了一队战士和神言者返回时，他们举行了仪式，得知树灵要求活人献祭，但作为回报，会赐予我们魔法或食物。树灵坚称只有一条人命才够分量。

column1: A tree spirit deep in the woods demanded a human sacrifice, offering magic or food in exchange.
column2: 森林深处的一个树灵要求活人献祭，以魔法或食物作为交换。

column1: Tell people to avoid the area.
column2: 告示众人避开该区域。

column1: Everyone gave the tree a wide berth from then on.
column2: 从那以后，每个人都远远避开那棵树。

column1: The hunters weren’t happy, but took this in stride.
column2: 猎人们不太高兴，但坦然接受了。

column1: Sacrifice a thrall.
column2: 献祭一名奴隶。

column1: What do you ask for in return?
column2: 你要求什么回报？

column1: “Give us magic.”
column2: “赐予我们魔法。”

column1: Grimly, the god-talkers sacrificed a thrall to the tree. They were cheered somewhat when they determined that the spirit had in fact given the clan magic.
column2: 神言者们阴沉着脸，向树献祭了一名奴隶。当他们确定树灵确实赐予了氏族魔法时，情绪稍微好了些。

column1: “Give us food.”
column2: “赐予我们食物。”

column1: Grimly, the god-talkers sacrificed a thrall to the tree.
column2: 神言者们阴沉着脸，向树献祭了一名奴隶。

column1: Hunters and gatherers brought in a windfall of food.
column2: 猎人和采集者带来了大量食物。

column1: Not long after, hunters brought in much game, including animals seldom seen on our tula. Fruits and berries appeared out of season, and edible mushrooms were everywhere.
column2: 不久后，猎人们打到了大量猎物，包括我们领地上罕见的动物。反季节的水果和浆果出现了，可食用的蘑菇随处可见。

column1: Sacrifice a clan member.
column2: 献祭一名氏族成员。

column1: Grimly, the god-talkers sacrificed an elderly carl to the tree. They were cheered somewhat when they determined that the spirit had in fact given the clan magic.
column2: 神言者们阴沉地，将一名老年自由民献祭给了那棵树。当他们确定那树灵确实赐予了氏族魔法时，总算稍微振作了一些。

column1: Grimly, the god-talkers sacrificed an elderly carl to the tree.
column2: 神言者们阴沉地，将一名老年自由民献祭给了那棵树。

column1: Conduct a ritual of protection.
column2: 举行一场保护仪式。

column1: The god-talkers said that they had driven out the tree spirit.
column2: 神言者们说，他们已将树灵驱逐出去。

column2: 神言者们无法保证我们不会再听到那树灵的消息。

column1: Send a party to chop down the tree.

column2: 我们派了一队人去砍倒那棵树。

column1: It took several days to locate the tree, but \x01@\x08 persisted. One man almost took off his own foot with an axe, and the tree managed to snatch up \x01@\x08 and battered \x08 severely with its branches before dropping \x08 from a great height. When the tree finally toppled, it somehow managed to crush one of the party.
column2: 花了好几天才找到那棵树的位置，但 \x01@\x08 坚持了下去。有一个人差点用斧头砍掉自己的脚，那棵树还设法一把攫住 \x01@\x08 ，用树枝猛击 \x08 数次，然后才将 \x08 从高处扔下。当树终于倒下时，它不知怎么竟压死了队中一人。

column1: We regretted the cost, but people were glad that this menace no longer grew on our tula.
column2: 我们为付出的代价感到遗憾，但人们很高兴这祸患不再生长在我们的领地上。

column1: \x01@\x01 held up \x04 axe and swore, “This is just the first blow.”
column2: \x01@\x01 高举 \x04 斧头发誓：“这只是第一击。”

column1: They returned with \x01@\x07 but had no better luck.
column2: 他们带着 \x01@\x07 回来了，但运气并未好转。

column1: \x01@\x01 said, “It is another trick of the elves,” and many people agreed with \x08.
column2: \x01@\x01 说：“这是精灵的又一个诡计。”许多人都附和 \x08。

column1: The people were afraid.
column2: 人们感到恐惧。

column1: If we avoid the tree, our hunters will have less land to hunt on.
column2: 如果我们避开那棵树，我们的猎人就少了可以狩猎的土地。

column1: It can’t be that hard to kill a tree.
column2: 砍倒一棵树能有多难。

column1: It can’t be that hard to kill a tree. Unless it’s a war tree planted by the elves.
column2: 砍倒一棵树能有多难。除非那是精灵种下的战争之树。

column1: Sacrificing a human life is extreme.
column2: 献祭一条人命太过极端。

column1: Sacrificing a human life is extreme, but if it is not to a Chaos deity, can sometimes be acceptable.
column2: 献祭一条人命太过极端，但只要不是献给混沌神祇，有时也可以接受。

column1: Doing nothing is not an option. People won’t stand for children being killed.
column2: 无所作为不是办法。人们不能容忍孩子被杀。

column1: Spirits sometimes lie, though it clearly does want a sacrifice.
column2: 神灵有时会说谎，不过它确实明显想要一个祭品。

column1: This spirit can probably be trusted to fulfill its promise. It is old and well-rooted, so I’m not sure a ritual would have much effect in its grove.
column2: 这个灵大概可以信守承诺。它古老且根深蒂固，我不确定在它的树丛里举行仪式会有多大作用。

column1: If we avoid the tree, gatherers like \x01@\x07 will have less land to forage on.

column1: We could use the food right now. And if we avoid the tree, gatherers like \x01@\x07 will have less land to forage on.
column2: 我们现在就需要食物。如果我们避开那棵树，像 \x01@\x07 这样的采集者就少了可以搜寻食物的地方。

column1: I don’t know if this is a dire enough situation that human sacrifice is warranted. It might be.
column2: 我不知道情况是否严重到值得进行人祭。也许确实如此。

column1: Killing is not the answer.
column2: 杀戮不是答案。

column1: This tree might not be easy to find.
column2: 这棵树可能不容易找到。

column1: We must protect our children.
column2: 我们必须保护我们的孩子。

column1: What if this very longhouse were made of the logs of such an evil tree? We could all be in danger!
column2: 万一这座长屋就是用那种邪恶之树的原木建造的呢？我们所有人都可能身处危险！

column1: I can’t find anything funny about this. But chopping it down sounds like fun.
column2: 我一点也不觉得这事好笑。但砍倒它听起来倒是挺有趣的。

column1: Sometimes the situation really does call for a sacrifice.
column2: 有时情况确实需要献祭。

column1: How can we consider killing one of our own? Has this clan come to that?
column2: 我们怎么能考虑杀死自己人？这个氏族已经沦落至此了吗？

column1: If we leave the tree alone, maybe it will leave us alone.
column2: 如果我们不招惹那棵树，也许它也不会招惹我们。

column1: \x01@\x07 has done us a great favor by locating one of the trees of evil, planted by the elves. Our axes can now strike a mighty blow against them!
column2: \x01@\x07 为我们立了大功，找到了精灵种下的一棵邪恶之树。现在我们的斧刃可以狠狠打击它们了！

column1: A woman from the \x01@! clan comes to sell us some thralls. “I will give you five thralls in exchange for as much magic as clans give when they repay a favor.”
column2: 一名来自 \x01@! 氏族的女子来向我们出售一些奴隶。“我用五个奴隶换取与氏族回报恩惠时等量的魔法。”

column1: A woman from the \x01@! clan came to sell us thralls in exchange for magic.
column2: 一名来自 \x01@! 氏族的女子来向我们出售奴隶，换取魔法。

column1: Accept her offer
column2: 接受她的提议

column1: She performed a ritual involving much \x02\x02rattling and yarn/dancing and yipping\x02, taking a portion of our clan magic.
column2: 她举行了一场仪式，其中涉及大量 \x02\x02咔嗒声与纱线/舞蹈与尖啸\x02，取走了我们的一部分氏族魔法。

column1: We accepted her deal.
column2: 我们接受了她的交易。

column1: Since our ancestors frowned upon taking thralls, the clan was happy that we had found a way to free some.
column2: 由于我们的祖先不赞成蓄奴，氏族很高兴我们找到了释放一些人的办法。

column1: Then we freed the thralls to become cottars in our clan.
column2: 然后我们释放了那些奴隶，让他们成为氏族中的佃农。

column1: Since our ancestors had taken thralls, the clan was happy that we were, too.
column2: 由于我们的祖先曾蓄养奴隶，氏族也很高兴我们同样这样做。

column2: 我们谈到了一个更好的价钱，接受了 \x01@\x14 个奴隶。

column2: 她举行了一场仪式，其中涉及 \x02\x02大量饮酒/长时间击鼓\x02，取走了我们的一部分氏族魔法。

column1: We asked for a better deal.
column2: 我们要求更好的条件。

column1: The attempt to bargain inflamed her. “You think I am a liar? That when I say I can afford to give five thralls, I can really afford six? We have been here a long time, much longer than anyone else, and where we come from, we call that disrespectful, and the shadow birds are chirping, chirping…” Her voice trailed off, then she closed one eye and looked at the clan chieftain. “You will regret this,” she said.
column2: 讨价还价激怒了她。“你以为我是骗子？以为我说我能给五个奴隶，其实能给六个？我们在这里已经很久了，比任何人都久，在我们来的地方，这叫不敬，影鸟正在啁啾，啁啾……”她的声音渐渐消失，然后闭上一只眼睛，看着氏族酋长。“你会后悔的，”她说。

column1: “We don’t need any thralls. Maybe you can perform a ritual for us.”
column2: “我们不需要奴隶。也许你可以为我们举行一场仪式。”

column1: She turned her head and spoke to her crayfish, “Did you hear that, Nipper? They want a ritual. You can have the thralls.” Then she addressed us, “I need your magic. What can I do for you?”
column2: 她转过头对自己的小龙虾说：“听到了吗，钳子？他们想要一个仪式。奴隶们归你了。”然后她对我们说：“我需要你们的魔法。我能为你们做什么？”

column1: “Curse a neighbor.”
column2: “诅咒一个邻居。”

column1: We asked her instead to curse one of our neighbors.
column2: 我们转而请她诅咒我们的一个邻居。

column1: She answered,
column2: 她回答道：

column1: “You must have mistaken me for a different kind of woman. Good day.” She turned on her heel and left, muttering something to her crayfish.
column2: “你们一定认错人了。我不是那种女人。日安。”她转身就走，一边对自己的小龙虾咕哝着什么。

column1: She began to shake and drool. “Do you take me for a sorceress? No. I do not sell curses. Now, if my crayfish wants to send a curse at you, that’s a different story.”
column2: 她开始发抖流涎。“你们当我是女巫吗？不。我不卖诅咒。不过，要是我的小龙虾想朝你丢个诅咒，那就是另一回事了。”

column1: We were glad to see her leave.
column2: 我们很高兴看到她离开。

column1: “Bless our clan.”
column2: “祝福我们的氏族。”

column1: We asked her instead to bless the clan. She replied,
column2: 我们转而请她祝福氏族。她答道：

column1: “Yes, I can do that. It will take a while, but blessed you will be.”
column2: “行，我能做到。得花点时间，但你们一定会受到祝福。”

column1: She performed a \x02\x02lengthy overnight/days-long\x02 ritual involving burning \x02\x02fragrant/odd-smelling\x02 herbs, rows of clay effigies, and \x02\x02bleating sounds/chanting nonsense\x02. Finally, she thanked us for our clan magic, and said that our blessing was on its way.
column2: 她举行了一个 \x02\x02漫长彻夜/持续数日\x02 的仪式，燃烧 \x02\x02芬芳/气味古怪\x02 的草药、一排排陶俑，以及 \x02\x02咩咩声/胡言乱语的吟唱\x02。最后，她感谢我们提供了氏族魔法，并说祝福正在路上。

column1: “Cure our sick.”
column2: “治好我们的病人。”

column1: “Yes, I can do that. Nipper will dine well.”
column2: “行，我能做到。钳子会好好吃一顿。”

column1: First she performed a ritual involving \x02\x02rattling and yarn/dancing and howling\x02, taking a portion of our clan magic. column1: The Arming of Orlanth.
column2: 奥兰斯特武装。

column1: The god-talkers performed the well-known ceremony flawlessly. Heler’s ritual representative laced up Orlanth’s armor, and gave him his sword Humakt, a pair of swift javelins called Lightning, and the stout Thunderbolt spear.
column2: 神言者完美地执行了那个众所周知的仪式。赫勒的仪式代表给奥兰斯特系上铠甲，将他的剑胡马克特、一对名为雷电的迅捷标枪以及坚固的雷矛交给了他。

column1: Despite the preparation, they said that the ceremony did not go well.
column2: 尽管做了准备，但他们说仪式进行得并不顺利。

column1: Despite the preparation, the god-talkers said that the ceremony did not go well. The dog-hide thongs on Orlanth’s greaves broke early in the ritual, and everyone was filled with unease.
column2: 尽管做了准备，但神言者说仪式进行得并不顺利。奥兰斯特护胫上的狗皮绑带在仪式初期就断裂了，所有人都充满了不安。

column1: The Honing of Humakt.
column2: 磨砺胡马克特。

column1: god-talkers performed the Honing of Humakt ritual.
column2: 神言者举行了磨砺胡马克特仪式。

column1: Afterwards, even the grimmest Humakti wore a smile. The sword dance had gone flawlessly, and the only blood shed that which the ceremony called for.
column2: 之后，即便最阴郁的胡马克特信徒也露出了笑容。剑舞完美无缺，流出的血只有仪式所要求的那份。

column1: Despite the preparation, the god-talkers said that the ceremony did not go well. Under a flurry of blows, the ritual sword became bent.
column2: 尽管做了准备，但神言者说仪式进行得并不顺利。在一阵猛烈的打击下，仪式剑被折弯了。

column1: Hyalor’s Horsetaming.
column2: 海亚洛的驯马。

column1: god-talkers performed the story of Hyalor Horsebreaker.
column2: 神言者表演了海亚洛驯马师的故事。

column1: The god-talkers reenacted Hyalor’s rescue of a shattered creature from death, and how he befriended her. Horse and rider moved as one.
column2: 神言者重现了海亚洛从死亡中救出一个破碎造物，以及他如何与她成为朋友的故事。马与骑手合为一体。

column1: Despite the preparation, the god-talkers said that the ceremony did not go well. The horse did not heal well, and balked and whirled.
column2: 尽管做了准备，但神言者说仪式进行得并不顺利。那匹马伤势恢复不佳，不肯前进且原地打转。

column1: Ernalda’s Tapestry.
column2: 厄纳尔达的织锦。

column1: women performed the Ernalda’s Tapestry ritual.
column2: 女人们举行了厄纳尔达的织锦仪式。

column1: The women knew that as the Great Weaver, Ernalda can change the threads and change how the world is connected. They spent a week in the loom house, weaving a tapestry to unfurl once the riders arrived.
column2: 女人们知道，作为伟大织工，厄纳尔达能够改变丝线，改变世界相连的方式。她们在织机房待了一周，编织一幅织锦，待骑手抵达时展开。

column1: Despite the preparation, the women said that the ceremony did not go well.
column2: 尽管做了准备，但女人们说仪式进行得并不顺利。

column2: 回忆说，是混沌马维夫科班摧毁了凯夫的神谕所。

column1: god-talkers performed the Issaries Goldentongue ritual.

column1: Their call and response was flawless, even as the god-talkers switched between languages. The high point of the ritual was the marriage with Therelma, the “Mother Language.”
column2: 他们的唱和完美无缺，即使神言者在不同语言间切换。仪式的高潮是与“母亲语言”塞雷尔玛的结合。

column1: Despite the preparation, the god-talkers said that the ceremony did not go well. Their mouths went dry and after hours of chanting they began to mumble.
column2: 尽管做了准备，但神言者说仪式进行得并不顺利。他们的喉咙干涩，吟唱数小时后开始含糊不清。

column1: I know most of you are thinking about how to fight the Horse-Spawn, but there is always another way.
column2: 我知道你们大多数人在想如何对抗马裔，但总有另一条路。

column1: The Horse-Spawn know their animals well, perhaps even as well as Hyalor, who first tamed the horse.
column2: 马裔对自己的动物了如指掌，也许甚至不亚于第一个驯服马的海亚洛。

column1: If we hope to negotiate with people who don’t speak our language, we should have every advantage.
column2: 如果我们希望与不讲我们语言的人谈判，就应该拥有一切优势。

column1: Our forces are strong. With the help of the gods, we will prevail.
column2: 我们的力量强大。在神的帮助下，我们必将获胜。

column1: Our forces are not strong. If the gods can help us avoid fighting, we should consider it.
column2: 我们的力量不够强大。如果神能帮助我们避免战斗，我们应该考虑一下。

column1: The Arming of Orlanth is our clan patron’s ritual, and prepares us for any fight.
column2: 奥兰斯特武装是我们氏族主神的仪式，为我们应对任何战斗做好准备。

column1: Hyalor Horsebreaker serves our clan patron.
column2: 海亚洛驯马师服务于我们的氏族主神。

column1: Ernalda is our clan’s patron. We can weave her tapestry
column2: 厄纳尔达是我们氏族的庇护神。我们可以编织她的织锦

column1: When Bad King Urgrain was attacked by the Hopping Army, he had his god-talkers perform every ceremony that might help. They were unable to complete any of them, and most were devoured.
column2: 当恶王乌格兰遭到跳跃军队攻击时，他让自己的神言者执行每一个可能奏效的仪式。他们一个都无法完成，而且大都被吞噬了。

column1: If we master their horses, we master the riders.
column2: 如果我们掌控了他们的马，就掌控了骑手。

column1: Ernalda can help us find another way.
column2: 厄纳尔达能帮我们找到另一条路。

column1: Sharpen our war skills.
column2: 磨砺我们的战争技能。

column1: The Arming of Orlanth helps in a variety of situations.
column2: 奥兰斯特武装适用于多种情况。

column1: Let us prepare for peace.
column2: 让我们为和平做准备。

column1: Let us prepare for war.
column2: 让我们为战争做准备。

column1: We can weave a tapestry to help with healing.
column2: 我们可以编织一幅帮助疗伤的织锦。

column1: I still think “Draining the Barrel” would be a much better ritual.
column2: 我还是觉得“榨干酒桶”会是个好得多的仪式。

column1: Even with a week to perform a ritual, we can still fail.
column2: 即便有一周时间执行仪式，我们仍然可能失败。

column1: None of this will help us against a massive army of horse riders.
column2: 这些都对抵抗一支庞大的骑兵大军毫无帮助。

column1: We burst from concealment and took the Horse-Spawn by surprise. They tried charging, but their horses kept stepping into small holes or falling into concealed pits. Finally, they withdrew in frustration. But they had loosed clouds of blazing arrows, killing or wounding many.
column2: 我们从隐蔽处冲出，打了马裔一个措手不及。他们试图冲锋，但他们的马不断踩进小坑或跌入暗坑。最后，他们沮丧地撤退了。但他们放出了大片燃烧的箭矢，杀死或杀伤了许多人。

column1: We captured \x01@\x08 horses.
column2: 我们俘获了 \x01@\x08 马匹。

column1: We rushed the Horse-Spawn before they had gotten far into our tula. They were not able to bring their superior numbers to bear against us, and finally fell back. But they fought fiercely, and many fell beneath their flaming lances.
column2: 我们在马裔深入我们的领地之前就对他们发起冲击。他们无法将数量优势施加于我们，最终败退。但他们战斗凶猛，许多人在他们燃烧的长枪下倒下。

column1: The Horse-Spawn charged, showering us with fiery arrows. But \x02\x02they could not daunt us/Orlanth blew the shafts away\x02. The battle \x02\x02went on and on/raged for hours\x02 but finally the Horse-Spawn pulled back. Many of our warriors lay on the battlefield.
column2: 马裔发起冲锋，向我们洒下火焰箭矢。但 \x02\x02他们无法吓倒我们/奥兰斯特吹走了箭矢\x02。战斗 \x02\x02持续了又持续/激烈进行了数小时\x02 但最终马裔撤退了。我们许多战士倒在战场上。

column1: We shared other loot with the warriors we had hired.
column2: 我们将其他战利品与我们雇佣的战士们分享了。

column1: The other clans that helped us received some of their own.
column2: 其他帮助我们的部落也分到了他们自己的一份。

column1: After the battle, we found Theya trampled into the mud. She was still alive, but \x02\x02seriously/grievously\x02 \x02\x02injured/wounded\x02.
column2: 战斗结束后，我们发现西娅被踩进了泥里。她还活着，但 \x02\x02严重/致命\x02 \x02\x02受伤/负伤\x02。

column1: The Horse-Spawn seemed to know exactly where we had set up our ambush, perhaps alerted by \x02\x02hawks/sun spirits\x02. Avoiding the pits we had laboriously dug, they rampaged across our tula.
column2: 马裔似乎确切知道我们在何处设下埋伏，或许是 \x02\x02鹰隼/太阳精魂\x02告的密。它们避开了我们费力挖掘的陷坑，在我们的领地上横冲直撞。

column1: We fled in disarray, and the Horse-Spawn slew many and wounded many more before plundering us.
column2: 我们溃散而逃，马裔在劫掠之前杀伤甚众。

column1: We rushed the Horse-Spawn before they had gotten far into our tula. They turned and fled, but were only luring us into a trap. They wheeled their horses and charged into our advance, \x02\x02spearing us left and right/impaling our warriors on burning lances\x02. They galloped back to the tula, plundering as they went.
column2: 我们趁马裔尚未深入领地便发起冲锋。它们转身奔逃，但这只是诱我们入瓮。它们调转马头，向我们冲锋的队列撞来， \x02\x02左右穿刺/用燃烧骑枪刺穿我们的战士\x02。它们纵马驰回领地，沿途劫掠。

column1: As we fled in disarray, the Horse-Spawn slew many and wounded many more before plundering us.
column2: 我们溃散而逃时，马裔杀伤甚众，劫掠一空。

column1: The Horse-Spawn charged, showering us with fiery arrows. Many fell then and there. The battle \x02\x02went on and on/raged for hours\x02 until we could fight no more. Many of our warriors lay on the battlefield as the Horse-Spawn plundered the tula.
column2: 马裔发起冲锋，如雨的火箭倾泻而下。许多人当场倒下。战斗 \x02\x02持续不止/肆虐数小时\x02 ，直到我们无力再战。当马裔劫掠领地时，我们许多战士已倒卧沙场。

column1: They did not spare our fortifications.
column2: 它们连我们的防御工事也不放过。

column1: For the last few days, single cows have disappeared from your herds. Finally, your carls have spotted a small group of armed ducks who waddled onto the edge of the tula and made off with a cow.
column2: 最近几天，我们的畜群不断有零星牛只失踪。最终，自由民发现一小队武装鸭人摇摇摆摆地走到领地边缘，偷走了一头牛。

column1: We demanded satisfaction from the ducks.
column2: 我们要求鸭人给个说法。

column1: Free the ducks from their tribute obligation if they deal with this.
column2: 若鸭人自行处理此事，便免除他们的进贡义务。

column1: And there were no further incidents.
column2: 此后便再无此类事件发生。

column1: Ambush the rustlers.
column2: 伏击盗牛贼。

column1: Our warriors were ready the next time the ducks tried to steal a cow, and slew them without remorse.
column2: 下次鸭人试图偷牛时，我们的战士已严阵以待，毫不留情地将他们尽数斩杀。

column1: The ducks struck once more, taking two more cows without being spotted. After that, there were no more raids.
column2: 鸭人再次得手，在无人察觉的情况下又偷走两头牛。此后，便无更多袭击。

column1: We waited in ambush, but there was only one more raid, and we did not spot it.
column2: 我们设伏等待，但只发生了一次袭击，而且我们未能察觉。

column1: We waited in ambush, but there were no more raids.
column2: 我们设伏等待，但再未发生袭击。

column1: There were no more raids, though our warriors thought they heard muffled quacking.
column2: 再无袭击发生，不过战士们说似乎听到了隐约的嘎嘎声。

column1: Raid the ducks in retaliation.
column2: 报复性地袭击鸭人。

column1: We raided the ducks to show them we did not take cattle theft lightly.
column2: 我们袭击了鸭人，让他们明白我们绝不容忍偷牛之事。

column1: Needless to say, there were no more cattle raids afterwards.
column2: 不用说，此后便再无盗牛事件。

column1: Let things go for now.
column2: 暂且搁置此事。

column1: We decided to let matters sit.
column2: 我们决定暂不追究。

column1: There were no more raids for several weeks.
column2: 此后数周再无袭击。

column1: Our ancestors were displeased we had taken no action against their enemies.
column2: 我们的先祖因我们未对仇敌采取行动而不悦。

column1: It is never a good time to be robbed, but our herds are sufficient, so things could be worse.
column2: 被抢劫从来不是好事，但我们的畜群还算充足，所以情况还不算太糟。

column1: We must not stand for this. Our herds are dwindling, and every loss is a serious one.
column2: 我们绝不能容忍此事。我们的畜群正在缩减，每一次损失都非同小可。

column1: Even though they are just ducks, they might drive us off their home territory.
column2: 尽管他们只是鸭人，但也许会把我们从家园土地上赶走。

column1: Our forces are large enough to attack them, should we wish to.
column2: 若我们愿意，兵力足以攻击他们。

column1: If we raid the ducks, we release them from their obligation to pay tribute.
column2: 如果我们袭击鸭人，他们就不再需要向我们进贡了。

column1: Just like people, the ducks are unhappy paying tribute.
column2: 和人类一样，鸭人也不愿进贡。

column1: Just like people, the ducks are unhappy paying tribute. So far they have been honorable about it, however.
column2: 和人类一样，鸭人也不愿进贡。不过，至今他们还算守信。

column1: The beastfolk are our ancient enemies. We cannot ignore this slight.
column2: 兽人是我们的宿敌。我们不能忽视这次冒犯。

column1: At least the beastfolk are not our ancient enemies.
column2: 至少兽人并非我们的宿敌。

column1: I could just—ducks must, must… Those sneaky, no, thieves.
column2: 我简直可以——鸭人必须，必须……这些鬼鬼祟祟的，不，是贼！

column1: “Birds sing not because they have answers but because they have songs.”
column2: “鸟儿歌唱，不是因为有了答案，而是因为有了歌谣。”

column1: What is a cow or two between neighbors?
column2: 邻里之间，一两头牛算什么？

column1: Robbed by ducks! This is too funny!
column2: 被鸭人抢劫！这太好笑了！

column1: Our ancestors are beside themselves.
column2: 我们的先祖激动得难以自持。

column1: It has been about seven years since \x02\x02our attempt to create a tribe failed/we failed to make a tribe\x02. I think that’s long enough that we could try again.
column2: 大约自 \x02\x02我们创建氏族的尝试失败/我们未能创建氏族\x02以来，已过七年。我想时间足够长了，我们可以再试一次。

column1: We have enough wealth to give gifts.
column2: 我们已积累足够财富来赠送礼物。

column1: Odayla can fight off the predicted vermin for us, if we sacrifice and honor him.
column2: 奥代拉能为我们击退预言的害虫，如果我们献祭并尊崇他。

column1: The rats will eat more than we would spend learning how to get rid of them! When will we know how to fight off the pests that eat our grain?
column2: 老鼠吃掉的东西会比我们花在学习如何消灭它们的代价还要多！我们何时才能学会抵御那些糟蹋粮食的害虫？

column1: Our weaponthanes long for us to gain Humakt's blessings for them since the omens point to battle.
column2: 由于凶兆指向战斗，我们的武器领主渴望我们为他们获得胡马克特的祝福。

column1: The fighter's morale is poor this year. They would cheer up if we could learn secrets from Humakt, and ask the god's blessings in battle.
column2: 今年战士们的士气低落。如果我们能从胡马克特那里学到奥秘，并祈求神明在战斗中的祝福，他们就会振奋起来。

column1: We must believe the omens, and we must sacrifice to Urox to protect us from Chaos.
column2: 我们必须相信这些凶兆，必须向乌洛克斯献祭以保护我们免受混沌侵扰。

column1: Our only hope against Chaos this year is to learn Urox's blessings, and then sacrifice for them.
column2: 今年我们对混沌的唯一希望就是学习乌洛克斯的祝福，然后为此献祭。

column1: Uralda's Calf Blessing is crucial this year, if we want to keep up the numbers of our herds.
column2: 如果我们想保持牲畜的数量，乌拉尔达的牛犊祝福今年至关重要。

column1: Uralda could take care of a bad calving omen, if we knew the right way to ask.
column2: 乌拉尔达能消解糟糕的产犊凶兆，如果我们知道正确祈求的方式。

column1: Ask Uralda to restore the flow of milk to the cow's udders.
column2: 祈求乌拉尔达恢复母牛乳房的产奶量。

column1: Uralda would bless our cows' udders, if we knew the right way to ask her.
column2: 乌拉尔达会祝福我们母牛的乳房，如果我们知道正确祈求她的方式。

column1: Pigs are a safeguard against a thin food supply. We must ask Ernalda's blessing to keep the litters numerous.
column2: 猪是应对食物短缺的一道保障。我们必须祈求厄尔纳尔达的祝福，让猪仔保持数量众多。

column1: If we ask Ernalda how to make sure the pigs have large, healthy litters, she might teach us.
column2: 如果我们祈求厄尔纳尔达指点如何确保母猪产下大量健康的猪仔，她或许会教导我们。

column1: Our reputation is bound to suffer unless we sacrifice to the Knowing God and ask his blessing on our dealings with other clans.
column2: 如果我们不向全知之神献祭并祈求他对我们与其他氏族交往的祝福，我们的声誉必然会受损。

column1: Ask the Knowing God how we can keep our reputation in the face of bad omens. Then beseech him to help us do so.
column2: 祈求全知之神告诉我们如何在凶兆面前维护声誉。然后恳求他帮助我们做到。

column1: A clan without law is not a clan. Ask Lhankor Mhy's favor so that we can avoid legal bickerings.
column2: 没有法律的氏族不成其为氏族。祈求兰科·米的恩惠，这样我们就能避免法律纠纷。

column1: Don't start squabbling now, and prove the bad law omens correct! Sacrifice to Lhankor Mhy to find our way out of this mess.
column2: 现在不要开始争吵，以免证实糟糕的法律凶兆！向兰科·米献祭，找到摆脱这场混乱的出路。

column1: I think the bad omen about our ancestors means we should learn more divine mysteries.
column2: 我认为关于我们祖先的凶兆意味着我们应该学习更多神圣的奥秘。

column1: You can sacrifice all you want, Eurmal is still looking for our new ring members.
column2: 随你怎么献祭，尤拉玛尔仍在寻找我们新环的成员。

column1: We must sacrifice to our ancestors so that they, in turn, can strengthen our clan magic. Not a bad bargain at all!
column2: 我们必须向我们的祖先献祭，这样他们反过来就能强化我们氏族的魔法。这交易一点也不差！

column1: When Ernalda weeps, we must beware. Sacrifice soon, and learn a blessing, so that she will aid our crops and not blast them.
column2: 当厄尔纳尔达哭泣时，我们必须警惕。尽快献祭，学习一项祝福，这样她就会帮助我们的庄稼而不是毁掉它们。

column1: If the crops suffer, we suffer thrice-fold. Listen to what the god-talkers said, and honor Ernalda, right away!
column2: 如果庄稼遭殃，我们就会遭受三倍的痛苦。听从神言者的话，立即尊崇厄尔纳尔达！

column1: Maran Gor's blessings are not sweet and light. An active curse from her is horrific. Sacrifice, and learn something of the underside.
column2: 马兰·戈尔的祝福并不甜美温和。她施放的主动诅咒相当可怕。献祭吧，了解一些阴暗面。

column1: The god-talkers said to sacrifice to Maran Gor. I would rather not risk an earthquake, thank you, so let us honor her soon.
column2: 神言者说该向马兰·戈尔献祭。我可不想冒地震的风险，谢谢，所以我们尽快尊崇她吧。

column1: Don't forget to honor Odayla soon, lest he fulfill his warning and take away the bounty he gives us.
column2: 别忘了尽快尊崇奥代拉，免得他兑现警告，收回他赐予我们的猎物。

column1: Uralda asked us to learn more blessings. We should consider this a command, and be glad to honor her this way.
column2: 乌拉尔达要求我们学习更多祝福。我们应该把这视为命令，并且乐意以这种方式尊崇她。

column1: Our cattle are our very sustenance - we must learn more of Uralda's secrets this year, or go hungry later.
column2: 我们的牛群就是我们的生计——今年我们必须学习更多乌拉尔达的奥秘，否则日后就要挨饿。

column1: Urox gave us a request, an order cleverly diguised as a request. Sacrifice, and we can rest easy knowing that our war magic is safe.
column2: 乌洛克斯给了我们一个请求，一个巧妙伪装成请求的命令。献祭吧，我们就能安心，知道我们的战争魔法安然无恙。

column1: A sacrifice to Urox will keep our war magic strong. Failure to sacrifice may weaken it.
column2: 向乌洛克斯献祭将保持我们战争魔法强大。不献祭可能会削弱它。

column1: Our magic is low, but we must do our utmost to attempt a heroquest this year as the gods requested.
column2: 我们的魔法不足，但我们必须竭尽全力，在今年按神祇的要求尝试一次英雄任务。

column1: Our magic is adequate. We can try to enter the Godplane, as the Lightbringers requested, without too much fear.
column2: 我们的魔法尚可。我们可以尝试进入神界，正如光明使者们所请求的那样，不必太过恐惧。

column1: Our magic is strong. This is a good time to honor the Lightbringers and go on a heroquest.
column2: 我们的魔法强大。现在是尊崇光明使者并踏上英雄任务的好时机。

column1: Heroquests are always risky, yet when the Lightbringers themselves ask us to try, we cannot refuse.
column2: 英雄任务总是充满风险，但光明使者们亲自请求我们尝试时，我们无法拒绝。

column1: Sacrifice to Vinga, then let me go exploring. Or, if you won't send me out, at least sacrifice as the goddess requested.
column2: 向文加献祭，然后让我去探索。或者，如果你不派我出去，至少按女神所请求的那样献祭。

column1: Vinga's heart is beating loudly in her breast this year - sacrifice and explorations are in order.
column2: 今年文加的心在胸中大声跳动——献祭与探索正当时。

column1: The only way to get a blessing from the Wind Spirits is to ask them each year with a sacrifice.
column2: 从风灵那里获得祝福的唯一方式，是每年通过献祭向它们祈求。

column1: The gods always make me nervous.
column2: 神明总是让我紧张。

column1: Lhankor Mhy is the god of literacy - and we don't even have a shrine to him!
column2: 兰科·米是读写之神——我们甚至没有他的神龛！

column1: We should sacrifice to Lhankor Mhy so he will gift us with knowledge of the Literacy blessing.
column2: 我们应该向兰科·米献祭，这样他才会赐予我们读写祝福的知识。

column1: There are still many divine blessings we don't know how to obtain.
column2: 还有许多神圣祝福我们不知道如何获取。

column1: Seldom do memorial stones stand by the wayside, unless one kinsman raises them for another.
column2: “路边鲜有纪念石矗立，除非有族人替另一族人立起。”

column1: A farmer without a plow is like a warrior without a sword.
column2: “没有犁的农夫，如同没有剑的战士。”

column1: It's a quiet house that the Talking God never visits.
column2: “交流之神从不造访的屋子，是寂静的。”

column1: At a grey-bearded sage you should never laugh; often what the old say is wise.
column2: “切勿嘲笑灰胡须的智者；老人所言往往明智。”

column1: The milk of human kindness is nothing compared to Uralda's.
column2: “人类的仁爱之乳，与乌拉尔达的相比不值一提。”

column1: We should build more temples, then people will have to come here to worship.
column2: 我们应该建造更多神庙，这样人们就不得不来这里崇拜了。

column1: Sacrifices to Humakt will improve our luck in battle. If we build a shrine, we'll get some benefits on an ongoing basis.
column2: 向胡马克特献祭会改善我们在战斗中的运气。如果我们建一座神龛，就能持续获得一些好处。

column1: Sacrifices to Humakt will improve our luck in battle.
column2: 向胡马克特献祭会改善我们在战斗中的运气。

column1: Allow me to point out that we are hard-pressed to afford our temples. We must focus on trade to improve our ability to worship.
column2: 请允许我指出，我们已难以负担现有神庙的费用。必须专注于贸易，以提升我们崇拜的能力。

column1: We don't have a shrine to Issaries! Our prosperity and friendships will suffer.
column2: 我们连伊萨里斯的神龛都没有！我们的繁荣与友谊将遭受损失。

column1: Enlarging our Issaries shrine would let us call on the Talking God for more of his blessings.
column2: 扩建伊萨里斯的神龛，我们就能召唤交流之神赐予更多祝福。

column1: A temple to Elmal will shine glory upon all of Dragon Pass.
column2: 为埃尔马尔建造一座神庙，将使荣耀照耀整个龙之隘口。

column1: If we don't bless the Earth Mother, how can we hope that she will bless us?
column2: 如果我们不祝福大地母亲，怎能指望她祝福我们？

column1: Custom requires that we have at least a shrine to Lhankor Mhy.
column2: 习俗要求我们至少要有一座兰科·米的神龛。

column1: If we enlarged our shrine to Lhankor Mhy, he would share more of his knowledge with us.
column2: 如果我们扩建兰科·米的神龛，他会与我们分享更多知识。

column1: Where is Orlanth's shrine?
column2: 奥兰斯的神龛在哪里？

column1: Sacrifices are due, first to Orlanth, King of the Gods, then to Ernalda, his wife. Then to all the other great gods.
column2: 献祭应当先献给奥兰斯，众神之王，然后是他的妻子厄尔纳尔达。之后再献给所有其他伟大神明。

column1: My goddess's needs are few, and her gifts come bearing spears.
column2: 我的女神所求不多，但她的赠礼带着长矛而来。

column1: Lhankor Mhy is the god of literacy.
column2: 兰科·米是读写之神。

column1: It is always a good idea to keep the gods happy.
column2: 让神明开心总是一个好主意。

column1: Did you know the people are worshipping a rock?
column2: 你知道吗，人们正在崇拜一块石头？

column1: I don't see why we can't build a shrine to Eurmal.
column2: 我不明白为什么我们不能为尤尔马尔建一座神龛。

column1: If we want to enact a heroquest, our chances would be better if we had a Trickster on the ring. We could then allocate more magic to quests.
column2: 如果我们想进行一次英雄任务，要是长老会里有一位恶作剧者，我们的成功机会会更大。这样我们就可以分配更多魔法用于任务。

column1: Before we can succeed at founding a tribe, we need to perform the "Making of the Storm Tribe" heroquest.
column2: 在成功建立一个部落之前，我们需要进行“风暴部落的创立”英雄任务。

column1: By reenacting the "Making of the Storm Tribe" myth, we will improve our standing with all the other clans.
column2: 通过重演“风暴部落的创立”神话，我们将提升与其他所有氏族的关系。

column1: Our clan magic is poor.
column2: 我们的氏族魔法很贫弱。

column1: Our clan magic is seriously depleted.
column2: 我们的氏族魔法严重耗尽。

column1: Ride washed and fed to the moot, even if you're not well dressed.
column2: “骑着洗净喂饱的坐骑去议会，哪怕你穿得并不体面。”

column1: Cattle die. Kings die. But a tribe lives forever.
column2: “牛会死。王会死。但部落永存。”

column1: This is a perfect opportunity to profit.
column2: 这是个获利的好机会。

column1: Will the next king remember any of this?
column2: 下一位国王会记得这些吗？

column1: If we support our friends now, they will remember us at the next election of a king.
column2: 如果我们现在支持我们的朋友，下届国王选举时他们会记得我们。

column1: Justice is best served by weighing each case.
column2: 最好的正义是权衡每一个案例。

column1: If we support those who don't like us, we may sway their opinions.
column2: 如果我们支持那些不喜欢我们的人，或许能改变他们的看法。

column1: There's really no bad choices.
column2: 真的没有坏选择。

column1: There's really no best choice. Or worst choice.
column2: 真的没有最好或最坏的选择。

column1: The only good part of a moot is the war-whooping.
column2: 议会唯一的好处就是战吼。

column1: Choices like this are why we should never have joined a tribe.
column2: 这样的选择正是我们当初不该加入部落的原因。

column1: We should repay our friends and support them.
column2: 我们应该回报朋友，支持他们。

column1: If only there were some way we could make everybody happy...
column2: 要是有什么办法能让每个人都开心就好了……

column1: With our good luck in relations this year, we can take whatever policy we like and still retain respect.
column2: 凭借今年在关系上的好运，我们可以采取任何政策，同时仍能保留尊敬。

column1: A sacrifice to Lhankor Mhy would help us retain our influence at the moot this year.
column2: 向兰科·米献祭会有助于我们今年在议会中保持影响力。

column1: Sacrifice to Lhankor Mhy to learn how to keep our good reputation in the face of this year's bad omen.
column2: 向兰科·米献祭，以学会如何面对今年的凶兆而保持良好声誉。

column1: If we had assigned magic to mysteries, then we could learn how to improve relations. Now we must just live with this year's bad omens.
column2: 如果我们曾分配魔法给奥秘，就能学会如何改善关系。现在，我们只能忍受今年的凶兆。

column1: We really can't make everyone happy. We need to pick.
column2: 我们真的无法让每个人都开心。必须做出选择。

column1: We may not be able to hold the throne forever.
column2: 我们可能无法永远持有王位。

column1: No clan can hold the throne forever.
column2: 没有氏族能永远持有王位。

column1: It's too soon after our last heroquest. Wait until next year.
column2: 距离上次英雄任务太近了。等到明年再说。

column1: We heroquested in the last couple years. Wait until later.
column2: 我们在过去几年里做过英雄任务。等晚些时候再说。

column1: We prepared for a quest during Sacred Time, and the omens are good. Our chances for success are as good as they'll ever be.
column2: 我们在神圣时间期间为任务做了准备，而且预兆良好。我们的成功机会已经尽可能好了。

column1: Although we prepared during Sacred Time, I think the omens are against our success in a quest.
column2: 虽然我们在神圣时间期间做了准备，但我认为预兆不利于我们任务的成功。

column1: We prepared for a quest during Sacred Time. Our chance of success is good.
column2: 我们在神圣时间期间为任务做了准备。成功机会不错。

column1: Although we haven't performed a heroquest this year, we didn't make the ritual preparations during Sacred Time, and we could easily fail.
column2: 虽然今年我们尚未举行英雄任务，但我们在神圣时间期间没有做好仪式准备，很容易失败。

column1: Seven different gods have representatives on our clan ring, which will make our heroquesting easier.
column2: 七个不同的神祇在我们氏族议会有代表，这将使我们的英雄任务更容易。

column1: We don't have seven different deities represented on our clan ring. This will make heroquesting harder.
column2: 我们没有七个不同神祇在我们氏族议会得到代表。这将使英雄任务更困难。

column1: Everyone knows that in the "Orlanth and Aroka" myth, Orlanth defeated drought. Unfortunately, no one knows the exact details.
column2: 人人都知道在“奥兰斯与阿罗卡”神话中，奥兰斯击败了干旱。不幸的是，无人知晓确切细节。

column1: Orlanth defeated Aroka, the Blue Dragon, to relieve a drought. We can do the same.
column2: 奥兰斯击败了蓝龙阿罗卡，以解除干旱。我们也能做到同样的事。

column1: We shouldn't heroquest now unless we have a crisis.
column2: 我们现在不应进行英雄任务，除非面临危机。

column1: Questing is always difficult. But until we recover from our last quest, it will be even harder.
column2: 任务总是艰难的。但在我们从上次任务中恢复之前，将会更加艰难。

column1: The quester must be tough enough to survive the rigors of a heroquest, and wise enough to perform the steps correctly. And ideally, a hero.
column2: 探索者必须足够坚韧才能承受英雄任务的严酷，并且足够智慧以正确执行步骤。而且，理想情况下，应是一位英雄。

column1: By succeeding at "Making of the Storm Tribe," we can enhance our stature with all the other clans.
column2: 通过成功完成“风暴部落的建立”，我们可以提升在所有其他氏族中的地位。

column1: With our favorable omens this year, we could consider attempting a heroquest.
column2: 鉴于今年我们有吉兆，可以考虑尝试一次英雄任务。

column1: Chaos is everywhere. We must quest to put it down.
column2: 混沌无处不在。我们必须通过任务来压制它。

column1: A lesser clan would fear to heroquest now. But we're above that.
column2: 一个弱小的氏族现在会害怕进行英雄任务。但我们已经超越那个层次。

column1: Let me lead a heroquest.
column2: 让我领导一次英雄任务。

column1: A heroquest would be harder now, but that would just increase the glory of success!
column2: 现在英雄任务会更困难，但这只会增加成功的荣耀！

column1: Questing is the solution to most of our problems.
column2: 执行任务是解决我们大多数问题的办法。

column1: We need to learn more of Orlanth's myths, so we can recreate them with a heroquest and gain kingship and true power.
column2: 我们需要了解更多奥兰斯的神话，以便通过英雄任务重现它们，从而获得王权和真正的力量。

column1: Orlanth's quests are the source of kingship and true power.
column2: 奥兰斯的任务是王权和真正力量的源泉。

column1: Not now.
column2: 现在不行。

column1: I like the quests where I get to dress up in costumes.
column2: 我喜欢那些我可以穿上戏服的任务。

column1: The gods don't favor those who visit the Other Side too often.
column2: 神明不会眷顾那些过于频繁拜访彼岸的人。

column1: Crossing to the Other Side and repeating the actions of our gods is the best way to honor them.
column2: 跨越到彼岸并重现我们神明的行为，是尊崇他们的最佳方式。

column1: We have no weaponthanes. We can't protect ourselves, let alone raid our neighbors.
column2: 我们没有武器领主。我们无法保护自己，更不用说劫掠邻居了。

column1: We don't have any weaponthanes. How can we expect to protect ourselves, much less raid our neighbors?
column2: 我们没有任何武器领主。我们怎能指望保护自己，更不用说劫掠邻居了？

column1: We are too weak to even think about raiding.
column2: 我们太过弱小，连考虑劫掠都不行。

column1: We could raid, and lose, and hurt, and die.
column2: 我们可能劫掠，然后失败、受伤、死亡。

column1: We have enough weaponthanes to go raiding.
column2: 我们有足够的武器领主去进行劫掠。

column1: Our forces are strong enough to go raiding now.
column2: 我们的力量现在足够强大，可以去劫掠了。

column1: Send a few women as auxiliaries. They can tend to the wounded and exhort the cowardly.
column2: 派几个女性作为辅助者。她们可以照料伤员，激励怯懦者。

column1: owe us a favor. We could ask for help in a raid, if we care to admit how weak we've gotten.
column2: 欠我们一个人情。如果我们愿意承认自己变得多么弱小，可以在劫掠时请求帮助。

column1: If we ask an ally to send fighters, we admit how we weak we are. And then we will owe them a favor.

column1: These moments in the Kero Fin shrine are some of the proudest moments of my life.
column2: 在凯罗·芬神殿的这些时刻，是我人生中最自豪的时刻之一。

column1: Lhankor Mhy's knowledge of reading and writing gives us the most benefit.
column2: 兰科·莫的读写知识给我们带来最大益处。

column1: We must ask Lhankor Mhy how to perform the Literacy magic.
column2: 我们必须向兰科·莫请教如何举行读写魔法。

column1: We don't need to ask about our enemies. We already know it's the elves!
column2: 我们无需打听敌人。我们早已知晓，就是精灵！

column1: We needn't ask about our enemies. We already know it's the undead!
column2: 我们无需打听敌人。我们早已知晓，就是亡灵！

column1: Ask who threatens us.
column2: 询问谁在威胁我们。

column1: We should find out what others think of us.
column2: 我们应该弄清楚别人如何看待我们。

column1: We should try to learn Divination.
column2: 我们应该尝试学习占卜。

column1: We should find out how strong others are.
column2: 我们应该查明其他人的实力有多强。

column1: Ask Lhankor Mhy to provide Clan Lore. That way, we can identify any treasures we may obtain.
column2: 请求兰科·米赐予氏族知识。这样我们就能识别可能获得的任何宝物。

column1: Lhankor Mhy can warn about our foes.
column2: 兰科·米可以警示我们关于敌人的情况。

column1: The Knowing God is always a bit stingy with his knowledge, if you ask me.
column2: 要我说，全知之神在知识上总是有点吝啬。

column1: Our reputation is bound to suffer unless we ask for a blessing on our dealings with other clans.
column2: 除非我们请求祝福与其他氏族的往来，否则我们的名声必然受损。

column1: Ask how we can save our reputation in the face of bad omens.
column2: 询问如何在面对恶兆时挽救我们的名声。

column1: Sacrifice so that we can avoid legal bickerings within the clan.
column2: 献祭以避开氏族内部的法律纠纷。

column1: Don't argue over this! We must sacrifice and find our way out of the mess we made with these petty disputes.
column2: 别为这个争吵了！我们必须献祭，找出摆脱这些琐碎争端所造成困局的办法。

column1: Don't send Uralda's daughters to the Unholy Trio.
column2: 不要把乌拉尔达的女儿们送给邪恶三神。

column1: Not even Eurmal would have anything to do with Malia.
column2: 就算是尤尔马尔也不会跟玛利亚扯上关系。

column1: How can we think of offering anything to a Chaos goddess?!
column2: 我们怎么能想到向混沌女神献祭任何东西？！

column1: Are you crazy?
column2: 你疯了吗？

column1: Once you propitiate Malia, you can't stop, or she will curse you.
column2: 一旦你安抚了玛利亚，就不能停下，否则她会诅咒你。

column1: Malia never deals fairly.
column2: 玛利亚从不公平交易。

column1: Why are we even discussing this?
column2: 我们到底为什么在讨论这个？

column1: Sacrifice to Malia is risky, but effective.
column2: 向玛利亚献祭有风险，但也有效。

column1: The good thing about Malia is that hardly anyone talks to her, so she will certainly answer us.
column2: 玛利亚的好处是几乎没人跟她说话，所以她肯定会回应我们。

column1: Malia can heal all our sick, so this could be a cheap way to improve health.
column2: 玛利亚能治愈我们所有的病患，所以这可能是改善健康的一个廉价办法。

column1: We have never given worship to the enemy gods, and this is no time to start.
column2: 我们从未崇拜过敌对神祇，现在也不是开这个头的时候。

column1: We may have occasionally propitiated enemy gods, but it's not a good idea.
column2: 我们偶尔也许安抚过敌对神祇，但这并不是个好主意。

column1: Not Malia!
column2: 不要玛利亚！

column1: Ernalda rules fertility, but her sister, Maran Gor, rules the dark world under our fields.
column2: 厄尔纳尔达掌管丰饶，而她的姐姐玛兰·戈尔则掌管我们田地下的黑暗世界。

column1: Maran Gor can shake the underpinnings of the earth.
column2: 玛兰·戈尔能动摇大地的根基。

column1: Odayla's friendship with Yinkin, god of alynxes, will keep our grain supplies safe.
column2: 奥达伊拉与艾林克斯猫之神因金之间的友谊，能确保我们的谷物储备安全。

column1: If it's war we intend, we must take ourselves to a real temple, not this mess of snares and bones.
column2: 如果我们想要战争，就必须前往一座真正的神庙，而不是这个布满陷阱和骨头的烂摊子。

column1: Before we knew how to farm, Odayla taught us to hunt. Every sacrifice to him increases our skill.
column2: 在学会耕种之前，奥达伊拉教会了我们狩猎。每次向他献祭都能提升我们的技能。

column1: Sacrifice so that our hunters can find game this year, in spite of the bad omens.
column2: 献祭，这样我们的猎人就能在今年找到猎物，尽管有恶兆。

column1: If we knew more blessings, we could avoid bad hunting this year.
column2: 如果我们知道更多祝福，就能避免今年狩猎不利。

column1: Ask the god to chase off the vermin for us.
column2: 请求神明为我们驱赶害虫。

column1: Learning how to get rid of rats and other creatures is wealth well spent.
column2: 学会如何清除老鼠和其他生物，这笔开销很值得。

column1: The best blessing of Orlanth Thunderous is the rain he brings to our crops.
column2: 雷鸣者奥兰茨最好的祝福是他带给庄稼的雨水。

column1: The best blessing of Orlanth Thunderous is his rain. We should learn this blessing.
column2: 雷鸣者奥兰茨最好的祝福是他的雨水。我们应该学习这个祝福。

column1: Orlanth's Rain blessing will counteract the bad omen for rain for the crops.
column2: 奥兰茨的雨之祝福将抵消影响作物雨水的恶兆。

column1: Orlanth could teach us how to make sure our crops receive enough rain.
column2: 奥兰茨可以教会我们如何确保庄稼获得足够的雨水。

column1: Surely we can do better than to sacrifice to a rock.
column2: 我们肯定能做得比向一块石头献祭更好。

column1: Tarard Riel may be only a rock, but he is very old, and has lived here all his life.
column2: 塔拉德·里尔也许只是一块岩石，但他非常古老，而且一生都住在这里。

column1: Let's give him some pebbles.
column2: 我们给他一些小石子吧。

column1: As a rock, Tarard Riel is distant kin of Ernalda the Earth Mother.
column2: 作为一块岩石，塔拉德·里尔是大地母亲厄尔纳尔达的远亲。

column1: Our shrine already provides Tarard Riel's blessing. We don't need to sacrifice.
column2: 我们的神龛已经提供塔拉德·里尔的祝福了。我们不需要献祭。

column1: We could use more food; ask Uralda to keep our cows from running dry.
column2: 我们需要更多食物；请求乌拉尔达让我们的母牛不要干奶。

column1: You can never have too many cows. Ask Uralda for the Calf Blessing.
column2: 牛再多也不嫌多。向乌拉尔达请求小牛祝福。

column1: All of Uralda's blessings are precious. We should sacrifice to learn more of them.
column2: 乌拉尔达的所有祝福都很宝贵。我们应该献祭以学习更多祝福。

column1: Uralda is a fine goddess. Feed her well, and listen to her advice.
column2: 乌拉尔达是一位好女神。好好供奉她，听从她的建议。

column1: This is women's magic.
column2: 这是女人的魔法。

column1: I know some fine magic that makes milk go bad.
column2: 我知道一些让牛奶变质的巧妙魔法。

column1: Ask for a Calf Blessing this year, to keep up the numbers of our herds.
column2: 今年请求小牛祝福，以维持我们牧群的数量。

column1: Humbly ask how to avoid a bad calving year.
column2: 谦卑地询问如何避免一个产犊不佳的年份。

column1: A proper sacrifice will restore the flow of milk in the cow's udders.
column2: 恰当的献祭能恢复母牛乳房中的奶水。

column1: If we ask, we learn the mystery of proper rites for our cows' milk.
column2: 如果我们请求，就能学到为我们母牛的乳汁举行恰当仪式的奥秘。

column1: We should definitely sacrifice to Urox. Because when we do, the Uroxi beat me up less. Half the time, anyway.
column2: 我们绝对应该向乌洛克斯献祭。因为每次献祭后，乌洛希揍我的次数就少一些。至少一半时间是这样。

column1: For fighting Chaos, Urox cannot be beat. Unfortunately, Urox does not just fight Chaos.
column2: 在对抗混沌方面，乌洛克斯无人能敌。不幸的是，乌洛克斯不仅仅对抗混沌。

column1: Protection from Chaos is good. Unthinking fury is... unwise.
column2: 抵御混沌是好事。但盲目的狂怒……不太明智。

column1: We're wasting time talking when we could be giving Urox some cows!
column2: 我们在废话上浪费时间，不如直接给乌洛克斯献祭几头牛！

column1: Sacrifice for protection from Chaos, soon, before it get worse!
column2: 尽快献祭以获得混沌防护，免得情况变得更糟！

column1: We must learn to detect Chaos better, and then sacrifice for that gift.
column2: 我们必须学会更好地侦测混沌，然后为这个天赋献祭。

column1: We shouldn't be sacrificing to a mere slip of a goddess.
column2: 我们不该向一位微不足道的女神献祭。

column1: With Vinga to inspire some of our women to fight, we will be stronger in battle.
column2: 有了温加来激励我们的一些妇女去战斗，我们在战斗中就会更强大。

column1: Ask Vinga for her Pathfinder blessing, then send out an exploring party.
column2: 向温加请求她的寻路者祝福，然后派出探险队。

column1: When we learn the Pathfinder blessing, we'll be able to send more exploring parties.
column2: 当我们学会寻路者祝福后，就能派出更多探险队了。

column1: I prefer women with long hair.
column2: 我更喜欢长发女人。

column1: I prefer women with short hair.
column2: 我更喜欢短发女人。

column1: If we go exploring this year, we must sacrifice first.
column2: 如果我们今年要外出探险，必须先献祭。

column1: We could learn the right blessing for exploration, if we are lucky.
column2: 如果运气好，我们能学到适合探险的祝福。

column1: The drawback to having a shrine to Vinga is that our women are less fertile.
column2: 为温加建一座神龛的缺点是，我们的妇女生育能力会降低。

column1: Our shrine to Vinga already provides us with her blessings.
column2: 我们对温加的神殿已经为我们带来了她的祝福。

column1: Vinga can grant us the magic which makes the women feel confident fighting at my side.
column2: 温加能赐予我们魔法，让女性们有信心在我身边作战。

column1: We're a Peace Clan. We don't want to encourage the women to fight.
column2: 我们是和平氏族。我们不希望鼓励女性去战斗。

column1: The drawback to sacrificing to Vinga is that our women would become less fertile.
column2: 向温加献祭的缺点是，我们的女性会变得不那么肥沃。

column1: These holy spirits can teach us the powers of Orlanth's winds.
column2: 这些圣灵可以教我们奥兰斯之风的力量。

column1: Uh... yes.
column2: 呃……是的。

column1: These spirits understand that all is in motion.
column2: 这些灵魂明白万物皆动。

column1: The Wind Spirits say they can help me bargain with other clans if we sacrifice to the Seeing Wind.
column2: 风灵说，如果我们向“预见之风”献祭，它们能帮我们与其他氏族谈判。

column1: These little wind spirits won't require sacrifices as large as those we'd give to greater gods.
column2: 这些小小的风灵需要的祭品，不会像我们献给大神的那样庞大。

column1: The spirits from the holy mountain honor us by their presence. We deserve to be king.
column2: 来自圣山的灵魂以他们的到场为荣。我们理应成为王。

column1: Don't you remember me saying that exploring Kero Fin would pay off?
column2: 你不记得我说过探索凯罗·芬会有回报吗？

column1: Flighty little things.
column2: 轻浮的小东西。

column1: The Wind Spirits aren't as powerful as Humakt, but they can certainly help us scout our enemies.
column2: 风灵没有胡马克特强大，但它们肯定能帮我们侦察敌人。

column1: When Ernalda weeps, we must beware. Learn a blessing, so that she will aid our crops and not blast them.
column2: 当厄娜尔达哭泣时，我们必须警惕。学习一个祝福，这样她会帮助我们的作物，而不是摧毁它们。

column1: Part of our clan magic is devoted to mysteries, so sacrificing for Mysteries is liable to be successful.
column2: 我们氏族魔法的一部分用于奥秘，所以为奥秘献祭很可能会成功。

column1: I think... no wait, we already... but we could... the gods don't always.
column2: 我想……不，等等，我们已经……但我们可以……神明并不总是。

column1: Sacrificing only gives us magic for a year, but we have more flexibility than building shrines or temples.
column2: 献祭只能给我们一年的魔法，但比建造神殿或神庙更灵活。

column1: Too bad our clan magic is so low. We will have to sacrifice more to make up for it.
column2: 可惜我们的氏族魔法太低了。我们得献祭更多来弥补。

column1: Our clan magic is strong enough to help attract the attention of the gods.
column2: 我们的氏族魔法足够强大，能吸引神明的注意。

column1: We don't have enough food, so we'll have to conduct an emergency slaughter.
column2: 我们没有足够的食物，所以必须进行紧急屠宰。

column1: We may not have enough food until the harvest comes in, so we might want to conduct an emergency slaughter.
column2: 我们可能撑不到收获就有足够的食物，所以也许该进行紧急屠宰。

column1: We should have enough food, so there's no need for an emergency slaughter.
column2: 我们应该有足够的食物，所以不需要紧急屠宰。

column1: And we're definitely short on cows.
column2: 而且我们确实缺牛。

column1: Our herders routinely slaughter livestock, but they try to keep the herds as large as possible.
column2: 我们的牧人平时也会屠宰牲畜，但他们尽量保持畜群尽可能庞大。

column1: Horse is pretty tasty, you know.
column2: 马肉挺好吃的，你知道。

column1: What if we slaughter too many? Our herds would never recover.
column2: 万一我们杀得太多呢？我们的畜群就再也恢复不过来了。

column1: If you'd listened to me earlier, we wouldn't be in this fix.
column2: 要是你早点听我的，我们就不会落到这步田地。

column1: Whatever we do, don't slaughter horses for food.
column2: 不管怎样，别杀马当食物。

column1: I'd be happy to kill as many animals as you'd like.
column2: 你想杀多少我都乐意。

column1: We're short on cows.
column2: 我们缺牛。

column1: I'm afraid we'll have to slaughter animals now.
column2: 恐怕我们得现在就宰杀动物了。

column1: We might run out of food if we don't slaughter a few animals now.
column2: 如果我们现在不宰杀一些动物，可能会耗尽食物。

column1: I don't see the need for an emergency slaughter.
column2: 我看不出有什么必要紧急屠宰。

column1: We can slaughter some animals, if we must, to make up for the poor barley harvest.
column2: 如果必须的话，我们可以宰杀一些动物来弥补大麦的歉收。

column1: We can slaughter some animals, if we must, to make up for the poor wheat harvest.
column2: 如果必须的话，我们可以宰杀一些动物来弥补小麦的歉收。

column1: Hunting will be good, why do we need to slaughter extra animals?
column2: 狩猎会很好，为什么需要额外宰杀动物？

column1: The game is scarce this year. Slaughter some animals so we have enough meat.
column2: 今年的猎物稀少。宰杀一些动物，这样我们才有足够的肉。

column1: Do not kill the cows! We can expect a multitude of calves this year.
column2: 别杀牛！今年我们可以期待很多牛犊。

column1: Slaughter anything but cows. The poor calving this year means we must hoard our cattle herds.
column2: 什么都能杀，但别杀牛。今年产犊差，我们必须保住牛群。

column1: Killing some of our herds will make up for the poor milking this year.
column2: 宰杀一部分牲畜能弥补今年产奶量低的问题。

column1: We must learn the blessings so we can build a shrine!
column2: 我们必须学习祝福，才能建造神殿！

column1: By all means, we should build a shrine!
column2: 无论如何，我们应该建一座神殿！

column1: People will come from other clans to worship when we build a temple.
column2: 其他氏族的人会来朝拜，当我们建造神庙时。

column1: When we build a great temple, we will be renowned throughout Dragon Pass.
column2: 当我们建起大神殿，我们将在龙隘闻名遐迩。

column1: As temples go, Odayla's are simple. But there's strength in this simplicity.
column2: 就神庙而言，奥达拉的很简单。但这种简单中有力量。

column1: Don't even think about getting rid of this temple!
column2: 想都别想拆掉这座神庙！

column1: Send
column2: 派遣

column1: to trade for goods so we can afford a great temple.
column2: 去交易货物，这样我们才能建得起大神殿。

column1: to improve our relations with our neighbors. Then they will be willing to come worship here, and we can support a great temple.
column2: 以改善我们与邻邦的关系。然后他们会愿意来这里朝拜，我们就能维持一座大神殿。

column1: We must keep our great temple. Skimp somewhere else.
column2: 我们必须保住大神殿。其他地方省省吧。

column1: How will Elmal guard the stead without a place in our tula?
column2: 如果没有在我们领地里的场所，埃尔马尔如何守卫家园？

column1: A warrior needs a sword. Our clan needs a temple to Humakt.
column2: 战士需要剑。我们的氏族需要一座胡马克特的神庙。

column1: Odayla? We need a temple to Humakt if we wish to avoid sacrificing ourselves on our the blades of our enemies.
column2: 奥达拉？如果我们不想在敌人的刀刃上牺牲自己，我们需要一座胡马克特的神庙。

column1: Like other weapons, Uroxi have their uses. But don't confuse anger with power.
column2: 像其他武器一样，尤洛克斯追随者有他们的用途。但别把愤怒和力量混为一谈。

column1: A shrine to the Talking God is a great bargain.
column2: 一座交流之神的神殿就很划算了。

column1: The bigger the temple, the more profitable our market.
column2: 神庙越大，我们的市场就越有利可图。

column1: Just remember, we're currently devoting
column2: 记住，我们目前正在投入

column1: I don't see the wisdom in devoting our resources to the Talking God.
column2: 我看不出把资源投入交流之神有什么明智之处。

column1: It's unprecedented for a clan of our stature to be without a shrine to Lhankor Mhy!
column2: 像我们这样地位的氏族却没有兰科·米的神殿，这是前所未有的！

column1: It goes without saying that we should enlarge our temple.
column2: 不言而喻，我们应该扩建我们的神庙。

column1: Our temple is a veritable library, a treasure trove of information. Don't even think of reducing its size!
column2: 我们的神庙是一座名副其实的图书馆，是信息的宝库。想都别想缩小它！

column1: If we must have a shrine to Urox, place it downwind.
column2: 如果必须有尤洛克斯的神殿，就把它建在下风处。

column1: In the Darkness, Odayla helped keep us all alive. If we thank him with a temple, he will bless our hunts now.
column2: 在黑暗时代，奥达拉曾帮我们所有人活下来。如果我们用一座神庙感谢他，他会祝福我们的狩猎。

column1: Odayla has blessed us. We owe him thanks.
column2: 奥达拉保佑了我们。我们欠他一份谢意。

column1: People joke about the "Storm Bull" behind my back. But who's stupid? Stupid is not having a shrine to Urox when Chaos is everywhere.
column2: 人们背后拿“风暴公牛”打趣。但谁傻？当混沌无处不在时却没有尤洛克斯的神殿，那才傻。

column1: Maran Gor is a terrible goddess, but she can bless our crops whenever blood is shed in our fields. It doesn't have to be our blood...
column2: 玛兰·戈尔是一位可怕的女神，但只要我们的田地上有鲜血流淌，她就能祝福我们的庄稼。这血不一定得是我们的……

column1: A man should not be too wise. You lead the richest life when you know just enough.
column2: “人不该过于睿智。懂个差不多，日子才过得最富足。”

column1: We really need at least a shrine to Chalana Arroy. It will provide magic that will keep everyone healthier.
column2: 我们至少需要一座查拉娜·阿罗伊的神殿。它能提供让所有人更健康的魔法。

column1: Enlarging our shrine would make my job easier.
column2: 扩大我们的神殿能让我工作更轻松。

column1: I hope you're not thinking of supporting only a shrine.
column2: 我希望你不是只打算支持一座神龛。

column1: The White Lady gives no rings, but her gifts are more generous than any warrior-leader's.
column2: 白女士不赐戒指，但她的馈赠比任何战士首领都慷慨。

column1: A healing shrine could help after battle.
column2: 一座治疗神殿能在战后派上用场。
